call: youngest son of Ham (ancestor of the Canaanites)
introduce: Canaan was the youngest of the four sons of Ham, Noah's son, and is recorded in Ham's genealogy as the ancestor of the Canaanite peoples. He is regarded as the forefather of the various tribes that settled in the land of Canaan in the ancient Near East.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Ham and was a grandson of Noah (Genesis 10:6). The border of the Canaanites extended from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha (Genesis 10:19).
event: After Ham saw the nakedness of Noah and went outside and told his two brothers, Noah awoke from his wine and learned what his youngest son had done to him, and he said that Canaan was to be cursed and be a servant of servants to his brothers (Genesis 9:22-25). Noah also said that Canaan would be the servant of Shem and the servant of Japheth (Genesis 9:26-27).

introduce: Gatam was a son of Eliphaz, the son of Esau, and thus a grandson of Esau. He is recorded as a son of Eliphaz in the genealogy of the Edomites and is listed among the chiefs descended from Eliphaz in the land of Edom.
lifetime: He is named as one of the sons of Eliphaz, the son of Esau (Genesis 36:11). He is also mentioned as one of the sons of Eliphaz in the genealogy of Chronicles (1 Chronicles 1:36).
event: He appears as one of the persons living in the land of Edom who are classified as chiefs of Edom as descendants of Eliphaz (Genesis 36:16).

introduce: Gadi is a figure who appears in 2 Kings; he was the father of Menahem, king of northern Israel.
lifetime: Gadi is recorded as the father of Menahem, king of northern Israel (2 Kings 15:14). The Bible gives no specific record of his birth, death, or life in general.
event: No achievement or event of his own is recorded; he is mentioned as the father of his son Menahem when Menahem went up from Tirzah to Samaria, struck down Shallum, and became king (2 Kings 15:14).

직업/직위: clan chief of the tribe of Manasseh

introduce: Kareah is a man recorded as the father of Johanan and Jonathan. His son Johanan appears among the captains of the forces who came to Mizpah to Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor (Jeremiah 40:7-8).
lifetime: Kareah is recorded as the father of Johanan and Jonathan (Jeremiah 40:8), and his son Johanan was active as a military leader in the turbulent period after the fall of the kingdom of Judah (Jeremiah 41:11).
event: Johanan is introduced as a son of Kareah among the captains of the forces who had been in the open country and came to Gedaliah at Mizpah right after the fall of Judah (Jeremiah 40:8, 13). Johanan informed Gedaliah that Baalis king of the Ammonites had sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to take his life, but Gedaliah did not believe him (Jeremiah 40:13-14); he also asked in secret to be allowed to kill Ishmael, but Gedaliah would not permit it (Jeremiah 40:15-16).

introduce: Gareb was an Ithrite whose name is recorded in the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:38). This list is recorded as thirty-seven in all (2 Samuel 23:39).
lifetime: Gareb was an Ithrite and is recorded in the list of David's mighty men together with Ira the Ithrite (2 Samuel 23:38; 1 Chronicles 11:40). The Bible gives no record of his birth, lineage, or period of activity.
event: Gareb's name merely appears in the list of David's mighty men; no other individual battle or event is recorded of him in the Bible (2 Samuel 23:38; 1 Chronicles 11:40).
character: Gareb is recorded as coming from the place named Ithri, and he is regarded as a loyal man who held his place steadfastly within the military structure throughout David's reign (2 Samuel 23:38). No detailed description of his character or individual traits is given in the Bible (2 Samuel 23:38).

introduce: Carkas was one of the seven eunuchs who served the king at close hand in the time of King Xerxes of the Persian Empire.
event: When King Xerxes, merry with wine on the seventh day of the feast, commanded that Queen Vashti be brought before the king, Carkas was one of the seven eunuchs who received the command and carried out the errand (Esther 1:10-11).
lifetime: He served as a palace eunuch attending King Xerxes of the Persian Empire at close range (Esther 1:10). The Bible gives no record of his specific birth, family, death, and so on.

introduce: Carshena was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to King Xerxes' presence and sat first in the kingdom (Esther 1:14).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who saw the king's face and sat first in the kingdom (Esther 1:14). His birth, family, and later deeds do not appear in the Bible.
event: When Queen Vashti did not obey King Xerxes' command delivered by the eunuchs, and the king asked the wise men who understood the times what should be done according to the law (Esther 1:13, 15), Carshena is named as one of the seven princes who were close to the king (Esther 1:14). The one recorded as answering before the king and the princes on that occasion is Memucan (Esther 1:16); no statement by Carshena is recorded.

직업/직위: one of the seven princes of Persia

call: son of Pedahzur (chief of the tribe of Manasseh)
introduce: Gamaliel is a figure in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament, a chief of the tribe of Manasseh and the son of Pedahzur. He was one of the leaders chosen as representatives of each tribe when the Israelites marched through the wilderness after the exodus.
lifetime: Gamaliel is recorded as the son of Pedahzur among the descendants of Manasseh (Numbers 1:10). He was one of those designated to assist Moses and Aaron as head of each tribe when they took the census (Numbers 1:4, 10). Later, in the order of march in the wilderness, he is recorded as chief of the descendants of Manasseh (Numbers 2:20), and he led the host of the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh (Numbers 10:23).
event: On the eighth day at the dedication of the tabernacle, he presented his offering as chief of the descendants of Manasseh (Numbers 7:54). His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary (both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering), one golden pan of ten shekels filled with incense, one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering, one male goat for a sin offering, and two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old for a sacrifice of peace offerings (Numbers 7:55-59).

직업/직위: clan chief of the tribe of Manasseh

introduce: Gamul is a descendant of Aaron in the Old Testament, the head of the twenty-second of the twenty-four priestly divisions chosen by lot to serve in the house of the LORD in the days of King David.
lifetime: As a descendant of Aaron, he took part in the casting of lots to determine the order for performing the duties of the temple (1 Chronicles 24:1-5). When David divided the priestly duties, the lot fell to him twenty-second, and he formed his own division (1 Chronicles 24:17). The Bible gives no specific record of his personal life, such as his birth or death (1 Chronicles 24:17).
event: According to the ordinance commanded by the LORD God of Israel through his ancestor Aaron, he took charge of the twenty-second division, which entered the house of the LORD to perform its service (1 Chronicles 24:17-19).

introduce: Carpus is a figure whose name is mentioned just once in the New Testament, in 2 Timothy 4:13; the apostle Paul left his cloak at his house in Troas.
lifetime: The Bible gives no record of Carpus's birth, family relationships, death, or other specific details of his life. His house is recorded as being in Troas (2 Timothy 4:13).
event: The apostle Paul left his cloak at Carpus's house in Troas and asked Timothy to bring it when he came. Paul also asked him especially to bring the books, above all the parchments (2 Timothy 4:13). The text does not make clear whether the books were at Carpus's house.

meaning: man of God, hero of God
introduce: Gabriel is portrayed in the Bible as an angel who carries God's messages to human beings. The Hebrew etymology of the name carries the sense that God is strong, and he is one of the very few beings in the Bible who is called by a proper name as an angel.
lifetime: He appeared to Daniel to interpret a vision for him (Daniel 8:16) and came to Daniel to give him wisdom and understanding concerning the seventy weeks (Daniel 9:21-22). Later, in the New Testament period, he appeared to Zechariah and foretold the birth of John the Baptist (Luke 1:13, 19), and he appeared to Mary, who lived in Nazareth, and announced the birth of Jesus (Luke 1:26-27, 31).
event: When Daniel saw the vision of the ram and the male goat, he was commanded to make Daniel understand the vision, and he told Daniel that the vision concerned the time of the end (Daniel 8:16-17); he also delivered to Daniel the revelation that seventy weeks had been decreed for his people and his holy city (Daniel 9:21-24). He also appeared to Zechariah as he was burning incense in the temple and announced that his wife Elizabeth would bear a son (Luke 1:11-13, 19), and to Mary he announced that she would conceive and bear a son and that the Holy Spirit would come upon her (Luke 1:30-35).
character: By introducing himself as one who stands in the presence of God, he shows that he holds the position of facing God directly (Luke 1:19). He displays an overwhelming presence that inspires fear in human beings, and he shows the trait of a messenger who conveys the will of God clearly (Daniel 8:17, Luke 1:28-30).

introduce: He is a son born to Ephah, the concubine of Caleb of the tribe of Judah. His existence is mentioned through the genealogical records of the Bible.
lifetime: It is recorded that Ephah, the concubine of Caleb of the tribe of Judah, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez (1 Chronicles 2:46). The same verse also records that Haran fathered Gazez.

introduce: The Casluhites appear in the genealogy of the Bible as descendants of Ham, the son of Noah, and as sons of Mizraim. They belong to the genealogy of Genesis 10, which explains the national origins of the peoples of the ancient Near East.
lifetime: The Casluhites are recorded as sons born to Mizraim (Genesis 10:13-14). It is recorded that the Philistine people came from the Casluhites (1 Chronicles 1:12).
event: The Casluhites became the ancestor of the Casluhite people (Genesis 10:14). The Bible records that the Philistines came from the Casluhites (Genesis 10:14).

introduce: Gaal was a man who stirred up the people of Shechem and led a revolt during the reign of Abimelech in the period of the judges; he was the son of Ebed and had moved to Shechem together with his brothers.
lifetime: Gaal came to Shechem with his brothers, and the men of Shechem put their confidence in him (Judges 9:26). When the men of Shechem gathered the grapes in the fields, held a festival, ate and drank in the temple of their god, and cursed Abimelech (Judges 9:27), Gaal said that they should not serve Abimelech (Judges 9:28). Zebul, the ruler of the city, heard Gaal's words and was angry, and sent messengers to Abimelech (Judges 9:30-31); Gaal went out before the men of Shechem and fought with Abimelech, but was driven away and fled (Judges 9:39-40). Afterward Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers so that they could not live in Shechem (Judges 9:41), and the Bible does not record what he did after that.
event: He made a speech to the men of Shechem criticizing Abimelech and inciting revolt (Judges 9:28). He fought a battle with Abimelech's army at the gate of Shechem (Judges 9:34-40). The result was that he was expelled from Shechem by Zebul (Judges 9:41).
character: Living in Shechem with the brothers who followed him, he had agitating, political eloquence enough to win the support of the men of Shechem (Judges 9:26-29). He showed an arrogant and reckless disposition, pouring out sharp invective without restraint against Abimelech and his deputy Zebul (Judges 9:28-29). Strategically, he showed rashness by underestimating Abimelech's army and going out of the city gate to confront it (Judges 9:36-40).

직업/직위: commander of the rebels at Shechem

introduce: Caiaphas was a man who served as high priest together with Annas at the time of Jesus' ministry (Luke 3:2), and the Gospel of John calls him the high priest that year (John 11:49; 18:13). He appears at the council plotting to put Jesus to death and at the trial of Jesus, and is recorded as the one who advised that it was expedient for one man to die for the people (John 18:14).
lifetime: Caiaphas was the son-in-law of the high priest Annas; Annas is recorded as the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year (John 18:13). Luke records that the word of God came to John when Annas and Caiaphas were high priests (Luke 3:2). The Bible gives no other record of his birth or lineage.
event: The chief priests and the elders of the people gathered in the palace of the high priest named Caiaphas and plotted to arrest Jesus by stealth and kill him (Matthew 26:3-4). When the council deliberated about Jesus, Caiaphas, the high priest that year, said that it was expedient for one man to die for the people so that the whole nation would not perish (John 11:47-50). Those who had seized Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest (Matthew 26:57), and the high priest questioned Jesus, tore his clothes, and said that he had spoken blasphemy (Matthew 26:62-65). Annas sent Jesus, still bound, to Caiaphas (John 18:24), and the Jews led Jesus from Caiaphas to the Praetorium (John 18:28). In Acts, Caiaphas met in the council with Annas, John, Alexander, and all who were of the high-priestly family (Acts 4:6), and at this gathering they questioned and threatened Peter and John and warned them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus (Acts 4:7-18).
character: He was a man of keen political sense who excelled at maintaining relations with Roman power (John 11:48). He showed a cool and strategic side, using public opinion for his purpose and handling legal procedures swiftly (John 11:50). He had an authoritarian disposition, sparing no means or method to protect religious custom and vested interests (Matthew 26:65).

introduce: Kenan is a man recorded in Genesis 5 and 1 Chronicles 1; he was the son of Enosh, who was the son of Seth, the father of Mahalalel, and a great-grandson of Adam. In Luke 3:37 he is recorded as Cainan.
lifetime: Enosh fathered Kenan at the age of 90 (Genesis 5:9), and Kenan fathered Mahalalel at the age of 70 (Genesis 5:12). After fathering Mahalalel, Kenan lived 840 years and fathered other sons and daughters, and in all he lived 910 years and died (Genesis 5:13-14).

introduce: Caesar is a title derived from the Latin Caesar and is the official title that designates the emperor, the supreme ruler of the Roman Empire of that time. The Caesar mentioned in the Bible was used less as a name pointing to a specific individual than as a designation symbolizing the office of Roman emperor and his system of rule.
lifetime: As ruler of the Roman Empire, Caesar exercised authority over a broad territory including the region of Judea. During the period of Jesus' ministry, people asked Jesus whether it was lawful or not to pay taxes to Caesar (Matthew 22:17; Mark 12:14; Luke 20:22). Jesus answered that they should render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's and to God the things that are God's (Matthew 22:21; Mark 12:17; Luke 20:25). Later, in the process of accusing Jesus, his accusers said that he forbade paying taxes to Caesar and claimed to be Christ, a king (Luke 23:2), and the Jews cried out to Pilate that if he released Jesus he was no loyal friend of Caesar, and that everyone who makes himself a king opposes Caesar (John 19:12).
event: When Jesus asked whose likeness and inscription were on the denarius, the answer came that they were Caesar's (Matthew 22:20-21; Mark 12:16; Luke 20:24). Those who accused Jesus charged that he forbade paying taxes to Caesar (Luke 23:2), and the Jews cried out to Pilate, invoking Caesar, that he must not release Jesus (John 19:12).

call: Caesar Augustus, the Roman emperor who issued the decree for the census
introduce: Caesar Augustus was the first emperor of the Roman Empire, whose personal name was Gaius Octavian. As the ruler who ended the civil wars of the Roman republican period and opened the imperial era, he appears as the Roman emperor at the time of Jesus' birth as recorded in the New Testament.
lifetime: The Bible has no record of his birth or life. Luke records the time when Caesar Augustus issued a decree that a census be taken of the whole world (Luke 2:1); for this census Joseph went up to Bethlehem with Mary, and there Jesus was born (Luke 2:3-7).
event: He issued a decree that a census be taken of the whole world (Luke 2:1), and everyone returned to his own town to register (Luke 2:3). This census is recorded as the first one, taken while Quirinius was governor of Syria (Luke 2:2).
character: To maintain order in the empire, he exercised centralized administrative power, and to govern his vast territory efficiently he carried out policies for taking censuses and collecting taxes (Luke 2:3).

introduce: Gaius of Macedonia was one of Paul's traveling companions who accompanied him in Ephesus during the apostle Paul's third missionary journey. He is distinguished as a different person from Gaius of Derbe (Acts 20:4).
lifetime: He is recorded as a Macedonian traveling with Paul (Acts 19:29). During the riot in Ephesus, he suffered the hardship of being seized, together with Aristarchus, by the mob of the whole city and dragged into the amphitheater (Acts 19:29).
event: In Ephesus, a silversmith named Demetrius, fearing that his business of making silver shrines of Artemis would fall into disrepute, gathered the workmen (Acts 19:24-27); the whole city was thrown into confusion, and the people seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who were traveling with Paul, and rushed together into the amphitheater (Acts 19:28-29). Nothing of his later deeds or specific ministry appears in this passage.
character: He was in a close relationship with Paul, to the point of accompanying Paul's missionary journeys, and he showed a devoted attitude, acting together with Paul's company even in the scene of a riot where personal danger was involved (Acts 19:29).

call: Adam's firstborn son (the first murderer of humanity)
introduce: He was the first son born to Adam and Eve and the man who killed his brother Abel. According to the biblical record, he is identified as the perpetrator of the first murder in human history.
lifetime: He was the first son born when Adam lay with Eve, and his occupation was farmer (Genesis 4:1-2). After he killed Abel, he departed from the presence of the LORD and dwelt in the land of Nod, east of Eden, and built a city, which he named Enoch after his son Enoch, born when he lay with his wife (Genesis 4:16-17). Among his descendants came the ancestors of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock, of all who play the lyre and the pipe, and of those who forge all implements of bronze and iron (Genesis 4:20-22).
event: When the offering of the produce of the ground that he brought to God was not accepted, he became angry and killed Abel (Genesis 4:3-8). Afterward he received from God the punishment of becoming a fugitive and wanderer on the earth, but fearing that he would be killed, he received a mark and was spared from being killed (Genesis 4:11-15). His descendant Lamech told his wives that he had killed a man, and said that if Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech is avenged seventy-sevenfold (Genesis 4:23-24).
character: When his offering was rejected, his countenance fell and he showed an inability to control his anger (Genesis 4:5-6). After his crime, rather than admitting his sin, he displayed a self-centered attitude, complaining that the punishment was too heavy (Genesis 4:13). Nevertheless, he was a man with a strong will for survival and the establishment of civilization, building a city and forming a family line (Genesis 4:17).

introduce: Gahar is the ancestor of a family recorded as "the descendants of Gahar" in the list of the Nethinim who returned from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: The descendants of Gahar are recorded in the list of the Nethinim among the numbered people of Israel who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem and Judah with Zerubbabel and others (Ezra 2:1-2, 43, 47). Nehemiah found the register of the genealogy of those who came back at first, and there too the descendants of Gahar are recorded among the Nethinim (Nehemiah 7:5-6, 46, 49).
event: He is recorded as the Gahar of the descendants of the Nethinim in the list of those who returned from Babylon (Ezra 2:47; Nehemiah 7:49). The Bible gives no record of the deeds of Gahar himself.

직업/직위: ancestor of a family of temple servants

introduce: Gaham was one of the children born to Nahor, Abraham's brother, and his concubine Reumah, and is a man belonging to the genealogy of Nahor's descendants (Genesis 22:24).
lifetime: Gaham is recorded as one of the four sons born to Nahor and his concubine Reumah (Genesis 22:24).

introduce: Galal is a Levite recorded in 1 Chronicles, a man whose name appears together with Bakbakkar, Heresh, and Mattaniah (1 Chronicles 9:15).
lifetime: In the list of Levites in 1 Chronicles 9:14-15, Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah are listed together. The one introduced next as "the son of Mica, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph" is Mattaniah, and this verse contains no record about Galal's own father or children (1 Chronicles 9:15).
event: His name is recorded in the list of Levites who returned from Babylon and lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:1-3, 14-15). Apart from this list, no deeds of Galal himself are recorded.

introduce: Kallai was from a priestly family and was the head of the house of Sallai, recorded as a head of the priests in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12, 20).
lifetime: He was the head of the house of Sallai, recorded as a head of the priests in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:10, 12, 20).
event: In the list of the heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12-21), he is listed as the head of the house of Sallai (Nehemiah 12:20). Apart from this list, no deeds of Kallai himself are recorded.

직업/직위: head of the family of Sallai

introduce: Caleb is a figure who appears in Numbers, Deuteronomy, and Joshua in the Old Testament, the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite. He was chosen as a spy representing the tribe of Judah during the exodus, and he is a historical figure who was allotted the region of Hebron after the wars of the conquest of Canaan.
lifetime: After coming out of Egypt, Caleb was chosen as a leader of the tribe of Judah among the spies whom Moses sent out from the wilderness of Paran at the command of the LORD (Numbers 13:3, 6). At the age of forty he was sent by Moses from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land (Joshua 14:7), and forty-five years later, at the age of eighty-five, he said that he was still strong (Joshua 14:10-11). Joshua blessed him and gave him Hebron as an inheritance (Joshua 14:13-14).
event: As one of the twelve spies, after spying out the land of Canaan he quieted the people before Moses and said, "Let us go up at once and take possession of the land" (Numbers 13:30). Together with Joshua son of Nun he tore his clothes and spoke, but the whole congregation threatened to stone them (Numbers 14:6; 14:10). In the time of the conquest of Canaan, he drove out of Hebron the sons of Anak, namely Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai (Joshua 15:14), and he said that he would give his daughter Acsah as wife to the one who attacked and took Kiriath-sepher, and when Othniel, Caleb's brother, took it, he gave Acsah to him as wife (Joshua 15:16-17).
character: Caleb is commended as one who wholly followed the LORD (Numbers 32:12). He did not yield to the opinion of the majority but reported the situation objectively and showed resolute firmness in holding to his conviction (Numbers 14:6-9). Even at an advanced age, he showed an active and venturesome disposition by volunteering to go out and fight the descendants of Anak in Hebron (Joshua 14:12).

직업/직위: clan chief of the tribe of Judah

introduce: Gallio is a man recorded in Acts 18:12 as proconsul of Achaia. He appears as the one who handled the complaint when the Jews brought Paul to the judgment seat in Corinth.
lifetime: When Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews rose up together against Paul and brought him to the judgment seat, and he faced the matter (Acts 18:12). The Bible gives no record of his birthplace, lineage, adoption, and the like.
event: When the Jews accused Paul, Gallio said that if it were some wrongdoing or vicious crime he would hear them (Acts 18:14), and that if it was a dispute about words and names and their own law, they should settle it themselves, for he refused to be a judge of such things (Acts 18:15). Then he drove them from the judgment seat (Acts 18:16). Afterward all of them seized Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him in front of the judgment seat, but Gallio paid no attention to any of this (Acts 18:17).
character: Rather than intervening in religious disputes or internal conflicts, he showed an official attitude of dealing only with Roman order of government and legal matters (Acts 18:15). By taking an indifferent stance toward civil and religious matters, he showed a pragmatic disposition that clearly set the scope of law enforcement (Acts 18:17).

introduce: Carmi was a grandson of Zerah of the tribe of Judah and the son of Zabdi, and is recorded as the father of Achan. In the Bible he is mentioned mostly in the context of establishing Achan's lineage.
lifetime: His name appears as Achan is introduced as "of the tribe of Judah, the great-grandson of Zerah, the grandson of Zabdi, and the son of Carmi," so he was a son of Zabdi and a grandson of Zerah (Joshua 7:1; Joshua 7:18). In 1 Chronicles 2:7 it is recorded, "The son of Carmi: Achar." The Bible gives no record of Carmi's own deeds or residence.
event: Carmi's son Achan took some of what was devoted to destruction, and the Israelites became guilty of a trespass (Joshua 7:1). In the process of bringing this to light, the tribe of Judah was taken (Joshua 7:16), the clan of Zerah and Zabdi were taken (Joshua 7:17), and finally, from the household of Zabdi, Achan son of Carmi was taken (Joshua 7:18). The Bible records no action of Carmi himself in this incident.

introduce: Caphtorites is a name recorded in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles as one of the descendants born to Mizraim. It is listed alongside the Casluhites, and it is recorded that the Philistines came from the Casluhites (Genesis 10:14).
lifetime: It is recorded that Mizraim fathered the Pathrusites, the Casluhites, and the Caphtorites (Genesis 10:14). They are listed in the same order in 1 Chronicles as well (1 Chronicles 1:12).
event: Apart from the genealogical record, the Bible reports no separate event concerning the Caphtorites. That the Philistines came forth is recorded in the same verse as being from the Casluhites (Genesis 10:14; 1 Chronicles 1:12).

introduce: Gabbai is a man recorded in the list of the inhabitants of Jerusalem in Nehemiah 11, written together with Sallai after Sallu among the descendants of Benjamin (Nehemiah 11:7-8).
lifetime: Gabbai's name is on the list of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:7-8). The text records, "And his followers Gabbai and Sallai, in all nine hundred twenty-eight" (Nehemiah 11:8).
event: No personal event is recorded in connection with Gabbai; his name appears only in the list of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:8).

직업/직위: leader of the tribe of Benjamin

introduce: Gad was a son born to Jacob and Leah's maidservant Zilpah, Jacob's seventh son, and the ancestor of the tribe of Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
lifetime: Gad is recorded as a son of Jacob born in Paddan-aram (Genesis 30:10-11; Genesis 35:26), and his sons are on the list of the family of Israel who went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:8; Genesis 46:16). Since Gad was an older brother of Joseph, he was among the party when Joseph's ten older brothers went down to Egypt to buy grain (Genesis 42:3-4). When Jacob blessed his sons before his death, he said of Gad, "will be attacked by raiders, but he will attack their heels" (Genesis 49:19). In later times, in the wilderness, those of the tribe of Gad fit for war were counted as forty-five thousand six hundred fifty (Numbers 1:24-25).
event: As a brother of Joseph, when Joseph's older brothers saw Joseph from afar they plotted to kill him (Genesis 37:18), and Joseph was sold to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver and went to Egypt (Genesis 37:28). The text does not separately record any action of Gad himself in this matter. Gad had seven sons (Genesis 46:16). In the wilderness period, the descendants of Gad, together with the descendants of Reuben, since they had a very great multitude of livestock and regarded the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead as a place suitable for livestock, asked Moses to give them that land as their possession (Numbers 32:1-5), and Moses gave the descendants of Gad, the descendants of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan (Numbers 32:33).
character: Through the prophecy that he would be attacked by an army but would instead pursue it from behind, Jacob hinted that Gad would become the ancestor of a tribe with a warlike disposition (Genesis 49:19). The Bible gives no specific description of Gad's personal character (not applicable).

직업/직위: progenitor of the tribe of Gad

introduce: Gaddi was a man of the tribe of Manasseh, the son of Susi. He is a figure recorded for the tribe of Manasseh among the men Moses sent, one from each tribe, to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:11).
lifetime: Gaddi is introduced as the son of Susi from the tribe of Joseph, that is, the tribe of Manasseh, and is on the list of those sent to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:11). They were the men who were heads of the children of Israel, whom Moses sent from the wilderness of Paran at the command of the LORD (Numbers 13:3).
event: When Moses, at the command of the LORD, sent from the wilderness of Paran one man from each tribe, each a leader among his tribe, Gaddi son of Susi was recorded for the tribe of Manasseh (Numbers 13:2-3; Numbers 13:11). The men sent returned after finishing their spying out of the land for forty days (Numbers 13:25). No deeds of Gaddi himself are recorded separately.

직업/직위: clan chief of the tribe of Manasseh

introduce: Gaddiel is a figure who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, one of the twelve spies chosen to spy out the land of Canaan. He is recorded as the representative of the tribe of Zebulun.
lifetime: Gaddiel was chosen as the representative of the tribe of Zebulun and carried out the mission of spying out the land of Canaan under Moses' direction (Numbers 13:10). He was the son of Sodi of the tribe of Zebulun (Numbers 13:10).
event: While the people of Israel were staying in the wilderness of Paran, Moses chose one man from each tribe to spy out Canaan, and Gaddiel was chosen as one of them (Numbers 13:2-3). Together with the other spies he looked over the whole land of Canaan for forty days and took part in returning and giving the report (Numbers 13:25).

직업/직위: clan chief of the tribe of Zebulun

introduce: Kadmiel was a Levite who took part in rebuilding the temple in Jerusalem and establishing the order of worship after the return from the Babylonian exile, and he is recorded in the lists of Levites together with Jeshua and Binnui.
lifetime: As one of the Levites who returned for the rebuilding of the temple after the return from the Babylonian exile, the descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the line of Hodaviah, are recorded in the list of returnees as seventy-four (Ezra 2:40). After the work on the temple began, Jeshua with his sons and brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, the descendants of Judah, and the descendants of Henadad with their brothers the Levites, joined together to supervise the work on the house of God (Ezra 3:9). Later, in the time of Nehemiah, together with the Levites Jeshua, Bani, and others, he stood on the raised platform and cried out in a loud voice to the LORD their God (Nehemiah 9:4); his name is on the list of those who sealed the covenant as a Levite (Nehemiah 10:9); and he is recorded in the list of Levites together with Jeshua, Binnui, and others (Nehemiah 12:8).
event: At the rebuilding of the temple, the Levites, Jeshua and his sons and Kadmiel and his sons and others, joined together to supervise the work on the house of God (Ezra 3:9). When the people of Israel gathered, fasting and confessing their sins, the Levites Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, and others stood on the raised platform and cried out in a loud voice to the LORD their God (Nehemiah 9:4), and the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, and others told the people to stand up and bless the LORD their God, who is from everlasting to everlasting (Nehemiah 9:5). Kadmiel's name was also entered as a Levite on the list of those who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:9). In Nehemiah 12:8 the Levites Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah are recorded, and it is said that Mattaniah with his brothers was in charge of the songs of thanksgiving (Nehemiah 12:8). His son Jeshua, as one of the leaders of the Levites, stood opposite his brothers to praise and give thanks (Nehemiah 12:24).

introduce: Gazzam is a figure who appears in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah in the Old Testament, and is recorded as one of the Nethinim who returned from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: Gazzam is a man included in the list of the Nethinim who returned from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:48). He appears in the same way in Nehemiah's list recording the genealogy of those who finished the Babylonian exile and returned to Jerusalem and Judah (Nehemiah 7:51).
event: As a member of the Nethinim who performed the service of the temple, he was included in the community of returnees (Ezra 2:48, Nehemiah 7:51).

직업/직위: ancestor of a family of temple servants

meaning: one who lives in black tents
introduce: Kedar is a man who appears in Genesis and 1 Chronicles, the second son of Ishmael. He is recorded as the grandson of Abraham and the ancestor of the descendants of Kedar, one of the tribes of the descendants of Ishmael (Genesis 25:13, 1 Chronicles 1:29).
lifetime: Kedar was born as a son of Ishmael (Genesis 25:13). Together with Ishmael's other brothers he became a chief, twelve princes according to their villages and encampments (Genesis 25:16).
event: Concerning the descendants of Kedar, Isaiah said that within a year all the glory of Kedar would come to an end, and that the remnant of the archers, the mighty men of the descendants of Kedar, would be few (Isaiah 21:16-17). In Ezekiel 27:21 it is recorded that Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were merchants who traded in lambs, rams, and goats. According to the biblical record, no independent achievement or particular event of Kedar himself is mentioned separately.

직업/직위: chief of the tribe of Kedar

introduce: Gether is a man recorded as a descendant of Shem, Noah's son, and a son of Aram (Genesis 10:23). His name also appears in the list of the descendants of Shem in 1 Chronicles 1:17.
lifetime: Gether is recorded in the genealogy as a son of Aram and a grandson of Shem (Genesis 10:23). In the list of the sons of Shem in 1 Chronicles 1:17, the names appear in the order Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech (1 Chronicles 1:17).

직업/직위: chief of the tribe of Gether

introduce: Kedemah is a man who appears in Genesis and 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, recorded as the twelfth son in the list of the sons of Ishmael, the descendant of Abraham and Hagar.
lifetime: Kedemah, as a son of Ishmael, is mentioned in the genealogy in which the family and names of Ishmael are recorded (Genesis 25:15). His name is also included once again by the chronicler in the list enumerating the descendants of Ishmael (1 Chronicles 1:31).

직업/직위: chief of the tribe of Kedemah

call: early ancestor of the tribe of Benjamin, the representative ancestor of the clan of Gera
introduce: Gera is one of the ancestors of the tribe of Benjamin; in Genesis he is listed as one of the sons of Benjamin (Genesis 46:21), and in 1 Chronicles he is recorded as one of the sons of Bela (1 Chronicles 8:3). The text does not make clear whether the two records refer to the same man.
lifetime: Gera's name appears in the list of the sons of Benjamin (Genesis 46:21) and in the list of the sons of Bela (1 Chronicles 8:3). In 2 Samuel and 1 Kings, Shimei son of Gera, a Benjaminite of Bahurim, appears as the man who cursed David (2 Samuel 16:5; 2 Samuel 19:16; 1 Kings 2:8), but the text does not state whether this Gera is the same man as the Gera above.

직업/직위: progenitor of the Gera clan of Benjamin

기타관계: Ehud#4647(kinsman of the tribe of Benjamin)

introduce: Keren-happuch is a figure who appears at the end of the book of Job, the third of the three daughters Job received after he passed through suffering and was restored.
lifetime: She was born as one of the three daughters when Job, by the grace of God, recovered twice as much property as before and received seven sons and three daughters (Job 42:13). Within Job's household she received, together with her brothers, a share of the inheritance her father gave (Job 42:15).
event: Keren-happuch is recorded by name as Job's third daughter (Job 42:14), and it is said that their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers (Job 42:15).
character: Her name, Keren-happuch, means "horn of eye paint" or "horn of perfume" in Hebrew, and this is connected with the record that Job's daughters were judged the most beautiful women in all the land in their time (Job 42:14-15).

introduce: Keros is a family of the Nethinim who appear in the list of returnees from the exile, or the man who represents that family. In the records of Ezra and Nehemiah he is classified as one of the Nethinim, the group of those who assisted with the work of the temple.
lifetime: He is one of the Nethinim who returned to Jerusalem and Judah under the leadership of Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:44). His name is likewise included in the list of returnees drawn up after Nehemiah rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 7:47).
event: As a member of the Nethinim devoted to the work of the temple, he was entered in the list of returnees (Ezra 2:44). In the course of Nehemiah's work of confirming the genealogy of the residents of the city and the returnees, his name was recorded once again (Nehemiah 7:47).

직업/직위: ancestor of a family of temple servants

call: firstborn son of Levi (ancestor of the Gershonite clan)
introduce: He was the eldest son of Levi, a grandson of Jacob, and the ancestor of the descendants of Gershon within the tribe of Levi.
lifetime: He is named first among the sons of Levi, whose names are recorded "according to their generations" (Exodus 6:16; Genesis 46:11). He is on the list of the family of Israel who went down to Egypt with Jacob and his sons (Genesis 46:8; Genesis 46:11), and his descendants were called the Gershonite clans (Numbers 3:21).
event: His descendants, the Gershonite clans, were assigned in the wilderness to carry and handle the curtains of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting and its covering, the screen at the entrance of the tent of meeting, the hangings of the courtyard, the screen at the entrance of the courtyard gate, their cords, and all the equipment (Numbers 4:24-26). When David divided the divisions according to the clans of the sons of Levi, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, Ladan and Shimei were recorded as the Gershonites, and chiefs came from among their sons (1 Chronicles 23:6-11).

introduce: Gershom was the eldest son born to Moses and Zipporah, the daughter of Jethro, the priest of Midian, and he belonged to the tribe of Levi. His name carries the meaning that Moses had become a sojourner in a foreign land.
lifetime: After Moses took Zipporah as his wife in Midian and she bore a son, Moses named him Gershom (Exodus 2:21-22). When Moses set his wife and sons on a donkey and returned to Egypt, he went along on the journey (Exodus 4:20). When Moses was in the wilderness, his father-in-law Jethro brought Moses' wife and two sons, one of whom was named Gershom (Exodus 18:3). In the time of David, Shebuel, a descendant of Gershom, was in charge of the treasuries (1 Chronicles 26:24).
event: At the lodging place on the way as Moses returned to Egypt, when the LORD sought to kill Moses, Zipporah took a flint, cut off the foreskin of "her son," threw it at Moses' feet, and said, "a bridegroom of blood" (Exodus 4:24-26). The text does not make clear whether that son was Gershom or Eliezer. Also, in the record of the descendants of Levi, Moses' sons are Gershom and Eliezer (1 Chronicles 23:15), and Shebuel among the sons of Gershom became chief (1 Chronicles 23:16).

introduce: Geber was a district governor over the land of Gilead in the days of King Solomon, recorded as the son of Uri (1 Kings 4:19).
lifetime: During the reign of King Solomon he was an official governing the land of Gilead east of the Jordan (1 Kings 4:19). He was in charge of the administration of the region of Gilead, which included the territory ruled by Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan (1 Kings 4:19).
event: Of the twelve district governors whom Solomon set over all Israel, each provided food for the king and his household one month in the year (1 Kings 4:7), and Geber was the governor in charge of the land of Gilead (1 Kings 4:19).

introduce: Geshan is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah and is recorded as a son of Jahdai (1 Chronicles 2:47). This verse is within the passage recording the descendants and concubines of Caleb (1 Chronicles 2:42-49).
lifetime: Geshan is mentioned as a son of Jahdai in the context of the genealogy recording the descendants and concubines of Caleb (1 Chronicles 2:42-49; 1 Chronicles 2:47). The Bible gives no record of the activities he carried out during his life or of a specific chronology (1 Chronicles 2:47).
event: The biblical text merely records Geshan as one of the sons of Jahdai and provides no specific information about any achievements or historical events he accomplished during his life (1 Chronicles 2:47).

introduce: He is an Arab who appears in the book of Nehemiah in the Old Testament, one of those who, together with Sanballat and Tobiah, opposed the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem. He is also written as "Gashmu" in Nehemiah 6:6.
lifetime: In the reign of King Artaxerxes, together with Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite, who had been a servant, he heard that Nehemiah and his company had begun to rebuild the wall, and he scorned and mocked them (Nehemiah 2:1; Nehemiah 2:19). Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of their enemies heard that Nehemiah had built the wall and no gap was left in it (Nehemiah 6:1).
event: Together with Sanballat and Tobiah, Geshem scorned and mocked, saying, "What is this you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?" (Nehemiah 2:19). While the doors had not yet been set in the gates of the wall, Sanballat and Geshem sent to Nehemiah, proposing that they meet together in one of the villages in the plain of Ono, but in fact they intended to harm Nehemiah (Nehemiah 6:1-2). Nehemiah said he was doing a great work and would not come down, yet they sent the same message four times (Nehemiah 6:3-4), and the fifth time Sanballat sent an unsealed letter in which was written that it was reported that "Gashmu also says that you and the Jews are plotting to revolt, and for this reason you are building the wall" (Nehemiah 6:5-6).
character: To maintain his own political influence, he showed a strategic side by forming alliances with neighboring powers (Nehemiah 2:19). He displayed a deceitful and political disposition, spreading false information and fabricating letters in order to eliminate another's political opponent (Nehemiah 6:5-8).

introduce: Chesed was one of the eight sons born to Nahor, Abraham's brother, and his wife Milcah, and he is recorded fourth in the list of Genesis 22:21-22 (Genesis 22:22).
lifetime: Chesed is recorded as a son of Nahor and Milcah (Genesis 22:22-23), and the brothers recorded in the same list are Uz, Buz, Kemuel, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel (Genesis 22:21-22).

introduce: Ge-harashim is a name that appears in 1 Chronicles 4:14; it is recorded that Joab, whom Seraiah fathered, was the father of Ge-harashim and that they were craftsmen. The text does not make clear whether this name is the name of a single person or the name of a group.
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 4:14 records, "Seraiah was the father of Joab, the father of those living in Ge-harashim, which was given this name because its people were craftsmen." This verse has no record of Ge-harashim's own birth or parents.
event: No individual event of Ge-harashim is recorded; it says only that they, who had Joab as their ancestor, were craftsmen (1 Chronicles 4:14).

meaning: valley of vision, valley of revelation
introduce: Gehazi is a figure who appears in 2 Kings in the Old Testament, a man who served as the attendant and assistant of the prophet Elisha. He assisted Elisha's ministry at his side and accompanied him on major events.
lifetime: Gehazi, as Elisha's attendant, went on ahead with Elisha's staff in his hand when the son of the Shunammite woman died and laid it on the boy's face, but the boy did not awaken (2 Kings 4:29; 2 Kings 4:31). After Naaman was healed and Elisha had accepted no payment, Gehazi ran after Naaman, falsely asked for goods, and received them, and because of this Naaman's leprosy clung to him and he became leprous (2 Kings 5:20-27). Later, when the king spoke with Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, and said, "Tell me all the great things that Elisha has done," Gehazi told the king how Elisha had restored the dead to life (2 Kings 8:4-5).
event: When the son of the Shunammite woman died, at Elisha's command he went on ahead and laid the staff on the boy's face, but there was no sound or sign of life, so he went back and told Elisha that the boy had not awakened (2 Kings 4:29; 2 Kings 4:31). When Naaman went back having received nothing from Elisha, Gehazi on his own ran after Naaman and said that two young men of the sons of the prophets had come, and asked for a talent of silver and two sets of clothing (2 Kings 5:20-22); Naaman gave him two talents of silver and two sets of clothing (2 Kings 5:23), and Gehazi hid those things in his house (2 Kings 5:24). Elisha rebuked him and said that Naaman's leprosy would cling to Gehazi and to his descendants forever, and as Gehazi went out from his presence, he became leprous, as white as snow (2 Kings 5:26-27). Also, when the king asked to be told the great things Elisha had done, while Gehazi was telling how Elisha had restored the dead to life, the boy's mother appealed to the king for her house and her land, and he said, "This is the woman, and this is her son" (2 Kings 8:4-5).
character: Accompanying his master Elisha, he witnessed from the closest position the miracles and the scenes of ministry that Elisha performed (2 Kings 4:29). He showed a strong greed for wealth and a readiness to lie, and displayed an opportunistic disposition that used authority to gain unjust profit (2 Kings 5:20-22). Since he spoke directly with the king even after contracting the disease, he was a man who could communicate with the royal court and had the eloquence to remember past events in detail and relate them (2 Kings 8:4-5).

call: Levite leader in the time of Josiah
introduce: Conaniah was one of the chiefs of the Levites who, at the Passover in the time of King Josiah, gave sheep and bulls to the Levites as offerings (2 Chronicles 35:9).
lifetime: Conaniah was one of the chiefs of the Levites, and his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel are recorded with him (2 Chronicles 35:9). This verse gives no record of any other lineage or details of his life.
event: At the Passover in the time of King Josiah, the chiefs of the Levites, namely Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, together with Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, gave the Levites 5,000 sheep and 500 bulls as Passover offerings (2 Chronicles 35:9).

기타관계: Jozabad#4332(fellow worker of the tribe of Levi)

introduce: Cornelius was a centurion of the regiment called the Italian Regiment, a Gentile who lived in Caesarea. In the record of Acts, his inviting Peter, hearing the word, and receiving the Holy Spirit appears as the turning point at which the gospel reached the Gentiles.
lifetime: He served as a centurion in Caesarea and was active as a commander of the Roman army (Acts 10:1). About the ninth hour, in a vision, he met an angel of God and was instructed to send for Peter (Acts 10:3). Afterward he sent men to Joppa to bring Peter, and in his house he heard Peter's preaching and received the Holy Spirit (Acts 10:7-8, 10:44).
event: As a Gentile, he heard the gospel through Peter and had the experience of receiving the Holy Spirit (Acts 10:44-48). This event became the decisive occasion on which the early Christian community, which had been centered on the Jews, established the necessity of the mission to the Gentiles (Acts 11:1-18). He called together his relatives and close friends to hear Peter's preaching with him (Acts 10:24).
character: He was a devout man who feared God with all his household (Acts 10:2). He gave generously to the people and always prayed to God (Acts 10:2). He also showed a humble and obedient attitude, to the point of falling down before Peter, who visited him, to pay him honor (Acts 10:25).

introduce: Koz is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as the ancestor connected with Anub and Zobebah and the several clans of Aharhel son of Harum (1 Chronicles 4:8).
lifetime: Koz fathered Anub and Zobebah, and he is also genealogically connected with the clans of Aharhel son of Harum (1 Chronicles 4:8).

introduce: Cozbi is a Midianite woman who appears in Numbers 25, the daughter of a chief among the Midianite tribes. She is mentioned as a party to the incident that occurred while the Israelites stayed at Shittim.
lifetime: Cozbi was the daughter of Zur, the head of a tribal family of the Midianite people (Numbers 25:15). While Israel was staying at Shittim, the people began to commit sexual immorality with the women of Moab and joined themselves to Baal-peor, and the anger of the LORD came upon them (Numbers 25:1-3); she was put to death by Phinehas together with Zimri son of Salu, a chief of a clan of the Simeonites (Numbers 25:7-8, 14-15).
event: An Israelite, Zimri, a chief of a clan of the Simeonites, brought a Midianite woman, Cozbi, to his brothers in the sight of Moses and the whole congregation (Numbers 25:6, 14-15). Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw this, rose from the midst of the congregation, took a spear in his hand, went after the Israelite man into his tent, and pierced the man and the woman through the belly, killing them both, and the plague was stopped from the Israelites (Numbers 25:7-8). Later the LORD said that the Midianites had seduced Israel in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of the Midianite chief who was killed on the day the plague came, and told Israel to attack them (Numbers 25:17-18).
character: The Bible describes her as the daughter of a chief, from the family of the head of a tribe among the Midianite people (Numbers 25:15). Her behavior is recorded at the point where it conflicted with the religious customs of the Israelite community of that time, and the incident connected with her remained as an example that starkly shows Israel's internal order and its relations with outside peoples (Numbers 25:14-15).

introduce: Col-hozeh is a man whose name appears in the book of Nehemiah in connection with his son Shallun and his grandson Maaseiah. His son Shallun, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate when the wall of Jerusalem was rebuilt (Nehemiah 3:15).
lifetime: Col-hozeh was the father of Shallun, ruler of the district of Mizpah (Nehemiah 3:15). Also, Maaseiah, who lived in Jerusalem, is recorded as "the son of Baruch, the son of Col-hozeh, the son of Hazaiah," so Col-hozeh is introduced as Maaseiah's grandfather (Nehemiah 11:5). The Bible has no separate record of Col-hozeh's own life.
event: Nothing is recorded as having been done by Col-hozeh himself. His son Shallun repaired the Fountain Gate, rebuilding it, roofing it, and installing its doors, bolts, and bars, and he repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah near the king's garden, as far as the stairs that descend from the City of David (Nehemiah 3:15). Among the leaders who lived in Jerusalem, Maaseiah is recorded as the grandson of Col-hozeh (Nehemiah 11:3, 5).

직업/직위: father of the ruler of the district of Mizpah

introduce: Chuza is a man recorded in Luke as "Herod's household manager," and the husband of Joanna, one of the women who ministered to Jesus (Luke 8:3).
lifetime: Chuza is recorded as Herod's household manager (Luke 8:3). His wife Joanna, together with Susanna and many other women, ministered to Jesus and the twelve out of their own means (Luke 8:1-3). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life, such as his birth and lineage.
event: There is no record that Chuza himself met Jesus face to face or was involved in any particular event. However, his wife Joanna is named among certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and sicknesses, and together with the other women she ministered to Jesus out of their own means (Luke 8:2-3).

introduce: Cushan-rishathaim is the king of Aram-naharaim who appears in the book of Judges, a man who oppressed Israel in the early period after the Israelites settled in the land of Canaan. His name is also interpreted as having the meaning of double wickedness.
lifetime: When the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD and forgot the LORD their God, the anger of the LORD came upon them (Judges 3:7-8). So the LORD sold Israel into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim, and Israel served him eight years (Judges 3:8). Afterward, when the Israelites cried out to the LORD, the LORD raised up a deliverer for them, Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother (Judges 3:9).
event: Cushan-rishathaim ruled over and oppressed Israel for eight years (Judges 3:8). But when Othniel, upon whom the Spirit of the LORD came, became a judge of Israel and went out to war, the LORD delivered Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim into his hand, and Othniel's hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim (Judges 3:10).

call: father of the false prophet Zedekiah
introduce: Chenaanah is a man mentioned in 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles, the father of the false prophet Zedekiah.
lifetime: Chenaanah's son Zedekiah is recorded as one of the prophets active in the days of King Ahab (1 Kings 22:11). The Bible gives no detailed record of Chenaanah's own life.
event: There is an incident in which his son Zedekiah made horns of iron before King Ahab and King Jehoshaphat and prophesied that the LORD would gore the Arameans with these horns and destroy them (1 Kings 22:11). The same incident is also recorded in 2 Chronicles 18:10 (2 Chronicles 18:10).

introduce: Chedorlaomer was the king of Elam, a man who led the alliance of allied kings together with Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, and Tidal king of Goiim (Genesis 14:1, 5). The five kings, including the king of Sodom, served him for twelve years and then rebelled (Genesis 14:4).
lifetime: Together with Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, and Tidal king of Goiim, he went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, that is, Zoar (Genesis 14:1-2). The five kings served him for twelve years, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled, and in the fourteenth year the kings allied with him came out and fought (Genesis 14:4-5). The four kings carried off all the goods and food of Sodom and Gomorrah, and also carried off Lot, Abram's nephew, who was living in Sodom (Genesis 14:11-12), but Abram took his 318 men and pursued them as far as Dan, and attacking them by night he routed them and pursued them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus, and recovered Lot and the goods (Genesis 14:14-16). Abram defeated Chedorlaomer and the kings with him and returned (Genesis 14:17).
event: In the fourteenth year, Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, and the Emites in Shaveh-kiriathaim, and the Horites in the area of Mount Seir as far as El-paran, and they turned back to En-mishpat, that is, Kadesh, and conquered the whole territory of the Amalekites and the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar (Genesis 14:5-7). Afterward the five kings, including the king of Sodom, joined battle with them in the Valley of Siddim (Genesis 14:8-9), and the four kings carried off all the goods and food of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 14:10-11). But they were pursued by Abram and defeated (Genesis 14:14-17).
character: He showed a strongly hegemonic disposition toward the surrounding nations, and he was a ruler who maintained such strong military control that he received tribute for twelve years (Genesis 14:4). He is also portrayed as a man of high position and authority in the Near East of that time, enough to lead a coalition of allied kings (Genesis 14:9).

introduce: Keturah is a woman who appears in Genesis, a later wife whom Abraham took (Genesis 25:1). 1 Chronicles 1:32 calls her Abraham's concubine. She bore Abraham six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah (Genesis 25:2).
lifetime: Abraham took another wife, and her name was Keturah (Genesis 25:1). She bore to Abraham Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah (Genesis 25:2). During his lifetime Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubines and sent them away from his son Isaac to the east, to the land of the east (Genesis 25:6).
event: From her son Jokshan came Sheba and Dedan (Genesis 25:3), and the sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah, all descendants of Keturah (Genesis 25:4). 1 Chronicles 1:32-33 calls her Abraham's concubine and records the names of the sons she bore once again (1 Chronicles 1:32-33).

introduce: Crescens is a figure whose name appears in 2 Timothy 4:10 in the New Testament; in the letter the apostle Paul sent to Timothy it is recorded that he went to Galatia.
lifetime: In his letter to Timothy, Paul wrote that Demas had gone to Thessalonica, Crescens to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia (2 Timothy 4:10). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.
event: Crescens went to Galatia (2 Timothy 4:10). The Bible has no record of the specific reason or purpose for his going to Galatia, or of what he did afterward.

introduce: Cherub is a name that appears in Ezra 2:59 and Nehemiah 7:61 together with Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Addan (Addon in Nehemiah), and Immer; it is recorded that there were people who came up from those places, but they could not show whether their families and genealogy belonged to Israel (Ezra 2:59, Nehemiah 7:61). In the context of the text, it appears not as the deeds of an individual but as the name of a place from which the returnees came up.
lifetime: Following the record of the return of those who had been carried captive by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and came back to Jerusalem and Judah (Ezra 2:1, Nehemiah 7:6), it is recorded that there were people who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan (Addon), and Immer (Ezra 2:59, Nehemiah 7:61). The Bible has no record of Cherub's own life.
event: Those who came up from Cherub, Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Addan (Addon), and Immer could not show whether their families and genealogy belonged to Israel (Ezra 2:59, Nehemiah 7:61).

introduce: He was a Jew living in the region of Corinth, the ruler of the synagogue at the time of the apostle Paul's ministry in Corinth.
lifetime: He was the ruler of the Jewish synagogue in Corinth and converted to the Christian faith through Paul's evangelistic work (Acts 18:8). After his conversion, he came to believe in Jesus together with his whole household (Acts 18:8). No specific record appears concerning his deeds after Paul left Corinth.
event: Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord together with all his household (Acts 18:8). He is also recorded as one of those among the Corinthians whom Paul baptized, along with Gaius (1 Corinthians 1:14). Later, Paul was brought before the judgment seat in Corinth (Acts 18:12-17), but the Bible has no record of what position Crispus held in that incident.
character: Although he held the high office of synagogue ruler, a leader of Judaism, he showed the resolve to accept the gospel that Paul preached (Acts 18:8). He took the leading role of bringing not only himself but his whole household to the Christian faith (Acts 18:8).

call: third son of Nahor and Milcah
introduce: Kemuel is the third of the eight sons born to Nahor, Abraham's brother, and his wife Milcah. Genesis 22:21 introduces him as "the father of Aram."
lifetime: Kemuel is mentioned as one of the sons of Nahor, and the fact of his birth is recorded within Abraham's family line (Genesis 22:21). The Bible contains no separate specific record concerning his life.

call: the Geshurites (Aramean kingdom in the northeast)
introduce: Geshur is the name of a people or kingdom that appears in the Bible as "the Geshurites" and "Talmai king of Geshur." The territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites is recorded together with Mount Hermon and the whole of Bashan (Joshua 13:11), and it was the maternal home of David's son Absalom and the place where Absalom fled and stayed (2 Samuel 3:3; 13:37-38).
lifetime: Absalom, the third of the sons whom David fathered in Hebron, was the son of Maacah, the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur (2 Samuel 3:2-3). After Absalom killed his half brother Amnon (2 Samuel 13:28-29), he fled to his maternal grandfather Talmai king of Geshur and stayed in Geshur three years (2 Samuel 13:37-38).
event: Because the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites and the Maacathites, Geshur and Maacah dwelt in the midst of Israel (Joshua 13:13). David's son Absalom, after killing Amnon, fled to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur (2 Samuel 13:37). Also, Geshur together with Aram took the towns of Jair and Kenath and its villages, sixty towns in all (1 Chronicles 2:23).
character: Geshur was an independent small Aramean kingdom of the ancient Near East and possessed its own kingship (2 Samuel 3:3). It maintained close diplomatic relations with the royal house of David, and it exercised independent political influence, enough to become a refuge for Absalom (2 Samuel 13:37). Geographically, it lay on the border of Bashan and had the character of a military stronghold (Joshua 13:11).

직업/직위: people of the kingdom of Geshur

introduce: Geuel is a figure who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, a chief of the tribe of Gad and one of the spies whom Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:2-3, 15).
lifetime: Geuel was the son of Machi of the tribe of Gad, and when Moses chose one man from each tribe of the Israelites to spy out the land of Canaan, he was chosen as the spy representing the tribe of Gad (Numbers 13:15).
event: Together with the other spies, Geuel spied out the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, toward Lebo-hamath (Numbers 13:21), and after finishing spying out the land for forty days, he returned (Numbers 13:25). On returning, he reported to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation, showing them the fruit of the land (Numbers 13:26-27). No other deeds of Geuel himself are recorded separately.

직업/직위: clan chief of the tribe of Gad

introduce: Keilah is a figure in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah who appears as "Keilah the Garmite" in 1 Chronicles 4:19. The text records one of the sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham, as "the father of Keilah the Garmite" (1 Chronicles 4:19). Interpretation of this verse is divided, and the KJV reads Hodiah herself as the wife of Naham's sister with "his wife Hodiah the sister of Naham" (1 Chronicles 4:19).
lifetime: In 1 Chronicles 4:19, "Keilah the Garmite" is introduced only through his father and is not recorded as the wife of Naham. His father was one of the sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham, and his brother Eshtemoa the Maacathite is recorded with him (1 Chronicles 4:19). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.

직업/직위: founder / chief of the town of Keilah

introduce: Claudia is a person whose name appears in 2 Timothy 4:21 in Paul's letter to Timothy as one who sends greetings to Timothy.
lifetime: At the end of Paul's letter to Timothy, she is recorded, together with Eubulus, Pudens, and Linus, along with all the brothers, as one who sends greetings to Timothy (2 Timothy 4:21). The Bible has no record of the rest of her life.
event: She is included in the statement at the end of Paul's letter to Timothy that Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers send greetings to Timothy (2 Timothy 4:21).

introduce: Claudius was the fourth emperor of the Roman Empire, a figure who stands in close contact with the early church in biblical history through the prophecy of a famine and the decree expelling the Jews.
lifetime: He was born in 10 BC and ruled the Roman Empire from AD 41 to 54. During his reign, Agabus prophesied that a great famine would come over the whole world in the days of Claudius (Acts 11:28). He is also recorded as the one who commanded all the Jews to leave Rome (Acts 18:2).
event: When a great famine came over the whole world in the days of Claudius, the disciples in Antioch determined, each according to his ability, to send relief to the brothers living in Judea (Acts 11:28-29). Also, because Claudius commanded all the Jews to leave Rome, Paul met in Corinth Aquila, who had recently come from Italy, and his wife Priscilla (Acts 18:1-2).

introduce: Claudius Lysias is a tribune of the Roman Empire who appears in Acts, a man who played an important role in protecting Paul in Jerusalem and escorting him to Caesarea.
lifetime: When Paul was in danger of being killed after being seized by the Jews in Jerusalem, as tribune he ran down with soldiers and centurions and had Paul brought into the barracks (Acts 21:31-34). When it became known that Paul was a Roman, those who were about to examine him withdrew, and the tribune also was afraid because he had bound Paul (Acts 22:29), and the next day, wishing to know the real reason why Paul was accused by the Jews, he released his bonds (Acts 22:30). Afterward, hearing of the plot of more than forty men to kill Paul, he had foot soldiers, horsemen, and spearmen made ready to escort him by night to Felix the governor in Caesarea (Acts 23:16-33).
event: He ordered Paul, whom he had brought into the barracks in Jerusalem, to be examined by flogging, but when they stretched him out with the thongs and it became known that Paul was a Roman, those who were about to examine him withdrew, and the tribune also was afraid (Acts 22:24-29). The next day he released his bonds, assembled the chief priests and the whole council, and brought Paul down and set him before them (Acts 22:30). When a great dispute arose in the council, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces, he ordered the soldiers to take him by force from among them and bring him into the barracks (Acts 23:10). Hearing through Paul's nephew that more than forty men were lying in wait to kill Paul (Acts 23:16-22), he called two centurions and had them prepare two hundred foot soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea at the third hour of the night (Acts 23:23-24), and in a letter to Felix the governor he reported that he had found nothing in Paul deserving death or imprisonment (Acts 23:25-30).
character: Faithful to his duty, he showed an attitude of observing the regulations so that a Roman citizen would not be treated unjustly (Acts 22:29). Also, from the fact that he mobilized a large military force to secure Paul's safety, it can be seen that he had a quick grasp of situations and an administrative side skilled in organizing operations (Acts 23:23-24).

직업/직위: Roman commander (commander of the Antonia Fortress in Jerusalem)

introduce: Chelal is a man whose name is recorded in Ezra 10 as one of the descendants of Pahath-moab who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:30, 44).
lifetime: As a descendant of Pahath-moab, his name is recorded in the list of those who took foreign women as wives in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:30, 44).
event: In the time of Ezra, his name was entered in the list of those who had taken foreign women, as one of the descendants of Pahath-moab (Ezra 10:30, 44). At that time the people made a covenant with God to send away all the wives they had taken from foreign women and their children, and Ezra had all Israel swear to act according to this word (Ezra 10:3-5), but there is no separate record concerning Chelal's own compliance.

직업/직위: leader of the descendants of Pahath-moab

introduce: Clement is a man mentioned by the apostle Paul in Philippians 4:3, where Paul urged that the women who had struggled with him in the gospel be helped, along with Clement and his other fellow workers (Philippians 4:3).
lifetime: His name is mentioned in Philippians 4:3 together with Paul's fellow workers (Philippians 4:3). The Bible contains no record of his birth, upbringing, or what happened after his death.
event: Paul asked that Clement and his other fellow workers be helped, and said that their names are in the Book of Life (Philippians 4:3).

call: disciple on the road to Emmaus
introduce: Cleopas is a figure mentioned in the Gospel of Luke in the New Testament as one of the two disciples who met the risen Jesus on the road from Jerusalem to Emmaus on the very day of his resurrection. The view that Cleopas (Κλωπᾶς, Clopas) and Alphaeus (Ἀλφαῖος, Alphaeus) are the same person is old and is a hypothesis that can be explained linguistically, but it cannot be established from the biblical text alone that they are the same person.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the two persons going on the day of the resurrection from Jerusalem to a village called Emmaus, the one named Cleopas (Luke 24:13, 18). In John 19:25, Mary the wife of Clopas appears among the women standing by the cross of Jesus, but the text does not state whether this Clopas is the same person as the Cleopas of Luke 24:18. There is no specific record of his earlier life or lineage.
event: On the road to Emmaus, without recognizing that the one walking with him was the risen Jesus, he explained the events that had taken place in Jerusalem (Luke 24:15-24). When they drew near the village and Jesus acted as though he were going farther, the two urged him strongly to stay with them (Luke 24:28-29), and when Jesus took bread and broke it as they sat at table, their eyes were opened and they recognized him (Luke 24:30-31). That very hour they rose and returned to Jerusalem and told the eleven apostles and those with them what had happened on the road and how Jesus had been made known to them in the breaking of the bread (Luke 24:33-35).
character: He was feeling grief and disappointment at the death of Jesus, which shows that his expectation, that Jesus was the one who would redeem Israel, had been dashed (Luke 24:17, 24:21). He had a spirit of hospitality, urging a stranger and traveler to stay with them, and he was a man of strong initiative who returned to Jerusalem in the night immediately after confirming the resurrection (Luke 24:29, 24:33).

introduce: Chloe is a woman whose name appears in 1 Corinthians 1:11; Paul said that it had been reported to him by "Chloe's people" that there were quarrels among the church in Corinth. The Bible contains no record of her personal background or detailed history.
event: It was reported to Paul by Chloe's people that there were quarrels in the church in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:11). On the basis of this news, Paul dealt in his letter with the quarrels of the church in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:10-12).
character: In the biblical record there is no direct description of what kind of character she had. However, since Paul specifically mentioned the people of her household, it can be presumed that she was someone whom Paul trusted sufficiently or had known (1 Corinthians 1:11).

직업/직위: believer in the church at Corinth

introduce: Caleb is a man mentioned as a son of Hezron in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:9). In 1 Chronicles 2:18 and 2:42 a Caleb is recorded as a son of Hezron or as a brother of Jerahmeel, so Caleb is attached to this entry as an alternate name, but he is a different person from Caleb son of Jephunneh, who spied out Canaan together with Joshua (Numbers 13:6).
lifetime: He is a son born to Hezron, who was a grandson of Judah and a son of Perez (1 Chronicles 2:9).
event: The descendants of Caleb, that is, the sons of Hur the firstborn of Ephrathah, namely Shobal, Salma, and Hareph, are recorded as the fathers of Kiriath-jearim, Bethlehem, and Beth-gader respectively (1 Chronicles 2:50-51). Among them, the descendants of Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim are recorded as Haroeh and half of the Manahathites (1 Chronicles 2:52).

직업/직위: clan chief of the tribe of Judah

introduce: Cheluhi is a man whose name is recorded in Ezra 10 as one of the descendants of Bani who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:34-35, 44).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the descendants of Bani in the list of those who took foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:34-35, 44).
event: In the time of Ezra, his name was entered in the list of those who had taken foreign women, as one of the descendants of Bani (Ezra 10:34-35, 44). At that time the people made a covenant with God to send away all the wives they had taken from foreign women and their children, and Ezra had all Israel swear to act according to this word (Ezra 10:3-5), but there is no separate record concerning Cheluhi's own compliance.

introduce: Chelub is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, the older brother of Shuhah and the father of Mehir (1 Chronicles 4:11).
lifetime: He was the brother of Shuhah and fathered Mehir, and Mehir was the father of Eshton (1 Chronicles 4:11). The Bible does not specify other major points of his birth or life.

introduce: Kelita is a man recorded as one of the Levites who took foreign women as wives in Jerusalem after the return from the exile. (In Ezra 10:23 he is recorded as "Kelaiah, that is, Kelita.")
lifetime: After returning from the Babylonian exile, his name appears as one of the Levites in the record of the investigation of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:17, 10:23).
event: When, in the time of Ezra, the people were made to swear to send away the wives they had taken from foreign women and their children (Ezra 10:3, 10:5), his name was entered, as one of the Levites, in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:23, 10:44).

introduce: Keziah is a figure who appears in Job 42:14, the second of the three daughters Job had after he overcame his trials and was restored.
lifetime: Keziah is one of the children born as a result of the blessing God bestowed on Job again after his suffering ended (Job 42:12-14). As Job's second daughter, her name is recorded together with Job's first daughter Jemimah and his third daughter Keren-happuch (Job 42:14).
event: Together with Job's other daughters, it is recorded of Keziah that "No women as beautiful as Job's daughters could be found in all the land," and their father Job granted them an inheritance among their brothers (Job 42:15).

introduce: Ginath is a figure who appears when, after the death of Zimri king of northern Israel, the people of Israel were divided into two parties and opposed each other over succession to the throne. Ginath's son Tibni is recorded as the man who contended with Omri for the throne (1 Kings 16:21).
lifetime: Ginath appears in the Bible only as the father of Tibni, in the role of explaining his lineage (1 Kings 16:21). No specific information about his life or activity is recorded.
event: Ginath's son Tibni engaged in a power struggle with Omri to take the throne of northern Israel, and as a result the people of Israel were divided in two and fell into conflict (1 Kings 16:21). Afterward, when Tibni died, Omri established his kingship, and in this process the name of Ginath was mentioned only to identify Tibni's father (1 Kings 16:22).

introduce: Chidon is a man whose name appears in 1 Chronicles 13 only in the expression "the threshing floor of Chidon." The biblical text has no record of his genealogy or status (1 Chronicles 13:9).
lifetime: When David was about to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim, they carried it on a new cart out of the house of Abinadab, and Uzzah and Ahio were driving the cart (1 Chronicles 13:5-7); the place where the oxen stumbled is recorded as "the threshing floor of Chidon" (1 Chronicles 13:9). There is no record of Chidon's own life.
event: No deeds of Chidon himself are recorded. At the threshing floor of Chidon, because the oxen stumbled, Uzzah reached out his hand and took hold of the ark (1 Chronicles 13:9), and the LORD struck Uzzah down, and he died there before God (1 Chronicles 13:10). The same incident is recorded in 2 Samuel 6:6 as "the threshing floor of Nacon" (2 Samuel 6:6).

기타관계: Uzzah#2778(figure in the threshing-floor incident with the ark)

introduce: Gideoni is a man recorded as the father of Abidan, a chief of the tribe of Benjamin. In Numbers his name appears only in the form "Abidan son of Gideoni," and no deeds of Gideoni himself are recorded (Numbers 1:11).
lifetime: There is no record of Gideoni's own life. His son Abidan was appointed as the man representing the tribe of Benjamin at the census (Numbers 1:11), was chief of the descendants of Benjamin in the arrangement of the camp in the wilderness (Numbers 2:22), presented his offering as chief of the descendants of Benjamin on the ninth day of the dedication of the tabernacle (Numbers 7:60), and led the host of the tribe of the descendants of Benjamin on the march (Numbers 10:24).
event: No event of Gideoni himself is recorded. His son Abidan presented his offering as chief of the descendants of Benjamin on the ninth day of the dedication of the tabernacle (Numbers 7:60), and the peace offering was two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old (Numbers 7:65).

meaning: one who cuts down, one who cuts off
introduce: Gideon, the son of Joash of the tribe of Manasseh, was one of the judges active in the period of the judges of Israel. He was a military leader who organized an army and waged war to deliver Israel from the oppression of Midian.
lifetime: Living in Ophrah, he was called by an angel while threshing wheat in a winepress (Judges 6:11).
