On the day he tore down the altar of Baal and cut down the Asherah pole, people began to call him Jerubbaal (Judges 6:32). Before the war with Midian he selected 300 mighty men and carried out a surprise operation (Judges 7:7). After the victory in the war, the Israelites asked him to rule over them, he and his son and his grandson, but he refused (Judges 8:22-23). In his later years he had many wives and children, and he died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash (Judges 8:30-32).
event: There is the incident in which he destroyed the altar of Baal belonging to his father and cut down the Asherah pole (Judges 6:25-27). He asked for the sign of confirming, by means of a fleece, where the dew would fall (Judges 6:37-40). He reduced an army of 32,000 to 300, surrounded the camp of Midian by night, and won by psychological warfare using trumpets and torches (Judges 7:16-22). He pursued the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and captured them (Judges 8:12) and killed them (Judges 8:21). He gathered gold earrings and made an ephod and placed it in his city Ophrah, but afterward it brought about the result that the people of Israel worshiped it in an unfaithful way (Judges 8:27).
character: He showed humility and low self-esteem, confessing that his clan was the weakest in Manasseh and that he was the youngest in his father's house (Judges 6:15). Before the war he showed a careful and cautious attitude, repeatedly seeking to confirm the will of God in order to gain assurance (Judges 6:39). During the war he showed a tactical side, controlling his warriors thoroughly and deploying them strategically (Judges 7:17). In peacetime he held the view of government that rejected the monarchy and held that the LORD would rule over Israel (Judges 8:23).

기타관계: Iezer#2869(kinsman of the tribe of Manasseh)

introduce: Kiriath-jearim is the entry that appears in the list of the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian exile as "the descendants of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, 743" (Ezra 2:25). The text has no individual introduction of Kiriath-jearim.
lifetime: It is recorded in the list of the people of Israel who were released from Babylon with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and others and returned to Jerusalem and Judah (Ezra 2:1-2, Ezra 2:25).
event: In the list of returnees, grouped together with Chephirah and Beeroth, "the descendants of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth" were recorded as 743 (Ezra 2:25).

meaning: city of forests, city of trees
introduce: Kiriath-jearim appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2) in connection with Shobal, and Shobal is recorded as "the father of Kiriath-jearim" (1 Chronicles 2:50, 2:52). The text records no deeds of Kiriath-jearim itself.
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 2:50, listing the descendants of Caleb, that is, the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, calls Shobal "the father of Kiriath-jearim." There is no other record of the life of Kiriath-jearim itself.
event: No event of Kiriath-jearim itself is recorded. The descendants of Shobal, the father of Kiriath-jearim, were Haroeh and half of the Manahathites (1 Chronicles 2:52), and it is recorded that the clans of Kiriath-jearim were the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites, and that from these came the two clans of the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites (1 Chronicles 2:53).

introduce: Chilion is a figure who appears in the book of Ruth in the Old Testament, one of the two sons of Elimelech, an Ephrathite of Bethlehem in Judah, and Naomi (Ruth 1:2).
lifetime: Chilion was an Ephrathite of Bethlehem in Judah, and when a famine came upon the land in the time when the judges ruled, he went with his parents and Mahlon to the country of Moab and lived there (Ruth 1:1-2). In Moab he took a Moabite woman, Orpah, as his wife (Ruth 1:4). After they had lived there about ten years, he died together with Mahlon (Ruth 1:4-5).
event: No special achievement or leading event of Chilion himself is recorded. He took a Moabite woman as his wife, and about ten years after settling there he died together with Mahlon (Ruth 1:4-5); later Boaz bought from the hand of Naomi all that belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon (Ruth 4:9).
character: The biblical text gives no specific description of Chilion's character or personal traits. All that is confirmed is that, as one of Elimelech's family, he settled and lived in Moab (Ruth 1:2, 1:4).

call: Name of a town in the genealogy of Judah ('Sheva, the father of Gibea')
introduce: Gibea is a name belonging to the genealogy of Caleb of the tribe of Judah; Sheva, born to Caleb's concubine Maacah, is recorded as "the father of Machbenah and the father of Gibea" (1 Chronicles 2:48-49). No deeds of Gibea himself are recorded.
lifetime: In 1 Chronicles 2:49, Sheva, born to Caleb's concubine Maacah, is recorded as "the father of Machbenah and the father of Gibea" (1 Chronicles 2:48-49). There is no other record of the life of Gibea himself.
event: No event of Gibea himself is recorded. In the same verse, Shaaph is recorded as "the father of Madmannah" and Sheva as "the father of Machbenah and the father of Gibea" (1 Chronicles 2:49).

직업/직위: founder / chief of the town of Gibea

introduce: Gibeon appears in the Benjamite genealogy of 1 Chronicles 8 and 9 in the phrase "Jeiel the father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon." The text records that Jeiel lived in Gibeon, and there is no personal record of Gibeon himself (1 Chronicles 8:29, 9:35).
lifetime: The life of Gibeon himself is not recorded. Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon, and his wife's name was Maacah (1 Chronicles 8:29, 9:35).
event: No event of Gibeon himself is recorded. As the sons of Jeiel are recorded Abdon the firstborn, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth (1 Chronicles 9:36-37), and Mikloth fathered Shimeam (Shimeah in 1 Chronicles 8:32), and these lived in Jerusalem alongside their relatives (1 Chronicles 9:38, 8:32).

직업/직위: woodcutter and water carrier for the temple

introduce: Kish was a man of standing in the tribe of Benjamin and the father of Saul, the first king of Israel. He was a Benjamite introduced as the son of Abiel and the grandson of Zeror (1 Samuel 9:1).
lifetime: Kish was the son of Abiel of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Samuel 9:1) and the father of Saul (1 Samuel 14:51). When his female donkeys were lost, he told his son Saul to take a servant and go look for them (1 Samuel 9:3). Through this matter Saul met Samuel and was anointed king.
event: His main deed appears in the incident of the lost female donkeys. Kish sent his son Saul and a servant to look for the lost female donkeys (1 Samuel 9:3), and this incident became the direct occasion for Saul to meet Samuel and be chosen as king (1 Samuel 9:3-5).
character: Kish is regarded in the Bible as a powerful man (1 Samuel 9:1). He is portrayed as a family man who deeply worried about the safety of his son Saul (1 Samuel 10:2), and he is a figure who shows the life of the typical landowning class of the tribe of Benjamin before the establishment of the early monarchy of Israel.

직업/직위: prominent man of the tribe of Benjamin

introduce: Gishpa was one of the chiefs of the Nethinim who lived on Ophel in Jerusalem after the return from the exile (Nehemiah 11:21).
lifetime: After returning from the Babylonian exile, in the course of the resettlement of the population of Jerusalem, he was recorded as one of the Nethinim living in the district of Ophel (Nehemiah 11:21).
event: Together with Ziha he became a chief of the Nethinim who lived on Ophel (Nehemiah 11:21).

introduce: Chislon is a man of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as the father of Elidad, who was named as a chief of the tribe of Benjamin when the land of Canaan was to be divided (Numbers 34:21).
lifetime: Chislon's own life is not recorded; his name appears only in the form "Elidad son of Chislon" in Numbers 34:21.
event: No event of Chislon himself is recorded. When the LORD said to choose one chief from each tribe to divide the land as an inheritance (Numbers 34:18), his son Elidad was named from the tribe of Benjamin (Numbers 34:21).

introduce: Kishi is a man of the descendants of Merari of the tribe of Levi, recorded as the father of Ethan, who held the duty of singing praise (1 Chronicles 6:44).
lifetime: Kishi was the son of Abdi and the father of Ethan (1 Chronicles 6:44). On the other hand, in 1 Chronicles 15:17 Ethan is recorded as the son of Kushaiah. Kishi, as a descendant of Merari, son of Levi, occupies a genealogical position within the family (1 Chronicles 6:44-47).
event: No deeds of Kishi himself are recorded. Among the group David appointed to have charge of the singing in the house of the LORD after the ark had come to rest, the one of the descendants of Merari who served on the left was Ethan, the son of Kishi (1 Chronicles 6:31, 6:44).

introduce: Ginnethon is a man whose name is recorded in the list of the priests who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1, 12:4).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1, 12:4), and these priests were the leaders of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:7).
event: No deeds of Ginnethon himself are recorded; his name is on the list of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1, 12:4).

introduce: Ginnethon is one of those who sealed the covenant after the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:6).
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, in the time of Nehemiah, he sealed the covenant as one of the priests (Nehemiah 10:6, 10:8).
event: In the process of the making of the covenant led by Nehemiah, his name was included in the list of those who officially sealed it (Nehemiah 10:1). He is mentioned as one of the priests and took part in the process of pledging to keep the ordinances of the community (Nehemiah 10:6).

직업/직위: priestly family head who sealed the covenant

introduce: Gilalai is a figure who appears in the book of Nehemiah in the Old Testament, a member of a priestly family who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem.
lifetime: Gilalai was one of the brothers of Zechariah, a descendant of the priests, and in the procession for the dedication of the wall led by Nehemiah he held the musical instruments of David the man of God (Nehemiah 12:35-36).
event: At the dedication held after the wall of Jerusalem was completed, Gilalai held the musical instruments of David the man of God, and Ezra the scribe went before them (Nehemiah 12:27, 12:36).

introduce: Chileab is the second son whom King David fathered in Hebron. In 1 Chronicles 3:1 he is recorded by the name Daniel.
lifetime: He was born in the time when David reigned in Hebron, to Abigail, who had been the wife of Nabal of Carmel (2 Samuel 3:3). The record of Chronicles mentions his name as Daniel (1 Chronicles 3:1).
event: No deeds of Chileab himself are recorded in the Bible. He is recorded only as the second son whom David fathered in Hebron (2 Samuel 3:2-3); there is no record that Chileab was involved in the matter of the firstborn Amnon being killed by the servants of Absalom (2 Samuel 13:28-29), of the third son Absalom having it proclaimed in Hebron that he had become king (2 Samuel 15:10), or of the fourth son Adonijah exalting himself and saying that he would be king (1 Kings 1:5).

call: son of Machir (ancestor of the Gileadite clan)
introduce: Gilead is a man belonging to the tribe of Manasseh in the genealogy of the Bible, the son of Machir, who was the son of Manasseh. He became the ancestor of the people called the descendants of Gilead.
lifetime: He was born through Machir, the son of Manasseh (Numbers 26:29). Since he was the son of Machir and the grandson of Manasseh, he was a great-grandson of Joseph, and he held an important position within the tribe of Manasseh in carrying on the family line (1 Chronicles 7:17).
event: What came from him was called the Gileadite clan (Numbers 26:29), and as descendants of Gilead the clans from Iezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Shemida, and Hepher are recorded (Numbers 26:30-32). Moses gave the land of Gilead to Machir the son of Manasseh, and he lived in it (Numbers 32:40).

introduce: Chimham is a man who appears as a son of Barzillai the Gileadite. He is mentioned in connection with the kindness Barzillai showed when King David crossed the Jordan River to flee from Absalom's rebellion (2 Samuel 19:37).
lifetime: When King David was returning across the Jordan, Barzillai asked that "your servant Chimham" cross over with the king and that the king do for him what seemed good to the king (2 Samuel 19:37). David answered that Chimham would cross over with him and that he would do for him whatever Barzillai pleased (2 Samuel 19:38). Afterward, when the king crossed on to Gilgal, Chimham crossed with him (2 Samuel 19:40).
event: In the course of King David's return, he accompanied the king across the Jordan as far as Gilgal (2 Samuel 19:40). In accordance with Barzillai's request, David promised to do for him what was good (2 Samuel 19:37-38).

introduce: Gibbar is a name recorded as a group of descendants who finished the Babylonian exile and returned to Judah and Jerusalem (Ezra 2:20). The biblical text records "the descendants of Gibbar, 95" as a group belonging to a family.
lifetime: He is included in the list of the descendants of those carried away captive by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon who returned to Jerusalem and Judah (Ezra 2:1). He is recorded as the descendants of Gibbar in the list of the people of Israel who came out with Zerubbabel and others (Ezra 2:2, 2:20).
event: At the time of the return from the Babylonian exile, ninety-five descendants of Gibbar were recorded in the list of returnees (Ezra 2:20).

직업/직위: ancestor of a family that returned with Zerubbabel (Gibeonite)

introduce: Giddalti is a man who, in the process of organizing the choirs of the tribe of Levi in the days of David, was classified as one of the sons of Heman.
lifetime: Giddalti is recorded ninth among the fourteen sons God gave to Heman (1 Chronicles 25:4-5). When David, together with the commanders of the army, set apart for service some of the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun (1 Chronicles 25:1), the sons of Heman were under the direction of their father to sing and serve in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 25:6).
event: When lots were cast to determine the duties of service in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 25:8), the twenty-second lot fell to the division of Giddalti, with his sons and brothers, twelve persons in all (1 Chronicles 25:29).

call: ancestor of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Giddel is a figure who appears in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah in the Old Testament, recorded as one of the ancestors of the Nethinim who finished the Babylonian exile and returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel.
lifetime: Giddel is mentioned as the ancestor of the descendants of Giddel, one of the families of the Nethinim. His descendants are recorded in the list of the Nethinim who returned from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:43, 2:47). The same list is also recorded in Nehemiah 7 (Nehemiah 7:46, 7:49).
event: The descendants of Giddel were recorded as Nethinim in the list of the people of Israel who came out with Zerubbabel and others (Ezra 2:2, 2:43, 2:47). When Nehemiah found the register of the genealogy of those who had come back at first, the descendants of Giddel were also included in that record as Nethinim (Nehemiah 7:5, 7:46, 7:49).

직업/직위: ancestor of temple servants who returned with Zerubbabel

call: son of Javan (ancestor of the coastland peoples)
introduce: Kittim is recorded as a grandson of Japheth, the son of Noah, and a son of Javan (Genesis 10:2-4).
lifetime: As a son of Javan, his name appears in the genealogy of Genesis 10 (Genesis 10:4) and is recorded also in 1 Chronicles 1 as a son of Javan (1 Chronicles 1:7). There is no other record of Kittim's own life.
event: No deeds of Kittim himself are recorded in the Bible; his name appears only as a son of Javan in Genesis 10:4 and 1 Chronicles 1:7.

introduce: Narcissus is a man whose household is mentioned in the passage of Romans 16 where the apostle Paul sends greetings. In the text it is not Narcissus himself but those of his household who are in the Lord that are recorded as the recipients of the greeting (Romans 16:11).
lifetime: Narcissus is recorded as a man who had a household (Romans 16:11). This letter was sent to the saints in Rome (Romans 1:7), and the recipients of the greeting are those of Narcissus' household who are in the Lord (Romans 16:11). The text has no record as to whether Narcissus himself was a believer.
event: Those of Narcissus' household who are in the Lord are mentioned as recipients of Paul's greeting (Romans 16:11). The Bible has no record of any particular event he carried out or any social achievement (Romans 16:11).

직업/직위: believer in Rome (head of the household of Narcissus)

introduce: He is a figure who appears in the Gospel of John in the New Testament, and he came to Jesus after hearing Philip's word. He is handed down as one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ, and in Matthew 10:3, Mark 3:18, Luke 6:14, and Acts 1:13 he is recorded together with Philip as Bartholomew. In the Gospel of John he appears under the name Nathanael, who is presumed to be the same person.
lifetime: He is recorded as being from Cana of Galilee (John 21:2), and he became Jesus' disciple after meeting him through Philip (John 1:45-49). He is one of the seven disciples who were together when Jesus revealed himself to the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias (John 21:1-2). If he is regarded as the same person as Bartholomew, he is also recorded in the list of the apostles who were in the upper room to which they went up when the disciples returned to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives (Acts 1:12-13).
event: When he first met Jesus through Philip's introduction, he showed a skeptical reaction, asking whether anything good can come out of Nazareth, but he received from Jesus the commendation of being a true Israelite in whom there is no deceit (John 1:46-47). When he heard Jesus' words that he had already seen him when he was under the fig tree, he immediately confessed him as the Son of God and the King of Israel (John 1:48-49). He is recorded as one of the disciples who were together when Jesus revealed himself to the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias (John 21:1-2).
character: He received from Jesus the commendation of being truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit (John 1:47). At first he showed a skeptical attitude that revealed regional prejudice, but after encountering the truth he showed the honesty of immediately revising his own view and acknowledging Jesus (John 1:46-49).

introduce: Nathan is one of the four sons born to King David and Bathsheba, a full brother of Solomon, who succeeded to David's throne. He is recorded as one of the persons mentioned when the genealogy of Jesus is dealt with in the New Testament.
lifetime: He is one of the sons whom David fathered in Jerusalem, and Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon, four in all, are recorded as the children of Bathshua (1 Chronicles 3:5). He is on the list of sons born in Jerusalem together with Solomon (1 Chronicles 14:4). In the genealogy of Jesus recorded in Luke, he is listed as a son of David (Luke 3:31).
event: The record of his birth in Jerusalem as a son of David is entered in 1 Chronicles 3:5 and 14:4. No record appears that he directly succeeded to the throne or led any large political event, and the main deed confirmed is that he is mentioned as a person who continues the line of the genealogy in Luke (Luke 3:31).

introduce: Nathan-melech is a man recorded as an official in the account of King Josiah's reform in 2 Kings 23. In the text his house is mentioned only as a reference point indicating a location.
lifetime: He is recorded as an official at the time when King Josiah was removing from the house of the LORD the things connected with idolatry, and his house was near the entrance of the house of the LORD (2 Kings 23:11).
event: The king removed the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun, and these horses were beside the house of the official Nathan-melech near the entrance to the house of the LORD (2 Kings 23:11). The king also burned the chariot of the sun with fire (2 Kings 23:11). The Bible has no record of any deeds of Nathan-melech himself.

call: Aaron's firstborn (the incident of the unauthorized fire)
introduce: Nadab was the eldest son born to Aaron and Elisheba, a son of Aaron, the first high priest of Israel, and a man who carried out the early priestly office.
lifetime: Nadab is recorded as one of those who, together with Aaron's sons Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, were brought near with Aaron to serve as priests (Exodus 28:1). On Mount Sinai he went up with Moses, Aaron, Abihu, and seventy elders of Israel and saw the God of Israel (Exodus 24:1, 9-11). Afterward, he and Abihu each took his censer, put in it unauthorized fire that the LORD had not commanded, and offered incense before the LORD, and he met his death (Leviticus 10:1-2). He had no children, and Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the presence of their father Aaron (Numbers 3:4).
event: When the people of Israel made the covenant at Mount Sinai, Nadab went up the mountain with the elders and was present at the seeing of God (Exodus 24:9-11). After receiving the ordination to the priesthood, he and Abihu each took his censer, put in it unauthorized fire that the LORD had not commanded, and offered incense before the LORD (Leviticus 10:1). For this, fire came out from before the LORD and consumed them, and Nadab died before the LORD (Leviticus 10:2). Moses relayed to Aaron the word of the LORD, "Among those who are near me I will be proved holy," and Aaron kept silent (Leviticus 10:3).

introduce: He was a Calebite who lived in Maon and whose business was in Carmel, a very wealthy man. He is the man who provoked David's anger by refusing when the young men David had sent greeted him and asked for food.
lifetime: Nabal was a man who lived in Maon, whose business was in Carmel, and who was rich with three thousand sheep and a thousand goats (1 Samuel 25:2). While he was shearing sheep in Carmel, David sent young men to greet him (1 Samuel 25:4-5), and after he insulted David's servants and sent them back (1 Samuel 25:14), he held a feast fit for a king in his house and got very drunk (1 Samuel 25:36). In the morning, when the wine had left him and he heard of this from his wife, he lost heart and his body became like a stone (1 Samuel 25:37), and about ten days later the LORD struck him, and he died (1 Samuel 25:38).
event: David had not harmed Nabal's shepherds in the wilderness (1 Samuel 25:7), but Nabal, saying, "Who is David? Who is the son of Jesse? Many servants nowadays break away from their masters," refused to give bread and water and meat (1 Samuel 25:10-11). Because of this David resolved not to leave alive any male of Nabal's house by morning, but Nabal's wife Abigail went out with provisions and persuaded David, and so David's vengeance was halted (1 Samuel 25:18-35). Nabal did not know of Abigail's meeting with David (1 Samuel 25:19, 36), but in the morning he heard of it from his wife, lost heart, and his body became like a stone, and about ten days later the LORD struck him, and he died (1 Samuel 25:37-38).
character: The Bible describes him as a stubborn man with evil deeds (1 Samuel 25:3). The meaning of his name itself denotes a fool, and indeed even his servants judged him to be a worthless man and said that no one could speak to him (1 Samuel 25:17). It can be seen that he was usually arrogant and harsh in temperament, so that people around him found him hard to deal with (1 Samuel 25:25).

직업/직위: wealthy owner of great flocks and herds

introduce: He was a man who lived in Jezreel in the time of King Ahab of the northern kingdom of Israel, a landowner who possessed a vineyard inherited from his ancestors.
lifetime: Naboth had a vineyard in Jezreel, and the vineyard was near the palace of Ahab king of Samaria (1 Kings 21:1). King Ahab proposed to turn the vineyard into a vegetable garden and offered either money or a better vineyard in exchange, but Naboth refused because it was the inheritance of his ancestors (1 Kings 21:2-3). Afterward the elders and nobles of the city, who had received letters written by Jezebel in Ahab's name, set two worthless men to testify falsely that Naboth had cursed God and the king, and Naboth was taken outside the city and stoned to death (1 Kings 21:8-14).
event: After the incident of refusing the king's proposal, Naboth was falsely accused by scoundrels through Jezebel's scheme (1 Kings 21:8-10). In the trial led by the elders and nobles of the city of Jezreel, he was saddled with the charge of blasphemy through the slander of false witnesses (1 Kings 21:13). Because of this incident Naboth was stoned to death, and his property reverted to King Ahab (1 Kings 21:15-16). A record remains that afterward the dogs licked up the blood of Naboth (1 Kings 21:19).
character: Treasuring the inheritance received from his ancestors, he showed a firm will to preserve it despite the king's coercive proposal (1 Kings 21:3). He held an independent attitude that did not yield to the king's power, and he was a man who tried to adhere to proper procedure in order to protect his own rights (1 Kings 21:3).

introduce: Nahbi is a man mentioned in Numbers in the Old Testament, a spy belonging to the tribe of Naphtali. He is one of the leaders whom Moses selected, one from each tribe, to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:14).
lifetime: Nahbi was the son of Vophsi of the tribe of Naphtali (Numbers 13:14). During the wilderness journey after the exodus, he was one of the men who were heads of the children of Israel, whom Moses sent from the wilderness of Paran at the command of the LORD to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:3, 13:14).
event: Nahbi carried out the mission of spying out the land of Canaan as one of the spies of the twelve tribes of Israel (Numbers 13:14). Together with the other spies, after spying out the whole land of Canaan for forty days, he took part in returning and giving the report (Numbers 13:25).

직업/직위: clan chief of the tribe of Naphtali

introduce: Naphish was one of the twelve sons of Ishmael, a grandson of Abraham, and is recorded as one of the chiefs of the descendants of Ishmael.
lifetime: Naphish was a son of Ishmael, born to Abraham and Hagar, and he is recorded eleventh in the list of Ishmael's sons (Genesis 25:13-15). The sons of Ishmael were called twelve princes according to their tribes (Genesis 25:16), and he is also recorded as a son of Ishmael in 1 Chronicles 1:31 (1 Chronicles 1:31).
event: 1 Chronicles 5:18-19 records that the descendants of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh made war against the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab. In this fight, by the help of God, the Hagrites and those with them were all defeated (1 Chronicles 5:19-20).

직업/직위: one of the twelve princes of Ishmael

call: Lazarus the beggar in the parable
introduce: He is a figure who appears in the parable of the rich man and the beggar Lazarus that Jesus Christ told, the protagonist of a narrative that symbolizes the socially weak and shows the reward of the world after death.
lifetime: A beggar named Lazarus, suffering from sores, lay at the gate of that rich man (Luke 16:20). He longed to be fed with what fell from the rich man's table, and dogs came and licked his sores (Luke 16:21). Afterward the beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham's side (Luke 16:22).
event: While alive, Lazarus lay as a beggar suffering from sores at the rich man's gate (Luke 16:20). After his death he was at Abraham's side, and the rich man, in torment in Hades, asked Abraham to send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool his tongue (Luke 16:23-24). Abraham told the rich man that Lazarus had received bad things in his lifetime, so that now Lazarus was comforted here while he was in agony (Luke 16:25), and also that a great chasm had been fixed between them and so no one could cross over (Luke 16:26).
character: In the biblical text there is no direct description of Lazarus' character (Luke 16:19-31). However, he was physically afflicted with sores, and he had the characteristics of an economically weak person placed in a situation where it was hard to obtain food by himself (Luke 16:20-21).

직업/직위: beggar in the parable (a righteous man)

call: son of Amminadab (commander of the tribe of Judah)
introduce: Nahshon is a man who appears in the Old Testament, a son of Amminadab of the tribe of Judah, who at the time of the exodus acted as a commander of the tribe of Judah and head of the family. He stands at a pivotal link in the genealogy that leads to King David and Jesus Christ.
lifetime: Nahshon was the son of Amminadab and the brother of Elisheba (Exodus 6:23). At the time of the exodus he took part in the census as commander of the descendants of Judah (Numbers 1:7). During the wilderness journey he also led the army of Judah as it marched under the standard of the camp of Judah (Numbers 10:14). According to 1 Chronicles, which records the genealogy of King David, he was a grandson of Ram, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, and a prince of the descendants of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:5, 9-10).
event: At the dedication of the tabernacle, Nahshon presented his offering on the first day, representing the tribe of Judah (Numbers 7:12). His offering was one silver dish of a hundred and thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, one golden pan of ten shekels, and burnt offerings, a sin offering, and peace offerings (Numbers 7:13-17). Also, since his sister Elisheba became Aaron's wife, Nahshon's family came into a marriage relationship with the priestly family (Exodus 6:23).

직업/직위: chief commander and leader of the tribe of Judah

introduce: Naarah is a woman mentioned in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, recorded as one of the wives of Ashhur of the tribe of Judah.
lifetime: She is recorded as one of the two wives of Ashhur, the father of Tekoa (1 Chronicles 4:5). Ashhur was the son whom Abijah, Hezron's wife, bore to him after Hezron died (1 Chronicles 2:24).
event: Naarah bore to Ashhur Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari (1 Chronicles 4:6).

introduce: He is recorded in 1 Chronicles 11 as a son of Ezbai and appears in the list of David's mighty men. In the parallel list of 2 Samuel 23:35, 'Paarai the Arbite' stands in the same place, so he is presumed to be the same person (presumed identity).
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Ezbai, and his name was entered on the list of David's mighty men together with Hezro the Carmelite (1 Chronicles 11:37).
event: Apart from his name being on the list of David's mighty men, no specific deeds of Naarai are recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 11:37).

introduce: Naamah is introduced in Genesis 4 as the sister of Tubal-cain, born to Zillah, the wife of Lamech, a descendant of Cain. She appears in the Bible as one of the women belonging to the genealogy of Cain.
lifetime: Naamah was the sister of Tubal-cain (Genesis 4:22). Tubal-cain was the son born to Zillah, the wife of Lamech (Genesis 4:19, 22). Nothing else is mentioned about her birth or the specific course of her life.
event: In the biblical record, no specific deed or particular event connected with Naamah is described (Genesis 4:22).

introduce: He is a man of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded in Genesis 46:21 as a son of Benjamin, Jacob's son.
lifetime: In the list recording the names of the family of Israel who went down to Egypt, he is recorded as one of the sons of Benjamin (Genesis 46:8, 21).
event: Apart from the list in Genesis 46:21, no individual achievement or particular event of Naaman is recorded.

직업/직위: progenitor of the Naamanite clan of Benjamin

introduce: Naam is a man who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, recorded as a descendant of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh of the tribe of Judah.
lifetime: Naam, as a descendant of Caleb the son of Jephunneh, is recorded together with Iru and Elah (1 Chronicles 4:15).
event: No special achievement or specific event concerning Naam is recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 4:15).

introduce: Naomi is a figure who appears in the book of Ruth in the Old Testament, the wife of Elimelech of Bethlehem and the mother-in-law of Ruth. She is one who moved to Moab to escape a famine, lost her husband and both her sons, and returned to her hometown.
lifetime: When a famine came in Bethlehem, she moved to the country of Moab with her husband Elimelech (Ruth 1:1). There her husband died, and her two sons Mahlon and Chilion took the Moabite women Orpah and Ruth as their wives, and about ten years after they had lived there, both sons also died (Ruth 1:3-5). Afterward, hearing that the LORD had given food to his people, she returned to Bethlehem with her daughter-in-law Ruth (Ruth 1:6-7, 19). After returning, she arranged the marriage of Ruth and Boaz, and she then took Obed, who was born to Boaz and Ruth, into her arms and raised him (Ruth 4:13-17).
event: After returning to Bethlehem, she said not to call her Naomi but to call her Mara, which means bitterness (Ruth 1:20). When Ruth asked to go to the field to glean, Naomi told her to go (Ruth 2:2). She said that Boaz was a close relative of theirs and one of their kinsman-redeemers, and she told Ruth what to do on the threshing floor (Ruth 2:20, 3:1-4). Afterward Boaz bought from Naomi's hand all that belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon, and took Ruth, Mahlon's wife, as his wife, to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance (Ruth 4:9-10).
character: To her daughters-in-law who wanted to follow her, she showed a realistic and caring side by urging them to return to their mothers' houses and find a new life (Ruth 1:8-9). She also revealed a pessimistic view of her own situation by calling herself one who had returned empty (Ruth 1:21). She appreciated the faithfulness of her daughter-in-law Ruth, and she had the aspect of a wise strategist who actively helped for Ruth's future (Ruth 3:1).

introduce: Naharai is a man whose name is on the list of David's mighty men, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah.
lifetime: Naharai is recorded on the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:37, 1 Chronicles 11:39). He was the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah (2 Samuel 23:37, 1 Chronicles 11:39).
event: Naharai is recorded as a Beerothite in 2 Samuel 23:37 and as a Berothite in 1 Chronicles 11:39. The Bible describes no specific battle record or individual event concerning him.

introduce: Nahamani is a man recorded in Nehemiah 7:7 as one of the people of Israel who, having been carried captive by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and then released, returned to Jerusalem and Judah and came out with Zerubbabel and others.
lifetime: Among those who were released from Babylon and returned to Jerusalem and Judah, he is recorded as one who came out with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, Baanah, and others (Nehemiah 7:6-7).
event: He is recorded only as one of the names of those who came out with Zerubbabel and others, in the passage recording the number of the people of Israel who came out together, and the Bible has no record of any individual deeds (Nehemiah 7:7).

직업/직위: leader who returned with Zerubbabel (one of the twelve)

introduce: Nahash is the king of the Ammonites who appears in 1 Samuel in the Old Testament, a man who came up and camped against Jabesh-gilead and stood against Israel in the early period when Saul was enthroned as king of Israel (1 Samuel 11:1, 12:12).
lifetime: Nahash the Ammonite came up and camped against Jabesh-gilead east of the Jordan, and all the men of Jabesh said to him, "Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you" (1 Samuel 11:1). Nahash replied that he would make a covenant with them on the condition that he might put out every one of their right eyes, and said that he would bring reproach upon all Israel in this way (1 Samuel 11:2). Afterward Saul divided the people into three companies and entered the camp of the enemy at dawn and struck the Ammonites, and the survivors were all scattered (1 Samuel 11:11).
event: The incident is recorded in which he camped against Jabesh-gilead and set the condition of putting out the right eyes of the men of Jabesh (1 Samuel 11:1-2). Saul summoned the people, numbered them at Bezek, and went out to rescue Jabesh (1 Samuel 11:7-9), and the next day Saul struck the Ammonites, and the survivors were so scattered that no two of them were left together (1 Samuel 11:11). Samuel later reminded the people that they had demanded a king when they saw that Nahash king of the Ammonites came against them (1 Samuel 12:12).
character: Nahash showed a disposition to propose a cruel method of shaming his opponents, putting out their right eyes, when he subdued enemies (1 Samuel 11:2). He showed the aspect of a warlike politician and commander who ventured aggressive military action against Israel (1 Samuel 11:1). Overconfident in his military superiority, he pressed the people of Israel to surrender on humiliating terms, but he failed to foresee Saul's counterattack and met defeat (1 Samuel 11:11).

introduce: Naham is a figure in the Judah genealogy in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, whose sister is mentioned as the wife of Hodiah (1 Chronicles 4:19).
lifetime: There is no record of Naham's life; it is recorded only that Naham's sister was the wife of Hodiah (1 Chronicles 4:19).
event: The sons of Naham's sister, the wife of Hodiah, are recorded as the father of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maacathite (1 Chronicles 4:19). No deeds of Naham himself are recorded.

introduce: Nahor was a descendant of Shem, the father of Terah and the grandfather of Abraham, a figure in the genealogy of humanity linking the patriarchal period after Noah's flood (Genesis 11:22). He is included in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke and in the list of Israel's ancestors in 1 Chronicles (1 Chronicles 1:26, Luke 3:34).
lifetime: Nahor was born as the son of Serug (Genesis 11:22). He became the father of Terah at the age of 29, and after fathering Terah he lived 119 years and had other children, so the two figures together make 148 years (Genesis 11:24-25). The genealogy of 1 Chronicles 1:26 also records them in the order of Serug, Nahor, and Terah (1 Chronicles 1:26).

call: Elkoshite prophet (author of the book of Nahum)
introduce: Nahum is a prophet known as the author of the book of Nahum in the Old Testament, and his name carries the meaning of comfort. He is recorded as an Elkoshite (Nahum 1:1), and the period of his ministry is not stated directly in the text.
lifetime: Nahum is recorded as being from Elkosh, and specific information about his life hardly appears in the biblical text (Nahum 1:1). The period when he was active is related to the fall of Nineveh, and the prevailing view is that it falls between the fall of Thebes in 663 BC and the destruction of Nineveh in 612 BC.
event: Nahum prophesied that Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, would be completely destroyed by the judgment of God (Nahum 1:1). Speaking of the evil and violence committed by Nineveh, he left a poetic prophecy that the city would become desolate (Nahum 3:1). He also cited the capture and captivity of Thebes as an example and warned that Assyria would meet the same miserable end (Nahum 3:8-10).
character: According to the biblical record, Nahum is characterized by proclaiming the message of judgment against Nineveh in an extremely intense and resolute tone (Nahum 2:1-13). He emphasized the wrath and vengeance of God and declared definitively that the destruction of Nineveh was inevitable (Nahum 1:2-6).

introduce: Naggai is one of the figures appearing in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in the Gospel of Luke in the New Testament, recorded as the son of Maath and the father of Esli.
lifetime: In the genealogy of Jesus in Luke, he is the son of Maath (Luke 3:26) and is recorded as the father of Esli (Luke 3:25).
event: In the biblical record, there is no record of any specific achievement or particular event carried out by Naggai (Luke 3:25).

introduce: Naphtuhim is the ancestor of a people appearing in the list of Noah's descendants that records the genealogy of the peoples of the ancient Near East, and is classified as one of the descendants of Mizraim, the son of Ham.
event: Naphtuhim, as a descendant born of Mizraim, the son of Ham, formed the origin of a people (Genesis 10:13). They are mentioned again in the Chronicles record as one of the descendants of Mizraim (1 Chronicles 1:11).

introduce: Nereus is a figure mentioned in the greetings that the apostle Paul sent to the believers of the church in Rome, and is one of the members of the early Christian community active in Rome.
lifetime: He appears among those to whom greetings are sent at the end of the letter Paul wrote to the Christians in Rome (Romans 16:15).
event: He is named together in the passage near the end of Paul's letter to the church in Rome where Paul says to greet Philologus, Julia, Nereus and his sister, Olympas, and all the saints who are with them (Romans 16:15).

직업/직위: believer in the church at Rome

introduce: Nergal-sharezer is one of the officials of the king of Babylon who sat in the Middle Gate when Jerusalem fell, as recorded in the book of Jeremiah, and he is recorded with the title Rabmag (Jeremiah 39:3, 39:13).
lifetime: When the city of Jerusalem fell on the ninth day of the fourth month of the eleventh year of Zedekiah, all the officials of the king of Babylon came and sat in the Middle Gate, and Nergal-sharezer was among them (Jeremiah 39:2-3). Afterward, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, Nebushazban the Rabsaris, Nergal-sharezer the Rabmag, and all the captains of the king of Babylon sent and took Jeremiah out of the court of the guard and entrusted him to Gedaliah to take him home (Jeremiah 39:13-14).
event: When Jerusalem fell, he sat in the Middle Gate together with the officials of the king of Babylon (Jeremiah 39:3). Together with the captains of the king of Babylon such as Nebuzaradan, he sent and took Jeremiah from the court of the guard and entrusted him to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan (Jeremiah 39:13-14).
character: According to the biblical record, he is portrayed as a commander with a cool-headed, military side who carried out orders during the invasion of Jerusalem (Jeremiah 39:3). He was a person with very great political influence within the Neo-Babylonian Empire, and through the office of Rabmag it can be seen that he had a close relationship with the royal house (Jeremiah 39:13).

introduce: Neri is a figure appearing in a biblical genealogy, mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in Luke as the father of Shealtiel and the son of Melchi.
lifetime: Neri is recorded as the son of Melchi and the father who fathered Shealtiel (Luke 3:27).

introduce: Neriah is a person whose name means in Hebrew "the LORD is my lamp"; he is known as the father of Baruch, the scribe of Jeremiah, and the son of Mahseiah.
lifetime: Neriah is the son of Mahseiah and the father of the scribe Baruch (Jeremiah 32:12). Also, his other son Seraiah is the one who went to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah (Jeremiah 51:59).
event: When his son Baruch wrote the words of the LORD on a scroll at the dictation of Jeremiah, Baruch was specified as the son of Neriah, and so his family line appears in the biblical record (Jeremiah 36:4, 36:32). Also, when his son Seraiah went to Babylon with the king in the fourth year of Zedekiah, the prophet Jeremiah gave him a command; Jeremiah wrote in a single book all the disaster that would come upon Babylon and told Seraiah to read those words when he came to Babylon (Jeremiah 51:59-61).

introduce: Nepheg is recorded as a descendant of Kohath of the tribe of Levi and a son of Izhar. Exodus 6:21 lists Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri as the sons of Izhar.
lifetime: Nepheg belongs to the genealogy of the tribe of Levi as a son of Izhar (Exodus 6:21). In the biblical record, no detailed information appears about his specific life after his birth.

introduce: Nogah is a figure mentioned as one of the sons King David fathered in Jerusalem. He is included in the list of David's children through the record of Chronicles.
lifetime: Nogah is recorded as one of the sons David had in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:7). Apart from this, there is no detailed biblical record of Nogah's life, birth date, or death.
event: No specific achievement or special event carried out by a person named Nogah is recorded in the biblical text (1 Chronicles 3:7).

introduce: Nodab is a party named in 1 Chronicles 5:19, one of those against whom the descendants of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh fought. He is recorded together with the Hagrites, Jetur, and Naphish, and is not a person belonging to the genealogy of the tribe of Gad.
lifetime: According to 1 Chronicles 5:18-19, the warriors of the descendants of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh fought against the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab (1 Chronicles 5:19). Nodab's personal life and family relationships are not recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 5:19).
event: Nodab, together with the Hagrites, Jetur, and Naphish, fought against the descendants of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 5:18-19). In this fight the Hagrites and those who were with them were all given into their hands, and they took away the livestock of their enemies, namely 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, and 2,000 donkeys, and took 100,000 people captive (1 Chronicles 5:20-21).

직업/직위: progenitor of a nomadic Arab tribe

introduce: Nobah is a person whose name appears in Numbers 32:42, recorded as having taken Kenath and its villages and called the place Nobah after his own name.
lifetime: Nobah is recorded in Numbers 32 following the account of the conquest of the Gilead region by the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh and by Jair (Numbers 32:39-42), and his family relationships and the rest of his life are not recorded in the Bible.
event: Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages and called it Nobah after his own name (Numbers 32:42).

직업/직위: military commander of the tribe of Manasseh (conqueror of Kenath)

introduce: He is one of the people of Israel who, in the time of Nehemiah, sealed the covenant after the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem.
lifetime: His name is included in the list of the leaders who sealed the covenant in the process of covenant renewal led by Nehemiah after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 10:19).
event: As one of the heads of the people, a leader-level figure of Israel who swore before God, under a curse, to follow the law of Moses, he sealed the document of the pledge (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:19).

직업/직위: leader of the people who sealed the covenant

introduce: Noah is a figure recorded in Genesis, the son of Lamech and the ninth-generation descendant in the line of Seth (Genesis 5:29). He is recorded as the one who preserved life from the judgment of the great flood (Genesis 7:1).
lifetime: Lamech fathered him at the age of 182, and named him Noah, saying that this son would comfort us in our toilsome labor (Genesis 5:28-29). He lived in the age before the flood, and Noah found favor with the LORD (Genesis 6:8). Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation, and he walked with God (Genesis 6:9). When the flood was on the earth, Noah entered the ark with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives to escape the flood (Genesis 7:1, 7:7).
event: He built the ark as God commanded (Genesis 6:14, 6:22; Hebrews 11:7). As the LORD commanded, he took the clean animals and the unclean animals (Genesis 7:2, 7:5) and entered the ark with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives to escape the flood (Genesis 7:7). He escaped the flood inside the ark, and afterward, at the command of God, he came out of the ark with his wife, his sons, and his sons' wives (Genesis 8:16).
character: Among the people of his time he was regarded as righteous and blameless (Genesis 6:9). He is portrayed as one who found favor before God (Genesis 6:8). With reverent fear concerning things not yet seen, he showed a prudent attitude in preparing the ark (Hebrews 11:7).

call: Levite who counted the vessels (son of Binnui)
introduce: Noadiah, a son of Binnui who appears in the book of Ezra, is a person who, after arriving in Jerusalem with Ezra from Babylon, was present when the silver, gold, and vessels were weighed out in the house of God and handed over to Meremoth.
lifetime: He is a son of Binnui, and after arriving in Jerusalem with Ezra, he was present on the fourth day when the silver, gold, and vessels were weighed out in the house of God and handed over to Meremoth the priest (Ezra 8:32-33).
event: After arriving in Jerusalem and staying three days, on the fourth day, when the silver, gold, and vessels were weighed out in the house of God and handed over to Meremoth son of Uriah the priest, he was there together with Eleazar son of Phinehas and Jozabad son of Jeshua (Ezra 8:33). Everything was counted and weighed, and the total weight was recorded in writing at once (Ezra 8:34).

직업/직위: Levite who counted the temple articles

introduce: Nohah is a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, a figure appearing in the genealogy of Benjamin recorded in 1 Chronicles 8 of the Bible.
lifetime: Nohah is mentioned as the fourth son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:2).

직업/직위: clan chief of the tribe of Benjamin (fourth son)

introduce: Luke is the person who wrote the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles in the New Testament, a companion on the apostle Paul's missionary journeys, and he is known to have been a physician by profession.
lifetime: From Acts 16:10 the narration changes to "we," and he set out with Paul's company for Macedonia and came from Troas to Philippi (Acts 16:10-12). Among those who sent greetings when Paul was imprisoned was Luke, the beloved physician (Colossians 4:14). Also, in a letter Paul wrote it is recorded that, with Demas having left, only Luke was with him (2 Timothy 4:10-11).
event: By writing the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles, he recorded the history of the early church and the deeds of Jesus (Luke 1:3, Acts 1:1). It is recorded in Acts that he accompanied Paul, in the narration using "we," on the voyage in which Paul boarded the ship bound for Italy as a prisoner and encountered the violent wind called Euroclydon (Acts 27:1, 27:14). Paul called him the beloved physician (Colossians 4:14).
character: He was a faithful co-worker who stayed by Paul's side to the end, even in the situation where Paul was in hardship, and helped his ministry (2 Timothy 4:11). On the basis of his professional background as a physician, he showed an observant eye that arranged the circumstances of events in his writings in detail and in an orderly way (Luke 1:3).

직업/직위: Gospel writer (author of Luke and Acts)

introduce: Lucius is a Cyrenian recorded in Acts as one of the prophets and teachers of the church at Antioch.
lifetime: He is mentioned as Lucius of Cyrene, one of the prophets and teachers who were in the church at Antioch (Acts 13:1). In Romans 16:21 Lucius, a kinsman of Paul, appears as one who sends greetings, but the text does not make clear whether he is the same person.
event: When the prophets and teachers of the church at Antioch were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said to set apart Barnabas and Saul, and so they fasted and prayed, laid hands on the two men, and sent them off (Acts 13:2-3). He is recorded as one of these prophets and teachers (Acts 13:1).

직업/직위: prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch

introduce: Nun is a figure appearing in the Old Testament, from the tribe of Ephraim, and the father of Joshua.
lifetime: Nun is the son of Elishama, a descendant of Ephraim, and his son is Joshua (1 Chronicles 7:26-27). In Numbers, Moses called Hoshea, the son of Nun of the tribe of Ephraim, Joshua (Numbers 13:8, 13:16). The Bible does not record the deeds of Nun himself; he is mentioned in the words that introduce Joshua as the son of Nun (Exodus 33:11, Numbers 11:28, 14:6).
event: Nun does not appear as the agent of any direct historical event and is recorded only as the father of Joshua. In the genealogy of the descendants of Ephraim he appears as the son of Elishama and the father of Joshua (1 Chronicles 7:26-27).

직업/직위: clan chief of the tribe of Ephraim

기타관계: Ammihud#2226(kinsman of the tribe of Ephraim)

introduce: Nympha is a believer to whom greetings were sent at the end of the letter the apostle Paul sent to the church at Colossae. (Colossians 4:15)
lifetime: She appears in the process of Paul conveying greetings to the believers of the church at Colossae, where he mentions the brothers at Laodicea, Nympha, and the church in her house. (Colossians 4:15)
event: There was a church in Nympha's house, and Paul sent greetings to Nympha and the church in her house. (Colossians 4:15)

introduce: Neco refers to Pharaoh Necho II of the Twenty-sixth Dynasty of ancient Egypt, and is mentioned in 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles as Neco king of Egypt and Pharaoh Neco. He was a ruler who exercised geopolitical influence amid the balance of power between Assyria and Babylon in the late seventh century BC.
lifetime: When Neco king of Egypt marched up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates, Josiah king of Judah went out to confront him (2 Chronicles 35:20); Neco sent messengers to Josiah telling him not to fight, but Josiah did not listen and fought on the Plain of Megiddo (2 Chronicles 35:21-22). After Josiah died, Neco imprisoned Jehoahaz at Riblah in the land of Hamath so that he could not become king, and made Eliakim the son of Josiah king, changing his name to Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:33-34). After that, the king of Egypt never came out of his land again, because the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to the king of Egypt, from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates River (2 Kings 24:7).
event: When Pharaoh Neco went up to the Euphrates River to fight the king of Assyria, King Josiah went out to confront him, and the king of Egypt met Josiah at Megiddo and killed him (2 Kings 23:29). Pharaoh Neco imprisoned Jehoahaz at Riblah in the land of Hamath so that he could not reign in Jerusalem, and imposed on that land a fine of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold (2 Kings 23:33; 2 Chronicles 36:3). He also made Eliakim the son of Josiah king and changed his name to Jehoiakim, and took Jehoahaz away to Egypt (2 Kings 23:34; 2 Chronicles 36:4).
character: To achieve his own military objectives, he pursued a coercive foreign policy, directly manipulating the kingship of the neighboring state of Judah and forcing it to pay tribute (2 Kings 23:33). By sending messengers to Josiah urging him not to fight against him, he showed himself attempting strategic judgment (2 Chronicles 35:21).

call: ancestor of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Nekoda is recorded as the ancestor of a family among the Nethinim who returned from the Babylonian captivity. His existence is confirmed by the mention of his descendants in the lists of returnees in Ezra and Nehemiah.
lifetime: There is no record directly describing Nekoda's life; he appears only as the descendants of Nekoda in the list of the Nethinim who returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:43, 2:48). Ezra 2 introduces this list as the number of the men of the people of Israel who came with Zerubbabel and others (Ezra 2:2). The same list is also recorded in Nehemiah (Nehemiah 7:46, 7:50).
event: His descendants were entered by name in the list of the returning Nethinim (Ezra 2:48, Nehemiah 7:50). The Nethinim are recorded as those whom David and the officials appointed to serve the Levites (Ezra 8:20).

직업/직위: ancestor of temple servants who returned with Zerubbabel

call: father of Ishmael (father of the assassin of the governor)
introduce: Nethaniah is the father of Ishmael, who killed Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor after the fall of Jerusalem. He is recorded as the son of Elishama, of the royal family.
lifetime: Nethaniah is recorded as the son of Elishama, a member of the royal family (2 Kings 25:25, Jeremiah 41:1). His son Ishmael went in the seventh month with ten men to Mizpah and struck down with the sword Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor over the land (Jeremiah 41:1-2). Nethaniah is mentioned mainly in the words introducing his son Ishmael (Jeremiah 40:8, 40:14).
character: At the time of the assassination of Gedaliah, the governor of Judah, he was present at the scene together with Ishmael, and through this event he was implicated in the process by which the remaining leadership structure of the kingdom of Judah collapsed (2 Kings 25:25).

직업/직위: member of the royal family of Judah

introduce: Nethanel is a figure appearing in the book of Numbers of the Old Testament, a commander of the descendants of Issachar and a son of Zuar. In the process of the exodus from Egypt he served as one of the leaders representing the tribes of Israel.
lifetime: Nethanel was a chief of the tribe of Issachar, and his name was recorded as one of the heads of the tribes who were to stand with Moses (Numbers 1:4-5, 1:8). His camping position was fixed as chief of the descendants of Issachar (Numbers 2:5), he presented his offering on the second day at the dedication of the tabernacle (Numbers 7:18), and when they marched he led the army of the tribe of the descendants of Issachar (Numbers 10:15).
event: In accordance with the command that the chiefs present their offerings for the dedication of the altar, one man each day (Numbers 7:11), he presented his offering on the second day as chief of Issachar (Numbers 7:18). His offering was one silver platter weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel; one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense; for a burnt offering one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old; for a sin offering one male goat; and for a peace offering two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old (Numbers 7:19-23).

직업/직위: commander and clan chief of the tribe of Issachar

introduce: Nethaniah is recorded as the son of Shelemiah and the father of Jehudi. Jehudi is the person whom the officials sent to Baruch to tell him to bring the scroll (Jeremiah 36:14).
lifetime: No special details are recorded.
event: In the biblical record no direct activity or achievement of Nethaniah himself appears; he is mentioned only as the father of Jehudi in the passage where his son Jehudi, sent by all the officials, went to Baruch and told him to bring the scroll that he had read in the hearing of the people (Jeremiah 36:14).

meaning: the LORD has given a willing heart
introduce: Nedabiah is mentioned as one of the sons of Jehoiachin king of Judah. His existence is confirmed through the genealogical records of the Bible.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Jehoiachin, king of Judah (1 Chronicles 3:18).

introduce: Nemuel is a figure appearing in the book of Numbers of the Old Testament, a grandson of Pallu, son of Reuben, the eldest son of Jacob, and a son of Eliab. He is recorded as a son of Eliab together with Dathan and Abiram.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Eliab, a descendant of Reuben (Numbers 26:9). Eliab is the son of Pallu (Numbers 26:8), and Pallu is a family of the descendants of Reuben (Numbers 26:5). His name appears within the genealogy of the descendants of Reuben at the time when Moses and Eleazar the priest counted those twenty years old and upward on the plains of Moab (Numbers 26:3-9).
event: Dathan and Abiram, who are recorded together with Nemuel as sons of Eliab, were those called from the congregation, but they joined the company of Korah and rebelled against the LORD by opposing Moses and Aaron (Numbers 26:9). The text does not record any deeds of Nemuel himself.

직업/직위: leader of the tribe of Reuben

introduce: Nebaioth is the eldest son of Ishmael and a grandson of Abraham, and is known as a chief of the Ishmaelite tribe.
lifetime: He was born as the firstborn son of Ishmael (Genesis 25:13). His name is mentioned first in the list of the sons of Ishmael (1 Chronicles 1:29). The sons of Ishmael were twelve princes according to their tribes (Genesis 25:16).
event: Esau took as his wife Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael and the sister of Nebaioth (Genesis 28:9). The book of Isaiah mentions the name of Nebaioth and records that the rams of Nebaioth would serve and go up on my altar with acceptance (Isaiah 60:7).

직업/직위: firstborn of Ishmael (progenitor of the Nabataeans)

introduce: Nebat is the father of Jeroboam I, the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel. In the Bible he appears mainly as a figure used to qualify his son Jeroboam.
lifetime: Nebat's son Jeroboam was an Ephraimite from Zeredah, and his mother was a widow named Zeruah (1 Kings 11:26). Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor, whom Solomon put in charge of the labor force of the house of Joseph (1 Kings 11:28). The Bible does not separately record Nebat's own origin or life.
event: In the biblical record no specific achievement or event of Nebat himself appears; he is mentioned only indirectly through the expression "Jeroboam son of Nebat," a designation that qualifies his son Jeroboam. This designation is used repeatedly when Jeroboam is described as the one who made Israel sin (1 Kings 16:26, 1 Kings 16:31, 2 Kings 3:3).

introduce: The Nebo mentioned in the Bible is broadly divided into a place name and a personal name; as a person, Nebo is recorded as one of the Israelites who finished the Babylonian captivity and returned to Judah in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah.
lifetime: He is included in the list of the Israelites who returned from the Babylonian captivity (Ezra 2:29). His name is mentioned once more in the list of returnees recorded by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 7:33).
event: Among the descendants of Nebo, Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah are recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:43-44).

introduce: Nebuchadnezzar II was the second king of the Neo-Babylonian Empire, who ruled from 605 to 562 BC and led the empire as the greatest power of the ancient Near East. In the Bible he is recorded as the ruler who destroyed the kingdom of Judah, demolished Jerusalem, and relocated the Jews to Babylon.
lifetime: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim, Nebuchadnezzar defeated the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt at Carchemish by the Euphrates River (Jeremiah 46:2), and the king of Babylon took all that belonged to the king of Egypt, from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates River (2 Kings 24:7). He came up in the time of Jehoiakim of Judah, and Jehoiakim served him for three years and then turned and rebelled (2 Kings 24:1). Afterward, in the time of Jehoiachin, when his servants besieged Jerusalem, he too came to the city (2 Kings 24:10-11), and in the ninth year of Zedekiah he came up against Jerusalem with all his army, encamped, and built a siege mound (2 Kings 25:1). In his nineteenth year Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, came to Jerusalem, burned the house of the LORD and the royal palace, and carried away the rest of the people into captivity (2 Kings 25:8-11). He testifies that he was driven away from men and ate grass like an ox (Daniel 4:33).
event: He said, "Is this not Babylon the Great, which I have built by my power and might as a royal city to display the glory of my majesty?" (Daniel 4:30). In the course of conquering Jerusalem, he brought the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon and put them in his own temple in Babylon (2 Chronicles 36:7), and he commanded the chief of his court officials to bring some of the Israelite youths of the royal family and the nobility and teach them the learning and language of the Chaldeans, and Daniel was among them (Daniel 1:3-4, 1:6). He also made a golden image on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon, set it up, and commanded all to fall down and worship (Daniel 3:1, 3:5).
character: He is portrayed as a person of arrogant character who took great pride in his own power and achievements (Daniel 4:30), and toward those who went against his will he sometimes imposed extreme and tyrannical punishments, such as throwing them into a furnace (Daniel 3:19-20). However, according to what was recorded through Daniel, he also showed the flexibility to acknowledge a supernatural being beyond his own wisdom and to revise his attitude when interpreting dreams or experiencing extraordinary phenomena (Daniel 2:47, 4:34-37).

직업/직위: second emperor of the Neo-Babylonian Empire

기타관계: Jehozadak#2605(leader of Judah he took captive)
Jehoiachin#2614(king of Judah he took captive)

introduce: He was the commander of the guard and military commander of Nebuchadnezzar II, king of the Neo-Babylonian Empire, and played a key role in the fall of Jerusalem and the final destruction of the kingdom of Judah.
lifetime: On the seventh day of the fifth month in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, he came to Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:8), burned the house of the LORD and the royal palace, and burned all the houses of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:9). He carried away the people who remained in the city, those who had surrendered to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude (2 Kings 25:11), and left in the land of Judah some of the poor who had nothing, giving them vineyards and fields (2 Kings 25:12, Jeremiah 39:10). While the captives of Jerusalem and Judah were being moved to Babylon, Jeremiah too was taken and bound in chains, and was released at Ramah (Jeremiah 40:1). There were people whom he had committed to Gedaliah (Jeremiah 41:10, 43:6).
event: The whole army of the Chaldeans under the captain of the guard broke down the walls around Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:10), and the captain of the guard took away the firepans and the bowls, whatever was of pure gold and whatever was of silver (2 Kings 25:15). He took the chief priest Seraiah, the second priest Zephaniah, and the three doorkeepers of the temple (2 Kings 25:18) and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah (2 Kings 25:20). When the king of Babylon gave orders concerning Jeremiah (Jeremiah 39:11-12), he, together with Nebushazban the chief officer, Nergal-sharezer the Rabmag, and others, sent and had Jeremiah taken out of the court of the guard and entrusted him to Gedaliah (Jeremiah 39:13-14). Also, at Ramah he released the chains from Jeremiah's hands, told him that if he came with him to Babylon he would treat him well and that he was free to go wherever he thought right, and sent him off with provisions and a gift (Jeremiah 40:4-5).
character: As a military commander he showed a cool-headed side that thoroughly carried out the orders of the king, his superior (2 Kings 25:8). In managing and dealing with the captives he used conciliatory and hardline measures as appropriate, and through his considerate attitude toward the prophet Jeremiah he is portrayed as a person with a practical sense for judging situations and grasping the circumstances (Jeremiah 40:2-5).

introduce: Nebushazban was the chief officer of the king of Babylon, and he is recorded as one of the Babylonian captains who, after the fall of Jerusalem, had Jeremiah brought out of the court of the guard.
lifetime: Nebushazban appears by name as the chief officer, together with Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, Nergal-sharezer the Rabmag, and all the captains of the king of Babylon, in Jeremiah 39:13 (Jeremiah 39:13). They sent and took Jeremiah out of the court of the guard and entrusted him to Gedaliah (Jeremiah 39:14).
event: After Jerusalem fell, together with Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, Nergal-sharezer the Rabmag, and others, he took part in sending and having Jeremiah brought out of the court of the guard and entrusted to Gedaliah (Jeremiah 39:13-14). No other personal deeds are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Nephusim is one of the descendants of the Nethinim who, after finishing the Babylonian captivity, returned to Jerusalem and Judah under the leadership of Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Ezra 2:50).
lifetime: His name is included in the list of those among the captives taken to Babylon who returned to Jerusalem and the homeland of Judah (Ezra 2:50).
event: He is recorded as one of the families of the Nethinim who assisted with the work of the temple, and he took part as a member of the community that returned from Babylon (Ezra 2:50).

직업/직위: ancestor of a family of temple servants

introduce: Nephushesim is a person recorded in the list of those who returned from the Babylonian captivity, and refers to a family of the Nethinim who performed temple service, or to its ancestor.
lifetime: The descendants of Nephushesim are included in the genealogy of the Nethinim who assist with the work of the temple among those who returned from the Babylonian captivity (Nehemiah 7:52). They are in the list recorded in "the genealogical register of those who had first returned" that Nehemiah found (Nehemiah 7:5).
event: After the Babylonian captivity he was entered in the list as a member of the Nethinim who returned to Jerusalem and assisted with the various duties of the temple (Nehemiah 7:52).

직업/직위: ancestor of a family of temple servants

introduce: Neziah is one of the Nethinim, the temple servants who finished the Babylonian exile and returned to Jerusalem and Judah in accordance with the decree of Cyrus king of Persia.
lifetime: He is included in the list of the Nethinim who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:54). Afterward his name is recorded once more in the genealogy of the descendants of the Nethinim who returned to Jerusalem (Nehemiah 7:56).
event: He is recorded in the list of returnees as the descendants of Neziah among the Nethinim, the group of temple servants (Ezra 2:54, Nehemiah 7:56).

직업/직위: ancestor of a family of temple servants

call: son of Shemaiah (royal descendant of David)
introduce: Neariah is a figure recorded in the Chronicles of the Old Testament, belonging to the genealogy of the Davidic royal house of the tribe of Judah. He is recorded as a son of Shemaiah, and is a member of the genealogy showing how the descendants of David continued after the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: Neariah is recorded as a son of Shemaiah, the son of Shecaniah, a descendant of David (1 Chronicles 3:22). The text lists Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat as the sons of Shemaiah, and it is written "six" (1 Chronicles 3:22). As sons of Neariah, three are recorded: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam (1 Chronicles 3:23).

직업/직위: clan chief of David's royal line

introduce: Nehushta is the mother of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem (2 Kings 24:8).
lifetime: Nehushta, as the daughter of Elnathan, is the mother of Jehoiachin king of Judah (2 Kings 24:8). Jehoiachin was the son of Jehoiakim who became king in his place when Jehoiakim died (2 Kings 24:6).
event: Her son Jehoiachin came to the throne at the age of eighteen and reigned in Jerusalem for three months (2 Kings 24:8). Jehoiachin went out to the king of Babylon together with his mother (2 Kings 24:12), and the king's mother was taken captive from Jerusalem to Babylon (2 Kings 24:15).

직업/직위: queen / queen mother of Judah (southern kingdom)

introduce: Nehum is one of the people of Israel who finished the Babylonian captivity and returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 7:7).
lifetime: He is recorded in the list together with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah, the group of leaders of the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian captivity (Nehemiah 7:7).
event: In the census of the exiles who returned to Jerusalem and to the cities of Judah, he was included in the list as one of the leaders (Nehemiah 7:7).

introduce: Nicanor is a person who was chosen as one of the seven deacons in the early church in Jerusalem (Acts 6:5).
lifetime: When, in the relief work in the early church, the Hellenists grumbled against the Hebrews, the apostles chose seven men to resolve this, and Nicanor was named as one of those seven (Acts 6:3-5). There is no record in the Bible of what specific course he took afterward (Acts 6:5).
event: When the twelve apostles delegated administrative and relief duties so as to concentrate on the ministry of the word, he received the laying on of hands from the apostles (Acts 6:6). Through this event he was included in the list as one of the seven, the group who carried out public duties of the church (Acts 6:5).
character: The Bible records that he was one of those praised by the people as full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom (Acts 6:3, 6:5). -

직업/직위: one of the seven deacons of the early Jerusalem church

introduce: Niger is a figure appearing in the Acts of the Apostles in the New Testament, mentioned as one of the group of leaders of the church at Antioch. His name derives from a Latin root and carries the meaning of black.
lifetime: He served as one of the prophets and teachers of the church at Antioch (Acts 13:1).
event: While fasting and ministering to the Lord in the church at Antioch, he took part in the process of setting apart Barnabas and Saul and sending them out as missionaries, according to the direction of the Holy Spirit (Acts 13:2).
character: Since the name Niger derives from Latin, it is a Roman-style name, and it suggests the possibility that he was of black African origin or a person with dark skin (Acts 13:1).

introduce: Nicodemus is a figure appearing in the Gospel of John in the New Testament, a ruler who was active as a Pharisee and a leader of the Jews.
lifetime: He was a member of the Sanhedrin, the highest decision-making body of Judaism, and, interested in the teaching of Jesus, he went to him at night and talked with him (John 3:1). Afterward he defended Jesus in the council and insisted on the legitimacy of legal procedure (John 7:50-51), and after the death of Jesus, to bury his body, he brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes and paid his respects (John 19:39).
event: He went to Jesus and conversed with him, holding a discussion about being born again and eternal life (John 3:2-15). When the Jewish leaders tried to arrest Jesus, he restrained his colleagues by asking whether it was in accordance with the law to judge a man before hearing him and knowing what he had done (John 7:50-51). To bury the body of Jesus, he brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes of about a hundred pounds, and wrapped the body in linen cloths together with the spices, according to the Jewish burial custom (John 19:39-40).
character: He had a cautious temperament, so wary of his identity being revealed that he visited Jesus at night (John 3:2). Within the council he showed a rational side, valuing legal procedure and fairness rather than unconditionally going along with the opinion of the majority (John 7:51). From the fact that after the death of Jesus he brought costly spices and took part in the burial publicly, it can be seen that he had the resolve to gradually make his own position toward Jesus known to the outside (John 19:39).

introduce: He was chosen as one of the seven servants in the early church in Jerusalem, and was a Gentile from Antioch who had converted to Judaism.
lifetime: To help with the relief ministry of the church in Jerusalem, he was chosen as one of the seven men praised as full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom (Acts 6:5).
event: To assist the ministry of the apostles, he received the laying on of hands and was appointed as one of the seven deacons (Acts 6:5-6). There is a view that the origin of the Nicolaitans mentioned in Revelation is connected with him, but the biblical text itself records no specific circumstances indicating that he directly spread heretical teaching (Revelation 2:6, 2:15).
character: He is portrayed as a person who had obtained a good reputation within the church community, being full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom (Acts 6:3, 6:5).

직업/직위: one of the seven deacons of the early Jerusalem church

introduce: He is a figure appearing in Genesis of the Old Testament, born of Cush, a ruler described as the first mighty one in the world in human history.
lifetime: Nimrod was a son of Cush (Genesis 10:8), and his kingdom began in Babylon, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar (Genesis 10:10). Afterward he moved to the region of Assyria and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah, and Resen (Genesis 10:11-12).
event: He was called the first mighty one on the earth (Genesis 10:8), and he became a mighty hunter before the LORD, so that he even came to be talked about in a proverb (Genesis 10:9). His kingdom began in Babylon, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar, and he went out into Assyria and built several cities (Genesis 10:10-12).
character: The Bible records him as a courageous hunter before the LORD (Genesis 10:9), and he was regarded as a person with overwhelming strength and power, to the point of being talked about by the people of his time (Genesis 10:8-9).

직업/직위: first mighty man on the earth

introduce: Nimshi is a figure recorded as the grandfather of Jehu, king of the northern kingdom of Israel. Jehu is introduced as "the son of Jehoshaphat, the grandson of Nimshi" (2 Kings 9:2).
lifetime: Nimshi is mentioned as the grandfather of Jehu. In 2 Kings 9:2 and 9:14 Jehu is introduced as "the son of Jehoshaphat, the grandson of Nimshi" (2 Kings 9:2, 9:14), and in 9:20 he is called "Jehu the grandson of Nimshi" (2 Kings 9:20). 1 Kings 19:16 also records him as "Jehu son of Nimshi" (1 Kings 19:16).
event: No direct activity or particular historical event is recorded in the Bible, and he is mentioned mainly to identify the family line through the epithet "grandson of Nimshi" (2 Kings 9:20) or "son of Nimshi" (1 Kings 19:16) when referring to Jehu.

introduce: Dathan is a figure appearing in the book of Numbers of the Old Testament, a son of Eliab of the tribe of Reuben and one of the main figures who joined in the rebellion of Korah.
lifetime: Dathan, as a person belonging to the tribe of Reuben, sided with Korah's company together with Abiram and challenged the authority of Moses (Numbers 16:1). He accused Moses of intending to kill them in the wilderness after bringing them up out of a land flowing with milk and honey, and refused to respond to Moses' summons (Numbers 16:12-14). In the end, because of the judgment of God, he, his family, and all the possessions belonging to him went down alive into Sheol as the ground split open, and met their death (Numbers 16:31-33).
event: Dathan formed a party together with Korah, Abiram, and On (Numbers 16:1), and rose up with 250 renowned chiefs of the congregation and opposed Moses (Numbers 16:2).
