When Moses sent to summon him, he said together with Abiram that they would not go up, accused Moses of bringing them up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill them in the wilderness and of trying to make himself king, and said that Moses had not brought them into a land flowing with milk and honey nor given them fields and vineyards as an inheritance (Numbers 16:12-14). In this incident the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households and all that belonged to them, and they perished, going down alive into Sheol (Numbers 16:32-33).
character: Dathan openly rebelled against the leadership of Moses and showed a willful and discontented attitude that expressed strong resistance (Numbers 16:12-14). He is portrayed as a person who, harboring discontent over the distribution of power and the leadership structure of the people, resisted the existing order (Numbers 16:3).

직업/직위: leader of the tribe of Reuben (rebel against Moses)

introduce: Thaddaeus is a figure appearing in the New Testament, one of the twelve disciples of Jesus, who is mentioned in the Gospels of Matthew and Mark. The meaning of his name is also interpreted as a broad-hearted person or a warm-hearted person.
lifetime: He was chosen by Jesus as one of the twelve disciples and called to be an apostle (Matthew 10:3, Mark 3:18).
event: Other than being included in the list of the twelve disciples of Jesus and appointed as an apostle, no specific deed or event that he carried out in a leading role is recorded in the Bible.
character: In the biblical record no particular temperament or personal characteristic is described as given to him, and in Luke and Acts he is referred to as Judas son of James, and there is a view in scholarship that presumes them to be the same person (Luke 6:16, Acts 1:13).

introduce: Tarea is a figure appearing in the family genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, a descendant of Kish, the ancestor of the royal house of Saul, and is recorded as a son of Micah.
lifetime: Tarea is recorded as a son of Micah (1 Chronicles 8:35, 9:41), and Pithon, Melech, and Ahaz are listed together as his brothers (1 Chronicles 8:35). Since Merib-baal, the son of Jonathan, fathered Micah (1 Chronicles 8:34), Tarea is a great-grandson of Jonathan, the son of Saul (1 Chronicles 8:33-35).

직업/직위: descendant of Jonathan of Saul's royal house

introduce: Darkon is a person recorded in the list of returnees from the exile, a name belonging to the group of descendants of the servants of Solomon.
lifetime: He is included among the company of returnees who came back from the Babylonian captivity to Jerusalem and Judah with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:56, Nehemiah 7:58).
event: Among the descendants of the servants of Solomon, he is entered in the list of returnees as the descendants of Darkon (Ezra 2:55-56, Nehemiah 7:57-58).

직업/직위: ancestor of a family of the descendants of Solomon's servants

introduce: Darda is a person mentioned in 1 Kings 4:31 of the Old Testament, recorded as one of the people compared with the wisdom of Solomon. He is introduced as a son of Mahol, and is mentioned together with Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, and Calcol.
lifetime: Darda is recorded as a son of Mahol (1 Kings 4:31). Apart from the fact that the Bible cites his name as an object of comparison, with Solomon being wiser than he, it provides no additional information about his birth, upbringing, or the specific deeds of his personal life.
event: Darda appears as an object of comparison to show how outstanding the wisdom of Solomon was. The biblical writer records that Solomon was wiser than all men, better than Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol (1 Kings 4:31). In itself, he has no recorded achievement of leading any specific event.
character: The Bible regards Darda as one of the wisest men of his time, surpassing the level of wisdom of ordinary people at that time (1 Kings 4:31). However, the Bible does not record in detail what characteristics of temperament or character he had, or in what specific field and in what form he exercised wisdom.

introduce: Tartan is the name of an office or title in the ancient Assyrian Empire, referring to the supreme commander who exercised actual military authority in the time of the Assyrian kings Sargon II and Sennacherib (2 Kings 18:17). This designation, written as Tartan in the Hebrew text, is a position meaning the commander in chief of the Assyrian army (Isaiah 20:1).
lifetime: At the command of Sargon II, king of Assyria, he carried out the mission of attacking and capturing Ashdod (Isaiah 20:1). Afterward, during the reign of Sennacherib, king of Assyria, he went up from Lachish to Jerusalem with a great army, together with the Rabshakeh and the Rabsaris, and pressed King Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:17).
event: The king of Assyria sent the Tartan, together with the Rabsaris and the Rabshakeh, with a great army from Lachish to Jerusalem to attack King Hezekiah, and they went up to Jerusalem and came and stood by the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the highway to the Launderer's Field (2 Kings 18:17). Isaiah 20:1 records that Sargon king of Assyria sent the commander in chief to Ashdod, and that he attacked and captured Ashdod (Isaiah 20:1).

meaning: one who holds royal authority, one who restrains
introduce: Darius I Hystaspes was the third king of Persia of the Achaemenid dynasty, and is recorded in the Bible as the one who, in the time of Ezra, Haggai, and Zechariah, permitted the Jews to rebuild the temple. He was a despotic monarch who ruled the great empire of the ancient Near East in a systematic way.
lifetime: The work on the house of God in Jerusalem had ceased until the second year of Darius king of Persia (Ezra 4:24); the elders of Judah reported this matter to Darius and waited for his reply (Ezra 5:5), and King Darius issued a decree and had the archives searched (Ezra 6:1). The word of Haggai and Zechariah came to the prophets in the second year of King Darius (Haggai 1:1, Zechariah 1:1). The temple was completed on the third day of the month of Adar in the sixth year of King Darius (Ezra 6:15). In his decree Darius had the whole cost of the building paid out of the royal treasury, that is, from the taxes of the region west of the river (Ezra 6:8).
event: Darius issued a decree and had the archives searched, that is, the place in Babylon where the treasures were stored, and in the scroll found in the palace at Ecbatana was recorded the decree issued in the first year of King Cyrus (Ezra 6:1-3). He commanded Tattenai the governor of the region west of the river, Shethar-bozenai, and others not to hinder the work on the house of God, but to let the governor of Judah and the elders rebuild the house on its site (Ezra 6:6-7). The cost of the building was to be paid promptly out of the royal treasury, that is, from the taxes of the region west of the river (Ezra 6:8), and the young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and oil, were to be given daily without fail, as the priests in Jerusalem requested (Ezra 6:9). He also included a clause that whoever altered this command would have a beam pulled out of his house and be hanged on it, and his house would be made a dunghill (Ezra 6:11).
character: Within his realm Darius showed a side that valued imperial administrative law and handled administration on legal grounds (Ezra 6:3). He respected the will of his predecessor Cyrus and sought to maintain the order of the empire (Ezra 6:14), and he employed a strategy of rule that minimized resistance from subject peoples by respecting their religious customs.

직업/직위: emperor of the Persian Empire (Darius I Hystaspes)

introduce: Damaris is a person recorded as "a woman named Damaris" among those who joined the apostle Paul and believed when he preached the gospel at the Areopagus in Athens (Acts 17:34).
lifetime: Her name is recorded among the few who heard the word that the apostle Paul proclaimed and believed (Acts 17:34).
event: She was recorded as one of the few who joined Paul and believed (Acts 17:34). Dionysius the Areopagite is mentioned as one who believed together with her (Acts 17:34).
character: In Athens, which was then the center of philosophy, she seems to have had an open mind, open enough to listen to and accept Paul's unfamiliar teaching, and since her name is explicitly given in history, it is highly likely that she was a person with a certain level of recognition within the society of the time (Acts 17:34).

introduce: She is a woman recorded as the wife of Er, the firstborn son of Judah, a son of Jacob, and through her father-in-law Judah she bore Perez and Zerah, playing a decisive role in continuing the line of Judah (Genesis 38:6, 38:29-30).
lifetime: She married Er, the son of Judah, but her husband Er was wicked and the LORD put him to death (Genesis 38:6-7). Afterward Judah told Onan to go in to his brother's wife and perform the duty of a husband's brother, but the LORD put Onan to death as well (Genesis 38:8-10), and Judah ordered Tamar to remain in her father's house and wait until his third son, Shelah, grew up (Genesis 38:11). When Shelah had grown up but she had not been given to him as a wife, Tamar took off her widow's garments, covered her face, and sat at the gate of Enaim; Judah thought she was a prostitute and went in to her (Genesis 38:14-18), and as a result she bore twins, Perez and Zerah (Genesis 38:27-30).
event: Tamar produced as evidence the seal, the cord, and the staff that she had received as a pledge from Judah, proving that she was pregnant with Judah's child, and through this she secured the legitimacy of continuing the family line (Genesis 38:18, 25-26). Through this event Perez was born, and Perez later became the foundation of the bloodline that continues into the genealogy of King David and of Jesus (Genesis 38:29, Matthew 1:3).
character: Even when she was marginalized by her husband's family and without the protection of custom, she showed a strategic side, acting meticulously to claim her rights (Genesis 38:14). Even before Judah, who had tried to have her killed, she calmly presented the evidence and had the boldness and decisiveness to turn the situation around (Genesis 38:25).

introduce: Taphath was a daughter of King Solomon, a woman who became the wife of Ben-abinadab, who was in charge of the whole district of the heights of Dor, one of the twelve governors Solomon set over Israel (1 Kings 4:7, 4:11).
lifetime: Taphath, as a daughter of Solomon, became the wife of Ben-abinadab, governor of the whole district of the heights of Dor (1 Kings 4:11). Ben-abinadab was one of the twelve governors whom Solomon set over all Israel (1 Kings 4:7, 4:11).
event: Apart from the record that, as a daughter of Solomon, she married Ben-abinadab, Taphath's own deeds are not recorded in the Bible. The provision of food for the king and the royal household, one month each year, is a record concerning the twelve governors (1 Kings 4:7, 4:11).

관계.배우자: Ben-abinadab#1207(governor of the region of Dor)

introduce: Tahpenes is a person recorded as the queen of Pharaoh, king of Egypt. When Hadad the Edomite went to Egypt and found favor with Pharaoh, Pharaoh gave him his sister-in-law, the younger sister of Tahpenes, as Hadad's wife (1 Kings 11:14, 11:18-19).
lifetime: Tahpenes is the queen of Pharaoh, king of Egypt (1 Kings 11:19). Pharaoh made his sister-in-law, the younger sister of Queen Tahpenes, the wife of Hadad the Edomite (1 Kings 11:19). The younger sister of Tahpenes bore a son, Genubath, to Hadad (1 Kings 11:20).
event: Tahpenes had the child Genubath, born to her younger sister, weaned in Pharaoh's palace, and Genubath was in Pharaoh's palace among the sons of Pharaoh (1 Kings 11:20).

기타관계: Hadad#3211(brother-in-law (younger sister's husband) / prince of Edom)

introduce: Tabrimmon is a person recorded as the father of Ben-hadad, king of Aram, who lived in Damascus (1 Kings 15:18).
lifetime: There is no record of Tabrimmon's own life. In 1 Kings 15:18 Ben-hadad, king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, is merely introduced as "the son of Tabrimmon, the grandson of Hezion" (1 Kings 15:18).
event: While Asa king of Judah was at war with Baasha king of Israel, he sent the silver and gold remaining in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the royal palace to Ben-hadad, king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, and asked for a treaty, and at this time Ben-hadad is mentioned as "the son of Tabrimmon" (1 Kings 15:16-19). Tabrimmon's own deeds are not recorded.

call: son of Tabeal (father of the puppet-king candidate)
introduce: Tabeal is a figure mentioned in the book of Isaiah of the Old Testament, recorded as the father of the candidate for puppet king whom Rezin king of Aram and Pekah king of northern Israel, when they allied to attack Ahaz king of Judah, intended to set up as king of Judah.
lifetime: No specific life or chronology of Tabeal is recorded; only the fact that his son was named as the candidate to be installed as king of Judah by the allied forces of Aram and northern Israel is stated (Isaiah 7:6).
event: The son of Tabeal is mentioned as the one whom Rezin king of Aram and the son of Remaliah (Pekah king of Israel) plotted to set up as king in the midst of Judah after attacking Judah, distressing it, and breaking into it (Isaiah 7:1, 7:5-6). The text records neither his name nor his deeds, and Tabeal appears only as his father.

introduce: She was a female disciple who lived in Joppa and was called Dorcas by her Greek name. She is a member of the early Christian community appearing in the Acts of the Apostles.
lifetime: While living as a disciple in Joppa she became sick and died (Acts 9:36-37), and since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples heard that Peter was there and sent two men to urge him to come without delay (Acts 9:38). After Peter sent everyone out, knelt down, and prayed, he turned to the body and said, "Tabitha, get up!" and she opened her eyes, saw Peter, and sat up (Acts 9:40), and Peter reached out his hand and raised her up, and calling the saints and widows, presented her alive to them (Acts 9:41).
event: She was abundantly occupied with good works and acts of charity (Acts 9:36). When she died, the widows who were with her stood weeping and showed Peter all the tunics and other garments that she had made while she was with them (Acts 9:39). Through the event of her being raised, all Joppa came to know of it, and many people came to believe in the Lord (Acts 9:42).
character: She lived a life devoted to good works and acts of charity, and put concrete service into practice within the community, such as giving practical help to the widows around her (Acts 9:36, 39).

직업/직위: woman disciple in the church at Joppa

introduce: Tarshish is a person recorded as one of the sons of Javan, a descendant of Japheth, the son of Noah (1 Chronicles 1:7). In Genesis 10:4 the name in the same genealogy is recorded as Tarshish.
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of the sons of Javan, son of Japheth (1 Chronicles 1:7; recorded as Tarshish in Genesis 10:4). Apart from the genealogical record, no specific information appears about his personal upbringing or life.
event: Apart from being recorded as a son of Javan, no event of Tarshish personally is recorded. Genesis 10:5 says that from these the peoples of various nations separated and settled in the lands of the coastlands, each according to its language, clan, and nation. The Bible also has Tarshish as a place name (Ezekiel 27:12) and the ships of Tarshish (1 Kings 10:22), but their relationship to this person is not stated in the text.

직업/직위: progenitor of a coastal trading people

introduce: He was the second king of the kingdom of Israel and the youngest of the eight sons of Jesse from Bethlehem. He was a shepherd until he was anointed by Samuel, and he was the ruler who governed all Israel and Judah from Jerusalem (1 Samuel 16:13, 17:12-14, 2 Samuel 5:5, 5:7).
lifetime: While tending sheep in Bethlehem he was anointed by the prophet Samuel (1 Samuel 16:13), and he served in the court of King Saul as a player of the harp (1 Samuel 16:23). Afterward he gained fame by striking down Goliath, but because of Saul's jealousy he went through a long period of exile (1 Samuel 17:50, 1 Samuel 22:1). After Saul died, he was first anointed king over the house of Judah (2 Samuel 2:4), and then he ruled Judah in Hebron for seven years and six months and ruled all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem for thirty-three years, so that he was king for forty years in all (2 Samuel 5:4-5, 1 Kings 2:11). In his later years he experienced the rebellion of his son Absalom (2 Samuel 15:10), and after Solomon was anointed and became king (1 Kings 1:39), David died and was buried in the City of David (1 Kings 2:10).
event: He killed Goliath, the Philistine champion, with a sling stone and led Israel to victory (1 Samuel 17:50). He took the stronghold of Zion in Jerusalem, which the Jebusites had occupied, and named it the City of David (2 Samuel 5:6-9). He struck and subdued the Philistines, Moab, Zobah, Aram, Edom, and others (2 Samuel 8:1-14). An incident is recorded in which he entered into an improper relationship with Bathsheba and caused her husband Uriah to die on the battlefield (2 Samuel 11:4-17). Also included is the incident in which, having ordered Joab to take a census of Israel and Judah, he was struck in his heart with remorse and received the discipline of the LORD (2 Samuel 24:1-15).
character: He had outstanding musical talent in playing the harp (1 Samuel 16:18), and showed the side of a brave warrior and strategist (2 Samuel 5:20). He sometimes took a flexible and prudent attitude according to the political situation, to the extent of sparing Saul, who had tried to kill him, twice (1 Samuel 24:10, 26:9). When his wrongdoing was pointed out, he showed himself to acknowledge it immediately (2 Samuel 12:13). On the other hand, in regard to the upbringing of his children, he also revealed a weakness in being unable to control conflicts within the family effectively (2 Samuel 13:21).

기타관계: Merab#902(woman promised to David in marriage)

introduce: Tahan was a member of the tribe of Ephraim; in the census record on the plains of Moab he is recorded as the ancestor of the Tahanite family among the clans of the descendants of Ephraim (Numbers 26:35). Whether he is related to Tahath in 1 Chronicles 7:20 is disputed and cannot be settled from the text, so the two are kept as separate entries.
lifetime: Tahan is recorded alongside Shuthelah and Becher among the clans of the descendants of Ephraim (Numbers 26:35). He is mentioned as the ancestor of the Tahan family in the list from the time when Moses and Eleazar the priest took the census of the total number of the sons of Israel on the plains of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho (Numbers 26:1-3, 26:35).
event: Tahan became the origin of the Tahanite clan named after him (Numbers 26:35).

직업/직위: progenitor of the Tahanite clan of Ephraim

introduce: Tahath is a descendant of Kohath of the tribe of Levi, and a son of Assir. In the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 6 he is recorded as one of the ancestors of Heman, who was in charge of singing in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 6:31-37).
lifetime: Tahath is a descendant of Kohath, the son of Levi, and is recorded as the son of Assir (1 Chronicles 6:37). His son is recorded as Uriel (1 Chronicles 6:24), and in the genealogy of Heman, Zephaniah is recorded as the son of Tahath (1 Chronicles 6:37).

introduce: He is the son born to Jacob by Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant, and the one who became the progenitor of the tribe of Dan, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. (Genesis 30:5-6)
lifetime:
He is Jacob's fifth son, born through Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant. (Genesis 30:5)
Rachel named him Dan, meaning that God had vindicated her and heard her plea and given her a son. (Genesis 30:6)
According to the family genealogy, he had a son named Hushim. (Genesis 46:23)
When famine struck the land of Canaan, he migrated to Egypt together with his father Jacob and the families of the other brothers. (Genesis 46:8-27)
Before Jacob died, he left a testament to Dan that he would judge his people as one of the tribes of Israel. (Genesis 49:16)
character:
Through the testament of his father Jacob he was compared to a snake by the road and a viper in the path. (Genesis 49:17)
He was described as having the characteristic of biting the horse's heels so that its rider falls backward. (Genesis 49:17)

직업/직위: progenitor of the tribe of Dan

introduce: Tanhumeth is a person recorded as the father of Seraiah. When they heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah as governor, among the commanders of the forces who went to Mizpah and came to Gedaliah was "Seraiah son of Tanhumeth" (2 Kings 25:23, Jeremiah 40:8).
lifetime: There is no record of Tanhumeth's own life. When the commanders of the forces and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah as governor and went to Mizpah to come to Gedaliah, Tanhumeth's name is mentioned as the father of Seraiah, who was among them (2 Kings 25:23, Jeremiah 40:8).
event: Tanhumeth's son Seraiah went to Mizpah together with Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, and others, and came to Gedaliah (called Gedaliah also in the book of Jeremiah) (2 Kings 25:23, Jeremiah 40:8). Tanhumeth's own deeds are not recorded.

call: son of Anak (Anakite giant of Hebron)
introduce: Talmai is one of the descendants of Anak who were in Hebron, a person recorded as an offspring of Anak (Numbers 13:22, Joshua 15:14).
lifetime: Talmai, an offspring of Anak, was in Hebron together with Sheshai and Ahiman (Numbers 13:22, Joshua 15:14). Caleb drove them out (Joshua 15:14), and Judah struck down the Canaanites living in Hebron and killed Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai (Judges 1:10).
event: When the spies of Israel arrived at Hebron, he was recorded as one of the descendants of Anak who were there (Numbers 13:22), and he was driven out by Caleb (Joshua 15:14) and killed by Judah (Judges 1:10).
character: The Bible describes Talmai as a member of the descendants of Anak, and records him as a person who shared the characteristics of a tribe of great stature and huge build (Numbers 13:33). As a native power in the Hebron region at that time, he was a threatening presence, to the point of being an object of fear to the spies of Israel (Numbers 13:28).

직업/직위: chief of the giants of Hebron

introduce: Talmon is a Levite who served as a gatekeeper in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian captivity. He is recorded together with Shallum, Akkub, and Ahiman in the list of gatekeepers in 1 Chronicles 9:17.
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian captivity he settled in Jerusalem and carried out the duty of gatekeeper (1 Chronicles 9:17). In Nehemiah 11:19 Akkub, Talmon, and their brothers are recorded as gatekeepers of the city, and in Nehemiah 12:25 he is mentioned as one of the gatekeepers who guarded the storerooms at the gates.
event: Talmon was a gatekeeper together with Shallum, Akkub, Ahiman, and their brothers, and Shallum was their chief (1 Chronicles 9:17). Nehemiah 11:19 says that Akkub, Talmon, and their brothers were gatekeepers of the city, 172 men in all. In Nehemiah 12:25 he is recorded, together with Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, and Akkub, as a gatekeeper who guarded the storerooms at the gates by divisions.

직업/직위: chief gatekeeper of the temple's East Gate

introduce: Talmon is mentioned as the ancestor of a family that carried out the duty of temple gatekeeper among the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian captivity. In the biblical record he appears not so much for any distinct personal deeds as a name indicating the genealogical origin of a family of gatekeepers.
lifetime: He is recorded as the ancestor of the descendants of the temple gatekeepers belonging to the list of returnees at the time of the return from the Babylonian captivity (Ezra 2:42). He is confirmed again as one of the ancestors of the gatekeeper families in the list of returnees in Nehemiah 7 (Nehemiah 7:45).
event: When Israel returned from the Babylonian captivity to Jerusalem, he formed a family that took the duty of gatekeeper, controlling and guarding access to the temple (Ezra 2:42). His descendants were classified as members, by family unit, who inherited and carried out the particular religious role of temple gatekeeper within the returning community (Nehemiah 7:45).

introduce: Dalphon is a person recorded as one of the ten sons of Haman in the time of Ahasuerus, king of Persia (Esther 9:7-10).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the ten sons of Haman (Esther 9:7-10), and when the Jews killed the ten sons of Haman in the citadel of Susa, he was killed along with the other brothers (Esther 9:6-10).
event: His name was recorded as one among the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews, whom the Jews killed in the citadel of Susa (Esther 9:7-10). Afterward, at the request of Esther, the king permitted it, and the bodies of the ten sons of Haman were hanged on the gallows (Esther 9:13-14).

introduce: Tabbaoth is the name of a family of the Nethinim, or of its representative, included in the list of those who returned from the Babylonian captivity to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:43). The Nethinim are lower-ranking temple workers set apart to serve in the temple.
lifetime: His name is entered in the list of the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian captivity (Ezra 2:43). Also, the descendants of Tabbaoth are included in Nehemiah's list recording the genealogy of those who came back from Babylon to Jerusalem (Nehemiah 7:46).
event: Within the returning community of Israel he was classified as a member of the Nethinim who returned to carry out the work of the temple (Ezra 2:43). At the time of the return from the Babylonian captivity, he belongs to the same status category as the other families of the Nethinim who returned together (Nehemiah 7:46).

직업/직위: ancestor of a family of temple servants

introduce: Tappuah is a person appearing in the record of Chronicles in the Bible, one of the members of the families of the tribe of Judah.
lifetime: Tappuah is mentioned as one of the sons of Hebron in 1 Chronicles 2, which records the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:43).
event: He is entered in the genealogy of the sons of Hebron: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema (1 Chronicles 2:43).

introduce: Tattenai is a person recorded as the governor of the region west of the Euphrates in the time of Darius, king of Persia. He appears as an official who, together with Shethar-bozenai and their associates, investigated the temple construction work of the Jews and sent a written report on the matter to King Darius (Ezra 5:3, 5:6).
lifetime: When the Jews who were under Persian rule after the Babylonian exile were rebuilding the temple in Jerusalem, he came, as governor of the region west of the Euphrates, together with Shethar-bozenai and their associates, and asked, "Who authorized you to rebuild this temple and restore this structure?" (Ezra 5:3). In this process he asked for the names of their leaders and wrote to King Darius (Ezra 5:6-17). Afterward, when the decree of King Darius was issued, he carried it out promptly (Ezra 6:13).
event: He asked the Jews carrying out the temple construction who had commanded them to build this temple and finish this structure (Ezra 5:3). After hearing the Jews' reply, on that basis he sent a letter to King Darius requesting an investigation (Ezra 5:6-17). After receiving a reply from King Darius that the early decree of King Cyrus had been found, he cooperated, in accordance with the king's command, so that the Jews could complete the temple work (Ezra 6:13). In particular, he faithfully carried out the king's instruction to supply the cost from the king's property so that the work would not be interrupted (Ezra 6:8).
character: He showed himself as a thorough and principled official who took immediate administrative measures regarding a large-scale building project taking place in his jurisdiction (Ezra 5:3). In the reporting process he also showed a prudent disposition that valued legal procedure, not judging by his own discretion but asking that the royal records be checked directly (Ezra 5:17). After the decision of his superior was issued, he did not oppose that command but carried out what had been directed as it was, revealing himself as a compliant and efficient administrator (Ezra 6:13).

직업/직위: governor of the region west of the Euphrates

introduce: Tertullus is the orator who came down with the high priest Ananias and certain elders and accused the apostle Paul before the governor Felix (Acts 24:1-2).
lifetime: The high priest Ananias came down with certain elders and the orator Tertullus and accused Paul before the governor (Acts 24:1). When Paul was called in, Tertullus brought the charge and accused Paul before Felix the governor as a pestilence and one who stirred up dissension among all the Jews throughout the world (Acts 24:2-5).
event: When he accused Paul before Felix the governor, he began with words that first praised the governor and asked him to hear them with indulgence (Acts 24:2-4). He claimed that Paul was a ringleader of the Nazarene sect and that they had seized him because he tried to desecrate the temple (Acts 24:5-6). But because Felix was well informed about this Way, he adjourned the hearing and said he would decide the case when Lysias the commander came down (Acts 24:22).
character: He is characterized by skill in rhetorical technique and by the use of ornate eloquence to persuade his audience (Acts 24:2-3). He shows himself as a professional advocate who developed a legal argument while skillfully flattering the governor, the man in power (Acts 24:2-8).

introduce: Tertius is a person who took part in the writing of the letter to the Romans in the New Testament as the apostle Paul's amanuensis. He served as the scribe who wrote down Paul's letter, and his is the only name of this kind mentioned in the Bible.
lifetime: The Bible does not record Tertius's birth or the details of his upbringing. In Romans 16:22 he appears as the one who wrote down this letter and who sends greetings in the Lord (Romans 16:22).
event: He personally wrote down the letter to the Romans, the letter the apostle Paul sent to the church in Rome, taking Paul's dictation (Romans 16:22). At the end of this letter he left a greeting in his own name (Romans 16:22).
character: In the biblical record no individual temperament or physical characteristic of Tertius is mentioned. However, from the content in which, working together with the apostle Paul, he courteously conveys greetings to the believers of the church in Rome, it can be inferred that he was a helper who had Paul's trust (Romans 16:22).

introduce: He is a figure appearing in the book of Esther, one of the two doorkeepers who guarded the palace gate of King Ahasuerus.
lifetime: As a doorkeeper who guarded the palace gate of King Ahasuerus, he took part in a plot to assassinate the king, was discovered, and was executed (Esther 2:21).
event: Together with Bigthan, a fellow doorkeeper, he plotted to assassinate the king (Esther 2:21). Mordecai learned of this and told Queen Esther, and Esther reported the matter to the king in the name of Mordecai (Esther 2:22). When the investigation showed it to be true, the two men were hanged on the gallows and executed (Esther 2:23).

직업/직위: royal eunuch who guarded the door

introduce: Demas is a figure in the Bible who is recorded among those who sent greetings as co-workers of the apostle Paul, but who is recorded as having later, loving this world, deserted Paul and left for Thessalonica (Colossians 4:14, Philemon 1:24, 2 Timothy 4:10).
lifetime: In Colossians 4:14 he is one who sends greetings together with Luke the beloved physician, and in Philemon 1:24 he is recorded as one of Paul's fellow workers. Afterward, in 2 Timothy 4:10, Paul records that Demas, loving this world, deserted him and went to Thessalonica.
event: In Paul's letters he is mentioned as one who sends greetings together with Luke (Colossians 4:14), and in Philemon as well his name is listed among those who send greetings as Paul's fellow workers, together with Mark, Aristarchus, and Luke (Philemon 1:24). But in 2 Timothy 4:10 it is recorded that, loving this world, he deserted Paul and went to Thessalonica.
character: According to the biblical record, Demas took part in the ministry together with Paul, but at a decisive time he put a love for the world first and left the community (2 Timothy 4:10). Paul called him his fellow worker (Philemon 1:24), but in the end he was portrayed as one who deserted Paul and left (2 Timothy 4:10).

introduce: Teman is the person recorded first among the sons of Eliphaz, son of Adah, the wife of Esau, and is a grandson of Esau and a great-great-grandson of Abraham (Genesis 36:10-11). Among the descendants of Eliphaz among the descendants of Esau, Chief Teman is recorded (Genesis 36:15).
lifetime: Teman is a son of Eliphaz, the son of Adah, the wife of Esau (Genesis 36:10-11). In Genesis 36:15, which records the chiefs among the descendants of Esau, his name is entered as Chief Teman among the descendants of Eliphaz.
event: As a chief among the descendants of Esau, Chief Teman was recorded first among the chiefs of the descendants of Eliphaz (Genesis 36:15). In 1 Chronicles 1:36 also he is recorded first among the sons of Eliphaz.

기타관계: Teman#3354(presumed place or clan named after him)

introduce: Demetrius is a figure appearing in the Acts of the Apostles in the New Testament, a silversmith in Ephesus who made silver shrines of Artemis and provided the craftsmen with no small income. He is recorded as the one who told the craftsmen and those in the same trade that, because of Paul's preaching, there was a danger that their business would fall into disrepute.
lifetime: He was a silversmith in Ephesus who made silver shrines of Artemis and provided the craftsmen with no small income (Acts 19:24). He gathered the craftsmen and those in such trades and said that Paul, not only in Ephesus but through nearly the whole province of Asia, had persuaded a great number of people to turn away, saying that things made by human hands are not gods (Acts 19:25-26). The crowd who heard this were filled with rage and shouted (Acts 19:28), and the whole city was thrown into confusion, and they seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who traveled with Paul, and rushed together into the theatre (Acts 19:29).
event: Demetrius said that because of Paul there was danger not only that their business would fall into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis would be regarded as nothing and that her majesty, honored by all Asia and the world, would be deposed (Acts 19:26-27). The crowd who heard this shouted, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!" and the whole city was thrown into confusion and rushed into the theatre (Acts 19:28-29). Later the city clerk quieted the crowd and said that if Demetrius and the craftsmen with him had a complaint, there were court days and proconsuls and they should bring charges against one another, and after speaking of the danger of being charged with rioting over the disturbance, he dismissed the assembly (Acts 19:35-41).
character: He was a practical person who, in order to protect his own economic interests, knew how to lead the situation in an organized way and use crowd psychology (Acts 19:24-25). He also showed a strategic side in that, to strengthen the religious custom that was the basis of his business, he put forward a religious pretext and attacked the thinking of others (Acts 19:27).

introduce: Temeni is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles chapter 4. In the genealogy of the tribe of Judah he appears as one of the sons born to Naarah, wife of Ashhur (1 Chronicles 4:5-6).
lifetime: Temeni is recorded as one of the sons whom Naarah bore to Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, who had two wives, Helah and Naarah; they were Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari, and he is listed among the offspring of Naarah (1 Chronicles 4:5-6).

introduce: Tebah is a figure recorded as one of the four sons (Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah) born to Reumah, the concubine of Nahor, the brother of Abraham (Genesis 22:24).
lifetime: He was the son of Nahor's concubine Reumah and is recorded together with Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah (Genesis 22:24). Uz, Buz, Kemuel, Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel are recorded separately as the offspring of Nahor's wife Milcah (Genesis 22:20-23).

introduce: Theophilus is a figure identified as the recipient of the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles; the etymology of his name carries the sense of one who loves God or one who is loved by God. The biblical text addresses him as "most excellent" (Luke 1:3), but there is no other record of his identity or position.
lifetime: He is the person to whom the author of the Gospel of Luke conveyed an orderly account of the deeds of Jesus (Luke 1:3). At the beginning of Acts, the author mentions once again that he had already written and sent Theophilus a first book about the deeds of Jesus (Acts 1:1).
event: The author of the Gospel of Luke wrote his account and sent it to Theophilus so that he might know the certainty of the things he had already been taught (Luke 1:4). At the beginning of Acts as well, the author addresses Theophilus and says that the former account dealt with all that Jesus began to do and to teach (Acts 1:1).
character: Given that the author of the Gospel of Luke addressed him with the honorific "most excellent," he is regarded as a person of authority and honor in society at that time (Luke 1:3). Judging from the author's writing, he appears to have been a person of high intellect who respected a systematic process of inquiry, one fit to receive the origins and historical facts of Christianity in a logical and orderly manner (Luke 1:3-4).

introduce: Telah was a descendant of the tribe of Ephraim, a person belonging to the line of Beriah, the son of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 7:23-25).
lifetime: Telah was the son of Resheph, the son of Beriah, the son of Ephraim, and his son was Tahan (1 Chronicles 7:25).

기타관계: Joshua#3179(kinsman of the tribe of Ephraim)

introduce: Telem is a figure who appears in Ezra chapter 10; he is recorded as one of the gatekeepers in the list of those among the descendants of the exiles who were investigated for having taken foreign women (Ezra 10:16-17, 24).
lifetime: When Ezra appointed certain heads of families, each designated by name, to investigate the matter of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:16-17), his name was entered as one of the gatekeepers in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:24).
event: In Ezra chapter 10, in the list drawn up from the investigation of those who had taken foreign women, his name was recorded in the gatekeepers' entry together with Shallum and Uri (Ezra 10:24).

introduce: Togarmah is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Genesis, a grandson of Japheth, son of Noah, and a son of Gomer. He is classified as one of the figures who form the genealogy of the peoples of the ancient Near East.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the three sons born to Gomer, the son of Japheth (Genesis 10:3). The descendants of Japheth settled in the coastlands, each according to its language, clan, and nation (Genesis 10:5).
event: It is recorded that the house of Togarmah traded for the wares of Tyre with horses, war horses, and mules (Ezekiel 27:14). In Ezekiel 38:6, the house of Togarmah from the far north is mentioned among the hordes that will be brought down along with Gog, together with all their flocks.

introduce: Rodanites is recorded as a son of Javan and a descendant of Japheth, the son of Noah. Within the genealogical system of Scripture, he is classified as one of the descendants of Javan (Genesis 10:4).
lifetime: As a son of Javan he appears as a member of the line of Japheth, and he is included in the list when the descendants of Javan settled in the coastlands, each according to its language, clan, and nation (Genesis 10:4, 1 Chronicles 1:7).

introduce: Dodavahu is a figure recorded in 2 Chronicles; he was a man of Mareshah and the father of Eliezer, who prophesied in the time of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah (2 Chronicles 20:37).
lifetime: He is recorded as a man of Mareshah, and his son Eliezer prophesied in the time of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah (2 Chronicles 20:37).
event: His son Eliezer prophesied the judgment of shipwreck against King Jehoshaphat, who had joined with Ahaziah and built ships at Ezion-geber (2 Chronicles 20:37).

introduce: A figure from the tribe of Issachar, mentioned as the father of Puah, who was the father of the judge Tola, and thus as Tola's grandfather; he is a person of familial background.
lifetime: Because Tola, the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, served as a judge, Dodo was the grandfather of the judge Tola (Judges 10:1). No other details of his birth or life are recorded.

introduce: He was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ; the Aramaic name Thomas means "twin," and in Greek he is called Didymus.
lifetime: He was called by Jesus to be an apostle and served as such (Matthew 10:3). When Jesus said, "Lazarus is dead; let us go to him," he said to the other disciples, "Let us also go, that we may die with Him" (John 11:14-16). There is a record that, having not seen the risen Jesus at first, he declared that he would not believe unless he saw the nail marks and put his finger and his hand into them (John 20:24-25). Eight days later, when Jesus came and spoke to him, he confessed, "My Lord and my God!" (John 20:26-28), and when Jesus revealed Himself to the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias, he was there with Peter and the other disciples (John 21:1-3).
event: When Jesus said, "Let us go to Lazarus," Thomas said to the other disciples, "Let us also go, that we may die with Him" (John 11:15-16). After Jesus' ascension, he returned from the Mount of Olives to Jerusalem and went up to the upper room with the other disciples, and they all joined together constantly in prayer (Acts 1:12-14). He said that to believe in Jesus' resurrection he would have to see the nail marks in His hands and put his finger into them (John 20:25); afterward, when Jesus came and told him to reach out his finger, he confessed, "My Lord and my God!" (John 20:27-28).
character: He showed a disposition to verify matters logically (John 20:25), and even in a dangerous situation he displayed the ability to assess the circumstances coolly and decide (John 11:16). He had strong loyalty toward his Master, and once he had confirmed a fact, he gave a resolute confession of faith (John 20:28).

introduce: Tob-adonijah was a Levite who was active in the time of Jehoshaphat, the fourth king of the kingdom of Judah. According to the biblical record, he is identified as one of those who, early in Jehoshaphat's reign, carried out the task of teaching the people at the king's command (2 Chronicles 17:8).
lifetime: In the third year of the reign of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, the king commanded officials, Levites, and priests to go around the cities throughout Judah and teach the Law. Tob-adonijah was included among the company of Levites dispatched at that time and took part in this nationwide teaching ministry (2 Chronicles 17:7-9).
event: At the king's command, together with the priests Elishama and Jehoram and others, he went around the various cities of Judah and fulfilled the responsibility of teaching the people with the Book of the Law of the LORD (2 Chronicles 17:8-9).

introduce: He was one of the Levites sent out for the teaching of the Law during the reign of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.
lifetime: In the third year after King Jehoshaphat began to reign, teaching was carried out in the various cities of Judah, and he is recorded as one of the Levites who were sent out at that time (2 Chronicles 17:7-8).
event: At the king's direction, together with the other Levites and the priests, he went around throughout Judah and taught the people the Book of the Law of the LORD (2 Chronicles 17:7-9).

introduce: Doeg is a figure who appears in 1 Samuel; he was an Edomite who held the position of chief of the herdsmen of King Saul. He is recorded as the direct perpetrator of the incident in which the priests who helped David and their dwelling place were wiped out.
lifetime: He was an Edomite and a servant of Saul, the chief of Saul's herdsmen (1 Samuel 21:7). On the day David came to the priest Ahimelech at Nob, he was detained there before the LORD (1 Samuel 21:1, 7). Later, Doeg, who stood among Saul's servants, reported that he had seen the son of Jesse come to Nob to Ahimelech son of Ahitub, and that Ahimelech had inquired of the LORD for David and given him provisions and also the sword of Goliath the Philistine (1 Samuel 22:9-10). When the king ordered the priests to be put to death, the servants were unwilling, but Doeg turned and struck down the priests, killing on that day eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod (1 Samuel 22:17-18), and he put to the sword Nob, the city of the priests, with its men and women, children and infants, and its cattle, donkeys, and sheep (1 Samuel 22:19).
event: He told Saul that Ahimelech had inquired of the LORD for David and given him provisions and the sword of Goliath (1 Samuel 22:9-10). When Saul's servants were unwilling to kill the priests, Doeg, at the king's command, turned and struck down the priests and killed eighty-five men (1 Samuel 22:17-18). He also put Nob, the city of the priests, to the sword, killing men and women, children and infants, and even the livestock (1 Samuel 22:19).
character: He was a man who used his power and position to commit brutal killing without hesitation in order to win the king's favor (1 Samuel 22:18). He placed the king's command above all other priorities, over such rules as the Sabbath or religious duties, and showed no hesitation at all in killing the priests of Nob, a religious center (1 Samuel 22:18). David described him as one with a deceitful tongue, and Psalm 52 refers to his evil deeds and his ruin (Psalms 52:1-5).

introduce: Tou is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles chapter 18 as king of Hamath. Hearing that David had struck down the whole army of Hadadezer, king of Zobah, he sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and bless him (1 Chronicles 18:9-10). The same incident is recorded in 2 Samuel 8:9-10 in connection with Toi, king of Hamath, and his son Joram.
lifetime: Tou, king of Hamath, hearing that David had struck down the whole army of Hadadezer, king of Zobah, sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and bless him (1 Chronicles 18:9-10). This was because Hadadezer had previously been at war with Tou many times, and David had struck down Hadadezer (1 Chronicles 18:10).
event: Hadoram, whom Tou had sent, brought articles of gold, silver, and bronze of every kind (1 Chronicles 18:10). In 2 Samuel 8:10 it is recorded that Joram brought articles of silver, gold, and bronze.

introduce: Tohu is a figure recorded in the genealogy of Elkanah in 1 Samuel 1:1; he was the great-grandfather of Elkanah, an Ephraimite who lived in Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim, and he was the son of Zuph (1 Samuel 1:1).
lifetime: 1 Samuel 1:1 records Elkanah as the son of Jeroham, the grandson of Elihu, the great-grandson of Tohu, and the great-great-grandson of Zuph. Accordingly, Tohu was the great-grandfather of Elkanah and the father of Elihu, and he belongs to the line that goes back to Zuph as his father. Apart from this verse, no deeds of Tohu himself are recorded.

introduce: Tychicus is a figure who appears in the New Testament, a fellow worker whom the apostle Paul called a beloved brother, a faithful minister, and a fellow servant in the Lord (Ephesians 6:21, Colossians 4:7).
lifetime: Acts 20:4 records among those accompanying Paul as far as Asia "Tychio, a man of Asia," who is generally regarded as the same person as Tychicus. While Paul was an ambassador in chains (Ephesians 6:20), Tychicus was mentioned as the one who would make known Paul's circumstances (Ephesians 6:21, Colossians 4:7). Paul said he had sent Tychicus to Ephesus (2 Timothy 4:12), and he said he would send Artemas or Tychicus to Titus (Titus 3:12).
event: In Ephesians 6:21 and Colossians 4:7, Paul says that Tychicus will make known to them his circumstances. In Colossians 4:8-9, Paul says that he is sending Tychicus together with Onesimus so that they may make known Paul's circumstances and encourage their hearts. Paul also said that he had sent Tychicus to Ephesus (2 Timothy 4:12).
character: Paul regarded him as a beloved brother, a faithful minister, and a fellow servant in the Lord (Ephesians 6:21, Colossians 4:7). Since he was a person Paul could trust and was continually entrusted with such tasks as delivering important letters and being dispatched to places of ministry, he is portrayed as a man of diligence and loyalty (Titus 3:12).

introduce: Dumah is a figure who appears in the Old Testament, recorded as one of the sons of Ishmael and as a chieftain of the Ishmaelite clans.
lifetime: Dumah was the sixth of the twelve sons of Ishmael, who was born to Abraham and Hagar (Genesis 25:14). As a descendant of Ishmael, he belonged to the line of chieftains who formed their own villages and encampments (Genesis 25:16).
event: Dumah, as a son of Ishmael, is recorded as one of the twelve princes (Genesis 25:16). Isaiah 21:11 records "an oracle concerning Dumah," but the text does not state how this verse is related to Dumah, the son of Ishmael.

직업/직위: one of the twelve princes of Ishmael

introduce: Tubal was a son of Japheth and a grandson of Noah, a figure who forms one branch of the Japhethite peoples in the genealogy of humankind (Genesis 10:2). In the genealogical record of the Hebrew Bible, he is identified as the fifth son when the descendants of Japheth are listed (1 Chronicles 1:5).
lifetime: Tubal was born to Japheth, a son of Noah, after the great flood, and belongs to the genealogy of the family community that came out of Noah's ark (Genesis 10:1-2). In the record of Chronicles in the Old Testament as well, he is listed in the same way as a son of Japheth within the genealogical system that begins with Adam (1 Chronicles 1:5).

meaning: Smith, ancestor of those who make instruments
introduce: Tubal-cain is a figure who appears in Genesis, a son born to Lamech and Zillah in the line of Cain. He is recorded as one who forged all kinds of sharp instruments of bronze and iron.
lifetime: Of the two wives whom Lamech took, Adah and Zillah, Zillah bore Tubal-cain (Genesis 4:19, 22). The line of Cain runs from Cain's son Enoch to Irad, Mehujael, Methusael, and Lamech (Genesis 4:17-18). Tubal-cain's sister was Naamah (Genesis 4:22).
event: He is recorded as one who forged all kinds of sharp instruments of bronze and iron (Genesis 4:22).

직업/직위: forger of bronze and iron tools (father of smiths)

introduce: Theudas is a figure mentioned by Gamaliel before the Council in Acts chapter 5; he was one who rose up and boasted of himself, and about four hundred people followed him, but he was killed (Acts 5:34-36).
lifetime: The Pharisee Gamaliel, speaking before the Council, mentioned Theudas as one who had risen up earlier and boasted of himself, and said that about four hundred people had followed him (Acts 5:34-36). Gamaliel then went on to speak of what happened when Judas of Galilee rose up at the time of the census (Acts 5:37). Theudas was killed, and all who followed him were scattered and came to nothing (Acts 5:36).
event: Theudas rose up and boasted of himself, and about four hundred men followed him, but when he was killed, all who had followed him were scattered and came to nothing (Acts 5:36).

introduce: Dedan is recorded as a son of Raamah, the son of Cush, the son of Ham (Genesis 10:6-7, 1 Chronicles 1:9). The name Dedan also appears in Scripture as that of a people and a place, but the text does not state how that is related to this person.
lifetime: Dedan is recorded as a son of Raamah, the son of Cush (Genesis 10:7, 1 Chronicles 1:9). Since Cush was a son of Ham (Genesis 10:6), Dedan was a grandson of Cush and a great-grandson of Ham.
event: Apart from his name being recorded as a son of Raamah, no deeds of this person himself are recorded in Scripture. The "Dedan" in Jeremiah 25:23, Ezekiel 27:15·20, and Isaiah 21:13 is a reference to a people or a place, and the text does not state its relation to Dedan, the son of Raamah.

introduce: Trophimus is a figure who appears in Acts and 2 Timothy in the New Testament; he was one of those who went with Paul as far as Asia, and he is recorded as a man of Ephesus (Acts 20:4, 21:29).
lifetime: Trophimus is recorded as one of those who went with Paul as far as Asia (Acts 20:4). In Jerusalem, the Jews had seen Trophimus the Ephesian with Paul in the city (Acts 21:29). In 2 Timothy 4:20, Paul says that he left Trophimus sick at Miletus.
event: In Jerusalem, the Jews saw Trophimus the Ephesian with Paul in the city and supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple (Acts 21:29). This is connected with the cry that Paul had brought Greeks into the temple and defiled the holy place (Acts 21:28); afterward the whole city was stirred up, and they seized Paul, dragged him out of the temple, and tried to kill him (Acts 21:30-31). Paul also mentioned that he had left Trophimus sick at Miletus (2 Timothy 4:20).
character: Scripture does not directly describe Trophimus' character, but from the fact that he accompanied Paul to the end on a journey from Asia to Rome in which Paul's sufferings had been foretold, and that Paul mentioned leaving him at Miletus because of illness, it can be seen that he maintained a close relationship of trust with Paul (Acts 20:4, 2 Timothy 4:20).

introduce: Tryphena is a figure who appears in Romans chapter 16 in the New Testament, one of the believers to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the church in Rome.
lifetime: Tryphena was mentioned as included in the list of greetings that Paul sent to the Christians in Rome (Romans 16:12). In the biblical record, no concrete information is confirmed about her background or any other part of her life.
event: Tryphena was acknowledged by Paul as one who works hard in the Lord (Romans 16:12). She is recorded as one who labored in the Lord together with Tryphosa (Romans 16:12).

직업/직위: believer in the church at Rome

introduce: Tryphosa is a woman mentioned among the greetings that the apostle Paul sent to the believers of the church in Rome, one of the members of the Christian community active in Rome (Romans 16:12).
lifetime: Nothing is recorded in Scripture about Tryphosa's early life or birth background. However, the fact that her name is mentioned in the course of Paul's greetings to the believers in Rome confirms that she was living as a member of the Roman church community at that time (Romans 16:12).
event: Tryphosa was greeted, together with Tryphena, as one who labored in the Lord (Romans 16:12). In the same verse, the description "who has worked hard in the Lord" and "beloved" is said of Persis, whom Paul bids to be greeted next (Romans 16:12).

직업/직위: believer in the church at Rome

introduce: Drusilla was the wife of Felix, the governor of Judea, and is recorded in Acts as a Jewess (Acts 24:24).
lifetime: As the Jewish wife of Felix, some days later she came with her husband Felix, and they sent for Paul and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus (Acts 24:24). Nothing else about her life is recorded in Scripture.
event: When Felix came with his wife Drusilla and sent for Paul and heard him about faith in Christ Jesus, she was present with him (Acts 24:24).

introduce: Tebaliah is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a member of a family of gatekeepers among the descendants of Merari of the tribe of Levi. He is recorded as the third son of the house of Hosah (1 Chronicles 26:11).
lifetime: Tebaliah was born as a son of Hosah, and during the reign of King David he was classified as a member of a family that performed the duty of gatekeepers of the temple as Levites (1 Chronicles 26:11).
event: When David assigned the duties of the Levites for the service of the temple, Tebaliah, as the third son of his father Hosah, had his name entered in the list of gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:11).

introduce: Deborah is recorded as the nurse of Rebekah (Genesis 35:8). When Rebekah went to Canaan, her nurse was sent with her (Genesis 24:59), and after Deborah died she was buried under the oak below Bethel (Genesis 35:8).
lifetime: Deborah was sent as Rebekah's nurse when Rebekah left with Abraham's servant (Genesis 24:59). When Jacob came to Bethel, Rebekah's nurse Deborah died and was buried under the oak below Bethel (Genesis 35:6-8). Her life in between is not recorded in Scripture.
event: In the course of Rebekah's marriage she was sent along as her nurse (Genesis 24:59). The tree where she died and was buried was named Allon-bachuth, which came to mean "the oak of weeping" (Genesis 35:8).
character: Over a long period, amid the bonds of family relationships, she stayed by Rebekah's side and showed devotion (Genesis 35:8). From the fact that Jacob's family mourned her death, it can be seen that she was more than a mere servant, having formed emotional ties as an important member of the household (Genesis 35:8).

introduce: Debir was the king of Eglon at the time of the conquest of Canaan, an Amorite ruler who stood in opposition to the tribes of Israel.
lifetime: Debir, king of Eglon, was one of the five kings whom Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem, sent for and summoned (Joshua 10:3). Because Gibeon had made peace with Joshua and the children of Israel, they sought to strike Gibeon (Joshua 10:4-5); but the LORD defeated them before Israel, so that they suffered great slaughter at Gibeon and were pursued on the slope going up to Beth-horon, as far as Azekah and Makkedah (Joshua 10:10). The five kings were found hiding in the cave at Makkedah (Joshua 10:17), and Joshua brought them out of the cave, struck them dead, and hung them on trees (Joshua 10:22-26).
event: Summoned by Adoni-zedek, he gathered with the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, and the king of Lachish, and with all their armies they went up, camped against Gibeon, and fought (Joshua 10:3-5). At the appeal of the men of Gibeon, Joshua went up from Gilgal with all his army and mighty men of valor (Joshua 10:6-7), and the LORD defeated them before Israel (Joshua 10:10). After being defeated in battle, he hid in the cave at Makkedah with the other five kings; at Joshua's command he was brought out of the cave, and the commanders put their feet on their necks (Joshua 10:22-24), and Joshua struck them dead and hung them on five trees (Joshua 10:26). At sunset their bodies were taken down from the trees and thrown into the cave where they had hidden (Joshua 10:27).

introduce: Deuel is a figure who appears in the Book of Numbers in the Old Testament, recorded as the father of Eliasaph, a commander of the descendants of Gad.
lifetime: Deuel is mentioned as the father of Eliasaph of the tribe of Gad (Numbers 1:14). In Numbers 2:14 the same Eliasaph is recorded as "the son of Reuel," so the father's name is written as Reuel.
event: No deeds of Deuel himself are recorded. His son Eliasaph, as a leader of the descendants of Gad, presented an offering (Numbers 7:42, 7:47) and led the army of the tribe of the descendants of Gad (Numbers 10:20).

직업/직위: father of the leader of the tribe of Gad (Deuel)

introduce: Tehinnah is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as a son born to Eshton and as the father of Ir-nahash (1 Chronicles 4:12).
lifetime: Tehinnah is recorded as a son of Eshton and is mentioned as the father of Ir-nahash (1 Chronicles 4:12). Eshton was a son of Mehir (1 Chronicles 4:11).
event: Tehinnah is recorded in the genealogy as the father of Ir-nahash. The text records that Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah, whom Eshton fathered, were all men of Recah (1 Chronicles 4:12).

call: Head of the twenty-third division of priests
introduce: Delaiah was the one who held the twenty-third division in the system of priestly duties organized in the time of King David. From the biblical record it can be confirmed that his family belonged to the ranks of the priestly order.
lifetime: When David divided the priestly divisions of the descendants of Aaron by lot, he was recorded as the twenty-third (1 Chronicles 24:5, 24:18). This division was one of the divisions made up of the descendants of Aaron's sons Eleazar and Ithamar (1 Chronicles 24:1-4).
event: Among the divisions determined by casting lots in David's time, the twenty-third was Delaiah (1 Chronicles 24:5, 24:18). In these divisions they entered the house of the LORD to serve according to the ordinance given to them by their father Aaron, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him (1 Chronicles 24:19).

introduce: Delilah was a woman who lived in the Valley of Sorek and a figure who appears in the Book of Judges. She is recorded as one who colluded with the lords of the Philistines to seduce Samson, the judge of Israel, find out the source of his strength, and have him bound.
lifetime: Samson loved a woman in the Valley of Sorek whose name was Delilah (Judges 16:4). The lords of the Philistines came up to her and proposed that she entice Samson and find out where his great strength came from (Judges 16:5). Pressing him with her words day after day and nagging him, she made Samson pour out his heart (Judges 16:16-17), and after learning Samson's heart, she summoned the lords of the Philistines to come up (Judges 16:18). She made Samson sleep on her knees, called a man, and had him shave off the seven locks of his head, so that his strength left him (Judges 16:19). Nothing is recorded in Scripture about her life after that.
event: She was offered eleven hundred pieces of silver each by the lords of the Philistines (Judges 16:5). She asked Samson about the source of his strength and was given three false answers, but she did not give up and persistently troubled him (Judges 16:6-15). In the end she made Samson disclose the secret of his dedication as a Nazirite and that his strength lay in his hair (Judges 16:17). After lulling Samson to sleep on her knees, she called a man and had the seven locks of his head shaved off, thereby weakening Samson's strength (Judges 16:19).
character: Despite Samson's repeated lies, she showed persistence and perseverance that did not yield (Judges 16:16). She had a cold-blooded side that deceived and betrayed Samson, her lover, for her own gain (Judges 16:18). She exercised the control to obtain the information she wanted by appealing to Samson's emotions and pressing him psychologically (Judges 16:15).

introduce: Tikvah is a figure mentioned in 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles in the Old Testament; he was the father of Shallum, the husband of the prophetess Huldah, and the grandson of Hasrah (Harhas).
lifetime: Tikvah (Tokhath) is recorded as the grandson of Harhas (Hasrah), and his son Shallum was keeper of the wardrobe in the time of Josiah, king of Judah. Shallum's wife, the prophetess Huldah, lived in the Second District of Jerusalem (2 Kings 22:14, 2 Chronicles 34:22).

introduce: Diklah is recorded as a descendant of Shem, the son of Noah, and as a son born to Joktan, the son of Eber (Genesis 10:27). The dwelling place of the descendants of Joktan was the eastern hill country on the way from Mesha toward Sephar (Genesis 10:30).
lifetime: Diklah is one of the thirteen sons born to Joktan, the son of Eber (Genesis 10:27). In 1 Chronicles as well, in the course of listing the genealogy of Shem, he is likewise identified as a son of Joktan (1 Chronicles 1:21).

직업/직위: progenitor of a tribe descended from Joktan

introduce: Tiglath-pileser was a king who ruled the Assyrian Empire around the eighth century BC; historically he is known as Tiglath-pileser III, and in the Bible he is also called Pul. He was a figure deeply involved, politically and militarily, with northern Israel and the kingdom of Judah in the period of the divided kingdom.
lifetime: As king of Assyria, he came against the land of northern Israel in the time of its king Menahem and sought to strike it, but when Menahem gave him a thousand talents of silver, he turned back and did not stay in the land (2 Kings 15:19-20). Later, in the time of King Pekah, he advanced again, captured many cities of Israel, and carried their inhabitants captive to Assyria (2 Kings 15:29). Also, when Ahaz, king of Judah, was attacked by Rezin and Pekah, he answered Ahaz's request, attacked Damascus, and killed Rezin (2 Kings 16:5-9).
event: When Menahem, king of northern Israel, wishing to strengthen the kingdom in his own hand, gave him a thousand talents of silver, he took the silver, turned back, and did not stay in the land (2 Kings 15:19-20). He captured Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali in Israel, and carried the people captive to Assyria (2 Kings 15:29). When Ahaz, king of Judah, sent messengers to ask for deliverance and sent the silver and gold from the house of the LORD and from the treasuries of the king's house as a gift, he came up, attacked and took Damascus, and killed Rezin (2 Kings 16:7-9). Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser, saw the altar there, and drew its pattern and the design of its construction and sent them to Uriah the priest (2 Kings 16:10). Yet Chronicles records that Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, came but did not help Ahaz and instead afflicted him (2 Chronicles 28:20).

introduce: Dinah was a daughter whom Jacob had by Leah (Genesis 30:21, 34:1). She was the sister of Simeon and Levi (Genesis 34:25) and is recorded as the central figure in an incident that took place near the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan.
lifetime: When Jacob came from Paddan-aram to the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan and pitched his tent (Genesis 33:18), Dinah went out to see the women of the land and was raped by Shechem, the son of Hamor, the prince of the land (Genesis 34:1-2). Afterward, Shechem loved Dinah and asked his father Hamor to get her for him as a wife, and Hamor came to speak with Jacob (Genesis 34:3-6); but Dinah's brothers Simeon and Levi, using circumcision as a pretext, wiped out the males of the city of Shechem, and the incident escalated (Genesis 34:13-26). Her life afterward is not specifically mentioned in Scripture (Genesis 46:15).
event: Dinah was taken by Shechem, the son of Hamor, the prince of the land, and experienced being raped (Genesis 34:2). Because of this, Simeon and Levi attacked the city, killed all its males, killed Hamor and his son Shechem with the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem's house (Genesis 34:25-26), and the other sons of Jacob plundered the city and took captive their children and wives (Genesis 34:27-29).

introduce: Tidal is recorded in Genesis chapter 14 as king of Goiim. Together with Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, and Chedorlaomer king of Elam, he was one of the four kings who fought against the five kings, including the king of Sodom and the king of Gomorrah (Genesis 14:1-2, 9).
lifetime: Tidal, as king of Goiim, together with Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, and Chedorlaomer king of Elam, fought against the five kings, including the king of Sodom and the king of Gomorrah (Genesis 14:1-2). These five kings served Chedorlaomer for twelve years and rebelled in the thirteenth year (Genesis 14:4), and in the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him came out and struck them (Genesis 14:5, 14:9).
event: Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him struck the Rephaites at Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, and the Emites at Shaveh-kiriathaim, and struck the Horites in their hill country of Seir (Genesis 14:5-6); they came to En-mishpat, that is, Kadesh, and struck all the country of the Amalekites and also the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar (Genesis 14:7). Tidal, as one of these four kings, joined battle with the five kings in the Valley of Siddim (Genesis 14:8-9), and the four kings seized all the goods and provisions of Sodom and Gomorrah and also carried off Abram's nephew Lot, who was living in Sodom (Genesis 14:11-12). But Abram, with his trained men, attacked them by night and defeated them, and pursued them as far as Hobah, to the left of Damascus, and recovered all the goods that had been taken, and Lot as well (Genesis 14:14-16).

introduce: He was a coworker of the apostle Paul and a Christian leader of Greek origin, a person who mainly carried out evangelistic work and administrative duties in the early church.
lifetime: As an uncircumcised Greek, he went up to Jerusalem with Paul, and this became the center of a dispute in the church at that time (Galatians 2:1-3). Paul called him his true son (Titus 1:4) and sent him to work in the church at Corinth and in the region of Crete (2 Corinthians 8:6, Titus 1:5). Later, when Paul was imprisoned in Rome, he went to the region of Dalmatia (2 Timothy 4:10).
event: He was urged by Paul to complete the matter of the collection for the church at Corinth (2 Corinthians 8:6), and with earnestness he went to Corinth of his own accord (2 Corinthians 8:17). When Paul came to Macedonia, Titus came and comforted Paul by reporting the comfort he had received from the Corinthians, and their longing, their mourning, and their zeal for Paul (2 Corinthians 7:5-7). Before this, Paul, not having found Titus at Troas, had no peace of mind and went on to Macedonia (2 Corinthians 2:12-13). In Crete he was entrusted with the task of appointing elders in every city (Titus 1:5). Paul urged him to come to Nicopolis quickly (Titus 3:12).
character: Paul called him his partner and fellow worker and thought highly of his trustworthiness (2 Corinthians 8:23). In obedience to the apostle Paul's instruction he volunteered for ministry in dangerous regions (2 Corinthians 8:17), and he shared a close personal bond with Paul, as when his spirit was refreshed through the comfort of the Corinthian believers (2 Corinthians 7:13). He was a faithful man who walked in the same Spirit as Paul and in the same steps (2 Corinthians 12:18).

introduce: Titus Justus was the owner of the house that Paul entered after leaving the synagogue in Corinth in Acts chapter 18, and he is recorded as a man who revered God (Acts 18:7).
lifetime: When the Jews opposed and reviled him, Paul moved from the synagogue and entered the house of a man called Titus Justus, and that house was next to the synagogue (Acts 18:6-7). Nothing about the rest of his life is recorded in Scripture.
event: The house Paul entered after leaving the synagogue in Corinth was the house of Titus Justus (Acts 18:7). That house was next to the synagogue (Acts 18:7).
character: Scripture describes him as a man who feared God (Acts 18:7). He was also a man who cooperated at close range with Paul and opened his private space for the sake of ministry (Acts 18:7).

직업/직위: believer in the church at Corinth (Titus Justus)

introduce: Tiras is recorded as a son of Japheth, the son of Noah (Genesis 10:2, 1 Chronicles 1:5). He is a member of the genealogy at the time when the descendants of Japheth, after Noah, divided into the peoples of many nations and spread out (Genesis 10:2-5).
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Japheth together with Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, and Meshech (Genesis 10:2, 1 Chronicles 1:5). The descendants of Japheth were divided into the peoples of many nations, and each settled in the coastlands according to its language, clan, and nation (Genesis 10:5). Specific details of Tiras' life, such as his birthplace, residence, and year of death, are not given in Scripture (Genesis 10:2, 1 Chronicles 1:5).
event: There is no record of any personal achievements or particular events (Genesis 10:2, 1 Chronicles 1:5). Apart from the biblical genealogical record, no social or political activity carried out by Tiras is mentioned (Genesis 10:2, 1 Chronicles 1:5).

introduce: She was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad and a descendant of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh (Numbers 26:33).
lifetime: When her father Zelophehad died without sons, his daughters made a claim for their inheritance before Moses, the priest Eleazar, and the congregation (Numbers 27:1-4). The LORD then told Moses that the words of the daughters of Zelophehad were right and that he should give them an inheritance among their father's brothers (Numbers 27:6-7); later, in keeping with the LORD's command that they marry only into a clan of their father's tribe (Numbers 36:6), they married the sons of their father's brothers (Numbers 36:10-12).
event: She became the occasion for the establishment of the statute of judgment that if there is no son, the inheritance shall pass to the daughter (Numbers 27:8-11; Numbers 27:4-8). Also, in the time of Joshua, she came before the priest Eleazar, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders and, as the LORD had commanded, received an inheritance among her father's brothers (Joshua 17:3-4).

직업/직위: daughter of Zelophehad (heir to an inheritance)

introduce: Tirhakah is the king of Cush who appears in 2 Kings and Isaiah. Before the king of Assyria sent messengers again to Hezekiah king of Judah, he is recorded as having heard it said that Tirhakah had come out to fight against him (2 Kings 19:9, Isaiah 37:9).
lifetime: Tirhakah is recorded as the king of Cush. While the king of Assyria was fighting against Libnah after leaving Lachish, he heard it said that Tirhakah king of Cush had come out to fight against him, and he sent messengers to Hezekiah again (2 Kings 19:8-9, Isaiah 37:8-9).
event: While the king of Assyria was fighting against Libnah (2 Kings 19:8), he heard it said that Tirhakah king of Cush had come out to fight against him (2 Kings 19:9). The text does not record what action Tirhakah actually took in this matter; having heard the report, the king of Assyria sent messengers to Hezekiah again (2 Kings 19:9).

직업/직위: Pharaoh of Egypt's 25th dynasty and king of Cush (Tirhakah)

introduce: Tirhanah is a figure recorded as a son of Caleb in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah. He is one of the sons born to Caleb's concubine Maacah (1 Chronicles 2:48).
lifetime: Tirhanah was born to Caleb of the tribe of Judah and his concubine Maacah (1 Chronicles 2:48). As a descendant of Caleb, he is placed within the bloodline of the tribe of Judah, and Sheber is mentioned as his brother (1 Chronicles 2:48).
event: Tirhanah is recorded as one of Sheber and Tirhanah, whom Caleb's concubine Maacah bore (1 Chronicles 2:48). There is no record in Scripture of any specific historical activity or particular event that he carried out during his life (1 Chronicles 2:48).

introduce: Tiria is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as a son of Jehallelel (1 Chronicles 4:16).
lifetime: Tiria was a son born to Jehallelel, a descendant of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:16).

introduce: Timaeus is a figure who appears in the Gospel of Mark in the New Testament, mentioned as the father of the blind beggar Bartimaeus.
lifetime: Timaeus is recorded only as the father of the blind beggar Bartimaeus (Mark 10:46). Nothing else about his life is recorded in Scripture.
event: There is no record of his involvement in any event directly; his name is mentioned only in the background of the event in which his son Bartimaeus was healed by Jesus at Jericho (Mark 10:46, 10:52).

introduce: Timothy is a figure who appears in the New Testament, a disciple and coworker of the apostle Paul and a leader active within the early Christian community. He was from Lystra, born to a Jewish mother, Eunice, and a Greek father.
lifetime: Timothy met Paul at Lystra, and because Paul wanted to take him along when he left, Paul had him circumcised (Acts 16:1-3). Even after Paul left Berea, Silas and Timothy remained there (Acts 17:14); from Athens Paul sent word that Silas and Timothy should come to him as quickly as possible (Acts 17:15), and Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia to Corinth (Acts 18:5). His name is recorded together with Paul's at the opening of Philippians and Colossians (Philippians 1:1, Colossians 1:1). When Paul was going to Macedonia, he urged him to stay in Ephesus (1 Timothy 1:3).
event: Paul called Timothy his faithful son and sent him to the church at Corinth (1 Corinthians 4:17), and sent him to strengthen the church at Thessalonica and encourage them in their faith (1 Thessalonians 3:2). Paul also sent him to Macedonia (Acts 19:22), and said he hoped to send him to the church at Philippi soon (Philippians 2:19). He urged him to stay in Ephesus in order that Timothy might instruct certain people not to teach different doctrines (1 Timothy 1:3-4).
character: Paul called Timothy his true son in the faith (1 Timothy 1:2). He was commended as one who, like a son serving his father, labored with Paul for the gospel (Philippians 2:22). He was also described as having the character of one who thinks deeply about the hearts of others and, unlike the rest, does not seek his own interests but puts the work of Jesus Christ first (Philippians 2:20-21). Timothy is recorded as having inherited a sincere faith from his maternal grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice (2 Timothy 1:5).

직업/직위: spiritual son of the apostle Paul
pastor of the church at Ephesus

introduce: Timon is a figure chosen as one of the seven deacons in the early church in Jerusalem.
lifetime: Timon is one of the seven men chosen by the whole multitude (Acts 6:5). Apart from this, no specific record of his birth or of his later deeds exists in Scripture.
event: When, in the church at Jerusalem, the Grecian Jews complained that their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution (Acts 6:1), the twelve apostles told the people to choose seven men who were well attested and full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom (Acts 6:3), and Timon was included among those chosen by the whole multitude (Acts 6:5). He was set before the apostles and received the laying on of hands from the apostles (Acts 6:6).

직업/직위: one of the seven deacons of the early Jerusalem church

introduce: He was the second emperor of the Roman Empire. In Scripture he is mentioned as the chronological marker indicating the time when John's ministry began (Luke 3:1-2).
lifetime: He succeeded to the throne after being adopted as a son by the emperor Augustus, and it is recorded that in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar the word of God came to John the son of Zechariah in the wilderness (Luke 3:1-2).
event: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip was tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene (Luke 3:1).

introduce: He was a man who contended with Omri for the throne after the death of Zimri, king of the northern kingdom of Israel.
lifetime: When Zimri, king of Israel, died, half of the people of Israel wanted to follow Tibni son of Ginath and make him king, while the other half followed Omri (1 Kings 16:21).
