The people who followed Omri prevailed over the people who followed Tibni son of Ginath, and when Tibni died, Omri became king (1 Kings 16:22).
event: When the people of Israel were divided into two after Zimri, half of them followed Tibni son of Ginath and wanted to make him king (1 Kings 16:21). He was defeated by the people who followed Omri, and when Tibni died, Omri became king (1 Kings 16:22).

직업/직위: rival for the throne of Israel (northern kingdom)

introduce: Dibri is a figure who appears in the Old Testament, a man of the tribe of Dan, recorded as the father of Shelomith (Leviticus 24:11).
lifetime: Dibri was a man of the tribe of Dan, and his daughter Shelomith is recorded as the mother of the son who, as the son of an Israelite woman, blasphemed and cursed the name of the LORD (Leviticus 24:10-11).
event: No specific achievements or events of Dibri himself are recorded; his name is mentioned only as the father of Shelomith (Leviticus 24:11).

introduce: He is a figure mentioned as the father of Gomer, the wife of the prophet Hosea.
lifetime: He is recorded as the father of Gomer, whom the prophet Hosea took as his wife (Hosea 1:3).
event: His daughter Gomer came to be married to the prophet Hosea (Hosea 1:3).

introduce: Dishan is recorded as a descendant of the Horite people who lived in the land of Edom and as a son of Seir.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Seir and is classified as one of the chiefs of the Horites (Genesis 36:21). His children were Uz and Aran (Genesis 36:28).
event: He was called Chief Dishan among the chiefs of the Horites, and according to their districts they were in the land of Seir (Genesis 36:30). His sons are recorded as Uz and Aran (1 Chronicles 1:42).

call: Fifth son of Seir (chief of the Horites)
introduce: Dishon was a chief of the Horite people who lived in the land of Seir, recorded as the fifth among the sons of Seir. He is one of the figures who show the native lineage of Seir, distinct from the descendants of Esau, the ancestor of the Edomites.
lifetime: Dishon was born as one of the sons of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36:21). He was one of the chiefs of the Horites in the land of Seir (Genesis 36:30).
event: As a chief in the land of Seir, Dishon had his name entered in the genealogy of the chiefs of the Horites together with his brothers Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Ezer, and Dishan (Genesis 36:20-21). The Horites to whom he belonged were the original inhabitants of that land (Genesis 36:20), but later the descendants of Esau destroyed the Horites in Seir and settled in their place (Deuteronomy 2:12).

introduce: Dionysius, who was a member of the Areopagus, is a figure who joined Paul and believed when the apostle Paul was in Athens (Acts 17:34).
lifetime: He is one of the few who joined Paul and believed after Paul spoke at the Areopagus in Athens (Acts 17:34). Nothing is recorded in Scripture about his earlier life, and his specific deeds after he believed are likewise not confirmed.
event: The only record about him is that, as a member of the Areopagus, he was among those who joined Paul and believed (Acts 17:34). His name is recorded together with that of a woman called Damaris (Acts 17:34).
character: From the fact that he was an official belonging to the high council called the Areopagus, we can tell that he was an intellectual of Athens in his day (Acts 17:34). He showed prudence and receptiveness in making his decision on the spot after hearing Paul's speech (Acts 17:34).

introduce: Diotrephes is a figure who appears in 3 John, mentioned in the letter that the elder who wrote it sent to Gaius as one who loves to be first in the church (3 John 1:1, 1:9).
lifetime: The elder who wrote the letter wrote a few words to the church, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, did not receive them (3 John 1:9).
event: With malicious words he spoke slanderously against those who had written the letter, and not only did he refuse to welcome the brothers, but he also forbade those who wanted to welcome them and put them out of the church (3 John 1:10).
character: He showed an authoritarian attitude, delighting in being first in that community (3 John 1:9), and he had an exclusive and dogmatic character, uttering evil words and slandering the apostle John (3 John 1:10).

직업/직위: wicked leader in the church who loved to be first

introduce: Tilon is a figure recorded as a son of Shimon in the genealogy of the descendants of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:20).
lifetime: In the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, his name is recorded together with Amnon, Rinnah, and Ben-hanan, the sons of Shimon (1 Chronicles 4:20).

기타관계: Zoheth#1634(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: Timna is recorded as a concubine of Eliphaz, the son of Esau, and as the mother of Amalek. In the genealogy of Genesis she is mentioned as a concubine of Eliphaz.
lifetime: Esau bore Eliphaz to his wife Adah (Genesis 36:4). Timna, the concubine of Eliphaz, bore Amalek to Eliphaz (Genesis 36:12). In the list of the sons of Eliphaz in 1 Chronicles 1:36 as well, the name Timna appears together with Amalek.
event: Her bearing Amalek as the concubine of Eliphaz is the whole of the record, and Amalek belongs to the descendants of Esau's wife Adah (Genesis 36:12).

introduce: Rekem is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 7:16 in the Old Testament, recorded as a male who was a grandson of Machir of the tribe of Manasseh, a son of Sheresh, and a brother of Ulam.
lifetime: Rekem was the son of Sheresh, the younger of the sons born to Machir's wife Maacah, and he is recorded together with his brother Ulam (1 Chronicles 7:16). Machir's wife Maacah bore a son and named him Peresh (1 Chronicles 7:16).

introduce: Ladan is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Ephraim, a son of Tahan, and is recorded as one of the direct ancestors of Joshua.
lifetime: In the genealogy of the tribe of Ephraim, Ladan was the son of Tahan and the father of Ammihud (1 Chronicles 7:26). Within the family tree of the tribe of Ephraim he serves as a link leading to Joshua (1 Chronicles 7:27).

introduce: Ramah is a member of the Jewish community that returned to Jerusalem and Judah in accordance with the decree of Cyrus, king of Persia, after the Babylonian exile. He is one of the figures who appear in the lists of the return from captivity recorded by Ezra and Nehemiah, included in the group of the people who had lived in a particular locality.
lifetime: He was recorded in the list of those who had been taken captive to Babylon and, having been released, returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town (Ezra 2:1). That list records that the men of Ramah and Geba numbered six hundred twenty-one (Ezra 2:26).
event: He joined the ranks of the return of the people of Israel from Babylon to Jerusalem and went back to his homeland together with his family and local community (Ezra 2:1, 2:26).

introduce: Ramiah is one of the members of the community of Israel who returned to Jerusalem after ending the Babylonian captivity, a figure recorded in the list during the resolution of the matter of marriages to foreign women led by Ezra.
lifetime: He was one of the children of Israel who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem, and a figure included in the list of those who had to take part in Ezra's resolve to send away their foreign wives (Ezra 10:25).
event: When Ezra drew up in Jerusalem the list of the children of Israel who had taken foreign women as wives, his name was entered in that list as one of the descendants of Parosh (Ezra 10:25).

introduce: He was the fifth-generation descendant in the line of Cain, a son of Methusael, and the seventh from Adam. He is the first person recorded in Scripture as having taken two wives.
lifetime: He was born to Methusael and took two wives, Adah and Zillah (Genesis 4:18-19). Through them he had the children Jabal, Jubal, Tubal-cain, and Naamah (Genesis 4:20-22).
event: He said to his wives Adah and Zillah that he had killed a man for wounding him and a young man for striking him, and that if Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold (Genesis 4:23-24).
character: He showed an arrogant and aggressive disposition, to the point of turning his act of killing into a song in poetic form and openly boasting of it (Genesis 4:23). He was characterized by arbitrarily interpreting the protection from God that Cain had once received as an indulgence for his own killing (Genesis 4:24).

직업/직위: first man recorded with more than one wife

introduce: Rapha is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as the fifth among the sons born to Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:1-2).
lifetime: Rapha is recorded as the fifth, following Bela the firstborn, Ashbel the second, Aharah the third, and Nohah the fourth of the sons born to Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:1-2).

introduce: Laban is a figure who appears in Genesis in the Old Testament, an Aramean who lived in the region of Paddan-aram, the son of Bethuel and the brother of Rebekah. As the maternal uncle and father-in-law of Jacob and the father of Leah and Rachel, he played a central role in Jacob's migration and settlement.
lifetime: When Abraham's servant came to find Rebekah as a bride, he spoke for the will of the household and sent Rebekah away (Genesis 24:29-50). Later, when Jacob fled to him, he received him and had him labor for fourteen years to obtain his daughters (Genesis 29:10-30). When Jacob wanted to return to Canaan, he negotiated with him over the matter of wages (Genesis 30:25-43), and when Jacob left secretly with his family, he pursued him, and at the hill country of Gilead they made a covenant and parted (Genesis 31:17-55).
event: When Jacob proposed to take the streaked, spotted, and dark animals as his wages, he agreed to do as he said (Genesis 30:31-34). When Jacob left secretly, he pursued him and confronted Jacob's family, and in the process he tried to find the household idols that Rachel had stolen but did not find them (Genesis 31:22-35). In the end, at the hill country of Gilead he set up a heap of stones with Jacob and made a covenant that neither would pass over that heap to harm the other, and that place was called Mizpah (Genesis 31:43-53).
character: Putting his own interest first, he showed a very calculating side, changing the terms of Jacob's wages ten times (Genesis 31:7). In giving his daughters to Jacob in marriage, he used deception, sending the elder, Leah, first by trickery and then demanding further labor (Genesis 29:23-27). In matters of faith, he knew the LORD, but judging from the fact that he kept household idols, he appears to be a person who had not completely set aside polytheistic customs (Genesis 30:27, 31:30).

직업/직위: maternal uncle and head of Laban's house

introduce: Raphu is a figure mentioned in the list of spies in Numbers chapter 13 as the father of Palti, who is recorded as the representative of the tribe of Benjamin (Numbers 13:9).
lifetime: Raphu is recorded in Numbers 13:9 only as the father of Palti, the spy of the tribe of Benjamin, and nothing else of his life is recorded. His son Palti was one of the leaders whom Moses sent, at the command of the LORD, to spy out the land of Canaan while the children of Israel were in the wilderness of Paran (Numbers 13:3, 13:9).
event: No deeds of Raphu himself are recorded. His son Palti, as a spy, together with the other spies, searched out the land, and after forty days returned and reported to the congregation (Numbers 13:21, 13:25-26).

introduce: Laadah is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a male recorded as a son or descendant of Shelah.
lifetime: As a descendant of Shelah, the son of Judah, he is mentioned as the father of Mareshah (1 Chronicles 4:21).
event: Apart from being recorded as the father of Mareshah, no specific achievements or events of Laadah himself are recorded (1 Chronicles 4:21).

introduce: Raamah is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Genesis in the Old Testament, recorded as one of the children of Cush, the son of Ham.
lifetime: As a son of Cush, he is mentioned together with his brothers Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, and Sabteca (Genesis 10:7). He is classified as belonging to the generation of Noah's great-grandsons (Genesis 10:6-7).
event: There is a record that Raamah had two sons, Sheba and Dedan (Genesis 10:7). The biblical text does not record any specific historical event or achievement that he led.

introduce: Raamiah is one of those who were entered in the list of the people of Israel who, having ended their life of captivity in Babylon, returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 7:7).
lifetime: His name is registered in the list of the descendants of Judah who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem (Nehemiah 7:7). The count of the people of Israel is recorded along with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah (Nehemiah 7:7). In Ezra it is recorded as Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah (Ezra 2:2).
event: Having ended his life of captivity in Babylon, he returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel.

introduce: Lael is recorded in Numbers 3:24 as the father of Eliasaph, who was to be the chief of the father's house of the Gershonites.
lifetime: Lael is mentioned in Numbers 3:24 only as the father of Eliasaph, and it is recorded that his son Eliasaph was to be the chief of the father's house of the Gershonites (Numbers 3:24). Lael's own life is not recorded.
event: No deeds of Lael himself are recorded. His son Eliasaph was appointed to be the chief of the father's house of the Gershonites (Numbers 3:24).

기타관계: Moses#930(fellow worker of the tribe of Levi)

introduce: Laish is recorded as a man who lived in Gallim, and he is the father of Palti (Paltiel), the husband whom Saul's daughter Michal took after having been David's wife.
lifetime: Saul gave his daughter Michal, who had been David's wife, to Palti son of Laish, who lived in Gallim (1 Samuel 25:44). Later Ish-bosheth took Michal from her husband Paltiel son of Laish (2 Samuel 3:15).
event: No deeds of Laish himself are recorded. His son Palti (Paltiel) was Michal's husband, but when Ish-bosheth took Michal from him, he followed her weeping as far as Bahurim, and when Abner told him to go back, he went back (2 Samuel 3:15-16).

introduce: Raham is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, the son of Shema and the father of Jorkeam (1 Chronicles 2:44).
lifetime: In the line of the descendants of Caleb of the tribe of Judah, he is recorded as the son of Shema, the son of Hebron (1 Chronicles 2:43-44).
event: Apart from the fact that he is recorded as the son of Shema and the father of Jorkeam, no particular achievements or specific events that he carried out are recorded (1 Chronicles 2:44).

기타관계: Hebron#4542(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: Rahab was a Canaanite woman who lived in the city of Jericho and a figure who played an important role in Israel's conquest of Canaan. She is recorded as having lived on the city wall and worked as a prostitute; afterward she dwelt among Israel (Joshua 6:25), and in the genealogy of Matthew 1:5 she appears as the wife of Salmon and the mother of Boaz.
lifetime: As a prostitute of the city of Jericho, she hid the Israelite spies in her house (Joshua 2:1). Through negotiation with the spies, she obtained a promise that her life and her family's lives would be spared when Israel took Jericho (Joshua 2:12-13). As the two men had told her, she tied a scarlet cord in the window (Joshua 2:18, 2:21), and after the walls of Jericho fell, the two men whom Joshua sent brought out Rahab, her father and mother, her brothers, and all who belonged to her, and saved them alive (Joshua 6:22-23, 6:25). Afterward she lived among the people of Israel, and she married Salmon and bore Boaz (Matthew 1:5).
event: When the king of Jericho sent men to have the spies brought out, she hid the two men among the stalks of flax on the roof and said she did not know where they had gone, thereby turning the pursuit aside (Joshua 2:3-7); later she let them down by a rope through the window and told them to go to the hills and hide for three days (Joshua 2:15-16). Joshua told the two men who had spied out the land to bring out the prostitute's house and all who belonged to her, as they had sworn (Joshua 6:22), and Rahab, her father's household, and all who belonged to her were kept alive and have lived in the midst of Israel to this day (Joshua 6:25).
character: She was a person with excellent powers of judgment, who, recognizing the divine power of Israel, an enemy nation, sought her own survival (Joshua 2:9-11). She recognized the importance of a covenant to the point of requesting a sign of an oath from the spies, and acted with care (Joshua 2:12-14). Also, through her act of hiding the spies at the risk of her own life, she showed a decisive character (Joshua 2:4).

introduce: Lahad is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as the son of Jahath, the son of Reaiah, the son of Shobal, and as the brother of Ahumai (1 Chronicles 4:2).
lifetime: It is recorded that Reaiah, the son of Shobal the son of Judah, fathered Jahath, and that Jahath fathered Ahumai and Lahad, and that these were the families of the Zorathites (1 Chronicles 4:1-2).

introduce: Rachel was the second daughter of Laban of Paddan-aram and one of the two wives of Jacob, the mother of Joseph and Benjamin. She was the younger sister of Leah and is recorded as the wife whom Jacob loved most.
lifetime: Rachel first met Jacob at the well near Haran (Genesis 29:4-12); while she was tending her father Laban's sheep (Genesis 29:9), she was given to Jacob as his wife after he had served seven years (Genesis 29:18, 29:28). Although Leah bore children, Rachel was barren (Genesis 29:31); through her maidservant Bilhah she obtained Dan and Naphtali (Genesis 30:6-8), and afterward she herself bore Joseph (Genesis 30:24). On the way back to Canaan with Jacob's family, on the road to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem, she bore Benjamin in hard labor, died, and was buried there (Genesis 35:16-19).
event: Rachel stole her father Laban's household idols (Genesis 31:19), and when Laban searched, she put the idols under the camel's saddle and sat on them to avoid her father (Genesis 31:34-35). She accompanied her husband Jacob in the migration from Paddan-aram to Canaan (Genesis 31:17), and on the road to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem, she bore Benjamin in hard labor, died, and was buried there by the road (Genesis 35:16-19).
character: Rachel is described as a woman beautiful in form and appearance (Genesis 29:17). While she was without children, she also showed strong jealousy toward the fruitfulness of her older sister Leah (Genesis 30:1), and as the wife whom Jacob loved most among his wives (Genesis 29:30), she remained as the maternal ancestor who bore Joseph and Benjamin, important figures in the history of the patriarchs.

introduce: Lahmi is a figure who appears in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles, recorded as the brother of Goliath the Gittite (1 Chronicles 20:5).
lifetime: Lahmi is recorded as the brother of Goliath the Gittite, and in the war with the Philistines he was killed by Elhanan son of Jair (1 Chronicles 20:5). 2 Samuel 21:19 records the same incident as a battle at Gob, with Elhanan recorded as the son of Jaare-oregim the Bethlehemite (2 Samuel 21:19).
event: During a war between Israel and the Philistines, the incident is recorded in which Elhanan killed Lahmi, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam (1 Chronicles 20:5).
character: Lahmi was a descendant of the Rephaim, a race of giants, and is depicted as a warrior of overwhelming build and strength, using as a weapon a spear shaft far larger than that of ordinary soldiers (1 Chronicles 20:5).

call: Son of Hezron (ancestor of David and Jesus)
introduce: Ram is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a son of Hezron, and is recorded as an ancestor of King David and Jesus.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Hezron, the grandson of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:9). He was born in the house of Perez as a son of Hezron and is mentioned as one who continues the line of generations in the genealogy (Matthew 1:3). Afterward he is recorded as the father of Amminadab (Ruth 4:19).
event: Ram is recorded as the son of Hezron and the father of Amminadab in the genealogy of David in Ruth (Ruth 4:19), and in the genealogy of Jesus in Matthew he likewise appears in the generation after Hezron and before Amminadab (Matthew 1:3-4). In 1 Chronicles it is recorded that Ram fathered Amminadab and Amminadab fathered Nahshon (1 Chronicles 2:10).

introduce: Lappidoth is a figure who appears in the Book of Judges in the Old Testament, a name mentioned as the husband of the judge Deborah.
lifetime: Lappidoth was the husband of Deborah, a prophetess and judge who lived in the hill country of Ephraim (Judges 4:4-5). No record of his birth background or any other details of his life appears in Scripture.
character: In the biblical record there is no mention of his personal character or any specific traits; all that is confirmed is that he was in a marriage relationship with the judge Deborah (Judges 4:4).

introduce: The Rabshakeh was a high official and military commander whom Sennacherib, king of Assyria, dispatched to Jerusalem to pressure Hezekiah, king of Judah. The Hebrew etymology derives from Rab-shakeh, an Assyrian official title, which is understood to be a title meaning the supreme commander of an army or the chief cupbearer.
lifetime: At the command of King Sennacherib, he went up to Jerusalem with a great army (2 Kings 18:17). Standing by the conduit of the upper pool (Isaiah 36:2), he delivered the words of the king of Assyria to the servants of King Hezekiah and to the people on the wall, urging them to surrender and come out (2 Kings 18:28-31). Afterward, on his way back, he heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, and he went to Libnah and met the king (2 Kings 19:8).
event: Before the servants of Hezekiah he cried out in a loud voice in the language of Judah, trying to break the people's will to resist (2 Kings 18:28). He mocked, saying that trusting in Egypt was no different from trusting in a broken reed of a staff (Isaiah 36:6). He also did not hesitate to insult the LORD, saying that among all the gods of the nations, which one had delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria, that the LORD should be able to deliver Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:35). His provocation became the occasion that drew out the response of King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah (2 Kings 19:1).
character: He was a man skilled in psychological warfare, who used naked threats and cynical rhetoric to bring his opponents to submission (2 Kings 18:19). He showed a shrewd and cunning side, to the point of speaking fluently in Hebrew, the language of Judah, and attempting to instill fear directly in the people on the wall (Isaiah 36:13). He revealed an arrogant character, deeply intoxicated by his own military superiority, as when he insulted the gods of the surrounding nations (2 Kings 19:10).

introduce: The Rabsaris was one of the three high officials whom Sennacherib, king of Assyria, sent from Lachish to Jerusalem, and in Scripture he is recorded by his title. The Hebrew Rab-saris is interpreted as an official title meaning chief of the eunuchs or a high court minister.
lifetime: He appears as one of the three envoys whom Sennacherib, king of Assyria, sent with a great army from Lachish to attack King Hezekiah in Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:17). Together with the Rabshakeh and the Tartan, he went up to Jerusalem and stood on the highway to the Launderer's Field, by the conduit of the upper pool (2 Kings 18:17).
event: At the command of Sennacherib, together with the Tartan and the Rabshakeh, he led a great army to Jerusalem and was dispatched for the task of attacking King Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:17). When they called for the king, Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna, and Joah went out (2 Kings 18:18); afterward the one who spoke is recorded as the Rabshakeh (2 Kings 18:19), and the Rabsaris' own words are not recorded in the text.

introduce: Raddai is a figure recorded as the fifth among the sons of Jesse (1 Chronicles 2:14). He was from the Bethlehem family of the tribe of Judah and was one of David's brothers.
lifetime: Raddai was born as a son of Jesse and is included in the list of David's brothers (1 Chronicles 2:14). The name Raddai does not appear when the sons of Jesse are listed in 1 Samuel chapters 16 and 17, and this list is confirmed only through the genealogical record of 1 Chronicles chapter 2 (1 Chronicles 2:13-14).

introduce: Lecah was a descendant of the tribe of Judah and a person related to the descendants of Shelah, the son of Judah. In the genealogical record of 1 Chronicles 4:21, Er, a descendant of Shelah, is recorded as "the father of Lecah" (1 Chronicles 4:21).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 4:21 records Er, a descendant of Shelah, as the father of Lecah (1 Chronicles 4:21). In this verse the one recorded as the father of Mareshah is Laadah, and the relationship between Lecah and Mareshah is not recorded in the text (1 Chronicles 4:21).
event: Apart from the genealogical information that Er was his father, the biblical text records no separate achievements or particular events concerning Lecah (1 Chronicles 4:21).

introduce: Rechab is a figure who appears in 2 Samuel in the Old Testament, the son of Rimmon the Beerothite and a commander in the army of Ish-bosheth, the son of King Saul. He is recorded as the one who, together with his brother Baanah, assassinated his own lord Ish-bosheth.
lifetime: Rechab was from Beeroth, belonging to the tribe of Benjamin, and was a military commander serving Ish-bosheth, the son of King Saul (2 Samuel 4:2). After killing Ish-bosheth, Rechab and Baanah took his head and traveled all night by way of the Arabah toward David at Hebron (2 Samuel 4:7). They presented Ish-bosheth's head to David and announced their deed as if it were news of victory, but David regarded it as an evil act and had them executed (2 Samuel 4:8-12).
event: Rechab and Baanah carried out the assassination by entering Ish-bosheth's house while he was taking his midday rest and stabbing him in the stomach (2 Samuel 4:5-6). They cut off Ish-bosheth's head, took it to Hebron, and delivered it to David (2 Samuel 4:7-8). David condemned the deed of those who had killed Saul's son, and, citing the precedent of having executed the one who had announced Saul's death, killed Rechab and Baanah on the spot, cut off their hands and feet, and had them hung up by the pool at Hebron (2 Samuel 4:10-12).
character: Rather than protect his lord Ish-bosheth, he killed him and sought a political reward from David, showing an opportunistic side (2 Samuel 4:8). He is judged to have been a man of cruelty who did not hesitate to make the extreme choice of betraying and murdering his lord, and who erred in his reading of the situation (2 Samuel 4:11-12).

call: One of the five kings of Midian
introduce: He is one of the five kings of Midian recorded in Numbers and Joshua, a tribal leader who appears in the wilderness period before the people of Israel entered Canaan.
lifetime: He is one of the five kings of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba (Numbers 31:8). He was killed when Israel struck Midian (Numbers 31:8).
event: In the war in which Israel struck Midian, he was killed together with the other four kings (Numbers 31:8). Joshua 13:21 records him with Evi, Zur, Hur, and Reba as the princes of Sihon, that is, the chiefs of Midian, and says that Moses killed them together (Joshua 13:21).

introduce: Regem-melech was a figure who was active in the time of Darius, king of Persia, after the Babylonian exile (Zechariah 7:1), and a member of the delegation sent by the people of Bethel.
lifetime: He is one of the members of the delegation that the people of Bethel sent to ask the priests and prophets who served in the house of the LORD about the will of God (Zechariah 7:2). These were the men who, together with Sharezer, were sent to the temple (Zechariah 7:2).
event: Regem-melech and Sharezer acted as the representatives whom the people of Bethel sent to ask those who served in the house of the LORD whether they should continue the fast of the fifth month (Zechariah 7:2-3).

직업/직위: leader of the delegation from Bethel

introduce: According to the genealogy of Scripture, Lamech was a descendant of Seth and the father of Noah, and the son of Methuselah. He was the ninth from Adam, the ancestor of humankind, and a person who lived in the time before the great flood. He appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke chapter 3 and is one of the early patriarchs of human history who continued the line of Seth (Luke 3:36).
lifetime: Methuselah fathered Lamech at the age of 187 (Genesis 5:25). Lamech, at the age of 182, fathered a son and named him Noah (Genesis 5:28). After he fathered Noah he lived 595 years more and fathered other children (Genesis 5:30), and he lived a total of 777 years and died (Genesis 5:31).
event: In fathering his son Noah, he foretold that the son's name would bring comfort concerning the toil of the ground (Genesis 5:29). In the genealogy of Scripture he is the ninth from Adam (Luke 3:36-38), and following Methuselah he maintained the line of the descendants of Seth (Genesis 5:25-31).

call: One of the five kings of Midian
introduce: Reba is one of the five kings of Midian who appear in Numbers and Joshua in the Old Testament, one who was killed when Israel struck Midian (Numbers 31:8).
lifetime: He is one of the five kings of Midian who were killed when Israel struck Midian (Numbers 31:8). Joshua 13:21 records him as one of the princes of Sihon, that is, the chiefs of Midian (Joshua 13:21).
event: As one of the five kings of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba (Numbers 31:8), he was killed together with the other four kings when Israel struck Midian, and Balaam the son of Beor was also killed with the sword (Numbers 31:8). Joshua 13:21 also records that Moses killed them together with Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the princes of Sihon, that is, the chiefs of Midian (Joshua 13:21).

introduce: Rhesa is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Luke, recorded as the son of Zerubbabel and the father of Joanan (Luke 3:27).
lifetime: Rhesa was born as a son of Zerubbabel, a descendant of David (Luke 3:27). He is named in the genealogy as a descendant of Zerubbabel and as the one who fathered Joanan (Luke 3:27).

introduce: Resheph is a figure mentioned in the genealogy of Chronicles in Scripture as a descendant of the tribe of Ephraim, and is recorded as one of the direct ancestors of Joshua.
lifetime: He was a son of Beriah, the son of Ephraim, and was a brother of Rephah (1 Chronicles 7:23, 7:25). Resheph's son was Telah, whose son was Tahan (1 Chronicles 7:25), and this genealogy continues through Ladan, Ammihud, Elishama, and Nun to Joshua (1 Chronicles 7:26-27).

call: Third son of Jacob (ancestor of the tribe of Levi)
introduce: Levi was the third son born to Jacob and Leah, and the ancestor of the tribe of Levi, which, among the twelve tribes of Israel, came to be wholly devoted to the priesthood and the service of the sanctuary.
lifetime: He was born as Leah's third son while Jacob was staying at Laban's house (Genesis 29:34). Among the family that went down to Egypt with Jacob, Levi's sons Gershon, Kohath, and Merari are recorded (Genesis 46:8-11), and Levi lived one hundred thirty-seven years (Exodus 6:16). His descendants later took on the role of maintaining the tabernacle system of Israel.
event: After the incident in which his sister Dinah was raped by Shechem, the son of Hamor, the prince of the land (Genesis 34:2), he took revenge together with Simeon, killing all the males of the city of Shechem and killing Hamor and his son Shechem with the sword (Genesis 34:25-26). Because of this he was rebuked by his father Jacob (Genesis 34:30), and at Jacob's death he heard that Simeon and Levi would be divided in Jacob and scattered in Israel (Genesis 49:5-7).
character: He reacted very fiercely and violently to the incident that had dishonored the family (Genesis 34:25), and conspiring with his brother Simeon, he showed the resolve to carry out revenge in a premeditated way (Genesis 34:27).

직업/직위: progenitor of the tribe of Levi

introduce: Rei is a figure who was active in the time of King David, mentioned as one of those who did not side with Adonijah when, at the end of David's reign, Adonijah tried to become king (1 Kings 1:8).
lifetime: When David was old, Adonijah exalted himself, saying, "I will be king" (1 Kings 1:5); Rei is recorded, together with the priest Zadok, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the prophet Nathan, and Shimei, as one who did not side with Adonijah (1 Kings 1:8).
event: When Adonijah conspired with Joab and the priest Abiathar to become king (1 Kings 1:5, 7) and invited the king's sons and the king's servants to a feast (1 Kings 1:9), Rei did not side with Adonijah (1 Kings 1:8). Beyond this, the text does not record any specific deeds of Rei.

introduce: Rohgah is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 7:34 in the Old Testament, recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher. He is recorded as a son of Shomer.
lifetime: Rohgah is recorded as one of Shomer's sons, Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram (1 Chronicles 7:34). Shomer was the son of Heber, the son of Beriah, the son of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:30-32).

introduce: Lotan was a descendant of Seir of the Horite people who lived in the land of Edom, and was one of the chiefs of the Horites (Genesis 36:29). According to the biblical record, as a son of Seir he had a family background that formed one branch of the Horite people.
lifetime: Lotan was born as one of the sons of Seir of the Horites (Genesis 36:20). He is classified as a chief of the Horites in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:21, 36:29). His brothers are recorded as Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan (1 Chronicles 1:38), and Timna was Lotan's sister (Genesis 36:22). He was also the father of Hori and Hemam (Homam in 1 Chronicles 1:39) (Genesis 36:22, 1 Chronicles 1:39).

introduce: Rhoda is a figure who appears in Acts in the New Testament, a maidservant who worked in the house of a woman named Mary in Jerusalem. In the original language of Scripture, her name carries the meaning "rose."
lifetime: When Peter, who had been imprisoned by Herod Agrippa I, came out of prison with the help of an angel and arrived at Mary's house and knocked at the gate, she was the one who came to answer (Acts 12:13). Hearing Peter's voice, in her joy she did not open the gate but ran inside and announced that Peter was standing at the gate (Acts 12:14).
event: While the believers were gathered and praying during Peter's imprisonment, she was the first to recognize him and bring the news to the people in the house (Acts 12:12-14). The people did not believe Rhoda's words and said she was out of her mind, but Rhoda insisted to the end that Peter was surely outside (Acts 12:15).
character: She seems to have been so familiar with Peter, or so well acquainted with his voice, that she recognized his voice at once (Acts 12:14). From the fact that she was flustered by the joyful news and ran inside without opening the gate, she is judged to have been frank in expressing emotion and hasty in temperament (Acts 12:14). She showed conviction, not bending her testimony despite the doubts of those around her (Acts 12:15).

meaning: One who has not received mercy
introduce: Lo-ruhamah was the daughter born to Gomer, the wife of the prophet Hosea in the Old Testament, and is recorded as the only daughter among Hosea's children. In Hebrew, this name carries the meaning of one who has not been shown compassion.
lifetime: Lo-ruhamah was a daughter born to the prophet Hosea and Gomer (Hosea 1:6). After she was born, the LORD commanded Hosea to call her name Lo-ruhamah (Hosea 1:6).
event: Her name was used as a sign symbolizing God's judging will no longer to have compassion on the house of Israel and not to forgive them (Hosea 1:6). It was prophesied that when Israel is later restored, her name will be changed to Ruhamah, that is, one who has received compassion (Hosea 2:1).

introduce: Rosh was one of the ten sons born to Benjamin, the son of Jacob, a figure included in the list when Jacob's family migrated to Egypt (Genesis 46:21).
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Benjamin, the son of Jacob, and in the course of the household of Jacob migrating to Egypt and arriving in the land of Goshen, he was recorded as a member of the family (Genesis 46:21, 46:28).
event: He was recorded as one of the seventy persons of the household of Jacob who came to Egypt (Genesis 46:21, 46:27).

introduce: Romamti-ezer was a member of the household of Heman, a group of Levite musicians who in the time of King David were in charge of praise and instrumental music in the temple. He is recorded as one of the sons of Heman.
lifetime: Romamti-ezer was born as one of the sons of Heman, a descendant of Kohath (1 Chronicles 25:4, 1 Chronicles 6:33). He performed his duties as one belonging to one of the twenty-four divisions of the temple choir organized by King David (1 Chronicles 25:31).
event: King David set apart those among the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun who played instruments in praise, and when the duties were determined by casting lots (1 Chronicles 25:8), Romamti-ezer was chosen twenty-fourth, with his sons and brothers, twelve in all (1 Chronicles 25:31). Together with his father Heman and his brothers, he was entrusted with praising in the house of God, playing lyres, harps, and cymbals (1 Chronicles 25:6).

introduce: Lo-ammi is the name that designates the third child of the prophet Hosea in the Old Testament, and in Hebrew it carries the meaning "not my people."
lifetime: He is recorded as a son born to the prophet Hosea and Gomer (Hosea 1:8).
event: God had the prophet name the child Lo-ammi in order to illustrate the situation in which the people of Israel had abandoned God (Hosea 1:9). This is an event that symbolically reveals the judgment on the northern kingdom of Israel and the severing of its relationship with God (Hosea 1:9).

introduce: Lois is a figure mentioned in 2 Timothy in the New Testament, the maternal grandmother of Timothy, a coworker of the apostle Paul. Paul wrote that the sincere faith that was in Timothy had first been in Lois and in Timothy's mother, Eunice.
lifetime: Lois was the mother of Eunice, Timothy's mother, and thus Timothy's maternal grandmother (2 Timothy 1:5). Scripture contains no record of her place of residence or of any other part of her life.
event: As he thought of the sincere faith in Timothy, Paul wrote that this faith had first been in his maternal grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice (2 Timothy 1:5). No other specific achievements or events are recorded in Scripture.
character: The apostle Paul referred to Lois' faith as sincere faith and thereby thought highly of her faithfulness in belief (2 Timothy 1:5).

introduce: Lydia is a woman who appears in Acts, from the city of Thyatira, a merchant who dealt in purple cloth. She is recorded as one who was converted when Paul and his companions preached the gospel at Philippi in the region of Europe.
lifetime: She was originally from the city of Thyatira and was living in Philippi, dealing in purple cloth (Acts 16:14). She was present when Paul spoke on the Sabbath at Philippi to the women gathered by the river, and having heard Paul's words, she and her household were baptized (Acts 16:14-15).
event: She was a worshiper of God, and as she listened to Paul, the Lord opened her heart to respond to what Paul said (Acts 16:14). After being baptized, she opened her home to Paul and his companions and prevailed upon them to stay, and after Paul and Silas were released from prison, they stopped at her house, met the brothers and encouraged them, and then left Philippi (Acts 16:15, 16:40).
character: As a businesswoman who dealt in purple cloth, she appears to have been a person of economic means; she had a strong spirit of hospitality, to the point of having Paul and his companions stay in her house, and a resolute character that actively carried out her own will (Acts 16:14-15).

introduce: Ludites is a figure who appears in Genesis, a descendant of Mizraim, the son of Ham. In the genealogy of the peoples of the ancient Near East, he is classified as one of the Egyptian-line peoples.
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of the descendants born from Mizraim, the son of Ham (Genesis 10:13). Apart from this, no specific record concerning his life exists in Scripture.
event: His name appears as a descendant of Mizraim in the genealogy of the peoples connected with Egypt (Genesis 10:13). No other specific historical achievements or events are recorded in Scripture.

introduce: Lysanias is a figure mentioned in Luke 3:1 in the New Testament, a political ruler holding the status of tetrarch who governed the region of Abilene in the period of the Roman Empire.
lifetime: In the fifteenth year of the reign of the Roman emperor Tiberius Caesar, he was serving as tetrarch of Abilene (Luke 3:1).
event: He had his name entered in the list of regional rulers together with Pontius Pilate, Herod, Philip, and others, who at that time governed Roman provinces and neighboring areas (Luke 3:1).

introduce: Rufus is a figure mentioned when the apostle Paul sends greetings to the believers of the church in Rome near the end of Romans in the New Testament, and he is presumed to be the son of Simon of Cyrene.
lifetime: Writing greetings to the believers in Rome, Paul wrote that they should greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother (Romans 16:13).
event: No direct achievements are recorded, but Paul mentions that he regards Rufus' mother as his own mother, which shows that there was a close bond between that family and Paul (Romans 16:13).
character: He received from Paul the assessment of being one chosen in the Lord, and is described as one whose mother maintained so close a relationship that she played a mother's role for Paul (Romans 16:13).

introduce: Lud is a figure mentioned as a son of Shem in the genealogy recorded in Genesis.
lifetime: He is one of the five sons born to Shem, the son of Noah (Genesis 10:22). He is recorded as one of the figures who formed the lineage of Shem in the course of the dispersion of humankind after the flood (Genesis 10:31).
event: His name appears as one of the sons of Shem (Genesis 10:22, 1 Chronicles 1:17), and no other specific events are recorded in Scripture.

introduce: Remaliah was the father of Pekah, the eighteenth king of northern Israel, and in the biblical record he is mentioned not so much for his own deeds as by the patronymic that refers to his son, "the son of Remaliah."
lifetime: Little is known about the life of Remaliah, and only the fact that he was the father of Pekah is recorded (2 Kings 15:25).
event: His son Pekah killed Pekahiah, the king of Israel, and became king in his place (2 Kings 15:25), and throughout his reign Pekah was called Pekah the son of Remaliah (2 Kings 15:27, 16:5). The book of Isaiah records that in the time of Ahaz, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up and attacked Jerusalem but could not overcome it (Isaiah 7:1).

introduce: Remaliah is a figure mentioned in 2 Kings and Isaiah in the Old Testament, the father of Pekah, king of northern Israel. In the biblical record he did not rule as king, and he appears mainly as a modifier in the designation of his son.
lifetime: Remaliah was the father of Pekah, the eighteenth king of northern Israel (2 Kings 15:25). No specific record of his birth or death appears in Scripture, and he is mentioned only in contexts that identify his son Pekah.
event: There is no record of any historical event or achievement led by Remaliah himself. Only the event of his son Pekah, called the son of Remaliah, taking the throne of northern Israel is mentioned (2 Kings 15:27). Also, in the book of Isaiah his name is cited in the historical situation in which Rezin king of Aram and Pekah the son of Remaliah joined together to attack Judah (Isaiah 7:1).

introduce: Lebanah is a figure whose name is recorded as "the descendants of Lebanah" in the list of the Nethinim among the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian captivity.
lifetime: In the list of those who had been taken captive by Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and returned to Jerusalem and Judah, the descendants of Lebanah are recorded as Nethinim (Ezra 2:1, 2:43-45). When Nehemiah found the register of the first to return, the descendants of Lebanah were likewise recorded among the Nethinim (Nehemiah 7:5-6, 7:46-47). Nothing is recorded in Scripture about the life of Lebanah himself.
event: The descendants of Lebanah are on the list of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:45, Nehemiah 7:47). The Nethinim were those whom David and the officials had set apart to serve the Levites (Ezra 8:20). Beyond this, no specific achievements or events of Lebanah himself are recorded in Scripture.

introduce: Rephaiah is a figure mentioned as the father of Arnan in the genealogy of the descendants of David recorded in 1 Chronicles chapter 3 in the Old Testament.
lifetime: Rephaiah is mentioned in the genealogy of the descendants of David in 1 Chronicles chapter 3 as "Arnan, the son of Rephaiah" and is recorded as the father of Arnan (1 Chronicles 3:21). In this verse he comes after Pelatiah, the son of Hananiah, and Jeshaiah, but the text does not state how Rephaiah is related to Hananiah or Zerubbabel. Nothing else about his life is recorded in Scripture.

introduce: Rephael was a grandson of Obed-edom and a son of Shemaiah, a descendant of Obed-edom who belonged to the divisions of the gatekeepers. He was from the tribe of Levi and a member of a family entrusted with guarding the gates of the temple (1 Chronicles 26:7-8).
lifetime: Rephael was born as a son of Shemaiah, the firstborn of Obed-edom (1 Chronicles 26:4, 26:7). The sons of Shemaiah were Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad, and these were all descendants of Obed-edom (1 Chronicles 26:7-8).
event: When the divisions of the gatekeepers were arranged in the time of King David, it was recorded that Shemaiah fathered a few sons who ruled over their father's house, for they were mighty men of valor (1 Chronicles 26:6), and Rephael was one of those sons (1 Chronicles 26:7). The descendants of Obed-edom, with their sons and brothers, were all recorded as able men, fit for the service (1 Chronicles 26:8). The duty that Rephael himself held is not separately recorded in the text.

introduce: Rezon was the ruler of Damascus and the son of Eliada, a figure who acted as an adversary in the northern region of Israel during the reign of Solomon.
lifetime: Rezon was one who had fled from Hadadezer, king of Zobah (1 Kings 11:23); when David killed the men of Zobah, he gathered men and became the leader of a band, went to Damascus, settled there, and became king there (1 Kings 11:24).
event: Throughout Solomon's life he was an adversary of Israel, and as king ruling over Aram he troubled Israel and maintained a hostile relationship (1 Kings 11:25).

introduce: Rezin was the last king of Aram-Damascus around the eighth century BC, a figure who formed a close political and military relationship with northern Israel and southern Judah. In Scripture he is recorded as the king of Aram who, in the time of Jotham and Ahaz, kings of Judah, attacked Judah together with Pekah, king of Israel (2 Kings 15:37, 16:5).
lifetime: In the time of Ahaz, king of Judah, Rezin, together with Pekah, king of northern Israel, went up to Jerusalem to wage war and besieged Ahaz but could not overcome him (2 Kings 16:5). He recovered Elath for Aram and drove the men of Judah out of Elath, and the Arameans came to Elath and settled there (2 Kings 16:6). Afterward the king of Assyria went up, attacked and took Damascus, carried its people captive to Giloh, and killed Rezin (2 Kings 16:9).
event: Rezin, together with Pekah king of Israel (the son of Remaliah), plotted to attack Judah and distress it and to set the son of Tabeal as king in the midst of it, but they could not overcome Jerusalem (Isaiah 7:1-6). When Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, asking for deliverance (2 Kings 16:7), the king of Assyria went up, took Damascus, and killed Rezin (2 Kings 16:9).

introduce: Reu is a Hebrew name meaning friend or pasture; he is a descendant of Shem recorded in the genealogy of Scripture, the son of Peleg, and a figure who appears as one of the ancestors of Abraham.
lifetime: Reu was born as a son of Peleg, fathered Serug at the age of 32, lived 207 years more and fathered other children, and died at the age of 239 (Genesis 11:18-21). His name is also stated in the genealogy of Chronicles (1 Chronicles 1:25).
event: No particular historical event or personal achievement is recorded in Scripture (Genesis 11:18-21).

introduce: Reumah is a figure who appears in Genesis in the Old Testament, recorded as a concubine of Nahor.
lifetime: In addition to the children that Nahor, Abraham's brother, had through Milcah, Nahor's concubine Reumah bore four sons (Genesis 22:24).
event: Nahor's concubine Reumah bore four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah (Genesis 22:24).

introduce: Reuben was the firstborn son born to Jacob and Leah, and the ancestor of the tribe of Reuben among the twelve tribes of Israel.
lifetime: He was born as Jacob's first son (Genesis 29:32) and was recorded as Jacob's firstborn (Genesis 35:23). Later, in Egypt, he said to his brothers, in regard to Joseph, "Did I not tell you not to sin against the boy?" and that now they must give an account for his blood (Genesis 42:22), and he went down to Egypt with Jacob and his sons (Genesis 46:8). When Jacob, before his death, called his sons and spoke, he called Reuben "my firstborn" (Genesis 49:1, 49:3).
event: He found mandrakes in the field and brought them to his mother Leah (Genesis 30:14), and he brought about the incident of lying with Bilhah, his father's concubine (Genesis 35:22). When Joseph was in danger of being killed by his brothers, he tried to rescue him and send him back home (Genesis 37:21-22), and when Joseph held Simeon as a hostage in Egypt, he proposed to his father Jacob that he take his own two sons as a pledge (Genesis 42:37).
character: By lying with his father's concubine he lost his authority as firstborn, and because of this he heard from Jacob that he was "turbulent as water" together with the prophecy that he would not excel (Genesis 49:3-4). Among his brothers he tried to play a relatively mediating role, but at the decisive moment he showed a somewhat indecisive side, unable to exert influence (Genesis 37:21-22).

직업/직위: progenitor of the tribe of Reuben

introduce: Reuel was a son of Esau, an ancestor of Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah, the chiefs of the Edomite people, and a figure who appears in Genesis and 1 Chronicles. He was the son whom Basemath, the daughter of Ishmael, bore to Esau.
lifetime: Esau's wife Basemath bore Reuel (Genesis 36:4, 36:10). Reuel is recorded as Esau's son in the genealogy of the descendants of Edom (1 Chronicles 1:35).
event: Reuel had Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah as sons (Genesis 36:13), and these were the chiefs in the land of Edom who came from Reuel (Genesis 36:17). Reuel's own deeds are not separately recorded in Scripture.

meaning: The Lord's enlargement, the LORD has made wide
introduce: He was a descendant of the tribe of Levi through Eliezer, the second son of Moses, and a prominent chief of the house of Moses recorded in 1 Chronicles (1 Chronicles 23:17).
lifetime: He was the only son of Eliezer, and the sons of Rehabiah were very many (1 Chronicles 23:17). His descendant Shelomoth and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the dedicated things of the sanctuary (1 Chronicles 26:25-26).
event: When the list of the descendants of Levi was drawn up in the time of King David, Isshiah, a chief among Rehabiah's sons, was recorded when it came to Rehabiah (1 Chronicles 24:21). Rehabiah's descendant Shelomoth and his brothers were in charge of the dedicated things that King David and the chiefs had set apart (1 Chronicles 26:25-28).

introduce: Lehabites is a figure who appears in Genesis and 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a name designating a descendant of Mizraim, the son of Ham, the son of Noah, and a people who lived in the region of Egypt, or their ancestor.
lifetime: Lehabites is recorded as one of the descendants born from Mizraim, the son of Ham (Genesis 10:13). He stands in a brotherly relationship with the Ludites, Anamites, Naphtuhites, Pathrusites, Casluhites, and Caphtorites, whom Mizraim fathered (Genesis 10:13-14, 1 Chronicles 1:11-12).
event: In the biblical record, no particular event or achievement carried out by Lehabites himself is described separately, and his name is mentioned only in the genealogy of the descendants of Mizraim (Genesis 10:13).

introduce: Rehoboam was a son of Solomon, the first king of the kingdom of Judah, and the successor of the house of David. During his reign the kingdom of Israel was divided into north and south.
lifetime: Born as Solomon's son, he took the throne after his father (1 Kings 11:43). He attended the assembly of Israel at Shechem and was made king (1 Kings 12:1), but by refusing the people's demand, he caused the northern tribes to rebel (1 Kings 12:16). Afterward he ruled the southern kingdom of Judah, centered on the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and became king at the age of 41 and reigned in Jerusalem for 17 years (1 Kings 14:21).
event: At Shechem, when the people demanded that the hard service and heavy yoke his father Solomon had imposed be made lighter, he rejected their demand and instead said that he would make the yoke heavier, and so he provided the direct cause of the division of Israel (1 Kings 12:4, 12:13-14). After the division there was constant war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam (1 Kings 14:30). In the fifth year after he became king, Shishak, king of Egypt, invaded Jerusalem and took away all the treasures of the temple and the royal palace, along with the gold shields that Solomon had made (1 Kings 14:25-26). For national defense he built and fortified various cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 11:5-12).
character: He disregarded the counsel of the elders and made an immature decision, choosing the hard-line opinion of the young men who had grown up with him (1 Kings 12:8-11). He did evil in the sight of the LORD, and caused religious confusion by setting up high places, pillars, and Asherah poles for the worship of idols (1 Kings 14:22-23). He had many wives and concubines and designated Abijah as his successor (2 Chronicles 11:21-22).

call: Leader of those returning with Zerubbabel
introduce: Rehum is one of the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian captivity, a figure included in the list of the leadership of the Jewish community. In the biblical record he is mentioned as one of the early leaders who returned with Zerubbabel.
lifetime: Rehum is recorded as one of those who came among the returnees who came back from Babylon to Jerusalem, together with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Baanah, and others (Ezra 2:2). The name Rehum also appears in the list of priests in Nehemiah 12:3, but the text does not make clear whether he is the same person as the Rehum of Ezra 2:2.
event: Ezra 2:2 enters Rehum's name in the list that records the count of the people of Israel who came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and others. Nehemiah 12:1-3 records Rehum in the list of priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua. No other specific events are recorded in Scripture.

introduce: Linus is a figure recorded in 2 Timothy 4:21 in the New Testament as one who sent greetings to Timothy together with Eubulus, Pudens, Claudia, and all the brothers.
lifetime: In the letter Paul sent to Timothy, he appears as one who greets Timothy together with Eubulus, Pudens, Claudia, and all the brothers (2 Timothy 4:21). There is no other record in Scripture about his life.
event: No specific achievements or events of Linus are recorded in Scripture, and his name appears only in the list of greetings (2 Timothy 4:21).

introduce: Riphath was a grandson of Noah's son Japheth and a son of Gomer, and appears in the genealogy of Noah's descendants in Genesis 10. In the parallel list of Gomer's descendants in 1 Chronicles 1:6 he is written as Diphath.
lifetime: Riphath was a son of Gomer, the son of Japheth, and is recorded as a brother of Ashkenaz and Togarmah (Genesis 10:2-3).

introduce: Ribai is the father of Ittai, one of the thirty-seven mighty men of David (2 Samuel 23:29, 23:39). He is recorded as a man of Gibeah, belonging to the descendants of Benjamin (2 Samuel 23:29, 1 Chronicles 11:31).
lifetime: Ribai was a man of Gibeah belonging to the descendants of Benjamin (2 Samuel 23:29). His son Ittai is recorded as one of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:29; he is written Ithai in 1 Chronicles 11:31). There is no other record in Scripture about his life.

introduce: Rebekah was from Paddan-aram, the daughter of Bethuel, a relative of Abraham, and the granddaughter of Nahor. She became the wife of Isaac and bore Jacob and Esau, and played a key role in carrying on the family line in the formation of the nation of Israel.
lifetime: Through the servant sent by Abraham, she was chosen as Isaac's bride and moved to Canaan (Genesis 24:15-67). After marriage she was childless for a long time, but through Isaac's prayer she conceived and bore the twins Esau and Jacob (Genesis 25:21-26). In her later years, after carrying out her plan to have Jacob receive the blessing in place of the firstborn Esau, she sent Jacob to flee to the house of her brother Laban (Genesis 27:42-45).
event: At the well she showed the kindness of drawing water not only for Abraham's servant but also for his camels, and was chosen as Isaac's wife (Genesis 24:18-20). While pregnant she suffered the pain of the children struggling within her womb and received a revelation from God that two nations would be born (Genesis 25:22-23). When Isaac was about to bless Esau after asking him for savory food, she helped Jacob disguise himself and advised him so that he might seize the blessing (Genesis 27:6-17).
character: She had the resolve and ability to act, serving even a stranger actively (Genesis 24:19-20). She favored Jacob among her sons (Genesis 25:28), and showed insight and boldness in drawing up and carrying out a meticulous and strategic plan to pass on the family blessing (Genesis 27:6-13).

introduce: Rizpah was a concubine of King Saul, the daughter of Aiah, and a figure who stood at the center of the tragic events that took place after Saul's death.
lifetime: Rizpah bore to King Saul two sons, Armoni and Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 21:8). After Saul died, Ish-bosheth rebuked Abner, who had been Saul's army commander, saying, "Why have you slept with my father's concubine?" and this became the occasion for Abner, angered by it, to say that he would transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul to David (2 Samuel 3:7-10). Afterward, when her two sons were executed by the Gibeonites in retaliation against the house of Saul, she spent a long time guarding the bodies (2 Samuel 21:9-10).
event: When the Gibeonites demanded Saul's descendants, David handed over Rizpah's two sons, Armoni and Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 21:8). Immediately after they were executed, Rizpah spread sackcloth on a rock and, from the beginning of the harvest until the rain fell from heaven, kept the birds of the air from touching the bodies by day and the wild animals by night (2 Samuel 21:10). When David heard of this, he had the bones of Saul and Jonathan gathered and buried in their tomb (2 Samuel 21:13-14).
character: Even in the tragic circumstances in which her children had been executed, she did not yield, but showed devotion by living in the open for a long time to protect the bodies (2 Samuel 21:10). This action of hers became the direct cause that led David, after the executions of the house of Saul were completed, to have the funeral of Saul and his descendants carried out with respect (2 Samuel 21:13-14).

introduce: Ishvi was a son of Saul, the first king of Israel, and a person belonging to the genealogy of the house of Saul.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Saul (1 Samuel 14:49). In the same verse Jonathan and Malchishua appear together as sons of Saul, and Saul's two daughters are recorded: the elder, Merab, and the younger, Michal (1 Samuel 14:49).

introduce: Rizia is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 7:39 in the Old Testament, one of the sons of Ulla recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.
lifetime: Rizia is recorded as one of Ulla's sons, Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia (1 Chronicles 7:39). The next verse records these among the chiefs of the descendants of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:40).

introduce: Likhi is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh, a son of Shemida (1 Chronicles 7:19).
lifetime: Likhi was a son of Shemida and is recorded as a brother of Ahian, Shechem, and Aniam (1 Chronicles 7:19).

introduce: Rinnah is a figure recorded as a son of Shimon in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles chapter 4). His name appears within the genealogical record of Scripture, but information about his detailed life or role is limited.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon (1 Chronicles 4:20).

introduce: Mark is a figure who appears in the New Testament; his given name was John, and he also used the Roman name Mark. He had a close relationship with the workers of the early church and served as a helper in the process of the spread of early Christianity.
lifetime: Mark was the son of Mary of Jerusalem and the cousin of Barnabas (Acts 12:12, Colossians 4:10). He accompanied Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary journey, but left the party at Perga in Pamphylia and returned to Jerusalem (Acts 13:13). Afterward, Paul and Barnabas had a sharp dispute over taking Mark along, and in the end Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus (Acts 15:37-39). In Paul's letters he is mentioned as a coworker who sends greetings (Colossians 4:10, Philemon 1:24), and Paul told Timothy to bring Mark with him, saying that he was useful to him in his ministry (2 Timothy 4:11). Peter showed his affection by calling him "my son" (1 Peter 5:13).
event: Because of the incident in which he dropped out midway through the first missionary journey of Paul and Barnabas, Mark was for a time not trusted by Paul as a partner in ministry (Acts 15:38). Later, however, Paul told Timothy to bring Mark with him, mentioning that he was useful to him in his work (2 Timothy 4:11). Early Christian literature and tradition identify him as the author of the Gospel of Mark.
character: He showed weakness in giving up midway during the early missionary work (Acts 13:13), but afterward, through the encouragement of Barnabas and his own effort, he grew into a person trusted again by Paul (2 Timothy 4:11). He had the character of a helper, assisting the ministries of Peter and Paul, the leading apostles of the day, and maintaining wide cooperative relationships (Colossians 4:10, 1 Peter 5:13).

직업/직위: fellow worker of the apostles Paul and Peter

introduce: Magog is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Genesis, one of the sons of Japheth, the son of Noah. He is classified as a figure who explains the genealogy of the peoples of the ancient Near East.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Japheth, the son of Noah (Genesis 10:2). As a descendant of Japheth, he is a figure recorded in the early genealogy of humankind (1 Chronicles 1:5).
event: No record of individual events or specific achievements appears in Scripture. His descendants, however, are mentioned in the book of Ezekiel and elsewhere as a name that forms a national origin (Ezekiel 38:2).

introduce: Machi is a figure recorded as the father of Geuel, whom the tribe of Gad sent to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:15).
lifetime: Machi is recorded only as the father of Geuel, the spy of the tribe of Gad (Numbers 13:15). There is no record in Scripture about Machi's own life.
event: No event of Machi himself is recorded in Scripture. His son Geuel, representing the tribe of Gad, was one of the spies sent by Moses; he searched out the land of Canaan and after forty days returned and reported to the congregation (Numbers 13:15, 13:25-26).

introduce: Machir appears in the Old Testament as a son of Manasseh and a grandson of Joseph. He was the ancestor of the family of the Machirites (Numbers 26:29), and is recorded as a warrior who obtained Gilead and Bashan (Joshua 17:1).
lifetime: Machir was the firstborn of Manasseh and fathered Gilead (Joshua 17:1, Numbers 26:29). His sons were brought up on the knees of Joseph (Genesis 50:23). Moses gave Gilead to Machir, and he dwelt there (Numbers 32:40), and half of the descendants of Machir, according to their families, received half of Gilead and the cities of the kingdom of Og king of Bashan (Joshua 13:31).
event: It is recorded that Machir, being a warrior, obtained Gilead and Bashan (Joshua 17:1). The descendants of Machir went to Gilead, drove out the Amorites who were there, and took the land (Numbers 32:39), and Moses gave Gilead to Machir, and he dwelt there (Numbers 32:40). In the song of Deborah and Barak there is the line that rulers came down from Machir (Judges 5:1, 5:14).
character: There is no record that directly describes Machir's character, but by describing him as a mighty man of valor, Scripture suggests that he excelled in battle and conquest (Numbers 32:39). His weight within the family can be seen in the fact that his descendants formed the largest force within the tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 17:1).

introduce: Manaen is a figure who appears in Acts in the New Testament, one of the group of leaders of the church at Antioch. He is recorded as a foster brother of Herod the tetrarch.
lifetime: He is recorded as a foster brother of Herod the tetrarch (Acts 13:1). Afterward he served as one of the prophets and teachers of the church at Antioch (Acts 13:1).
event: While fasting and serving the Lord in the church at Antioch, he took part in the process of setting apart Barnabas and Saul for a missionary journey at the direction of the Holy Spirit (Acts 13:2).
character: He had the background of having been brought up together with Herod the tetrarch, and a notable feature is that, despite this background, he took up and served in the weighty role of prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch (Acts 13:1).

introduce: Manahath is a figure recorded in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles as a son of Shobal, a descendant of Seir of the Horite people.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the children of Shobal, the son of Seir of the Horites (Genesis 36:23). He appears as a son of Shobal in 1 Chronicles 1:40 as well (1 Chronicles 1:40).
event: There is no record in Scripture of Manahath's own deeds. His father Shobal is recorded as one of the chiefs of the Horites in the land of Seir (Genesis 36:29).

introduce: A man of the tribe of Dan who lived in the land of Zorah, and the father of Samson.
lifetime: His wife was originally unable to conceive, but the angel of the LORD appeared and announced the birth of a son (Judges 13:2-3). Having heard this news from his wife, Manoah prayed to the LORD and pleaded that the angel be allowed to appear to them again (Judges 13:8). From the angel who then appeared, he heard how the child was to be raised and what was forbidden, and he killed a young goat and offered it as a sacrifice (Judges 13:10-20). After his son Samson grew up, he tried to dissuade Samson from marrying a Philistine woman, but did not know that the intent was from the LORD (Judges 14:2-4).
event: He saw the angel of the LORD appear, and the flame rise from the altar, and the angel ascend in the flame (Judges 13:20). Through this event Manoah and his wife realized that the one before them was the angel of the LORD and were seized with fear (Judges 13:21-22). After Samson died, his brothers and the whole house of his father brought the body and buried it in the burial place of Manoah between Zorah and Eshtaol (Judges 16:31).
character: He believed the revelation that his wife had received and showed prudence in asking for specific instructions on how the child should be raised (Judges 13:8). After seeing the divine being, he was a man of such strong reverence that he was gripped by the thought, "We have seen God; we will surely die" (Judges 13:22). He was faithful in communicating with his family, as when he was reassured after hearing his wife explain the situation (Judges 13:23).

직업/직위: clan chief of the tribe of Dan

introduce: One of the sons of Japheth, the son of Noah, recorded in Genesis; he is mentioned as the ancestor of a certain people of the ancient Near East.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son born to Noah's son Japheth after the flood of Noah (Genesis 10:2). Japheth's other sons were Gomer, Magog, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras (Genesis 10:2).
event: After the flood, his descendants were divided into nations, each settling in its own land according to its language, clan, and nation (Genesis 10:5). Madai is regarded as the ancestor of the ancient Medes, and is interpreted historically and anthropologically as the origin of the people who formed the region of Media (Genesis 10:2).

introduce: Matred appears in the genealogy of the kings who ruled the land of Edom; she was the daughter of Mezahab and the mother of Mehetabel. Her daughter Mehetabel is recorded as the wife of Hadad king of Edom (Hadad also in 1 Chronicles 1:50) (Genesis 36:39, 1 Chronicles 1:50).
lifetime: Matred was the daughter of Mezahab, and her daughter Mehetabel became the wife of Hadad king of Edom (Genesis 36:39). In 1 Chronicles 1:50 as well, Mehetabel is recorded as the daughter of Matred and the granddaughter of Mezahab (1 Chronicles 1:50).
event: No political achievement or particular event of Matred herself is recorded; her name appears only in the introduction of Mehetabel, as her mother and the daughter of Mezahab (Genesis 36:39, 1 Chronicles 1:50).

introduce: Matri is the name of a clan belonging to the tribe of Benjamin, which appears in 1 Samuel 10:21 as "the family of Matri." There is no record in Scripture about Matri as an individual (1 Samuel 10:21).
lifetime: When Samuel set up Saul as king and had the tribe of Benjamin come near by families, the family of Matri was chosen (1 Samuel 10:21).
event: After Israel demanded that a king be set up and the tribes were brought forward, the tribe of Benjamin was chosen (1 Samuel 10:20); then, when the tribe of Benjamin came forward by families, the family of Matri was chosen, and from among them Saul the son of Kish was chosen (1 Samuel 10:21).

introduce: Mareshah is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as the father of Hebron and the grandson of Caleb.
lifetime: He was born as the son of Mesha, the son of Caleb, and is recorded as the father of Hebron (1 Chronicles 2:42).
event: There is no record of Mareshah's own deeds; he is recorded only as the father of Hebron (1 Chronicles 2:42).

introduce: A woman who lived in Bethany, a sister of Lazarus and Mary, who welcomed Jesus into her home and served him during his ministry.
lifetime: When Jesus visited a village in Bethany, she welcomed him into her house (Luke 10:38). When her brother Lazarus was sick, she sent word to Jesus asking for help (John 11:3), and after Lazarus died, when Jesus arrived at Bethany, she went out of the village to meet him (John 11:20). When Jesus visited Bethany again, she served the meal at the gathering where Mary poured out the perfume (John 12:2).
event: To serve Jesus with great hospitality she took on all the work in the kitchen, but she complained directly to Jesus that Mary was not helping her (Luke 10:40). After her brother Lazarus died, when he had been in the tomb four days, she met Jesus and talked with him about the resurrection (John 11:21-27). She also voiced the practical concern that the body would be decaying and smell, when Jesus commanded that the stone of Lazarus's tomb be removed (John 11:39).
character: She showed a practical and active disposition, busily moving about to serve the guest who had visited her (Luke 10:40). She is recorded as frank and direct, not hiding her feelings or circumstances but complaining to Jesus or raising questions directly (Luke 10:40, John 11:21, John 11:39). At the same time, she also gave an answer of faith, confessing that Jesus is the Christ (John 11:27).

introduce: Marsena is one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who, during the reign of King Xerxes of the Persian Empire, had access to the king and held the highest positions in the kingdom (Esther 1:14).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to the king, saw the king's face, and held the highest positions in the kingdom (Esther 1:14).
event: When Queen Vashti did not obey the king's command, the king, following the custom of consulting those who knew the law and judgment, asked what should be done with her according to the law (Esther 1:13, 1:15), and Marsena's name is recorded in connection with this matter as one of the seven princes who had access to the king (Esther 1:14). The one recorded as answering before the king and the princes is Memucan (Esther 1:16), and no statement of Marsena himself is recorded.

introduce: A woman from Nazareth who was betrothed to Joseph, a descendant of David, and who conceived and gave birth to Jesus. According to Scripture, as the mother of Jesus she is a key figure mentioned from the early part of his life, through part of his public ministry, and on to the community of the early church after the resurrection.
lifetime: She was told by the angel Gabriel that she would conceive by the Holy Spirit (Luke 1:30-31), and she gave birth to Jesus in Bethlehem (Luke 2:6-7). Afterward she fled to Egypt to escape the persecution of King Herod (Matthew 2:13-14), and then returned and settled in Nazareth (Matthew 2:23). During Jesus' public ministry she took part in the wedding feast at Cana (John 2:1-3), she stayed beside the cross at his execution (John 19:25), and after the ascension she was among the community devoting themselves to prayer with the disciples (Acts 1:14).
event: She accepted the angel's announcement of the conception and conceived Jesus (Luke 1:38). In Jesus' boyhood she went through the incident of losing him and finding him again in the temple (Luke 2:48). At the wedding feast at Cana she told Jesus that the wine had run out (John 2:3). During Jesus' public ministry, while he was speaking to the crowds, she stood outside with his brothers, wanting to speak to him (Matthew 12:46). At the cross, Jesus pointed to the disciple whom he loved and said to his mother, "Here is your son," and from that hour that disciple took Mary into his own home (John 19:26-27).
character: When she heard the angel's announcement, she showed carefulness, wondering and asking a question (Luke 1:34). She showed a disposition to keep all that happened to her deep in her heart and ponder it (Luke 2:19). It is recorded that she had the human side of searching for Jesus in great anguish when he was missing in the temple (Luke 2:48). In the early part of her son's public ministry, she sometimes showed concern, not fully understanding Jesus' actions (Mark 3:21).

introduce: Mamre was an Amorite who lived near the oak grove of Mamre at Hebron, a brother of Eshcol and Aner, and an ally of Abram (Genesis 13:18, 14:13).
lifetime: While Abram was living near the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, Mamre is recorded as a brother of Eshcol and a brother of Aner, who were allies of Abram (Genesis 14:13). Abram said that Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre, who had gone with him, should take their share (Genesis 14:24).
event: When Abram heard that his nephew Lot had been taken captive by four kings, he pursued them and recovered Lot and the goods (Genesis 14:12-16); Mamre is mentioned as one who went with Abram, along with Aner and Eshcol (Genesis 14:24). Abram said that what the young men had eaten and the share of the men who went with him, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre, would be excluded from what he took, but that they should take their share (Genesis 14:24).
character: Mamre showed the resolve to maintain a military and political alliance with Abraham based on trust (Genesis 14:13). Also, as Abraham's allied force, he held the standing of a companion who received just treatment after the victory in the war (Genesis 14:24).

introduce: Mahseiah is a figure who appears in the book of Jeremiah in the Old Testament, recorded as the father of Neriah and the grandfather of Baruch and Seraiah (Jeremiah 32:12, 51:59).
lifetime: His name appears only in the phrases introducing the two men, "Baruch son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah" in Jeremiah 32:12 and "Seraiah son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah" in Jeremiah 51:59. Mahseiah's own deeds are not recorded in Scripture.
event: No event of Mahseiah himself is recorded. His grandson Baruch was the man to whom Jeremiah handed the deed of purchase for the field at Anathoth (Jeremiah 32:12), and his other grandson Seraiah was the quartermaster who received a message from Jeremiah when he went to Babylon with the king in the fourth year of Zedekiah (Jeremiah 51:59).

introduce: Mash is a figure mentioned as a son of Aram in the genealogy of Noah's descendants recorded in Genesis chapter 10; he is classified as a grandson of Shem and one of the four sons of Aram.
lifetime: Mash was born as a son of Aram, the son of Shem (Genesis 10:23). He was recorded in the genealogy as a descendant of Aram in the course of the multiplication of the descendants of Shem after Noah's flood (Genesis 10:22, 23).

call: Son of Reumah, concubine of Nahor
introduce: One of the four children that Nahor, the brother of Abraham, had by his concubine Reumah.
lifetime: He was born to Nahor and his concubine Reumah, and is recorded together with Tebah, Gaham, and Tahash as children of Nahor's concubine Reumah (Genesis 22:24).

introduce: Maadai is one of the descendants of Bani recorded in Ezra chapter 10 as having taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:34, 10:44).
lifetime: Maadai is recorded as one of the descendants of Bani (Ezra 10:34).
event: He was included in the list of the descendants of Bani who were investigated and recorded as having taken foreign women (Ezra 10:34, 10:44). At that time the people made a covenant and took an oath before God to send away their foreign wives and the children born to them (Ezra 10:3, 10:5).

introduce: Maadiah is a priest recorded in the list of the priests who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1, 12:5).
lifetime: His name is on the list of the priests and Levites who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1, 12:5). The priests on this list are recorded as having been the chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:7).
