event: Scripture does not separately record any deeds of Maadiah himself; his name appears only in the list of the chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:5, 12:7).

introduce: Maasai was a member of a priestly family who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile; he was the son of Adiel, the grandson of Jahzerah, the great-grandson of Meshullam, the great-great-grandson of Meshillemith, and the fifth-generation descendant of Immer (1 Chronicles 9:12).
lifetime: After returning from Babylon, he settled and lived in Jerusalem as a member of a priestly family (1 Chronicles 9:12). As the son of Adiel, his name is entered in the genealogy of the priestly lineage (1 Chronicles 9:12).
event: As one of the priests living in Jerusalem, he was included in the genealogy of the family that carried out duties related to the temple (1 Chronicles 9:12). In the record of 1 Chronicles chapter 9, he is listed as a member of a prominent priestly family holding duties in the house of God (1 Chronicles 9:12).

call: Musician who praised before the ark in the days of David
meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: One of the Levite musicians of David's time recorded in 1 Chronicles, he was appointed to play the harp when David moved the ark of God to Jerusalem.
lifetime: When David commanded the chiefs of the Levites to appoint singers and make a joyful sound loudly with harps, lyres, and cymbals, Maaseiah was included in that list and chosen as one who played the harp (1 Chronicles 15:18, 15:20).
event: When David brought the ark of God up to the place he had prepared for it, he commanded the chiefs of the Levites to appoint singers (1 Chronicles 15:16), and Maaseiah is recorded as one of the brothers appointed accordingly (1 Chronicles 15:18). He is recorded as one who played the harp to accompany the high female voices (Alamoth) (1 Chronicles 15:20).

introduce: Maaz is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2:27).
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel, and Maaz, Jamin, and Eker appear together as the sons of Ram (1 Chronicles 2:27).

call: Chief of the twenty-fourth division of priests
introduce: According to the classification of the priestly divisions recorded in 1 Chronicles chapter 24, he is the priestly chief corresponding to the twenty-fourth division. He is the one who held the last position among the twenty-four priestly divisions that King David organized for the service of the temple.
lifetime: In the reign of King David, when the divisions were assigned by lot in order to systematize the duties of the priests, he was chosen as the head of the twenty-fourth division (1 Chronicles 24:18).
event: When David, together with Zadok of the descendants of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the descendants of Ithamar, divided the descendants of Aaron and assigned them their respective duties of service (1 Chronicles 24:3), they were divided by casting lots (1 Chronicles 24:5), and Maaziah is recorded as the twenty-fourth division (1 Chronicles 24:18).

introduce: Maath is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus recorded in Luke chapter 3, an ancestor in the family line who is the son of Mattathias and the father of Naggai (Luke 3:25-26).
lifetime: In the genealogy of Luke chapter 3 he is recorded in the position following as the son of Mattathias and the father of Naggai (Luke 3:25-26).

introduce: Maai is a figure who appears in the book of Nehemiah in the Old Testament, a member of a priestly family who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem.
lifetime: He came from a priestly family and took part in the dedication ceremony held after the wall of Jerusalem was rebuilt (Nehemiah 12:36).
event: He took the musical instruments of David the man of God and, led by Ezra, took part in the procession for the dedication of the wall (Nehemiah 12:36).

introduce: Maoch is a figure recorded as the father of Achish. When David fled from Saul and went to the land of the Philistines, Achish king of Gath, to whom he went, is introduced as the son of Maoch (1 Samuel 27:2).
lifetime: Scripture has no record about Maoch's own life; his name appears only in the account that David crossed over with six hundred men to Achish son of Maoch (1 Samuel 27:2).
event: No event of Maoch himself is recorded. David crossed over with six hundred men to his son Achish, and David and his men, each with his household, dwelt with Achish in Gath (1 Samuel 27:2-3).

introduce: Maon is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, the son of Shammai and the father of Beth-zur. Shammai was fathered by Rekem, the son of Hebron (1 Chronicles 2:43-45).
lifetime: In the genealogy of 1 Chronicles chapter 2, it is recorded that Rekem, the son of Hebron, fathered Shammai, and that the son of Shammai was Maon (1 Chronicles 2:43-45).
event: Maon is recorded as the father of Beth-zur (1 Chronicles 2:45). No other deeds are recorded in Scripture.

meaning: Gift of God, gift of the LORD
introduce: Matthew is a figure who appears in the New Testament, one of the twelve disciples of Jesus. He is known to have been a tax collector who sat at the tax booth in Capernaum, and he was also called by the name Levi.
lifetime: He met Jesus while working at the tax booth in Capernaum (Matthew 9:9). When Jesus called him to follow him, he got up and followed Jesus (Mark 2:14), and it is recorded that he left everything and followed (Luke 5:28). Afterward he was chosen as one of Jesus' twelve disciples, and his name was included in the list of the disciples (Matthew 10:3).
event: He invited Jesus to his house and held a great banquet attended by tax collectors and sinners (Luke 5:29). When the Pharisees saw Jesus and his disciples eating there and criticized them, Jesus answered them (Matthew 9:11-13). After Jesus' ascension, he went up to the upper room in Jerusalem and devoted himself to prayer together with the other apostles (Acts 1:13-14).
character: He had another name, Levi, and is recorded as the son of Alphaeus (Mark 2:14). Because of the nature of his occupation as a tax collector, he belonged to a class classified as sinners in Jewish society at that time (Matthew 9:10). The moment he was called by Jesus, he showed the resolve to leave behind his tax booth duties and possessions and follow Jesus (Luke 5:27-28).

introduce: Maharai was one of the mighty men who distinguished themselves in David's military organization and carried out military duties during David's reign. He is recorded as a Netophathite.
lifetime: He is recorded as a Netophathite in the list of the mighty men belonging to David's Thirty (2 Samuel 23:28). He appears as Maharai the Netophathite in 1 Chronicles 11:30 as well.
event: Among the twelve divisions of David's army, each taking its turn to serve 24,000 men a month, he was appointed commander of the tenth division and served in that role (1 Chronicles 27:13).
character: In the biblical record there is no specific description of Maharai's personal character or physical features.

introduce: Mahazioth is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles chapter 25, one of the Levites assigned to the temple choir organization in the time of King David.
lifetime: He was one of the sons of Heman and, together with his father Heman, belonged to the group of temple musicians appointed by David (1 Chronicles 25:4).
event: In the time of King David, those who were to give praise in the temple received their duties by casting lots (1 Chronicles 25:8), and Mahazioth was chosen twenty-third, with his sons and brothers, twelve in all, belonging to him (1 Chronicles 25:30).

introduce: Mahalalel is a figure who appears in Genesis in the Bible, a fourth-generation descendant of Adam, a great-grandson of Seth, and the son of Kenan. He is one of the patriarchs of the line of Seth who make up the genealogy before Noah.
lifetime: Kenan fathered Mahalalel at the age of 70 (Genesis 5:12). Mahalalel fathered Jared at the age of 65, lived 830 years after that and had other sons and daughters, and died having lived a total of 895 years (Genesis 5:15-17).
character: As a figure who continues the genealogy of Adam, his name is interpreted as meaning a hymn of praise or praising God (Genesis 5:12). Within the flow of the genealogy recorded in Scripture, no particular deeds or traits are described about him other than the record that he lived long and had children (Genesis 5:15-17).

introduce: Mahalath is a figure who appears in Genesis in the Old Testament, a daughter of Ishmael, a sister of Nebaioth, and a wife of Esau. She is also called by the name Basemath.
lifetime: When Esau saw that the daughters of the Canaanites did not please his father Isaac (Genesis 28:8), he went to Ishmael and took as his wife Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, the son of Abraham (Genesis 28:9). Another record in Scripture says that he took Basemath, the daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth (Genesis 36:3).
event: In addition to his own wives, Esau took as his wife Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth (Genesis 28:9). The son born to her and Esau is Reuel (Genesis 36:4).

introduce: Mahath is a Levite of the descendants of Kohath, the son of Amasai and the father of Elkanah. In the genealogy of 1 Chronicles chapter 6 he is recorded as an ancestor of Heman, a descendant of Kohath, to whom David entrusted the work of singing praise (1 Chronicles 6:31-35).
lifetime: In the genealogy of Heman, a descendant of Kohath, in 1 Chronicles chapter 6, he is recorded as the son of Amasai and the father of Elkanah (1 Chronicles 6:33-35).
event: Scripture does not record any deeds of Mahath himself; he is mentioned only in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 6:35 as the father of Elkanah and the son of Amasai.
character: In the Scriptural record, no description of his personal character or specific traits appears (1 Chronicles 6:35, 2 Chronicles 29:12). Still, it can be confirmed that, as a member of a lineage that carried out the duties of the tribe of Levi handed down through the generations, he was faithfully assigned to public duties (2 Chronicles 29:12).

introduce: Maher-shalal-hash-baz is a figure who appears in the book of Isaiah in the Old Testament, a son of the prophet Isaiah. His name carries the meaning of quickly obtaining spoil.
lifetime: He was born when the prophet Isaiah lay with his wife and she bore a son (Isaiah 8:3). Even before he was born, it was announced beforehand that he would be called by the name the LORD commanded (Isaiah 8:1).
event: In accordance with the LORD's command, a sign-act was carried out in which his name was written on a tablet (Isaiah 8:1). He was used as a sign of the prophecy that before the child could speak, the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria would be carried off before the king of Assyria (Isaiah 8:4).

introduce: Mahol is a figure who appears in 1 Kings in the Old Testament, recorded as the father of Heman, Calcol, and Darda, who are compared with the wisdom of Solomon.
lifetime: Scripture does not record any specific birth or background of Mahol's life, and mentions only the fact that he was the father of Heman, Calcol, and Darda (1 Kings 4:31).
event: It is recorded that Solomon's wisdom was greater than that of Ethan the Ezrahite and of Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol (1 Kings 4:31). Mahol's own deeds are not recorded.

meaning: What is like the generosity of God?
introduce: Machnadebai is an Israelite mentioned in the list of those who had foreign wives during Ezra's reform after the return from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: Machnadebai is recorded as one of the descendants of Bani who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem (Ezra 10:40).
event: Machnadebai had taken a foreign woman as his wife, and was included in the list of those who pledged to send away that wife and the children born to her, in accordance with the divorce measure led by Ezra (Ezra 10:40).

introduce: Machbanai is a figure mentioned in 1 Chronicles chapter 12, one of David's mighty men who came to him and gave military support while David was staying at Ziklag to escape Saul.
lifetime: Machbanai is recorded as one of the mighty men of the sons of Gad who joined David (1 Chronicles 12:13). He belonged to the band that was with David when David had taken refuge at Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:1).
event: Machbanai is identified as the eleventh of the eleven chief mighty men of the sons of Gad who joined David's camp (1 Chronicles 12:13). Those who joined David at that time were mighty men trained for war, able to handle shield and spear (1 Chronicles 12:8). They crossed the Jordan River, joined David, and carried out a military role in helping him (1 Chronicles 12:15).

introduce: Machbenah is a name that appears in the genealogy of Caleb in the tribe of Judah; he is recorded as Machbenah, whose father was Sheva, born to Caleb's concubine Maacah (1 Chronicles 2:48-49).
lifetime: Sheva, born to Caleb's concubine Maacah, is recorded as "the father of Machbenah and Gibea," and Machbenah is entered in this genealogy (1 Chronicles 2:48-49).
event: Scripture does not record any deeds of Machbenah himself; Sheva is mentioned only as the father of Machbenah and Gibea (1 Chronicles 2:49).

introduce: He is a figure whose name is recorded as "the descendants of Magbish" in the list of the people of Israel who finished their captivity in Babylon and returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:1-2, 2:30).
lifetime: He is a member of the community of returnees who came back from the Babylonian captivity to Jerusalem and Judah (Ezra 2:30).
event: In the list of returnees in Ezra chapter 2, one hundred fifty-six of the descendants of Magbish are recorded (Ezra 2:30).

introduce: Magpiash is a figure who appears in the book of Nehemiah in the Old Testament, one of the leaders of the community of Israel that returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He is a man who put his name on the list of those who sealed the covenant, drawn up under the leadership of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:20).
lifetime: After returning from Babylon, at the time the covenant was made he is recorded as one of the chiefs of the people among those who sealed it (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:20).
event: Among those who sealed it were Nehemiah the governor and the chiefs of the people (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:14), and Magpiash is on the list of those chiefs (Nehemiah 10:20). The rest of the people, the priests, and the Levites also swore to observe the law of God (Nehemiah 10:28-29).

introduce: Malcam is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the sons born to Hodesh, the wife of Shaharaim (1 Chronicles 8:9).
lifetime: Malcam is recorded as the fourth among the sons whom Shaharaim fathered in the land of Moab by his wife Hodesh, after he had sent away his two wives Hushim and Baara (1 Chronicles 8:8-9).

introduce: Malchus is a figure who appears in the New Testament, a servant of the high priest who was at the scene when Jesus Christ was arrested.
lifetime: Malchus was serving as a servant of the high priest (John 18:10), and accompanied the party at the scene of the arrest of Jesus (John 18:10).
event: In the course of Jesus' arrest, he was wounded when his right ear was cut off by the sword that Peter swung (John 18:10). Afterward Jesus touched his ear and healed it (Luke 22:51).

introduce: Malchiram is a figure belonging to the royal lineage of the tribe of Judah, one of the sons of Jeconiah, who was carried captive, in the genealogy of the house of David (1 Chronicles 3:17-18).
lifetime: Malchiram is recorded as one of the sons of Jeconiah (Jehoiachin) king of Judah (1 Chronicles 3:17-18). In 1 Chronicles 3:17-18, the sons of Jeconiah the captive are recorded as Shealtiel, followed by Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.

introduce: Malchishua is a figure mentioned as one of the sons of King Saul (1 Samuel 14:49).
lifetime: Malchishua is recorded as a son of Saul (1 Samuel 14:49). The Philistines pursued Saul and his sons closely and killed Saul's sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua (1 Samuel 31:2).
event: When the Philistines pursued Saul and his sons closely, he was killed together with his father King Saul and his brothers Jonathan and Abinadab (1 Samuel 31:2). The next day the Philistines saw that Saul and his three sons had died on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31:8), and they cut off Saul's head and stripped off his armor (1 Samuel 31:9).

introduce: Malchijah is a figure belonging to the genealogy of the Gershonites of the tribe of Levi, a Levite who appears in the genealogical record of 1 Chronicles chapter 6 (1 Chronicles 6:40).
lifetime: Malchijah was the son of Ethni and the father of Baaseiah (1 Chronicles 6:40-41). He is recorded in the genealogy of the Levites as one of the ancestors of Asaph, and that lineage runs through Gershon to Levi (1 Chronicles 6:39-43).

introduce: Malchiel is the eighth son of Jacob, the grandson of Asher, who was born to Zilpah, the maidservant of Leah, and the son of Beriah. He is the ancestor of the Malchielite family, one of the families of the tribe of Asher.
lifetime: Malchiel was the son of Beriah, the son of Asher, and the brother of Heber (Genesis 46:17). He is recorded among the names of the family of Israel that went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:8, 46:17). Afterward the Malchielite family that descended from him was recorded as one of the families of the tribe of Asher in the census taken by Moses and the priest Eleazar on the plains of Moab (Numbers 26:3, 26:45).
event: Malchiel became the ancestor of the Malchielite family, and this family was named as one of the families of the descendants of Beriah in the census taken on the plains of Moab after the plague (Numbers 26:1-3, 26:45). He is also recorded as a son of Beriah together with Heber, and is mentioned as the father of Birzaith (1 Chronicles 7:31).

introduce: Mahlah is one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who appear in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament, a figure mentioned in the legal case concerning Israel's system of inheriting land.
lifetime: She was born as a daughter of Zelophehad the son of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh, and when her family faced the danger of losing its inheritance after her father died in the wilderness, she came with her sisters before Moses, the priests, and the congregation (Numbers 27:1). Afterward, in accordance with the ruling God gave to Moses, she received her father's portion as an inheritance (Numbers 27:6-7). Also, in accordance with the regulation that they marry within their kin to keep the inheritance from passing to another tribe, she married the sons of her father's brothers (Numbers 36:11).
event: She and her four sisters, claiming the right of inheritance of their father's line, petitioned the leaders of the time, and this led to the precedent that if there is no son, a daughter may inherit her father's estate (Numbers 27:4-7). Afterward she obeyed God's command to marry within the same clan so that the inheritances of the tribes would not be mixed (Numbers 36:10-12).
character: She showed an active attitude, stating her position logically and without fear before the congregation in order to secure the rightful claim of her family (Numbers 27:2). She also showed compliance with the decision that was made, within the prescribed legal framework, to preserve the tribe's inheritance (Numbers 36:11).

introduce: He is known as the author of the book of Malachi, the last of the minor prophets in the Old Testament, and his Hebrew name Malachi has the meaning "my messenger."
lifetime: In Malachi 1:1, with no record about his family or birth, it is recorded only as a warning that the LORD spoke to Israel through Malachi (Malachi 1:1). Because the temple sacrifices (Malachi 1:7-10) and a governor (Malachi 1:8) are mentioned in the book, he is understood to have been active in Judean society after the Babylonian exile.
event: He pointed out and warned against the priests' formal sacrifices and corruption (Malachi 1:6-14). He rebuked the people of Judah for marrying the daughter of a foreign god (Malachi 2:11), and defined the failure to give tithes and offerings as robbing God (Malachi 3:8-9). He also delivered the word of the LORD that he would send the prophet Elijah before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes (Malachi 4:5).
character: He used a firm and direct manner of speech that criticized head-on the spiritual decline of the religious leaders and the people of his day (Malachi 2:1-3). Through the dialectical rhetorical technique of question and answer, he is characterized by logically refuting the false assurance of his audience (Malachi 3:13-15).

직업/직위: last prophet of the Old Testament (author of Malachi)

introduce: Mallothi is a Levite who was active in the time of David, a son of Heman and one of the musicians belonging to the organization of the choir.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the fourteen sons of Heman (1 Chronicles 25:4-5). He belonged to the group that David set apart for service from among the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun (1 Chronicles 25:1, 25:6), and when duties were obtained by casting lots, he was chosen nineteenth (1 Chronicles 25:8, 25:26).
event: He was chosen nineteenth in the casting of lots, and his sons and brothers, twelve in all, were with him (1 Chronicles 25:26). Under the direction of his father Heman, he was a member of the group who took cymbals, harps, and lyres and served by singing in the house of the LORD God (1 Chronicles 25:6).

introduce: He is the son of Elimelech and Naomi, and the husband of Ruth the Moabite woman. The Hebrew name Mahlon is known to mean sickliness or illness.
lifetime: When a famine came in Bethlehem of Judah, he went with his parents and his brother Chilion to the country of Moab and stayed there (Ruth 1:1-2). After his father Elimelech died (Ruth 1:3), he took Ruth, a Moabite woman, as his wife (Ruth 1:4, 4:10), but about ten years after they had lived there, he died together with Chilion (Ruth 1:4-5).
event: About ten years after living in the country of Moab, he died together with his brother Chilion (Ruth 1:4-5). Afterward Boaz bought from the hand of Naomi all that had belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon (Ruth 4:9), and acquired Ruth the Moabite woman, the wife of Mahlon, to be his wife, to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance (Ruth 4:10).

introduce: A descendant of Merari, the son of Levi, he is a figure recorded in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles chapter 6 as the son of Hashabiah and the father of Abdi (1 Chronicles 6:44-45).
lifetime: Malluch was the son of Hashabiah and the father of Abdi (1 Chronicles 6:44-45). Ethan, the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, was his great-grandson, and Ethan, among the group that David put in charge of singing praise in the house of the LORD, served on the left as a descendant of Merari (1 Chronicles 6:31, 6:44).
event: Scripture has no record of Malluch's own duties or events; he appears only in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 6:44-45 as the son of Hashabiah and the father of Abdi. The one who performed the duty of singing praise was his great-grandson Ethan (1 Chronicles 6:44).

call: Chief of praise among the descendants of Asaph
introduce: A great-grandson of Asaph of the tribe of Levi recorded in 1 Chronicles chapter 9, and the son of Mica. He is on the list of the Levites who were carried captive to Babylon and returned to live in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:1-3, 9:15).
lifetime: Mattaniah is recorded as the son of Mica, the grandson of Zichri, and the great-grandson of Asaph (1 Chronicles 9:15).
event: His name is recorded as a Levite together with Bakbakkar, Heresh, and Galal (1 Chronicles 9:15). Nehemiah 11:17 records that Mattaniah, the son of Mica, the son of Zabdi, the great-grandson of Asaph, became the leader who began the thanksgiving in prayer.

introduce: Mattatha is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in the Gospel of Luke in the New Testament. He is recorded as the son of Nathan and the father of Menna (Luke 3:31).
lifetime: Mattatha is the son of Nathan and the father of Menna (Luke 3:31). Apart from that, no record has been handed down about his specific birth or his life as a whole.
event: In the Scriptural record, no separate achievement or particular event related to Mattatha is mentioned (Luke 3:31).

introduce: Mattathias is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in Luke chapter 3, mentioned as a descendant of Nathan the son of David and as the son of Amos (Luke 3:25). In addition, another Mattathias is recorded as the son of Semein, so there are two persons of the same name (Luke 3:26).
lifetime: Mattathias is placed in the genealogy of Jesus as the son of Amos and the father of Joseph (Luke 3:24-25). Amos is the son of Nahum (Luke 3:25). The other Mattathias is recorded as the son of Semein and the father of Maath (Luke 3:26).

call: Ancestor of Jesus Christ (father of Jacob)
introduce: Matthan is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Matthew in the New Testament, recorded as the son of Eleazar and the father of Jacob (Matthew 1:15).
lifetime: Matthan was the son of Eleazar and fathered Jacob (Matthew 1:15). Jacob fathered Joseph, the husband of Mary (Matthew 1:16).
event: In the list of the genealogy of Jesus Christ that runs from Matthew 1:1 through 1:17, Matthan has his name entered as the father of Jacob (Matthew 1:15).

introduce: Matthat is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus recorded in the Gospel of Luke, mentioned as the son of Levi, the grandfather of Joseph, and the father of Heli.
lifetime: Matthat is a figure who continues the genealogy of Jesus, the son of Levi and the father of Heli (Luke 3:23-24).

introduce: Mattattah is a member of the community of Israel that returned from the Babylonian captivity in the time of Ezra. He is recorded as a person belonging to the descendants of Hashum (Ezra 10:33).
lifetime: As a person belonging to the family of Hashum, he lived in the community of Jerusalem after returning from captivity (Ezra 10:33). He is one of those who put their names on the list in the process of resolving the matter of marriage to foreign women, led by Ezra (Ezra 10:33).
event: Mattattah had taken a foreign woman as his wife, and under Ezra's reform measures was singled out as one who had to sever ties with them (Ezra 10:33). He is included in the list, stated in Ezra chapter 10 verse 33, of the men of Israel who had foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:33).

introduce: Mattenai is a figure who appears in the book of Ezra in the Bible, one of the descendants of Hashum.
lifetime: Mattenai is one of those recorded among the descendants of Hashum as having taken foreign women (Ezra 10:33, 10:44). The descendants of Hashum are also recorded in the list of those who returned from the captivity (Ezra 2:19).
event: He is mentioned as one of the sons of Israel who had taken foreign women as wives, and is included in the list of the event that led to the proposal to make a covenant with God to send away all the wives and their children, and to the response of the assembly (Ezra 10:3, 10:12) (Ezra 10:33, 10:44).

introduce: A Levite, the firstborn of Shallum of the descendants of Korah, who was in charge of the work of baking in pans (1 Chronicles 9:31).
lifetime: He is recorded as a Levite, the firstborn of Shallum of the descendants of Korah (1 Chronicles 9:31). It is recorded that the descendants of Korah were in charge of the work of service and guarded the gates of the tabernacle (1 Chronicles 9:19).
event: As a Levite, the firstborn of Shallum of the descendants of Korah, he was in charge of the baking in pans (1 Chronicles 9:31).

introduce: Mattithiah is one of the Levites appointed in the time of David to serve before the ark of the LORD (1 Chronicles 16:4-5).
lifetime: When David appointed Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, to celebrate, to give thanks, and to praise (1 Chronicles 16:4), Mattithiah is among those recorded next after Asaph the chief (1 Chronicles 16:5). The text does not record his father or his family.
event: When David appointed Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, Mattithiah is recorded by name among those who played the harps and lyres (1 Chronicles 16:4-5).

call: Musician who praised before the ark of the covenant (lyre player)
introduce: Mattithiah is one of the brothers who were appointed as singers from among the Levites when David moved the ark of the covenant; he is recorded as one who played the lyre (1 Chronicles 15:16-21).
lifetime: When David commanded the chiefs of the Levites to appoint their brothers as singers, he is one of the brothers appointed next after Heman, Asaph, and Ethan had been appointed (1 Chronicles 15:16-18).
event: Mattithiah, together with Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah, is recorded as one who led by playing the lyre according to the eighth (Sheminith) (1 Chronicles 15:21).
character: Mattithiah was one of the musicians who led with lyres tuned to the eighth note (1 Chronicles 15:21). His personal character is not specifically recorded in the text.

introduce: Matthias is the man chosen by the apostles to take over the duties of Judas Iscariot after Judas betrayed Jesus and died. He is the figure recorded in Scripture as having been added to the number of the eleven apostles (Acts 1:26).
lifetime: It was said that the one to be appointed in place of Judas Iscariot must be chosen from among the men who had accompanied the apostles all the time, from the baptism of John until the day Jesus was taken up (Acts 1:21-22). Matthias was put forward as one of the two candidates (Acts 1:23), and by casting lots he was added to the number of the eleven apostles (Acts 1:26).
event: To appoint someone to take over the apostolic ministry, he was put forward as one of two men, along with Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also surnamed Justus (Acts 1:23). After the assembled company prayed, asking the Lord to show which of the two he had chosen, they cast lots, and Matthias was chosen and added to the number of the eleven apostles (Acts 1:24-26).

introduce: Madmannah is a name that is mentioned in the expression in 1 Chronicles 2:49, in the genealogy of Caleb of the tribe of Judah, which calls Shaaph "the father of Madmannah" (1 Chronicles 2:49).
lifetime: It is recorded that Caleb's concubine Maacah bore Sheber and Tirhanah, and also bore Shaaph the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbenah and Gibea (1 Chronicles 2:48-49). Madmannah's own birth or life is not recorded in the text.
event: Scripture has no record of any deeds or events of Madmannah himself; he appears only in the expression "Shaaph the father of Madmannah" in 1 Chronicles 2:49.

introduce: Massa is a figure who appears in Genesis in the Old Testament, the seventh of the twelve sons of Ishmael. As a grandson of Abraham and a descendant of Ishmael, he is recorded as one of the chiefs of the Ishmaelite tribes.
lifetime: Massa was born to Abraham's son Ishmael (Genesis 25:13). He was born as the seventh of Ishmael's twelve sons (Genesis 25:14).
event: As a son of Ishmael, he was one of the twelve princes of Ishmael, named according to their villages and encampments (Genesis 25:16).

introduce: Medad is one of the seventy elders whom Moses appointed while the people of Israel were passing through the wilderness. Although he did not go out to the tent of meeting, he is recorded as one on whom the Spirit of God rested and who prophesied.
lifetime: Medad, who had remained in the camp of Israel, received the Spirit of God together with Eldad and prophesied in the camp (Numbers 11:26). At that time a young man reported this to Moses (Numbers 11:27), and Joshua the son of Nun, Moses' assistant, asked Moses to stop them, but Moses did not accept this and said he wished that the LORD would put his Spirit on all the people so that all would be prophets (Numbers 11:28-29).
event: When Moses gathered seventy elders and placed them around the tent, the LORD caused the Spirit that was on Moses to rest on the seventy elders also (Numbers 11:24-25), and the Spirit also rested on Eldad and Medad, who were among those listed but had not gone out to the tent and had stayed in the camp, and they prophesied in the camp (Numbers 11:26-27).

introduce: Merab is the eldest daughter of Saul, the first king of Israel, whom Saul said he would give to David as his wife (1 Samuel 14:49, 18:17).
lifetime: Saul said he would give his eldest daughter Merab to David as his wife (1 Samuel 18:17), but when the time came to give Merab to David, he gave her as a wife to Adriel the Meholathite (1 Samuel 18:19). Those born to Merab were the five sons of Adriel, and they were handed over to the Gibeonites and put to death (2 Samuel 21:8-9).
event: Saul told David to be valiant and fight the LORD's battles, and said he would give his eldest daughter Merab to him as his wife (1 Samuel 18:17). But Merab was given to Adriel as a wife (1 Samuel 18:19). Later, the five sons of Adriel born to Merab were handed over to the Gibeonites, together with Saul's two sons Armoni and Mephibosheth, and were hanged before the LORD on the mountain and died (2 Samuel 21:8-9).

introduce: Meres is one of the seven princes mentioned in the time of Xerxes king of Persia. He is recorded as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to the king, saw the king's face, and held the highest positions in the kingdom (Esther 1:14).
lifetime: In the time of Xerxes king of Persia, he is recorded as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to the king, saw the king's face, and held the highest positions in the kingdom (Esther 1:14).
event: When Queen Vashti did not obey the command of King Xerxes, the king asked what should be done with her according to the law (Esther 1:15). The one recorded as having answered in the presence of the king and the princes is Memucan (Esther 1:16), who proposed issuing a decree that Vashti should never again come before the king (Esther 1:16-19). Meres' own statement is not recorded in the text.

introduce: Mered is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah as a son of Ezrah.
lifetime: A descendant of the tribe of Judah and a son of Ezrah, he fathered Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah, the father of Eshtemoa (1 Chronicles 4:17). He also took Bithiah, the daughter of Pharaoh, as his wife, and his wife Jehudijah bore Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah (1 Chronicles 4:18).

call: Son of Shaharaim and Hodesh (chief of Benjamin)
introduce: Mesha is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles chapter 8, a son whom Shaharaim had by his wife Hodesh. He belongs to the genealogical line of the tribe of Benjamin and is classified as one of the children mentioned in the family line of Shaharaim.
lifetime: Mesha is recorded as one of the sons Shaharaim had by his wife Hodesh after he sent away his wives in the land of Moab (1 Chronicles 8:9). No specific information about his life as a whole is found in the Scriptural record.
character: The text of Scripture gives no description whatsoever of Mesha's character or outward features, and mentions him only as a son of Shaharaim whose name is entered in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:9).

introduce: Me-zahab is a figure whose name appears as the grandfather of Mehetabel, the wife of Hadad king of Edom. Mehetabel, the wife of Hadad, is recorded as the daughter of Matred and the granddaughter of Me-zahab (Genesis 36:39, 1 Chronicles 1:50).
lifetime: Scripture does not record any deeds of Me-zahab himself; it gives only the identifying information that Mehetabel, the wife of Hadad king of Edom (Hadad in 1 Chronicles 1:50), was the daughter of Matred and the granddaughter of Me-zahab (Genesis 36:39, 1 Chronicles 1:50).

introduce: Meshach is a figure in the Book of Daniel from the tribe of Judah, one of four wise young men educated in the court of King Nebuchadnezzar during the Babylonian exile. His original Hebrew name was Mishael, and he was renamed with the Babylonian name Meshach.
lifetime: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon invaded, he was taken captive and educated in the royal palace of Babylon (Daniel 1:3-4). The chief of the eunuchs changed his name from Mishael to Meshach (Daniel 1:7). At Daniel's request, the king appointed him to administer the affairs of the province of Babylon (Daniel 2:49). He refused to bow down to the golden image the king had set up and was thrown into the fiery furnace, but he survived (Daniel 3:12-26). Afterward King Nebuchadnezzar promoted him still higher in the province of Babylon (Daniel 3:30).
event: He refused the king's food, choosing vegetables and water instead, and appeared healthier than the other youths (Daniel 1:11-15). He was accused of not bowing down to the golden image Nebuchadnezzar had set up, yet he did not yield in his conviction (Daniel 3:12-18). Because of the king's fury he was thrown into the furnace heated seven times hotter, but he survived unharmed (Daniel 3:19-27). Through this event Nebuchadnezzar came to praise the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego (Daniel 3:28), and the king promoted them still higher in the province of Babylon (Daniel 3:30).
character: He was a man of such firm resolve that he defied the king's command in order to keep his religious practices and convictions (Daniel 3:16-18). Even in hardship he showed a spirit of unity and cooperation with his companions (Daniel 2:17-18). He possessed the intellectual ability to master the learning and wisdom of Babylon (Daniel 1:17-20).

직업/직위: one of the three friends who survived the furnace in Babylon (Mishael)

call: Son of Japheth (ancestor of the northern peoples)
introduce: Meshech is mentioned as the sixth of the seven sons of Japheth, the son of Noah (Genesis 10:2).
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Japheth in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles (Genesis 10:2, 1 Chronicles 1:5). Nothing else about his life is recorded in Scripture.
event: No deeds or events of Meshech as an individual are recorded in Scripture. The "Meshech" in the Book of Ezekiel, who traded with Tyre together with Tubal and Javan (Ezekiel 27:13) and is mentioned as the people or nation of "Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal" ruled by Gog, corresponds to the entry of the same name (3488).

call: Chief in the genealogical list of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:34)
introduce: Meshobab is a man whose name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:34. After the account of the dwelling places and genealogy of the descendants of Simeon, he appears in the list that follows, together with Jamlech and Joshah son of Amaziah (1 Chronicles 4:33-34).
lifetime: In Scripture Meshobab appears only in the list of 1 Chronicles 4:34, and those registered by name in that list are recorded as princes in their families (1 Chronicles 4:34, 4:38). Nothing else about his life is recorded in Scripture.

introduce: Menna is a figure in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Luke, mentioned as a descendant of Nathan the son of David and an ancestor of Jesus.
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Mattatha and the father of Melea (Luke 3:31).

introduce: Melchi is a figure in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Luke, recorded as the son of Jannai and the father of Levi.
lifetime: He was born as the son of Jannai and is the father of Levi (Luke 3:24).

introduce: He is a figure recorded in Scripture as the king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He was active in the land of Canaan in the time of Abraham and is portrayed as one who combined the offices of king and priest.
lifetime: He appears when Abraham, returning after defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings with him, is met by the king of Sodom (Genesis 14:17). He brought out bread and wine to welcome Abraham, and Abraham gave him a tenth of the spoils (Genesis 14:18-20). Later the Letter to the Hebrews notes that there is no record of his lineage or of the beginning or end of his life (Hebrews 7:3).
event: He blessed Abraham and praised God Most High (Genesis 14:19-20). He received a tenth of everything from Abraham (Genesis 14:20). This event is later cited as the basis for discussing a priestly order that precedes the Levitical priesthood (Hebrews 7:6-9).
character: He is portrayed as one without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, resembling the Son of God (Hebrews 7:3). Although he did not belong to the tribe of Levi, he received tithes from Abraham, and, as in the saying "the lesser is blessed by the greater," he was greater than Abraham and pronounced a blessing on him (Hebrews 7:6-7).

introduce: Melea is a figure in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke in the New Testament, a Jewish man mentioned as the son of Menna and the father of Eliakim.
lifetime: He was born as the son of Menna in the genealogy of Jesus recorded by Luke, and he fathered Eliakim (Luke 3:31).

introduce: According to the Scriptural record, Melech was a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, a figure connected with the family line of King Saul. He is recorded as a son of Micah.
lifetime: Merib-baal the son of Jonathan fathered Micah, and Melech is recorded as one of the sons of that Micah (1 Chronicles 8:34-35). In the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin he is classified as a descendant of the house of Saul (1 Chronicles 9:41).
event: No personal achievements or specific events are recorded in Scripture. It is mentioned only that, as a son of Micah, his name appears in the genealogy of the house of Saul (1 Chronicles 8:35, 9:41).

call: Leader of the return under Zerubbabel
meaning: Worshiper of Marduk, a little man
introduce: He was one of the leaders of Israel who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, after the Babylonian exile. He is a different person from the Mordecai who appears in the Book of Esther, and he is recorded in the list of those who returned from the exile.
lifetime: While living in the Babylonian exile, he joined the first group of returnees who came back to Jerusalem by the decree of King Cyrus (Ezra 2:2). He is recorded in the count of the people of Israel, which names him along with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, Baanah, and others (Ezra 2:2). In the parallel list of Nehemiah 7:7 he is recorded along with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, Baanah, and others (Nehemiah 7:7).
event: His name appears in the list recording the count of the people of Israel who came with Zerubbabel and others (Ezra 2:2, Nehemiah 7:7). No other deeds or roles of his are recorded in Scripture.

introduce: He appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah as a son born to Caleb and his concubine Ephah. In 1 Chronicles 2:46 he is recorded, together with Haran and Gazez, as a son born to Caleb's concubine Ephah.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons born to Caleb's concubine Ephah, and no specific record of his life exists beyond that (1 Chronicles 2:46).

introduce: Moses was a leader and lawgiver of ancient Israel who delivered the Hebrews from slavery in Egypt and led them to the border of the land of Canaan. He is regarded as having played the principal role in the accounts of Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy.
lifetime: Born into the tribe of Levi, he was brought up in the Egyptian royal household as the son of a princess (Exodus 2:1-10). After killing an Egyptian who was oppressing his own people, he fled to the land of Midian and tended the flock of Jethro (Exodus 2:11-22, 3:1). When forty years had passed, an angel appeared to him in the flame of a burning bush in the wilderness of Mount Sinai (Acts 7:30); called by God at Mount Horeb, he returned to Egypt and led the people of Israel out in the Exodus (Exodus 3:1-10). He received the law at Mount Sinai and guided the people in the wilderness for forty years (Deuteronomy 8:2); then on the plains of Moab he went up Mount Nebo, looked over the promised land, and died in the land of Moab (Deuteronomy 34:1-5).
event: Before Pharaoh in Egypt he announced the ten plagues and brought about the release of the slaves (Exodus 7–12). Through the parting of the Red Sea he brought the people out (Exodus 14:21-22), and at Mount Sinai he received the law, including the Ten Commandments, delivered it to the people, and oversaw the building of the tabernacle (Exodus 20–40). He also sent twelve spies into Canaan (Numbers 13:1-20), judged the people during the journey through the wilderness (Exodus 18:13), and when he said that he could not bear the burden of the people alone, the LORD had seventy elders share that burden (Numbers 11:14-17).
character: He showed caution in hesitating over the call to leadership, citing his lack of eloquence (Exodus 4:10). Whenever the people rebelled, he showed patience, interceding in prayer for them rather than becoming angry (Numbers 14:13-19). The Scripture describes him as the meekest of all the people on the face of the earth at that time (Numbers 12:3). He is recorded as having remained vigorous and active to an advanced age, his strength unabated (Deuteronomy 34:7).

introduce: Molid is a figure in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, one of the sons whom Abishur, the son of Shammai, fathered by his wife Abihail (1 Chronicles 2:28-29).
lifetime: He came from the family of Jerahmeel, the firstborn son of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2:25). Shammai was born of Onam, the son of Jerahmeel, and Abishur of Shammai (1 Chronicles 2:26, 2:28); and Abishur fathered two sons, Ahban and Molid, by his wife Abihail (1 Chronicles 2:29).

introduce: Meshullam was a member of the tribe of Benjamin and of a family that settled in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (1 Chronicles 9:8).
lifetime: Meshullam was the son of Shephatiah, the grandson of Reuel, and the great-grandson of Ibnijah (1 Chronicles 9:8).
event: Meshullam is recorded as one of the descendants of Benjamin who returned from the Babylonian exile and lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:3, 9:8). His relatives are recorded as heads of their families (1 Chronicles 9:9).

call: Son of Merari (ancestor of the Mushite clan)
introduce: Mushi was a descendant of Levi, the younger of the two sons of Merari the son of Levi (Exodus 6:19). He became the ancestor of the family called the Mushites within the tribe of Levi (Numbers 3:20).
lifetime: Mushi was born as a son of Merari, the grandson of Jacob and son of Levi (Exodus 6:19). He had as sons Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth (1 Chronicles 23:23), and Scripture records his genealogy as a descendant of Levi (1 Chronicles 6:19).
event: Mushi and his brother Mahli were recorded as heads of the Levites in order of age (Exodus 6:19), and the family of Mushi belonged to the family of Merari (Numbers 3:33). The sons of Merari were responsible for the frames, posts, bases, and the posts around the court of the tabernacle (Numbers 3:36-37). In the genealogy of the Levites in the time of David as well, Mahli and Mushi are mentioned as sons of Merari (1 Chronicles 23:21).

introduce: Meshillemoth is a man recorded as the father of Berechiah, one of the leaders of the Ephraimites (2 Chronicles 28:12).
lifetime: In the days of Ahaz king of Judah, when Pekah king of Israel killed many of the people of Judah and took captives to Samaria (2 Chronicles 28:5-8), Meshillemoth's son Berechiah, together with several other leaders of the Ephraimites, stood up and opposed those coming from the war (2 Chronicles 28:12). Nothing is recorded in Scripture about Meshillemoth himself.
event: No event involving Meshillemoth himself is recorded in Scripture. When his son Berechiah, together with Azariah son of Jehohanan, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai, opposed those coming from the war and said that the captives must not be brought in here (2 Chronicles 28:12-13), the armed men left the captives and the plunder before the officials and the whole assembly (2 Chronicles 28:14).

introduce: A man of the tribe of Benjamin, a descendant of Benjamin the son of Jacob, recorded in the genealogy of the house of Benjamin.
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of the sons of Benjamin, and his name is recorded together with Huppim in the list of Genesis 46:21 (Genesis 46:21).
character: Apart from the appearance of his name in the family genealogy as a member of the tribe of Benjamin, Scripture makes no mention of his personal character or any distinctive features (Genesis 46:21). In some translations and manuscripts the spelling of his name appears interchangeably with Shuppim, but this is interpreted not as a characteristic of the person himself but as a result of the development of the genealogical record (1 Chronicles 7:6).

introduce: He was the sixteenth king of the northern kingdom of Israel, the son of Gadi, who reigned in Samaria for ten years (2 Kings 15:17).
lifetime: He went up from Tirzah to Samaria, struck down Shallum, and seized the throne (2 Kings 15:14). During his reign he ruled Israel for ten years while governing Samaria (2 Kings 15:17). When Pul king of Assyria invaded during his reign, he gave him a thousand talents of silver in an attempt to strengthen his hold on the throne (2 Kings 15:19). After his death his son Pekahiah succeeded him as king (2 Kings 15:22).
event: He rebelled at Tirzah, killed Shallum, and took control of the kingship (2 Kings 15:14). To buy off the Assyrian invasion, he forcibly exacted silver from all the wealthy men of Israel and paid it as tribute to Pul king of Assyria (2 Kings 15:20). Coming from Tirzah, he attacked Tiphsah and everyone in it and its vicinity because they would not open their gates, and he committed the cruel act of ripping open the pregnant women in it (2 Kings 15:16).
character: He is recorded as one who did evil and did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam all his days (2 Kings 15:18). To maintain his power he resorted to violent means, and in order to rely on a foreign power he pursued a policy of economically exploiting the people (2 Kings 15:16, 15:20).

call: Firstborn of Joseph (ancestor of the tribe of Manasseh)
introduce: Manasseh was a grandson of Jacob and the elder son whom Joseph had in Egypt. He was born to Joseph and Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On (Genesis 41:50-51), and became the ancestor of the tribe of Manasseh, one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
lifetime: Manasseh was born while Joseph was serving as prime minister of Egypt (Genesis 41:51). After Jacob moved to Egypt, shortly before his death, he claimed as his own the two sons born to Joseph in Egypt, Ephraim and Manasseh (Genesis 48:5). In blessing the two sons, Jacob placed his right hand on the younger son Ephraim and his left hand on the elder son Manasseh, prophesying that Ephraim would be the greater (Genesis 48:14-19). In the census of Numbers the tribe of Manasseh was counted at 32,200 (Numbers 1:35).
event: In the conquest of Canaan the tribe of Manasseh received an inheritance on both the east and the west of the Jordan (Joshua 17:1-6). When their father had no sons, the daughters of Zelophehad, a great-great-grandson of Manasseh, asked Moses for an inheritance (Numbers 27:1-7), and this became a precedent in Israelite inheritance law that daughters can also have the right of inheritance. Also, the judge Gideon was from the tribe of Manasseh (Judges 6:15) and subdued Midian (Judges 8:28).
character: Scripture does not record anything specific about Manasseh's personal character or temperament. However, his name carries the meaning that Joseph had been made to forget all his hardship and all his father's household (Genesis 41:51). At the time of Jacob's blessing, though he was the firstborn, he was assigned a rank lower than Ephraim; yet within the tribal structure of Israel he held a militarily and economically important position (Genesis 48:20, Numbers 26:34).

introduce: Medan is the third of the six sons born to Abraham and his later wife Keturah. In the ancient Israelite genealogy he is classified as a son of Abraham by a secondary wife.
lifetime: He was born as one of the sons Abraham had by taking Keturah as his later wife (Genesis 25:1-2). During his lifetime Abraham gave gifts to his sons by concubines and sent them away eastward from his son Isaac (Genesis 25:6).
event: No personal achievements or specific events directly mentioned are recorded in Scripture. His name appears only in the lists of the sons of Keturah in Genesis 25:2 and 1 Chronicles 1:32.

introduce: Methuselah is a figure in the Book of Genesis, the son of Enoch in the line of Seth and the grandfather of Noah. He is known as the person recorded in Scripture to have lived the longest life.
lifetime: Methuselah was the son whom Enoch fathered at the age of 65 (Genesis 5:21). He fathered Lamech at the age of 187 (Genesis 5:25), and after fathering Lamech he lived 782 years and had other children, and he died having lived a total of 969 years (Genesis 5:26-27).
event: His lifespan overlaps the era before Noah's flood, and the figure of 969 years remains the longest recorded human lifespan in Scripture (Genesis 5:27).
character: The biblical text contains no direct description of his personal character or specific traits. Nothing is said about him other than that he was a person who inherited the lineage of Seth within the genealogical system that began with Adam (Genesis 5:21-27).

introduce: A descendant of Cain recorded in Genesis, the son of Mehujael and the father of Lamech.
lifetime: Methusael was born as the son of Mehujael, the son of Irad (Genesis 4:18). He fathered Lamech, who afterward took Adah and Zillah as wives and fathered Jabal, Jubal, Tubal-cain, and others (Genesis 4:18-22).
event: There is no information in Scripture about any specific achievement or special event of his. However, within the genealogy of Cain he occupies the position of the fourth-generation descendant and served as a link between generations (Genesis 4:18).

introduce: Merari was a son of Levi, recorded as the youngest of the three sons of Levi along with Gershon and Kohath (Exodus 6:16). From him came the family of Mahli and the family of Mushi (Numbers 3:33).
lifetime: He was one of those who went down with the family of Jacob when they went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:8, 46:11). He had two sons, Mahli and Mushi (Exodus 6:19), and through them the genealogy of the clans of the descendants of Merari was formed (Numbers 3:20).
event: In the transport of the tabernacle, the descendants of Merari were assigned the duty of caring for and carrying the frames of the tabernacle and its crossbars, the posts and bases, as well as the posts of the court of the tabernacle with their bases, tent pegs, and cords (Numbers 3:36-37). When a census was taken in the wilderness of Sinai, the males of the descendants of Merari from a month old and upward totaled 6,200 (Numbers 3:34). Also, in the time of David, Ethan, one of the descendants of Merari, performed the service of singing on the left (1 Chronicles 6:44), and the Korahites and the descendants of Merari were included in the divisions of the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:19).

introduce: Meraiah was a head of the priests in the days of Joiakim, belonging to the house of Seraiah (Nehemiah 12:12).
lifetime: Meraiah is recorded as the head of the priestly family of Seraiah in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12). Nothing else about his life is recorded in Scripture.
event: Meraiah's name is recorded as the head of the house of Seraiah in the list of the heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12). No other personal achievements are recorded in Scripture.

introduce: Meraioth is a man recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6, appearing in the line of Eleazar as the son of Zerahiah and the father of Amariah (1 Chronicles 6:4-7). This genealogy continues through Ahitub to Zadok (1 Chronicles 6:7-8).
lifetime: Meraioth was the son of Zerahiah and the father of Amariah (1 Chronicles 6:6-7). His son Amariah fathered Ahitub, and Ahitub fathered Zadok (1 Chronicles 6:7-8). This sequence is recorded in the same way in 1 Chronicles 6:50-53 as well.
event: Meraioth's name is recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Aaron from Eleazar to Zadok, and apart from what appears in the genealogy, no personal deeds of his are recorded in Scripture (1 Chronicles 6:6-7, 1 Chronicles 6:52).

call: Son of the priest Uriah (counter of the vessels of the temple / repairer of the wall)
introduce: Meremoth is a figure in the Old Testament books of Ezra and Nehemiah, the son of the priest Uriah. He is recorded as one who, after the return from the Babylonian exile, performed the practical duties of managing the vessels of the temple and repairing the wall of Jerusalem.
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of the priest Uriah (Ezra 8:33). When Ezra's company reached Jerusalem and stayed three days, on the day of the offering the silver, the gold, and the vessels were weighed in the house of God and put into his hand (Ezra 8:32-33). At the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem, Meremoth son of Uriah, the grandson of Hakkoz, repaired a section (Nehemiah 3:21).
event: The silver, the gold, and the vessels brought by Ezra's company were weighed in the house of God and put into the hand of Meremoth son of the priest Uriah, and all of it was counted and weighed, and its weight was written down at that time (Ezra 8:33-34). Also, in the work of repairing the wall of Jerusalem, Meremoth son of Uriah, the grandson of Hakkoz, repaired a section from the door of the house of Eliashib to the end of the house of Eliashib (Nehemiah 3:21). In Nehemiah 3:4 also, Meremoth son of Uriah, the grandson of Hakkoz, is recorded as having made repairs.

introduce: Merodach-baladan was a king of Babylon who sent a letter and a gift to Hezekiah king of Judah. Scripture records him as the son of Baladan and king of Babylon (Isaiah 39:1).
lifetime: He was the son of Baladan and king of Babylon (Isaiah 39:1). When he heard that Hezekiah king of Judah had been sick and had recovered, he sent a letter and a gift to Hezekiah (Isaiah 39:1, 2 Kings 20:12). Hezekiah was pleased with the envoys he sent and showed them his treasure house and all that was in his realm (Isaiah 39:2).
event: When he heard that Hezekiah had been sick and had recovered, he sent a letter and a gift (Isaiah 39:1). Hezekiah was pleased with the envoys and showed them everything in his palace and throughout his realm: the silver and gold, the spices and precious oil, and what was in his armory and treasuries (Isaiah 39:2). The text gives no record of the purpose for which Merodach-baladan sent the letter and gift.
character: His personal character is not directly described in Scripture, but he showed diplomatic skill, actively engaging with the neighboring kingdom of Judah in order to stand against the dominance of Assyria at that time (2 Kings 20:12). He appears as a ruler with a strategic side, confirming Hezekiah's standing and gathering information for the sake of his own country's interests (Isaiah 39:2).

introduce: Memucan was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to the king in the time of Xerxes king of Persia and sat first in the kingdom (Esther 1:14). He is recorded as the one who answered before the king and the princes concerning the matter of Queen Vashti (Esther 1:16).
lifetime: During the reign of Xerxes king of Persia, he was one of the seven princes who had access to the king and sat first in the kingdom (Esther 1:14). When Queen Vashti did not obey the king's command and the king asked how she should be dealt with, he answered before the king and the princes (Esther 1:15-16).
event: After Queen Vashti's act of disobedience, before the king and the princes he proposed that a decree be issued that Vashti should never again come before the king, and that her royal position be given to one better than she (Esther 1:16-19). He also said that when the decree was proclaimed throughout the kingdom, all women, high and low alike, would honor their husbands (Esther 1:20). The king and the princes were pleased with his word, and the king did as Memucan proposed (Esther 1:21).
character: As a wise official well versed in the king's law and judgment, he had a cool and logical mind (Esther 1:13-15). He showed a realistic and systematic judgment, fearing that the queen's conduct would have a bad influence on all women and undermine order throughout the whole kingdom (Esther 1:16-18).

기타관계: Tarshish#3345(fellow of the seven princes of Persia)

introduce: Mebunnai is one of the Thirty, the elite group of warriors of King David recorded in Scripture. He is known as a Hushathite and served in David's military organization.
lifetime: He was a Hushathite and his name is on the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:27).
event: His name is recorded in the list of the Thirty among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:24-27). Scripture does not describe any specific battle record or individual exploit of his.

introduce: Mephibosheth was the son of Jonathan, the son of King Saul, and thus Saul's grandson. In the time of the Davidic dynasty he was treated with honor as a descendant of the house of Saul.
lifetime: When he was five years old and the news that Saul and Jonathan had died came from Jezreel, his nurse picked him up and fled in haste, and he fell and became lame (2 Samuel 4:4). Afterward he stayed in the house of Machir son of Ammiel at Lo-debar, and when called by David he came to David (2 Samuel 9:4-6). For Jonathan's sake David showed him kindness, restored to him all the fields of Saul, and let him always eat at his table, and he lived in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 9:1, 9:7-13). At the time of Absalom's rebellion he incurred David's misunderstanding through the words of his servant Ziba, but when David returned he explained his circumstances to him (2 Samuel 16:1-4, 2 Samuel 19:24-30).
event: Because of the kindness David showed for Jonathan's sake, he ate at the king's table in Jerusalem like one of the king's sons (2 Samuel 9:10-13). At the time of Absalom's rebellion, David listened to Ziba and gave Ziba everything that belonged to Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 16:3-4); but after David returned, the king asked why he had not gone with him, and when the king told him to divide the fields with Ziba, Mephibosheth said, "Let him take it all, since my lord the king has come home safely to his palace" (2 Samuel 19:25-30). When the Gibeonites asked for the descendants of Saul to be handed over, David spared Mephibosheth because of the oath he had made with Jonathan by the LORD (2 Samuel 21:6-7).
character: He described himself as a dead dog and showed the utmost humility and lowliness before David (2 Samuel 9:8). Until David returned from his flight, he did not wash his feet, trim his beard, or wash his clothes, expressing mourning and loyalty (2 Samuel 19:24). Rather than political ambition, he showed a disposition to respect the king's authority and to accept the situation given to him (2 Samuel 19:30).

call: Grandfather of Meshullam, repairer of the wall
introduce: Meshezabel is a figure in the Book of Nehemiah in the Old Testament, the one of whom Berechiah is introduced in Nehemiah 3:4 as "the grandson of Meshezabel." Meshullam, the repairer of the wall, is the son of that Berechiah.
lifetime: He is mentioned in the genealogy of Meshullam, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah. The text records Berechiah as the grandson of Meshezabel and Meshullam as the son of that Berechiah (Nehemiah 3:4).
event: There is no record that he himself took part in the work of repairing the wall; his grandson Berechiah's son Meshullam repaired a section of the wall (Nehemiah 3:4).

introduce: A member of the Korahites of the tribe of Levi, he served as a gatekeeper of the temple in the time of David. He belonged to the house of Asaph among the Korahites and held an important role in the security duties of the temple.
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Kore, of the descendants of Asaph of the Korahite clan (1 Chronicles 26:1). In the casting of lots to determine the divisions of the gatekeepers in the time of David, Shelemiah drew the east, and his son Zechariah drew the north (1 Chronicles 26:14). He had seven sons, including his firstborn Zechariah (1 Chronicles 26:2-3).
event: In the casting of lots to determine the divisions of the gatekeepers, he drew the east (1 Chronicles 26:14). Also his sons and brothers, eighteen in all, were capable men (1 Chronicles 26:9).
character: He is regarded as a man who produced capable men among the members of his family (1 Chronicles 26:9). He is also recorded as having accepted his turn fairly in the casting of lots in order to carry out the duty of gatekeeper of the temple (1 Chronicles 26:14).

introduce: Meshullam is a man recorded as an ancestor of Shaphan the scribe in the time of Josiah king of Judah. The text introduces Shaphan as "the son of Azaliah, the grandson of Meshullam" (2 Kings 22:3).
lifetime: In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, in the passage where the king sends the scribe Shaphan to the house of the LORD, Shaphan is introduced as the son of Azaliah, the grandson of Meshullam, and thus his name appears (2 Kings 22:3). Nothing else about his life is recorded in Scripture.
event: Meshullam is mentioned by name only, as an ancestor of the scribe Shaphan who was sent to the house of the LORD in the eighteenth year of King Josiah (2 Kings 22:3). There is no record in Scripture that he took part directly in the repair of the temple or achieved anything special.

introduce: Meshullemeth is the mother of Amon king of Judah. She is recorded as the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah (2 Kings 21:19).
lifetime: Meshullemeth is the mother of Amon, the son of Manasseh (2 Kings 21:18-19). She was the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah, and her son Amon became king at the age of twenty-two and reigned in Jerusalem two years (2 Kings 21:19).
event: No political achievement or specific event of Meshullemeth's own is recorded in Scripture. She is mentioned by name only as the mother of Amon king of Judah (2 Kings 21:19).

introduce: Meshillemoth is a man of a priestly family who appears in the Book of Nehemiah in the Old Testament, recorded as the great-grandfather of Amashai.
lifetime: Meshillemoth is an ancestor mentioned in Nehemiah 11:13 where Amashai is introduced as "the son of Azarel, the grandson of Ahzai, the great-grandson of Meshillemoth, and the great-great-grandson of Immer" (Nehemiah 11:13). The same verse also introduces Amashai as a great-great-grandson of Immer.
event: His name is recorded as an ancestor of Amashai in the list of the priests who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 11:10-13). No other personal deeds of his are recorded in Scripture.

introduce: Meshillemith is a man recorded in the priestly list in 1 Chronicles 9 as an ancestor of Maasai. Maasai is introduced as his great-great-grandson and a fifth-generation descendant of Immer (1 Chronicles 9:12).
lifetime: Meshillemith is an ancestor mentioned in 1 Chronicles 9:12 where Maasai is introduced as "the son of Adiel, the grandson of Jahzerah, the great-grandson of Meshullam, the great-great-grandson of Meshillemith, and the fifth-generation descendant of Immer" (1 Chronicles 9:12). Nothing else about his life is recorded in Scripture.
event: His name is recorded as an ancestor of Maasai in the list of the priests who returned from Babylon and lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:1-3, 9:10-12). No other personal deeds of his are recorded in Scripture.

introduce: Meonothai is a man who appears in 1 Chronicles 4, the genealogy of the descendants of Judah, and is recorded as the father of Ophrah (1 Chronicles 4:14).
lifetime: He appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Judah in 1 Chronicles 4 and fathered Ophrah (1 Chronicles 4:14). Who his father was is not recorded in this verse.
event: He is recorded as the father of Ophrah, and nothing else of his deeds appears in Scripture (1 Chronicles 4:14).

introduce: Meunim is the name of a family of the Nethinim who appear in the lists of returnees in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah in the Old Testament.
lifetime: In the list of the people of Israel who returned from Babylon and came with Zerubbabel, it is recorded as "the descendants of Meunim" among the Nethinim (Ezra 2:2, 2:43, 2:50).
event: Its name is registered as "the descendants of Meunim" in the list of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:50, Nehemiah 7:52). No other personal deeds are recorded in Scripture.

call: Wife of Hadad king of Edom
introduce: Mehetabel was the wife of Hadad king of Edom, recorded as the daughter of Matred and the granddaughter of Me-zahab.
lifetime: She appears in the historical genealogy as the wife of Hadad king of Edom (Genesis 36:39). The family line of her father Matred and her grandfather Me-zahab is stated in Scripture (1 Chronicles 1:50).

introduce: Mehuman is one of the seven eunuchs who served in the presence of Xerxes king of Persia (Esther 1:10).
lifetime: He appears as one of the seven eunuchs in attendance whom Xerxes king of Persia commanded to summon Queen Vashti, before the king deposed her (Esther 1:10).
event: He is recorded as one of the seven eunuchs whom the king, merry with wine, commanded to bring Queen Vashti before the king wearing her royal crown, to show her beauty to the peoples and the princes (Esther 1:10-11). Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command delivered by the eunuchs (Esther 1:12).

introduce: Mehujael is a figure in the Book of Genesis, a descendant of Cain, the son of Irad and the father of Methusael.
lifetime: He appears in the genealogy of Cain, was born of Irad, and fathered his son Methusael (Genesis 4:18). He stands in the middle generation of the genealogy from Cain down to Lamech (Genesis 4:17-18).
event: There is no mention in Scripture of any specific achievement or special event of his (Genesis 4:18).

introduce: Mehida is a name recorded as "the descendants of Mehida" among the Nethinim in the lists of returnees from the exile in Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7. Scripture reveals almost nothing of his specific deeds or social standing.
lifetime: He is recorded as "the descendants of Mehida" among the Nethinim in the list of the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:52, Nehemiah 7:54).
event: His name is registered as "the descendants of Mehida" in the list of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:52, Nehemiah 7:54). No other personal deeds are recorded in Scripture.

introduce: Mehir was a descendant of the tribe of Judah, a man who appears in 1 Chronicles 4:11. He is recorded as the son of Chelub and the father of Eshton.
lifetime: Mehir is recorded as the son born to Chelub, the brother of Shuhah, and is the father of Eshton (1 Chronicles 4:11). He is mentioned within the genealogy of the descendants of Judah, but no specific life span or period of activity beyond that appears in the biblical record (1 Chronicles 4:11).
event: No special historical event or achievement that Mehir led or was involved in is recorded in Scripture (1 Chronicles 4:11).

introduce: Melatiah is recorded as a Gibeonite, one of the people mobilized in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:7).
lifetime: When the wall of Jerusalem was repaired after the return from the Babylonian exile, he took part in the wall work together with the men of Gibeon (Nehemiah 3:7).
event: In the work on the wall of Jerusalem, Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite, together with the men of Gibeon and of Mizpah, who were under the jurisdiction of the governor west of the River, repaired a section (Nehemiah 3:7).

call: Man of Ephraim (maker of an idol)
introduce: He was a man who lived in the hill country of Ephraim, who set up a private shrine in his own house and made and operated religious images. His story is recorded in Judges 17 and 18 and is cited as a representative example of the religious confusion of the time of the judges.
lifetime: After hearing his mother's words of cursing, he confessed that he had taken the 1,100 shekels of silver she had lost, and returned the silver to his mother (Judges 17:2-3). His mother gave two hundred shekels of the silver to a silversmith to carve and cast an image, and that image was in Micah's house (Judges 17:4). Living in the hill country of Ephraim, he made an ephod and household idols and made one of his sons a priest (Judges 17:5). Later he met a young Levite and hired him as his personal priest (Judges 17:10-12). Spies of the tribe of Dan visited his house (Judges 18:2), and later, when the tribe of Dan moved to capture Laish, they took away Micah's image and his priest (Judges 18:17-20). Micah tried to recover his property but failed because of the difference in strength and returned home (Judges 18:23-26).
event: Micah had a shrine, and he made an ephod and household idols and appointed one of his sons as priest (Judges 17:5). He consecrated the Levite from Bethlehem and installed him as his own priest (Judges 17:12). In the course of the migration of the tribe of Dan, his image and priest were taken from him (Judges 18:18-20). As a result, the tribe of Dan set up Micah's image for themselves (Judges 18:30-31).
character: Fearing the curse his mother had pronounced, he showed a cautious and fearful disposition in returning the stolen silver (Judges 17:2). By making a religious image and appointing a private priest, he pursued a self-centered religious practice rather than the orthodox system of faith of the time (Judges 17:5). When the tribe of Dan took his image, he pursued them and tried to get it back, but he showed a realistic side in recognizing his own weakness before a group with overwhelming force and withdrawing (Judges 18:23-26).

introduce: Micaiah son of Imlah was a prophet who was active in the time of Ahab king of northern Israel, who opposed the many false prophets and delivered the true word of the LORD.
lifetime: Before Jehoshaphat king of Judah took part in the war at Ramoth-gilead at Ahab's request, Ahab gathered four hundred prophets and had them prophesy victory, but at Jehoshaphat's demand Micaiah was summoned (1 Kings 22:6-9). On the way to being summoned, he was urged by the messenger to speak in accord with the king's wishes, but he answered that he would declare only what the LORD said (1 Kings 22:13-14). After finishing his prophecy in the presence of Ahab, he was struck on the cheek by Zedekiah, and by Ahab's order he was put in prison and made to eat the bread of affliction and drink the water of affliction (1 Kings 22:24-27).
event: As the false prophets were confident of victory in the run-up to the war at Ramoth-gilead, Micaiah prophesied that the people of Israel would be scattered on the mountains like sheep without a shepherd, foretelling Ahab's death in battle (1 Kings 22:17). He also related that he had seen the council of the LORD in a vision, and testified that a spirit seeking to entice Ahab to his death had become a lying spirit and entered the mouths of all the prophets (1 Kings 22:19-23). He declared that if what he had spoken did not come to pass, the LORD had not spoken through him, thus expressing his confidence in his prophecy (1 Kings 22:28).
character: Even amid the threatening situation of the many and the pressure of the king, he did not yield, and he had an upright character that honestly delivered only the word he had received from God (1 Kings 22:14). Before the powerful who persecuted him, he showed a resoluteness that did not back down, maintaining that his prophecy would surely be fulfilled (1 Kings 22:28).

call: Father of Sethur (father of a spy)
meaning: Who is a man like God?
introduce: He is a man mentioned in Scripture as the father of Sethur, a spy of the tribe of Asher recorded in Numbers 13.
lifetime: He is mentioned as a man of the tribe of Asher, and apart from the fact that his son Sethur served as one of the twelve spies chosen to explore the land of Canaan, there is no record whatever about his life (Numbers 13:13).
event: His son Sethur, as a chief of the tribe of Asher, is recorded among the men whom Moses sent to explore the land of Canaan at the command of the LORD (Numbers 13:2-3, 13:13). Nothing about Michael's own deeds is recorded in Scripture.

introduce: Michal was the second daughter of Saul, the first king of Israel, and the first wife of David. She is a figure who symbolizes the political conflict and union between the house of Saul and the house of David, and her record remains in the Old Testament books of 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel.
lifetime: Michal, the daughter of King Saul, fell in love with David and became his wife (1 Samuel 18:20, 27). Later, when Saul tried to kill David, she let David escape through a window and gained time by placing an idol in the bed (1 Samuel 19:12-13). After David fled, Saul gave Michal to Palti son of Laish, who lived in Gallim (1 Samuel 25:44). After David became king, he demanded that Saul's son Ish-bosheth bring Michal back, and he got her back (2 Samuel 3:13-15). Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death (2 Samuel 6:23).
event: Saul gave his daughter Michal to David as a wife, intending that she be a snare to him and that he be struck down by the hand of the Philistines (1 Samuel 18:21, 27). When David was threatened with murder by Saul, she let him down through a window and saved his life (1 Samuel 19:11-12). When she saw David dancing as he brought the ark of God to Jerusalem, she despised him in her heart (2 Samuel 6:16). When David returned to bless his household, she went out to meet him and said sarcastically that he had shamelessly uncovered himself like one of the vulgar fellows (2 Samuel 6:20), and she had no child to the day of her death (2 Samuel 6:23).
character: She loved David sincerely (1 Samuel 18:20), but she was torn between her father Saul's political aims and her pride as a member of the royal house. She valued formality and dignity so highly that she regarded David's dancing in a linen ephod as frivolous behavior unbecoming of a king (2 Samuel 6:20). Her life reflects the tragic fate, and the psychological change that came with it, that she suffered as power passed from the house of Saul to the house of David.

직업/직위: daughter of King Saul (David's first wife / princess)

introduce: Michri is a man who appears as an ancestor in the genealogy of Elah (Elah the son of Uzzi, the grandson of Michri) in the list of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem in 1 Chronicles 9.
lifetime: Michri appears only as an ancestor in the genealogical expression in 1 Chronicles 9:8, "Elah the son of Uzzi, the grandson of Michri." Ibneiah the son of Jeroham in the same verse is a separately listed person and is not recorded as the father of Michri. This list records the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:3, 8).
event: The biblical text describes no specific achievement or particular event of Michri; his name appears only within the genealogy of Elah in the list of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:8).

introduce: Mikloth is a figure in the Chronicles of the Old Testament, recorded as one of the sons of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon of the tribe of Benjamin.
