lifetime: Shamsherai is recorded, together with Shehariah, Athaliah, Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri, as one of the sons of Jeroham (1 Chronicles 8:26-27). It is recorded that they were all heads of families, chiefs throughout their generations, and that they dwelt in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).

introduce: Shammah is a person recorded as one of the 37 mighty men of David, the military organization of King David. He is classified as a Harodite and served as a member of David's elite troops (2 Samuel 23:25, 1 Chronicles 11:27).
lifetime: Shammah the Harodite appears by name in the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:25, 1 Chronicles 11:27). In 1 Chronicles 27:8, Shammah the Izrahite is recorded as the fifth commander for the fifth month, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand men (1 Chronicles 27:8).
event: In the time of King David he was the fifth commander in the division of the fifth month and was in charge of a division of twenty-four thousand men (1 Chronicles 27:8). His name is also listed in the roll of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:25, 1 Chronicles 11:27).

introduce: Sabtah is one of the descendants of Noah recorded in Genesis 10 and 1 Chronicles 1, a son of Cush the son of Ham, listed in Genesis 10:7.
lifetime: He is mentioned as a son of Cush, and in the same verse Seba, Havilah, Raamah, and Sabteca are recorded together with him as sons of Cush (Genesis 10:7). The record of Chronicles likewise records him as a son of Cush (1 Chronicles 1:9).

introduce: Sabteca is a person recorded in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a grandson of Ham and a son of Cush (Genesis 10:7).
lifetime:
He was born to Cush, a son of Ham (Genesis 10:6-7).
His brothers were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, and Raamah (1 Chronicles 1:9).
No further record of specific deeds, place of residence, or death after his birth appears in the Bible (Genesis 10:7).

introduce: Zabdi was a man of the tribe of Judah, a son of Zerah, the grandfather of Achan, and the father of Carmi. In the biblical record he appears mainly as a person who continues the family genealogy.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Zerah of the tribe of Judah (Joshua 7:1). As the grandfather of Achan and the father of Carmi, he formed a family line (Joshua 7:18).
event: In Joshua 7, in the process of casting lots to find Achan, who after the battle at the city of Jericho had stolen things devoted to the LORD, his clan, the Zerahites, was singled out (Joshua 7:17). In that process the household of Zabdi was taken, and he is mentioned in the genealogical path by which Zabdi's grandson Achan was finally revealed as the culprit (Joshua 7:18).

call: Father of Jashobeam (father of a military commander)
introduce: Zabdiel is a person recorded as the father of Jashobeam, who served as the commander of the first division in David's military organization. In the Bible he is mentioned mainly in the context of genealogical information that identifies his son's status.
lifetime: The Bible records nothing about Zabdiel's personal life; his existence is confirmed only through the fact that his son Jashobeam served as one of the military commanders in the time of King David (1 Chronicles 27:2).

introduce: Zabbai is a person who appears in Ezra and Nehemiah in the Old Testament; he is recorded in Ezra 10:28 as one of the descendants of Bebai, and in Nehemiah 3:20 he appears as the father of Baruch, who repaired a section of the wall (Ezra 10:28, Nehemiah 3:20).
lifetime: He is recorded among the descendants of Bebai in the list of those who took foreign women as wives in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:28, 10:44). Nehemiah 3:20 records that Zabbai's son Baruch diligently repaired a section of the wall, and in this verse no deed of Zabbai himself is recorded.
event: His name appears among the descendants of Bebai in the list of those who took foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:28, 10:44). His son Baruch diligently repaired a section from the angle of the wall to the doorway of the house of Eliashib the high priest (Nehemiah 3:20).

introduce: Shabbethai is a Levite who appears in Ezra 10 and Nehemiah 11. He is a person recorded together with Meshullam in Ezra 10:15, when the matter of marriage to foreign women was being dealt with.
lifetime: He is a Levite whose name appears in Ezra 10:15, and in Nehemiah 11:16 as well, Shabbethai, a leader of the Levites, is recorded together with Jozabad.
event: Ezra 10:15 records that Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah rose up to oppose that matter, and that Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them (Ezra 10:15). Nehemiah 11:16 records that Shabbethai and Jozabad, leaders of the Levites, were in charge of the outside work of the house of God (Nehemiah 11:16).

introduce: She appears in the time of the early Jerusalem church; she was the wife of Ananias and one of the parties to the incident of selling their property and laying it at the feet of the apostles.
lifetime: Together with Ananias, she sold their property, kept back part of the price, and brought only the rest to the apostles (Acts 5:1-2). Not knowing that her husband had died first, she appeared before Peter, and when asked whether this was the price of the land, she answered that it was (Acts 5:7-8). Immediately after being singled out by Peter she died on the spot, and the people carried her out and buried her (Acts 5:9-10).
event: In conspiracy with her husband, she hid part of the property and deceived the apostles by presenting it as if she had given all of it (Acts 5:2). Under Peter's questioning she gave false testimony, and as a result she met her death just as Peter had foretold (Acts 5:8-10). The people who heard of this incident and the members of the church were seized with great fear (Acts 5:11).
character: She planned to dispose of her property and give it to the church, but she had the intention of concealing part of the financial gain (Acts 5:2). She actively took part in her husband's crime, and showed a deceptive attitude, answering the apostle's question by distorting the facts (Acts 5:8-9).

직업/직위: believer in the early Jerusalem church

introduce: Zattu is a name recorded in the list under the title "descendants of Zattu" among the people of Israel who ended their life in exile in Babylon and returned to Jerusalem. The descendants of Zattu appear in the list of returnees (Ezra 2:8, Nehemiah 7:13), in the list of the matter of the foreign women (Ezra 10:27), and in the list of the heads of the people who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:14).
lifetime: He is mentioned as the ancestor of the descendants of Zattu, one of the families of returnees who came back from Babylon to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:8). Later, in the time of Ezra, some of the descendants of Zattu were included in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:27). The number of the descendants of Zattu recorded in the list of returnees is given differently in the two lists: nine hundred forty-five in Ezra 2:8 and eight hundred forty-five in Nehemiah 7:13. Zattu's name appears again in the list of the heads of the people among those who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:14).
event: The descendants of Zattu are recorded in the list of returnees as nine hundred forty-five in Ezra 2:8 and eight hundred forty-five in Nehemiah 7:13. In Ezra 10:27, Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza, of the descendants of Zattu, are entered in the list of those who took foreign women. In Nehemiah 10:14, Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani, and others are recorded as the heads of the people among those who sealed the covenant.

introduce: Sergius Paulus is the proconsul of the island of Cyprus who appears in Acts 13. He is recorded as a man of intelligence who summoned Barnabas and Saul at Paphos and wished to hear the word of God (Acts 13:7).
lifetime: He was proconsul at Paphos on the island of Cyprus (Acts 13:6-7), and as a man of intelligence he summoned Barnabas and Saul and wished to hear the word of God (Acts 13:7). When Paul fixed his gaze on Elymas and rebuked him, he saw him become blind, and believed (Acts 13:11-12).
event: At Paphos he was together with the Jewish false prophet and sorcerer Bar-Jesus (Elymas) (Acts 13:6-7). When Elymas opposed Barnabas and Saul and tried to keep the proconsul from believing (Acts 13:8), Saul, who is also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fixed his gaze on him and rebuked him, saying that the hand of the Lord was upon him and that he would be blind and not see the sun for a time, and immediately a mist and darkness fell upon him (Acts 13:9-11). When the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord (Acts 13:12).
character: The Bible explicitly says that he was a man of intelligence (Acts 13:7). Without relying only on the existing sorcerers and religious figures, he is portrayed as a person who showed curiosity toward the new teaching, Paul's gospel, and who had intellectual inquisitiveness and objective judgment (Acts 13:7).

introduce: Semein is a person who appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in Luke 3, recorded as the son of Josech and the father of Mattathias (Luke 3:26).
lifetime: In the genealogy of Luke 3:26, Semein is placed as the son of Josech and the father of Mattathias (Luke 3:26). As for specific dates of his life or the region of his activity, the Bible makes no mention (Luke 3:26).

introduce: Zecher is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the sons of Jeiel, the father of Gibeon (1 Chronicles 8:29-31).
lifetime: Zecher is recorded as a son of Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, together with Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab, Gedor, and Ahio (1 Chronicles 8:29-31). Jeiel lived in Gibeon (1 Chronicles 8:29). The Bible has no record of Zecher's personal life.
event: His name is recorded as one of the sons of Jeiel (1 Chronicles 8:31). It is recorded that this group lived in Jerusalem opposite their relatives (1 Chronicles 8:32).

call: Son of Hamor (chief of the Hivites)
introduce: Shechem was the son of Hamor, of the Hivite clan that ruled the region of Shechem in the land of Canaan, and was a person who acted as chief of that region at the time.
lifetime: When Jacob's daughter Dinah went out to see the women of the land, he saw her, took her, raped her, and defiled her (Genesis 34:1-2). He was deeply drawn to Dinah and loved her (Genesis 34:3), and asked his father Hamor to get this girl for him as his wife (Genesis 34:4). When the sons of Jacob set circumcision as a condition, he agreed, and he and all the males of his city were circumcised (Genesis 34:15-24). On the third day after the circumcision, while they were in pain, he was attacked by surprise by Simeon and Levi and was put to death by the edge of the sword (Genesis 34:25-26).
event: Hamor proposed to Jacob's family intermarriage, living together, and trading (Genesis 34:9-10), and Shechem also told Dinah's father and brothers that he would give whatever they asked, if only he might find favor in their eyes (Genesis 34:11). He is recorded as the most honored of all his father's house (Genesis 34:19). Together with Hamor he spoke to the men of their city at the city gate (Genesis 34:20-23), and all who went out of the gate of the city listened to Hamor and Shechem and were circumcised (Genesis 34:24). His raping of Dinah became the reason the sons of Jacob were greatly angered (Genesis 34:7), and the cause of Simeon and Levi killing all the males of the city and of Jacob's other sons plundering the city (Genesis 34:25-29).
character: He showed strong attachment to Dinah and displayed an impulsive side, sparing no means or methods to satisfy his own desire (Genesis 34:3). He had more influence than his father Hamor and was a man with the power to persuade the whole tribe in order to carry out his will (Genesis 34:19). He was strongly obsessed with obtaining what he wanted even at a cost, and as a result brought his own people into danger (Genesis 34:11-12, 34:24-26).

introduce: Zenas is a person who appears in the epistle to Titus in the New Testament; he is mentioned in the letter the apostle Paul sent to Titus, and the Korean Revised Version calls him "the lawyer" (Titus 3:13).
lifetime: Zenas is a person mentioned together with Apollos in the letter the apostle Paul sent to Titus, who was staying in Crete (Titus 3:13). Paul instructed Titus to send them on their way, supplying everything they needed so that they would lack nothing for their journey (Titus 3:13).
event: Zenas is mentioned as one who was to be sent on ahead quickly together with Apollos, and Paul asked Titus for practical support so that their journey might go smoothly (Titus 3:13). There is no record in the Bible of what ministry Zenas specifically performed.

introduce: Shenazzar is a person belonging to the royal genealogy of Judah in the period of the Babylonian exile, recorded as one of the sons of King Jeconiah (1 Chronicles 3:18).
lifetime: Shenazzar is recorded, in the list of the sons of Jeconiah who was taken captive, after Malchiram and Pedaiah, and his name is entered in the genealogy as a descendant of Jeconiah of the royal house of Judah (1 Chronicles 3:17-18).

introduce: Zethan is a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:10. He is a son of Bilhan, and Bilhan is a son of Jediael; he is mentioned as a member within the genealogical system of the house of Benjamin.
lifetime: Zethan was born as a son of Bilhan (1 Chronicles 7:10). He is one of the sons of Bilhan (Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar), a person who forms part of the line of descent within the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:10).

introduce: Zethar is a person mentioned as one of the seven eunuchs who served at the court of Xerxes, king of the Persian Empire.
lifetime: On the last day of the seven-day banquet that King Xerxes gave, the king commanded the seven eunuchs who served in his presence to bring Queen Vashti before the king wearing her royal crown, so as to display her beauty to all the peoples and officials (Esther 1:10-11). Zethar is recorded as one of the seven eunuchs whom the king commanded at this time (Esther 1:10).
event: He is one of the seven eunuchs who received the king's command to bring Vashti before the king (Esther 1:10-11). When Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command delivered by the eunuchs, the king was furious (Esther 1:12). What Zethar specifically did is not recorded in the text.

introduce: Zetham is a person belonging to the family line of the Gershonites of the tribe of Levi, and a son of Ladan.
lifetime: Zetham is recorded as a descendant of Ladan, a descendant of Gershon the son of Levi (1 Chronicles 23:8). He is mentioned as one of the three sons of Ladan the Gershonite (Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel) (1 Chronicles 23:8).

call: Grandson of Esau, chief of Edom
introduce: He is the grandson of Esau and a son of Reuel, one of the chiefs, the leaders of the Edom (Esau) clan.
lifetime: He is a son of Reuel, born to Esau's wife Basemath (the daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth) (Genesis 36:3-4, 36:13). In the text listing the sons of Reuel he is recorded second, after Nahath (Genesis 36:13, 1 Chronicles 1:37), and he is one of the chiefs who came from Reuel in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:17).
event: He is recorded where the genealogy of the Edomite clan is listed in the Bible. Among the descendants of Esau's son Reuel are Chief Nahath, Chief Zerah, Chief Shammah, and Chief Mizzah, and it is recorded that these are the chiefs who came from Reuel in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:17).

call: Levite leader who returned with Ezra (man of understanding)
introduce: Sherebiah is one of the Levite leaders who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra at the return from the Babylonian exile. He is recorded as one whom Ezra brought from the bank of the river that flows to Ahava (Ezra 8:18), and he was set apart as one of the twelve leading priests (Ezra 8:24).
lifetime: When Ezra was looking for descendants of Levi at the river that flows to Ahava (Ezra 8:15), Sherebiah is recorded as one who was brought to him, with his sons and brothers, eighteen persons (Ezra 8:18). Ezra set apart twelve of the leading priests, namely Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers (Ezra 8:24), and weighed out and gave to them the silver, the gold, and the vessels that the king, his counselors, his officials, and all the Israelites there had offered for the house of God (Ezra 8:25).
event: Ezra set apart Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers, weighed out the silver, the gold, and the vessels and entrusted them to them, and charged them to guard them carefully until they weighed them in the chambers of the house of the LORD in Jerusalem (Ezra 8:24-29). Then the priests and the Levites received the silver, the gold, and the vessels by weight to bring them to the house of God in Jerusalem (Ezra 8:30).
character: Sherebiah is described as a man of understanding (Ezra 8:18), and being recognized for his leadership within the tribe of Levi, he was entrusted with important asset management and educational duties. He showed an organized side, taking charge of practical matters in harmony with his colleagues in the process of public worship and covenant renewal (Nehemiah 9:4, Nehemiah 10:12).

introduce: Zeresh is the wife of Haman, a high official of the Persian Empire, and a person who appears in the book of Esther in the Bible. She is portrayed as one who was deeply involved in her husband's political circumstances and personal plans of revenge and who gave counsel.
lifetime: As Haman's wife, together with his friends, she advised Haman to set up a gallows fifty cubits high and to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on it (Esther 5:14). Later, when Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that had happened to him, Zeresh, together with the wise men, said that if Mordecai was indeed of the Jewish people, before whom Haman had begun to be humiliated, he would not prevail against him but would surely fall (Esther 6:13).
event: When Haman said that nothing satisfied him as long as he saw Mordecai sitting at the king's gate (Esther 5:13), Zeresh, together with all his friends, advised him to set up a gallows fifty cubits high and to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on it, and Haman was pleased with the advice and set up the gallows (Esther 5:14). Later, when Haman told what had happened to him because of Mordecai, Zeresh said that if Mordecai was of the Jewish people, Haman would not prevail against him but would surely fall (Esther 6:13).
character: She had a cool-headed and strategic side that actively supported her husband's political ambitions. She was a person with realistic judgment, able to grasp Haman's fate accurately as circumstances changed and even to foresee his defeat (Esther 6:13).

call: Firstborn of Zebulun (founder of the Seredite clan)
introduce: Sered is a son of Zebulun, a son of Jacob, and the person who became the founder of the Seredite clan.
lifetime: As a son of Zebulun, he became the ancestor of the Seredite clan (Numbers 26:26).
event: When Israel was numbered in the plains of Moab after the Exodus, Sered was recorded as the founder of the Seredite clan named after him (Numbers 26:26).

introduce: Shemeber is a person who appears in Genesis in the Old Testament, a ruler who reigned as king of Zeboiim in the time of Bera, king of Sodom.
lifetime: When Chedorlaomer king of Elam and his allies attacked five cities including Sodom and Gomorrah, he took part in the war as king of Zeboiim (Genesis 14:2). In the war fought in the Valley of Siddim, he formed an allied force with Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, and the king of Zoar, and engaged the army of Chedorlaomer (Genesis 14:8).
event: He fought in the Valley of Siddim against Chedorlaomer and the other three kings (Genesis 14:8-9), but since the Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits, when the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some of the men fell into them, and the rest fled to the hill country (Genesis 14:10). The four kings took all the goods and food of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 14:11). The text does not separately record the end of Shemeber king of Zeboiim.

call: Original owner of the hill of Samaria
introduce: Shemer is a person who appears in 1 Kings 16, a landowner recorded as the original owner of the hill of Samaria.
lifetime: Omri king of Israel bought the hill of Samaria from him for two talents of silver (1 Kings 16:24).
event: He sold the hill of Samaria that he owned to King Omri, and because of this Omri built a city on that hill and named it Samaria, after the name of Shemer, the former owner of the hill (1 Kings 16:24).

introduce: Shemed is a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, a person who appears in the genealogy of the house of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles 8.
lifetime: Shemed is a son of Elpaal and belongs to the genealogy of the descendants of Elpaal, one of the families of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:12).
event: Among the sons of Elpaal, Eber, Misham, and Shemed, Shemed is recorded as the one who built Ono and Lod and their villages ("he ... built") (1 Chronicles 8:12).

introduce: Zebedee was a fisherman of the region of Galilee, known as the father of James and John, disciples of Jesus, and as the husband of Salome.
lifetime: He appears as a fisherman on the shore of Galilee who was in a boat with hired servants, mending nets (Matthew 4:18, 4:21, Mark 1:20). "The mother of Zebedee's sons" was among the women who served Jesus (Matthew 27:55-56), and, regarding her as the same person as Salome in Mark 15:40, which records the same scene, his wife is called Salome. His two sons, James and John, were called by Jesus, and leaving the boat and their father, they followed Jesus (Matthew 4:21-22).
event: Zebedee was present, mending nets in the boat with his two sons, when Jesus called his two sons (Matthew 4:21), and when his sons left the boat and their father and followed Jesus, he was left behind in the boat (Matthew 4:22, Mark 1:20). Salome, regarded as his wife, was among the women who were watching from a distance (Mark 15:40), and is recorded as one of the women who had bought spices to anoint Jesus after the Sabbath had passed (Mark 16:1).

introduce: Sheshan is a descendant of the tribe of Judah, a person who appears in the genealogy that continues through the house of Jerahmeel. In the biblical record, the family genealogy relating to the descendants of Sheshan is shown in detail.
lifetime: Sheshan was the grandson of Appaim and the son of Ishi (1 Chronicles 2:31). Having no sons but only daughters, he gave his daughter to his Egyptian servant Jarha to be his wife (1 Chronicles 2:34-35).
event: Since Sheshan had no sons but only daughters, he gave his daughter to Jarha, an Egyptian who was his servant, to be his wife, and through her Jarha fathered Attai (1 Chronicles 2:34-35). Attai fathered Nathan, and Nathan fathered Zabad (1 Chronicles 2:36).

introduce: Sheshai is one of the descendants of Anak who appear in Numbers in the Bible, a member of the race of giants who lived in the region of Hebron in the land of Canaan. He is mentioned together with Ahiman and Talmai, the sons of Anak, and is recorded as one of the representative figures of the race of giants whom the Israelite spies saw.
lifetime: Sheshai was living in Hebron at the time the land of Canaan was spied out (Numbers 13:22). The spies saw the men of great stature among the descendants of Anak and were afraid, saying that in their own eyes they were like grasshoppers (Numbers 13:33). Afterward Caleb drove out from Hebron the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai (Joshua 15:14), and Judah attacked the Canaanites who lived in Hebron and killed them (Judges 1:10).
event: He was a member of the descendants of Anak living in Hebron and was among the descendants of Anak whom the spies saw (Numbers 13:22, 13:28). Afterward he was driven out by Caleb together with Ahiman and Talmai (Joshua 15:14), and Judges 1:10 records that Judah killed them.
character: The Bible describes him, as a son of Anak, as a being of very great physical size and strong power (Numbers 13:33). He appears as a figure symbolizing the powerful warrior class, or ruling class, of the region of Canaan at that time (Joshua 15:14).

introduce: Sheshbazzar is a person who was called prince (governor) of Judah in the time of Cyrus, king of Persia, and who brought the vessels of the temple from Babylon to Jerusalem (Ezra 1:8, 1:11, 5:14). There is a view that he is the same person as Zerubbabel, but the text of the Korean Revised Version does not state this. Zerubbabel is recorded as the son of Shealtiel (Nehemiah 12:1, Matthew 1:12).
lifetime: Cyrus king of Persia commanded Mithredath, the keeper of the treasury, to bring out the vessels of the house of the LORD and count them out to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah (Ezra 1:8). When the captives were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem, Sheshbazzar brought all those vessels (Ezra 1:11). He is called a governor appointed by King Cyrus (Ezra 5:14), and it is reported that he came to Jerusalem and laid the foundation of the house of God, but that the building had not yet been completed up to that time (Ezra 5:16).
event: King Cyrus gave to Sheshbazzar the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar had carried from the house of God in Jerusalem and put in the temple of Babylon (Ezra 5:14), and the total of those vessels was five thousand four hundred (Ezra 1:11). King Cyrus told him to take these vessels, put them in the temple in Jerusalem, and rebuild the house of God on its site (Ezra 5:15), and Sheshbazzar came to Jerusalem and laid the foundation of the house of God (Ezra 5:16).
character: According to the Bible, Sheshbazzar is called by the title of prince of Judah, and is portrayed as a person with administrative authority, trusted by the Persian royal court, who managed the vessels of the temple and led the return (Ezra 1:8). Some regard him as the same person as Zerubbabel or as another leader of the same period.

introduce: She is a woman recorded as a daughter of Ephraim, and the person who built Lower and Upper Beth-horon and Uzzen-sheerah.
lifetime: She is recorded as a daughter of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 7:24).
event: She built Lower Beth-horon and Upper Beth-horon, and also Uzzen-sheerah (1 Chronicles 7:24).

기타관계: Joshua#3179(kinsman of the tribe of Ephraim)

introduce: In the Bible, Seir is a Horite, and Genesis 36:20 records him as "Seir the Horite, an original inhabitant of that land." Among his descendants arose the chiefs of the Horite clan in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:21).
lifetime: Seir was a Horite and is recorded as an original inhabitant of that land (Genesis 36:20). His descendants are Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan (Genesis 36:20-21, 1 Chronicles 1:38), and they are the chiefs who arose from the Horite clan among the descendants of Seir in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:21).
event: Esau, that is, Edom, lived in Mount Seir (Genesis 36:8), and the descendants of Esau destroyed the Horites who had lived in Seir and settled in their place in that land (Deuteronomy 2:12).

introduce: Shelesh is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher recorded in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a son of Helem (1 Chronicles 7:35).
lifetime: Shelesh is recorded as a son of Helem, a descendant of Asher, and his position in the genealogy belongs within a family of the tribe of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:35).

introduce: Zelek is a person who appears in 2 Samuel in the Bible, an Ammonite recorded as one of the thirty mighty men of King David.
lifetime: He was chosen as one of David's thirty mighty men and served (2 Samuel 23:37).
event: He was recognized as a brave warrior within David's military organization and entered his name in the list of David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23:37).
character: Although he was from Ammon and not an Israelite, he gained King David's military trust and served as an elite warrior (2 Samuel 23:37).

introduce: Sheleph is a son of Joktan, the son of Eber, and one of the persons who continue the genealogy of Shem (Genesis 10:24-26, 1 Chronicles 1:18-20).
lifetime: Sheleph is recorded as a son of Joktan (Genesis 10:26, 1 Chronicles 1:20). Eber had two sons, Peleg and Joktan (Genesis 10:25), and Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, and others (Genesis 10:26).
event: The biblical text does not record any specific accomplishments or particular events of Sheleph himself; he merely occupies a position of being mentioned side by side with other persons such as Almodad, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah in the genealogical lists of Genesis 10 and 1 Chronicles 1 (Genesis 10:26, 1 Chronicles 1:20).

introduce: Seled is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a son of Nadab and a brother of Appaim (1 Chronicles 2:30). Nadab is a son of Shammai, Shammai is a son of Onam, and Onam is recorded as a son of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2:25-28).
lifetime: Seled is a descendant of Hezron the son of Perez, and belongs to the line that continues from Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron, through Onam, Shammai, and Nadab (1 Chronicles 2:5, 2:25-28, 2:30). He died without sons (1 Chronicles 2:30).

introduce: He was a man of the time of King Hezekiah of Judah; in Isaiah 22:15 he is called one "in charge of the treasury and occupying the palace," and in 2 Kings 18:18 and Isaiah 36:3 he is recorded as a scribe.
lifetime: In Isaiah 22:15 he is recorded as one "in charge of the treasury and occupying the palace." When the Rabshakeh sent by the king of Assyria came to Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:17), Shebnah the scribe went out to the Rabshakeh together with Eliakim, who was over the household, and Joah the recorder (2 Kings 18:18), and they asked the Rabshakeh to speak to them in Aramaic (2 Kings 18:26, Isaiah 36:11). Afterward Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebnah the scribe were sent, together with the senior priests, clothed in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz (2 Kings 19:2, Isaiah 37:2).
event: The LORD had Isaiah speak to Shebnah and rebuked him for having hewn out a tomb for himself on the height and carved a dwelling for himself in the rock (Isaiah 22:15-16). He also said that he would drive him from his office and bring him down from his position (Isaiah 22:17-19), and that he would call Eliakim son of Hilkiah and entrust to him Shebnah's robe, sash, and authority (Isaiah 22:20-21). In 2 Kings 18:18 and Isaiah 36:3, Eliakim is recorded as the one over the household and Shebnah as the scribe.
character: He had a strong tendency to show off himself, and as a high official of the time he displayed a luxurious and arrogant attitude, such as making a splendid tomb on a height (Isaiah 22:16). He was capable enough to handle the central practical affairs of state, but he fell because he used his position to maintain private power and honor (Isaiah 22:15-19).

직업/직위: King Hezekiah's palace administrator (in charge of the treasury), later scribe

introduce: Seth is a person who appears in Genesis, the third son born to Adam and Eve. He is recorded as the offspring God gave in place of Abel, who was killed by Cain.
lifetime: Adam fathered Seth when he was 130 years old and had a son in his own likeness, after his image (Genesis 5:3). Seth fathered Enosh at 105 years, lived 807 more years after that and had other children, and died at 912 years (Genesis 5:6-8).
event: Eve named him Seth, meaning that God had given her another seed in place of Abel, whom Cain had killed (Genesis 4:25). There is a record that from the time of Seth's son Enosh people began to call on the name of the LORD (Genesis 4:26). Seth's descendants later became an important channel continuing the genealogy of humanity before the flood of Noah (Genesis 5:6-32).

introduce: Soco is a name mentioned in 1 Chronicles 4:18 in the expression "Heber the ancestor of Soco." The same verse says that Jehudijah bore Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel, and among them Heber is recorded as the ancestor of Soco (1 Chronicles 4:18).
lifetime: Heber, who is recorded as the ancestor of Soco, is a son born to Jehudijah, and is mentioned together with Jered (the ancestor of Gedor) and Jekuthiel (the ancestor of Zanoah) (1 Chronicles 4:18). There is no record of the life of Soco himself.
event: No specific accomplishments or special events that he performed are stated in the biblical record (1 Chronicles 4:18).

introduce: Sotai is a person whose name is recorded as "descendants of Sotai" among the descendants of Solomon's servants in the list of the people of Israel who returned from Babylon (Ezra 2:55).
lifetime: In the list of those who were carried away captive by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, were released, and returned to Jerusalem and Judah, "the descendants of Sotai" are recorded among the descendants of Solomon's servants (Ezra 2:1, Ezra 2:55). They appear as "the descendants of Sotai" also in the same list in Nehemiah 7 (Nehemiah 7:6, Nehemiah 7:57).
event: No specific accomplishments or individual events concerning Sotai himself are recorded; only the fact that his descendants entered the list of returnees as descendants of Solomon's servants is reported (Ezra 2:55, Nehemiah 7:57).

introduce: Sodi is a person who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, a man of the tribe of Zebulun and the father of Gaddiel, who was chosen as a spy.
lifetime: Sodi is recorded as the father of Gaddiel, a chief of the tribe of Zebulun (Numbers 13:10). He was one man of a family of the tribe of Zebulun, and his name is mentioned in the Bible because his son Gaddiel was chosen by Moses as one of the representatives of the twelve tribes to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:2).
event: No direct activities or accomplishments of Sodi himself are recorded in the Bible; his existence is confirmed only through the fact that his son Gaddiel carried out the mission of spying out Canaan as the representative of the tribe of Zebulun (Numbers 13:10).

introduce: Shomer is a person who appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Asher in 1 Chronicles 7, a son born to Heber, the son of Beriah (1 Chronicles 7:31-32).
lifetime: Shomer appears in the record that Heber fathered Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and Shua (1 Chronicles 7:32), and his sons are Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram (1 Chronicles 7:34).
event: Apart from the fact that he is recorded in the genealogy as a son of Heber and that he had sons, no specific activities or historical events appear in the biblical record (1 Chronicles 7:32-34).

introduce: Zophah is a person who appears in 1 Chronicles 7 in the Old Testament, a descendant belonging to the genealogy of the tribe of Asher. He is recorded as a son of Helem.
lifetime: Zophah is recorded as a son of Helem, a descendant of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:35). The sons of Helem are Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal, and Zophah is a brother to these (1 Chronicles 7:35). The sons of Zophah are Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah, and others (1 Chronicles 7:36).

call: Son of Pyrrhus of Berea (companion of Paul)
introduce: Sopater is a person who appears in Acts in the New Testament, a son of Pyrrhus of Berea, and one of the party who traveled with Paul as far as Asia (Acts 20:4).
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Pyrrhus of Berea (Acts 20:4). When Paul, after spending three months in Greece, resolved to return through Macedonia because of a plot by the Jews, his name is listed among those who accompanied him as far as Asia (Acts 20:3-4).
event: He is recorded as one of the party who went with Paul as far as Asia (Acts 20:4). They went on ahead and waited for Paul's party at Troas (Acts 20:5).

introduce: Shobach is a person recorded in the Old Testament, the commander of the army of Aram (Syria). He was in the position of commanding the army of King Hadadezer (2 Samuel 10:16).
lifetime: Shobach is recorded as the commander of the army of Hadadezer king of Aram (2 Samuel 10:16). When Hadadezer summoned the Arameans from beyond the river, Shobach led them and came to Helam (2 Samuel 10:16). David gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, came to Helam, and fought against the Arameans (2 Samuel 10:17), and when the Arameans fled before Israel, David struck down Shobach, the commander of the army, and Shobach died there (2 Samuel 10:18).
event: He came to Helam leading the Arameans whom Hadadezer had summoned from beyond the river (2 Samuel 10:16). When David heard of this, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, came to Helam, and fought; the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed the men of seven hundred Aramean chariots and forty thousand horsemen, and struck down Shobach and killed him (2 Samuel 10:17-18). 1 Chronicles 19:18 records that David killed the men of seven thousand Aramean chariots and forty thousand foot soldiers and killed Shobach the commander of the army (1 Chronicles 19:18).

introduce: Shobal is a son of Seir recorded in Genesis, and one of the chiefs of the Horite clan who lived in the land of Edom.
lifetime: Shobal is a descendant of Seir and appears in the genealogy of the leaders of the Horite clan who lived in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:20). As a son of Seir, he was classified as a chief of the Horite clan (Genesis 36:29).
event: He is recorded as "Chief Shobal" among the chiefs of the Horite clan (Genesis 36:29).

call: Ancestor of gatekeepers who returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Shobai is a person who appears in Ezra and Nehemiah, recorded as "descendants of Shobai" among the descendants of the gatekeepers in the list of the returnees from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: In the list of the people of Israel who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel and others, "the descendants of Shobai" are mentioned among the descendants of the gatekeepers (Ezra 2:2, Ezra 2:42). In the list in Nehemiah as well, they appear as "the descendants of Shobai" among the gatekeepers (Nehemiah 7:45).
event: No specific deeds of Shobai himself are recorded. "The descendants of Shobai" are included in the list of the descendants of the gatekeepers, and the total of the gatekeepers' descendants is given as one hundred thirty-nine in Ezra 2:42 and one hundred thirty-eight in Nehemiah 7:45.

introduce: Sophereth is a person recorded in the book of Nehemiah in the Old Testament, whose name is entered as "the descendants of Sophereth" in the list of the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from Babylon (Nehemiah 7:57).
lifetime: His name is in the list of the descendants of Solomon's servants among those who were carried away captive by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and returned to Jerusalem and Judah (Nehemiah 7:6, Nehemiah 7:57). In the same list in Ezra 2:55 he appears as "the descendants of Hassophereth" (Ezra 2:55).
event: He is included in the list of those who returned from Babylon, and his name is entered among those recorded in the genealogical register of those who first returned, which Nehemiah obtained (Nehemiah 7:5, Nehemiah 7:57).

introduce: Zobebah is a person mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a son of a man named Koz (1 Chronicles 4:8).
lifetime: Zobebah is recorded as a son of Koz, a descendant of Judah, and in the context of the genealogical record he is classified as a member of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:8).
event: No specific accomplishments or particular events connected with Zobebah are recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 4:8).

introduce: Shobek is a person whose name is recorded in the list of "the heads of the people" among those who sealed the covenant, swearing to keep the law in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14, Nehemiah 10:24).
lifetime: Together with Nehemiah, he entered his name in the list of those who sealed, swearing to keep the law of God (Nehemiah 10:1, Nehemiah 10:24, Nehemiah 10:29).
event: His name was included in the list of those who sealed, who as representatives of the people of Israel resolved to follow and keep the law of the LORD (Nehemiah 10:24). This shows that he held a leading status among the returned people of that time (Nehemiah 10:14-27).

introduce: Shobi is from Rabbah, the land of the Ammonites, a son of Nahash the Ammonite, and one of those who helped David when David's son Absalom rebelled and David fled to Mahanaim east of the Jordan (2 Samuel 17:27).
lifetime: Shobi is recorded as a son of Nahash the Ammonite (2 Samuel 17:27). When David stayed at Mahanaim fleeing from Absalom, Shobi, together with Machir and Barzillai, provided food and bedding to David and the soldiers who followed him (2 Samuel 17:27-29).
event: Shobi supplied David and his company with beds, basins, earthen vessels, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, roasted mung beans, honey, curds, sheep, and cheese (2 Samuel 17:28-29). Concerned that David's company would be hungry and weary in the wilderness, he prepared and brought these provisions (2 Samuel 17:29).

meaning: at peace by relying on authority
introduce: Sosthenes is a person recorded as the synagogue leader in Corinth, who was seized by everyone and beaten after the Jews brought Paul to the judgment seat (Acts 18:12-17).
lifetime: While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews rose up together and brought Paul to the judgment seat, but when Gallio refused to hear the case and drove them away (Acts 18:12-16), everyone seized Sosthenes the synagogue leader and beat him in front of the judgment seat, and Gallio paid no attention to this (Acts 18:17).
event: He was seized by everyone and beaten in front of the judgment seat, and the proconsul Gallio paid no attention to this (Acts 18:17).

introduce: Sosipater is a person to whom Paul, near the end of Romans, sent greetings to the believers in Rome, with the words "my relatives Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater" (Romans 16:21).
lifetime: Sosipater appears in Romans 16:21 as one who was with Paul and, together with Timothy, Lucius, and Jason, sent greetings to the believers in Rome. There is no other record of his life.
event: No specific deeds or events of Sosipater himself are recorded; his name appears only as one of those who send greetings in Romans 16:21.

introduce: Zohar is a person who appears in Genesis in the Old Testament, a name mentioned as the father of Ephron the Hittite.
lifetime: In the biblical record, apart from the fact that Zohar was a father who had a son, Ephron, no specific information about his life as a whole appears (Genesis 23:8).
event: Zohar does not appear as the subject of any direct event; his name is mentioned as the father of Ephron when his son Ephron sold the cave of Machpelah to Abraham (Genesis 23:8).

introduce: Shoham is a person recorded as a son of Jaaziah among the descendants of Merari of the tribe of Levi (1 Chronicles 24:27).
lifetime: Shoham is recorded as a descendant of Merari and a son of Jaaziah (1 Chronicles 24:27). No specific record of his time of birth, year of death, or life as a whole appears in the Bible (1 Chronicles 24:27).
event: In the process of organizing the duties of the descendants of Levi in the time of King David, he is mentioned as one in the genealogy of the descendants of Merari (1 Chronicles 24:26-27). Shoham is recorded as one of those born of Jaaziah (1 Chronicles 24:27). There is no record of the specific duties he performed or of any special events (1 Chronicles 24:27).

introduce: Zoheth is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles 4:20 in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as one of the sons of Ishi, Zoheth and Ben-zoheth (1 Chronicles 4:20).
lifetime: Zoheth is recorded as a son of Ishi and is a person classified within the genealogy of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:20). No other specific record of his birth, death, or life as a whole appears in the Bible (1 Chronicles 4:20).
event: No record exists in the Bible of specific accomplishments or special events that Zoheth carried out during his lifetime (1 Chronicles 4:20).

기타관계: Tilon#620(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: He is the third king of the united kingdom of Israel, born between David and Bathsheba, who ascended the throne after David and led Israel to its golden age (1 Kings 1:11-13).
lifetime: Born as a son of King David, he was designated heir to the throne through the mediation of the prophet Nathan (1 Kings 1:32-35). After David's death, in order to consolidate his royal power, he eliminated political enemies such as Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei (1 Kings 2:23-46). He formed ties with Pharaoh king of Egypt and took his daughter (1 Kings 3:1); besides Pharaoh's daughter he loved many foreign women, and when he was old his wives turned his heart to follow other gods (1 Kings 11:1-4). After a reign of forty years he died in Jerusalem and was buried in the City of David (1 Kings 11:42-43).
event: Carrying out David's will, he built and dedicated the temple in Jerusalem (1 Kings 6:1-38). He also carried out large-scale building projects, including his own palace, over thirteen years (1 Kings 7:1-12). He set twelve officers over all Israel, each to provide food for the king and the royal household for one month in the year (1 Kings 4:7). The queen of Sheba visited to test his wisdom, and there was an exchange of treasures (1 Kings 10:1-10). He accumulated enormous wealth through trade, but in his later years, because he built high places for Chemosh of Moab and Molech of the Ammonites, the LORD said that He would take the kingdom from him and give it to his servant (1 Kings 11:7-13).
character: He is recorded as having wisdom and understanding beyond comparison with the kings of the surrounding nations (1 Kings 4:29-31), and with outstanding literary talent he composed many proverbs and songs (1 Kings 4:32). In the early part of his reign he showed outstanding insight in making judicial decisions (1 Kings 3:16-28). In his old age, however, his heart was turned aside by the influence of foreign women, and he showed a deterioration in the discipline of his rule and in his religious identity (1 Kings 11:4-6).

introduce: Shuni is the third of the seven sons born to Gad, a son of Jacob, and the ancestor of the Shunite clan that makes up the tribe of Gad, one of the tribes of Israel.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons of Gad who accompanied Jacob when Jacob left the land of Canaan and migrated to Egypt (Genesis 46:16).
event: As a member of the tribe of Gad who came out of Egypt, he became the ancestor of the Shunite house, and later, when a census was taken in Numbers, the Shunite house composed of his descendants was mentioned as part of the tribe of Gad (Numbers 26:15).

call: Firstborn of Ephraim (founder of the Shuthelahite clan)
introduce: Shuthelah, a son of Ephraim the son of Joseph, is the person who became the founder of the Shuthelahite clan within the tribe of Ephraim (Numbers 26:35, 1 Chronicles 7:20).
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Ephraim and appears first in the list of the clans of the descendants of Ephraim (Numbers 26:35). 1 Chronicles 7:20 records Bered as a son of Shuthelah, son of Ephraim, and Numbers 26:36 records the descendants of Shuthelah as the Eranite family born of Eran (1 Chronicles 7:20, Numbers 26:36).
event: No specific event of Shuthelah himself, the son of Ephraim, is recorded, and in Numbers 26:35 he appears as the ancestor of the Shuthelahite family born of Shuthelah. It was Ezer and Elead, fathered by "Shuthelah the son of Zabad," who went down to take the livestock of the men of Gath and were killed by the native men of Gath (1 Chronicles 7:21).

call: One of the five kings of Midian
introduce: Zur is the head of a clan of the Midianite people, recorded as one of the five kings of Midian (Numbers 31:8). He is also the father of the Midianite woman Cozbi who was killed (Numbers 25:15).
lifetime: Zur is mentioned as one of the five kings of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba (Numbers 31:8). He was the head of a clan of the Midianite people and the father of Cozbi (Numbers 25:15). When the Israelites went to war with Midian, he was killed together with the other kings of Midian (Numbers 31:8).
event: When the whole congregation of the Israelites was weeping at the entrance to the tent of meeting, an Israelite brought a Midianite woman to his brothers (Numbers 25:6), and this Midianite woman who was afterward killed was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur (Numbers 25:15). Afterward, in the war between the Israelites and Midian, Zur was killed along with the other kings of Midian (Numbers 31:8).

introduce: Zurishaddai is a person who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, recorded as the father of Shelumiel, chief of the tribe of Simeon (Numbers 1:6).
lifetime: Zurishaddai is mentioned only in the expression "Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai" in Numbers 1:6, 2:12, 7:36, 10:19. There is no record of his own life.
event: No event concerning Zurishaddai himself is recorded. His son Shelumiel was chief of the descendants of Simeon (Numbers 2:12), presented his offering on the fifth day (Numbers 7:36), and led the army of the tribe of the descendants of Simeon (Numbers 10:19).

introduce: Zuriel is a person mentioned in Numbers in the Bible, recorded as a chief of the family of the descendants of Merari.
lifetime: Zuriel is recorded as the son of Abihail who was to be chief of the families and clans of Merari (Numbers 3:35).
event: The family of Merari, of which Zuriel was to be chief, was to camp on the north side of the tabernacle (tent) (Numbers 3:35).

call: Grandson of Moses (chief of the temple storehouses)
introduce: Shubael is a son of Gershom and a grandson of Moses, a person from the tribe of Levi who was in charge of the storehouses in the time of David. In the Korean Revised Version he appears under the name Shebuel in 1 Chronicles 23:16 and 1 Chronicles 26:24.
lifetime: He was one of the sons of Gershom the son of Moses (1 Chronicles 23:15-16), and among the descendants of Levi he is recorded as Shubael among the sons of Amram, and among his sons is Jehdeiah (1 Chronicles 24:20). In the passage recording the duties of the Levites in the time of David, he appears as the one in charge of the storehouses (1 Chronicles 26:24).
event: Shubael (Shebuel) became chief among the sons of Gershom (1 Chronicles 23:16) and was put in charge of the storehouses (1 Chronicles 26:24).
character: As a direct descendant of Moses, Shubael held a trusted position within the tribe of Levi and is regarded as a person with the practical ability and credibility to manage the important finances of the temple (1 Chronicles 26:24). He was also called by the alternate name Shebuel, which shows that this is the same person (1 Chronicles 25:4).

introduce: Susanna is one of the women who followed Jesus during His Galilean ministry and served Him and His companions out of her own means (Luke 8:3).
lifetime: She is a person who accompanied Jesus as He went through every city and village proclaiming the kingdom of God and preaching the gospel (Luke 8:1, Luke 8:3).
event: During the ministry of Jesus and the twelve disciples, she used her own possessions to meet their needs and gave financial support (Luke 8:3).

introduce: Susi, a man of the tribe of Joseph, that is, the tribe of Manasseh, is recorded as the father of Gaddi, who was chosen to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:11).
lifetime: Susi is recorded only as the father of Gaddi, whom the tribe of Manasseh sent to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:2-3, 13:11). There is no record in the text about Susi's own life.
event: Nothing that Susi himself did is recorded. Those who spied out the land of Canaan were the chiefs of the tribes, including his son Gaddi, and they spied out the land from the Wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, toward Lebo-hamath (Numbers 13:21), and reported to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of the Israelites at Kadesh in the Wilderness of Paran (Numbers 13:26).

introduce: Suah is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher, a son of Zophah (1 Chronicles 7:36).
lifetime: He is the first name listed among the sons of Zophah, a descendant of Asher, and is recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:36, 7:40).

call: Father of Nethanel (father of the chief of Issachar)
introduce: Zuar is recorded as the father of Nethanel, chief of the tribe of Issachar. In Numbers his name appears in the expression "Nethanel son of Zuar" (Numbers 2:5, 7:18, 10:15).
lifetime: Zuar appears only as the father of Nethanel, and there is no record of his own life. His son Nethanel was the one who would stand as head of the tribe of Issachar when the people were counted (Numbers 1:8, in this verse the father's name is written as Zuriel), was chief of the descendants of Issachar when they camped (Numbers 2:5), and led the army of the tribe of the descendants of Issachar when they marched (Numbers 10:15).
event: Nothing Zuar himself did is recorded. His son Nethanel, as chief of Issachar on the second day of the dedication of the tabernacle, presented as his offering one silver platter, one silver bowl, one gold dish, and burnt, sin, and peace offerings (Numbers 7:18-23).

introduce: Shuhah is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as the brother of Chelub (1 Chronicles 4:11).
lifetime: Apart from being mentioned as the brother of Chelub within the family line of the tribe of Judah, there is no concrete record of his life (1 Chronicles 4:11).
event: The Bible does not describe any particular achievement or individual event that Shuhah carried out himself (1 Chronicles 4:11).

introduce: Shuham is a person who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, a son of Dan the son of Jacob, and the ancestor of the Shuhamite clan within the tribe of Dan.
lifetime: Shuham, as a son of Dan, appears under the name Hushim in Genesis 46:23 and is on the list of Jacob's family who went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:8, 46:23). Of the descendants of Dan, the Shuhamite family came from Shuham (Numbers 26:42).
event: When Moses and Eleazar the priest counted the Israelites in the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho (Numbers 26:1-4), it is recorded that among the clans of the descendants of Dan, the Shuhamite family came from Shuham (Numbers 26:42). Because Genesis records the son of Dan as Hushim, they are regarded as the same person (Genesis 46:23).

introduce: Syntyche is a woman who appears in Philippians in the New Testament, a believer of the church in Philippi, whom Paul called by name and exhorted together with Euodia (Philippians 4:2).
lifetime: She is mentioned as a woman believer who labored together with the apostle Paul for the gospel within the church in Philippi (Philippians 4:3).
event: Paul urged Euodia and Syntyche to be of the same mind in the Lord (Philippians 4:2). The text has no record of what conflict there may have been between the two.
character: Paul mentioned Syntyche as one of the fellow workers whose names are in the Book of Life, and assessed her as a person who had struggled together with him for the gospel (Philippians 4:3).

introduce: Zur is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in 1 Chronicles 8, a son of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon (1 Chronicles 8:29-30).
lifetime: Zur is a son of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon, and his name comes after the firstborn Abdon (1 Chronicles 8:30, 9:35-36). Zur's own dwelling place and deeds are not recorded in the text.
event: Zur's own deeds are not recorded. His father Jeiel lived in Gibeon and his wife's name was Maacah (1 Chronicles 8:29), and Zur is on the list of Jeiel's sons together with his brothers Abdon, Kish, Baal, and Nadab (1 Chronicles 8:30).

introduce: Zuph is a person recorded in the genealogy as an ancestor of Samuel. In 1 Samuel 1:1, Elkanah, Samuel's father, is introduced as "a great-great-grandson of Zuph."
lifetime: In the genealogy of the Kohathite descendants in 1 Chronicles 6, Zuph is recorded as the son of Elkanah and the father of Toah (1 Chronicles 6:33-35). In 1 Samuel 1:1, Elkanah is introduced as the son of Jeroham, the grandson of Elihu, the great-grandson of Tohu, and the great-great-grandson of Zuph, so Zuph is an ancestor of Samuel.
event: There is no record in the Bible that he led any specific event historically or left any particular achievement. His name appears only as a genealogical link showing that Elkanah, Samuel's father, was a great-great-grandson of Zuph (1 Samuel 1:1, 1 Chronicles 6:35).

introduce: Shuppites is a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, a son of Ir and a brother of Huppim, a person who appears in 1 Chronicles 7:12 and 7:15.
lifetime: Shuppites is recorded together with Huppim as a son of Ir (1 Chronicles 7:12). Also, Machir took as wife the sister of Huppim and Shuppim, whose name was Maacah (1 Chronicles 7:15).
event: No specific deeds or historical events of Shuppites himself are described. The text merely mentions the fact that Machir took as wife Maacah, the sister of Huppim and Shuppim (1 Chronicles 7:15).

기타관계: Hupham#3147(kinsman of the tribe of Benjamin)

call: Sixteenth-generation descendant of Aaron (scribe and priest)
introduce: Ezra is a scribe and priest recorded as a sixteenth-generation descendant of Aaron (Ezra 7:5, 7:11). In the time of Artaxerxes king of Persia he came up from Babylon to Jerusalem, and he is the man who resolved to study the law of the LORD and to practice it, and to teach statutes and ordinances in Israel (Ezra 7:6-10). He is recorded in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah.
lifetime: Ezra is introduced as the son of Seraiah, the grandson of Azariah, and the great-grandson of Hilkiah, and his genealogy extends to the sixteenth-generation descendant of Aaron the high priest (Ezra 7:1-5). He came up from Babylon in the fifth month of the seventh year of Artaxerxes king of Persia (Ezra 7:6, 7:8); he set out from Babylon on the first day of the first month and, with the help of the good hand of God upon him, arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month (Ezra 7:9). Afterward, in the seventh month, he read the book of the law before the people who gathered (Nehemiah 8:1-3).
event: Ezra received a decree from King Artaxerxes (Ezra 7:11-12). The king ordered all the treasurers west of the river to carry out promptly what Ezra requested (Ezra 7:21), and told Ezra, according to the wisdom of God, to appoint those who knew the law as magistrates and judges to judge all the people west of the river, and to teach those who did not know it (Ezra 7:25). When the officials reported the sin of intermarrying with the foreign peoples, he tore his garments and sat appalled (Ezra 9:1-5), then fell down before the house of God weeping and confessed the sin, and a great many people gathered before him and wept bitterly (Ezra 10:1). Afterward, regarding the matter of those who had taken foreign women as wives, Ezra made the priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear to act according to this word (Ezra 10:5).
character: He was a scholar who resolved to study and practice the law of the LORD and to teach statutes and ordinances in Israel (Ezra 7:10). Being convinced of the help of the hand of God, he did not ask the king for a military escort, and showed prudence and resolve by fasting and praying for the safety of the return journey (Ezra 8:21-23). He was a person whose authority was so recognized that when he read the law, the people stood up in respect (Nehemiah 8:5).

기타관계: Noadiah#385(fellow worker of the tribe of Levi)

introduce: Shecaniah is a person who appears in the genealogy of David's descendants in 1 Chronicles 3, the father of Shemaiah (1 Chronicles 3:22). His name is recorded in the passage listing the descendants of Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3:19-22).
lifetime: Shecaniah's son is Shemaiah, and Shemaiah's sons are six persons: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat (1 Chronicles 3:22). The Bible does not describe the specific dates of his life or the period of his activity (1 Chronicles 3:22).
event: Apart from the fact that his name is entered in the biblical genealogy as a descendant of David, there is no record that he led any particular political or religious event historically (1 Chronicles 3:22).

introduce: He is the father of Abi, the mother of Hezekiah, and appears in the passage that clarifies the family and bloodline of King Hezekiah.
lifetime: Zechariah is recorded as the father of Abi, the mother of King Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:2). Hezekiah is the son of Ahaz king of Judah (2 Kings 18:1).
event: The Bible does not record Zechariah's own deeds, but only introduces his daughter Abi as the mother of Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:2).

introduce: Sceva is introduced in Acts 19 as "a priest of the Jews," and he is mentioned in connection with the incident in which his seven sons tried to invoke the name of Jesus over a man with an evil spirit and were put to shame.
lifetime: Sceva is introduced as a priest of the Jews, and his seven sons also did the work of invoking the name of the Lord Jesus over those with evil spirits (Acts 19:13-14). The Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus came to know of this (Acts 19:17). There is no record about Sceva's own life.
event: Sceva's seven sons tried to drive out an evil spirit, saying, "I command you by the Jesus whom Paul preaches," but the evil spirit answered, "Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are you?" and the man with the evil spirit leaped on the two of them, overpowered them, and they fled from that house naked and wounded (Acts 19:13-16).
character: Although from a priestly family, they were described as practitioners of magic, which was guarded against in Jewish society at the time (Acts 19:13-14).

call: Youngest son of Hiel the Bethelite
introduce: He is the youngest son of Hiel the Bethelite, recorded as having died when his father built Jericho.
lifetime: When his father Hiel built Jericho, he lost his firstborn Abiram when he laid its foundation, and lost his youngest son Segub when he set up its gates (1 Kings 16:34).
event: He died when the gates were being set up during the building of Jericho, and this came about according to the word the LORD spoke through Joshua son of Nun (1 Kings 16:34, Joshua 6:26).

introduce: Senaah is a name that appears in Ezra and Nehemiah in the Old Testament, either a person or the name of his family, mentioned in the lists of the descendants who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: The descendants of Senaah are on the list of the people of Israel who returned from Babylon and came out with Zerubbabel and others, and their number is recorded as 3,630 in Ezra 2:35 and 3,930 in Nehemiah 7:38 (Ezra 2:1-2, 2:35, Nehemiah 7:38). Nehemiah 3:3 records that the descendants of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate, laying its beams and setting up its doors, bolts, and bars.
event: The descendants of Hassenaah (thought to be of the same family as the descendants of Senaah) built the Fish Gate during the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem, laying its beams and setting up its doors, bolts, and bars (Nehemiah 3:3).

introduce: Stachys is a person mentioned near the end of Romans in the New Testament, one of the members of the early Christian community named when the apostle Paul sent greetings to the Christians in Rome.
lifetime: He is a person called "my beloved Stachys" in the letter Paul sent to the church community in Rome (Romans 16:9).
event: Paul told them to greet Urbanus, "our fellow worker" in Christ, and "my beloved" Stachys (Romans 16:9). Stachys' specific activities are not recorded.
character: He received from the apostle Paul the title "my beloved," which suggests that he was in a relationship of deep trust with Paul (Romans 16:9).

introduce: Shethar-bozenai is an official whose name appears together with Tattenai, governor west of the river, and his associates in the time of Darius king of Persia, connected with the incident in which they asked the Jews who were building the temple who had commanded them to build, and sent a letter to King Darius (Ezra 5:3, 5:6).
lifetime: In the second year of Darius king of Persia (Ezra 4:24), Tattenai the governor west of the river, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates went to the Jews and asked who had caused them to build the temple and finish the wall (Ezra 5:3). They wrote down the answer of the elders of Judah (Ezra 5:9-11) and sent a letter to King Darius (Ezra 5:6-17).
event: In the letter he sent together with Tattenai and his associates, he asked that the king's treasury be searched to confirm whether King Cyrus had issued a decree ordering the building of the temple (Ezra 5:17). In response King Darius issued a decree and had the house of the archives searched, and in the palace at Ecbatana in Media a scroll recording Cyrus' decree was found (Ezra 6:1-3). King Darius commanded Tattenai, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates to stay away from that place, not to hinder the work on the temple, and to give the expenses promptly from the king's property, that is, from the taxes of the region west of the river (Ezra 6:6-8), and they carried out the decree promptly (Ezra 6:13).
character: As an official faithful to his duties, he did not handle the matter in a biased way but followed the procedure of asking the central government to verify the facts (Ezra 5:8). Also, when King Darius' command came down, he obeyed immediately and helped the Jews carry out the temple rebuilding work thoroughly (Ezra 6:13).

introduce: Stephanas is a person who appears in 1 Corinthians in the New Testament, and his household is introduced as the first fruits of Achaia (1 Corinthians 16:15). Paul records that he baptized the household of Stephanas (1 Corinthians 1:16).
lifetime: The household of Stephanas was the first fruits of Achaia and had devoted themselves to serving the saints (1 Corinthians 16:15). Paul rejoiced at the coming of Stephanas with Fortunatus and Achaicus (1 Corinthians 16:17).
event: Stephanas came to Paul with Fortunatus and Achaicus and supplied what was lacking on the part of the church in Corinth (1 Corinthians 16:17), and Paul said that they had refreshed his spirit and that of the church in Corinth, and told them to acknowledge such men (1 Corinthians 16:18). Paul exhorted them, "submit to such as these and to everyone who works and labors with them" (1 Corinthians 16:16).
character: As the first person to accept the gospel in the region of Achaia, Stephanas took the lead in laying the foundation of the early community of faith (1 Corinthians 16:15). He had a voluntary will to serve others, and showed a disposition as a helper who looked after the needs of the church and assisted the workers (1 Corinthians 16:15, 17).

introduce: He was chosen as one of the seven deacons in the early Jerusalem church and is recorded as the first martyr in the history of Christianity. As a Hellenistic Jew he spread the Christian gospel, came into conflict with the Jewish religious leaders, and was executed.
lifetime: He was chosen as one of seven men to resolve the matter of relief in the Jerusalem church (Acts 6:1-6). Afterward, while debating with the people of the synagogues, he was brought before the council in front of false witnesses (Acts 6:9-13), and after finishing his defense the people stoned him and he died (Acts 7:58-60).
event: Full of grace and power, he did great wonders and signs among the people (Acts 6:8). Some men rose up from the synagogues of the Freedmen, the Cyrenians, the Alexandrians, and those from Cilicia and Asia and debated with him, but they could not withstand his wisdom and the Holy Spirit by whom he spoke (Acts 6:9-10). Before the council he spoke at length about the history of Israel beginning with Abraham (Acts 7:2-53), and, full of the Holy Spirit, he gazed up into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God (Acts 7:55-56).
character: He was regarded as a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit (Acts 6:5). He showed the outward trait of his face changing like that of an angel (Acts 6:15), and showed an attitude of asking forgiveness for those who were killing him (Acts 7:60). He also had thorough knowledge of the scriptural record and boldly expressed his convictions (Acts 7:2-53).

introduce: Shedeur is a person who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, recorded as the father of Elizur, chief of the tribe of Reuben.
lifetime: Shedeur appears in Numbers in the expression "Elizur son of Shedeur" (Numbers 1:5, 2:10), and Elizur is recorded as chief of the descendants of Reuben. There is no record of Shedeur's own life.
event: Nothing Shedeur himself did is recorded. His son Elizur was the one who would stand as head of the tribe from Reuben when the people were counted in the wilderness of Sinai (Numbers 1:1-5), was chief of the descendants of Reuben (Numbers 2:10), presented his offering as chief of the descendants of Reuben on the fourth day of the dedication of the tabernacle (Numbers 7:30), and led the army of Reuben when they marched (Numbers 10:18).

introduce: Sethur is a person who represents the tribe of Asher among the tribes of Israel, a leader who appears in the list of spies recorded in Numbers. He is recorded as a son of Michael (Numbers 13:13).
lifetime: Sethur was selected from the tribe of Asher according to the command of God and carried out the task of a spy (Numbers 13:13). He was one of the representatives of the twelve tribes of Israel whom Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:2-3).
event: Following Moses' instruction, Sethur was given the task of spying out the land of Canaan as the representative of the tribe of Asher (Numbers 13:13). Together with the representatives of the other tribes, he took part in the process of examining the condition of Canaan and returning to report (Numbers 13:25-26).

introduce: He is a person who became a scribe in the time of King David. In the Korean Revised Version he is written as Seraiah in 2 Samuel 8:17, as Sheva in 2 Samuel 20:25, and as Shavsha in 1 Chronicles 18:16, and he is generally regarded as the same person as Shisha in 1 Kings 4:3.
lifetime: He became a scribe during the reign of King David (2 Samuel 8:17, 1 Chronicles 18:16). 1 Kings 4:3 records that Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, were scribes as officials of Solomon (1 Kings 4:3).
event: He held the office of scribe among the officials of King David (2 Samuel 8:17, 2 Samuel 20:25, 1 Chronicles 18:16). Apart from his office, what he specifically did is not recorded in the Bible.
character: He is recorded as King David's scribe (2 Samuel 8:17). In the parallel accounts he appears under the name Sheva or Shavsha (2 Samuel 20:25, 1 Chronicles 18:16). His personal character is not specifically recorded.

call: High priest of the line of Aaron (ancestor of Ezra)
introduce: Zerahiah is a person recorded as a descendant of Aaron and an ancestor of Ezra. His name appears in the genealogy of Aaron in 1 Chronicles and in the genealogy of Ezra in Ezra 7.
lifetime: Zerahiah is recorded as the son of Uzzi and the father of Meraioth in the genealogy continuing from Aaron the high priest (1 Chronicles 6:6, 6:51). His name also appears in the genealogy of Ezra (Ezra 7:1-5; Ezra 7:4).
event: No record of his specific political activity or temple ministry appears in the Bible, and his name is recorded in the genealogy of the line of Aaron (1 Chronicles 6:6, 6:51, Ezra 7:4).

introduce: Zeror is a person of the tribe of Benjamin, the father of Abiel and the grandfather of Kish, the father of Saul. Therefore he is Saul's great-grandfather.
lifetime: 1 Samuel 9:1 introduces Kish as the son of Abiel and the grandson of Zeror, so Zeror is the father of Abiel (1 Samuel 9:1). Saul is the son of this Kish (1 Samuel 9:2).

introduce: Zeruah is a person who appears in 1 Kings 11:26, recorded as the mother of Jeroboam son of Nebat and as a widow.
lifetime: She is recorded as the mother of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and she was a widow (1 Kings 11:26). That she was an Ephraimite from Zeredah, as stated in the same verse, is a description of her son Jeroboam (1 Kings 11:26).
event: Nothing Zeruah herself did is recorded; she is introduced only as the mother of her son Jeroboam in the account that he lifted up his hand against the king (1 Kings 11:26).

introduce: Zeruiah is a sister of King David and the mother of the three generals Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. No mention of Zeruiah's husband appears in the biblical record, and her children were active as key figures forming David's military foundation.
lifetime: Zeruiah is mentioned as a sister of David (1 Chronicles 2:16). Her sons are the three brothers Abishai, Joab, and Asahel (1 Chronicles 2:16, 2 Samuel 2:18). Her son Joab became commander of the army in David's time (2 Samuel 8:16), and Abishai, Joab's brother, once commanded a third of the army (2 Samuel 18:2).
event: Her sons took part in military actions at David's side. Joab struck down and killed Abner (2 Samuel 3:27), stabbed Amasa with the sword and killed him (2 Samuel 20:10), and became commander over all the army of Israel (2 Samuel 20:23). Abishai asked the king to let him cut off the head of Shimei when Shimei cursed David (2 Samuel 16:9), and helped David strike down and kill a Philistine (2 Samuel 21:17). Asahel was as swift of foot as a wild gazelle (2 Samuel 2:18) but was struck and killed by the spear of Abner (2 Samuel 2:23).
character: Rather than Zeruiah's own direct deeds, the Bible emphasizes the influence of her house through the designation "sons of Zeruiah," which refers to her sons. David also voiced the hardship of finding it difficult to control the sons of Zeruiah, who went beyond his control and at times acted violently (2 Samuel 3:39). This shows that the house of Zeruiah held an independent military standing and resolve within David's kingship.

introduce: Serug is a person who appears in the genealogy of Genesis, a descendant of Shem and the great-grandfather of Abraham. He is classified as one of the patriarchs who carried on the lineage of humanity after the flood of Noah.
lifetime: Serug was born as the son of Reu (Genesis 11:20), and at the age of 30 he became the father of Nahor (Genesis 11:22). After becoming the father of Nahor he lived 200 more years and had other children, and died at the age of 230 (Genesis 11:22-23).
event: Serug served as a bridge transmitting the lineage of Shem, which began from Eber, to Abraham (Genesis 11:16-26). Apart from this, no special historical event or accomplishment that he led is recorded in the Bible (Genesis 11 as a whole).

introduce: Shema is one of the persons who stood at the right hand of Ezra when Ezra read the book of the law in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 8:4).
lifetime: As a member of the community that returned from the Babylonian exile, he was one of the people who stood at the right of Ezra when Ezra stood on the wooden platform and read the book of the law in the square before the Water Gate (Nehemiah 8:3-4).
event: When Ezra stood on the platform and opened the book of the law, he is recorded as one of Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, who stood at his right (Nehemiah 8:4-5).

introduce: Semachiah is a person recorded together with the sons of Shemaiah among the descendants of Obed-edom, introduced as a capable man together with Elihu, a brother of Elzabad. He is one of the descendants of Obed-edom who belonged to the division of the gatekeepers in the time of David.
lifetime: Semachiah was recorded, following the sons of Shemaiah the firstborn of Obed-edom (Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad), together with Elihu, a brother of Elzabad, and was called a capable man (1 Chronicles 26:4, 7). As a descendant of Obed-edom he belonged to the division of the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:7-8, 12).
event: It is recorded that the descendants of Obed-edom, their sons and brothers, were all capable men who did their work well (1 Chronicles 26:8), and Semachiah, together with Elihu, a brother of Elzabad, was called a capable man (1 Chronicles 26:7). As a head of the gatekeepers he belongs to the list of those who served in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:12).

introduce: Shemariah is a man of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the warriors who joined David when David was staying at Ziklag to escape the persecution of Saul.
lifetime: As a man of the tribe of Benjamin, he is a person who took part when Saul's kinsmen gathered at Ziklag to follow David (1 Chronicles 12:1-7).
event: He is included in the list of those who came to David while he was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul son of Kish and who were among the warriors who helped him in battle (1 Chronicles 12:1-2, 5).

introduce: Shemaah is a man of Gibeah, recorded as the father of two sons, Ahiezer and Joash, who were among the warriors who came to David and helped him in battle when David was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul (1 Chronicles 12:1-3). His two sons are introduced as kinsmen of Saul of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 12:2-3).
lifetime: He is recorded as a man of Gibeah (1 Chronicles 12:3), and his two sons are introduced as kinsmen of Saul of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 12:2-3).
event: His sons Ahiezer and Joash were among the warriors who came to David and helped him in battle when David was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul; Ahiezer was their chief and Joash was next (1 Chronicles 12:1-3). They were men who carried bows and could use both the right hand and the left to sling stones and shoot arrows (1 Chronicles 12:2).

call: Prophet in the time of Rehoboam
introduce: Shemaiah is a prophet called a man of God who was active in the time of Rehoboam of the southern kingdom of Judah. In the situation of political and military conflict between Judah and Israel in the early period of the divided kingdom, he carried out the role of conveying the will of God.
lifetime: When Rehoboam gathered 180,000 chosen warriors of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin to oppose the rebellion of the ten tribes of Israel, Shemaiah, as a man of God, received the word of the LORD and delivered to Rehoboam and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin the word not to go up and fight (1 Kings 12:21-24, 2 Chronicles 11:1-4). Afterward, when Rehoboam's kingdom was established and strong he forsook the law of the LORD, and when Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, Shemaiah went to Rehoboam and the princes and delivered the word that because they had forsaken the LORD, the LORD had also given them into the hand of Shishak (2 Chronicles 12:1-5). No specific record of Shemaiah's birth or death appears in the Bible.
event: By conveying the command of God not to fight against the children of Israel but to return each to his own house, he prevented the tragedy of fighting among kinsmen (1 Kings 12:24, 2 Chronicles 11:4). Also, at the time of Shishak's invasion, when Rehoboam and the princes humbled themselves, he prophesied by the word of the LORD that came to Shemaiah that they would not be destroyed but would obtain deliverance, and that they would become servants of Shishak so that they might learn the difference between serving the LORD and serving the kingdoms of the world (2 Chronicles 12:7-8). Shemaiah is also mentioned as the person who compiled the chronicle records of the acts of Rehoboam (2 Chronicles 12:15).
character: He had the firmness to convey the word of God bluntly even before the king and high officials (2 Chronicles 12:5).
