In a national crisis he was a person who defined his actions by prophetic authority rather than political judgment, and he possessed both the scribal ability and the influence to leave the records of the kings of Judah to later generations through his own writings (2 Chronicles 12:15).

call: Grandson of Issachar, one of the six sons of Tola
introduce: He is a person belonging to the tribe of Issachar, one of the six sons of Tola the son of Issachar. He and his brothers are recorded as heads of the house of their father Tola and as mighty men of valor in their generations.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Tola the son of Issachar (1 Chronicles 7:1-2). Together with his brothers he was a head of the house of their father Tola and a mighty man of valor in his generation, and by the time of David their number was 22,600 (1 Chronicles 7:2).
event: The chronicler recorded the sons of Tola, Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, as heads of the house of their father Tola and mighty men of valor in their generations (1 Chronicles 7:2).

introduce: Shemida is a descendant of Gilead belonging to the tribe of Manasseh, the person who became the ancestor of the Shemidaite family among the descendants of Gilead.
lifetime: Shemida is recorded as a descendant of Gilead, and from him came the Shemidaite family (Numbers 26:29-32). Gilead was the son of Machir and the grandson of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 7:17). The sons of Shemida are Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam (1 Chronicles 7:19). In Joshua 17:2, the descendants of Shemida are included among the families that received lots as the rest of the descendants of Manasseh (Joshua 17:2).
event: Shemida became the ancestor of the house that bore his name and formed an independent family system within the tribe of Manasseh (Numbers 26:32). His descendants, as male descendants of the tribe of Manasseh, were included in the list when the land of Canaan was distributed (Joshua 17:2).

introduce: Zemirah is one of the descendants of the tribe of Benjamin who appears in 1 Chronicles 7:8 in the Old Testament, a person recorded as a son of Becher, the son of Benjamin.
lifetime: Zemirah is recorded as a son of Becher in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:8). The sons of Becher are Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth (1 Chronicles 7:8).

call: Musician who praised before the ark of the covenant (harp player)
introduce: Shemiramoth is a Levite who was active in the time of David, one of the musicians who were in charge of praise when David moved the ark of the covenant of God to Jerusalem and afterward at the tabernacle. He held the duty of playing the harp.
lifetime: When David moved the ark of God and commanded the chiefs of the Levites to appoint singers, he was one of the men appointed as brothers (1 Chronicles 15:16-18). He was recorded as one who played the harp according to Alamoth, that is, to accompany soprano voices (1 Chronicles 15:20). Afterward, when David placed the ark of God in the tent he had pitched and appointed Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, he was again recorded as one who played the harp and lyre in the group whose chief was Asaph (1 Chronicles 16:1, 4-5).
event: When David moved the ark, he was appointed to play the harp according to Alamoth, that is, to accompany soprano voices (1 Chronicles 15:20). When Levites were appointed to minister before the ark and praise the LORD, he was recorded, together with those next after Asaph the chief, as one who played the harp and lyre (1 Chronicles 16:4-5).
character: In the biblical record, no specific information is given about his personal character or outward features.

call: Son of Cush (ancestor of the Seba people)
introduce: He is a person who appears in Genesis and 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a son of Cush and a grandson of Ham. As a descendant of Noah, he is a figure regarded as the founder of a people recorded in the early genealogy of humanity.
lifetime: He is recorded as the first of the five sons of Cush the son of Ham (Genesis 10:7). He is likewise mentioned as a son of Cush in 1 Chronicles 1:9 (1 Chronicles 1:9).
event: No direct deeds or specific events are described in the Bible; he appears only as a name in the genealogy of peoples (Genesis 10:7).

introduce: Shephatiah is the fifth son whom David fathered in Hebron, and his mother is Abital. He is one of the princes whose names are entered in the genealogy of David's dynasty, but no specific deeds of his are recorded in the Bible.
lifetime: He was born as the fifth of the sons whom David fathered in Hebron (2 Samuel 3:4). His mother is Abital (1 Chronicles 3:3).

introduce: Shupham was a son of Benjamin and is recorded as the ancestor of the Shuphamite family in the list of the clans of the descendants of Benjamin in the book of Numbers (Numbers 26:38-39).
lifetime: In Numbers 26:38-39 the clans of the descendants of Benjamin are listed as the clan of Bela, the clan of Ashbel, and the clan of Ahiram, followed by the clan of Shupham and the clan of Hupham (Numbers 26:39). There is no text stating that he is the same person as Shephuphan, the son of Bela in 1 Chronicles 8:5.

introduce: He is a person who appears in Judges 9, recorded as the governor of the city when Abimelech ruled over Shechem (Judges 9:28, 30).
lifetime: He is recorded as the governor of the city of Shechem during the reign of Abimelech (Judges 9:28, 30). When Gaal spoke words of contempt for Abimelech, he heard them and was angry, and secretly sent messengers to Abimelech to tell him that Gaal and his brothers were stirring up the people of the city of Shechem to oppose Abimelech (Judges 9:30-31). After Gaal fought with Abimelech and was driven away and fled, he drove out Gaal and his brothers so that they could not dwell in Shechem (Judges 9:39-41).
event: He informed Abimelech of the news that Gaal was stirring up the men of Shechem and advised him to prepare in advance (Judges 9:31-33). When Gaal said that people were coming down from the top of the mountain, he answered that Gaal was seeing the shadows of the mountains as men (Judges 9:36), and then, citing Gaal's words that he would not serve Abimelech, told him to go out and fight (Judges 9:38). After Gaal fled, driven away by Abimelech, Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers so that they could not dwell in Shechem (Judges 9:39-41).
character: He was a man with strong loyalty to Abimelech, who had appointed him (Judges 9:30). He shows a strategic side, calmly answering Gaal's provocative words and leading him into a trap (Judges 9:38). He was an official with political sense who, by drawing out Gaal's true colors, gave Abimelech justification for suppressing the rebellion (Judges 9:38-39).

introduce: He is the sixth son born to Jacob and Leah and the tenth son of Jacob (Genesis 30:20). He is the person who became the ancestor of the tribe of Zebulun among the twelve tribes of Israel.
lifetime: He was born as Leah's sixth son. Leah said that God had given her a generous gift and that she had borne six sons to her husband, so now her husband would dwell with her, and she named him Zebulun (Genesis 30:20). When Jacob left the land of Canaan and moved with his family to Egypt, he took three sons with him (Genesis 46:14).
event: He is recorded among the twelve sons of Jacob as a son of Leah (Genesis 35:23). When Jacob blessed his twelve sons before his death, Zebulun received the prophecy that he would dwell by the seashore and become a place where ships are moored (Genesis 49:13).

직업/직위: progenitor of the tribe of Zebulun

call: Grandson of Moses (chief of the temple treasures)
introduce: Shebuel is a descendant of Gershom of the tribe of Levi, a grandson of Moses, and a person who was in charge of the storehouses in the time of David. He is also recorded as having become chief among the sons of Gershom (1 Chronicles 23:16, 26:24).
lifetime: Shebuel became chief among the sons of Gershom the son of Moses (1 Chronicles 23:15-16). When David was old and made Solomon king and gathered the Levites (1 Chronicles 23:1-2), he was recorded among the Levites whose duties were assigned as the one in charge of the storehouses (1 Chronicles 26:24).
event: Shebuel, a descendant of Gershom the son of Moses, was in charge of the storehouses (1 Chronicles 26:24). Shelomoth and his brothers, born of his brother Eliezer, were in charge of all the storehouses of the holy things (1 Chronicles 26:25-26).
character: In the biblical record no description of his personal temperament or inner traits appears. Yet from the fact that David trusted him as an administrator of the temple and entrusted him with important treasures, it can be seen that he held a trusted position within his family (1 Chronicles 26:24).

call: Son of Shobal (chief of the Horites)
introduce: Shepho is a person recorded as a son of Shobal, a descendant of Seir of the Horite people (1 Chronicles 1:38, 40). In the list of the children of Shobal in Genesis 36:23, he appears in the same place as Zepho.
lifetime: Shepho is a son of Shobal, a descendant of Seir of the Horite people in the land of Edom (1 Chronicles 1:38, 40). The sons of Shobal are Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam (1 Chronicles 1:40). Genesis 36:20-23 also lists Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam as children of Shobal, a descendant of Seir of the Horite people (Genesis 36:23).

introduce: Zebina is a person who appears in Ezra in the Old Testament, recorded as one of the descendants of Nebo (Ezra 10:43).
lifetime: He was a person belonging to the house of Nebo among the Israelites who returned from the Babylonian exile, and he is included in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:43).
event: In the course of the procedure of separation and divorce from foreign women led by Ezra, his name is mentioned as one of the offenders who had foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:43).

introduce: Zebidah is a person recorded as the mother of Jehoiakim king of Judah and the wife of Josiah.
lifetime: Zebidah is the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah and the mother of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah (2 Kings 23:34, 36). Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king and ruled eleven years in Jerusalem (2 Kings 23:36).

introduce: Sheariah is a person recorded as a descendant of the house of King Saul among the families of the tribe of Benjamin. He appears at the end of the genealogy listing the descendants of Jonathan, Saul's son, in 1 Chronicles 8 and 9.
lifetime: Sheariah is one of the six sons of Azel (Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan) (1 Chronicles 8:38). Azel belongs to a genealogy that continues down to the descendants of Merib-baal the son of Jonathan, Saul's son (1 Chronicles 8:33-38). The same list of six sons is recorded in the same order in 1 Chronicles 9:44 (1 Chronicles 9:44).

introduce: Sheal is a person who appears in Ezra 10 in the Old Testament, one of the descendants of Bani who had taken foreign women as wives within the community of Israel after the return from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 10:29).
lifetime: As a descendant of Bani, he lived as a member of the community of returned exiles (Ezra 10:29). When Ezra dealt with the problem of intermarriage in Jerusalem and carried out reform, he was included in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:29).
event: In accordance with the covenant led by Ezra to send away the foreign wives and their offspring, he was recorded in the list of men who had married foreign women (Ezra 10:29).

introduce: He is a son of Jehoiachin king of Judah, a person who carried on the bloodline of the royal house of David, and a royal descendant of Judah who was active in the period of the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Jeconiah who was taken captive to Babylon (1 Chronicles 3:17). In the genealogy of Jesus Christ in Matthew, it is recorded that after the exile to Babylon Jeconiah became the father of Shealtiel (Matthew 1:12). He is recorded as the father of Zerubbabel (Ezra 3:2, Nehemiah 12:1), and Zerubbabel is called governor of Judah in Haggai (Haggai 1:1).
event: In the genealogy of Matthew 1:12, Shealtiel is recorded as the one who fathered Zerubbabel. His son Zerubbabel, together with Jeshua the son of Jozadak, built the altar of God (Ezra 3:2) and began the building of the house of God (Ezra 5:2).

introduce: Shear-jashub is a person who appears in the book of Isaiah in the Old Testament, a son of the prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 7:3). His name carries the meaning that a remnant will return.
lifetime: He is a son of the prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 7:3). In the time of Ahaz king of Judah, in the situation where Rezin king of Aram and Pekah king of Israel had come up and attacked Jerusalem (Isaiah 7:1), the LORD told Isaiah to go out with his son Shear-jashub and meet Ahaz at the end of the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the highway to the Launderer's Field (Isaiah 7:3).
event: The LORD commanded Isaiah to go out with his son Shear-jashub and meet Ahaz at the end of the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the highway to the Launderer's Field (Isaiah 7:3). No words or actions of Shear-jashub himself are recorded in the text. Isaiah says that he and the children the LORD gave him became signs and symbols in Israel (Isaiah 8:18).

introduce: Zeeb is one of the princes of Midian, a person who held a leading position in the Midianite camp that confronted Gideon's army.
lifetime: Zeeb was one of the princes of Midian; he was captured together with Oreb and put to death at the winepress of Zeeb (Judges 7:25). His name is later mentioned together with Oreb in the Psalms as an example of the judgment that is sought upon enemies (Psalms 83:11).
event: Gideon sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim to strike the Midianites and to seize the fords as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan (Judges 7:24), and the two princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb, were captured; Zeeb was put to death at the winepress of Zeeb, and the heads of Oreb and Zeeb were brought to Gideon from the other side of the Jordan (Judges 7:25). Gideon said that God had delivered the Midianite princes Oreb and Zeeb into the hand of the men of Ephraim (Judges 8:3). The psalmist, asking that the nobles of his enemies become like Oreb and Zeeb, mentions him as a prince of Midian (Psalms 83:11).

introduce: Seorim is a person who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a descendant of Aaron and a person of the Levite priestly house mentioned in the process of reorganizing the priestly order in the time of King David.
lifetime: Seorim is recorded as the one on whom the fourth lot fell in the record of dividing the divisions of the descendants of Aaron in the time of David (1 Chronicles 24:8). It is not made clear in this verse whether he belongs to the descendants of Eleazar or to those of Ithamar.
event: When the descendants of Aaron were divided into the descendants of Eleazar and the descendants of Ithamar and lots were cast to fix the divisions in the time of David (1 Chronicles 24:3-5), Seorim was recorded fourth, after Jehoiarib the first, Jedaiah the second, and Harim the third (1 Chronicles 24:7-8).

introduce: Sheva is a person recorded as a scribe during the reign of King David. The biblical record reveals no information about his family line or private life, and he is named only as one on the list of David's officials.
lifetime: He is recorded as a scribe in the list of David's officials (2 Samuel 20:25). In this list Joab is recorded as commander of all the army of Israel, and Zadok and Abiathar as priests (2 Samuel 20:23-25).
event: He is recorded as holding the office of scribe in the list of David's officials (2 Samuel 20:25). Beyond that, no specific deeds are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Shehariah is a person recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the sons of Jeroham and a member of a house of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:26-27).
lifetime: Shehariah, as a son of Jeroham, is a person belonging to the family line of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:26-28).

introduce: Zohar is one of the six sons born to Simeon, a son of Jacob, a person who appears in the early genealogy of the tribes of Israel (Genesis 46:10).
lifetime: When Jacob left the land of Canaan with his sons and moved to Egypt, he put his name on the list of the family of Israel who went down to Egypt as a son of Simeon (Genesis 46:8-10). In the list of the sons of Simeon in Exodus 6:15, he is written as Zoar in the same place.
event: Apart from being entered in the genealogy as a son of Simeon at the time of the move to Egypt, no specific achievement or event that he personally carried out is recorded in the Bible (Genesis 46:10).

introduce: Shelomoth is a Levite who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a son of Izhar and a person belonging to the descendants of Kohath.
lifetime: He is recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Levi as a son of Izhar (1 Chronicles 24:22).
event: In the passage recording the divisions in the time of David, in the list of "the rest of the sons of Levi," Shelomoth is recorded among the sons of Izhar, and Jahath among the sons of Shelomoth (1 Chronicles 24:20, 1 Chronicles 24:22). 1 Chronicles 23:18 also records Shelomith as a chief among the sons of Izhar. The Shelomoth who was in charge of the storehouses of the holy things (1 Chronicles 26:25-26) belongs to the genealogy of those born of Eliezer the son of Moses (Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, Zichri, Shelomoth), and is therefore a different person from this one (1 Chronicles 23:15, 1 Chronicles 26:25).

introduce: Shelomi is a person who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, a man of the tribe of Asher, recorded as the father of Ahihud (Numbers 34:27). His son Ahihud was a man chosen from the tribe of Asher for the work of dividing the land of Canaan as an inheritance.
lifetime: Shelomi was a man of the tribe of the descendants of Asher, and in the text he is mentioned only as the father of Ahihud (Numbers 34:27). The LORD told Moses to choose one chief from each tribe to divide the land as an inheritance, and from the tribe of Asher, Ahihud the son of Shelomi was entered on the list (Numbers 34:18, Numbers 34:27).
event: Nothing Shelomi himself did is recorded. His son Ahihud, as chief of the tribe of the descendants of Asher, was entered on the list of those through whom the LORD would have the land of Canaan divided as an inheritance among the Israelites (Numbers 34:27, Numbers 34:29).

introduce: She is a person who appears in Leviticus in the Old Testament, the daughter of Dibri of the tribe of Dan. As an Israelite woman, she is recorded as the mother of a son born to her by an Egyptian man.
lifetime: She is recorded as the daughter of Dibri of the tribe of Dan (Leviticus 24:11), and her son is described as the son of an Israelite woman whose father was an Egyptian (Leviticus 24:10).
event: Her son went out among the Israelites and, fighting with an Israelite in the camp (Leviticus 24:10), blasphemed and cursed the name of the LORD, so the assembly brought him to Moses (Leviticus 24:11). They put him in custody and waited for the command of the LORD (Leviticus 24:12), and according to the command of the LORD (Leviticus 24:13-14) the Israelites brought the one who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him (Leviticus 24:23).

introduce: Zelophehad is a person who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, a son of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh, a grandson of Gilead, and a great-grandson of Machir. He died leaving only five daughters and no sons, and became the central figure of an important legal case concerning the law of inheritance.
lifetime: Zelophehad met his death in the wilderness among the Israelites who came out of Egypt. His daughters said that he had not been among the company of Korah that gathered against the LORD but had died in his own sin, and that he had no sons (Numbers 27:3). He had five daughters, Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah, but no sons (Numbers 26:33).
event: After Zelophehad's death, his five daughters asked Moses, the priest Eleazar, and the congregation to give them an inheritance so that their father's name would not be removed from his family (Numbers 27:1-4). Because of this, a ruling and statute was given that where there is no son the inheritance should pass to the daughter (Numbers 27:6-11). Afterward the heads of the families of the descendants of Gilead raised the problem that if the daughters married men of other tribes their inheritance would be diminished, and accordingly the command was given that the daughters of Zelophehad might marry whom they pleased, but only into a family of their ancestral tribe (Numbers 36:1-12).

introduce: Shelumiel is a person who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, a commander of the tribe of Simeon and a son of Zurishaddai.
lifetime: Shelumiel was appointed commander of the descendants of Simeon when the census was taken in the wilderness of Sinai after the exodus of the Israelites (Numbers 1:6). He served as one of the commanders representing each of the tribes of Israel (Numbers 2:12).
event: At the ceremony of presenting the dedication offerings made after the tabernacle was completed, he presented his offering on behalf of the tribe of Simeon (Numbers 7:36). The offerings he presented were the prescribed sacrifices, one silver platter, one silver bowl, and the bull, ram, and lambs and so on (Numbers 7:37-41). He also commanded the army of the tribe of Simeon in its marching column (Numbers 10:19).

introduce: Zichri is a person recorded as a grandson of Kohath of the tribe of Levi and a son of Izhar. Within the genealogical system of the Bible, he appears as one member who attests the bloodline of the Levite family.
lifetime: Zichri was born as a son of Izhar, the son of Kohath (Exodus 6:18, Exodus 6:21). The Bible says nothing more about his deeds or personal life after his birth.

introduce: Zina is a person recorded as a son of Shimei, one of the houses of the descendants of Gershon (1 Chronicles 23:10).
lifetime: Zina is a descendant of Gershon the son of Levi, and the descendants of Gershon are Ladan and Shimei (1 Chronicles 23:6-7). The sons of Shimei are four persons, Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah, and Zina is recorded as the second of them (1 Chronicles 23:10).
event: The text of the Bible records no particular event or concrete achievement that Zizah himself carried out. However, when David divided the descendants of Levi into divisions (1 Chronicles 23:6), he was recorded in the genealogy as a member of the house of Shimei, next after Jahath the chief (1 Chronicles 23:10-11).

introduce: Shinab is one of the kings of the ancient Near East recorded in the Bible, the king of Admah who appears in Genesis 14 (Genesis 14:2).
lifetime: As king of Admah, Shinab, together with Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, that is Zoar, fought against the four kings: Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim (Genesis 14:1-2). Nothing is recorded in the Bible about his later deeds or the time of his death.
event: Shinab, together with the five kings, served Chedorlaomer for twelve years and rebelled in the thirteenth year (Genesis 14:4), and in the fourteenth year, when Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him came out, he engaged them in battle in the Valley of Siddim (Genesis 14:5, Genesis 14:8-9). In this battle, when the king of Sodom and the king of Gomorrah fled, their soldiers fell into the tar pits and the rest fled to the hills (Genesis 14:10), and the four kings took all the goods and provisions of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 14:11).

call: Firstborn of Canaan (ancestor of the Sidonians)
introduce: Sidon is the firstborn of Canaan, the son of Ham the son of Noah, recorded as the ancestor of the Sidonian people who settled in the ancient Levant region. His name is directly related to the name of Sidon, an ancient city-state on the Mediterranean coast.
lifetime: He is recorded as the firstborn of Canaan the son of Ham, and Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn and Heth (Genesis 10:15, 1 Chronicles 1:13).
event: No individual deeds of Sidon are recorded in the Bible. In Genesis 10:19, which speaks of the borders of Canaan, the place name Sidon appears as the starting point of the border (Genesis 10:19).

introduce: He is a false prophet who was active in the time of Ahab king of Israel, a person called the son of Chenaanah. He is recorded as one of those who prophesied victory before the allied army of King Ahab and King Jehoshaphat attacked Ramoth-gilead.
lifetime: He appeared as one of the prophets when Ahab king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah consulted before going to attack Ramoth-gilead (1 Kings 22:11). He prophesied, making iron horns and assuring the kings of victory (2 Chronicles 18:10). Afterward, when the true prophet Micaiah prophesied disaster, he struck Micaiah on the cheek and reproached him (1 Kings 22:24).
event: He made iron horns and said that the word of the LORD was that the king would gore the Arameans with these until they were destroyed (1 Kings 22:11). When Micaiah said that the LORD had put a lying spirit in the mouth of the king's prophets (1 Kings 22:19-23), Zedekiah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, by which way did the Spirit of the LORD leave me to speak to you (1 Kings 22:24).
character: He showed an active drive in using a visual symbol, the iron horns, to display his own authority (1 Kings 22:11). He revealed an exclusive and violent disposition, such as physically attacking Micaiah, the true prophet who presented an opinion different from his own (1 Kings 22:24). To please the king, he distorted the will of God and showed an opportunistic side, guaranteeing victory together with many prophets (2 Chronicles 18:10).

introduce: Shitrai was a person who managed the herds of cattle grazing in Sharon during the reign of King David (1 Chronicles 27:29). He was singled out as one of the high officials who managed King David's property (1 Chronicles 27:29).
lifetime: In the time of David, Shitrai was active, holding the post of overseeing the herds in the plain of Sharon (1 Chronicles 27:29). When he was appointed, or what his life was afterward, is not recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 27:29).
event: King David appointed several managers to look after his livestock, and Shitrai carried out the role of being responsible for the herds grazing in Sharon (1 Chronicles 27:29). This means that he was active as a member of the organization that systematically managed David's royal property (1 Chronicles 27:29).

introduce: Sithri is a great-grandson of Levi and a son of Uzziel, a person mentioned together with Mishael and Elzaphan (Exodus 6:22). He is a cousin of Moses and Aaron, the leaders of Israel's exodus (Exodus 6:18-22).
lifetime: Sithri was born as a son of Uzziel (Exodus 6:22). His family line belongs to the genealogy that continues through Kohath the son of Levi and Uzziel the son of Kohath (Exodus 6:16, Exodus 6:18, Exodus 6:22).
event: In the biblical text there is no record that Sithri established any independent achievement or led any particular event (Exodus 6:22). His name is mentioned only as one of the sons of Uzziel in the process of listing the genealogy of the descendants of Levi (Exodus 6:22).

introduce: Simon Peter was a fisherman who cast nets at the shore of Galilee, the son of John and the brother of Andrew (Matthew 4:18, John 1:40, John 1:42). He was active as a key figure among the disciples who followed Jesus, and is recorded under the names Peter, Cephas, and Simeon in addition to Simon. Jesus called him Simon son of Jonah (Matthew 16:17), and said that He would call Simon the son of John Cephas in the future, which translated is Peter (John 1:42).
lifetime: A fisherman, he first met Jesus when his brother Andrew found him first and brought him to Jesus (John 1:40-42); in the midst of fishing he met Jesus and showed such awe that he asked Him to depart from him (Luke 5:8). In the end he was called by Jesus and became a disciple (Matthew 4:18-20). He followed Jesus and received His teaching, and it is also recorded that Jesus entered the house of Simon and Andrew with James and John (Mark 1:29). When Jesus went up the mountain of the transfiguration, He took him along with James and his brother John (Matthew 17:1); at the time of Jesus' arrest he drew his sword and cut off the right ear of the servant of the high priest (John 18:10); and after denying Jesus three times as Jesus had said, he remembered those words and wept bitterly (Matthew 26:75). After the resurrection of Jesus he was with the disciples when Jesus appeared to them at the Sea of Tiberias (John 21:1-2, John 21:7), and afterward he was active as a leading figure of the Jerusalem church (Acts 1:13, Galatians 2:9). The names Simon, Simeon, Cephas, and Peter are used together (Galatians 1:18, Acts 15:14, 2 Peter 1:1).
event: He made the confession to Jesus that He is the Christ, the Son of the living God (Matthew 16:16). When many disciples had withdrawn and Jesus asked the twelve whether they too wished to go away, he answered, "To whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life" (John 6:66-68). On the mountain of transfiguration he saw Jesus together with Moses and Elijah and said that he would build three shelters (Matthew 17:1-4). When Jesus was about to wash the disciples' feet, he at first would not let Him wash his own, but afterward asked that not only his feet but also his hands and head be washed (John 13:6, John 13:9). When the disciples were uncertain about whom Jesus was speaking of, he motioned with his head to the disciple reclining on Jesus' breast, telling him to ask who it was that Jesus meant (John 13:22-24). At the time Jesus was arrested he was the one who cut off with a sword the right ear of Malchus, the servant of the high priest (John 18:10). On the day of Pentecost he raised his voice and spoke before the people of Jerusalem (Acts 2:14), and those who received his word were baptized, so that about three thousand were added to the disciples that day (Acts 2:41). At the Beautiful Gate of the temple he raised up a man lame from birth in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth (Acts 3:6-7). When he was preaching at the house of Cornelius and the Holy Spirit came down on the Gentiles, he commanded that they be baptized (Acts 10:44-48). At the council in Jerusalem he said that God had chosen that the Gentiles should hear the word of the gospel from his mouth (Acts 15:7), and it is recorded that in Antioch, when he was eating with the Gentiles but drew back out of fear of the circumcision party, he was rebuked by Paul (Galatians 2:11-14).
character: He showed himself aware of his own sinfulness and feeling fear before Jesus (Luke 5:8). Through his own hasty judgment he tried to walk on the water, but began to sink out of fear (Matthew 14:28-30). He had a side that expressed his own will strongly, such as first refusing to let Jesus wash his feet and then asking that his head and hands be washed as well (John 13:8-9). When Jesus foretold that He would suffer, he tried to stop Him and was rebuked (Matthew 16:22-23). On the other hand, he answered Jesus' questions immediately and played a leading role among the disciples (Matthew 16:16). Paul mentioned him as one of those regarded as pillars of the church (Galatians 2:9).

introduce: He is a person recorded as the first of the six sons born to Abraham and his later wife Keturah (Genesis 25:1-2).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons born to Keturah, Abraham's later wife (Genesis 25:1-2, 1 Chronicles 1:32). Abraham gave gifts to his sons by concubines as well, and during his own lifetime sent them away from his son Isaac to the east country (Genesis 25:6).
event: In the biblical record no specific deeds or accomplishments of Zimran himself are mentioned. There is only the record that Abraham's sons by concubines were sent away from Isaac to the east (Genesis 25:6).

introduce: Shimrath is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the descendants of the tribe of Benjamin to which the house of King Saul belonged.
lifetime: Shimrath is recorded as one of the sons of Shimei together with Adaiah and Beraiah, and belongs to the genealogy of the house of the tribe of Benjamin that lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:21, 1 Chronicles 8:28).

introduce: Shimron is a person recorded in the Bible, one of the sons of Issachar the son of Jacob and a grandson of Jacob.
lifetime: Shimron is mentioned as one of the sons of Issachar who went down with Jacob when he moved to Egypt (Genesis 46:13). As a descendant of Jacob, he is classified as a member of a house that formed a tribe of Israel (Numbers 26:24).
event: Shimron became the ancestor of the Shimronite clan (Numbers 26:24). Also, in 1 Chronicles 7:1, Shimron's name is included when the genealogy of the sons of Issachar is listed (1 Chronicles 7:1).

introduce: Zimri is a person who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, a chief of the tribe of Simeon and a son of Salu. He is recorded as one of the central figures in the incident at Shittim, when in the course of the exodus the Israelites committed immorality with Moabite women and took part in idol worship.
lifetime: Zimri was a son of Salu and a chief of one of the clans of the Simeonites (Numbers 25:14). While Israel was staying at Shittim and committing immorality with the women of Moab (Numbers 25:1), he came to his brothers bringing the Midianite woman Cozbi in the sight of Moses and the whole congregation (Numbers 25:6, Numbers 25:14-15), and was put to death by Phinehas the son of the priest Eleazar (Numbers 25:7-8).
event: While the Israelites were staying at Shittim, committing immorality with the women of Moab and bowing down to the gods of those women (Numbers 25:1-2), Zimri brought the Midianite woman Cozbi in the sight of Moses and the whole congregation as the whole congregation was weeping at the entrance to the tent of meeting (Numbers 25:6, Numbers 25:14-15). Seeing this, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the grandson of the priest Aaron, rose up, took a spear in his hand, followed that Israelite man into his tent, and pierced the Israelite man and the woman through the belly, killing both of them, and the plague was stopped from the Israelites (Numbers 25:7-8).

introduce: Shimrith is a Moabite woman, recorded as the mother of Jehozabad, one of the servants who conspired against Joash king of Judah (2 Chronicles 24:26).
lifetime: Shimrith is recorded as a woman from Moab, and her son Jehozabad appears as one of those who conspired against King Joash (2 Chronicles 24:26).
event: Her son Jehozabad is recorded as one of those who conspired against King Joash, together with Zabad the son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman (2 Chronicles 24:26). The servants of Joash conspired and struck him down and killed him (2 Chronicles 24:25).

introduce: Shimeah is a descendant of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon of the tribe of Benjamin, and a son of Mikloth. He is recorded in 1 Chronicles 8 and 9 as one of the persons who make up the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: Shimeah is mentioned as a descendant of Jeiel, who lived in Gibeon, in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:29-32). As a son of Mikloth, he lived in Jerusalem alongside his brothers, opposite them (1 Chronicles 8:32; 1 Chronicles 9:38 writes the name as Shimeam).
event: It is recorded that Shimeah, whom Mikloth fathered, lived with this group in Jerusalem alongside his brothers, opposite them (1 Chronicles 8:32; 1 Chronicles 9:38).

call: Ammonite woman (mother of the assassin of Joash)
introduce: Shimeath is the mother of one of the servants who conspired against and killed Joash king of Judah. She is recorded as an Ammonite woman, and appears within the biblical text with very limited personal details.
lifetime: Shimeath was a woman from Ammon, and her son is recorded as a servant who conspired against Joash. The son's name appears as Jozabad in 2 Kings 12:21 and as Zabad in 2 Chronicles 24:26.
event: The servant recorded as Shimeath's son (Jozabad in 2 Kings 12:21, Zabad in 2 Chronicles 24:26) conspired together with the servants of Joash and killed King Joash at the house of Millo, on the road that goes down to Silla (2 Kings 12:20-21).

call: Second son of Jacob (ancestor of the tribe of Simeon)
introduce: Simeon is the second son born to Jacob and Leah, and the ancestor of the tribe of Simeon, one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
lifetime: He is the second son of Jacob, born through Leah (Genesis 29:33). After the incident at Shechem he led the act of revenge (Genesis 34:25), and together with his brothers he envied Joseph, threw him into a pit, and sold him into slavery in Egypt (Genesis 37:28). When they went to buy grain in Egypt, where Joseph was prime minister, he was taken hostage by Joseph and imprisoned in Egypt (Genesis 42:24), and later he moved with the family of Jacob to Egypt and settled there (Genesis 46:10).
event: When his younger sister Dinah was raped by the chief of Shechem, he and Levi used circumcision as a pretext to kill the men of Shechem (Genesis 34:25-26). When Joseph was testing his brothers, Joseph bound Simeon and imprisoned him before their eyes (Genesis 42:24). Just before his death, Jacob mentioned the cruel violence Simeon had committed and prophesied that he would be scattered among his brothers (Genesis 49:5-7).
character: Simeon is described as a person with a passionate and violent disposition. He could not control his own emotions and showed a cold-bloodedness in devising a scheme for revenge (Genesis 34:13), and this temperament became the reason Jacob assessed him as an instrument of cruelty (Genesis 49:5).

introduce: Shimei is a son of Gershon of the tribe of Levi, the ancestor of the Shimeite clan belonging to the descendants of Gershon among the Levites (Exodus 6:17).
lifetime:
He was born as a son of Gershon the son of Levi (Numbers 3:17-18).
His brother was Libni (Exodus 6:17).
He had four sons: Jahath, Zina (Ziza), Jeush, and Beriah (1 Chronicles 23:10).
Because Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, they were counted as one clan (1 Chronicles 23:11).
event:
The Shimeite family, named after him, formed one branch of the Gershonite families (Numbers 3:21).
The Gershonite families (the Libnite family and the Shimeite family) camped behind the tabernacle, that is, on the west (Numbers 3:23).
The descendants of Gershon were in charge of the tabernacle and the tent, its covering, and the curtain of the entrance to the tent of meeting (Numbers 3:25-26).

introduce: Ziphion is a descendant of Gad the son of Jacob, a person included in the list of Jacob's family who left the land of Canaan and moved to Egypt.
lifetime: Ziphion is a son of Gad, one of Gad's sons Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli (Genesis 46:16). His name is on the list of the Israelite family who went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:8, 46:16).

call: Grandfather of Oholibamah (chief of the Hivites)
introduce: Zibeon is a person who appears in Genesis in the Old Testament, a chief of the Horite people who lived in the hill country of Seir. He is the father of Anah and is recorded as the grandfather of Oholibamah, one of Esau's wives.
lifetime: Zibeon was a descendant of Seir of the Horite people, the original inhabitants of the land of Seir (Genesis 36:20), and had Aiah and Anah as children (Genesis 36:24). His granddaughter Oholibamah became a wife of Esau (Genesis 36:2, 36:14).
event: Zibeon's son Anah found hot springs in the wilderness while he was tending his father Zibeon's donkeys (Genesis 36:24). Zibeon is recorded as one of the chiefs of the Horites in the land of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan (Genesis 36:29-30).

introduce: Shiphi is a person belonging to the tribe of Simeon, a son of Allon and the father of Ziza, recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:37.
lifetime: Shiphi is recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Simeon as the son of Allon and the father of Ziza (1 Chronicles 4:37). Ziza is introduced as the son of Shiphi and the grandson of Allon (1 Chronicles 4:37).
event: No deeds of Shiphi himself are recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 4:37).

introduce: Zibiah is the mother of Joash, a king of the kingdom of Judah, and a woman from Beersheba.
lifetime: When Joash the son of Ahaziah (2 Kings 11:2) became king in the seventh year of Jehu, the name of his mother is recorded as Zibiah (2 Kings 12:1). She is recorded as a woman of Beersheba (2 Kings 12:1).
event: Her son Joash became king of Judah at the age of seven and ruled in Jerusalem for forty years, and the name of his mother is recorded as Zibiah (2 Chronicles 24:1; 2 Kings 12:1).

introduce: Zibia is a person recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the sons whom Shaharaim fathered by his wife Hodesh (1 Chronicles 8:9).
lifetime: Zibia is a son born of Hodesh, among the children Shaharaim had in the land of Moab after he sent away his two wives Hushim and Baara (1 Chronicles 8:8-9). He is recorded as one of Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam, Jeuz, Sachia, and Mirmah (1 Chronicles 8:9-10).

introduce: Ziza is a person from the house of the descendants of Simeon, mentioned as one of the chiefs who moved in search of pasture in the time of King Hezekiah (1 Chronicles 4:37-41).
lifetime: Ziza, as a descendant of Simeon, is recorded as the son of Shiphi, the grandson of Allon, the great-grandson of Jedaiah, the great-great-grandson of Shimri, and the fifth-generation descendant of Shemaiah (1 Chronicles 4:37). Together with those who were enrolled by name before him, he is recorded as a chief of his own clan (1 Chronicles 4:38).
event: Ziza, together with the chiefs enrolled by name before him, sought pasture for their flocks and reached the territory of Gedor on the east side of the valley (1 Chronicles 4:39). They found rich and good pasture (1 Chronicles 4:40), and in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah they struck down the tents of the people who were there and destroyed the Meunites, and then settled in their place (1 Chronicles 4:41).

introduce: Shishak is the king of Egypt who invaded Judah in the fifth year of King Rehoboam, attacked Jerusalem, and seized the treasures of the house of the LORD and of the royal palace (1 Kings 14:25-26).
lifetime: When Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, Jeroboam fled to Egypt, came to Shishak king of Egypt, and stayed in Egypt until Solomon died (1 Kings 11:40). Afterward, in the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak came up and attacked Jerusalem (1 Kings 14:25).
event: Shishak, leading 1,200 chariots, 60,000 horsemen, and a countless host of Libyans, Sukkites, and Cushites who came with him out of Egypt, took the fortified cities of Judah and came to Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 12:3-4). He took everything from the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the royal palace, and also took the gold shields that Solomon had made (1 Kings 14:26; 2 Chronicles 12:9). Afterward Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and committed them to the hands of the captains of the guard who kept the entrance of the palace (2 Chronicles 12:10).

introduce: He was the commander of the army of Jabin king of Canaan and lived in Harosheth-hagoyim (Judges 4:2). He is the person who led the army at the time when King Jabin had harshly oppressed the Israelites for twenty years with nine hundred iron chariots (Judges 4:2-3).
lifetime: As commander of Jabin's army, he gathered nine hundred iron chariots and all his troops from Harosheth-hagoyim to the river Kishon (Judges 4:13), and confronted the army of Barak, who came down from Mount Tabor at the word of Deborah (Judges 4:6-7, 4:14). After being defeated in the battle, he fled and reached the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite (Judges 4:17). While he was sound asleep there, he was killed when the peg Jael drove pierced his temple (Judges 4:21).
event: Sisera gathered nine hundred iron chariots and all the troops with him from Harosheth-hagoyim to the river Kishon (Judges 4:13). When the LORD routed Sisera and all his chariots and all his army with the edge of the sword before Barak, Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot, and all his army fell by the sword (Judges 4:15-16). Afterward Jael welcomed him, brought him into her tent, and covered him, but Sisera was killed in the tent by the peg Jael drove (Judges 4:18-22).
character: He was a capable military strategist of his time who commanded a mighty force of iron chariots, but when the tide of battle turned against him he abandoned his chariot and fled (Judges 4:15). Judging that there was peace with the house of Heber the Kenite, he chose Jael's tent as a refuge, but was deceived by the enemy and met his end defenseless (Judges 4:17, 4:21).

introduce: Sismai is a person belonging to the genealogy of the house of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah, the son of Elasah and the father of Shallum (1 Chronicles 2:39-40).
lifetime: Sismai is recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah as the son fathered by Elasah the son of Helez, and he fathered Shallum (1 Chronicles 2:40).

introduce: Siaha is a person who appears in Ezra and Nehemiah in the Old Testament, one of the families of the Nethinim who returned to Jerusalem after finishing their time in the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: Among those who returned from the Babylonian exile, his name is included among the descendants of Siaha in the list of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:44). In the register of the first to return, which Nehemiah obtained, the same list is found, and there it is recorded as "the descendants of Sia" (Nehemiah 7:5, 7:47).
event: As a member of the Nethinim who carried out the work of temple service in the temple at Jerusalem, he was included in the community of returned exiles and came back to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:44). In the register of the first to return, which Nehemiah obtained, this family is also recorded as Nethinim (Nehemiah 7:5, 7:47).

introduce: Ziha is one of the families of the Nethinim who appear in Ezra and Nehemiah in the Old Testament. He is included in the list of those who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:43).
lifetime: The descendants of Ziha were entered as Nethinim in the list of the people of Israel who came out with Zerubbabel and others after the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:2, 2:43). Their names are mentioned again in the register of the first to return, which Nehemiah obtained (Nehemiah 7:5, 7:46).
event: The descendants of Ziha were entered in the list of the returned exiles as one family of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:43; Nehemiah 7:46). It is recorded that later, when the Nethinim lived in Ophel, Ziha and Gishpa became their chiefs (Nehemiah 11:21).

introduce: Sihon was the king of the Amorite people who ruled centered on Heshbon, east of the Jordan. He appears in biblical history as one who clashed with Israel on the route as the people of Israel headed toward Canaan.
lifetime: Sihon struck the former king of Moab and seized all his land as far as the Arnon, and Heshbon was his capital city (Numbers 21:26). Afterward he would not permit the passage through his land that the messengers sent by Israel requested (Numbers 21:21-23). He fought with Israel at Jahaz but was defeated, and Israel took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok (Numbers 21:23-24). The land he had ruled was afterward given by Moses to the descendants of Gad, the descendants of Reuben, and the half tribe of Manasseh (Numbers 32:33).
event: Sihon struck the former king of Moab and seized all his land as far as the Arnon (Numbers 21:26). He would not permit Israel to pass through, but gathered all his people, came out into the wilderness, and attacked Israel (Numbers 21:23). In this battle Sihon, with his sons and all his people, was defeated by Israel, and Israel took all his cities (Deuteronomy 2:32-34). It is recorded that Moses struck down and killed Sihon the Amorite king who lived in Heshbon (Deuteronomy 1:4). Joshua 12:2 records that the land he ruled extended from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon valley to half of Gilead, that is, to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.
character: Sihon had a military and defensive temperament that responded firmly to protect his own territory (Numbers 21:23). He was a ruler with expansionist ambition, enough to conquer by force the territory of another people, Moab (Numbers 21:26). Also, he showed a disposition in foreign relations of giving priority to a show of force rather than compromise, to the point of rejecting Israel's request for peaceful passage and immediately mobilizing military power (Deuteronomy 2:30).

introduce: Zillethai is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as one of the sons of Shimei (1 Chronicles 8:19-21).
lifetime: Zillethai is named in the genealogy as one of the sons of Shimei: Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath (1 Chronicles 8:19-21).

introduce: Zilpah is the maidservant of Leah, the wife of Jacob, whom Laban of Paddan-aram gave as a servant when he gave his daughter Leah in marriage to Jacob (Genesis 29:24). She is one of the four women who bore children to Jacob, and in the midst of the rivalry between Leah and Rachel she gave birth to children of Jacob and became a member of Jacob's family line.
lifetime: When Leah saw that she had stopped bearing, she gave her maidservant Zilpah to Jacob to be his concubine (Genesis 30:9). When Zilpah bore Jacob a son, Leah named him Gad (Genesis 30:10-11), and when she then bore a second son, Leah named him Asher (Genesis 30:12-13). The offspring of Zilpah are Gad and Asher, and they are sons of Jacob (Genesis 35:26). The descendants born to Jacob by Zilpah, whom Laban had given to his daughter Leah, are sixteen in all (Genesis 46:18).
event: As the maidservant of Leah, Zilpah bore Gad and Asher to Jacob (Genesis 30:10-13; 35:26). The descendants born to Jacob by Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah, are sixteen and are recorded in the genealogy of the house of Jacob (Genesis 46:18).

introduce: Shilshah is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher recorded in 1 Chronicles 7 in the Old Testament, recorded as one of the sons of Zophah (1 Chronicles 7:36-37).
lifetime: Shilshah is recorded as one of the sons fathered by Zophah the son of Helem among the descendants of Asher (Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah, Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera) (1 Chronicles 7:35-37). He is mentioned as a genealogical member who forms the genealogy of the tribe of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:37).

introduce: The mother of Jehoshaphat, the fourth king of the kingdom of Judah, is Azubah. The father of Azubah is Shilhi.
lifetime: Shilhi is the father of Azubah and the maternal grandfather of King Jehoshaphat (1 Kings 22:42), (2 Chronicles 20:31).

introduce: Zimmah is a descendant of Gershon of the tribe of Levi, a son of Jahath, and a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Levi in 1 Chronicles 6 (1 Chronicles 6:20).
lifetime: Zimmah is recorded as the son of Jahath the son of Libni, who was born of Gershon the son of Levi, and his son is recorded as Joah (1 Chronicles 6:20-21).

introduce: Shimshai is a scribe who, in the time of Artaxerxes king of Persia, together with Rehum the commander, sent the king a letter accusing the people of Jerusalem (Ezra 4:8). The decree the king issued was also sent to Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates living in Samaria (Ezra 4:17).
lifetime: Shimshai is one of those who sent King Artaxerxes a letter accusing the people of Jerusalem (Ezra 4:8-9). When the copy of the decree of King Artaxerxes was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates, they went in haste to Jerusalem and restrained the Jews by force so that the work ceased (Ezra 4:23).
event: Shimshai's name was entered as scribe in the letter sent to King Artaxerxes together with Rehum (Ezra 4:8). That letter said that if the Jews built the city and finished the walls, they would no longer pay tribute, customs, or toll, and that in the end it would be to the harm of the kings (Ezra 4:12-13). The king sent a decree to Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates, commanding them to make those men stop the work so that the city would not be built (Ezra 4:17-21), and when the copy of the decree was read, they went in haste to Jerusalem and by force made them stop the work (Ezra 4:23).

introduce: Ziph is a name connected with the house of Caleb of the tribe of Judah, and in 1 Chronicles 2:42 Mesha, the firstborn of Caleb, is recorded as "the father of Ziph."
lifetime: Following the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, he is recorded as a descendant of Mesha, a son of Caleb (1 Chronicles 2:42).
event: In the biblical record no specific deeds or particular events of this person himself are described separately (1 Chronicles 2:42).

introduce: Shiphtan is a person recorded as the father of Kemuel, who was chosen from the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim to divide the land (Numbers 34:24).
lifetime: There is no record in the Bible about Shiphtan's own life; Numbers 34:24 merely introduces Kemuel of the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim as "the son of Shiphtan."
event: Nothing Shiphtan himself did is recorded. The LORD told them to choose one chief from each tribe to divide the land as an inheritance (Numbers 34:18), and in that list Kemuel of the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim is recorded as the son of Shiphtan (Numbers 34:24).

introduce: Sippai is one of "the sons of the giant" who was killed by Sibbecai the Hushathite when war was fought with the Philistines at Gezer (1 Chronicles 20:4).
lifetime: Sippai is recorded as a man whom Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down from among the sons of the giant when war was fought with the Philistines at Gezer (1 Chronicles 20:4). 2 Samuel 21:18 records that in the war at Gob, Sibbecai struck down and killed Saph from among the sons of the giant.
event: In the war with the Philistines at Gezer, Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down and killed Sippai from among the sons of the giant (1 Chronicles 20:4). Nothing that Sippai himself did is recorded in the text.
character: Sippai is of the giant race classified as descendants of the Rephaim (1 Chronicles 20:4).

introduce: Zipporah is one of the seven daughters of the priest of Midian and the wife of Moses. She was given to Moses as a wife when he fled from Egypt to the land of Midian, and she bore two sons.
lifetime: While Moses, fleeing from the face of Pharaoh, was staying in the land of Midian and sitting by a well, he came to know that household through the occasion of helping the seven daughters of the priest of Midian, who were being driven away by the shepherds, and watering their flock (Exodus 2:15-17). When Moses was pleased to live with them, her father gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses (Exodus 2:21). Zipporah bore two sons by Moses, Gershom and Eliezer (Exodus 2:22, 18:3-4). When Moses was in danger of death at a lodging place on the way as he was returning to Egypt, Zipporah cut off her son's foreskin (Exodus 4:24-25). Afterward Moses' father-in-law Jethro brought Zipporah, Moses' wife, whom Moses had sent back, together with her two sons, to Moses in the wilderness, and they were reunited (Exodus 18:2-6).
event: As Moses was returning to Egypt after being called by God, the LORD met Moses at a lodging place on the way and was about to kill him (Exodus 4:24). At that time Zipporah took a flint, cut off her son's foreskin, threw it at Moses' feet, and said, "Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me" (Exodus 4:25). Afterward the LORD let Moses alone, and the "bridegroom of blood" that Zipporah spoke of was because of circumcision (Exodus 4:26).
character: Zipporah is portrayed as a person who acts swiftly and decisively in a crisis (Exodus 4:25). Recognizing that Moses, her own family, was under threat of death, she immediately performed the rite of circumcision and resolved the problem (Exodus 4:25). Also, as a foreigner she became the wife of Moses, a Hebrew leader, and lived a life of sharing hardship with him (Exodus 2:21-22).

introduce: Zippor is a person recorded as the father of Balak. The Bible mentions him only in the expression "Balak son of Zippor" (Numbers 22:2).
lifetime: Zippor is mentioned only as the father of Balak, and no specific dates or activities of his life are recorded (Numbers 22:2). The verses where Balak is called "the son of Zippor" are Numbers 22:2, 22:4, 22:10, 22:16, 23:18, Joshua 24:9, and Judges 11:25.
event: In the biblical text no specific event or accomplishment that Zippor himself carried out appears. There is only the record that his son Balak, as king of Moab, summoned Balaam to have him curse Israel (Numbers 22:4-6, Joshua 24:9).

introduce: Sibbecai is a person who appears in the Old Testament, one of the mighty men who were David's elite troops, recorded as a Hushathite.
lifetime: Sibbecai is recorded among David's mighty men as "Sibbecai the Hushathite" (1 Chronicles 11:26-29). He was the eighth commander, for the eighth month, in the divisions of the army that David set up, a Hushathite of the Zerahite clan, and his division numbered 24,000 men (1 Chronicles 27:11).
event: In the war with the Philistines at Gob, Sibbecai struck down and killed Saph from among the sons of the giant (2 Samuel 21:18). Also, in the war with the Philistines at Gezer, he struck down and killed Sippai from among the sons of the giant (1 Chronicles 20:4).
character: In the biblical record Sibbecai is portrayed as a core military leader of David, a man of outstanding martial strength (2 Samuel 23:27). He possessed such outstanding fighting ability that he brought down a Philistine giant, and he held an important position in the military system of the early Davidic dynasty (1 Chronicles 27:11).

introduce: Shiphrah is one of the Hebrew midwives who appear in the early part of Exodus, a person who disobeyed the command of the king of Egypt and let the Hebrew baby boys live.
lifetime: The king of Egypt told the Hebrew midwives Shiphrah and Puah to kill the baby if it was a boy when a Hebrew woman gave birth (Exodus 1:15-16). But the midwives feared God, disobeyed the king of Egypt's command, and let the boys live (Exodus 1:17). Afterward, when the king summoned the midwives and asked why, the midwives answered Pharaoh that the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women but are vigorous and give birth before the midwife arrives (Exodus 1:18-19).
event: Shiphrah, together with Puah, disobeyed the king of Egypt's command and let the boys live (Exodus 1:17). God was good to those midwives, and the people multiplied and became strong, and because the midwives feared God, God made their households prosper (Exodus 1:20-21).
character: Shiphrah is portrayed as a person with an attitude of fearing God rather than fearing the king's command (Exodus 1:17). She also had the wisdom and boldness to respond logically without being flustered even before the king of Egypt (Exodus 1:19).

introduce: Zeus is the name of a god in Acts. The crowd that saw the lame man stand up at Lystra called Barnabas Zeus (Acts 14:12), and the priest of the temple of Zeus outside the city brought bulls and wreaths, wishing to offer sacrifice (Acts 14:13). In the words of the city clerk of Ephesus too, an image that fell from Zeus is mentioned (Acts 19:35).
event: The crowd that saw what Paul did at Lystra cried out in the Lycaonian language that the gods had come down in the likeness of men, and they called Barnabas Zeus, and since Paul was the chief speaker, they called him Hermes (Acts 14:11-12). The priest of the temple of Zeus outside the city came to the gate with bulls and wreaths and wished to offer sacrifice together with the crowd (Acts 14:13). Barnabas and Paul tore their clothes, rushed into the crowd, and cried out that they too were men of the same nature, urging them to turn from these vain things to the living God, and with difficulty restrained the crowd from offering sacrifice (Acts 14:14-15, 14:18).

introduce: Zillah is a person in the Bible's record belonging to the line of Cain, one of the two wives of Lamech. She is recorded as the mother who bore Tubal-cain.
lifetime: Zillah is mentioned as a wife of Lamech, a woman whom Lamech took as a wife besides Adah (Genesis 4:19). She bore Tubal-cain to Lamech (Genesis 4:22). Also, when Lamech sang to his wives, he called Zillah by name and made her an addressee of the conversation (Genesis 4:23).
event: Zillah bore Tubal-cain, and Tubal-cain was a maker of various sharp implements out of copper and iron (Genesis 4:22). Her husband Lamech called Zillah and Adah and told them that he had killed a man, saying that they should listen to his song (Genesis 4:23).

introduce: Agabus was a prophet who was active in the era of the early church; moved by the Holy Spirit, he served by foretelling future events.
lifetime: Agabus was one of the prophets who came down from Jerusalem to Antioch (Acts 11:27-28). Later he came down from Judea to Caesarea, met Paul, and performed an act foretelling his binding (Acts 21:10-11). No other record of his birth or detailed life has been handed down.
event: Rising up among the prophets who came from Jerusalem to Antioch, he said by the Holy Spirit that there would be a great famine over all the world, and this came to pass in the days of Claudius (Acts 11:27-28). Also, at Caesarea he came to Paul, took Paul's belt, bound his own feet and hands, and said that the Holy Spirit declared: "So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man who owns this belt and deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles" (Acts 21:10-11).
character: He is portrayed as a person with prophetic authority who received revelation from the Holy Spirit directly (Acts 11:28). Going beyond mere verbal prophecy, he used a visual prophetic technique, conveying his message through symbolic action (Acts 21:11).

introduce: Achaicus is mentioned in 1 Corinthians 16:17 as one of those who came to Paul together with Stephanas and Fortunatus.
lifetime: He came to Paul together with Stephanas and Fortunatus, and Paul rejoiced at their coming (1 Corinthians 16:17). The rest of his life is not recorded in Scripture.
event: Paul said that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus had supplied what was lacking on the part of the Corinthians. He also said that they had refreshed his spirit and theirs, and urged the Corinthians to give recognition to such men (1 Corinthians 16:17-18).

introduce: Agag is recorded as a king of the Amalekites in the time of Saul. When Saul struck Amalek, he was taken captive and was then put to death by Samuel (1 Samuel 15:8, 15:33). The name "Agag" also appears in Numbers 24:7.
lifetime: Agag was taken captive when Saul struck Amalek (1 Samuel 15:8). Afterward he was brought before Samuel at Samuel's command (1 Samuel 15:32), and Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the LORD at Gilgal (1 Samuel 15:33).
event: Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep and of the oxen, or the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good, and were not willing to destroy them utterly (1 Samuel 15:9). Samuel had Agag brought, and when Agag said, "Surely the bitterness of death is past" (1 Samuel 15:32), Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the LORD at Gilgal (1 Samuel 15:33). Esther 3:1 records Haman as "the son of Hammedatha the Agagite," but the relationship of this man to King Agag is not stated in the text.
character: In 1 Samuel 15:32, Agag is portrayed as expressing a sense of relief at the moment his death was imminent, saying that the bitterness of death was surely past. This brief statement shows that he had not fully grasped his fate, or that he was facing the terror of death (1 Samuel 15:32).

introduce: Agee is recorded as the father of Shammah, one of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:11).
lifetime: Little is known about the life of Agee; 2 Samuel 23:11 records "Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite," and the only thing confirmed is that he was Shammah's father.
event: No independent achievement or event of Agee himself is recorded in Scripture. However, it is recorded that his son Shammah, when the Philistines gathered in a troop at a plot of ground full of lentils, stood in the midst of that plot and struck down the Philistines (2 Samuel 23:11-12).

introduce: A figure who appears in Proverbs 30, recorded as the son of Jakeh. He is regarded as one of the authors of Proverbs, and his words are classified as the proverbs of Agur.
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Jakeh (Proverbs 30:1). Proverbs 30:1 introduces his proverbs as addressed to Ithiel and Ucal. There is no other record concerning his birth or origin.
event: He left a proverb confessing his lack of knowledge by likening himself to a beast (Proverbs 30:2-3). He offered a prayer to God asking that He give him neither poverty nor riches but feed him with the food that is needful (Proverbs 30:8-9). He observed and recorded the order of the various phenomena and things of the world (Proverbs 30:15-31), and these records are now preserved in Proverbs 30 of the Bible.
character: He humbly lowered himself, describing himself as a dull person who had not learned the knowledge of God (Proverbs 30:2-3). He showed a strong ethical stance of keeping falsehood and lies far from him (Proverbs 30:8). He displayed a prudence that aims at the middle way, guarding against the ill effects that excessive wealth or extreme poverty can bring (Proverbs 30:8-9).

introduce: Aquila is a figure in the New Testament, a Jew born in Pontus, who was active as a coworker of the apostle Paul together with his wife Priscilla. His occupation was making tents.
lifetime: A Jew born in Pontus, he had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to leave Rome (Acts 18:2). Paul went to them, stayed with them, and worked (Acts 18:2-3). Afterward, when Paul sailed for Syria, Priscilla and Aquila went with him, and Paul left them at Ephesus (Acts 18:18-19). In Romans 16:3-5 Paul tells the believers to greet Prisca and Aquila, and to greet the church that is in their house.
event: He met Paul at Corinth and worked together with him at the same trade of making tents (Acts 18:2-3). At Ephesus, when Apollos began to speak boldly in the synagogue, Priscilla and Aquila heard him, took him aside, and explained the way of God to him more accurately (Acts 18:24-26). Paul said of them that they risked their own necks for his life (Romans 16:4).
character: He showed a devoted attitude, to the point of offering his own house as a meeting place for the church (1 Corinthians 16:19). He also had a cooperative disposition, letting the apostle Paul, who had come from elsewhere, stay in his home and supporting him in both economic and practical ways (Acts 18:2-3). He is a figure marked by the unity in ministry between husband and wife, being always mentioned together with his wife Priscilla (Acts 18:18, Romans 16:3).

기타관계: Claudius#237(Roman emperor who ordered the expulsion)

introduce: Agrippa is a king who appears in Acts 25–26. He came to Caesarea with Bernice, visited the governor Festus, and heard the defense of the apostle Paul.
lifetime: King Agrippa came to Caesarea with Bernice and greeted Festus (Acts 25:13). He told Festus that he wished to hear Paul himself (Acts 25:22), and the next day he entered the audience hall with Bernice amid great pomp (Acts 25:23). He permitted Paul to speak (Acts 26:1), and Paul said that he knew all the customs and questions of the Jews (Acts 26:3).
event: When Paul asked, "King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets?", Agrippa said, "In a short time you would persuade me to be a Christian" (Acts 26:27-28). The king, the governor, Bernice, and those who sat with them withdrew and said to one another that this man was doing nothing to deserve death or imprisonment (Acts 26:30-31), and Agrippa said to Festus that this man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar (Acts 26:32).
character: Herod Agrippa I, to strengthen his own political position, fell in step with the leaders of Judaism and took the political course of persecuting Christians (Acts 12:3). Herod Agrippa II had considerable knowledge of Jewish customs and religious matters, and when he listened to the apostle Paul's defense he showed a certain degree of intellectual interest in the message Paul delivered (Acts 26:3, 26:27-28).

meaning: The LORD protects, the LORD appears
introduce: Achish was a king of the Philistine region of Gath, a ruler who appears in the Old Testament book of 1 Samuel. He is a figure closely connected with the military threat of Saul, the first king of Israel, and with David's exile.
lifetime: When David fled from Saul, he first went down to Gath and entrusted himself to Achish (1 Samuel 21:10). Afterward, feeling his life threatened, David feigned madness and escaped from there (1 Samuel 21:13). After some time David went to Achish again with six hundred followers and asked for refuge, and Achish received him and granted him the city of Ziklag (1 Samuel 27:2-6). Afterward Achish tried to bring David along as his bodyguard in the battle against Israel, but this came to nothing because of the opposition of the Philistine commanders (1 Samuel 29:2-4).
event: Achish gave Ziklag to David (1 Samuel 27:6). When the Philistines gathered their forces to fight against Israel, Achish told David that he must go out with him and join the army, and said he would make him his bodyguard for life (1 Samuel 28:1-2). Achish called David and said that from the day David came to him he had found no fault in him, so it was good to have him go out and come in with the army, but since the lords did not approve of him, he should go back in peace (1 Samuel 29:6-7).
character: Achish held David's ability in high regard and showed a flexible diplomatic attitude, wishing to make him one of his close associates (1 Samuel 29:3). By accepting the opinion of the surrounding commanders and excluding David from the battle, he also showed himself to be a reasonable ruler (1 Samuel 29:9-10). However, he trusted David completely, to the point of being deceived by David's false conduct and believing that David had betrayed Israel and was loyal to him (1 Samuel 27:12).

call: Son of Seir (chief of the Horites)
introduce: Anah, son of Seir, was one of the chiefs of the Horite clans in the land of Edom, a figure recorded in Genesis 36 and 1 Chronicles 1. He is recorded as a son of Seir together with Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
lifetime: Anah is recorded as a descendant of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36:20, 1 Chronicles 1:38), and as one of the chiefs that came from the Horites of the land of Seir (Genesis 36:21, 36:29). The genealogy of Anah is also confirmed in 1 Chronicles 1:38.
event: What Anah, son of Seir, did himself is not recorded in the text. The Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness in Genesis 36:24 is recorded as one of the "children of Zibeon," and in 36:25 Dishon and Oholibamah are recorded as the children of that Anah, so he must be distinguished from the Anah, son of Seir, in 36:20.

introduce: Ananiah appears in a genealogy as the grandfather of Azariah, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem, and as the father of Maaseiah (Nehemiah 3:23).
lifetime: Nehemiah 3:23 introduces Azariah as the grandson of Ananiah and the son of Maaseiah. Ananiah's own life is not recorded in this verse.
event: Azariah, the grandson of Ananiah and son of Maaseiah, repaired the section of the wall near his own house (Nehemiah 3:23). Ananiah's own deeds are not recorded.

introduce: A person named Anani is mentioned in the Bible only once, in a genealogy from after the Babylonian exile. He is recorded as one of the descendants of Zerubbabel.
lifetime: Anani was born as a son of Elioenai, a descendant of Jeconiah, king of Judah (1 Chronicles 3:24).
event: His name is listed as the seventh son in the genealogical record of Zerubbabel's family line (1 Chronicles 3:24).

call: Husband of Sapphira (believer of the early church)
introduce: He was a member of the early Jerusalem church who sold his property, kept back part of it, and presented the rest to the apostles, and then died.
lifetime: Ananias was a believer in the Jerusalem church, and he sold his property and laid the proceeds at the apostles' feet (Acts 5:1-2). He conspired with his wife Sapphira to keep back part of the amount he had received from the sale, but was found out by Peter, and fell down and died immediately (Acts 5:3-5).
event: He kept back part of the price of the land he had sold, and brought only a portion and laid it at the apostles' feet (Acts 5:2). Peter rebuked him, saying that Satan had filled his heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and keep back part of the proceeds of the land, and when Ananias heard these words he fell down and breathed his last, and great fear came upon all who heard of it (Acts 5:3-5). Afterward the young men rose, wrapped up his body, carried it out, and buried it (Acts 5:6).
character: He showed the intention of voluntarily disposing of his property to contribute to the community, but in the process a deceptive trait appears, in that he concealed part of his property and made a false report (Acts 5:2). The apostle Peter characterized his act as one in which Satan had filled his heart, so that he lied to the Holy Spirit and kept back part of the proceeds of the land (Acts 5:3).

introduce: Anamim is a name recorded in the genealogy of Genesis 10 as one of the descendants of Mizraim, a descendant of Ham, the son of Noah.
lifetime: He is recorded as a descendant of Mizraim, a son of Ham (Genesis 10:6, 10:13). Scripture conveys no record about him other than the name.
event: It is said that after the flood the nations of the earth were divided from the clans of the descendants of Noah (Genesis 10:32), and Anamim is recorded as one of the names born from Mizraim among them (Genesis 10:13, 1 Chronicles 1:11).

introduce: Anaiah was a figure of the time of Nehemiah. He was one of those who stood at the right hand of Ezra the scribe when he stood on the wooden platform (Nehemiah 8:4), and his name is also recorded in the list of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:22).
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile and the completion of the wall of Jerusalem, he took part in the covenant ceremony of sealing, in which the people resolved to keep the law of God (Nehemiah 10:22).
event: Anaiah was among those who stood at the right hand of Ezra the scribe when he stood on the wooden platform made for the occasion (Nehemiah 8:4). Also, among the list of those who sealed, the name of Anaiah is recorded among the chiefs of the people (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:14, 10:22).

introduce: Anan was one of the people of Israel who took part in the covenant renewal movement led by Nehemiah, governor of Judah in the Persian Empire period (Nehemiah 10:26).
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile and the completion of the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem, he was included in the list when the leaders, the Levites, and the priests, with Nehemiah at the center, sealed the document of the covenant made with God (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:26).
event: He took part as a signatory to the covenant document in which the people of Judah swore before God, accepting a curse upon themselves, to walk in the law, not to intermarry with the foreign peoples, and to keep the Sabbath and the festivals (Nehemiah 10:26, 10:29-31).

introduce: Aner is a figure who appears in the book of Genesis, belonging to the Amorites, and is recorded as one of the allies who had made a covenant with Abram at Hebron.
lifetime: Aner was an Amorite who lived at Hebron, and he was in an alliance with Abram, having a brotherly relationship with Mamre and Eshcol (Genesis 14:13). He is mentioned together with Abram in the process of dividing the spoil, after Abram fought a war to rescue Lot, who had been taken captive from the region of Sodom (Genesis 14:24).
event: When Abram defeated Chedorlaomer and his allied kings and returned after recovering Lot and the goods of Sodom, Aner, together with Mamre and Eshcol, was specified as an ally with the right to receive his proper share of the spoil (Genesis 14:24).

introduce: Anub is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as a son of Koz.
lifetime: Anub was born of Koz, and his name was entered in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah together with the families of Aharhel the son of Harum, and Zobebah (1 Chronicles 4:8).

introduce: A descendant of the tribe of Manasseh, a son of Shemida, and a figure who appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Manasseh.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Shemida of the tribe of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 7:19).
event: In the biblical record, no separate deeds or specific events are mentioned concerning Aniam (1 Chronicles 7:19).

introduce: Atarah is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as the wife of Jerahmeel and the mother of Onam (1 Chronicles 2:26).
lifetime: She is mentioned as the wife of Jerahmeel, a great-grandson of Judah and son of Hezron, and through her he had a son named Onam (1 Chronicles 2:26).
event: She bore her child Onam, and because of this she was recorded as one of the blood members of the house of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2:26).

introduce: Adaiah is a figure who appears in the Old Testament book of 2 Kings, recorded as Adaiah of Bozkath, the father of Jedidah, mother of Josiah king of Judah; that is, Josiah's maternal grandfather.
lifetime: He is recorded by the name Adaiah of Bozkath, and his daughter Jedidah was the mother of King Josiah (2 Kings 22:1).

introduce: Artaxerxes I was the fifth king of Persia in the Achaemenid dynasty, the son of Xerxes I and the father of Darius II. He reigned from 465 to 424 BC. In the Bible he appears as the one who permitted the return of the Jews and the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem. In Ezra 6:14 he is also mentioned, together with Cyrus and Darius, as a king of Persia who issued the decree that formed the basis for the building of the temple (Ezra 6:14).
lifetime: He succeeded to the throne after his father Xerxes I was assassinated. He issued a decree to Ezra, directing that any of the people of Israel who wished to go up to Jerusalem might go with him, and sent Ezra to Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the king and his seven counselors (Ezra 7:13-14). Nehemiah was this king's cupbearer (Nehemiah 1:11), and in the twentieth year of the king, the king was pleased with his request to let him rebuild the city and sent him to Judah (Nehemiah 2:1-6).
event: To Ezra, the Jewish scribe, he issued a decree appointing him, as one who knew the law of God, to set magistrates and judges to judge the people beyond the River and to teach those who did not know it, and providing silver, gold, and supplies for the house of God (Ezra 7:12-26). At Nehemiah's request, he permitted him to be given letters to the governors beyond the River, and timber for the beams for the gates of the citadel belonging to the temple, for the wall of the city, and for the house Nehemiah would occupy (Nehemiah 2:7-8).
