introduce: Abishai is a figure who appears in the Old Testament, a son of Zeruiah, David's sister, and a brother of Joab and Asahel. He was active as one of the key military leaders in David's army.
lifetime: When David was fleeing from Saul, he went down with David to Saul's camp (1 Samuel 26:6), and after David became king he served as a military commander as the brother of Joab (2 Samuel 2:24, 2 Samuel 10:10). When David was fleeing because of Absalom's rebellion, he was at David's side when Shimei cursed at Bahurim (2 Samuel 16:5-9), and afterward he took charge of a third of David's army and went out to fight Absalom's army (2 Samuel 18:2). At the time of Sheba's rebellion, at David's command he led the servants and pursued Sheba the son of Bichri (2 Samuel 20:6-7).
event: When David went down to Saul's camp, he volunteered to go with him, and seeing Saul sleeping in the camp, he said he would strike him with the spear, but did not carry it out because David restrained him (1 Samuel 26:6-9). When Ishbi-benob tried to kill David, he helped David and struck down and killed that Philistine (2 Samuel 21:16-17). He also struck down and killed eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt (1 Chronicles 18:12). He asked to be allowed to cut off the head of Shimei, who was cursing David, and later also said that Shimei deserved to die (2 Samuel 16:9, 2 Samuel 19:21).
character: His loyalty to David was very strong, and toward those who threatened David he showed a very immediate and aggressive attitude (2 Samuel 16:9). He was so skilled in martial arts that he was classified as one of the chiefs of the mighty men in David's military organization (2 Samuel 23:18).

기타관계: Absalom#2240(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

meaning: The Father is exalted, the Father is salvation
introduce: Abishua is a figure recorded in the Old Testament book of 1 Chronicles, a descendant of Aaron and a man of the tribe of Levi. He is the son of Phinehas and the grandson of Eleazar.
lifetime: Abishua was born as the son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, and became the father of Bukki (1 Chronicles 6:4-5). In the genealogy of Aaron's descendants in 1 Chronicles 6:50 also, following Eleazar and Phinehas, it is recorded "his son was Abishua," and then his son is Bukki (1 Chronicles 6:50-51).
event: No specific deeds of Abishua are recorded in the Bible; his name appears only in the genealogy of Aaron's descendants as the son of Phinehas and the father of Bukki (1 Chronicles 6:4-5, 1 Chronicles 6:50-51).

introduce: Abishur is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 2 in the Old Testament, a man belonging to the genealogy of the tribe of Judah. He is the son of Shammai and the brother of Nadab, and his wife is Abihail.
lifetime: Abishur is the son of Shammai, who was the son of Onam, and is the brother of Nadab (1 Chronicles 2:28). By his wife Abihail he fathered Ahban and Molid (1 Chronicles 2:29).
character: The biblical text does not give any separate personal description or specific deeds of Abishur, and records him only as one of the persons who make up the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:29).

introduce: Aphiah was a man of the tribe of Benjamin, an ancestor of Kish, the father of King Saul (1 Samuel 9:1).
lifetime: A man of the tribe of Benjamin, he corresponds to the fourth-generation ancestor of Kish; Kish is recorded as "the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah" (1 Samuel 9:1).
event: He appears only in the paternal genealogy of the house of Saul as the fourth-generation ancestor of Saul's father Kish, and no specific deeds of his are recorded in the Bible (1 Samuel 9:1).

introduce: Abiathar is a figure who appears in the Old Testament, the son of the priest Ahimelech and a high priest active in the period of the Davidic dynasty. After escaping the slaughter by Saul and fleeing to David, he performed the principal priestly duties throughout David's reign.
lifetime: When his father Ahimelech and the priestly family were wiped out at Nob by King Saul, he escaped as one of Ahimelech's sons and fled to David (1 Samuel 22:20). He came down to David at Keilah with the ephod and was with David while David was pursued by Saul (1 Samuel 23:6). After David became king he is also recorded as a priest together with Zadok (2 Samuel 20:25), and his son Ahimelech also became a priest (2 Samuel 8:17). At the time of the rebellion of David's son Absalom, Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed there (2 Samuel 15:24-29), and when David was old and Adonijah tried to become king, he conspired with Joab and helped him (1 Kings 1:7), and was ordered by Solomon to go to his home at Anathoth and was dismissed from the priesthood (1 Kings 2:26-27).
event: When David was pursued by Saul, using the ephod that Abiathar had brought, David inquired of the LORD whether Saul would come down to Keilah and whether the men of Keilah would deliver him into Saul's hand (1 Samuel 23:6-12). When David set out in flight because of Absalom's revolt, Zadok and the Levites came out carrying the ark of the covenant of God and Abiathar also went up, but David told them to carry the ark back into the city, and Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed there (2 Samuel 15:24-29). David told Hushai to report whatever he heard in the king's house to the two priests, Zadok and Abiathar (2 Samuel 15:35). He was dismissed from the priesthood by Solomon for having helped Adonijah, and this fulfilled the word the LORD had spoken at Shiloh concerning the house of Eli (1 Kings 2:26-27).
character: He showed strong loyalty, accompanying David from the early stage of David's political and military journey, but in his later years he made the political misjudgment of supporting Adonijah instead of Solomon (1 Kings 1:7). As a descendant of the priest Eli he was a person who continued the genealogy of the priestly family, but he is marked by finally losing the support of the throne and withdrawing in the power struggle.

introduce: A man belonging to the Kohathite descendants of the tribe of Levi, recorded as one of the sons of Korah.
lifetime: As a son of Korah he is recorded as a brother together with Assir and Elkanah, and is called "the Korahite clans" (Exodus 6:24). The Bible records nothing else about the individual life of Abiasaph.
event: When Korah rebelled against Moses and Aaron, the sons of Korah did not take part in the rebellion and survived (Numbers 26:11). Abiasaph was included in the genealogy as one of these surviving sons of Korah (Exodus 6:24).

introduce: Abi-albon is one of the thirty-seven mighty men of David's military organization, a man of Arbath.
lifetime: During David's reign he was active as one of David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23:31). In the record of Chronicles he is also mentioned by the name Abiel (1 Chronicles 11:32).
event: He is recorded as one of the prominent mighty men who helped David, but the specific battles he personally fought or particular events are not recorded in detail in the Bible (2 Samuel 23:31).

introduce: The son of Jeroboam I, the first king of northern Israel, who fell ill and died at a young age.
lifetime: Abijah, the son of Jeroboam, fell ill and took to his bed (1 Kings 14:1). Jeroboam had his wife disguise herself and go to Ahijah the prophet at Shiloh to inquire what would happen to the boy (1 Kings 14:2-3). Ahijah, by the word of the LORD, recognized her as Jeroboam's wife in disguise, and told her that when she entered the city the child would die (1 Kings 14:5-12). Abijah died when Jeroboam's wife returned to Tirzah and reached the threshold of the house (1 Kings 14:17).
event: After Abijah died, all Israel mourned for him and buried him (1 Kings 14:18). The prophet Ahijah said that because only Abijah had a good heart toward the LORD in the house of Jeroboam, he alone would be able to enter the tomb (1 Kings 14:13).
character: Abijah is regarded as the only one among the members of Jeroboam's house who had a good heart toward the LORD (1 Kings 14:13).

call: King of Judah in the south (son of Rehoboam)
introduce: The second king of the kingdom of Judah, the son of Rehoboam and the father of Asa. In Chronicles he is also recorded by the name Abijah.
lifetime: He became king in place of his father, Rehoboam king of Judah (1 Kings 14:31). His reign lasted three years, and he ruled in Jerusalem (1 Kings 15:2). His mother was Maacah, and she was the daughter of Abishalom (1 Kings 15:2).
event: During his reign there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam (1 Kings 15:7). When he was confronting Jeroboam, he stood on Mount Zemaraim and addressed Jeroboam and the host of Israel, criticizing the idolatry and the political legitimacy of northern Israel (2 Chronicles 13:4-12). In the war, by the help of God, he routed the army of Jeroboam and achieved the military success of taking several cities including Bethel (2 Chronicles 13:17-20).
character: He committed all the sins that his father Rehoboam had done, and his heart was not like the heart of his ancestor David, so that he was not wholly true to God (1 Kings 15:3). Nevertheless, for David's sake, the LORD gave him a lamp in Jerusalem by raising up his son after him (1 Kings 15:4).

call: Son of Zeror (grandfather of King Saul)
introduce: A man of the tribe of Benjamin, the paternal grandfather of King Saul, recorded as the son of Zeror.
lifetime: Abiel is mentioned as Saul's grandfather in the family line of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Samuel 9:1). He had a son Kish, and Kish became Saul's father (1 Samuel 9:1, 1 Samuel 14:51). 1 Samuel 14:51 mentions Saul's father Kish and Abner's father Ner, and then records "the sons of Abiel."
event: No political event or military achievement that he led directly is recorded in the Bible. However, his name is stated as a key figure in the family tree that forms the genealogy of the house of Saul (1 Samuel 9:1).

introduce: Abihail is a figure who appears in the Old Testament book of Numbers, recorded as the father of Zuriel, chief of the Merarite descendants of the tribe of Levi.
lifetime: Abihail is mentioned in Numbers 3:35 in the expression "Zuriel the son of Abihail." The Bible has no record of Abihail's own life (Numbers 3:35).
event: The Bible has no record of Abihail's own deeds. His son Zuriel became chief of the Merarite family and clan, and this family camped on the north side of the tabernacle, and the descendants of Merari were in charge of the frames, bars, pillars, sockets, and so on of the tabernacle (Numbers 3:35-36).

introduce: Abihu was the second son of Aaron and Elisheba, the younger brother of Nadab and the elder brother of Eleazar and Ithamar. As a member of the priestly family he took part in the process of establishing Israel's early sacrificial system, but he was put to death for using fire that God had not commanded.
lifetime: Abihu was called to perform the priestly office as a son of Aaron (Exodus 28:1). On Mount Sinai he went up with Moses, Aaron, and Nadab, together with seventy of the elders of Israel, and they saw the God of Israel and ate and drank (Exodus 24:9-11). Afterward, at the ordination of the priests, he was clothed and set apart together with the sons of Aaron (Leviticus 8:13), but while offering incense before the LORD with other fire that the LORD had not commanded, he was consumed and died by fire that came out from before the LORD (Leviticus 10:1-2). Since he had no sons, his brothers Eleazar and Ithamar performed the priestly office in the presence of their father Aaron (Numbers 3:4).
event: When Israel was camped at Mount Sinai, he was present when he went up with Moses, Aaron, and Nadab, together with seventy of the elders of Israel, and saw the God of Israel (Exodus 24:9-10). The ordination of the priests lasted seven days, and during that time there was a command not to go out from the entrance of the tent of meeting (Leviticus 8:33). The heart of the incident is that when Abihu, together with Nadab, put other fire that the LORD had not commanded in their censers and offered incense before the LORD, fire came out from before the LORD and consumed them (Leviticus 10:1-2). After this incident Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan and had them carry their bodies out of the camp, and told Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar not to let their hair hang loose or tear their clothes (Leviticus 10:4-6).

introduce: A man of the tribe of Benjamin, a son of Bela and a grandson of Benjamin. He appears as one of the nine sons of Bela in the genealogy of the house of Benjamin recorded in the genealogies of Chronicles.
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of the sons born to Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:3).

introduce: Azaniah is a figure recorded as the father of Jeshua, a Levite who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:9).
lifetime: Nehemiah 10:9 records "Jeshua the son of Azaniah" as a Levite who sealed the covenant, and Azaniah himself is mentioned only as his father. The Bible has no record of Azaniah's own life (Nehemiah 10:9).
event: The Bible has no record of Azaniah's own events. His son Jeshua is recorded among the Levites who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:1, Nehemiah 10:9).

introduce: One of the mighty men from the tribe of Benjamin who joined David during his exile at Ziklag, mentioned in 1 Chronicles 12. He is classified as a Korahite, and is recorded as one of those who came to Ziklag to help David.
lifetime: He appears in the list of mighty men who joined David, who was staying at Ziklag to escape Saul's persecution (1 Chronicles 12:6). As a man of the tribe of Benjamin, he is one who joined David's forces although he was a kinsman of Saul (1 Chronicles 12:2).
event: When David was at Ziklag to escape Saul, he is recorded as one of the mighty men who came to help him (1 Chronicles 12:1). They were archers who could use both the right hand and the left to sling stones or shoot arrows (1 Chronicles 12:2).
character: He has the bloodline background of being a Korahite, and is a figure with the valiant military trait of having supported David although he belonged to the same tribe as Saul (1 Chronicles 12:2). He possessed skilled combat ability, able to shoot accurately with the bow and the sling (1 Chronicles 12:2).

introduce: Asarelah is a figure mentioned in 1 Chronicles, a descendant of Asaph, whose name appears in the genealogy of the family connected with the choir.
lifetime: Asarelah is included in the list of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah (1 Chronicles 25:2). The one chosen seventh when lots were cast to assign duties was Jesarelah (corresponding to Asarelah in 25:2), and his sons and brothers, twelve in all, are recorded with him (1 Chronicles 25:14).
event: His name was recorded in the list of those whom David and the commanders of the army set apart for service from among the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun (1 Chronicles 25:1-2), and as an example, when duties were obtained by lot, the seventh fell to Jesarelah (corresponding to Asarelah in 25:2) (1 Chronicles 25:8, 14). This was the duty of prophesying with harps, lyres, and cymbals (1 Chronicles 25:1).

introduce: Azariah is the chief of the officers, recorded as the son of Nathan in the list of King Solomon's officials (1 Kings 4:5). He is a different person from Azariah the son of Zadok in the same list (1 Kings 4:2).
lifetime: Azariah the son of Nathan is recorded among Solomon's officials as the chief of the officers, and his brother Zabud was a chief minister and the king's friend (1 Kings 4:5).
event: He appears in the list of Solomon's officials as the chief of the officers (1 Kings 4:5). No other deeds of his are recorded.

introduce: Azaz is a figure of the descendants of the tribe of Reuben, recorded as the son of Shema, the grandson of Joel, and the father of Bela.
lifetime: Azaz is recorded as the son of Shema and the grandson of Joel (1 Chronicles 5:8). His son Bela dwelt in Aroer and his settlement extended as far as Nebo and Baal-meon (1 Chronicles 5:8).
event: Azaz is recorded as the father of Bela (1 Chronicles 5:8). The settlement extending from Aroer to Nebo and Baal-meon, and the going eastward to dwell and the increase of livestock in the land of Gilead, are the record concerning his son Bela (1 Chronicles 5:8-9).

call: Musician of the ark of the covenant (lyre player)
introduce: A Levite active in the time of David, one of the musicians recorded as leading with harps according to the eighth when the ark of the covenant was carried up from the house of Obed-edom.
lifetime: When David moved the ark of the covenant from the house of Obed-edom, he commanded the heads of the Levites to appoint their brothers as singers and to sound the instruments (1 Chronicles 15:16, 25). At that time Azaziah was recorded as one of those who led with harps according to the eighth (1 Chronicles 15:21).
event: In the bringing up of the ark of the covenant, he is recorded as one who was given the duty of leading with harps according to the eighth (1 Chronicles 15:21). This was part of David's commanding the Levites to appoint singers and instrumentalists (1 Chronicles 15:16).

call: Chief of the tribe of Simeon
introduce: Asaiah is a figure who appears in the Old Testament book of 1 Chronicles, one of the chiefs of the tribe of Simeon. His name appears in the list concerning the chiefs of the descendants of Simeon who sought pasture and settled in new land in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah.
lifetime: Asaiah is a descendant of Simeon whose name is listed in 1 Chronicles 4:36 together with Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Adiel, and others. This verse does not record his father or family line. Like those registered by name in this list, he is recorded as a chief of his clan (1 Chronicles 4:38).
event: The chiefs registered by name, to whom Asaiah belonged, sought pasture for their flocks and came to the entrance of Gedor, on the east side of the valley, and found rich and good pasture (1 Chronicles 4:39-40). These registered above by name, in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, struck down the tents of the people there and destroyed the Meunites who were there utterly, and dwelt in their place (1 Chronicles 4:41). From of old the descendants of Ham had lived there (1 Chronicles 4:40).

introduce: Asahel was a son of Zeruiah, David's sister, and as a brother of Joab and Abishai he was active in David's early military system. He is recorded as one of David's thirty mighty men.
lifetime: He is one of the three sons of David's sister Zeruiah, Joab, Abishai, and Asahel (1 Chronicles 2:16; 2 Samuel 2:18). After David became king of Judah at Hebron, he faced the army led by Abner at the pool of Gibeon (2 Samuel 2:13). While pursuing Abner, he was stabbed by Abner with the butt end of his spear and died (2 Samuel 2:23). Afterward the people buried him in the tomb of his father at Bethlehem (2 Samuel 2:32).
event: His name is listed among David's thirty (2 Samuel 23:24). He ran after Abner from Gibeon without turning to the right or to the left (2 Samuel 2:19), and when Abner told him to turn aside, seize one of the young men and take his spoil, and stop pursuing, he did not want to turn aside and kept on pursuing (2 Samuel 2:21-22). In the course of this Abner struck him in the belly with the butt end of his spear, and he fell and died on the spot (2 Samuel 2:23).
character: The Bible states explicitly that he was as swift of foot as a wild gazelle (2 Samuel 2:18). From the fact that he met misfortune by pursuing Abner, the enemy commander, recklessly, relying only on his own speed on the battlefield, one can see that he was somewhat impetuous and hot-blooded in temperament (2 Samuel 2:21).

기타관계: Absalom#2240(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: Azaliah is a figure recorded as the father of Shaphan, who was sent to repair the temple in the time of Josiah king of Judah.
lifetime: Azaliah appears only in 2 Chronicles 34:8 as "Shaphan the son of Azaliah," who was sent to repair the house of the LORD in the eighteenth year of Josiah. In 2 Kings 22:3 also his son is recorded as Shaphan the scribe and is called the son of Azaliah. The deeds of Azaliah himself are not recorded.
event: His son Shaphan was sent to repair the house of the LORD in the eighteenth year of Josiah (2 Chronicles 34:8), and Shaphan the scribe received the book of the law that Hilkiah the high priest had found (2 Chronicles 34:15).

기타관계: Josiah#2723(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: The eighth son born to Jacob by Leah's maidservant Zilpah, and the ancestor of the tribe of Asher, one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
lifetime: He was born at Paddan-aram and was the second son whom Leah's maidservant Zilpah bore to Jacob (Genesis 30:12-13, 35:26). Later he went down to Egypt with Jacob's family, and the names of his sons are recorded in the list (Genesis 46:8, 17).
event: His four sons Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah and his sister Serah are recorded in the list (Genesis 46:17), and when Jacob blessed his children just before his death, he heard these words about Asher: "Asher’s food will be rich; he shall provide royal delicacies." Also, when Moses blessed the people of Israel before his death, Asher received this blessing: "May Asher be the most blessed of sons; may he be a delight to his brothers, and may he dip his foot in oil" (Deuteronomy 33:1, 24).

직업/직위: progenitor of the tribe of Asher

introduce: Azor is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in Matthew 1, and in the genealogy he holds the position of being mentioned as the son of Eliakim and the father of Zadok.
lifetime: Azor is recorded as the son of Eliakim (Matthew 1:13), and as the father of Zadok he continues the line of the genealogy (Matthew 1:14).

introduce: Azubah is recorded as the mother of King Jehoshaphat, the son of Asa. She was the daughter of Shilhi.
lifetime: Azubah is recorded as the daughter of Shilhi and the mother of Jehoshaphat (1 Kings 22:42; 2 Chronicles 20:31). Her son Jehoshaphat, as the son of Asa, became king of Judah and ruled twenty-five years in Jerusalem (1 Kings 22:41-42).
event: In the biblical record there is no record of any specific political achievement or particular event carried out by Azubah as queen mother. Her name is mentioned only in the context of identifying the family line and mother of King Jehoshaphat (2 Chronicles 20:31).

introduce: Asyncritus is one of the persons to whom the apostle Paul sent greetings near the end of the New Testament book of Romans, a believer who belonged to the community of the church in Rome.
lifetime: He is a person mentioned in the letter Paul sent to the Christians in Rome, one to whom Paul sent greetings, listing the various brothers in the church in Rome (Romans 16:14).
event: In the biblical record there is no account of his working together with Paul or leading any special religious event; the only fact confirmed is that he was included in the list of believers in the church in Rome whom Paul knew and received greetings (Romans 16:14).

call: Ancestor of a family that returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Azgad is a name that designates the ancestor of the descendants of Azgad who appear in the list of the descendants who returned from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem and Judah.
lifetime: The descendants of Azgad are recorded in the list of the descendants who were taken captive to Babylon and returned to Jerusalem and Judah (Ezra 2:1, 12; Nehemiah 7:17).
event: In the list of returnees in Ezra 2, the descendants of Azgad are recorded as 1,222 (Ezra 2:12). In Nehemiah 7, the descendants of Azgad also appear in the register of the genealogy of those who first returned, which Nehemiah found, and their number is 2,322, recorded differently from the number in Ezra 2 (Nehemiah 7:5, 17).

introduce: Ashkenaz is a figure who appears in Genesis and 1 Chronicles, the son of Gomer, son of Japheth, son of Noah. His name is recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Japheth in Genesis 10 and 1 Chronicles 1.
lifetime: Ashkenaz is recorded as a son of Gomer, a grandson of Japheth, and a great-grandson of Noah (Genesis 10:3). In 1 Chronicles also, in the same way, his name is entered in the list of the descendants of Japheth as a son of Gomer (1 Chronicles 1:6).
event: In the biblical record, no achievement or historical event specifically carried out by Ashkenaz himself is described, and he is mentioned only as one branch of the genealogy of the nations (Genesis 10:3, 1 Chronicles 1:6).

introduce: Asnah is the name of a family recorded under the heading of the Nethinim in the list of returnees in Ezra 2.
lifetime: In the list of those who were taken captive to Babylon and returned to Jerusalem and Judah, he is recorded among the Nethinim as the ancestor of the descendants of Asnah (Ezra 2:1, 43, 50).
event: In the Nethinim section of the list of returnees, the descendants of Asnah are recorded together with the descendants of Meunim and the descendants of Nephusim (Ezra 2:50). After they returned, the Nethinim dwelt in their cities (Ezra 2:70). The descendants of Asnah are not recorded in the parallel list in Nehemiah 7:46-56 (Nehemiah 7:52).

meaning: One belonging to Neith, the Egyptian goddess
introduce: She was the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On in Egypt, the wife of Joseph, and the mother of Manasseh and Ephraim.
lifetime: After Pharaoh put the signet ring on Joseph's hand, clothed him in garments of fine linen, hung a gold chain around his neck, and set him over all the land of Egypt (Genesis 41:41-42), he gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah and gave him Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, as his wife (Genesis 41:45). Before the years of famine came she bore Joseph two sons (Genesis 41:50), and Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh and the second Ephraim (Genesis 41:51-52).
event: After Joseph was set over Egypt, Pharaoh gave him Asenath in marriage, and she became Joseph's wife (Genesis 41:45); before the years of famine came she bore Joseph two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim (Genesis 41:50-52; 46:20).

call: Descendant of the royal house of David (son of Neariah)
introduce: Azrikam is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles, mentioned as a descendant of the tribe of Judah who continued the line of the royal house of David, and as a son of Neariah.
lifetime: Azrikam appears as one of the descendants of Zerubbabel, a descendant of David, and in the genealogical system after the Babylonian exile he is recorded as a son of Neariah (1 Chronicles 3:23).

call: Son of Manasseh (ancestor of the Asriel clan)
introduce: Asriel was a person belonging to the tribe of Manasseh; in Numbers he is recorded as the name of a family of the descendants of Gilead, and in 1 Chronicles as a son of Manasseh by his wife. The Asriel family, named after him, is in the tribe of Manasseh.
lifetime: In Numbers 26:29-31, Asriel appears as the ancestor of the Asriel family among the descendants of Gilead son of Machir. In Joshua 17:2 he appears as one of the remaining descendants of Manasseh, the descendants of Asriel, and in 1 Chronicles 7:14 he is recorded as one of "the sons of Manasseh, born of his wife."
event: The Asriel family descended from Asriel was recorded as one of the families of the tribe of Manasseh at the census of Israel (Numbers 26:31), and also when lots were cast for the land of Canaan, it appears among the remaining descendants of Manasseh (Joshua 17:2).

call: Barhumite (one of David's thirty mighty men)
introduce: Azmaveth the Barhumite is a person recorded as one of the thirty mighty men, David's military organization.
lifetime: He is recorded as a Barhumite in the list of David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23:31). In the record of Chronicles, he is written as Azmaveth the Baharumite and appears again in the list of mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:33).
event: As one of David's thirty mighty men, he served as a key combatant within David's military system (2 Samuel 23:31). There is no record in Scripture of any specific military exploit or individual event of his (1 Chronicles 11:33).

introduce: Aspatha is a person mentioned along with Haman in the time of King Ahasuerus of the Persian Empire, and is one of the ten sons of Haman who appear in the book of Esther.
lifetime: Aspatha is one of the ten sons of Haman and a grandson of Hammedatha the Agagite (Esther 9:7, 10). When the Jews killed their enemies in Susa, the ten sons of Haman were put to death (Esther 9:6-10).
event: After Haman's plan to move against the Jews came to nothing, when the Jews slaughtered those who hated them, all ten sons of Haman, including Aspatha, were killed (Esther 9:7-10). Afterward his body was hung on the gallows and displayed along with those of his brothers (Esther 9:13-14).

introduce: A descendant of Shelah of the tribe of Judah, a member of a family whose hereditary occupation was weaving fine linen.
lifetime: He is recorded as a descendant of Shelah, the son of Judah, and was active among the families of the linen workers (1 Chronicles 4:21).
event: The family of Ashbea was a group made up of craftsmen who specialized in weaving fine linen (1 Chronicles 4:21).

meaning: One with a long upper lip
introduce: Ashbel was a person of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as a grandson of Jacob and one of the sons of Benjamin.
lifetime: Ashbel is recorded as a son of Benjamin in the list in Genesis 46:21, and in 1 Chronicles 8:1 he is recorded as the second son of Benjamin. As a descendant of Benjamin, he is included in the list of the family of Israel who went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:8, 21).
event: The Ashbelite clan formed from his descendants was recorded as a division of the tribe of Benjamin at the census (Numbers 26:38). In 1 Chronicles he is again mentioned as the second son of Benjamin, and was recorded together with his brothers (1 Chronicles 8:1).

기타관계: Nohah#387(kinsman of the tribe of Benjamin)

introduce: Ashpenaz is a person recorded as the chief of the eunuchs in the time of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He appears in connection with bringing, by the king's command, some of the Israelites of the royal family and of the nobility.
lifetime: King Nebuchadnezzar commanded Ashpenaz, the chief of the eunuchs, to bring some of the Israelites, of the royal family and of the nobility (Daniel 1:3). After being nourished for three years on the food and wine the king had assigned, they were to stand before the king (Daniel 1:5). The chief of the eunuchs gave new names to Daniel and the three others (Daniel 1:7).
event: When Daniel asked the chief of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself with the king's delicacies and wine, God caused Daniel to find favor and compassion with the chief of the eunuchs, but the chief of the eunuchs, fearing the king, said that if their faces looked haggard, his own head would be in danger (Daniel 1:8-10). Daniel asked the overseer whom the chief of the eunuchs had appointed to test them for ten days and give them vegetables to eat, and the overseer listened to him and tested them for ten days (Daniel 1:11-14).
character: Ashpenaz was the one with whom God caused Daniel to find favor and compassion (Daniel 1:9). He showed an attitude of strict observance of the king's command, yet at the same time showed prudence in accepting a trial alternative in consideration of the circumstances of the young men under his charge (Daniel 1:10-14).

introduce: Azbuk is a person recorded in Nehemiah 3:16 only as the father of Nehemiah, "ruler of a half-district of Beth-zur."
lifetime: Azbuk appears in Nehemiah 3:16 only as "Nehemiah son of Azbuk," and his son Nehemiah is recorded as the ruler of a half-district of Beth-zur at the time of the repair of the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:16). The deeds of Azbuk himself are not recorded.
event: His son Nehemiah repaired a section of the wall up to a point opposite the tombs of David, as far as the artificial pool and the House of the Mighty (Nehemiah 3:16).

introduce: Ashvath is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher in 1 Chronicles 7, a son of Japhlet.
lifetime: Ashvath is recorded as one of the sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath (1 Chronicles 7:33). Japhlet was a son born to Heber, the son of Beriah, the son of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:30-32).
event: Apart from his name being recorded in the genealogy, no deeds of Ashvath himself are recorded in Scripture (1 Chronicles 7:33).

introduce: Ashhur is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as a son of Hezron and the father of Tekoa.
lifetime: After Hezron died in Caleb-ephrathah, his wife Abijah bore Ashhur to him (1 Chronicles 2:24). Ashhur had two wives, Helah and Naarah (1 Chronicles 4:5).
event: He is recorded as the father of Tekoa (1 Chronicles 2:24; 4:5). Naarah bore to him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari, and the sons of Helah were Zereth, Zohar, and Ethnan (1 Chronicles 4:6-7).

introduce: Aziza is a person recorded as one of the descendants of Zattu in the list, in the book of Ezra, of those who took foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:27).
lifetime: In the time of Ezra he was recorded as one of the descendants of Zattu in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:27, 10:44). No other record about his life appears in Scripture.
event: His name was entered in the list of those who had taken foreign women, which came to light when Ezra confessed sin before the house of God (Ezra 10:1, 10:27, 10:44). There is no record in these verses of any confession or action by him personally.

introduce: Asiel is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles, a person whose name appears in the genealogies and lists of two different tribes. There is no evidence in the biblical record that they are the same person; he appears distinguished as a descendant of the tribe of Simeon and as a Levite of David's time.
lifetime: Asiel of the tribe of Simeon is recorded as an ancestor of Jehu son of Joshibiah; the text calls Jehu the son of Joshibiah, grandson of Seraiah, and great-grandson of Asiel (1 Chronicles 4:35). Asiel the Levite of David's time is recorded together with Zechariah, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah as one who played the harps to accompany the women's voices (1 Chronicles 15:20).
event: No deeds of Asiel of the tribe of Simeon himself are recorded, but his great-grandson Jehu was recorded among those listed by name as chiefs of their clan (1 Chronicles 4:35, 4:38). When David commanded the chiefs of the Levites to appoint singers (1 Chronicles 15:16), Asiel the Levite was recorded as one who played the harps to accompany the women's voices (1 Chronicles 15:20).

introduce: Archelaus was a son of Herod, and the person who succeeded his father Herod as king of Judea. In the Gospel of Matthew he is mentioned in connection with Joseph, who, hearing that he was king of Judea, was afraid, departed to the region of Galilee, and came to live in Nazareth (Matthew 2:22-23).
lifetime: Archelaus was a son of Herod (Matthew 2:22). After Herod died (Matthew 2:19), he succeeded his father Herod as king of Judea (Matthew 2:22). Joseph, who had returned from Egypt, was afraid to go there when he heard that Archelaus was king of Judea, and being directed in a dream, he departed to the region of Galilee and came to live in a town called Nazareth (Matthew 2:22-23).
event: He succeeded his father Herod as king of Judea, and when Joseph heard this news, he was afraid to go to Judea (Matthew 2:22).
character: According to historical records, he had a cruel and oppressive disposition no less than that of his father Herod the Great, and this reputation of his served as a threatening factor that made Jesus' family reluctant to return to Judea at that time (Matthew 2:22).

introduce: Achim is a person who appears in the genealogy of Jesus recorded in the New Testament Gospel of Matthew, and is stated explicitly to be the son of Zadok and the father of Eliud.
lifetime: As the son of Zadok he received the family line and begot Eliud (Matthew 1:14).

introduce: Archippus is a person who appears in the New Testament, whose name occurs in the apostle Paul's letters Colossians and Philemon.
lifetime: In Colossians, Paul told the Colossians to say to Archippus that he should take heed to the ministry he had received in the Lord and fulfill it (Colossians 4:17). In Philemon he called him "our fellow soldier Archippus" and recorded him among those who received the letter (Philemon 1:2).
event: Near the end of Colossians, Paul had a word of exhortation conveyed to Archippus to take heed to the ministry he had received in the Lord and fulfill it (Colossians 4:17). The letter to Philemon states that it is written to Philemon and to our sister Apphia, together with Archippus and the church in Philemon's house (Philemon 1:1-2).
character: Paul described him as his companion and soldier, giving him the identity of a co-worker in ministry (Colossians 4:17, Philemon 1:2).

meaning: Brother of Rah, follower of a brother
introduce: He is a person of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in 1 Chronicles 8:1, mentioned as the third of the sons born to Benjamin.
lifetime: Among those born to Benjamin, he was recorded third, after Bela the firstborn and Ashbel the second (1 Chronicles 8:1).
event: Within the biblical record, no special achievement carried out by Aharah personally, and no specific recorded event, is found (1 Chronicles 8:1).
character: The biblical text gives no information about this person's character or outward features (1 Chronicles 8:1).

기타관계: Nohah#387(kinsman of the tribe of Benjamin)

introduce: Ahasuerus, mentioned in Ezra 4:6, is a king of Persia, at whose accession the adversaries of Judah submitted a written accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem (Ezra 4:6).
lifetime: At the accession of Ahasuerus, those who opposed Judah submitted a written accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem (Ezra 4:6).
event: Apart from the fact that the adversaries of Judah submitted a written accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem at the accession of Ahasuerus, no specific political achievement or event carried out by him is recorded in this text (Ezra 4:6).

introduce: Ahaz was the twelfth king to rule the southern kingdom of Judah, around the eighth century BC, a son of Jotham and the father of Hezekiah. During his reign he suffered a crisis caused by the invasion of Aram and northern Israel, and he sent messengers to the king of Assyria to ask for deliverance.
lifetime: Ahaz became king at the age of 20 and ruled in Jerusalem for 16 years (2 Kings 16:2). He faced a great crisis when Pekah king of northern Israel and Rezin king of Aram came up to Jerusalem and besieged it (2 Kings 16:5, Isaiah 7:1). In this crisis he sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria to ask for help (2 Kings 16:7). Afterward he went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and when he saw the altar there, he sketched the pattern of its construction and design and sent it to Uriah the priest, and Uriah made the altar accordingly (2 Kings 16:10-11). He died at the age of 36 and was buried in the city of David (2 Kings 16:20).
event: Ahaz took the silver and gold found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's palace and sent it as a gift to the king of Assyria, and the king of Assyria came up, attacked and captured Damascus, and put Rezin to death (2 Kings 16:8-9). On account of the king of Assyria he removed the bases of the basins, the bronze Sea, and the porch of the temple (2 Kings 16:17-18), and he gathered the articles of the house of God and cut them in pieces, shut the doors of the house of the LORD, and built altars in every corner of Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 28:24). The Edomites attacked Judah and carried away captives, and the Philistines also raided the cities of the lowland and the Negev of Judah and captured them (2 Chronicles 28:17-18); Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came, but instead of helping him, he oppressed him (2 Chronicles 28:20).
character: Following the abominations of the nations, he made his own son pass through the fire (2 Kings 16:3). He practiced polytheistic worship, sacrificing and burning incense on the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree (2 Kings 16:4). In a national crisis he refused to ask for the sign offered by the prophet Isaiah and held to his own political judgment (Isaiah 7:12). During his reign, unusually among the kings of Judah, he actively embraced foreign culture and took steps to destroy the existing religious system (2 Chronicles 28:2-4).

introduce: Ahasbai is a person recorded as the father of Eliphelet in the list of David's mighty men in 2 Samuel 23, and is introduced as the son of a Maacathite (2 Samuel 23:34).
lifetime: In Scripture he is recorded only as the son of a Maacathite and the father of Eliphelet, and there is no record of his birth or activity (2 Samuel 23:34).
event: There is no record of anything Ahasbai himself did or of any event concerning him. His son Eliphelet was recorded in the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:34).

introduce: The eighth king of northern Israel, a son of Ahab and Jezebel. He succeeded his father and reigned in Samaria for two years (1 Kings 22:51).
lifetime: He became king after Ahab died and reigned for two years (1 Kings 22:51). During his reign Moab rebelled against Israel (2 Kings 1:1), and when he fell ill he tried to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, and was rebuked by Elijah (2 Kings 1:2-4). Afterward he fell from the lattice of his upper room, and being injured, he did not recover and died (2 Kings 1:2, 17), and since he had no son, his brother Joram succeeded to the throne (2 Kings 1:17).
event: After Ahab died, Moab rebelled against Israel (2 Kings 1:1). When Ahaziah fell from the lattice of his upper room in Samaria and became ill, he sent messengers to ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether he would recover from this illness (2 Kings 1:2). When Elijah rebuked this with the word of the LORD, the king sent a captain of fifty and his fifty men to Elijah, and this happened three times (2 Kings 1:9-15).
character: He followed the way of his parents Ahab and Jezebel and caused Israel to sin (1 Kings 22:52). He showed an attitude of relying on a foreign god, Baal-zebub, instead of the LORD (2 Kings 1:2). He revealed a stubborn and hostile disposition, to the point of sending soldiers to arrest Elijah (2 Kings 1:9-13).

introduce: Aharhel is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a son of Harum (1 Chronicles 4:8). In the same verse it is recorded that Koz begot Anub and Zobebah and the clans of Aharhel.
lifetime: Aharhel was a son of Harum (1 Chronicles 4:8), and his name is recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah in 1 Chronicles 4. The historical background of the time in which he lived and the specific events of his life are not recorded in Scripture (1 Chronicles 4:8).

introduce: Ahab was the seventh king of the northern kingdom of Israel, a son of Omri, who ruled in Samaria for about 22 years. According to the biblical record, he is depicted as having done more evil than all the kings before him.
lifetime: Born a son of Omri, he became king of Israel and took as his wife Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians (1 Kings 16:29-31). He won two victories in wars against the Aramean army led by Ben-hadad, but afterward he was killed in the battle of Ramoth-gilead when he was struck by an arrow that a man drew and shot (1 Kings 20:1-30, 22:34-37).
event: He encouraged idolatry on a national scale, building a temple for Baal in Samaria and setting up an altar for Baal (1 Kings 16:32). He made an Asherah pole and provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger more than all the kings of Israel before him (1 Kings 16:33). When Naboth refused to give him his vineyard, he was sullen, and his wife Jezebel sent letters in Ahab's name, set up false witnesses, and had Naboth stoned to death, and Ahab went down to take possession of the vineyard (1 Kings 21:1-16). He made an alliance with King Jehoshaphat and fought against Aram, and in the process he ignored the warning of the prophet Micaiah (1 Kings 22:4-28).
character: Under the influence of Jezebel, he showed a weak and passive side, taking the lead in idolatry (1 Kings 21:25). When he heard Elijah's rebuke after the affair of Naboth's vineyard, he showed a brief repentance, tearing his clothes, putting sackcloth on his body, and fasting (1 Kings 21:27). He did not hesitate to employ unethical means to maintain his power, and he regarded the warnings of the prophets as political threats and was hostile to them (1 Kings 21:20, 22:8).

introduce: Aher is a person recorded as the father of Hushim in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles 7 (1 Chronicles 7:12).
lifetime: In 1 Chronicles 7:12 he is recorded only as the father of Hushim, in the words "the son of Aher was Hushim," and no other record about his life appears in Scripture (1 Chronicles 7:12).

call: Son of Bela (ancestor of the Ahohite clan)
introduce: A person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the sons of Bela (1 Chronicles 8:3-4).
lifetime: He was born as a son of Bela, the son of Benjamin, and his name appears in 1 Chronicles, which records the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:4).
event: No deeds of Ahoah himself are recorded in Scripture; his name is merely listed in the list of the sons of Bela (1 Chronicles 8:3-4).

call: Son of Abinadab (guide of the cart that carried the ark)
introduce: Ahio is a person who appears in 2 Samuel, a son of Abinadab. He is recorded as having driven, together with Uzzah, the new cart on which the ark of God was loaded, when David was about to bring up the ark of God.
lifetime: Ahio, a son of Abinadab, drove the cart together with Uzzah when the ark of God was loaded on a new cart and brought out from Abinadab's house on the hill (2 Samuel 6:3).
event: Ahio, together with his brother Uzzah, drove the ark of God loaded on the new cart (2 Samuel 6:3). He went before the ark (2 Samuel 6:4).

meaning: Brother of water, brother of the meadow
introduce: Ahumai is a descendant of the tribe of Judah and a son of Jahath, a person who appears in the genealogical record of 1 Chronicles 4:2. He is a grandson of Reaiah son of Shobal, and was born of Jahath together with Lahad; these are mentioned as the clans of the Zorathites (1 Chronicles 4:2).
lifetime: Ahumai was born a son of Jahath and belongs to the genealogical line of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:2). Information about the time of his birth or the specific period of his activity is not confirmed in the biblical record (1 Chronicles 4:2).

introduce: Ahuzzam is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as one of the sons born to Ashhur by Naarah, one of his two wives (1 Chronicles 4:6).
lifetime: He is a son born between Ashhur, a descendant of Judah, and Naarah.

introduce: Ahuzzath is a person who appears in the book of Genesis in the Old Testament, recorded as a friend of Abimelech king of Gerar.
lifetime: Abimelech came from Gerar to Isaac, bringing his friend Ahuzzath and Phicol the commander of his army (Genesis 26:26).
event: He came to Isaac with Abimelech, and after eating and drinking at the feast Isaac gave, they swore an oath to one another in the morning and went away in peace (Genesis 26:26-31).

introduce: Ahzai is a person recorded in the list of priests in Nehemiah 11 as the grandfather of Amashai, who was a head of a family; he was the son of Meshillemoth and the father of Azarel.
lifetime: Nehemiah 11:13 calls Amashai "the son of Azarel, the son of Ahzai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer," and so Ahzai is recorded as the father of Azarel and the son of Meshillemoth (Nehemiah 11:13). No record about Ahzai's own life appears in Scripture.
event: There is no record of Ahzai's own deeds, but his grandson Amashai was recorded as head of his brothers among the priests (Nehemiah 11:13).

introduce: A person mentioned in 1 Chronicles 5:15, who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Gad; he was a son of Abdiel and a grandson of Guni.
lifetime: He is a chief recorded among the descendants of Gad as the son of Abdiel, the son of Guni (1 Chronicles 5:15). The descendants of Gad lived in the land of Bashan, in Gilead and its towns, and throughout the pasturelands of Sharon (1 Chronicles 5:11, 5:16).
event: It is recorded that Ahi, the son of Abdiel, the son of Guni, became a chief (1 Chronicles 5:15).

introduce: Ahikam was a high official who served in the Kingdom of Judah in the time of Josiah and Jehoiakim, a son of Shaphan the scribe, and is known as the one who protected the prophet Jeremiah.
lifetime: During the reign of King Josiah he served together with his father Shaphan, who was the king's scribe (2 Kings 22:12). Later, in the time of King Jehoiakim, when Jeremiah was in danger of death, he protected him by not handing him over into the hands of the people, so that they could not kill him (Jeremiah 26:24). His son Gedaliah (the name is spelled in a variant form in the book of Jeremiah) was appointed by the king of Babylon as governor of the land of Judah (2 Kings 25:22, Jeremiah 40:5).
event: When King Josiah found the book of the law, he was one of the delegation who, by the king's command, went to the prophetess Huldah to inquire of God's will (2 Kings 22:12). Also, in the time of King Jehoiakim, he defended Jeremiah, who had been accused of proclaiming God's word in the temple, and protected him so that he would not be put to death by the people (Jeremiah 26:24).
character: According to the biblical record, he is regarded as an administrator trusted by the royal house, and a person who, within the real power structure, held convictions of his own, to the point of maintaining a friendly relationship with the prophet Jeremiah and protecting him even in a period of political upheaval (Jeremiah 26:24).

introduce: Ahinadab was one of the officials in charge of the twelve administrative districts of Israel in the reign of King Solomon, a son of Iddo (1 Kings 4:14).
lifetime: Ahinadab was appointed as one of King Solomon's twelve district governors and administered the district of Mahanaim (1 Kings 4:14). No record of his birth or of his later life appears in Scripture (1 Kings 4:14).
event: As the son of Iddo, Ahinadab carried out the office of governor of the district of Mahanaim (1 Kings 4:14). As one of King Solomon's twelve governors, he belonged to the administrative system that provided food for the king and the royal household, one month each year (1 Kings 4:7, 4:14).

introduce: Ahinoam was the wife of Saul, the first king of Israel, and is recorded as the daughter of Ahimaaz (1 Samuel 14:50).
lifetime: She was the daughter of Ahimaaz and the wife of Saul (1 Samuel 14:50). 1 Samuel 14:49 records Saul's sons Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua and his two daughters Merab and Michal, but the text does not state that these were the children of Ahinoam.
event: There is no record of anything Ahinoam herself did or of any political event; the text records only her name and her father as the wife of Saul (1 Samuel 14:50).

introduce: Ahithophel was a Gilonite and a counselor in the time of King David; he was David's counselor, but afterward he joined Absalom's rebellion and opposed David.
lifetime: He was a Gilonite, David's counselor (2 Samuel 15:12). When David's son Absalom rebelled, Absalom sent for him from his city of Giloh (2 Samuel 15:12), and he was among those who conspired with Absalom (2 Samuel 15:31). When Absalom said that the counsel of Hushai was better than his own plan (2 Samuel 17:14), he returned to his hometown and hanged himself (2 Samuel 17:23).
event: His counsel was so outstanding that in those days it was regarded as being like inquiring of the word of God (2 Samuel 16:23). When Absalom entered Jerusalem, he advised Absalom to lie with the concubines whom David had left behind, completely severing the relationship with David (2 Samuel 16:21). He also proposed pursuing and eliminating David at once, but when his strategy came to nothing because Absalom accepted Hushai's proposal, he put his household in order and took his own life (2 Samuel 17:1-23).
character: He was a man of extraordinary counsel and insight who served as a key adviser to the house of David (2 Samuel 16:23). On the other hand, he showed an opportunistic and cold-blooded disposition, to the point of betraying his lord for the sake of his own political standing (2 Samuel 17:1). When his counsel was not accepted, he made an immediate decision and took an extreme course, being a man of strong pride and quick judgment of situations (2 Samuel 17:23). From the record that he was the father of Eliam and the grandfather of Bathsheba, it can be seen that he had a close blood relationship with the royal house (2 Samuel 11:3, 23:34).

call: Grandson of Eli (brother of Ichabod, father of Ahijah)
introduce: Ahitub was a grandson of Eli, the son of Phinehas, and a brother of Ichabod (1 Samuel 14:3). Ahijah, who wore the ephod, is recorded as his son (1 Samuel 14:3), Ahimelech the priest of Nob is also recorded as "the son of Ahitub" (1 Samuel 22:9, 22:11), and Ahimelech's son Abiathar fled and went to David (1 Samuel 22:20).
lifetime: Ahitub was a brother of Ichabod, a son of Phinehas, and a grandson of Eli, who had been the priest of the LORD at Shiloh (1 Samuel 14:3). His son Ahimelech is recorded as the priest of Nob (1 Samuel 22:9, 22:11).
event: In the biblical record, no specific deeds or particular events of Ahitub himself are described separately. In 1 Samuel he is introduced only as the father of Ahijah and Ahimelech (1 Samuel 14:3, 22:9).

introduce: Ahira is a person who appears in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament, a son of Enan (Numbers 1:15). He was a leader who represented the tribe of the descendants of Naphtali, one of the tribes of Israel (Numbers 1:15).
lifetime: Ahira was chosen as the representative of the tribe of Naphtali when Israel was counted in the wilderness of Sinai (Numbers 1:15). Afterward, in the course of the march through the wilderness, he served as the commander who led the division of the tribe of the descendants of Naphtali, which belonged to the camp of Dan (Numbers 2:29, 10:27). At the time of the dedication of the tabernacle he took part in the offering of gifts on behalf of his tribe (Numbers 7:78).
event: At the census of Israel his name was entered as the representative of the tribe of Naphtali (Numbers 1:15). On the twelfth day of the dedication of the tabernacle, as the leader of the descendants of Naphtali, he offered one silver plate, one silver bowl, one gold spoon, and the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the peace offerings (Numbers 7:78-83). During the march in the wilderness he led the division of the tribe of Naphtali, last in order in the camp of Dan (Numbers 10:27).

introduce: Ahiram is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the sons of Benjamin, and the ancestor of the Ahiramite clan within the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: He is mentioned as a descendant of Benjamin, and according to the genealogical record in Numbers he is among the sons of Benjamin (Numbers 26:38).
event: At the time of the census of the people of Israel, the Ahiramite clan came to be derived from Ahiram (Numbers 26:38).

introduce: Ahimaaz is a person recorded as the father of Ahinoam, the wife of Saul, the first king of Israel (1 Samuel 14:50).
lifetime: The biblical record about Ahimaaz stops at the statement that Ahinoam, the wife of Saul, was his daughter (1 Samuel 14:50); his own life and deeds are not recorded.
character: As the father of Saul's wife Ahinoam, he is mentioned in the record only as Saul's father-in-law, and the Bible gives no description of what character he had in his lifetime or of any specific deeds he showed (1 Samuel 14:50).

introduce: Ahiman is a person mentioned in the Bible as one of the descendants of Anak who lived in Hebron. He is known as one of the three sons of Anak, of the giant race of the ancient land of Canaan, and he appears as a figure in the course of the tribes of Israel spying out and conquering Canaan.
lifetime: Ahiman was born of Anak and lived in Hebron (Numbers 13:22). He is recorded, together with Sheshai and Talmai, as one of the descendants of Anak who were based in the region of Hebron (Numbers 13:22). Afterward there is a record that when Caleb of the tribe of Judah took Hebron, he and his brothers were driven out (Joshua 15:14).
event: When the spies reached Hebron, Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, descendants of Anak, were there (Numbers 13:22). The spies reported that they had seen the descendants of Anak there, and called them men of great stature, the descendants of the Anak who come from the Nephilim, mighty men (Numbers 13:28, 13:32-33); these words refer not to Ahiman individually but to the descendants of Anak as a whole. Afterward Joshua 15:14 records that Caleb drove out of Hebron the sons of Anak, namely, his three sons Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, and Judges 1:10 records that Judah struck down the Canaanites who lived in Hebron and killed Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
character: The Bible describes Ahiman as a member of the race of giants, as a descendant of Anak with an extremely outstanding physical build (Numbers 13:33). The spies of that time regarded him and his brothers as beings who struck fear into the people of Israel because of their massive bodies (Numbers 13:31-33).

introduce: Ahimoth is a person belonging to the genealogy of the descendants of Kohath of the tribe of Levi, a son of Elkanah, recorded together with Amasai as the sons of Elkanah (1 Chronicles 6:25).
lifetime: Ahimoth is recorded as one of the sons of Elkanah, Amasai and Ahimoth (1 Chronicles 6:25). This verse is within the passage recording the genealogy of those descended from Kohath (1 Chronicles 6:22-25).

introduce: A man of the tribe of Dan, recorded as the father of Oholiab, who was appointed for the making of the tabernacle (Exodus 31:6).
lifetime: No deeds of Ahisamach himself are recorded in Scripture. His son Oholiab, as a man of the tribe of Dan, was appointed together with Bezalel for the making of the tabernacle (Exodus 31:6), and God inspired him to teach (Exodus 35:34).
event: No event of Ahisamach himself is recorded. His son Oholiab was gifted and was an engraver and an embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen (Exodus 38:23). God filled him with a wise heart and enabled him to do the work of engraving, embroidering, weaving, and so on (Exodus 35:35).

introduce: Ahishahar is a person who appears in 1 Chronicles 7:10 in the Old Testament, a son of Bilhan of the tribe of Benjamin and a grandson of Jediael.
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Bilhan, the son of Jediael of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:10). The sons of Bilhan were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar, and Ahishahar comes last in that list (1 Chronicles 7:10).
event: His name is entered in the list of the sons of Bilhan (1 Chronicles 7:10). Then 1 Chronicles 7:11 records: "All these sons of Jediael were heads of their families, mighty men of valor, and those of their descendants fit for battle numbered 17,200" (1 Chronicles 7:11). No deeds of Ahishahar himself are recorded.

introduce: Ahishar was a high official who oversaw the internal affairs of the royal house in the time of Solomon in the kingdom of Israel.
lifetime: During the reign of King Solomon he held the office of minister of the palace, in charge of the household of the royal house (1 Kings 4:6).
event: His name is entered as minister of the palace in the list enumerating the officials of King Solomon (1 Kings 4:2-6). No other deeds are recorded.

introduce: Ahian is a person who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, recorded as one of the sons of Shemida of the tribe of Manasseh.
lifetime: Ahian is mentioned as one of the sons of Shemida (Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam), and his genealogical position belongs within the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 7:19).
event: Nothing is recorded in Scripture about his personal achievements or specific historical events (1 Chronicles 7:19).
character: According to the biblical record, no information about his personal character or physical features is confirmed (1 Chronicles 7:19).

meaning: Brother of the LORD, friend of the LORD
introduce: Ahijah was a prophet from Shiloh who was active in northern Israel from the time of Solomon to the time of Jeroboam I. He is recorded as the one who prophesied the division of the Davidic dynasty and designated Jeroboam as king of Israel.
lifetime: During the reign of Solomon, Ahijah met Jeroboam on the road, tore the new garment he was wearing into twelve pieces, and delivered the word of the LORD that he would give him ten tribes, saying, "Take ten pieces for yourself" (1 Kings 11:29-31). Afterward, when Jeroboam's son Abijah fell ill (1 Kings 14:1), Jeroboam's wife came to Shiloh in disguise; Ahijah could not see because his eyes were dim with age (1 Kings 14:4), but the LORD had told him beforehand (1 Kings 14:5), and when she came in at the door, he recognized her by the sound of her footsteps and spoke (1 Kings 14:6). He then delivered the word of the LORD's judgment on the house of Jeroboam (1 Kings 14:7-14).
event: He foretold the division of Israel and conveyed God's will to give ten tribes to Jeroboam (1 Kings 11:31). Also, when Jeroboam's wife came to ask about her son's illness, he pointed out Jeroboam's evil deeds and proclaimed a message of judgment that his house would be completely cut off (1 Kings 14:7-11). It is also mentioned that the acts of Solomon are recorded in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite (2 Chronicles 9:29).
character: Even in the circumstance of being old and dim of sight, he had the spiritual discernment to see through the queen's disguise (1 Kings 14:4-5). Even before Jeroboam, who was at the center of power, he showed a resolute character, conveying God's judgment directly and without fear (1 Kings 14:7-14).

call: Son of Ammishaddai (commander of the tribe of Dan)
introduce: Ahiezer is a person who appears in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament, a commander of the tribe of Dan and a son of Ammishaddai. In the course of the census and the arrangement of the camps during the journey through the wilderness, he is mentioned as the leader representing his tribe.
lifetime: On the first day of the second month of the second year after the Israelites came out of Egypt, at the census carried out at the tent of meeting in the wilderness of Sinai, he was chosen as the commander representing the tribe of Dan (Numbers 1:12). At the time of the dedication of the tabernacle he took part in the order of presenting gifts on behalf of his tribe (Numbers 7:66).
event: In Numbers 1, when Moses and Aaron convened the heads of the tribes, he took part in the census as the commander representing the tribe of Dan (Numbers 1:12). On the eleventh day of the dedication of the tabernacle, as the leader of the descendants of Dan, he presented his gifts: one silver plate and one silver bowl (both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering), one gold spoon filled with incense, for the burnt offering one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old, for the sin offering one male goat, and for the peace offering two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old (Numbers 7:66-71).

introduce: Ahio is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded in 1 Chronicles 8:14-16 as one of the sons of Beriah.
lifetime: Ahio, a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, is recorded along with Shashak and Jeremoth, and others, as "all sons of Beriah" (1 Chronicles 8:14-16). It is recorded that Beriah and Shema became heads of the inhabitants of Aijalon and drove out the inhabitants of Gath (1 Chronicles 8:13). There is no further explanation in Scripture of the period in which Ahio specifically lived or of his personal life (1 Chronicles 8:14).

introduce: Ahihud is a person who appears in the Old Testament; in Numbers and in 1 Chronicles he is recorded as persons of the same name belonging to different tribes.
lifetime: In Numbers he is recorded as a descendant of the tribe of Asher, the son of Shelomi, a chief of the tribe of the descendants of Asher who was chosen as a representative of the tribe when the land of Canaan was divided (Numbers 34:27). In 1 Chronicles 8:7 he is mentioned, in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, as a son begotten together with Uzza (1 Chronicles 8:7).
event: According to the record of Numbers 34, Ahihud was one of the chiefs chosen and appointed from each tribe, as a chief of the tribe of the descendants of Asher, to divide the land of Canaan as an inheritance (Numbers 34:18, 34:27). In 1 Chronicles 8:7 it is only recorded that "he also begot Uzza and Ahihud," and no deeds of Ahihud himself are recorded.

introduce: Ahilud is a person who appears in the Old Testament, recorded as the father of persons who held office within the administrative system of the royal houses of David and Solomon.
lifetime: He is mentioned as the father of Jehoshaphat, and appears as the ancestral origin of the person who held the office of court recorder during the reign of King David (2 Samuel 8:16). Also, in the time of King Solomon he appears in connection with an administrative post as the father of Baana, an official of Israel (1 Kings 4:12).
event: His son Jehoshaphat was the recorder during the reign of David (2 Samuel 8:16, 20:24), and he is recorded as the recorder in Solomon's time as well (1 Kings 4:3). Another son, Baana, was one of the twelve governors Solomon appointed, and was in charge of Taanach, Megiddo, and all the land of Beth-shean (1 Kings 4:12).

introduce: Akkub was a descendant of David, one of the persons who continued the genealogy of the royal house of Judah after the Babylonian exile. He is included in the list of David's descendants recorded in 1 Chronicles 3, and is mentioned as a son of Elioenai.
lifetime: In the genealogy of the descendants of Jeconiah, who was taken captive (1 Chronicles 3:17-24), he is recorded as one of the seven sons of Elioenai son of Neariah (1 Chronicles 3:24).
event: His name is merely entered in the list of the descendants of the house of David, and no personal deeds of his are recorded in Scripture (1 Chronicles 3:24).

call: Father of Baal-hanan, king of Edom
introduce: Achbor is a person recorded as the father of Baal-hanan, king of Edom. In the genealogy of the kings of Edom in Genesis 36:38 and 1 Chronicles 1:49, Baal-hanan is introduced as "the son of Achbor."
lifetime: Achbor is recorded as the father of Baal-hanan, king of Edom (1 Chronicles 1:49). Scripture has no record of the period he lived or of his life.
event: There is no record in Scripture that Achbor himself left any specific deeds. He is mentioned only in the course of introducing his son Baal-hanan, who became king of Edom (Genesis 36:38, 1 Chronicles 1:49).

introduce: Acsah is a woman who appears in the biblical record, mentioned as the daughter of Caleb and the wife of Othniel.
lifetime: Acsah was born the daughter of Caleb of the tribe of Judah (Joshua 15:16). Caleb declared that he would give his daughter Acsah as wife to the man who struck down Kiriath-sepher and took it, and Othniel, the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz, took it and she married him (Joshua 15:17, Judges 1:12, Judges 1:13). In 1 Chronicles 2:49 also, at the end of the passage recording the descendants of Caleb's concubine Maacah (1 Chronicles 2:48-49), it is said, "Caleb's daughter was Acsah" (1 Chronicles 2:49).
event: When Acsah left to be married, she urged her husband Othniel to ask her father for a field, and got down from her donkey, and when Caleb asked what she wanted (Joshua 15:18, Judges 1:14), she asked for a blessing and said, "Since you have sent me to the land of the Negev, give me also springs of water." So Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs (Joshua 15:19, Judges 1:15).

introduce: A woman who appears in the Gospel of Luke in the New Testament, the daughter of Phanuel of the tribe of Asher. She is recorded as a prophetess who did not leave the temple in Jerusalem and prayed with fasting night and day.
lifetime: Anna lived with her husband for seven years after marrying, and became a widow after he died (Luke 2:36). Afterward, for eighty-four years of widowhood, she did not leave the temple, but served with fasting and prayer (Luke 2:37).
event: At the very time when Simeon blessed the parents who had brought the infant Jesus to the temple, she came forward and gave thanks to God (Luke 2:34, 2:38). She also spoke about the child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem (Luke 2:38).
character: Anna was a woman of very advanced age who served in the temple night and day (Luke 2:37). The Bible states explicitly that she was a prophetess (Luke 2:36).

introduce: Annas is a person who appears in the Gospels and Acts as high priest, and is the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year (John 18:13). Luke 3:2 records that the word of God came to John the son of Zechariah during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas.
lifetime: The word of God came to John the son of Zechariah while Annas and Caiaphas were high priests (Luke 3:2). Annas was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year (John 18:13). After Jesus was arrested and bound, He was first led away to Annas (John 18:13), and Annas sent Him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest (John 18:24). Afterward, at the council that examined the apostles, Annas the high priest was present together with Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and the family of the high priest (Acts 4:6).
event: After Jesus was arrested, He was first led to Annas (John 18:13), and Annas sent Him, still bound, to Caiaphas (John 18:24). Annas the high priest was present at the council convened over what the apostles had been saying to the people (Acts 4:6), and that council charged Peter and John not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus (Acts 4:18).
character: He had the aspect of a politician who valued the actual power of his family above the official position. Even during the time when his son-in-law Caiaphas was high priest, he was mentioned together with him as high priest, so firm was his political standing (Luke 3:2). Moreover, in order to protect his family and vested interests, he took an authoritarian and decisive course, harshly suppressing and threatening Jesus and the early Christian apostles (Acts 4:18, Acts 5:28).

introduce: Anthothijah is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in 1 Chronicles 8 in the Old Testament, one of the members who make up the genealogy of the house of Benjamin.
lifetime: Anthothijah is recorded as one of the sons of Shashak, a descendant of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:24).

introduce: Andrew is a person who appears in the New Testament, a brother of Peter and a fisherman from Bethsaida in Galilee. He is recorded as one of the two who were disciples of John the Baptist and then followed Jesus.
lifetime: Andrew was from Bethsaida and was a brother of Simon Peter (John 1:44). At first he was a disciple of John the Baptist, and after meeting Jesus for the first time he brought his brother Simon to Jesus (John 1:40-42). Afterward, while casting a net by the Sea of Galilee, he received the call of Jesus and began in earnest to follow Him (Matthew 4:18-20). His name is included in the list of Jesus' twelve disciples (Mark 3:18).
event: At the scene of the miracle of the five loaves and two fish, he told Jesus that a boy had five barley loaves and two small fish (John 6:8-9). When some Greeks in Jerusalem wished to see Jesus, he reported this to Jesus together with Philip (John 12:20-22). He also asked Jesus on the Mount of Olives, together with Peter, James, and John, about the destruction of the temple and its signs (Mark 13:3-4).
character: Andrew often played the role of a mediator who introduced others to Jesus. He brought his brother Simon to Jesus (John 1:41-42) and guided Greeks to Jesus, showing a tendency to connect people in the formation of the early church (John 12:22). He also had a practical side, grasping the situation on the scene at the time of the five loaves and two fish and making a suggestion (John 6:9).

introduce: Andronicus is a person mentioned in the New Testament letter to the Romans, a believer of the early church whom the apostle Paul greeted, calling him "my relative" (Romans 16:7).
lifetime: Andronicus believed in Christ before Paul did, and was a person respected among the apostles (Romans 16:7). He had the experience of being imprisoned together with Paul (Romans 16:7).
event: Andronicus is recorded as one who, together with Junia, was well known among the apostles (Romans 16:7). He was also once imprisoned together with Paul (Romans 16:7).
character: Andronicus is mentioned as a relative of Paul and shares the ethnic characteristic of being a Jew (Romans 16:7). He held a position of recognition among the apostles (Romans 16:7).

introduce: Antipas is a person who appears in the New Testament book of Revelation, mentioned as a faithful witness of the church in Pergamum. He is recorded as one who kept his faith and was martyred in Pergamum, which is described as the place where Satan's throne is.
lifetime: Antipas was killed where Satan's throne is, that is, where Satan dwells, and Jesus Christ called him "My faithful witness" (Revelation 2:13). Scripture has no record of what activity he carried out there.
event: Antipas fulfilled the role of a faithful witness until he was killed in Pergamum, which is called the place where Satan dwells (Revelation 2:13).
character: He is described as a faithful witness of Jesus Christ, one who did not abandon his faith even in an environment of extreme persecution and threat (Revelation 2:13).

introduce: Ahlai is a person of the tribe of Judah recorded in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a son of Sheshan (1 Chronicles 2:31).
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Sheshan, the son of Ishi, the son of Appaim (1 Chronicles 2:31). Ahlai is a person mentioned in the genealogy of the line of Sheshan (1 Chronicles 2:31).

introduce: Alvan is a descendant of Seir the Horite, who lived in the region of Edom, a son of Shobal son of Seir. In the genealogy of 1 Chronicles he is recorded as one of the sons of Shobal (1 Chronicles 1:40).
lifetime: Alvan was born a son of Shobal son of Seir (1 Chronicles 1:38, 1:40), and his brothers were Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam (1 Chronicles 1:40).
event: Alvan is recorded as a son of Shobal and as one of the persons who make up the genealogy of the descendants of Seir (Genesis 36:23). Apart from this, the Bible records no concrete achievement or event that he personally carried out (Genesis 36:23).

call: Son of Jehoaddah (descendant of the house of Saul)
introduce: Alemeth is a person of the tribe of Benjamin, belonging to the genealogy of the house of Saul, recorded as a descendant of Merib-baal, the son of Jonathan.
lifetime: Alemeth is a descendant of Merib-baal, the son of Jonathan, and was born a son of Jehoaddah (1 Chronicles 8:36). He is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 8 and 9 as one of the persons who make up the genealogy of the house of Saul (1 Chronicles 9:42).
event: No specific historical event or independent achievement concerning Alemeth appears in the biblical record. He is mentioned mainly within the context of listing the genealogies of the tribe of Benjamin and the house of Saul (1 Chronicles 8:36, 9:42).

introduce: Alexander is a person mentioned in the Gospel of Mark in the New Testament, a son of Simon of Cyrene. He is introduced, together with Rufus, as a son of Simon (Mark 15:21).
lifetime: He was born the son of Simon of Cyrene and the brother of Rufus (Mark 15:21). No detailed record of his life as a whole remains in Scripture; when Simon, coming in from the country and passing by, was forced to carry the cross of Jesus, he was introduced as "the father of Alexander and Rufus" (Mark 15:21).
event: Scripture records no event or achievement of Alexander himself, and his name appears only in the verse that introduces his father Simon as "the father of Alexander and Rufus" (Mark 15:21).

introduce: Allon is a person of the tribe of Simeon who appears in the genealogical record of 1 Chronicles 4:37. He is recorded as the son of Jedaiah and the father of Shiphi.
lifetime: In the genealogy of the descendants of Simeon, Allon is recorded as the son of Jedaiah and the father of Shiphi (1 Chronicles 4:37). 1 Chronicles 4:37 describes the son of Shiphi as "the grandson of Allon, great-grandson of Jedaiah, great-great-grandson of Shimri, and fifth-generation descendant of Shemaiah."
event: No deeds of Allon himself are recorded in Scripture. The chiefs of the descendants of Simeon who were listed by name, including his grandson (the son of Shiphi), went in the days of Hezekiah to the east side of the valley at the border of Gedor, obtained pasture there, and utterly destroyed the Meunites who were there (1 Chronicles 4:37-41).

introduce: A son borne by Rizpah, the concubine of King Saul, who was handed over to the Gibeonites as a sacrificial offering and executed.
lifetime: Armoni was born of King Saul and Rizpah daughter of Aiah, and in the reign of King David, at the demand of the Gibeonites, he was put to death together with people of Saul's house (2 Samuel 21:8).
event: When a three-year famine occurred in the time of David, David learned that the cause was that Saul had slaughtered the Gibeonites, and in order to atone for this he handed over seven of Saul's descendants to the Gibeonites. At this time Armoni, together with Mephibosheth, was handed over to the Gibeonites and was hanged on the mountain at the beginning of the barley harvest (2 Samuel 21:1, 21:8, 21:9).

introduce: Almodad is a person mentioned as a descendant of Shem, the son of Noah, and as one of the sons of Joktan. He is one of the ancient persons who can be identified through the genealogies of the Bible.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons born to Joktan the son of Eber (Genesis 10:26). As a person in the genealogy continuing the line of Shem, he belongs to the grandson generation of Eber, the ancestor of the Hebrew people (Genesis 10:25-26).
event: Almodad, together with his brothers, lived in the eastern hill country on the way from Mesha to Sephar (Genesis 10:30).

introduce: Amnon was David's eldest son, born to King David and Ahinoam the Jezreelitess. He ended his life when he was killed by his half-brother Absalom because of the incident in which he violated his half-sister Tamar.
lifetime: He was born as David's firstborn to Ahinoam the Jezreelitess (2 Samuel 3:2). Afterward he fell lovesick for his half-sister Tamar, and on the advice of Jonadab he pretended to be ill, called Tamar to his bedroom, and raped her (2 Samuel 13:1-14). After this incident he suddenly came to hate Tamar intensely and drove her outside (2 Samuel 13:15-17), and two years later he was invited to the sheepshearing feast hosted by Absalom, and when he went he was killed by Absalom's servants (2 Samuel 13:28-29).
event: As the eldest son of the house of David, he is remembered not for political achievements but for a personal sexual crime.
