The incident of forcibly violating his half-sister Tamar became the fuse of a tragic fratricidal strife in the house of David (2 Samuel 13:14). The change of heart and cruel attitude he showed immediately after raping Tamar earned the resentment of Tamar's brother Absalom, and eventually brought about his being killed through Absalom's meticulous plan of revenge (2 Samuel 13:28-29).
character: He showed a tendency to act impulsively, unable to restrain his own desires. He revealed a lack of judgment of the situation and of ethical discernment, to the point of carrying out as it was the crafty scheme proposed by his cousin Jonadab (2 Samuel 13:5-6). He also showed a fickle side, in that his feeling toward Tamar changed abruptly from love to bitter hatred, and he displayed an immaturity that did not consider the political and familial repercussions his actions would bring (2 Samuel 13:15).

call: Son of Ram (direct ancestor of David and Jesus)
introduce: Amminadab is a person who appears in the genealogies of the Hebrew Bible, the son of Ram and the father of Nahshon. He was born in the family of the tribe of Judah, and is recorded as a direct ancestor in the line leading to King David and Jesus.
lifetime: Amminadab was the son of Ram and begot Nahshon (Ruth 4:19). His son Nahshon was the commander of the descendants of Judah at the time of the Exodus (Numbers 1:7). Also, his daughter Elisheba became the wife of Aaron and bore Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar (Exodus 6:23). In the Hebrew genealogy he is located in the middle generations, starting from Judah the son of Jacob and extending to David (1 Chronicles 2:10).
event: His son Nahshon was the leader of the descendants of Judah in the wilderness (Numbers 2:3), and his daughter Elisheba became the wife of Aaron (Exodus 6:23).
character: In the biblical record there is no description of Amminadab's personal character or specific deeds, but his blood-relationship position is emphasized as an ancestor continuing the line of the tribe of Judah and as the father of Nahshon, the brother-in-law of Aaron (Matthew 1:4).

introduce: Ammizabad was the son of Benaiah, the commander over the division of the third month in the military organization established in the time of King David, and he was a man who belonged to that division (1 Chronicles 27:5-6).
lifetime: In David's time the army of Israel was divided into divisions that served in rotation month by month (1 Chronicles 27:1). Ammizabad was among the division of the third month, whose commander was Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada the chief priest, Ammizabad's father (1 Chronicles 27:5-6).
event: In King David's military organization, the division of 24,000 men assigned to the third month was under Benaiah, and it is recorded that his son Ammizabad was among that division (1 Chronicles 27:5-6). This was part of the arrangement by which David divided the army of Israel into divisions that served in monthly rotation throughout the year (1 Chronicles 27:1).

call: Father of Ahiezer, chief of the tribe of Dan
introduce: Ammishaddai is a figure who appears in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament and is recorded as the father of Ahiezer, chief of the tribe of Dan (Numbers 1:12).
lifetime: Ammishaddai was the father of Ahiezer, chief of the sons of Dan, and his name appears in the records of the Book of Numbers concerning the list of the chiefs of the tribe of Dan, the arrangement of the camp, the offerings, and the march (Numbers 1:12, 2:25, 7:66, 10:25). The Bible records nothing else of his life.
event: No deeds of Ammishaddai himself are recorded. His son Ahiezer, as chief of the sons of Dan, presented his offering on the eleventh day (Numbers 7:66) and led the army of Dan (Numbers 10:25).

call: Spy of the tribe of Dan (son of Gemalli)
introduce: Ammiel is a figure who appears in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament, one of the twelve spies chosen to spy out the land of Canaan on behalf of the tribe of Dan. He was the son of Gemalli, and was one of the representatives whom the people of Israel sent out after the exodus in order to spy out the land of Canaan.
lifetime: He was a man chosen from among the chiefs of the tribe of Dan, one of the heads of the children of Israel whom Moses sent from the wilderness of Paran to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:2-3). He is recorded as the son of Gemalli, and he carried out his mission as the spy representing the tribe of Dan (Numbers 13:12).
event: He took part on behalf of the tribe of Dan when the children of Israel spied out the land of Canaan, and as a member of the spies he explored the region of Canaan and returned (Numbers 13:12). Afterward the spies, including him, showed the fruit of the land to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation of the children of Israel and reported on the condition of the land (Numbers 13:26).

call: Father of Talmai king of Geshur
introduce: Ammihud is a man recorded as the father of Talmai, king of Geshur (2 Samuel 13:37). Talmai was the father of Maacah, the mother of David's son Absalom (2 Samuel 3:3).
lifetime: He is recorded as the father of Talmai, king of Geshur (2 Samuel 13:37). The Bible records nothing else of his life.
event: After killing Amnon, Absalom fled to Talmai the son of Ammihud (2 Samuel 13:37) and stayed in Geshur for three years (2 Samuel 13:38). No deeds of Ammihud himself are recorded.

call: Commander of the tribe of Ephraim (great-grandfather of Joshua)
introduce: Ammihud is a figure who appears in Numbers and 1 Chronicles; in the genealogy of the tribe of Ephraim he is recorded as the father of Elishama and the great-grandfather of Joshua.
lifetime: Ammihud begat Elishama, chief of the tribe of Ephraim; his son Elishama in turn begat Nun, and Nun begat Joshua (1 Chronicles 7:26-27). He is mentioned in the genealogy as a direct ancestor of Joshua, the leader of the conquest of Canaan.
event: The book of Numbers states plainly that Elishama, chief of the sons of Ephraim, was the son of Ammihud (Numbers 1:10, 2:18, 7:48). No deeds of Ammihud himself are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Ampliatus is a figure who appears near the end of the book of Romans in the New Testament, one of those whom the apostle Paul mentioned when he sent greetings to the Christians in Rome.
lifetime: He is a man mentioned when Paul conveyed greetings to the saints in Rome (Romans 16:8). The Bible records no personal details of his life, such as his birth or upbringing.
event: He was called by the apostle Paul "my beloved in the Lord" (Romans 16:8).
character: He was trusted and held in affection by the apostle Paul, to the point of being regarded as beloved in the Lord (Romans 16:8). The name Ampliatus is a name of Latin origin meaning "enlarged" or "broad," and it was one of the names commonly used in Roman society at that time among the lower classes or slaves (Romans 16:8).

call: Son of Bani (a Levite of Merari)
meaning: The one who is my mighty strength
introduce: Amzi is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles, belonging to the descendants of Merari in the tribe of Levi. He is recorded as the son of Bani and is mentioned in the genealogy connected with the service of the temple.
lifetime: Amzi was the son of Bani, a descendant of Merari (1 Chronicles 6:46). He belongs to the ancestral line of Ethan of the sons of Merari (the father of Hilkiah, the son of Bani), among those whom David appointed as singers (1 Chronicles 6:44-47).
event: When David appointed the Levites to the service of song in the house of the LORD after the ark had come to rest (1 Chronicles 6:31), his descendant Ethan is recorded as one of the sons of Merari who served at the left hand (1 Chronicles 6:44-46). No deeds of Amzi himself are recorded in the Bible.

call: Father of Adoniram (father of the overseer of forced labor)
introduce: Abda is a man mentioned in the biblical record as the father of Adoniram. He appears as the one who indicates the family background of Adoniram, who was the official over the forced labor during the reign of King Solomon.
lifetime: Abda is recorded as the father of Adoniram, an official of Solomon (1 Kings 4:6). Beyond this, there is no biblical record of Abda's birth, upbringing, or the specific course of his life.

introduce: Abdon was a judge from the tribe of Ephraim, the son of Hillel the Pirathonite. He is recorded as one who was active in the latter part of the period of the judges of Israel.
lifetime: He was born as the son of Hillel from Pirathon (Judges 12:13). He was active for eight years as a judge governing Israel (Judges 12:14). After finishing his task as judge he died and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites (Judges 12:15).
event: He served as judge of Israel for eight years (Judges 12:14). It is recorded that he had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys (Judges 12:14).
character: He had many children and grandchildren, and the record that they rode on seventy donkeys suggests that at that time he had secured economic wealth and social standing for his family (Judges 12:14). Apart from this, the Bible records nothing about his personal character or his specific manner of governing.

call: Son of Malluch (a Levite of Merari)
introduce: Abdi was a Levite of the descendants of Merari in the tribe of Levi, the son of Malluch and an ancestor of Ethan.
lifetime: Abdi belonged to the family line of Merari the Levite, and is a member of the ancestral line mentioned when David organized the Levites and entrusted them with the work of praise (1 Chronicles 6:44).
event: Abdi is recorded as an ancestor of Ethan the Levite, who was appointed to the work of praise (Ethan was the son of Kishi, and Kishi the son of Abdi) (1 Chronicles 6:44). No deeds of Abdi himself are recorded in the Bible.

call: Son of Guni (chief of the tribe of Gad)
introduce: Abdiel is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles, recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Gad as the son of Guni and the father of Ahi, who became a chief.
lifetime: Abdiel is mentioned in the genealogy of the sons of Gad as the son of Guni and the father of Ahi (1 Chronicles 5:15). The sons of Gad, among whom his son Ahi became chief, lived in Gilead and Bashan and in their towns, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon (1 Chronicles 5:15-16).
event: No deeds of Abdiel himself are recorded, and his son Ahi became a chief of the sons of Gad (1 Chronicles 5:15).

introduce: Appaim is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a member of the house of Jerahmeel, a descendant of Perez the son of Judah.
lifetime: Appaim was the son of Nadab (1 Chronicles 2:30) and the father of Ishi (1 Chronicles 2:31).

call: A believer of the early church
introduce: Apphia is a figure mentioned in the book of Philemon in the New Testament, a woman who appears as one of the recipients of Paul's letter.
lifetime: In the greeting of the letter Paul sent to Philemon, Paul mentions Apphia and calls her a sister (Philemon 1:2). In the same greeting Apphia is mentioned, together with Philemon and Archippus, as a recipient of the letter (Philemon 1:1-2).
event: Paul specified the recipients of the letter as Philemon, the sister Apphia, Archippus, and the church in Philemon's house (Philemon 1:1-2).
character: Paul showed respect for her by calling her "our sister" (Philemon 1:2). She was also regarded, together with Philemon, as a member of the community that cooperated with the apostle Paul in carrying out the work of the gospel (Philemon 1:2).

introduce: Absalom was the third son of David, born to King David and Maacah, the daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur. He was the man who raised a rebellion in order to usurp David's throne, and in the Bible he is a major figure who symbolically shows the internal strife and conflict of David's house over the kingship.
lifetime: He was born to David and Maacah (2 Samuel 3:3), and he killed his half-brother Amnon, who had raped his sister Tamar, and fled to Geshur (2 Samuel 13:28-29). Afterward he returned to Jerusalem through the mediation of Joab and was reconciled with his father the king, David (2 Samuel 14:33), but he began the work of winning the hearts of the people in order to seize the kingship (2 Samuel 15:6). He proclaimed himself king in Hebron and raised a rebellion against David (2 Samuel 15:10), and he led an army in pursuit of David, but was defeated by David's army in the battle in the forest of Ephraim (2 Samuel 18:6-7). While fleeing, his hair caught in the branches of an oak tree, and he was killed by Joab (2 Samuel 18:9-14).
event: Two years later, at the festival of sheepshearing, he had Amnon, who had defiled his sister Tamar, killed (2 Samuel 13:23-29). Beside the gate of Jerusalem, he pretended to judge the lawsuits of the people passing by on the road, and so captured their hearts (2 Samuel 15:2-5). He plotted a rebellion in Hebron and caused David to flee from Jerusalem (2 Samuel 15:14), and on the counsel of Ahithophel he lay with David's concubines before the eyes of all the multitude of Israel, showing his intention to seize the kingship formally (2 Samuel 16:21-22).
character: He was outstanding in appearance, so that he was praised for his beauty in all Israel, and the hair of his head was very thick and heavy (2 Samuel 14:25-26). He showed meticulousness and ruthlessness in waiting two years to kill Amnon in order to achieve his purpose (2 Samuel 13:23). He also had the political skill of a demagogue, going up to people himself and kissing them in order to win their favor (2 Samuel 15:5). After his sons had died, having no son to keep his name in remembrance, he set up a pillar for himself in the King's Valley to commemorate himself (2 Samuel 18:18).

introduce: Adna was one of the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian exile, a man of the descendants of Pahath-moab (Ezra 10:30).
lifetime: Adna is a man mentioned as one of the descendants of Pahath-moab in the list, in Ezra 10, of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:30, 10:44).
event: Adna's name was recorded as one of the descendants of Pahath-moab in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:30, 10:44).

call: Grandson of Sheshan (a descendant of Judah)
introduce: Attai is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles; in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah he is recorded as the son born to the daughter of Sheshan and Jarha, an Egyptian servant, and as the father of Nathan.
lifetime: Sheshan of the tribe of Judah had no sons but only daughters, so he gave his daughter to Jarha, an Egyptian servant, to be his wife, and Jarha begat Attai by her (1 Chronicles 2:34-35). Attai begat Nathan (1 Chronicles 2:36).
event: In the biblical record there is no account of any specific achievement or particular event of Attai himself; his name is registered only as a member who forms part of the family tree of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:35).

introduce: Addi is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus recorded in the Gospel of Luke in the New Testament, the son of Cosam and the father of Melchi.
lifetime: Addi is a figure placed in the line of Jesus that descends through the descendants of Nathan and David (Luke 3:28).
event: In the biblical record nothing is mentioned of any specific achievement or special event that Addi carried out during his lifetime.

call: Third son of Ishmael, ancestor of a nomadic tribe of Arabia
meaning: God's discipline, God's miracle, God's glory
introduce: He was the third of the twelve sons begotten by Ishmael, the son of Hagar, Abraham's concubine. He was born in accordance with the promise that God would cause Ishmael to beget twelve princes (Genesis 17:20, 25:13).
lifetime: He was born as a son of Ishmael (Genesis 25:13). Together with his brothers he was one of the twelve princes who were named, as the sons of Ishmael, according to their villages and encampments (Genesis 25:16), and the descendants of Ishmael dwelt from Havilah as far as Shur, which is before Egypt in the direction of Asshur, and settled in the presence of all their brothers (Genesis 25:18).
event: According to the word spoken to Abraham that Ishmael would beget twelve princes (Genesis 17:20), the sons of Ishmael became twelve princes by their tribes, and Adbeel was one of them (Genesis 25:13, 25:16). The Bible has no record of Adbeel's individual deeds, and his name appears only in the list of the sons of Ishmael (Genesis 25:13, 1 Chronicles 1:29).

introduce: Azzan is a figure who appears in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament, introduced as a chief of the tribe of the sons of Issachar and recorded as the father of Paltiel (Numbers 34:26).
lifetime: Azzan is recorded as the father of Paltiel in the expression "Paltiel the son of Azzan, prince of the tribe of the sons of Issachar" (Numbers 34:26). The one who appears in the list of those chosen to divide the inheritance of the land of Canaan is his son Paltiel (Numbers 34:17-18, 34:26).
event: The Bible has no record of deeds of Azzan himself. When one chief from each tribe was chosen for the distribution of the inheritance, as God commanded Moses (Numbers 34:18), from the tribe of Issachar Azzan's son Paltiel was entered on the list (Numbers 34:26, 34:29).

call: Son of Shem (founder of the Assyrian Empire)
introduce: Asshur is a man recorded as one of the five sons of Shem, the son of Noah (Genesis 10:22). His name appears as a son of Shem in the genealogy of the nations after the flood in Genesis 10.
lifetime: Asshur was born as a son of Shem (Genesis 10:22), and in the record of 1 Chronicles as well his name is included in the list of the descendants of Shem (1 Chronicles 1:17). No detailed account of the whole course of his life is recorded in the Bible.
event: The Bible has no record of Asshur's individual deeds, and his name appears only in the list of the sons of Shem (Genesis 10:22, 1 Chronicles 1:17). It is Nimrod, who began his kingdom in the land of Shinar, who is recorded as having built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah, and Resen (Genesis 10:10-12).

call: A leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Azzur is a man among the heads of the people in the Jewish community that returned after the end of the Babylonian exile. His name is entered in the list of those who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:17).
lifetime: Azzur is recorded in Nehemiah 10 as one of the heads of the people who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:17). There is a record that our princes, our Levites, and our priests made a firm covenant, wrote it, and sealed it (Nehemiah 9:38).
event: Azzur was included in the list of the heads of the people who sealed the covenant in which the people swore with a curse that they would separate themselves from the foreigners and observe the law of God (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:17, 10:28-29).

introduce: Assir is a man belonging to the descendants of Korah in the tribe of Levi, a male whose place in the family line is confirmed through the genealogical records of the Bible (Exodus 6:24).
lifetime: Assir is recorded as one of the sons of Korah (Exodus 6:24; 1 Chronicles 6:22). Assir the son of Ebiasaph in 1 Chronicles 6:23, 37 is a different person.

introduce: Aeneas is a figure who appears in the book of Acts in the New Testament, a man who lived in the region of Lydda and who had suffered from paralysis for eight years.
lifetime: Aeneas lived in Lydda, and having been struck with paralysis he had been lying on his bed for eight years (Acts 9:33).
event: When Peter visited the saints at Lydda, he found Aeneas lying there paralyzed (Acts 9:32-33). Peter said to him, "Jesus Christ heals you; get up and make your bed" (Acts 9:34). Immediately Aeneas got up from his bed, and when all who lived at Lydda and Sharon saw this, they turned to the Lord (Acts 9:34-35).

introduce: Jacan is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles, recorded in the genealogy of the sons of Gad as one of the seven sons of Abihail.
lifetime: Jacan was a son of Abihail (1 Chronicles 5:14), and he is recorded as one of the seven kinsmen of the clan, together with Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Zia, and Eber (1 Chronicles 5:13). The sons of Gad lived in the land of Bashan (1 Chronicles 5:11), and it is said that they lived in Gilead and Bashan and in their towns, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon (1 Chronicles 5:16).

introduce: Jakeh is a man who appears in Proverbs 30, recorded as the father of Agur. Information in the Bible about his specific identity or background is limited.
lifetime: It is recorded that Agur the son of Jakeh delivered the words of the proverbs (Proverbs 30:1). The Bible has no record of what age he lived in or what kind of life he specifically lived.
character: The biblical record contains no direct description of his character or personal traits (Proverbs 30:1). He is known only as a name in the family line, in that his son Agur is mentioned as the one who wrote the proverbs.

call: The apostle James (son of Zebedee), James the Greater
introduce: He was the son of Zebedee and the brother of the apostle John, and one of the twelve disciples of Jesus. According to the Gospel records, he was one of the core disciples who, together with Peter and John, accompanied Jesus at the major scenes of his ministry, and he is recorded as the first of the apostles to be martyred.
lifetime: While mending nets in a boat with his father Zebedee by the Sea of Galilee, he was called by Jesus and became a disciple (Matthew 4:21). Afterward, during the public ministry of Jesus, he accompanied him at the major events, and when King Herod set out to harm some of the church, he was put to death with the sword (Acts 12:1-2).
event: He was present, together with Peter and John, at the raising of the daughter of Jairus (Mark 5:37). He witnessed the transfigured appearance of Jesus when Jesus took Peter, James, and John up a high mountain (Matthew 17:1-2). In the place called Gethsemane, Jesus took him along with Peter and John, and he heard the words telling him to stay and keep watch (Mark 14:32-34). He was put to death with the sword by King Herod (Acts 12:1-2).
character: Together with John he received from Jesus the nickname Boanerges, meaning "sons of thunder" (Mark 3:17). He had a hot-tempered and hasty disposition, to the point of proposing to call down fire from heaven to destroy a village of Samaria when it would not receive Jesus (Luke 9:54). Through his mother he also revealed a longing for high position, to the point of asking to sit at the right and left hand in the kingdom of Jesus (Matthew 20:20-21).

call: Son of Isaac (father of the twelve tribes of Israel)
meaning: One who grasped the heel, one who takes by force
introduce: Jacob, born as the second son of Isaac and Rebekah, is a man who was later called Israel. He had the sons who became the ancestors of the twelve tribes, and he established his standing as a patriarch within the patriarchal social structure of the ancient Near East.
lifetime: Jacob was born holding the heel of his twin brother Esau (Genesis 25:26). In order to obtain the birthright in place of his brother he made use of a bowl of lentil stew (Genesis 25:29-34), and he deceived his father Isaac and seized the blessing of the firstborn (Genesis 27:1-29). Afterward, to escape his brother's threat to kill him, he fled to Haran, where his maternal uncle Laban lived (Genesis 27:41-45). There he took Leah and Rachel as his wives and had children (Genesis 29:15-30), and after twenty years of labor he returned to Canaan leading great flocks (Genesis 31:41). In his old age he moved to Egypt, which his son Joseph was governing, and died there (Genesis 46:1-7, 47:28).
event: At Bethel, while sleeping with a stone for a pillow, Jacob experienced a vision in which God gave him a promise (Genesis 28:10-22). Working for Laban in Haran for wages, he accumulated property of his own (Genesis 30:25-43). On the way back to Canaan, at the ford of the Jabbok, he wrestled with an angel and received the name Israel (Genesis 32:22-32). Returning to his homeland, he met his brother Esau again and was reconciled with him (Genesis 33:1-16), and he purchased land at Shechem and tried to settle there (Genesis 33:18-19). Also, because of a famine, he made the decision to lead his family to move to the land of Goshen in Egypt (Genesis 46:1-34).
character: Jacob had a calculating character, sparing no cunning or means to achieve his purposes (Genesis 27:18-24). He showed a survival ability to adapt quickly to changes in circumstances (Genesis 29:1-30), and in his dealings with his maternal uncle Laban he displayed the wisdom of using circumstances to his advantage, as in regulating the breeding of the flocks (Genesis 30:37-43). He also showed favoritism within his family; in particular he loved his son Joseph, born of Rachel, above the others, and so gave occasion for conflict among the brothers (Genesis 37:3). Even while enduring hardship, he was a man with a strong will to make his household prosper (Genesis 32:9-12).

직업/직위: father of the twelve tribes of Israel

call: Son of Simeon (ancestor of the Jachinite clan)
introduce: Jachin was the fourth son of Simeon, who was born to Jacob and Leah, and so a grandson of Jacob and the ancestor of the Jachinite clan within the tribe of Simeon. 1 Chronicles 4:24 records him as Jarib, referring to the same person.
lifetime: As a son of Simeon who lived in the land of Canaan, he moved to Egypt with Jacob and settled there as a member of the tribe of Simeon (Genesis 46:10).
event: As a son of Simeon, he became the source from which the Jachinite clan, the family unit of the tribe of Simeon, was formed (Numbers 26:12).

call: Son of Shimei (a chief of Benjamin)
introduce: Jakim is recorded as a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin. He is included in the list of the sons of Shimei in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin that runs from 1 Chronicles 8:1 to 8:28 (1 Chronicles 8:19, 8:21).
lifetime: Within the genealogical system of the tribe of Benjamin, Jakim is classified as one of the sons of Shimei (1 Chronicles 8:19-21). It is recorded that the men of this genealogy were all heads of fathers' houses, chiefs throughout their generations, and lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).

introduce: Jaanai is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 5, a member of a family belonging to the tribe of Gad among the tribes of Israel. He is recorded as one of the persons who make up the genealogy of the tribe of Gad (1 Chronicles 5:12).
lifetime: Jaanai is recorded in the genealogy of the sons of Gad together with Joel the chief, then Shapham, Jaanai, and Shaphat who lived in Bashan (1 Chronicles 5:12). The sons of Gad lived opposite the Reubenites in the land of Bashan, as far as Salecah (1 Chronicles 5:11).

introduce: Jada is a man recorded as a descendant of Jerahmeel among the families of the tribe of Judah. He was the son of Onam and the younger brother of Shammai, and is included in the genealogy of the house of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2:28, 2:32).
lifetime: Jada was a son of Onam, born to Atarah the wife of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2:26, 2:28), and the younger brother of Shammai (1 Chronicles 2:32). The sons of Jada were Jether and Jonathan, and Jether died without sons (1 Chronicles 2:32).

introduce: Jahdai is a man whose name appears in the passage of 1 Chronicles 2 dealing with the genealogy of Caleb of the tribe of Judah, and he is recorded as the father of Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph (1 Chronicles 2:47).
lifetime: Jahdai is recorded as having had as sons Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph (1 Chronicles 2:47). His parents, and his exact blood relationship to Caleb, are not made clear in the text (1 Chronicles 2:42-49).
event: The biblical text does not mention any specific achievement of Jahdai or any event he experienced (1 Chronicles 2:47).

기타관계: Caleb#243(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: Jahdo is a man recorded in the genealogy of the sons of Gad, recorded as the sixth-generation ancestor of Abihail (1 Chronicles 5:14).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 5:14 lists the ancestors of Abihail in the order Huri, Jaroah, Gilead, Michael, Jeshishai, Jahdo, Buz, and records Abihail as the sixth-generation descendant of Jahdo. In this genealogy Jahdo corresponds to the generation before Jeshishai and the generation after Buz (1 Chronicles 5:14).
event: The Bible has no record of any personal achievement or particular event of Jahdo; his name appears only in the genealogy of Abihail's ancestors (1 Chronicles 5:14).

introduce: Jadon is a Meronothite who appears in the book of Nehemiah, a man who took part in the work of repairing the wall of Jerusalem.
lifetime: Jadon, together with Melatiah the Gibeonite, repaired a section of the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:7).
event: Jadon, together with Melatiah the Gibeonite, repaired the wall along with the men of Gibeon and the men of Mizpah, who belonged to the jurisdiction of the governor of the province west of the River (Nehemiah 3:7).

introduce: Jathniel is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles, one who served as a gatekeeper of the tribe of Levi during the reign of King David. He is classified as one of the descendants of Korah.
lifetime: Jathniel is included in the list of the gatekeepers of the sons of Korah, and in the time of David he performed the duty of guarding the gates of the temple (1 Chronicles 26:2).
event: Jathniel is recorded as the fourth among the sons of Meshelemiah in the course of the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:1-2). The sons of Meshelemiah and his brothers, eighteen in all, were said to be able men (1 Chronicles 26:9).
character: In the biblical record there is no description of Jathniel's inner character or specific traits (1 Chronicles 26:2).

introduce: Jahdiel is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 5, one of the chiefs who were active as leaders in the families of the half-tribe of Manasseh.
lifetime: Jahdiel is recorded as one of the chiefs of the half-tribe of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 5:24). The descendants of the half-tribe of Manasseh multiplied until they extended from Bashan to Baal-hermon and Senir and Mount Hermon (1 Chronicles 5:23).
event: Together with Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, and Hodaviah, Jahdiel is recorded as a chief of the half-tribe of Manasseh, all of them chiefs famous for their valor (1 Chronicles 5:24).
character: According to the biblical record, Jahdiel was regarded as a mighty warrior within the half-tribe of Manasseh, and held the public standing of a famous head of his family (1 Chronicles 5:24).

introduce: Jarah is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in 1 Chronicles 9, one of the members who make up the family tree of the house of Saul.
lifetime: Jarah is recorded as the son of Ahaz and as the great-grandson of Merib-baal the son of Jonathan the son of Saul (Merib-baal, Micah, Ahaz, Jarah) (1 Chronicles 9:39-42). He begat Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri (1 Chronicles 9:42).

기타관계: Jonathan#4603(kinsman of the tribe of Benjamin)

introduce: Jair is a man from Bethlehem recorded as the father of Elhanan (2 Samuel 21:19).
lifetime: Jair was a man of Bethlehem, and his identity is confirmed as the father of Elhanan from the record that his son Elhanan, in the war with the Philistines at Gob, killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath of Gath (2 Samuel 21:19).
event: No deeds of Jair himself are recorded. In 2 Samuel 21:19 his son Elhanan killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath of Gath in the war with the Philistines at Gob, and Jair appears there as identifying information introducing Elhanan.

introduce: Jared is a man mentioned in the genealogy recorded in Genesis as a descendant of Seth, the father of Enoch and the grandfather of Methuselah. He is classified as the sixth generation from Adam.
lifetime: Jared was born as the son of Mahalalel and begat Enoch at the age of 162 (Genesis 5:18). After begetting Enoch he lived another 800 years, begetting children, and died having enjoyed a total of 962 years (Genesis 5:19-20).
event: The Bible has no description of any specific achievement or particular event carried out by Jared. Only numerical records concerning his life and descendants are transmitted through the genealogy of Genesis 5 (Genesis 5:18-20).

introduce: Jaroah is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 5, included in the genealogy of the sons of Gad. He was the son of Gilead, the father of Huri, and the grandfather of Abihail (1 Chronicles 5:14).
lifetime: Jaroah was born as a son of Gilead and was a member of the family line belonging to the sons of Gad (1 Chronicles 5:14). His son was Huri and his grandson was Abihail (1 Chronicles 5:14).

introduce: Jarha is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2), an Egyptian servant belonging to Sheshan.
lifetime: Jarha was an Egyptian servant of Sheshan (1 Chronicles 2:34). Sheshan had no sons but only daughters, and he gave his daughter to his servant Jarha to be his wife, and Jarha begat Attai by her (1 Chronicles 2:35).
event: Jarha took the daughter of Sheshan as his wife and begat Attai (1 Chronicles 2:35). A genealogy is recorded running from Attai through Nathan, Zabad, Ephlal, Obed, Jehu, Azariah, Helez, Elasah, Sismai, Shallum, Jekamiah, to Elishama (1 Chronicles 2:36-41).

introduce: Jahmai is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 7:2, a man belonging to the genealogy of the tribe of Issachar. He is recorded as the son of Tola and as one of the grandson generation of Issachar.
lifetime: Jahmai was born as a son of Tola (1 Chronicles 7:2). Within the family of the tribe of Issachar he is mentioned together with his father Tola and his brothers Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Ibsam, and Shemuel (1 Chronicles 7:2).
event: As a son of Tola, he was recorded as one of the heads of the house of his father Tola. The descendants of Tola were mighty men of valor throughout their generations, and in the time of David their number reached 22,600 (1 Chronicles 7:2).

introduce: Jamlech is one of the chiefs whose names are entered in the genealogy of the sons of Simeon, together with Meshobab and Joshah the son of Amaziah (1 Chronicles 4:34-38).
lifetime: In the genealogy of the sons of Simeon, Jamlech's name is recorded together with Meshobab and alongside Joshah the son of Amaziah (1 Chronicles 4:34). It is recorded that all those listed above by name were chiefs of their clans (1 Chronicles 4:38), and that in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah they struck the tents of the Meunites, destroyed them utterly, and lived there afterward (1 Chronicles 4:41).
event: As one of those listed above by name, Jamlech went to the border of Gedor, on the east side of the valley, in search of pasture for the flocks, and in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah he destroyed the Meunites who were there and lived there in their place (1 Chronicles 4:39-41). In 1 Chronicles 4:34 only his name appears, and no individual deeds of his are recorded separately.

introduce: Jabal is a man who appears in the book of Genesis, a descendant of Cain, the son born to Lamech and Adah. He is recorded as the ancestor of those who dwell in tents and keep livestock.
lifetime: Jabal was the son of Lamech and was born of Adah (Genesis 4:20). He became the ancestor of those who live in tents and keep livestock (Genesis 4:20). No further detailed account of his life, or any record of his death, appears in the Bible.
event: Jabal became the ancestor of those who dwell in tents and keep livestock (Genesis 4:20). The Bible also records that his brother Jubal became the ancestor of all who play the harp and flute (Genesis 4:21).

call: Father of Shallum (father of a king of northern Israel)
introduce: Jabesh is a man recorded as the father of Shallum, king of northern Israel. Detailed biographical information about him in the Bible is very limited, and his name appears only as "Shallum the son of Jabesh" in the passage introducing his son Shallum (2 Kings 15:10, 13, 14).
lifetime: Jabesh was the father of Shallum, king of northern Israel (2 Kings 15:10). No specific deeds from his life as a whole, nor any information about his birth or death, are recorded.
event: The Bible contains no account of any direct political achievement or specific event of Jabesh himself. There is, however, the record that his son Shallum conspired against Zechariah, struck him down before the people, reigned in his place (2 Kings 15:10), and ruled in Samaria for one month (2 Kings 15:13).

introduce: He was one of the three sons of Noah, a figure involved in the repopulation of humanity after the flood. His descendants were divided into various nations and settled in the lands of the coasts (Genesis 10:2-5).
lifetime: As a son of Noah (Genesis 6:10), he entered the ark with Noah's wife and the three daughters-in-law at the time of the flood judgment (Genesis 7:13). After the flood ended he came out of the ark together with Noah, his wife, his brothers, and the daughters-in-law (Genesis 8:18). Afterward, as a brother of Shem and Ham, he formed one branch as the peoples spread over all the earth from these three sons of Noah (Genesis 9:18-19).
event: When his father Noah was drunk and uncovered, he approached backward together with Shem and covered him with a garment (Genesis 9:23). Afterward he heard from Noah the words, "May God enlarge Japheth, and let him dwell in the tents of Shem" (Genesis 9:27). His descendants were divided into various nations and settled in the lands of the coasts, each according to language, clan, and nation (Genesis 10:5).
character: He showed prudence and respect in covering his father's fault, and displayed an attitude of cooperating with his fellow brother (Genesis 9:23). He received from Noah the assessment that he would be enlarged (Genesis 9:27).

introduce: Japhlet is a man recorded in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a male mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher. He is recorded as the son of Heber and is classified as one of the members of the families of the tribe of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:32).
lifetime: Japhlet was born as a son of Heber, the son of Beriah (1 Chronicles 7:31-32). In the genealogical system of the sons of Asher his name is entered as the son of Heber; his brothers Shomer and Hotham are recorded with him (1 Chronicles 7:32), and his sons Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath are recorded (1 Chronicles 7:33).

introduce: Japhia is the king of Lachish, of the Amorite people in the south of Canaan, who appears in the book of Joshua in the Old Testament. He was a ruler who formed a coalition and resisted Israel at the time of the Israelite conquest of Canaan.
lifetime: On hearing the news that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel, he joined the Amorite coalition formed under the leadership of Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem (Joshua 10:3). He was defeated in battle against the army of Israel led by Joshua and fled; afterward he was found hiding in the cave at Makkedah and was executed at Joshua's command (Joshua 10:16-26).
event: When Gibeon made a peace treaty with Israel, in response he attacked Gibeon together with the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, and Eglon (Joshua 10:3-5). Afterward he fought against the army of Israel on the slope of Beth-horon but was utterly defeated (Joshua 10:10-11). After the war ended he was brought out of the cave at Makkedah and put to death by Joshua, then hung on a tree, and at sunset his body was taken down and thrown into the cave where they had hidden (Joshua 10:22-27).

introduce: Japhia is one of the sons whom King David had in Jerusalem, a man included in the list of David's children recorded in 1 Chronicles 3 (1 Chronicles 3:7).
lifetime: Japhia is one of the sons whom David begat in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:7). He is listed in the roster of David's sons together with Ibhar and Elishama (1 Chronicles 3:6-7).

call: King of Hazor in the time of Joshua
meaning: One of discernment, a wise man
introduce: Jabin was the king who ruled Hazor, the center of the northern region of Canaan, and the man who led in forming the northern Canaanite coalition during the time when the people of Israel were conquering Canaan.
lifetime: Jabin reigned as king of Hazor and made alliances with the various towns of the northern region and resisted Israel (Joshua 11:1). To stop Israel's invasion he summoned Jobab king of Madon, the king of Shimron, the king of Achshaph, and the various kings of the northern region, and formed a coalition (Joshua 11:1-3). Afterward he fought at the waters of Merom against the army of Israel led by Joshua but was defeated; in the course of this his city Hazor was captured, and Jabin himself was put to death by Joshua with the edge of the sword (Joshua 11:8-10).
event: Jabin gathered the various city-states of the north of Canaan and organized a great coalition; it is recorded that this army had very many horses and chariots, and its number was like the sand that is on the seashore (Joshua 11:4). He confronted Israel at the waters of Merom, but suffered a heavy blow from Joshua's surprise attack (Joshua 11:7). Joshua, victorious in the war, captured Hazor and destroyed the kingdom of Hazor by striking down its king, Jabin, with the edge of the sword (Joshua 11:10-11).

introduce: Jashar is a name that appears in the Bible only as the title of a book, "the Book of Jashar." Content recorded in this book is quoted in Joshua 10 and 2 Samuel 1, and the Bible contains no explanation of the author or nature of this book.
event: The Book of Jashar is mentioned as the book in which it is recorded that the sun stayed in the midst of heaven and did not hasten to go down for almost a whole day. This passage is connected with the event in which Joshua told the sun to stand still over Gibeon and the moon over the Valley of Aijalon (Joshua 10:12-13). It is also mentioned that the song of the bow, which David commanded to be taught to the people of Judah, was written in the Book of Jashar (2 Samuel 1:18).

introduce: Jahzerah is a figure in the genealogy of the priestly families who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian captivity, recorded in 1 Chronicles 9; he was the son of Meshullam, the father of Adiel, and the grandfather of Maasai (1 Chronicles 9:12).
lifetime: Jahzerah is recorded as the grandfather of the priest Maasai, the father of Adiel, and the son of Meshullam (1 Chronicles 9:12). His descendant Maasai is listed among the priests who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:10-12).
event: No deeds of Jahzerah himself are recorded. He is mentioned in the genealogy only as the grandfather of Maasai (1 Chronicles 9:12), and at the end of the same list of priests there follows the record that their brothers, heads of their fathers' houses, who were able men for the work of the service of the house of God, numbered 1,760 in all (1 Chronicles 9:13).

introduce: He was a mighty man who was active during the reign of David, the son of a Hachmonite and recorded as chief of the thirty (1 Chronicles 11:11). It is the common view that he is the same person as the Tahchemonite Josheb-basshebeth in 2 Samuel 23:8, that is, the Eznite Adino, the chief of the captains.
lifetime: Jashobeam is recorded as chief of the thirty among David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:11). He is also recorded as the commander of the division for the first month, among the divisions that served month by month in David's time; that division numbered twenty-four thousand (1 Chronicles 27:2).
event: He lifted up his spear and killed three hundred at one time (1 Chronicles 11:11). 2 Samuel 23:8 records that the chief of the captains, who is also called Josheb-basshebeth, struck down eight hundred at one time. 1 Chronicles 11:10 records that the chiefs of such mighty men, together with all Israel, strengthened David's hand so that he obtained the kingdom, and made him king.
character: According to the biblical record, he was a commander of outstanding military prowess who enjoyed David's absolute trust. That he was appointed head, the supreme commander within the army, suggests that he was the warrior of the greatest fighting strength in David's army (1 Chronicles 11:11). Because he was in charge of the first month among David's twelve courses, he is regarded as the man of the highest priority in the military organization (1 Chronicles 27:2).

introduce: He is the man who, during the second missionary journey of the apostle Paul, welcomed Paul and Silas in Thessalonica and provided them lodging. He is one of the early Christian believers mentioned in the book of Acts and in Romans in the New Testament.
lifetime: He was pointed out as the man who had taken Paul and Silas into his house in Thessalonica (Acts 17:7). When the Jews caused an uproar and rushed upon his house looking for Paul's party and did not find them, Jason and some brothers were dragged before the city officials (Acts 17:5-6), and after taking bond from Jason and the rest, they released them (Acts 17:9). In Romans 16:21 Jason is mentioned as one who sends greetings, together with Paul's fellow worker Timothy and his kinsmen Lucius and Sosipater.
event: Pointed out by the Jews as the man who had taken in Paul and Silas in Thessalonica, he had his house attacked and was dragged together with the brothers before the city officials and accused (Acts 17:5-7). The crowd and the city officials were troubled, but after taking bond from Jason and the rest, they let them go (Acts 17:8-9).
character: He showed courage and boldness in trying to protect Paul's party even when his own safety was threatened (Acts 17:7). From the fact that he paid bond and was released in the course of the hearing, he is presumed to have been a man of some wealth or social standing in the local community at that time (Acts 17:9). From the fact that Paul called him his kinsman, he seems to have had a blood relationship with Paul or a very close Jewish tie (Romans 16:21).

introduce: Jashubi-lehem is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as a descendant of Shelah and a descendant of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:21).
lifetime: Jashubi-lehem is a man born into the house of Shelah the son of Judah, and in the genealogy he is placed in the line of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:21). No specific record of his life appears in the Bible (1 Chronicles 4:22).
event: He is mentioned together with Jokim, the men of Cozeba, Joash, and the one who ruled in Moab, and the text states that all these records are ancient (1 Chronicles 4:22). However, no detailed account of what he specifically did is recorded (1 Chronicles 4:22).

call: Third son of Issachar (ancestor of the Jashubite clan)
introduce: Jashub is the third son of Issachar, who was born to Jacob and Leah, and the man who became the ancestor of the Jashubite clan within the tribe of Issachar.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons born to Issachar, the son of Jacob (Numbers 26:24). Within the family tree of Issachar he is mentioned together with Tola, Puah, and Shimron (1 Chronicles 7:1).
event: When the children of Israel came out of Egypt and were numbered in the wilderness, Jashub was included in that list as the ancestor of the Jashubite clan, which took its name from him (Numbers 26:24).

introduce: Jahzeiah is a man who took a position opposed to the manner of dealing proposed by the congregation in Ezra 10:14 regarding the problem of marriage to foreign women within the Israelite community that had returned from the Babylonian captivity. He is recorded in Ezra 10:15 as one who opposed that matter together with Jonathan the son of Asahel.
lifetime: He was a member of the Israelite community that had returned from Babylon to Jerusalem, and is recorded as the son of Tikvah. Regarding the manner of dealing proposed by the congregation in Ezra 10:14, he rose up together with Jonathan the son of Asahel and opposed it (Ezra 10:10-15).
event: Regarding the manner of dealing proposed by the congregation in Ezra 10:14, he rose up together with Jonathan the son of Asahel and opposed the matter, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them (Ezra 10:15). His deeds after this event, and his specific status, are not recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Jahzeel is a man recorded as one of the four sons of Naphtali, the son of Jacob. He is one of the descendants of Jacob whose name was recorded when Jacob's family went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:24).
lifetime: Jahzeel was born as a son of Naphtali (Genesis 46:24), and when Jacob left Canaan and moved to the land of Goshen in Egypt, he went down to Egypt with his grandfather Jacob, and his name was entered in the list of the family of Israel (Genesis 46:8, 46:24). The one recorded as Jahziel in the list of the sons of Naphtali in 1 Chronicles 7:13 is regarded as the same person.
event: Jahzeel was a member of the family community, as a son of Naphtali, when Jacob went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:8, 24). Afterward, no record of his personal achievements or of any particular event is found within the biblical text.

introduce: Jaziz is a man who appears as one of those placed in charge of King David's property during the reign of King David. According to the biblical record he is a Hagrite (1 Chronicles 27:30-31).
lifetime: Jaziz was placed in charge of the flocks among David's property (1 Chronicles 27:30). The Bible contains no detailed record of at what point during David's reign he was appointed to this office.
event: Jaziz was placed in charge of the flocks belonging to King David's property (1 Chronicles 27:30). This is a fact recorded in the list of those who were in charge of King David's property (1 Chronicles 27:25-31).

introduce: Jahziel is one of the sons of Naphtali, a man recorded as a grandson of Bilhah. According to the genealogical record of 1 Chronicles 7:13, he belongs to the tribe of Naphtali.
lifetime: Jahziel was born as a son of Naphtali and is recorded as a grandson of Bilhah (1 Chronicles 7:13). He is one of Naphtali's sons: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum (1 Chronicles 7:13).

introduce: Akan is a figure who appears in Genesis and 1 Chronicles, the son of Ezer and a descendant of Seir of the Horite people. In the list of Ezer's children in Genesis 36:27 he is recorded in the form Akan, and his father Ezer is one of the chiefs of the Horite people (Genesis 36:21, 30).
lifetime: Akan is recorded as the son of Ezer, a descendant of Seir (1 Chronicles 1:42). His name is also entered in the list of Ezer's children in Genesis (Bilhan, Zaavan, Akan) (Genesis 36:27).
event: No special historical event or specific achievement carried out by Akan himself is recorded in the Bible; all there is is that his name is entered in the genealogy as a son of Ezer (1 Chronicles 1:42, Genesis 36:27).

introduce: Jaakobah is a man whose name is entered as a chief of the sons of Simeon, recorded in 1 Chronicles 4, and one of the group of leaders who went to the border of Gedor in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:36-41).
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of the chiefs of the sons of Simeon, and his name is recorded together with Elioenai, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, and Benaiah (1 Chronicles 4:36). It is recorded that all those listed above by name were chiefs of their clans (1 Chronicles 4:38).
event: As one of those listed above by name, when their clan multiplied all the more he went to the border of Gedor, on the east side of the valley, in search of pasture for the flocks (1 Chronicles 4:38-39). That place was a wide and secure land with rich and good pasture, where from of old the descendants of Ham had lived (1 Chronicles 4:40), and in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah they struck down their tents and destroyed the Meunites utterly, and lived there in their place (1 Chronicles 4:41).

introduce: Jaareshiah is a man recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, the son of Jeroham, and one of those recorded as chiefs (1 Chronicles 8:27-28).
lifetime: Jaareshiah is mentioned as one of the sons of Jeroham, chiefs of the tribe of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:27-28).

call: Chief of the Rechabite clan (grandson of Habazziniah)
introduce: Jaazaniah is a Rechabite who appears in the book of Jeremiah, the grandson of Habazziniah and the son of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 35:3). He is recorded as belonging to the Rechabite clan, who lived keeping the command of their ancestor Jonadab (Jeremiah 35:3, 35:6-10).
lifetime: Jaazaniah is recorded as the grandson of Habazziniah and the son of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 35:3). When the prophet Jeremiah, according to the word of the LORD, took the Rechabite clan into one of the chambers of the house of the LORD, Jaazaniah, his brothers, and all his sons were present there together (Jeremiah 35:2-3).
event: Jeremiah set before the Rechabites bowls full of wine and cups and urged them to drink, but they refused, saying that they would not drink wine, following the command of their ancestor Jonadab (Jeremiah 35:5-6). Jaazaniah was among the Rechabites whom Jeremiah had brought (Jeremiah 35:3). They answered that, according to the command of their ancestor, they did not build houses, sow seed, or keep vineyards, but dwelt in tents all their lives (Jeremiah 35:7-10). On the occasion of this event, Jeremiah set the obedience of the Rechabites in contrast with the disobedience of the people of Judah (Jeremiah 35:12-19).
character: Jaazaniah was a man who strictly observed the rules of the family established by his ancestor Jonadab (Jeremiah 35:8). He showed strong self-control and a compliant attitude, holding firmly to the tradition and command of the family to the end without being shaken by outside urging or circumstances (Jeremiah 35:10).

introduce: Jaazaniah is mentioned as one of the commanders of the forces of Judah who went to Mizpah on hearing the news that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah governor. He is recorded as the son of the Maacathite (2 Kings 25:23).
lifetime: After Gedaliah was placed in charge of the people whom Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had left in the land of Judah (2 Kings 25:22), when the commanders of the forces and their men came to Gedaliah, who was at Mizpah, Jaazaniah also had his name entered as one of them (2 Kings 25:23). He is recorded as the son of the Maacathite (2 Kings 25:23).
event: He appears as one of the commanders of the forces who, on hearing that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah governor, went to Mizpah and came to Gedaliah (2 Kings 25:23). Gedaliah swore to them and their men, saying that they should not fear the servants of the Chaldeans, but dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon (2 Kings 25:24).

introduce: Jaasu is a man recorded under the heading of the sons of Bani in the list of those who, after returning from the Babylonian captivity, had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:34, 10:37, 10:44).
lifetime: Jaasu was one of the descendants of Bani and is included in the list at the time when Ezra, having returned to Jerusalem, investigated the problem of marriages to foreigners (Ezra 10:34, Ezra 10:37).
event: In connection with the covenant to send away the foreign women and those born of them (Ezra 10:3), his name was entered under the heading of the sons of Bani in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:37, 10:44).

introduce: Jaaziah is a man recorded as a descendant of Merari of the descendants of Levi (1 Chronicles 24:27). Those born of him were Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri (1 Chronicles 24:26-27).
lifetime: Jaaziah was a descendant of Merari (1 Chronicles 24:27), and his son Beno is recorded (1 Chronicles 24:26), and it is said that those born of him were Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri (1 Chronicles 24:27).

call: One of David's thirty mighty men (a Mezobaite)
introduce: Jaasiel is a Mezobaite whose name is entered near the end of the list of the mighty men who were with David, recorded in 1 Chronicles 11 (1 Chronicles 11:47).
lifetime: Jaasiel is a Mezobaite who entered his name in the list of the mighty men who were with David (1 Chronicles 11:47). The Bible contains no specific record of his birth or other personal life.
event: He is included in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:47). Nothing is recorded about any specific battle he fought or any achievement of his own.

introduce: Jaala is the name of a family among the descendants of Solomon's servants, recorded in the list of those who returned from the captivity as "the descendants of Jaala" (Ezra 2:55-56).
lifetime: The descendants of Jaala belong to the list of the descendants of Solomon's servants and are recorded among those who returned from the Babylonian captivity to Jerusalem and Judah (Ezra 2:1, 2:56). In the list in Nehemiah 7 as well, they appear as the descendants of Jaala among the descendants of Solomon's servants (Nehemiah 7:58).
event: The descendants of Jaala were included in the list of those who returned from Babylon (Ezra 2:56). The descendants of Solomon's servants, together with the Nethinim, numbered 392 (Ezra 2:58).

introduce: Jael was the wife of Heber the Kenite, and a woman who played an important role in the conflict between Israel and Sisera, the commander of the army of Jabin king of Canaan, in the time of the judges. She is recorded as the woman who put to death the Canaanite general Sisera, who was hostile to the army led by Deborah and Barak, judges of Israel.
lifetime: Jael lived in a tent as the wife of Heber the Kenite (Judges 4:17). Her husband Heber, a Kenite of the descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, had separated himself from his clan and pitched his tent by the oak at Zaanannim near Kedesh (Judges 4:11), and Jabin king of Hazor was at peace with the house of Heber (Judges 4:17). When Sisera fled on foot and reached Jael's tent, Jael went out, welcomed him and took him in, and killed Sisera as he lay fast asleep (Judges 4:17-21). Afterward, in the Song of Deborah, Jael was praised as blessed above other women (Judges 5:24).
event: When Sisera, the commander of the Canaanite army, fled to her tent, Jael welcomed him, took him in, and killed him (Judges 4:17-21). After giving Sisera milk to drink and covering him to put him at ease (Judges 4:19), while he was fast asleep she took a tent peg, with a hammer in her hand went softly to him, and drove the peg into his temple and killed him (Judges 4:21). When Barak came pursuing Sisera, Jael went out to meet him and showed him Sisera lying dead (Judges 4:22).
character: Jael is portrayed as a strategic person who made swift and bold decisions in a critical situation (Judges 4:18, 4:21). She employed the deception of showing hospitality in order to put Sisera at ease, and showed skill in handling weapons (Judges 4:18, 4:21). The Song of Deborah praises her as most blessed among women in tents, and describes her deed as valiant and resolute (Judges 5:24-27).

introduce: Javan was the fourth son of Japheth, the son of Noah, and a man whose name is used in the Hebrew Bible to refer to the region of Greece and its inhabitants.
lifetime: Javan is mentioned as a son of Japheth in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles (Genesis 10:2, 1 Chronicles 1:5). This belongs to the record of the descendants begotten by the sons of Noah after the flood (Genesis 10:1). His sons were Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittites, and the Rodanites (Genesis 10:4), and in 1 Chronicles the name Tarshish appears in a variant spelling (1 Chronicles 1:7).
event: In the genealogy of Genesis, Javan is recorded among the descendants of Japheth, who are said to have been divided according to their languages, clans, and nations and to have settled in the lands of the coasts (Genesis 10:5). In the oracle concerning Tyre, Javan is mentioned, together with Tubal and Meshech, as one who traded with Tyre in slaves and vessels of bronze (Ezekiel 27:3, 27:13). The "king of Greece" in Daniel 8:21 is written in the Hebrew original as Javan (יָוָן) (Daniel 8:21).

introduce: Jairus is one of the synagogue leaders who appears in the Gospels; when his only daughter, twelve years old, was dying, he came to Jesus, fell at his feet, and begged him (Mark 5:22-23, Luke 8:41-42).
lifetime: Jairus is recorded as one of the synagogue leaders (Mark 5:22, Luke 8:41). He had an only daughter, twelve years old, and when she was dying he came to Jesus and begged him to come to his house (Luke 8:41-42).
event: Jairus fell at the feet of Jesus and begged him to come to his dying daughter and lay his hands on her so that she might live (Mark 5:22-23). While Jesus was on the way, after the woman who had suffered from a flow of blood was healed, while he was still speaking, people came from the synagogue leader's house and told him that his daughter had died (Mark 5:25-35). Even so, Jesus told him not to be afraid but only to believe, and went with him to his house, took the child by the hand and told her to arise, and the girl immediately arose and walked (Mark 5:36-42).
character: In spite of his own social position, Jairus showed a humble and desperate attitude, falling down before Jesus and begging in order to save his daughter (Mark 5:22). Also, through the fact that he trusted Jesus despite the hopeless news around him and went with him to his house, his persevering side can be seen (Mark 5:36).

introduce: Jair was a descendant of the tribe of Manasseh who conquered the land of Gilead east of the Jordan, took its towns, and formed Havvoth-jair, named after himself.
lifetime: Jair was the son of Segub, born of Hezron and the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead (1 Chronicles 2:21-22), and Numbers and Deuteronomy record him as a son of Manasseh (Numbers 32:41, Deuteronomy 3:14). He went to the land of Gilead, took its villages, and called them Havvoth-jair (Numbers 32:41), and he held twenty-three towns in the land of Gilead (1 Chronicles 2:22).
event: Jair took the villages of the region of Gilead and called them Havvoth-jair (Numbers 32:41). He took the whole region of Argob, that is, Bashan, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and called it by his own name, Havvoth-jair (Deuteronomy 3:14). Joshua 13:30 records that all the towns of Jair in the territory of Bashan, sixty cities, belong to the territory given to the half-tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 13:29-30).

call: A mighty man of Benjamin at Ziklag
introduce: Jahaziel was a man of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the mighty men who came to help David during the time when David stayed at Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:4).
lifetime: He is recorded in the list of the Benjamites who joined David to help him when David was living at Ziklag, fleeing from King Saul (1 Chronicles 12:4).
event: He joined David's army and was classified as a mighty man equipped with the ability to carry out wars and battles (1 Chronicles 12:1-4).

call: Son of Shobal (ancestor of the Zorathite clan)
introduce: Jahath is a man recorded as the grandson of Shobal, the son of Judah, and as the son of Reaiah (1 Chronicles 4:1-2). He begat Ahumai and Lahad, who are the clans of the Zorathites (1 Chronicles 4:2).
lifetime: Jahath was a son begotten by Reaiah, the son of Shobal, the son of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:1-2), and he begat Ahumai and Lahad (1 Chronicles 4:2). These are recorded as the clans of the Zorathites (1 Chronicles 4:2).
event: Jahath is recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Judah as the father of Ahumai and Lahad, who are the clans of the Zorathites (1 Chronicles 4:2). Apart from this, no specific achievement or individual historical event is recorded (1 Chronicles 4:2).

introduce: Jannai is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Luke, one of the earlier group of figures recorded as the son of Joseph and the father of Melchi.
lifetime: In the genealogy of Luke he is recorded as the son of Joseph and the father of Melchi (Luke 3:24).

introduce: Jannes is a man mentioned in 2 Timothy as one who, together with Jambres, opposed Moses (2 Timothy 3:8). The Bible does not state his identity, and it is generally understood in connection with the Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses at the time of the exodus (Exodus 7:11).
lifetime: The biblical text does not deal with Jannes's life as a whole, and mentions only the fact that he, together with Jambres, opposed Moses (2 Timothy 3:8).
event: Jannes, together with Jambres, opposed Moses (2 Timothy 3:8). The apostle Paul compared them to later people who oppose the truth, saying that they would not get very far and that their folly would be plain to all (2 Timothy 3:8-9). The names Jannes and Jambres do not occur in the text of Exodus, but there is a record that when the staff that Aaron threw down became a serpent, the Egyptian magicians also did the same by their secret arts (Exodus 7:10-12).
character: He is described as one whose mind is corrupt and who is rejected concerning the faith (2 Timothy 3:8). The Bible assesses him as having a disposition to oppose the truth (2 Timothy 3:8).

introduce: Jalam is a figure who appears in the book of Genesis in the Old Testament, a son of Esau born in the land of Canaan to Esau's wife Oholibamah, and a man recorded as a chief (Genesis 36:5, 36:18).
lifetime: Jalam is a son born between Esau and his wife Oholibamah (Genesis 36:5, 36:14). Among the sons of Esau's wife Oholibamah, he is recorded as a chief together with Jeush and Korah (Genesis 36:18).
event: His name was entered as a son of Oholibamah in the record of the descendants of Esau in Genesis 36 (Genesis 36:5, 36:14), and he is also recorded as a chief (Genesis 36:18). No other specific event that he carried out is mentioned.

introduce: Jahleel is the third of the three sons of Zebulun, and within the family line of the tribe of Zebulun, one of the twelve tribes of Israel, he is the man who became the ancestor of the Jahleelite clan.
lifetime: He was born to Zebulun, the son of Jacob (Genesis 46:14), and he is recorded as the third son in the genealogy of the tribe of Zebulun (Numbers 26:26).
event: He became the ancestor of the Jahleelite clan, which bore his name, and later, when the total number of the children of Israel was counted at the plains of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho, the family of Jahleel was recorded as one clan of the sons of Zebulun (Numbers 26:3, 26:26).

introduce: Jambres is a man mentioned in 2 Timothy as one who, together with Jannes, opposed Moses (2 Timothy 3:8). This name does not occur in the Old Testament text, and it is generally understood in connection with the Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses at the time of the exodus (Exodus 7:11).
lifetime: The biblical text does not deal with the life of Jambres, and mentions only the fact that he, together with Jannes, opposed Moses (2 Timothy 3:8).
event: Jambres, together with Jannes, opposed Moses (2 Timothy 3:8). The apostle Paul compared them to later people who oppose the truth, saying that they would not get very far and that their folly would be plain to all (2 Timothy 3:8-9). The names Jannes and Jambres do not occur in the text of Exodus, but there is a record that when the staff that Aaron threw down became a serpent, the Egyptian magicians also did the same by their secret arts (Exodus 7:10-12).
character: He is described as one whose mind is corrupt and who showed a state of being rejected with regard to the truth (2 Timothy 3:8). He is assessed as having had a stubborn disposition that deceived others and defied the authority of God (2 Timothy 3:8).

call: A leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: He is a man whose name is entered among "the heads of the people" in the list of those who sealed when, in the time of Nehemiah, they made a firm covenant, wrote it, and sealed it (Nehemiah 9:38, 10:14, 10:21).
lifetime: In the list of those who sealed in Nehemiah 10, his name is recorded under the section of the heads of the people, following Meshezabel and Zadok (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:21).
event: When in the time of Nehemiah they made a firm covenant, wrote it, and sealed it (Nehemiah 9:38), his name is included in the list of those who sealed (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:14, 10:21).

introduce: Eker is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, the son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2:27).
lifetime: Eker is one of the sons begotten by Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel, and his name can be identified in the family line of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2:27).

introduce: Eglah was one of the six wives of King David, and the woman who bore a child to David in Hebron. Etymologically in Hebrew the name means a heifer, and she is mentioned in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles in the course of explaining David's family tree.
lifetime: Eglah became David's wife during the time he reigned in Hebron (2 Samuel 3:5). She bore Ithream, David's sixth son (2 Samuel 3:5). She is recorded last in the list of the six sons whom David begat in Hebron (1 Chronicles 3:3).
event: Apart from bearing David's son Ithream, no record of any specific achievement that she carried out directly, or of any separate event, is found in the Bible (2 Samuel 3:5).

introduce: He was the king of Moab who oppressed Israel for eighteen years in the time of the judges. According to the biblical record, he appears as an instrument to punish Israel when they did evil in the sight of the LORD, and he was killed by Ehud, a Benjamite.
lifetime: When the children of Israel sinned against the LORD, the LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against them (Judges 3:12). He gathered the Ammonites and the Amalekites, attacked Israel, and took the city of palms (Judges 3:13). Afterward he ruled over Israel for eighteen years, receiving tribute (Judges 3:14), and immediately after receiving the tribute presented by the judge Ehud, he was stabbed to death by Ehud's sword (Judges 3:21-22).
event: He conquered Israel and for eighteen years made the children of Israel serve him (Judges 3:14). After he received the tribute presented by Ehud, while he was sitting alone in his cool upper room, Ehud drew with his left hand the sword that he had strapped under his clothes on his right thigh and thrust it into the king's body, and he died (Judges 3:16, 3:20-22). After he died, Ehud shut and locked the doors of the upper room and went out, so the king's servants, after waiting a long time, took the key and opened the doors and went in, and found the king already dead and fallen on the floor (Judges 3:23-25).
character: The Bible describes him as a very fat man (Judges 3:17). In the course of receiving tribute from Israel, he showed a careless or complacent attitude, as in meeting Ehud alone (Judges 3:19-20).

introduce: Enan is a figure who appears in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament, a man belonging to the tribe of Naphtali and the father of Ahira (Numbers 1:15).
lifetime: Enan is mentioned as the father of Ahira, chief of the sons of Naphtali (Numbers 1:15). When they camped in the wilderness as well, the chief of the sons of Naphtali is recorded as Ahira the son of Enan (Numbers 2:29). Enan's name is mentioned again in the statement that on the twelfth day, at the dedication of the tabernacle, Ahira the son of Enan, chief of the sons of Naphtali, presented his offering (Numbers 7:78), and he is stated once more as his father in the statement that the army of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali was led by Ahira the son of Enan (Numbers 10:27).
event: Enan's son Ahira, as chief of the sons of Naphtali, presented as his offering at the dedication of the tabernacle one silver platter, one silver bowl, one golden spoon, and so on (Numbers 7:78-80), and that offering was recorded as "the offering of Ahira the son of Enan" (Numbers 7:83). Enan appears in the Bible as the father of Ahira, who led the army of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali (Numbers 10:27).

introduce: Enosh is a figure who appears in the book of Genesis in the Bible, the grandson of Adam and the son of Seth. He is recorded in the early genealogy of humanity as the second-generation descendant in the line of Seth.
lifetime: Enosh is the son whom Seth begat at the age of 105 (Genesis 5:6). He begat Kenan at the age of 90 (Genesis 5:9), after begetting Kenan he begat children for 815 years (Genesis 5:10), and he lived a total of 905 years and died (Genesis 5:11).
event: There is a record that it was only after his birth that people began to call upon the name of the LORD (Genesis 4:26).

call: Firstborn son of Cain (the origin of the city of Enoch)
introduce: Enoch is a figure who appears in the book of Genesis in the Bible, a son born to Cain and his wife. Cain built a city and named it Enoch after his name (Genesis 4:17).
lifetime: Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden, and lay with his wife and she bore Enoch (Genesis 4:16-17). Enoch begat Irad (Genesis 4:18).
event: After Cain begat Enoch, he built a city and named the city Enoch after the name of his son (Genesis 4:17). This verse is the place where the building of a city is first recorded in the Bible.

description.출신: land of Nod, east of Eden
직업/직위: namesake of the city of Enoch

introduce: Ethan is a man recorded as "Ethan the Ezrahite" in 1 Kings 4:31 and as "Ethan the Ezrahite" in the heading of Psalm 89. He is mentioned as a man known for wisdom in the time of Solomon (1 Kings 4:31).
lifetime: 1 Kings 4:31 records that Solomon was wiser than all other men, wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol, so that his fame spread throughout all the surrounding nations (1 Kings 4:31). This verse contains no other record of his life.
event: It is recorded that Solomon's wisdom was greater than that of Ethan the Ezrahite, so Ethan was mentioned as one of the people known for wisdom at that time (1 Kings 4:31). In the heading of Psalm 89 there is the notation "A Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite" (Psalms 89:1).
character: Ethan was equipped with outstanding intellectual ability, being recognized by the people of his time as a wise man (1 Kings 4:31), and he was a man who combined musical artistry and played a central role in the worship of the temple (1 Chronicles 15:19). As a Levite he showed a devoted side, faithfully carrying out his religious duties (1 Chronicles 15:17).

introduce: Eden is a Levite who appears in 2 Chronicles 29:12, a son of Joah among the Gershonites. He is included in the list of the Levites who rose up to cleanse the temple in the time of King Hezekiah.
lifetime: When Hezekiah king of Judah cleansed the temple, the Levites arose, and Eden is recorded among them as the son of Joah, the son of Zimmah, among the Gershonites (2 Chronicles 29:12).
event: Eden is in the list of the Levites who arose in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 29:12). Those Levites gathered their brothers, sanctified themselves, and cleansed the house of the LORD in accordance with what the king had commanded by the word of the LORD (2 Chronicles 29:15), and all the uncleanness that the priests had brought out from inside the temple, the Levites took and carried out to the brook Kidron (2 Chronicles 29:16).

call: Son of Mushi (a Levite of Merari)
introduce: Eder is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles, among the descendants of Levi a descendant of Merari, and is recorded as the son of Mushi.
lifetime: Eder, as a son of Mushi, a descendant of Merari, belongs to the genealogy of the tribe of Levi (1 Chronicles 23:23). He is a man included in the list when the genealogy of the Levites was arranged in the time of David (1 Chronicles 24:30).
event: David divided the Levites into courses according to the clans of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, the sons of Levi (1 Chronicles 23:6), and the sons of Mushi, Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth, are also Levites recorded according to their clans (1 Chronicles 24:30), and they cast lots, just as their brothers the sons of Aaron did, before King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the fathers' houses of the priests and the Levites (1 Chronicles 24:31).

introduce: Ethnan is a figure in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah recorded in 1 Chronicles, one of the sons of Helah, wife of Ashhur the father of Tekoa (1 Chronicles 4:5, 4:7).
lifetime: Ethnan is recorded as a son of Helah, together with Zereth and Zohar (1 Chronicles 4:7). Helah is one of the two wives of Ashhur the father of Tekoa (1 Chronicles 4:5).

introduce: Ethni is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the Gershonites of the tribe of Levi, one of the members of the family connected with the temple choir in the time of David (1 Chronicles 6:41).
lifetime: Ethni is recorded as the son of Zerah and the father of Malchijah (1 Chronicles 6:41). The genealogy to which he belongs continues the ancestral line of Asaph (1 Chronicles 6:39-41), and this line passes through Ethan, Zimmah, Shimei, and Jahath, and reaches Gershon and Levi (1 Chronicles 6:42-43).

introduce: He is a fellow worker of Paul who appears in the New Testament. In Acts 19:22 he appears as one who helped Paul, and in Romans 16:23 he is introduced as "the city treasurer."
lifetime: Paul stayed in Asia a little longer, and from among those who helped him he sent two men, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia (Acts 19:22). In Romans 16:23 he appears as one who sends greetings as "the city treasurer," and it is generally held that this city is Corinth, where Paul wrote Romans. 2 Timothy 4:20 records that Erastus stayed in Corinth.
event: He was a man who held the office of managing finances as "the city treasurer" (Romans 16:23). Paul sent him to Macedonia together with Timothy from among those who helped him (Acts 19:22).

introduce: Eran is a descendant of the tribe of Ephraim, the son of Shuthelah, who was a son of Ephraim, and the man who became the ancestor of the Eranite clan.
lifetime: Eran was born as a son of Shuthelah, the son of Ephraim (Numbers 26:36). He was recorded as the founder of the Eranite clan in the list of the census carried out when the people of Israel, having come out of Egypt, were staying on the plains of Moab (Numbers 26:36).
event: When Moses and Eleazar the priest counted the number of the children of Israel on the plains of Moab (Numbers 26:3), he was mentioned as the ancestor of the Eranite family, one of the families of the tribe of Ephraim (Numbers 26:36). This count is followed by the command to distribute the land by it as an inheritance (Numbers 26:53).

introduce: Eliashib is a man recorded among the sons of Bani in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:34-36, 10:44).
lifetime: Eliashib is one of the descendants of Bani, and his name is entered in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:34-36, 10:44).
event: When, in the time of Ezra, those among the people of Israel who had taken foreign women were exposed, Eliashib was recorded in that list, together with Vaniah and Meremoth among the sons of Bani (Ezra 10:36, 10:44).

meaning: My eyes are toward the LORD
introduce: Elioenai is a name that appears in 1 Chronicles and elsewhere, mentioned chiefly in the genealogies of the royal house of David and of the period after the Babylonian exile. The name means "my eyes are toward the LORD," and there are several persons in the Bible who bear this name.
lifetime: In the genealogy of the tribe of Judah a man named Elioenai appears; he is the son of Neariah and a descendant belonging to the generation after the Babylonian exile (1 Chronicles 3:23). Also in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, Elioenai is mentioned as a son of Becher (1 Chronicles 7:8).
