Besides these, Elioenai is also recorded among the descendants of Pashhur of the priestly families in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:22).
event: Elioenai the son of Neariah, as a descendant of the royal house of David, is recorded as one of those who continue the genealogy of the royal house of Judah, and he had seven sons (1 Chronicles 3:23-24). Elioenai of the tribe of Benjamin was one of the sons of Becher, and those sons were said to be heads of their fathers' houses and mighty men of valor (1 Chronicles 7:8-9). Elioenai of the priestly family was entered in the list of those who had taken foreign women, and the priests in this list gave their hands in a pledge to send away their wives (Ezra 10:18-19, 10:22).

introduce: He was the eldest son born to Judah and the daughter of Shua the Canaanite, and the first husband of Tamar.
lifetime: He was a son born to Judah and the daughter of Shua the Canaanite (Genesis 38:2-3). Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar (Genesis 38:6), but because Er was wicked in the sight of the LORD, the LORD put him to death (Genesis 38:7), and since his brother received the command to raise offspring for his brother, it appears that he died without children (Genesis 38:8-9).
event: Because he did evil in the sight of the LORD, the LORD put him to death (Genesis 38:7). After his death, his wife Tamar was to enter into a levirate marriage with his brother Onan (Genesis 38:8).
character: According to the biblical record, it is stated only that he did evil in the sight of the LORD, and no description of his specific character or personal traits appears (Genesis 38:7).

기타관계: Onan#2648(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: Ephah is a person who had a relationship with Caleb of the tribe of Judah, and in the biblical record she is classified as his concubine. She is one of the women whose names are entered in the genealogy of the descendants of Caleb.
lifetime: Caleb of the tribe of Judah had wives Azubah and Jerioth (1 Chronicles 2:18), and besides these a concubine, Ephah (1 Chronicles 2:46). Ephah bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez (1 Chronicles 2:46).
event: Ephah, as Caleb's concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez, and it is recorded that Haran begat Gazez (1 Chronicles 2:46).

introduce: Epaphras is a figure who appears in the New Testament, a fellow servant with Paul and a faithful minister of Christ from whom the Colossian believers learned the gospel. His name is mentioned in Colossians and Philemon.
lifetime: He was a man who came from among the Colossian believers (Colossians 4:12), and the Colossian believers learned the gospel from him (Colossians 1:7). He was the one who made known to Paul the love of the Colossian believers in the Holy Spirit (Colossians 1:8), and is recorded as a fellow prisoner with Paul (Philemon 1:23).
event: As a faithful minister of Christ he brought the gospel to the Colossian believers (Colossians 1:7). He conveyed their love in the Holy Spirit to Paul (Colossians 1:8). He also labored much for the Colossian believers and for those in Laodicea and Hierapolis (Colossians 4:13).
character: Paul evaluated him as a beloved fellow servant and a faithful minister of Christ (Colossians 1:7). He always labored earnestly in prayer for the saints, longing that they might stand mature and fully assured in all the will of God (Colossians 4:12). He is also described as a zealous man who gave great labor for the church (Colossians 4:13).

introduce: Epaphroditus was a member of the church at Philippi and a man sent to assist the ministry of the apostle Paul; when Paul was imprisoned in Rome, he attended to him and carried out the role of delivering the gift of support.
lifetime: The church at Philippi sent Epaphroditus to Rome to assist Paul's ministry (Philippians 2:25). While serving Paul in Rome, he fell ill and came near to death, but recovered, and afterward was to return to Philippi carrying Paul's letter (Philippians 2:27, 2:30).
event: Epaphroditus safely delivered to Paul the gift of support sent by the church at Philippi (Philippians 4:18). In the course of attending to Paul he contracted a serious illness and nearly died, but by the mercy of God he recovered (Philippians 2:27). Paul, sending him back to the church at Philippi, exhorted them to welcome him with joy and to hold such men in honor (Philippians 2:28-29).
character: Paul described Epaphroditus as "my brother and fellow worker and fellow soldier" (Philippians 2:25). He showed an attitude of putting the ministry of the apostle Paul and the gospel of the church before his own health, and had the character of such consideration for others that, knowing that the saints of the church at Philippi were distressed over his illness, he himself was distressed (Philippians 2:26-30).

call: Son of Shobal (chief of the Horites)
introduce: Ebal is a descendant of Seir of the Horite people mentioned in Genesis 36 and 1 Chronicles 1, a son of Shobal.
lifetime: Ebal is recorded as one of the children of Shobal, a son of Seir of the Horite people (Genesis 36:23). The descendants of Seir of the Horite people were in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:20-21). In the genealogy of the descendants of Seir in 1 Chronicles as well, his name is recorded as a son of Shobal (1 Chronicles 1:40).
event: In the genealogy of the descendants of Seir in Genesis and 1 Chronicles, his name appears only as one of the sons of Shobal, and no deeds of Ebal himself are recorded (Genesis 36:23, 1 Chronicles 1:38-40). Those listed as chiefs of the Horite people are Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, and Anah (Genesis 36:29).

introduce: Ephai is a Netophathite whose sons are mentioned in Jeremiah 40:8. The text records that his sons were among those who went to Mizpah to Gedaliah, the governor whom the king of Babylon had appointed, and it does not record any deeds of Ephai himself (Jeremiah 40:8).
lifetime: When the commanders of the forces in the open country and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam as governor and went to Mizpah, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite were among that company (Jeremiah 40:7-8). There is no record of Ephai himself in the Bible.
event: No deeds of Ephai himself are recorded in the text. His sons came to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and Gedaliah swore to them and their men, saying that they should not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans but should dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon (Jeremiah 40:8-9).

introduce: He is a figure who appears in Romans 16 of the apostle Paul, a member of the church in Rome mentioned when Paul sent greetings to the Christians in Rome.
lifetime: He is mentioned as the first fruit offered to Christ in Asia, and he was living in Rome (Romans 16:5).
event: It is recorded that he was the first ripened fruit to Christ in Asia (Romans 16:5).
character: Paul referred to him as "beloved," which shows that they had a particularly close relationship (Romans 16:5).

call: Son of Shelah (ancestor of the Hebrew people)
meaning: (Ebel) the region on the other side, (Epher) young deer
introduce: Eber was a descendant of Shem after the flood of Noah, the son of Shelah and the father of Peleg and Joktan. Genesis 10:21 calls Shem the father of all the children of Eber, and Eber is a figure who stands at a middle stage in the line of Shem in the genealogy of humanity.
lifetime: Eber was the son whom Shelah begat at the age of thirty (Genesis 11:14). He begat Peleg at the age of thirty-four (Genesis 11:16), and after begetting Peleg he lived four hundred and thirty years, begetting children (Genesis 11:17).
event: After begetting Peleg, Eber continued his family line, begetting children for 430 years (Genesis 11:17). In the time of his son Peleg the earth was divided (Genesis 10:25), and the place where the descendants of Joktan lived was the eastern hill country on the way from Mesha toward Sephar (Genesis 10:30).

call: Father of Gaal (father of the rebel against Shechem)
introduce: Ebed is the father of Gaal, who rebelled against the rule of Abimelech at Shechem in the time of the judges. In the biblical record he appears mainly in the context of explaining the family line and ancestry of Gaal.
lifetime: Ebed is mentioned as the father of Gaal, a man of Shechem (Judges 9:26). Beyond this, there is no specific record in the Bible of Ebed's individual life or social position.
event: When Ebed's son Gaal came to Shechem with his brothers, the men of Shechem put their trust in him (Judges 9:26), and Gaal said that he would not serve Abimelech and made known his intention to remove Abimelech (Judges 9:28-29). Ebed is mentioned only as Gaal's father, and no deeds of Ebed himself are recorded in the text.

introduce: He was a Cushite eunuch who served in the royal palace in the time of King Zedekiah, at the end of the kingdom of Judah. The name Ebed-melech has in Hebrew the meaning "servant of the king."
lifetime: He appears when Jeremiah prophesied the destruction of Jerusalem and the officials who heard it threw Jeremiah into the cistern of Malchijah, the king's son, in the court of the guard (Jeremiah 38:1-7). He reported to King Zedekiah concerning the treatment of Jeremiah and received the king's command to draw him up out of the cistern (Jeremiah 38:8-10). Afterward, on the day Jerusalem fell, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah that he would deliver Ebed-melech, and he was commanded to convey it to Ebed-melech (Jeremiah 39:15-18).
event: He took rags and worn-out clothes from the room under the treasury of the royal palace and let them down by ropes to Jeremiah in the cistern, told him to put them under his armpits, and drew Jeremiah up out of the cistern (Jeremiah 38:11-13). The LORD said that on that day he would deliver him so that he would not die by the sword, because he had put his trust in the LORD (Jeremiah 39:17-18).
character: He was bold enough to persuade King Zedekiah while the king was sitting in the gate of the city (Jeremiah 38:7-8), and he took careful thought, when drawing Jeremiah up out of the cistern, that he not be hurt (Jeremiah 38:12). He is described as a man who had a heart of trust in the LORD (Jeremiah 39:18).

introduce: Ephod, who appears in Numbers 34:23, is a man recorded as the father of Hanniel, chief of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh among the descendants of Joseph. The text does not record any deeds of Ephod himself (Numbers 34:23).
lifetime: Ephod appears in Numbers 34:23 only as the father of Hanniel. His son Hanniel is recorded as chief of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh (Numbers 34:23). There is no specific record of Ephod himself.
event: The LORD spoke to Moses of Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun as those who would divide the land as an inheritance (Numbers 34:17), and commanded him to choose one chief from each tribe for dividing the land of inheritance (Numbers 34:18). The one recorded at this time as chief of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh is not Ephod but his son Hanniel (Numbers 34:23).

introduce: Ephrathah is a person found in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as the mother of Hur, the son of Caleb (1 Chronicles 2:50).
lifetime: The Bible records that Caleb took Ephrathah (Ephrath) as his wife and begat Hur, his firstborn (1 Chronicles 2:19). Shobal, the father of Kiriath-jearim, is introduced as a son of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah (1 Chronicles 2:50), and 1 Chronicles 4:4 also records Hur as the firstborn of Ephrathah.
event: She became Caleb's wife and bore Hur (1 Chronicles 2:19).

introduce: He is the second son born to Joseph and his wife Asenath, a grandson of Jacob, and the man who became the ancestor of the tribe of Ephraim. His name was given in the sense that "God has made me flourish in the land of my labor" (Genesis 41:52).
lifetime: He was born as the second of the two sons whom Joseph had in Egypt, and was included as the younger son when his grandfather Jacob adopted Joseph's two sons as his own sons (Genesis 41:52, 48:5). When Jacob blessed Ephraim and Manasseh, he laid his right hand on Ephraim's head and gave a blessing that set him before Manasseh, the firstborn (Genesis 48:14-19).
event: In Jacob's blessing Ephraim was set before Manasseh, and it was said that the descendants of the younger brother would become many nations (Genesis 48:19-20). Ephraim later grew into the central tribe of the northern kingdom of Israel, and after the conquest of Canaan the descendants of Ephraim were allotted the borders of their inheritance according to their families (Joshua 16:5).

직업/직위: progenitor of the tribe of Ephraim

기타관계: Eleadah#2487(kinsman of the tribe of Ephraim)

introduce: He was the son of Zohar the Hittite, who lived in Hebron in the land of Canaan, and the man who sold Abraham the field containing the cave of Machpelah.
lifetime: When Abraham asked for the cave of Machpelah in Hebron in order to bury his wife Sarah, he appears as one of the Hittites sitting at the gate of the city (Genesis 23:10). Through negotiation with Abraham he handed over his field and the cave in it for four hundred shekels of silver (Genesis 23:16).
event: He carried out the sale in which he handed over to Abraham his field and the cave in it (Genesis 23:16-17). The field and the cave were established as Abraham's possession in the presence of the Hittites who went in at the gate of the city (Genesis 23:18), and the Hittites fixed it as Abraham's possession for a burying place (Genesis 23:20).
character: At the beginning of the transaction he showed courtesy by offering to give the cave to Abraham without payment (Genesis 23:11), but afterward he asked for its proper value and carried on a practical negotiation (Genesis 23:15). He is presumed to have been a man of influence among his own people, the Hittites (Genesis 23:10).

introduce: Ephlal is a figure who appears in the family tree of the tribe of Judah, recorded as the son of Zabad and the father of Obed (1 Chronicles 2:37).
lifetime: Ephlal was a descendant of Attai, whom the daughter of Sheshan bore to the servant Jarha; Attai begat Nathan, Nathan begat Zabad, Zabad begat Ephlal, and Ephlal begat Obed (1 Chronicles 2:35-37).

introduce: He was a king of the Assyrian Empire who reigned around the seventh century BC, and in the Bible he is referred to as the king of Assyria. As the son of Sennacherib, he succeeded to the throne after the murder of his father.
lifetime: He was the son of Sennacherib; while his father Sennacherib was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword and fled to the land of Ararat, and he became king in his place (2 Kings 19:37, Isaiah 37:38).
event: In Ezra 4, the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin came to Zerubbabel and the heads of the families and said that they had been sacrificing to God since the days of Esar-haddon king of Assyria, who had brought them here (Ezra 4:2). No other deeds of Esar-haddon himself are recorded in the text.

introduce: Esau is the elder of the twins born to Isaac and Rebekah, and the elder brother of Jacob. He became the ancestor of the people of Edom (Genesis 36:9), and because he asked for the red stew (the red thing), the nickname Edom came to be his (Genesis 25:30).
lifetime: When Esau was born his body was red and all over like a hairy garment, so he was named Esau (Genesis 25:25). He became a skilled hunter and a man of the field (Genesis 25:27). At the age of forty he took as wives Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite (Genesis 26:34). Afterward, besides his first wives, he took in addition as a wife Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son (Genesis 28:9), and he moved to Mount Seir and settled there (Genesis 36:8).
event: When Esau came in from the field and was very hungry, he got a bowl of red stew to eat from Jacob and sold his birthright to Jacob (Genesis 25:34). Isaac told Esau to bring game and prepare a savory dish, but when Jacob took the blessing instead, Esau sought to kill Jacob (Genesis 27:41). Later, when Jacob was returning to his homeland, Esau went out to meet him with a company of 400 men, and they resolved their conflict and were reconciled with each other (Genesis 33:4).
character: Isaac loved Esau more because he had a taste for wild game (Genesis 25:28). He is described as a man faithful to his impulsive desires, and showed a tendency to give away the value of the birthright easily for a bowl of red stew (Genesis 25:34). Also, after the blessing was taken from him by Jacob, he showed strong anger, seeking to kill him (Genesis 27:41), but at their reunion he also showed an emotional bond by embracing Jacob (Genesis 33:4).

introduce: Eshek is a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, a man recorded within the genealogy of the house of Saul as the younger brother of Azel. In 1 Chronicles 8 he appears as the father of Ulam the firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third (1 Chronicles 8:39).
lifetime: Eshek is introduced as the younger brother of Azel, and it is recorded that he had as sons Ulam, Jeush, and Eliphelet (1 Chronicles 8:39). As for his life, his name appears only in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, and no specific circumstances of his life are recorded.
event: No specific deeds or events of Eshek himself are recorded in the Bible. It is said, however, that the sons of his firstborn Ulam were all mighty men of valor and skilled archers, and had many sons and grandsons, 150 in all (1 Chronicles 8:40).

introduce: Ezer is a descendant of Ephraim, the son of Jacob, and a man belonging to the tribe of Ephraim. He is recorded as one of the sons of Ephraim who were killed by the men of Gath. There is also a view that reads "he" in 1 Chronicles 7:21 as referring to the immediately preceding Shuthelah (the son of Zabad), but because 7:22 says "their father Ephraim," he is recorded here as a son of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 7:21-22).
lifetime: As a son of Ephraim, he was killed by the men of Gath in the course of an attempt to plunder the livestock of the region of Gath (1 Chronicles 7:21).
event: An incident occurred in which the sons of Ephraim went down to the region of Gath and tried to seize the livestock of its inhabitants (1 Chronicles 7:21). In the course of this, Ezer and Elead, sons of Ephraim, were killed by the native inhabitants of Gath (1 Chronicles 7:21).

introduce: Eshcol is a brother of Mamre the Amorite, a man recorded as one who made a covenant of alliance with Abram together with Aner (Genesis 14:13).
lifetime: He is recorded as a brother of Mamre the Amorite and a brother of Aner, and appears as one who was in alliance with Abram (Genesis 14:13).
event: When Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him plundered the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah and carried off Lot, Abram recovered Lot (Genesis 14:11-16). Abram told the king of Sodom that the share of Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre, who had gone with him, they should take (Genesis 14:24).

introduce: Eshton is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as the son of Mehir, the son of Chelub, a member of the family line (1 Chronicles 4:11).
lifetime: Eshton is recorded as the son of Mehir, whom Chelub, the brother of Shuhah, begat (1 Chronicles 4:11). He begat Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah the father of Ir-nahash, and it is recorded that these were all men of Recah (1 Chronicles 4:12).
event: No specific achievement or event that Eshton carried out himself is recorded in the Bible, and only the genealogical record that he begat Tehinnah is transmitted (1 Chronicles 4:12).

introduce: Eshtemoa is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 4:19 in the Old Testament, a name recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
lifetime: Eshtemoa is recorded as a Maacathite among the sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham (1 Chronicles 4:19).
event: No record of the specific deeds or achievements of Eshtemoa individually appears in the Bible, and he appears only as a name in the genealogy (1 Chronicles 4:19).

introduce: Ezri is a man who, in the time of King David, had charge of the workers who tilled the fields, and he was the son of Chelub (1 Chronicles 27:26).
lifetime: During the reign of King David he belonged to the organization that managed the king's property (1 Chronicles 27:26).
event: As one of those placed in charge of King David's property, he had charge of the workers who tilled the fields (1 Chronicles 27:26, 27:31).

기타관계: David#468(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: Eshban is a figure who appears in the book of Genesis in the Old Testament, a descendant of Hori the Seirite and the son of Dishon.
lifetime: Eshban belonged to the genealogy of the Horite people who lived in the land of Seir, and was born as a son of Dishon (Genesis 36:26).
event: Nothing is recorded in the Bible about any specific deeds or particular events of Eshban himself (Genesis 36:26).

introduce: Ezbai is a man whose name appears in the list of David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles 11 in the expression "Naarai the son of Ezbai," and he is the father of Naarai (1 Chronicles 11:37).
lifetime: There is no specific record in the Bible of the life of Ezbai himself, and in the list of David's mighty men the name of his son Naarai is entered (1 Chronicles 11:37).
event: No record of any deeds or events of Ezbai himself appears in the Bible. The one entered in the list of mighty men is his son Naarai (1 Chronicles 11:37).

call: Son of Gad (ancestor of the Ezbonite clan)
introduce: Ezbon is one of the seven sons of Gad, the son of Jacob, a man specified in the genealogy of the tribe of Gad, and the ancestor of the family that is written as Ozni in the list of the clans of the sons of Gad.
lifetime: He is one of the sons born to Gad, the son of Jacob (Genesis 46:16). As a descendant of Gad, he is included in the list of the family of Jacob who migrated to Egypt (Genesis 46:16).
event: The family descended from him is recorded as the Oznite family in the list of the clans of the sons of Gad, and became one of the houses that make up the genealogy of the tribe of Gad (Numbers 26:16).

introduce: Esli is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Luke in the New Testament, a man recorded as the son of Naggai and the father of Nahum (Luke 3:25).
lifetime: In the genealogy of Jesus recorded in Luke, Esli appears, as "the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai," as the generation above Nahum and the generation below Naggai (Luke 3:25). That is, he is recorded as the son of Naggai and as the father who begat Nahum (Luke 3:25).

introduce: Evi is a man mentioned as one of the five kings of Midian (Numbers 31:8).
lifetime: Evi is recorded as one of the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba (Numbers 31:8). In Joshua 13:21, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba appear as the princes of Sihon who lived in the land of Sihon, that is, nobles of Midian, and it says that Moses killed them together with Sihon (Joshua 13:21). He is one of the five kings who were put to death when the children of Israel struck Midian at the command of the LORD (Numbers 31:7-8).
event: Evi lived in the territory of Sihon together with the five kings of Midian and lived there as a noble of that land (Joshua 13:21). Afterward, when the children of Israel won the victory in the war against Midian, he was recorded as one of the five kings of Midian who were killed (Numbers 31:8).

introduce: Evil-merodach was the second king of the Neo-Babylonian Empire and a son of Nebuchadnezzar II. He is known in the Bible as Evil-merodach and in Babylonian records by the name Amel-Marduk, and his reign is known to have been from 562 to 560 BC.
lifetime: In the first year of his reign as king of Babylon, in the thirty-seventh year after Jehoiachin was taken captive, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, he released Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison and lifted up his head (2 Kings 25:27).
event: His most representative act was to release Jehoiachin from prison thirty-seven years after he was taken captive (2 Kings 25:27). He spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and raised his seat above the seats of all the kings who were with him in Babylon (2 Kings 25:28). He also had Jehoiachin change his prison garments, and he ate at the king's table regularly all the days of his life (2 Kings 25:29).

call: Son of Korah (ancestor of the Korahite line)
introduce: Elkanah is a descendant of Kohath of the tribe of Levi, a man recorded as one of the sons of Korah (Exodus 6:24). In the genealogy of the descendants of Kohath in 1 Chronicles 6, he appears, after Assir, as "his son Elkanah, his son Ebiasaph," in the generation above Ebiasaph (1 Chronicles 6:23).
lifetime: Elkanah is mentioned as one of the sons of Korah (Exodus 6:24), and it is recorded that the sons of Korah did not die when the company of Korah perished (Numbers 26:9-11). In 1 Chronicles his name is included in the record of the families of the tribe of Levi (1 Chronicles 6:23).
event: In the biblical record no independent achievement or specific event of Elkanah individually is described separately, and his name is listed mainly as one of the figures who make up the genealogy of the tribe of Levi (Exodus 6:24, 1 Chronicles 6:23).

introduce: Eldaah is a figure who appears in Genesis and 1 Chronicles, a descendant of Keturah, the later wife of Abraham, and is recorded as one of the five sons of Midian.
lifetime: Eldaah is named last among the sons of Midian and is recorded as a descendant of Keturah (Genesis 25:4). In 1 Chronicles as well he is mentioned as one of the five sons of Midian (1 Chronicles 1:33).

introduce: Eldad is a man recorded as one of the seventy elders who stayed in the camp of Israel in the time of Moses.
lifetime: He was included in the list when Moses appointed seventy elders to govern the people (Numbers 11:24). Although he did not go to the tent of meeting but remained in the camp, the Spirit of the LORD came upon him there and he prophesied (Numbers 11:26).
event: Although they remained in the camp when Moses went out to the tent of meeting, the Spirit of the LORD came upon Eldad and Medad and they prophesied (Numbers 11:26). When a young man reported this to Moses, Joshua asked him to forbid it, but Moses did not stop them, saying that he wished the Spirit of the LORD would come upon all the people (Numbers 11:27-29).

introduce: Elah is one of the chiefs of Edom who came from Esau. The Bible lists the names of the chiefs who came from Esau according to their clans, their dwelling places, and their names, and among them records chief Elah (Genesis 36:40-41).
lifetime: Elah's name appears in the list of the chiefs who came from Esau between chief Oholibamah and chief Pinon (Genesis 36:41). He appears in the same order in 1 Chronicles, which lists the chiefs of Edom (1 Chronicles 1:52).
event: No specific deeds of Elah himself are recorded in the Bible, and his name is merely entered in the list of the chiefs of Edom who came from Esau (Genesis 36:40-41, 1 Chronicles 1:52).

introduce: Elnathan was the father-in-law of Jehoiakim king of Judah, and the son of Achbor. As a figure who appears in the book of Jeremiah in the Old Testament, he was a man who was active in the political situation in Jerusalem before the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: Nehushta, the mother of Jehoiachin the son of Jehoiakim (2 Kings 24:6), is recorded as the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem (2 Kings 24:8). When Jeremiah had the word of God written on a scroll and had it read through Baruch, he appears as one of the officials who, on hearing its contents, sought to report it to the king (Jeremiah 36:12, 36:16).
event: When Jeremiah had Baruch read the word of God in the temple, he was one of the officials gathered in the chamber of the scribe who heard its contents (Jeremiah 36:12). Afterward Elnathan and the other officials asked Baruch how he had written down Jeremiah's prophecies, and before reporting the contents to the king they advised Baruch to hide for his safety (Jeremiah 36:16-19). When King Jehoiakim burned the scroll that Jeremiah had written, Elnathan is recorded as one of those who urged the king not to burn the scroll (Jeremiah 36:25).
character: From the fact that he tried to dissuade the king when the king was about to burn the scroll containing Jeremiah's prophecies, he is assessed as a man who viewed the king's violent decision critically (Jeremiah 36:25). However, the Bible does not state whether he fully accepted Jeremiah's prophecies, and describes him only as one of the nobles who, in the political situation of that time, expressed his opposition to the king's decision (Jeremiah 36:25).

call: Priest of the sons of Pashhur
introduce: Elasah is a man recorded as belonging to a priestly family within the community of Israel after the return from the Babylonian captivity.
lifetime: Elasah comes from a priestly family classified as descendants of Pashhur (Ezra 10:22). His name was mentioned in the list when Ezra, having returned to Jerusalem, carried out the investigation of those who had foreign wives (Ezra 10:22).
event: Elasah was pointed out as one of the men among the Jews who had returned to Jerusalem who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:22). Afterward he was included in the list of those who pledged, in accordance with Ezra's investigation and exhortation, to send away their foreign wives (Ezra 10:22).

introduce: Elnaam is a man whose name appears in the list of David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles 11 in the expression "Jeribai the son of Elnaam," and he is the father of Jeribai (1 Chronicles 11:46).
lifetime: There is no specific record in the Bible of the life of Elnaam himself, and in the list of David's mighty men the name of his son Jeribai is entered (1 Chronicles 11:46). No record of the time when he was born or died appears in the Bible either.
event: No record of any deeds or events of Elnaam himself exists in the Bible. The one entered in the list of mighty men is his son Jeribai (1 Chronicles 11:46).

call: Firstborn of Shem (ancestor of the Elamite people)
introduce: Elam is a man whose name appears first among the sons of Shem, the son of Noah, in the genealogy recorded in Genesis 10. He is regarded as the ancestor of the Elamite people of the ancient Near East, and his descendants are known to have settled on the plateau region north of the Persian Gulf, east of the Tigris River, and to have formed the kingdom of Elam.
lifetime: Elam was born as a son of Shem, and in the process of humanity's dispersion after the flood of Noah he formed one line of the house of Shem (Genesis 10:22). No detailed record of his life remains in the Bible, and his name also appears in the list of the descendants of Shem in 1 Chronicles (1 Chronicles 1:17).
event: No individual achievement of Elam himself is recorded. In Genesis 14 there is a record that Chedorlaomer king of Elam, together with Amraphel king of Shinar and others, fought against the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, and others, plundered the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah, and carried off Lot, but Abram pursued them, struck them and defeated them, and recovered Lot and his possessions (Genesis 14:1-16). Also, the book of Daniel records that when Daniel saw the vision in the third year of King Belshazzar, he was in the citadel of Susa, in the province of Elam (Daniel 8:1-2).

introduce: Eliada is a name that in Hebrew carries the meaning "God has known," and in the Bible he is recorded as a son of King David who was born in Jerusalem. Beeliada is a form in which the element בַּעַל/בְּעַל (Baʿal, Baal) is placed before Eliada, and its meaning is "Baal knows/the Lord knows." Because using the title Baal for the LORD came to be avoided in Israel, it may have been changed to Eliada (God knows).
lifetime: Eliada is mentioned as one of the sons David had in Jerusalem, and is included in the lists of sons born in Jerusalem in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles (2 Samuel 5:13-16, 1 Chronicles 3:8). In 1 Chronicles 14:7 he is recorded in the same list under the name Beeliada (1 Chronicles 14:7).

introduce: Elon is a man of the Hittite people who appears in the book of Genesis in the Old Testament, recorded as the father-in-law of Esau, who had a daughter who became Esau's wife. In Genesis 26:34 his daughter Basemath, and in Genesis 36:2 his daughter Adah, appear as Esau's wife.
lifetime: Elon was a member of the Hittite people who lived in the land of Canaan (Genesis 26:34, 36:2). His daughter Basemath (Genesis 26:34) or Adah (Genesis 36:2) became Esau's wife and entered into a marriage relationship with Esau.
event: Through his daughter's becoming Esau's wife, he played a part in the marriage relationship by which Esau took a Canaanite woman as wife (Genesis 26:34, 36:2). No specific deeds of Elon himself are recorded in the Bible.

call: Chief of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:36)
meaning: My eyes look up to you, O Lord
introduce: Elioenai is one of the chiefs of the tribe of Simeon recorded in 1 Chronicles 4, a man whose name is listed together with Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, and Benaiah (1 Chronicles 4:36, 4:38).
lifetime: He is one of those listed as chiefs of the main clans of the descendants of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:36, 4:38), and his name is mentioned in the genealogy in which it is recorded that their family increased greatly (1 Chronicles 4:38).
event: As one of "these listed by name," he sought pasture for the flocks and reached the border of Gedor, east of the valley, and found rich and good pasture (1 Chronicles 4:39-40). In the days of Hezekiah king of Judah he struck the tents of the descendants of Ham who had lived there from of old and destroyed the Meunites who were there, and then settled in that place (1 Chronicles 4:40-41).

기타관계: Neariah#3338(kinsman of the tribe of Simeon)

introduce: Eluzai is a warrior from the tribe of Benjamin, one of those who joined David when David stayed at Ziklag to escape from Saul.
lifetime: He was a kinsman of Saul from the tribe of Benjamin, and was among the mighty men who came to David and helped him in the battle when David was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul the son of Kish (1 Chronicles 12:1-2, 12:5).
event: While David stayed at Ziklag, warriors of the tribe of Benjamin came to him, and Eluzai belonged to that group and took part in helping David (1 Chronicles 12:5).

introduce: Eleadah is a descendant of the tribe of Ephraim, a man recorded in the genealogy of Shuthelah, the son of Ephraim, as the son of Tahath and the father of another Tahath (1 Chronicles 7:20).
lifetime: Eleadah belongs to the genealogy that runs from Shuthelah, the son of Ephraim, through Bered to Tahath, and it is recorded that his son was Tahath (1 Chronicles 7:20). The one who begot Ezer and Elead is not Eleadah but his descendant Shuthelah (the son of Zabad) (1 Chronicles 7:21).
event: No individual deeds of Eleadah are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Elasah is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, the son of Helez and the father of Sismai. (1 Chronicles 2:39-40)
lifetime: Elasah is recorded as the son of Helez, the son of Azariah. (1 Chronicles 2:39) His son was Sismai, and Sismai begot Shallum. (1 Chronicles 2:40)

introduce: Eleazar was the third son of Aaron and a priest of the tribe of Levi, and after Aaron's death he served as the second high priest of Israel. Throughout the Exodus and the period of the conquest of Canaan he carried out his duties as priest and played the role of maintaining order in the sanctuary of Israel.
lifetime: Eleazar was born as a son of Aaron and Elisheba (Exodus 6:23). After his older brothers Nadab and Abihu died offering strange fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, Eleazar and Ithamar served in the priestly office in the presence of their father Aaron (Leviticus 10:1-2, Numbers 3:4). When Aaron died on Mount Hor, Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on his son Eleazar (Numbers 20:25-28), and thus he succeeded to the office of second high priest. After the death of Moses, together with Joshua the son of Nun and the heads of the tribes, he distributed the inheritance that the children of Israel took in the land of Canaan (Joshua 14:1), and finished dividing the land by casting lots before the LORD at the door of the tent of meeting at Shiloh (Joshua 19:51). When he died, the people buried him in the hill that had been given to his son Phinehas in the hill country of Ephraim (Joshua 24:33).
event: After the rebellion of the company of Korah, the priest Eleazar took the bronze censers that those who had been burned had offered, and had them hammered out into a covering for the altar, to be a sign to the children of Israel (Numbers 16:37-39). When the people of Israel sinned at Shittim by serving Baal of Peor, the one who pierced the Israelite man and the Midianite woman with a spear and stopped the plague was Phinehas, the son of Eleazar (Numbers 25:7-8). After the war with Midian he told the soldiers who had gone to battle the law that the LORD had commanded Moses, saying that gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin and lead, everything that can stand the fire, should be put through the fire, and it shall be clean, and also purified with the water of purification (Numbers 31:21-23). When the land of Canaan was divided, together with Joshua the son of Nun and the heads of the tribes, he cast lots at Shiloh and divided the inheritance (Joshua 19:51).

call: Son of Ephraim (killed by the men of Gath)
introduce: Elead is a man recorded as a son of Ephraim who, together with Ezer, was killed by the native men of Gath (1 Chronicles 7:21-22). Some read "he" in 1 Chronicles 7:21 as referring to Shuthelah (the son of Zabad) just before, but since 7:22 says "their father Ephraim," it is recorded here as a son of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 7:21-22).
lifetime: Elead is a descendant of Shuthelah, the son of Ephraim, and is recorded as one of those murdered by the men of Gath (1 Chronicles 7:21).
event: Elead was killed by the natives of Gath, and the reason the men of Gath killed Elead and his brothers was that they had tried to take away the livestock of the men of Gath (1 Chronicles 7:21).

introduce: Eli was a priest of Israel and a judge who performed his duties at the sanctuary in Shiloh. He belonged to the family line of Ithamar, a descendant of Aaron, and served as the highest leader of Israel.
lifetime: Eli served as the priest of the LORD at Shiloh and acted as judge for a long time (1 Samuel 4:18). When he saw Hannah praying at the sanctuary he mistook her for drunk and rebuked her (1 Samuel 1:12-14). He watched as the young Samuel, who was sleeping in the sanctuary, was called by God, and taught him how to respond to the LORD (1 Samuel 3:8-9). In his old age, hearing the news of the war with the Philistines and that the ark of the covenant had been captured, he fell backward from his seat, broke his neck, and died (1 Samuel 4:17-18).
event: Although his two sons Hophni and Phinehas committed improper acts as priests and extorted the sacrificial food, Eli was unable to restrain them strictly (1 Samuel 2:22-25). Because of this he heard from a man of God a prophecy that his house would fall (1 Samuel 2:31-34). Right after Israel was defeated by the Philistines and the ark of the covenant was captured, he heard the news that his two sons had died in battle (1 Samuel 4:11-17).
character: Eli was in a physical condition in which, being advanced in years, his eyes had grown dim and he could not see well (1 Samuel 3:2). He gave verbal admonition about his children's wrong conduct, but showed a weak side in that he could not actually restrain them or remove them from their duties (1 Samuel 2:23-24). He was somewhat dull in judgment, as when he misunderstood Hannah's prayer, but he also showed spiritual insight in telling the young Samuel, who was being called by God, that it was the voice of the LORD (1 Samuel 1:14, 1 Samuel 3:9).

introduce: Elika is a man classified as one of the thirty-seven mighty men who served David during David's reign (2 Samuel 23:25).
lifetime: Elika was a Harodite and was active as a member of David's company of mighty men (2 Samuel 23:25).
event: His name is included in the list of David's mighty men, and he is recorded as one of those who made up David's military foundation (2 Samuel 23:25).

introduce: Elidad is a man who appears in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament, the son of Chislon of the tribe of Benjamin, and one of the tribal chiefs chosen to divide the inheritance of the land of Canaan.
lifetime: Elidad is recorded as a chief of the tribe of Benjamin, as the son of Chislon (Numbers 34:21). The LORD told Moses to choose one chief from each tribe to divide the land as an inheritance, and among those names is Elidad of the tribe of Benjamin (Numbers 34:18-21).
event: When the LORD told Moses to choose one chief from each tribe to divide the land as an inheritance, his name was recorded as the man representing the tribe of Benjamin (Numbers 34:18, 34:21). In the same passage, the ones named as those who would divide the land as an inheritance are the priest Eleazar and Joshua the son of Nun (Numbers 34:17).

introduce: An Ephrathite from Bethlehem of the tribe of Judah, a man who was active in the period of the judges. His name carries the meaning "My God is King."
lifetime: When a famine came in Bethlehem, he took his wife Naomi and his two sons Mahlon and Chilion and moved to the country of Moab (Ruth 1:1, 1:2). He died while living in Moab (Ruth 1:3).
event: When a famine came in the land in the days when the judges ruled, he moved his dwelling to the country of Moab and died there (Ruth 1:1, 1:3). After he died, Naomi and her two sons remained (Ruth 1:3), but the two sons also died and only Naomi was left (Ruth 1:5). Afterward, the book of Ruth records that Boaz bought from the hand of Naomi all that had belonged to Elimelech and Chilion and Mahlon (Ruth 4:3, 4:9).

call: Firstborn of Esau (ancestor of the chiefs of Edom)
introduce: Eliphaz is the firstborn son born to Esau, the son of Isaac, and his wife Adah, and the chiefs who were in the land of Edom came from his descendants and through him (Genesis 36:4, 36:15-16).
lifetime: Eliphaz is the firstborn son of Esau, born between Esau and Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite (Genesis 36:2, 36:4, 36:15). Esau led his wives and his children out of the land of Canaan and lived in Mount Seir (Genesis 36:6-8).
event: The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz (Genesis 36:11). His concubine Timna bore Amalek to Eliphaz (Genesis 36:12). From the descendants of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn, came chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, and chief Kenaz (Genesis 36:15), and in the land of Edom there were chiefs who came from Eliphaz (Genesis 36:16).

introduce: Eliphal is a man recorded as one of the thirty mighty men of David, who made up David's military organization (1 Chronicles 11:35).
lifetime: Eliphal was included in the list as one of David's thirty mighty men during the reign of King David (1 Chronicles 11:35).
event: As a member of the mighty men who were David's strong military foundation, he is mentioned as having contributed to the strengthening of David's rule and to his military campaigns (1 Chronicles 11:35).

introduce: Eliphelet is one of the sons King David had in Jerusalem, a man who appears at the end of the list of David's children in 1 Chronicles 14:7. He is a different person from the Elpelet who appears in verse 5.
lifetime: Eliphelet is mentioned as one of the sons David begot in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:8). He is listed last in order among the children born to David's wives (1 Chronicles 14:7).

introduce: Eliphelehu is a man who, when the ark of God was moved in the time of King David, was one of the brothers appointed by the heads of the Levites, and was entrusted with the duty of playing the lyre (1 Chronicles 15:18, 15:21).
lifetime: When David commanded the heads of the Levites to appoint their singing brothers, he was recorded as one of the brothers appointed after Heman, Asaph, and Ethan (1 Chronicles 15:16-18). Together with Mattithiah, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah, he was one who led with the lyre according to Sheminith (1 Chronicles 15:21).
event: When the ark of God was moved, Eliphelehu, together with Mattithiah, Mikneiah, and others, was entrusted with the duty of leading with the lyre according to Sheminith (1 Chronicles 15:21).

introduce: A prophet of the northern kingdom of Israel who was active in succession to Elijah. He was from Abel-meholah, the son of Shaphat, and began his ministry when he was called by Elijah (1 Kings 19:16).
lifetime: When Elijah called Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him, by throwing his cloak over him (1 Kings 19:19), he took one yoke of oxen, burned the equipment of the oxen, boiled their flesh and gave it to the people to eat, and then followed Elijah and served him (1 Kings 19:21). When Elijah went up in a whirlwind, he took up Elijah's cloak and succeeded to the prophetic office (2 Kings 2:13). Afterward he was active centered on Samaria, and from the time of Jehoram to the time of King Jehoash he served as an adviser in the political and religious spheres of the northern kingdom of Israel (2 Kings 13:14). He remained active until he fell ill in his last years and met his death, and it is recorded that even after his death a corpse that touched his bones came back to life (2 Kings 13:21).
event: He struck the waters of the Jordan with Elijah's cloak so that they parted, and crossed the Jordan (2 Kings 2:14). He healed the bad water of Jericho with salt and made it fit to drink (2 Kings 2:21). To the allied army of Israel, Judah, and Edom he conveyed the word of the LORD to dig many ditches in the valley, and as the word said, water came flowing from the direction of Edom and filled the land (2 Kings 3:16-20). He filled a widow's jar of oil so that she could pay her debt (2 Kings 4:6), and restored to life the dead son of the Shunammite woman (2 Kings 4:35). He healed the leprosy of Naaman, commander of the army of Aram, by having him wash seven times in the Jordan (2 Kings 5:14). Whenever the king of Aram attacked Israel, he informed the king of his strategy in advance so that he could defend (2 Kings 6:12).
character: He was so resolute that he immediately cut his ties with his family in order to follow Elijah, who had called him (1 Kings 19:21). His zeal for the ministry was so strong that he asked of Elijah that a double portion of the work of the Spirit be upon him (2 Kings 2:9). He showed integrity by refusing to accept a gift from Naaman, the commander of the army of Aram (2 Kings 5:16), but showed fairness in sternly rebuking his servant Gehazi when he falsely took a gift (2 Kings 5:26). The incident in which he cursed the boys who mocked him at Bethel and bears came out shows his forceful way of dealing with challenges to his authority (2 Kings 2:24).

기타관계: Naaman#3316(king of Aram, prophet, military commander)

introduce: Elishama is a man who appears in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament, a chief and commander of the tribe of Ephraim. He is the son of Ammihud, and in the process of the march and the arrangement of the camps of the children of Israel he is mentioned as the one representing his tribe.
lifetime: Elishama was born as the son of Ammihud and became commander of the descendants of Ephraim (Numbers 1:10). When the people of Israel were numbered in the wilderness, he was appointed as the head representing his tribe (Numbers 2:18). Also, at the time of the dedication of the tabernacle, as commander of the descendants of Ephraim he took part in presenting his offering (Numbers 7:48).
event: During the wilderness journey of Israel, Elishama served as the commander who led the camp of the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim (Numbers 2:18). At the dedication of the tabernacle, on the seventh day, as chief of the descendants of Ephraim, he presented offerings including a silver plate, a silver bowl, a gold spoon, and a burnt offering, a sin offering, and peace offerings (Numbers 7:48-53). Later, in the recording of Joshua's genealogy, he is also mentioned as Joshua's grandfather (1 Chronicles 7:26-27).

call: Son of Uzziel (chief of the Kohathite Levites)
introduce: Elizaphan is a descendant of Kohath of the tribe of Levi, the son of Uzziel, the uncle of Aaron, and the chief of the Uzziel clan, one of the families of the descendants of Kohath.
lifetime: In the wilderness, Elizaphan the son of Uzziel was appointed to be chief of the families and clans of the Kohathites (Numbers 3:30). In the time of David, among the descendants of Elizaphan, chief Shemaiah and two hundred of his brothers are recorded (1 Chronicles 15:8).
event: When Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan (Elizaphan), the sons of Uzziel, the uncle of Aaron, and commanded them to carry Nadab and Abihu from before the sanctuary to outside the camp, they carried them out of the camp in their tunics as Moses had said (Leviticus 10:4-5). In Numbers 3:30 it is recorded that he is to be the chief of the families and clans of the Kohathites.

introduce: Elishaphat is one of the captains of hundreds of Judah who made a covenant with the priest Jehoiada, took part in the process of ending the rule of Athaliah and enthroning Joash as king of the kingdom of Judah.
lifetime: While Joash hid in the house of God for six years, Athaliah ruled the land (2 Chronicles 22:12), and in the seventh year the priest Jehoiada took courage and made a covenant with five captains of hundreds, among whom Elishaphat is recorded as one, as the son of Zichri (2 Chronicles 23:1).
event: Together with the other captains of hundreds he went about through Judah and gathered the Levites from all the towns of Judah and the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel, and came to Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 23:2). The priest Jehoiada gave the captains of hundreds the spears, the large shields and the small shields of King David that were in the house of God (2 Chronicles 23:9).

introduce: A figure who appears in the Gospel of Luke in the New Testament, the wife of Zechariah, a priest who was a descendant of Aaron, and the mother of John the Baptist.
lifetime: She was a descendant of Aaron and married Zechariah (Luke 1:5). She had no children until she reached old age, but the angel Gabriel appeared to Zechariah as he was burning incense in the sanctuary and foretold the birth of a son (Luke 1:7, 1:13, 1:19). After conceiving she remained in seclusion for five months (Luke 1:24), and in the house of Zechariah in a town in the hill country of Judea she received the greeting of Mary (Luke 1:39-40). Afterward she bore a son (Luke 1:57), and on the eighth day, at the gathering that came to circumcise the child, she said that his name must be John (Luke 1:59-60).
event: When Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the child in her womb leaped, and Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, called Mary the mother of my Lord and said she was blessed (Luke 1:41-45). On the eighth day, when those who came to circumcise him wanted to name him Zechariah after his father, she answered that he must be called John (Luke 1:59-60), and Zechariah also wrote on a writing tablet that his name is John (Luke 1:63).
character: Together with her husband Zechariah she was recognized as righteous before God, and is described as walking blamelessly in all the commandments and statutes of the Lord (Luke 1:6). Even at an advanced age she fully accepted the prophecy of the birth, and she showed a firm attitude, not yielding even to her relatives' suggestion of the customary naming (Luke 1:60).

introduce: Elisheba is a female figure recorded as the wife of Aaron, the daughter of Amminadab of the tribe of Judah, and the sister of Nahshon. She is recorded as the mother of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
lifetime: Aaron took as his wife Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon (Exodus 6:23). She bore four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar (Exodus 6:23).
event: No deeds of Elisheba herself are recorded in the Bible; there is only the record that, as the wife of Aaron, she bore Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar (Exodus 6:23). Her sons Nadab and Abihu died while offering incense before the LORD with strange fire that the LORD had not commanded (Leviticus 10:1-2).

introduce: Elizur is a man mentioned in the book of Numbers, a chief of the tribe of Reuben and the son of Shedeur. In the census of the community of Israel and the arrangement of the camps, he appears as the leader representing his tribe.
lifetime: At the time of the census taken in the wilderness of Sinai, he was appointed commander of the descendants of Reuben (Numbers 1:5). Afterward, in the process of presenting offerings for the dedication of the tabernacle, he served as one of the commanders of the tribes (Numbers 7:30).
event: At the census of Israel he carried out his duty as the representative of the tribe of Reuben (Numbers 1:5). During the period of presenting offerings for the dedication of the tabernacle, on the day of offering assigned to him he presented, on behalf of his tribe, a silver plate, a silver bowl, a gold spoon, and other things before God as offerings (Numbers 7:30-35).

call: Son of Hilkiah (palace steward under Hezekiah)
introduce: Eliakim the son of Hilkiah was a high official who served as palace steward in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah. At the time of the Assyrian invasion he is recorded as a man who handled the diplomatic and administrative affairs of the royal court of Judah and enjoyed the king's trust.
lifetime: Eliakim is mentioned as the son of Hilkiah and is recorded as the palace steward in the time of King Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:18). In Isaiah 22:15-21 is recorded the word in which the LORD said that he would drive Shebna, who was in charge of the treasury and held the palace, out of his office, and would call his servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, clothe him with a robe and a sash, and commit the government into his hand. When Sennacherib of Assyria besieged Jerusalem, he, as one close to the king, together with Shebna the scribe and Joah the recorder, went out to negotiate with the Assyrian envoy Rabshakeh (Isaiah 36:3). Afterward, at the command of King Hezekiah, he put on sackcloth and went to the prophet Isaiah, and asked for his intercession in the national crisis (2 Kings 19:2).
event: Together with Shebna and Joah, he asked Rabshakeh to speak in the Aramaic language and not in the language of Judah in the hearing of the people on the wall (2 Kings 18:26). Afterward, when Rabshakeh cried out loudly in the language of Judah (2 Kings 18:28), he, together with Shebna and Joah, tore his clothes and went to Hezekiah and told him the words of Rabshakeh (2 Kings 18:37, Isaiah 36:22). After Hezekiah put on sackcloth and went to the house of the LORD, he, together with Shebna and the elders of the priests, put on sackcloth and went to the prophet Isaiah, delivering Hezekiah's message and the request that he pray for the remnant that was left (Isaiah 37:1-4).
character: The Bible describes him as a man whom God calls "my servant," and on whose shoulder God places the key of the house of David, giving him authority (Isaiah 22:20-22). He enjoyed the deep trust of King Hezekiah and faithfully carried out his duty as the king's representative in the national crisis (2 Kings 19:2). He received the prophecy that he would be in a firm position like a peg, a source of glory for his family and house (Isaiah 22:23-24).

introduce: Eliada is a prominent military commander of the tribe of Benjamin who was active in the time of King Jehoshaphat of the kingdom of South Judah. He is recorded as one of the men who played a central role in Jehoshaphat's military system.
lifetime: He was a mighty man of valor from Benjamin, and in the time of King Jehoshaphat he commanded two hundred thousand armed with bow and shield (2 Chronicles 17:17). All these served the king (2 Chronicles 17:19). No specific record of his birth or death over the course of his life remains.
event: Eliada assisted King Jehoshaphat, commanding two hundred thousand soldiers armed with bow and shield (2 Chronicles 17:17). This was part of the corps system that Jehoshaphat deployed at that time to strengthen the national defense, and Eliada is mentioned as one who contributed to consolidating the military power of Judah.
character: The Bible does not simply call him a mighty man but calls him a "mighty man of valor," emphasizing his outstanding military ability and courage (2 Chronicles 17:17). As a man of the tribe of Benjamin, he had the characteristic of being the leader of a special force skilled in handling bow and shield (2 Chronicles 17:17).

introduce: Eliahba is a Shaalbonite, a man whose name is recorded in the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:32, 1 Chronicles 11:33).
lifetime: In the list of mighty men in 2 Samuel 23, Eliahba the Shaalbonite is recorded together with Jonathan the son of Jashen (2 Samuel 23:32), and in the list in 1 Chronicles 11 he is recorded as Eliahba the Shaalbonite together with Azmaveth the Baharumite (1 Chronicles 11:33). Beyond that, there is no record about his own family or deeds.
event: No individual deeds of Eliahba are recorded in the Bible; his name is entered in the list of David's mighty men as a Shaalbonite (2 Samuel 23:32, 1 Chronicles 11:33).

introduce: He is the son of Abinadab of Kiriath-jearim, a man who was consecrated and set apart to guard the ark of the LORD that had returned from the Philistines (1 Samuel 7:1).
lifetime: He was entrusted with the responsibility of guarding the ark of the LORD in the house of Abinadab in Kiriath-jearim, and this took place after the ark of God was moved to Kiriath-jearim (1 Samuel 7:1).
event: The men of Kiriath-jearim moved the ark of the LORD and brought it into the house of Abinadab, who lived on the hill, and consecrated his son Eleazar to guard the ark of the LORD (1 Samuel 7:1).

call: Son of Deuel (commander of the tribe of Gad)
introduce: Eliasaph is a man who appears in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament, a commander of the tribe of Gad and the son of Deuel. He is recorded as one of the leaders representing each tribe when the people of Israel, after the exodus from Egypt, were counted in the wilderness or marched.
lifetime: He was chosen as the commander of the tribe of Gad when Moses and Aaron counted the people according to the genealogies of the children of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai (Numbers 1:14). Afterward, when the camp of Israel pitched camp, he was also recorded as the chief of the descendants of Gad (Numbers 2:14).
event: When the children of Israel set out from Mount Sinai and marched, he served as the commander leading the tribe of Gad (Numbers 10:20). Also, at the time of the dedication of the tabernacle, when the commanders of each tribe of Israel presented offerings, he took part as the son of Deuel, representing the tribe of Gad (Numbers 7:42). The offering he presented then was one silver platter, one silver bowl, and one gold spoon filled with incense (Numbers 7:43-44).

introduce: Eliashib is a priest recorded as the eleventh division when David divided the divisions of the priests.
lifetime: He is recorded as the eleventh in the list of the divisions of the priests in 1 Chronicles 24 (1 Chronicles 24:12). Nothing else of his life is recorded in this verse.
event: He was recorded as the eleventh when the divisions of the priests were set (1 Chronicles 24:12).
character: There is no specific record of his personal character. He is recorded as the eleventh in the priestly divisions of David's time (1 Chronicles 24:12).

introduce: Eliab is a man who appears in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament, a commander of the tribe of Zebulun and the son of Helon.
lifetime: Eliab is mentioned as the representative of the tribe of Zebulun when the people of Israel were counted and the army was organized in the wilderness after the exodus (Numbers 1:9). He was recorded as the chief of the descendants of Zebulun when they pitched camp around the tent of meeting in the wilderness of Sinai (Numbers 2:7).
event: In the period of the dedication offerings presented after the tabernacle was completed, Eliab, as chief of the tribe of Zebulun, presented his offering on the third day (Numbers 7:24). The offering he presented was one silver platter, one silver bowl, one gold spoon filled with incense, for the burnt offering one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old, for the sin offering one male goat, and for the peace offerings two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old (Numbers 7:25-29).

introduce: A prophet from Tishbe in Gilead who was active in the time of King Ahab and King Ahaziah of the northern kingdom of Israel. He appeared to defend the orthodoxy of faith in the LORD at a time when Baal worship was flourishing, and his course included prophesying a famine, performing miraculous wonders, and designating a successor.
lifetime: He first appeared as a Tishbite living in Gilead and foretold a drought to Ahab (1 Kings 17:1). Afterward he stayed by the brook Cherith and at the house of the widow of Zarephath (1 Kings 17:5, 17:9), and confronted the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:19). He fled to Mount Horeb to escape the threat of Jezebel (1 Kings 19:8), and appointed Elisha as his successor (1 Kings 19:16). At the end of his life he went up to heaven in a whirlwind (2 Kings 2:11).
event: He prophesied that no rain would fall on Israel for several years (1 Kings 17:1). He restored to life the dead son of the widow of Zarephath (1 Kings 17:22). On Mount Carmel he confronted the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and, by calling down fire, proved that the LORD is the true God (1 Kings 18:22, 18:38). He warned of judgment over the incident of the seizure of Ahab's vineyard (1 Kings 21:19). He brought down fire from heaven in judgment on the captain of fifty and his soldiers sent by King Ahaziah (2 Kings 1:10). He struck the waters of the Jordan with his cloak so that they parted (2 Kings 2:8).
character: He showed human anguish, as when he lost heart and asked to die, or hid under the broom tree in the wilderness (1 Kings 19:4). He was a hairy man and wore a leather belt (2 Kings 1:8). With a fiery, passionate temperament, he delivered messages of judgment without hesitation even before the king (1 Kings 18:18). Even in the New Testament era, a person who would minister in the spirit and power of Elijah was foretold (Luke 1:17), and he was imprinted as a symbolic figure of the Israelite prophetic tradition.

introduce: Elienai is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as one of the sons of Shimei (1 Chronicles 8:20-21).
lifetime: Elienai is a son of Shimei (1 Chronicles 8:20-21), and is included in the genealogy of the chiefs of the tribe of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).

introduce: Eliezer is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Luke, a descendant of Nathan, the son of David, and recorded as one of the ancestors of Jesus.
lifetime: In the genealogy of Jesus in Luke, Eliezer is the son of Jorim and is recorded as the father of the ancestor named Jesus who is recorded in 3:29 of the same genealogy (Luke 3:29). He is included in the group of persons that continues along the line of Nathan, the son of King David (Luke 3:31).

call: Servant of Abraham (a man of Damascus)
introduce: Eliezer is a household retainer of Abraham, a man whom Abraham regarded as his heir in the days when he had no child, and he is recorded as a man of Damascus.
lifetime: In the days when he had no child, Abram said, "My heir is Eliezer of Damascus," and immediately afterward said that one born in his house would be his heir (Genesis 15:2-3). There is a view that sees the old servant in charge of all that Abraham owned, who was sent to Abraham's homeland to seek a wife for Isaac in Genesis 24, as Eliezer, but the KRV text does not give that servant's name (Genesis 24:2, 24:4).
event: He was mentioned as Abram's heir when Abram spoke of having no child (Genesis 15:2-3). In Genesis 24 there is an account in which the old servant in charge of all that Abraham owned comes to the city of Nahor in Mesopotamia to seek a wife for Isaac and meets Rebekah (Genesis 24:2, 24:10-15), but the text does not give this servant's name.
character: He showed thorough obedience to his master's command, and when carrying out his mission he had the prudence to seek God's guidance through prayer (Genesis 24:12-14). He deeply respected his master's family and acted with great responsibility and care in the process of seeking a spouse for Isaac (Genesis 24:33-49). Also, after completing his mission he immediately reported to his master and arranged the meeting of Isaac and Rebekah, showing a loyal side (Genesis 24:66-67).

introduce: Eliel is one of the ancestors in the genealogy of Samuel recorded in 1 Chronicles 6, a man who appears as the son of Toah and the father of Jeroham.
lifetime: In the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 6:34 he is recorded as the son of Toah and the father of Jeroham. Since the son of Jeroham is Elkanah and the son of Elkanah is Samuel, Eliel is Samuel's great-grandfather (1 Chronicles 6:34).
event: No specific deeds or particular events of his are recorded in the Bible.
character: He is mentioned as a Levite belonging to the tribe of Zuph (1 Samuel 1:1). The Bible provides no separate information about his personal character or personal traits. -

기타관계: Samuel#1462(fellow worker of the tribe of Levi)

introduce: Eliud is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Matthew in the New Testament, a member of the Jewish bloodline that continues from the royal house of David.
lifetime: He is the son of Achim and the father of Eleazar (Matthew 1:14-15). He succeeded to the family line after Achim, and by begetting Eleazar he stands in the course by which the genealogy of David is passed on to Jesus (Matthew 1:15).

meaning: My god is Haph (an Egyptian god)
introduce: A man who served as a scribe of the kingdom of Israel in the time of Solomon. He is recorded as the son of Shisha.
lifetime: Elihoreph is recorded as the son of Shisha, and was appointed together with Ahijah as a scribe of King Solomon and was active (1 Kings 4:3).
event: Under King Solomon's system of rule he carried out the office of scribe, in charge of national administration and records (1 Kings 4:3).

introduce: Elmadam is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Luke, recorded as the son of Cosam and the father of Er (Luke 3:28).
lifetime: Elmadam was born as the son of Cosam, and his son is Er (Luke 3:28).

introduce: Elpaal is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, a son of Shaharaim (1 Chronicles 8:8, 8:11).
lifetime: Elpaal was one of the children whom Shaharaim fathered in the country of Moab after sending away his two wives Hushim and Baara, and was a son born to him by Hushim together with Abitub (1 Chronicles 8:8, 8:11). The sons of Elpaal are recorded as Eber, Misham, and Shemed (1 Chronicles 8:12), and Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab are also recorded as sons of Elpaal (1 Chronicles 8:18).

introduce: Elpelet is one of the sons David had in Jerusalem, a man recorded in 1 Chronicles 14:5 after Ibhar and Elishua (1 Chronicles 14:4-5).
lifetime: Elpelet is included in the list of sons born to David in Jerusalem after David moved his residence to Jerusalem by way of Hebron (1 Chronicles 14:5).

introduce: Elzabad is one of the mighty men who joined David while David was staying at Ziklag to escape from Saul, and is a man belonging to the descendants of Gad (1 Chronicles 12:12).
lifetime: Elzabad is recorded as the ninth among the eleven Gadite mighty men who came back to David when he was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul the son of Kish (1 Chronicles 12:1, 12:8-13).
event: The Gadite mighty men who came back to David were men trained for battle (1 Chronicles 12:8). Elzabad was one of them, and these descendants of Gad became captains of the army, the least over a hundred men and the greatest over a thousand (1 Chronicles 12:12-14).

meaning: My eyes are toward the LORD
introduce: Eliehoenai is the seventh son of Meshelemiah, who belonged to the division of the gatekeepers of the Korahites (1 Chronicles 26:1-3).
lifetime: Eliehoenai is recorded as the seventh among the sons of Meshelemiah the son of Kore of the Korahites (1 Chronicles 26:1-3). His brothers are Zechariah, Jediael, Zebadiah, Jathniel, Elam, and Jehohanan (1 Chronicles 26:2-3).
event: When the divisions of the gatekeepers were set, he was entered in the list of gatekeepers together with his father Meshelemiah and his brothers (1 Chronicles 26:1-3). The sons and brothers of Meshelemiah, eighteen in all, were able men (1 Chronicles 26:9).

introduce: Elhanan is a man who appears in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, one of David's mighty men.
lifetime: Elhanan is recorded as the son of Dodo of Bethlehem. In 2 Samuel 23:24 his name is entered in the list of the thirty mighty men together with Asahel, the brother of Joab (2 Samuel 23:24), and in 1 Chronicles 11:26 Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem is recorded among the mighty men of the armies (1 Chronicles 11:26).

introduce: Elhanan is a man who appears in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, one of David's mighty men. He is recorded as the man who put down one of the giant race of the Philistines.
lifetime: Elhanan is recorded as the son of Jaare-oregim the Bethlehemite (2 Samuel 21:19). In 1 Chronicles 20:5 he is recorded as Elhanan the son of Jair (1 Chronicles 20:5).
event: Elhanan is famous for the incident in the war with the Philistines at Gob in which he killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite (2 Samuel 21:19). In 1 Chronicles 20:5 as well there is the same account of killing Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite (1 Chronicles 20:5).

introduce: Ethbaal is recorded as the king of the Sidonians and the father of Jezebel, wife of Ahab king of the northern kingdom of Israel (1 Kings 16:31).
lifetime: He is recorded as king of the Sidonians, and his daughter Jezebel became the wife of Ahab, king of the northern kingdom of Israel (1 Kings 16:31).
event: In the KRV, apart from the record that his daughter Jezebel became Ahab's wife, none of his deeds appears (1 Kings 16:31).
character: As a ruler of priestly origin, he was a strategic man who used religious influence as a political base, and showed a realistic manner of rule that secured the standing of his nation through marriage alliances with neighboring powers (1 Kings 16:31).

introduce: Jekamiah is a man who appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah, the son of Shallum and the father of Elishama (1 Chronicles 2:41).
lifetime: Jekamiah was born to Shallum the son of Sismai and begot Elishama (1 Chronicles 2:40-41). Thus he is included in the genealogy of the house of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:33, 2:41).
event: In the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 2 in which the descendants of Jerahmeel are listed, he is recorded as a member of the genealogy as the son of Shallum and the father of Elishama (1 Chronicles 2:41).

introduce: Jekameam is a descendant of the tribe of Levi and a son of Hebron, a man who appears in the records of the genealogy of the Levites and the division of duties in the time of David.
lifetime: Jekameam is a descendant of Hebron, who was a grandson of Levi and a son of Kohath (1 Chronicles 23:19). He is recorded as the fourth of the sons of Hebron, and when David organized the descendants of Levi he was included in the list as one of the descendants of Hebron (1 Chronicles 24:23).

introduce: Jecoliah is the mother of Uzziah king of Judah, and is a woman of Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 26:3).
lifetime: Jecoliah is a woman of Jerusalem, and her name is recorded as the mother when Uzziah the son of Amaziah became king at the age of sixteen (2 Chronicles 26:1, 26:3).

introduce: Jekuthiel is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a son born of Jehudijah and recorded as the ancestor of Zanoah (1 Chronicles 4:18).
lifetime: Jekuthiel is mentioned as a descendant of the tribe of Judah, and in 1 Chronicles 4:18 it is recorded that Jehudijah bore Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah, together with Jered the father of Gedor and Heber the father of Soco (1 Chronicles 4:18).

call: Head of the second division of priests
introduce: Jedaiah is the head of the priestly family that took charge of the second division when the organization of the priests was arranged into twenty-four divisions in the time of David.
lifetime: King David divided the divisions by casting lots in order to manage the descendants of the priest Aaron efficiently, and at this time Jedaiah was assigned the second turn (1 Chronicles 24:7). Afterward, descendants of the house of Jedaiah are included in the list of the priests who returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 12:6).
event: In the time of David he took part in the casting of lots to carry out the priestly duties, and had the second division confirmed for him (1 Chronicles 24:7). At the time of the return from the Babylonian exile, 973 descendants of the house of Jedaiah returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:36). Also, in the days of Joiakim, as heads of the priests, Uzzi is recorded for the family of Jedaiah (Nehemiah 12:19), and Nethanel is also recorded for the family of Jedaiah (Nehemiah 12:21).

introduce: Jether is the eldest son of the judge Gideon, a man who appears in the incident of Gideon putting to death the Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna (Judges 8:20).
lifetime: Jether is recorded as the firstborn son of the judge Gideon (Judges 8:20). He received an order from his father Gideon to kill the kings of Midian (Judges 8:20).
event: Gideon commanded his son Jether to draw his sword and kill the captured Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna in order to put them to death (Judges 8:20). But Jether, being still a young boy, was afraid and could not draw his sword (Judges 8:20).
character: Jether was a boy at the time, and was still too young to carry out an execution and had a fearful heart (Judges 8:20).

introduce: Jetur is a man recorded in 1 Chronicles 5:19 together with the Hagrites, Naphish, and Nodab, and appears as a party that fought against the descendants of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
lifetime: Jetur is recorded as having fought, together with the Hagrites, Naphish, and Nodab, against the descendants of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 5:19). The Bible does not state his birth or lineage in this verse.
event: While the descendants of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh were fighting against the Hagrites and Jetur and Naphish and Nodab (1 Chronicles 5:19), by God's help the Hagrites and those with them were defeated by their hands (1 Chronicles 5:20). In this battle the descendants of Reuben seized fifty thousand camels, two hundred fifty thousand sheep, and two thousand donkeys, and took a hundred thousand people captive (1 Chronicles 5:21).

introduce: Jetur is a son of Ishmael, the son of Abraham, one of the twelve sons of Ishmael (Genesis 25:15-16, 1 Chronicles 1:31).
lifetime: Jetur is recorded as a son of Ishmael (Genesis 25:15, 1 Chronicles 1:31). He is included in the list that enumerates the names of the sons of Ishmael, and the Bible does not provide specific information about his deeds after birth or about his dwelling place.
event: Within the biblical text, no special achievement or individual incident carried out by the person Jetur himself is recorded. He appears only in the genealogical list in which he is mentioned side by side with his brothers as a son of Ishmael (Genesis 25:15, 1 Chronicles 1:31).

introduce: Jedidah is the mother of Josiah king of Judah (2 Kings 22:1). Since Josiah is the son of Amon, she is understood to be the wife of Amon king of Judah (2 Kings 21:24, 21:26). She is recorded as the daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath.
lifetime: Jedidah is recorded as the daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath, and is the mother of Josiah, who became king (2 Kings 22:1). Josiah is the son of Amon king of Judah (2 Kings 21:24, 21:26).

call: Son of Benjamin (head of a clan of mighty men)
introduce: Jediael is a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, a man mentioned in the record of Chronicles as one of the sons of Benjamin.
lifetime: Jediael is recorded as a son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:6). His son is recorded as Bilhan (1 Chronicles 7:10), and his family is known to have produced brave warriors (1 Chronicles 7:11).
event: The sons of Jediael were heads of their families and mighty men of valor, and among their descendants those fit to go out to battle numbered seventeen thousand two hundred (1 Chronicles 7:11). The family of Jediael was composed of mighty men of valor, with a military organization, fit to go out to war (1 Chronicles 7:11).
character: The descendants of Jediael are described in the biblical record as mighty men of valor, which suggests that the family to which he belonged was a group equipped with military ability and organization (1 Chronicles 7:11).

introduce: Jediael is a man who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, belonging to the Korahite clan, descendants of Levi. He is a son of Meshelemiah, a family of those who served as gatekeepers of the temple in the time of King David (1 Chronicles 26:2).
lifetime: Jediael was born as the second son of Meshelemiah, a descendant of Korah (1 Chronicles 26:2). Within the system of temple gatekeepers organized by King David, he carried out the gatekeeper's duty together with his family (1 Chronicles 26:1-2).
event: King David divided the temple gatekeepers by their families and had each take charge of a different gate, and Jediael, together with his brothers, took the gatekeeper's duty within this system (1 Chronicles 26:1-2). There is no separate record of the specific gatekeeping assignment he held (1 Chronicles 26:2).

call: Firstborn of Hezron (ancestor of the Jerahmeelite clan)
introduce: Jerahmeel is the firstborn of Hezron of the tribe of Judah, a great-grandson of Judah and a grandson of Perez (1 Chronicles 2:5, 2:9, 2:25). In 1 Samuel 27:10 "the Negev of the Jerahmeelites" is mentioned, and this is understood to refer to the clan of his descendants.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2:9) and is Hezron's firstborn (1 Chronicles 2:25). He had Ram the firstborn, and Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah (1 Chronicles 2:25), and he had another wife, Atarah, who was the mother of Onam (1 Chronicles 2:26).
event: When David dwelt in Ziklag, in the country of the Philistines (1 Samuel 27:6-7), and Achish asked whom he had raided, David answered, "the Negev of Judah, the Negev of the Jerahmeelites, and the Negev of the Kenites" (1 Samuel 27:10). But the text records that the ones David actually raided were the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites (1 Samuel 27:8-9).

introduce: Jeremai is a man belonging to the descendants of Hashum among the people of Israel who returned to Jerusalem after finishing the life of Babylonian captivity. (Ezra 10:33)
lifetime: Jeremai is a descendant of Hashum, and his name was recorded when Ezra drew up in Jerusalem the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives. (Ezra 10:33)
