event: Jeremai is one of the men included in the list in accordance with the covenant led by Ezra to send away the foreign women and their children. (Ezra 10:33)

introduce: Jeremoth is a man recorded in 1 Chronicles, one of the sons of Becher who appear in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: Jeremoth is recorded as one of the sons of Becher. All the sons of Becher were heads of their families and mighty men of valor (1 Chronicles 7:8-9).
event: Jeremoth is recorded together with the sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth (1 Chronicles 7:8), and they were all heads of their families and mighty men of valor, and when their descendants were counted by genealogy they numbered twenty thousand two hundred (1 Chronicles 7:9).
character: In the biblical record there is no specific description of any particular deeds or character that he personally showed (1 Chronicles 7:8).

call: First king of the northern kingdom of Israel (son of Nebat)
introduce: Jeroboam the son of Nebat was the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel in the era of the divided kingdom, a man who after Solomon's death led the rebellion of the tribes of Israel and divided the kingdom.
lifetime: He was from the tribe of Ephraim and a superintendent of Solomon's building works, but after hearing the prophecy of the prophet Ahijah he plotted a rebellion and fled to Egypt (1 Kings 11:26-40). After Solomon's death he returned and was acclaimed king by the northern tribes at Shechem and took the throne, and thus came to rule the northern kingdom of Israel, separated from the south, Judah (1 Kings 12:1-20). After becoming king he set up golden calf images at Bethel and Dan and secured religious centers, and he died after reigning twenty-two years (1 Kings 14:20).
event: To keep the people of Israel from going down to the temple in Jerusalem, he set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan and called them the gods of Israel (1 Kings 12:28-29). He appointed priests from among the ordinary people who were not Levites and established his own festivals, thereby setting up a national religious system distinct from the faith system centered on the temple (1 Kings 12:31-33). Also he built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there, and from there went out and built Penuel (1 Kings 12:25).
character: Fearing that his authority would be threatened by the temple system of Judah in the south, he showed a cool, pragmatic side that put political survival first (1 Kings 12:26-27). Despite the warning of the prophet Ahijah, he held firmly to the religious policy he had devised, taking a very resolute attitude in political decisions (1 Kings 14:7-16). After his death his house was ceaselessly cited in the history of Israel as the benchmark of a negative judgment because of the political and religious policies he carried out (1 Kings 15:30).

직업/직위: first king of Israel (northern kingdom; son of Nebat)

introduce: Jeroham is a man who appears in 1 Samuel 1:1, the father of Elkanah, who was the father of the prophet Samuel, and corresponds to Samuel's paternal grandfather (1 Samuel 1:1, 1 Chronicles 6:34). 1 Samuel 1:1 calls Elkanah an Ephraimite, and 1 Chronicles 6 records his genealogy among the descendants of Kohath of the tribe of Levi.
lifetime: Jeroham is the son of Elihu, the grandson of Tohu, and the great-grandson of Zuph (1 Samuel 1:1). His son Elkanah lived in Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim (1 Samuel 1:1), and 1 Chronicles 6:34 records that Samuel was the son of Elkanah and Elkanah was the son of Jeroham. Accordingly, Jeroham is Samuel's grandfather.
character: Within the biblical record there is no description of Jeroham's character or specific activities, and his name is only mentioned as a person who makes up the genealogy of Samuel (1 Samuel 1:1).

introduce: Jerusha is the mother of Jotham king of Judah. Since Jotham is the son of Uzziah (2 Kings 15:32), she is understood to be the wife of Uzziah, and her father is Zadok (2 Kings 15:33, 2 Chronicles 27:1).
lifetime: Jerusha was born as the daughter of Zadok and married Uzziah king of Judah (2 Kings 15:33, 2 Chronicles 27:1). She is recorded as the mother of Jotham, who afterward became king (2 Kings 15:33, 2 Chronicles 27:1).

introduce: Jericho is recorded as the name of a person among the people of Israel who returned to Jerusalem through the decree of Cyrus king of Persia after the Babylonian exile. In the genealogical records of Ezra and Nehemiah it appears as a name indicating the group name of the returnees, their ancestor, or the regional identity of the place where they lived.
lifetime: The descendants of Jericho were included in the company of returnees who were released from Babylonian captivity and came back to Jerusalem and Judah with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:1-2, 2:34). Nehemiah found the genealogical register of those who had first returned, and in that record too the descendants of Jericho are recorded (Nehemiah 7:5-6, 7:36).
event: The descendants of Jericho appear in the lists of Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7 with a total of 345 people (Ezra 2:34). In the genealogical register of Nehemiah 7 as well they are recorded as the same 345, from which it can be seen that they were included as members of the returned community in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 7:36).

call: Son of Bela (head of a Benjamite clan)
introduce: Jerimoth is a figure in 1 Chronicles, a son of Bela of the tribe of Benjamin and one of the heads of the family.
lifetime: Jerimoth is recorded as a son of Bela, the son of Benjamin; all five sons of Bela were heads of their fathers' house and mighty men of valor (1 Chronicles 7:7).
event: Jerimoth was one of the five sons of Bela, namely Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri, who were all heads of their fathers' house and mighty men of valor, and who numbered 22,034 when enrolled by genealogy (1 Chronicles 7:7).
character: The Bible does not state anything specific about his personal character, but since his name is entered in the genealogy together with the mighty warriors of Benjamin, it can be seen that he held considerable military and social standing within the tribe (1 Chronicles 7:7).

introduce: Jeribai is a man recorded among David's mighty men, the members of David's military organization (1 Chronicles 11:46).
lifetime: Jeribai is recorded as a son of Elnaam and is included in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:46). The Bible contains no specific record of his birth or personal life beyond this.
event: Apart from the fact that his name is entered in the list of mighty men gathered to strengthen the authority of King David and to consolidate the kingdom, there is no record of any specific military achievement or particular event involving him (1 Chronicles 11:46).

introduce: Jeriah is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles, mentioned as one of the descendants of Hebron of the tribe of Levi in the time of David.
lifetime: Jeriah is recorded as the chief of the sons of Hebron and a head of the family (1 Chronicles 23:19, 24:23). In the fortieth year of David's reign, he is said to have become head of the Hebronites according to their genealogy and families (1 Chronicles 26:31).
event: In the fortieth year of David's reign, mighty men of valor were found at Jazer in Gilead among the Hebronites, of the family of Jeriah (1 Chronicles 26:31). Among his brothers 2,700 were men of valor and heads of families, and King David put them in charge of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king (1 Chronicles 26:31-32).
character: According to the Bible, Jeriah and his kinsmen were regarded as valiant and capable men, and they were trusted by King David and carried out weighty administrative and military duties (1 Chronicles 26:31-32).

introduce: Jeriel is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 7:2 and is recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Issachar. He was a son of Tola and a member of the house of Tola, one of the heads of Tola's house.
lifetime: Jeriel was a son of Tola, the son of Issachar, and is mentioned in the genealogy of Tola's house (1 Chronicles 7:1-2). The Bible does not record specific information about his life, such as his birthplace, residence, or death.
event: The sons of Tola, Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, were all heads of their father Tola's house, mighty men of valor throughout their generations, and in the days of David their number reached 22,600 (1 Chronicles 7:2).

introduce: Jerioth is a woman whose name appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah; Caleb the son of Hezron is recorded as having had sons by his wife Azubah and by Jerioth (1 Chronicles 2:18).
lifetime: Jerioth appears in the genealogy of Caleb the son of Hezron. The text records that Caleb had sons by his wife Azubah and by Jerioth (1 Chronicles 2:18), and that after Azubah died Caleb married Ephrath (1 Chronicles 2:19). Jerioth's parentage and her exact relationship to Caleb are not stated in the text.
event: The sons whom Caleb had by Azubah and Jerioth are Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon (1 Chronicles 2:18). The text does not say who the mother of each of these three sons was.

introduce: Jemuel is a son of Simeon, one of the descendants of Jacob, and appears in the early genealogy of the tribe of Simeon.
lifetime: Jemuel is recorded as one of the six sons of Simeon (Genesis 46:10). His name is included among the sons of Israel who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household (Genesis 46:8-10).

introduce: Jemimah is recorded as the first of the three daughters Job received again after his trials had ended. The Hebrew name Jemimah carries the meaning of a dove.
lifetime: She was born after Job had overcome all his suffering and been blessed again by God. Job named the children he had the second time, and he called the name of the first daughter Jemimah (Job 42:13, 14).
event: After Job was blessed in his later years more than at the beginning (Job 42:12), their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers (Job 42:15).
character: The Bible records that she and her sisters were the most beautiful of all the women in the land (Job 42:15).

introduce: Jeberekiah is a figure from the time of King Ahaz of Judah, a name mentioned in the period when the prophet Isaiah was active. He is recorded as the father of a man named Zechariah.
lifetime: Jeberekiah is understood to have lived in the time of King Ahaz of Judah, contemporary with the prophet Isaiah, and no deeds of his own are recorded in the Bible. His son Zechariah is named in Isaiah 8:2 as one of the 'faithful witnesses.'
event: The LORD told Isaiah to take a large tablet and write on it in common characters, 'Maher-shalal-hash-baz' (Isaiah 8:1), and said that He would call faithful witnesses to attest it: Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberekiah (Isaiah 8:2).

introduce: Jephunneh is a figure in the Old Testament, the father of Caleb, and is classed as a Kenizzite. According to the biblical record his lineage is connected with the tribe of Judah, but various theories exist concerning the origin of the name Kenizzite.
lifetime: Jephunneh is mentioned as the father of Caleb, who was one of the spies sent to Canaan (Numbers 13:6). He is called a Kenizzite in connection with the Israelites' passage through the wilderness after they came out of Egypt (Numbers 32:12). The Bible has no specific record of his birth or death.
event: There is no record of any direct activity of Jephunneh, but his name is mentioned along with his son Caleb in connection with Caleb's fulfilling the mission of spying out Canaan. When Moses sent out from the wilderness of Paran a man from each tribe, every one a leader, to spy out the land of Canaan, Caleb the son of Jephunneh was the one from the tribe of Judah (Numbers 13:2-6). Later Caleb came to Joshua at Gilgal and spoke, identifying himself as Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite (Joshua 14:6), and Joshua gave Hebron to Caleb the son of Jephunneh as an inheritance (Joshua 14:13-14).

introduce: In the Korean Revised Version (Gaeyeok Hangeul) of Jeremiah, 'Jezaniah' appears in two places. One is Jezaniah the son of the Maacathite, who with the commanders of the forces in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah (Jeremiah 40:7-8). The other is Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, who came to Jeremiah with the commanders of the forces and Johanan the son of Kareah (Jeremiah 42:1). It is not clear from the text whether the two accounts refer to the same man.
lifetime: Jezaniah the son of the Maacathite went to Mizpah to Gedaliah together with Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, Johanan, Jonathan, Seraiah, and others (Jeremiah 40:8). Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah came to Jeremiah together with Johanan the son of Kareah, all the commanders of the forces, and all the people from the least to the greatest (Jeremiah 42:1).
event: Jezaniah the son of the Maacathite went with his men to Mizpah to Gedaliah (Jeremiah 40:8). Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, together with the commanders of the forces, Johanan, and the people, came to Jeremiah the prophet and asked him to pray to the LORD his God for all the remnant, that the LORD might show them the way they should go and the thing they should do (Jeremiah 42:1-3).
character: Jezaniah of the Rechabites is portrayed as a man who followed his family's tradition of strictly keeping the commands of his ancestor (Jeremiah 35:5). Jezaniah the son of Shaphan appears as one of the leaders who led or went along with the religious corruption of Israel (Ezekiel 8:11). Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah is a man who, in the midst of Judah's political turmoil, weighed his survival and where to go, and exercised military leadership (Jeremiah 42:1).

introduce: Jeshaiah is a figure of the royal line of Judah after the Babylonian exile, included in the genealogy descending from the house of David. According to the Chronicles record, he is mentioned as the grandson of Zerubbabel and the son of Hananiah.
lifetime: Jeshaiah is recorded as the son of Hananiah, the son of Zerubbabel, and is listed in David's genealogy together with Pelatiah, the son of Hananiah (1 Chronicles 3:19, 3:21). The biblical text does not state specific details of his life, such as his birthplace or the time of his activity.

introduce: Jeshohaiah was a man of the tribe of Simeon, one of the men in the list of the descendants of Simeon recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:36.
lifetime: Jeshohaiah is recorded in the list of the descendants of Simeon together with Elioenai, Jaakobah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, and Benaiah (1 Chronicles 4:36), and it is said that all those listed above were heads of their families (1 Chronicles 4:38). He is mentioned in the list connected with the descendants of Simeon who obtained pasture and settled in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:34-41).
event: Together with the other heads of families he went to the entrance of Gedor, to the east side of the valley, seeking pasture for their flocks (1 Chronicles 4:39). That was land where the descendants of Ham had lived from of old (1 Chronicles 4:40). Those listed above, in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, attacked their tents, destroyed the Meunites who were found there, and settled in their place (1 Chronicles 4:41).

introduce: Jesimiel is one of the figures who appear in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon recorded in 1 Chronicles 4, and is included in the list of leading men of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:36).
lifetime: Jesimiel is recorded in the list of the descendants of Simeon together with Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, and Benaiah (1 Chronicles 4:36), and it is said that all those listed above were heads of their families (1 Chronicles 4:38).
event: Together with those listed above, in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, he went and destroyed the tents of the people there, struck down the Meunites, destroyed them completely, and settled in their place (1 Chronicles 4:41).

introduce: Jeshishai is a figure in 1 Chronicles 5, a member of a family belonging to the genealogy of the descendants of Gad.
lifetime: In the genealogy of the descendants of Gad, Jeshishai is recorded as an ancestor five generations before Abihail. 1 Chronicles 5:14 records Abihail as the son of Huri, the son of Jaroah, the son of Gilead, the son of Michael, the son of Jeshishai, the son of Jahdo, the son of Buz (1 Chronicles 5:14).

기타관계: Abihail#3939(kinsman of the tribe of Gad)

introduce: Jeziel is of the tribe of Benjamin and a kinsman of Saul, and is one of the mighty men who joined David while he stayed at Ziklag.
lifetime: Jeziel is classed as a Benjamite, of Saul's tribe (1 Chronicles 12:2), and is recorded as a son of Azmaveth (1 Chronicles 12:3). His name is recorded among the mighty men who came to David and helped him in battle while he was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul the son of Kish (1 Chronicles 12:1-3).
event: He took part as one of the mighty men who came to help David when he lived at Ziklag to escape Saul (1 Chronicles 12:3). He is mentioned in the list together with those who were skilled at shooting arrows and at hurling stones or shooting arrows with either the right hand or the left (1 Chronicles 12:2).

introduce: He is a descendant of Levi and of Gershom, and appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Levi in 1 Chronicles 6.
lifetime: Jeatherai is a descendant of Gershom and is recorded as the son of Zerah. The genealogy continues through Gershom's line of Libni, Jahath, Zimmah, Joah, Iddo, and Zerah down to Jeatherai (1 Chronicles 6:20-21).

introduce: Jeush is one of the three sons born to Esau, the ancestor of Edom, by his wife Oholibamah, and appears in Esau's genealogy.
lifetime: Jeush was born to Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, and his brothers were Jalam and Korah (Genesis 36:18). He is recorded as one of Esau's sons born in the land of Canaan (Genesis 36:5).
character: The Bible states nothing about Jeush's character or individual traits; he is mentioned only as a son of Esau included among the chiefs in the family line of the Edomites (Genesis 36:18).

call: Descendant of Zerah of the tribe of Judah
introduce: Jeuel was a descendant of the tribe of Judah who lived in Jerusalem after returning from exile. He is recorded as a descendant of Zerah.
lifetime: Jeuel is a man recorded among the Zerahites who, having been carried away captive to Babylon, returned and lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:1-3, 9:6).
event: Among the Zerahites who lived in Jerusalem, Jeuel and his 690 brothers were recorded (1 Chronicles 9:6).

call: Head of the tribe of Reuben
introduce: He is a Reubenite mentioned in 1 Chronicles 5, a brother of Beerah, and one of the men who became heads according to their clans and genealogies (1 Chronicles 5:7).
lifetime: In the genealogy of the descendants of Reuben, he is recorded among the brothers of Beerah, together with Zechariah, as a head according to clans and genealogies (1 Chronicles 5:7). Beerah was the leader of the Reubenites, whom Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria carried into exile (1 Chronicles 5:6).
event: His name is recorded together with Zechariah as one who became a head according to clans and genealogies (1 Chronicles 5:7).

call: Descendant of Judah in the line of Caleb
introduce: Jehallelel is a figure in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:16 as the father of Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
lifetime: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel are recorded as the sons of Jehallelel (1 Chronicles 4:16). This verse comes right after 4:15, which records the descendants of Caleb the son of Jephunneh, but the relationship between Jehallelel and Caleb is not stated in the text (1 Chronicles 4:15-16).
character: The Bible contains no description of Jehallelel's personal character or specific traits (1 Chronicles 4:16). However, by being mentioned together with his sons Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel, he shows his position as a member of the family line of Caleb's house in the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:16).

introduce: Jehezkel is a man who held the twentieth place among the priestly families organized in the time of David. As a descendant of Aaron, he is a member of the priestly genealogy (1 Chronicles 24:16).
lifetime: David divided the descendants of Aaron by lot and assigned each their duty of service (1 Chronicles 24:3-5), and Jehezkel is recorded as twentieth in that division (1 Chronicles 24:16).
event: When David divided the descendants of Aaron into twenty-four divisions, Jehezkel was recorded as the twentieth in order (1 Chronicles 24:16).

call: A Levite sent out by Jehoshaphat (teacher of the law)
introduce: He is a Levite who, during the reign of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, was sent at the king's command to go around the cities of Judah and teach the people the book of the law of the LORD.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the Levites who were sent along with the officials, when, in the third year of King Jehoshaphat's reign, he sent his officials to teach in the cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:7-8).
event: Sent out by King Jehoshaphat, he carried out the task of going around the cities of Judah and teaching the people the book of the law of the LORD (2 Chronicles 17:9).

call: Son of Rechab (ancestor of the Rechabites)
introduce: He was the son of Rechab and a man who cooperated with Jehu, king of the northern kingdom of Israel, in purging the worshipers of Baal. He is known as a descendant of the Kenites, and he laid the family foundation of the descendants of Rechab, who kept their own distinctive tradition within Israelite society.
lifetime: As Jehu was leaving, he met Jehonadab the son of Rechab coming to meet him. When Jehu asked whether his heart was right, Jehonadab answered that it was, and after he clasped hands with Jehu he got up into the chariot (2 Kings 10:15). Jehu had him ride in his chariot and brought him to Samaria (2 Kings 10:16-17). Afterward his descendants, the Rechabites, did not drink wine according to the command of Jonadab the son of Rechab (Jeremiah 35:6), did not build houses, and lived in tents all their lives (Jeremiah 35:7-10).
event: When Jehu gathered all the prophets of Baal, all his worshipers, and all his priests (2 Kings 10:19-21), Jehonadab went with Jehu into the house of Baal (2 Kings 10:23). In Jeremiah 35 the Rechabites say that their ancestor Jonadab commanded them not to drink wine, not to build houses, not to sow seed or have vineyards, but to live in tents all their lives, and that they had obeyed as he commanded (Jeremiah 35:6-10).
character: He had a strict character, holding fast to his convictions, and showed resolute decisiveness to the point of supporting Jehu's reforms (2 Kings 10:15). He held conservative values that prized the traditions of a nomadic people, and these traits became the basis on which his descendants for a long time refused a settled way of life and continued to live in tents (Jeremiah 35:7).

call: Father of Jeshua the high priest
introduce: Jehozadak was a son of Seraiah the high priest, and went into exile when the people of Judah were carried away to Babylon (1 Chronicles 6:14-15). His son is recorded as Joshua the high priest in Haggai and Zechariah (Haggai 1:1).
lifetime: Jehozadak is recorded as the son of Seraiah the high priest (1 Chronicles 6:14). When the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, Jehozadak also went to Babylon (1 Chronicles 6:15). The book of Haggai records Joshua the high priest as the son of Jehozadak (Haggai 1:1).
event: Apart from the record of the deportation in 1 Chronicles 6:15, nothing is separately recorded of Jehozadak's own deeds. His son Jeshua appears in Ezra 3:2 as the one who, with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, built the altar of the God of Israel (Ezra 3:2), and in Haggai, called 'Joshua the high priest, the son of Jehozadak,' he obeyed the voice of the LORD together with Zerubbabel and the remnant of the people and did the work (Haggai 1:12-14).

introduce: Jehozabad was one of the servants who killed Joash king of Judah, and is recorded in 2 Kings 12:21 as the son of Shomer. In 2 Chronicles 24:26, Jehozabad the son of Shimrith, a Moabite woman, appears among those who conspired.
lifetime: A servant of Joash king of Judah, he is recorded as one of the servants who struck him down when Joash's servants rose up, conspired, and killed him at the house of Millo, on the road that goes down to Silla (2 Kings 12:20-21). Joash was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and his son Amaziah reigned in his place (2 Kings 12:21).
event: Jozabad the son of Shimeath and Jehozabad the son of Shomer are recorded as the servants who struck down Joash, and this took place at the house of Millo on the road that goes down to Silla (2 Kings 12:20-21). Chronicles records as the conspirators Zabad the son of Shimeath, an Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith, a Moabite woman (2 Chronicles 24:26).

introduce: Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was a man who served as recorder, one of the chief administrative offices of the royal court, during the reign of the Davidic dynasty. He was a high official responsible for keeping and preserving the records of state within the central administration of the kingdom of Israel.
lifetime: He is recorded as recorder in the time of King David (2 Samuel 8:16, 20:24, 1 Chronicles 18:15), and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud is also recorded as recorder in the list of King Solomon's officials (1 Kings 4:3).
event: In King David's time it is recorded that Joab was commander of the army and Adoniram was over the forced labor, and that Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud became recorder (2 Samuel 8:16, 20:24). In King Solomon's time, Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud is recorded as recorder when Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, were secretaries (1 Kings 4:3).

introduce: Jehoshabeath is a woman who appears in 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles, recorded as the daughter of King Jehoram, the sister of Ahaziah, and the wife of Jehoiada the priest. In 2 Kings 11:2 she appears under the name Jehosheba.
lifetime: Jehoshabeath was the daughter of King Jehoram and the sister of Ahaziah (2 Chronicles 22:11). After Ahaziah died, when his mother Athaliah destroyed all the royal offspring (2 Kings 11:1), she stole Joash the son of Ahaziah away from among the king's sons who were being murdered, and hid him with his nurse in a bedroom, so that he was kept from Athaliah (2 Kings 11:2). Joash stayed hidden with her in the house of the LORD for six years (2 Kings 11:3, 2 Chronicles 22:12).
event: She is recorded as the wife of Jehoiada the priest, and she rescued Joash from Athaliah's massacre and hid him so that Athaliah could not kill him (2 Chronicles 22:11). Joash was hidden in the house of the LORD for six years, during which Athaliah ruled the land (2 Kings 11:3); in the seventh year Jehoiada made a covenant with the captains of hundreds and showed them the king's son (2 Kings 11:4).
character: According to the Bible, she was the wife of Jehoiada the high priest and the daughter of King Jehoram, and thus held a twofold standing as a member of both the royal house and a priestly family (2 Chronicles 22:11). In that she protected a child of the royal house and took him to a safe place amid an urgent political purge, she is regarded as a very prudent and courageous person of decisive action (2 Kings 11:2).

call: Eleventh king of the northern kingdom of Israel (son of Jehu)
introduce: He was the eleventh king of the northern kingdom of Israel, a son of Jehu, and the second ruler of the dynasty of Jehu. He reigned over Israel in Samaria for seventeen years (2 Kings 13:1).
lifetime: He succeeded Jehu on the throne (2 Kings 10:35) and reigned seventeen years (2 Kings 13:1). During his reign the LORD gave Israel continually into the hand of Hazael king of Aram and into the hand of Ben-hadad his son (2 Kings 13:3). The king of Aram destroyed the people of Jehoahaz and made them like the dust at threshing, leaving him no more than fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers (2 Kings 13:7).
event: Jehoahaz did evil in the sight of the LORD and followed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel sin; he did not turn from them (2 Kings 13:2). When the king of Aram oppressed Israel, Jehoahaz sought the favor of the LORD and the LORD listened to him (2 Kings 13:4); the LORD gave Israel a deliverer, so that the people of Israel escaped from the hand of the Arameans and lived in their own tents as before (2 Kings 13:5). Nevertheless they did not turn from the sins of the house of Jeroboam but walked in them, and the Asherah pole also remained standing in Samaria (2 Kings 13:6).
character: He is a man who continued idolatry throughout his reign and kept up religious and political compromise (2 Kings 13:2). He sought the LORD in the crisis from outside, but after the crisis had passed he showed no will to change his basic policy or to remove the idols (2 Kings 13:6).

introduce: Jehoaddan is the mother of Amaziah king of Judah, and is recorded as a woman of Jerusalem (2 Kings 14:2, 2 Chronicles 25:1).
lifetime: Jehoaddan was a woman of Jerusalem (2 Kings 14:2) and the mother of Amaziah king of Judah. Amaziah began to reign at the age of twenty-five and reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem (2 Kings 14:2, 2 Chronicles 25:1).
character: The Bible says nothing about her personal character or specific deeds (2 Kings 14:2, 2 Chronicles 25:1).

introduce: Jehoiachin was the nineteenth king of the southern kingdom of Judah, a son of Jehoiakim, also called Jeconiah or Coniah. He was the grandson of Josiah and the son of Jehoiakim (2 Kings 24:6). After reigning three months he was carried away captive to Babylon, and the king of Babylon made his uncle Mattaniah king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:8, 24:15, 24:17).
lifetime: He began to reign at the age of eighteen and reigned three months in Jerusalem (2 Kings 24:8). When the king of Babylon was at Jerusalem, he went out to the king of Babylon with his mother, his servants, his officials, and his eunuchs, and was taken prisoner (2 Kings 24:12). He was carried away captive to Babylon (2 Kings 24:15), and in the thirty-seventh year of his captivity, in the first year of the reign of Evil-merodach king of Babylon, he was released from prison and his head was lifted up (2 Kings 25:27). Evil-merodach spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the thrones of all the kings who were with him in Babylon; he changed his prison garments, and Jehoiachin ate regularly before the king all the days of his life (2 Kings 25:28-29).
event: The king of Babylon carried off all the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the royal palace, and cut in pieces all the gold vessels of the house of the LORD that Solomon had made (2 Kings 24:13). All the people of Jerusalem, all the officials, and all the mighty men of valor, ten thousand captives in all, together with the craftsmen and the smiths, were carried away, and seven thousand men of valor and a thousand craftsmen and smiths were also taken captive to Babylon (2 Kings 24:14-16).
character: According to the Bible, his conduct was judged to be evil in the sight of the LORD (2 Kings 24:9). Concerning his fate, Jeremiah prophesied that he would be recorded as childless and that none of his offspring would sit on the throne (Jeremiah 22:30). During the Babylonian exile he carried political and symbolic significance, still being regarded among the captives as the king of Judah (2 Kings 25:27).

introduce: He was the eighteenth king of the southern kingdom of Judah. His original name was Eliakim, but Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt renamed him Jehoiakim. He was the second son of King Josiah, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
lifetime: Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in place of his father Josiah and changed his name to Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:34). In his time Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and he served him three years and then turned and rebelled against him (2 Kings 24:1). The LORD sent against Jehoiakim bands of the Chaldeans, the Arameans, the Moabites, and the Ammonites to destroy Judah (2 Kings 24:2). Chronicles records that Nebuchadnezzar came up and bound him with chains to take him to Babylon (2 Chronicles 36:6), while Kings records that he slept with his fathers and that his son Jehoiachin reigned in his place (2 Kings 24:6).
event: As Pharaoh Neco commanded, he taxed the land in order to give him the silver and the gold, and he exacted the silver and the gold from the people of the land, each according to his assessment (2 Kings 23:35). When Jehudi read the scroll that Baruch had written from Jeremiah's dictation (Jeremiah 36:4), the king cut it off with a penknife piece by piece, and threw it into the fire in the firepot until the whole scroll was consumed (Jeremiah 36:23). Nebuchadnezzar brought some of the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon and put them in his temple (2 Chronicles 36:7).
character: He refused the words of the prophets who prophesied against him and showed a stubbornness that destroyed their message (Jeremiah 36:23). He ruled oppressively, as when he made the people work unjustly in order to build his palace and luxurious houses (Jeremiah 22:13-14). In his diplomatic relations with outside powers he took the political course of breaking faith and rebelling (2 Kings 24:1).

call: Father of Benaiah (leader of the line of Aaron)
introduce: Jehoiada is a man recorded as the father of Benaiah in the time of David. 1 Chronicles 27:5 records him as Jehoiada the chief priest, and 2 Samuel 23:20 introduces Benaiah as the son of Jehoiada, the grandson of a valiant man of Kabzeel.
lifetime: In 2 Samuel 8:18, 23:20, 1 Kings 1:8, 1 Chronicles 18:17, and 27:5, Jehoiada appears only in the phrase introducing his son Benaiah, and no deeds of his own are recorded in the text. In 1 Chronicles 27:5 he is called 'Jehoiada the chief priest.'
event: His son Benaiah was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites (2 Samuel 8:18) and was the third commander of the army for the third month, with 24,000 men in his division (1 Chronicles 27:5). This is a record about his son Benaiah, and nothing is recorded as an event of Jehoiada himself.
character: He is portrayed as a commander who acted with trust within David's royal military system, and as a man who combined the religious standing of a descendant of Aaron with military leadership (1 Chronicles 27:5).

introduce: Jehoiarib is a man of a priestly family who appears in the Old Testament, recorded as the one on whom the first lot fell when the priestly divisions were organized in the time of David (1 Chronicles 24:7).
lifetime: When King David divided the descendants of Aaron and assigned their duties, Jehoiarib is recorded as the one on whom the first lot fell (1 Chronicles 24:3-7). In recording those who returned from captivity in Babylon and lived in Jerusalem, 1 Chronicles 9 lists among the priests Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin (1 Chronicles 9:1-3, 9:10).
event: David, together with Zadok of the descendants of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the descendants of Ithamar, divided the descendants of Aaron and assigned each their duty of service (1 Chronicles 24:3), and Shemaiah the scribe recorded their names; the first lot fell to Jehoiarib and the second to Jedaiah (1 Chronicles 24:6-7).

call: Son of Meshelemiah (gatekeeper of the temple)
introduce: Jehohanan is a figure in 1 Chronicles, the sixth son of Meshelemiah, of a family of gatekeepers among the Korahites.
lifetime: Jehohanan is recorded as the sixth son of Meshelemiah, the son of Kore, of the Korahites, of the descendants of Asaph (1 Chronicles 26:1-3). His name is recorded in the divisions of the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:1), and lots were cast for every gate, small and great alike, according to their families (1 Chronicles 26:13).
event: In the divisions of the gatekeepers, Jehohanan is recorded as a son of Meshelemiah (1 Chronicles 26:1-3). The heads of the gatekeepers cast lots for each gate according to their families (1 Chronicles 26:12-13), and 1 Chronicles 26:14 records that the lot for the east fell to Shelemiah and that for the north to his son Zechariah. The gate assigned to Jehohanan is not recorded in the text.

introduce: Jehudi is a man who was active in the time of Jehoiakim king of Judah, an official of the king who was involved in the process of reading the scroll that Jeremiah had dictated.
lifetime: Jehudi was the son of Nethaniah, the grandson of Shelemiah, and the great-grandson of Cushi (Jeremiah 36:14). He is mentioned as one of the servants of Jehoiakim king of Judah (Jeremiah 36:21).
event: When the officials heard from Micaiah the words of the scroll (Jeremiah 36:11-13), they sent Jehudi the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, to Baruch, telling him to bring the scroll that he had read in the hearing of the people (Jeremiah 36:14). It was Baruch who read the scroll in the hearing of the princes (Jeremiah 36:15). Afterward the king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and Jehudi took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe and read it in the hearing of the king and of all the princes standing beside the king (Jeremiah 36:21). It was the ninth month, and the king was sitting in the winter house with a fire burning in the firepot before him (Jeremiah 36:22). When Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king would cut them off with a penknife and throw them into the fire in the firepot, until the whole scroll was consumed (Jeremiah 36:23).

introduce: She is mentioned as a woman of the tribe of Judah and is recorded as the wife of Ezrah (1 Chronicles 4:18).
lifetime: She bore to Ezrah Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel (1 Chronicles 4:18).

introduce: He appears in 2 Chronicles 29:14 and is a Levite of the descendants of Heman who took part in the cleansing of the temple in the time of King Hezekiah.
lifetime: Jehiel was a Levite, one of the descendants of Heman, and is recorded as one of the Levites who arose to cleanse the temple in the time of King Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 29:12-14).
event: When King Hezekiah commanded that the temple be consecrated, Jehiel is recorded, together with Shimei, as a Levite who arose from the descendants of Heman; they gathered their brothers, consecrated themselves, and cleansed the house of the LORD in keeping with the command of the king and the words of the LORD (2 Chronicles 29:14-15).

introduce: Jehizkiah is one of the chiefs of the sons of Ephraim, a leader who was active in the time of the northern kingdom of Israel (2 Chronicles 28:12).
lifetime: In the time of Ahaz king of Judah, Pekah king of Israel killed many in Judah and carried many captives to Samaria (2 Chronicles 28:5-8); Jehizkiah is recorded as one of several chiefs of the sons of Ephraim who stood against those coming from the war (2 Chronicles 28:12).
event: When Oded, a prophet of the LORD, met the army returning to Samaria and told them to send the captives back (2 Chronicles 28:9-11), Jehizkiah the son of Shallum rose up together with Azariah the son of Johanan, Berechiah the son of Meshillemoth, and Amasa the son of Hadlai, and stood against those coming from the war (2 Chronicles 28:12). These men took the captives and from the plunder clothed all who were naked, gave them sandals, fed them and gave them drink, and anointed them; and they put all the feeble on donkeys and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brothers (2 Chronicles 28:15).

introduce: Jehiah is a figure in 1 Chronicles, a Levite who served as a gatekeeper in the process of moving the ark of God in the time of King David.
lifetime: Jehiah is recorded as one of those who guarded the gate before the ark of God (1 Chronicles 15:24). The Bible has no other record of his family or life.
event: When David moved the ark of God, Jehiah is recorded, together with Obed-edom, as one who guarded the gate before the ark (1 Chronicles 15:24).

call: Son of Ladan (head of the Gershonites, in charge of the temple treasures)
introduce: Jehiel is a Levite chief recorded as a son of Ladan the Gershonite (1 Chronicles 23:7-8). When David gathered offerings for the building of the temple, those who had precious stones entrusted them to Jehiel the Gershonite and brought them to the treasury of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 29:8).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 23:8 records, 'The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, and Zetham and Joel—three in all.' 1 Chronicles 26:21-22 says that the chief belonging to Ladan the Gershonite was 'Jehieli' and that his sons Zetham and Joel were in charge of the treasury of the house of the LORD, so they appear to be of the same family.
event: In David's time, when the people willingly gave offerings for the temple, those who had precious stones entrusted them to the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite and brought them to the treasury of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 29:8).

introduce: Jehieli is a figure in 1 Chronicles, recorded as a head of the house belonging to Ladan the Gershonite (1 Chronicles 26:21). His sons were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:22).
lifetime: Jehieli is recorded as a head belonging to Ladan the Gershonite (1 Chronicles 26:21), and his sons were Zetham and his brother Joel (1 Chronicles 26:22). The Bible has no other record concerning his birth, death, and so on.
event: Jehieli's sons Zetham and his brother Joel were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:22). No deeds of Jehieli himself are recorded in the Bible.
character: The Bible says nothing about his personal character or specific traits. It records only that he was a descendant of Ladan and that his family held the duty of managing the treasuries of the temple (1 Chronicles 26:21).

introduce: Jethro is recorded as the priest of Midian and the father of Zipporah, the wife of Moses (Exodus 3:1; 18:1-2). In Exodus 2:18 he appears under the name Reuel, and in Numbers 10:29 he is also called 'Reuel the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses.' In Exodus 4:18 Moses tells his father-in-law Jethro that he will return. He was the head of the household that invited Moses and gave him food when Moses fled from Egypt to Midian, and he was also Moses' father-in-law (Exodus 2:20).
lifetime: He lived in the land of Midian as a priest who had seven daughters (Exodus 2:16). Since Moses was willing to dwell with him, he gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses (Exodus 2:21). Later, when Moses said he would return to Egypt, he let him go in peace (Exodus 4:18), and after the exodus Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, came to Moses in the wilderness with Moses' sons and his wife (Exodus 18:5). In Numbers 10:29-31 there is a scene in which Moses asks Hobab the son of Reuel the Midianite to go with them as a guide in the wilderness.
event: When the people of Israel were in the wilderness, Moses' father-in-law saw Moses judging the people alone from morning till evening (Exodus 18:13-14), told him that this was not good, and advised him to appoint able and capable men as officers over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens to judge the people at all times (Exodus 18:17-23). Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he had said (Exodus 18:24).
character: Although he was a priest of a foreign nation, he took an interest in Moses' work and in the God of Israel and acknowledged His power (Exodus 18:11). He is regarded as a man of insight and practical administrative ability, able to observe another's excessive burden of work and propose an efficient system of management (Exodus 18:17-18).

introduce: Jehdeiah is a descendant of Levi, recorded as the son of Shubael, the son of Amram (1 Chronicles 24:20).
lifetime: In the list recording the duties of the descendants of Levi in the time of David, he is recorded, among 'the rest of the sons of Levi,' as the son of Shubael, the son of Amram (1 Chronicles 24:20). The Bible has no other record about his life.
event: The Bible records no deeds of Jehdeiah himself, and he is mentioned only as a son of Shubael (1 Chronicles 24:20).

introduce: Jerah is a descendant of Shem, the son of Noah, and a son of Joktan, the son of Eber (Genesis 10:24-26). He belongs to the Semitic genealogy and is classified, from a genealogical point of view, as one of the descendants of Shem (1 Chronicles 1:20).
lifetime: Jerah is recorded as a son of Joktan (Genesis 10:26), and his name is included in the genealogical list made up of the descendants of Shem (1 Chronicles 1:20). The Bible contains no specific chronological record concerning his birth, death, or period of activity (Genesis 10:26, 1 Chronicles 1:20).

introduce: Jeremiah of Libnah was the father of Hamutal, who was the wife of Josiah king of Judah and the mother of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah (2 Kings 23:31, 24:18).
lifetime: Jeremiah of Libnah entered into a blood relationship with the royal house when his daughter Hamutal married Josiah king of Judah (2 Kings 23:31, 2 Kings 24:18). Through Hamutal he became the maternal grandfather of two kings, Jehoahaz and Zedekiah.
event: No specific political activity or public record of his is written in the Bible; it is only recorded that Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, was the mother of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah (2 Kings 23:31, 2 Kings 24:18).

introduce: Jered is a figure in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a son born to Jehudijah and recorded as the father of Gedor (1 Chronicles 4:18).
lifetime: Jered is recorded as one of the three sons born to Jehudijah (Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel), and the Bible has no record of any other matter, such as the time of his birth or his deeds after death (1 Chronicles 4:18).
event: Jered is recorded as the father of Gedor (1 Chronicles 4:18). This verse records no children or deeds of Jered himself.

introduce: Jeshebeab is the head of the fourteenth division among the twenty-four divisions determined by lot to carry out priestly duties in the time of David (1 Chronicles 24:13).
lifetime: King David cast lots in order to organize the temple service centering on the families of Eleazar and Ithamar, the descendants of Aaron the priest, and Jeshebeab is explicitly named as the head of the family recorded fourteenth at that time (1 Chronicles 24:13).
event: When David determined the order of duties in the temple, Jeshebeab was recorded by lot as the one responsible for leading the fourteenth division (1 Chronicles 24:13).

call: Third son of Naphtali (ancestor of the Jezerite clan)
introduce: Jezer is the third son of Naphtali, the son of Jacob, and is recorded as a grandson of Bilhah (Genesis 46:24-25, 1 Chronicles 7:13). He is one of the ancestors who make up the family line of the tribe of Naphtali, one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Naphtali, the son of Jacob (Genesis 46:24), and in the list of the clans of the descendants of Naphtali in Numbers 26 his name appears as 'of Jezer, the Jezerite family' (Numbers 26:49).
event: The Jezerite family, descended from Jezer, is recorded in Numbers as one of the clans of the descendants of Naphtali (Numbers 26:49). In Chronicles he is mentioned as one of the sons of Naphtali and said to be a grandson of Bilhah (1 Chronicles 7:13).

call: Jesus Christ (the Messiah who became flesh)
meaning: the one who will save his people; Savior
introduce: Jesus is a figure who continues the genealogical line as a descendant of David and a descendant of Abraham, and is portrayed as the one who became flesh and dwelt among people (Matthew 1:1, John 1:14). He was named as the one who will save his people from their sins (Matthew 1:21).
lifetime: The angel Gabriel appeared to Mary, a virgin betrothed to Joseph, a descendant of David, announced that she would bear a son, and instructed her to name him Jesus (Luke 1:26-31). Mary conceived by the Holy Spirit (Matthew 1:18-20), and he was born in Bethlehem in Judea in the days of Herod the king (Matthew 2:1); the Word became flesh and dwelt among us (John 1:14).
event: He is recorded as the one who fulfills the covenantal genealogy that runs from David and Abraham (Matthew 1:1). He was given the identity of the Savior who will save his people from their sins (Matthew 1:21).

introduce: Jeshua is a figure in 1 Chronicles, a man of a priestly family belonging to the ninth of the twenty-four divisions assigned by lot to carry out priestly duties in the time of King David.
lifetime: When David, together with Zadok of the descendants of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the descendants of Ithamar, divided the duties of the descendants of the priests (1 Chronicles 24:3), Jeshua was recorded ninth in the list of divisions (1 Chronicles 24:11).
event: In order to organize the duties of the priests, King David divided the descendants of Eleazar and Ithamar and cast lots (1 Chronicles 24:3-5), and at that time Jeshua's name was entered in the list as the ninth division (1 Chronicles 24:11).

introduce: Jezrahiah is one of those who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, and appears in the record of Nehemiah 12 as the overseer of the singers (Nehemiah 12:42).
lifetime: When the wall of Jerusalem was completed and the dedication was held (Nehemiah 12:27), he is recorded as the overseer of the singers (Nehemiah 12:42). The Bible has no record of his specific birth, death, or family background.
event: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem the singers sang loudly, and their overseer was Jezrahiah (Nehemiah 12:42). Apart from this event, no other biblical deeds of his, nor any involvement in a particular event, can be confirmed.

introduce: Jehu the son of Hanani was a prophet active in the time of Baasha king of the northern kingdom of Israel and of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, who carried out the role of delivering to the kings the message of judgment entrusted to him by God (1 Kings 16:1, 2 Chronicles 19:2).
lifetime: He delivered the word of the LORD in the time of Baasha king of the northern kingdom of Israel (1 Kings 16:1-4) and in the time of Jehoshaphat king of Judah (2 Chronicles 19:2, 2 Chronicles 20:34). To King Baasha he prophesied the destruction of his house (1 Kings 16:1-4), and when King Jehoshaphat returned in safety to Jerusalem, he went out to meet him and rebuked him for helping the wicked (2 Chronicles 19:1-2). The acts of Jehoshaphat, from beginning to end, were written in his record, which was entered in the Book of the Kings of Israel (2 Chronicles 20:34).
event: He pointed out that Baasha had walked in the way of Jeroboam and provoked God to anger, and prophesied the judgment that his house would become like the house of Jeroboam (1 Kings 16:2-3). Also, when King Jehoshaphat returned in safety to Jerusalem, he met him and rebuked him, saying that it was not right to help the wicked and to love those who hate the LORD, and made known that the wrath of the LORD would come upon the king (2 Chronicles 19:1-2). The acts of Jehoshaphat from beginning to end were all written in his record, and that record was entered in the Book of the Kings of Israel (2 Chronicles 20:34).
character: He showed an upright attitude, delivering God's message without flinching even before rulers (2 Chronicles 19:2). In pointing out the faults of kings, he maintained an objective attitude, putting the authority of the written prophecy ahead of personal feeling (1 Kings 16:1-4).

introduce: Ocran is a man recorded in the book of Numbers as the father of Pagiel, a chief of the descendants of Asher (Numbers 1:13).
lifetime: In Numbers, Ocran appears only as the father of Pagiel, born of Asher (Numbers 1:13, 2:27), and there is no record of his birth or life. It was his son Pagiel who led the army in the arrangement of the encampment and in the march of the tribe of Asher (Numbers 2:27, 10:26).
event: No deeds of Ocran himself are recorded in the Bible. At the dedication of the tabernacle, it was Pagiel the son of Ocran who, as chief of the descendants of Asher, presented the offering (Numbers 7:72, 7:77).

introduce: Onan was the second son of Judah and the younger brother of Er, a figure connected with the ancient Israelite custom of levirate marriage.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Judah (Genesis 38:4), and after his brother Er died, at the command of his father Judah he was required to go in to his brother's wife Tamar and carry out a levirate marriage in order to continue his brother's line (Genesis 38:8).
event: Knowing that the offspring would not be his own, whenever he went in to her he spilled his seed on the ground so as not to give offspring to his brother (Genesis 38:9). Because what he did was evil in the sight of the LORD, he too was put to death (Genesis 38:10).
character: He showed a tendency to evade family custom and duty when he judged that it would not benefit himself, and as a result he ended his life by refusing the duty of levirate marriage (Genesis 38:9-10).

introduce: Onam was a member of the Horite people who lived in the land of Edom, a descendant of Shobal the son of Seir, and is recorded as one of the descendants of Seir.
lifetime: He is recorded as a child of Shobal, a descendant of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36:23). The descendants of Seir, to whom Shobal belonged, were the Horites, the original inhabitants of that land, and they lived in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:20-21).
character: The Bible gives no information about his personal character or specific traits (Genesis 36:23).

introduce: Onesimus is a figure in the New Testament letter to Philemon, a slave belonging to Philemon (Philemon 1:16). While he was away from his master, he was called by the imprisoned Paul 'my son, whom I have begotten in my chains' (Philemon 1:10, 1:15), and Paul is the one who sends him back to his master (Philemon 1:12). Colossians 4:9 introduces him as 'one of you.'
lifetime: He was originally a slave belonging to Philemon but was separated from him for a while (Philemon 1:15-16). He was called by Paul, who was in prison, 'my son, whom I have begotten in my chains' (Philemon 1:10), and when Paul sent him back to Philemon he urged him to receive him no longer as a slave but as more than a slave, a beloved brother (Philemon 1:12, 1:16). In Colossians, Paul sends Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, together with Tychicus, so that they might make known all about Paul's affairs (Colossians 4:7-9).
event: Paul called Onesimus his very heart and wanted to keep him with himself to serve him on his behalf in his imprisonment for the gospel, but he sent him back, saying that he would do nothing without Philemon's consent (Philemon 1:12-14). He also asked Philemon to welcome him as he would welcome Paul himself (Philemon 1:17). Onesimus was sent with Tychicus and was given the task of informing the Colossians about the state of affairs where Paul was (Colossians 4:7-9).
character: Paul had formed with him a relationship of trust, to the point of calling him his very heart (Philemon 1:12). He was once useless to his master, but after meeting Paul he is regarded as having changed into one who is useful to both his master and Paul (Philemon 1:11). Paul also called him a beloved brother (Colossians 4:9).

introduce: Onesiphorus is a figure in the New Testament letter of 2 Timothy, a Christian who often refreshed the apostle Paul when he was in prison, was not ashamed of his chains, and diligently searched for Paul in Rome and found him (2 Timothy 1:16-17).
lifetime: Onesiphorus often refreshed Paul and was not ashamed of Paul's chains (2 Timothy 1:16); when he was in Rome he diligently searched for Paul and found him (2 Timothy 1:17). He also rendered much service to Paul at Ephesus (2 Timothy 1:18). Paul asked that the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus (2 Timothy 1:16) and told Timothy to greet his household (2 Timothy 4:19).
event: When Paul was in chains, Onesiphorus was not ashamed of it and often refreshed Paul (2 Timothy 1:16). When he was in Rome he diligently searched for Paul and found him (2 Timothy 1:17). Paul said that how much he served him at Ephesus Timothy knew very well (2 Timothy 1:18).
character: He was a man of courage, who went out to look for the imprisoned Paul without fearing the harm that might come to himself (2 Timothy 1:16). He was not ashamed of Paul's situation and showed compassion (2 Timothy 1:16), and he showed a diligent and devoted attitude, such that Paul remembered him (2 Timothy 1:17).

introduce: He was the father of the prophet Azariah, who was active in the time of Asa king of Judah, and a man of a prophetic family.
lifetime: According to the biblical record he is introduced as the father of the prophet Azariah (2 Chronicles 15:1), and no specific chronology of his birth or period of activity is given.
event: The prophet Azariah is mentioned as the son of Oded (2 Chronicles 15:1), and it is recorded that King Asa, hearing 'the prophecy of Oded the prophet,' took courage, removed the abominable idols, and repaired the altar of the LORD (2 Chronicles 15:8). No words of Oded himself nor any other specific deeds are recorded in the Bible.
character: Since the biblical record mentions him only to show the paternal line when introducing his son Azariah, there are no materials from which his personal character or specific traits can be determined (2 Chronicles 15:8).

introduce: Othni is a figure in 1 Chronicles, a descendant of Obed-edom in the divisions of the gatekeepers of the tribe of Levi in the time of King David, recorded as a son of Shemaiah (1 Chronicles 26:4-8).
lifetime: Othni is recorded as a son of Shemaiah (1 Chronicles 26:7), and Shemaiah was the firstborn of Obed-edom (1 Chronicles 26:4). As a descendant of Obed-edom he was a man included in the divisions of the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:1, 26:8, 26:12).
event: Othni is recorded as a son of Shemaiah together with his brothers Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad (1 Chronicles 26:7). All the descendants of Obed-edom were men of ability, fit for the work of the service (1 Chronicles 26:8).
character: The Bible describes Othni and his brothers as men of outstanding ability who were able to carry out their duties well (1 Chronicles 26:7).

introduce: Oren is a man of the house of Hezron in the tribe of Judah, one of the sons of Jerahmeel.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2:25). Hezron was a son of Perez, the son of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:4-5).
event: No specific deeds or particular events concerning Oren appear in the biblical record; his name is entered as a son of Jerahmeel only in the course of listing the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:25).

기타관계: Hezron#3248(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: Oreb is a prince of Midian who appears in the time of the book of Judges in the Old Testament. Judges records him, together with Zeeb, as one of the two princes of Midian.
lifetime: The men of Ephraim, who were called out by Gideon, seized the fords as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan (Judges 7:24), and they captured the two princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb, and killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb (Judges 7:25). Later Gideon said that God had given the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb, into the hands of the men of Ephraim (Judges 8:3).
event: Oreb, one of the two princes of Midian, was captured by the men of Ephraim and killed at the rock of Oreb (Judges 7:25). The men of Ephraim brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon across the Jordan (Judges 7:25). The psalmist asked that the nobles of the enemy might be made like Oreb and Zeeb (Psalms 83:11).

introduce: A woman from the region of Moab, she was the wife of Chilion, a son of Elimelech and Naomi who had moved from Bethlehem. She appears in the Bible as the sister-in-law of Ruth and a daughter-in-law of Naomi.
lifetime: She married Naomi's son Chilion in the land of Moab and started a household, but became a widow when her husband died (Ruth 1:4-5). When her mother-in-law Naomi decided to return to her homeland of Bethlehem, she set out with her mother-in-law toward the land of Judah, but along the way resolved to return to Moab and bade her farewell (Ruth 1:7-14).
event: Despite Naomi's discouragement she tried to go with her mother-in-law to Bethlehem, but after Naomi's repeated urging she kissed her and returned to her own people and her gods (Ruth 1:14-15).
character: She was a person of loyalty and filial devotion who respected and loved her mother-in-law Naomi and tried to accompany her to the end (Ruth 1:10). Torn between the practical difficulty of leaving her homeland and family and adapting to a new environment, and her mother-in-law's counsel, she chose in the end to return to her own original society (Ruth 1:14-15).

introduce: He is a chief of the land of Edom, recorded as a descendant of Esau. He is one of the figures who appear when the genealogy of Esau is set out in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.
lifetime: Esau was the ancestor of Edom, and by his wife Adah he fathered Eliphaz, and Eliphaz had several children, including Omar (Genesis 36:10-11). Omar, a grandson of Esau and a son of Eliphaz, entered his name in the line of chiefs of the Edomite people (1 Chronicles 1:35-36).
event: His name is entered in the list of the chiefs of the Edomite people (Genesis 36:15).

call: Sixth king of the northern kingdom of Israel
introduce: He was the sixth king of the northern kingdom of Israel, and had been a commander of the army. When the Israelites in the camp heard that Zimri had conspired and had struck down the king, they made him king (1 Kings 16:16), and he bought the hill of Samaria and built a city on it (1 Kings 16:24).
lifetime: While serving as commander of the army of Israel, he was acclaimed king by the Israelites in the camp (1 Kings 16:16). Afterward he went up from Gibbethon with all Israel and besieged Tirzah, and Zimri set the king's house on fire over himself and died (1 Kings 16:17-18). Then the people of Israel were divided into two parts, half following Tibni the son of Ginath and half following Omri; the people who followed Omri prevailed over those who followed Tibni, and when Tibni died, Omri became king (1 Kings 16:21-22). He reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah (1 Kings 16:23). He built a city on the hill of Samaria (1 Kings 16:24), and after he died he was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab reigned in his place (1 Kings 16:28).
event: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver and built a city on the hill, and named the city Samaria after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill (1 Kings 16:24). He did evil in the sight of the LORD, more than all who were before him, and walked in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat (1 Kings 16:25-26). In later times a prophet rebuked the keeping of the statutes of Omri (Micah 6:16).
character: He was judged to have done evil, and to have committed greater evil in the sight of the LORD than all the kings before him (1 Kings 16:25). Through the course called the way of Omri, he became a standard of negative rule for later kings as well (Micah 6:16). He is portrayed as a man of outstanding military ability and political skill who, in the religious sphere, did not follow Israel's traditional system of faith (1 Kings 16:26).

meaning: servant of Edom; one who serves
introduce: Obed-edom was a Gittite. After Uzzah died in the time of David, David did not take the ark to the City of David but had it carried aside to his house, and so he was the man who kept the ark of God in his house for three months (2 Samuel 6:10-11).
lifetime: When Uzzah took hold of the ark of God and died (2 Samuel 6:6-7), David was unwilling to take the ark of the LORD into the City of David, and had it carried aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite (2 Samuel 6:10). The ark remained in his house three months (2 Samuel 6:11), and afterward David brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom to the City of David with rejoicing (2 Samuel 6:12).
event: While the ark was in his house, the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household (2 Samuel 6:11; 1 Chronicles 13:14). When this was told to David, David went and brought up the ark from the house of Obed-edom to the City of David (2 Samuel 6:12).
character: He was a man bold enough to take the ark of God into his own house even in the midst of fear (2 Samuel 6:10). Some regard him as the same person as the Levite gatekeeper Obed-edom of 1 Chronicles 15–26, but the text does not say so.

call: Son of Boaz and Ruth (grandfather of David)
introduce: Obed was the son born to Boaz and Ruth the Moabitess, the father of Jesse and the grandfather of King David. The name Obed carries the meaning 'one who serves.'
lifetime: He was born through the marriage of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:13). He was born through Ruth, the daughter-in-law of Naomi, and became Naomi's grandson (Ruth 4:17). He fathered Jesse, and Jesse was the father of David (Ruth 4:17, 4:21, 4:22). In the genealogies of the New Testament he is mentioned as an ancestor of Jesus Christ (Matthew 1:5, Luke 3:32).
event: The women who were Naomi's neighbors said that a son had been born to Naomi and gave him the name Obed (Ruth 4:17). The women of Bethlehem said that this child would be a restorer of life to Naomi and a nourisher of her old age (Ruth 4:15), and Naomi took the child and laid him in her lap and became his nurse (Ruth 4:16).

introduce: Ophrah is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 4:14, recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah as a son fathered by Meonothai (1 Chronicles 4:14).
lifetime: Ophrah is identified as a son of Meonothai in the genealogical record that says 'Meonothai fathered Ophrah' (1 Chronicles 4:14). The Bible has no other record about his personal life.
event: No special achievement or historical event performed by Ophrah personally is recorded in the Bible; only the genealogical information that he was a son of Meonothai is given (1 Chronicles 4:14).

introduce: Ozem is a figure in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded in 1 Chronicles 2 as the sixth son of Jesse (1 Chronicles 2:13-15).
lifetime: Ozem was born as a son of Jesse, and his father Jesse was also the father of David (1 Chronicles 2:13, 1 Chronicles 2:15). He is recorded as a member of a family of the tribe of Judah, but the Bible has no specific record of his personal life after his birth or of the time of his death (1 Chronicles 2:15).

introduce: Ashurbanipal is a figure who appears in Ezra 4:10 as 'the great and noble Ashurbanipal.' The text records that he settled people in the city of Samaria and in the rest of the region Beyond the River.
lifetime: In Ezra 4, in the letter reported by Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe and their associates, the name of 'the great and noble Ashurbanipal' appears, and the text says that he settled people in the city of Samaria and in the rest of the region Beyond the River (Ezra 4:9-10). The Bible has no other record about his life.
event: Ashurbanipal is mentioned as the one who settled people in the city of Samaria and in the rest of the region Beyond the River (Ezra 4:10). No other personal deeds of his are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Ohad is one of the sons of Simeon, a grandson of Jacob, and a member of the house of Simeon, which makes up one of the tribes of Israel.
lifetime: Ohad was born as a son of Simeon (Genesis 46:10). He is included in the list of Jacob's descendants at the time Jacob migrated to Egypt (Genesis 46:10). He is also mentioned as a son of Simeon in the record of Exodus that lists the genealogy of Simeon (Exodus 6:15).

introduce: He is a figure whose name appears in the listing of the sons of Zerubbabel, belonging to the family line of Zerubbabel, a descendant of David (1 Chronicles 3:19-20).
lifetime: His name appears in 1 Chronicles 3:19-20 where, after Zerubbabel's sons Meshullam, Hananiah, and Shelomith, five men are listed: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-hesed (1 Chronicles 3:19-20).
character: According to the biblical record, he is one of the persons included in the genealogical list of Judah after the return from the Babylonian exile (1 Chronicles 3:20).

call: Daughter of Anah (third wife of Esau)
introduce: Oholibamah is the daughter of Anah and is recorded as a wife of Esau. She was a wife whom Esau took from among the women of Canaan, and she bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
lifetime: She was the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite (Genesis 36:2, 36:14). She married Esau and bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah (Genesis 36:5). As one of the wives whom Esau took from among the women of Canaan, her name is entered in the record of Esau's descendants (Genesis 36:14).
event: Her children Jeush, Jalam, and Korah are recorded as chiefs among the descendants of Esau (Genesis 36:18). When Esau took his wives and children and went away from his brother Jacob, she was one of those wives who went with him (Genesis 36:6), and Esau lived in the hill country of Seir (Genesis 36:8).

introduce: Oholiab was a man who took part in building the tabernacle in the time of the exodus, a son of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan (Exodus 31:6). He was a skilled engraver and an embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarns and fine linen (Exodus 38:23).
lifetime: He was from the tribe of Dan, a son of Ahisamach, and together with Bezalel of the tribe of Judah he was appointed to make what the LORD had commanded Moses (Exodus 31:2, 31:6). The LORD stirred him and Bezalel to teach, and filled them with skill, so that they did the work of engraving, embroidering, and many other kinds of work (Exodus 35:34-35).
event: Oholiab is named together with Bezalel among those whom the LORD had endowed with wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work for the sanctuary (Exodus 36:1), and his name appears together with Bezalel again when Moses called the skilled men whose hearts were stirred to come and do the work (Exodus 36:2). He was with Bezalel, and was a skilled engraver and an embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarns and fine linen (Exodus 38:22-23).
character: He is portrayed as a man who possessed not only technical skill but also the ability to teach (Exodus 35:34). He showed outstanding talent in engraving, in craftsmanship, and in fine embroidery, and cooperated with many artisans to complete the project of making the tabernacle (Exodus 35:35).

introduce: Og was the last Amorite king of Bashan, and according to the biblical record he was one of the remnant of the Rephaim, the race of giants. He was a ruler who governed a vast territory east of the Jordan.
lifetime: Og, as king of Bashan, lived at Ashtaroth (Deuteronomy 1:4). When Israel went up the way to Bashan, he came out with all his people to fight at Edrei, but he was defeated and killed (Numbers 21:33-35; Deuteronomy 3:1-3). His land was afterward given to the half-tribe of Manasseh (Deuteronomy 3:13; Joshua 13:30-31).
event: He was a king who ruled sixty fortified cities east of the Jordan (Deuteronomy 3:4). In the battle with Israel, Og went out to Edrei with all his army but was killed (Numbers 21:33-35). His iron bedstead, nine cubits long and four cubits wide, was of enormous size, and was afterward kept at Rabbah (Deuteronomy 3:11).
character: Og was a man of exceedingly large and massive physique, so that he is described as the last remaining one of the Rephaim of Bashan (Deuteronomy 3:11). He exercised military influence enough to rule great cities (Deuteronomy 3:4), and he showed a resistant side in leading his army in person to oppose Israel's advance (Numbers 21:33).

introduce: Olympas is one of those greeted at the end of the letter to the Romans by the apostle Paul, a Christian who belonged to the church in Rome.
lifetime: He is mentioned when Paul sends greetings near the end of his letter to the church in Rome (Romans 16:15). He is recorded as one to be greeted together with Philologus, Julia, Nereus and his sister, and 'all the saints who are with them' (Romans 16:15).
event: His name is on the list of greetings in Romans 16 (Romans 16:15). No special ministry performed by Olympas, nor any particular event, is recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Othniel is recorded as the first judge of Israel, a son of Kenaz of the tribe of Judah and a younger brother of Caleb. When Israel was oppressed by neighboring nations, he was a leader upon whom the Spirit of God came, who delivered Israel and maintained peace for forty years.
lifetime: He is mentioned as a son of Kenaz of the tribe of Judah and a younger brother of Caleb (Judges 1:13). By striking and taking Kiriath-sepher (Debir), he took Caleb's daughter Acsah as his wife (Judges 1:11-13). Later, when Israel, which had been serving Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia, cried out to the LORD, he became the deliverer whom the LORD raised up (Judges 3:8-9). During the time he acted as judge the land had rest for forty years, and then Othniel the son of Kenaz died (Judges 3:11).
event: In accordance with Caleb's word that he would give his daughter Acsah as wife to the one who struck and took Kiriath-sepher, he took that city (Judges 1:12-13). The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he became a judge of Israel and went out to war, and he prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia (Judges 3:10). After that the land had rest for forty years (Judges 3:11).
character: The Spirit of God came upon him, and because of this he became a judge of Israel and went out to war (Judges 3:10). He showed courage in conquering Kiriath-sepher and was trusted as a member of the house of Caleb (Judges 1:13). The Bible portrays him as one who delivered Israel and records that peace continued during his rule (Judges 3:11).

introduce: Vaniah is one of the descendants of Bani whose marriage to a foreign woman came to light in Jerusalem, after the return from the Babylonian exile, during the religious reform of Ezra (Ezra 10:36).
lifetime: Among the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian exile he is classified as a descendant of Bani, and his name was entered in the penitential movement led by Ezra to send away the foreign wives and their children (Ezra 10:36).
event: He is included in the list of those found to have married foreign women, and nothing further appears about him beyond the event recorded in that list, such as taking part in the measure that followed (Ezra 10:36).

introduce: Vashti was queen to Xerxes, king of the Persian Empire, and appears at the beginning of the book of Esther. She is recorded as one who was deposed because she refused the king's command.
lifetime: Vashti, as queen of King Xerxes, gave a feast for the women in the royal palace (Esther 1:9) when in the third year of his reign the king gave a feast for his officials and servants (Esther 1:3). The king commanded that she be brought wearing her royal crown to show her beauty to the peoples and the officials, but she refused to come (Esther 1:11-12). By this she incurred the king's anger, and finally a decree was issued that she should never again come before the king, and her royal position was to be given to another (Esther 1:19-21).
event: During the king's feast she held a separate feast for the women alone (Esther 1:9). When King Xerxes tried to show off her beauty by having her come before the king wearing the royal crown, she refused (Esther 1:11-12). Because of this refusal, the king's advisers feared that women throughout Persia would come to despise their husbands, and the king decided that she should never again come before him and that her position be given to another (Esther 1:16-19).
character: Following her own conviction, she showed the resolve to firmly refuse the king's authoritative demand (Esther 1:12). In the male-centered culture of the Persian court of the time, she appears to have had an independent will, so much that she placed her own judgment above the king's command (Esther 1:12).

introduce: Vaizatha is one of the ten sons of Haman, a member of Haman's family in the Persian Empire under King Xerxes (Esther 9:9).
lifetime: As one of the ten sons of Haman (Esther 9:7-10), he was killed with his brothers in the citadel of Susa when the Jews struck down their enemies (Esther 9:6-10).
event: In the citadel of Susa the Jews killed the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews, but did not lay a hand on their plunder (Esther 9:10). At Esther's request the king granted that the bodies of the ten sons of Haman be hanged on the gallows (Esther 9:13-14).

introduce: Jochebed was from the tribe of Levi, the wife of Amram, and the mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. She was born a daughter of Levi and was a figure active in the age before the exodus of ancient Israel.
lifetime: Born as a daughter of Levi, she married Amram (Exodus 6:20; Numbers 26:59). By Amram she bore Aaron and Moses and their sister Miriam (Numbers 26:59). When Pharaoh commanded that every boy be thrown into the river (Exodus 1:22), a woman of Levi bore a son and hid him for three months (Exodus 2:1-2).
event: When she could hide Moses no longer, she took a basket made of bulrushes, daubed it with bitumen and pitch, put the child in it, and placed it among the reeds by the bank of the river (Exodus 2:3). Moses' sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him (Exodus 2:4), and Pharaoh's daughter came down to the river and found the basket (Exodus 2:5-6). When the sister offered to call a nurse and called the child's mother, Pharaoh's daughter told her to take the child and nurse him for her, and the mother took the child and nursed him (Exodus 2:7-9).

introduce: Jogli is a man recorded in Numbers 34:22 as the father of Bukki, a leader of the tribe of the descendants of Dan. The leader of the tribe of Dan who was chosen for the dividing of the land of Canaan was his son Bukki.
lifetime: Numbers 34:22 says, 'Bukki son of Jogli, a leader from the tribe of Dan;', and thus introduces Jogli only as the father of Bukki. No deeds of Jogli himself are recorded in the Bible.
event: No event performed by Jogli personally is recorded in the Bible. When Israel divided the land of inheritance, one leader was chosen from each tribe (Numbers 34:18), and from the tribe of the descendants of Dan, Bukki the son of Jogli was chosen (Numbers 34:22).

introduce: Jokim is a man whose name appears in 1 Chronicles 4:22, recorded in the enumeration of the descendants of Shelah the son of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:21-22).
lifetime: In the enumeration of the descendants of Shelah the son of Judah, his name appears in the phrase 'Jokim, the men of Cozeba, Joash, the one who ruled in Moab, and Jashubi-lehem,' and the text says that these rest on ancient records (1 Chronicles 4:21-22). No specific record of his life, such as when he was born or died, has been left.
event: 1 Chronicles 4:23 records that all these were potters who lived among plantations and hedges, dwelling there with the king and doing the king's work. No separate event concerning Jokim himself is recorded.

introduce: He is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus recorded in the Gospel of Luke, mentioned as the son of Eliakim and the father of Joseph.
lifetime: Jonam, recorded as a descendant of David, is the son of Eliakim and the father of Joseph (Luke 3:30).
event: In the biblical record no specific achievement or event of his appears (Luke 3:30).

introduce: Joda is one of the figures in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in Luke 3, recorded as the son of Joanan and the father of Josech (Luke 3:26-27).
