lifetime: In the genealogy of Luke, Joda is recorded as the son of Joanan and the father of Josech (Luke 3:26-27). This genealogy comes down through Nathan the son of David (Luke 3:31), and there is no other record of his life.

introduce: Jotham is a man recorded as a son of Jahdai, one of the families of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:47).
lifetime: As a son of Jahdai, his name is entered in the genealogical line of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:47).
event: From the biblical record no specific achievement of Jotham or information about any particular event can be confirmed (1 Chronicles 2:47).

call: Youngest son of Gideon (the parable of Mount Gerizim)
introduce: Jotham is the youngest son of Gideon the judge. When Abimelech killed his seventy brothers, he hid himself and was the only one left, and he is recorded as having warned Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem through a parable from the top of Mount Gerizim (Judges 9:5, 9:7).
lifetime: After Gideon died, when Abimelech killed his brothers, Jotham hid and escaped the calamity (Judges 9:5). Afterward he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and delivered a warning to Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem by means of a parable (Judges 9:7). After finishing his speech he fled from Abimelech to Beer and lived there (Judges 9:21).
event: From the top of Mount Gerizim he told the parable of the trees that went out to anoint a king over them (Judges 9:8-15), and said to the leaders of Shechem, who had made Abimelech king, that fire would come out from Abimelech and consume the leaders of Shechem, and that fire would come out from the leaders of Shechem and consume Abimelech (Judges 9:16-20). Afterward God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech (Judges 9:23); Abimelech was killed when a woman threw an upper millstone on him (Judges 9:53-54), and the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal came upon them (Judges 9:57).
character: Even in the crisis of his brothers being slaughtered, he showed the ability to cope by calmly escaping to Mount Gerizim (Judges 9:5). He is portrayed as a man with the eloquence and courage to criticize his opponents logically through a parable before a large crowd (Judges 9:7-20).

call: Son of Toi king of Hamath (tribute to David)
introduce: Joram is a son of Toi king of Hamath (Tou in Chronicles), and appears as one who, sent by his father in the time of David, went to greet King David (2 Samuel 8:10).
lifetime: Toi, the father of Joram, heard that David had struck down the whole army of Hadadezer (2 Samuel 8:9), and sent his son Joram to greet King David and bless him. This was because Hadadezer had been at war with Toi, and David had struck down Hadadezer (2 Samuel 8:10). The Chronicles record spells the father Tou and the son Hadoram (1 Chronicles 18:9-10).
event: Joram came to King David bringing articles of silver, gold, and bronze (2 Samuel 8:10). King David dedicated these also to the LORD, together with the silver and gold he had taken from all the nations he had subdued (2 Samuel 8:11-12).

introduce: Jorai is a man recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Gad as one of the sons of Abihail (1 Chronicles 5:13-14).
lifetime: Jorai is one of the seven men Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber, all of whom are recorded as sons of Abihail (1 Chronicles 5:13-14). The descendants of Gad lived in the land of Bashan (1 Chronicles 5:11).

introduce: Jorkeam is a figure classified in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah as a descendant of Caleb, the son of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2:44). He is included in the family tree that mentions the descendants of Hebron (1 Chronicles 2:43-44).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 2:44 records that Shema fathered Raham, and Raham was the father of Jorkeam. Shema was a son of Hebron (1 Chronicles 2:43), and Hebron was a son of Mareshah, the son of Caleb (1 Chronicles 2:42).

기타관계: Caleb#243(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: Jorim is a figure in the genealogy of Jesus in the New Testament Gospel of Luke, recorded as the son of Matthat and the father of Eliezer (Luke 3:29).
lifetime: Jorim is recorded in the genealogy of Luke as the son of Matthat, and the generation below him is Eliezer (Luke 3:29). He is classified as a man belonging to the line of Nathan the son of David (Luke 3:31).

introduce: Jobab is a figure recorded in Genesis and Chronicles, one of the thirteen sons fathered by Joktan, the son of Eber, a descendant of Shem the son of Noah. He is recorded in the genealogy of Shem together with the other sons of Joktan (Genesis 10:26-29).
lifetime: Jobab is recorded as a son of Joktan (Genesis 10:29). As a descendant of Eber his name is entered in the genealogy of Shem, and the place where the sons of Joktan lived was the hill country of the east on the way from Mesha toward Sephar (Genesis 10:30). The author of Chronicles likewise records Jobab, a son of Joktan, in the course of listing the descendants of Shem (1 Chronicles 1:23).
event: No independent activity of Jobab himself or any particular historical event is recorded in the Bible. He is recorded in the genealogy of Shem only as one of the sons of Joktan (Genesis 10:26-29).

introduce: Joshah is one of the chiefs of the tribe of Simeon, whose name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:34 (1 Chronicles 4:34).
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of the chiefs of the tribe of Simeon and as a son of Amasiah (1 Chronicles 4:34, 4:38). In the time of King Hezekiah he is recorded among those listed above who came to the border of Gedor, on the east side of the valley, and found pasture (1 Chronicles 4:39, 4:41).
event: With his family he took part in a military and pioneering undertaking: on the east of the border of Gedor they found wide and good land to feed their flocks, struck down the people who lived there, and took possession of the land (1 Chronicles 4:39, 4:41).

introduce: Jozabad is recorded as one of the servants who struck down and killed Joash king of Judah. He appears in 2 Kings 12:21 as the son of Shimeath, and 2 Chronicles 24:26 records as those who conspired against Joash Zabad the son of Shimeath, an Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith, a Moabite woman.
lifetime: Jozabad was the son of Shimeath and a man who joined the conspiracy that killed King Joash (2 Kings 12:21). Apart from the fact that he took part in the rebellion to strike down Joash king of Judah, the Bible leaves no particular record of his birth or later life (2 Kings 12:21).
event: As the son of Shimeath, Jozabad was one of the servants who struck down and killed King Joash (2 Kings 12:21). The servants of Joash conspired and killed him at the house of Millo, on the road that goes down to Silla (2 Kings 12:20). Joash was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and his son Amaziah reigned in his place (2 Kings 12:21).

introduce: Jozabad is one of the mighty men of the tribe of Benjamin who came to help David when he stayed at Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:1).
lifetime: He came to Ziklag to follow David, from the tribe of Benjamin, the kinsmen of Saul (1 Chronicles 12:2). He is recorded as one of the men of the tribe of Benjamin who gathered to help David in the time when he was fleeing from Saul (1 Chronicles 12:4).
event: When David was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul the son of Kish, Jozabad the Gederathite is recorded among the mighty men who came to him to help in battle (1 Chronicles 12:1, 12:4). His name was entered in the list that introduces him as a kinsman of Saul from the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 12:2, 12:4).

introduce: Joshaviah is a man mentioned among David's mighty men, the military organization of David (1 Chronicles 11:46).
lifetime: During the reign of David, he entered his name in the list as one of the mighty men who assisted David and carried out his military undertakings (1 Chronicles 11:46).
event: As a military comrade and mighty man of King David, he was included in the list of David's army recorded in 1 Chronicles 11 (1 Chronicles 11:46).

introduce: Joses is a figure in the New Testament Gospel of Mark who is mentioned only as the son of Mary, one of the women who watched the crucifixion of Jesus from a distance. His name appears in the expression 'Mary the mother of Joses' (Mark 15:40, 15:47).
lifetime: Mark 15:40 introduces Joses as Mary's son by speaking of 'Mary the mother of James the Less and of Joses.' The Bible has no record of Joses' own birth or life.
event: No deeds of Joses himself are recorded in the Bible. His mother Mary was among the women who watched the crucifixion of Jesus from a distance (Mark 15:40), and together with Mary Magdalene she saw where Jesus was laid (Mark 15:47).

introduce: Josech is a figure in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke, a male ancestor of Israel recorded as the son of Joda and the father of Semein (Luke 3:26).
lifetime: Josech is mentioned as the son of Joda in the genealogy of Jesus that runs from Luke 3:23 to 3:38 (Luke 3:26). As the father of Semein, he stands in a middle generation in the genealogy (Luke 3:26).

call: Son of Jacob (prime minister of Egypt)
introduce: He was the son born to Jacob and Rachel and the origin of the tribe of Joseph among the tribes of Israel. He was sold from Canaan to Egypt, began in the status of a slave, and rose to become prime minister of Egypt.
lifetime: He was a son whom Jacob had in his old age, wore a robe of many colors, and received his father's special love (Genesis 37:3). Because of his brothers' jealousy he was sold, through Midianite merchants, to the Ishmaelites for twenty shekels of silver and went to Egypt (Genesis 37:28), where he came to live in the house of Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard (Genesis 37:36, 39:1). He was falsely accused by Potiphar's wife and put in prison (Genesis 39:20), but when he stood before Pharaoh at the age of thirty, he was made ruler over all the land of Egypt by Pharaoh (Genesis 41:41, 41:46). Afterward, as Pharaoh commanded, he gave his father and brothers the best of the land of Egypt, the land of Rameses, as a possession (Genesis 47:11), and he died at the age of 110 (Genesis 50:26).
event: He interpreted Pharaoh's dream as one dream and declared that seven years of plenty would be followed by seven years of famine (Genesis 41:25-32). During the seven years of plenty he gathered grain and stored it in the cities (Genesis 41:48-49), and when the famine came he opened all the storehouses and sold to the Egyptians, and the people of every land also came to Joseph to buy grain (Genesis 41:56-57). During the famine he bought all the land of Egypt and gave it to Pharaoh, so that the land became Pharaoh's (Genesis 47:20). To the brothers who had sold him into Egypt he said not to be distressed, saying that God had sent him, and he had his father and household come down to him (Genesis 45:4-11).
character: He had outstanding insight in interpreting dreams and analyzing future circumstances (Genesis 41:15-16). He showed the cool temperament of an administrator who is not shaken even in a crisis (Genesis 41:33-36), and he strove to maintain personal morality, as when he firmly refused the advances of Potiphar's wife (Genesis 39:8-9). In the process of reuniting with his family he also showed a strategic side, hiding his identity and testing them (Genesis 42:7-24), but in the end he revealed a strong emotional bond with his own flesh and blood (Genesis 45:1-2).

introduce: Josheb-basshebeth is mentioned as one of David's mighty men, the military organization of David. He is recorded as a Tahchemonite and served as a military leader during David's reign.
lifetime: Among David's mighty men he is also called Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite or Adino the Eznite, and is recorded as the chief of the captains (2 Samuel 23:8). 1 Chronicles 11:11 gives Jashobeam, the son of a Hachmonite, as the chief of the thirty (1 Chronicles 11:11).
event: He killed eight hundred men at one time (2 Samuel 23:8). In 1 Chronicles 11:11, which appears to be a parallel record, Jashobeam is said to have lifted up his spear and killed three hundred at one time, so there is a difference in the number (1 Chronicles 11:11).
character: He was called a Tahchemonite, and was regarded as a man with the most outstanding martial strength among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:8). He has the character of a representative warrior who symbolized David's military power on the front line of battle (1 Chronicles 11:11).

introduce: Joshbekashah is a man belonging to the line of Heman among the descendants of Levi, one of the members of the choir organized to carry out the ministry of praise in the temple in the reign of King David (1 Chronicles 25:4).
lifetime: Joshbekashah is one of the fourteen sons of Heman (1 Chronicles 25:4-5). The sons of Heman were under the direction of their father, and served by singing in the house of the LORD God with cymbals, harps, and lyres (1 Chronicles 25:6). When lots were cast for the duties, the seventeenth fell to Joshbekashah, his sons, and his brothers, twelve in number (1 Chronicles 25:8, 25:24).
event: In the time of David, when those who served by singing obtained their duties by lot (1 Chronicles 25:1, 25:8), the seventeenth duty fell to Joshbekashah (1 Chronicles 25:24).

introduce: Josiphiah is recorded as the father of one of the descendants of Shelomith in the list of heads of families who came up from Babylon with Ezra (Ezra 8:1, 8:10).
lifetime: Ezra 8:10 records that from the descendants of Shelomith, 'the son of Josiphiah' came up with 160 men who were with him. Josiphiah is mentioned only as the father of this son, whose name is omitted, and there is no record concerning Josiphiah himself.
event: The Bible records no deeds of Josiphiah himself (Ezra 8:10).

introduce: Joshibiah is a figure in 1 Chronicles, recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon as the grandson of Seraiah and the father of Jehu (1 Chronicles 4:35).
lifetime: Joshibiah is recorded as a grandson of Seraiah, and his son Jehu is entered in the list of the chiefs of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:35, 4:38).
event: The Bible records no deeds of Joshibiah himself. But the men in the list in which his son Jehu is recorded came, in the time of Hezekiah, to the border of Gedor on the east side of the valley, found pasture, struck down and utterly destroyed the Meunites who were there, and lived there in their place (1 Chronicles 4:39-41).

call: Sixteenth king of the southern kingdom of Judah
meaning: the LORD is salvation; He heals
introduce: He was the sixteenth king of the southern kingdom of Judah, who came to the throne at the age of eight and ruled thirty-one years. He succeeded his father, King Amon, and is regarded as one who walked in the way of David and did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
lifetime: Josiah came to the throne at the age of eight and reigned in Jerusalem thirty-one years (2 Kings 22:1). In the eighth year of his reign he began to seek the God of David, and in the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the Asherah poles, the carved images, and the cast images (2 Chronicles 34:3). After a law book was found during the repair of the temple, he carried out religious reform, and in the eighteenth year of his reign he kept the Passover (2 Kings 23:23). Afterward he was killed when he confronted Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt at Megiddo (2 Kings 23:29).
event: During the repair of the temple, Hilkiah the high priest found the book of the law in the house of the LORD (2 Kings 22:8). When Josiah heard the words of the book of the law, he tore his clothes at once (2 Kings 22:11). He read in the hearing of the people all the words of the book of the covenant found in the house of the LORD and made a covenant before the LORD (2 Kings 23:2-3), tore down and burned the altar and the high place at Bethel, and burned the Asherah pole (2 Kings 23:15). He also removed the mediums, the spiritists, the household gods, the idols, and all the abominations that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem (2 Kings 23:24). When Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the river Euphrates against the king of Assyria, King Josiah went out to meet him and was killed at Megiddo (2 Kings 23:29, 2 Chronicles 35:20-24).
character: Josiah did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, walked in all the way of David, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left (2 Kings 22:2). When he heard the words of the book of the law his heart was tender, and he humbled himself before the LORD, tore his clothes, and wept; because of this God promised him that the disaster would not come in his time (2 Kings 22:19). While overseeing the repair of the temple, he trusted the workmen's faithfulness so much that no accounting was required of them (2 Kings 22:7). It is recorded that there was no king before him, and none after him, who turned to the LORD with all his heart, all his soul, and all his might, according to all the law of Moses, as Josiah did (2 Kings 23:25).

call: Son of Asaph (recorder under King Hezekiah)
introduce: He is recorded as the recorder, the son of Asaph, in the time of King Hezekiah of the kingdom of Judah. When the Rabshakeh sent by the king of Assyria came to Jerusalem and called for the king, he was one of the three, with Eliakim and Shebnah, who went out to him.
lifetime: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up and took the fortified cities of Judah (2 Kings 18:13), and when the Rabshakeh and others sent by the king of Assyria came to Jerusalem with a great army and called for the king, Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebnah the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph, the recorder, went out to him (2 Kings 18:17-18, Isaiah 36:2-3).
event: When the Rabshakeh spoke, Eliakim, Shebnah, and Joah asked the Rabshakeh to speak in Aramaic and not in the language of Judah in the hearing of the people on the wall (2 Kings 18:26). The people were silent, for the king had commanded them not to answer (2 Kings 18:36), and the three men tore their clothes, went to Hezekiah, and told him the words of the Rabshakeh (2 Kings 18:37, Isaiah 36:22).
character: He was an official trusted enough to negotiate directly with the enemy army in place of the king in a national crisis, and one who tried to coolly adjust his diplomatic words according to the king's instructions (2 Kings 18:26). Even under the Assyrian threat he faithfully carried out the king's order to keep silent to the end and held his place (2 Kings 18:36).

introduce: A figure entered in the genealogy of Jesus.
lifetime: Joanan is recorded in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke as the son of Rhesa and the father of Joda, and the father of Rhesa is Zerubbabel (Luke 3:26-27).
event: No deeds of Joanan himself are recorded in the Bible; his name is entered in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke (Luke 3:27).

introduce: Joash is a man born as a son of Becher in a family of the tribe of Benjamin. He is one of the figures who appear in the text of 1 Chronicles that records the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, and is mentioned mainly as a member who makes up the family tree of the descendants of Benjamin.
lifetime: Joash is recorded as one of the sons of Becher (1 Chronicles 7:8). The Bible has no record of his time of birth, his specific period of activity, or his children.
character: The biblical record says nothing about his character or personal traits (1 Chronicles 7:8).

introduce: Joanna is a figure in the Gospel of Luke in the New Testament, the wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, and one of the women disciples who financially supported the earthly ministry of Jesus.
lifetime: She is recorded as the wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, and on the basis of her experience of having been healed of evil spirits and diseases she joined the group of women who followed Jesus (Luke 8:2-3). Afterward, after Jesus had been crucified, at early dawn when the Sabbath was past, she visited the tomb with the other women and prepared spices to treat the body (Luke 24:1, 10).
event: Together with Susanna and many others she served Jesus and his company out of their own means (Luke 8:3). Her name is recorded among the women who went to the tomb at dawn on the first day after the Sabbath with spices (Luke 24:1, 24:10), and they heard the words of the two men in dazzling clothes at the tomb, who said that Jesus had risen (Luke 24:4-7). These women returned and told all these things to the eleven apostles and to all the others, and Joanna is recorded by name among those women (Luke 24:9-10).
character: Although she had the high social standing of being the wife of Herod's steward, she followed Jesus and was a person with such a strong sense of mission that she willingly devoted her own means (Luke 8:3). After being healed she continued to follow Jesus, and she showed a consistent course of conduct that extended to preparing to care for the body after his death and to bearing witness to the resurrection (Luke 8:2, Luke 24:10).

introduce: Joiakim was a priest of the period of the return from exile, a son of Jeshua the high priest, and a man who held an important place in the genealogy of the priestly families.
lifetime: Joiakim is recorded as the son of Jeshua and the father of Eliashib (Nehemiah 12:10). In the days of Joiakim the heads of the priestly families were recorded (Nehemiah 12:12). Also recorded are those who lived in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra the priest and scribe (Nehemiah 12:26).
event: In the days of Joiakim there were heads of priestly families, such as Meraiah for the family of Seraiah and Hananiah for the family of Jeremiah (Nehemiah 12:12). The Bible does not record Joiakim's own deeds separately; he is mentioned among the persons of the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe (Nehemiah 12:26).

introduce: Joiada is the son of Eliashib recorded in the genealogy that continues from Jeshua to Joiakim and Eliashib (Nehemiah 12:10).
lifetime: Joiada was a son of Eliashib and the father of Jonathan (Nehemiah 12:10-11). In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, the heads of the families of the Levites were recorded in the book, and the priests were recorded in the book in the reign of Darius the Persian (Nehemiah 12:22). His line continues to Jonathan and Jaddua (Nehemiah 12:11).
event: One of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, had become a son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite, and so Nehemiah chased him away from himself (Nehemiah 13:28).

introduce: Joiarib is a name recorded in connection with the genealogy of the priestly families; in Nehemiah 11:10 his son Jedaiah appears as one of the priests who lived in Jerusalem, and in Nehemiah 12:19 the family of Joiarib is mentioned.
lifetime: When David, together with Zadok the priest and others, divided the duties of the priests, the one on whom the first lot fell was Jehoiarib (1 Chronicles 24:3-7). In the time of Nehemiah, Jedaiah the son of Joiarib and Jachin are recorded among the priests who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:10).
event: He was recorded as the one first chosen when the divisions of the priests were divided by lot in the time of David (1 Chronicles 24:7). Nehemiah 12:19 records Mattenai as head of the family of Joiarib (Nehemiah 12:19).

introduce: One of David's mighty men, a Korahite of the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of the mighty men who came to help David when he was staying at Ziklag, hiding from the face of Saul (1 Chronicles 12:1-6).
event: He joined David's army and served as one skilled with the bow and able to hurl stones or shoot arrows with either the right hand or the left (1 Chronicles 12:1-2).

introduce: Joel is the eldest son of the prophet Samuel, a descendant of Levi, and a figure active in the transitional period between the time of the judges and the early period of the Israelite monarchy.
lifetime: Joel, a son of Samuel, was appointed judge at Beersheba (1 Samuel 8:2). When his father Samuel was old, his sons took over the office of judge and served (1 Samuel 8:1).
event: Together with his brother Abijah, Joel served as judge at Beersheba, but unlike his father he did not walk uprightly (1 Samuel 8:2-3). He took bribes and perverted justice, and acted dishonestly (1 Samuel 8:3). This conduct became the direct cause of the elders of Israel asking Samuel for a king (1 Samuel 8:4-5).
character: Joel abandoned justice and showed a greedy character that pursued private gain (1 Samuel 8:3). His conduct contrasted with the uprightness of his father Samuel, and he became the figure who supplied the grounds on which the people of Israel demanded the monarchy (1 Samuel 8:3-5).

introduce: Joelah is a figure in 1 Chronicles, a mighty man of the tribe of Benjamin who was active in the time of King David.
lifetime: Joelah was a son of Jeroham, a man of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 12:7). He was one of the mighty men of the tribe of Benjamin who went to David and joined him when David stayed at Ziklag to escape Saul (1 Chronicles 12:1-2).
event: He is recorded as one of the mighty men who came to help in battle when David was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul (1 Chronicles 12:1, 12:7).
character: According to the biblical record, Joelah was a skilled warrior of the tribe of Benjamin who was able to hurl stones or shoot arrows with either the right hand or the left (1 Chronicles 12:2).

introduce: Joed is recorded as the grandfather of Sallu, a descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 11:7).
lifetime: According to Nehemiah 11:7, Sallu was the son of Meshullam, the grandson of Joed, and the great-grandson of Pedaiah, so Joed was the son of Pedaiah and the father of Meshullam. Joed himself has only his name recorded in this genealogy (Nehemiah 11:7).
event: No deeds of Joed himself are recorded, and his grandson Sallu is recorded as a descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:7).

call: Son of Beriah (head of a Benjamite clan)
introduce: Joha is a figure in 1 Chronicles, one of the sons of Beriah recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: Joha was a son of Beriah of the tribe of Benjamin, and his brothers were Michael and Ishpah (1 Chronicles 8:16).
character: The biblical record says nothing about Joha's personal character or any particular action of his (1 Chronicles 8:16).

introduce: Johanan the son of Kareah was one of the commanders of the army of Judah who was active in the time of Gedaliah, the governor appointed by the king of Babylon at the end of the kingdom of Judah. After Ishmael killed Gedaliah, he led the remaining people down to Egypt.
lifetime: He was one of the commanders of the forces in the open country who heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam governor over the land (Jeremiah 40:7-8). He went to Mizpah to Gedaliah (Jeremiah 40:8) and told him that Ishmael was seeking to take his life (Jeremiah 40:13-14). After Ishmael killed Gedaliah, he led the remnant of Judah and set out to go to Egypt (Jeremiah 41:16-17), and he led the prophet Jeremiah and Baruch the son of Neriah as well, and came to Tahpanhes in the land of Egypt (Jeremiah 43:4-7).
event: He told Gedaliah that Ishmael intended to kill him, and secretly asked permission to kill Ishmael without anyone knowing, but Gedaliah did not permit it (Jeremiah 40:13-16). After Ishmael killed Gedaliah and carried off the people, he went with all the commanders of the forces to fight Ishmael and brought back from Gibeon the people he had carried off (Jeremiah 41:11-16). Afterward he asked Jeremiah, together with the people, to pray to the LORD (Jeremiah 42:1-3), but when Jeremiah delivered the word of the LORD not to go to Egypt, he called Jeremiah a liar, and, not obeying the voice of the LORD to remain in the land of Judah, he led all the commanders of the forces and the people and entered Tahpanhes in Egypt (Jeremiah 43:2-7).
character: He was a military leader with the ability to assess a situation and rally an organization (Jeremiah 40:13). He tended to give priority to his own political or military judgment, and chose a practical alternative for breaking through the crisis he faced rather than the counsel of outside powers or of the prophet (Jeremiah 43:2-4).

introduce: John the Baptist is recorded in the New Testament as the one who prepared for the beginning of the public ministry of Jesus, and was born a son of Zechariah the priest and Elizabeth. He was a man who was active preaching and urging repentance in the wilderness of Judea.
lifetime: He was born to Zechariah and Elizabeth (Luke 1:13), and when the angel appeared to Mary, Elizabeth was already in her sixth month (Luke 1:36). As he grew, he became strong in spirit and was in the wilderness until the day of his manifestation to Israel (Luke 1:80). In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, the word of God came to him in the wilderness (Luke 3:1-2). Afterward he was active baptizing near the Jordan River, was arrested by Herod and put in prison (Matthew 14:3), and was beheaded in prison (Matthew 14:10).
event: In the wilderness of Judea he proclaimed a baptism of repentance and baptized many people (Mark 1:4). It is recorded that he baptized Jesus in the Jordan River (Matthew 3:13-16). He defined his own ministry by making clear that the one coming after him was Jesus (John 1:26-27). He said that it was not lawful for Herod to take his brother Philip's wife Herodias (Mark 6:17-18), and because of this he was put in prison and then beheaded in prison when the daughter of Herodias asked for his head (Mark 6:24-28).
character: He wore a garment of camel's hair with a leather belt around his waist and lived on locusts and wild honey (Matthew 3:4). He used critical and unflinching speech, calling the Pharisees and Sadducees, the people in power, a brood of vipers (Matthew 3:7). He described himself as the voice of one crying in the wilderness, and carried out the mission of preparing the way of Jesus (John 1:23). As he saw his disciples moving over to Jesus, he said, He must increase; I must decrease. (John 3:30).

introduce: He is a son of Eber and a younger brother of Peleg, a fourth-generation descendant of Shem who appears in Genesis 10. He is a figure who appears in the process by which humanity scattered over the face of the earth after Noah's flood in the genealogy of Shem.
lifetime: Eber lived four hundred and thirty years after fathering Peleg at the age of thirty-four, and had other children (Genesis 11:16-17), and Joktan was a brother of Peleg (Genesis 10:25). Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Obal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab (Genesis 10:26-29).
event: The place where the sons of Joktan lived was the hill country of the east on the way from Mesha toward Sephar (Genesis 10:30). They were descendants of Shem, according to their clans, their languages, their lands, and their nations (Genesis 10:31).

introduce: Jokshan is the second of the six sons whom Abraham fathered by Keturah, whom he took as a later wife after his wife Sarah died.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons whom Abraham fathered by Keturah (Genesis 25:2). His brothers were Zimran, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah (Genesis 25:2). During his lifetime Abraham gave gifts to these sons and sent them away from his son Isaac to the east (Genesis 25:6).
event: Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan, and the descendants of Dedan became the Asshurites, the Letushites, and the Leummites (Genesis 25:3). The Bible gives no separate account of the detailed deeds or historical events of these lines.

introduce: He is the son of David's brother Shammah (Shimea in 1 Chronicles 20:7) and therefore David's nephew.
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of David's brother Shammah (2 Samuel 21:21). In 1 Chronicles 20:7 he appears as Jonathan, the son of David's brother Shimea (1 Chronicles 20:7).
event: At the war in Gath he killed a tall man, a descendant of the giant, who had defied Israel (2 Samuel 21:20-21). The same event is recorded in 1 Chronicles (1 Chronicles 20:6-7).
character: As a member of the same family as his uncle David, he possessed valor, and he had the martial strength to defeat the physically overwhelming Philistine giants (2 Samuel 21:21). His presence shows that David's family members served on the military front to defend David's kingship and the security of the nation (1 Chronicles 20:7).

call: righteous man of the land of Uz (protagonist of the book of Job)
introduce: A man who lived in the land of Uz, the protagonist of the book of Job, and recorded as the greatest of all the people of the east.
lifetime: He lived in the land of Uz and had a prosperous household with seven sons and three daughters (Job 1:2). Through Satan's testing he lost all his property and children and suffered with boils on his body (Job 1:13-19, 2:7), and afterward he argued with his friends about his suffering (Job 3:1-31:40). At the end of his suffering he recovered twice as much property and had children again, and he lived 140 years and died (Job 42:10-17).
event: In a conversation between God and Satan, Satan was permitted to test Job, and Job was tested by losing all his possessions (Job 1:6-12). He engaged in a long dispute, in three rounds, with Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar, who came to him over his suffering (Job 4:1-25:6). He received an answer from God out of the storm (Job 38:1), and he prayed for his friends so that they were not dealt with according to their folly (Job 42:8-10).
character: He is described as blameless and upright, one who feared God and shunned evil (Job 1:1). Out of concern that his children might have sinned, he showed prudence by offering burnt offerings regularly (Job 1:5). Even in extreme suffering he strove not to sin with his lips (Job 2:10), and he fell into such deep anguish that he cursed the day of his birth (Job 3:1). He held firm convictions about himself, to the point of asserting his own righteousness and demanding to plead his case before God (Job 13:3).

description.민족: Aramean / righteous man of the East
직업/직위: righteous man of patience (protagonist of Job)

introduce: Ucal appears in Proverbs 30 and is recorded as one of the two men, Ithiel and Ucal, to whom Agur son of Jakeh spoke his words (Proverbs 30:1).
lifetime: The biblical text records that these words are the proverbs of Agur son of Jakeh and that he spoke them to Ithiel and Ucal, but nothing is recorded about the circumstances of Ucal's birth or the period of his life (Proverbs 30:1).
event: There is no record of Ucal's own deeds. The confession and prayer of Proverbs 30:2-9 are the words of Agur, not of Ucal, and Ucal appears only as one who heard those words (Proverbs 30:1).
character: There is no specific record of his personal character. He is introduced as one of those to whom Agur spoke his words, together with Ithiel (Proverbs 30:1).

call: son of Ammihud (chief of Perez of Judah)
introduce: Uthai appears in 1 Chronicles; he is a descendant of Perez of the tribe of Judah and a son of Ammihud. He is recorded as one of the descendants of Judah who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (1 Chronicles 9:3-4).
lifetime: He is one of the descendants of Perez son of Judah, a son of Ammihud, a grandson of Omri, a great-grandson of Imri, and a great-great-grandson of Bani (1 Chronicles 9:4). His name is recorded among the descendants of Judah who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:3-4).
event: After Judah was taken captive to Babylon because of its transgression, and the first returned to their own towns, he was recorded as one of the descendants of Judah who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:1-4).

introduce: A man greeted by the apostle Paul in Romans 16, a believer in Rome whom Paul called "our fellow worker in Christ."
lifetime: In the letter Paul sent to the believers in Rome, he is mentioned as Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ (Romans 16:9).
event: He is recorded as a fellow worker who labored with the apostle Paul for the gospel in Christ, and his name was included when Paul sent greetings to the believers of the church in Rome (Romans 16:9).
character: The biblical text contains no description of his specific character or personal traits (Romans 16:9).

introduce: Uri is a son of Hur of the tribe of Judah and a grandson of Caleb. He is recorded as the father of Bezalel.
lifetime: He is the son of Hur, who was born to Caleb son of Hezron and Ephrath, and he is recorded as the father of Bezalel (1 Chronicles 2:18-20). In Exodus, Bezalel is introduced as the grandson of Hur and the son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah (Exodus 31:2).
event: There is no record of Uri's own deeds; his son Bezalel is introduced as one whom the LORD called by name (Exodus 31:2, 35:30). Bezalel was filled with the Spirit of God to work in gold, silver, and bronze, to cut stones, and to carve wood (Exodus 31:3-5), and he made all that the LORD had commanded Moses (Exodus 38:22).

introduce: Uriah appears in 2 Samuel; he was a soldier of Hittite origin and one of the Thirty, the mighty men of King David's army. He was the husband of Bathsheba and is known as the central figure in a tragic episode involving David.
lifetime: He was a Hittite among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23:39). During the war with Ammon he came back to Jerusalem, but he swore that, while the ark, Israel, Judah, Joab, and the king's servants were camping in the open field, he would not go to his house to lie with his wife (2 Samuel 11:11). Afterward he personally carried the letter David had written to Joab, and Joab placed him where the mighty men were, and as he fought he died together with several of David's servants (2 Samuel 11:14-17). Later the prophet Nathan said that David had killed Uriah with the sword of the Ammonites (2 Samuel 12:9).
event: King David summoned Uriah from the battlefield in order to conceal that he had lain with Uriah's wife Bathsheba, but Uriah kept the discipline of a soldier and did not go down to his house (2 Samuel 11:9-10). When his plan failed, David sent Joab a secret letter ordering that Uriah be sent to the fiercest part of the fighting so that he would die (2 Samuel 11:14-15). Uriah himself carried to Joab the letter containing the scheme for his own death, and as a result he was killed in battle (2 Samuel 11:14-17).
character: He was a strict soldier who placed great value on military discipline and solidarity with his comrades (2 Samuel 11:11). Even though King David gave him leave and sent him home, he was so responsible that he refused to enjoy comfort alone while his fellow soldiers were suffering in the field (2 Samuel 11:11). This attitude frustrated the king's intention and, as a result, became the decisive occasion for his death.

introduce: Uriel is a descendant of Kohath among the Levites, recorded as a chief when the ark of God was brought up in the time of David.
lifetime: He is a person in the line of Kohath of the tribe of Levi, and he is recorded as a chief among the descendants of Kohath when David gathered the descendants of Aaron and the Levites to bring the ark of God up to the place he had prepared (1 Chronicles 15:3-5).
event: When David gathered the Levites to move the ark of God, Uriel was recorded as chief of the Kohathites, together with 120 of his relatives (1 Chronicles 15:5). David summoned him along with Zadok and Abiathar and commanded him, as a chief of the Levites, to consecrate himself and bring up the ark of the LORD (1 Chronicles 15:11-12).

introduce: Uzal is a fifth-generation descendant of Shem and a son of Joktan, a figure in the genealogy that branched off from Shem's line after Noah's flood (Genesis 10:26-27). He is one of those mentioned in the lineage that continued through Shem's son Arphaxad, grandson Shelah, great-grandson Eber, and Eber's son Joktan (Genesis 10:22-27, 1 Chronicles 1:17-21).
lifetime: He is a son of Joktan, and his brothers are recorded as Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Diklah, Obal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab (Genesis 10:26-29). In the genealogy of Chronicles he is also recorded as one of the sons of Joktan (1 Chronicles 1:20-21).

meaning: strong, the strength of the LORD
introduce: Uzai is recorded as the father of Palal, who took part in repairing the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 3:25).
lifetime: Nothing is recorded about Uzai himself; he appears in Nehemiah 3:25 only as the father of Palal (Nehemiah 3:25).
event: His son Palal repaired the section opposite the angle of the wall and the tower projecting from the upper palace of the king, near the court of the guard (Nehemiah 3:25).

introduce: Uz appears in the book of Genesis; he is recorded as the first of the four sons of Aram, a son of Shem. He is mentioned as a descendant of Aram in the genealogy formed by Shem's descendants after Noah's flood.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Aram and a grandson of Shem (Genesis 10:23). He belongs to Shem's line of descent within the genealogical system of the ancient Near East (1 Chronicles 1:17).
event: The biblical record contains no account of any specific deeds or particular events of Uz himself. Apart from being included in the earliest genealogy of humankind as a descendant of Aram, no further events are recorded (Genesis 10:23).

introduce: Uzzi appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin and is one of the sons of Bela (1 Chronicles 7:7).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the five sons of Bela, a son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:7). This genealogy is presented in the context of describing the composition of the families of the tribe of Benjamin and the census of their descendants (1 Chronicles 7:6-7).
event: He is mentioned as one of those classified as heads of families and mighty men, and together with his brothers Ezbon, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri, he is stated to have been a member of a family that numbered 22,034 mighty men (1 Chronicles 7:7).

introduce: In the Bible he appears as one of those who married foreign women after the return from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: In the time of Ezra, he is recorded as one of the descendants of Bani in the list of those who took foreign women (Ezra 10:34).
event: In Ezra 10:34 his name appears among the descendants of Bani together with Maadai and Amram, and all of them are recorded as having taken foreign women (Ezra 10:44).

introduce: According to the biblical record, Unni belongs to the tribe of Levi, and his name is recorded among the Levites who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel and Jeshua.
lifetime: Unni is a Levite in the list of the priests and Levites who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1), and he is recorded as a brother of Bakbukiah (Nehemiah 12:8-9).
event: Together with his brother Bakbukiah, Unni is recorded as one who stood opposite them in the services according to their duties (Nehemiah 12:9).

introduce: Unni is a Levite who appears in 1 Chronicles; he was appointed as one of the harp players when the ark of God was moved during the reign of King David.
lifetime: Unni is included in the list of the brothers of the singers whom the Levites appointed when David moved the ark of God (1 Chronicles 15:18). Together with Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah, he is recorded as one who played the harps according to Alamoth (1 Chronicles 15:20).
event: When David moved the ark of God, Unni was one of the brothers appointed next after Heman, Asaph, and Ethan (1 Chronicles 15:17-18). He is recorded as one who played the harps according to Alamoth (1 Chronicles 15:20).

introduce: Ulla is a person recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher, introduced as the father of Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia (1 Chronicles 7:39-40).
lifetime: The sons of Ulla are recorded as Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia (1 Chronicles 7:39).

introduce: Ulam is a person recorded in 1 Chronicles; in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh he is the son of Sheresh, born to Machir's wife Maacah, and a brother of Rekem (1 Chronicles 7:16).
lifetime: Ulam is the son of Sheresh and a brother of Rekem (1 Chronicles 7:16). Sheresh was a son born to Machir's wife Maacah and a younger brother of Peresh, and Machir was a son of Manasseh and the father of Gilead (1 Chronicles 7:14-16).
event: Ulam had a son named Bedan (1 Chronicles 7:17). The text records that all these were descendants of Gilead (1 Chronicles 7:17).

introduce: He was a son of Abinadab of Kiriath-jearim and one of the residents of the house where the ark of the covenant had been kept; in the time of David, while the ark of the covenant was being moved to Jerusalem, he touched the ark of God directly and died.
lifetime: When the ark of God was brought out on a new cart from the house of Abinadab on the hill, he drove the new cart together with Ahio as a son of Abinadab (2 Samuel 6:3). When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon and the oxen stumbled, he took hold of the ark of God, and the LORD was angry with him because of his error and struck him down there, and he died beside the ark of God (2 Samuel 6:6-7). The place where he died was named Perez-uzzah by David (2 Samuel 6:8).
event: While the ark of the covenant was being moved, when the oxen stumbled he reached out his hand and took hold of the ark of God (2 Samuel 6:6). Because of this error he incurred the anger of the LORD and died on the spot (2 Samuel 6:7). After his death David was unwilling to bring the ark of the LORD into the City of David, and took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite (2 Samuel 6:10-11).

introduce: Uzzi is a person recorded in the genealogy of Chronicles; he is a descendant of Aaron and a Levite belonging to the high priestly line. He is recorded as the son of Bukki and the father of Zerahiah.
lifetime: Uzzi was born as a son of Bukki in the house of Aaron the high priest (1 Chronicles 6:5). As a member of the high priestly line, he fathered his son Zerahiah (1 Chronicles 6:6).
event: The biblical record contains no account of any independent achievement or particular event of Uzzi himself; he is mentioned only as a figure carrying on the hereditary line of the high priestly family (1 Chronicles 6:5-6).

introduce: Uzziah was the 10th king of the southern kingdom of Judah, a son of Amaziah, and his mother was Jecoliah of Jerusalem (2 Kings 15:1-2). He was also called by the name Azariah, and he reigned over the kingdom of Judah for 52 years (2 Kings 15:2). His reign overlapped with the period of the prophet Isaiah's activity (Isaiah 6:1).
lifetime: Uzziah became king at the age of 16 and reigned in Jerusalem for 52 years (2 Chronicles 26:3). He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done, but he did not remove the high places, so the people still sacrificed and burned incense there (2 Kings 15:3-4). He tried to enter the temple to burn incense, and leprosy broke out on his forehead (2 Chronicles 26:16-20); he was a leper until the day of his death and lived in a separate house, while his son Jotham had charge of the palace and governed the people of the land (2 Kings 15:5; 2 Chronicles 26:21). After his death he was buried with his ancestors in the City of David (2 Kings 15:7), but 2 Chronicles records that because he was a leper he was buried in the ground adjoining the burial grounds of the kings, beside his ancestors (2 Chronicles 26:23).
event: Uzziah fought against the Philistines and broke down the walls of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, and he built cities in the territory of Ashdod and among the Philistines (2 Chronicles 26:6). God helped him against the Philistines, the Arabs living in Gur-baal, and the Meunites, and the Ammonites paid him tribute (2 Chronicles 26:7-8). Militarily, he had an army of 307,500 and prepared shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and slingstones (2 Chronicles 26:13-14). In Jerusalem he also had skilled craftsmen design devices and placed them on the towers and corners of the wall to shoot arrows and large stones (2 Chronicles 26:15). However, when he tried to enter the temple to burn incense, he was stopped by the priest Azariah and eighty brave priests of the LORD, and in that process leprosy broke out on his forehead (2 Chronicles 26:16-20).
character: He sought God throughout the days of Zechariah, who understood the visions of God, and as long as he sought God, God gave him success (2 Chronicles 26:5). But when his kingdom became strong, his heart grew proud and he did evil, and by trying to enter the temple of the LORD to burn incense he encroached on the office of the priests (2 Chronicles 26:16). After leprosy broke out in the temple, he had to live in isolation as a leper until the day of his death (2 Chronicles 26:21).

call: son of Kohath (chief of the tribe of Levi)
introduce: He was a son of Kohath of the tribe of Levi and the founder of the Uzzielite house, one of the clans of the Kohathites. As a relative of Aaron and Moses, he holds an important place in the genealogy of the Levites.
lifetime: He is recorded as the fourth of Kohath's four sons, Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel (Exodus 6:18). He had three sons, Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri (Exodus 6:22). In the Levitical genealogy he maintained his hereditary standing as a son of Kohath (Numbers 3:19).
event: When the Kohathites were carrying out their duty of transporting the furnishings of the tabernacle, his son Elizaphan was appointed chief of the families and clans of the Kohathites (Numbers 3:30). In addition, his sons Mishael and Elzaphan, at the command of Moses, carried the dead Nadab and Abihu from before the sanctuary to the outside of the camp (Leviticus 10:4-5).

introduce: Vophsi was a man of the tribe of Naphtali, recorded as the father of Nahbi, the representative of the tribe of Naphtali who was sent to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:14).
lifetime: Beyond being introduced in Numbers 13:14, "from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi," as the father of Nahbi, nothing about his own life is recorded in the Bible.
event: The Bible records no deeds of Vophsi himself. His son Nahbi is recorded as the representative of the tribe of Naphtali among the leaders of the Israelites whom Moses sent out from the Wilderness of Paran at the command of the LORD (Numbers 13:3, 13:14).

introduce: Jucal was a man active in the time of Zedekiah, king of Judah; he was a son of Shelemiah and appears in the historical records connected with the ministry of Jeremiah.
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of those whom King Zedekiah of Judah sent to ask Jeremiah to pray for them (Jeremiah 37:3, written as Jehucal). As a son of Shelemiah, he is recorded as one of those who heard what Jeremiah was saying to all the people (Jeremiah 38:1).
event: He was sent at the command of King Zedekiah of Judah to ask Jeremiah for prayer (Jeremiah 37:3). Afterward he is recorded as one of those who heard Jeremiah's words (Jeremiah 38:1), and then the officials told the king to put Jeremiah to death on the ground that he was weakening the hands of the people (Jeremiah 38:4), and Jeremiah was thrown into the cistern of Malchijah (Jeremiah 38:6).
character: He took the side of those opposing Jeremiah's prophetic message, and at a time of national crisis he showed the disposition of a hardline official who regarded Jeremiah's pacifist views as treason and attempted to have him physically eliminated (Jeremiah 38:4).

기타관계: Zedekiah#3813(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: Eunice appears in 2 Timothy; she is the mother of Timothy, and Lois is Timothy's grandmother on his mother's side (2 Timothy 1:5). She was a believing Jewish woman, and her husband was a Greek (Acts 16:1).
lifetime: Eunice was Timothy's mother, and Timothy had known the Scriptures from infancy (2 Timothy 3:15). When Paul came to Derbe and Lystra, it is recorded that the mother of the disciple Timothy who was there was a believing Jewish woman and his father was a Greek (Acts 16:1).
event: A sincere faith dwelt first in Eunice, and Paul said that he was convinced that it was in Timothy also (2 Timothy 1:5).
character: The apostle Paul regarded the faith that Eunice held as a sincere faith (2 Timothy 1:5). Although she was of Jewish descent, she had the background of having married a Greek, and she is depicted as one who nevertheless handed down a legacy of faith to her child (Acts 16:1, 2 Timothy 1:5).

introduce: Junia appears in Romans in the New Testament; she is a woman whom the apostle Paul, in the closing greetings of his letter to the believers in Rome, told them to greet together with Andronicus. The text records that they were well known to the apostles (Romans 16:7).
lifetime: The Bible contains no specific record of Junia's birthplace or upbringing. However, together with Andronicus she is mentioned as a relative of Paul and one who was imprisoned with him (Romans 16:7).
event: She is recorded as one who was esteemed among the apostles (Romans 16:7). She is also recorded as one who was in Christ before Paul (Romans 16:7).
character: She is introduced as a relative of Paul who was imprisoned with him, is held in high regard by the apostles, and was in Christ before Paul (Romans 16:7).

introduce: Eutychus is a figure in an incident that took place at Troas during the apostle Paul's third missionary journey; he was a young man who, while listening to Paul's sermon, was sitting in a window and could not overcome his drowsiness, fell from the third story and died, and was brought back to life by Paul.
lifetime: Eutychus was a young man at a meeting in Troas where Paul, intending to leave the next day, continued speaking until midnight (Acts 20:7-9). As Paul talked on and on, he fell into a deep sleep, and unable to overcome his drowsiness, he fell from the third story (Acts 20:9). Afterward Paul went down, took him in his arms, and said that his life was in him (Acts 20:10), and the people brought the boy back alive (Acts 20:12).
event: While listening to Paul's all-night sermon in an upper room in Troas, he sat at the window and dozed off, and fell from the third story to the ground and died (Acts 20:9). Paul went down to him, bent over and embraced him, and told the people that his life was still in him (Acts 20:10). Afterward Eutychus was brought to the people alive, and because of this the people were not a little comforted (Acts 20:12).
character: He had a scholarly and zealous attitude, to the point of attending the meeting in order to hear Paul's long discourse to the end late into the night, but he showed the ordinary human limitation of being unable to withstand physical fatigue and feeling drowsy (Acts 20:7, 20:9).

introduce: Judith was a daughter of Beeri the Hittite and one of the wives of Esau, the son of the patriarch Isaac.
lifetime: Judith was a daughter of Beeri the Hittite (Genesis 26:34). She became a wife of Esau, the son of Isaac (Genesis 26:34).
event: Judith married Esau when he was forty years old (Genesis 26:34). Her marriage to Esau became a grief of mind to Isaac and Rebekah (Genesis 26:35).

introduce: Jubal appears in the book of Genesis in the Old Testament; he is a descendant of Cain and a son born to Lamech and Adah. He became the father of all who play the harp and flute.
lifetime: Jubal was a son of Lamech, in the line descending from Cain's son Enoch through Irad, Mehujael, and Methusael (Genesis 4:17-18). He was a younger brother of Jabal, born to Adah (Genesis 4:19-21).
event: Jubal became the father of all who play the harp and flute (Genesis 4:21).

introduce: Jushab-hesed appears in 1 Chronicles; he is one of the descendants of the tribe of Judah recorded through the genealogy of the royal house of David.
lifetime: In the context recording the descendants of Zerubbabel, Jushab-hesed is listed as one of five persons together with Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, and Hasadiah (1 Chronicles 3:19-20).

introduce: A woman member of the church at Philippi, whom the apostle Paul urged in Philippians to be of the same mind in the Lord (Philippians 4:2).
lifetime: In Philippians Paul exhorts Euodia (Philippians 4:2), and then urges that the women who had labored with him in the gospel be helped (Philippians 4:3).
event: Paul exhorted Euodia and Syntyche each to be of the same mind in the Lord (Philippians 4:2).
character: She was acknowledged by the apostle Paul as one who had labored together with him for the gospel, and from the assessment that her name was in the book of life, it can be seen that she was a key member and leading figure of the church (Philippians 4:3). Judging from the fact that she received the exhortation to be of the same mind in the Lord, she may have been a person with strong opinions or influence within the community (Philippians 4:2).

introduce: Julia appears in Romans in the New Testament; she is a woman whose name was mentioned when the apostle Paul sent greetings to the Christians in Rome.
lifetime: She is one of the people Paul told the church in Rome to greet at the end of his letter, and she is mentioned together with Philologus, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas (Romans 16:15). The Bible contains no record of her birthplace, upbringing, or time of death.
event: She is recorded as one of those whom Paul told the church to greet (Romans 16:15). The Bible contains no account of any specific achievement she performed or any particular event.

introduce: A centurion of the Imperial Regiment, a Roman soldier who was charged with escorting the apostle Paul as he was taken to Rome.
lifetime: As a centurion of the Imperial Regiment, he was responsible for escorting Paul and the other prisoners to Italy (Acts 27:1). When the ship carrying Paul and the other prisoners put in at Sidon, he allowed Paul to go to his friends and receive care (Acts 27:3). Afterward he went through the wreck of the ship that had met the storm (Acts 27:41). When the soldiers, fearing that the prisoners would escape, planned to kill them, he wanted to save Paul and blocked their plan (Acts 27:42-43).
event: When the ship was in danger of being wrecked by the violent wind called the Northeaster, he ordered those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land (Acts 27:43). By having the rest come ashore on planks or on things from the ship, he saw to it that everyone who had been on board reached land safely (Acts 27:44).
character: In dealing with Paul he treated him kindly and showed the flexibility of allowing him to receive help from his friends (Acts 27:3). He also put more trust in the words of the pilot and the owner of the ship than in the words of Paul (Acts 27:11), and he had the decisiveness to preserve Paul's life by blocking the soldiers' immediate attempt to kill the prisoners (Acts 27:43).

introduce: Eubulus is a man named in the concluding part of 2 Timothy in the New Testament, whom Paul mentioned as sending greetings to Timothy.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the people who send greetings in the letter Paul sent to Timothy (2 Timothy 4:21).
event: His name was mentioned in the course of Paul conveying, in the letter to Timothy, that Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers send greetings (2 Timothy 4:21).

introduce: Ichabod was a son born to the wife of Phinehas, the daughter-in-law of the priest Eli, on the day Israel was defeated in the war with the Philistines and the ark of God was taken. His name carries the meaning that the glory has departed from Israel.
lifetime: Immediately after she heard the news that Israel had been defeated in the war with the Philistines and the ark had been captured, his mother went into labor and gave birth to him (1 Samuel 4:19-21). He was born in the time of the fall of the house of Eli, and his name was given by his mother at his birth (1 Samuel 4:21).
event: On the day he was born, his father Phinehas and his uncle Hophni were both killed in battle (1 Samuel 4:11). In addition, his grandfather, the priest Eli, on hearing that the ark had been captured, fell backward from his seat and broke his neck and died (1 Samuel 4:18). Immediately after giving birth to him, his mother died, leaving the words that the glory of Israel had been carried away (1 Samuel 4:21-22).

call: son of Joseph (Issachar's spy of Canaan)
introduce: Igal appears in Numbers 13; among the men Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan, he was the one representing the tribe of Issachar, and he is recorded as "Igal son of Joseph" (Numbers 13:7).
lifetime: He was one of the leaders sent by Moses at the command of the LORD while the Israelites were staying in the Wilderness of Paran (Numbers 13:3). He was recorded in the tribe of Issachar by the name Igal son of Joseph (Numbers 13:7).
event: At the command of Moses he spied out the land from the Wilderness of Zin to Rehob at the entrance of Hamath, and returned after forty days (Numbers 13:21, 13:25). Afterward, together with the other spies, at Kadesh in the Wilderness of Paran, he reported to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation that the inhabitants of the land were strong and the cities were fortified (Numbers 13:26-28).

introduce: The fourth son of Aaron and a priest, a man of the tribe of Levi who carried out duties connected with the service of Israel's tabernacle.
lifetime: He was born to Aaron and Elisheba and was a brother of Nadab, Abihu, and Eleazar (Exodus 6:23). After his older brothers died, he served in the priesthood together with Eleazar (Numbers 3:4), and in the wilderness he supervised the moving and care of the tabernacle (Numbers 4:28).
event: He was in charge of examining and recording the list of materials, such as gold, silver, and bronze, that were used when the tabernacle was set up (Exodus 38:21). He directed and supervised the work of carrying the curtains, boards, pillars, and so on of the tabernacle that were handled by the descendants of Gershon and the descendants of Merari (Numbers 4:28, 4:33).

introduce: Ithran is a person recorded as a son of Dishon, who was a son of Anah of the Horite clan that lived in the land of Seir (Genesis 36:26).
lifetime: Ithran is recorded as a son of Dishon, the son of Anah of the Horite clan (Genesis 36:20, 26). The sons of Dishon, namely Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran, are listed, and Ithran is one of them (1 Chronicles 1:41).
event: In the biblical record, no specific achievement or special event performed by Ithran is described; he is merely listed as a son of Dishon (Genesis 36:26; 1 Chronicles 1:41).

introduce: Ithream was the sixth son of David, born in Hebron during the time David reigned there.
lifetime: He was one of the sons David fathered in Hebron, born through David's wife Eglah (2 Samuel 3:5). The record in Chronicles also states that he was one of the six sons David fathered in Hebron (1 Chronicles 3:3).
event: Apart from the record of his birth during David's reign in Hebron, there is no record in the Bible of any public achievement or particular event he carried out.
character: The biblical text contains no description of Ithream's temperament or physical features.

introduce: Ithmah is a person recorded as one of David's mighty men, the military organization of King David (1 Chronicles 11:46).
lifetime: During David's reign he supported David and served as one of his mighty men, and his name was entered in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:46).
event: He is mentioned as a military helper of King David, included in the list of David's mighty men, and this list is set in the context of enumerating those who formed David's military foundation (1 Chronicles 11:46).

introduce: Jidlaph appears in the book of Genesis; he is one of the eight sons of Nahor and Milcah.
lifetime: He is the seventh of the sons born to Nahor and Milcah (Genesis 22:22).

introduce: Ithiel is recorded as the sixth ancestor of Sallu, a descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem. In Sallu's genealogy he is the son of Jeshaiah, the seventh ancestor, and corresponds to the father of Maaseiah (Nehemiah 11:7).
lifetime: Ithiel was recorded as the sixth ancestor in the genealogy of Sallu (the son of Meshullam), a descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:4, 7). In this genealogy, Jeshaiah stands above Ithiel and Maaseiah below him (Nehemiah 11:7). Nothing about Ithiel's own deeds is recorded in the Bible.
event: Nothing that Ithiel himself did is recorded; his name appears only as an ancestor in the genealogy of Sallu, a descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:7).

introduce: Irad appears in the book of Genesis; he is a descendant of Cain and a son of Enoch.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son born to Enoch, the son of Cain (Genesis 4:18).
event: He is mentioned as the father of Mehujael and is a person who continues the genealogical line of Cain's family (Genesis 4:18).

introduce: Iru is a descendant of Caleb of the tribe of Judah and a person belonging to the genealogy of Caleb son of Jephunneh (1 Chronicles 4:15).
lifetime: Iru is mentioned as one of the sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh, namely Iru, Elah, and Naam (1 Chronicles 4:15).

introduce: Ir-nahash is a person mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah in 1 Chronicles 4 in the expression "Tehinnah the father of Ir-nahash." Tehinnah is recorded as one fathered by Eshton (1 Chronicles 4:12).
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Tehinnah, and Tehinnah is one fathered by Eshton (1 Chronicles 4:12).
event: Apart from this verse, no specific achievement or event carried out by Ir-nahash is recorded (1 Chronicles 4:12).

introduce: Iri is a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the descendants of Benjamin named in 1 Chronicles 7:7. He is recorded as a person within the family line that continues through Benjamin's sons Bela, Becher, and Jediael.
lifetime: Iri is mentioned as one of the sons of Bela, and his father Bela was a son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:6-7). As one of the heads of the family, he is included in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:7).
event: Iri was classified as a head of the family together with Bela's sons Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri (1 Chronicles 7:7). All of them are recorded as mighty men, and the number of the army counted according to their genealogy was 22,034 (1 Chronicles 7:7).

introduce: Irijah is recorded as a grandson of Hananiah and a son of Shelemiah, and he was the captain of the guard at the Gate of Benjamin (Jeremiah 37:13). When Jeremiah left Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin and reached the Gate of Benjamin, he seized him and said that he was deserting to the Chaldeans.
lifetime: He was captain of the guard at the Gate of Benjamin in Jerusalem in the last days of the kingdom of Judah (Jeremiah 37:13). When Jeremiah reached the Gate of Benjamin, he seized him, and although Jeremiah denied it, he would not listen and dragged him to the officials (Jeremiah 37:13-14).
event: When Jeremiah reached the Gate of Benjamin, he seized him and said that he was deserting to the Chaldeans (Jeremiah 37:13). Although Jeremiah denied it, Irijah would not listen and dragged him to the officials, and the officials were angry and beat Jeremiah and put him in the house of Jonathan the scribe (Jeremiah 37:14-15).

introduce: Imrah is a person of the tribe of Asher and a son of Zophah (1 Chronicles 7:36).
lifetime: He is a person recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher as a son of Zophah, a descendant of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:36).
event: 1 Chronicles 7:40 records all the descendants of Asher, including Imrah, as heads of families, choice mighty men of valor, and chiefs of the princes, and says that those fit for military service numbered 26,000 when counted by genealogy (1 Chronicles 7:40). No deeds of Imrah himself are recorded.

call: son of Bani (descendant of Perez of Judah)
introduce: Imri is a descendant of Perez son of Judah, recorded as the great-grandfather of Uthai, who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:4).
lifetime: In the genealogy of Uthai in 1 Chronicles 9:4, he is recorded as the son of Bani and the father of Omri. Uthai is the son of Ammihud, the grandson of Omri, the great-grandson of Imri, and the great-great-grandson of Bani (1 Chronicles 9:4).

introduce: Imlah appears in 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles; he is the father of the prophet Micaiah.
lifetime: The only information the Bible records about Imlah's life is that he was the father of a prophet named Micaiah (1 Kings 22:8, 2 Chronicles 18:7).
event: Imlah himself performed no achievement and no event is recorded of him; he is mentioned only as an identification of his son, in the context where the king of Israel speaks to Jehoshaphat of "Micaiah son of Imlah" as a man through whom they could inquire of the LORD and has him summoned (1 Kings 22:8-9, 2 Chronicles 18:7-8).

introduce: Ibneiah is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles 9 and belongs to the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: He is a member of a family of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem, and he is a son of Jeroham (1 Chronicles 9:8).
event: He is included in the list of the descendants of Benjamin who settled and lived in Jerusalem after the return of Israel from captivity (1 Chronicles 9:3, 9:8).

introduce: Ibnijah is a descendant of Benjamin mentioned in 1 Chronicles, and he is recorded as the great-grandfather of Meshullam, who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:8).
lifetime: Ibnijah was the father of Reuel and the grandfather of Shephatiah. 1 Chronicles 9:8 records Meshullam, a descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem, as "the great-grandson of Ibnijah, the grandson of Reuel, and the son of Shephatiah" (1 Chronicles 9:3, 8).
event: Nothing about Ibnijah's own deeds is recorded; his name appears only as an ancestor of Meshullam, a descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:8).

introduce: Iphdeiah appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8) and is a son of Shashak (1 Chronicles 8:25).
lifetime: Iphdeiah is recorded as a son of Shashak, and Penuel is also recorded as a son of Shashak (1 Chronicles 8:25).

introduce: Ibri is a person of the tribe of Levi mentioned in 1 Chronicles 24, a descendant begotten by Jaaziah of the descendants of Merari (1 Chronicles 24:27).
lifetime: Ibri is recorded as one of Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri, the sons begotten by Jaaziah of the descendants of Merari (1 Chronicles 24:26-27).
event: It is recorded that the descendants of Levi were chosen by lot like their brothers the descendants of Aaron, in the presence of King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the priests and the heads of the Levites, and Ibri's name appears at that time among the sons of Jaaziah of the descendants of Merari who were recorded (1 Chronicles 24:27, 31).

introduce: He was the son born to Abraham and Sarah, and he forms the second generation in the genealogy of the patriarchs of the Hebrew people. His name carries the meaning of laughter, and he played the central role of inheriting Abraham's covenant legacy.
lifetime: He was born as the son whom Sarah bore when Abraham was a hundred years old (Genesis 21:2, 21:5), and in his childhood he was mocked by Hagar's son Ishmael (Genesis 21:9). He went through the crisis of nearly being offered as a burnt offering by Abraham on a mountain in the land of Moriah (Genesis 22:2, 22:9), and at the age of 40 he married Rebekah (Genesis 25:20). At the age of 60 he had Esau and Jacob (Genesis 25:26), and after sojourning in Hebron he died at the age of 180 and was gathered to his people (Genesis 35:27-29).
event: While living in Gerar he sowed in that land and reaped a hundredfold in that year (Genesis 26:6, 26:12). He dug again the wells that had been dug in the time of Abraham and stopped up by the Philistines, and he went up to Beersheba and made a covenant with Abimelech by oath (Genesis 26:18-33). In his old age, with failing eyesight, he tried to bless his elder son Esau, but through the deception of his wife Rebekah and his younger son Jacob he ended up giving the blessing of the firstborn to Jacob (Genesis 27:1-29).
character: On the whole he showed a gentle and passive disposition, and in conflict situations he took an attitude of yielding rather than direct confrontation (Genesis 26:20-22). He was a man who respected and obeyed his father's authority (Genesis 22:7-9), and he had a liking for meat, especially game (Genesis 25:28).

call: son of Obed, father of David
introduce: Jesse was a descendant of the tribe of Judah, a man from Bethlehem, and is recorded as the father of King David (1 Samuel 16:1). 1 Chronicles 2:12-15 records him as the son of Obed and as the father who begot David as his seventh son (1 Chronicles 2:12-15).
lifetime: Jesse was the son of Obed, who was born to Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:13, 4:17, 4:21). He lived in Bethlehem and had eight sons (1 Samuel 16:10-11, 17:12). Samuel came to Bethlehem, consecrated Jesse and his sons, and invited them to the sacrifice (1 Samuel 16:5); Jesse had seven of his sons pass before Samuel, but none was chosen, and David, the youngest, who was keeping the sheep, was sent for and anointed by Samuel (1 Samuel 16:10-13). Afterward, when Saul sent messengers asking for his son David, who tended the sheep, Jesse loaded a donkey with bread, wine, and a young goat and sent them to Saul by the hand of David (1 Samuel 16:19-20). When David was facing the Philistine army, Jesse was old and advanced in years, and his three oldest sons had gone to the battle with Saul (1 Samuel 17:12-13).
event: Jesse had seven of his sons pass before Samuel, and when Samuel asked whether these were all his sons, he answered that the youngest was still keeping the sheep, and so David was sent for and anointed (1 Samuel 16:10-13). During the war with the Philistines, he had David take roasted grain and bread to the camp, give them to his brothers, and see how they were doing (1 Samuel 17:17-18).

call: queen of northern Israel (princess of Sidon)
introduce: Jezebel was the daughter of Ethbaal, king of Sidon, a city-state of ancient Phoenicia, and the queen of Ahab, the seventh king of northern Israel. She cut off the prophets of the LORD (1 Kings 18:4), and 450 prophets of Baal and 400 prophets of Asherah ate at her table (1 Kings 18:19).
lifetime: As the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians, she became the wife of Ahab, king of Israel (1 Kings 16:31). After Ahab died, his sons Ahaziah and Jehoram became kings in turn (1 Kings 22:40, 2 Kings 3:1), and in the time of Jehoram his mother Jezebel was still alive (2 Kings 9:22). When Jehu came to Jezreel, Jezebel painted her eyes, adorned her head, and looked out of the window (2 Kings 9:30); at Jehu's word a couple of eunuchs threw her down from the window, and Jehu trampled her body (2 Kings 9:32-33). They tried to bury her but found nothing except her skull, her feet, and the palms of her hands (2 Kings 9:35), and Jehu said that it was according to the word of Elijah that the dogs would eat the flesh of Jezebel in the plot of ground at Jezreel (2 Kings 9:36).
event: 450 prophets of Baal and 400 prophets of Asherah ate at Jezebel's table (1 Kings 18:19). When Ahab told Jezebel what Elijah had done, Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah threatening to take his life, and Elijah fled (1 Kings 19:1-3). Saying that she would give Naboth's vineyard to Ahab, Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them, and sent them to the elders and nobles, and had Naboth stoned to death on the testimony of false witnesses (1 Kings 21:7-14); when she heard that Naboth was dead, she told Ahab to take the vineyard, and Ahab went down to take possession of it (1 Kings 21:15-16).
character: Jezebel was a person who showed a strong and resolute drive to achieve her own political aims. As revealed in the matter of Naboth, she used her authority to exercise the influence to dispose of the lives and property of others (1 Kings 21:7). In religion, she took a leading, forceful attitude of establishing within Israel the Baal faith of her own background (1 Kings 18:4). Even on the brink of death, she tried not to lose her dignity, painting her eyes and adorning her head, which plainly shows her tough character (2 Kings 9:30).

직업/직위: queen of Israel (northern kingdom; Sidonian princess)

introduce: Zohar appears in 1 Chronicles 4 and is a person recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah. He is a son of Helah, a wife of Ashhur the father of Tekoa (1 Chronicles 4:5, 4:7).
lifetime: Zohar is recorded as one of Helah's sons Zereth, Zohar, and Ethnan (1 Chronicles 4:7). Helah is one of the two wives of Ashhur the father of Tekoa (1 Chronicles 4:5).

introduce: Iscah is a female figure who appears in the genealogy of Genesis; she is the daughter of Haran, the sister of Milcah, and a sibling of Lot.
lifetime: Genesis 11:29 records that Haran was the father of Milcah and also the father of Iscah (Genesis 11:29). Haran was a brother of Abram and Nahor and fathered Lot (Genesis 11:26-27).

introduce: Izri is a descendant of the tribe of Levi, belonging to the fourth of the twenty-four divisions determined by lot to be in charge of the service of praise in the temple during the reign of King David.
lifetime: Izri is recorded as one of the sons of Jeduthun (1 Chronicles 25:3). He was in charge of the fourth division chosen by lot in the choir that David organized (1 Chronicles 25:11).
event: David and the commanders of the army set apart some of the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to serve by singing spiritual songs with lyres, harps, and cymbals (1 Chronicles 25:1), and both small and great alike received their duties by casting lots in the same way (1 Chronicles 25:8). Izri was chosen fourth in that casting of lots, and he, his sons, and his brothers together, twelve in all, made up that division (1 Chronicles 25:11).

introduce: A descendant of the tribe of Judah, recorded as one of the descendants of the ancestor Etam.
lifetime: A person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah and is recorded as one of the descendants of the ancestor Etam (1 Chronicles 4:3).
event: He is recorded together with Jezreel and Idbash as a descendant of the ancestor Etam, and their brother-in-law Hazzelelponi is mentioned with them. Beyond the record that confirms his position within the family, no specific historical achievement or event appears (1 Chronicles 4:3).

기타관계: Hazzelelponi#2999(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: Ismachiah is recorded as one of those who were overseers of the gifts of the temple in the time of Hezekiah, king of Judah (2 Chronicles 31:13).
lifetime: At the command of King Hezekiah and Azariah, who was in charge of the house of God, Ismachiah became an overseer under Conaniah and his brother Shimei (2 Chronicles 31:13). Conaniah the Levite had charge of the contributions, tithes, and dedicated things, and his brother Shimei was second (2 Chronicles 31:12).
event: Together with Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Mahath, and Benaiah, he became an overseer under Conaniah and his brother Shimei (2 Chronicles 31:13).

기타관계: Conaniah#3274(fellow worker of the tribe of Levi)

introduce: Ishmaiah appears in 1 Chronicles; he is a son of Obadiah and is recorded as the officer over Zebulun among those in charge of the tribes of Israel (1 Chronicles 27:19).
lifetime: Ishmaiah is recorded as a son of Obadiah, and he was the officer over Zebulun among those in charge of the tribes of Israel (1 Chronicles 27:16, 27:19).
