call: son of Ephod (chief of the tribe of Manasseh)
introduce: Hanniel is a man who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, the chief of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh among the chiefs, one from each tribe, chosen to divide the land of Canaan as an inheritance. He is recorded as the son of Ephod (Numbers 34:18, 34:23).
lifetime: Before the people of Israel divided the land of Canaan as an inheritance, the LORD commanded Moses to choose one chief from each tribe, and Hanniel was recorded by name as the chief of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh among the sons of Joseph (Numbers 34:18, 34:23).
event: He was recorded as one of the chiefs of the tribes chosen to divide the land of inheritance at the command of the LORD. As those who were to divide the land as an inheritance, the priest Eleazar and Joshua the son of Nun are named (Numbers 34:17), and Hanniel was entered in that list as the chief of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh (Numbers 34:18, 34:23).

introduce: Hallohesh is a man recorded in Nehemiah 3:12 as the father of Shallum, in the words "Shallum the son of Hallohesh, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem" (Nehemiah 3:12).
lifetime: Nehemiah 3:12 only introduces Hallohesh as the father of Shallum, and there is no record of Hallohesh's own life in the Bible (Nehemiah 3:12).
event: Nothing Hallohesh himself did is recorded. His son Shallum and his daughters repaired a section of the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:12).

introduce: Hallohesh is one of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant during the renewal of the covenant that took place after the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:24).
lifetime: Hallohesh is recorded as a chief of the people among those who sealed the covenant of Nehemiah 10 (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:14, 10:24).
event: Together with the chiefs of the people of Israel, he was entered in the list of those who sealed the covenant that was written down (Nehemiah 9:38, 10:24). This covenant was an oath to keep the law of God given through Moses the servant of God (Nehemiah 10:29).

introduce: Harhaiah is a man whose name appears in Nehemiah 3:8 in the words "Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths," recorded as the father of Uzziel (Nehemiah 3:8).
lifetime: Harhaiah's own life and deeds are not recorded in the Bible; his name appears in Nehemiah 3:8 as "Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths" (Nehemiah 3:8).
event: Those who repaired in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem were not Harhaiah but his son Uzziel and others, and next to them Hananiah, one of the perfumers, and others repaired Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall (Nehemiah 3:8).

introduce: Harhur refers to a family of the Nethinim, among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem and Judah by the decree of Cyrus king of Persia after the Babylonian exile, or to the ancestor of that family (Ezra 2:51).
lifetime: Harhur is recorded as one of the descendants of the Nethinim, and his name is included in the list of the community that returned from Babylon (Ezra 2:51, Nehemiah 7:53).
event: The descendants of Harhur belonged to the company of the Nethinim who were counted among the people of Israel who came out with Zerubbabel and others (Ezra 2:2, 2:51). When, after the city was built, Nehemiah found the genealogical register of those who had come up at the first, the same entry was recorded there (Nehemiah 7:1, 7:5, 7:53).

introduce: Hammath is a man recorded in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 2 as "the father of the house of Rechab," an ancestor of the Kenite clan (1 Chronicles 2:55).
lifetime: Hammath is recorded as an ancestor in the genealogy of the family, being the origin of the house of Rechab (1 Chronicles 2:55).
event: 1 Chronicles 2:55 records that the clans of the scribes who lived at Jabez, namely the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites, were the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab (1 Chronicles 2:55).

introduce: Hammolecheth is a woman who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, recorded as a descendant of the tribe of Manasseh and the sister of Gilead (1 Chronicles 7:17-18).
lifetime: As the sister of Gilead, she bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah (1 Chronicles 7:18).
event: Apart from the record that, as the sister of Gilead, she bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah, no specific account of any historical event can be found (1 Chronicles 7:18).

introduce: Hammuel is a man recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:26, belonging to the genealogy of the descendants of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:24-26).
lifetime: In the genealogy that runs from Shaul the son of Simeon to Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, and Mishma his son, Hammuel is the son of Mishma, and his son is Zaccur (1 Chronicles 4:24-26).

meaning: a compound of the ancient Persian words hamma (to be equal) and data (giver)
introduce: A man who appears in the book of Esther, the father of Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite.
lifetime: He is recorded as the father of Haman the Agagite (Esther 3:1).
event: He is mentioned as the lineage background of Haman, in the course of his son Haman obtaining the approval of Ahasuerus king of Persia for his plan to destroy the Jews (Esther 3:1).

introduce: Happizzez is a man recorded as the eighteenth of the divisions of the descendants of Aaron in the time of David, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 24.
lifetime: Happizzez is recorded as the eighteenth of the twenty-four priestly divisions apportioned by lot in the time of King David (1 Chronicles 24:15). His life and specific personal history do not appear in the biblical record.
event: King David, together with Zadok of the descendants of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the descendants of Ithamar, divided the descendants of Aaron and assigned each their duties of service (1 Chronicles 24:3), and Happizzez was recorded as the eighteenth in the divisions drawn by lot (1 Chronicles 24:15).

introduce: A man who appears in the genealogy of the house of David recorded in 1 Chronicles 3, a son of Shemaiah, belonging to the line of Shecaniah, a descendant of David.
lifetime: In the genealogy of David's descendants in 1 Chronicles 3, his name is stated among the sons of Shemaiah the son of Shecaniah (1 Chronicles 3:22).
event: The Bible contains no record of any specific historical achievement or particular event that he carried out. The only thing is that he is mentioned as a person who continued the genealogy of the house of David (1 Chronicles 3:22).

introduce: Hattil is a man recorded as "the descendants of Hattil" in the list of those who returned to Jerusalem and Judah from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 7).
lifetime: Hattil's name is recorded in the list of returnees in Nehemiah 7 as a family belonging to the descendants of Solomon's servants (Nehemiah 7:57, 7:59). In Ezra 2:57 the same family appears as "the descendants of Hattil" (a variant spelling of the name).
event: Among the descendants of Solomon's servants, he is listed as the descendants of Hattil, together with the descendants of Shephatiah, the descendants of Pochereth-hazzebaim, and the descendants of Amon (Nehemiah 7:59). The biblical text records no specific deeds of Hattil himself.

introduce: Hasshub was a man who took part in the work of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile, one of the descendants of Pahath-moab.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Pahath-moab (Nehemiah 3:11).
event: When the wall of Jerusalem was repaired, together with Malchijah the son of Harim he repaired another section of the wall and the Tower of the Ovens (Nehemiah 3:11).

introduce: Hassenuah is a man whose name appears in the genealogies of the descendants of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles 9 and Nehemiah 11; his son Judah is recorded as having become second over the city of Jerusalem.
lifetime: Sallu is recorded as the son of Meshullam, the grandson of Hodaviah, and the great-grandson of Hassenuah (1 Chronicles 9:7). Accordingly, in this genealogy Hodaviah is the son of Hassenuah. In Nehemiah 11:9, Judah son of Hassenuah is recorded as having become second over the city.
event: Hassenuah's own deeds are not recorded in the text. It is recorded that his son Judah, when Joel the son of Zichri was the overseer, became second and governed the city (Nehemiah 11:9).

introduce: A believer belonging to the church in Rome, one to whom the apostle Paul sent greetings near the end of the letter to the Romans.
lifetime: He appears as one of the persons to whom greetings were sent when Paul wrote his letter to the saints in Rome (Romans 16:14).
event: He is included in Paul's list of greetings recorded in Romans 16, where the record remains that greetings are to be given to Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers who are with them (Romans 16:14).

introduce: Hermes is mentioned as one of the persons to whom the apostle Paul sent greetings near the end of the letter he sent to the Christians in Rome.
lifetime: Hermes is named, together with the saints in the church in Rome, as one to whom Paul sent greetings, and nothing is recorded about his later life or background (Romans 16:14).
event: His name appears in the content of Paul's letter in Romans 16:14, in which greetings are to be given to Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers who are with them (Romans 16:14).

introduce: A man who appears in 2 Timothy in the New Testament, recorded as one of those who left Paul in Asia during Paul's ministry.
lifetime: When Paul was imprisoned in Rome, some of those who were in Asia turned away from Paul and left, and he is mentioned as one of them (2 Timothy 1:15).
event: He is singled out as one of those who rejected Paul and left him when Paul was in a difficult situation (2 Timothy 1:15).

introduce: Hegai was a eunuch who was in charge of the women in the palace of Ahasuerus king of Persia.
lifetime: Hegai was the eunuch in charge of the women in the palace of King Ahasuerus, and the virgins gathered by the king were committed to his hand (Esther 2:3). When Esther was taken to the king's palace, she was placed under Hegai's care (Esther 2:8). Hegai was pleased with Esther and showed her kindness; he gave her the things needed for her purification, her portion of food, and the seven maids customarily given her from the king's palace (Esther 2:9).
event: Hegai moved Esther and her maids to the best place in the harem (Esther 2:9). When Esther's turn came to go in to the king, she asked for nothing except what Hegai, the king's eunuch in charge of the women, advised (Esther 2:15).
character: Hegai was an official who faithfully followed the king's commands, and he showed Esther favor and kindness (Esther 2:9). Among the women he managed, he especially thought well of Esther and gave her special treatment, and so served as a helper in the process by which she gained the king's favor (Esther 2:9).

introduce: Henadad was the ancestor of a Levite family, whose descendants appear in the supervision of the temple work in the time of Ezra and in the repair of the wall in the time of Nehemiah.
lifetime: In Ezra 3:9 "the sons of Henadad" appear with their brothers the Levites, and in Nehemiah 3 two sons of Henadad, both named Binnui, are recorded as men who repaired the wall (Ezra 3:9, Nehemiah 3:18, Nehemiah 3:24).
event: When the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem began, Jeshua, Kadmiel, the sons of Henadad, and their brothers the Levites rose up together to supervise the workmen in the house of God (Ezra 3:9). In the time of Nehemiah, Henadad's son Binnui, as ruler of half the district of Keilah, repaired the wall (Nehemiah 3:18), and Henadad's son Binnui also repaired a section (Nehemiah 3:24). Among the Levites who sealed the covenant, Binnui is among the descendants of Henadad (Nehemiah 10:9).
character: He showed a cooperative disposition, actively joining in and fulfilling responsibility for the great national and religious undertakings of rebuilding the temple and repairing the wall, and as a transitional figure linking the time of Ezra and the time of Nehemiah he continued his activity (Ezra 3:9, Nehemiah 3:18, Nehemiah 10:9).

introduce: Heresh is one of the Levites who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 9; his name is listed together with Bakbakkar, Galal, and Mattaniah (1 Chronicles 9:15).
lifetime: Heresh's name is entered in the list of Levites in 1 Chronicles 9:15 together with Bakbakkar, Galal, and Mattaniah (1 Chronicles 9:15). The text does not record Heresh's own lineage or personal history.
event: He is included in the list of the Levites who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:15). The lineage that follows, "the son of Mica, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph," is a description of Mattaniah (1 Chronicles 9:15).

introduce: Herodias is a woman who appears in the Gospels of the New Testament; she was originally the wife of Philip, Herod's brother, and Herod took her as his wife, and she is recorded in connection with the death of John the Baptist.
lifetime: She was originally the wife of Philip, Herod's brother (Matthew 14:3), but Herod took her as his wife (Mark 6:17). John told Herod that it was not right for him to have taken that woman (Matthew 14:4), and Herod the tetrarch was rebuked by John for the matter of Herodias, his brother's wife (Luke 3:19).
event: For the sake of Herodias, Herod sent and seized John and put him in prison (Mark 6:17), and Herodias regarded John as an enemy and wanted to kill him but could not (Mark 6:19). On Herod's birthday, when the daughter of Herodias danced at the banquet and pleased Herod, the daughter, prompted by her mother, asked for the head of John the Baptist on a platter (Matthew 14:6, 14:8), and John was beheaded in prison (Mark 6:27).
character: She showed strong hostility toward one who was a threat to her political position and honor (Mark 6:19), and she had a cold and vengeful side, using family relationships to achieve her purpose (Matthew 14:8).

introduce: Herodion is a person mentioned by the apostle Paul near the end of the letter to the Romans in the New Testament when he sent greetings to the Christians in Rome. He is called by the title "kinsman," which suggests a blood relationship with Paul or origin from the same people.
lifetime: Herodion is referred to as Paul's kinsman in the letter that the apostle Paul sent to the church in Rome (Romans 16:11). Beyond that, no record of his birthplace, upbringing, or the latter part of his life appears in the Bible.
event: Herodion is one of the persons mentioned when Paul sent greetings to the saints in Rome, calling him "my kinsman" (Romans 16:11).

introduce: A man recorded in the New Testament as the king of Judea at the time of the birth of Jesus (Matthew 2:1, Luke 1:5). He is recorded as the king who, realizing that he had been tricked by the wise men, became furious and killed the boys in Bethlehem.
lifetime: He was king of Judea when Jesus was born (Matthew 2:1). He called the wise men from the east, asked them the time when the star appeared, and told them to report to him when they found the child, but when he realized he had been tricked by the wise men, he killed all the boys in Bethlehem and in all that region who were two years old and under (Matthew 2:7-8, 2:16). After Herod died, when Joseph heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he departed to the region of Galilee (Matthew 2:19, 2:22).
event: When he heard the news that Jesus had been born, King Herod and all Jerusalem with him were troubled (Matthew 2:3), and Herod, realizing that he had been tricked by the wise men, became furious and sent and killed all the boys in Bethlehem and in all that region who were two years old and under (Matthew 2:16).
character: To protect his own power, he had a paranoid and ruthless nature, to the point of cruelly putting to death everyone he suspected, including family members and close associates (Matthew 2:16). He showed outstanding ability to maintain power by reading the political currents of Rome, and he was a ruler with the ambition to display his achievements by erecting large-scale buildings (John 2:20).

introduce: A descendant of Zerah of the tribe of Judah, one of the wise men whose wisdom Solomon's wisdom is recorded in 1 Kings 4:31 as having surpassed. In the Bible he is mentioned as a wise man distinct from Heman the temple singer of the tribe of Levi, who has the same name.
lifetime: In the genealogy of the tribe of Judah he is recorded as one of Zerah's sons Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara (1 Chronicles 2:6). In 1 Kings 4:31, "Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol" are listed as men less wise than Solomon (1 Kings 4:31).
event: His name appears as an object of comparison where it says that Solomon's wisdom surpassed the wisdom of all the people of the east and all the wisdom of Egypt (1 Kings 4:30), and that Solomon was wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol, so that his fame was in all the surrounding nations (1 Kings 4:31).
character: Being highly renowned as a wise man, he was used as a benchmark with which Solomon's wisdom was compared (1 Kings 4:31). The Bible evaluates him, together with the sons of Mahol, as one with the greatest wisdom of his time (1 Kings 4:31).

introduce: A descendant of the Horite clan who lived on Mount Seir.
lifetime: He is recorded as a descendant of Seir and a son of Lotan of the Horite clan (Genesis 36:22).
event: He is recorded among the children of Lotan, a descendant of Seir of the Horite clan, in the genealogy of the Horites in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:20, 36:22). In 1 Chronicles 1:39 he appears as Homam (1 Chronicles 1:39).

introduce: Heber is a person who appears in Genesis and 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher as a son of Beriah and a brother of Malchiel.
lifetime: Heber is recorded as a son of Beriah the son of Asher, and is mentioned as one of the lines in the genealogy of the descendants of Asher (Genesis 46:17). 1 Chronicles 7:31 also records that the sons of Beriah were Heber and Malchiel (1 Chronicles 7:31).
event: Numbers 26:45 records that among the descendants of Beriah there was the Heberite family from Heber, and 1 Chronicles 7:32 records that Heber fathered Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and their brother-in-law Shua (Numbers 26:45, 1 Chronicles 7:32). No independent event or achievement of Heber himself is described in the biblical text.

call: third son of Kohath (uncle of Moses)
introduce: A descendant of Levi and a son of Kohath, the ancestor of the Hebronite descendants within the tribe of Levi.
lifetime: He was born a son of Kohath and was a brother of Amram, Izhar, and Uzziel (Exodus 6:18). He is recorded as a grandson of Levi and the third son of Kohath (Numbers 3:19).

introduce: Hezro was a Carmelite whose name is listed in the roll of David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23:35).
lifetime: In the time when David ruled, he is recorded in the roll of his mighty men as Hezro the Carmelite (2 Samuel 23:35). In 1 Chronicles 11:37 he appears in the same list as Hezro the Carmelite (1 Chronicles 11:37).

introduce: Hezion is a man mentioned only once in the Old Testament, in 1 Kings 15:18, recorded as the king of Aram who lived in Damascus; Ben-hadad, the son of Tabrimmon, is his grandson.
lifetime: Hezion is recorded as the king of Aram who lived in Damascus (1 Kings 15:18). The text mentions him in the words introducing the lineage "Ben-hadad the son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion" (1 Kings 15:18).
event: The biblical text does not describe any specific acts of rule or achievements of Hezion himself, and mentions only his name in the course of introducing Ben-hadad king of Aram, to whom Asa king of Judah sent silver and gold (1 Kings 15:18).

introduce: The head of the priestly family who was in charge of the seventeenth division when the priestly organization was divided into twenty-four divisions in the time of David. Hezir, as a descendant of Aaron, is one of those chosen by lot to carry out the duties of the temple sacrifices.
lifetime: When, in the time of King David, the descendants of the priest Aaron were divided into twenty-four divisions to take charge of the temple service, he was designated as the head of the seventeenth division (1 Chronicles 24:1, 24:15).
event: When David organized the priests for the orderly operation of the temple, he was chosen by lot as the head of the seventeenth division, and through this the order of the temple service was established (1 Chronicles 24:15).

introduce: Helkai is one of the heads of the priests in the time of Joiakim recorded in Nehemiah 12, belonging to the clan of Meraioth.
lifetime: Helkai is recorded in the list of those who were heads of the priests in the time of Joiakim as the head of the clan of Meraioth (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:15).
event: In the list of the priestly heads in the time of Joiakim, his name is entered as the head of the clan of Meraioth, together with Adna of the clan of Harim (Nehemiah 12:15).

call: Netophathite (commander for the twelfth month in David's army)
introduce: Heldai is a man recorded as the twelfth commander, for the twelfth month, in the military organization of King David. He is recorded as a Netophathite of the line of Othniel.
lifetime: In the time of King David, the divisions serving the king took turns month by month throughout the year, each division numbering twenty-four thousand (1 Chronicles 27:1), and Heldai is recorded among them as the twelfth commander, for the twelfth month (1 Chronicles 27:15).
event: He is recorded as the twelfth commander, for the twelfth month, among the twelve divisions of David's military organization, in charge of a division of twenty-four thousand (1 Chronicles 27:15).

call: Pelonite (commander for the seventh month in David's army)
introduce: Helez was appointed commander of the army for the seventh month in David's army and is classed as one of David's thirty mighty men. The biblical record calls him a Pelonite.
lifetime: In the system of twelve divisions organized for David in his time, he is recorded as the seventh commander, for the seventh month (1 Chronicles 27:10). His name is also in the list of David's mighty men, appearing as Helez the Paltite in 2 Samuel 23:26 and as Helez the Pelonite in 1 Chronicles 11:27 (2 Samuel 23:26, 1 Chronicles 11:27).
event: In David's military organization he is recorded as the commander of the division for the seventh month, made up of twenty-four thousand men, and is said to be a Pelonite of the sons of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 27:10). He is also a person whose name is on the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:27).

call: son of Gilead (ancestor of the Helekite clan)
introduce: Helek is a son of Gilead the son of Machir, a descendant of Manasseh, and the ancestor of the Helekite clan, a subclan of the tribe of Manasseh, one of the tribes of Israel.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons of Gilead, who was born to Machir (Numbers 26:29-30). In the record of the census on the plains of Moab, he appears as the one who formed the Helekite family, a family of the tribe of Manasseh (Numbers 26:30).
event: When the people of Israel took the census on the plains of Moab, Helek was named as the ancestor of the Helekite clan that took his name (Numbers 26:30). Later, in the time of Joshua, in the process of receiving the land of Canaan by distribution, he was included, as a member of the tribe of Manasseh, in the system by which inheritance was allotted to each according to their clans (Joshua 17:2).

call: chief of the tribe of Asher
introduce: Helem is a man recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Beriah of the tribe of Asher, a younger brother of Shomer and the father of Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal (1 Chronicles 7:35).
lifetime: Helem is recorded as a younger brother of Shomer in the genealogy of the descendants of Beriah the son of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:30-32; 1 Chronicles 7:34-35). His family is included in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:40).
event: His sons recorded are Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal (1 Chronicles 7:35). All those recorded in this genealogy were descendants of Asher, heads of families, choice men, mighty warriors, chiefs of the princes, and those fit for service in war, counted by genealogy, numbered twenty-six thousand (1 Chronicles 7:40).

introduce: Heled was one of the thirty mighty men in the military organization of King David, a son of Baanah the Netophathite. He is recorded as one of the principal figures within David's elite military organization.
lifetime: He is singled out as one of David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23:29). Also, in the record of Chronicles, he is recorded as Heled the son of Baanah the Netophathite (a variant form of the name), and his name is entered once more in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:30).
event: Apart from being included in the list of mighty men who solidified King David's military foundation, no specific battle achievement or separate event that he himself carried out is recorded in detail in the Bible (2 Samuel 23:29).
character: In the biblical record nothing is mentioned about his personal character or physical features (1 Chronicles 11:30).

introduce: A man who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, the father of Eliab, the chief of the tribe of Zebulun (Numbers 1:9).
lifetime: In Numbers, Helon is mentioned only in the form "Eliab the son of Helon," introduced as the father of Eliab, the chief of the sons of Zebulun (Numbers 1:9, 2:7, 7:24). Helon's own deeds are not recorded.
event: His son Eliab, as the chief of the sons of Zebulun, brought his offering on the third day of the dedication (Numbers 7:24). The offering was one silver platter, one silver bowl, one gold dish, and the burnt offering, sin offering, and peace offering sacrifices (Numbers 7:25-29). Eliab also led the army of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun (Numbers 10:16).

introduce: A person who appears in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke in the New Testament, recorded as an ancestor of Joseph (Luke 3:23).
lifetime: Luke 3:23-24 states "Joseph, the son of Heli, the son of Matthat," and so he is recorded as the immediate forebear of Joseph. Going further up, the line reaches Nathan the son of David (Luke 3:31). Matthew 1:16 records Jacob as the one who fathered Joseph, so the relationship between the two genealogies is explained in different ways.

introduce: Hephzibah is the mother of Manasseh, the son of Hezekiah king of Judah (2 Kings 20:21, 21:1). Her name carries the meaning in Hebrew, "my delight is in her."
lifetime: The Bible does not record Hephzibah's origin or family line; her name appears only as the mother of Manasseh (2 Kings 21:1).
event: Her son Manasseh began to reign at the age of twelve and reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem (2 Kings 21:1).

call: second son of Canaan (ancestor of the Hittites)
introduce: A son of Ham the son of Noah and the second son of Canaan, the ancestor of the Hittites mentioned in the Bible.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons born to Canaan the son of Ham (Genesis 10:15).
event: His descendants settled in the land of Canaan and formed the group called the Hittites, who in later history developed into a people who had dealings with Abraham (Genesis 10:15, Genesis 23:3).

introduce: Hoglah is one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who appear in Numbers in the Old Testament. Zelophehad is recorded as belonging to the family of Manasseh the son of Joseph, a great-great-grandson of Manasseh, great-grandson of Machir, grandson of Gilead, and son of Hepher (Numbers 27:1).
lifetime: When her father Zelophehad died in the wilderness and had no sons, she, together with her sisters Mahlah, Noah, Milcah, and Tirzah, stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting before Moses, the priest Eleazar, the leaders, and the whole congregation, and asked that they be given an inheritance among their father's brothers (Numbers 27:1-4). Afterward, in accordance with the command that they should marry only into the family of their ancestral tribe, she married one of the sons of her father's brothers (Numbers 36:6, 36:11).
event: Hoglah and her sisters asked for an inheritance, saying that their father's name should not be removed from his family because he had no son (Numbers 27:4), and when Moses brought their case before the LORD, the LORD said that the daughters of Zelophehad spoke rightly and told him to give them an inheritance (Numbers 27:5-7). This became a statute of judgment that if a man died without a son, his inheritance should pass to his daughter (Numbers 27:8-11). They also, as the LORD commanded that the inheritance should not pass from one tribe to another, married the sons of their father's brothers within the same tribe (Numbers 36:5-12).

introduce: Hodaviah is a man recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin; his name appears in the genealogy of Sallu, a descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:3, 9:7).
lifetime: Sallu is the son of Meshullam, the grandson of Hodaviah, and the great-grandson of Hassenuah (1 Chronicles 9:7). In this genealogy Hodaviah is the son of Hassenuah, the father of Meshullam, and the grandfather of Sallu.
event: The Bible records no specific event of Hodaviah himself, and his name is mentioned only in the genealogy of Sallu, a descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:7).

call: chief of the half-tribe of Manasseh
introduce: One of the heads of the half-tribe of Manasseh recorded in 1 Chronicles, a man who lived in the region of Bashan east of the Jordan.
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of the chiefs of the families that were heads of the half-tribe of Manasseh, together with Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, as mighty men of valor and famous chiefs (1 Chronicles 5:24).
event: The people of the half-tribe of Manasseh to which he belonged sinned against the God of their fathers and prostituted themselves to the gods of the peoples of the land whom God had destroyed before them (1 Chronicles 5:25), and because of this the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh were carried away captive by the king of Assyria (1 Chronicles 5:26).
character: The biblical text classifies him as a mighty man of valor and a famous chief, but nothing separate is described about his personal character or specific deeds (1 Chronicles 5:24).

introduce: Hodesh is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the wives of Shaharaim.
lifetime: Hodesh appears as "his wife Hodesh" in the record that Shaharaim had children in the land of Moab after he sent away his two wives Hushim and Baara (1 Chronicles 8:8-9). Those she bore to him were Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam (1 Chronicles 8:9), Jeuz, Sachia, and Mirmah (1 Chronicles 8:10).

introduce: Hodevah is a man whose name appears in the list of returnees in Nehemiah 7 as the name of a family among the Levites (Nehemiah 7:43).
lifetime: Nehemiah 7:43 records, "The Levites: the descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the descendants of Hodevah, seventy-four." In the parallel text of Ezra 2:40 it appears as "the descendants of Hodaviah."
event: No specific event of Hodevah himself is recorded, and his descendants (the descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiel) are recorded in the list of returnees as seventy-four (Nehemiah 7:43).

call: Figure in Judah's genealogy whose wife was Naham's sister
introduce: Hodiah is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, and her name appears in 1 Chronicles 4:19.
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 4:19 records that "the sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham, were the father of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maacathite."

기타관계: Naham#359(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: Hothir is a man who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, one of the descendants of Levi who were in charge of praise and instrumental music in the temple in the time of King David.
lifetime: Hothir was one of the sons of Heman, belonging to the family appointed by David to the duty of praise that he had set apart (1 Chronicles 25:1, 25:4). In the order of the duties assigned by lot he was recorded twenty-first, with twelve in all, his sons and brothers (1 Chronicles 25:28).
event: Hothir, as one of the sons of Heman in the duty of praise that David set apart for service, belonged to those who sang in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps, and lyres (1 Chronicles 25:4-6). His duty was determined by lot, small and great alike, and he was chosen twenty-first (1 Chronicles 25:8, 25:28).

introduce: Horam was king of Gezer at the time of the war of the conquest of Canaan, the man who came up to help Lachish when Joshua struck Lachish (Joshua 10:33).
lifetime: Horam is recorded as king of Gezer, and he came up to help Lachish at the time when Joshua advanced with all Israel to Lachish, fought, and took the city (Joshua 10:31-32). Joshua struck him and his people until he left no survivor (Joshua 10:33).
event: Horam, coming up to help Lachish, was defeated by Joshua, and the Bible records that not one of him and his people was left (Joshua 10:33).

introduce: Hori was a native who lived in the hill country of Seir in the land of Edom, a grandson of Seir and a son of Lotan (Genesis 36:20-22).
lifetime:
He was born to Lotan, a son of Seir of the Horite clan (1 Chronicles 1:38-39).
His brother was Hemam (Homam in 1 Chronicles 1:39), and his aunt was Timna (Genesis 36:22).
Beyond the mention of his name in the genealogy of the Bible, no specific record concerning his birth or death appears (1 Chronicles 1:39).

introduce: Hubbah is a man of the tribe of Asher recorded in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a son of Shomer (1 Chronicles 7:34).
lifetime: Hubbah is recorded as one of the sons of Shomer: Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram (1 Chronicles 7:34). Shomer is recorded as a son of Heber (1 Chronicles 7:32).

introduce: Hobaiah is the name of a priestly family that returned from the Babylonian captivity, and it appears as "the descendants of Hobaiah" in the list of returnees in Nehemiah 7 (Nehemiah 7:63).
lifetime: In Nehemiah 7:63 it is "the descendants of Hobaiah" among the priests, and in the parallel text Ezra 2:61 it is recorded as "the descendants of Hobaiah" (a variant spelling of the name). They were recorded together with the descendants of Hakkoz and the descendants of Barzillai.
event: The descendants of Hobaiah searched for their registration among those enrolled by genealogy but did not find it, and so were regarded as unclean and could not carry out the priestly office (Nehemiah 7:64, Ezra 2:62), and the governor ordered that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest arose with Urim and Thummim (Nehemiah 7:65, Ezra 2:63).

call: Levite of Merari (head of the gatekeepers of the west gate of the temple)
introduce: Hosah is a man who appears in 1 Chronicles, a gatekeeper belonging to the descendants of Merari of the tribe of Levi. He is recorded as one who carried out duties connected with the temple service in the time of David.
lifetime: Hosah is recorded as a descendant of Merari, and he had sons. The firstborn was Shimri, who was not originally the firstborn but whom his father Hosah made the firstborn; the second was Hilkiah, the third Tebaliah, and the fourth Zechariah, and the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen in all (1 Chronicles 26:10-11). He is also recorded as one of those whom David appointed as gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 16:38).
event: Hosah, as the head of a division of gatekeepers, was one of those who served in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:12); by lot he and Shuppim were assigned the west, and they kept watch opposite each other beside the gate of Shallecheth, on the road that goes up (1 Chronicles 26:13, 26:16).

introduce: Hoshama is a descendant of the house of David in the tribe of Judah, a man recorded in the genealogy as one of the sons of Jeconiah the captive (1 Chronicles 3:17-18).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons of Jeconiah the captive (1 Chronicles 3:17-18). They are recorded in the order Shealtiel, Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah, so his name stands sixth of the seven sons (1 Chronicles 3:17-18).

introduce: Hoshaiah is a man who appears in the book of Jeremiah in the Old Testament as "Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah" (Jeremiah 42:1) and "Azariah the son of Hoshaiah" (Jeremiah 43:2), and is recorded only as the father of his sons.
lifetime: Hoshaiah's own life and deeds are not recorded in the Bible; he is mentioned only before the names of his sons Jezaniah and Azariah (Jeremiah 42:1, 43:2).
event: His son Jezaniah came to Jeremiah together with all the commanders of the forces and Johanan the son of Kareah (Jeremiah 42:1). And his son Azariah, together with Johanan the son of Kareah and all the arrogant men, said to Jeremiah, "You are telling a lie," and rejected the word of the LORD that they should not go to Egypt (Jeremiah 43:2).

introduce: Hozai is a person mentioned in 2 Chronicles 33:19 under the name "the records of Hozai." This record contains facts about the prayer and sin of Manasseh king of Judah (2 Chronicles 33:19).
lifetime: Hozai's birth, family line, and time of activity are not recorded in the Bible, and he is mentioned only as "the records of Hozai" in 2 Chronicles 33:19.
event: Manasseh's prayer and how God received his plea, all his sin and unfaithfulness, and the sites where he built high places and set up Asherah poles and idols before he humbled himself, were written in the records of Hozai (2 Chronicles 33:19).

introduce: Hoshaiah is a man mentioned together with half of the leaders of Judah who went up on the wall at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 12:32).
lifetime: When the wall of Jerusalem was completed and the dedication was held, the leaders of Judah went up on the wall and were divided into two companies to proceed in procession; he is recorded, together with half of the leaders of Judah, as one who followed one of the companies (Nehemiah 12:27, 12:31-32). Hoshaiah's family line and the rest of his life are not recorded.
event: In Nehemiah 12:31, when the great company of those who gave thanks was divided into two companies to proceed in procession on the wall, one company went to the right toward the Dung Gate, and Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah followed behind them (Nehemiah 12:31-32).

introduce: Hoham was an Amorite king who ruled Hebron in the time of Joshua. When Gibeon made peace with Israel, he appears as a member of the alliance of five kings of southern Canaan formed to oppose it.
lifetime: When Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel (Joshua 10:1), he sent word to Hoham king of Hebron and others, asking them to join in striking Gibeon (Joshua 10:3-4). Hoham, as king of Hebron, assembled together with the other four kings to attack Gibeon (Joshua 10:5). After being defeated by the army of Israel, he was found hiding in the cave at Makkedah and was reported to Joshua (Joshua 10:16-17), and afterward he was put to death by Joshua (Joshua 10:26).
event: When Gibeon made peace with Israel, to punish this he formed a military alliance with the five kings of southern Canaan and attacked Gibeon (Joshua 10:5). Defeated in battle with Israel and fleeing, he hid in the cave at Makkedah, but at Joshua's command he was brought out of the cave (Joshua 10:16, 10:22-23). At Joshua's command the commanders of Israel put their feet on his neck, and afterward Joshua killed him and hung him on a tree, and in the evening the bodies were taken down and thrown into the cave (Joshua 10:24-27).

introduce: A son of Eli the priest who carried out priestly duties at the sanctuary at Shiloh. He is mentioned together with Phinehas as one of Eli's two sons and was active in the early part of 1 Samuel (1 Samuel 1:3).
lifetime: Born a son of Eli the priest, he served as a priest at the sanctuary of the LORD at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1:3). When the ark of the covenant of God was brought from Shiloh to the camp of Israel, he was with the ark together with Phinehas (1 Samuel 4:4), and in the battle between Israel and the Philistines he was killed together with Phinehas (1 Samuel 4:11).
event: In taking the sacrificial offerings, he disregarded the established ordinance and committed the act of having the priest's servant forcibly take the meat (1 Samuel 2:13-16). He also engaged in improper conduct, such as lying with the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting (1 Samuel 2:22), and the sin of these young men was very great in the sight of the LORD, for they despised the offering of the LORD (1 Samuel 2:17). In the battle with the Philistines the ark was captured and he was killed together with Phinehas (1 Samuel 4:11).
character: He showed conduct of one who did not know the LORD, and had the attitude of abusing the priestly office for private gain (1 Samuel 2:12). He heard the admonition of his father Eli, but did not listen to his words because the LORD had already determined to put them to death (1 Samuel 2:25).

introduce: Huram is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin in the Old Testament, a son of Bela (1 Chronicles 8:3-5).
lifetime:
He was born a son of Bela, the firstborn of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:1-5).
His brothers were Addar, Gera, Abihud, Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah, Gera, and Shephuphan (1 Chronicles 8:3-5).
Beyond this, no specific record of his life or death appears in the Bible (1 Chronicles 8:5).

introduce: Hurai is a man who appears in the list of David's mighty men in the time of the reign of King David, recorded as one who lived by the brooks of Gaash (1 Chronicles 11:32). In the parallel list of mighty men in 2 Samuel, in the same place appears "Hiddai from the brooks of Gaash" (2 Samuel 23:30).
lifetime: Hurai is recorded as one who lived by the brooks of Gaash (1 Chronicles 11:32). His name is entered in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:32).

introduce: Hur was one of the five kings of Midian, a man mentioned in the course of Israel's conquest of Midian.
lifetime: When the people of Israel struck Midian as the LORD had commanded Moses, he was named among the five kings of Midian (Numbers 31:7-8). He is one of the kings of Midian who were killed by Israel (Numbers 31:8).
event: When the people of Israel struck Midian and killed every male, they also killed the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba (Numbers 31:7-8).

introduce: Huri is a man who appears in 1 Chronicles 5:14, one of the ancestors of the families that make up the genealogy of the tribe of Gad. As the son of Jaroah and the father of Abihail, he serves as an intermediate link that forms the family tree of the tribe of Gad (1 Chronicles 5:14).
lifetime: Huri was a descendant of the tribe of Gad; his father was Jaroah and his son was Abihail (1 Chronicles 5:14). The text records Abihail as Huri's son, Jaroah's grandson, Gilead's great-grandson, and Michael's great-great-grandson, and above them Jeshishai, Jahdo, and Buz are listed in order (1 Chronicles 5:14).

introduce: Hymenaeus is a person who appears in the New Testament, mentioned in the letters of the apostle Paul as a critical example of one who opposed the sound teaching of the church and spread false doctrine.
lifetime: In connection with the church in the region of Ephesus, he was active within the community under the guidance of the apostle Paul (1 Timothy 1:3, 1:19-20). He is mentioned together with Alexander and was delivered to Satan by the apostle Paul (1 Timothy 1:20). He is also recorded as one who, together with Philetus, spread false teaching about the resurrection (2 Timothy 2:17).
event: By claiming that the resurrection had already taken place, he brought about the result of overthrowing the faith of believers (2 Timothy 2:18). Such teaching became a cause of people advancing further in ungodliness (2 Timothy 2:16). Therefore Paul delivered Hymenaeus, together with Alexander, to Satan, so that they might be disciplined and not blaspheme (1 Timothy 1:20).
character: He engaged in profane and empty chatter (2 Timothy 2:16), and in misinterpreting the word of God he showed words and conduct that harmed the community (2 Timothy 2:17). Paul judged that his words and conduct had the nature of spreading like a malignant growth (2 Timothy 2:17).

meaning: he protects the dwellers of the coast
introduce: Hupham was a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, a man belonging to the genealogy of Benjamin the son of Jacob. In the census list of the people of Israel recorded in Numbers 26, he is mentioned as the ancestor of the Huphamite family, one of the clans of the descendants of Benjamin (Numbers 26:38-39).
lifetime: Hupham is the man whose name became that of the Huphamite family, one of the clans of the tribe of Benjamin, and his name can be confirmed in the second census conducted on the plains of Moab as "of Hupham, the Huphamite family" (Numbers 26:39).
event: When Moses and the priest Eleazar counted the clans of each tribe of Israel on the plains of Moab, he was included in that genealogy as the ancestor of the Huphamite clan of the tribe of Benjamin (Numbers 26:3, 26:39).

introduce: Hushah is a name in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah; 1 Chronicles 4:4 records Ezer as "the father of Hushah" (1 Chronicles 4:4).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 4:4 records Ezer, the father of Hushah, as descended from Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, the father of Bethlehem (1 Chronicles 4:4). No other record about Hushah himself appears in this verse.
event: The biblical text contains no separate record of any specific achievement Hushah performed or of any historical event connected with him (1 Chronicles 4:4).

introduce: Husham was one of the kings who ruled the land of Edom, a man from the land of the Temanites (Genesis 36:34). He is recorded as a ruler who continued the line of succession to the throne among the descendants of Esau, the ancestor of Israel (1 Chronicles 1:45).
lifetime: Husham was a man of the land of the Temanite clan, and after Jobab died he became king of Edom in his place (Genesis 36:34, 1 Chronicles 1:45). After his death, Hadad the son of Bedad became king in his place (Genesis 36:35, 1 Chronicles 1:46).
event: As ruler of the land of Edom, he became king in place of Jobab after his death, and after Husham died, Hadad the son of Bedad became king in his place (Genesis 36:34, Genesis 36:35).

introduce: Hushai was an Archite who was active in the time of King David, a friend and political counselor of David. At the time of Absalom's rebellion he acted as David's spy and played a decisive role in preserving the legitimacy of David's dynasty.
lifetime: When David left Jerusalem to flee from the rebellion of his son Absalom, Hushai met David, and David told him to return to Jerusalem and defeat the counsel of Ahithophel, Absalom's counselor (2 Samuel 15:32-34). As David commanded, he went to Absalom and said, "Long live the king!" and that he would serve the king (2 Samuel 16:16-19), and afterward he refuted Ahithophel's strategy and gained time for David to escape (2 Samuel 17:5-14).
event: When Ahithophel proposed in the camp of Absalom's rebel army a strategy of immediately pursuing David, Hushai stressed David's valor and military experience and proposed a strategy of delay (2 Samuel 17:7-13). Because Absalom and all the men of Israel said that the counsel of Hushai was better than the counsel of Ahithophel, Hushai's strategy was adopted (2 Samuel 17:14), and David was able to cross the Jordan and escape (2 Samuel 17:22). He informed the priests Zadok and Abiathar of this information so that it would be passed on to David (2 Samuel 17:15-16).
character: He was a loyal friend to David (2 Samuel 15:37) and a diplomat of outstanding strategic insight. In the enemy camp he hid his identity and possessed highly skilled psychological tactics and persuasiveness for winning the other side's trust (2 Samuel 16:18-19). As a faithful retainer trusted by David, he used his wisdom even in dangerous situations and contributed to the restoration of the kingship (2 Samuel 17:14).

introduce: Hur was a man of the tribe of Judah, the son whom Caleb son of Hezron fathered by Ephrath, the father of Uri and the grandfather of Bezalel (1 Chronicles 2:19-20). The Book of Exodus introduces Bezalel, the craftsman of the tabernacle, as "the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah" (Exodus 31:2; 35:30; 38:22). Whether he is the same Hur who helped Moses together with Aaron in Exodus 17 and 24 is not indicated in the text (Jewish tradition regards them as the same person).
lifetime: Hur is recorded as the firstborn son of Caleb and Ephrath (Ephrathah) (1 Chronicles 2:19, 50; 4:4). He fathered Uri, and Uri fathered Bezalel (1 Chronicles 2:20). First Chronicles records Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim, Salma the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph the father of Beth-gader as sons of Hur (1 Chronicles 2:50-51), and it also records Penuel and Ezer as descendants of Hur (1 Chronicles 4:4).
event: Hur's grandson Bezalel was filled with the Spirit of God and made the tabernacle and its furnishings (Exodus 31:2-5; 38:22), and the bronze altar that Bezalel made was still before the tabernacle of the LORD in the time of Solomon (2 Chronicles 1:5).

introduce: Huldah was a female prophet who was active in the time of King Josiah of the kingdom of Judah. She lived in the Second District of Jerusalem and was the wife of Shallum, who was in charge of the wardrobe at that time.
lifetime: Huldah received the delegation that King Josiah sent to ascertain the content of the book of the law found while the temple was being repaired (2 Kings 22:14). She was living in the Second District of Jerusalem at that time (2 Chronicles 34:22). Her husband Shallum, a grandson of Harhas and son of Tikvah, held the office in charge of the wardrobe (2 Kings 22:14). In 2 Chronicles 34:22 Shallum is recorded as the son of Tokhath, the grandson of Hasrah.
event: Fearing the wrath of God that would come upon Judah because of the words of the book of the law that was found, King Josiah sent men to Huldah to inquire of the will of God (2 Kings 22:13). Huldah prophesied that the God of Israel would bring disaster upon the king of Judah and the people, but since King Josiah, on hearing the words of the law, had become tender-hearted and humbled himself before God, she replied that the disaster would not be brought in the king's lifetime (2 Kings 22:15-20). Hearing this prophecy, King Josiah gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem and carried out a reform by renewing the covenant in the temple (2 Kings 23:1-3).
character: Huldah was recognized as a prophet of such authority that the priests and the king's envoys went to her in person to inquire of the will of God (2 Kings 22:14). She had a close relationship with the royal house, and as a prophet she carried out the role of pointing out the king's wrongdoing and delivering a firm and clear oracle concerning the fate of the nation (2 Kings 22:16-17).

introduce: Huppah is a man recorded in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, the ancestor of the family that was in charge of the thirteenth division of the priestly divisions established in the time of David.
lifetime: Huppah was a member of a priestly family of the descendants of Aaron, and when David divided the duties of the descendants of Levi and determined the priestly divisions, he was the one in charge of the thirteenth division (1 Chronicles 24:13).
event: When King David organized the duties of the priests and Levites, he was recorded as the head of the thirteenth of the twenty-four divisions determined by lot (1 Chronicles 24:13).

introduce: Hiram was king of Tyre, a ruler who maintained close diplomatic and economic relations with King David and King Solomon of Israel. He is recorded as having sent David messengers, cedar, carpenters, and stonemasons to help build his palace, and as having supplied Solomon with cedar, cypress, and gold (2 Samuel 5:11, 1 Kings 9:11).
lifetime: When David became king, he sent a delegation with cedar, carpenters, and stonemasons so that David's palace might be built (2 Samuel 5:11). When he heard that David had died and Solomon had become king, he sent envoys to him to confirm the friendly relationship (1 Kings 5:1). Afterward he made a treaty with Solomon and began supplying materials for the building of the temple (1 Kings 5:12). After Solomon's building of the temple and the palace was completed, he received twenty cities in the land of Galilee in payment for the cost of the building but was not pleased with them (1 Kings 9:11-12).
event: He supported the building of David's palace with cedar and craftsmen (2 Samuel 5:11). For Solomon's building of the temple he cut cedar and cypress timber of Lebanon and sent it floating by sea, and Solomon in return provided wheat and oil (1 Kings 5:8-11). He sent his own servants, sailors familiar with the sea, with Solomon's servants in ships to bring gold from Ophir (1 Kings 9:27-28). He also sent a hundred twenty talents of gold to Solomon (1 Kings 9:14). He received twenty cities in the land of Galilee from Solomon but called them the land of Cabul (1 Kings 9:11-13).
character: All his life he loved David and maintained a friendly relationship with his son Solomon as well (1 Kings 5:1). He had a practical diplomatic sense, actively cooperating with the reign and building projects of Solomon, who is described as a wise son (1 Kings 5:7). He showed a clear and realistic attitude in economic interests, as when he immediately expressed his displeasure that the cities received from Solomon did not meet his standards (1 Kings 9:12-13).

introduce: Hizki is a person who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as one of the sons of Elpaal (1 Chronicles 8:17-18).
lifetime: Hizki is recorded as one of the sons of Elpaal of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:17-18). No other specific record of his life appears in the Bible.

call: thirteenth king of Southern Judah (a good reformer)
introduce: Hezekiah was the thirteenth king to rule the kingdom of Southern Judah around the eighth century BC, the son of King Ahaz and a successor of the house of David (2 Kings 18:1). He ascended the throne at the age of twenty-five and reigned in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years (2 Chronicles 29:1), and he is recorded as one who carried out a religious reform, rejecting the king of Assyria and refusing to serve him, and removing the high places (2 Kings 18:4, 18:7).
lifetime: He ascended the throne at the age of twenty-five and reigned for twenty-nine years (2 Kings 18:2). Immediately after taking the throne he repaired the doors of the temple and summoned the priests and the Levites to perform a rite of consecration (2 Chronicles 29:3-5). When Sennacherib of Assyria invaded, he received Sennacherib's letter and went up to the house of the LORD to pray (2 Kings 19:14-15); and after he fell ill and was at the point of death but recovered, he received the envoys of Babylon (2 Kings 20:12).
event: He carried out a religious reform in which he removed the high places, broke the pillars, and cut down the Asherah pole (2 Kings 18:4). In preparation for the Assyrian invasion he repaired the broken-down wall, stopped the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon, and directed the water straight down to the west side of the city of David (2 Chronicles 32:5, 32:30). He restored the festival of the Passover and invited the people, including those from Northern Israel, to Jerusalem to keep it together (2 Chronicles 30:1). Furthermore, when the army of Sennacherib king of Assyria threatened Jerusalem and Hezekiah, together with Isaiah, cried out in prayer to heaven (2 Chronicles 32:20), the angel of the LORD struck down 185,000 soldiers in the camp of Assyria (2 Kings 19:35).
character: Compared with the earlier kings of Judah, he was judged to have followed all that David had done (2 Kings 18:3). In a national crisis he showed the attitude of seeking the counsel of the prophet Isaiah and offering prayer in the temple (2 Kings 19:14). Yet he also displayed an ostentatious side, showing the envoys of Babylon all his treasure houses and military supplies (2 Kings 20:13). There is a record that in his later years, after being proud of heart because of his healing and the extension of his life, he turned back from it and humbled himself (2 Chronicles 32:26).

introduce: Hiel is a person recorded as a Bethelite in the time of Ahab of the kingdom of Northern Israel, and the man who built Jericho.
lifetime: Hiel built Jericho in the time of King Ahab (1 Kings 16:34). When he laid its foundation he lost Abiram his firstborn, and when he set up its gates he lost Segub his youngest son (1 Kings 16:34).
event: He built Jericho (1 Kings 16:34). In this matter it came about according to the word that the LORD spoke by Joshua the son of Nun (1 Kings 16:34, Joshua 6:26).

call: the man from whom the Valley of the Son of Hinnom took its origin
introduce: Hinnom is a person who appears in the name of the "Valley of the Son of Hinnom" south of Jerusalem (the place where Topheth was); the Korean Revised Version calls this valley "the valley of the son of Hinnom" or "the valley of Hinnom", and there is no record about Hinnom himself. This valley is recorded as the place where the idolatry of making children pass through the fire to Molech was practiced (2 Kings 23:10, Jeremiah 32:35).
lifetime: At the distribution of the land of Canaan in the time of Joshua it is mentioned as the valley that formed the boundary between the tribe of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin (Joshua 15:8, 18:16), and in Old Testament history the valley bearing his name appears as an important geographical setting.
event: In the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, kings of Southern Judah such as Ahaz and Manasseh practiced the idolatry of burning their children (2 Chronicles 28:3, 33:6), King Josiah defiled Topheth in that valley (2 Kings 23:10), and through the prophet Jeremiah a judgment was proclaimed that the place would be called the Valley of Slaughter (Jeremiah 7:31-32).

call: father of Eliakim (father of the palace administrator)
introduce: He is the father of Eliakim, who served as palace administrator in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah.
lifetime: He is mentioned as the father of Eliakim the palace administrator in the time of King Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:18). Also, as the father of Eliakim the palace administrator (the spelling in the book of Isaiah is Eliakim), among those who went out to Rabshakeh, he is recorded as "the son of Hilkiah" in Isaiah 36:3 as well (Isaiah 36:3).
event: He is mentioned only by the identity "the son of Hilkiah", in passages that record not any specific deeds of his own but his son Eliakim going out as palace administrator to meet Rabshakeh (2 Kings 18:18, 18:37). He is also mentioned indirectly as his father when Eliakim (the spelling in the book of Isaiah is Eliakim), having heard the words of Rabshakeh, tore his clothes and went to Hezekiah to report those words (Isaiah 36:22).

introduce: The name Hillel mentioned in the Bible refers to a man from Pirathon, who was the father of Abdon, a judge of Israel (Judges 12:13).
lifetime: Hillel was a Pirathonite, and Pirathon is in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites (Judges 12:13, 12:15). He is recorded as the father of the judge Abdon (Judges 12:13, Judges 12:15).
event: Apart from the record that his son Abdon judged Israel for eight years, no specific achievement or event of Hillel himself is mentioned (Judges 12:13-14). There is only the record that Abdon died and was buried in Pirathon (Judges 12:15).

introduce: Joshua the son of Nun was a leader of ancient Israel, the man who, after the death of Moses, led the people of Israel and carried out the war of conquest of Canaan. A member of the tribe of Ephraim, he took charge of military operations and administrative assistance in the course of the exodus.
lifetime: Joshua first showed military leadership by commanding the battle against Amalek at Rephidim (Exodus 17:9). Afterward, as Moses' assistant, he did not depart from the tent of meeting and attended Moses (Exodus 33:11). He was active as one of the twelve sent to spy out Canaan (Numbers 13:8), and after Moses he was appointed the supreme leader of Israel (Deuteronomy 34:9). After leading the war of conquest of Canaan, he died at the age of 110 (Joshua 24:29).
event: He crossed the Jordan River and entered Canaan (Joshua 3:17), and carried out the tactics by which the city of Jericho fell (Joshua 6:20). After the defeat in the battle of the city of Ai, he regrouped and completed its capture (Joshua 8:28), and he led to victory the treaty with the inhabitants of Gibeon and the battles with the coalitions of southern and northern Canaan (Joshua 10:42, 11:23). Afterward he finished the work of distributing the conquered land of Canaan among the tribes of Israel (Joshua 18:10, 19:51).
character: He showed himself as a loyal aide who carried out Moses' commands thoroughly (Numbers 27:18). Also, at the time of spying out Canaan, unlike the other spies, he was not swept along by the majority opinion but had the resolute attitude of making an independent judgment (Numbers 14:6-7). In his old age he exercised influence as a leader by urging the people to make a decision at Shechem (Joshua 24:15).
