Eliel#4208(fellow worker of the tribe of Levi)
Jerimoth#4243(fellow worker of the tribe of Levi)

introduce: Chenaanah appears in 1 Chronicles chapter 7 as a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, a son of Bilhan the son of Jediael (1 Chronicles 7:10).
lifetime: Chenaanah is recorded as the son of Bilhan the son of Jediael of the tribe of Benjamin, and his brothers are Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar (1 Chronicles 7:10).
event: The text records that these sons of Jediael were heads of their families and mighty men of valor, and that among their descendants those fit to go out to war numbered 17,200 (1 Chronicles 7:10-11).
character: According to the biblical record, together with his brothers he was classed as a mighty man of valor and held the position of a core leader making up the military strength of the family (1 Chronicles 7:11).

call: Son of Shiphtan (leader of the tribe of Ephraim)
introduce: Kemuel is a figure who appears in the book of Numbers, a leader of the tribe of Ephraim and a son of Shiphtan (Numbers 34:24).
lifetime: Kemuel is recorded as the leader of the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim among those whom the LORD appointed to distribute the inheritance to the Israelites in the land of Canaan (Numbers 34:18, 34:24, 34:29).
event: When the LORD told Moses to choose one leader from each tribe to distribute the land of inheritance, Kemuel son of Shiphtan, leader of the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim, was recorded in that list (Numbers 34:17-18, 34:24).

call: The Geshurite clan of the south
introduce: A people who lived in the southern part of the land of Canaan, and a group mentioned as one of the areas that Israel had not conquered in the time of Joshua.
lifetime: When the land of Canaan was being allotted to Israel, the whole territory of the Geshurites is recorded, together with all the regions of the Philistines, among the remaining land not conquered by Joshua (Joshua 13:2-3). In David's time they appear as inhabitants who had lived from ancient times in the land toward Shur and Egypt (1 Samuel 27:8).
event: While David lived in Ziklag, he raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites, leaving neither man nor woman alive, and took sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and clothing, and returned to Achish (1 Samuel 27:6-9). When Achish asked whom he had raided, David answered that it was the Negev of Judah, the Negev of the Jerahmeelites, and the Negev of the Kenites (1 Samuel 27:10).

call: Father of Ezri (father of the royal agricultural overseer)
introduce: Chelub is a figure mentioned as the father of Ezri, who was over the field workers who tilled the soil, in the list of those in charge of the property of King David (1 Chronicles 27:25-26, 27:31).
lifetime: Chelub is recorded only as the father of Ezri (1 Chronicles 27:26). The text has no record of his tribe or genealogy.

introduce: Kish is a figure recorded in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles chapter 9 as a son of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon, and one of the brothers who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:35-38).
lifetime: Kish is recorded as a son of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon (1 Chronicles 9:35-36). Jeiel lived in Gibeon, and his wife's name was Maacah (1 Chronicles 9:35).
event: His brothers are recorded as Abdon the firstborn, and Zur, Baal, Ner, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth, and they lived in Jerusalem opposite one another (1 Chronicles 9:36-38). No specific event carried out by Kish himself is recorded.

introduce: Kish is a man belonging to the descendants of Merari of the tribe of Levi, a son of Mahli. He holds a place within the genealogical system of the Levites in the record of Chronicles.
lifetime: Kish was born as a son of Mahli, a descendant of Merari (1 Chronicles 23:21). When Eleazar son of Mahli died without sons and had only daughters, the sons of Kish, his brother, married them (1 Chronicles 23:21-22).
event: Kish had a son, Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 24:29). No special achievement or historical event carried out by Kish himself is specifically recorded in the biblical text.

call: Son of Abdi (Levite in Hezekiah's time)
introduce: Kish was a descendant of Levi who took part in the work of cleansing the temple in the time of King Hezekiah. He is recorded as a son of Abdi, a descendant of Merari.
lifetime: When Hezekiah king of Judah began the work of consecrating the temple, the Levites set to work, and among them the name of Kish is recorded as the son of Abdi, a descendant of Merari (2 Chronicles 29:12).
event: The Levites whose names are listed in 2 Chronicles 29:12 assembled their brothers, consecrated themselves, and cleansed the house of the LORD according to the command of the king by the words of the LORD (2 Chronicles 29:15). The Levites carried out to the Kidron Valley the unclean things that the priests had brought out from inside the temple (2 Chronicles 29:16).

introduce: Kish was a man of the tribe of Benjamin, the great-grandfather of Mordecai, and a figure who appears in the family genealogy of Queen Esther.
lifetime: He was a man of the tribe of Benjamin. Since Esther 2:5 records Mordecai as "the great-grandson of Kish and the grandson of Shimei," Kish is the father of Shimei. Esther gives no record of Kish's father (Esther 2:5).
event: Kish is recorded only as the great-grandfather of Mordecai, and there is no record of his deeds or of any particular event (Esther 2:5). The exile from Jerusalem is recorded concerning Mordecai (Esther 2:6).

introduce: Gilead is a figure who appears in the book of Judges, recorded as the father of Jephthah the Gileadite, a mighty man of valor (Judges 11:1).
lifetime: A prostitute bore Jephthah to Gilead (Judges 11:1), and Gilead's wife also bore sons (Judges 11:2). No other record concerning his birth or lineage appears in these verses.
event: The sons born to his wife grew up and drove Jephthah out, saying to him, "You shall have no inheritance in our father's house, because you are the son of another woman" (Judges 11:2). This was done by the sons of Gilead's wife, and the text does not record any action of Gilead himself.

call: Son of Michael of the tribe of Gad
introduce: Gilead is a figure of the tribe of Gad who appears in 1 Chronicles 5:14, the great-grandfather of Abihail, a son of Michael, and the father of Jaroah. The Gilead of this entry is recorded as a person's name, not a place name.
lifetime: In the genealogy of Abihail of the tribe of Gad, Abihail is the son of Huri, the grandson of Jaroah, the great-grandson of Gilead, and the great-great-grandson of Michael (1 Chronicles 5:14). Therefore Gilead is the son of Michael and the father of Jaroah.

call: The territory and hill country of Gilead east of the Jordan
introduce: The Gilead of this entry is not a person but a place name (a territory and hill country). In the text it appears as Mount Gilead (Genesis 31:21), the hill country of Gilead (Deuteronomy 3:12), and the land of Gilead, their possession (Joshua 22:9). The Gilead who is the son of Machir and becomes the name of the Gilead family (Numbers 26:29) has a separate person entry.
lifetime: Since this is a place name, there is no record of birth, death, or other matters of an individual's life. There is a record that Jacob crossed the river with all that he had and fled toward Mount Gilead (Genesis 31:21).
event: Moses gave half of the hill country of Gilead and its cities, from Aroer by the Arnon Valley, to the Reubenites and the Gadites (Deuteronomy 3:12). The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh left the Israelites at Shiloh and returned to Gilead, their possession, which they had acquired (Joshua 22:9).

introduce: Giddel is a figure classified as one of the descendants of Solomon's servants recorded in the list of those who returned from exile (Ezra 2:56, Nehemiah 7:58).
lifetime: His name is included in the list of those who returned to Jerusalem and Judah with Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:2, 2:56). His name and affiliation are also recorded identically in the list that Nehemiah compiled in examining the genealogy of the returnees from exile (Nehemiah 7:5, 7:58).
event: As a member of the community of Israel, he was included in the census list of the returnees who came back from Babylon to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:56, Nehemiah 7:58).

call: The coasts and islands of Kittim
introduce: In the Bible, Kittim is used mainly as a son of Javan, and as a term designating a place on the Mediterranean coast or the people living there. From the standpoint of ancient Near Eastern studies, Kittim is interpreted as meaning the Mediterranean island of Cyprus or the coastal region nearby.
lifetime: Kittim was recorded in the genealogy after Noah's flood as a grandson of Noah's son Japheth and a son of Javan (Genesis 10:4).
event: Kittim also appears as the name of coasts and islands. In Balaam's prophecy, it says that ships will come from the coasts of Kittim to afflict Asshur and to afflict Eber (Numbers 24:24), and in the oracle concerning Tyre, word was said to have reached Tyre from the land of Kittim (Isaiah 23:1). Jeremiah said to cross over to the islands of Kittim and look, and to send to Kedar and observe (Jeremiah 2:10), and in Ezekiel 27:6 the boxwood of the islands of Kittim appears as material for the deck of Tyre. In Daniel 11:30 there is a prophecy that ships of Kittim will come against him.

introduce: Nacon is a name that appears in 2 Samuel 6:6 in the place name "the threshing floor of Nacon." In 1 Chronicles 13:9 the location of the same event is recorded as "the threshing floor of Chidon." The text has no record of who Nacon was.
lifetime: The Bible has no record of Nacon's personal life, birth, or family relationships. There is only the record that in David's time the company carrying the ark of God came to the threshing floor of Nacon (2 Samuel 6:6).
event: As David's company was moving the ark of God, when they came to the threshing floor of Nacon the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out his hand and took hold of the ark (2 Samuel 6:6). The anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah for his irreverence, and He struck him down there, and he died beside the ark (2 Samuel 6:7), and David called that place Perez-uzzah (2 Samuel 6:8). Chronicles records the same place as the threshing floor of Chidon (1 Chronicles 13:9).

Chidon#251(name in the parallel record of 1 Chronicles 13:9)

introduce: Nathan was a prophet and recorder who was active in the era of the Davidic dynasty, and as an adviser to the royal house he was deeply involved in political and religious decision-making. At key turning points of history, such as the succession to the throne and the question of building the temple in the times of David and Solomon, he expressed an official view.
lifetime: When David said that he was living in a house of cedar while the ark of God remained within curtains, Nathan at first told him, "Do all that is in your heart" (2 Samuel 7:2-3), but that night the word of the LORD came to Nathan, and he was made to deliver the message that not David but the offspring who would come from his body would build the house (2 Samuel 7:4-5, 7:12-13). When David committed his sin concerning Bathsheba, he confronted and rebuked him (2 Samuel 12:1-7), and in David's old age, when Adonijah made himself king, he worked with Bathsheba to bring about Solomon's accession (1 Kings 1:11-14). When Solomon became king, he anointed him king at Gihon together with Zadok the priest (1 Kings 1:39, 1:45).
event: Using the parable of the rich man's flocks and herds and the poor man's little ewe lamb, he pointed out David's sin, and David said, "I have sinned against the LORD," and repented (2 Samuel 12:1-13). The acts of King David from first to last were recorded in the records of Nathan the prophet (1 Chronicles 29:29), and the acts of Solomon from first to last were also recorded in the records of Nathan the prophet (2 Chronicles 9:29).
character: At the king's side he showed the courage to speak bluntly, and in pointing out David's sin he used a parable, speaking with the wisdom of letting the other person come to realize it for himself (2 Samuel 12:1-4). He had a strategic political sense, as when he cooperated closely with Bathsheba to establish the succession to the throne (1 Kings 1:11-14).

introduce: Nathan of Zobah is a figure recorded as the father of Igal, who is listed among David's mighty men.
lifetime: He is mentioned as the father of Igal, one of the Thirty, the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:36).

introduce: Nathan is a figure recorded as the father of Azariah, the chief of the governors, in the list of officials in the time of King Solomon. In the same verse his other son Zabud is recorded as a high official and the king's friend (1 Kings 4:5).
lifetime: The Bible has no record of Nathan's own birth or position. However, his son Azariah is listed in the roster of King Solomon's officials as chief of the governors (1 Kings 4:5).
event: The Bible has no record of Nathan's own deeds. His son Azariah is recorded as chief of the governors, and his son Zabud as a high official and the king's friend (1 Kings 4:5).

introduce: Nathan is a descendant of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah, the son of Attai and the father of Zabad (1 Chronicles 2:36).
lifetime: In the genealogy of the descendants of Jerahmeel, son of Hezron, son of Perez, son of Judah, he was born as the son of Attai and fathered Zabad (1 Chronicles 2:5, 2:9, 2:36).

introduce: He is mentioned as a brother of Joel, one of David's mighty men. His blood relationship is confirmed in the list of David's mighty men that appears in 1 Chronicles chapter 11.
lifetime: A man of David's time, he is recorded as belonging to the same family line as his brother Joel (1 Chronicles 11:38).

introduce: Nathan is a figure who appears in Ezra 8:16, one of the chiefs whom Ezra, who had come up from Babylon, summoned when he saw at the river that flows toward Ahava that there were no descendants of Levi.
lifetime: He was one of the chiefs summoned out when Ezra assembled the people at the river that flows toward Ahava, and he was sent to the region of Casiphia (Ezra 8:15-17).
event: At Ezra's request, together with the leading men Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, Meshullam, and Joiarib, he went to the region of Casiphia and carried out the task of bringing back Levites and temple servants (Nethinim) who would serve in the temple (Ezra 8:16-17).

introduce: Nathan was a member of the Jewish community that returned after the Babylonian exile, a descendant of Bani.
lifetime: He is a man included in the list during the process, led by Ezra, of sending away foreign wives (Ezra 10:39). He is recorded as one of the descendants of Bani (Ezra 10:34).
event: He had taken a foreign woman as his wife, and his name was entered in the list in accordance with the covenant, made at Ezra's initiative, to send away the foreign wives and their children (Ezra 10:39).

call: Ancestor of the clan of Nathan
introduce: The Nathan mentioned in Zechariah 12:12 appears as a name designating a branch of the house of David. In the scene in which each family line of the house of David takes part in the mourning in Jerusalem, it is described as a genealogical unit meaning the descendants of Nathan, a son of David.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son whom David fathered in Jerusalem, born together with Shimea, Shobab, and Solomon to Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel (1 Chronicles 3:5). In Zechariah 12:12 the clan of Nathan appears mourning separately from the house of David.
event: Nathan is recorded as a son of David born in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:5). Zechariah 12:12 says that when every clan in the land mourns on its own, the house of David mourns by itself and the clan of the house of Nathan mourns by itself.

call: Second king of the northern kingdom of Israel (son of Jeroboam)
introduce: Nadab was the second king of the northern kingdom of Israel, a son of Jeroboam I, the first king. He ascended the throne after his father, but his reign was short.
lifetime: In the second year of Asa king of Judah, he became king of Israel and ruled for two years (1 Kings 15:25). While besieging Gibbethon, he was assassinated by Baasha (1 Kings 15:27). After he died, Baasha became king in his place (1 Kings 15:28).
event: Nadab led his army and carried out a siege in order to attack Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines (1 Kings 15:27). During his reign Baasha son of Ahijah of the house of Issachar conspired against him and killed him (1 Kings 15:27). After he was killed, the whole house of Jeroboam was wiped out (1 Kings 15:29).
character: Nadab did evil in the sight of the LORD and walked in the way of his father Jeroboam (1 Kings 15:26). He walked in the sin of his father by which he had caused Israel to sin (1 Kings 15:26).

introduce: Nadab is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, one of the two sons of Shammai, the son of Onam, son of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2:26, 2:28).
lifetime: Nadab was born as a descendant of Jerahmeel in the house of Hezron of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:25, 2:28). His father Shammai had two sons, Nadab and Abishur (1 Chronicles 2:28).
event: The sons of Nadab were Seled and Appaim; Seled died without sons, and the son of Appaim was Ishi (1 Chronicles 2:30-31). In the biblical record there is no account of any independent achievement or specific event of Nadab himself.

call: Son of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon
introduce: A man of the tribe of Benjamin who is mentioned as one of the sons of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon, and his brothers are Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Gedor, Ahio, Zecher, and Mikloth (1 Chronicles 8:30-32). In the parallel record in 1 Chronicles 9:36-37, Ner appears between Baal and Nadab, and Zechariah appears instead of Zecher.

introduce: He was a man who lived in Bethany, the brother of Mary and Martha. He had a close relationship with Jesus, and he appears in the biblical record because of the event in which Jesus raised him from the dead.
lifetime: He lived in Bethany with his sisters and was close to Jesus (John 11:1). He became sick and died, but was raised to life again by Jesus (John 11:43-44). Afterward, when a feast was held for Jesus at Bethany, he was among those who sat at the table with Him (John 12:2). When it became known that he had been raised, many Jews flocked to see him (John 12:9), and the chief priests plotted to put even Lazarus to death (John 12:10). It was because of Lazarus that many of the Jews went away and believed in Jesus (John 12:11).
event: When he fell sick, his sisters sent word to Jesus, but Jesus arrived late, and Lazarus had already been in the tomb for four days (John 11:3, 11:17). After Jesus had the stone taken away and called out in a loud voice, the dead man came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen (John 11:39, 11:43-44). After this event the Jewish leaders plotted to kill Jesus (John 11:53).
character: He maintained a relationship so close that Jesus called him "our friend Lazarus" (John 11:11). In the biblical record he is not shown speaking or acting on his own, and he mainly served as the object that testifies to the miracle of Jesus (John 12:17).

call: Mnason of Cyprus (a believer from Cyprus)
introduce: Mnason is a man of Cyprus who appears in Acts 21:16, an early disciple. It is recorded that Paul's party intended to stay at his house when they went up to Jerusalem.
lifetime: As a man of Cyprus he is recorded as an "early disciple" (Acts 21:16). When Paul's party went up to Jerusalem, some of the disciples from Caesarea went with them and brought Mnason along, so that the party might stay at his house (Acts 21:15-16).
event: The disciples from Caesarea took Mnason along with Paul's party so that the party might stay at his house (Acts 21:16). When the party arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed them gladly (Acts 21:17).
character: The Bible describes him as an early disciple, which suggests that he was a person who had held to the Christian faith from the beginning (Acts 21:16). In addition, by gladly lodging Paul's party who had come from elsewhere in his own home, he appears as one who fulfilled a role of hospitality and service within the community (Acts 21:16).

introduce: Naamah is the mother of Rehoboam, the first king of the kingdom of Judah, and one of the wives of King Solomon. She is recorded as an Ammonite, and was a figure who brought the blood of a foreign woman into the lineage of the Davidic dynasty.
lifetime: She is recorded as the mother of Rehoboam son of Solomon, and she was an Ammonite (1 Kings 14:21, 14:31). Besides Pharaoh's daughter, Solomon loved many foreign women, including Ammonite women (1 Kings 11:1).
event: Naamah's name and origin are mentioned as the mother of Rehoboam in the records that he became king at the age of forty-one and reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, and that when he died he was buried in the City of David (1 Kings 14:21, 14:31; 2 Chronicles 12:13).
character: The Bible does not describe Naamah's character or personal traits in any specific way. It stresses only the fact that she was an Ammonite woman (1 Kings 14:21).

call: Son of Bela (ancestor of the Naamite clan)
introduce: Naaman is a man of the tribe of Benjamin, a son of Bela, and the ancestor of the Naamite clan. As a grandson of Benjamin, the son of Jacob, and a son of Bela, he is recorded in the genealogy of the house of Benjamin.
lifetime: Naaman is recorded as one of the sons of Bela, the son of Benjamin (Numbers 26:40; 1 Chronicles 8:3-4).
event: Naaman became the ancestor who formed the family branch called the Naamite clan among the descendants of the tribe of Benjamin (Numbers 26:40). This record is mentioned in the process of classifying the detailed families of the tribe of Benjamin in connection with the census of Israel.

introduce: Naaman is a man of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, listed as one of the sons of Ehud, and belongs to a family recorded as heads of the inhabitants of Geba (1 Chronicles 8:6-7).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons of Ehud of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:6-7).
event: 1 Chronicles 8:6-7 records that the sons of Ehud, as heads of the inhabitants of Geba, were carried into exile to Manahath, and Naaman's name appears in that context together with Ahijah and Gera. The record that follows, "he fathered Uzza and Ahihud," concerns not Naaman but the person whose name appears with him in the preceding verse, so Uzza and Ahihud cannot be regarded as Naaman's brothers (1 Chronicles 8:6-7).

call: Commander of the army of Aram (healed of leprosy)
introduce: As commander of the army of the king of Aram, he was a powerful man in the king's favor, but while suffering from leprosy he experienced healing through Elisha, the prophet of Israel.
lifetime: He held the position of commander of the army of Aram and was in a position of esteem with the king (2 Kings 5:1). Having listened to the words of a young servant girl taken captive from Israel, he obtained the king's permission and visited Israel (2 Kings 5:2-5). He was healed of his leprosy by washing himself seven times in the Jordan River (2 Kings 5:14), and afterward he confessed that he would serve the God of Israel and returned to his own country (2 Kings 5:17).
event: He was a mighty man of valor, the commander of the army of the king of Aram, of whom it is recorded that the LORD had formerly given victory to Aram through him (2 Kings 5:1). At Elisha's direction he immersed himself seven times in the Jordan River and experienced the event of being completely healed of leprosy (2 Kings 5:14). After being healed he tried to offer a gift in gratitude but was refused, and he confided to Elisha the difficulty of his duty to support his master the king of Aram when he worshiped in the temple of Rimmon (2 Kings 5:15-18).
character: He was flexible in dealing with circumstances, to the extent of listening to the advice of a young servant girl of lower standing than himself (2 Kings 5:4). He also showed a somewhat hot-tempered side, as when he vented his anger that Elisha did not come out himself but sent a messenger with instructions (2 Kings 5:11-12). After he was healed, he was a man of firm conviction, to the point of declaring that even after returning to his own country he would offer burnt offerings or sacrifices to no god other than the God of Israel (2 Kings 5:17).

introduce: Nahash is a figure mentioned in 2 Samuel 17:25 as the father of Abigail. Abigail is recorded as having lain with Ithra the Israelite and borne Amasa, and as the sister of Zeruiah, the mother of Joab.
lifetime: The Bible has no specific record of Nahash's life. It is recorded only that his daughter Abigail lay with Ithra and bore Amasa, and that she was the sister of Zeruiah, the mother of Joab (2 Samuel 17:25).
event: No historical event or achievement that Nahash carried out on his own initiative is recorded. His name appears only in 2 Samuel 17:25, which introduces his daughter Abigail.

introduce: Nahor is a figure recorded as a son of Terah and a brother of Abraham and Haran, the younger brother of Abraham (Genesis 11:26, 22:20). He married Milcah and had eight sons, and he also had children by his concubine Reumah, and his son Bethuel fathered Rebekah (Genesis 22:20-24).
lifetime: Nahor is one of the three brothers, Abram, Nahor, and Haran, whom his father Terah fathered (Genesis 11:26-27). He married Milcah (Genesis 11:29), and Milcah was the daughter of his brother Haran (Genesis 11:29). Milcah bore him eight sons: Uz, Buz, Kemuel the father of Aram, Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel (Genesis 22:20-23), and his concubine Reumah also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah (Genesis 22:24). Of these, Bethuel fathered Rebekah (Genesis 22:23).
event: No specific acts of his life are directly described in the Bible. His son Kemuel is recorded as the father of Aram, and Bethuel as the father of Rebekah (Genesis 22:21-23). The place Abraham's servant reached when he went to Mesopotamia is referred to as the city of Nahor (Genesis 24:10), and when Laban made an oath with Jacob he invoked "the God of Abraham, the God of Nahor" (Genesis 31:53).

call: Son of Esli (an ancestor of Jesus)
introduce: A figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke, recorded as the son of Esli and the father of Amos (Luke 3:25). There is no record that clarifies any relation to Nahum, the prophet of the Old Testament.
lifetime: In the genealogy of Jesus in Luke chapter 3, he is recorded as the son of Esli and the father of Amos (Luke 3:25).

introduce: Nepheg is one of the sons David had in Jerusalem, a figure recorded as one of David's children within the royal genealogy of David.
lifetime: Nepheg is one of the sons David fathered in Jerusalem after he had come up from Hebron (2 Samuel 5:13-15). He is also recorded in the list of the sons born in Jerusalem in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 3:5-7, 14:3-6).

call: Daughter of Zelophehad (heiress of an inheritance)
introduce: Noah is one of the five daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh, who appear in the book of Numbers (Numbers 26:33). When their father died without sons, she, together with her sisters, was one who petitioned for an inheritance so that their father's name would not be removed from his family (Numbers 27:1-4).
lifetime: As a daughter of Zelophehad, when her father died in the wilderness without sons (Numbers 27:3), she stood together with her sisters at the entrance of the tent of meeting before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation, and asked for an inheritance among their father's brothers so that their father's name would not be removed (Numbers 27:2-4). In the distribution of the land of Canaan she went with her sisters before Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the leaders and received an inheritance (Joshua 17:3-4), and in keeping with the command to marry only into a family of the tribe of their ancestors, she married the sons of her father's brothers so that the inheritance would remain in the tribe of her father's family (Numbers 36:6, 11-12).
event: She set a legal precedent in the history of Israel by having a woman's right of inheritance recognized. Moses brought their petition before the LORD, and the LORD said that the daughters of Zelophehad were right and that their father's inheritance should be given to them, and the regulation was given that if there is no son, the inheritance is to be given to the daughter (Numbers 27:5-8). She also carried out the provision that they must marry within the same tribe to prevent the inheritance from passing to another tribe (Numbers 36:6-12).
character: She had the logical thinking and decisiveness to assert her own rights boldly. While respecting the customs and traditions of the community, she showed the initiative to bring about a reasonable legal change (Numbers 27:1-4). She valued her family and her father's name, and had a sense of responsibility to protect its honor (Numbers 36:11).

meaning: The LORD has made Himself known
introduce: Noadiah is a figure who appears in the book of Nehemiah in the Old Testament, recorded as a prophetess who belonged to the forces obstructing the rebuilding of the wall and tried to intimidate Nehemiah.
lifetime: She was active at the time of the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile, and is mentioned as a member of the outside opposing forces that tried to make Nehemiah afraid and stop his work (Nehemiah 6:14).
event: She allied herself with those who opposed the rebuilding of the wall, such as Sanballat and Tobiah, and tried to intimidate Nehemiah (Nehemiah 6:14).
character: She was designated a false prophet by Nehemiah and is portrayed as a person with a political and hostile disposition who tried to obstruct the rebuilding of the wall (Nehemiah 6:14).

call: Ancestor of a returning family of unknown genealogy
introduce: Nekoda is a figure whose name appears, in the lists of those who returned from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2, Nehemiah 7), as the ancestor of the descendants of Nekoda. His descendants are recorded, together with the descendants of Delaiah and the descendants of Tobiah, among those who could not prove whether their family and descent belonged to Israel (Ezra 2:59-60).
lifetime: The descendants of Nekoda were included in the list of the people who came up from Babylon, and their number is recorded as 652 in the book of Ezra (Ezra 2:60) and as 642 in the book of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 7:62).
event: The descendants of Nekoda, together with the descendants of Delaiah and the descendants of Tobiah, were recorded as those who could not prove whether their family and descent belonged to Israel (Ezra 2:59-60, Nehemiah 7:61-62).

call: Son of Asaph (singer of the fifth division)
introduce: Nethaniah is a man among the descendants of Asaph of the tribe of Levi, who took charge of the fifth division in the temple choir in the time of King David.
lifetime: David, together with the commanders of the army, set apart for service some of the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun (1 Chronicles 25:1), and among them Nethaniah, as a son of Asaph, sang spiritual songs at the command of the king (1 Chronicles 25:2). The one chosen fifth in the lot to determine the divisions was Nethaniah, and 12 in all were with him, his sons and his brothers (1 Chronicles 25:12).
event: Within the system of 24 divisions that David organized for temple service, Nethaniah, together with his brothers, played the lyre, harp, and cymbals and carried out the work of temple praise according to the command of the king (1 Chronicles 25:2, 1 Chronicles 25:6).
character: In the biblical record, there is no mention of Nethaniah's personal character or specific traits.

introduce: Nethaniah was a Levite who was active in the time of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, one of those who, at the king's command, carried out the mission of teaching the law throughout Judah.
lifetime: In the third year of the reign of King Jehoshaphat, the king chose officials and Levites and sent them to the cities of Judah, and on that occasion Nethaniah was sent along with them as an itinerant teacher (2 Chronicles 17:7-8).
event: As a member of the delegation sent by King Jehoshaphat, he went around the cities of Judah and taught the people with the Book of the Law of the LORD (2 Chronicles 17:9).

introduce: Nethanel is a son of Jesse, a figure recorded as fourth in the list of Jesse's sons in 1 Chronicles 2:13-15 and one of David's brothers (1 Chronicles 2:14). In 1 Samuel 16:6-9 and 17:13 only the names Eliab, Abinadab, and Shammah appear, and the name Nethanel does not.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Jesse and one of David's brothers (1 Chronicles 2:14-15). His father Jesse is recorded as a man of Bethlehem (1 Samuel 16:1).
event: In the biblical record there is no record that Nethanel achieved anything special or played a leading role in any particular event. His only mention is his inclusion in the list naming David's brothers in 1 Chronicles 2:14.

call: Priest who blew the trumpet before the ark
introduce: Nethanel was a priest who was active in the time of David, a figure recorded as one of those who blew the trumpets before the ark of God when it was moved (1 Chronicles 15:24).
lifetime: When David moved the ark of God to Jerusalem, Nethanel was recorded, together with the priests Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer, as one of those who blew the trumpets before the ark of God (1 Chronicles 15:24).
event: When David and the elders of Israel and the commanders of thousands brought up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-edom (1 Chronicles 15:25), he was recorded as one of the priests who blew the trumpets before the ark of God (1 Chronicles 15:24).

call: Father of Shemaiah (father of the scribe)
introduce: Nethanel is a figure who appears in Chronicles of the Old Testament, recorded as the father of Shemaiah the scribe. He is a person mentioned in the process of organizing the Levites in the time of David.
lifetime: Nethanel is recorded as a Levite and is the father of Shemaiah the scribe (1 Chronicles 24:6).
event: When the divisions of the Levites were being arranged in the time of King David, Shemaiah the scribe, the son of Nethanel, carried out the role of recording the list before the king, the officials, Zadok the priest, and Ahimelech (1 Chronicles 24:6).

introduce: Nethanel is a figure recorded as a gatekeeper of the tribe of Levi in the time of David and as the fifth son of Obed-edom.
lifetime: He is recorded as fifth among the sons of Obed-edom (1 Chronicles 26:4). The sons of Obed-edom, who belonged to the divisions of the gatekeepers, received their office as heads of divisions of gatekeepers and were those who served in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:1, 12).
event: As a son of Obed-edom, Nethanel belonged to the divisions of the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:4, 12). God blessed Obed-edom, so that he had many sons, and his descendants were all men of ability who did their duties well (1 Chronicles 26:5, 8). When lots were cast for guarding the gates, the lot for the south fell to Obed-edom, and the lot for the storehouses fell to his sons (1 Chronicles 26:13-15).
character: The descendants of his family, Obed-edom, were all regarded as men of ability, and, including Nethanel, they were robust and trusted men fit to carry out the duties of gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:8).

introduce: Nethanel was active in the reign of Jehoshaphat, the fourth king of the southern kingdom of Judah, and was one of the officials sent out to the provinces to carry out the king's command.
lifetime: In the third year of his reign King Jehoshaphat sent officials, Levites, and priests to go around the cities of Judah and teach, and on that occasion Nethanel was appointed as one of the officials and sent out (2 Chronicles 17:7).
event: At the command of King Jehoshaphat, together with Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, and Micaiah, he went around the many cities of Judah and carried out the mission of teaching the people the Book of the Law of the LORD (2 Chronicles 17:7-9).

call: Levite leader in the time of Josiah
introduce: Nethanel is a figure recorded as one of the chiefs of the Levites when the Passover was kept in the time of Josiah king of Judah. He is one of the chiefs who, together with Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah, Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, gave to the Levites 5,000 sheep and 500 bulls as Passover offerings (2 Chronicles 35:9).
lifetime: At the Passover kept in the eighteenth year of King Josiah (2 Chronicles 35:19), Nethanel is recorded as one of the chiefs of the Levites (2 Chronicles 35:9).
event: Nethanel, together with the chiefs of the Levites, Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah, Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, gave to the Levites 5,000 sheep and 500 bulls as Passover offerings (2 Chronicles 35:9). This was done along with what Josiah gave to the assembled people (2 Chronicles 35:7) and what the officials gave to the people, the priests, and the Levites (2 Chronicles 35:8).

기타관계: Jozabad#4332(fellow worker of the tribe of Levi)

introduce: Nethanel is a figure recorded as a descendant of Pashhur among the group of priests who had taken foreign women as wives in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:18, 22).
lifetime: He is recorded as a man belonging to the descendants of Pashhur among the group of priests in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:18, 22).
event: Among the group of priests who had taken foreign women, he was a descendant of Pashhur, and his name was entered together with Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Jozabad, and Elasah (Ezra 10:18-22).

call: Priest of the family of Jedaiah
introduce: Nethanel is a figure recorded as the head of the family of Jedaiah in the list of the heads of the priestly families in the time of Joiakim, after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 12:12, 21).
lifetime: In the time of Joiakim, he was recorded as the head of the family of Jedaiah among those who were heads of the priests (Nehemiah 12:12, 21).
event: In the list of the heads of the priests in the time of Joiakim, Hashabiah is recorded for the family of Hilkiah, and Nethanel for the family of Jedaiah (Nehemiah 12:21).

call: Priest who praised at the dedication of the wall
introduce: Nethanel is a figure recorded as one of the brothers of Zechariah, who held a trumpet, a descendant of the priests who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 12:35-36).
lifetime: When Nehemiah divided the great company giving thanks and praise into two groups and had them proceed in line on the wall (Nehemiah 12:31), he was recorded as a brother of Zechariah, a descendant of the priests, and was among those who held the musical instruments of David the man of God (Nehemiah 12:35-36).
event: At the dedication of the wall, he, together with his brothers Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Judah, and Hanani, held the musical instruments of David the man of God, and Ezra the scribe marched in front of them (Nehemiah 12:36).

introduce: Neariah is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles chapter 4, a descendant of the tribe of Simeon and a son of Ishi. He is mentioned as one of the chiefs of the descendants of Simeon who went to Mount Seir and struck the Amalekites.
lifetime: Neariah is recorded as a son of Ishi (1 Chronicles 4:42). He was one of the sons of Ishi, Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, who were set as leaders of five hundred men of the descendants of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:42).
event: Neariah, together with the sons of Ishi, Pelatiah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, became the leaders of five hundred men of the descendants of Simeon and went to Mount Seir (1 Chronicles 4:42). They struck the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped and have lived there to this day (1 Chronicles 4:43).

기타관계: Elioenai#2484(kinsman of the tribe of Simeon)

meaning: One who holds royal power; one who restrains
introduce: Darius is a king of Persia who is mentioned only once in Nehemiah 12:22 as "Darius king of Persia." The text says only that the priests were also recorded in the book in his time, and although there is a view that identifies this Darius as Darius II, the text does not make clear which Darius it is.
lifetime: The Bible has no record of his life. Nehemiah 12:22 says only that in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua the heads of the families of the Levites were all recorded in the book, and that in the time of Darius king of Persia the priests were also recorded in the book (Nehemiah 12:22).
event: The Bible has no record of any event or achievement of his. His name appears only as an expression indicating the period when the priests were recorded in the book (Nehemiah 12:22).

meaning: One who holds royal power; one who restrains
introduce: Darius is a figure who appears in the book of Daniel, portrayed as a ruler who, immediately after the fall of Babylon, succeeded to the throne of Babylon as a Mede. In the world of historical scholarship, various discussions continue about his identity, including the theory that he is the same person as Cyrus the Great, the theory that he is a person named Gobaru (Gubaru), and the theory that he is a hypothetical figure of Media.
lifetime: After Belshazzar king of Babylon was slain, he received the kingdom of Babylon at the age of sixty-two (Daniel 5:30-31). He appointed 120 satraps throughout the kingdom to govern it, placed three administrators over them, and appointed Daniel as one of them to oversee the affairs of state (Daniel 6:1-2).
event: When the satraps asked him to establish a decree, sealed with the royal signet on a written order, that for thirty days anyone who petitioned any god or man other than the king would be thrown into the den of lions (Daniel 6:7-8), King Darius sealed the written order and issued the decree (Daniel 6:9). Although Daniel knew this and prayed, the king was greatly distressed and tried to rescue him, but since the decree could not be altered he had Daniel thrown into the den of lions, and the next day, confirming that Daniel was alive, he had him brought up out of the den (Daniel 6:14-23). Afterward he had the men who had accused Daniel thrown into the den of lions together with their wives and children, and he issued a decree to all the peoples under his rule proclaiming that they should fear the God of Daniel (Daniel 6:24-27).
character: Darius recognized Daniel's exceptional ability and had the discernment to employ talent, to the extent of planning to set him over the whole kingdom (Daniel 6:3). When Daniel was thrown into the den of lions, he spent the night fasting and distressed, worrying about him (Daniel 6:18). After confirming that Daniel was alive, he was overjoyed and took steps to have him brought up out of the den (Daniel 6:23).

introduce: Tamar is a daughter of King David and Maacah and a full sister of Absalom. After being violated by force by her half brother Amnon, she lived desolate in the house of Absalom.
lifetime: When David's son Amnon fell in love with his half sister Tamar and became ill, he pretended to be sick on the scheme of Jonadab and asked the king to let Tamar come and prepare food and feed him, and David sent Tamar to Amnon's house (2 Samuel 13:1-7). Amnon violated Tamar by force, and immediately hated her intensely and drove her out (2 Samuel 13:14-17). Tamar protested that sending her away was worse than the evil he had done before, but Amnon would not listen (2 Samuel 13:16), and afterward she lived desolate in the house of her brother Absalom (2 Samuel 13:20).
event: Against Amnon's forcible demand, Tamar said, "Such a thing ought not to be done in Israel," and told him not to do this disgraceful thing (2 Samuel 13:12-13). After the incident she tore her robe of many colors, put ashes on her head, laid her hand on her head, and went away crying loudly (2 Samuel 13:19). Absalom hated Amnon for having dishonored his sister Tamar (2 Samuel 13:22), and two years later Absalom's servants killed Amnon at his command (2 Samuel 13:28-29, 13:32).
character: She showed an attitude of striving to keep her purity, and when she was treated unjustly she had the discernment to explain logically to the princes the impropriety of marriage between close relatives (2 Samuel 13:13). After the tragic incident she despaired of her situation and lived cut off from the outside world in the house of Absalom (2 Samuel 13:20).

introduce: A woman who was the daughter of Absalom and inherited the bloodline of the Davidic royal house of the kingdom of Judah.
lifetime: She is the only daughter born to Absalom, a son of King David (2 Samuel 14:27). She is a granddaughter of King David. 2 Chronicles 11:20 records that Rehoboam married Maacah the daughter of Absalom, but the text does not make clear whether this Maacah is the same person as Tamar.
event: Among the three sons and one daughter whom Absalom fathered, she was the daughter, and the Bible records that her name was Tamar and that she was a woman of beautiful countenance (2 Samuel 14:27).
character: In the biblical record her personal character and specific deeds are not described. However, an assessment of her outstanding beauty is mentioned (2 Samuel 14:27).

call: Samaritan official (accuser against the rebuilding of the wall)
introduce: Tabeel is a figure recorded as having sent a letter to Artaxerxes king of Persia, in the time of Artaxerxes, together with Bishlam, Mithredath, and their associates. That letter was written in Aramaic script and in the Aramaic language (Ezra 4:7).
lifetime: In the time of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Tabeel, together with Bishlam, Mithredath, and their associates, wrote a letter to the king (Ezra 4:7). The preceding part of this verse is the context recording how the people of the land obstructed the building of the people of Judah and sent in accusations (Ezra 4:4-6). The Bible has no record of his later life or his background.
event: Tabeel, together with Bishlam, Mithredath, and their associates, wrote a letter to Artaxerxes king of Persia (Ezra 4:7). Verse 4:7 does not record the content of this letter; from 4:8 onward a separate letter is introduced which Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe sent to King Artaxerxes accusing the people of Jerusalem.

introduce: Tarshish is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, appearing in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin as a son of Bilhan, and a great-grandson of Benjamin.
lifetime: Tarshish was born to Bilhan, the son of Jediael, the son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:6, 7:10). He is recorded as one of the seven sons of Bilhan (1 Chronicles 7:10).
character: Concerning Tarshish, the Bible mentions only that he was a son of Bilhan and that Bilhan's descendants, as brave warriors, made up the house of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:10). Beyond that, nothing is recorded about the personal character or specific deeds of the individual Tarshish.

call: One of the seven princes of Persia
introduce: Tarshish is one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who, in the time of Xerxes king of Persia, had access to the king, observed the king's countenance, and sat first in the kingdom (Esther 1:14).
lifetime: In the time when Xerxes king of Persia reigned, his name is recorded as one of the seven princes who had access to the king, observed the king's countenance, and sat first in the kingdom (Esther 1:14). His origin and the rest of his life are not recorded in the Bible.
event: When Queen Vashti did not obey the command of King Xerxes, his name appears as one of the seven princes just before the passage in which the king asks, "According to law, what should be done with her?" (Esther 1:14-15). The one who answered before the king and the princes is recorded as Memucan (Esther 1:16), and it was also Memucan who said that Vashti should be deposed and that a decree should be issued and written among the laws of Persia and Media (Esther 1:16-21). No statement or action of Tarshish himself is recorded.

기타관계: Memucan#969(fellow of the seven princes of Persia)

introduce: Tahan is a descendant of the tribe of Ephraim, a figure recorded as the son of Telah, the son of Resheph, the son of Beriah. His place in the genealogy is confirmed through the genealogy of Ephraim in 1 Chronicles chapter 7 (1 Chronicles 7:25).
lifetime: As a descendant of Beriah, the son of Ephraim, his line continues from Beriah through Resheph and Telah to Tahan (1 Chronicles 7:23-25). He is recorded as the son of Telah and the father of Ladan (1 Chronicles 7:25-26).
event: In the biblical record no information appears about any specific achievement or event that he carried out (1 Chronicles 7:25).

introduce: Tahath is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Ephraim, a descendant of Shuthelah, the son of Ephraim, a son of Bered, and the father of Eleadah (1 Chronicles 7:20). Whether he is related to Tahan in Numbers 26:35 is disputed and is not settled by the text, so he is kept as a separate entry.
lifetime: In the line that continues from Shuthelah, the son of Ephraim, through Bered, Tahath is recorded in the genealogy as the son of Bered, the grandson of Shuthelah, and the father of Eleadah (1 Chronicles 7:20).

introduce: Tahath is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Ephraim, one of the descendants of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 7:20). He is recorded as a descendant of Shuthelah, the son of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 7:20).
lifetime: Tahath is mentioned within the genealogy of the descendants of Shuthelah, the son of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 7:20). He is the Tahath who appears as the son of Eleadah, following Shuthelah's son Bered, his son Tahath, and his son Eleadah (1 Chronicles 7:20).
event: No specific historical achievement carried out by Tahath, nor any event that he led, is recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 7:20).

introduce: Talmai is a king of Geshur who appears in the Old Testament, the father of Maacah, a wife of David, and the maternal grandfather of Absalom.
lifetime: Talmai was the king of Geshur in Aram (2 Samuel 3:3, 15:8), and his daughter Maacah is recorded as the mother of Absalom, a son of David (2 Samuel 3:3).
event: When David's son Absalom fled after killing his half brother Amnon, Talmai received Absalom in Geshur, his own residence, and let him stay there for three years (2 Samuel 13:37-38).

introduce: Tema is the ninth of the twelve sons of Ishmael, a son of Abraham, recorded in Genesis. He is recorded as one of the twelve princes born to Ishmael.
lifetime: Tema, as a son of Ishmael born between Abraham and Hagar, entered his name in the genealogy of the family line (Genesis 25:12, 25:15). The names of the sons of Ishmael are recorded as names according to their villages and encampments (Genesis 25:16).
event: As a son of Ishmael, Tema was included among the names of the sons whom his father Ishmael fathered (1 Chronicles 1:30). No separate deeds of Tema himself, nor any specific account of a particular event, are found in the biblical text.

call: Returning family of the Nethinim (descendants of Temah)
introduce: Temah is a figure recorded as one of the families of the Nethinim who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile. He is the name of an ancestor who appears in the lists of those who returned from Babylon in the records of Ezra and Nehemiah.
lifetime: Temah is included in the list of the families of the Nethinim who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:53). He is mentioned in the same way in the list of the returnees from exile that Nehemiah recorded (Nehemiah 7:55).
event: Temah entered his name in the list of the returnees from exile not through individual achievement but as a member of a family, being one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:53). His family was classed as one of the Nethinim who serve in the temple at Jerusalem and joined the ranks of the returnees (Nehemiah 7:55).

meaning: What is at the right hand
introduce: Teman is one of the chiefs of the land of Edom, a figure associated with the descendants of Esau, the ancestor of the Edomite clans. His name appears in the list of chiefs in Genesis 36:42, and the text does not make clear whether he is the same person as Teman the grandson of Esau and son of Eliphaz (Genesis 36:11).
lifetime: Teman is mentioned in the list of the chiefs of Edom and is recorded as one of the chiefs in connection with the region where the descendants of Edom lived (Genesis 36:42). The same name is also found in Chronicles in the course of listing the chiefs of Edom (1 Chronicles 1:53).
event: The name Teman, included in the list of the chiefs of Edom, indicates that he held the position of a leader governing a tribe (Genesis 36:42). Beyond that, no specific event or historical activity is recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 1:53).

meaning: What is at the right hand
introduce: Teman is both a place name in the region of Edom and the name of a person who appears in the genealogy of the chiefs of Edom. According to Genesis and 1 Chronicles, he is recorded as a grandson of Esau and a son of Eliphaz. The region of Teman in the land of Edom is described in biblical literature as a center of wisdom, and it is frequently cited as the name of a particular region.
lifetime: Teman is recorded as the first-named among the sons of Eliphaz, the son of Esau (Genesis 36:11, 1 Chronicles 1:36). He is also recorded first among the chiefs descended from Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn (Genesis 36:15).
event: Teman's name stands first in the list of chiefs descended from Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn (Genesis 36:15). The name Teman is also used as a name designating a region of Edom, so that Jeremiah 49:7, in the words concerning Edom, says, "Is there no longer wisdom in Teman?", and it also appears as a place name of Edom in Ezekiel 25:13 and Amos 1:12.
character: The Bible does not directly describe Teman's personal character. However, the name Teman is repeatedly mentioned in connection with the wisdom of the region where his descendants lived, and the people of Teman in particular are described in the literature of that age as having understanding and wisdom (Jeremiah 49:7, Habakkuk 3:3).

기타관계: Teman#503(presumed founder of the place name)

call: A believer who received testimony to the truth
introduce: He is a figure who appears in the Third Epistle of John, one who received testimony from everyone and from the truth itself, and a believer to whom the elder (the author) who wrote the letter also bears witness (3 John 1:12).
lifetime: The Bible leaves no specific record of his background or early life. However, in the Third Epistle of John he is mentioned as one who received testimony from everyone and from the truth itself (3 John 1:12).
event: His specific activities or historical events are not recorded in detail. However, he received testimony both from everyone and from the truth, and the writer of the letter also said, "We also testify, and you know that our testimony is true" (3 John 1:12).
character: He was a faithful man, to the extent of being described as having received a good report from all people and testimony even from the truth itself (3 John 1:12). The apostle John knew him personally and confirmed that his conduct was worthy of the truth (3 John 1:12).

call: Father of Eleazar (father of one of David's Three mighty men)
introduce: Dodo is a figure recorded as the father of Eleazar, one of David's Three mighty men, and as an Ahohite. He appears in the biblical record as a person who shows the military command structure and family background of David's time.
lifetime: Dodo is mentioned as a man of Ahoah, and since his son Eleazar was active as one of the Three mighty men, the core military force of David, it can be confirmed that his family held an important position in the military organization of David's royal house (2 Samuel 23:9).
event: The biblical text does not record any specific military achievement or event of Dodo himself; his name appears mainly in contexts explaining the genealogical origin of his son Eleazar (1 Chronicles 11:12).

introduce: Dodo is a figure mentioned in the biblical record as the father of Elhanan, one of David's mighty men. In the biblical text he appears under the designation Dodo of Bethlehem, as part of the genealogical information related to the military organization in the time of David's reign.
lifetime: Dodo is recorded as being from Bethlehem (2 Samuel 23:24). His son Elhanan was active as one of David's Thirty mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:26). The Bible does not describe a specific chronology of Dodo's personal life, birth, or death.
event: There is no record in the Bible of any direct military achievement of the name Dodo itself or of his participation in a particular event. However, from the fact that his son Elhanan was chosen and served as a major warrior in David's army, it can be seen that Dodo's family had a close relationship with the military foundation of David's royal house (2 Samuel 23:24).

call: Ancestor of a returning family without genealogy
introduce: He is the ancestor of a family in the lists of returnees from Babylon, whose name appears as "the descendants of Tobiah" in Ezra 2:60 and Nehemiah 7:62. Together with the descendants of Delaiah and the descendants of Nekoda, they are recorded as people who could not prove whether their family and descent belonged to Israel (Ezra 2:59-60, Nehemiah 7:61-62).
lifetime: He is on the list of those who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem as "the descendants of Tobiah," and is included among those who could not prove whether their family and descent belonged to Israel (Ezra 2:59-60). When Nehemiah found the genealogy of those who had come back at the first, the name is also entered in that record under the same circumstances (Nehemiah 7:5, 7:61-62).
event: They were recorded as unable to prove whether their family and descent belonged to Israel (Ezra 2:59-60, Nehemiah 7:61-62). The matter of those who sought their registration among the genealogical records but could not find it, and so were excluded from the priesthood, is the record that follows concerning the priestly families (the descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai) (Ezra 2:61-62).

introduce: Tobiah was a man of Ammonite origin who opposed the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah. In the biblical record he is called an Ammonite, is named together with Sanballat and Geshem as an enemy of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 6:1), and is portrayed as a man who exchanged letters with the nobles of Judah and formed marriage ties, so that there were many in Judah who were sworn to him (Nehemiah 6:17-18).
lifetime: Together with Sanballat the Horonite and Geshem the Arab, he despised and mocked what Nehemiah and his party were doing (Nehemiah 2:19). He was in a relationship of exchanging letters with the nobles of Judah, became son-in-law to Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan also took the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah, forming marriage ties with influential persons within Judah (Nehemiah 6:17-18). Afterward the priest Eliashib, being connected with Tobiah, prepared a large room in the house of God for him, but when Nehemiah learned of it he threw Tobiah's household goods out of the room and purified the room (Nehemiah 13:4-9).
event: When Sanballat was mocking the Jews, Tobiah stood beside him and said, "If even a fox climbs up on the wall they are building, it will break down their wall of stones" (Nehemiah 4:3). It was Sanballat and Geshem who tried to lure Nehemiah out to the plain of Ono (Nehemiah 6:2), and Nehemiah realized that the matter of Shemaiah, who had prophesied falsely after taking a bribe, originated with Tobiah and Sanballat (Nehemiah 6:12-13). Nehemiah prayed to God to remember Tobiah and Sanballat, and the prophetess Noadiah and the rest of the prophets, as those who wanted to make him afraid (Nehemiah 6:14). The nobles of Judah spoke of Tobiah's good deeds before Nehemiah and reported Nehemiah's words to Tobiah, and Tobiah continually sent letters to Nehemiah to make him afraid (Nehemiah 6:19).
character: He was a man of outstanding political skill, to the extent of penetrating deep into Judean society through politically motivated marriages (Nehemiah 6:18). To maintain his influence he showed a calculating and scheming disposition, manipulating the nobles and gathering information (Nehemiah 6:19). Moreover, since he had a close relationship even with the high priest Eliashib, to the extent of privately using a storeroom inside the temple at Jerusalem, he had a power-seeking aspect that sought to exploit even religious authority (Nehemiah 13:4-5).

introduce: Tobijah is a figure who appears in Zechariah 6:10 and 14, whose name is given together with Heldai and Jedaiah, among the exiles who had returned from Babylon. Zechariah received the command to take silver and gold from them and make a crown, and that crown was to be placed in the temple of the LORD as a memorial to them, Tobijah included.
lifetime: As one of the exiles who had returned from Babylon, together with Heldai and Jedaiah he was staying at the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah (Zechariah 6:10). His name appears in the word to give the crown, as a memorial, in the temple of the LORD, together with Helem, Jedaiah, and Hen son of Zephaniah (Zechariah 6:14).
event: Zechariah received the command to take silver and gold from Tobijah, Heldai, and Jedaiah, make a crown, and set it on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest (Zechariah 6:10-11). There was a word that the crown was to be given, in the temple of the LORD, as a memorial to Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen son of Zephaniah (Zechariah 6:14). No words or actions of Tobijah himself are recorded in the text.

call: Name of a town in the genealogy of Judah ('Ashhur, the father of Tekoa')
introduce: Tekoa is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, belonging to the house of Hezron, the grandson of Judah, and 1 Chronicles records Ashhur as "the father of Tekoa" (1 Chronicles 2:24, 4:5).
lifetime: After Hezron died, his wife Abijah bore Ashhur, and Ashhur is recorded as the father of Tekoa (1 Chronicles 2:24). Ashhur's two wives were Helah and Naarah (1 Chronicles 4:5), and the text does not record by which wife Tekoa was born.
event: Tekoa's own deeds are not recorded in the text, and his name appears in the expression "Ashhur the father of Tekoa" (1 Chronicles 2:24, 4:5).

introduce: Dedan is a son of Jokshan, who was born to Keturah, Abraham's later wife, and is therefore a grandson of Abraham (Genesis 25:1-3, 1 Chronicles 1:32).
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Jokshan, the son whom Abraham had through his later wife Keturah (1 Chronicles 1:32, Genesis 25:3).
event: His descendants are the Asshurites, the Letushites, and the Leummites (Genesis 25:3).

introduce: Dedan is a figure who appears in Genesis of the Old Testament, recorded as a descendant of Cush, the son of Ham, and a son of Raamah. In the genealogy of humanity he is classified as a member of the Hamite peoples.
lifetime: Dedan was a son born to Raamah, the son of Cush, and a brother of Sheba (Genesis 10:7). He corresponds to the generation of a great-grandson of Ham, the son of Noah (Genesis 10:6-7). No specific anecdote about his personal life is recorded in the Bible.
event: The Bible does not record any event carried out by Dedan himself, but the name Dedan also appears as a word referring to a people and to caravans. Isaiah 21:13, in the oracle concerning Arabia, calls out "caravans of Dedanites"; Ezekiel 27:15 says, "The men of Dedan were your traders," and speaks of many coastlands bringing ivory and ebony and trading with Tyre. Jeremiah 25:23 lists Dedan, together with Tema and Buz, among the nations that will drink the cup of the wrath of the LORD (Jeremiah 25:15, 25:23).

introduce: Deborah is a figure of the period of the judges in the book of Judges of the Old Testament, a female leader who lived in the hill country of Ephraim and served as the fourth judge of Israel. She was the wife of Lappidoth and was called a prophetess, and she carried out the role of judging the disputes of the Israelites of that time.
lifetime: Deborah lived under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim and was in charge of judging the people (Judges 4:4-5). She summoned Barak son of Abinoam, from Kedesh in Naphtali, and commanded him to go up to Mount Tabor leading an army of ten thousand men (Judges 4:6). After the victory in the battle against Sisera, the commander of the army of Jabin king of Canaan, she sang the song of victory together with Barak (Judges 5:1-31).
event: When Israel had been oppressed for twenty years by Jabin king of Canaan, Deborah summoned Barak and delivered the command of the LORD to go to Mount Tabor with ten thousand men of the descendants of Naphtali and Zebulun (Judges 4:2-3, 4:6). When Sisera gathered nine hundred iron chariots and all his army, Deborah told Barak to rise up, and when Barak went down from Mount Tabor, the LORD routed Sisera and all his chariots and all his army with the edge of the sword, and the land had peace for forty years (Judges 4:13-16, 5:31). Deborah sang together with Barak (Judges 5:1), and that song contains the participation of the tribes of Israel and the course of the war (Judges 5:14-18).
character: Deborah was a person with public influence and authority, to the extent of taking on the judging of the people (Judges 4:5). When Barak asked her to go with him, she showed decisiveness and initiative in leadership by firmly revising the plan of operation in her response (Judges 4:8-9). She also stressed that the victory in the war came from the LORD, and showed the side of a mediator who made key judgments in the political and military phases of ancient Israel (Judges 4:14, 5:3).

call: Ancestor of a family that returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Delaiah is one of the Israelites who, after finishing the Babylonian exile, returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel. He is recorded as one of the ancestors of the people who could not prove their family through the genealogy.
lifetime: Delaiah is a man included in the list of those who returned from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:60). He returned together with Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer, but they could not prove whether the families and genealogies of their ancestors belonged to Israel (Ezra 2:59-60, Nehemiah 7:61-62).
event: Delaiah was included in the company that came back from the Babylonian exile and took part in the journey of returning to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:60). After the return, in the process of verifying families and genealogies, he was classed among the group who could not prove their own origin (Nehemiah 7:62).

call: Father of Shemaiah (father of the false prophet)
introduce: Delaiah is a figure who appears in the book of Nehemiah in the Old Testament; he is the son of Mehetabel and the father of Shemaiah. He is mentioned in connection with the figures who were active during the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem.
lifetime: Delaiah is recorded as the son of Mehetabel (Nehemiah 6:10). His son Shemaiah is recorded as one who engaged in prophetic activity during the time when Nehemiah was building the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 6:10, 6:12).
event: It is recorded that when Nehemiah went to the house of Delaiah's son Shemaiah, who was shut up at home, Shemaiah said they should take refuge inside the inner sanctuary of the house of God (Nehemiah 6:10). Nehemiah realized that he was not one sent by God but had prophesied after receiving a bribe from Tobiah and Sanballat (Nehemiah 6:12), and that bribe was meant to make Nehemiah afraid and sin (Nehemiah 6:13). No direct deeds or achievements of Delaiah himself are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Delaiah is a figure who appears in the book of Jeremiah, a son of Shemaiah and one of the officials of Judah. He is one of the officials who heard the words of Jeremiah's scroll read by Baruch and decided to report them to the king.
lifetime: He is one of the officials who were sitting in the chamber of the scribe in the king's palace after Baruch read the words of Jeremiah in the house of the LORD in the ninth month of the fifth year of Jehoiakim king of Judah (Jeremiah 36:9-12). When the officials asked and Baruch read the scroll in their hearing, they heard all those words, were alarmed, and decided to report them to the king (Jeremiah 36:15-16).
event: Micaiah told the officials who were in the chamber of the scribe in the king's palace the news that Baruch had read the words of Jeremiah in the house of the LORD (Jeremiah 36:11-13), and Delaiah was one of those officials, present when they heard the words of the scroll that Baruch read again and decided to report them to the king (Jeremiah 36:12, 36:15-16). Afterward, together with Elnathan and Gemariah, he urged the king not to burn the scroll, but the king would not listen (Jeremiah 36:25).
character: When he heard the words of judgment that Jeremiah had recorded, together with Gemariah and Elnathan he showed a reaction of fear without tearing his clothes, but in the end he showed the resolve to plead with King Jehoiakim not to burn the scroll (Jeremiah 36:25).

introduce: Delaiah is a figure who carried on the bloodline of the royal house of David, mentioned as a son of Elioenai in the genealogy of David's descendants in 1 Chronicles chapter 3.
lifetime: Delaiah is a son of Elioenai, a descendant of David (1 Chronicles 3:24). He is one of the generations recorded in the genealogy of the royal house of David (1 Chronicles 3:24).
event: His name is recorded in the genealogy of David's descendants as one of the seven sons of Elioenai (1 Chronicles 3:24).

call: Father of Jahzeiah (father of one who opposed the investigation of foreign marriages)
introduce: Tikvah is a figure recorded as the father of Jahzeiah, who opposed the handling of the matter of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:15).
lifetime: The Bible has no record of Tikvah's own life, and his son Jahzeiah appears among the descendants of the exiles in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:15-16).
event: No event of Tikvah himself is recorded in the Bible. His son Jahzeiah rose up together with Jonathan son of Asahel and opposed that matter, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them (Ezra 10:15).

introduce: Dishon is a descendant of the Horite clan who lived in the land of Seir, a son of Anah and a brother of Oholibamah (Genesis 36:25). He is classified as a person who continues the lineage of the Horite clan within the genealogy of Edom (1 Chronicles 1:41).
lifetime: Dishon, as a son of Anah, is a man belonging to the family line of the Horite clan (Genesis 36:25). He is mentioned between Anah and Ezer in the list in Chronicles enumerating the sons of Seir (1 Chronicles 1:38), and his sons are recorded as Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran (1 Chronicles 1:41).
event: The biblical text does not describe in detail any personal achievement or specific event of Dishon (Genesis 36:25, 1 Chronicles 1:41).

introduce: Timna is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the Edomite clans, recorded as a daughter of Seir and a sister of Lotan.
lifetime: She was born as a daughter of Seir of the Horite clan and formed a sibling relationship with Lotan (Genesis 36:22).
event: Her name is recorded as the sister of Lotan in the genealogy of the descendants of Seir of the Horite clan in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:22; 1 Chronicles 1:39), and no other deeds are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Timna is a figure whose name is recorded in the list of the chiefs of Edom. Genesis records him as one of the chiefs descended from Esau (Genesis 36:40), and Chronicles records him as one of the chiefs of Edom after Hadad died (1 Chronicles 1:51).
lifetime: In the list enumerating the names of the chiefs descended from Esau according to their clans, their dwelling places, and their names, "Chief Timna" comes first (Genesis 36:40). The Bible has no account of his life.
event: He is recorded as Chief Timna in the list of the chiefs of Edom (Genesis 36:40; 1 Chronicles 1:51), and no other events are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Ladan is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, a chief belonging to the descendants of Gershon among the descendants of Levi. He held a position of leadership, heading a family within the tribe of Levi, and is mentioned in connection with temple affairs and administrative order during the reign of King David.
lifetime: Ladan is a son of Gershon, the son of Levi, and the sons of Gershon are recorded as Ladan and Shimei (1 Chronicles 23:7). His sons are the chief Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel (1 Chronicles 23:8). Among the descendants of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the chief is recorded as Jehieli (1 Chronicles 26:21).
event: When David divided the descendants of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, the sons of Levi, into divisions according to their clans, Ladan was recorded among the descendants of Gershon (1 Chronicles 23:6-7). Among Ladan's descendants, Zetham the son of Jehieli and his brother Joel were put in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:21-22).

introduce: Ram is a figure belonging to the line of Perez, the son of Judah, who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah. The Ram mentioned in 1 Chronicles 2:25 and 27 is recorded as the firstborn of Jerahmeel and as a member of a family of the tribe of Judah.
lifetime: Ram was born as the firstborn of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron, the grandson of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:5, 2:25). He had younger brothers: Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah (1 Chronicles 2:25). His sons are Maaz, Jamin, and Eker (1 Chronicles 2:27). Jerahmeel had another wife, Atarah, who was the mother of Onam (1 Chronicles 2:26).

introduce: Ram is a name that appears in Job chapter 32 in the introduction "Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram," and is a designation referring to the clan to which Elihu belonged (Job 32:2). Elihu appears as a figure distinct from Job's three friends (Job 32:1-6).
lifetime: The Bible introduces Elihu as "the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram" (Job 32:2). There is no record of Ram's own generational position or life. The fact that Elihu was younger than Job and his three friends appears in Job 32:6.
event: No specific deeds or events of Ram himself are recorded in the Bible, and he appears only in the designation "the family of Ram," to which Elihu belonged (Job 32:2).

call: Father of Jehonadab (founder of the Rechabite clan)
introduce: Rechab is recorded as the father of Jehonadab, who went with Jehu into the temple of Baal, and his descendants were called the Rechabites (2 Kings 10:15, 10:23; Jeremiah 35:2, 35:6). 1 Chronicles 2:55 records that the Kenites, including the clans of the scribes, came from "Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab."
lifetime: The Bible gives no account of Rechab's own life. 1 Chronicles 2:55 records that the Kenites came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab (1 Chronicles 2:55), and Jehonadab is recorded as the son of Rechab (2 Kings 10:15; he is recorded as Jonadab in Jeremiah 35:6).
event: No deeds of Rechab himself are recorded. His son Jehonadab came to meet Jehu, took his hand, and rode up into his chariot (2 Kings 10:15), and went with Jehu into the temple of Baal (2 Kings 10:23).
character: The biblical text does not directly describe Rechab's personal character, but his descendants held to the strict tradition of abstaining from wine and living as nomads that he established, generation after generation (Jeremiah 35:6-10). This tradition became the background for his name settling into a family designation, the Rechabites (Jeremiah 35:2).

call: Descendant of Hammath (ancestor of the Kenite scribes)
introduce: Rechab is the name of a house connected with the Kenites and recorded as "Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab" (1 Chronicles 2:55); he is mentioned as the ancestor of the Rechabites, who later in Judah kept abstinence from wine and life in tents (Jeremiah 35:6-10).
lifetime: The Bible records that the Kenites, including the clans of the scribes, came from "Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab," showing that the house of Rechab belongs to the line of Hammath (1 Chronicles 2:55). Nothing is recorded about Rechab's specific life or the time of his activity, and his son Jonadab left a command to his descendants (Jeremiah 35:6).
event: No direct achievements are recorded. Rechab's son Jonadab commanded his descendants never to drink wine, never to build houses, and to live in tents all their lives, and his descendants obeyed (Jeremiah 35:6-10). 1 Chronicles 2:55 records that the Kenites, the clans of the scribes who were the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites, came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab (1 Chronicles 2:55).

call: Father of Malchijah (rebuilder of the Dung Gate)
introduce: He is recorded as the father of Malchijah, who took part in rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 3:14).
lifetime: The Bible has no record of Rechab's own life; he appears in the record only as the father of Malchijah, who took part in repairing the wall of Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 3:14).
event: No deeds of Rechab himself are recorded. His son Malchijah, as ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Dung Gate, set up its doors, and fitted it with bolts and bars (Nehemiah 3:14).

introduce: Rechab is recorded as the father of Jonadab, and his descendants were called the Rechabites (Jeremiah 35:2, 35:6). Rechab's son Jonadab commanded his descendants to keep certain rules of life, and the Rechabites obeyed them (Jeremiah 35:6, 35:18).
event: No deeds of Rechab himself are recorded. His son Jonadab commanded his descendants never to drink wine, never to build houses, never to sow seed, never to plant vineyards, and to live in tents all their lives (Jeremiah 35:6-7), and the Rechabites obeyed and kept that command (Jeremiah 35:8-10). When Jeremiah brought the Rechabites into a chamber of the house of the LORD and offered them wine, they would not drink it because of Jonadab's command (Jeremiah 35:2-6). The LORD pointed to the obedience of the descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab to rebuke the disobedience of the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem (Jeremiah 35:14-17).

introduce: Rekem is recorded as one of the sons of Hebron in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:43). He is classified as one of the descendants of Judah connected with the house of Caleb (1 Chronicles 2:42).
lifetime: As a son of Hebron, his name is entered in the list of Hebron's descendants (1 Chronicles 2:43). He is also listed together with Hebron's sons Korah, Tappuah, and Shema (1 Chronicles 2:43). Rekem later became the father of Shammai (1 Chronicles 2:44).

introduce: Rephah appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Ephraim and is one of the sons of Beriah, the son of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 7:23, 7:25).
lifetime: Rephah is a son of Beriah and is recorded along with Resheph as one of Beriah's sons (1 Chronicles 7:25). Resheph's son is Telah (1 Chronicles 7:25).
