introduce: A figure in the genealogy of Jesus recorded in the Gospel of Luke, mentioned as the son of Melchi and the father of Matthat. He is a different person from Levi the son of Jacob or Levi the priestly tribe, and is classified as one of the ancestors in the line of Jesus' physical descent.
lifetime: He is the son of Melchi and the father of Matthat (Luke 3:24). In the genealogy of Luke 3:23-24, he is the one who comes after Heli and Matthat in the upward direction from Joseph.

introduce: Lydia in this entry is not an individual but the name of a people. Isaiah mentions "the archers of Lud" among the nations to which survivors will be sent (Isaiah 66:19), and Ezekiel records that Persia, Lydia, and Put served as warriors in the army of Tyre (Ezekiel 27:10).
lifetime: For the Lud people of this entry there is no record corresponding to an individual's life; they are only mentioned as a people who draw the bow (Isaiah 66:19) and as warriors in the army of Tyre (Ezekiel 27:10).
event: The prophet Isaiah mentioned Lud, who draw the bow, as one of the nations (Isaiah 66:19), and Ezekiel recorded that Lydia served as warriors in the army of Tyre (Ezekiel 27:10). Jeremiah 46:9 records "men of Lydia drawing the bow" who appear together with the Egyptian army (Jeremiah 46:9).

introduce: A woman from Moab who married Mahlon, a son of the Israelite Elimelech, and after being widowed followed her mother-in-law Naomi to Bethlehem and remarried to Boaz.
lifetime: In the land of Moab she married Mahlon son of Elimelech, but her husband died (Ruth 1:4-5). She resolved to return to Bethlehem with her mother-in-law Naomi (Ruth 1:16-19). In Bethlehem she went to glean in the field of Boaz and met him there (Ruth 2:2-3). Afterward, following Naomi's instructions, she proposed to Boaz at the threshing floor (Ruth 3:7-9), and she married Boaz and bore Obed (Ruth 4:13-17).
event: In spite of Naomi's urging, she did not remain in the land of Moab but insisted on going with her to Israel, and succeeded in returning (Ruth 1:16). She gleaned in the field of Boaz and supported Naomi (Ruth 2:17-18). By marrying Boaz on the basis of the kinsman-redeemer system, she carried on the line of the house of Elimelech (Ruth 4:9-10). She formed the lineage that made her the great-grandmother of King David (Ruth 4:21-22).
character: She showed utmost devotion to her mother-in-law Naomi (Ruth 1:16-17). She was regarded by Boaz as a woman of noble character (Ruth 3:11), and her neighbors also judged her to be a daughter-in-law better than seven sons (Ruth 4:15). She is portrayed as one who listened to the counsel of others, observed custom, and worked faithfully (Ruth 2:2, 3:5).

introduce: Rephaiah is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles 4 of the Old Testament, introduced as a son of Ishi, one of the houses of the tribe of Simeon.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Ishi in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:42).
event: Five hundred of the Simeonites, with Ishi's sons Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel as their leaders, went to Mount Seir, struck down the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped, and settled there (1 Chronicles 4:42-43). Rephaiah is one of these four brothers.

introduce: Rephaiah is a figure appearing in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, one of the sons of Tola of the tribe of Issachar, and is recorded as a head of a family.
lifetime: Rephaiah was born as a son of Tola, the son of Issachar (1 Chronicles 7:1-2). Together with Uzzi, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, he was a head of the house of their father Tola (1 Chronicles 7:2).
event: In the days of King David, the total number of the descendants of Tola, including Rephaiah, who were classified as mighty men of valor was 22,600 (1 Chronicles 7:2).
character: In the biblical record there is no description of his personal character or specific traits (-)

introduce: Rephaiah is recorded as a son of Binea in the family tree of the house of Saul. He is a member of the genealogy of the house of Saul of the tribe of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles 8 and 9.
lifetime: In the genealogy of the house of Saul of the tribe of Benjamin, Rephaiah is recorded as the son of Binea, whom Moza fathered among the descendants of Saul's son Jonathan, and his son is Elasah (1 Chronicles 9:39-43). In 1 Chronicles 8:37, which hands down the same genealogy, this name is recorded as "Raphah."
character: The Bible gives no specific account of Rephaiah's personal deeds or character (1 Chronicles 8:37, 1 Chronicles 9:43).

call: Son of Hur (ruler of a district of Jerusalem)
introduce: Rephaiah is one of those who took part in the work of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah; he was the son of Hur and ruler over half of the district of Jerusalem.
lifetime: He is recorded as ruler of half of the district of Jerusalem during the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 3:9).
event: During the work of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem, he repaired a section of the wall (Nehemiah 3:9).

call: Ancestor of the temple servants (Nethinim) who returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Rezin is a figure appearing in Ezra and Nehemiah of the Old Testament, an ancestor of one of the Nethinim who ended their life of exile in Babylon and returned to Jerusalem.
lifetime: He lived during the Babylonian exile, and his house is recorded as one of the families of the Nethinim who returned to Jerusalem after the decree of King Cyrus of Persia (Ezra 2:48). His descendants were included in the list of those who returned to Jerusalem under the leadership of Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 7:50).
event: His descendants, the sons of Rezin, are recorded among the Nethinim in the list of the people of Israel who returned from exile to Jerusalem and Judah together with Zerubbabel and others (Ezra 2:1-2, 2:43, 2:48). They also appear as the descendants of Rezin among the Nethinim in the list of returnees recorded in Nehemiah 7 (Nehemiah 7:46, 7:50).

introduce: Reaiah is a figure appearing in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Reuben as the son of Micah and the father of Baal.
lifetime: In the genealogy of the descendants of Reuben that continues from Shemaiah son of Joel, he is recorded as the son of Micah son of Shimei, and his son is Baal (1 Chronicles 5:4-5).
event: In the biblical record, no particular achievement or historical event that he carried out is specified (1 Chronicles 5:5).

call: Ancestor of a family of returning temple servants (Nethinim)
introduce: In the time of Ezra and Nehemiah, he is the ancestor of Reaiah, or a figure representing the house of Reaiah, one of the families of the Nethinim who ended their life of exile in Babylon and returned to Jerusalem.
lifetime: He appears in the genealogy of the Nethinim recorded in the list of returnees from the Babylonian exile, and is stated to be one of the ancestors of the Nethinim who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:47, Nehemiah 7:50).
event: He is recorded as Reaiah's descendants in the list of the Nethinim who returned from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:43, 2:47; Nehemiah 7:46, 7:50). The Bible records no other deeds.

introduce: Reuel is a Benjamite who appears in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:8 as "Reuel, the great-grandson of Ibnijah." He is one person in the genealogical record of the Benjamites who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:8).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 9:8 speaks of "Meshullam, the son of Shephatiah, the grandson of Reuel, the great-grandson of Ibnijah," and records Reuel as a descendant of Ibnijah and an ancestor of Shephatiah. He belongs to the genealogy of the Benjamites who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:3, 7-8).
event: The Bible does not mention that Reuel led any particular event or left any historical achievement. His name appears only as an ancestor of Meshullam in the genealogy of the Benjamites who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:8).

call: Governor of Samaria (obstructer of the rebuilding of the temple)
introduce: Rehum was a governor of Samaria who was active in the time of King Artaxerxes of the Persian Empire, and he submitted a petition to the king in order to obstruct the Jews' work of rebuilding the city of Jerusalem.
lifetime: In the time of King Artaxerxes of Persia, he carried out official duties as an officer of Samaria, and together with Shimshai the scribe and their associates he drew up a letter opposing the rebuilding of Jerusalem and reported it to the king (Ezra 4:8-9). He was involved in obtaining from the king an order to stop the Jews' building of the wall (Ezra 4:23).
event: Together with Shimshai the scribe, he drew up an accusation to the effect that the Jews' rebuilding of the wall would be harmful to the king (Ezra 4:11-16). This petition contained the argument that Jerusalem had been a rebellious city in the past and that, if it were rebuilt, they would refuse the king's taxes and tribute (Ezra 4:13). As a result he obtained a reply from the king ordering the work to be stopped, and when the copy of that decree was read, he went in haste to Jerusalem with Shimshai the scribe and their associates and stopped the work by force and power over the people of Judah (Ezra 4:23).
character: He used his administrative authority to try to exert direct influence on the decisions of the central government, and showed a strategic side in checking the growth of a particular group under the banner of political justification (Ezra 4:17-22).

introduce: A Levite recorded as the son of Bani, who took part in the work of repairing the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah.
lifetime: He took part in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem led by Nehemiah and, as a son of Bani the Levite, repaired one section of the wall (Nehemiah 3:17).
event: When the wall of Jerusalem was repaired, Rehum, as a son of Bani the Levite, took charge of one section of the wall and repaired it (Nehemiah 3:17).

introduce: Rehum was a member of the community of Israel that returned to Judah after the Babylonian exile, and a figure whose name was entered on the covenant document sealed in the time of Nehemiah.
lifetime: As one of the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian exile, he took part in the sealing together with the representatives of the people in the covenant renewal led by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:25).
event: When the firm covenant, drawn up chiefly by Nehemiah the governor of Judah, the priests, and the Levites, was put into writing and sealed, he was recorded as one of the leaders of the people who signed the list (Nehemiah 10:25).

introduce: Libni is a great-grandson of Levi, a grandson of Merari, and a son of Mahli, a figure belonging to the descendants of Merari in the tribe of Levi.
lifetime: Libni is recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Merari as the son of Mahli, the son of Merari (1 Chronicles 6:19, 29). His son is Shimei (1 Chronicles 6:29).
event: The Bible records no deeds of Libni himself; in the genealogy of the descendants of Merari in 1 Chronicles 6:29 he appears only as the son of Mahli and the father of Shimei. The descendants of Merari were put in charge of the frames, crossbars, posts, and bases of the tabernacle (Numbers 3:36-37).

call: Son of Laadah (descendant of Shelah, son of Judah)
introduce: Mareshah is a figure mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as a descendant of Shelah, the son of Judah, and as the son of Laadah.
lifetime: As the son of Laadah, a descendant of Shelah the son of Judah, he has his place within a family of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:21).
event: The Bible records no deeds of Mareshah himself; in 1 Chronicles 4:21 he appears only in the expression "Laadah the father of Mareshah."

introduce: Mary Magdalene was from Magdala in the region of Galilee, a woman disciple and witness who followed Jesus during his public ministry. According to the Gospel accounts, she is portrayed as a figure who played a key role from the early days of Jesus' ministry through the crucifixion and up to the scene of the resurrection.
lifetime: She is recorded as the woman called Mary Magdalene, out of whom seven demons had gone (Luke 8:2). Together with many women she served Jesus and his disciples out of their own means (Luke 8:3), and she was among the women who had followed Jesus from Galilee and served him (Matthew 27:55-56). She stood by the cross of Jesus (John 19:25), saw where Jesus was laid (Mark 15:47), went to the tomb early on the first day of the week while it was still dark (John 20:1), and became the first person to whom the risen Jesus appeared (Mark 16:9; John 20:14-16).
event: On the first day of the week she came to the tomb, saw that the stone had been removed, and ran to tell Simon Peter and the other disciple whom Jesus loved (John 20:1-2). While weeping bitterly by the tomb, she spoke with the risen Jesus who appeared to her (John 20:14-16). Jesus told her to tell his brothers that he was ascending to God, and she went to the disciples and told them she had seen the Lord (John 20:17-18).
character: She showed a devoted attitude: even in the crisis when Jesus was suffering, she did not flee but stayed by the cross to the end (Matthew 27:56). She was also a person of deep attachment and loyalty to Jesus, going to the tomb early in the morning as soon as the Sabbath had passed (Mark 16:1). When she met the risen Jesus, she recognized him, immediately called him Teacher, and followed his command, which shows her trust and obedience (John 20:16-18).

introduce: A figure appearing in the New Testament, one of the women who were present at the scene of Jesus' crucifixion. She is recorded under the designation "the wife of Clopas," an expression used to distinguish her from the other Marys.
lifetime: She is mentioned as one of the women who stood by the cross when Jesus was crucified (John 19:25).
event: At the crucifixion of Jesus, she stood by the cross together with Jesus' mother, his mother's sister, and Mary Magdalene (John 19:25).

introduce: Mary of Bethany is a figure appearing in the New Testament, the sister of Martha and Lazarus, who lived in the village of Bethany near Jerusalem. She is recorded in the Gospels as someone who had a close relationship with Jesus.
lifetime: When her brother Lazarus was ill, she and her sister sent word to Jesus (John 11:3), and after Lazarus died she came to where Jesus was, fell at his feet, and wept (John 11:32-33). When Martha welcomed Jesus into her house, her sister Mary sat at the Lord's feet and listened to his word (Luke 10:38-39), and when a dinner was given for Jesus at Bethany before his passion, she poured out the perfume (John 12:2-3).
event: When Martha welcomed Jesus into her house, Mary chose to sit at Jesus' feet and listen to his word rather than attend to the housework (Luke 10:38-40). When Jesus came after Lazarus had already been in the tomb four days, Mary came to where Jesus was, fell at his feet, and mourned her brother's death (John 11:17, 32). At the dinner for Jesus, she brought a pint of very expensive pure nard perfume, poured it on Jesus' feet, and wiped his feet with her hair (John 12:3).
character: Unlike her sister Martha, who was busy preparing food, Mary showed an attentive attitude, focusing on Jesus' teaching (Luke 10:39-40). She showed a devoted side by freely using her own costly perfume (John 12:3), and she is portrayed as acting with a view to preparing for Jesus' death and burial (John 12:7).

call: Mary, the mother of John Mark
introduce: Mary was a believer in the early Jerusalem church and the mother of John, who was called Mark (Acts 12:12).
lifetime:
She lived in Jerusalem and owned her own house (Acts 12:12).
She had a son John, who was called Mark (Acts 12:12).
A servant girl named Rhoda came to answer the gate when Peter knocked at the door of her house (Acts 12:13).
Mark is recorded as the nephew of Barnabas, so he was a relative of Barnabas (Colossians 4:10).
event:
During the persecution by King Herod, many people had gathered in her house and were praying (Acts 12:12).
After Peter was delivered from prison with the help of an angel, he went to her house (Acts 12:12).

introduce: Mary of Rome is a figure mentioned by the apostle Paul in his letter to the church in Rome, a woman named when Paul sent greetings to the Christians in Rome. The Bible has no detailed record of her lineage, background, or specific activities.
lifetime: In the course of sending greetings to the believers in Rome, Paul mentioned a person named Mary (Romans 16:6). The Bible has no record of what kind of life she specifically lived within the community of the church in Rome.
event: Mary is recorded as a person who worked very hard for the saints in Rome (Romans 16:6). Paul acknowledged this labor of hers and named her in his letter to the church in Rome in order to remember her contribution.
character: The Bible describes her as one who worked very hard, which suggests that she was zealously active in the Roman church community of that time and devoted to helping other believers or serving the church (Romans 16:6). No further information about her temperament or specific character is mentioned.

introduce: Maacah was the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur, one of the wives of David, and the mother of Absalom (2 Samuel 3:3).
lifetime: As the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur, she became a wife of David and bore Absalom in Hebron (2 Samuel 3:2-3). After that, her doings are not recorded in the Bible.
event: The Bible records no deeds of Maacah herself. Her son Absalom, after killing Amnon (2 Samuel 13:28-29), fled to Talmai king of Geshur, Maacah's father (2 Samuel 13:37; 3:3).

call: Father of Achish king of Gath
introduce: Maacah is mentioned as the father of Achish, who was king of the Philistine region of Gath. His name appears only once in the Old Testament, in 1 Kings chapter 2, verse 39, and there is no detailed record about him.
event: While his son Achish was king of Gath, two servants of Shimei ran away to Achish, and Shimei went to Gath to look for his servants and came to Achish (1 Kings 2:39-40). In this passage Maacah is mentioned only as the father of Achish king of Gath, and there is no record that Maacah himself led or took part in the events.

introduce: Maacah, the daughter of Absalom (Abishalom), became the wife of Rehoboam and bore Abijah king of Judah (2 Chronicles 11:20), and in the time of King Asa she held the position of queen mother (1 Kings 15:10, 13).
lifetime: She is recorded as the daughter of Absalom (2 Chronicles 11:20), and she married Rehoboam and bore Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith (2 Chronicles 11:20). Of all his wives and concubines, Rehoboam loved Maacah the daughter of Absalom most, and he appointed her son Abijah as chief and meant to make him king (2 Chronicles 11:21-22). In the time of King Asa she held the position of queen mother as his mother (1 Kings 15:10, 13).
event: She made a detestable wooden image for Asherah (1 Kings 15:13). Because of this, she was removed from her position as queen mother by King Asa, and Asa cut down the image she had made and burned it at the Kidron brook (2 Chronicles 15:16).
character: According to the biblical record, she showed a religious inclination of leading or supporting idol worship (1 Kings 15:13), and as a powerful holder of real authority in the royal court she maintained her influence up to the time of King Asa (1 Kings 15:10).

introduce: Maacah is recorded as a concubine of Caleb, the son of Hezron of the tribe of Judah. She is mentioned in the genealogy of the house of Judah as a woman who bore children (1 Chronicles 2:18, 48).
lifetime: As Caleb's concubine she bore the sons Sheber and Tirhanah (1 Chronicles 2:48). No detailed record of her origin or death appears in the Bible.
event: No specific event is recorded as her achievement; only the record that she bore sons in the course of the increase of Caleb's descendants is found (1 Chronicles 2:48).

introduce: A woman mentioned as the wife of Machir of the tribe of Manasseh; she married Machir, the father of Gilead, and had children.
lifetime: She is recorded as the wife of Machir the son of Manasseh, and through her two sons, Peresh and Sheresh, were born (1 Chronicles 7:16).
event: She bore Peresh and Sheresh to Machir, and the Bible records nothing about her doings afterward or any special event (1 Chronicles 7:16).

introduce: A woman recorded as the wife of Jeiel, the ancestor of the people of Gibeon, who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: She is the wife of Jeiel, who is recorded as having lived in Gibeon (1 Chronicles 8:29; 9:35). As Jeiel's sons, his firstborn Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, Zecher, and others are listed (1 Chronicles 8:30-31), but the text does not state whether these sons were born of Maacah.
event: The Bible records no deeds of Maacah herself. The family line of Jeiel, to whom she is mentioned as wife, is connected to the genealogy of King Saul running through Ner, Kish, and Saul in 1 Chronicles 9:36-39.

introduce: Maacah is recorded as the father of Hanan, one of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:43).
lifetime: The Bible does not record Maacah's own life; his name appears in the list of David's mighty men as the father of his son Hanan (1 Chronicles 11:43).
event: His son Hanan is recorded in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:43). No office or event of Maacah himself is recorded.

introduce: Maacah is recorded in 1 Chronicles 27:16 as the father of Shephatiah, the chief of the Simeonites.
lifetime: The Bible does not record Maacah's own life; in the list of those who were over the tribes, his son Shephatiah appears as the chief of the Simeonites (1 Chronicles 27:16).
event: In the list of the officers over the tribes of Israel in 1 Chronicles 27:16 it is recorded, "over the Simeonites was Shephatiah son of Maacah," and no office or event of Maacah himself is recorded.

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: Maaseiah was active in the time of the kingdom of Judah, a son of Adaiah and one of the commanders of hundreds who made a covenant with Jehoiada the priest (2 Chronicles 23:1).
lifetime: In the seventh year, when Jehoiada strengthened himself and made a covenant with the commanders of hundreds, he was one of the commanders who took part in that covenant (2 Chronicles 23:1).
event: Together with Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, and Elishaphat son of Zichri, he made a covenant with Jehoiada the priest (2 Chronicles 23:1). These went about in Judah and gathered the Levites from all the towns of Judah and the heads of the families of Israel, and came to Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 23:2).

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: Maaseiah was a man recorded as "the officer" who took the count of the soldiers in the time of King Uzziah of the kingdom of Judah (2 Chronicles 26:11).
lifetime: Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer took the count of the number of King Uzziah's fighting soldiers (2 Chronicles 26:11).
event: According to the number counted by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer, Uzziah's fighting soldiers went out to war by divisions, under the authority of Hananiah, one of the king's officers (2 Chronicles 26:11). No other deeds of Maaseiah himself are recorded.

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: A figure recorded as a son of Ahaz, king of the kingdom of Judah, and a member of the royal family.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Ahaz king of Judah and was killed in the course of the war with Pekah, king of northern Israel (2 Chronicles 28:7).
event: When Pekah king of Israel invaded Judah, he was killed by Zichri, a man of Ephraim (2 Chronicles 28:7). As the king's son, he lost his life together with Azrikam the governor of the palace and Elkanah the second to the king (2 Chronicles 28:7).

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: A figure recorded in the time of Josiah king of Judah as the governor of the city (the chief official of the town). In the biblical text he appears as "Maaseiah the governor of the city" (2 Chronicles 34:8).
lifetime: In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, when the king had finished purifying the land and the temple and intended to repair the house of God, he sent him together with Shaphan son of Azaliah and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder (2 Chronicles 34:8).
event: Together with Shaphan son of Azaliah and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder, whom the king sent for the repair of the temple, he went to Hilkiah the high priest and handed over the money that had been brought into the house of God (2 Chronicles 34:8-9).

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: The Maaseiah who appears in Ezra 10 came from a priestly family and is a man whose name is recorded among the priests who, after the return from exile, had taken foreign women as wives. He is recorded among the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers (Ezra 10:18).
lifetime: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah are recorded as the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers, and they belong to the company of the priests who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:18).
event: His name was recorded among those of the company of the priests who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:18). In this passage they pledged by giving their hand to send their wives away, and for their guilt they offered one ram as a guilt offering (Ezra 10:19).

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: In Ezra 10, Maaseiah is a man whose name is recorded as a descendant of Harim among the priests who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:21).
lifetime: Ezra 10:21 records, "From the descendants of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah," and this is included in the company of the priests who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:18, 21).
event: In the list of priests in Ezra 10, his name is recorded among the descendants of Harim who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:21).

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: Maaseiah is recorded as a descendant of Pashhur among the company of the priests who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:18, 22).
lifetime: In the process of setting right the matter of marriages with foreign women led by Ezra, his name is recorded as a descendant of Pashhur among the priests who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:18, 22).
event: He was included as a descendant of Pashhur in the list recorded of the company of the priests who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:18, 22).

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: A man of the descendants of Pahath-moab among the people of Israel who ended their life of exile in Babylon and returned to Jerusalem in the time of Ezra.
lifetime: As a member of the community that returned from the Babylonian exile, he is included in the list at the time when Ezra investigated those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:30).
event: When Ezra investigated the matter of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:16-17), he was recorded in the list as one of the descendants of Pahath-moab who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:30, 10:44).

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: Maaseiah is recorded as the father of Azariah, and in Nehemiah 3:23 he is introduced as the grandson of Ananiah (Nehemiah 3:23).
lifetime: In the passage recording the repair of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, his name appears along with the statement that his son Azariah repaired the section near his own house (Nehemiah 3:23). The Bible has no record of Maaseiah's own doings.
event: His son Azariah repaired the section near his own house (Nehemiah 3:23).

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: Maaseiah is one of those who stood at the right of Ezra the teacher when he read the book of the Law after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 8:4).
lifetime:
There is no specific record in the Bible of Maaseiah's birth, family line, or death (Nehemiah 8:4).
His name is recorded among those who stood at the right of Ezra when he stood on the wooden platform specially built, in the period of the return from exile (Nehemiah 8:4).
event: When Ezra the scribe stood on the special wooden platform set up in the square before the Water Gate and read the book of the Law, he stood at Ezra's right (Nehemiah 8:1-4).

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: Maaseiah was a Levite active in the time of Ezra after the return from the Babylonian exile, and he is recorded as one of those who made the people standing in the square before the Water Gate understand the Law when Ezra read the book of the Law (Nehemiah 8:7).
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, when Ezra read the book of the Law before the people gathered in the square before the Water Gate in Jerusalem, his name is recorded among those who made the people understand the Law as they stood in their places (Nehemiah 8:7).
event: When Ezra read the book of the Law, Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites made the people standing in their places understand the Law (Nehemiah 8:7). It is further recorded that they read the book of the Law of God and gave the sense of it, so that the people understood everything that was read (Nehemiah 8:8).

call: Official in the time of Nehemiah
meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: Maaseiah was one of the heads of the people of the community of Judah who had returned from the Babylonian exile, and is recorded as one of those who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14, 25).
lifetime: His name is recorded as one of the heads of the people among those who sealed the covenant to keep the Law of God in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:1, 14, 25).
event: He was among those who sealed the covenant, swearing with a curse to follow the Law of God and to keep all the commandments, ordinances, and statutes of the LORD (Nehemiah 10:29). This covenant included not giving their daughters to the peoples of the land and not taking their daughters for their sons (Nehemiah 10:30), and not buying goods on the Sabbath or on a holy day (Nehemiah 10:31).

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: A figure of the tribe of Judah, one of the descendants who, after the return from the Babylonian exile, settled and lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:5).
lifetime: He was a descendant of Judah and the son of Baruch, the grandson of Col-hozeh, and the great-grandson of Hazaiah. He is also recorded as the great-great-grandson of Adaiah, the fifth-generation descendant of Joiarib, the sixth-generation descendant of Zechariah, and the seventh-generation descendant of the Shilonite (Nehemiah 11:5). His name is recorded in the list of the descendants of Judah who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 11:4-5).
event: He is recorded as one of the descendants of Judah who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:4-5). At that time the heads of the people stayed in Jerusalem, and of the rest of the people, lots were cast so that one in ten would come and live in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:1).

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: Maaseiah is recorded as the fifth ancestor of Sallu in the genealogy of Sallu of the descendants of Benjamin, and in the genealogy he is the son of Ithiel (Nehemiah 11:7).
lifetime: There is no specific record of Maaseiah himself in the Bible. His descendant Sallu is recorded as one of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 11:4, 7).
event: The Bible has no record of Maaseiah's own doings, and his descendant Sallu appears as a descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:7).

call: Priest in the time of Nehemiah
meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: Maaseiah is recorded as a figure of a priestly family who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 12:42).
lifetime: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, his name is recorded among those who were with Jezrahiah, the overseer of the singers (Nehemiah 12:42).
event: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, when the two thanksgiving choirs took their stand in the house of God (Nehemiah 12:40), Maaseiah was with Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer, and the singers sang loudly, and their overseer was Jezrahiah (Nehemiah 12:42).

call: Priest in the time of King Zedekiah
meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: Maaseiah is a figure recorded as a priest and the father of Zephaniah (Jeremiah 21:1, 29:25, 37:3).
lifetime: His son Zephaniah is recorded as an envoy sent by King Zedekiah to Jeremiah (Jeremiah 21:1, 37:3). The Bible has no record of Maaseiah's own doings.
event: His son Zephaniah, son of Maaseiah the priest, went as an envoy sent by King Zedekiah to Jeremiah and asked him to inquire of the LORD, since Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon was attacking, that he might withdraw from them (Jeremiah 21:1). This was the doing of his son Zephaniah, and Maaseiah's own doings are not recorded.

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: Maaseiah is recorded as the father of Zedekiah, the prophet who prophesied falsely to the Judean exiles in Babylon in the time of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 29:21).
lifetime: There is no record of Maaseiah himself in the Bible, and his son Zedekiah is mentioned as one who prophesied falsely to the exiles (Jeremiah 29:21).
event: His son Zedekiah, together with Ahab son of Kolaiah, was singled out as one who prophesied falsely in the name of the LORD, and received the word that he would be delivered into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and be put to death before the eyes of the exiles (Jeremiah 29:21). The Judean exiles in Babylon would use them as a curse, as those whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire (Jeremiah 29:22).

meaning: Work of the LORD, deed of the LORD
introduce: Maaseiah, the son of Shallum, is recorded as a doorkeeper in the house of the LORD in the time of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 35:4).
lifetime: In the time of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah (Jeremiah 35:1), he is recorded as a doorkeeper in the house of the LORD (Jeremiah 35:4).
event: Jeremiah brought the Rechabites into the chamber of the sons of Hanan in the house of the LORD, and that chamber was beside the chamber of the officials, above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum the doorkeeper (Jeremiah 35:3-4). In this episode no action of Maaseiah is recorded; only the location of his chamber is mentioned.

introduce: A figure of a priestly family active in the time of Nehemiah, one of the leaders who took part in making the covenant of the community after the return from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: In the time of Nehemiah, his name is recorded as a priest among those who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:8).
event: When Nehemiah, the officials, and the priests sealed the covenant, he entered his name on the list as a priest (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:8).

call: Ancestor of Shephatiah (of the line of Perez of Judah)
introduce: Mahalalel is recorded as the fifth ancestor of Athaiah, a descendant of Perez of the tribe of Judah, and is the father of Shephatiah. He is mentioned in the genealogies of the Bible as a figure who carries on the line of the house of Perez.
lifetime: Nehemiah 11:4 introduces Athaiah, a descendant of Perez, as the great-great-grandson of Shephatiah and the fifth-generation descendant of Mahalalel, and accordingly Mahalalel is the father of Shephatiah (Nehemiah 11:4).
event: The Bible has no record of Mahalalel's own doings, and his descendant Athaiah is recorded as a descendant of Judah (a descendant of Perez) who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:4).

introduce: Mahalath was a wife of Rehoboam, the first king of the kingdom of Judah, and was a daughter born to Jerimoth the son of David and to Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse.
lifetime: She was born as a daughter of Jerimoth, a son of King David, and afterward married Rehoboam king of Judah and became his wife (2 Chronicles 11:18). The sons of Rehoboam, Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham, are recorded next (2 Chronicles 11:19).
event: She became the wife of Rehoboam (2 Chronicles 11:18). It is then recorded that she bore sons, namely Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham (2 Chronicles 11:19).

call: Levite leader in charge of offerings in the time of Hezekiah
introduce: Mahath was one of the Levites appointed in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah as overseers of the temple's contributions, the tithes, and the dedicated things (2 Chronicles 31:12-13).
lifetime: He is a Levite recorded as the son of Amasai of the Kohathites, and his name appears among the Levites who rose up to cleanse the temple in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 29:12). By the order of King Hezekiah and of Azariah, who was over the house of God, he became one who took care of the offerings under Conaniah and his brother Shimei (2 Chronicles 31:12-13).
event: When Hezekiah gave the command to prepare chambers in the house of the LORD and to bring in the contributions, the tithes, and the dedicated things, Mahath, together with Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, and Benaiah, became an overseer under Conaniah and his brother Shimei (2 Chronicles 31:11-13).
character: According to the biblical record, as a Levite he was faithful in the duties entrusted to him, and in particular, having won the trust of King Hezekiah regarding his duties, he was given the weighty task of managing the holy things of the temple (2 Chronicles 31:13). He cooperated with his colleagues and contributed to establishing a fair system of distribution (2 Chronicles 31:15).

introduce: Malchijah is a figure of a priestly family recorded as the father of Pashhur, and he appears as an ancestor in the genealogy of Adaiah the priest who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:12, 1 Chronicles 9:12).
lifetime: There is no record of Malchijah himself in the Bible, and his descendant Adaiah is recorded as a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 11:12, 1 Chronicles 9:12).
event: The Bible has no record of Malchijah's own doings, and his descendant Adaiah is recorded as one of his brothers, eight hundred and twenty-two in number, who did the work of the house of God (Nehemiah 11:12).

introduce: Malchijah is a figure appearing in the Bible, one of the descendants of Parosh, an Israelite recorded in the time of Ezra as having taken a foreign woman as his wife.
lifetime: Malchijah is a figure recorded in the list at the time of the dismissal of the foreign wives led by Ezra after the return from exile (Ezra 10:25). He is mentioned as one of the descendants of Parosh who had foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:25).
event: He is recorded as one of those involved in the dismissal of the foreign wives led by Ezra in order to keep the community of Israel pure (Ezra 10:25). When Ezra confessed the sin and urged them to separate from the foreign women, the assembly answered that they would do as he said (Ezra 10:10-12).

introduce: He is one of those who ended their exile in Babylon and returned to Jerusalem in the time of Ezra. He is recorded as a descendant of Parosh, and his name appears in connection with the matter of marriages within the community of Ezra.
lifetime: In the time of Ezra, his name is recorded as a descendant of Parosh in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:25, 10:44).
event: He is recorded as one of the descendants of Parosh who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:25, 10:44). It is recorded that when Ezra urged them to separate from the foreign women, the assembly answered that they would do as he said (Ezra 10:11-12).

introduce: Malchijah is a figure who appears in the book of Ezra and belongs to the descendants of Harim. After the return from exile, in the time of Ezra, he is recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women.
lifetime: In the time of Ezra, his name is recorded as a descendant of Harim in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:31).
event: He was included in the list as one of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:31).

introduce: Malchijah, a son of Harim, took part in the repair of the wall of Jerusalem under Nehemiah (Nehemiah 3:11).
lifetime: He took part in the repair of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, and together with Hasshub son of Pahath-moab he repaired another section and the Tower of the Ovens (Nehemiah 3:11).
event: Malchijah son of Harim, together with Hasshub son of Pahath-moab, repaired a section of the wall of Jerusalem and the Tower of the Ovens (Nehemiah 3:11).

call: Son of Rechab (repairer of the Dung Gate)
introduce: Malchijah was a man who took part in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah after the return from exile; he was a leader ruling the district of Beth-haccherem and a son of Rechab (Nehemiah 3:14).
lifetime:
He was born as a son of Rechab and held the office of ruling the district of Beth-haccherem (Nehemiah 3:14).
When the wall of Jerusalem was rebuilt under the leadership of Nehemiah after the Babylonian exile, he took part in it (Nehemiah 3:14).
No specific record of his birth, family background, or death otherwise appears in the Bible (Nehemiah 3:14).
event:
During the work of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem, he repaired the Dung Gate, one of the gates of the city of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:14).
He completed the building work of setting up the gate of the Dung Gate, hanging its doors, and fitting it with bolts and bars (Nehemiah 3:14).

introduce: Malchijah is a figure recorded as a goldsmith, who took part in the repair of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 3:31).
lifetime: Malchijah the goldsmith took charge of the section opposite the Inspection Gate in the work of repairing the wall (Nehemiah 3:31).
event: Malchijah the goldsmith repaired the section opposite the Inspection Gate, extending from the house of the temple servants and the merchants to the upper room at the corner of the wall (Nehemiah 3:31).

call: Leader who stood at Ezra's left
introduce: Malchijah is one of those who stood at the left of the wooden platform (Nehemiah 8:4) when Ezra read the book of the Law in the square before the Water Gate (Nehemiah 8:1-3).
lifetime: His name is recorded among those who stood at the left when Ezra stood on the wooden platform specially built (Nehemiah 8:4). No other record of his birth, family line, or death appears in the Bible.
event: He was one of those who stood at the left when Ezra stood on the wooden platform. At the right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, and at the left stood Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hash-baddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam (Nehemiah 8:4).

call: Priest at the dedication of the wall
introduce: Malchijah is a figure of the time of Nehemiah, recorded as one of the priests who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem after the return from exile.
lifetime: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, his name is recorded among those who were with Jezrahiah, the overseer of the singers (Nehemiah 12:42).
event: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, when the two thanksgiving choirs took their stand in the house of God (Nehemiah 12:40), Malchijah was with Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Elam, and Ezer, and the singers sang loudly (Nehemiah 12:42).

call: Son of the king (owner of the cistern into which Jeremiah was thrown)
introduce: Malchijah was a figure active in the time of Zedekiah king of Judah, called in the biblical record "Malchijah, the king's son." The cistern into which Jeremiah was thrown is recorded as his cistern (Jeremiah 38:6).
lifetime: Malchijah is recorded as "the king's son," and the king of that time was Zedekiah (Jeremiah 38:5-6). His cistern was in the court of the guard (Jeremiah 38:6).
event: Jeremiah was thrown into his cistern. Those who told the king to put Jeremiah to death were the officials (Jeremiah 38:4), and the ones who threw Jeremiah into the cistern are recorded as "they" (Jeremiah 38:6). There was no water in the cistern, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into the mud (Jeremiah 38:6). What Malchijah himself did is not recorded in the text.

introduce: Malluch is a descendant of Bani, recorded as one of those within the community of Israel who married foreign women after the Babylonian exile (Ezra 10:29).
lifetime: He was one of the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian exile, and in the process of the separation from foreign women led by Ezra he was included in the list as a descendant of Bani (Ezra 10:29).
event: In Ezra's religious reform, it was revealed that he was married to a foreign woman, and his name was recorded in the list of those who would send away the woman and the children born of her (Ezra 10:29).

introduce: Malluch is one of the members of the community of Israel who ended their life of exile in Babylon and returned to Jerusalem. He is recorded as a descendant of Harim and appears in the list in the course of resolving the matter of marriages with foreign women led by Ezra.
lifetime: Malluch is a figure recorded in the list of the time of Ezra as a descendant of Harim (Ezra 10:31-32). He is included in the list on which names were entered to put an end to this when it came to light, after the return from exile, that the nobles and the people had married foreign women (Ezra 10:32).
event: As one of the people of Israel who had taken foreign women as wives, Malluch went through the event of having his own name stated in Ezra's investigation (Ezra 10:32). As a member of the descendants of Harim, he was recorded in the list of the assembly drawn up to carry out the religious ordinance in question (Ezra 10:32).

introduce: Malluch was a figure of a priestly family active in the time of Nehemiah after the Babylonian exile, recorded as one of the leaders who sealed the covenant document made after the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem.
lifetime: As a member of a priestly family that returned from the Babylonian exile, he took part in the covenant renewal led by Nehemiah and put his seal to it (Nehemiah 10:4, 10:8).
event: In the covenant where Nehemiah and the priests are listed as those who sealed it, Malluch's name was entered as one of the list of priests (Nehemiah 10:1-8). This covenant was an oath to follow the Law given by Moses the servant of God and to keep all the commandments, ordinances, and statutes of the LORD (Nehemiah 10:29).

call: Leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Malluch was one of those who took part in the social and religious rebuilding of the community of Israel after the return from the Babylonian exile, and belonged to the leading class in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:27).
lifetime: Malluch is included in the list of leaders who signed the sealed covenant document drawn up by the people of Israel in order to keep the Law of God and maintain a pure community (Nehemiah 10:27).
event: Malluch is recorded as one of the signatories in the event of the making of Nehemiah's covenant, in which they pledged to forbid intermarriage with foreigners, to observe the Sabbath and the festivals, and to pay the temple tax (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:27).

introduce: Mattaniah is a descendant of the tribe of Levi and a son of Heman, one of the musicians who were in charge of praise and instrumental music in the temple in the time of David.
lifetime: Mattaniah was a son of Heman the Levite and a member of the temple choir organization established by David (1 Chronicles 25:4). The sons of Heman were trumpet blowers (1 Chronicles 25:5).
event: He was chosen for the ninth division in the choir organization designated by David through the casting of lots, and his sons and brothers, twelve in all, were with him (1 Chronicles 25:16). Together with his brothers he devoted himself to playing instruments and praising in the house of God (1 Chronicles 25:6).

call: Descendant of Asaph (Levite in the time of Hezekiah)
introduce: Mattaniah is a Levite classified as a descendant of Asaph, and took part in cleansing the temple in the time of King Hezekiah.
lifetime: Among the Levites who rose up in the time of King Hezekiah, Mattaniah is recorded as one of the descendants of Asaph, together with Zechariah (2 Chronicles 29:12-13). In this passage there is no record of his father or ancestors.
event: He took part, as one of the descendants of Asaph among the Levites who rose up when King Hezekiah cleansed the temple (2 Chronicles 29:13). These gathered their brothers, consecrated themselves, and cleansed the house of the LORD as the king had commanded by the word of the LORD (2 Chronicles 29:15).

introduce: Mattaniah is a figure recorded in the list as one of the descendants of Elam who returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: He is one of the descendants of Elam among the people who returned to Jerusalem after ending the Babylonian exile (Ezra 10:26). In Ezra's investigation, he was singled out as one of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:26).
event: When Ezra, after arriving in Jerusalem, investigated those who had married foreign women, he belonged to the list of the descendants of Elam, and his name is entered in the list along with theirs (Ezra 10:26).

introduce: Mattaniah is one of the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian exile, a figure belonging to the descendants of Zattu.
lifetime: Mattaniah is a member of the community of Israel that returned from Babylon to Jerusalem, and is recorded in the list as one of the descendants of Zattu (Ezra 10:27).
event: After the return to Jerusalem, Mattaniah was singled out as one of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:27). Over this matter the people made a covenant with God to send away all these wives and their children and to act according to the Law (Ezra 10:3), and Ezra made them swear to do as this had been said (Ezra 10:5). The list ends with the words, "All these had taken foreign wives" (Ezra 10:44).

introduce: Mattaniah is a figure mentioned as a member of the descendants of Pahath-moab within the community of Israel after the Babylonian exile. According to the biblical record, he appears as one of those who had taken foreign women as wives.
lifetime: Mattaniah is recorded as a descendant of Pahath-moab among the people of Israel who ended their exile in Babylon and returned (Ezra 10:30). He was entered in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives, and for these there was a proposal to make a covenant with God to send away all the wives and their children (Ezra 10:3, 10:44).
event: He is a figure who had his name entered in the list of the people of Israel who had married foreign women, and he was included in the list in the course of dealing with the matter of foreign wives in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:30). This list was drawn up by investigating those who had taken foreign women in accordance with the covenant to act according to the Law (Ezra 10:3) (Ezra 10:17, 10:44).

introduce: Mattaniah is a figure recorded as a descendant of Bani in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:34-37, 10:44).
lifetime:
He is recorded as one of the descendants of Bani (Ezra 10:34, 10:37).
He was entered in the list as one who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:44).
His name was entered in the list drawn up after Ezra had the priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear to do as had been said, to send away the foreign wives and their children (Ezra 10:3, 10:5) (Ezra 10:37).
event: In the time of Ezra, with the oath to send away the foreign wives and their children and to act according to the Law having been taken (Ezra 10:3, 10:5), his name was recorded in the list of the descendants of Bani who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:34-37, 10:44).

call: Grandfather of Hanan (ancestor who oversaw the storehouses)
introduce: A figure whose name appears only in the genealogy "Hanan son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah" in the book of Nehemiah; he is the father of Zaccur and the grandfather of Hanan (Nehemiah 13:13).
lifetime: Mattaniah's name appears only in the passage where Hanan, whom Nehemiah appointed as assistant to the storehouse keepers, is introduced as "the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah" (Nehemiah 13:13).
event: Mattaniah's own activities are not recorded in the text. His grandson Hanan was appointed as an assistant among those who were set over the storehouses, together with Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah the Levite (Nehemiah 13:13).

call: Priest of the temple of Baal
introduce: Mattan was the priest of Baal who was killed before the altar when, after Jehoiada set the king's son on the throne as king, all the people tore down the temple of Baal (2 Kings 11:18).
lifetime: After Jehoiada had the king and the people make a covenant with the LORD that they should be the LORD's people, all the people went to the temple of Baal, tore it down, and killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altar (2 Kings 11:17-18). The Bible has no record of his family line or origin.
event: All the people went to the temple of Baal, tore it down, smashed its altars and idols, and killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altar (2 Kings 11:18, 2 Chronicles 23:17). This took place immediately after Jehoiada had the king and the people make a covenant that they should be the LORD's people (2 Kings 11:17, 2 Chronicles 23:16). The text does not separately record anything Mattan did.
character: Mattan served as the religious pillar that helped the Baal religion, which had flowed in from northern Israel, take root within the kingdom of Judah. As a spokesman of the system of Baal worship, he stood in a position opposed to the traditional faith system of Judah, and in the midst of the coup he was recorded as a symbolic figure who had to be dealt with first (2 Kings 11:18).

call: Father of Shephatiah (father of an official of Judah)
introduce: A figure recorded only as the father of Shephatiah (Jeremiah 38:1).
lifetime: Mattan's name appears only in the passage of Jeremiah 38:1 where "Shephatiah son of Mattan" is introduced. His son Shephatiah is recorded as one of those who heard what Jeremiah was saying to all the people in the time of King Zedekiah (Jeremiah 38:1).
event: What Mattan himself did is not recorded in the text. His son Shephatiah heard Jeremiah's words together with Gedaliah, Jucal, and Pashhur (Jeremiah 38:1), and afterward the officials told the king to put Jeremiah to death (Jeremiah 38:4).

call: Son of Levi (an ancestor of Jesus)
introduce: Matthat is a figure appearing in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Luke, recorded as a descendant of Nathan, the son of David.
lifetime: Matthat is recorded as the son of Levi and the father of Jorim (Luke 3:29). His line goes upward through Nathan to David (Luke 3:29-31). The name Matthat also appears in Luke 3:24, but he is another person, recorded as the father of Heli.

introduce: Mattenai is a figure recorded as one of the descendants of Bani in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:37, 10:44).
lifetime: Mattenai is recorded as one of the descendants of Bani (Ezra 10:34, 10:37). He is on the list of those who had taken foreign women, and this list was drawn up by investigating the matter of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:17, 10:44).
event: When Ezra prostrated himself before the house of God and confessed the sin (Ezra 10:1), Shecaniah proposed that they make a covenant with God to send away all these wives and their children (Ezra 10:2-3), and Ezra made the priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear to do as this had been said (Ezra 10:5). In the investigation that followed, Mattenai was entered in the list of the descendants of Bani who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:37, 10:44). The text records no separate word or action of his.

call: Priest of the house of Joiarib
introduce: Mattenai is a figure who appears in the list recording the priestly families of Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile, and in the time of Joiakim he was one of the heads of the priestly families (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:19).
lifetime: In the time of Joiakim the son of Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:10, 12:12), Mattenai is recorded as the head of the house of Joiarib (Nehemiah 12:19).
event: In the time of Joiakim, Mattenai was recorded in the list as a head of the priestly families, representing the house of Joiarib (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:19). No other deeds are recorded in the text.

call: Co-worker who read the Law with Ezra
introduce: Mattithiah is one of those who stood at the right of Ezra the teacher when he stood on the wooden platform in Jerusalem after the return from exile. Nehemiah 8:4 gives no explanation of his family or his duties.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the persons who stood at Ezra's right hand when Ezra read the book of the Law to the people in the square before the Water Gate of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 8:4).
event: He was one of the people who stood at the right of the wooden platform when Ezra the teacher stood on the specially built wooden platform (Nehemiah 8:4). When Ezra, standing above all the people, opened the book, all the people stood up (Nehemiah 8:5).

call: Firstborn of Jeduthun (fourteenth division of the temple praise)
introduce: Mattithiah is a descendant of Levi and a son of Jeduthun, a figure who led the fourteenth division of the musician lines in charge of the praise service in the temple in the time of David.
lifetime: He was a son of Jeduthun among those whom David set apart from the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun for service (1 Chronicles 25:1, 25:3), and under his father's direction he took the harp, sang spiritual songs, and gave thanks and praise to the LORD (1 Chronicles 25:3).
event: When those who gave praise, small and great alike, drew lots to obtain their duties (1 Chronicles 25:8), Mattithiah was chosen fourteenth, and his sons and brothers, twelve in all, were with him (1 Chronicles 25:21). Under his father's direction he was among those who served by singing in the house of the LORD God with cymbals, harps, and lyres (1 Chronicles 25:6).
character: According to the biblical record, he is portrayed as one who obeyed the duty, by the king's command, of taking instruments, prophesying, and giving praise in the temple of God (1 Chronicles 25:6). He is recorded as one of the six sons who represented the house of his father Jeduthun (1 Chronicles 25:3).

introduce: A man of the descendants of Nebo who, after the return from exile, took a foreign woman as his wife within the community and had to repent of it and deal with it.
lifetime: He belongs to the descendants of Nebo among the people of Israel who ended their life of exile in Babylon and returned to Jerusalem (Ezra 10:43).
event: When Ezra investigated the list of those among the returned exiles who had taken foreign women as wives, his name was included in that list (Ezra 10:43). Over this matter the people made a covenant with God to send away all the wives and their children and to act according to the Law (Ezra 10:3), and the list ends with the words, "All these had taken foreign wives" (Ezra 10:44).

introduce: Mesha is the king of Moab who appears in 2 Kings of the Old Testament. After the death of Ahab king of Israel, he refused to pay tribute to Israel and rebelled. The Bible records him as a sheep breeder who rendered to the king of Israel the wool of a hundred thousand lambs and a hundred thousand rams.
lifetime: After Ahab died, Mesha king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel (2 Kings 3:5). He went through a crisis in which the cities of Moab were torn down and the springs were stopped up by the combined army of Israel, Judah, and Edom (2 Kings 3:25). Seeing that the battle was too fierce for him, he tried to break through with seven hundred swordsmen to the king of Edom but could not (2 Kings 3:26), and he offered his firstborn son, who was to succeed him as king, as a burnt offering on the wall. Great fury came upon Israel, and they departed and returned each to his own land (2 Kings 3:27).
event: As ruler of Moab, he took an independent political course to break free from Israel's rule (2 Kings 3:5). In the invasion by the combined army of Israel, Judah, and Edom, the cities of Moab were torn down and only the stones of Kir-haraseth were left (2 Kings 3:25), and Mesha offered his firstborn son as a burnt offering on the wall (2 Kings 3:27). The text records that afterward great fury came upon Israel, and they departed and returned each to his own land (2 Kings 3:27).
character: The Bible describes him as a sheep breeder and mentions the economic background of rendering enormous quantities of wool as tribute (2 Kings 3:4). He also showed a resolute and extreme political determination, sacrificing his own child in order to achieve his purpose (2 Kings 3:27).

introduce: A figure appearing in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as the firstborn of Caleb and the father of Ziph (1 Chronicles 2:42).
lifetime: He is recorded as the firstborn of Caleb, the brother of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2:42).
event: He is recorded as the father of Ziph (1 Chronicles 2:42). No other specific historical activity or event appears in the biblical record.

call: The peoples of Rosh, Tubal, and Meshech
introduce: Meshech is a descendant of Japheth, a son of Noah, and is classified as a people living in the north in the ethnic genealogy of the ancient Near East. In the biblical record, Meshech is mentioned less as the life of a particular individual than as the ancestor of a people or nation formed in later times.
lifetime: As a son of Japheth, his name first appears in the genealogy of Genesis (Genesis 10:2). After that there is no direct record of his life, and he is mentioned again in the book of Ezekiel in the expression by which Gog is called "the chief prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal" (Ezekiel 38:2).
event: Together with Javan and Tubal, he is recorded as a merchant who traded in slaves and bronze utensils (Ezekiel 27:13). In Ezekiel 38:2 and 39:1, Gog is called "the chief prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal" and appears as the object of God's opposition. Also, in Ezekiel 32:26, Meshech, together with Tubal and all their multitudes, is recorded as being among those who were uncircumcised and slain by the sword, who had spread terror in the land of the living, and who lie in the grave.

introduce: In the Bible, Meshech appears as one of the sons of Japheth (Genesis 10:2) and as a name referring to a people or a particular geographical location that existed in the ancient Near East. The Meshech mentioned in Psalm 120 appears as a place-name symbolizing the painful environment in which the psalmist lives and suffers.
event: He is recorded as the sixth son in the genealogy of Japheth, a son of Noah (Genesis 10:2). In the prophecy of the prophet Ezekiel, Meshech appears with Tubal and Javan as a merchant trading in slaves and bronze utensils (Ezekiel 27:13), and Gog is called "the chief prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal" (Ezekiel 38:2, 39:1). The psalmist laments, "Woe to me that I dwell in Meshech, that I live among the tents of Kedar," and wrote that he had lived long with those who hate peace, and that though he is for peace, when he speaks, they are for war (Psalms 120:5-7).
character: Within the Bible, Meshech is portrayed as a people of warlike disposition and is classified as a force that was a military threat in alliance with Tubal, Magog, and others (Ezekiel 38:2). In Psalm 120, the psalmist mentions the place-name Meshech as a place of suffering in order to express a hostile environment lacking peace (Psalms 120:5).

call: Son of Aram (the Mash of 1 Chronicles 1:17 and Genesis 10:23)
introduce: Meshech is the name recorded at the end of the list of the sons of Shem in 1 Chronicles chapter 1, verse 17. In the parallel genealogy of Genesis chapter 10, verse 23, "Mash" is recorded in the same place as a son of Aram. He is a different person from Meshech the son of Japheth (Genesis 10:2; 1 Chronicles 1:5).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 1:17 records the sons of Shem as Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech. In the parallel record of Genesis, Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram are the sons of Shem (Genesis 10:22), and Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash are recorded as the sons of Aram (Genesis 10:23). There is no other record concerning his life.

introduce: Melchi is a figure appearing in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Luke in the New Testament, recorded as the son of Addi and the father of Neri.
lifetime: He was born as the son of Addi and became the father of Neri (Luke 3:27-28).

call: Cousin of Esther (prime minister of Persia)
introduce: Mordecai is a figure appearing in the book of Esther in the Old Testament, a great-grandson of Kish of the tribe of Benjamin and a son of Jair. He was a Jew carried off as a captive from Jerusalem at the time of the Babylonian exile, and he sat at the king's gate in Susa, the capital of the Persian Empire. As the cousin and guardian of Esther, he raised her, and afterward he was appointed as a prominent official of Persia.
lifetime: When Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon carried off Jeconiah and the people from Jerusalem, he was taken captive with them (Esther 2:5-6). He raised his cousin Esther, who had lost her parents early, as his own daughter (Esther 2:7). Even after Esther was chosen as queen of Xerxes king of Persia, he sat at the king's gate and watched over her welfare (Esther 2:11, 2:19). After thwarting Haman's plot, he received the ring that the king had taken back from Haman and was put in charge of Haman's house (Esther 8:1-2), and he became second to King Xerxes and was held in high honor among the Jews (Esther 10:3).
event: He learned of the plan of the king's eunuchs Bigthan and Teresh to assassinate King Xerxes and reported it to the king through Esther, thereby saving the king's life (Esther 2:21-23). Because he would not kneel or bow down to Haman the Agagite, Haman made a plan to destroy all the Jews (Esther 3:2-6). He persuaded Esther to appear before the king for the sake of her people, and so reversed the crisis of the massacre of the Jews (Esther 4:13-17). The decree written as Mordecai directed was delivered to the Jews in every province, so that the Jews were able to protect their own lives and stand against those who sought to strike them (Esther 8:9-11). In commemoration of this victory he established the feast of Purim and had it observed forever (Esther 9:20-22).
character: He had an uprightness that would not bend his convictions, and when he refused to bow down to Haman he made it clear that he was a Jew (Esther 3:4). When he exposed the plot to assassinate the king, he showed a cautious attitude, reporting in Esther's name without putting his own merit forward (Esther 2:22). In the crisis of his people he actively shared in the suffering of the community, fasting, putting on sackcloth, and mourning (Esther 4:1-3). Even after rising to a high office, he sought the good of his own people and pursued their peace (Esther 10:3).

call: Son of Zimri (descendant of the house of Saul)
introduce: Moza is a figure appearing in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, one of the descendants recorded in the genealogy of the house of Saul. He is a son of Zimri and is mentioned in the course of the succession of Saul's family line.
lifetime: Moza is recorded in the genealogy of the house of Saul of the tribe of Benjamin as the son of Zimri (1 Chronicles 8:36). He is the father of Binea (1 Chronicles 8:37) and belongs to the genealogy of descendants that continues from Merib-baal, the son of Saul's son Jonathan (1 Chronicles 8:34-37).

introduce: In the Bible, Moab is recorded as the son born to Lot and his elder daughter, and as the ancestor of the Moabites. They were a people who lived on the plateau of the plains of Moab east of the Dead Sea and who, historically, maintained a relationship with the nation of Israel that was both close and marked by conflict.
lifetime: He was the son borne by Lot's elder daughter by her father Lot, and was named Moab (Genesis 19:37). God gave Ar to the descendants of Lot as a possession, and in that land there lived in earlier times strong and tall people called the Emim (Deuteronomy 2:9-11).
event: After the exodus, Israel sent messengers asking to pass through, but the king of Moab would not permit it (Judges 11:17), and Balak king of Moab summoned Balaam to have him curse Israel (Numbers 22:2-6). Eglon king of Moab oppressed Israel for eighteen years but was killed by the judge Ehud (Judges 3:12-22). King David conquered Moab and made it pay tribute (2 Samuel 8:2), but afterward, in the time of Solomon, through marriages with foreign women the worship of the Moabite god Chemosh appeared (1 Kings 11:1-7). Later, Mesha king of Moab refused to pay tribute to Israel and rebelled (2 Kings 3:4-5).
character: Although the Moabites maintained a kinship relationship with Israel because of the bloodline background of their ancestor Moab, historically they showed a hostile and wary attitude (Deuteronomy 23:3-4). Religiously, they were characterized by serving Chemosh as their chief god (Numbers 21:29).

call: Overseer of the temple repairs in the time of Josiah
introduce: Meshullam was a Levite of the descendants of Kohath who was put in charge of overseeing the temple repair work in the time of King Josiah of the kingdom of Judah.
lifetime: Meshullam, a Levite of the descendants of Kohath, is recorded as an overseer together with Zechariah in the work of repairing the house of the LORD in the time of King Josiah (2 Chronicles 34:12).
event: In the work of repairing the house of the LORD in the time of King Josiah, he became an overseer and directed the work together with the Levites, Jahath and Obadiah of the descendants of Merari, and Zechariah of the descendants of Kohath (2 Chronicles 34:12).
character: No direct description of Meshullam's character appears in the biblical record (no record). However, he is regarded as having had administrative trustworthiness as an official who supported the reform policy of King Josiah and faithfully carried out the national task of purifying the temple (2 Chronicles 34:12).

introduce: Mushi is a descendant of the tribe of Levi and a member of the house of Merari. He is mentioned in the process of the census of the Levites and the division of their duties (Numbers 3:33).
lifetime: Mushi, as a son of Merari the son of Levi, together with Mahli makes up the genealogy of the descendants of Merari (Numbers 3:20, 3:33). Also, the Mushite family is entered in the list recording the Levite clans (Numbers 26:58).
event: Mushi became the ancestor of the Mushite family, one of the houses of the descendants of Merari (Numbers 3:33). The descendants of Merari were put in charge of the frames of the tabernacle and its crossbars, posts, and bases, and all its equipment and everything used for it, as well as the posts around the court with their bases, tent pegs, and ropes (Numbers 3:36-37).

call: Fourteenth king of Judah (son of Hezekiah)
introduce: He was the fourteenth king of the southern kingdom of Judah, born to King Hezekiah and Hephzibah. He ascended the throne at the age of twelve and reigned in Jerusalem for fifty-five years, the longest reign among the successive kings of the Davidic dynasty.
lifetime: He ascended the throne at the age of twelve and reigned fifty-five years (2 Kings 21:1). He completely reversed the religious reform policy of his father Hezekiah and promoted the worship of Baal and of the sun, moon, and stars (2 Kings 21:3). He suffered the hardship of being captured by the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, taken to Babylon, and bound in chains (2 Chronicles 33:11). In his affliction he sought the LORD and returned to Jerusalem and was restored to the throne, and afterward he devoted himself to building walls and strengthening his military power, and when he died he was buried in the garden of his palace, that is, the garden of Uzza (2 Chronicles 33:13, 20; 2 Kings 21:18).
event: He built an outer wall outside the City of David, in the valley west of Gihon, and heightened the wall, and he stationed army commanders in all the fortified cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 33:14). He removed the foreign idols, repaired the altar of the house of the LORD, and commanded the people of Judah to serve the LORD (2 Chronicles 33:15-16). Before his affliction, he set up the Asherah pole he had made in the house of the LORD, built altars for the sun, moon, and stars in the house of the LORD and in its two courts, made his son pass through fire, practiced divination, and engaged in sorcery (2 Kings 21:4-7, 2 Chronicles 33:4-7).
character: In the early part of his reign he did evil in the sight of the LORD, committing deeds more evil than the original inhabitants of Canaan, and he shed so much innocent blood that he filled Jerusalem from one end to the other (2 Kings 21:16). After being captured and suffering, he humbled himself and showed an attitude of earnest prayer before the LORD, and after his restoration he removed idol worship and walked in the fear of the LORD (2 Chronicles 33:12-13, 16).

introduce: Manasseh, one of the descendants of Pahath-moab, is a figure recorded as having taken a foreign woman as wife in the time of Ezra.
lifetime: He is recorded in the list of those who took foreign women, as one of the descendants of Pahath-moab (Ezra 10:30, 10:44). Apart from this list, the Bible has no record of his life.
event: When Ezra investigated the matter of those who had taken foreign women, his name was recorded among the descendants of Pahath-moab who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:16-17, 10:30, 10:44). The covenant to send away the foreign wives and their children is recorded in Ezra 10:3, but there is no direct record that Manasseh himself carried it out.

introduce: Manasseh is a figure who appears in Ezra 10; he is one of the descendants of Hashum who, after the return from the Babylonian exile, took foreign women as wives in Jerusalem and so transgressed the law.
lifetime: He was a member of the Jewish community that had returned from the Babylonian exile, and is one of the descendants of Hashum recorded in the list at the time of the expulsion of the foreign wives led by Ezra (Ezra 10:33).
event: In the time of Ezra he was recorded as one of the descendants of Hashum in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:33, 10:44). The covenant to send away the foreign wives and their children is recorded in Ezra 10:3, but there is no direct record that Manasseh himself took part in it.

introduce: Meraioth is a figure of the priestly family of the tribe of Levi, descended from Aaron, and is one of the important figures in the line of Zadok. In the genealogical records of Chronicles and Nehemiah he is mentioned as the son of Ahitub and the father of Zadok.
lifetime: Meraioth, as the son of Ahitub, stands in the genealogy of the high priestly family (1 Chronicles 9:11). He is also recorded as the father of Zadok (Nehemiah 11:11), which shows that he was a link in the lineage that carried out the priestly duties as a descendant of Aaron.
event: The Bible has no record of Meraioth's own deeds. His great-great-grandsons Azariah (1 Chronicles 9:11) and Seraiah (Nehemiah 11:11) are recorded as the ones in charge of the house of God.

call: Priestly house that returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Meraioth is the name of a priestly family recorded in the book of Nehemiah; it appears in the list of priestly clans (Nehemiah 12:12-15) who were active in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: Nehemiah 12 records the heads of the priestly families in the days of Joiakim, and in the clan of Meraioth the head was Helkai (Nehemiah 12:12, 15). There is no record of Meraioth as an individual, nor of his parents or children.

introduce: Meremoth is a figure belonging to the descendants of Bani among the people of Israel who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: He is recorded in the post-exilic list as one of the descendants of Bani (Ezra 10:36).
event: In the investigation, led by Ezra, of those who had taken foreign women, his name was included in the list of those among the descendants of Bani who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:34-36, 10:44).

introduce: Meremoth is a figure of the priestly families who sealed the covenant in the process of renewal of the community in the time of Nehemiah after the return from exile. His name appears in the list of the sealing priests in Nehemiah 10.
lifetime: Meremoth is recorded as one of the priests who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:1-8).
event: Together with the governor Nehemiah, his name was recorded as one of the priests who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:1-8).

call: Son of King Saul and Rizpah
introduce: A son born to King Saul and his concubine Rizpah, one of the descendants of Saul, the first king of Israel. He shares his name with Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan, and he is a figure who met a tragic death in the course of the fall of the house of Saul.
lifetime: When the Gibeonites sought vengeance on the house of Saul, he was singled out as one of the seven descendants of Saul (2 Samuel 21:8). He was born as a son of Rizpah (2 Samuel 21:8); he was handed over to the Gibeonites and, together with the other descendants of Saul, was hanged on the mountain at the beginning of the barley harvest (2 Samuel 21:9).
event: When a famine of three years occurred in the days of King David and David inquired into its cause, it was revealed that Saul had slaughtered the Gibeonites (2 Samuel 21:1). When the Gibeonites demanded seven descendants of Saul from David, David gave them seven men, including Mephibosheth and Armoni, the sons of Saul's concubine Rizpah (2 Samuel 21:8). He was killed by the Gibeonites, and afterward his mother Rizpah spread sackcloth on the rock and kept the birds and the wild animals from touching the bodies, so that they would not be desecrated (2 Samuel 21:10).

call: Leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Meshezabel was a figure active in the rebuilding of the community in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile; he was one of the heads of the people who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah, and is mentioned as the father of Pethahiah.
lifetime: As one of the people who returned from the Babylonian exile, he appears among those who signed the covenant led by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:21). Nehemiah 11:24 records that his son Pethahiah, of the descendants of Zerah the son of Judah, was at the king's hand in all matters concerning the people.
event: He put his name on the sealed document by which the people of Israel pledged to separate from the foreigners and swore to keep the law before God (Nehemiah 10:21). Also his son Pethahiah, of the descendants of Zerah the son of Judah, was at the king's hand in all matters concerning the people (Nehemiah 11:24).
