introduce: Binnui is a figure who took part in the repair of the wall of Jerusalem and in the reform of the community of Israel in the time of Nehemiah, recorded as a descendant of Henadad.
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile he took part in the work of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:24). Afterward, in the course of the people of Israel keeping the law of God and making the covenant, he was recorded in the list of the Levites who sealed as "Binnui of the descendants of Henadad" (Nehemiah 10:9).
event: At the time of repairing the wall of Jerusalem he took a section as a son of Henadad and repaired the stretch from the house of Azariah past the angle to the corner of the wall (Nehemiah 3:24). He was recorded in the list of the Levites who sealed the covenant as "Binnui of the descendants of Henadad" (Nehemiah 10:9).

call: Head of a priestly family that returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Bilgah is a figure who appears in the book of Nehemiah in the Old Testament, a member of a priestly family who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel and Jeshua after the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: His name is recorded in the list of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1, 12:5). In the list of the heads of the priests in the time of Joiakim it says "of Bilgah, Shammua," so the one recorded as head of the clan of Bilgah is Shammua (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:18).
event: His name was entered in the list of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua, and this list is recorded as that of the priests and the heads of their associates in the days of Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:5, 12:7). The one recorded as head of the clan of Bilgah in the time of Joiakim is Shammua (Nehemiah 12:18), and no events of Bilgah himself are recorded.

introduce: Bilhan is a figure of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in 1 Chronicles 7, the son of Jediael and the father of Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar (1 Chronicles 7:10).
lifetime: Bilhan is recorded as the son of Jediael the son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:6, 7:10). 1 Chronicles 7:11 calls "these sons of Jediael" heads of their families and mighty men of valor, and it is not a statement that calls Bilhan alone a head.
event: As the sons of Bilhan, Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar are recorded (1 Chronicles 7:10). These sons of Jediael were heads of their families and mighty men of valor, and among their descendants those fit to go out to war numbered seventeen thousand two hundred (1 Chronicles 7:11).

call: Father of John the Baptist (priest of the division of Abijah)
introduce: Zechariah is a figure who appears in the Gospel of Luke in the New Testament, a priest belonging to the division of Abijah. He is the father of John the Baptist and lived in the region of Judea with his wife Elizabeth.
lifetime: Zechariah served as a priest in the land of Judea in the days of King Herod, and took as his wife Elizabeth, a descendant of Aaron (Luke 1:5). Together with his wife he was righteous before God and faithfully walked in all the commandments and regulations (Luke 1:6). Though he had no children into old age, while burning incense in the temple he heard from the angel Gabriel the prophecy of the birth of a son (Luke 1:11-13), and after he obtained John the Baptist, he was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied (Luke 1:67).
event: According to his turn he entered the temple to carry out his priestly duty and was given the task of burning incense (Luke 1:8-9). While he was burning incense an angel of the Lord appeared and announced the birth of his son John, but when he did not believe it he was struck temporarily with the punishment of being unable to speak (Luke 1:18-20). After the son was born, when he wrote that his name was John, his speech was opened again (Luke 1:63-64), and because of this event great fear came on the neighbors and it became the talk of the region (Luke 1:65).
character: He was a thoroughgoing keeper of the law, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and regulations of the Lord (Luke 1:6). Even though he had no children into old age, he carried out his duty as a priest with piety (Luke 1:7-9), and he also showed a human doubt in not trusting at once the prophecy of the angel (Luke 1:18). Afterward, through the punishment he confirmed his reverence toward God, and as moved by the Holy Spirit he showed the aspect of a prophet who proclaimed prophecy (Luke 1:64-67).

introduce: The fourth son of Obed-edom, of the descendants of Korah of the tribe of Levi. He is recorded as one of those who served as gatekeepers of the temple in the time of David.
lifetime: Born as one of the sons of Obed-edom, he carried out the duty of gatekeeper of the temple together with his father Obed-edom and his brothers (1 Chronicles 26:4).
event: In the system of temple gatekeepers organized by David, he took charge of guarding the gates of the temple as the fourth son (1 Chronicles 26:4). He was included in the list as a member when his whole family was appointed as gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:8).

introduce: Zadok is a figure who appears in the Old Testament, the father of Jerusha, the mother of Jotham king of Judah, that is, Jotham's maternal grandfather (2 Kings 15:33). His status or office is not recorded in the text.
lifetime: Zadok is recorded as the father of Jerusha, the mother of King Jotham (2 Kings 15:33; 2 Chronicles 27:1). No specific chronology or deeds of his life are recorded in the Bible.
event: No personal achievement of his is recorded separately in the Bible, but his daughter Jerusha became the wife of Uzziah king of Judah and the mother of Jotham, and so he was incorporated into the royal family line (2 Kings 15:33).

introduce: Zadok is a figure who appears in the Old Testament, a priest active in the time of David and Solomon. He is the son of Ahitub and the father of Shallum, and since Shallum fathered Hilkiah, Zadok is the grandfather of Hilkiah (1 Chronicles 6:12-13). He belongs to the line of Eleazar, a descendant of Aaron (1 Chronicles 6:50-53).
lifetime: In the reign of David he became a priest together with Ahimelech the son of Abiathar (2 Samuel 8:17). When David left Jerusalem because of the rebellion of Absalom, Zadok came out carrying the ark of the covenant of God together with all the Levites, but at David's command he carried the ark back to Jerusalem and stayed there (2 Samuel 15:24-29). When Adonijah sought the throne in David's last years, Zadok did not side with Adonijah (1 Kings 1:8), and at David's command he took part, together with Nathan the prophet, in anointing Solomon king over Israel (1 Kings 1:32-39). Afterward King Solomon put Zadok the priest in the place of Abiathar (1 Kings 2:35). He is recorded as the son of Ahitub and the father of Shallum (1 Chronicles 6:12).
event: When David left Jerusalem, Zadok and Abiathar, having received David's command to carry the ark of God back to the city, carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed there (2 Samuel 15:25, 15:29). David told Hushai to report to the two priests, Zadok and Abiathar, whatever he heard in the palace, and had them send word to him by Ahimaaz the son of Zadok and Jonathan the son of Abiathar (2 Samuel 15:35-36). When Solomon was set up as king, Zadok the priest, together with Nathan the prophet and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada and others, led Solomon down to Gihon (1 Kings 1:38), and took the horn of oil from the tabernacle and anointed Solomon (1 Kings 1:39). Afterward King Solomon put Zadok the priest in the place of Abiathar (1 Kings 2:35).
character: He showed great loyalty, obeying David's command and staying behind in Jerusalem even in a dangerous situation to carry out a secret mission (2 Samuel 15:27-28). In the matter of the succession to the throne, too, he had the political judgment to grasp David's will and act accurately (1 Kings 1:32-34). Also the descendants of Zadok were recognized as a priestly house with the legitimacy to carry out the office in the temple of Jerusalem in later generations (Ezekiel 44:15).

introduce: Zadok is a figure recorded as "Zadok, a young man of valor" in the list of army commanders who came to Hebron to make David king (1 Chronicles 12:23-38), and he is mentioned together with twenty-two commanders of his family (1 Chronicles 12:28).
lifetime: The tribe to which Zadok belonged and the specific details of his life are not recorded in the text. When the commanders who had prepared for battle came to Hebron to turn the kingdom of Saul over to David (1 Chronicles 12:23), following the records of the descendants of Levi (12:26) and Jehoiada, head of the house of Aaron (12:27), he is the one recorded as "Zadok, a young man of valor, with twenty-two commanders from his family" (1 Chronicles 12:28).
event: He was recorded in the list of the soldiers who came to Hebron to make David king, together with the twenty-two commanders of his family (1 Chronicles 12:28). All these soldiers came to Hebron with a whole heart, to make David king over all Israel (1 Chronicles 12:38).
character: The young warrior Zadok appears in the list of those who came to Hebron to turn the kingdom over to David (1 Chronicles 12:23, 28). His personal character is not specifically described, and the description of the Benjaminite archers in 1 Chronicles 12:2 cannot be applied to this Zadok.

introduce: Zadok the son of Baana is a figure who took part in the work of repairing a part of the wall when Nehemiah rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem. As a member of the returned community of Israel, there is a record that he joined in the work of repairing the wall.
lifetime: Zadok the son of Baana took part in the rebuilding work when the community that had returned from the Babylonian exile rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:4). No detailed record of his life as a whole or of his family appears in the Bible.
event: He is recorded as having repaired the section next to Meshullam when the wall of Jerusalem was repaired (Nehemiah 3:4). The location and size of the section he was in charge of are not recorded separately in the text.

introduce: A namesake of Zadok the son of Baana, a figure of a priestly family who took part in the work of repairing the wall of Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile. He is recorded in Nehemiah 3:29 as the son of Immer.
lifetime: As the son of Immer, when the wall of Jerusalem was repaired, he repaired the section opposite his own house (Nehemiah 3:29). Nothing further is recorded in the Bible about the time of his return or about his life.
event: Zadok the son of Immer, when the wall of Jerusalem was repaired, repaired the section opposite his own house (Nehemiah 3:29). This record follows the record that above the Horse Gate the priests each repaired the section opposite his own house (Nehemiah 3:28).

introduce: Zadok, recorded in Nehemiah 10, is mentioned as one of the leaders who sealed the covenant in Jerusalem after the return from the exile (Nehemiah 10:21).
lifetime: A figure after the return from the Babylonian exile, together with Nehemiah the governor, the son of Hacaliah, he put his name among the heads of the people in the list of those who sealed (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:14, 10:21).
event: He is recorded as one of the heads of the people who sealed together with Nehemiah the governor, the son of Hacaliah (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:14, 10:21). This covenant was an oath to keep all the commandments, ordinances, and statutes of the LORD, following the law of God given through Moses the servant of God (Nehemiah 10:28-29).

introduce: Zadok was a scribe active in Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah in the Old Testament. He was responsible for managing the storerooms of the temple and played an important role in the process of religious reform and the restoration of administrative order.
lifetime: Nehemiah appointed Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites as treasurers over the storerooms (Nehemiah 13:13). This was when Nehemiah learned that the Levites' portions had not been given and that the house of God had been forsaken, and set things right (Nehemiah 13:10-13).
event: Zadok became a treasurer over the storerooms together with Shelemiah the priest and Pedaiah the Levite, and Hanan was next to them (Nehemiah 13:13). This was when all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, new wine, and oil into the storehouses (Nehemiah 13:12), and their duty was to distribute the supplies to their brothers (Nehemiah 13:13). They were considered trustworthy and were entrusted with this task (Nehemiah 13:13).
character: Nehemiah records that Zadok was considered trustworthy (Nehemiah 13:13).

introduce: Zadok appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Matthew in the New Testament. He is recorded as the son of Azor and the father of Achim, one of the ancestors in the line of Israel.
lifetime: Zadok was born to Azor and became the father of Achim, and he is named within the genealogical line of Scripture (Matthew 1:14).
event: The biblical record mentions no particular social activity or historical event of his; he appears only as a link of descent in the genealogy of Jesus Christ (Matthew 1:14).

call: Returnee who married a foreign woman and then repented
meaning: The LORD has set free; my ruler
introduce: A man recorded among the descendants of Bani in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra, after the return from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 10:34, 10:40, 10:44).
lifetime: A man of Ezra's time, a member of the Israelite community of faith that returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
event: In the time of Ezra, his name appears with Machnadebai and Shashai among the descendants of Bani in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:40, 10:44). The text does not separately record any later deeds of this individual.
character: Since, after hearing Ezra's rebuke, he realized his sin and resolved to send away the foreign women even at the cost of pain, it can be seen that he repented and was willing to obey the word of God and restore holiness.

call: Envoy of Judah sent from Bethel
introduce: Sharezer is recorded as one of those whom the people of Bethel sent, together with Regem-melech and his men, to plead for the favor of the LORD (Zechariah 7:2).
lifetime: In the fourth year of King Darius, on the fourth day of the ninth month, when the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, the people of Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and their men to plead for the favor of the LORD (Zechariah 7:1-2).
event: As the people of Bethel had sent them, Sharezer, together with Regem-melech and his men, pleaded for the favor of the LORD, and asked the priests and the prophets at the house of the LORD of Hosts whether they should weep and fast in the fifth month as they had done for many years (Zechariah 7:2-3).

introduce: Shamma appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher and is recorded as a son of Zophah. He is one of the members who make up the line of descent within the family tree of the tribe of Asher.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Zophah, who was a son of Helem, a descendant of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:35-37).

call: Father of Jaazaniah (father of an idolatrous elder)
introduce: Shaphan was a scribe, a high official, who was active in the time of King Josiah of the kingdom of Judah. He was the son of Azaliah (2 Kings 22:3) and is recorded as the one who read before the king the book of the law found in the temple at Jerusalem (2 Kings 22:10). Ezekiel 8:11 records that his son Jaazaniah stood among the seventy elders of the house of Israel with a censer in his hand.
lifetime: In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, Shaphan received the book of the law that Hilkiah the high priest had found in the temple, took it to the king, and read it aloud (2 Kings 22:8-10). He was one of those who, at the king's command, went to Huldah the prophetess to ask about the words of the book of the law (2 Kings 22:12-14). In Ezekiel's vision, Shaphan's son Jaazaniah stood among the seventy elders of the house of Israel, each with a censer in his hand (Ezekiel 8:11).
event: Shaphan the scribe, whom King Josiah had sent to repair the temple, received the book of the law that Hilkiah had found, went to the king to report, and read it in the king's presence (2 Chronicles 34:8, 34:15-18). At the king's command, he went with Ahikam, Achbor, Asaiah, and others to Huldah the prophetess and inquired of her (2 Kings 22:12-14).
character: According to the biblical record, he appears as a capable scribe trusted by the king and accurate in handling administrative affairs (2 Kings 22:10). However, since Ezekiel 8:11 shows that his son Jaazaniah took part in a secret gathering worshiping foreign idols, scholars discuss the possibility that the house of Shaphan showed a double attitude, between public religious reform and private idolatry (Ezekiel 8:11).

introduce: Shaphat is a man of Abel-meholah who appears in the Old Testament and is the father of the prophet Elisha (1 Kings 19:16).
lifetime:
He lived in the region of Abel-meholah and had a son, Elisha (1 Kings 19:16).
His son Elisha met Elijah while plowing with twelve yoke of oxen ahead of him (1 Kings 19:19).
Since Elisha, called by the prophet Elijah, asked to be allowed to kiss his father and mother before leaving, it can be seen that his parents were still alive at that time (1 Kings 19:20).

introduce: Shaphat was a descendant of David and appears in the genealogy of the royal house of David recorded in 1 Chronicles 3. He is recorded as the grandson of Shecaniah and the son of Shemaiah.
lifetime: In the genealogy of the house of David, he is recorded as one of the sons of Shemaiah, the son of Shecaniah, and is therefore the grandson of Shecaniah (1 Chronicles 3:22).
event: In the genealogy of David's descendants in 1 Chronicles 3, his name is recorded as one of the sons of Shemaiah (Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat) (1 Chronicles 3:22).

call: Chief of the tribe of Gad
introduce: Shaphat is a man recorded in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a figure in the genealogy belonging to the descendants of Gad, a son of Jacob.
lifetime: A man among the descendants of Gad who lived in Bashan, he is recorded as "Shaphat in Bashan," together with Joel, Shapham, and Jaanai in the list of chiefs (1 Chronicles 5:11-12).
event: He is on the list of chiefs of the descendants of Gad (Joel, Shapham, Jaanai, Shaphat) (1 Chronicles 5:12), and this record was entered in the genealogies in the days of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel (1 Chronicles 5:17).

introduce: A man who, in the time of King David, was in charge of the herds in the valleys; he was one of the officials in charge of David's property.
lifetime: As the son of Adlai, he was in charge of King David's herds in the valleys (1 Chronicles 27:29). The herds grazing in Sharon were under Shitrai the Sharonite.
event: Among the officials in charge of David's property, he was in charge of the herds in the valleys (1 Chronicles 27:29).

introduce: Zabad appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah and is the grandson of Attai in the line of the house of Jerahmeel recorded in 1 Chronicles 2.
lifetime: He was the son of Nathan, whom Attai fathered; Zabad fathered Ephlal, and Ephlal fathered Obed (1 Chronicles 2:36-37).

introduce: A man recorded as the son of Tahath in the genealogy of the descendants of Ephraim; his son was Shuthelah (1 Chronicles 7:20-21).
lifetime: He is recorded as a descendant of Ephraim, the son of Tahath and the father of Shuthelah (1 Chronicles 7:20-21).
event: The Bible records no deeds of Zabad himself. In 1 Chronicles 7:21, after Zabad's son Shuthelah, there follows a record that Ezer and Elead were killed by the natives of Gath, but Zabad is not recorded as one of those killed.

call: Son of Ahlai (one of David's mighty men)
introduce: Zabad is a man recorded as one of David's mighty men and is the son of Ahlai. The Bible records no specific deeds of his; his name appears in the list of David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles 11.
lifetime: He is recorded as "Zabad son of Ahlai" in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:41).

introduce: Zabad (called Zabad in 2 Chronicles 24:26 and Jozabad in 2 Kings 12:21) was one of the two servants who conspired against and killed Joash, king of Judah, and was the son of Shimeath, an Ammonite woman.
lifetime: He was a servant of Joash, king of Judah, and his mother was an Ammonite woman (2 Chronicles 24:26).
event: He is recorded as one of the servants who struck down and killed Joash, king of Judah (2 Kings 12:21). 2 Chronicles 24:26 records the conspirators as Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonitess and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabitess (while 2 Kings 12:21 gives Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer), and reports that the servants struck Joash down on his bed (2 Chronicles 24:25). 2 Kings 12:20 gives the place as the house of Millo, on the road down to Silla.

introduce: Zabad is a man recorded in Ezra 10; his name appears among the descendants of Zattu in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra, after the return from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 10:27, 10:44).
lifetime: As one of the descendants of Zattu, he was recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:27, 10:44).
event: His name is on the list of those who had taken foreign women, together with Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, and Aziza of the descendants of Zattu (Ezra 10:27, 10:44). The text does not separately record any later deeds of this individual.

introduce: Zabad is a man recorded in the book of Ezra, specified as one of the descendants of Hashum after the return of Israel from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: Zabad, a descendant of Hashum, appears in the list in the course of resolving the matter of marriages to foreign women led by Ezra (Ezra 10:33, 10:44).
event: In the time of Ezra, his name is on the list of those who had taken foreign women, together with Mattenai, Mattattah, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei of the descendants of Hashum (Ezra 10:33, 10:44).

introduce: A man belonging to the descendants of Nebo, included in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra.
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, in the time of Ezra, his name is mentioned as one of the descendants of Nebo in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:43-44).
event: He is recorded, together with Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah of the descendants of Nebo, as one who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:43-44). The text does not separately record any later deeds of this individual.

introduce: Zaccur was one of the Israelites who, having finished the Babylonian exile, returned to Jerusalem under the leadership of Ezra. He is recorded together with Uthai among the descendants of Bigvai (Ezra 8:14).
lifetime: Zaccur went up to Jerusalem with Ezra from Babylon in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes (Ezra 7:7-8, 8:1). In the list of returnees he is recorded with Uthai among the descendants of Bigvai (Ezra 8:14).
event: When Ezra gathered the people at the river that flows toward Ahava and they camped there three days in tents, as he examined the people and the priests (Ezra 8:15), Uthai and Zaccur of the descendants of Bigvai were recorded among the heads of families who came up from Babylon and in their genealogical register (Ezra 8:1), and 70 men were with them (Ezra 8:14).

call: Son of Simeon (born of a Canaanite woman)
introduce: A man in the genealogies recorded in Genesis, a son whom Simeon, a son of Jacob, had by a Canaanite woman (Genesis 46:10).
lifetime: A son of Simeon, son of Jacob, he is recorded as the child of a Canaanite woman in the list of Jacob's family who went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:10).
event: Apart from his name being entered in the list of those who went down to Egypt, there is no record of any specific activity or historical event. His name appears in the lists of Simeon's sons (Genesis 46:10; Exodus 6:15; 1 Chronicles 4:24), and Shallum is recorded as his son (1 Chronicles 4:25).

introduce: A man who appears in the genealogy recorded in 1 Chronicles; a Levite of the descendants of Kohath and a son of Uzziah.
lifetime: He is recorded as a descendant of Kohath and a son of Uzziah (1 Chronicles 6:24).
event: The biblical record mentions no particular event or specific historical achievement of his (1 Chronicles 6:24).

introduce: The first king of the monarchy period of Israel, a son of Kish of the tribe of Benjamin. He was anointed through Samuel and set up as king.
lifetime: He went out to look for lost donkeys, met Samuel, and was told by prophecy that he would be king (1 Samuel 9:3-17). He was formally chosen as king of Israel by lot at Mizpah (1 Samuel 10:20-21). He was defeated by the Philistine army at the battle of Gilboa and fell in battle together with his sons (1 Samuel 31:2-6).
event: When Nahash the Ammonite threatened Jabesh-gilead, he summoned the army of Israel and won a great victory (1 Samuel 11:11). In the war with the Philistines he stationed troops at Michmash, and the LORD delivered Israel that day (1 Samuel 13:2; 14:23). He was commanded to utterly destroy Amalek, but spared King Agag and took plunder (1 Samuel 15:8-9). As David's fame grew, Saul was displeased and angry, and from that day on kept a jealous eye on David (1 Samuel 18:7-9); he told his son Jonathan and all his servants to kill David (1 Samuel 19:1). Before the war with the Philistines, he went to the medium at Endor and tried to bring up the spirit of the dead Samuel (1 Samuel 28:7-14).
character: When first chosen as king, he showed humility, calling himself of the least of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Samuel 9:21). In appearance he was tall and handsome, and there was no one among the people like him (1 Samuel 9:2). In his later years he showed intense inferiority toward David and paranoid suspicion, and a tendency toward disobedience and willful decisions (1 Samuel 18:8-9). To protect his own authority, he often went through emotional upheavals (1 Samuel 20:30-33).

introduce: Zaccur is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, one of the descendants of Simeon, the second son of Jacob. He is recorded as the son of Hammuel within the genealogical system of the tribe of Simeon.
lifetime: Zaccur continued the line of Shaul, a son of Simeon, and as a son of Hammuel he had his name entered in the family genealogy of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:26).
event: The biblical record contains no information on any specific achievement or particular event that Zaccur himself led (1 Chronicles 4:26).

introduce: Zaccur belongs to the line of Merari, of the descendants of Levi, and to one of the genealogies of the Levites organized for service at the temple in the reign of King David (1 Chronicles 24:27).
lifetime: Zaccur is mentioned as one of those born to Jaaziah, a descendant of Merari, and his family line was maintained within the descent of the tribe of Levi (1 Chronicles 24:27).
event: When lots were cast for the descendants of Levi before King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the priestly and Levitical families, Zaccur was recorded among those born to Jaaziah, a descendant of Merari (1 Chronicles 24:27, 24:31).

introduce: He belongs to the descendants of Gershon of the tribe of Levi, and as a son of Asaph he was a man in charge of the ministry of praise at the temple in the time of David.
lifetime: When King David organized the choir to serve at the temple, he was chosen as one of the sons of Asaph and took part in the ministry (1 Chronicles 25:2).
event: When David divided the choir into 24 divisions by casting lots, Zaccur, as a son of Asaph, was given the duty of the third division (1 Chronicles 25:10).

introduce: Zaccur took part in rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem after the return from exile and is recorded as the son of Imri. He was a Jew who contributed to the work by taking a share of a certain section during the rebuilding of the wall led by Nehemiah.
lifetime: He joined in the project of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah. His father was Imri (Nehemiah 3:2).
event: Taking part in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem, Zaccur son of Imri, together with others, repaired a portion of the wall (Nehemiah 3:2). The section he was assigned corresponds to a particular stretch of the wall of Jerusalem, and he carried out the task of repairing it as his responsibility (Nehemiah 3:2).

introduce: Zaccur was a man of the tribe of Levi in the Jewish community that returned from the Babylonian exile in the Persian period (Nehemiah 10:12).
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, he appears as one of the Levites who put their names to the sealed covenant document drawn up in Jerusalem under the leadership of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:12).
event: He was included in the list of Levites who sealed the covenant document in which they resolved to keep the law of God, to forbid intermarriage with foreigners, and to observe the Sabbath and the festivals (Nehemiah 10:1; 10:12; 10:28-31).

call: Father of Hanan (father of a temple storehouse keeper)
introduce: Zaccur is a figure who appears in the book of Nehemiah and is recorded as the grandson of Mattaniah and the father of Hanan (Nehemiah 13:13).
lifetime: Zaccur is recorded only as the grandson of Mattaniah and the father of Hanan, and no record of his own life appears in the Bible (Nehemiah 13:13).
event: No deeds of Zaccur himself are recorded. When all Judah brought the tithes into the storehouses (Nehemiah 13:12), Nehemiah appointed Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites as treasurers and made Hanan son of Zaccur their assistant; this was because they were considered trustworthy, and their duty was to distribute to their brothers (Nehemiah 13:13).
character: The biblical text assesses Zaccur as trustworthy and mentions that he was qualified to carry out his duties together with the other administrators (Nehemiah 13:13).

call: Head of a priestly family that returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Sallai is the name of a priestly family recorded as "the family of Sallai" in the list of priestly heads in Nehemiah 12. In the days of Joiakim, Kallai is recorded as head of that family (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:20).
lifetime: In the list recording the heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim, it appears as "of Sallai, Kallai" (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:20). No record of Sallai's own life appears in the Bible.
event: The biblical record contains no specific event or achievement carried out by Sallai himself (Nehemiah 12:20).

call: Son of Meshullam (Benjamite leader who returned)
introduce: Sallu was one of the leaders of the tribe of Benjamin who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile, and is recorded as the son of Meshullam and the grandson of Hodaviah.
lifetime: A descendant of a Benjamite family who returned to Jerusalem in the Persian period after the Babylonian exile, he had his name entered in the list of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:7; Nehemiah 11:7).
event: He is recorded as one of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah; Sallu and those after him, Gabbai and Sallai and others, numbered 928 in all (Nehemiah 11:7-8).

call: Husband of Huldah (keeper of the wardrobe)
introduce: Shallum was a man of the time of Josiah, king of Judah, the son of Tikvah and the grandson of Harhas (2 Chronicles 34:22 records him as the son of Tokhath and the grandson of Hasrah). He was keeper of the wardrobe and is recorded as the husband of Huldah the prophetess (2 Kings 22:14).
lifetime: Shallum was the son of Tikvah and the grandson of Harhas, and was keeper of the wardrobe (2 Kings 22:14). 2 Chronicles 34:22 records him as the son of Tokhath and the grandson of Hasrah. His wife was Huldah the prophetess, and Huldah lived in the Second District of Jerusalem (2 Kings 22:14).
event: Huldah, Shallum's wife, when King Josiah was troubled by the book of the law found in the temple, received the messengers whom the king sent and delivered the prophecy of the disaster that would come upon Judah (2 Kings 22:14). No specific deeds of Shallum himself are recorded; he is only introduced as keeper of the wardrobe (2 Kings 22:14; 2 Chronicles 34:22).

introduce: Shallum is a figure recorded in the genealogy of Chronicles, mentioned as the son of Sismai, a descendant of the tribe of Judah, and the father of Jekamiah.
lifetime: Shallum was born as the son of Sismai within the line of the tribe of Judah, and Jekamiah is recorded as his son (1 Chronicles 2:40).
event: The biblical record gives no information on any personal achievement or particular event of Shallum (1 Chronicles 2:40).

introduce: A figure in the family tree of the tribe of Simeon, the son of Shaul, belonging to the genealogical line of the tribe of Simeon.
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Shaul, son of Simeon, and his son was Mibsam (1 Chronicles 4:25).

introduce: Shallum was a descendant of Naphtali, the son of Jacob and Bilhah, and is recorded as one of the sons of Naphtali. He is mentioned as the ancestor of the Shillemite clan (Numbers 26:49).
lifetime: Shallum was born as a son of Naphtali, and he is mentioned as one of the persons continuing the genealogy of the tribe of Naphtali (1 Chronicles 7:13).

call: Son of Kore (chief of the gatekeepers)
introduce: Shallum was a son of Kore, a grandson of Ebiasaph, and one of the Korahites. He is recorded as one of the chiefs who carried out the office of gatekeeper at the temple in Jerusalem.
lifetime: As a descendant of Korah, Shallum was a member of the family that held the duty of temple gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 9:17). After finishing the Babylonian exile and returning to Jerusalem, he served at the temple (1 Chronicles 9:19). As head of the gatekeepers, he bore the responsibility, with his brothers, of managing the gates of the temple (1 Chronicles 9:18).
event: Shallum was chief of the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 9:17), and with the Korahites of his own family he took on the work of the service and guarded the gates of the tabernacle (1 Chronicles 9:19). These men, recorded as gatekeepers, had formerly been the gatekeepers at the King's Gate on the east, of the camp of the Levites (1 Chronicles 9:18).

introduce: A man recorded in 2 Chronicles 28:12 as the father of Jehizkiah, a chief of the Ephraimites.
lifetime: Shallum is recorded only as the father of Jehizkiah, a chief of the Ephraimites (2 Chronicles 28:12), and no record of his own life appears in the Bible.
event: No event carried out by Shallum himself is recorded. His son Jehizkiah, together with Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, and Amasa son of Hadlai, as chiefs of the Ephraimites, stood up and opposed those coming from the battlefield (2 Chronicles 28:12); these named chiefs clothed the captives and fed them, put the feeble on donkeys, and brought them to Jericho, the City of Palms, and then returned to Samaria (2 Chronicles 28:15).

introduce: A man recorded as one of the gatekeepers in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:24, 10:44).
lifetime: In Ezra 10, Shallum, Telem, and Uri are listed as the gatekeepers who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:24). No other record of his life appears in the Bible.
event: He is recorded as one of the gatekeepers in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:24, 10:44).

introduce: Shallum is a man recorded in Ezra 10 as one of the descendants of Bani who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:34, 10:42, 10:44).
lifetime: His name is recorded among the descendants of Bani (Ezra 10:34, 10:42), and no other record of his life appears in the Bible.
event: He was included in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:42-44).

introduce: Shallum, a son of Hallohesh, took part in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the Persian period. He held the post of ruler over half of a district of Jerusalem.
lifetime: He took part in the work as ruler of half of the district of Jerusalem during the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem led by Nehemiah, governor of Judah (Nehemiah 3:12).
event: Together with his daughters, he was responsible for repairing a section of the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:12).
character: Although the biblical record makes no mention of his sons, he is portrayed as a man who had his daughters accompany him to the wall-rebuilding site and take part in the work together (Nehemiah 3:12).

introduce: A man recorded as the uncle of Jeremiah and the father of Hanamel (Jeremiah 32:7). He appears in the book of Jeremiah in the Old Testament and is classed as a man who was related by blood to Jeremiah in the last days of the kingdom of Judah.
lifetime: In Jeremiah 32:7 he is introduced as Jeremiah's uncle and recorded as the father of Hanamel. His identity is mentioned only in connection with the incident in which his son Hanamel asked Jeremiah to buy his field in Anathoth; there is no record of Shallum's own residence or property (Jeremiah 32:7-8).
event: No event carried out by Shallum himself is recorded. His son Hanamel came to Jeremiah, who was in the court of the guard, and asked him to buy his field in Anathoth (Jeremiah 32:7-8), and Jeremiah bought the field, weighing out seventeen shekels of silver (Jeremiah 32:9).

introduce: Shallum is a figure who appears in the book of Jeremiah, the father of Maaseiah, recorded as "Shallum the doorkeeper" (Jeremiah 35:4).
lifetime: In Jeremiah 35:4 he is introduced as "Shallum the doorkeeper" and recorded as the father of Maaseiah. No other record of his life appears in the Bible.
event: No deeds of Shallum himself are recorded. Jeremiah brought the Rechabites into the house of the LORD and into the chamber of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God; that chamber was beside the chamber of the officials and above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum the doorkeeper (Jeremiah 35:2, 35:4).

call: Ahohite (one of David's thirty mighty men)
introduce: Zalmon is a figure who appears in 2 Samuel in the Old Testament, recorded as one of the Thirty, David's elite military corps. He is mentioned together with his place of origin, as an Ahohite, and 1 Chronicles 11:29 gives him as Ilai the Ahohite.
lifetime: He is recorded as having his name entered in the list of David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23:28).
event: He is recorded as Zalmon the Ahohite in the list of David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23:24, 23:28). Beyond this, the Bible records no specific event or achievement carried out by Zalmon himself.

call: Son of Agee (one of David's three mighty men)
introduce: Shammah is recorded as one of the three greatest of David's mighty men, those of the finest fighting strength in David's military organization, and is the son of Agee the Hararite (2 Samuel 23:11).
lifetime: Shammah is recorded as a son of Agee the Hararite and one of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:11). Shammah the Hararite also appears in the part of the list of David's mighty men that enumerates the thirty (2 Samuel 23:24, 2 Samuel 23:33), but the text does not state that this is the same person.
event: When the Philistines gathered in a troop in a field full of lentils and the people fled from the Philistines, Shammah took his stand in the middle of that field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines, and the LORD brought about a great victory (2 Samuel 23:11-12).
character: He was a soldier of resolve and valor who, in an unfavorable battle situation of being outnumbered and with his comrades retreating, did not leave the field but held his position to the end and carried out the defense (2 Samuel 23:11-12).

introduce: Shammai is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as the son of Rekem and the father of Maon.
lifetime: Shammai is recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Caleb of the tribe of Judah as a son of Rekem, son of Hebron (1 Chronicles 2:42-44). He had a son named Maon, and Maon is recorded as the father of Beth-zur (1 Chronicles 2:45).
event: No specific event of Shammai himself is recorded; in the genealogy, his son Maon is introduced as the father of Beth-zur (1 Chronicles 2:45).

introduce: Shammai is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as one of the children born to Mered, a son of Ezrah (1 Chronicles 4:17).
lifetime: Shammai is a son of Mered, son of Ezrah, and is mentioned in the genealogy as one of Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa, whom Mered fathered (1 Chronicles 4:17). The text calls them sons of Bithiah, the daughter of Pharaoh whom Mered had taken (1 Chronicles 4:18).
event: No specific event relating to Shammai is recorded; he is listed as one of the children born to Mered (1 Chronicles 4:17-18).

introduce: Shammua is one of the four sons born to King David and Bathsheba, a man born in Jerusalem.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons whom David fathered in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:5). He is listed first of the four, Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon, born of Bathsheba (Bathshua in 1 Chronicles 3:5) (1 Chronicles 3:5).

introduce: Shammua is a Levite, recorded as the son of Galal, the grandson of Jeduthun, and the father of Abda (Nehemiah 11:17).
lifetime: Shammua was a son of Galal, and his son Abda is recorded among the Levites who lived in Jerusalem, the holy city, in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 11:17-18). No deeds of Shammua himself are recorded in the text.
event: No specific event of Shammua himself is recorded in the Bible; it tells only that his son Abda was entered in the list of Levites who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:17).

call: Priest of the family of Bilgah
introduce: Shammua is a man of the family of Bilgah, recorded as a head of the priests in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12, Nehemiah 12:18).
lifetime: He is recorded as head of the family of Bilgah among those who became heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12, Nehemiah 12:18).
event: His name was entered as head of the family of Bilgah in the list of the heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12, Nehemiah 12:18).

introduce: Zabdi appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in 1 Chronicles 8 and is one of the descendants of the house of Benjamin.
lifetime: Zabdi was a son of Shimei (1 Chronicles 8:19-21), and this list that includes the sons of Shimei is a list of those who were heads of families and chiefs throughout their generations and lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).

introduce: Zabdi is a figure mentioned in 1 Chronicles 27, a royal official in the reign of King David who was in charge of the wine vats that stored the produce of the vineyards. He is recorded as a man of Shepham (1 Chronicles 27:27).
lifetime: King David appointed those responsible for each field in order to manage his royal property, and Zabdi was in charge of the wine vats for the produce of the vineyards (1 Chronicles 27:27).
event: Zabdi was in charge of the wine vats for the produce of the vineyards. The one in charge of the vineyards themselves was Shimei the Ramathite (1 Chronicles 27:27).
character: Zabdi the Shiphmite is the one in David's list of estate officials who was in charge of the wine in the vineyards' wine vats (1 Chronicles 27:27). The Ramathite in the same verse is Shimei, who was in charge of the vineyards.

introduce: Zabdi appears in the genealogical records of the Bible as the grandfather of Mattaniah and the son of Asaph. He belongs to the family line of the descendants of Levi who lived in Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah.
lifetime: Zabdi is recorded as the son of Asaph and the grandfather of Mattaniah (Nehemiah 11:17). The one whose name is entered in Nehemiah 11 as a Levite who lived in the holy city is his grandson Mattaniah (Nehemiah 11:17).
event: No specific event relating to Zabdi himself is recorded in the Bible, but from the fact that his descendant Mattaniah served as the one who led in thanksgiving at the time of prayer, it can be seen that his family was involved in the service of the temple (Nehemiah 11:17).

introduce: Zabdiel was a man from a priestly family who lived in Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, the son of Haggedolim, who became overseer of 128 of his brothers who were mighty men of valor.
lifetime: His name is mentioned in the list of those who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 11:14).
event: As the son of Haggedolim, he became overseer of 128 mighty men of valor among his brothers who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:14).
character: From the fact that the biblical record puts him in a position of overseeing mighty men of valor, it can be seen that he was a man who was trusted and had leadership among his fellow priests (Nehemiah 11:14).

call: Son of Gilead (ancestor of the Shechemite family of Manasseh)
introduce: Shechem was a son of Gilead and the ancestor of the Shechemite family within the tribe of Manasseh. He is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh that appears in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament.
lifetime: Shechem is recorded as a great-grandson of Manasseh, son of Joseph, and a son of Gilead (Numbers 26:29-31). As one of the descendants of Gilead, and as the ancestor of a family that received an inheritance by lot in the land of Canaan, his name was recorded in the genealogy (Numbers 26:31, Joshua 17:2).
event: His name appears as the families of the tribe of Manasseh are listed when the people of Israel took a census on the plains of Moab (Numbers 26:31). In Joshua 17:2 the descendants of Shechem are recorded among the families that cast lots by their clans, as the rest of the descendants of Manasseh (Joshua 17:2).

introduce: Shechem is a man belonging to the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh, recorded as one of the sons of Shemida (1 Chronicles 7:19).
lifetime: Shechem was a son born to Shemida (1 Chronicles 7:19). The Shemida family descended from Shemida is listed among the descendants of Gilead, of the descendants of Manasseh (Numbers 26:29-32).
event: The biblical text records no specific achievement or event concerning Shechem (1 Chronicles 7:19).

call: One of the seven highest leaders of Persia
introduce: Shethar was one of the seven leaders of Persia and Media who, in the time of Ahasuerus, king of Persia, had access to the king, watched the king's countenance, and held the first seats in the kingdom (Esther 1:14).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the seven leaders of Persia and Media who, in the time of Ahasuerus, king of Persia, had access to the king and held the first seats in the kingdom (Esther 1:14).
event: When Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command, the king asked the wise men who knew the customs and laws how to deal with her, and Shethar's name was recorded as one of the seven leaders who had access to the king at that time (Esther 1:12-14). The one named in the text as answering before the king and the leaders on that occasion is Memucan (Esther 1:16-21); no words of Shethar himself are recorded.
character: He had the standing of a legal expert thoroughly versed in the laws and customs of Persia (Esther 1:13). As one of the king's closest associates, he had the authority to influence the king's judgment directly and held a political position in which he played a central role in national decision-making (Esther 1:14).

call: Father of King Jobab (man of Bozrah)
introduce: Zerah was a man from Bozrah in the land of Edom, recorded as the father of Jobab, who was king of Edom. In the genealogies of the Bible and the records of Chronicles he is mentioned as an important family member continuing the line of the kings of Edom.
lifetime: Zerah was the father of Jobab, who became king in place of Bela, king of Edom, after Bela died (Genesis 36:33). He is recorded as a man of Bozrah, and the record that his son Jobab became king in place of Bela also appears in 1 Chronicles 1:44 (1 Chronicles 1:44).
event: No record of his own reign or specific achievements is given in detail in the Bible; he appears mainly as a figure who accounts for the family basis of King Jobab within the genealogy of the early dynasty of Edom (Genesis 36:33).

introduce: Zerah is one of the twins born to Judah and Tamar who appear in Genesis, and is the brother of Perez. The Hebrew name Zerah carries the meaning of brightness or a rising sun.
lifetime: When Tamar was pregnant with twins by Judah, one of them first put out a hand during the labor but drew it back, and Perez was born first (Genesis 38:27-28). Zerah was born immediately afterward, and his name was entered in the family tree of the tribe of Judah (Genesis 38:30, 1 Chronicles 2:4).
event: At the birth, the midwife tied a scarlet thread on Zerah's hand to mark that he had put out his hand first (Genesis 38:28). This was a measure to distinguish the order between the twins, but as it turned out Perez came to be born first (Genesis 38:29-30). Afterward his descendants were called the Zerahites and formed one branch in the genealogy of Israel (Numbers 26:20).

introduce: Zerah is a man of the line of Gershom, a descendant of Levi, a son of Adaiah and the father of Ethni (1 Chronicles 6:41). In the biblical record he is mentioned mainly in the course of listing the genealogy of the tribe of Levi. His descendant Asaph took charge of the work of singing praise in the house of the LORD according to the duty David established (1 Chronicles 6:31, 1 Chronicles 6:39).
lifetime: Zerah is stated in the genealogy as a descendant of Jahath, son of Gershom, and the father of Ethni (1 Chronicles 6:41). His line continues from Gershom through Jahath, Shimei, Zimmah, Ethan, Adaiah, Zerah, Ethni, Malchijah, Baaseiah, Michael, Shimea, Berechiah, and Asaph (1 Chronicles 6:39-43).

call: King of Cush (invader with an army of a million)
introduce: A Cushite who appears in 2 Chronicles, who in the time of Asa, king of Judah, invaded Judah with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots (2 Chronicles 14:9).
lifetime: A Cushite, he mobilized a great army and invaded the kingdom of southern Judah, and a record is confirmed of his facing Asa's army in the Valley of Zephathah at Mareshah (2 Chronicles 14:9-10). No record of his deeds after his defeat in the war, or of his death, appears in the Bible.
event: He came as far as Mareshah with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots (2 Chronicles 14:9). But when Asa cried out to the LORD his God, the LORD struck down the Cushites before Asa and Judah, and the Cushites fled (2 Chronicles 14:11-12). Asa and those who followed him pursued the Cushites as far as Gerar, and the Cushites fell until none of them remained alive (2 Chronicles 14:13).

introduce: Serah was a daughter of Asher, son of Jacob, a woman recorded in the list of the time Jacob's family went down to Egypt as the sister of the sons of Asher. She is one of the few women whose names are exceptionally entered in the genealogical records of the Bible.
lifetime: She was born to Asher, son of Jacob, and was recorded as the sister of the sons of Asher in the list of the family of Israel that went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:17). In the census of the people of Israel, too, the name of Asher's daughter was recorded as Serah (Numbers 26:46). Her name is confirmed again as a descendant of Asher in the genealogy of Chronicles (1 Chronicles 7:30).
character: According to the biblical record, she is mentioned together with the sons of Asher, and so holds a place by descent as a member of the tribe of Asher (Numbers 26:46). Serah has the demographic peculiarity of being a woman of the generation of Jacob's granddaughters whose name is, rarely, entered directly in the genealogies of the Bible (Genesis 46:17).

introduce: Sherebiah was a Levite who was active in the Persian period after the return from the Babylonian exile; he is recorded as a Levite in the time of Ezra and took part in helping the people understand the law in the time of Nehemiah.
lifetime: Sherebiah is recorded as a Levite who was brought, with his sons and brothers, 18 in all, when Ezra, before going up from Babylon, was seeking those who would minister in the house of God at the river that flows toward Ahava (Ezra 8:15-18). Afterward, when Ezra read the law, he was recorded among the Levites who made the people understand the law (Nehemiah 8:7), and his name was entered as a Levite among those who sealed the covenant under Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:12).
event: When Ezra was seeking ministers for the house of God at the river of Ahava, Sherebiah was brought to Ezra with his sons and brothers, 18 in all (Ezra 8:17-18). When Ezra read the law, he took part with the Levites in making the people understand the law (Nehemiah 8:7), and when the people repented, he stood with the Levites on the platform and cried out in a loud voice to the LORD their God (Nehemiah 9:4). He was also recorded together with Hashabiah and Jeshua son of Kadmiel as a leader of the Levites, among those who praised and gave thanks to God division by division as David had commanded (Nehemiah 12:24).
character: Sherebiah, a Levite well versed in the law, showed the side of an educator who interpreted and conveyed the word correctly to the people (Nehemiah 8:7). He also bore order and administrative responsibility as a leader of the Levites, and stood in the position of a key manager of the temple praise and the sacrificial duties handed down through the generations (Nehemiah 12:24).

introduce: Sheresh is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 7:16 in the Old Testament and belongs to the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh. He is recorded as one of the sons born to Maacah, the wife of Machir.
lifetime: Sheresh was born to Machir, son of Manasseh, and his wife Maacah (1 Chronicles 7:16). He is recorded as the brother of Peresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rekem (1 Chronicles 7:16).

introduce: Zereth is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a son of Helah, wife of Ashhur the father of Tekoa (1 Chronicles 4:5, 1 Chronicles 4:7).
lifetime: Zereth is recorded as a son of Helah. Helah was one of the two wives of Ashhur the father of Tekoa (1 Chronicles 4:5), and Zohar and Ethnan are recorded with Zereth as sons of Helah (1 Chronicles 4:7).

introduce: Shemer is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament and belongs to the descendants of Merari of the tribe of Levi. He is a son of Mahli and, as a descendant of Merari, one of the persons who make up the genealogy of the Levites.
lifetime: Shemer is recorded as a son of Mahli, Mahli as a son of Mushi, and Mushi as a son of Merari (1 Chronicles 6:47). He is a member of the house of Merari in the genealogy of the tribe of Levi, and his son Bani is recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:46 (1 Chronicles 6:46).

introduce: Zophar the Naamathite is a character in the book of Job and one of Job's three friends. He is recorded as having visited to comfort Job when Job was suffering.
lifetime: Together with Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite, he heard of the calamity that had come upon Job and came, by agreement, to comfort him (Job 2:11). As Job's suffering dragged on, he rebutted Job's claims and answered twice (Job 11:1, 20:1). In the end, when Job was approved by God, he had to offer a burnt offering with the other friends and seek forgiveness through Job's prayer (Job 42:7-9).
event: When Job maintained his innocence, Zophar rebuked him, saying that such a flood of words should not go unanswered, and asking how a man with swollen lips could be justified (Job 11:2-4). He said that he had heard in Job's words a rebuke that shamed him, and answered in haste, saying that the triumph of the wicked is brief and the joy of the godless momentary (Job 20:2-5). In the end God was angry with Zophar, and corrected the friends' error by having them offer a burnt offering through Job and ask for his prayer (Job 42:7-9).
character: Zophar tends to use more emotional and acerbic language than the other friends (Job 11:2-3). He regards human wisdom as limited and takes a hard line, pressing Job with a strict logic of his own (Job 11:6-7). He also shows a stubborn side, never accepting Job's claims to the end and holding to his own position (Job 20:2-3).

call: Descendant of Hur, son of Hezron of the tribe of Judah
introduce: A man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as the son of Hur and the father of Kiriath-jearim.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, a descendant of Caleb, and is introduced as the father of Kiriath-jearim (1 Chronicles 2:50).
event: He is recorded as the father of Kiriath-jearim, and from his descendants come Haroeh and half of the Manahathites (1 Chronicles 2:52). Also, Reaiah son of Shobal fathered Jahath, and these are recorded as the clans of the Zorathites (1 Chronicles 4:2).

call: Son of Elkanah (Kohathite Levite, father of Nahath)
introduce: Zophai is a descendant of Kohath of the tribe of Levi, recorded in the genealogy of the Bible as the son of Elkanah and the father of Nahath (1 Chronicles 6:26).
lifetime: In the genealogy of the descendants of Kohath in 1 Chronicles 6, in the record of Elkanah's descendants, he appears as the son of Elkanah and the father of Nahath, in the words "Zophai his son, Nahath his son" (1 Chronicles 6:26). After Nahath follow Eliab, Jeroham, and Elkanah (1 Chronicles 6:27).

call: Fellow believer and co-worker of Paul
introduce: Sosthenes was a man who cooperated with Paul in the early Christian community, a believer mentioned together with Paul at the opening of 1 Corinthians.
lifetime: His name appears with Paul at the very beginning of 1 Corinthians as "our brother Sosthenes," and this letter is addressed to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2).
event: At the beginning of 1 Corinthians his name is entered alongside the apostle Paul as "our brother Sosthenes" (1 Corinthians 1:1).

introduce: Shuthelah is a descendant of the tribe of Ephraim, recorded as the son of Zabad in the genealogy that continues from Shuthelah, a son of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 7:20-21).
lifetime: In the genealogy that runs from Shuthelah, son of Ephraim, through Bered, Tahath, Eleadah, Tahath, and Zabad, he is recorded as the son of Zabad (1 Chronicles 7:20-21).
event: 1 Chronicles 7:21 records that this Shuthelah fathered Ezer and Elead, and that they went down to take the livestock of the men of Gath and were killed by the natives of Gath (1 Chronicles 7:21).

call: Son of Heman (13th division of the temple praise)
introduce: Shubael was a descendant of the tribe of Levi, one of the sons of Heman, and came from a family that performed the duty of praise at the temple in the time of David. In the list of the sons of Heman (1 Chronicles 25:4) he is recorded as Shebuel, and in the casting of lots among the 24 divisions in charge of the temple music ministry he received the thirteenth division (1 Chronicles 25:20).
lifetime: He received his duty as a son of Heman among those whom David set apart for service from the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun (1 Chronicles 25:1, 25:4). In the lot, Shubael came out thirteenth, and he, his sons, and his brothers, twelve in all, made up one division (1 Chronicles 25:9, 25:20).
event: Shubael was under his father Heman and served by singing in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps, and lyres (1 Chronicles 25:6). He received his post as the thirteenth division by lot (1 Chronicles 25:8, 25:20), and this was part of the system of temple music ministry that David established.
character: The biblical record gives no information about his personal character or specific features.

introduce: A Canaanite who appears in Genesis and came into relationship with Judah, son of Jacob. He is recorded as the father-in-law of Judah, the father of the daughter of Shua who became Judah's wife.
lifetime: When Judah left his brothers and was living near Hirah the Adullamite, he saw there the daughter of a Canaanite named Shua and took her as his wife (Genesis 38:2). Afterward three sons, Er, Onan, and Shelah, were born between Judah and the daughter of Shua (Genesis 38:3-5).

introduce: Shuah is one of the six sons born to Keturah, whom Abraham took as a later wife, and is recorded last (sixth) in the list in Genesis 25:2 (Genesis 25:1-2). He is among the sons of the concubine line in the arrangement in which everything he owned went to Isaac while the sons of the concubines were given gifts and sent to the east (Genesis 25:5-6).
lifetime: Abraham gave gifts to the sons born to the later wife Keturah and, while he was still alive, sent them away from his son Isaac to the east (Genesis 25:1-6). As a son of Keturah, Shuah is among these sons (Genesis 25:2, 25:6). No record of Shuah's personal life or time of death appears in the Bible.
event: No deeds of Shuah himself are recorded in the Bible; his name appears only in the lists in Genesis 25:2 and 1 Chronicles 1:32. There is a record that Abraham gave gifts to the sons of the concubines and sent them to the east (Genesis 25:6).

introduce: Shua appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher and is recorded among the children born to Heber, together with Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham (1 Chronicles 7:32).
lifetime: Shua is recorded as the daughter of Heber, son of Beriah, son of Asher, and is a sister of Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham (1 Chronicles 7:30-32).

introduce: Shuah is the Shuhite clan that appears in the book of Job as the name denoting the origin of Bildad, one of Job's three friends ("Bildad the Shuhite") (Job 2:11). Genesis records Shuah among the sons whom Abraham fathered by Keturah (Genesis 25:2), but the relationship between the two names is not stated in the KRV text.
lifetime: Genesis has Shuah among the sons whom Abraham fathered by Keturah (Genesis 25:2), and Abraham gave gifts to the sons of the concubines and sent them away from his son Isaac to the east while he was still alive (Genesis 25:6). The Bible has no separate record of the dwelling place or life of the Shuhite clan.
event: One of Job's three friends is introduced as "Bildad the Shuhite" (Job 2:11), and Bildad begins the speeches in reply to Job (Job 8:1, 18:1). No specific achievement or event of Shuah himself is recorded in the Bible.

call: Third son of Zophah (chief of Asher)
introduce: A man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher, recorded third among the sons of Zophah.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Zophah, son of Helem of the tribe of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:35-36). In the list of the sons of Zophah, Shual comes after Suah and Harnepher (1 Chronicles 7:36).

call: Gatekeeper who guarded the west gate of the temple
introduce: Shuppim is a figure who appears in the Old Testament book of 1 Chronicles, recorded as one of those who held the office of temple gatekeeper in the time of King David.
lifetime: In David's time, when the gatekeepers cast lots by clans to guard each gate, the lot for the west fell to Shuppim together with Hosah (1 Chronicles 26:13, 26:16).
event: Together with Hosah, Shuppim kept watch beside the Shallecheth Gate on the highway, guard opposite guard (1 Chronicles 26:16).

call: Returning clan head of the descendants of Shephatiah
introduce: Shecaniah is a figure who appears, in the list of clan heads who came up from Babylon with Ezra in the time of King Artaxerxes, as a family name in the phrase "the descendants of Shecaniah, that is, the descendants of Parosh" (Ezra 8:1, 8:3).
lifetime: Ezra 8:3 records, "Of the descendants of Shecaniah, that is, of the descendants of Parosh, Zechariah," and says that from this family Zechariah came up with one hundred fifty men registered in the genealogy (Ezra 8:3). There is no record of Shecaniah's own life.
event: No personal deeds of Shecaniah are recorded in the Bible. His name appears only as a family name in the list of clan heads who came up with Ezra (Ezra 8:1-3).

call: Returning clan head of the descendants of Zattu
introduce: He is one of the Israelites who, after the Babylonian exile, returned to Jerusalem under the leadership of Ezra.
lifetime: His name appears as a family name in the list of clan heads who came up from Babylon with Ezra in the time of King Artaxerxes (Ezra 8:1, 8:5). Ezra 8:5 records that "the descendants of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel" came up with three hundred men who were with him; the son of Jahaziel was the head of the family of the descendants of Shecaniah, and there is no record that Shecaniah himself was a son of Jahaziel.
event: No personal deeds of Shecaniah are recorded; from his family (the descendants of Shecaniah), the son of Jahaziel came up with Ezra with three hundred men (Ezra 8:5).

call: Son of Jehiel (leader of the covenant renewal)
introduce: A man of the descendants of Elam who was active in Jerusalem after the return from exile, a leading figure who confessed to Ezra the problem of marriages to foreign women and proposed reform.
lifetime: As a son of Jehiel, he was a member of the community of those who returned from the Babylonian exile and was active in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:2). While Ezra was praying and confessing, weeping and prostrating himself before the house of God, he spoke to Ezra in the midst of a very large assembly of the people (Ezra 10:1-2), and acknowledged that they had been unfaithful to God by taking foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:2).
event: He proposed that they make a covenant with God to send away all the foreign wives and their children and to act according to the law (Ezra 10:3). He also urged Ezra to arise and act courageously, saying that the matter was his to carry out, and promised that they would support him (Ezra 10:4).

call: Father of Shemaiah (father of the keeper of the East Gate)
introduce: Shecaniah is a figure who appears only as the father of Shemaiah in the account of the rebuilding of the wall in Nehemiah 3 (Nehemiah 3:29).
lifetime: Nehemiah 3:29 records "Shemaiah the son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate," and so introduces Shecaniah as the father of Shemaiah. There is no record of Shecaniah's own life (Nehemiah 3:29).
event: Nothing that Shecaniah himself did is recorded; his son Shemaiah repaired the section of the wall next to Zadok the son of Immer (Nehemiah 3:29).

introduce: Shecaniah is a figure active in the time of Nehemiah, recorded in the Bible as the son of Arah and the father-in-law of Tobiah (Nehemiah 6:18).
lifetime: He is introduced in Nehemiah 6:18 as the son of Arah, and Tobiah became his son-in-law (Nehemiah 6:18). His place of residence and the rest of his life are not recorded in the Bible.
event: No personal deeds of Shecaniah are recorded; only the fact that Tobiah became his son-in-law appears. Because of this marriage, and because Tobiah's son Jehohanan took the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah, many in Judah were bound by oath to Tobiah (Nehemiah 6:18).
character: He was related by blood to the leaders of Judah, and he kept up a close relationship in which he supported Tobiah, who belonged to the party opposing the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem, and relayed good reports about him to the influential (Nehemiah 6:18-19).

introduce: Shecaniah is a figure whose name appears in the list of priests who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1, 12:3).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the priests who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1), and his name stands in the list of priests following Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra, and others (Nehemiah 12:3).
event: He is included in the list recorded as the priests and the heads of their brothers in the days of Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:3, 12:7). No specific deeds of his are recorded.

introduce: He is a figure who was responsible for the tenth division when the priestly organization was arranged into twenty-four divisions in the time of David.
lifetime: In the reign of King David, when the duties of the descendants of Levi were apportioned, he took part in the casting of lots that fixed the divisions of the priests, and was assigned the office of the tenth division (1 Chronicles 24:7, 24:11).
event: When David divided the descendants of Aaron the priest into twenty-four divisions for the service of the temple, Shecaniah was in charge of the tenth turn and came to perform the duties of the temple (1 Chronicles 24:11).

call: Levite who distributed the temple offerings
introduce: Shecaniah is a figure involved in distributing the temple offerings in the time of King Hezekiah; under Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, the keeper of the East Gate, he held an office in the cities of the priests and gave the offerings to his brothers (2 Chronicles 31:14-15).
lifetime: Shecaniah was active in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah; when Hezekiah reformed the worship of the temple and assigned the portions of the priests and the Levites (2 Chronicles 31:4), he took charge of the distribution of the offerings under Kore (2 Chronicles 31:14-15).
event: Together with Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, and Amariah, he served under Kore in the cities of the priests, and distributed the offerings to his brothers by their divisions, great and small alike (2 Chronicles 31:15).

introduce: A figure in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, the son of Hezron and recorded as the father of Jair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.
lifetime: Hezron, a descendant of Perez the son of Judah, married the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead when he was sixty years old, and she bore him Segub (1 Chronicles 2:21). Segub became the father of Jair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead (1 Chronicles 2:22).
event: No personal deeds of Segub are recorded; it is recorded that his son Jair had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead (1 Chronicles 2:22).

call: Last high priest of southern Judah
introduce: Seraiah was a high priest who served in the final period of the kingdom of southern Judah; when Jerusalem fell to Babylon, he was seized, together with Zephaniah the deputy priest and the three doorkeepers, by Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, and was put to death by the king of Babylon at Riblah (2 Kings 25:18-21).
lifetime: Seraiah belongs to the line of high priests as the son of Azariah and the father of Jehozadak (1 Chronicles 6:14). He served as high priest toward the end of the reign of King Zedekiah and held the office until the fall of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:18). After Jerusalem was conquered by the Babylonian army, he was taken with the high officials of Judah to Riblah in the land of Hamath (2 Kings 25:19-20). There he was put to death by the king of Babylon (2 Kings 25:21).
event: As high priest of the temple in Jerusalem, he carried out the duty of overseeing the priests (2 Kings 25:18). When Jerusalem fell, he was arrested by the captain of the guard together with Zephaniah the deputy priest and the three doorkeepers (Jeremiah 52:24). He was then brought to Riblah and came before the king of Babylon, and at Riblah in the land of Hamath he was killed together with the others (Jeremiah 52:26-27). Ezra 7:1 records Ezra as a son of Seraiah (Ezra 7:1). His son Jehozadak went into exile together with the people of Judah and Jerusalem when the LORD carried them away by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar (1 Chronicles 6:15).

introduce: Seraiah is a figure active after the fall of Jerusalem, the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, recorded as one of the commanders of the forces of Judah (2 Kings 25:23).
lifetime: After the Babylonian army had completely captured Jerusalem, when Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor (spelled differently in the Korean text of 2 Kings 25:23), was at Mizpah, Seraiah went to Gedaliah at Mizpah as one of the commanders of the forces, together with Ishmael, Johanan, and others (2 Kings 25:23, Jeremiah 40:7-8).
event: Seraiah is not mentioned individually in the text after Jeremiah 40:8. After Gedaliah was killed by Ishmael (Jeremiah 41:2), Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces led the people into Egypt (Jeremiah 43:4-7), but the text does not state whether Seraiah was among them.

call: Son of Kenaz (younger brother of Othniel)
introduce: Seraiah is a figure who appears in the Old Testament book of 1 Chronicles, recorded as a son of Kenaz and a younger brother of Othniel, the first judge of Israel.
lifetime: He was a son of Kenaz and a brother of Othniel (1 Chronicles 4:13), and he fathered Joab. Joab was the ancestor of the people of Ge-harashim (1 Chronicles 4:14).
event: There is no record in the Bible of any specific deed or particular event of his (1 Chronicles 4:13).

introduce: Seraiah is a figure recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon in 1 Chronicles, the son of Asiel and the father of Joshibiah (1 Chronicles 4:35).
lifetime: He was the son of Asiel, and his grandson Jehu is recorded among the chiefs of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:35, 4:38). Seraiah himself is mentioned in this genealogy only as an ancestor.
event: No specific deeds of Seraiah himself are recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 4:35).
character: The Bible gives no description of his personal character or specific traits. It is mentioned, however, that as a chief leading his family he held a public position in which he carried out his duties (1 Chronicles 4:38).

call: Clan head of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Seraiah is a figure whose name appears among the priests who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1). The one recorded as head of the priestly family of Seraiah in the days of Joiakim is Meraiah (Nehemiah 12:12).
lifetime: In the list of the priests and Levites who returned with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Jeshua, Seraiah is recorded first among the priests (Nehemiah 12:1). In the days of Joiakim, Meraiah was head of the family of Seraiah (Nehemiah 12:12).
event: No specific deeds of Seraiah himself are recorded in the Bible. The one recorded as head of the priestly family of Seraiah in the days of Joiakim is Meraiah (Nehemiah 12:12).

call: Son of Azriel (servant of the king)
introduce: Seraiah is a figure active in the time of Jehoiakim king of Judah, the son of Azriel, mentioned as an official who carried out the king's commands (Jeremiah 36:26).
lifetime: After Jehoiakim king of Judah burned the scroll written by Baruch (Jeremiah 36:23), the king commanded Jerahmeel the king's son, Seraiah the son of Azriel, and Shelemiah the son of Abdeel to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet (Jeremiah 36:26).
event: He is recorded as one of the three who received the command of King Jehoiakim to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet (Jeremiah 36:26). But the LORD hid Baruch and Jeremiah (Jeremiah 36:26).

introduce: Seraiah is a figure from the time of Zedekiah king of Judah, a grandson of Mahseiah and a son of Neriah. When he went to Babylon with the king in the fourth year of Zedekiah, he received a word commanded by the prophet Jeremiah, and he was the quartermaster (Jeremiah 51:59).
lifetime: In the fourth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, he went to Babylon with the king (Jeremiah 51:59). Jeremiah wrote on a scroll all the disaster that would come upon Babylon (Jeremiah 51:60), and commanded Seraiah, when he came to Babylon, to read all these words (Jeremiah 51:61), and when he had finished reading, to tie a stone to the scroll and cast it into the Euphrates, and to say that Babylon would sink and not rise again (Jeremiah 51:63-64).
event: He was commanded by Jeremiah to read in Babylon the words concerning Babylon, and when he had finished reading, to tie a stone to the scroll and cast it into the Euphrates (Jeremiah 51:61, 51:63).
character: As a close associate of King Zedekiah, he had such standing and trust that he accompanied the king on his journey (Jeremiah 51:59). He also accepted the request of Jeremiah and faithfully carried out the task of reading aloud in Babylon itself the prophecy that Jeremiah had sent and of disposing of it (Jeremiah 51:61-63).

call: Descendants of Pahath-moab (father of one who returned with Ezra)
introduce: Zerahiah is a figure recorded in the list of returning clan heads in Ezra 8 as the father of Eliehoenai, of the descendants of Pahath-moab (Ezra 8:4).
lifetime: In the list of clan heads who came up from Babylon with Ezra in the time of King Artaxerxes (Ezra 8:1), Eliehoenai the son of Zerahiah is recorded among the descendants of Pahath-moab (Ezra 8:4). There is no record about Zerahiah himself.
event: No personal deeds of Zerahiah are recorded in the Bible. Ezra 8:4 records that his son Eliehoenai was with two hundred men.

introduce: Shemariah is a son of Rehoboam king of Judah, a prince born to Mahalath (2 Chronicles 11:19).
lifetime: Shemariah is one of the three sons born to Rehoboam by Mahalath, whom he took as wife, the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David and of Abihail (2 Chronicles 11:18-19).

introduce: Shemariah is a figure who appears in Ezra 10 of the Old Testament, one of the people of Israel who had taken foreign women as wives in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 10:32).
lifetime: He was a member of the Jewish community that returned from the Babylonian captivity, and in the course of Ezra's reform movement his name is recorded in the list of those who had foreign wives (Ezra 10:32).
event: He is included in the list of those who took part in the pledge to separate from their foreign wives, carried out under the leadership of Ezra (Ezra 10:32).

introduce: Shemariah is a figure who appears in Ezra 10 of the Old Testament, one of the descendants of Israel who had taken foreign women as wives after the return from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 10:41).
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, in the time of Ezra, his name was recorded among the descendants of Bani in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:34), (Ezra 10:41).
event: When Ezra pointed out the problem of the marriages of the people of Israel to foreign women and urged repentance, his name was recorded, as one of them, in the list of the guilty who were to send away their wives (Ezra 10:41).

introduce: Shemaiah is a figure in the genealogy of the house of David recorded in 1 Chronicles 3, the son of Shecaniah (1 Chronicles 3:22).
lifetime: Shemaiah was born as a son of Shecaniah, a descendant of Zerubbabel of the royal house of David (1 Chronicles 3:22).
event: Shemaiah was a son of Shecaniah, and his sons are recorded as six: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat. No specific achievement or event that he personally carried out is described in the text of the Bible (1 Chronicles 3:22).

introduce: Shemaiah is a figure recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon in 1 Chronicles 4 as an ancestor of Ziza (1 Chronicles 4:37).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 4:37 records Ziza the son of Shiphi as "the grandson of Allon, the great-grandson of Jedaiah, the great-great-grandson of Shimri, and the fifth-generation descendant of Shemaiah," and so makes clear that Shemaiah was an ancestor of Ziza (1 Chronicles 4:37).
event: No specific deeds of Shemaiah himself are recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 4:37).

introduce: Shemaiah is a figure recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben in the Old Testament, the son of Joel (1 Chronicles 5:4).
lifetime:
He was born as a son of Joel, a man of the tribe of Reuben, and had a son, Gog (1 Chronicles 5:4).
