Among his descendants, Beerah became a leader of the Reubenites but was taken into captivity by Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria (1 Chronicles 5:6).
Beyond this, no specific record of his birth or death appears (1 Chronicles 5:4).

introduce: Shemaiah is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 9:14, a member of the tribe of Levi who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He belonged to the descendants of Merari and was the son of Hasshub, the grandson of Azrikam, and the great-grandson of Hashabiah.
lifetime: He was a man in the genealogical line of the descendants of Merari of the tribe of Levi, and is included in the list of Levites who returned from the Babylonian captivity and lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:14).
event: He is recorded among the Levites who lived in Jerusalem as one of the descendants of Merari (1 Chronicles 9:14). No specific deeds of his are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: He is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 9:16, a man of the tribe of Levi recorded as the father of Obadiah.
lifetime: He was one of the Levites who returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, and he had a son, Obadiah (1 Chronicles 9:16).

introduce: Shemaiah was a descendant of Levi, recorded as one of the Levites who were consecrated in the process of bringing the ark of the covenant up to Jerusalem in the reign of King David.
lifetime: Shemaiah was a descendant of Elizaphan, and is mentioned as one of the Levites when David assembled them to bring the ark of the covenant up (1 Chronicles 15:8). He was among those summoned together when David called the priests Zadok and Abiathar, and the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab (1 Chronicles 15:11).
event: As one of the six chiefs of the Levites whom David called (Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab), he was commanded to consecrate himself with his brothers and to carry up the ark of the LORD (1 Chronicles 15:11-12). The descendants of Levi carried the ark of God on their shoulders with poles, as prescribed (1 Chronicles 15:15).

introduce: Shemaiah is a figure who appears in the Old Testament book of 1 Chronicles, recorded as the son of Nethanel and a Levite scribe.
lifetime: In the time of King David, as a Levite, he carried out the task of writing in the presence of the king, the princes, the priests, and the whole assembly of Israel (1 Chronicles 24:6).
event: When David divided the descendants of Aaron the priest by their divisions, he took the part of the scribe who recorded that list (1 Chronicles 24:6).

introduce: Shemaiah was the firstborn son of Obed-edom, of the descendants of Korah of the tribe of Levi, who served as a temple gatekeeper in the time of King David (1 Chronicles 26:1-4).
lifetime: He was born as the first son of Obed-edom, who performed the duty of temple gatekeeper (1 Chronicles 26:4). He had Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad, and others as sons (1 Chronicles 26:7).
event: In the time of King David, he was included in the division of those who served by guarding the gates of the temple, holding the office of ruling (1 Chronicles 26:1-12). The sons born to him became leaders who ruled over the houses of their fathers (1 Chronicles 26:6).
character: He is called a mighty man who ruled over his family, and together with his descendants he was regarded as one with the strong ability to carry out well the duties of temple gatekeeper (1 Chronicles 26:6-8).

call: A Levite in the time of Jehoshaphat
introduce: A Levite who was active in the time of King Jehoshaphat of the kingdom of southern Judah and who carried out the ministry of teaching the law.
lifetime: In the third year of King Jehoshaphat's reign, together with the king's officials, he went around the cities of Judah and carried out the task of teaching the people the book of the law of the LORD (2 Chronicles 17:7, 17:8).
event: Included in the teaching delegation that King Jehoshaphat sent out, he went through all of Judah together with the Levites and the priests, giving itinerant instruction in the book of the law of the LORD (2 Chronicles 17:7, 17:9).
character: According to the Bible, he was trusted by King Jehoshaphat and carried out the national task of teaching the law; he is regarded as an official of the Levitical line who shared religious and educational roles in cooperation with the priests (2 Chronicles 17:8).

call: A Levite in the time of Hezekiah
introduce: Shemaiah was a Levite active in the time of King Hezekiah of the kingdom of southern Judah, who carried out the duty of managing and distributing the offerings of the temple.
lifetime: Under Kore the Levite, together with Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Amariah, and Shecaniah, he held an office in the cities of the priests (2 Chronicles 31:14-15).
event: At the time of King Hezekiah's religious reform, he was responsible for distributing the portions due to the priests and the Levites. He took the role of distributing fairly, according to their genealogies, the offerings, tithes, and consecrated things brought into the temple at Jerusalem to the priests and Levites who lived in the cities (2 Chronicles 31:12-15).
character: He is recorded as having faithfully carried out the duty of caring for his fellow Levites who served in the temple and of distributing goods fairly according to the established rules (2 Chronicles 31:15).

call: A Levite in the time of Josiah
introduce: Shemaiah was a Levite in the time of King Josiah of southern Judah and a brother of Conaniah. He is recorded among the chiefs of the Levites when Josiah kept the Passover (2 Chronicles 35:9).
lifetime: At the Passover that was kept in the eighteenth year of King Josiah (2 Chronicles 35:1, 35:19), Conaniah and his brother Shemaiah, together with Nethanel, Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, are recorded as chiefs of the Levites (2 Chronicles 35:9).
event: At Josiah's Passover, the chiefs of the Levites, Conaniah and his brother Shemaiah, Nethanel, Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, gave the Levites five thousand sheep and five hundred bulls as Passover offerings (2 Chronicles 35:9).

introduce: He is a figure who appears in the list of those who returned from the Babylonian exile, as a descendant of Adonikam.
lifetime: He is included in the list of the Israelites who returned to Jerusalem under the leadership of Ezra after the Babylonian exile (Ezra 8:13).
event: When Ezra reviewed the returnees who had assembled by the river Ahava, he is recorded as having joined the returning company from among the descendants of Adonikam, together with Eliphelet and Jeiel (Ezra 8:13).

call: A priest in the time of Ezra
introduce: Shemaiah is a figure recorded as one of the descendants of Harim among the group of priests who took foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:18, 10:21).
lifetime: Ezra 10 records those among the group of priests who had taken foreign women, and among them is the name of Shemaiah, as one of the descendants of Harim (Ezra 10:18, 10:21). No other deeds of his are recorded.
event: In the time of Ezra, he was recorded in the list of the priests who had taken foreign women, as one of the descendants of Harim (Ezra 10:21).

call: Musician at the dedication of the wall (brother of Zechariah)
introduce: A figure of a priestly family who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, and who, together with the musicians recorded as descendants of Asaph, walked in procession carrying the instruments of David the man of God (Nehemiah 12:36).
lifetime: At the time the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem was completed after the return from the Babylonian exile, he belonged to the group of Levites and priests who were mobilized for the dedication of the wall (Nehemiah 12:36).
event: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, he joined the procession that followed the priest Ezra, going around the wall and playing the instruments of David (Nehemiah 12:36).

call: A priest in the time of Nehemiah
introduce: A figure of a priestly family who appears in the records concerning the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah. Several people named Shemaiah appear in the Bible, but the Shemaiah of the time of Nehemiah is mentioned as a member of a family that carried out the priestly office.
lifetime: His name is entered in the record of the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 12:42).
event: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, he was with Maaseiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer, following the priests who held the trumpets, and the singers sang loudly (Nehemiah 12:41-42).

introduce: In the time of Nehemiah, while the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem was being hindered, he was a figure who threatened Nehemiah and tried to discourage him with a false prophecy.
lifetime: In the period when Nehemiah was building the wall of Jerusalem, he appears as the son of Delaiah, the son of Mehetabel (Nehemiah 6:10). When he shut himself in, Nehemiah went to his house, and Shemaiah said that they should go to the house of God, inside the temple, and shut its doors (Nehemiah 6:10).
event: He was bribed by Sanballat and Tobiah and gave a false prophecy to Nehemiah (Nehemiah 6:12). He said to Nehemiah that they should go inside the temple of the house of God and shut the doors, and delivered this in the form of a prophecy (Nehemiah 6:10). This was a scheme to make Nehemiah afraid, lead him to sin, and thereby give them an evil report with which to reproach him (Nehemiah 6:13).
character: He claimed that he had received a prophecy from God, but in fact he was a false prophet who had been hired (Nehemiah 6:12). He laid a careful plan to deceive Nehemiah, and showed a cunning disposition in trying to discredit Nehemiah through a sin that Nehemiah would commit himself (Nehemiah 6:13).

introduce: A figure of a priestly family who appears as one of the leaders who sealed the covenant document after the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah.
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, he was one who, together with Nehemiah, made a solemn covenant before God and sealed it (Nehemiah 10:8).
event: When the leaders of the people, with Nehemiah at their head, resolved to keep the law, to forbid marriage with foreigners, and to keep the Sabbath, he took part in putting his name to the covenant document and sealing it (Nehemiah 10:1).

introduce: A figure recorded as the son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate, at the time of Nehemiah's rebuilding of the wall, and one of those who repaired the wall of Jerusalem.
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, he took part in the work of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem and repaired the section next to Zadok the son of Immer (Nehemiah 3:29).
event: As the son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate, he repaired the section of the wall next to the part repaired by Zadok the son of Immer (Nehemiah 3:29).

introduce: Shemaiah is a figure whose name is recorded among the company that went in procession on the wall at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 12:31-34).
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem led by Nehemiah, his name is listed among the company that went in procession on the wall (Nehemiah 12:31-34).
event: When the great company giving thanks and praise at the dedication was divided into two companies and went in procession on the wall, his name was recorded among the procession of one company (Nehemiah 12:31-34). The two companies took their stand in the house of God (Nehemiah 12:40), and on that day the company offered great sacrifices (Nehemiah 12:43).

introduce: A man from Kiriath-jearim, the father of the prophet Uriah (Jeremiah 26:20).

Shemaiah the Nehelamite was among the captives carried away to Babylon, and he sent a letter to Zephaniah the priest in Jerusalem and others, urging them to rebuke Jeremiah; he is a figure who prophesied though the LORD had not sent him, and made the people trust in a lie.
lifetime: He was among the captives carried away to Babylon, and in his own name he sent a letter to all the people in Jerusalem, to Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, reproaching them for not rebuking Jeremiah, who made himself out to be a prophet (Jeremiah 29:25-27). The LORD then told Jeremiah to send a letter to all the exiles, saying that Shemaiah had prophesied to the people and made them trust in a lie, though the LORD had not sent him (Jeremiah 29:30-32).
event: In the letter he sent to Zephaniah the priest, he said that the LORD had appointed Zephaniah priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be the chief officer in the house of the LORD, to put in stocks and neck irons every madman who acts like a prophet, and asked why he had not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth; and he accused Jeremiah of writing to those in Babylon that the exile would be long, so that they should build houses and settle down (Jeremiah 29:26-28). Zephaniah the priest read Shemaiah's letter to Jeremiah (Jeremiah 29:29). Then the LORD said through Jeremiah that he would punish Shemaiah and his descendants, so that none of his would be left to dwell among this people, and that he would not see the good that the LORD would do for the people (Jeremiah 29:31-32).
character: He acted as a ringleader who denied Jeremiah's prophecy of the delay of the return and stirred up opposition among the mainstream religious leaders of Jerusalem and the lower classes of Judea of that time (Jeremiah 29:24-27). He showed an authoritarian and aggressive attitude, such as pressing the overseers of the temple to arrest Jeremiah, and showed a meticulousness in using official letters to push through his own views (Jeremiah 29:25-29).

call: An official in the time of Jehoiakim
introduce: Shemaiah is a figure recorded in Jeremiah 36:12 as the father of Delaiah the prince.
lifetime: No deeds of Shemaiah himself are recorded in the Bible; his son Delaiah was among the princes who were sitting in the chamber of the scribe in the king's house in the fifth year of Jehoiakim king of Judah (Jeremiah 36:9-12).
event: No events of Shemaiah himself are recorded. His son Delaiah, together with the princes, heard in the scribe's chamber the words of the scroll that Baruch read aloud, was alarmed, and said that they would tell the king (Jeremiah 36:12-16).

introduce: Sheba is a figure recorded as a descendant of Shem and one of the sons whom Joktan fathered (Genesis 10:28).
lifetime: As a grandson of Eber and a son of Joktan, his name is entered in the genealogy of Shem (Genesis 10:24-26, 28).

call: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat (teacher of the law)
introduce: Shemiramoth was a Levite active in the time of King Jehoshaphat of the kingdom of southern Judah, who, at the king's command, went around all of Judah and taught the people the law.
lifetime: In the third year of King Jehoshaphat's reign, the king sent officials, priests, and Levites to the cities of Judah to teach the people the book of the law of the LORD (2 Chronicles 17:7-9). At that time Shemiramoth was singled out as one of the Levites whom Jehoshaphat sent (2 Chronicles 17:8).
event: Together with the other Levites, Shemiramoth carried out the task of going throughout all the cities of Judah with the book of the law of the LORD and teaching the people (2 Chronicles 17:9). In this way the people in all the cities of Judah were instructed (2 Chronicles 17:9).

introduce: Sheba was a man of the tribe of Benjamin, the son of Bichri, a rebel who in the time of King David blew a trumpet and stirred up the men of Israel to stop following David and to follow him instead (2 Samuel 20:1-2).
lifetime: When conflict arose between the men of Judah and the men of Israel as David was returning to Jerusalem after putting down the rebellion of Absalom (2 Samuel 19:41-43), Sheba blew a trumpet and cried out that they had no share in David, and all the men of Israel followed him, but the men of Judah clung to the king (2 Samuel 20:1-2). He was besieged by the people who were with Joab at Abel of Beth-maacah, and his life ended when the people of that city cut off his head and threw it to Joab (2 Samuel 20:15-22).
event: When he blew the trumpet and proclaimed that they had no share in David, all the men of Israel stopped following David and followed him (2 Samuel 20:1-2). When all the people who were with Joab went to Abel of Beth-maacah, besieged Sheba, and built up a siege ramp in order to batter down the wall (2 Samuel 20:15), a wise woman of the city spoke, and the people of the city cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab; Joab blew the trumpet, the troops dispersed, and the rebellion ended (2 Samuel 20:16-22).
character: He is described as a worthless man, and had the temperament of an agitator who challenged David's rule (2 Samuel 20:1). For his own advantage he fomented the division of Israel, and in a crisis he took the course of fleeing into a city (2 Samuel 20:14).

introduce: A son of Jokshan, who was born to Abraham and his concubine Keturah, and so a grandson of Abraham.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons born to Jokshan, whom Abraham had through Keturah (Genesis 25:3).
event: There is no information in the Bible describing his life or any specific deeds.
character: The biblical text contains no information describing his temperament or personal characteristics.

introduce: Shephatiah is a figure recorded in the Old Testament book of 1 Chronicles, mentioned as the father of Meshullam of the tribe of Benjamin and as a son of Reuel.
lifetime: He is one of the figures who make up the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, and his son Meshullam appears as one of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:3, 9:7-8).
event: No specific deeds or social achievements in his life appear in the biblical record, and his existence can be confirmed only through his name in the genealogy (1 Chronicles 9:8).

introduce: One of David's mighty men mentioned in 1 Chronicles 12, a man from Haruph. He is classed among the skilled warriors who joined David when he stayed at Ziklag to escape from Saul.
lifetime: When David was in hiding because of Saul the son of Kish, he came to Ziklag and helped him (1 Chronicles 12:1). He is included in the list of the mighty men who came to help David (1 Chronicles 12:5).
event: He is entered by name as one qualified to join David's army and fight at his side (1 Chronicles 12:5). He was a man of the tribe of Benjamin, and though he was a kinsman of Saul, he was one of the mighty men who went over to David to support him (1 Chronicles 12:2).
character: He was a warrior skilled with the bow, with the talent of using both the right and the left hand to sling stones or shoot arrows (1 Chronicles 12:2).

call: Chief officer of the tribe of Simeon
introduce: Shephatiah is a figure who appears in the Old Testament book of 1 Chronicles, the chief officer who ruled over the tribe of Simeon in the reign of King David.
lifetime: As the son of Maacah, he is recorded as the chief officer of the Simeonites among those who were in charge of the tribes of Israel in the time of King David (1 Chronicles 27:16).
event: As the chief officer of the Simeonites, he was one of those in charge of the tribes of Israel (1 Chronicles 27:16). The specific duties of that office and the circumstances of his appointment are not recorded in the text.

introduce: One of the sons of Jehoshaphat, the fourth king of the kingdom of southern Judah, a figure who appears in the royal genealogy.
lifetime: As a son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, he is recorded as a son of Jehoshaphat together with Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, and Michael, the brothers of Jehoram (2 Chronicles 21:2).
event: Jehoshaphat gave generous gifts of silver, gold, and valuable things, and fortified cities in Judah, to his sons, such as Shephatiah, the brothers of Jehoram, but gave the kingdom to Jehoram the firstborn (2 Chronicles 21:2-3).

call: Ancestor of a family that returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Shephatiah is a figure whose family name is entered in the list of the people who were released from the Babylonian captivity and returned to Jerusalem and Judah with Zerubbabel and others; his descendants numbered three hundred seventy-two (Ezra 2:4).
lifetime: In the list of the people who were released from the Babylonian captivity and returned to Jerusalem and Judah, three hundred seventy-two descendants of Shephatiah are recorded (Ezra 2:1-4), and in the list recorded by Nehemiah too, three hundred seventy-two descendants of Shephatiah are likewise recorded (Nehemiah 7:9).
event: No personal deeds of Shephatiah are recorded in the Bible, and his name appears in the list of the returned people of Israel under the family name "the descendants of Shephatiah" (Ezra 2:4, Nehemiah 7:9).

call: Descendants of a servant of Solomon
introduce: Shephatiah is the name of a family recorded as "the descendants of Shephatiah" among the descendants of the servants of Solomon, and this family is entered in the list of the people who returned from the Babylonian captivity.
lifetime: The descendants of Shephatiah are recorded in the list of the descendants of the servants of Solomon (Ezra 2:55, 57), and in the list recorded by Nehemiah too the same family appears among the descendants of the servants of Solomon (Nehemiah 7:57, 59).
event: No personal deeds of Shephatiah are recorded in the Bible, and his name appears as a family name among the descendants of the servants of Solomon in the list of the returned people (Ezra 2:55, 57, Nehemiah 7:57, 59).

call: Ancestor of a family that returned with Ezra
introduce: Shephatiah, the son of Michael, is a figure whose name is entered, "of the descendants of Shephatiah," among the clan heads who came up from Babylon with Ezra in the time of King Artaxerxes (Ezra 8:1, 8).
lifetime: In the list of the clan heads who came up from Babylon with Ezra in the time of King Artaxerxes, Zebadiah the son of Michael is recorded among the descendants of Shephatiah (Ezra 8:1, 8).
event: He was one of the clan heads who came up from Babylon with Ezra, and the men who were with him numbered eighty (Ezra 8:1, 8).

introduce: Shephatiah, of the descendants of Perez of the tribe of Judah, was the son of Mahalalel, and his great-great-grandson Athaiah is recorded as one of the descendants of Judah who lived in Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 11:4).
lifetime: In the genealogy of Nehemiah 11:4, Shephatiah appears as an ancestor of Athaiah; Athaiah was the son of Uzziah, the grandson of Zechariah, the great-grandson of Amariah, the great-great-grandson of Shephatiah, and the fifth-generation descendant of Mahalalel (Nehemiah 11:4).
event: No deeds of Shephatiah himself are recorded in the Bible; his great-great-grandson Athaiah is recorded as one of the descendants of Judah who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:4).

introduce: Shephatiah the son of Mattan was one of the princes of Jerusalem in the time of King Zedekiah at the end of the kingdom of Judah, and one of those who heard what Jeremiah said to the people (Jeremiah 38:1).
lifetime: Shephatiah the son of Mattan, in Jerusalem, which was under threat from the army of the king of Babylon, together with Pashhur and others heard what Jeremiah said to all the people (Jeremiah 38:1), and told the king that Jeremiah must be put to death (Jeremiah 38:4).
event: The princes told King Zedekiah that Jeremiah was not seeking the welfare of the people but their harm, and was weakening the hands of the soldiers who were left in this city and of all the people, and that he should be put to death (Jeremiah 38:4). When King Zedekiah said that Jeremiah was in their hands (Jeremiah 38:5), they threw Jeremiah into the cistern of Malchijah the king's son, which was in the court of the guard (Jeremiah 38:6), but Ebed-melech the Cushite spoke to the king, and Jeremiah was drawn up out of the cistern (Jeremiah 38:7-13).
character: For the sake of his own political standing and the security of the state, he was a man who defined Jeremiah's prophecy of peace as treason and responded harshly (Jeremiah 38:4).

introduce: Zebadiah was a man of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the sons of Beriah, and one of the clan heads who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:15-16, 8:28).
lifetime: In the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, he is recorded as one of the sons of Beriah (Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth, Zebadiah, Arad, Eder, Michael, Ishpah, and Joha) (1 Chronicles 8:14-16), and these clan heads lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).
event: His name is entered among the sons of Beriah in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, and it is recorded that those clan heads lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:15-16, 8:28).

introduce: Zebadiah is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as one of the sons of Elpaal (1 Chronicles 8:17-18).
lifetime: Zebadiah, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, is recorded as a son of Elpaal together with Meshullam, Hizki, Heber, Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab (1 Chronicles 8:17-18), and these clan heads lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).

introduce: Zebadiah was a man of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the mighty men who came to David and joined him when David was staying at Ziklag to escape from Saul (1 Chronicles 12:1-7).
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Jeroham of Gedor, and belonged to David's military organization made up of descendants of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 12:7). He is included in the list of the Benjamites who joined at the time when Saul's kinsmen were going over to David (1 Chronicles 12:2).
event: His name is entered among those who came to David and helped him in battle when David was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul the son of Kish (1 Chronicles 12:1-2, 12:7). They were kinsmen of Saul of the tribe of Benjamin, who were armed with bows and used both the right and the left hand to sling stones and shoot arrows (1 Chronicles 12:2).

introduce: Zebadiah was the third son of Meshelemiah the son of Kore, a Korahite of the descendants of Asaph, and a Levite who belonged to the divisions of temple gatekeepers established in the time of King David (1 Chronicles 26:1-2).
lifetime: He was the third son of Meshelemiah the son of Kore (1 Chronicles 26:1-2), and his family belonged to the divisions of the gatekeepers and served in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:12, 26:19).
event: The offices of the gatekeepers were assigned by casting lots, by families, for each gate, small and great alike (1 Chronicles 26:13), but the gate that Zebadiah himself was assigned is not recorded in the text.

introduce: Zebadiah is a figure who appears in the Old Testament book of 1 Chronicles, a son of Asahel, who was the brother of Joab and one of the commanders of David's army.
lifetime: As a son of Asahel, his name is entered in the military organization of the reign of King David (1 Chronicles 27:7).
event: In the army that David organized, he was given the task of commanding twenty-four thousand soldiers as the division commander for the fourth month (1 Chronicles 27:7).

call: A Levite in the time of Jehoshaphat
introduce: One of the Levites active in the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah, who carried out the duty of teaching the law.
lifetime: In the third year of King Jehoshaphat's reign, when the king sent his officials to the cities of Judah to teach (2 Chronicles 17:7), he sent Levites and priests with them, and Zebadiah is recorded as one of those Levites (2 Chronicles 17:8).
event: At the command of King Jehoshaphat, together with Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah, he went around the cities of Judah and taught the people the book of the law of the LORD (2 Chronicles 17:7, 17:9).

introduce: Zebadiah was an elder of the tribe of Judah active in the time of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, the son of Ishmael, who in the course of reorganizing Judah's judicial system took the role of overseeing all the affairs belonging to the king.
lifetime: When Jehoshaphat king of Judah appointed judges in every city of the land and also appointed men in Jerusalem to judge (2 Chronicles 19:5, 8), he had all the affairs belonging to the king overseen by Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the elder of the tribe of Judah (2 Chronicles 19:11).
event: King Jehoshaphat arranged that all the affairs belonging to the LORD be overseen by Amariah the chief priest, and all the affairs belonging to the king by Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the elder of the tribe of Judah (2 Chronicles 19:11).

introduce: Zepho is a descendant of Esau, the ancestor of Edom, recorded as one of the five sons of Eliphaz, Esau's son (Genesis 36:11, 1 Chronicles 1:36).
lifetime: Esau fathered Eliphaz through Adah (Genesis 36:4), and the sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz (Genesis 36:11). In the same list in 1 Chronicles 1:36, the name is written differently in the Korean text, with Sebi in place of Sebo. Timna, the concubine of Eliphaz, bore Amalek to Eliphaz (Genesis 36:12).

introduce: Sheva is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the house of Caleb of the tribe of Judah, recorded as the father of Machbenah and Gibea.
lifetime: Sheva is one of the sons born to Maacah, the concubine of Caleb (1 Chronicles 2:48-49).

introduce: Shelomith is a Levite who appears in 1 Chronicles 26, the man who was in charge of the treasuries of the holy things of the house of God in the reign of King David. He is a descendant of Eliezer the son of Moses, and is recorded as the son of Zichri.
lifetime: Shelomith is recorded as the son of Zichri in the genealogy that runs from Eliezer through Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, and Zichri (1 Chronicles 26:25). He and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the holy things dedicated by King David, the heads of families, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the army commanders (1 Chronicles 26:26).
event: Shelomith and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the holy things (1 Chronicles 26:26), which had been dedicated from the plunder won in battles for the repair of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:27). The holy things dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah were also under the care of Shelomith and his brothers (1 Chronicles 26:28).
character: According to the biblical record, Shelomith was recognized as a legitimate direct descendant in the line of Moses, and he held an administrative position trusted enough that the valuable sacred objects dedicated to the temple by the royal household and the army commanders were entrusted to him (1 Chronicles 26:25-28).

introduce: Shelomith is a descendant of the tribe of Judah, a daughter of Zerubbabel, a figure of the period of the return from the Babylonian exile. She is a woman whose existence is confirmed through the genealogy of the house of David recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:19.
lifetime: She is mentioned as a daughter of Zerubbabel, together with his sons Meshullam and Hananiah (1 Chronicles 3:19). Specifics of her life, such as her birthplace, the time of her death, or whether she married, are not recorded in the Bible.
event: No specific achievements or special events of hers appear in the biblical record; she is identified only as a person included in the list of Zerubbabel's children who carries on the genealogy (1 Chronicles 3:19).

call: Clan head of the house of Ladan
introduce: Shelomoth is a figure among the sons of Shimei, one of the families of the Gershonites of the tribe of Levi (1 Chronicles 23:9). His name is mentioned in the course of the reorganization of the Levites in the time of King David.
lifetime: Shelomoth was one of the three sons of Shimei (Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran) among the Gershonites Ladan and Shimei, and is recorded as one of the clan heads of Ladan (1 Chronicles 23:7, 9). When David numbered the Levites who were thirty years old and upward and divided them into divisions, his name was recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Levi (1 Chronicles 23:3, 6, 9).
event: David divided the Levites into divisions according to their clans (1 Chronicles 23:6), and at that time Shelomoth was included in that genealogy as a son of Shimei and one of the clan heads of Ladan (1 Chronicles 23:9). No specific event or achievement that he personally carried out is recorded in the text of the Bible (1 Chronicles 23:9).

introduce: Shelomith is a figure recorded as one of the children born to Rehoboam king of Judah and Maacah the daughter of Absalom (2 Chronicles 11:20).
lifetime: Rehoboam married Maacah the daughter of Absalom, and Maacah bore Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith (2 Chronicles 11:20).

call: Son of Josiphiah (one who returned with Ezra)
introduce: Shelomith is a figure recorded as the son of Josiphiah, of the descendants of Shelomith, among the clan heads who finished the Babylonian captivity and went up from Babylon to Jerusalem with Ezra (Ezra 8:1, 10).
lifetime: In the seventh year of King Artaxerxes, when some of the people of Israel went up to Jerusalem (Ezra 7:7), he was one of the clan heads who went up from Babylon with Ezra (Ezra 8:1). In the list he is recorded as the son of Josiphiah, of the descendants of Shelomith (Ezra 8:10).
event: Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, of the descendants of Shelomith, joined the company of Ezra's return with one hundred sixty men who were with him (Ezra 8:10). This is one example showing the movement by family units and the organized composition of the return from the exile (Ezra 8:1, 10).

introduce: Zichri is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as one of the sons of Shimei (1 Chronicles 8:19-21).
lifetime: Zichri is recorded among the sons of Shimei, together with Jakim, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath (1 Chronicles 8:19-21). The biblical text leaves no separate record of the specifics of his life after his name appears (1 Chronicles 8:19).

introduce: Zichri is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the sons of Shashak (1 Chronicles 8:22-25).
lifetime: Zichri is recorded as one of the sons of Shashak of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:23, 25). The Bible does not mention his birth or death or the specific period of his activity.

introduce: Zichri is a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, a son of Jeroham (1 Chronicles 8:27). He is recorded as one of the chiefs of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).
lifetime: Zichri is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the clan heads of the tribe of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:27). He was a son of Jeroham, and his name is entered among the chiefs who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).
event: He is included in the list of the chiefs of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem and forms part of the genealogy (1 Chronicles 8:27). There is no record of any other historical event or specific achievement (1 Chronicles 8:28).

introduce: Zichri is a descendant of Asaph of the tribe of Levi, recorded as the grandfather of Mattaniah, who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the exile (1 Chronicles 9:15).
lifetime: Zichri is recorded as a descendant of Asaph, the father of Mica and the grandfather of Mattaniah (1 Chronicles 9:15). Nehemiah 11:17 gives the same genealogy as Mattaniah the son of Mica, the grandson of Zabdi. The Bible does not separately record Zichri's own deeds.
event: Zichri's grandson Mattaniah, a Levite who lived in Jerusalem, became the elder who led the words of thanksgiving at prayer (Nehemiah 11:17). What Zichri himself did is not recorded in the text (1 Chronicles 9:15).

call: Son of Joram (ancestor of the keeper of the temple treasuries)
introduce: Zichri is a figure who appears in the Old Testament book of 1 Chronicles, the son of Joram, a descendant of Eliezer the son of Moses, and of the house of the Levites. He is recorded as the father of Shelomoth, who held the office of managing the treasuries of the temple.
lifetime: Zichri is the son of Joram, who was born of Eliezer (1 Chronicles 26:25). No detailed record of his life has been handed down, and being mentioned in the biblical genealogy as a descendant of the Levites is all there is.
event: Shelomoth, the son of Zichri, and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the holy things (1 Chronicles 26:26). Shelomoth and his brothers managed the holy things dedicated by King David, the heads of families, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and all the army commanders, and those holy things were for the repair of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:26-28).

call: Father of Eliezer (father of the chief officer of Reuben)
introduce: Zichri is a figure mentioned in the Old Testament book of 1 Chronicles, recorded as the father of Eliezer, the chief officer of the Reubenites (1 Chronicles 27:16).
lifetime: Zichri is recorded as the father of Eliezer, who was the chief officer of the Reubenites in the list of those in charge of the tribes of Israel (1 Chronicles 27:16). The text does not separately record Zichri's own life.
event: No specific achievements or particular events of Zichri himself are recorded in the Bible. It is recorded only that his son Eliezer was the chief officer of the Reubenites (1 Chronicles 27:16).

introduce: Zichri is a figure recorded as the father of Amasiah, who commanded two hundred thousand mighty men of valor in the time of Jehoshaphat king of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:16).
lifetime: The Bible does not record Zichri's own deeds, but records that his son Amasiah, in the time of King Jehoshaphat, willingly offered himself to the LORD and commanded two hundred thousand mighty men of valor (2 Chronicles 17:16).
event: Zichri's son Amasiah, who willingly offered himself to the LORD, commanded two hundred thousand mighty men of valor (2 Chronicles 17:16). What Zichri himself did is not recorded in the text.

introduce: Zichri is a figure recorded as the father of Elishaphat, the commander of hundreds who made a covenant with Jehoiada the priest (2 Chronicles 23:1).
lifetime: The Bible does not record Zichri's own deeds. In the seventh year, when Jehoiada the priest made a covenant with the commanders of hundreds, his son Elishaphat appears as one of those commanders (2 Chronicles 23:1).
event: His son Elishaphat was one of the commanders of hundreds who made a covenant with Jehoiada, together with Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, and Maaseiah son of Adaiah (2 Chronicles 23:1). What Zichri himself did is not recorded in the text.

introduce: Zichri is a figure recorded as a mighty man of Ephraim in the time of Ahaz king of Judah, who killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the governor of the palace, and Elkanah the second to the king (2 Chronicles 28:7).
lifetime: He is recorded as a mighty man of Ephraim during the reign of Ahaz king of Judah (2 Chronicles 28:1) (2 Chronicles 28:7). At the same time Pekah the son of Remaliah killed 120,000 valiant men of Judah in one day (2 Chronicles 28:6).
event: Zichri, the mighty man of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the governor of the palace, and Elkanah the second to the king (2 Chronicles 28:7). The killing of 120,000 valiant men of Judah in one day is recorded not as the deed of Zichri but as that of Pekah the son of Remaliah (2 Chronicles 28:6).
character: The Bible calls him a mighty man of Ephraim, which indicates that he played a leading role in the military action (2 Chronicles 28:7).

introduce: Zichri is a figure recorded as the father of Joel, the overseer of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the exile (Nehemiah 11:7-9).
lifetime: Zichri's name appears in Nehemiah 11:9 as the father of his son Joel. The Bible does not separately record Zichri's own life (Nehemiah 11:9).
event: Zichri's son Joel became the overseer of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:7-9). Zichri's own deeds are not recorded in the text.

call: Priest of the house of Abijah
introduce: Zichri is recorded as the representative of the house of Abijah in the list of priestly heads in the time of Joiakim after the return from the exile (Nehemiah 12:12, 17).
lifetime: In the days of Joiakim, Zichri is recorded as the representative of the house of Abijah among those who were heads of the priests (Nehemiah 12:12, 17). The Bible does not separately record Zichri's own deeds.
event: In the days of Joiakim, his name was recorded as the representative of the house of Abijah in the list of priestly heads (Nehemiah 12:12, 17). The text does not record any specific thing he did.

call: Last king of Judah, the twentieth
introduce: Zedekiah was the twentieth and last king of the kingdom of southern Judah, and his given name was Mattaniah. He was set on the throne by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he reigned during the period when the dynasty came to an end with the fall of Jerusalem.
lifetime: After Jehoiachin was taken to Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made Jehoiachin's uncle Mattaniah king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:17). He became king at the age of twenty-one and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem (2 Kings 24:18). In the ninth year of his reign the Babylonian army besieged Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:1), and in the eleventh year the wall was breached and the city fell (2 Kings 25:2-4). He fled and was pursued into the plains of Jericho; he was brought to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where his sons were killed before his eyes, and then his two eyes were put out, and he was bound in chains and taken to Babylon (2 Kings 25:5-7).
event: The most conspicuous event of his reign was the rebellion against Babylon. Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon (2 Kings 24:20) and sent envoys to Egypt to obtain horses and an army (Ezekiel 17:15). As a result, Nebuchadnezzar's invasion led to the burning of the house of the LORD and the king's palace (2 Kings 25:9). He summoned the prophet Jeremiah to the palace and questioned him secretly (Jeremiah 37:17), and had him brought to the third entrance of the house of the LORD and questioned him again (Jeremiah 38:14).
character: Zedekiah did evil in the sight of the LORD and followed all that Jehoiakim had done (2 Kings 24:19). He shows an indecisive character swayed by the officials around him; he permitted Jeremiah to be thrown into the cistern and then sent men to rescue him, showing himself wavering (Jeremiah 38:5-10). Although he listened to Jeremiah's prophecy, he feared the king of Babylon and consulted him in secret in the inner court of the palace; he is portrayed as a timid and fearful person (Jeremiah 38:16-19).

기타관계: Jucal#2785(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

introduce: Zedekiah was one of the princes who sat in the chamber of the scribe in the king's house in Jerusalem in the time of Jehoiakim king of Judah, the son of Hananiah (Jeremiah 36:12).
lifetime: In the fifth year of Jehoiakim king of Judah, after Baruch the scribe read in the house of the LORD the book in which the words of Jeremiah were written (Jeremiah 36:9-10), he appears as one of the princes who were sitting in the chamber of the scribe in the king's house (Jeremiah 36:12).
event: When Micaiah reported to the princes all the words he had heard from Baruch's reading (Jeremiah 36:11-13), all the princes, including Zedekiah, sent Jehudi to summon Baruch (Jeremiah 36:14) and had him read the scroll (Jeremiah 36:15); hearing all the words, they were alarmed and looked at one another, and said that they would tell the king all these words (Jeremiah 36:16). This is recorded as something all the princes did together, and no deed of Zedekiah individually is recorded.

call: King of northern Israel (assassin of Elah)
introduce: Zimri was the fifth king of the northern kingdom of Israel, who assassinated King Elah and seized the throne, but whose reign lasted only seven days.
lifetime: Zimri was an officer who commanded half of the chariots of Elah the son of Baasha, king of northern Israel (1 Kings 16:9). While King Elah was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, the steward of his household, Zimri conspired against the king, went in, struck him down and killed him, and became king in his place (1 Kings 16:9-10). Afterward Zimri killed the entire house of Baasha (1 Kings 16:11-12), and the people in the camp who were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines, heard that Zimri had conspired and killed the king, and on that day made Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel (1 Kings 16:15-16). When Omri went up with all Israel and besieged Tirzah (1 Kings 16:17), Zimri saw that the city was captured, went into the citadel of the royal palace, burned the palace down over himself, and died in it (1 Kings 16:18).
event: When Zimri became king, he killed the entire house of Baasha and did not leave a single male, whether relative or friend (1 Kings 16:11-12). He was king in Tirzah for seven days (1 Kings 16:15), and when he was besieged by Omri he set fire to the royal palace and died in it (1 Kings 16:18).
character: Zimri showed the traits of a traitor who assassinated Elah, who had been his lord (1 Kings 16:9), and immediately after seizing power he revealed a violent and cruel disposition by eliminating his political enemies at once (1 Kings 16:11). Faced with a threat from outside, rather than overcoming the situation he met an extreme end, choosing to set fire to the palace and take his own life (1 Kings 16:18).

call: Descendant of the house of Saul
introduce: Zimri was a man of the tribe of Benjamin who appears in the genealogy of the house of Saul. He is the son of Jehoaddah, a descendant of King Saul, and is recorded as a descendant of Merib-baal.
lifetime: Zimri belongs to a lower generation of the family tree that begins with Jonathan the son of Saul. Jonathan's son was Merib-baal, Merib-baal fathered Micah, and Micah fathered Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz. Later Ahaz fathered Jehoaddah, and Jehoaddah was the father of Zimri (1 Chronicles 8:33-36). In the same genealogy, the son of Ahaz is recorded as Jarah in 1 Chronicles 9:42 (1 Chronicles 9:42).

introduce: Zimri is the name of a people (nation) referred to in the book of Jeremiah as "all the kings of Zimri", recorded as one of the nations that would drink the cup of the wrath of the LORD (Jeremiah 25:15, 25:25).
lifetime: Zimri is not an individual but the name of a people (nation) listed as those whose kings must drink the cup of the wrath of the LORD (Jeremiah 25:15-26). This word came to Jeremiah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, that is, the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon (Jeremiah 25:1).
event: Among the words Jeremiah received, all the kings of Zimri are recorded as those who would drink the cup of wrath, together with all the kings of Elam and all the kings of Media (Jeremiah 25:25). There is no other record of Zimri in the Bible.

introduce: Shimri is a figure whose name appears as an ancestor in 1 Chronicles 4:37 in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon. This verse records Ziza as "the fifth-generation descendant of Shemaiah and the great-great-grandson of Shimri" (1 Chronicles 4:37).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 4:37 records that Ziza was the son of Shiphi, the grandson of Allon, the great-grandson of Jedaiah, the great-great-grandson of Shimri, and the fifth-generation descendant of Shemaiah, and so introduces Shimri as an ancestor of Ziza. Shimri's own deeds are not recorded (1 Chronicles 4:37).
event: No deeds of Shimri himself are recorded in the Bible. The attack, in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, on the Meunites at the border of Gedor on the east side of the valley, whom they destroyed utterly (1 Chronicles 4:39-41), was the deed of the chiefs whose names were recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:34-37, and Shimri appears among them only as an earlier ancestor of Ziza.

introduce: Shimri is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 11:45 only as "Jediael the son of Shimri", recorded as the father of Jediael, who is entered in the list of David's mighty men, and of his brother Joha the Tizite (1 Chronicles 11:45).
lifetime: Shimri's own deeds are not recorded in the Bible. His son Jediael and his brother Joha the Tizite were entered in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:45).
event: No events of Shimri himself are recorded in the Bible; only the fact that his sons Jediael and Joha were entered in the list of David's mighty men is handed down in 1 Chronicles 11:45.

introduce: A man of the descendants of Merari of the tribe of Levi, a son of Hosah, who belonged to the divisions of gatekeepers in the time of David. He was the chief son of Hosah, though he was not the firstborn by birth, and his father made him the chief (1 Chronicles 26:10).
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Hosah, of the descendants of Merari, among the divisions of the gatekeepers of the descendants of Levi in the time of David (1 Chronicles 26:1, 26:10). Although he was not the firstborn, his father made him the chief; the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen in all, and all of them were heads of the gatekeepers serving in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:10-12).
event: Shimri was not the firstborn, but his father Hosah made him the chief (1 Chronicles 26:10). The gatekeepers were assigned to guard each gate by casting lots by clans, small and great alike (1 Chronicles 26:13), but the gate assigned to Shimri is not recorded in the text.
character: The Bible says nothing about his personal character or specific traits. Only information on his family lineage and his rank in his duties is recorded (1 Chronicles 26:10-11).

introduce: Shimri was one of the Levites who led the cleansing of the temple and the restoration of worship in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah, a man of the descendants of Elizaphan (2 Chronicles 29:13).
lifetime: When Hezekiah king of Judah commanded the Levites to consecrate themselves and to consecrate the house of the LORD (2 Chronicles 29:4-5), he was recorded among the Levites who arose, as one of the descendants of Elizaphan (2 Chronicles 29:12-13). His name was entered as a descendant of Elizaphan together with Jeiel (2 Chronicles 29:13).
event: At the command of King Hezekiah, when the Levites gathered their brothers, consecrated themselves, and cleansed the house of the LORD, Shimri too was recorded as one of the Levites who arose, and the Levites carried all the uncleanness found in the temple out to the brook Kidron (2 Chronicles 29:12-16).

introduce: Shimea is a figure belonging to the descendants of Merari of the tribe of Levi, recorded as the son of Uzza and the father of Haggiah (1 Chronicles 6:29-30).
lifetime: In the genealogy that runs from Mahli, born of Merari, through Libni, Shimei, and Uzza, Shimea is the son of Uzza and the father of Haggiah (1 Chronicles 6:29-30). He is classed as belonging to the house of Merari the son of Levi (1 Chronicles 6:16, 6:29).

introduce: Shimea is a figure belonging to the descendants of Gershon of the tribe of Levi, the grandfather of Asaph, who was in charge of singing praise in the time of King David. Asaph was the son of Berechiah, and Berechiah was the son of Shimea (1 Chronicles 6:39).
lifetime: Shimea appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Gershon of the tribe of Levi, and is recorded as the son of Michael, the father of Berechiah, and the grandfather of Asaph (1 Chronicles 6:39-40).
event: No direct record of his activity appears, but he is mentioned as a figure in the line of Asaph, among those whom David put in charge of singing in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 6:31, 6:39-40).

introduce: Shimeathites is the name of the clan of Shimeath, one of the clans of scribes who lived at Jabez, recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:55.
lifetime: Among the clans of scribes who lived at Jabez were the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites, who are recorded as the Kenite clans that came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab (1 Chronicles 2:55).
event: They are classed as members of a family or group that carried out the office of scribe centered on the place called Jabez, and as descendants of the Kenites they share a blood lineage with Hammath, the ancestor of the house of Rechab (1 Chronicles 2:55).

call: The tribe of Simeon and its inheritance
introduce: Simeon means the second son of Jacob and the ancestor of the tribe of Simeon, one of the twelve tribes of Israel; the Simeon mentioned in Joshua 19 refers to the party to whom this tribe's inheritance was allotted after the conquest of Canaan (Joshua 19:1).
lifetime: Because the inheritance of the descendants of Judah was too large, the tribe of Simeon received its inheritance within the inheritance of the descendants of Judah (Joshua 19:9). By lot this tribe was allotted its inheritance second (Joshua 19:1), and came to possess towns, including Beersheba or Sheba, and Moladah, together with their villages (Joshua 19:2-8).
event: By being allotted towns located within the territory of the tribe of Judah, the tribe of Simeon settled in a geographically close relationship with the tribe of Judah (Joshua 19:9). The towns allotted to them were thirteen towns, and four towns, Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan, together with their villages (Joshua 19:6-8).

call: The righteous man who praised the infant Jesus
introduce: Simeon is a figure who appears in the Gospel of Luke in the New Testament, who lived in Jerusalem and was waiting for the consolation of Israel. He is recorded as the man who, following the leading of the Holy Spirit, met the infant Jesus, recognized him as the Lord's Christ, and blessed him.
lifetime: Nothing is recorded in the Bible about the early life of Simeon. He lived in Jerusalem, and he had received a revelation from the Holy Spirit that he would not die before he had seen the Lord's Christ (Luke 2:25-26). Afterward, moved by the Spirit, he went into the temple, and at the scene where the parents brought in the infant Jesus for the rite of purification, he took him in his arms and praised God (Luke 2:27-28).
event: The most important deed of Simeon is the event of meeting the infant Jesus in the temple. Holding the child in his arms, he praised God and declared that his eyes had seen the Lord's salvation (Luke 2:28-30). He also prophesied to the child's parents, Joseph and Mary, that because of the child many in Israel would fall and rise, and that he would be a sign that is opposed (Luke 2:34). To Mary in particular he added the prophecy that a sword would pierce her own soul (Luke 2:35).
character: The Bible describes Simeon as righteous and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel (Luke 2:25). The Holy Spirit was upon him (Luke 2:25), and he appears as a person of spiritual sensitivity who, moved by the Spirit, went into the temple (Luke 2:27).

introduce: Simeon is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the lineage of Jesus Christ, one of the persons in the line that continues from Nathan the son of David (Luke 3:30).
lifetime: In the genealogy of Luke 3, Simeon is recorded as the son of Judah and the father of Levi (Luke 3:29-30). As a physical ancestor of Jesus, he belongs to the family line of Nathan (Luke 3:31).

introduce: Shimeon is one of the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian captivity in the time of Ezra, belonging to the descendants of Harim. He is a figure whose name was recorded in a list in the religious circumstances of that day, when men had taken foreign women as wives.
lifetime: In the time of Ezra, he was entered as one of the descendants of Harim in the list drawn up by investigating those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:16-17, 10:31, 10:44). Nothing else is recorded about his life.
event: After Ezra the priest pointed out the sin of taking foreign women as wives and urged them to separate from the foreign women (Ezra 10:10-11), the matter of those who had taken foreign women was investigated, and Shimeon was recorded in the list as one of the descendants of Harim who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:16-17, 10:31, 10:44).

call: Son of Gera (the one who cursed David)
introduce: A Benjamite who carried on the bloodline of the house of Saul, the son of Gera of the tribe of Benjamin, and was active in the time of the Davidic dynasty.
lifetime: When David left Jerusalem because of the rebellion of his son Absalom and came to Bahurim, he cursed David and threw stones at him (2 Samuel 16:5-6). When David returned to Jerusalem, he begged David's forgiveness at the Jordan, and David swore that he would not put him to death (2 Samuel 19:16-23). In accordance with David's last charge, Solomon had Shimei live in Jerusalem and commanded him not to leave, but when he went to Gath to look for his servants, he was executed by Solomon's order (1 Kings 2:8-9, 2:36-46).
event: As David fled, he followed him and poured out curses, accusing him of being a man who had destroyed the house of Saul (2 Samuel 16:7-8). When David returned, he met David at the Jordan with a thousand men of Benjamin and acknowledged his wrongdoing (2 Samuel 19:17-20). Although Solomon had set the condition that he not leave Jerusalem, he went to Gath to look for his servants, and for that reason he was executed by Benaiah (1 Kings 2:42-46).
character: He showed an opportunistic side, abruptly changing his attitude according to circumstances for the sake of his own power or survival (2 Samuel 16:5, 19:20). When David was in danger of collapse he showed the boldness to pour out curses, but as soon as David regained power he immediately prostrated himself and begged forgiveness, a survival-centered behavior (2 Samuel 16:13, 19:18). By ignoring Solomon's warning and leaving Jerusalem, he showed himself careless and irresponsible about a promise concerning his own safety (1 Kings 2:40).

introduce: Shimei is a figure whose name is recorded among those who did not side with Adonijah in 1 Kings 1:8 (1 Kings 1:8).
lifetime: When Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying that he would be king, and conspired with Joab and Abiathar the priest and gained their help (1 Kings 1:5, 1:7), Shimei is recorded, together with Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Rei, and David's mighty men, as one who did not side with Adonijah (1 Kings 1:8). This verse does not record his father or his origin.
event: When Adonijah tried to make himself king, Shimei was recorded as one of those who did not take his side (1 Kings 1:5, 1:8).
character: He showed an opportunistic side, abruptly changing his attitude according to the state of power he held (2 Samuel 16:5, 19:18). When David was in distress he did not hesitate to heap insults on him, but when the kingship became firm he showed a calculating side by being the first to go out to meet him (2 Samuel 16:5, 19:18). Even after receiving Solomon's stern warning, he lacked the ability to restrain his own conduct, to the point of violating the king's command and leaving his place of residence for personal gain (1 Kings 2:36-40).

introduce: Shimei the son of Elah was appointed one of the twelve officers over all Israel during the reign of King Solomon, and was the man responsible for providing food for the royal household in the territory of the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: He served as one of the twelve officers whom King Solomon appointed over all Israel (1 Kings 4:7). As the officer over Benjamin, he carried out the duty of providing food for the king and the royal household, each for one month in the year (1 Kings 4:7, 4:18).
event: As one of the twelve officers Solomon appointed, he took charge of Benjamin and provided food for the king and the royal household one month in the year (1 Kings 4:7, 4:18). He is a different person with the same name from Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite who cursed David.

introduce: A figure mentioned as a brother of Zerubbabel in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah recorded in 1 Chronicles 3. He is classed as a member of the royal family that carries on the genealogy of the house of David.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Pedaiah, of the line of David (1 Chronicles 3:19). He is explicitly named as one of the brothers of Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3:19).
event: In the biblical record there is no detailed account of any specific achievement or public event that he himself carried out (1 Chronicles 3:19).
character: The text of the Bible gives no information on his personal character or outward features (-).

introduce: The Shimei who appears in 1 Chronicles 4:26-27 is a figure included in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon. He is recorded as the son of Zaccur, the son of Hammuel, the son of Mishma.
lifetime: Shimei is the son of Zaccur, Zaccur is the son of Hammuel, and Hammuel is the son of Mishma (1 Chronicles 4:26). This genealogy runs from Shaul the son of Simeon through Shallum and Mibsam to Mishma (1 Chronicles 4:24-26). Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters (1 Chronicles 4:27).
event: His brothers did not have many children, but Shimei had many, so that he formed a scale that contrasted with the population situation of the tribe of Simeon, whose clans did not multiply like the descendants of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:27).

introduce: The Shimei mentioned in 1 Chronicles 5:4 is a figure belonging to the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben, recorded as the son of Gog, a descendant of Shemaiah the son of Joel.
lifetime: Shimei is one of the figures who make up the genealogy of the descendants of Reuben, the son of Gog, and the father of Micah (1 Chronicles 5:4-5). Gog is the son of Shemaiah the son of Joel (1 Chronicles 5:4).

introduce: The Shimei mentioned in 1 Chronicles 6:29 is a descendant of the tribe of Levi, a figure belonging to the genealogy of the descendants of Merari (1 Chronicles 6:29).
lifetime: Shimei is a descendant of Mahli, born of Merari the son of Levi, and is the son of Libni and the father of Uzza (1 Chronicles 6:16, 6:29). He is recorded as a person who carries on the family genealogy of the descendants of Merari (1 Chronicles 6:29).

introduce: The Shimei recorded in 1 Chronicles 6 belongs to the genealogy of the descendants of Gershon of the tribe of Levi; he is the son of Jahath the son of Gershon, and the father of Zimmah (1 Chronicles 6:42-43).
lifetime: Shimei is a member of the line that begins from Levi, the ancestor in the genealogy of the house of Gershon, and passes through Gershon and Jahath (1 Chronicles 6:16, 6:43). His son is Zimmah, and Zimmah is recorded as the father of Ethan (1 Chronicles 6:42). He is recorded as a person who carries on the bloodline of the descendants of Gershon in the genealogy of the tribe of Levi.

introduce: Shimei was a Levite of the descendants of Gershon, recorded with Ladan as a descendant of Gershon, and is the father of Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran (1 Chronicles 23:7-9).
lifetime: Shimei is listed in the genealogy of the Levites with Ladan as a descendant of Gershon (1 Chronicles 23:7). His sons are the three, Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran, and the text records that these were the heads of the house of Ladan (1 Chronicles 23:9).
event: As a descendant of Gershon, his sons Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran were recorded as heads of families (1 Chronicles 23:9). This is a line distinguished from the heads Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel, the sons of Ladan (1 Chronicles 23:8-9).

introduce: The Shimei who appears in the record of Chronicles is a Levite, a member of the group of musicians organized for temple worship and praise in the time of King David. He is classed as one of the descendants of Jeduthun or of his house, and was a singer who carried out a particular duty in the service of the temple.
lifetime: Among the divisions of duty of those whom David, together with the commanders of the army, set apart for service from the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, the tenth was Shimei (1 Chronicles 25:1, 25:17). He, together with his sons and brothers, numbered twelve (1 Chronicles 25:17).
event: In the time of David, those set apart as singers obtained their offices by casting lots alike, whether great or small, teacher or pupil (1 Chronicles 25:8), and Shimei was chosen for the tenth division (1 Chronicles 25:17). They served by singing in the house of the LORD God (1 Chronicles 25:6).
character: Shimei was regarded by David as a man who had received a prophetic gift, and he had musical expertise in praising with instruments (1 Chronicles 25:3). As of the house of Jeduthun, he lived a life centered on duty, thoroughly set apart for the service of the temple (1 Chronicles 25:1).

introduce: Shimei the Ramathite was the one in charge of the vineyards among those who were in charge of King David's property during his reign (1 Chronicles 27:27, 27:31).
lifetime: King David appointed several stewards to manage his possessions, and among them Shimei was chosen as the steward responsible for the vineyards (1 Chronicles 27:27).
event: Shimei was the steward in charge of the vineyards among those in charge of King David's property. The wine vats that stored the produce of the vineyards were under Zabdi the Shiphmite (1 Chronicles 27:27).
character: The Bible says nothing specific about his personal character or traits (-)

introduce: Shimei was a Levite who took part in the cleansing of the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah, one of the descendants of Heman (2 Chronicles 29:14).
lifetime: Shimei was a descendant of Heman, and was mobilized as a member of the tribe of Levi when King Hezekiah cleansed and restored the temple for the spiritual renewal of Israel (2 Chronicles 29:14).
event: When Hezekiah king of Judah gave the command to cleanse the temple, Shimei took part in the work of cleansing the temple together with the descendants of Jeduthun (2 Chronicles 29:14).

introduce: A Levite appointed in the time of King Hezekiah to manage the temple offerings, tithes, and dedicated things.
lifetime: In the reign of King Hezekiah, in the work of taking charge of the contributions, tithes, and dedicated things brought into the temple, as a Levite he held the position next after his brother Conaniah (2 Chronicles 31:12). The text records him as the brother of Conaniah the Levite, and says that Conaniah was the chief officer in the matter and Shimei was second (2 Chronicles 31:12).
event: When King Hezekiah promoted the cleansing of the temple and the restoration of worship, he carried out the duty of faithfully managing the contributions, tithes, and holy things that the people brought. Together with Conaniah, he was responsible for Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah being overseers under their charge, which was what King Hezekiah and Azariah, the ruler of the house of God, commanded (2 Chronicles 31:13).
character: He was trusted by King Hezekiah and Azariah, and showed systematic administrative ability in carrying out public work in cooperation with fellow Levites (2 Chronicles 31:12-13).

introduce: Shimei is a Levite recorded in the list of those among the descendants of the captives who had taken foreign women as wives in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:16-17, Ezra 10:23). The Bible records nothing of his lineage or specific ministry.
lifetime: He is recorded as a Levite among those who had taken foreign women as wives in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:23). He was included in that list when Ezra investigated the matter of marriage with foreign women (Ezra 10:16-17, Ezra 10:23).
event: In the record of the investigation of those who had taken foreign women, his name was entered together with the Levites Jozabad, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer (Ezra 10:23). When Ezra said that they should put away the foreign women (Ezra 10:10-11), he had the priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear to do as this word said (Ezra 10:5).
character: As a member of the tribe of Levi, he belonged to a family that carried out duties related to the service of the temple (Ezra 10:23). Through his marriage with a foreigner he is a figure who shows one aspect of the process of religious and social assimilation that the Levites of that time were undergoing (Ezra 10:23).

introduce: He is a figure belonging to the descendants of Hashum among the people of Israel who returned to Jerusalem after ending their captivity in Babylon in the time of Ezra.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the descendants of Hashum who had taken foreign women as wives in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:33).
event: When Ezra dealt with the problem of intermarriage with foreigners, his name is recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives, as a descendant of Hashum (Ezra 10:33). Earlier, the people had made a covenant with God and sworn to send away the foreign women and their children (Ezra 10:3, Ezra 10:5).

introduce: He is one of the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian captivity in the time of Ezra, belonging to the family of the descendants of Bani (Binnui).
lifetime: In the time of Ezra, his name is recorded as one of the descendants of Bani among those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:34, Ezra 10:38).
event: He was included in the list when Ezra investigated those among the people of Israel who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:38). Earlier, the people had made a covenant with God and sworn to send away the foreign women and their children (Ezra 10:3, Ezra 10:5).

introduce: A descendant of Benjamin, the son of Kish and the grandfather of Mordecai (Esther 2:5).
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Kish and the grandfather of Mordecai (Esther 2:5). The one recorded in the text as having been carried away together when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took Jeconiah king of Judah and the people captive from Jerusalem is Mordecai (Esther 2:6); there is no record about Shimei himself.
event: No deeds of Shimei himself are recorded in the Bible; he is mentioned only as the father of Jair and the grandfather of Mordecai in Mordecai's genealogy (Esther 2:5).

introduce: Ziza is a son of Rehoboam king of Judah, a figure born through Maacah, Rehoboam's wife (2 Chronicles 11:20).
lifetime: Ziza is recorded as one of the sons borne by Maacah the daughter of Absalom, the wife of Rehoboam (2 Chronicles 11:20).

call: Father of Adina (father of a chief of Reuben)
introduce: Shiza is a figure who appears in the Old Testament book of 1 Chronicles, recorded as the father of Adina, a chief of the tribe of Reuben.
lifetime: Shiza came from a family of the descendants of Reuben, and his son Adina was a chief of the Reubenites and served as one of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:42).
event: No historical event or specific achievement that Shiza himself carried out appears in the biblical record (1 Chronicles 11:42).

introduce: Shisha is a figure known as the father of Elihoreph and Ahijah, who were in charge of records and administrative affairs in the time of King Solomon. In the biblical record he appears as the one who forms the family background of his sons, who carried out the office of scribe.
lifetime: Shisha is the father of Elihoreph and Ahijah, high officials of Solomon's time (1 Kings 4:3).

call: Ancestor of Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: A figure who appears in the genealogy of the Nethinim, recorded as the ancestor of one of those who returned to Jerusalem in the return from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: He is mentioned as an ancestor in the list of the Nethinim who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel from the Babylonian captivity (Ezra 2:53). His name is likewise confirmed in the list of the returnees from Babylon recorded by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 7:55).
event: His family was recorded in the list of the Nethinim as the descendants of Sisera (Ezra 2:43, Ezra 2:53, Nehemiah 7:55). The Nethinim are those whom David and the officials set apart to minister to the Levites (Ezra 8:20).

call: Chief of thousands of Manasseh (one who defected at Ziklag)
introduce: Zillethai is one of the chiefs of thousands who came over from the tribe of Manasseh to David when David went to Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:20).
lifetime: He is a chief of thousands of Manasseh, recorded together with Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, and Elihu, who came over to David from the tribe of Manasseh when David went to Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:20). This company helped David against the band of raiders, and all of them were mighty men of valor and became commanders in the army (1 Chronicles 12:21).
event: As one of the chiefs of thousands who came over to him from the tribe of Manasseh when David went to Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:20), he helped David against the band of raiders together with this company (1 Chronicles 12:21).
character: He is a man who recognized David's military capacity, left Saul's camp, and swore loyalty to David; as a military head of the tribe of Manasseh, he is regarded as a warrior of outstanding martial strength (1 Chronicles 12:20-21).

introduce: A descendant of Gershon of the Levites, the son of Shimei and the father of Ethan, recorded in the genealogy of Asaph (1 Chronicles 6:42-43).
lifetime: He is the son of Shimei (1 Chronicles 6:42); Shimei is the son of Jahath, and Jahath is the son of Gershon (1 Chronicles 6:43). His family line belongs to the genealogy of the ancestors of the house of Asaph, who were in charge of praise in the temple in the time of David (1 Chronicles 6:39-43).
event: His name is included in the genealogy of the ancestors of those who carried out the duty when David appointed Levites to the duty of singing in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 6:31-42).

call: Father of Joah (father of a Levite in Hezekiah's time)
introduce: Zimmah is a man of the tribe of Levi who appears in the record of Chronicles, the father of Joah the Gershonite (2 Chronicles 29:12). The Bible does not record Zimmah's own deeds.
lifetime: Zimmah is recorded as the father of Joah the Gershonite, and in the time of King Hezekiah his son Joah was among the Levites who arose to cleanse the temple (2 Chronicles 29:12).
event: When Hezekiah king of Judah gathered the priests and Levites in order to cleanse the temple (2 Chronicles 29:4-5), Zimmah's son Joah was also among the Levites who arose; these Levites gathered their brothers and consecrated themselves, and then cleansed the house of the LORD as the king had commanded (2 Chronicles 29:12, 2 Chronicles 29:15).

introduce: Ziph is a figure belonging to the family line of the tribe of Judah, recorded as a son of Jehallelel. His name is mentioned within the genealogical system of the tribe of Judah, and specific description of a historical reality is extremely limited.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Jehallelel in the genealogy of the descendants of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:16). The Bible says nothing about his birthplace, the time of his death, or the range of his activity in life.
event: No specific historical event or achievement that a person called Ziph led or took part in is recorded in the biblical text (1 Chronicles 4:16).

call: Father of Shecaniah, the father-in-law of Tobiah
introduce: Arah is a figure of the time of Nehemiah, recorded as the father of Shecaniah, the father-in-law of Tobiah (Nehemiah 6:18).
lifetime: Shecaniah the son of Arah is the father-in-law of Tobiah (Nehemiah 6:18). The Bible has no record of Arah's own tribe or life.
event: His son Shecaniah entered into a relationship of in-laws with Tobiah, and as a result there occurred the incident in which many nobles of Judah allied themselves with Tobiah, spoke in his favor, or reported Nehemiah's doings to Tobiah (Nehemiah 6:17-19).

call: Disciple in Damascus (the one who laid hands on Paul)
introduce: Ananias is a figure who appears in the book of Acts in the New Testament, a disciple who lived in Damascus. After Saul met Jesus on the way to Damascus, he is recorded as the man who, at the Lord's direction, went to Saul and laid his hands on him (Acts 9:10-17).
lifetime: He was a disciple living in Damascus, and when Saul had come to Damascus and could not see, he received a command in a vision from the Lord to go to Saul (Acts 9:8-11). As the Lord directed, he went to the street called Straight, found Saul in the house of Judas, and laid his hands on him (Acts 9:11-17). Afterward something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, he regained his sight, and he was baptized (Acts 9:18).
event: Directed by the Lord in a vision, he went to Saul and laid his hands on him, telling him that Jesus had sent him so that Saul might regain his sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit (Acts 9:17). According to Paul's testimony, Ananias was a devout man according to the law, well spoken of by all the Jews who lived there (Acts 22:12).
character: At first he voiced concern at the Lord's command, citing that Saul was one who persecuted the saints, but then he showed himself obeying at once (Acts 9:13-17). He was known among the Jews as a man who kept the law well and had a good reputation (Acts 22:12).

introduce: Ananias is a figure recorded as high priest in the book of Acts, who appears when Paul made his defense before the Sanhedrin and when he was accused before the governor (Acts 23:2, Acts 24:1).
lifetime: Acts records him as high priest. When Paul stood before the Sanhedrin, he commanded those standing beside Paul to strike him on the mouth (Acts 23:2), and five days later he came down with some elders and an orator, Tertullus, and accused Paul before the governor (Acts 24:1). His family line and term of office are not recorded in the Bible.
event: When Paul made his defense before the Sanhedrin, he commanded those standing beside him to strike Paul on the mouth, and for this he was rebuked by Paul as a whitewashed wall (Acts 23:2-3). Afterward he came down with the elders and the orator Tertullus and accused Paul before the governor, and Tertullus charged Paul with being a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes and one who tried to desecrate the temple (Acts 24:1-6).
character: Ananias commanded those standing beside Paul to strike him on the mouth. Paul pointed out that, although Ananias claimed to judge according to the law, he was breaking the law by having him struck (Acts 23:2-3).

introduce: Anathoth is a figure recorded as one of the sons of Becher the son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:6, 1 Chronicles 7:8).
lifetime: In the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, he is recorded as a son of Becher the son of Benjamin, and his brothers were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, and Alemeth (1 Chronicles 7:6, 1 Chronicles 7:8). All of these were said to be heads of their fathers' houses and mighty men of valor (1 Chronicles 7:9).
event: The sons of Becher were all heads of their fathers' houses and mighty men of valor, and when their descendants were counted by genealogy they numbered twenty thousand two hundred (1 Chronicles 7:9).

call: Leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Anathoth is one of the heads of the people who, in the time of Nehemiah, swore to observe the law of God and sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:14, Nehemiah 10:19).
lifetime: His name is recorded in the list of the heads of the people who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14, Nehemiah 10:19).
