This covenant contained the pledges to separate from the foreign peoples, to observe the law of God, not to give their daughters and sons in marriage to the peoples of the land, and not to buy goods on the Sabbath or on holy days (Nehemiah 10:28-31).
event: His name is recorded in the list of those who sealed, among the heads of the people (Nehemiah 10:14, Nehemiah 10:19). No other deeds of his are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: A descendant of Gershon of the Levites, recorded as a son of Ethan (1 Chronicles 6:42-43).
lifetime: Adaiah is the son of Ethan; Ethan is the son of Zimmah, Zimmah is the son of Shimei, Shimei is the son of Jahath, and Jahath is the son of Gershon (1 Chronicles 6:42-43).

introduce: Adaiah is a figure of the tribe of Benjamin who appears in 1 Chronicles 8, a son of Shimei (1 Chronicles 8:21).
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Shimei in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, and the heads of this genealogy lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:21, 1 Chronicles 8:28).

call: Son of Jeroham (head of the priests)
introduce: Adaiah is a figure recorded in the book of 1 Chronicles, the son of Jeroham and one of the priests. He belonged to the group of priests who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: Adaiah is the son of Jeroham, the grandson of Pashhur, and the great-grandson of Malchijah (1 Chronicles 9:12). In Nehemiah 11:12 the same name is recorded as the son of Jeroham, but there he is recorded differently: as the grandson of Pelaliah, the great-grandson of Amzi, the great-great-grandson of Zechariah, the fifth-generation descendant of Pashhur, and the sixth-generation descendant of Malchijah (Nehemiah 11:12). He is recorded as one of the priests who lived in Jerusalem after he had been taken captive to Babylon and returned (1 Chronicles 9:1-3, 9:10-12).
event: He is recorded as one of the priests who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:10-12). In the same passage it says that his brothers, heads of their fathers' houses, who were able men for the work of the service of the house of God, numbered one thousand seven hundred sixty in all (1 Chronicles 9:13), and Nehemiah 11:12 records that his brothers who did the work in the temple numbered eight hundred twenty-two in all. Adaiah's own specific deeds are not recorded in the text.
character: The Bible describes him as a mighty man of valor, a term that carries the meaning of a capable worker who carries out service in the temple of God (1 Chronicles 9:13).

introduce: Adaiah is the father of Maaseiah, who is recorded in 2 Chronicles 23:1 as "Maaseiah the son of Adaiah" (2 Chronicles 23:1).
lifetime: The Bible has no record of Adaiah's own life, and his son Maaseiah is recorded as one of the commanders of hundreds who made a covenant with Jehoiada in the seventh year (2 Chronicles 23:1).
event: His son Maaseiah was one of the five commanders of hundreds with whom Jehoiada made a covenant (2 Chronicles 23:1). Adaiah's own deeds are not recorded in the text.

introduce: The Adaiah who appears in Ezra 10 is a figure classed as a descendant of Bani among the Jews who returned from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 10:29).
lifetime: He is one of the descendants of Bani (Ezra 10:29). In the time of Ezra, his name was entered in the list drawn up by investigating those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:29, 10:44).
event: When Ezra urged the returnees from the exile to separate from their foreign wives, he was mentioned as one who was included in the list of those who had wives (Ezra 10:29).

introduce: A figure whose name is recorded in the list of those who were to send away their foreign women for the purity of the community of Israel after the return from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 10:39).
lifetime: One of the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian exile, he is included in the list of the pledge of divorce from foreign women led by Ezra (Ezra 10:39).
event: In the course of the religious reform led by Ezra, it was found that he had taken a foreign woman as wife, and so his name came to be entered in that list (Ezra 10:39).

introduce: Adaiah is a figure recorded in the genealogy of Maaseiah in Nehemiah 11:5, the son of Joiarib and the father of Hazaiah (Nehemiah 11:5).
lifetime: In the genealogy of Nehemiah 11:5, Adaiah is the son of Joiarib, the grandson of Zechariah, and the father of Hazaiah, recorded as an ancestor of Maaseiah (Nehemiah 11:5). The Bible has no record of Adaiah's own birth or death.
event: No deeds of Adaiah himself are recorded in the Bible, and in Nehemiah 11:5 his name appears as an ancestor of Maaseiah, who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:5).

introduce: Athaiah is a figure of the descendants of Perez of the tribe of Judah who settled in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 11:4).
lifetime:
He was born as the fifth-generation descendant of Mahalalel of the tribe of Judah, the grandson of Zechariah, and the son of Uzziah (Nehemiah 11:4).
As a descendant of Perez, his name was recorded among the descendants of Judah who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:3-4).
The Bible has no record of any specific time of his birth or of his death (Nehemiah 11:4).
event: He was recorded as a descendant of Perez in the list of the descendants of Judah who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:3-4). No specific deeds of his are recorded in the Bible.

call: King of Persia (recipient of the letter of accusation in Ezra 4:7)
introduce: The Artaxerxes mentioned as king of Persia in Ezra 4 is the one who received the letter sent up by Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeal, and their associates, and by Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe, and who issued the decree to stop the building of the city of Jerusalem (Ezra 4:7-8, 4:21). The text arranges the account of this king between Ahasuerus (Ezra 4:6) and the second year of Darius (Ezra 4:24), and does not record which king he is the same as.
lifetime: At the beginning of the reign of Ahasuerus king of Persia, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem (Ezra 4:6), and in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeal, and the rest of their associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia (Ezra 4:7). Afterward Artaxerxes issued a decree to stop the building of the city of Jerusalem (Ezra 4:21), and Rehum and Shimshai, who received that decree, stopped the work by force and power, so that the work on the house of God ceased until the second year of Darius king of Persia (Ezra 4:23-24).
event: When the letter sent up by Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and others accused Jerusalem of being a rebellious city and said that, if its walls were finished, they would not pay tribute, custom, or toll, and the kings would suffer loss (Ezra 4:12-13), Artaxerxes had a search made, and said that this city had from of old made insurrection against kings and that rebellion and sedition had been fostered in it (Ezra 4:19), and he commanded that those men be made to cease, that the city not be built, and that they wait until a decree was issued again (Ezra 4:21). When a copy of his decree was read before Rehum, Shimshai, and their associates, they went in haste to Jerusalem and by force and power made the Jews cease (Ezra 4:23).
character: He showed the aspect of a firm and resolute ruler who put forward the authority of the central government in order to remove elements of unrest in the provinces (Ezra 4:21). He had a bureaucratic tendency to trust the reports and accusations of outsiders and swiftly issue administrative orders (Ezra 4:17-18), and he maintained the realistic ruling stance of giving first consideration to the security of the empire and the securing of taxes (Ezra 4:13).

introduce: The Athaliah mentioned in 1 Chronicles 8:26 is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of those listed as sons of Jeroham in 1 Chronicles 8:27 (1 Chronicles 8:26-27).
lifetime: Athaliah is a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin and one of the sons of Jeroham, and belongs to the family line of those who were heads of fathers' houses, chiefs throughout their generations, and who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:27-28).

introduce: A Levite active in the reign of Jehoshaphat, the fourth king of the kingdom of southern Judah, who, at the king's command, was sent out to go around the cities of all Judah and teach the people the book of the law of the LORD.
lifetime: In the third year of King Jehoshaphat's reign, he was one of the Levites sent to the cities of Judah together with the princes Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah (2 Chronicles 17:7-8). He was sent along with the priests Elishama and Jehoram (2 Chronicles 17:8).
event: As one of the Levites whom King Jehoshaphat sent, he took part in going around all the cities of Judah with the book of the law of the LORD and teaching the people (2 Chronicles 17:8-9).

call: Leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Adonijah is a figure recorded as one of the heads of the people who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14-16). Though the name is the same, he is a different person from Adonijah the son of David.
lifetime: When the community that had returned from the Babylonian exile made a covenant to keep and do the law of God, Adonijah's name is recorded as one of the heads of the people (Nehemiah 10:14-16, 10:29).
event: He is recorded as one of those who, together with the heads of the people, sealed the covenant, binding themselves with a curse and an oath to walk in God's law given through Moses the servant of God and to keep and do it (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:14-16, 10:29).
character: His name is recorded among the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:16). His personal character and appearance are not described in the text.

introduce: Adnah is a figure who appears in the Chronicles of the Old Testament, recorded as one of the supreme commanders who led the army in the time of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.
lifetime: Adnah served as a military commander of Judah in the time of King Jehoshaphat, and had under him three hundred thousand mighty men of valor (2 Chronicles 17:14).
event: In the organization of King Jehoshaphat's army, he was the chief of the commanders of thousands belonging to Judah and led three hundred thousand mighty men of valor (2 Chronicles 17:14).
character: The Bible calls him a mighty man of valor, and records that the army he commanded was likewise composed of mighty men of valor (2 Chronicles 17:14).

call: Priest of the house of Harim
introduce: Adna is a figure who appears in the book of Nehemiah in the Old Testament, recorded as Adna of the house of Harim, a head of the priests in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:15).
lifetime: He belonged to the house of Harim, one of the priestly families (Nehemiah 12:15). Among those who were heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim, Adna is recorded for the house of Harim (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:15).
event: In the listing of the heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim, his name is recorded as head of the house of Harim (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:15).

introduce: Athlai is a figure recorded in the book of Ezra, one of the people of Israel recorded as having taken a foreign woman as wife after the return from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 10:28).
lifetime: He is recorded as a member of the descendants of Bebai who returned from the Babylonian exile, and in the investigation into separation from foreign wives led by Ezra his name was entered in the list (Ezra 10:28).
event: When Ezra investigated in Jerusalem those who had married foreign women and decided to send them away, Athlai was included in that list of the investigation as a descendant of Bebai who had a foreign wife (Ezra 10:28).

call: Father of Maasai (father of a priest of the house of Immer)
introduce: Adiel is a figure recorded as the father of Maasai, a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile, and he is the son of Jahzerah (1 Chronicles 9:12).
lifetime: Adiel is the son of Jahzerah and the father of Maasai. Maasai is recorded as the son of Adiel, the grandson of Jahzerah, the great-grandson of Meshullam, the great-great-grandson of Meshillemith, and the fifth-generation descendant of Immer (1 Chronicles 9:12).
event: The Bible does not record Adiel's own deeds. His son Maasai is recorded in the list of the priests who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:10-12).

call: Father of Azmaveth (father of the keeper of the royal treasuries)
introduce: Adiel is a figure recorded as the father of Azmaveth, who was over the king's treasuries in the time of King David (1 Chronicles 27:25).
lifetime: Adiel had a son, Azmaveth, who is recorded as the one over the king's treasuries (1 Chronicles 27:25). There is no record of Adiel himself in the text.
event: Adiel's name is mentioned because his son Azmaveth is recorded as having been over the king's treasuries (1 Chronicles 27:25). Adiel's own deeds are not recorded in the text.

call: Ancestor of a returning house in Ezra's time (father of Ebed)
introduce: Adin is one of the ancestors of the Jewish families that returned from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem, a figure who appears in the lists of the books of Ezra and Nehemiah.
lifetime: Four hundred fifty-four of the descendants of Adin returned with Zerubbabel from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem and Judah (Ezra 2:15). In the list of the heads of families who went up from Babylon with Ezra, Ebed the son of Jonathan, from the descendants of Adin, is recorded together with fifty men who were with him (Ezra 8:1, 8:6).
event: In the list of the heads who went up with Ezra, Ebed the son of Jonathan is recorded among the descendants of Adin, and the men with him numbered fifty (Ezra 8:6).

call: Leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Adin is one of the Jewish leaders who returned from the Babylonian exile, a figure who took part in the renewal and sealing of the covenant led by Nehemiah.
lifetime: Four hundred fifty-four of the descendants of Adin are recorded in the list of the people who returned from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:15), and afterward he appears as one of the leaders who sealed when Nehemiah and the people swore to keep the law of God and signed (Nehemiah 10:16).
event: He is recorded as one of those who, together with the chiefs of the people in the time of Nehemiah, put their seal to the covenant in which they swore with a curse to keep and do the law of God (Nehemiah 10:14-16, 10:29).

call: Ancestor of a family that returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Arah refers to a person, or the ancestor of a house, who returned to Jerusalem and Judah with Zerubbabel according to the decree of Cyrus king of Persia after the Babylonian exile. As a name recorded in the lists of the return in Ezra and Nehemiah, it was used not only for a particular individual but as a collective name for the house that took him as its founder.
lifetime: Seven hundred seventy-five of the descendants of Arah, who had lived in Babylon, returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:5). Afterward six hundred fifty-two of the descendants of Arah were also included in the list of the return recorded in connection with Nehemiah (Nehemiah 7:10).
event: The descendants of Arah are recorded in the list of the returnees who came back with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:5) and in the list of the return in Nehemiah 7:10.

introduce: Aram is the son of Kemuel, whom Nahor, the brother of Abraham, and Milcah bore. As the grandson of Nahor, he is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the house of Abraham.
lifetime: He was born to Kemuel the son of Nahor (Genesis 22:21). The Bible does not deal specifically with his deeds after his birth or with any record after his death.

call: Son of Shomer of the tribe of Asher
introduce: Aram is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher, the son of Shomer (1 Chronicles 7:34). Shomer is the son of Heber, Heber is the son of Beriah, and Beriah is the son of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:30-32).
lifetime: He was born as a son of Shomer, and his brothers were Ahi, Rohgah, and Hubbah (1 Chronicles 7:34).

introduce: Ard is a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, a figure recorded as the ancestor of the house of Ard, one of the families of Bela the son of Benjamin (Numbers 26:40).
lifetime: Ard was born as a son of Bela (Numbers 26:40).
event: When the people of Israel were counted in the census on the plains of Moab, he was included in the list as a member of the house of Ard, belonging to the family of Bela of the tribe of Benjamin (Numbers 26:40).

call: Two warriors of Moab (killed by Benaiah)
introduce: Ariel is a figure who appears in 2 Samuel 23:20 and 1 Chronicles 11:22 in the expression "the two sons of Ariel of Moab." The text records his name only as the father of the two men struck down by Benaiah, David's mighty man, and does not record Ariel's own deeds.
lifetime: The Bible has no record of Ariel's own life. It is recorded that Benaiah the son of Jehoiada struck down the two sons of Ariel of Moab (2 Samuel 23:20, 1 Chronicles 11:22).
event: His two sons were struck down by Benaiah, David's mighty man (2 Samuel 23:20, 1 Chronicles 11:22).
character: In the biblical record he is portrayed as a powerful warrior representing Moab. Since striking them down is regarded as a great feat of valor in the account of Benaiah's exploits, it can be seen that he was a man of very outstanding martial strength in his time (2 Samuel 23:20).

call: Captain of the guard of King Nebuchadnezzar
introduce: Arioch was the captain of the guard of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, a figure who carried out the king's commands. In the biblical record he appears mainly as a helper or executor in the key events connected with Daniel.
lifetime: He was captain of the guard when King Nebuchadnezzar gave the command to destroy all the wise men of Babylon (Daniel 2:12, 2:14). In accordance with the king's command he went out to slay the wise men of Babylon (Daniel 2:14), and when Daniel said not to destroy the wise men but to bring him in before the king, he brought Daniel in before the king in haste and reported to him (Daniel 2:24-25).
event: When the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans could not make known the king's dream, the king became angry and commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be destroyed (Daniel 2:2, 2:10-12), and Arioch received that command and went out to slay the wise men (Daniel 2:14). When Daniel asked Arioch, the king's captain, why the king's decree was so urgent, Arioch made the matter known to Daniel (Daniel 2:15), and afterward when Daniel came and asked to be brought in before the king, he brought him in before the king in haste and said that he had found a man among the exiles of Judah (Daniel 2:24-25).
character: Arioch had the temperament of a cool and upright soldier who carried out the command of the king, his superior, without delay (Daniel 2:14). Also, judging from the fact that he understood Daniel's urgent situation and brought him to the king at once, he had the administrative side of one who judges situations quickly and knows how to be flexible (Daniel 2:25).

introduce: Amariah is a descendant of the tribe of Levi, a figure in the line of Aaron the high priest, and one person in the priestly genealogy connected with the house of Zadok.
lifetime: Amariah is recorded as the son of Azariah and the father of Ahitub (1 Chronicles 6:11). His son Ahitub fathered Zadok (1 Chronicles 6:12). This Amariah belongs to the priestly genealogy of 1 Chronicles 6 that runs down through the descendants of Aaron (1 Chronicles 6:3-12).

introduce: Amariah is a figure recorded as a descendant of Kohath of the tribe of Levi and a son of Hebron. In the genealogy of the Bible he appears as the second of the sons of Hebron (1 Chronicles 23:19).
lifetime: In the time of King David, when the duties of the descendants of Levi were divided, he was mentioned as one of the sons of Hebron (1 Chronicles 23:19). He belongs to the genealogy of the descendants of Kohath, and when David organized the Levites, he was included in the list as one of the members of the family (1 Chronicles 24:23).
event: When David, grown old, made Solomon king over Israel and then numbered the Levites and divided them into their divisions, the sons of Hebron were recorded as a clan of the descendants of Kohath, and the descendants of Levi took the office of assisting the descendants of Aaron and serving in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 23:1-6, 23:12, 23:19, 23:24-28). Apart from this, no individual achievement or particular event of Amariah himself is described in the Bible.

call: High priest in the time of Jehoshaphat
introduce: A high priest in the time of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, the man appointed to preside over all matters of the LORD in the system of justice that Jehoshaphat set up in Jerusalem.
lifetime: When Jehoshaphat appointed Levites, priests, and heads of the families of Israel in Jerusalem to give judgment (2 Chronicles 19:8), it was determined that Amariah the chief priest would preside over all matters of the LORD (2 Chronicles 19:11).
event: Jehoshaphat commanded those who gave judgment that Amariah the chief priest would preside in all matters of the LORD, that Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, would preside in all matters of the king, and that the Levites would be officials before them (2 Chronicles 19:9-11).
character: He was a man who received from King Jehoshaphat the final authority over all matters of the LORD, and in the running of the state he was recognized at once for religious expertise and administrative trustworthiness (2 Chronicles 19:11).

call: Levite who distributed the temple offerings
introduce: The Amariah recorded in 2 Chronicles 31:15 is a Levite who was entrusted with managing and distributing the offerings of the temple in the time of King Hezekiah's religious reform.
lifetime: In the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, he held his office in the cities of the priests under Kore the Levite, the keeper of the east gate (2 Chronicles 31:14-15).
event: Under Kore, who was over the offerings, tithes, and most holy things brought to the temple in the time of Hezekiah, he was in the cities of the priests together with Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, and Shecaniah, and held the office of distributing to their brothers by divisions, to great and small alike (2 Chronicles 31:12-15).

introduce: A figure belonging to the descendants of Bani, recorded in the time of Ezra as one of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:42, 10:44).
lifetime: As a member of the community that returned after the Babylonian exile, he is mentioned in the course of Ezra's reform (Ezra 10:42).
event: When Ezra sought to forbid and set right marriage to foreign women, his name was included in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:42).

introduce: He is one of the priests who, in the time of Nehemiah, took part in the sealing in Jerusalem, pledging to observe the law of God.
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, he is recorded as one of the priests who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:3, 10:8). The same name also appears in the list of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1-2).
event: At the covenant ceremony led by Nehemiah, his name was entered among those who sealed, as one of the priests (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:3, 10:8). In the listing of those who were heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim, "the house of Amariah" appears, and its head is Jehohanan (Nehemiah 12:12-13).

introduce: Amariah is a descendant of Perez of the tribe of Judah, a figure who in the genealogy of Nehemiah 11:4 appears as the great-grandfather of Athaiah, a descendant of Perez who lived in Jerusalem, and in the generation of a son of Shephatiah.
lifetime: Nehemiah 11:4 calls Athaiah, a descendant of Perez who lived in Jerusalem, the son of Uzziah, the grandson of Zechariah, the great-grandson of Amariah, and the great-great-grandson of Shephatiah; thus Amariah corresponds to the generation of a son of Shephatiah and a father of Zechariah. Amariah's own residence and deeds are not recorded.
event: No individual event of Amariah is recorded in the Bible. His great-grandson Athaiah is listed as a chief of the descendants of Perez who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:3-4).

introduce: Amariah is a figure recorded as the great-grandfather of the prophet Zephaniah. In the genealogy of Zephaniah 1:1 he is in the generation of a son of Hezekiah and appears as the father of Gedaliah.
lifetime: Zephaniah 1:1 calls Zephaniah the son of Cushi, the grandson of Gedaliah, the great-grandson of Amariah, and the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah, so Amariah appears as the father of Gedaliah and in the generation of a son of Hezekiah (Zephaniah 1:1). Amariah's own deeds are not recorded.

introduce: Amasa is a figure who appears in 2 Chronicles 28:12, a leader of the tribe of Ephraim and a son of Hadlai. He is recorded as one who played the role of a mediator in the situation of conflict between the northern kingdom of Israel and the southern kingdom of Judah.
lifetime: Amasa was active as one of the heads of the sons of Ephraim during the time when King Pekah ruled (2 Chronicles 28:12). Before the army of northern Israel, which had won the war against Ahaz king of Judah and brought back many captives, he supported the warning of the prophet Oded and urged that the treatment of their kinsmen be improved (2 Chronicles 28:12).
event: He opposed the attempt of the army of Israel to make slaves of the captives taken from Judah (2 Chronicles 28:12). Afterward, together with the other heads of Ephraim, he restrained the army and set the captives free, provided them with clothing and food from the spoil, and carried the feeble on donkeys and brought them as far as Jericho (2 Chronicles 28:13-15).
character: He showed a resolute leadership able to criticize, from a religious and ethical standpoint, the conduct of an army intoxicated with its own victory (2 Chronicles 28:12). Also, judging from his providing mercy and protection to those who had been taken captive from another land, he was a man with the influence to lead opinion among his own people and carry out humanitarian measures (2 Chronicles 28:15).

call: Chief of the thirty (joined David at the stronghold)
introduce: Amasai is recorded as "the chief of the Thirty" among the descendants of Benjamin and Judah who came to David at the stronghold, when David was hiding from Saul the son of Kish (1 Chronicles 12:16, 12:18).
lifetime: Among the company of the descendants of Benjamin and Judah who came to David when he reached the stronghold, he was chief of the Thirty, and, moved by the Spirit, he said that they would belong to David (1 Chronicles 12:16, 12:18).
event: When the descendants of Benjamin and Judah came to David at the stronghold, David went out to meet them and asked their purpose (1 Chronicles 12:16-17); the Spirit came upon Amasai, the chief of the Thirty, and Amasai said, "We are yours, O David! We are with you, O son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you." Then David received them and made them commanders of his troops (1 Chronicles 12:18).
character: Through the expression that the Spirit came upon him, he is portrayed as one who recognized David's legitimacy and supported him (1 Chronicles 12:18). Also, although he came from the tribe of Benjamin, he had the resolve to set Saul aside and pledge loyalty to David (1 Chronicles 12:2).

introduce: In the time of Jeroboam II king of northern Israel, he was priest of Bethel; he is the one who accused the prophet Amos to the king of conspiring against the king, and told him not to prophesy at Bethel (Amos 7:10-13).
lifetime: As priest of Bethel, he sent word to Jeroboam king of Israel and accused Amos of conspiring against the king (Amos 7:10). He told Amos to flee to the land of Judah and prophesy there (Amos 7:12), and said that Bethel was the king's sanctuary and the king's house, so he should never again prophesy at Bethel (Amos 7:13).
event: Amaziah reported to the king that Amos was saying, "Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel must go into exile away from his land," and said that the land could not bear all his words (Amos 7:10-11). Amos answered that he was neither a prophet nor the son of a prophet, but a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore figs (Amos 7:14), and by the word of the LORD delivered to Amaziah the sentence that his wife would become a prostitute in the city, his sons and daughters would fall by the sword, and he himself would die in an unclean land (Amos 7:16-17).
character: He showed a political leaning of close alliance with state power, defending the vested interests of the royal house (Amos 7:13). He displayed an aggressive attitude of using religious authority to suppress the activity of a critical prophet and attempting physical expulsion (Amos 7:12-13). Using his position, he showed an administrative side that employed a religious sanctuary as an instrument of state rule (Amos 7:13).

call: Father of Joshah (father of a chief of Simeon)
introduce: A figure recorded as the father of Joshah in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon in 1 Chronicles 4 (1 Chronicles 4:34).
lifetime: In the listing of the chiefs of the tribe of Simeon, the name of his son Joshah appears (1 Chronicles 4:34, 4:38). The Bible has no record concerning Amaziah himself.
event: The Bible records no event of Amaziah himself. However, the chiefs enrolled by name in 1 Chronicles 4:34-37, including his son Joshah, sought pasture for their flocks and came to the border of Gedor, and in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah they destroyed the people there and lived in their place (1 Chronicles 4:38-41).

introduce: Amaziah is a Levite who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, belonging to the descendants of Merari, the son of Hilkiah and the father of Hashabiah (1 Chronicles 6:45).
lifetime: In the genealogy of the ancestors of Ethan, of the descendants of Merari, he appears as the son of Hilkiah and the father of Hashabiah (1 Chronicles 6:44-45). This genealogy is that of Ethan, of the descendants of Merari, among the company that David appointed to be in charge of singing praise in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 6:31, 6:44).
event: The Bible records no event of Amaziah himself. His descendant Ethan, as one of the singers David appointed, carried out his duty on the left hand (1 Chronicles 6:31-32, 6:44).

introduce: The Amalekites were a people who stood in a relationship of hostility with the nation of Israel. In the Bible they appear as the people who fought Israel at Rephidim after Israel came out of Egypt (Exodus 17:8), and in the report of the spies they are recorded as a people living in the land of the Negeb (Numbers 13:29).
lifetime: The Amalekites are recorded as a people living in the land of the Negeb (Numbers 13:29). When Israel came out of Egypt and passed through the wilderness, they fought Israel at Rephidim (Exodus 17:8). Afterward they continued in a hostile relationship with Israel, and Balaam composed an oracle saying that Amalek was first among the nations but that its end would be destruction (Numbers 24:20). Moses told Israel to remember how, on the way out of Egypt, Amalek did not fear God and attacked the weak who lagged behind Israel, and told them to blot out their name from under heaven (Deuteronomy 25:17-19). In the time of Samuel the LORD told Saul to strike Amalek and devote to destruction all that they had, sparing nothing (1 Samuel 15:2-3), but Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep and the oxen (1 Samuel 15:8-9).
event: When Israel came out of Egypt and reached Rephidim, the Amalekites fought against Israel (Exodus 17:8). Balaam composed an oracle saying that Amalek was first among the nations but that its end would be destruction (Numbers 24:20). Moses told the people of Israel to remember how Amalek had attacked the weak who lagged behind the weary Israel, and to blot out their name from under heaven (Deuteronomy 25:17-19). Saul struck Amalek as the LORD had commanded and utterly destroyed the people, but he spared Agag and the best of the sheep and the oxen (1 Samuel 15:3, 15:7-9).

introduce: A figure mentioned in Ezra 10:34, one of the descendants of Bani included in the list of those who had married foreign women after the return from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the descendants of Bani among those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:34, 10:44).
event: When Ezra drew up in Jerusalem the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives, his name was included in that list (Ezra 10:34).

introduce: Amram is the son of Kohath the son of Levi, and the father of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. He is the figure who became the founder of the family of the descendants of Amram within the tribe of Levi (Exodus 6:18, Numbers 26:59).
lifetime: Amram was the son of Kohath, and he took Jochebed as wife and fathered Aaron, Moses, and Miriam (Exodus 6:18, 6:20, Numbers 26:59). His descendants, as the Amramite family, belong to the families of Kohath together with the Izharite family, the Hebronite family, and the Uzzielite family (Numbers 3:27).
event: In the biblical text no independent achievement or particular event of Amram himself is directly recorded. His name is mentioned only in the context of explaining the origin of the family of the descendants of Amram within the genealogical system of the tribe of Levi and in the census records of Numbers (Numbers 3:27, 1 Chronicles 26:23).

introduce: Abigail is a figure recorded as a daughter of Jesse, a daughter of Nahash, and a sister of David. Abigail is in a relationship of sisters with Zeruiah.
lifetime: She is recorded as a sister of the sons of Jesse: Eliab, Abinadab, Shimea, Nethanel, Raddai, Ozem, and David (1 Chronicles 2:13-16). It says that Jether the Ishmaelite was the father of Amasa (1 Chronicles 2:17), and 2 Samuel records that Ithra the Israelite lay with Abigail the daughter of Nahash and she bore Amasa, and that Abigail was the sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother (2 Samuel 17:25).
event: Her son Amasa became the commander of Absalom's army at the time Absalom rebelled against David (2 Samuel 17:25).

introduce: Abinadab is the second of the eight sons of Jesse of Bethlehem, and one of David's brothers. He is a figure mentioned in the biblical record in connection with David's family line.
lifetime: Abinadab is recorded as the second son of Jesse (1 Chronicles 2:13). Jesse's three eldest sons, namely Eliab the firstborn, Abinadab next, and Shammah the third, went to the battle following Saul (1 Samuel 17:13). When Samuel was seeking the one to anoint among the sons of Jesse, Jesse called Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel (1 Samuel 16:8).
event: As one of the three eldest sons, he followed Saul, who was encamped in the valley of Elah in confrontation with the Philistines, and went to the battle (1 Samuel 17:2, 17:13). When Samuel was seeking the one to be anointed among the sons of Jesse, his father Jesse called him and made him pass before Samuel, but the LORD did not choose him (1 Samuel 16:8).

introduce: A son of Saul, the first king of Israel, whose name appears together with Jonathan and Malchishua. He was born into the house of Saul, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:33, 9:39).
lifetime: He is listed as a son of Saul together with Jonathan, Malchishua, and Esh-baal (1 Chronicles 8:33, 9:39). On Mount Gilboa the Philistines pursued Saul and his sons, overtook them, and killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua (1 Samuel 31:1-2, 1 Chronicles 10:2).
event: When the men of Israel fled before the Philistines on Mount Gilboa, the Philistines pursued Saul and his sons and killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua (1 Samuel 31:1-2), and Saul and his three sons died together on that day (1 Samuel 31:6). 1 Chronicles 8:33 and 9:39 once more state that he was a son of Saul (1 Chronicles 8:33, 9:39).

introduce: Abiram is the firstborn son whom Hiel of Bethel lost when he built Jericho and laid its foundation in the time of Ahab king of northern Israel.
lifetime: Abiram is recorded as the firstborn son of Hiel of Bethel (1 Kings 16:34). His father Hiel lost Abiram when he built Jericho and laid its foundation (1 Kings 16:34).
event: The death of Abiram occurred in the course of the fulfillment of the curse that Joshua had pronounced long before against the rebuilding of Jericho (Joshua 6:26). When Hiel laid the foundation of Jericho he lost Abiram his firstborn, and when he set up its gates he lost Segub his youngest son, according to the word of the LORD that He had spoken by Joshua the son of Nun (1 Kings 16:34).

introduce: A son of the judge Gideon, one of the early figures whom the men of Shechem made king. With the support of the men of Shechem he killed his half-brothers and seized power, but he died in a revolt and battle after ruling three years.
lifetime: He was a son born to Gideon's concubine in Shechem (Judges 8:31), and after Gideon died he went to Shechem and spoke to his mother's brothers and the family of his maternal grandfather (Judges 9:1). To win the support of the men of Shechem he made use of his mother's kin, and in the end he hired reckless and worthless men with seventy pieces of silver received from the temple of Baal-berith, and they followed him (Judges 9:1-4). At Ophrah he killed seventy half-brothers on one stone, and only Jotham the youngest survived (Judges 9:5). He was made king by the men of Shechem (Judges 9:6), but afterward he came into conflict with the men of Shechem, who resented his rule (Judges 9:22-23). While attacking the tower of Thebez, he was struck on the head by an upper millstone thrown by a woman and had his skull broken, and in the end he asked his armor-bearer to thrust him through with a sword and so died (Judges 9:50-54).
event: All the men of Shechem and all Beth-millo gathered and made him king by the oak of the pillar at Shechem (Judges 9:6). After Jotham's parable-curse, when the men of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech, he attacked and took the city of Shechem, tore it down, and sowed it with salt (Judges 9:44-45). When the men of the tower of Shechem entered the stronghold of the house of El-berith, he showed a cruel method of suppression, setting that place on fire (Judges 9:46-49).
character: He had a cold and cruel nature, to the point of killing all his own flesh and blood in order to gain power (Judges 9:5). He was strongly politically ambitious and showed cunning in rallying the inhabitants of Shechem (Judges 9:1-3), but he showed an autocratic tendency, not hesitating to use force to protect his own authority (Judges 9:44-49). Even at the moment of death he valued pride and face, asking his armor-bearer to kill him so as not to leave the dishonorable record that he had been killed by a woman (Judges 9:54).

introduce: Ahimelech is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 18:16, recorded as a son of the priest Abiathar. In 2 Samuel 8:17 the same genealogical notation appears under the name Ahimelech (the Korean text writes the name differently in the two passages), and he is a man who became a priest together with Zadok in the time of David.
lifetime: Ahimelech, the son of Abiathar, is recorded as a priest together with Zadok the son of Ahitub in the reign of David (1 Chronicles 18:16). 2 Samuel 8:17 writes him in the same list as "Ahimelech the son of Abiathar" (2 Samuel 8:17), and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar also appears in 1 Chronicles 24:6 (1 Chronicles 24:6).
event: In the kingdom of David he became a priest together with Zadok the son of Ahitub (2 Samuel 8:17, 1 Chronicles 18:16). His name is included in the list in 1 Chronicles 18:16 that explains the system of David's offices.
character: In the biblical record no information about his personal character or specific deeds is given -

call: Eighth division of priests (the division of Zechariah)
introduce: Abijah is the head of the eighth of the twenty-four divisions of priests recorded in 1 Chronicles 24, one of the heads of the divisions organized in the time of David to divide the priestly duties (1 Chronicles 24:3-5, 24:10).
lifetime: When David divided the duties of the priests, the order was determined by casting lots, and the eighth to be drawn was Abijah (1 Chronicles 24:5, 24:10). The name Abijah also appears in the list of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 12:4), and in the list of the heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim it is recorded as "of Abijah, Zichri" (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:17).
event: When the divisions of the priests were divided by lot in the time of David, the eighth to be drawn was Abijah (1 Chronicles 24:10). Afterward, in the days of Herod king of Judea, Zechariah, a priest of the division of Abijah, performed the priestly duty in the order of that division, and when the lot fell to him he entered the temple of the Lord to burn incense (Luke 1:5, 1:8-9).

introduce: Abi is the wife of Ahaz, the twelfth king of the kingdom of Judah, and the mother of Hezekiah, the thirteenth king. In Chronicles she is also recorded as Abijah.
lifetime: As the daughter of Zechariah she married Ahaz king of Judah and bore a son, Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 29:1). In 2 Kings her name is recorded as Abi (2 Kings 18:2).
event: The Bible records no specific deed or event of Abi herself; her name is mentioned only as his mother in the account of the accession of Hezekiah the son of Ahaz (2 Kings 18:1-2; 2 Chronicles 29:1).

introduce: Abijah is one of the priests who sealed the covenant that the people made in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:7-8).
lifetime: Following Nehemiah the governor, the son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah, his name is recorded as a priest in the list of those who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:7-8).
event: As one of those who sealed the covenant together with Nehemiah, he entered his name in the list of priests of which it is written, "These are the priests" (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:7-8). Abijah's own specific deeds are not recorded.

introduce: Abijah is a figure whose name is entered in the list of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1, 12:4). The meaning of the name is "the LORD is my father."
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1, 12:4). In the days of Joiakim, Zichri is recorded as head of "the house of Abijah" (Nehemiah 12:17).
event: In the days of Jeshua, he is recorded as one of the priests and the chiefs of their brothers (Nehemiah 12:4, 12:7). No other specific deeds are recorded.

introduce: The second son of Samuel and younger brother of Joel, he served as a judge at Beersheba.
lifetime: He was born a son of Samuel, and was appointed by his father Samuel as a judge over Israel at Beersheba (1 Samuel 8:2).
event: During his tenure as a judge of Israel he did not follow his father's ways, but turned aside after gain, took bribes, and perverted justice (1 Samuel 8:3). This became the occasion for the elders of Israel to come to Samuel and demand that he appoint a king (1 Samuel 8:4-5).
character: He is portrayed as a corrupt judge who took bribes and abandoned fair judgment (1 Samuel 8:3).

introduce: Abijah is the wife of Hezron. However, the text state of 1 Chronicles 2:24 is uncertain. On the basis of the Septuagint and grammatical difficulties, the ESV, NET, RSV, and others emend the text, and do not take Abijah as a personal name, but understand Ephrathah as the wife of Hezron and the woman who afterward bore Ashhur to Caleb.
lifetime: As the wife of Hezron she bore a son, Ashhur (1 Chronicles 2:24).
event: After Hezron died, Abijah bore to her husband Hezron a son, Ashhur, and Ashhur became the father of Tekoa (1 Chronicles 2:24).

introduce: A descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, a son of Becher, a figure recorded in the genealogy of the house of Benjamin.
lifetime: He is stated in the genealogy of Chronicles as a son born to Becher the son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:8).
character: As a member of a family of the tribe of Benjamin, he is mentioned as one who carries on that line of descent (1 Chronicles 7:8).

call: Man of Anathoth (one of David's Thirty)
introduce: Abiezer is a figure who appears in 2 Samuel in the Old Testament, one of the Thirty, the group of valiant soldiers who served King David. His place of origin is Anathoth, a city of the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: His name is recorded as a man of Anathoth in the list of the mighty men of King David (2 Samuel 23:27; 1 Chronicles 11:28).
event: His name is entered in the lists of David's mighty men in 2 Samuel 23:27 and 1 Chronicles 11:28. In 1 Chronicles 27 it is recorded that, among the divisions that served by turns month by month through the year, the commander of the ninth month, the ninth division, was Abiezer the Anathothite of the descendants of Benjamin, and that his division numbered twenty-four thousand (1 Chronicles 27:12).
character: Apart from his being from Anathoth of the tribe of Benjamin, no specific record of his personal character or physical features appears in the Bible -

introduce: Abihail is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 2:29, a woman recorded as the wife of Abishur in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
lifetime: She married Abishur, a descendant of Judah, and formed a household, and between them she bore sons, Ahban and Molid (1 Chronicles 2:29).
event: By bearing two sons to Abishur, Ahban and Molid, she played the role of carrying on the family tree of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:29).

call: Son of Huri (chief of the tribe of Gad)
introduce: Abihail is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a man of the tribe of Gad who lived in the region of Bashan and Gilead, and a son of Huri. Seven men, beginning with Michael, are recorded as his sons.
lifetime: He is the son of Huri, and corresponds to the grandson of Jaroah, the great-grandson of Gilead, the great-great-grandson of Michael, the fifth-generation descendant of Jeshishai, the sixth-generation descendant of Jahdo, and the seventh-generation descendant of Buz (1 Chronicles 5:14). Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber, seven in all, are his sons and are recorded as brothers of the clan of the tribe of Gad (1 Chronicles 5:13-14).
event: The descendants of Gad lived opposite the Reubenites in the land of Bashan (1 Chronicles 5:11), and the men of the tribe of Gad lived in Gilead in Bashan and in its towns, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon (1 Chronicles 5:16). This genealogy was recorded in the days of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel (1 Chronicles 5:17).

기타관계: Jeshishai#2592(kinsman of the tribe of Gad)

introduce: Abihail is a woman recorded as the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse, and the mother of Mahalath, who became the wife of Rehoboam (2 Chronicles 11:18).
lifetime: She is recorded as the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse, and her child Mahalath, as the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David, became the wife of Rehoboam king of Judah and bore sons, Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham (2 Chronicles 11:18-19).
event: The Bible records no specific deeds of Abihail herself, and only the fact that Mahalath was her offspring is mentioned (2 Chronicles 11:18).

introduce: Abihail is a figure recorded as the father of Esther and the uncle of Mordecai. Esther is called "the daughter of Abihail" (Esther 2:15; 9:29).
lifetime: He is the uncle of Mordecai (Esther 2:15). His daughter Hadassah, that is, Esther, was brought up as his own daughter by her cousin Mordecai after her parents died (Esther 2:7).
event: No specific achievement or individual event of his life itself is recorded in the Bible. Only Esther is called "the daughter of Abihail" (Esther 2:15; 9:29).

introduce: Abiud is a figure recorded as a son of Zerubbabel in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Matthew (Matthew 1:13).
lifetime: As a son of Zerubbabel, in the genealogy of Jesus in Matthew, it is recorded that Zerubbabel was the father of Abiud and Abiud was the father of Eliakim (Matthew 1:13).
event: No specific historical activity or political achievement that he carried out is recorded in the Bible (Matthew 1:13).
character: In the biblical record nothing is mentioned about his personal character or personal traits (-)

introduce: A figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a descendant of Zerah the son of Judah and a son of Ethan.
lifetime: As a figure who carries on the genealogical line of the tribe of Judah, he is recorded as having been born to Ethan, a descendant of Zerah (1 Chronicles 2:8).
event: In the biblical record no specific achievement or event connected with this person is mentioned (1 Chronicles 2:8).

introduce: A figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as a descendant of Jerahmeel the son of Hezron and a son of Jehu.
lifetime: In the genealogy of the house of Hezron, the grandson of Judah, he is mentioned as Azariah the son of Jehu (1 Chronicles 2:38).
event: In the biblical record no specific historical achievement or event that he carried out is described in detail (1 Chronicles 2:38).

introduce: Azariah is a figure recorded in the genealogy as the grandson of Zadok the priest and the son of Ahimaaz. His son is Johanan (1 Chronicles 6:8-9).
lifetime: In the priestly genealogy that runs from Zadok the son of Ahitub to Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, he was born as a son of Ahimaaz and fathered Johanan (1 Chronicles 6:8-9).
event: The Bible records no specific deed or event of this Azariah himself (1 Chronicles 6:9).
character: There is no specific record of his personal character. In the priestly genealogy he appears as the son of Ahimaaz and the father of Johanan (1 Chronicles 6:9).

call: Son of Johanan (high priest of Solomon's temple)
introduce: Azariah is of the priestly house of the tribe of Levi, descended from Aaron, a man who performed the priestly office in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem. He is recorded as the son of Johanan (1 Chronicles 6:10).
lifetime: Azariah was born as a son of Johanan (1 Chronicles 6:10), and is a descendant in the priestly genealogy that runs through Ahitub, Zadok, Ahimaaz, Azariah, and Johanan (1 Chronicles 6:8-10). He performed the priestly office in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 6:10).
event: The Bible states that Azariah served as priest in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 6:10). Beyond that, no record of any specific deeds or particular events appears in the Bible.

call: Son of Hilkiah (father of the high priest Seraiah)
introduce: Azariah is a figure of a priestly family who served in the temple in Jerusalem in the last days of the kingdom of Judah, recorded as the son of the high priest Hilkiah and the father of Seraiah.
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 9:11 identifies him as the son of Hilkiah, the grandson of Meshullam, and the great-grandson of Zadok (1 Chronicles 9:11). 1 Chronicles 6:13-14 records him as the son of Hilkiah and the father of Seraiah (1 Chronicles 6:13-14).
event: He is recorded as the one who was ruler of the house of God (1 Chronicles 9:11).

introduce: A figure who appears in the genealogy recorded in 1 Chronicles 6, a member of the family line that runs to Heman, a descendant of Levi and of Kohath. He is the son of Zephaniah and is mentioned as the father of Joel.
lifetime: As an ancestor of Heman, a descendant of Kohath, he carries on the bloodline of the tribe of Levi (1 Chronicles 6:33, 6:36). He was born as a son of Zephaniah (1 Chronicles 6:36), and fathered Joel and so carried on the line of the family (1 Chronicles 6:36).
character: Listed in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 6, he is recorded as a figure who attests the genealogical legitimacy of Heman, of the priestly line of the tribe of Levi and of the family of singers (1 Chronicles 6:36).

call: Son of Oded (prophet of King Asa's reform)
introduce: Azariah the son of Oded was a prophet active in the time of King Asa of the kingdom of Judah, who, moved by the Spirit of God, spoke the word of God to the king and the people.
lifetime: When King Asa defeated Zerah the Cushite and was returning to Jerusalem, he met him and delivered the word of God (2 Chronicles 15:1). Based on what he prophesied, King Asa was led to carry out a religious reform that removed the idols from all of Judah and Benjamin (2 Chronicles 15:8).
event: He delivered a warning and encouragement that, since God was with Asa, God would be with the king if the king was with God, but if he forsook God, God would forsake him (2 Chronicles 15:2). Referring to the past confusion when Israel had long been without the true God, without a teaching priest, and without the law, he proclaimed the message that if they turned to God in their distress, He would let them find Him (2 Chronicles 15:3-4). Hearing this prophecy, King Asa resolved to remove the abominable idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and to repair the altar of the LORD (2 Chronicles 15:8).
character: Moved by the Spirit of God, he had the boldness to go before the king without fear and speak plainly (2 Chronicles 15:1). He is portrayed as one equipped with prophetic insight, recalling past history and urging a decision in the present (2 Chronicles 15:3-7).

introduce: One of the sons of King Jehoshaphat of Judah, whose name is recorded in 2 Chronicles 21. He is mentioned among the brothers whom Jehoram killed with the sword after Jehoram took the throne and gained strength.
lifetime: He was born as a son of King Jehoshaphat of Judah (2 Chronicles 21:2). Afterward, when Jehoshaphat died and his brother Jehoram took the throne, Jehoram, after he gained strength, killed his brothers with the sword, and Azariah is included among all those brothers (2 Chronicles 21:4).
event: King Jehoshaphat gave his sons, Azariah among them, great gifts of silver, gold, and precious things, together with fortified cities in Judah (2 Chronicles 21:3). But after Jehoram rose to his father's throne and gained strength, he killed all his brothers with the sword (2 Chronicles 21:4).

call: Son of Jeroham (captain of a hundred)
introduce: Azariah was a captain of a hundred who was active in the time of Joash king of Judah, and he was the son of Jeroham (2 Chronicles 23:1).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the captains of hundreds with whom the priest Jehoiada took courage and made a covenant in the seventh year (2 Chronicles 23:1).
event: He is recorded as one of the five captains of hundreds who made a covenant with Jehoiada (2 Chronicles 23:1). Jehoiada then gave the captains the weapons (2 Chronicles 23:9), and Joash was made king (2 Chronicles 23:11). The text does not separately record what role Azariah himself played in this event.

call: Son of Obed (captain of a hundred)
introduce: Azariah was one of the captains of hundreds who made a covenant with the priest Jehoiada in the seventh year, and he was the son of Obed (2 Chronicles 23:1).
lifetime: In the seventh year Jehoiada took courage and made a covenant with the captains of hundreds, including Azariah the son of Obed (2 Chronicles 23:1). They went throughout Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah and the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel, and came to Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 23:2).
event: One of the five captains of hundreds who made a covenant with Jehoiada; afterward Jehoiada gave the captains the weapons (2 Chronicles 23:9) and Joash was made king (2 Chronicles 23:11). The text does not separately record what task Azariah the son of Obed himself carried out in this event.

call: The high priest who confronted King Uzziah
introduce: Azariah was a high priest active in the time of Uzziah in the southern kingdom of Judah, who restrained the king from a religious act within the temple that went beyond the king's authority.
lifetime: Azariah served as high priest in the days of King Uzziah (2 Chronicles 26:20). He went in after King Uzziah, who meant to burn incense in the temple, and stood against the king together with eighty priests, men of valor (2 Chronicles 26:17-18). When leprosy broke out on the king's forehead, he and all the priests hurried the king out of the temple (2 Chronicles 26:20), and Uzziah lived as a leper in a separate house until the day of his death (2 Chronicles 26:21).
event: When King Uzziah entered the temple of the LORD to burn incense, Azariah stopped him, saying that burning incense was not for the king but for the priests, the descendants of Aaron (2 Chronicles 26:17-18). Seeing that leprosy had broken out on the king's forehead, he and all the priests hurried him out of the temple (2 Chronicles 26:20). Uzziah lived as a leper in a separate house until the day of his death, and his son Jotham managed the royal palace (2 Chronicles 26:21).
character: He showed firmness in not backing down even before the king's power in order to defend the authority of the religious law and the priestly office (2 Chronicles 26:17). He had the leadership to rally many priests and respond in an organized way, and when leprosy, a contagious disease, appeared, he showed a cool-headed, procedure-abiding side by taking immediate steps to isolate the king (2 Chronicles 26:18-20).

introduce: A figure who appears in 2 Chronicles 28, a leading chief of the tribe of Ephraim in the time of Pekah of the northern kingdom of Israel, and the son of Johanan.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the heads of the sons of Ephraim who, when Pekah king of Israel attacked the kingdom of Judah and returned to Samaria with many captives, demanded that the captives of Judah be released (2 Chronicles 28:12).
event: When the army of Israel led by King Pekah was about to take the captives seized in Judah as slaves rather than send them back to Jerusalem, he strongly opposed this together with a prophet named Oded (2 Chronicles 28:9-12). Azariah and the other leaders insisted that bringing the people of Judah in as captives was a great sin for Israel and that they must therefore be released (2 Chronicles 28:13). As a result their argument was accepted, and the captured men of Judah were given clothing, sandals, and food, and were brought to Jericho, the city of palm trees, and returned to their brothers (2 Chronicles 28:15).
character: He appears to be a man who valued public justice and national discipline so highly that he directly opposed the victors' plan to enslave prisoners of war (2 Chronicles 28:12). He also held a political standing that, in cooperation with fellow leaders, let him influence the king's decision (2 Chronicles 28:12).

call: Son of Jehallelel (Levite in Hezekiah's time)
introduce: A Levite who appears in 2 Chronicles, one of the Levites who set about cleansing the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah. He belonged to the descendants of Merari and is recorded as the son of Jehallelel (2 Chronicles 29:12).
lifetime: He is one of the Levites who arose when Hezekiah king of Judah commanded the priests and Levites to consecrate the house of the LORD (2 Chronicles 29:4-5, 29:12). He is recorded as the son of Jehallelel among the descendants of Merari (2 Chronicles 29:12), and in this cleansing the Levites carried the unclean things that the priests had brought out of the temple outside to the Kidron Valley (2 Chronicles 29:16).
event: Together with the other Levites who received King Hezekiah's command, he cleansed the inside of the temple (2 Chronicles 29:15). When the priests brought all the unclean things out of the temple into the court, the Levites took them and carried them outside to the Kidron Valley (2 Chronicles 29:16).
character: He is mentioned as a man in a leading position among the Merarites who took part in the work of purifying the temple (2 Chronicles 29:12). He showed a compliant attitude in carrying out the king's command at once (2 Chronicles 29:15).

call: High priest of the house of Zadok (in Hezekiah's time)
introduce: The high priest of the house of Zadok who was active in the time of King Hezekiah of the kingdom of Judah (2 Chronicles 31:10). He is recorded as the one who was ruler over the house of God (2 Chronicles 31:13).
lifetime: As the high priest of the house of Zadok, he answered when Hezekiah questioned the priests and Levites about the heaps of offerings (2 Chronicles 31:9-10). He is recorded as "Azariah, the ruler of the house of God" (2 Chronicles 31:13).
event: When King Hezekiah asked about the heaps of offerings, he answered that since the people began to bring the offerings into the house of the LORD they had eaten and had plenty left over, because the LORD had blessed his people (2 Chronicles 31:10). Afterward, at Hezekiah's command, rooms were prepared in the house (2 Chronicles 31:11), and appointing the overseers of the offerings under Conaniah and Shimei was by the command of King Hezekiah and Azariah, the ruler of the house of God (2 Chronicles 31:12-13).

introduce: Azariah is a figure of the priestly line who appears in the genealogy of Ezra 7, one of the ancestors of Ezra. In the genealogy of Ezra 7:3 he is recorded as the generation after Meraioth and before Amariah.
lifetime: In the genealogy showing that Ezra was the sixteenth-generation descendant of Aaron the chief priest, Azariah is recorded as Ezra's eighth-generation ancestor; the generation above him is Meraioth and the generation below him is Amariah (Ezra 7:3, 7:5).
character: The Bible does not describe any personal character or specific deeds of Azariah; he appears only as a person who continues the hereditary line of the high priestly house (1 Chronicles 6:7, Ezra 7:3).

introduce: Azariah was one of those who took part in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem led by Nehemiah, the son of Maaseiah and the grandson of Ananiah. When the wall was rebuilt, he repaired the section next to his own house (Nehemiah 3:23).
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, he took part in the project of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:23).
event: In the course of repairing the wall of Jerusalem, Azariah son of Maaseiah, the son of Ananiah, repaired the part near his own house (Nehemiah 3:23).

call: Leader of the returnees with Zerubbabel
introduce: Among the people of Israel who were released from the Babylonian exile and returned to Jerusalem and Judah, he is a man who came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and others, and is recorded in the list of returnees in Nehemiah 7 (Nehemiah 7:6-7).
lifetime: Among those released from Babylon who returned to Jerusalem and Judah, he is recorded as one who came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, Baanah, and others (Nehemiah 7:6-7).
event: His name is on the list that records the count of the people of Israel who came with Zerubbabel and the others (Nehemiah 7:7). The Bible has no record of any specific deeds or particular achievements after the return.

introduce: The Azariah who appears in Nehemiah 8:7 is one of the Levites who helped in reading and explaining the law in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: When Ezra read the book of the law to the people in the square before the Water Gate in Jerusalem, he carried out the role of helping the people to understand the law (Nehemiah 8:7).
event: He assisted Ezra's reading of the law and taught the people so that the people of Israel could understand its content as they heard it (Nehemiah 8:7). Also, when the people wept as they heard the words of the law, the Levites who were teaching the people said that this day was holy to God and that they should not mourn or weep, and so quieted all the people (Nehemiah 8:9, 8:11).

introduce: One of the priests who set their seal when a binding covenant was made and written down in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:2, 10:8).
lifetime: In the time of Nehemiah, when the leaders, Levites, and priests of Israel made a binding covenant, wrote it down, and set their seal to it (Nehemiah 9:38), his name was entered on the list of those who sealed it (Nehemiah 10:1-2). He is recorded as a priest together with Maaziah, Bilgai, Shemaiah, and others on this list (Nehemiah 10:8).
event: He was recorded as one of those who set their seal to the binding covenant (Nehemiah 9:38, 10:1-2). This covenant included the oath to separate from the foreign peoples and keep the law of God, not to give their daughters to the peoples of the land nor take their daughters for their sons, and not to buy goods on the Sabbath or on holy days (Nehemiah 10:28-31).

call: Praiser at the wall dedication (prince of Judah)
introduce: A figure whose name is recorded in one of the companies in the thanksgiving procession at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem led by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 12:31, 12:33).
lifetime: When the wall of Jerusalem was completed and the dedication was held, Nehemiah brought the leaders of Judah up on top of the wall and arranged a great company giving thanks into two processions; his name is recorded in the list of the company that went to the right toward the Dung Gate (Nehemiah 12:27, 12:31-33).
event: In the thanksgiving procession that went to the right toward the Dung Gate at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, his name was recorded side by side with Hoshaiah and those following him with half of the leaders of Judah, and with Ezra, Meshullam, and others (Nehemiah 12:31-33).

call: Son of Hoshaiah (leader of the flight to Egypt)
introduce: Azariah was the son of Hoshaiah, who in the time of Jeremiah, together with Johanan the son of Kareah and all the arrogant men, said to Jeremiah, "You are telling a lie" (Jeremiah 43:2).
lifetime: When Jeremiah had finished telling all the people all the words of the LORD, Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, together with Johanan the son of Kareah and all the arrogant men, spoke to Jeremiah (Jeremiah 43:1-2). The subject of the going into Egypt and coming to Tahpanhes afterward is recorded as Johanan and all the commanders of the forces and all the people (Jeremiah 43:4-7).
event: Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, together with Johanan and the arrogant men, told Jeremiah that the LORD had not sent him to say, "Do not go to Egypt to live there," and that he was telling a lie; and he said that Baruch the son of Neriah was inciting Jeremiah against them to deliver them into the hand of the Chaldeans, to put them to death or carry them off to Babylon (Jeremiah 43:2-3). Then it was Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces and all the people who did not obey the voice of the LORD to stay in the land of Judah, but took Jeremiah, Baruch, and others and came to Tahpanhes in the land of Egypt (Jeremiah 43:4-7).
character: He was a man who put his own political judgment and practical survival first, and showed a tendency to value military and practical security over the prophet's counsel (Jeremiah 43:2-3). Also, when Jeremiah's prophecy did not agree with their intentions, he had a willful side, forcibly denying it and acting on his own (Jeremiah 43:2).

introduce: Azarel appears to be a son of Heman who was assigned the duty of temple praise in the time of King David (corresponding to Uzziel in 1 Chronicles 25:4), and he was chosen eleventh of the divisions of the praise service (1 Chronicles 25:18).
lifetime: When David set apart for service some of the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun (1 Chronicles 25:1), the duties were obtained by casting lots (1 Chronicles 25:8), and he was chosen eleventh; with his sons and brothers there were twelve (1 Chronicles 25:18).
event: King David set apart those who were to give praise from among the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun (1 Chronicles 25:1), and Azarel was chosen by lot for the eleventh division, so that with his sons and brothers they numbered twelve (1 Chronicles 25:8, 25:18).

call: Son of Jeroham (chief of the tribe of Dan)
introduce: Azarel is recorded as a leader who ruled the tribe of Dan in the time of King David. He appears in the list of the commanders of the tribes of Israel in 1 Chronicles 27 and is mentioned as the son of Jeroham (1 Chronicles 27:22).
lifetime: He is one of those who were over the tribes of Israel during the reign of King David (1 Chronicles 27:16, 27:22). He is recorded as the chief of Dan (1 Chronicles 27:22).
event: He was entered in the list of those over the tribes of Israel as the chief of Dan (1 Chronicles 27:16, 27:22). No other specific deeds of his are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Azarel was one of the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian exile in the time of Ezra, and a man belonging to the descendants of Bani.
lifetime: Azarel is a man included in the list made when Ezra investigated in Jerusalem those who had taken foreign women as wives and drew up their names (Ezra 10:41).
event: He is recorded as one of the descendants of Bani who took foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:34, 10:41, 10:44).

call: Priest of the house of Immer
introduce: Azarel was a man of a priestly family who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile, and the father of Amashai. He was the son of Ahzai, the grandson of Meshillemoth, and the great-grandson of Immer (Nehemiah 11:13).
lifetime: In the list of priests living in Jerusalem in Nehemiah 11, his name is recorded through his son Amashai (Nehemiah 11:10-13). Amashai is recorded as the son of Azarel, the grandson of Ahzai, the great-grandson of Meshillemoth, and the great-great-grandson of Immer (Nehemiah 11:13).
event: Azarel's own deeds are not recorded in the Bible. His son Amashai is recorded together with 242 of his brothers who were heads of fathers' houses (Nehemiah 11:13).

introduce: Asarel is a figure in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah mentioned in 1 Chronicles 4, and the son of Jehallelel.
lifetime: As the son of Jehallelel, he belongs to the genealogy of Asarel, a descendant of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:16).

call: Father of Hoshea (father of the chief of Ephraim)
introduce: Azaziah is a figure recorded as the father of Hoshea, the chief of the sons of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 27:20).
lifetime: In the list of those over the tribes of Israel in the time of David, he is recorded as the father of Hoshea, the chief of the sons of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 27:20). No specific record of his life, such as his birth or death, appears in the Bible.
event: His son Hoshea is recorded as the chief of the sons of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 27:20). Azaziah's own deeds are not recorded in the Bible.

call: Levite in charge of temple offerings
introduce: Azaziah was a Levite appointed in the time of King Hezekiah as one who took care of the offerings of the temple. He worked under the Levite Conaniah and his brother Shimei (2 Chronicles 31:12-13).
lifetime: When Hezekiah king of Judah purified the temple and reorganized the sacrificial system, he took on the duty of managing the temple's gifts, tithes, and dedicated things (2 Chronicles 31:13). He served under the supervision of Conaniah and carried out the work under appointment by King Hezekiah and Azariah, the ruler of the temple (2 Chronicles 31:13).
event: Under Conaniah and his brother Shimei he became one of those who took care of the offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated things brought into the temple, and this was by the command of King Hezekiah and Azariah, the ruler of the house of God (2 Chronicles 31:12-13).

introduce: Asaiah is a figure of the Levite line of the descendants of Merari, whose name appears in the genealogy of a family connected with the service of the temple (1 Chronicles 6:30).
lifetime: Asaiah is a descendant of Mahli the son of Merari, and in the genealogy he is the son of Haggiah (1 Chronicles 6:29-30). The Bible does not record specific details of his life, such as his birth, upbringing, or time of death (1 Chronicles 6:30).
event: In the biblical record there is no indication that Asaiah led any particular event or left any independent achievement, and there is no record beyond confirming his place within the genealogical system of the tribe of Levi (1 Chronicles 6:30).

introduce: Asaiah is the firstborn of the Shilonites recorded in 1 Chronicles, one of the descendants of Judah who lived in Jerusalem.
lifetime: As the firstborn among the Shilonites, he is recorded as a descendant of Judah who lived in Jerusalem after returning from Babylon (1 Chronicles 9:3, 9:5).
event: He is included in the list of the descendants of Judah who lived in Jerusalem, and as the firstborn of his family he holds a place in the genealogy (1 Chronicles 9:5).

call: Chief of the sons of Merari (bearer of the ark)
introduce: A man belonging to the descendants of Merari of the tribe of Levi, and one of the chiefs appointed in the time of King David to bring the ark of God up to Jerusalem.
lifetime: When King David gathered the descendants of Aaron and the Levites to move the ark of God, he was recorded as chief of the sons of Merari, together with 220 of his brothers (1 Chronicles 15:4, 15:6).
event: David called the Levites, including him, and commanded them, as the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites, to consecrate themselves and carry up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place he had prepared for it (1 Chronicles 15:11-12). He is recorded as chief of the sons of Merari, together with 220 of his brothers (1 Chronicles 15:6).

introduce: Asaiah was a servant of the king who was active in the time of King Josiah of the southern kingdom of Judah (2 Kings 22:12).
lifetime: He attended the king closely and fulfilled the role of a servant who received the king's commands directly and carried them out (2 Chronicles 34:20).
event: When the high priest Hilkiah found the book of the law in the temple in the time of King Josiah, he was included in the delegation sent at the king's command to inquire of the LORD about the words of the book of the law (2 Kings 22:12-13). Together with the other members of the delegation, Hilkiah, Ahikam, Achbor, and Shaphan, he went to the prophetess Huldah, the wife of Shallum, and conveyed the king's wishes (2 Kings 22:14). Having heard from the prophetess Huldah the disaster that would come upon Judah and the word of the LORD to King Josiah, he returned to the king and reported back (2 Chronicles 34:22-28).

introduce: Asahel is one of the Levites sent out to teach the law during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of the southern kingdom of Judah.
lifetime: In the third year of his reign King Jehoshaphat sent officials and Levites to the cities of Judah to teach the people the book of the law of the LORD (2 Chronicles 17:7-9). Asahel belonged to the company of Levites appointed at that time and carried out a teaching ministry, going about throughout Judah (2 Chronicles 17:8).
event: Having received the command of King Jehoshaphat, Asahel, together with his fellow Levites, took the book of the law and went around through all the cities of Judah teaching the people (2 Chronicles 17:9).

introduce: One of the Levites who served in the temple in the time of King Hezekiah of Judah, appointed as an overseer to take care of the gifts and offerings of the temple.
lifetime: While King Hezekiah carried out the purification of the temple and the rebuilding of the sacrificial system, he took the post of supervising the offerings of the temple under the direction of Conaniah and Shimei (2 Chronicles 31:13).
event: By the command of King Hezekiah and Azariah, the ruler of the house of God, he became, under Conaniah and his brother Shimei, one of those who took care of the offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated things brought into the temple (2 Chronicles 31:12-13).

call: Father of Jonathan, who opposed the investigation of foreign marriages
introduce: Asahel is recorded as the father of Jonathan, who opposed the matter of those who had taken foreign women as wives in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:15).
lifetime: The information recorded in the Bible about the life of Asahel is very limited, and he is mentioned only through his son Jonathan (Ezra 10:15).
event: Asahel's son Jonathan is recorded as one who, together with Jahzeiah the son of Tikvah, stood up and opposed the handling of those who, after the return from the Babylonian exile, had married foreign women (Ezra 10:15). Asahel himself does not appear as the one acting in that event and is mentioned only as Jonathan's father.

call: Son of Eleasah (descendant of the royal house of Saul)
introduce: Azel is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the royal house of Saul, a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin and the son of Eleasah.
lifetime: Azel is recorded as the son of Eleasah in the genealogy of the descendants of Merib-baal, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul (1 Chronicles 8:34-37).

introduce: A woman belonging to Caleb of the tribe of Judah, recorded in the genealogy as his wife.
lifetime: She is recorded as the wife of Caleb the son of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2:18). From the record that after Azubah died Caleb also married Ephrath, and that Ephrath bore Hur by him (1 Chronicles 2:19), it can be known that Azubah was Caleb's wife before Ephrath.
event: Caleb had sons Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon by his wife Azubah and by Jerioth (1 Chronicles 2:18). After Azubah died, Caleb took Ephrath as his wife (1 Chronicles 2:19).

call: Ancestor of a family that returned with Ezra (father of Johanan)
introduce: Azgad is a figure who appears in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah as the name of a clan (family). In Ezra 8:12, Johanan the son of Hakkatan, of the descendants of Azgad, is recorded among the heads of families who came up from Babylon with Ezra (Ezra 8:1, 8:12).
lifetime: There is no record of the life of Azgad himself, and his name appears as the name of a clan (family). Among the heads of families who came up from Babylon with Ezra in the time of King Artaxerxes, from the descendants of Azgad there was Johanan the son of Hakkatan (Ezra 8:1, 8:12).
event: Azgad's own deeds are not recorded. Among the descendants of Azgad, Johanan the son of Hakkatan is recorded as a head of a family who came up from Babylon with 110 men (Ezra 8:12).

call: Leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Azgad is a name recorded among the leaders of the people who set their seal to the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14-15).
lifetime: His name is recorded in the list of the leaders of the people among those who set their seal to the covenant led by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:14-15).
event: He is included in the list of the leaders of the people who set their seal to the covenant (Nehemiah 10:29) in which they swore to keep all the commandments, ordinances, and statutes of the LORD, following the law of God given through Moses the servant of God (Nehemiah 10:14-15).

call: Descendant of the royal house of Saul (son of Azel)
introduce: Azrikam is a figure recorded in the Chronicles genealogy, one of those who make up the family tree of the royal house of Saul of the tribe of Benjamin, and is stated to be a son of Azel.
lifetime: Azrikam is recorded as one of the six sons of Azel (1 Chronicles 8:38, 9:44), and Azel is a descendant of Merib-baal the son of Jonathan (1 Chronicles 8:34-38).
event: No specific achievement or particular event of Azrikam himself is mentioned in the biblical record; he is recorded only as one who makes up the family tree of the royal house of Saul (1 Chronicles 8:38).
