introduce: A figure who appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Merari of the tribe of Levi recorded in 1 Chronicles; he is the son of Hashabiah, the father of Hasshub, and the grandfather of Shemaiah (1 Chronicles 9:14).
lifetime: It is recorded that Shemaiah of the descendants of Merari was the son of Hasshub, the grandson of Azrikam, and the great-grandson of Hashabiah; Azrikam therefore appears as the son of Hashabiah and the one who fathered Hasshub (1 Chronicles 9:14, Nehemiah 11:15).

call: Governor of the palace to King Ahaz
introduce: Azrikam is a figure recorded as the governor of the palace in the time of Ahaz king of Judah. In the record that in Ahaz's time Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, killed 120,000 valiant men in Judah, he is said to have been killed by Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim (2 Chronicles 28:6-7).
lifetime: He was governor of the palace in the time of Ahaz king of Judah (2 Chronicles 28:1, 28:7), and was killed by Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim (2 Chronicles 28:7).
event: Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, killed Azrikam the governor of the palace, together with Maaseiah the king's son and Elkanah, who was second to the king (2 Chronicles 28:7). This is an event recorded at the time when Ahaz did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD and the LORD delivered him into the hand of the king of Israel (2 Chronicles 28:1, 28:5-7).

call: Father of Jerimoth (father of the chief of Naphtali)
introduce: Azriel is a figure recorded as the father of Jerimoth, the chief of Naphtali among the chiefs who were over the tribes of Israel in the time of David (1 Chronicles 27:16, 27:19).
lifetime: There is no record of Azriel's own life; his son Jerimoth is recorded as the chief of Naphtali (1 Chronicles 27:19).

call: Father of Seraiah (father of the king's officer)
introduce: Azriel is recorded as the father of Seraiah. Among those whom the king commanded in the time of Jehoiakim king of Judah to seize the scribe Baruch and the prophet Jeremiah was Seraiah the son of Azriel (Jeremiah 36:26).
lifetime: There is no record of Azriel's own life. His son Seraiah, in the time of Jehoiakim king of Judah, received the king's command together with Jerahmeel the king's son and Shelemiah the son of Abdeel (Jeremiah 36:1, 36:26).
event: Azriel's own deeds are not recorded. His son Seraiah, at the king's command, tried to seize the scribe Baruch and the prophet Jeremiah, but the LORD hid them (Jeremiah 36:26).

call: Descendant of the royal house of Saul (son of Jehoaddah)
introduce: Azmaveth, who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, is a man who carried on the bloodline of the royal house of Saul; he is the son of Jehoaddah and is recorded as a descendant of Merib-baal, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul.
lifetime: According to 1 Chronicles 8:36, Azmaveth (spelled Azmaveb in the KRV) is the son of Jehoaddah and the brother of Alemeth and Zimri. In the genealogy he is mentioned as a descendant of the royal house of Saul, in the line running from Jonathan the son of Saul to his son Merib-baal, Micah, Ahaz, and Jehoaddah (1 Chronicles 8:33-36). 1 Chronicles 9:42 records that Ahaz fathered Jarah, and that Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri (1 Chronicles 9:42).
character: In the biblical record there is no mention of his character or specific activities; his name is entered only as a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin who preserves the family tree of the royal house of Saul (1 Chronicles 8:36, 1 Chronicles 9:42).

introduce: In the book of Daniel he is a man recorded as a Mede by descent, and the father of Darius, who was made king over the realm of the Chaldeans (Daniel 9:1). The Bible has no record of his personal deeds.
lifetime: According to the biblical record, he is a man belonging to the Median people (Daniel 9:1). His son Darius was made king over the realm of the Chaldeans (Daniel 9:1).
event: His deeds are not recorded in the Bible; he is mentioned only as the father of Darius in the verse that states the first year in which Darius was made king over the realm of the Chaldeans (Daniel 9:1).

introduce: Ahasuerus (Xerxes) was the fourth king of the Achaemenid dynasty of the Persian Empire and is historically regarded as the same person as Xerxes I. He ruled a vast territory of 127 provinces from India to Cush, and is the monarch who forms the main setting of the biblical book of Esther.
lifetime: In the third year of his reign he gave a banquet in the citadel of Susa for all his officials and servants (Esther 1:3); after deposing Queen Vashti, he gathered young women from the provinces and took Esther as queen (Esther 2:16-17). He accepted the request of Esther, who had learned of Haman's plot to destroy the Jews, and stopped it, and he permitted the Jews to defend themselves and to destroy those who opposed them (Esther 8:11).
event: In the third year of his reign he gave a banquet for all his officials and servants and displayed the riches and splendor of his kingdom for 180 days (Esther 1:3-4); after that he gave a banquet for seven days for all the people, great and small, in the citadel of Susa (Esther 1:5). At Haman's suggestion he sent an edict throughout the land to destroy all the Jews on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar (Esther 3:8-9, 3:13), but afterward he heard Esther's plea and had Haman hanged on the gallows (Esther 7:9-10), and issued an edict permitting the Jews to protect their own lives (Esther 8:11). Also, when Queen Vashti did not obey the king's command, he consulted the seven princes of Persia and Media, following the custom of asking the wise men who knew the law and judgment (Esther 1:13-16).
character: He valued his own authority, and when Queen Vashti did not respond to his summons, he deposed her at once (Esther 1:19). He sometimes showed a hot-tempered and capricious disposition, but showed a flexible attitude when he accepted the pleas or counsel of Esther (Esther 7:2-3). He tended to be easily swayed by the words of close associates such as Haman, who had gained his trust (Esther 3:10-11).

call: Son of Micah (descendant of the royal house of Saul)
introduce: A descendant of the royal house of Saul, of the line of Merib-baal the son of Jonathan, recorded as the son of Micah. He is a man of the tribe of Benjamin who appears in the genealogy of the house of Saul described in 1 Chronicles 8 and 9.
lifetime: Ahaz is the son of Micah (1 Chronicles 8:35, 9:41), and Micah was fathered by Merib-baal the son of Jonathan (1 Chronicles 9:40). That is, he belongs to the genealogy of the royal house of Saul running through Saul, Jonathan, Merib-baal, and Micah (1 Chronicles 9:39-41), and he fathered Jehoaddah (1 Chronicles 8:36). 1 Chronicles 9:42 records that Ahaz fathered Jarah (1 Chronicles 9:42).
event: No record of any special historical achievement or particular event appears in the Bible. He is only recorded as one of the sons of Micah, and as having fathered Jehoaddah (Jarah in 9:42) (1 Chronicles 8:35-36, 1 Chronicles 9:41-42).

introduce: The sixth king of the southern kingdom of Judah, the son of Jehoram and Athaliah, who carried on the line of the house of David. He was a grandson, through his mother, of Ahab king of the northern kingdom of Israel, and his reign is recorded as one year.
lifetime: He was the son of Jehoram king of Judah and became king at the age of 22 (2 Kings 8:26). His mother Athaliah was a daughter of Ahab, king of the northern kingdom of Israel (2 Kings 8:18, 8:26). He went with Joram the son of Ahab to Ramoth-gilead and fought against Hazael king of Aram (2 Kings 8:28), and when Joram was wounded and returned to Jezreel, he went down to Jezreel to visit him (2 Kings 8:29). He went out with Joram to meet Jehu at Jezreel, and when he saw Jehu kill Joram, he fled, but Jehu pursued and struck him, and he fled as far as Megiddo and died there (2 Kings 9:21-27).
event: He walked in the way of the house of Ahab and did evil in the sight of the LORD (2 Kings 8:27), and his mother counseled him to do wickedly (2 Chronicles 22:3). He went with Joram the son of Ahab to Ramoth-gilead and fought against Hazael king of Aram (2 Chronicles 22:5), and when Joram was wounded and returned to Jezreel, he went down to Jezreel to visit him (2 Kings 8:29). Seeing Jehu kill Joram, he fled, but was pursued by Jehu as far as Megiddo, and died there (2 Kings 9:27). His servants carried his body in a chariot to Jerusalem and buried him in the City of David (2 Kings 9:28).
character: He kept close ties of blood with the house of Ahab and followed their manner of rule (2 Kings 8:27). Politically he strengthened the alliance with the northern kingdom of Israel (2 Kings 8:28), and by acting together with the king of Israel at the time of Jehu's coup, he became a direct victim of that coup (2 Kings 9:27).

introduce: A false prophet among the captives of Judah who had been carried off to Babylon, the son of Kolaiah (Jeremiah 29:21). He is recorded as one who, together with Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, prophesied lies to the captives in the name of the LORD.
lifetime: He was active during the Babylonian exile, and together with Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah he prophesied lies in the name of the LORD (Jeremiah 29:21). He was delivered into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and was put to death by being roasted in the fire, and the captives of Judah in Babylon made a curse of him and Zedekiah (Jeremiah 29:21-22).
event: He prophesied lies in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel (Jeremiah 29:21). He committed adultery with his neighbors' wives, and spoke in the name of the LORD a lie that the LORD had not commanded (Jeremiah 29:23). Because of this he was delivered to the king of Babylon and put to death, and as one roasted in the fire he became a curse (Jeremiah 29:21-22).
character: He showed a deceitful disposition, using the pretext of the word of God to satisfy his own selfish desires (Jeremiah 29:23). He showed morally corrupt conduct, such as taking his neighbor's wife, and tried to deny the authority of Jeremiah, the true prophet of God (Jeremiah 29:23).

introduce: "Ahohite" is a designation used in the Bible to indicate the origin or affiliation of a particular person, and this name also appears among the sons of Bela, the firstborn son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:1, 8:4).
lifetime: Dodai the Ahohite (Dodo in 1 Chronicles 11:12) was the father of Eleazar, one of the three mighty men who were with David (2 Samuel 23:9, 1 Chronicles 11:12). Dodai the Ahohite was also the commander of the division for the second month (1 Chronicles 27:4). Also Zalmon the Ahohite (2 Samuel 23:28) and Ilai the Ahohite (1 Chronicles 11:29) are recorded in the list of David's mighty men.
event: Eleazar, one of David's mighty men, struck down the Philistines in battle until his hand grew weary and clung to the sword, and that day the LORD brought about a great victory (2 Samuel 23:9-10). 1 Chronicles 11 records that Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite was with David at Pas-dammim, and when the Philistines gathered there, he stood in the midst of that field and defended it and struck down the Philistines, and the LORD saved them with a great deliverance (1 Chronicles 11:12-14).

call: Wife of King David (mother of Amnon)
introduce: A woman from Jezreel, one of the wives of David, the second king of Israel, and the mother of David's eldest son Amnon.
lifetime: At the time when David was fleeing from King Saul, he took Ahinoam of Jezreel as his wife (1 Samuel 25:43). Afterward, when David became king over the house of Judah in Hebron, she moved to Hebron with him (2 Samuel 2:2). In the days when David reigned in Hebron, she bore David's eldest son, Amnon (2 Samuel 3:2).
event: When the Amalekites raided Ziklag and carried off David's wives, Ahinoam was taken captive together with Abigail, and she came back again when David pursued the Amalekites and rescued them (1 Samuel 30:5, 30:18).

call: Father of the high priest Zadok (son of Amariah)
introduce: Ahitub is a figure who appears in Old Testament genealogies, the son of Amariah and the father of the priest Zadok (1 Chronicles 6:7-8). He belonged to the priestly family in the line of Eleazar, the son of Aaron (1 Chronicles 6:3-8).
lifetime: Ahitub is the son of Amariah (1 Chronicles 6:7, 6:52) and fathered his son Zadok (1 Chronicles 6:8, 6:53). In the time of David, Zadok the son of Ahitub became priest together with Ahimelech the son of Abiathar (2 Samuel 8:17).
event: According to the biblical record, no historical event that Ahitub himself led or carried out is specifically stated, and he is mentioned mainly only as one who continues the genealogy of the priestly family. However, his son Zadok became priest in the time of David (2 Samuel 8:17).

call: Grandson of Azariah in Solomon's time and father of Zadok II
introduce: Ahitub appears in the genealogies of Chronicles in the Old Testament as a figure in the line of the priestly house, a descendant of Eleazar. He is the grandson of Azariah, who served as priest in the temple Solomon built in Jerusalem, the son of Amariah, and the father of Zadok (1 Chronicles 6:10-12). He also appears as an ancestor in the same line (Ahitub–Zadok–Meshullam–Hilkiah) in the genealogy of Azariah (Seraiah in Nehemiah), who was in charge of the house of God, in 1 Chronicles 9:11 and Nehemiah 11:11, which describe him as "a great-grandson of Zadok, a great-great-grandson of Meraioth, and a fifth-generation descendant of Ahitub."
lifetime: Ahitub was the son of Amariah and fathered Zadok (1 Chronicles 6:11-12). Since Amariah was the son of Azariah, who served as priest in the temple Solomon built in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 6:10-11), Ahitub was the grandson of that Azariah. 1 Chronicles 9:11 and Nehemiah 11:11 record this line as "the son of Hilkiah, the grandson of Meshullam, the great-grandson of Zadok, the great-great-grandson of Meraioth, and the fifth-generation descendant of Ahitub," placing Meraioth between Zadok and Ahitub.
character: In the biblical record nothing is mentioned about his personal character or specific activities; only his name is attested, as an ancestor continuing the genealogy of the high-priestly house (1 Chronicles 6:11-12).

call: Son of the priest Zadok (David's messenger)
introduce: The son of the priest Zadok in the time of King David, who served as a messenger helping David during Absalom's rebellion (2 Samuel 15:27).
lifetime: He was born as the son of the high priest Zadok (2 Samuel 15:27). When Absalom rose in rebellion and David had to leave Jerusalem, he stayed by En-rogel together with Jonathan the son of Abiathar and took the role of conveying to David the situation inside the city (2 Samuel 17:17). After David's army defeated Absalom's army, he asked General Joab and ran as a messenger to bring David the news of victory (2 Samuel 18:19-23).
event: While on his way to tell David of the counsel of Ahithophel, which Hushai had reported to the two priests Zadok and Abiathar, he was discovered by a young man, but he escaped the danger by hiding in a well in the courtyard of a man's house in Bahurim, and he brought the news to David, so that David crossed the Jordan with all the people (2 Samuel 17:15-22). After Absalom's death, although he set out later than the Cushite, he ran by way of the plain and reached King David ahead of the Cushite and announced the news of victory (2 Samuel 18:23-28). When David asked about the welfare of Absalom, he answered that when Joab sent him he had seen a great commotion but did not know what it was (2 Samuel 18:29).
character: He was very swift at running, and had a manner of running so distinctive that the watchman recognized him as Ahimaaz merely from seeing him run from afar (2 Samuel 18:27). King David had said of him that he was a good man and would bring good news (2 Samuel 18:27). Joab tried to dissuade him from going as a messenger, but he asked again and again and insisted on going, showing initiative and tenacity (2 Samuel 18:22-23).

introduce: Ahimaaz was one of the twelve officers who, during the reign of King Solomon, were in charge of the administration and supply of provisions in the region of Naphtali, one of the northern tribes.
lifetime: He took Basemath, the daughter of King Solomon, as his wife and became the king's son-in-law (1 Kings 4:15).
event: As the officer of the region of Naphtali, he carried out the task of providing food for the royal household one month in the year (1 Kings 4:7, 1 Kings 4:15).

introduce: A man recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:17 as a gatekeeper together with Shallum, Akkub, and Talmon. Among the gatekeepers, their chief was Shallum (1 Chronicles 9:17).
lifetime: Ahiman appears as a gatekeeper in the record of those who lived in their cities after the return from the exile (1 Chronicles 9:2-3, 9:17). The gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their brothers, and Shallum was their chief (1 Chronicles 9:17).
event: He is recorded as one of the gatekeepers, and these gatekeepers were stationed at the king's gate on the east, as the gatekeepers of the camp of the descendants of Levi (1 Chronicles 9:18). The specific deeds of Ahiman himself are not recorded.
character: The Bible portrays Ahiman as a man faithful, together with the other gatekeepers, in guarding the gates of the temple (1 Chronicles 9:17). He is recorded as one who, according to his Levite lineage, faithfully carried out the duty handed down from his ancestors (1 Chronicles 9:19).

introduce: Ahimelech the Hittite was a man who was with David during the time when David was fleeing from Saul. When David asked who would go down with him to Saul's camp, he is recorded as one who was asked together with Abishai, brother of Joab the son of Zeruiah (1 Samuel 26:6).
lifetime: When David was in the wilderness on the side of the hill of Hachilah and learned that Saul had encamped (1 Samuel 26:1-5), he asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai who would go down with him to Saul's camp (1 Samuel 26:6). It is recorded that Abishai answered that he would go with him (1 Samuel 26:6).
event: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai who would go down with him to Saul's camp, but the one who answered was Abishai, and those who went to Saul's camp by night are recorded as David and Abishai (1 Samuel 26:6-7). There is no record that Ahimelech went down to the camp.
character: He is a man with such strong loyalty to David that he was asked to volunteer for the dangerous mission of infiltrating Saul's camp (1 Samuel 26:6). His background as a Hittite shows that, although he was not a man of the tribes of Israel, he was deeply involved in David's military course (1 Samuel 26:6).

meaning: brother of the LORD, friend of the LORD
introduce: The father of Baasha, the third king of Israel, and a man from the tribe of Issachar.
lifetime: A man of the house of Issachar, whose son Baasha conspired against Nadab and became king of Israel (1 Kings 15:27, 15:33).

meaning: brother of the LORD, friend of the LORD
introduce: A figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, the son of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2:25).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:4-5, 2:9, 2:25).
character: In the biblical record his name is listed in the register together with Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel, and his other brothers (1 Chronicles 2:25).

meaning: brother of the LORD, friend of the LORD
introduce: Ahijah is a man recorded as a Pelonite in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:36).
lifetime: He is recorded together with the chiefs of David's mighty men, who, together with all Israel, strengthened David's kingdom and made him king (1 Chronicles 11:10, 11:36).
event: In the list of David's mighty men his name is recorded as Ahijah the Pelonite, together with Hepher the Mecherathite (1 Chronicles 11:36). His specific deeds are not recorded in the Bible.

meaning: brother of the LORD, friend of the LORD
introduce: Ahijah is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a Levite who, in the time of King David, was in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated things.
lifetime: Among the Levites, he is recorded as the one in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated things (1 Chronicles 26:20).
event: He was in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated things (1 Chronicles 26:20). Apart from this verse, there is no specific record of his duties or deeds.

meaning: brother of the LORD, friend of the LORD
introduce: Ahijah is a man recorded as one of the leaders who sealed the document of the covenant that the people of Israel made with God after the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem led by Nehemiah.
lifetime: A man who was active in the time of Nehemiah after the return from the Babylonian exile, he appears as one of the leaders who, representing the people of Israel, put their seal to the written covenant (Nehemiah 10:1).
event: Together with Nehemiah and the leaders, priests, and Levites of Israel, he put his name by seal to the document of the covenant in which they swore to keep the law, to forbid marriage with foreigners, and to keep the Sabbath (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:26).

meaning: brother of the LORD, friend of the LORD
introduce: Ahijah was a priest active in the time of King Saul, the son of Ahitub, brother of Ichabod, the grandson of Phinehas, and the great-grandson of Eli, who had been the LORD's priest at Shiloh (1 Samuel 14:3). He is recorded as one who carried on the priestly family of Shiloh. Both Ahijah and Ahimelech appear as sons of Ahitub, so they may be the same person, but the Bible has no explicit statement that they are one and the same.
lifetime: As a descendant of the house of Eli, he was there wearing an ephod when Saul was staying at Migron on the outskirts of Gibeah (1 Samuel 14:2-3). He was at Saul's side when Saul commanded him to bring the ark of God (1 Samuel 14:18).
event: During the war with the Philistines, Saul commanded Ahijah to bring the ark of God (1 Samuel 14:18). While Saul was speaking to the priest, the tumult in the Philistine camp kept increasing, and Saul said to the priest, "Withdraw your hand" (1 Samuel 14:19). When Saul was staying at Migron on the outskirts of Gibeah, Ahijah was there wearing an ephod (1 Samuel 14:2-3).
character: He was a man closely allied with royal power, maintaining the authority of the priesthood within Saul's system of government and taking part in the king's military decisions (1 Samuel 14:3). From the fact that he handled the ephod and held the official duty of seeking God's answer, he is judged to have held to the traditional forms of the priesthood (1 Samuel 14:18).

meaning: brother of the LORD, friend of the LORD
introduce: Ahijah was a scribe in the time of Solomon in the kingdom of Israel, and the son of Shisha.
lifetime: He is recorded as a scribe, together with Elihoreph the son of Shisha, during the reign of Solomon (1 Kings 4:3).
event: Under the government of King Solomon he held office as the king's scribe, together with Elihoreph (1 Kings 4:3).

meaning: brother of the LORD, friend of the LORD
introduce: Ahijah is a man who appears in the context introducing the sons of Ehud in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles 8; his name is mentioned together with Naaman and Gera (1 Chronicles 8:6-7).
lifetime: Ahijah came from a Benjaminite family; in 1 Chronicles 8:6-7 his name is mentioned together with Naaman and Gera in connection with the sons of Ehud, heads of the families living in Geba, going to Manahath (1 Chronicles 8:6-7).
event: His name is mentioned only in connection with the heads of the families living in Geba moving to Manahath, and no specific deeds of Ahijah himself are recorded (1 Chronicles 8:6-7).

call: Man of Gibeah (chief of the warriors who came over to Ziklag)
introduce: Ahiezer is a man who appears in 1 Chronicles 12, a Gibeathite of the tribe of Benjamin. As a kinsman of King Saul, he was one of the mighty men who came over to David and joined him when David was staying at Ziklag.
lifetime: He was a Gibeathite of the tribe of Benjamin and a kinsman of Saul (1 Chronicles 12:2-3). He went to David, who had fled from Saul to Ziklag, and joined the ranks of the mighty men who helped him (1 Chronicles 12:1-2).
event: He was a man of Benjamin among the mighty men who came to David and helped him in battle while David was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul the son of Kish, and he was recorded as their chief (1 Chronicles 12:1-3). He and Joash were the two sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite (1 Chronicles 12:3).
character: He is described as a man of skilled fighting ability, able to shoot arrows and sling stones with either the right hand or the left (1 Chronicles 12:2). By choosing to leave his kinsman King Saul and follow David, he showed military decisiveness (1 Chronicles 12:2).

introduce: Ahio is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the members who make up the family tree of the royal house of Saul.
lifetime: Ahio is recorded as one of the sons of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon, of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:31). His name appears once more in the same genealogical record, in the list of the sons of Jeiel, the inhabitant of Gibeon (1 Chronicles 9:37).

call: Head of the gatekeepers who returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Akkub is a man recorded as a gatekeeper, and in the list of those who returned from the Babylonian exile, the descendants of Akkub are entered among the descendants of the gatekeepers among the people of Israel who came with Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 9:17; Ezra 2:42).
lifetime: In the list of the people of Israel who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and others, the descendants of Akkub are included among the descendants of the gatekeepers (Ezra 2:2, 42; Nehemiah 7:45).
event: The gatekeepers are recorded as Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their brothers, and Shallum was their chief (1 Chronicles 9:17).

introduce: Akkub was one of the Jews who returned from the Babylonian exile and served as a gatekeeper of Jerusalem. He appears in the biblical records of the genealogies and the duties of the gatekeepers.
lifetime: In the time of Nehemiah, he is recorded as a gatekeeper of the city of Jerusalem, together with Talmon and their brothers (Nehemiah 11:19). His name appears among the gatekeepers who served in the days of Joiakim, of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest and scribe (Nehemiah 12:25-26).
event: Together with Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, and Talmon, he served as a gatekeeper and, by division, guarded the storehouses at the gates (Nehemiah 12:25). These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest and scribe (Nehemiah 12:26).

call: Ancestor of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Akkub is the ancestor of a family recorded in the list of those who returned from the Babylonian exile as the descendants of Akkub among the Nethinim. The Nethinim were those whom David and the officials gave to serve the Levites (Ezra 8:20).
lifetime: His name is entered as the descendants of Akkub among the Nethinim in the list of the people of Israel who came with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:2, 43-45).
event: The descendants of Akkub are included among the Nethinim who returned from Babylon to Judah (Ezra 2:43-45). Akkub's own deeds are not recorded.

introduce: Akkub is a man recorded as one of those who made the people understand the law when Ezra was reading the book of the law after the return from the Babylonian exile. His name appears in the reading and teaching of the law in the square before the Water Gate in the time of Nehemiah.
lifetime: He was active as a member of the community that returned from the Babylonian exile, and took part in the reading of the law in the square before the Water Gate after the wall was completed (Nehemiah 8:1-3, 7). His name is recorded among those who made the people understand the law (Nehemiah 8:7).
event: When Ezra read the book of the law in the square before the Water Gate, Akkub, together with the others, took part in making the people, who stood in their places, understand the law (Nehemiah 8:3, 7). They read the book of the law and gave the sense of it, so that the people understood the reading (Nehemiah 8:8).
character: He was a Levite with the knowledge and eloquence to teach the people the word of God, being well versed in the law (Nehemiah 8:7). He appears to have had the interpretive ability to help the people understand its content clearly, going beyond reading the words of Scripture piece by piece (Nehemiah 8:8).

call: Servant of King Josiah (son of Micaiah)
introduce: Achbor was a man active in the time of King Josiah of the kingdom of Judah, the son of Micaiah, and one of those sent at the king's command to inquire of the LORD about the words of the book that had been found (2 Kings 22:12-14). His son Elnathan was one of the officials in the time of King Jehoiakim (Jeremiah 36:12).
lifetime: He appears as one of those whom the king commanded, together with the priest Hilkiah, Ahikam, Shaphan, and Asaiah, to go and inquire of the LORD about the words of the book that Josiah king of Judah had found (2 Kings 22:12-13). They went together to the prophetess Huldah (2 Kings 22:14), and the messengers, having heard Huldah's words, reported back to the king (2 Kings 22:20). His son Elnathan was one of those whom King Jehoiakim sent to Egypt to bring back Uriah (Jeremiah 26:22).
event: At the command of King Josiah, he went with Shaphan the scribe, Hilkiah the high priest, Ahikam, and others to the prophetess Huldah, received an oracle concerning the disaster that would come upon the kingdom of Judah, and reported it to the king (2 Kings 22:12-20). The record in Chronicles also calls him Abdon (2 Chronicles 34:20).

introduce: Ahlai is a man recorded as the father of one of David's mighty men in the time of David's reign.
lifetime: He is recorded as the father of Zabad, a mighty man in the time of David (1 Chronicles 11:41).
event: His son Zabad is entered in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:26, 41).

introduce: Alemeth is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a son of Becher of the tribe of Benjamin. He is mentioned as one of the persons recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: Alemeth was born as a son of Becher and is a man included in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:8).
event: No biblical record of any specific achievement or particular event of Alemeth has been found (1 Chronicles 7:8).

call: Notable of the high priestly family in Jerusalem
introduce: A figure who appears in the book of Acts, one of the notables belonging to the high priestly family. He is recorded as one of the members of the Sanhedrin council that gathered to interrogate Peter and John in the early period when the apostles of the early church were active in Jerusalem.
lifetime: At the gathering of the religious leaders, elders, and scribes of Jerusalem, he took part, together with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, and others, in the interrogation of Peter and John (Acts 4:6).
event: After the incident in which Peter healed the lame man at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, they summoned the apostles before the council and demanded by what power and in whose name they had done this (Acts 4:7). Hearing the boldness of the apostles' testimony, they marveled, though they knew that they were uneducated, ordinary men, and afterward they sternly warned the apostles not to speak or teach in the name of Jesus (Acts 4:13-18).

introduce: A coppersmith mentioned in 2 Timothy in the New Testament, who did the apostle Paul great harm and strongly opposed the message of Paul and his companions (2 Timothy 4:14-15).
lifetime: He is a man mentioned in the letter the apostle Paul sent to Timothy (2 Timothy 4:14). Paul said that he had done him much harm and told Timothy to beware of him, because he had greatly opposed the message of Paul and his companions (2 Timothy 4:14-15).
event: He was a coppersmith and did Paul much harm (2 Timothy 4:14). Paul said that the Lord would repay him according to his deeds (2 Timothy 4:14), and told Timothy to beware of him, because he had greatly opposed the message of Paul and his companions (2 Timothy 4:15).
character: He is portrayed as a man who opposed Paul in connection with his own trade activities (2 Timothy 4:14). He showed an attitude of stubborn resistance to Paul's teaching and revealed a hostile disposition that hindered the spread of the gospel (2 Timothy 4:15).

introduce: A figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah; Amnon, recorded as a son of Shimon, is mentioned within the genealogy of the descendants of Judah.
lifetime: Amnon, who as a son of Shimon has his name entered in the genealogy of Judah, is mentioned in the course of the family line to which he belongs (1 Chronicles 4:20).
event: According to the biblical record, no specific achievement that Amnon himself carried out, nor any separate historical event, is described (1 Chronicles 4:20).

기타관계: Tilon#620(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

call: Chief of the sons of Uzziel (bearer of the ark)
meaning: my noble people, a generous people
introduce: Amminadab was a chief of the sons of Uzziel among the descendants of Kohath of the tribe of Levi, called in the time of David to carry the ark of God up to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 15:10-12).
lifetime: David called the priests Zadok and Abiathar, and the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab (1 Chronicles 15:11). As a chief of the sons of Uzziel he was recorded together with 112 of his brothers (1 Chronicles 15:10), and David called them heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites and commanded them to carry up the ark (1 Chronicles 15:12).
event: He was one of the heads of the Levites who were commanded, at David's order, to consecrate themselves and carry up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place David had prepared (1 Chronicles 15:12). Then the priests and the Levites consecrated themselves and went up carrying the ark, and the descendants of Levi carried the ark of God on their shoulders with poles (1 Chronicles 15:14-15).

introduce: Ammiel is a figure who appears in 2 Samuel in the Old Testament, the father of Machir, who lived in Lo-debar. Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan was in the house of his son Machir (2 Samuel 9:4).
lifetime: Ammiel is recorded as the father of Machir of Lo-debar (2 Samuel 9:4), and his son Machir, when David came to Mahanaim at the time of the rebellion of David's son Absalom, brought needed supplies such as beds, basins, earthen vessels, wheat, and barley (2 Samuel 17:27-29).
event: His own deeds are not recorded, but Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan was in the house of his son Machir, and David sent and brought him from that house (2 Samuel 9:4-5). Also his son Machir was one of those who brought supplies for the people who were with David when David came to Mahanaim (2 Samuel 17:27-29).

introduce: The sixth son of Obed-edom, a descendant of Korah of the tribe of Levi, who served in the office of temple gatekeeper in the time of David.
lifetime: He is recorded as the sixth of the eight sons of Obed-edom (1 Chronicles 26:5). God blessed Obed-edom (1 Chronicles 26:5), and the descendants of Obed-edom, they and their sons and their brothers, were all able men with strength for the service (1 Chronicles 26:8).
event: When lots were cast by families for the gatekeepers to guard each gate (1 Chronicles 26:13), his father Obed-edom drew the south, and his sons drew the storehouse (1 Chronicles 26:15).

call: Chief of the tribe of Simeon (father of Shemuel)
introduce: Ammihud is a figure who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, recorded as the father of Shemuel, who was chosen as the chief to divide the land as an inheritance from the tribe of Simeon (Numbers 34:20).
lifetime: Ammihud is mentioned as the father when his son Shemuel was chosen as the leader of his tribe for the distribution of the land of Canaan (Numbers 34:18-20).
event: When God named to Moses the leaders who were to divide the land of Canaan as an inheritance, from the tribe of the descendants of Simeon Shemuel the son of Ammihud took that office (Numbers 34:20). Beyond this, no special achievement or event carried out by Ammihud himself is recorded in the Bible.

call: Chief of the tribe of Naphtali (father of Pedahel)
introduce: Ammihud is a figure who appears in Numbers in the Old Testament, the father of Pedahel, a chief of the tribe of Naphtali (Numbers 34:28).
lifetime: His son Pedahel is recorded as the chief chosen from the tribe of the descendants of Naphtali when the people of Israel divided the land of Canaan as an inheritance (Numbers 34:18, 28).
event: When the LORD named those who were to divide the inheritance among the people of Israel in the land of Canaan, Pedahel the son of Ammihud was chosen as the chief of the tribe of the descendants of Naphtali (Numbers 34:28-29). Ammihud's own deeds are not recorded.

call: Son of Zechariah (ancestor of the returned priests)
meaning: he who is my strong power
introduce: Amzi is a man recorded in the genealogy of Nehemiah 11:12, the son of Zechariah and the father of Pelaliah, and the great-grandfather of Adaiah of the priestly family who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 11:12).
lifetime: In Nehemiah 11:12, Adaiah is recorded as the son of Jeroham, the grandson of Pelaliah, the great-grandson of Amzi, and the great-great-grandson of Zechariah, and in that genealogy Amzi is the son of Zechariah and the father of Pelaliah (Nehemiah 11:12). That genealogy runs in the order of Malchijah, Pashhur, Zechariah, Amzi, Pelaliah, Jeroham, Adaiah.
event: Amzi's own deeds are not recorded. In Nehemiah 11:12 his great-grandson Adaiah is introduced together with his brothers who did the work of the house, and Amzi's name appears in that genealogy (Nehemiah 11:12).

call: Son of Shammua (Levite head who returned from exile)
introduce: Abda was a Levite who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile, recorded as the son of Shammua (Nehemiah 11:17).
lifetime: He is included in the list of the Levites who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 11:15-18). He is the son of Shammua, and his genealogy continues as the grandson of Galal and the great-grandson of Jeduthun (Nehemiah 11:17).
event: Abda's own specific deeds are not recorded, and in Nehemiah 11:17 his name appears as the son of Shammua in the list of the Levites who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:17).

call: Son of Shashak of the tribe of Benjamin
introduce: A figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin; he is a namesake of the judge Abdon who appears in Judges 12, and belongs by descent to the sons of Benjamin.
lifetime: He is distinguished from Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite mentioned in Judges 12:13, and is recorded as one of the sons of Shashak of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:22-25).

call: Firstborn son of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon
introduce: A figure who appears in the genealogy of the inhabitants of Gibeon of the tribe of Benjamin, the firstborn son of Jeiel.
lifetime: He is recorded as the firstborn son of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon (1 Chronicles 8:29-30; 9:35-36).
event: As the firstborn of Jeiel, below him are recorded Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, and Zecher (1 Chronicles 8:30-31), and 1 Chronicles 9:36-37 also adds Ner, Zechariah, and Mikloth.

introduce: Abdi is a man of the family of the descendants of Elam among the people of Israel who returned from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem in the time of Ezra.
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, he is recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives in Jerusalem (Ezra 10:26).
event: In the course of the religious reform led by Ezra, he was included in the list of those who pledged to put away their marriages with foreign women and send them away (Ezra 10:26).

call: Father of Shelemiah (father of a royal officer)
introduce: Abdeel is a man recorded in Jeremiah 36:26 as the father of Shelemiah. The text does not record any deeds or office of Abdeel himself.
lifetime: Shelemiah the son of Abdeel was one of those whom King Jehoiakim commanded to seize the scribe Baruch and the prophet Jeremiah, but the LORD hid them (Jeremiah 36:26).
event: No event of Abdeel himself is recorded in the Bible; he is mentioned only as the father in the account that his son Shelemiah was commanded by the king to seize Baruch and Jeremiah (Jeremiah 36:26).

call: Mighty man of Gad who came to Ziklag
introduce: Attai is one of the Gadite mighty men who came back to David at the stronghold in the wilderness (1 Chronicles 12:8, 12:11).
lifetime: Attai belonged to the tribe of Gad and is recorded as the sixth among the Gadite mighty men who came back to David (1 Chronicles 12:9-11).
event: The Gadite mighty men who came back to David were trained for battle and able to handle shield and spear (1 Chronicles 12:8), and Attai is recorded as the sixth among them (1 Chronicles 12:11). These descendants of Gad became commanders of the army, the least of them over a hundred men and the greatest over a thousand (1 Chronicles 12:14).

introduce: Attai is a figure recorded as one of the children of Maacah, the wife of Rehoboam, the first king of the kingdom of Judah, and the daughter of Absalom.
lifetime: Attai is mentioned as one of Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith, whom Rehoboam had by his wife Maacah (2 Chronicles 11:20). Maacah was the daughter of Absalom, and Rehoboam loved her more than all his wives and concubines (2 Chronicles 11:21), and he appointed her son Abijah as chief, to be head among his brothers (2 Chronicles 11:22).

call: Father of the false prophet Hananiah
introduce: Azzur is a man recorded as the father of the prophet Hananiah in the time of Zedekiah (Jeremiah 28:1).
lifetime: Jeremiah 28:1 records that in the fifth month of the fourth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, the prophet Hananiah the son of Azzur, from Gibeon, spoke in the house of the LORD. There is no record of Azzur's own life.
event: In the biblical text no direct achievement or event of Azzur himself is described; he is mentioned only as the father of his son Hananiah in the course of the latter's delivering of false prophecy (Jeremiah 28:1).

introduce: Azzur is a man recorded in Ezekiel 11:1 as the father of Jaazaniah, a prince. The text does not record any deeds of Azzur himself.
lifetime: There is no record of Azzur's own life, and his son Jaazaniah was one of the twenty-five men whom Ezekiel saw in a vision at the east gate of the house of the LORD, called a prince of the people (Ezekiel 11:1).
event: His son Jaazaniah was introduced as a prince together with Pelatiah the son of Benaiah (Ezekiel 11:1), and these men were told that they were the men who devise iniquity and give wicked counsel in this city (Ezekiel 11:2). They said that the time to build houses is not near; this city is the cauldron, and we are the meat (Ezekiel 11:3). No event of Azzur himself is recorded.

call: The apostle James (son of Alphaeus), James the Less
meaning: one who takes hold of the heel
introduce: James the son of Alphaeus is one of the twelve apostles of Jesus who appear in the New Testament, and is also called James the Less to distinguish him from his namesake James the son of Zebedee.
lifetime: He was chosen and called by Jesus as one of the twelve apostles (Mark 3:18). He was active as an apostle during Jesus' public ministry, and after Jesus' ascension he is mentioned as one of the apostles who gathered in the upper room in Jerusalem (Acts 1:13).
event: He followed Jesus with the twelve apostles and was appointed as an apostle (Matthew 10:3), and afterward was with the other apostles in the upper room in Jerusalem (Acts 1:13), where they all with one accord devoted themselves to prayer (Acts 1:14).
character: Apart from the blood relationship information that he was the son of Alphaeus, the biblical record gives no depiction of his specific character or individual words and deeds.

call: James the brother of the Lord (author of the letter of James)
meaning: one who takes hold of the heel
introduce: A figure recorded as one of the brothers of Jesus of Nazareth, a leader of the early church in Jerusalem, and a major figure of the New Testament known as the author of the letter of James.
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of the brothers of Jesus, namely James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas (Matthew 13:55). During Jesus' public ministry he did not believe in Jesus (John 7:5), but the risen Jesus appeared to him personally (1 Corinthians 15:7). Afterward he worked with the apostles as a pillar of the church in Jerusalem (Galatians 2:9).
event: When Peter related how he had come out of prison, he asked that this be told to James and the brothers (Acts 12:17). At the council in Jerusalem, James gave his opinion that it was right not to trouble those among the Gentiles who turn to God, but to write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols, from sexual immorality, from what has been strangled, and from blood (Acts 15:13, 19-20). When Paul went in to James in Jerusalem, all the elders were present (Acts 21:18), and when Paul related one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles, James and the elders glorified God and urged Paul to carry out the rite of purification (Acts 21:19-24).
character: He was regarded as a devout man who strictly kept the law of Judaism (Acts 21:20), and worked as a leader with strong authority within the church (Galatians 1:19).

meaning: one who takes hold of the heel
introduce: This refers to James, who is mentioned in the New Testament as the father of the apostle Judas.
lifetime: In the Bible he is mentioned only as the father of the apostle Judas in Luke 6:16 and Acts 1:13, and there is no record of his life.
event: His son Judas (Thaddaeus) was called by Jesus Christ and fulfilled his mission as one of the twelve apostles (Luke 6:16, Acts 1:13).

meaning: one who took hold of the heel, a supplanter
introduce: A figure who appears in Matthew 1:15, the grandson of Eleazar and the son of Matthan, and the father of Joseph, who continues the line of descent in the genealogy of Jesus.
lifetime: Matthan the son of Eleazar fathered Jacob (Matthew 1:15), and Jacob fathered Joseph the husband of Mary (Matthew 1:16).
event: According to the biblical record, apart from the fact that, as a figure who makes up the genealogy of Jesus, Jacob fathered Joseph the husband of Mary, there is no record of any special social achievement or particular event that he carried out (Matthew 1:15-16).

call: Head of a priestly family after the return from exile
introduce: Jachin is a man recorded as one of the priests who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile. He appears as a priest in the lists of 1 Chronicles 9 and Nehemiah 11 (1 Chronicles 9:10; Nehemiah 11:10).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 9:10 records Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin side by side among the priests, and Nehemiah 11:10 records Jachin as a priest together with Jedaiah the son of Joiarib.
event: His name is entered in the list of the priests who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:10; Nehemiah 11:10). No specific event of Jachin himself is recorded in these verses.

call: Head of the twenty-first division of priests
introduce: Jachin is one of the heads of the priestly families determined by lot when David reorganized the priestly order. He is a man who was assigned a division of temple service for the performance of priestly duties.
lifetime: When King David, assisting the priests Zadok and Ahimelech, divided the twenty-four divisions that were to serve in the temple, Jachin was chosen as head of the twenty-first division (1 Chronicles 24:17).
event: When David divided the priestly families by lot in order to systematize the temple service, Jachin was recorded as the one in charge of the twenty-first turn (1 Chronicles 24:17).

call: Head of the twelfth division of priests
introduce: Jakim is the head of the priestly family who was in charge of the twelfth division among the twenty-four divisions of temple priests organized in the time of King David.
lifetime: King David classified the descendants of Aaron the priest into twenty-four groups according to the lines of Zadok and Ahimelech, and Jakim was designated by lot as the one in charge of the twelfth division, the twelfth in order (1 Chronicles 24:1, 24:12).
event: When David assigned the duties of the priests, Jakim was recorded as the twelfth among the divisions determined by lot (1 Chronicles 24:12). These divisions entered the house of the LORD to minister according to their ordinance (1 Chronicles 24:19). The Bible has no further record of what service he specifically performed afterward as head of his family (1 Chronicles 24:12).

introduce: Jarib is a man named as one of the leaders among the company that Ezra gathered by the river that flows to Ahava (Ezra 8:15-16).
lifetime: After Ezra gathered the company by the river that flows to Ahava and found that there were none of the sons of Levi among them (Ezra 8:15), he called all the leaders, and Jarib is on that list (Ezra 8:16). Ezra sent them to the region of Casiphia to go to Iddo, the leader of that place (Ezra 8:17).
event: He was among those sent, at Ezra's instruction, to tell Iddo and his brother, the Nethinim living in the region of Casiphia, to bring men to minister for the house of God (Ezra 8:17). By the good hand of God upon them, they brought a man of discretion from among the sons of Mahli the son of Levi, and Sherebiah with his sons and brothers, eighteen men, and others (Ezra 8:18).

call: Priest of the descendants of Jeshua
introduce: Jarib is a member of the community of Israel who returned from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem, a man belonging to a priestly family (Ezra 10:18).
lifetime: Ezra 10:18 records, as priests who had taken foreign women, the son of Jozadak of the descendants of Jeshua and his brothers Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah, and Jarib is one of them.
event: After the investigation by the heads of families commissioned by Ezra into those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:16-17), Jarib was entered in the list as one of the company of priests who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:18); they gave their hands in pledge to put away their wives, and for their guilt offered a ram of the flock as a guilt offering (Ezra 10:19).

introduce: Jabez is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, one of the persons recorded in 1 Chronicles 4. His name carries the meaning of pain, and the background information about him in the Bible is described in an extremely limited way.
lifetime: Jabez is mentioned as a descendant of Judah, and his mother named him Jabez, saying that she bore him in pain (1 Chronicles 4:9). Beyond this, there is no record of his specific year of birth or of his deeds after death.
event: Jabez prayed to God that He would enlarge his territory and keep him from harm so that he would be free from pain, and God granted what he asked (1 Chronicles 4:10). He was also esteemed as more honorable than his brothers (1 Chronicles 4:9).
character: The Bible esteems him as more honorable than his brothers (1 Chronicles 4:9). He also showed a faithful attitude in making supplication to God (1 Chronicles 4:10).

introduce: Japhia is one of the sons of King David recorded in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a man born in Jerusalem.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons born to David by the wives and concubines he took additionally in Jerusalem after he came up from Hebron (2 Samuel 5:13-15; 1 Chronicles 3:5-7). No specific dates or activities concerning his life are recorded in the Bible.

call: King of Hazor in the time of Deborah
introduce: Jabin was a king who ruled the region of Hazor in Canaan and who severely oppressed Israel for twenty years in the time of the judges. According to the biblical record, he reigned in Hazor, and the commander of his army was Sisera (Judges 4:2).
lifetime: Jabin was a Canaanite king who reigned in Hazor (Judges 4:2); after Ehud died, when the people of Israel again did evil in the sight of the LORD, the LORD sold them into his hand (Judges 4:1-2). With nine hundred chariots of iron he cruelly oppressed the people of Israel for twenty years (Judges 4:3). The LORD routed Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, with all his chariots and army before Barak (Judges 4:7, 15-16), and on that day God subdued Jabin the king of Canaan before the people of Israel (Judges 4:23); the hand of the people of Israel pressed harder and harder against Jabin until they destroyed him (Judges 4:24).
event: With nine hundred chariots of iron, Jabin cruelly oppressed the people of Israel for twenty years (Judges 4:3). His commander Sisera gathered his chariots and troops to the river Kishon (Judges 4:13) but was routed before Barak and fled, and was killed by the hand of Jael (Judges 4:15, 21), and God subdued Jabin the king of Canaan before the people of Israel (Judges 4:23). The people of Israel pressed harder and harder against Jabin until they destroyed him (Judges 4:24).
character: The Bible portrays Jabin as a symbol of power that oppresses and mistreats Israel, and presents him in particular as a central military figure who controlled the surrounding peoples with the cutting-edge weapon of the day, iron chariots (Judges 4:3). As king of Canaan he exercised strong rule, but he met the fate of being conquered by Israel, as Deborah had prophesied (Judges 4:9, 4:24).

introduce: Jashub was a man who lived in the community of Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile, one of the descendants of Bani (Ezra 10:29).
lifetime: Jashub is a man who entered his name in the list of the sons of Israel who had taken foreign women as wives after Ezra returned to Jerusalem (Ezra 10:29).
event: As a descendant of Bani, Jashub was recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:29, 10:44). This list corresponds to the one drawn up by investigation under the covenant to send away the foreign women and their children (Ezra 10:3, 10:12).

call: Son of Shaphan (elder of idolatry in the temple)
introduce: Jaazaniah is the son of Shaphan, and appears as one of the elders who secretly worshiped idols inside the temple in Jerusalem at the end of the kingdom of Judah.
lifetime: As the son of Shaphan, he is a man who stood among the seventy elders of the house of Israel at the scene of idol worship inside the temple in Jerusalem that Ezekiel saw in a vision (Ezekiel 8:11).
event: Together with the other elders, he stood in the temple before a wall on which were drawn images of beasts and creeping things, holding a censer, while the fragrance of the cloud of incense went up (Ezekiel 8:10-11). These elders are recorded as those who act in the dark, each in his room of images (Ezekiel 8:12).
character: Although a member of the religious leadership of the time, he held an exclusive view of faith, believing that the LORD does not see them and has forsaken the land (Ezekiel 8:12).

call: Son of Azzur (wicked prince of Judah)
introduce: Jaazaniah is a man mentioned as one of the princes and leading class of Jerusalem at the end of the kingdom of Judah. He is recorded as the son of Azzur, and in Ezekiel's vision he appears as one of the leaders who plot evil and devise wicked counsel in the city of Jerusalem.
lifetime: Jaazaniah was a prince who was active in the period before Jerusalem was destroyed by Babylon. He was one of the twenty-five men whom Ezekiel saw in a vision at the east gate of the house of the LORD, and he was singled out as one of those who devise iniquity and give wicked counsel in this city (Ezekiel 11:1-2).
event: He was shown to Ezekiel as one of the twenty-five men at the east gate of the house of the LORD, the gate facing east (Ezekiel 11:1). What these men said was that the time to build houses is not near; this city is the cauldron, and they are the meat (Ezekiel 11:3).
character: The Bible defines him as a man who gives wicked counsel to the people (Ezekiel 11:2). He is portrayed as a man who, being optimistic about the safety of Jerusalem, made wrong judgments and so led the people in the wrong direction as a leader (Ezekiel 11:3).

introduce: Jaasiel was a leader who was over the tribe of Benjamin in the time of David, the son of Abner, and is recorded as the chief of Benjamin.
lifetime: Jaasiel was recorded as the chief of Benjamin in the list of those over the tribes of Israel in the time of David (1 Chronicles 27:21). He is the son of Abner (1 Chronicles 27:21).
event: 1 Chronicles 27 lists those who were over the tribes of Israel (1 Chronicles 27:16-22), and Jaasiel is recorded among them as the chief of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 27:21).

call: Musician who carried the ark in praise
introduce: Jaaziel is a man who was appointed as one of the brothers of the Levites who sang in the course of moving the ark of God in the time of David.
lifetime: Jaaziel was of the lineage of the tribe of Levi, and was one of the brothers whom David commanded the heads of the Levites to appoint as singers when moving the ark of God (1 Chronicles 15:16, 15:18).
event: In the course of bringing up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, David had the Levites appoint as singers, after Heman, Asaph, and Ethan, brothers such as Zechariah, Ben, and Jaaziel (1 Chronicles 15:16-18).

introduce: A man from Gilead who is classified in the biblical record as one of the judges of Israel. He is known as one of the minor judges who governed Israel in the time of the judges, and a short record about him remains in Judges 10.
lifetime: Jair was a Gileadite who became a judge of Israel and judged Israel twenty-two years (Judges 10:3). He had thirty sons, who ruled thirty cities, and these cities, located in the land of Gilead, are called Havvoth-jair to this day (Judges 10:4). After he died, he was buried in Kamon (Judges 10:5).
event: No specific war or political event that occurred during his term as judge is described in the Bible. As his main achievement it is recorded that he had his thirty sons govern thirty cities in the region of Gilead, thereby extending the influence of his family (Judges 10:4). A historical feature is that the cities he ruled came to be called Havvoth-jair (Judges 10:4).
character: The biblical record gives no direct description of his personal character or attitude of faith. Yet from the record that he had his thirty sons ride thirty donkeys and rule the cities, it may be inferred that as a powerful local family they possessed considerable social standing and wealth (Judges 10:4).

introduce: Jair was a man of the tribe of Benjamin who, in the time of the Babylonian exile, is mentioned as the father of Mordecai, the cousin and helper of Esther.
lifetime: Jair is a man of the tribe of Benjamin recorded as the father of Mordecai. Since Mordecai is said to be the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, Jair belongs to a genealogy in which he is the son of Shimei and the grandson of Kish (Esther 2:5). The one recorded as having been carried away by Nebuchadnezzar is Mordecai (Esther 2:6).
character: Jair is recorded as the father who fathered Mordecai in a family of the tribe of Benjamin (Esther 2:5). In the biblical text no direct account of his personal character or specific deeds appears.

introduce: Jair was a descendant of the tribe of Manasseh who conquered the region east of the Jordan and took possession of part of that land. According to the biblical record, he is classified as a descendant of Machir the son of Manasseh.
lifetime: Jair, as a son of Manasseh, took the villages of the land of Gilead (Numbers 32:41). He called the villages he had taken east of the Jordan Havvoth-jair after his own name (Numbers 32:41, Deuteronomy 3:14). Joshua 13:29-30 records that the territory Moses gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh included all the towns of Jair in Bashan, sixty cities.
event: Jair took many villages of the region of Gilead (Numbers 32:41). He called the land he had taken Havvoth-jair collectively, a place name derived from his name (Deuteronomy 3:14). Joshua 13:29-30 records that from Mahanaim, all Bashan, that is, the whole kingdom of Og, and all the towns of Jair in Bashan, sixty cities, were the territory that Moses gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh.

call: Priest who blew the trumpet before the ark
introduce: Jahaziel is a priest who appears in 1 Chronicles 16:6, one of those appointed to blow the trumpets continually before the ark of God after David placed it in the tent.
lifetime: Jahaziel, as a priest, is one of those appointed to minister before the ark after David placed the ark of God in the tent he had pitched (1 Chronicles 16:1, 16:4, 16:6). This text gives no record of his lineage.
event: After David placed the ark in the tent and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, when he appointed Levites to minister before the ark, the priest Jahaziel, together with Benaiah, was assigned the duty of blowing the trumpets continually before the ark of the covenant of God (1 Chronicles 16:1-6).

introduce: Jahaziel is a descendant of the tribe of Levi who appears in the genealogy as the third son of Hebron.
lifetime: Jahaziel was born as a son of Hebron, the son of Kohath the son of Levi (1 Chronicles 23:12, 23:19). He is recorded as one of the descendants of Hebron who make up the genealogy of the Levites (1 Chronicles 24:23).
character: Apart from his genealogical position as the third son of Hebron, the biblical record makes no mention of any specific deeds or personal character of Jahaziel (1 Chronicles 23:19).

introduce: Jahaziel is a Levite who appears in 2 Chronicles, a descendant of Asaph and the son of Zechariah. When the allied forces of Moab and Ammon invaded Judah, he received the Spirit of God in the presence of King Jehoshaphat and prophesied the outcome of the battle.
lifetime: Jahaziel was the great-great-grandson of Mattaniah of the descendants of Asaph, the great-grandson of Jeiel, the grandson of Benaiah, and the son of Zechariah (2 Chronicles 20:14). He was active in the assembly of Judah in the time when King Jehoshaphat reigned (2 Chronicles 20:14).
event: When the Moabites and Ammonites came up to fight against Judah, Jahaziel prophesied in the midst of the assembly by the strength of the Spirit of the LORD (2 Chronicles 20:14). He declared that the battle was not Judah's but God's, that tomorrow they should go out against the enemy, but there would be no need to fight, and that they should take their positions, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD (2 Chronicles 20:15-17). Afterward Jehoshaphat and the people went out with the singers in front according to his prophecy, and the enemy forces actually destroyed one another and perished (2 Chronicles 20:21-23).
character: As a channel through whom the Spirit of God came, Jahaziel boldly conveyed God's message to the king and the people (2 Chronicles 20:14). He is portrayed as a man who won trust by proclaiming to the whole community of Judah in a time of crisis that they should not be afraid (2 Chronicles 20:15).

call: Father of Shecaniah (one who returned with Ezra)
introduce: Jahaziel is a man who appears in Ezra, recorded as the father of a head of a family among the descendants of Shecaniah who came up from Babylon with Ezra.
lifetime: In the list of the heads of families who came up from Babylon with Ezra in the time of King Artaxerxes, Jahaziel is recorded as the father of one of the descendants of Shecaniah (Ezra 8:1, 8:5). Jahaziel's own deeds are not recorded in the text.
event: Among those who came up from Babylon with Ezra, from the descendants of Shecaniah the son of Jahaziel came up with three hundred men (Ezra 8:5).

introduce: Jahath is the son of Libni, a descendant of Gershom of the tribe of Levi, and is a figure mentioned in the genealogy of the descendants of Gershom in 1 Chronicles 6.
lifetime: Jahath is a descendant of Gershom the son of Levi, the son of Libni who was born of Gershom, and the son of Jahath is Zimmah (1 Chronicles 6:20).
event: The Bible does not record any specific deeds of Jahath, and his name is entered as the son of Libni in the genealogy of the descendants of Gershom (1 Chronicles 6:20).

introduce: Jahath is a son of Shimei, a descendant of Gershom of the tribe of Levi, and is recorded as the head among the sons of Shimei (1 Chronicles 23:10-11).
lifetime: In the process of arranging the genealogies of the Levites in the time of King David, he was recorded as a son of Shimei, a descendant of Gershom. He was recorded first among the sons of Shimei and was their head (1 Chronicles 23:10-11).
event: When David in his last years reorganized the duties of the Levites, his name was stated as a person making up the family genealogy of the descendants of Gershom (1 Chronicles 23:10). He is mentioned as one of the sons of Shimei together with his brothers Zina (Ziza), Jeush, and Beriah, and since Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, they were counted as one family (1 Chronicles 23:10-11).

introduce: Jahath is a descendant of Izhar of the tribe of Levi, a man recorded in the genealogy of the divisions of the descendants of Levi in the time of David (1 Chronicles 24:22).
lifetime: Jahath is a grandson of Izhar the son of Kohath the son of Levi, a man recorded when David divided the divisions of the descendants of Levi (1 Chronicles 23:12, 24:22). As the son of Shelomoth the son of Izhar, he stands in the genealogy within his family (1 Chronicles 24:22).
event: When King David divided the duties of the Levites by lot for the temple service, Jahath was included in the division of the descendants of Izhar and his name was recorded (1 Chronicles 24:22).

call: Levite overseer of the temple repairs
introduce: Jahath is a Levite who appears in the latter half of Chronicles, belonging to the descendants of Merari, one of the overseers mobilized for King Josiah's temple repair project.
lifetime: Jahath was a Levite of the descendants of Merari, and is recorded as an overseer of the temple repair work in the eighteenth year of the reign of King Josiah (2 Chronicles 34:8, 34:12).
event: In the course of King Josiah's repairing and purifying of the temple in Jerusalem, the Levites Jahath and Obadiah took the role of overseeing the temple work (2 Chronicles 34:12).
character: Jahath is mentioned as a Levite with the ability to oversee the work wisely, and these men were also skilled with musical instruments (2 Chronicles 34:12).

기타관계: Obadiah#4598(fellow worker of the tribe of Levi)

call: High priest at the end of the Persian period
introduce: Jaddua is the son of Jonathan, and in the priestly genealogy of the book of Nehemiah he is the one in the line running Joiada, Jonathan, Jaddua (Nehemiah 12:10-11).
lifetime: Jaddua is recorded as the son of Jonathan the son of Joiada (Nehemiah 12:11). In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites were recorded in the book (Nehemiah 12:22).
event: Nehemiah 12:22 says that in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites were recorded in the book, and the priests too in the reign of Darius the Persian. No specific deeds of Jaddua himself are recorded in the text.

call: Son of Jared (the righteous man who was taken up)
introduce: The son of Jared and father of Methuselah, who by the genealogy of the Bible is the seventh generation from Adam. He is classed as one with the unique record in human history of walking with God without seeing death and being taken.
lifetime: Enoch fathered Methuselah at the age of 65, and afterward walked with God 300 years and fathered sons and daughters (Genesis 5:21-22). The total of his days was 365 years; he walked with God while he stayed in the world, and then he was no more, for God took him (Genesis 5:23-24).
event: There is a record that Enoch was taken so that he did not see death (Hebrews 11:5). He prophesied about the coming of God to execute judgment on all the ungodly deeds that the ungodly had committed and on all the harsh words that ungodly sinners had spoken against the Lord (Jude 1:14-15).
character: The Bible states twice that he walked with God (Genesis 5:22, 5:24). Before he was taken he was commended as having pleased God, and he is cited as an example of the principle that whoever would draw near to God must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him (Hebrews 11:5-6).

call: Ancestor of Asaph in the line of Gershom
introduce: Ethan is a man belonging to the genealogy of the descendants of Gershom of the tribe of Levi, recorded as an ancestor of the house of Asaph, who later, in the time of King David, was entrusted with the ministry of praise in the temple.
lifetime: Ethan is a descendant of Gershom, the son of Levi, and is the son of Zimmah and the father of Adaiah (1 Chronicles 6:42). He appears as a genealogical link in the line of the descendants of Gershom down to Asaph (1 Chronicles 6:43). That Zerah was a son of Adaiah does not appear in the Korean Revised Version (Gaeyeok Hangeul), but it is found in the Hebrew text.
event: In the biblical record no specific deeds or particular events of Ethan himself appear, and he is mentioned only within the genealogical list of 1 Chronicles 6 as one who connects ancestor and descendant (1 Chronicles 6:42).

call: Head musician of the line of Merari (Jeduthun)
introduce: Ethan, a descendant of Merari of the tribe of Levi, was a man in charge of praise and instrumental music in the temple in the time of David. There is a view that he is the same person as Jeduthun, who appears in the same duty of praise in Chronicles, and he served as one of the chief leaders of praise in the time of David.
lifetime: As a Levite, he carried out the ministry of praise in the temple at David's command. He is the son of Kishi, a descendant of Merari (1 Chronicles 6:44), and is mentioned as one of the three leaders of praise whom David appointed (1 Chronicles 25:1). For the service of the temple he was organized with his sons as a choir and served (1 Chronicles 25:3).
event: David set apart from among the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun those who were to serve by prophesying with lyres, harps, and cymbals (1 Chronicles 25:1). Ethan was assigned the duty of praising God by sounding bronze cymbals (1 Chronicles 15:19), and when the ark of the covenant was moved to Jerusalem he was appointed together with Heman and Asaph (1 Chronicles 15:17). Also, at the installation of the ark in Solomon's temple, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and brothers stood east of the altar holding cymbals, harps, and lyres (2 Chronicles 5:12).
character: He is also described as a prophet in the Bible and was given the title of the king's seer (2 Chronicles 35:15). Through his musical talent he showed the leadership to organize the worship of the community and establish order in it (1 Chronicles 25:3). He is also called by the name Jeduthun and contributed to establishing the system of temple praise (1 Chronicles 16:41).

기타관계: Uzziel#4421(fellow worker of the tribe of Levi)

call: Son of Zerah of the tribe of Judah
introduce: Ethan is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, the son of Zerah the son of Judah and the father of Azariah (1 Chronicles 2:6, 2:8).
lifetime: Ethan is the son of Zerah the son of Judah, a brother of Zimri, Heman, Calcol, and Dara (1 Chronicles 2:6), and the father of Azariah (1 Chronicles 2:8).
event: The Bible records no specific deeds of this Ethan, and his name is entered in the genealogy of the descendants of Zerah of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:6, 2:8).

call: Levite who distributed the holy offerings in Hezekiah's time
introduce: Eden is a Levite who appears in 2 Chronicles in the Old Testament, one of those who, in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah, held an office in the cities of the priests under Kore and distributed the holy offerings to their brothers by divisions.
lifetime: During the religious reform of Hezekiah king of Judah, he held an office in the cities of the priests under Kore, the Levite keeper of the East Gate (2 Chronicles 31:14-15). Eden, together with Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, faithfully distributed to their brothers by divisions, old and young alike (2 Chronicles 31:15).
event: When the gifts offered to God and the most holy things were distributed in the time of Hezekiah, Eden, under Kore, together with Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, held an office in the cities of the priests and distributed to their brothers by divisions, old and young alike (2 Chronicles 31:14-15).

introduce: Eder is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, a son of Beriah and a member of a family among the descendants of Benjamin belonging to the class of chiefs (1 Chronicles 8:15).
lifetime: Eder is recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin as a son of Beriah (1 Chronicles 8:15-16), and is mentioned as one of the chiefs who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).
event: As one of the sons of Beriah, Eder has his name entered in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin and was included in the list of the heads who, as chiefs throughout their generations, lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:15-16, 8:28).

introduce: A man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah as a descendant of Shelah the son of Judah, recorded as the father of Lecah.
lifetime: He is recorded as a descendant of Shelah the son of Judah and is the father of Lecah (1 Chronicles 4:21).
event: 1 Chronicles 4:21 lists together, among the descendants of Shelah, Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the families of the house of linen workers, that is, the house of Ashbea. No specific deeds of Er himself are recorded in the text.

call: Father of Joshua (an ancestor of Jesus)
introduce: Er is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in Luke, recorded as the son of the ancestor Joshua, who appears with him in the genealogy, and the father of Elmadam (Luke 3:28-29).
lifetime: In the genealogy of Luke, Er is recorded as the son of the ancestor Joshua, and the line continued through his son Elmadam (Luke 3:28-29).

introduce: Ephah is a man who appears in 1 Chronicles 2 in the Old Testament, a son of Jahdai, one of the families of the tribe of Judah. As a descendant in the genealogy of Jahdai, he has his name entered in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
lifetime: As a son of Jahdai, he belongs to the family genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:47). Beyond that, the Bible contains no record of his birth or of the specifics of his life.

introduce: Ephah is the man recorded first among the sons of Midian, the son whom Abraham had by his concubine Keturah (Genesis 25:2, 25:4).
lifetime: Ephah is recorded as a son of Midian, the son whom Abraham fathered by his concubine Keturah, and together with the other sons of Midian he is called a descendant of Keturah (Genesis 25:1-2, 25:4).
event: In Isaiah 60:6 the name of Ephah appears in the prophecy that "the young camels of Midian and Ephah will cover your land." In the same verse, those who come bringing gold and frankincense and proclaiming the praises of the LORD are the people of Sheba (Isaiah 60:6).

call: Son of Joktan (ancestor of an Arabian tribe)
introduce: A man who appears as a son of Joktan in the genealogy of Shem in Genesis 10. He is recorded as Obal in Genesis 10:28 and as Ebal in 1 Chronicles 1:22 (as spelled in the Korean Revised Version).
lifetime: He is a grandson of Eber and is recorded as one of the thirteen sons of Joktan (Genesis 10:25-29).
event: No specific achievement or historical event of his is recorded in the Bible (Genesis 10:26-29).

call: Son of Abihail (chief of the tribe of Gad)
introduce: Eber is a man who appears in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a resident of the region of Bashan belonging to the tribe of Gad, and a son of Abihail.
lifetime: He is a man of the tribe of Gad recorded as one of the seven sons of Abihail (1 Chronicles 5:13-14).
event: He is recorded as one of the seven kinsmen of the families (Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber) of the Gadite chiefs Joel, Shapham, Jaanai, and Shaphat, and the Gadites lived in Bashan and Gilead and their villages (1 Chronicles 5:12-13, 5:16).

introduce: Eber is a son of Elpaal of the tribe of Benjamin, a man recorded as one of the sons of Elpaal together with Misham and Shemed (1 Chronicles 8:12).
lifetime: He was born as a son of Elpaal, and Misham and Shemed are his brothers (1 Chronicles 8:12).
event: It is recorded that among the sons of Elpaal, Shemed built Ono and Lod with its villages, and no specific deeds of Eber himself are recorded (1 Chronicles 8:12).

introduce: Eber is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as one of the sons of Shashak (1 Chronicles 8:22-25).
lifetime: Eber is recorded as one of the sons of Shashak, together with Ishpan, Eliel, Abdon, Zichri, Hanan, Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah, Iphdeiah, and Penuel (1 Chronicles 8:22-25), and the men in this genealogy were all heads of families, chiefs throughout their generations, who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).

call: Priest of the house of Amok
introduce: Eber is a man of a priestly family recorded in Nehemiah 12:20 as the head of the house of Amok.
lifetime: Eber is recorded as the one representing the house of Amok among those who were heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:20).
event: In the list of the heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim, his name appears as "of Amok, Eber" (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:20).

introduce: Epher is a man recorded as one of the five sons of Midian, whom Abraham had by his concubine Keturah (Genesis 25:4).
lifetime: He was born as a son of Midian, the son Abraham obtained through Keturah, and is mentioned together with the other sons of Midian, Ephah, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah (Genesis 25:4).

call: Son of Ezra of the tribe of Judah
introduce: Epher is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a son of Ezra. He is a figure who makes up part of the genealogy of the tribe of Judah recorded in 1 Chronicles.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons of Ezra: Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon (1 Chronicles 4:17).
event: The Bible has no record of what Epher did (1 Chronicles 4:17).

call: Head of the half-tribe of Manasseh
introduce: Epher, who appears in 1 Chronicles 5:24, is one of the seven heads of the half-tribe of Manasseh.
lifetime: Epher is recorded as a head of the descendants of the half-tribe of Manasseh, who extended from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon (1 Chronicles 5:23-24). The heads were Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel (1 Chronicles 5:24).
event: Epher was recorded as one of the heads famed for their valor (1 Chronicles 5:24). Beyond this, nothing is stated in the Bible about historical events or specific achievements.

call: Son of Jonathan (head of the families who returned with Ezra)
