introduce: Ebed is the son of Jonathan, a head of the descendants of Adin among the heads of families who came up from Babylon with Ezra in the time of King Artaxerxes (Ezra 8:1, 8:6).
lifetime: Ebed is recorded as the son of Jonathan among the descendants of Adin, and is one of the heads of families who came up from Babylon with Ezra while King Artaxerxes was on the throne (Ezra 8:1, 8:6). The men with him numbered fifty (Ezra 8:6).
event: All the record there is of him is that he is recorded as the head of the descendants of Adin among the heads of families who came up from Babylon with Ezra (Ezra 8:1, 8:6).

call: The tribe of Ephraim and its inheritance
introduce: Ephraim, born to Joseph and the Egyptian woman Asenath as the second son, is the ancestor of the tribe of Ephraim, one of the twelve tribes of Israel (Genesis 41:52). In the Bible, Ephraim sometimes refers to the individual, but the name is also used broadly for the tribe he formed or for the region where that tribe lived.
lifetime: He was born while Joseph, the son of Jacob, was in Egypt, and Joseph named his second son Ephraim, saying that God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction (Genesis 41:52). Jacob claimed Ephraim and Manasseh as his own (Genesis 48:5), and in blessing them he laid his right hand on the head of the younger son Ephraim and his left hand on the head of the firstborn Manasseh (Genesis 48:14). Manasseh and Ephraim, the descendants of Joseph, received their inheritance, and the descendants of Ephraim had a border according to their families (Joshua 16:4-5).
event: From Jacob, Ephraim received a prophetic blessing that his younger brother would be greater than Manasseh and that his descendants would become a multitude of nations (Genesis 48:19). In later times the name Ephraim also referred to that tribe: in the Song of Deborah it says, "from Ephraim those whose root is in Amalek" (Judges 5:14), and in the days of Ahaz king of Judah, at the news that "Aram is in league with Ephraim," the heart of the house of David and of his people shook (Isaiah 7:1-2).

call: Priest at the dedication of the wall
introduce: Ezer is a man who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, and is recorded together with the priests who held trumpets.
lifetime: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, Ezer is recorded as one of those who were with the priests holding trumpets, among those standing in the house of God (Nehemiah 12:40-42).
event: After the two companies giving thanks took their stand in the house of God, Ezer was there with Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, and Elam, and the singers sang loudly (Nehemiah 12:42).

introduce: Ezer is a man recorded as the father of Hushah, a descendant of Hur of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:4).
lifetime: In 1 Chronicles 4:4, Ezer is recorded as "Ezer the father of Hushah," and is introduced together with Penuel as a descendant of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, the father of Bethlehem (1 Chronicles 4:4).

call: Chief mighty man of Gad at Ziklag
introduce: Ezer is a man recorded in 1 Chronicles 12 as the chief of the Gadite mighty men who came back to David (1 Chronicles 12:8-9).
lifetime: Ezer is recorded as the chief of the mighty men among the Gadites who came back to David at the stronghold in the wilderness (1 Chronicles 12:8-9).
event: The Gadites, Ezer among them, were all mighty men, trained for battle and able to handle shield and spear; their faces were like the faces of lions and they were as swift as gazelles on the mountains, and Ezer was their chief (1 Chronicles 12:8-9).

introduce: A man who took part in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, the son of Jeshua and a ruler who governed Mizpah.
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, in the course of repairing the wall of Jerusalem, he took charge of his own section and took part in the work (Nehemiah 3:19).
event: As the ruler of Mizpah he repaired a part of the wall, and that section reached to the armory at the turning of the wall (Nehemiah 3:19).

call: Son of Seir (chief of the Horites)
introduce: Ezer is a figure who appears in Genesis, a son of Seir and classified as one of the chiefs of the Horites.
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of the sons of Seir among the descendants of the Horites (Genesis 36:21). He belonged to the descendants of Seir who lived in the land of Edom, and together with his brothers he served as a chief of the Horites (Genesis 36:20-21).
event: As a chief of the Horite clans who lived in the land of Edom, he entered his name in the list (Genesis 36:21). Among the chiefs of the Horites he is recorded as "the chief Dishon, the chief Ezer, the chief Dishan" (Genesis 36:29-30).

introduce: Ezbon is a man of the tribe of Benjamin who appears in the genealogy of the family of Benjamin. He is recorded as one of the sons of Bela.
lifetime: Ezbon is mentioned as one of the five sons born to Bela the son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:7). He is included among those classed as heads in the family of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:7).

introduce: Ehud is a man recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles 7, the son of Bilhan the son of Jediael (1 Chronicles 7:10). He is a different person from the judge Ehud the son of Gera (Judges 3:15).
lifetime: The son of Jediael was Bilhan, and the sons of Bilhan are recorded as Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar (1 Chronicles 7:10). These sons of Jediael are recorded as heads of their fathers' houses and mighty men of valor (1 Chronicles 7:11).
event: No deeds of Ehud himself are recorded. Among the descendants of Jediael, to which he belonged, those fit for military service were counted as 17,200 men (1 Chronicles 7:11).

introduce: An Ephraimite who lived in Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim, the son of Jeroham and the father of Samuel (1 Samuel 1:1, 1:19-20).
lifetime: In the time of the priest Eli he lived in Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim, and every year he went up to Shiloh to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of hosts (1 Samuel 1:1-3). He had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah, and when Hannah bore no children, he said to the weeping Hannah, "Am I not more to you than ten sons?" (1 Samuel 1:2, 1:8). After Hannah weaned Samuel, she took him up to Shiloh and gave the child to the LORD (1 Samuel 1:24-28). Afterward too he went up with his wife every year to offer the sacrifice, and the priest Eli blessed him and his wife, and the LORD gave Hannah three more sons and two daughters (1 Samuel 2:19-21).
event: He kept the custom of going up to Shiloh every year to sacrifice to the LORD (1 Samuel 1:3). On the day of sacrifice he loved Hannah and gave her a double portion (1 Samuel 1:5), and when Hannah was distressed he comforted her (1 Samuel 1:8). When Hannah said that once the child was weaned she would bring him and present him to the LORD, Elkanah said, "Do what seems best to you … only may the LORD establish his word" (1 Samuel 1:22-23).
character: Although his wife Hannah had borne no child, he loved her deeply and showed a kindness in giving her a double portion and comforting her (1 Samuel 1:5). He also had an accepting attitude within the household, as in respecting his wife's vow and allowing her to carry it out (1 Samuel 1:23). He was a faithful man who carried out his religious duty every year at the appointed time (1 Samuel 1:3).

call: Levite of the line of Kohath
introduce: Elkanah is a Levite of the descendants of Kohath who appears in the genealogy of Heman in 1 Chronicles 6; he is the son of Mahath and the father of Zuph (1 Chronicles 6:35). He is a different person both from Elkanah the father of Samuel (1 Chronicles 6:34) and from Elkanah the son of Joel who fathered Amasai (1 Chronicles 6:36).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 6:35 records, 'Zuph was the son of Elkanah, Elkanah the son of Mahath, and Mahath the son of Amasai.'

call: Father of Asa (ancestor of the Netophathites)
introduce: Elkanah is a Levite who appears in 1 Chronicles 9, recorded as the father of Asa and the grandfather of Berechiah (1 Chronicles 9:16).
lifetime: Elkanah is recorded as the father of Asa. His grandson Berechiah was one of the Levites and lived in the villages of the Netophathites (1 Chronicles 9:16).
event: Nothing is recorded about any specific duty he performed or any historical event. His name appears only in the introduction of Berechiah as "the son of Asa, the son of Elkanah" (1 Chronicles 9:16).

call: Korahite (mighty man at Ziklag / gatekeeper of the ark)
introduce: A mighty man of the Korahites mentioned in 1 Chronicles 12, one of those who joined David when he stayed at Ziklag to escape from Saul.
lifetime: He is one of the mighty men who came to David while David was hiding at Ziklag from the presence of Saul (1 Chronicles 12:1). He is included in the list of those who came to David as Korahites (1 Chronicles 12:6).
event: At Ziklag he was with David, and showed military ability, skilled with the bow and able to sling stones or shoot arrows with either hand (1 Chronicles 12:1-2). Although of the tribe of Benjamin, a kinsman of Saul, he supported David and joined the ranks of the mighty men with him (1 Chronicles 12:2).
character: He was a man with skilled fighting ability, proficient with the bow and able to sling stones or shoot arrows with both the right and the left hand (1 Chronicles 12:2). As a Korahite he was esteemed as a brave warrior within David's military organization (1 Chronicles 12:6).

introduce: A man who held the office of chief minister in the time of King Ahaz of the kingdom of Judah. According to the biblical record, he is a high official whose name is recorded together with Maaseiah the king's son and Azrikam the governor of the palace (2 Chronicles 28:7).
lifetime: He held the office of chief minister in the time of Ahaz king of Judah (2 Chronicles 28:7). His death is recorded in the period when Pekah the son of Remaliah killed 120,000 mighty men in Judah in one day (2 Chronicles 28:6-7).
event: Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the governor of the palace, and Elkanah the chief minister (2 Chronicles 28:7). The specific place where Elkanah was killed is not recorded in the Bible.

call: Father of Shimei (father of Solomon's officer)
introduce: Ela is the father of Shimei, one of the twelve officers who governed the administrative districts of Israel in the time of King Solomon.
lifetime: Shimei the son of Ela was appointed, as one of King Solomon's twelve officers, over Benjamin, the territory of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Kings 4:18).

call: Fourth king of the northern kingdom of Israel
introduce: The fourth king of the northern kingdom of Israel and the son of Baasha, who reigned for about two years, from 886 to 885 BC.
lifetime: After his father Baasha died he succeeded him as king (1 Kings 16:6), and in the second year of his reign, while he was drunk in Tirzah, he was killed in a conspiracy by his servant Zimri (1 Kings 16:8-10).
event: While he was drinking and getting drunk in the house of Arza, the steward of the palace, Zimri, the commander of half of the chariots, conspired against him and killed him (1 Kings 16:9-10). After his death Zimri made himself king and killed every male of the house of Baasha, wiping out that family completely (1 Kings 16:11-12).

introduce: Elah is a man recorded as the father of Hoshea, the nineteenth king of the northern kingdom of Israel. In the biblical record he appears as the person who explains the lineage of Hoshea, who was king (2 Kings 15:30).
lifetime: Elah is mentioned as the father of Hoshea, king of the northern kingdom of Israel (2 Kings 15:30).

introduce: A son of Caleb of the tribe of Judah, a man mentioned within Caleb's family.
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of Caleb's children and belongs to Caleb's family tree (1 Chronicles 4:15).

introduce: Elah is a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, one of those who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: Elah is recorded as the son of Uzzi, the grandson of Michri (1 Chronicles 9:8). His name is entered in the list of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:3, 9:8).
event: His name was recorded in the list of those who lived in Jerusalem after they were carried captive to Babylon and returned (1 Chronicles 9:1-3, 9:8). The Bible does not record any office or deeds of his.

introduce: Elnathan is one of the leaders (heads of families) of the community that returned to Jerusalem with Ezra after the Babylonian exile. He is recorded as one of those whom Ezra called by the river that flows to Ahava and sent to Iddo, the leader of the region of Casiphia.
lifetime: Elnathan is a man of the class of heads of families who accompanied Ezra when he prepared the second return from Babylon to Jerusalem (Ezra 8:16). While they were staying by the river that flows to Ahava during the journey of return, he was called by Ezra and sent to Iddo, the leader of the region of Casiphia, and was instructed to convey to Iddo and his brothers, the Nethinim, the message to bring men to minister for the house of God (Ezra 8:15-17).
event: At Ezra's command Elnathan was sent to Iddo, the leader of the region of Casiphia, and to his brothers, the Nethinim, and took part in conveying the message to bring men to minister for the house of God (Ezra 8:16-17). By the good hand of God upon them, they brought a man of discretion from among the sons of Levi, and Sherebiah with his sons and brothers, eighteen men, and Hashabiah and Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari with his brothers and sons, twenty men, and 220 of the Nethinim (Ezra 8:18-20).
character: According to the biblical record, Elnathan is portrayed as a man with the leadership for Ezra to trust him and entrust him with an important mission. He was a leader with the practical ability to carry out at once the administrative needs of the community (Ezra 8:16-17).

introduce: Elasah is the son of Shaphan the scribe of the kingdom of Judah, and a man who carried out the role of delivering the letter that Jeremiah sent to the people of Judah who had been taken captive to Babylon.
lifetime: Elasah is the son of Shaphan (Jeremiah 29:3). He is recorded as one of those whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, together with Gemariah the son of Hilkiah (Jeremiah 29:3).
event: Together with Gemariah, Elasah was entrusted with the letter that Jeremiah sent from Jerusalem to the remaining elders among the exiles who had been carried to Babylon, and to the priests, the prophets, and all the people (Jeremiah 29:1, 29:3).

introduce: Elam appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin. He is a son of Shashak and one of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:24-25).
lifetime: Elam is recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin as a son of Shashak (1 Chronicles 8:24-25). The men recorded in this genealogy were all heads of families, chiefs according to their generations, and they lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).

call: Son of Meshelemiah (gatekeeper of the temple)
introduce: Elam is the fifth son of Meshelemiah, a Korahite and gatekeeper, and a man who served as a gatekeeper of the temple in the time of David.
lifetime: Elam was born as a son of Meshelemiah the Korahite (1 Chronicles 26:1-3). In the reign of King David he was appointed a gatekeeper of the temple and carried out his duties (1 Chronicles 26:1).
event: Together with his other brothers he belonged to the divisions of the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:1-3). The duty of guarding the gates was assigned by casting lots for each gate, by families, small and great alike (1 Chronicles 26:13). At that time his father Meshelemiah (Shelemiah) received the east gate, and his son Zechariah received the north gate (1 Chronicles 26:14), but the gate that fell to Elam himself is not recorded in the Bible. It is recorded that Meshelemiah's sons and brothers, eighteen men, were capable men (1 Chronicles 26:9).
character: The Bible describes Elam and his brothers as mighty men of valor, and records that they were men with the ability to carry out the duties assigned to them (1 Chronicles 26:6-9).

call: Ancestor of a family returning with Zerubbabel (1)
introduce: Elam is recorded as one of the ancestors of the Israelite families who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile. There are several namesakes in the Bible, and here Elam is treated as the representative ancestor of the returning family mentioned in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah.
lifetime: The descendants of Elam were among those who returned from the land of Babylon to Jerusalem and Judah after the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:7). The list of Elam's descendants appears again in the genealogy of those who returned with Ezra (Ezra 8:7). The list of returnees in Nehemiah 7 likewise records the same 1,254 descendants of Elam (Nehemiah 7:12).
event: 1,254 descendants of Elam returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:7). Later, at Ezra's second return, Jeshaiah the son of Athaliah, of the descendants of Elam, returned together with seventy men who were with him (Ezra 8:7). In the time of Ezra, Shecaniah the son of Jehiel, of the descendants of Elam, confessed to Ezra the sin of having taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:2). Also, Elam was included in the list of the heads of the people who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14).

introduce: Elam is the name of a family in the list of the returnees from the Babylonian exile, and also a man identified as the ancestor of that family. In the biblical record, this name refers to a particular individual and at the same time to the family community that includes his descendants.
lifetime: The descendants of "the other Elam" are included in the list of those who finished the Babylonian exile and returned to Jerusalem and Judah under the leadership of Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:31, Nehemiah 7:34). Their number is 1,254 in the record of Ezra (Ezra 2:31), and also 1,254 in the record of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 7:34).
event: These descendants of Elam, called "the other Elam" in Ezra 2:31 and "the rest of Elam" in Nehemiah 7:34, are recorded separately, distinguished from the descendants of Elam recorded earlier (Ezra 2:7, Nehemiah 7:12), and their number is the same, 1,254 (Ezra 2:31, Nehemiah 7:34). The Bible does not explain the relationship between the two families of Elam.

call: Ancestor of a family returning with Ezra
introduce: The Elam mentioned in Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7 is the name of the ancestor who represents the descendants who returned from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem. Although men with the same name appear several times in the Bible, Elam as the ancestor of a returning family appears as a key marker in the community's census and the registration of genealogies.
lifetime: He is mentioned as the ancestor of the descendants of Elam who returned to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:7). His descendants are included in the list of those who came back from Babylon to Jerusalem, and the number of descendants of Elam who returned at that time was 1,254 (Nehemiah 7:12).
event: Among the descendants of Elam, Jeshaiah the son of Athaliah returned with Ezra together with seventy men who were with him (Ezra 8:7). Also, six of the descendants of Elam, Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah, were recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:26). Later, in the time of Nehemiah, the name of Elam is recorded in the list of the heads of the people who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:14).

introduce: He appears in the lists of the Jews in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah, and refers to the ancestor of the descendants of Elam, one of the families of those who returned from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: He is recorded as the ancestor of the 1,254 descendants of Elam who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:7). Later, at Ezra's second return, seventy men of the descendants of Elam accompanied him (Ezra 8:7).
event: Shecaniah, one of the descendants of Elam, confessed to Ezra the wrongdoing of the people of Israel who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:2). Also, Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah, descendants of Elam, were included in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives and then divorced them and sent them away (Ezra 10:26). In the time of Nehemiah, Elam, one of the representatives of the descendants of Elam, put his name on the list of leaders who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14).

introduce: He is a man who returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile and took part in the sealing at the renewal of the covenant under Nehemiah. He is classed as a leader-level figure, distinguished from the namesakes who appear in the records of Ezra and Nehemiah.
lifetime: After returning from the Babylonian captivity, he was included in the group of leaders working for the restoration of the Jerusalem community (Nehemiah 10:14). He was one of the chiefs who put the seal on the covenant document when the people of Israel swore to keep the law of the LORD (Nehemiah 10:1).
event: By signing and sealing the covenant document drawn up under Nehemiah, he joined in the formal pledge to keep the law, to care for the temple, and to preserve the religious purity of the community (Nehemiah 10:1). This shows that within the returned community he held a position of leadership with social and religious responsibility (Nehemiah 10:14).

call: Priest at the dedication of the wall
introduce: Elam is recorded as a priestly family who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, or as the man who represents that family.
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, when the two companies giving thanks took their stand in the house of God, he is recorded as one who was there with Maaseiah, Shemaiah, and the others, in the place where the priests held trumpets (Nehemiah 12:40-42).
event: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, Elam was there with Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, and Ezer, and the singers sang loudly under the direction of Jezrahiah (Nehemiah 12:42). The Bible does not record any specific role Elam had.

call: Second son of Zebulun (ancestor of the Elonite clan)
introduce: Elon is the second of the three sons of Zebulun, a son of Jacob, and the ancestor of the Elonite clan within the tribe of Zebulun.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons of Zebulun who went down to Egypt with Jacob (Genesis 46:14). Later, his descendants were recorded as "the Elonite clan" among the clans of the descendants of Zebulun at the census in the wilderness (Numbers 26:26).
event: He gave rise to the Elonite clan bearing his name, which is mentioned as a unit of the tribe of Zebulun at the census of Israel (Numbers 26:26).

introduce: Elon is a figure mentioned in the Book of Judges in the Old Testament, a judge of Israel who followed Ibzan. He is recorded as a Zebulunite (Judges 12:11).
lifetime: As a man of the tribe of Zebulun, he was appointed judge and governed Israel for ten years (Judges 12:11). After finishing his term as judge, he died and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun (Judges 12:12).
event: The period during which he served as a judge of Israel was ten years in all (Judges 12:11). According to the biblical record, nothing is recorded about any specific war or political event during the time he governed Israel.

call: Son of Becher of the tribe of Benjamin
meaning: My eyes look up to you, Lord
introduce: Elioenai is a man of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as one of the sons of Becher. He is a figure in the genealogy that appears in 1 Chronicles 7:8.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Becher of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:8). His family line continues the genealogy of the descendants of Becher, one of the subdivisions of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:8).
event: In the biblical record he is listed together with the other sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth (1 Chronicles 7:8). They are recorded as all being heads of their families and mighty men of valor (1 Chronicles 7:9).

call: Priest in the time of Ezra (the same person as in Nehemiah 12:41)
meaning: My eyes look up to you, Lord
introduce: Elioenai is a priest who was active in the Persian period after the return from exile, and a man identified in the process led by Ezra and Nehemiah of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem and restoring the rituals of the temple.
lifetime: In the time of Ezra he is recorded as a descendant of Pashhur in the list of priests who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:22). Later, he is mentioned as one of the priests who held trumpets at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 12:41).
event: In the time of Ezra he was recorded as one of the descendants of Pashhur among those who had taken foreign women, and they all pledged, giving their hand, to send away their wives (Ezra 10:19, 10:22). Also, after Nehemiah divided the great company giving thanks into two companies and had them proceed in procession on the wall, he was recorded as one of the priests who held trumpets together with the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, and others (Nehemiah 12:31, 12:41).

meaning: My eyes look up to you, Lord
introduce: Elioenai is one of the descendants of Zattu, a man recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:27).
lifetime: In the time of Ezra he is recorded as one of the descendants of Zattu in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:27).
event: Among the descendants of Zattu, Elioenai was recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women, together with Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza (Ezra 10:27). All the men on this list pledged, giving their hand, to send away their wives (Ezra 10:19).

call: Son of Rapha (Rephaiah), father of Azel
introduce: Eleasah is a man who appears in the genealogy of the house of Saul of the tribe of Benjamin, a descendant of Merib-baal the son of Jonathan, and the son of Raphah the son of Binea (1 Chronicles 8:34-37).
lifetime: Eleasah is recorded as the son of Raphah the son of Binea and the father of Azel (1 Chronicles 8:37). In 1 Chronicles 9:43, the son of Binea is recorded as Rephaiah, his son as Eleasah, and his son as Azel (1 Chronicles 9:43).

call: Son of Dodo (one of David's Three mighty men)
introduce: Eleazar the son of Dodo is classed as one of the three mighty men with the greatest military strength in David's army. He is recorded as an Ahohite, and during David's reign he made his name great by his outstanding feats of arms in times of military crisis.
lifetime: Eleazar, as one of the three mighty men who were with David, helped David and took part in the battle against the Philistines (2 Samuel 23:9). Among David's mighty men he was acknowledged as one of the chief three and held a key position in David's military organization (1 Chronicles 11:12).
event: When the Philistines gathered for battle, the men of Israel withdrew, but Eleazar, together with the mighty men, defied them, went out, and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and clung to the sword (2 Samuel 23:9-10). That day the LORD brought about a great victory, and the people came back after him only to plunder (2 Samuel 23:10). When the Philistines gathered at Pas-dammim and attacked, the people fled, but they took their stand in the middle of the barley field, defended the field, and killed the Philistines, and the LORD saved them with a great salvation (1 Chronicles 11:13-14).
character: On the battlefield he showed a tough endurance, resisting to the end without retreating (2 Samuel 23:10). He is portrayed as a man who combined determination and courage, holding his ground even in the urgent situation when others were withdrawing (1 Chronicles 11:13).

introduce: A man of the house of Merari among the descendants of Levi, the son of Mahli, whose name is entered in the genealogy of the descendants of Merari.
lifetime: Eleazar was the son of Mahli the son of Merari (1 Chronicles 23:21), and he died without sons, leaving only daughters (1 Chronicles 23:22).
event: His daughters were married to the sons of Kish, their kinsmen (1 Chronicles 23:22).

call: Priest at the dedication of the wall
introduce: He is one of the men who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, and his name is recorded together with Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Uzzi, and others (Nehemiah 12:42).
lifetime: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem led by Nehemiah, when the company of the two giving thanks that Nehemiah followed with half of the people took its stand in the house of God, Eleazar was there with Maaseiah and others, in the place where the priests held trumpets (Nehemiah 12:38-42).
event: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, Eleazar was there with Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer, and the singers sang loudly under the direction of Jezrahiah (Nehemiah 12:42). The Bible does not record any specific role Eleazar had.

call: Son of Phinehas (keeper of the temple vessels)
introduce: He is a man recorded as a son of Phinehas. In the time of Ezra, he appears as one who was present at the weighing out and handing over of the silver, the gold, and the vessels in the house of God in Jerusalem.
lifetime: After Ezra's company arrived in Jerusalem and stayed three days (Ezra 8:32), on the fourth day in the house of God it is recorded that Eleazar the son of Phinehas was there with Jozabad the son of Jeshua the Levite and Noadiah the son of Binnui (Ezra 8:33).
event: When the silver, the gold, and the vessels were weighed in the house of God and placed into the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest, Eleazar was there with Jozabad and Noadiah (Ezra 8:33). It says that everything was counted and weighed and the total weight was written down at that time, but the text does not state who carried out that work (Ezra 8:34).

introduce: He is a man who appears in the genealogy of Jesus recorded in the Gospel of Matthew in the New Testament, the son of Eliud and the father of Matthan.
lifetime: Eleazar belongs to the family line that continues the royal line of David and Solomon, and was born as the son of Eliud (Matthew 1:15). He fathered Matthan, and this genealogy, beginning with Abraham, forms the line that reaches Jesus (Matthew 1:15-16).
event: According to the biblical record, no specific achievements or particular events of his are mentioned, and his name is entered in the genealogy only as an ancestor of Jesus (Matthew 1:15).

introduce: He is a man recorded among the descendants of Parosh, "among the Israelites," in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:25).
lifetime: At the time of the investigation of those who had taken foreign women, his name was entered among the descendants of Parosh of Israel, together with Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Malchijah, and Benaiah (Ezra 10:25). Ezra 10:44 records that all those entered on this list were men who had taken foreign women.
event: When Ezra investigated the matter of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:16-17), his name was entered in that list as one of the descendants of Parosh (Ezra 10:25, 10:44). The text does not record any other deeds of this individual.

introduce: Eliphaz is a figure who appears in the Book of Job in the Bible, one of the three friends who came to comfort Job in his suffering. He is known to have come from Teman, a region of Edom, and in his debate with Job he is the one who mainly develops a theology of retribution.
lifetime: When he heard the news that Job had suffered extreme affliction, he set out from his home in Teman and came to see Job together with Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite (Job 2:11). Seeing Job's wretched condition, he sat with him seven days and seven nights (Job 2:13), and afterward he conversed and argued with Job in three rounds (Job 4:1-5:27, 15:1-35, 22:1-30). After the LORD spoke to Job, He said He was angry with Eliphaz, and commanded him to take seven bulls and seven rams, go to Job, and offer a burnt offering; Eliphaz did so together with Bildad and Zophar. The LORD accepted Job's prayer with favor, and when Job prayed for his friends, He restored Job's fortunes (Job 42:7-10).
event: Based on a spiritual experience of his own, he tried to explain to Job the cause of his suffering (Job 4:12-21). When Job insisted on his innocence, he rebuked him and accused him with the logic of retribution (Job 15:2-16). Later he insisted that the reason Job was suffering was his hidden sins, and urged him to repent (Job 22:5-11). At the end, the LORD was angry, saying that Eliphaz and his two friends had not spoken of God what is right, as Job had; and He said that since Job would pray for them, He would not deal with them according to their folly (Job 42:7-8).
character: He is a man who values tradition and experience, and tends to trust his own wisdom and the teaching of the ancestors (Job 15:18). He was active in discernment to the point of being the first of Job's friends to begin to speak (Job 4:1), and shows a very strong confidence in his own reasoning. He has a strong tendency to judge the pain of others by his own standard of moral judgment (Job 22:6-9), and in his debate with Job he sometimes used emotional language (Job 15:3-6).

call: Son of Ahasbai (one of David's mighty men)
introduce: Eliphelet is one of the thirty-seven mighty men, David's military organization, and is recorded as a son of Ahasbai.
lifetime: Eliphelet's name is entered in the list of David's mighty men, and he is introduced as the son of Ahasbai, the grandson of a Maacathite (2 Samuel 23:34).
event: During David's reign he assisted David and acted as a mighty man, but the Bible does not describe in detail any specific battle he fought himself or any individual achievement of his (2 Samuel 23:34).

call: Third son of Eshek (descendant of Saul)
introduce: He is a man of the tribe of Benjamin who appears in the genealogy of the house of Saul. He is a son of Eshek, recorded as the third of Eshek's three sons.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Eshek, the brother of Azel (1 Chronicles 8:39). The sons of Eshek are Ulam the firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third (1 Chronicles 8:39).
character: As a descendant of Saul he is classed as one who continues the genealogy of the house of Saul, and his family is described as one that in later generations produced many mighty men who were skilled archers (1 Chronicles 8:40).

call: Leader of the descendants of Adonikam
introduce: Eliphelet is one of the descendants of Adonikam who returned from the Babylonian exile, a leader-level man who came back to Jerusalem with Ezra.
lifetime: In the seventh year of King Artaxerxes, he is recorded as one of the descendants of Adonikam among those who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem (Ezra 8:13).
event: When Ezra recorded the list of the heads of families who came up from Babylon, Eliphelet was entered among the descendants of Adonikam, the last ones, together with Jeuel and Shemaiah, and there were sixty men with them (Ezra 8:1, 8:13).

introduce: Eliphelet is a member of the house of Hashum, a man mentioned as having a foreign wife when Ezra was arranging the list of the Jews who had returned.
lifetime: As one of the descendants of Hashum who came back from the Babylonian exile, his name was entered in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:33, 10:44).
event: In the course of the investigation led by Ezra into the matter of marriage with foreign women (Ezra 10:16-17), his name was included in the list of those who had taken foreign women, together with Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei of the descendants of Hashum (Ezra 10:33). The text merely records that all the men on this list had taken foreign women and that some of them had women who had borne children; it does not state that Eliphelet himself sent away his wife and children (Ezra 10:44).

call: Eldest son of Javan (ancestor of the coastland peoples)
introduce: Elishah is the one whose name is written first among the four sons born to Javan the son of Japheth, who was a son of Noah. In the genealogy recorded in Genesis 10, he belongs to the descendants of Japheth, among those who were divided into various nations and settled in the lands by the sea.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Javan, and when humanity was scattered over the face of the earth after Noah's flood, he continued the line as a member of the descendants of Japheth (Genesis 10:4, 1 Chronicles 1:7).
event: The descendants of Japheth settled in the lands by the sea, divided according to their languages, clans, and nations (Genesis 10:5). Ezekiel 27:7 records that Tyre made its awning of blue and purple from "the coasts of Elishah"; the "Isle of Elishah" here is a place name connected with the name of this man.

introduce: Elishama is one of the sons born to King David in Jerusalem, and is included in the list of the princes born in Jerusalem during David's reign. However, he is a different person from the other Elishama who appears in 1 Chronicles 3:6. That is, David had two sons named Elishama.
lifetime: He is mentioned in the list of the sons David had in Jerusalem, and that list appears in common in 2 Samuel chapter 5, verse 16 (2 Samuel 5:16), 1 Chronicles chapter 3, verse 8 (1 Chronicles 3:8), and 1 Chronicles chapter 14, verse 7 (1 Chronicles 14:7).
event: He is recorded as one of the sons born in Jerusalem after David left Hebron and settled there (2 Samuel 5:16). In the Chronicles record he is confirmed again as one of the names of the sons David fathered in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:8, 1 Chronicles 14:7).

introduce: Elishua is one of the sons David had in Jerusalem, a man recorded as Elishama in 1 Chronicles chapter 3, verse 6, and as Elishua in 2 Samuel chapter 5, verse 15, and 1 Chronicles chapter 14, verse 5.
lifetime: After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he is recorded as the sixth of the sons born in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:15). In 1 Chronicles chapter 3, verse 6, he is included in the list of the sons David fathered in Jerusalem, and in 1 Chronicles chapter 14, verse 5, he is mentioned in the same position (1 Chronicles 3:6, 1 Chronicles 14:5). However, he is a different person from the other Elishama who appears in 1 Chronicles 3:8. That is, David had two sons named Elishama.

introduce: Elishama is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, recorded as a son of Jekamiah (1 Chronicles 2:41).
lifetime: In the family genealogy of the tribe of Judah, he is recorded as the son born to Jekamiah the son of Shallum (1 Chronicles 2:41). The text does not record any other deeds of his.

call: Grandfather of Ishmael, the assassin of Governor Gedaliah
introduce: Elishama is a man recorded as "of the royal family" (in Jeremiah, "a kinsman of the king"), the grandfather of Ishmael who killed Gedaliah (spelled differently in the book of Jeremiah), whom the king of Babylon had put in charge. He is distinguished from Elishama the son of David.
lifetime: Elishama is recorded as of the royal family, and appears as the father of Nethaniah and the grandfather of Ishmael (2 Kings 25:25, Jeremiah 41:1).
event: No specific achievements or historical events from his own life are recorded in the Bible. His name is mentioned only in the family background of the incident in which his grandson Ishmael struck down and killed Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had put in charge (2 Kings 25:25).

introduce: He is a man recorded as a scribe in the time of Jehoiakim king of Judah. In Jeremiah 36 his name appears in connection with the scribe's chamber where the officials gathered.
lifetime: Elishama is recorded as a scribe in the time of Jehoiakim king of Judah (Jeremiah 36:1, 36:12). When the officials gathered in the scribe's chamber of the king's palace, the name of Elishama the scribe appears among them (Jeremiah 36:12).
event: When Micaiah went down to the king's palace and reported that Baruch had read in the house of the LORD from the book in which Jeremiah's words were written, all the officials were sitting in the scribe's chamber, including Elishama the scribe (Jeremiah 36:10-13). The officials decided to hear those words from Baruch and report them to the king (Jeremiah 36:16), and they put the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe and went to the king to report (Jeremiah 36:20). When the king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, Jehudi took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe and read it in the hearing of the king and the officials (Jeremiah 36:21).

introduce: Elishama is a priest who, during the reign of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, was sent by the king's command to the cities of the land and carried out the role of teaching the people the book of the law.
lifetime: In the third year of his reign King Jehoshaphat sent his officials to teach in the cities of Judah, and with them he sent the Levites and the priests Elishama and Jehoram (2 Chronicles 17:7-8).
event: Together with the officials, the Levites, and the priest Jehoram, Elishama took the book of the law of the LORD and went around all the cities of Judah, teaching the people (2 Chronicles 17:9).

call: Son of Parnach (leader of the tribe of Zebulun)
introduce: Eli-zaphan is a figure who appears in the Book of Numbers in the Old Testament, a leader of the tribe of Zebulun and the son of Parnach. He is mentioned in the list of the leaders chosen from each tribe when the people of Israel divided the land of Canaan as an inheritance (Numbers 34).
lifetime: Eli-zaphan is recorded as the son of Parnach and a leader of the tribe of the descendants of Zebulun (Numbers 34:25). In the plains of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho (Numbers 33:50), his name was entered as the representative of the tribe of Zebulun among the leaders whom each tribe was told to choose for dividing the land as an inheritance (Numbers 34:18, 34:25).
event: The LORD told Moses that the men to divide the land as an inheritance would be the priest Eleazar and Joshua the son of Nun, and that one leader should be chosen from each tribe to divide the land (Numbers 34:17-18); Eli-zaphan is the leader from the tribe of Zebulun who was entered on that list (Numbers 34:25). The text does not record any other personal deeds of his.

call: House of Elizaphan (Levites who cleansed the temple)
introduce: Elizaphanites (Elizaphan) is a man recorded as the ancestor of a Levite family; in 2 Chronicles 29, Shimri and Jeuel are mentioned as "the descendants of Elizaphan."
lifetime: Elizaphan's own life is not recorded in this passage. When the Levites rose up to cleanse the temple in the time of King Hezekiah, the names of Shimri and Jeuel appear "of the descendants of Elizaphan" (2 Chronicles 29:12-13).
event: Elizaphan's own deeds are not recorded. His descendants Shimri and Jeuel rose up among the Levites, gathered their brothers, consecrated themselves, and cleansed the house of the LORD according to what the king had commanded by the word of the LORD (2 Chronicles 29:13-15).

call: Priest at the dedication of the wall
introduce: He is one of the priests who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah.
lifetime: When the wall of Jerusalem was rebuilt after the return from the Babylonian exile, he was mentioned in the list of the priests who took part in its dedication (Nehemiah 12:41).
event: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, when the two companies giving thanks took their stand in the house of God (Nehemiah 12:40), he was one of the priests who held trumpets together with Maaseiah, Miniamin, and others (Nehemiah 12:41).

introduce: Eliakim is a figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in the Gospel of Matthew in the New Testament, the son of Abihud and the father of Azor.
lifetime: Eliakim belongs to the line of the genealogy after the Babylonian exile and was born as the son of Abihud (Matthew 1:13). By fathering Azor, he played the part of carrying on the line of descent that runs from the house of David to Jesus (Matthew 1:13).

call: Father of Rezon, king of Aram
introduce: Eliada is a man recorded as the father of Rezon, the king of Aram who became an adversary of Solomon (1 Kings 11:23, 11:25).
lifetime: Eliada is mentioned only through the introduction of his son, "Rezon the son of Eliada" (1 Kings 11:23), and his own life is not recorded in the Bible.
event: The Bible does not record any deeds of Eliada himself. His son Rezon, who had fled from his master Hadadezer king of Zobah, was raised up by God as an adversary of Solomon (1 Kings 11:23); when David killed the men of Zobah, Rezon gathered men, became captain of a band, went to Damascus, settled there, and became king there (1 Kings 11:24).

introduce: Eliathah is one of the sons of Heman, a Levite musician who was in charge of temple praise in the time of David, and a man who carried out musical duties connected with temple worship.
lifetime: Eliathah is mentioned as one of the sons of Heman, a Kohathite descendant of Levi who was a leader of the choir (1 Chronicles 25:4).
event: When David divided the descendants of Levi into twenty-four divisions for the service of the temple, Eliathah, as a son of Heman, was assigned to the twentieth division, and carried out the duty of praising by playing musical instruments in the temple (1 Chronicles 25:4, 25:27).

call: Son of Lael (chief of the Gershonite Levites)
introduce: Eliasaph is a figure who appears in the Book of Numbers in the Old Testament, who was a chief of the descendants of Gershon of the tribe of Levi. His name carries the meaning "God supplements" or "God has added."
lifetime: He came from the family of the descendants of Gershon of the tribe of Levi, and is the son of Lael (Numbers 3:24). When the descendants of Levi were counted in the wilderness of Sinai, he was designated to be the chief of the Gershonite families, and the descendants of Gershon were in charge of the tabernacle, the tent, its coverings, the curtain of the Tent of Meeting, the hangings of the court, and so on (Numbers 3:14, 3:24-26).
event: When the descendants of Levi were counted and set up by family, he was designated to be the chief of the Gershonite families (Numbers 3:24). The descendants of Gershon whom he led were in charge of the tabernacle, the tent, its coverings, the curtain of the Tent of Meeting, the hangings of the court and the curtain of the court gate surrounding the tabernacle and the altar, and the cords used for them (Numbers 3:25-26).

introduce: Eliashib is a man recorded in 1 Chronicles in the Old Testament, a descendant of David who belonged to the royal house of David. He is classed as one of the descendants of David mentioned through the genealogy of Zerubbabel.
lifetime: Eliashib is a man in the genealogy of the descendants of Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3:19-24); he is mentioned as one of the seven sons of Elioenai the son of Neariah (1 Chronicles 3:23-24), and is one of those who carried on the line of the house of David after the Babylonian exile.
character: The Bible does not describe Eliashib's personal character or deeds in detail, and only makes clear his place of succession in the line, as a man recorded in the genealogy of the house of David (1 Chronicles 3:24).

call: High priest in the time of Nehemiah
introduce: Eliashib is recorded as the high priest at Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah. With his fellow priests he rebuilt the Sheep Gate and consecrated it, but he is also recorded as having prepared a room in the house for Tobiah when he was placed over the chambers of the house of God and had an association with him (Nehemiah 3:1, 13:4-7).
lifetime: Eliashib was the grandson of the high priest Jeshua and the son of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:10). When Nehemiah rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem, he rose up as high priest with his fellow priests and built the Sheep Gate (Nehemiah 3:1). Afterward, as the priest appointed over the chambers of the house of God, he was associated with Tobiah (Nehemiah 13:4) and provided him with a large room (Nehemiah 13:5, 13:7).
event: With his fellow priests he built the Sheep Gate, consecrated it, and set up its doors; he also built the wall and consecrated it as far as the Tower of the Hundred and the Tower of Hananel (Nehemiah 3:1). On the other hand, because of his association with Tobiah, he provided for him a large room that had formerly been the place where they stored the grain offerings, the frankincense, the vessels, the tithes of grain, new wine, and oil prescribed for the Levites, the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the contributions for the priests; Nehemiah regarded this as an evil thing (Nehemiah 13:4-5, 13:7). Furthermore, one of the sons of Joiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had become a son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite, and Nehemiah drove him away from himself (Nehemiah 13:28).
character: As the religious head of Jerusalem at that time, Eliashib was active in public affairs, such as taking the lead in the building work (Nehemiah 3:1), yet he showed a pragmatic side that valued family ties and political relationships. He formed bonds with foreign powers such as Tobiah the Ammonite, and by joining his household in marriage with influential foreigners he showed a tendency to put political survival and the maintenance of relationships ahead of religious purity (Nehemiah 13:4, 13:28).

call: Temple singer who married a foreign woman
introduce: Eliashib was a man of the time of Ezra and Nehemiah in the Old Testament who performed duties connected with the temple. His name is recorded in the list of those in the community, after the return from exile, who had married foreign women.
lifetime: After the return from exile, Eliashib lived in Jerusalem and served as one of the temple singers (Ezra 10:24). His name was recorded as one of the singers in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:24, Ezra 10:44).
event: He performed his duties as a singer in the temple (Ezra 10:24). Later, when Ezra carried out the prohibition of intermarriage with foreigners and the purification of the community, he went through the event of having his name mentioned in that list as one who had foreign wives (Ezra 10:24).
character: Although he held the public office of leading praise in the temple, he is found to have failed to keep the rule, then in force in the community, against marriage with foreigners (Ezra 10:24). This is one glimpse of the mixing with foreign culture, and of the conflict in the process of keeping the law, that existed within the returned community at that time.

introduce: Eliashib was one of the Israelites who returned from the Babylonian captivity, belonging to the descendants of Zattu (Ezra 10:27).
lifetime: In the time of Ezra he is recorded, as one of the descendants of Zattu, in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:27, Ezra 10:44).
event: In the time of Ezra his name was entered in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:27, Ezra 10:44).

introduce: Ammiel was one of the Thirty-seven mighty men of David's military organization, a son of Ahithophel the Gilonite and the father of Bathsheba. In the record of Chronicles he also appears under the name Ammiel.
lifetime: As one of the 37 mighty men of King David, he took part in military activity (2 Samuel 23:34). His father Ahithophel was David's counselor, and his daughter Bathsheba became the wife of King David (2 Samuel 11:3). In Chronicles his name is recorded as Ammiel (1 Chronicles 3:5).
event: As a member of the 37 mighty men, David's elite military organization, he assisted the king and carried out military duties (2 Samuel 23:39). A series of circumstances connected with his family, namely the event in which his daughter Bathsheba came into relationship with David and the event in which his father Ahithophel joined Absalom's rebellion, are closely tied to the major political and domestic events of the house of David (2 Samuel 11:3, 2 Samuel 15:12).

call: Son of Pallu (father of Dathan and Abiram)
introduce: Eliab was a man of the tribe of Reuben, the son of Pallu, and his sons were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. He is recorded as one who continued the genealogy of the line of Reuben among the descendants of Jacob (Numbers 26:5, Numbers 26:8-9).
lifetime: Eliab is recorded as the son of Pallu, the son of Reuben (Numbers 26:5, Numbers 26:8). He was the father of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram (Numbers 26:9).
event: His sons Dathan and Abiram formed a faction with Korah, rose up against Moses and Aaron, and rebelled against the LORD (Numbers 16:1, Numbers 26:9). Because of this the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, and their tents (Deuteronomy 11:6).

introduce: Eliab was the firstborn son of Jesse, a Bethlehemite of the tribe of Judah, and the eldest brother of David (1 Samuel 17:13).
lifetime:
He was born as the firstborn of Jesse and had several younger brothers, including David (1 Chronicles 2:13).
When the prophet Samuel came to Bethlehem to anoint a new king, Eliab was the first of Jesse's sons to be called out, but he was not chosen (1 Samuel 16:6-7).
In the days of King Saul, when the Philistine army invaded, he was called up to the army of Israel together with his two younger brothers Abinadab and Shammah and took part in the battle in the Valley of Elah (1 Samuel 17:13).
When David, who had come to the battlefield on an errand from his father, was speaking with the men, Eliab heard him, became angry with him, and rebuked him (1 Samuel 17:28).
Later his daughter Abihail became the mother of Mahalath, a wife of Rehoboam king of Judah (2 Chronicles 11:18).
event:
He stood before the prophet Samuel as a candidate for the kingship, but the LORD said that He did not look at his appearance or his height, and did not choose him (1 Samuel 16:6-7).
He joined Saul's army and went out to the battlefield where they faced the Philistine champion Goliath (1 Samuel 17:13).
He rebuked his brother David, who had come to the battlefield, asking with whom he had left the sheep and pointing out his pride and the hardness of his heart (1 Samuel 17:28).
character:
He was so impressive in appearance and height that the prophet Samuel, on seeing him, thought he was the one the LORD would anoint (1 Samuel 16:6).
He showed an authoritative and stern manner, such as when he burned with strong anger and was furious at his brother David who had come to the battlefield (1 Samuel 17:28).

기타관계: Mahalath#3453(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

call: Levite musician who praised before the ark
introduce: Eliab was a Levite who served in the time of David; when the ark of God was brought to Jerusalem, he was one of the musicians appointed from among the brothers of the singers to play the harps (1 Chronicles 15:16-20).
lifetime: Eliab was one of the brothers appointed, after Heman, Asaph, and Ethan, when David commanded the chiefs of the Levites to appoint singers (1 Chronicles 15:17-18). In the course of bringing up the ark of God he was designated to play the harps according to Alamoth (1 Chronicles 15:20). Afterward his name was recorded among the Levites appointed to minister before the ark of the LORD and to praise, as one who played the harps and lyres (1 Chronicles 16:4-5).
event: When David was about to bring up the ark of God, Eliab was designated to play the harps according to Alamoth (1 Chronicles 15:20). He was also recorded among the Levites appointed to minister before the ark of the LORD, to extol, thank, and praise the LORD, the God of Israel, as one who played the harps and lyres (1 Chronicles 16:4-5).

introduce: He was a man of the descendants of Gad, one of the mighty men who came over to David at his stronghold in the wilderness (1 Chronicles 12:8-9).
lifetime: He was included in the band of mighty men from Gad who came to David at his stronghold in the wilderness (1 Chronicles 12:8-9).
event: Among the Gadite mighty men who came over to David, his name is mentioned third, after Ezer and Obadiah; they were men whose faces were like the faces of lions and who were as swift as gazelles on the mountains (1 Chronicles 12:8-9).

introduce: Eliab appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Levi recorded in 1 Chronicles 6, mentioned as a descendant of Kohath and an ancestor of Samuel. He is recorded as the son of Nahath.
lifetime: Eliab was born within the Levitical line as the son of Nahath, a descendant of Kohath (1 Chronicles 6:27). His lineage forms a genealogy that runs from him, the son of Nahath, to Jeroham, and from Jeroham to Elkanah (1 Chronicles 6:27).
event: The Bible mentions no special accomplishment or specific event of Eliab personally; his name is merely listed in the genealogy as an ancestor of Samuel (1 Chronicles 6:27).

call: Son of Jeroham of the tribe of Benjamin
introduce: He is a man in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in 1 Chronicles 8, one of the sons of Jeroham, together with Jaareshiah and Zichri (1 Chronicles 8:27).
lifetime: Elijah is recorded as one of the sons of Jeroham of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:27). These were all heads of fathers' houses, chiefs throughout their generations, and they lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).

call: Priest of the descendants of Harim
introduce: Elijah was a man of the time of Ezra in the Old Testament, belonging to the priestly line among the descendants of Harim. As a member of the community in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, he is recorded among the group of priests who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:18, Ezra 10:21).
lifetime: Elijah is recorded as one of the descendants of Harim in the group of priests who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:18, Ezra 10:21).
event: In the time of Ezra, Elijah was included in the list as one of the priests who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:18, Ezra 10:21).

introduce: Elijah, a descendant of Elam, is a man recorded in the time of Ezra as one of the Israelites who, among the community that returned from the Babylonian captivity, had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:25-26).
lifetime: As one of the descendants of Elam, he is recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:26, Ezra 10:44).
event: In the process of settling the matter of marriage with foreign women in the time of Ezra, his name was entered in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:26, Ezra 10:44).

introduce: He is the second son born to Moses and Zipporah, the daughter of Jethro the priest of Midian. His name was given in the sense that "the God of my father helped me and saved me from the sword of Pharaoh" (Exodus 18:4).
lifetime: He was a son whom Moses had by marrying Zipporah in Midian (Exodus 2:21, Exodus 18:3-4). When Moses returned to Egypt, Moses' wife and sons set out together on the journey (Exodus 4:20), and Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took Zipporah, whom Moses had sent back, and her two sons and came to Moses in the wilderness (Exodus 18:2-5). Afterward he is recorded, as a descendant of Moses, in the genealogy of the tribe of Levi (1 Chronicles 23:15-17).
event: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought Zipporah, whom Moses had sent back, and her two sons, namely Gershom and Eliezer, to Moses, who was encamped at the mountain of God (Exodus 18:2-5). In the genealogy of the descendants of Levi, his only son was Rehabiah the chief, and the sons of Rehabiah were very many (1 Chronicles 23:17).

introduce: Eliezer, son of Becher, was a man of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament. The sons of Becher are all recorded as heads of their fathers' houses and mighty men of valor (1 Chronicles 7:8-9).
lifetime: Eliezer is recorded as one of the sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:6, 1 Chronicles 7:8).
event: The Bible records no specific event of Eliezer personally; his name is recorded among the sons of Becher (1 Chronicles 7:8).

call: Priest who blew the trumpet before the ark
introduce: Eliezer was a man of the priestly families of the tribe of Levi in the time of David, one of the priests appointed to blow the trumpets, to carry out the temple music and ritual procedures in the course of bringing up the ark.
lifetime: Eliezer was included in the list of appointments of the Levites whom David organized to bring the ark of God up to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 15:24).
event: When the ark of God was carried to the place David had prepared for it, Eliezer served as one of the priests who blew the trumpets before the ark (1 Chronicles 15:24).

introduce: Eliezer appears in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament; he was a leader of the tribe of Reuben and the son of Zichri. He is recorded as the officer over the tribe of Reuben in the time of King David (1 Chronicles 27:16).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the officers whom David appointed to administer the tribes of Israel. Eliezer the son of Zichri was appointed the officer of the tribe of Reuben (1 Chronicles 27:16).
event: Under the governing order of King David, he served as the chief person responsible for the administrative affairs of the tribe of Reuben (1 Chronicles 27:16).

introduce: He was a son of Dodavahu of Mareshah and a prophet who served in the time of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.
lifetime: He appears as the man who prophesied against Jehoshaphat when Jehoshaphat king of Judah associated with Ahaziah king of Israel and the two kings joined together to make ships at Ezion-geber (2 Chronicles 20:35-37).
event: Pointing out that Jehoshaphat had associated with Ahaziah, who did very wickedly, he prophesied that the LORD would break what the king had made (2 Chronicles 20:37). Afterward the ships were wrecked and were not able to go to Tarshish (2 Chronicles 20:37).
character: He showed the resolute attitude of a prophet who did not hesitate to speak plainly to the king of Judah, and he fulfilled the role of a mediator conveying the will of God (2 Chronicles 20:37).

introduce: Eliezer was one of the chiefs whom Ezra summoned by the river that runs to Ahava, among the company that went up to Jerusalem with Ezra after the Babylonian exile (Ezra 8:15-16).
lifetime: When Ezra gathered the people at the river that runs to Ahava, encamped there three days, and reviewed them, he found none of the sons of Levi, and he summoned chiefs including Eliezer (Ezra 8:15-16). Ezra sent them to Iddo, the chief at the place Casiphia, to bring men to minister for the house of God (Ezra 8:16-17).
event: As one of the chiefs whom Ezra summoned, he was sent to Iddo at the place Casiphia and received the words concerning bringing men to minister for the house of God (Ezra 8:16-17).

call: Priest of the descendants of Jeshua
introduce: Eliezer was one of the priests who had taken foreign women as wives in the time of Ezra after the return from the Babylonian captivity; he is recorded among the sons of Jeshua the son of Jozadak and his brothers (Ezra 10:18).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the descendants of Jeshua among the company of priests who returned after the Babylonian exile (Ezra 10:18).
event: He is included in the list of priests who had married foreign women, and at Ezra's demand he pledged to send away his wife and offered a ram of the flock as a guilt offering to atone for his sin (Ezra 10:18-19).

call: Levite who married a foreign woman
introduce: Eliezer is a man recorded as a Levite in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:23).
lifetime: In the list of Levites in Ezra 10:23 he is recorded together with Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, and Judah (Ezra 10:23).
event: In the time of Ezra his name was entered as a Levite in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:23, Ezra 10:44).

introduce: Eliezer is a man who appears in Ezra 10, one of the descendants of Harim who, after the return from Babylon, had taken foreign women as wives in Jerusalem.
lifetime: As a descendant of Harim, Eliezer's name was recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:31, Ezra 10:44).
event: Eliezer is a man included in the list of those who had taken foreign women, and this is an event that appeared in the course of the religious and social purification movement to restore the purity of the community that returned from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 10:31, Ezra 10:44).

call: Chief of the half-tribe of Manasseh
introduce: Eliel is a man who appears in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, one of the chiefs of the half-tribe of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 5:24).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the chiefs of that tribe at the time when the descendants of the half-tribe of Manasseh increased and lived from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon (1 Chronicles 5:23-24).
event: 1 Chronicles 5:24 lists as chiefs of the half-tribe of Manasseh Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, and records that they were mighty men of valor, famous men, and heads of their fathers' houses. Eliel is one of them.

introduce: Eliel is a man in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, one of the sons of Shimei (1 Chronicles 8:20-21).
lifetime: Eliel is one of the sons of Shimei of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:20-21), and the people of this genealogy are recorded as heads of fathers' houses, chiefs throughout their generations, who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).

introduce: Eliel appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin; in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 8 he is recorded among the sons of Shashak (1 Chronicles 8:22-25).
lifetime: Eliel, one of the sons of Shashak of the tribe of Benjamin, belongs to the genealogy of the chiefs who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:22, 1 Chronicles 8:25, 1 Chronicles 8:28).

introduce: A Mahavite whose name is recorded in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:46).
lifetime: He is recorded as Eliel the Mahavite in the list of the mighty men who helped David when he became king (1 Chronicles 11:10, 1 Chronicles 11:46).
event: He is recorded under the name Eliel the Mahavite in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:46), and no specific accomplishment of his is recorded in the Bible.
character: There is no personal description specially mentioned, but from the fact that he is classed as one of David's thirty mighty men, it can be seen that he was a soldier with outstanding fighting ability for his time (1 Chronicles 11:46).

introduce: One of the great mighty men who distinguished themselves in David's army, recorded in the list together with Obed and Jaasiel the Mezobaite (1 Chronicles 11:47).
lifetime: Apart from the fact that he served as one of David's mighty men, the Bible gives no specific record of his family or life (1 Chronicles 11:47).

introduce: Eliel was a mighty man of the tribe of Gad who joined David when David stayed at Ziklag to escape King Saul.
lifetime: Eliel was one of the mighty men who gathered at the stronghold in the wilderness to help David while David lived at Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:8).
event: Eliel is mentioned seventh among the Gadite mighty men who came to help David (1 Chronicles 12:11). With the mighty men who had gathered to help David, he crossed the Jordan when it was overflowing its banks and put to flight all those in the valleys (1 Chronicles 12:15).
character: According to the biblical record, he had the valor of one whose face was like the face of a lion and who was as swift as a gazelle on the mountains (1 Chronicles 12:8). Their commanders are described as having the ability to match at least a hundred men (1 Chronicles 12:14).

introduce: Eliel was a man who served in the time of King David in the family of the Hebronites of the tribe of Levi. He appears as one of the group of leaders of the Levites summoned when David was about to bring the ark of God up to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 15:9).
lifetime: Eliel carried on the lineage of the tribe of Levi as a descendant of Hebron (1 Chronicles 15:9). When David summoned the priests and the Levites to bring up the ark of the covenant, he was chosen as head of the descendants of Hebron and carried out his duty (1 Chronicles 15:11).
event: Eliel took part in David's work of bringing up the ark of the covenant, leading 80 of the descendants of Hebron (1 Chronicles 15:9). He also received instructions from David, together with the priests Zadok and Abiathar and the other heads of the Levites, to consecrate themselves and prepare to bring up the ark of the covenant (1 Chronicles 15:11-12).

introduce: Eliel was a Levite appointed in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah to oversee the temple offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated things.
lifetime: By the order of King Hezekiah and of Azariah, who was over the house of God, he was put in charge of the care of the contributions, and he served as one of the overseers under Conaniah and his brother Shimei (2 Chronicles 31:13).
event: When, by Hezekiah's order, chambers were prepared in the house of the LORD and the contributions, the tithes, and the dedicated things were brought in (2 Chronicles 31:11-12), Eliel became an overseer under Conaniah and his brother Shimei (2 Chronicles 31:13). Conaniah was in charge of the work and Shimei was second (2 Chronicles 31:12).
character: The Bible makes no specific mention of his personal character, but from the fact that he was selected by King Hezekiah as one of the trusted officials managing the finances of the temple, it can be seen that his ability in public duties was recognized (2 Chronicles 31:13).

call: Chief of thousands of Manasseh (warrior at Ziklag)
introduce: Elihu was a mighty man of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David's army when David stayed at Ziklag to escape King Saul. He is recorded as having held the office of commander of thousands in David's army.
lifetime: He was one of the men of the tribe of Manasseh who deserted to David when he went to Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:20). He was a commander of thousands of the tribe of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 12:20).
event: When David was about to go with the Philistines to fight against Saul, he deserted to David together with the chiefs of the tribe of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 12:19-20). With this company he helped David against the band of raiders (1 Chronicles 12:21).
character: According to the biblical record, he is described as a mighty man of valor with outstanding fighting ability (1 Chronicles 12:21). As one of the commanders of thousands of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David's camp, he is regarded as a man possessing military leadership (1 Chronicles 12:20).

introduce: He was a member of the descendants of Korah recorded in 1 Chronicles, who performed the office of temple gatekeeper. A descendant of Obed-edom, he is recorded as a brother of Elzabad, following the list of the sons of Shemaiah (1 Chronicles 26:7-8).
lifetime: In the division of the duties of the Levites in the time of David, he is recorded as a descendant of Obed-edom, belonging to the divisions of the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:1, 26:8). Elihu and Semachiah, the brothers of Elzabad, are recorded as capable men (1 Chronicles 26:7).
event: When David organized the Levites for the service of the temple, Elihu served with his brothers in the duty of temple gatekeeper (1 Chronicles 26:7).
character: Apart from the fact that, as a descendant of Obed-edom, he was regarded as a capable man fit to perform the duty of gatekeeper, the Bible gives no separate description of his specific character or traits (-)

introduce: Elihu is a man mentioned in 1 Chronicles 27:18, who was the officer of the tribe of Judah in the reign of King David. He is recorded as one of David's brothers.
lifetime: He is one of the sons of Jesse and corresponds to a brother of David (1 Chronicles 27:18). When King David appointed officers to administer the tribes of Israel, he was appointed the one in charge of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 27:18).
event: Under the order of King David, he fulfilled the role of overseeing all the affairs of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 27:18).

call: Son of Barachel (fourth speaker in Job)
introduce: Elihu is a figure who appears in the book of Job, the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram (Job 32:2). He is the fourth speaker, who appears after the dispute between Job and his three friends has ended and sets out his own view.
lifetime: Elihu joined the conversation in anger when he saw that Job's three friends, Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar, could no longer answer (Job 32:3). Watching his elders unable to reply, he gained the opportunity to speak, and at the conclusion of the dispute between Job and his three friends he delivered a long speech (Job 32:6).
event: Elihu criticized the three friends for condemning Job and yet failing to offer a fitting answer (Job 32:3). He argued that God is greater than man and does not explain His doings (Job 33:12-13). He also insisted that suffering may at times be God's way of turning man back from pride and delivering him from the pit (Job 33:17-18). Emphasizing God's almighty power and that He does not pervert justice, he pointed out that Job had multiplied words without knowledge (Job 35:16).
character: Elihu stated that, considering himself young in comparison with Job's three friends, he had held back from speaking until then (Job 32:6). Confident that he possessed wisdom and understanding, he showed an attitude of stating his opinion frankly and without restraint (Job 32:18-20). Rather than displaying personal hostility toward Job, he attempted a logical and systematic argument from a God-centered viewpoint (Job 34:10-12).

introduce: A member of the descendants of Korah of the tribe of Levi and a descendant of Obed-edom, he performed the duty of gatekeeper at the temple in Jerusalem in the time of David.
lifetime: As a son of Shemaiah from the house of Obed-edom, he was among those who obtained the office of head of a division of the gatekeepers in the temple guard system organized by King David (1 Chronicles 26:7-8, 26:12).
event: As a descendant of Obed-edom, he belonged to those capable men who performed that duty well (1 Chronicles 26:8). It is recorded that the south gate fell by lot to Obed-edom and the storehouse to his sons (1 Chronicles 26:15), but there is no record of the gate assigned to Elzabad personally.
character: His house, made up of mighty men, is described as a group recognized, by reason of its number and the nature of its duty, for specialized ability related to guarding the temple (1 Chronicles 26:8).

call: Son of Zerahiah (chief who returned with Ezra)
meaning: My eyes are toward the LORD
introduce: Eliehoenai was one of the Israelites who returned from the Babylonian captivity to Jerusalem with Ezra, and a leading man of the descendants of Pahath-moab.
lifetime: He was one of the chiefs who went up from Babylon with Ezra in the reign of King Artaxerxes (Ezra 8:1). He was the son of Zerahiah and went up with 200 men (Ezra 8:4).
event: Among the chiefs who went up from Babylon with Ezra, he went up with two hundred men, representing the descendants of Pahath-moab (Ezra 8:1, 8:4). There is no record in the Bible of his deeds after that.

introduce: Jekamiah is a figure mentioned in 1 Chronicles 3, recorded as one of the sons of Jehoiachin king of Judah (who is recorded as Jeconiah in 1 Chronicles 3:16-17).
lifetime: His name is recorded among the sons of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah) (1 Chronicles 3:17-18).

introduce: Jedaiah is one of the priestly houses that, having finished the Babylonian exile, returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel. He is a figure who appears in the records of Nehemiah and Ezra and is included in the lists of the priestly line in the process of Israel's religious rebuilding.
lifetime: His name is mentioned in the list of priests who returned from the Babylonian exile, who were the chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:6-7).
event: He is a man whose name appears in the list of priests who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1, 12:6). Corresponding to the names in this list, in the days of Joiakim, Uzzi is recorded as the head of the house of Jedaiah (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:19).

call: Son of Joiarib (chief of the priests)
introduce: Jedaiah is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles and the book of Nehemiah, the son of Joiarib and a head of a priestly house in the age of the return from exile. The name Jedaiah implies the meaning "the LORD knows," and he is recorded as an important figure who continued the line of the genealogy in connection with the priestly office.
lifetime: Among the names recorded as chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua, among the priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua, there is Jedaiah (Nehemiah 12:1, 12:7). As Jedaiah the son of Joiarib he is recorded in the list of priests who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:10).
event: Among the priests who lived in Jerusalem, Jedaiah the son of Joiarib and Jachin are recorded (Nehemiah 11:10). In the days of Joiakim, Nethanel was the head of the house of Jedaiah (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:21).

introduce: Jedaiah is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles 4, a descendant belonging to the genealogy of the houses of the tribe of Simeon. He is recorded in the genealogy as the son of Shimri and the father of Allon (1 Chronicles 4:37).
lifetime: Jedaiah is recorded as the son of Shimri of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:37). His name appears in the genealogy that identifies the ancestry of one of those listed as chiefs of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:37-38).
event: The Bible has no record of Jedaiah's own deeds; he appears only in the genealogy, as the son of Shimri and the father of Allon (1 Chronicles 4:37).

introduce: Jedaiah was one of the Jewish leaders who returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, and a man who took part in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem led by Nehemiah. His name carries the meaning "the LORD knows."
lifetime: As the son of Harumaph, he was active as a member of the community that returned from Babylon (Nehemiah 3:10). At the time of the repair of the wall, he bore the responsibility of repairing the section of the wall opposite his own house (Nehemiah 3:10).
event: When Nehemiah repaired the wall of Jerusalem, Jedaiah, as the son of Harumaph, fulfilled the role of repairing the part of the wall facing his own house (Nehemiah 3:10).

call: Son of Shimri (one of David's thirty mighty men)
introduce: Jediael is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 11, recorded in the list of David's mighty men as the son of Shimri.
lifetime: He is recorded in the list of David's mighty men under the name Jediael the son of Shimri (1 Chronicles 11:45).
event: As one of David's mighty men, he was recorded in the list together with his brother Joha the Tizite (1 Chronicles 11:45).

call: Chief of thousands of Manasseh (deserter at Ziklag)
introduce: Jediael was one of the military commanders of the tribe of Manasseh who deserted to David when David stayed at Ziklag to escape Saul.
