lifetime: He originally belonged to the tribe of Manasseh and was one of the commanders of thousands who deserted to David when he went to Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:20).
event: As a commander of thousands of the tribe of Manasseh, he helped David against the band of raiders (1 Chronicles 12:20-21). The Bible records this company as all of them being mighty men of valor and having become commanders in the army (1 Chronicles 12:21).
character: The Bible classes him as one of the mighty men of valor who helped David and describes him as a man of outstanding military ability (1 Chronicles 12:21).

call: Son of Kish, a descendant of Merari of the tribe of Levi
introduce: Jerahmeel was a man of the descendants of Merari of the tribe of Levi, the son of Kish. He is one of the persons in the genealogy of the house of Merari mentioned when the duties of the Levites were divided in the time of David.
lifetime: Jerahmeel is recorded as a descendant of Merari the Levite and the son of Kish (1 Chronicles 24:29). He was included in that genealogy when King David had the descendants of Levi recorded by their families and had them cast lots (1 Chronicles 24:26-31).
event: When the descendants of Levi were recorded by their families in the time of David, Jerahmeel was recorded as a son born to Kish, of the descendants of Mahli the son of Merari (1 Chronicles 23:21, 24:28-29). The Bible has no record of his specific duties.

introduce: Jeremoth is a man recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, the son of Beriah and classed as one of the leaders of the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: Jeremoth is recorded as a son of Beriah of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:14, 8:16). He is recorded as a head and chief of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).
event: He lived in Jerusalem and fulfilled the role of a leader guiding his own house (1 Chronicles 8:28). The Bible has no record of any other specific historical accomplishment or particular event.

introduce: Jerimoth was a descendant of Merari of the tribe of Levi, the son of Mushi. He is a man whose name is mentioned in the process of arranging the genealogies and duties of the Levites in the time of David.
lifetime: He was born as the son of Mushi, a descendant of Merari of the tribe of Levi (1 Chronicles 23:21). In the process of surveying the genealogies of the Levites and dividing their duties at the end of King David's reign, he was recorded, together with his father Mushi, as a man forming one house of the descendants of Merari (1 Chronicles 23:23).
event: When David reorganized the duties of the Levites, he was included with his house in the list of the descendants of Merari (1 Chronicles 23:23). Jerimoth is a descendant of Levi recorded as one of the descendants of Mahli and Mushi, the sons of Merari (1 Chronicles 24:30).

introduce: Jerimoth was a man of the tribe of Levi who was entrusted with the service of praise at the temple in the time of David, one of the sons of Heman.
lifetime: Jerimoth is recorded as one of the sons of Heman, a descendant of Kohath, who performed the duty of praise (1 Chronicles 25:4). When King David divided the duties of the temple, he served according to the order determined by lot (the fifteenth) (1 Chronicles 25:8, 25:22).
event: King David set apart, from among the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, those who were to take charge of the work of giving praise, and Jerimoth was given the duty of the fifteenth division among them (1 Chronicles 25:4, 1 Chronicles 25:22).

introduce: Jerimoth was the officer who administered the tribe of Naphtali in the time of King David, and his father was Azriel.
lifetime: When those who administered the tribes of Israel were appointed in the time of David, he was recorded as the officer of the tribe of Naphtali (1 Chronicles 27:16, 27:19).
event: He was recorded as the officer of Naphtali in the list of those who administered the tribes of Israel in the time of David, and the Bible has no record of any other specific deeds (1 Chronicles 27:19).

introduce: Jeremoth was one of the descendants of Elam, a man recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra.
lifetime: The descendants of Elam appear in the list of the people of Israel who came out with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:2, 2:31), and among these descendants of Elam, Jeremoth is recorded as one who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:26, 10:44).
event: When Ezra, after arriving at Jerusalem, investigated those who had intermarried with foreigners, he was singled out as one who had taken a foreign wife, and his name was entered in that list (Ezra 10:26).

introduce: Jeremoth was one of the descendants of Zattu who returned from the Babylonian captivity, and is recorded as a man who had married a foreign woman in the time of Ezra.
lifetime: As one who returned from the Babylonian captivity, Jeremoth was a man included in that list in the course of the reform carried out by Ezra to settle the marriage relationships with foreign women (Ezra 10:27).
event: Jeremoth was mentioned as a subject of the movement for religious and social purity led by Ezra, and was singled out as one of those implicated in the pledge to send away their foreign wives (Ezra 10:27).

introduce: Jeremoth was a member of the community of Israel who returned to Jerusalem under the leadership of Ezra after the Babylonian exile, a man belonging to the descendants of Bani.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the descendants of Bani among the people of Israel who returned after finishing the Babylonian captivity (Ezra 10:29).
event: When, after returning to Jerusalem, Ezra discovered that the people of Israel had intermarried with foreign women and urged them to repent of it, he was a man included in that list of repentance (Ezra 10:29).

call: Thirteenth king of the northern kingdom of Israel (Jeroboam II)
introduce: Jeroboam II was the thirteenth king of the northern kingdom of Israel and the fourth king of the dynasty of Jehu. He was the son of Jehoash and reigned forty-one years, the longest in the history of Israel.
lifetime: He succeeded his father Jehoash on the throne and reigned in Samaria forty-one years (2 Kings 14:23). His reign coincided with the period in which the northern kingdom of Israel enjoyed its political and economic heyday. He carried out the task of restoring the territory of Israel, as the prophet Jonah had prophesied (2 Kings 14:25).
event: He restored the territory of Israel from the entrance of Hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, and this came about through the prophecy of the prophet Jonah (2 Kings 14:25). He also brought Damascus and Hamath back into the domain of Israel, proving his military strength (2 Kings 14:28). In his time, along with the expansion of territory, trade flourished and economic prosperity was achieved, but socially the gap between rich and poor and moral decay deepened (Amos 6:4-6).
character: He did evil in the sight of the LORD and did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin (2 Kings 14:24). Under his rule Israel enjoyed outward prosperity, but it was criticized by the prophets of the day for the deep-rooted injustice and oppression within society (Amos 2:6-7).

call: Chief of the tribe of Benjamin
introduce: Jeroham is a man who appears in the record of Chronicles, a chief and leader of a house belonging to the tribe of Benjamin. His name is found in the genealogy of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem.
lifetime: He lived in Jerusalem as one of the heads of the tribe of Benjamin, and Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah, Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri are his sons (1 Chronicles 8:26-28).
event: He was recorded, together with his sons, in the list of the chiefs of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:26-28).

introduce: Jeroham was a man of the tribe of Benjamin, the father of Ibneiah, who lived in Jerusalem.
lifetime: Jeroham was a descendant of Benjamin, and his son Ibneiah is recorded in the list of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:3, 9:7-8).
event: No specific accomplishment or event of Jeroham is recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 9:8). However, his son Ibneiah is included in the list of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile (1 Chronicles 9:3, 9:8).

introduce: Jeroham is a man who appears in the list of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the father of Adaiah the priest. As a descendant of Malchijah, he is recorded as one who continued the genealogy of the priestly house that settled in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: Jeroham is recorded as the son of Pashhur (1 Chronicles 9:12), and in Nehemiah 11:12 he is recorded as the son of Pelaliah. His son Adaiah is mentioned as one of the priests who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile (1 Chronicles 9:10-12, Nehemiah 11:12).
event: Apart from the fact that his son Adaiah entered his name as a member of the house that performed the priestly duty of ministering in the house of God at the temple in Jerusalem, no specific accomplishment or event of Jeroham himself is recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 9:12, Nehemiah 11:12).

call: Man of Gedor (father of warriors at Ziklag)
introduce: Jeroham was a man of Gedor, and his sons Joelah and Zebadiah are recorded as among the mighty men who came to David and helped him in the fight when David was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul the son of Kish (1 Chronicles 12:1, 12:7).
lifetime: Jeroham is recorded as a man of Gedor, and his sons Joelah and Zebadiah appear in the list of the mighty men who came to David while David was at Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:1-7). The Bible has no record of Jeroham's own deeds.
event: The Bible has no record of an event of Jeroham himself, and his sons Joelah and Zebadiah are recorded as among the mighty men who came to Ziklag to help David (1 Chronicles 12:7).

call: Father of Azarel (father of the officer of Dan)
introduce: Jeroham is recorded as the father of Azarel, who was the officer of the tribe of Dan in the time of David (1 Chronicles 27:22).
lifetime: Jeroham is recorded only as the father of Azarel, the officer of the tribe of Dan. Among the officers who administered the tribes of Israel, the officer of Dan was his son Azarel (1 Chronicles 27:16-22).
event: His son Azarel is recorded as the officer of the tribe of Dan in the time of David (1 Chronicles 27:22), and no event of Jeroham himself is recorded in the Bible.

call: Father of Azariah (father of a commander of hundreds)
introduce: Jeroham is recorded as the father of Azariah, the commander of hundreds who made a covenant with the priest Jehoiada and took part in the process of ending the rule of Athaliah and setting Joash on the throne as king (2 Chronicles 23:1).
lifetime: In 2 Chronicles 23:1, among the commanders of hundreds with whom Jehoiada made a covenant in the seventh year is Azariah the son of Jeroham, and the Bible has no record of Jeroham's own deeds.
event: His son Azariah is recorded as having made a covenant with Jehoiada together with the other commanders of hundreds (2 Chronicles 23:1). What Jeroham himself did is not recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Jerimoth was a man of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the mighty men who joined David's army when David stayed at Ziklag to escape Saul (1 Chronicles 12:5).
lifetime: Jerimoth was among the mighty men who came and helped David while David was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul the son of Kish (1 Chronicles 12:1). With them he came to David, accompanied David, and provided military help (1 Chronicles 12:5).
event: While David was hiding at Ziklag from the presence of Saul, he was recorded as one of the mighty men who came to David and helped him (1 Chronicles 12:1). As one of the mighty men of the tribe of Benjamin, he joined the military ranks of David (1 Chronicles 12:5).

introduce: Jerimoth was a son of David, and his daughter Mahalath became the wife of Rehoboam, the first king of the kingdom of Judah in the south (2 Chronicles 11:18).
lifetime: He was born into the royal house as a son of King David and became the father-in-law of King Rehoboam (2 Chronicles 11:18).
event: His daughter Mahalath became the wife of Rehoboam and bore Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham (2 Chronicles 11:18-19).

introduce: He is a man who appears in 2 Chronicles, one of the overseers who took care of the offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated things of the temple in the time of King Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 31:12-13).
lifetime: By the order of King Hezekiah and of Azariah, who was over the house of God, he became one of those who, under Conaniah and his brother Shimei, took care of the contributions, the tithes, and the dedicated things that came into the storehouse of the temple (2 Chronicles 31:13).
event: When King Hezekiah had the chambers of the temple prepared and restored worship, he was appointed one of those who took care of the contributions and the tithes under Conaniah and his brother Shimei (2 Chronicles 31:11-13).
character: As one of the persons in charge of temple management appointed by King Hezekiah and Azariah, he performed administrative duties, faithfully following the king's command (2 Chronicles 31:13). Together with his colleagues he diligently bore his duties and showed the organizing ability to handle smoothly the work of distribution among the Levites (2 Chronicles 31:15).

introduce: He is mentioned as a descendant of the tribe of Asher, and is recorded as the son of Jether (1 Chronicles 7:38).
lifetime: He belongs to the genealogy of the descendants of Asher, and as the son of Jether he is placed in the genealogy of the house of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:38).

introduce: Jeshaiah was a Levite who served in the time of David, a member of the temple choir, recorded as a son of Jeduthun.
lifetime: King David set apart six sons of Jeduthun, Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, to prophesy with the lyre, to give thanks, and to praise under the direction of their father Jeduthun (1 Chronicles 25:3).
event: When the order of the temple choir was determined by lot, Jeshaiah was drawn eighth, and with him were his sons and brothers, twelve in all (1 Chronicles 25:15).

introduce: Jeshaiah was a descendant of the tribe of Levi, a grandson of Eliezer the son of Moses and the son of Rehabiah. He is recorded as an ancestor of Shelomith, who was in charge of the treasuries of the dedicated things (1 Chronicles 26:25-26).
lifetime: Jeshaiah is a descendant of Eliezer the son of Moses and is recorded as the son of Rehabiah (1 Chronicles 26:25). His descendant Shelomith and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the dedicated things in the time of King David (1 Chronicles 26:25-26).
event: No event of Jeshaiah himself is recorded in the Bible. However, his descendant Shelomith and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the dedicated things that King David and the heads of fathers' houses and the commanders had dedicated (1 Chronicles 26:26).

introduce: Jeshaiah was one of the people of Israel who returned to Jerusalem under the leadership of Ezra after the Babylonian exile. He is recorded with the family information that he was the son of Athaliah.
lifetime: He joined the ranks of Ezra's second return from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem (Ezra 8:7). As the son of Athaliah he was chosen from among the descendants of Elam and set out on the journey of return (Ezra 8:7).
event: After returning to his homeland under Ezra's leadership, his name was entered in the list of returnees (Ezra 8:7). He was a man who came up from among the descendants of Elam, and the men with him numbered seventy (Ezra 8:7).

introduce: Jeshaiah was one of the Levites of the descendants of Merari who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra at the return from the Babylonian captivity (Ezra 8:19).
lifetime: When Ezra gathered the people at the river that runs to Ahava and reviewed them for three days, there were none of the descendants of Levi among them, and Ezra had men brought to minister (Ezra 8:15-17). Jeshaiah is one of the descendants of Merari who were brought in answer to that request (Ezra 8:19).
event: The men whom Ezra sent to Iddo, the chief at the place Casiphia, brought Hashabiah and, of the descendants of Merari, Jeshaiah with his brothers and his sons, twenty in all (Ezra 8:17-19).

introduce: Jeshaiah is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, the father of Ithiel and the seventh-generation ancestor of Sallu.
lifetime: Jeshaiah is recorded in Nehemiah 11:7 as the seventh-generation ancestor of Sallu, a descendant of Benjamin, and Ithiel is his son (the sixth-generation ancestor of Sallu) (Nehemiah 11:7).

introduce: Jeush is a man who appears in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, the son of Bilhan of the tribe of Benjamin and a member of a house that continued the genealogy through many generations.
lifetime: Jeush is the son of Bilhan, Bilhan is the son of Jediael, and Jediael is the son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:6, 7:10). He is one of the brothers among the sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar (1 Chronicles 7:10).
event: The house of Jeush, as heads of their fathers' houses and mighty men of valor, formed a military force numbering 17,200 (1 Chronicles 7:11).
character: Jeush was a member of a family so outstanding in fighting ability that it was classed among the heads of the mighty men within the houses of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:11).

introduce: Jeush is a man who appears in 1 Chronicles 23 of the Old Testament, a son of Shimei, a descendant of Gershon of the tribe of Levi. He is a man mentioned in the process of arranging the genealogies of the Levites in the time of King David.
lifetime: Jeush was born as one of the three sons of Shimei, a descendant of Gershon the son of Levi (1 Chronicles 23:10). His brothers were Jahath and Beriah, and these are recorded as the direct line continuing the genealogy of the house (1 Chronicles 23:10).
event: In his last years King David reorganized the duties of the Levites, and at that time Jeush, together with his brother Beriah, was counted as one family because they did not have many sons (1 Chronicles 23:11).

introduce: Jeush was a son of Rehoboam, the first king of the kingdom of Judah, and one of the children of Rehoboam born of Mahalath (2 Chronicles 11:19).
lifetime: He was born as a prince whom Rehoboam king of Judah in the south had by Mahalath, David's granddaughter (2 Chronicles 11:19).
event: He is recorded as a son whom Rehoboam had by Mahalath (2 Chronicles 11:19), and he was among the sons when Rehoboam dispersed all his sons throughout all the districts of Judah and Benjamin, in every fortified city (2 Chronicles 11:23).

introduce: Jeuz is a man recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, a son whom Shaharaim had by Hodesh (1 Chronicles 8:8-10).
lifetime: Jeuz is recorded as one of the sons whom Shaharaim had by his wife Hodesh (1 Chronicles 8:9-10). His father Shaharaim, after sending away his two wives Hushim and Baara, had several sons, including Jeuz, by Hodesh in the land of Moab (1 Chronicles 8:8-10).

introduce: Jeush is a man who appears in the genealogy of the houses of the tribe of Benjamin, a son of Eshek, a descendant of King Saul.
lifetime: Jeush is the son of Eshek, and he had as brothers Ulam the firstborn and Eliphelet the third (1 Chronicles 8:39). His lineage is recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin that continues to Saul (1 Chronicles 8:33-40).
character: Jeush belongs to a family that, as descendants of Eshek in the house of King Saul, were the offspring of mighty men who were skilled in shooting the bow (1 Chronicles 8:40).

call: Levite of the descendants of Elizaphan
introduce: Jeuel is a man who appears in 2 Chronicles 29:13 of the Old Testament, one of the Levites who took part in the purification of the temple during the religious reform of King Hezekiah of Judah.
lifetime: Jeuel was a man of the genealogy of the Levites of the descendants of Kohath, and was one of the descendants chosen to take part in the work of purifying the temple when King Hezekiah cleansed the temple (2 Chronicles 29:13).
event: At the command of King Hezekiah, as one of the descendants of Elizaphan, he rose up with the Levites and took part in the work of cleansing the house of the LORD (2 Chronicles 29:13, 29:15).

call: Returnee of the descendants of Adonikam
introduce: He is a man belonging to the descendants of Adonikam, among the chiefs who went up from Babylon to Jerusalem with Ezra in the time of King Artaxerxes (Ezra 8:1, 8:13).
lifetime: He is recorded together with Eliphelet and Shemaiah as one of the later descendants of Adonikam, and belongs to the genealogical register of the heads of families who came up from Babylon with Ezra during the reign of King Artaxerxes (Ezra 8:1, 8:13).
event: At the time of Ezra's second return he accompanied Ezra as one of the descendants of Adonikam and returned to Jerusalem (Ezra 8:13).

introduce: Jeiel is a man of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in the genealogy of Chronicles; he is called "the father of Gibeon" and lived in Gibeon. His genealogy connects with the lineage of King Saul (1 Chronicles 8:29-33, 9:35-39).
lifetime: As "the father of Gibeon," Jeiel lived in Gibeon, and his wife's name was Maacah (1 Chronicles 8:29, 9:35). Recorded as his sons are Abdon the firstborn, and Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, and Zecher (1 Chronicles 8:30-31), and in 1 Chronicles 9:36-37 Ner, Zechariah, and Mikloth are also listed.
event: In the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 9:36, 9:39, his son Ner is recorded as having fathered Kish and Kish as having fathered Saul, so the line of Jeiel connects with King Saul. The Bible does not separately record any personal deeds of his.

call: Son of Hotham (one of David's mighty men)
introduce: Jeiel is a man recorded in the list of David's mighty men, recorded as a son of Hotham the Aroerite (1 Chronicles 11:44).
lifetime: In the list enumerating David's mighty men, his name is entered together with Shama the son of Hotham (1 Chronicles 11:44). The rest of his life is not recorded in the Bible.
event: Apart from his name being entered in the list of David's mighty men, no specific event or accomplishment of his is recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 11:44).

introduce: He was a descendant of Levi who in the time of David took charge of the duty of playing lyres and harps in praise before the ark of the covenant, and he is also recorded as a Levite who was a gatekeeper.
lifetime: When David brought up the ark of the covenant, after the Levites had appointed Heman, Asaph, and Ethan, Jeiel was appointed from among their brothers together with Obed-edom the gatekeeper (1 Chronicles 15:17-18). Afterward his name is also entered in the list of the Levites who praised before the ark of the covenant (1 Chronicles 16:5).
event: In the course of bringing up the ark of the covenant, Jeiel was listed together with Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, and Azaziah as one who led on the lyres according to the eighth (1 Chronicles 15:21). After the ark was installed, his name is entered among the company who, with Asaph as chief, played the harps and lyres and extolled, thanked, and praised the LORD (1 Chronicles 16:4-5). He is also recorded as a gatekeeper together with Obed-edom the gatekeeper (1 Chronicles 15:18).
character: He was a man chosen by David as one able to bear at the same time two specific assignments among the offices of the tribe of Levi, the ministry of praise and the ministry of gatekeeper (1 Chronicles 15:18). Even among those who praised, he performed the function of a specialized player who handled the harp (1 Chronicles 15:20).

introduce: Jeiel was a descendant of Asaph and belonged to the tribe of Levi. He is recorded in the genealogy of Chronicles as an ancestor of Jahaziel and is classed as one who continued the genealogy of a house connected with the service of the temple.
lifetime: Jeiel was the son of Mattaniah, a descendant of Asaph, and is recorded as the great-grandfather of the Levite Jahaziel (2 Chronicles 20:14).
event: No specific deeds or events concerning his own life are separately recorded in the Bible, but he is mentioned as the family background of Jahaziel when Jahaziel received the Spirit of God and prophesied in the time of King Jehoshaphat (2 Chronicles 20:14).

introduce: Jeiel was a scribe in the time of Uzziah king of Judah, a man who, together with Maaseiah the officer, took a count of the number of the soldiers (2 Chronicles 26:11).
lifetime: While serving as a scribe in the time of Uzziah king of Judah, he took, together with Maaseiah the officer, a count of Uzziah's fighting men. That army was under the authority of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders (2 Chronicles 26:11).
event: According to the number counted by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer, Uzziah's army went out to war by divisions under the authority of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders (2 Chronicles 26:11).

call: Levite chief in the time of Josiah
introduce: Jeiel was one of the chiefs of the Levites in the time of Josiah king of Judah, a man who, together with the other chiefs, gave the Levites offerings for the Passover at Josiah's Passover (2 Chronicles 35:9).
lifetime: At the time King Josiah kept the Passover, he is recorded as one of the chiefs of the Levites, namely Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, and Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad (2 Chronicles 35:9).
event: Together with the other chiefs of the Levites, Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, Hashabiah, and Jozabad, he gave the Levites five thousand sheep and five hundred bulls as Passover offerings (2 Chronicles 35:9).

introduce: He is a man named among the descendants of Nebo, an Israelite included in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives at the time of Ezra's religious reform.
lifetime: As a member of the community that returned from the Babylonian captivity, he is recorded as one of the descendants of Nebo in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:43-44).
event: His name was entered in the list as one of the descendants of Nebo who had taken foreign women. It is recorded that among the people in this list there were also women who had borne children (Ezra 10:43-44).

call: Father of Azariah (father of a Levite in Hezekiah's time)
introduce: Jehallelel is recorded as the father of Azariah, a Levite in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah. Azariah is listed among the descendants of Merari (2 Chronicles 29:12).
lifetime: In 2 Chronicles 29:12 he is mentioned only as the father of "Azariah the son of Jehallelel," among the descendants of Merari, among the Levites who arose in the time of Hezekiah, and the Bible has no record of Jehallelel's own life.
event: The Bible has no record of Jehallelel's own deeds. His son Azariah is listed among the descendants of Merari, among the Levites who arose in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 29:12).

call: Priest of the house of Shemaiah
introduce: Jonathan was a man of the house of Shemaiah, a priestly house of the Levites who served in the time of Nehemiah, a priest whose name is entered in the genealogy connected with the service of the temple.
lifetime: Among those who became heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim, he is recorded as the head of the house of Shemaiah (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:18).
event: In the list of the heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim in Nehemiah 12, he is listed as the head of the house of Shemaiah (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:18). No other specific deeds are recorded in the Bible.

call: Ninth king of the northern kingdom of Israel
introduce: He was the ninth king of the northern kingdom of Israel, a son of Ahab and Jezebel, and he took the throne after Ahaziah (2 Kings 3:1). He ruled in Samaria for about twelve years (2 Kings 3:1).
lifetime: Jehoram became king in place of Ahaziah after Ahaziah died without a son (2 Kings 1:17). When Mesha king of Moab rebelled against Israel, he allied with Jehoshaphat king of Judah in the south and the king of Edom and attacked Moab (2 Kings 3:5-9). He gained the upper hand when water was supplied through the prophecy of Elisha, but he withdrew his forces after witnessing the king of Moab offer his firstborn son as a burnt offering (2 Kings 3:20-27). Afterward, when Ben-hadad king of Aram attacked Israel, he escaped the crisis with the help of Elisha (2 Kings 6:8-12). In the end, because of the revolt of Jehu, he was struck by Jehu's arrow at Jezreel and died (2 Kings 9:24).
event: In the war with Moab he faced the crisis of a lack of water, but with the help of Elisha he dug trenches in the valley and filled them with water and won the victory (2 Kings 3:16-24). Thanks to the information Elisha sent during the war with Aram, he was able to avoid the ambush plans of the king of Aram several times (2 Kings 6:8-12). When Samaria was completely besieged by the army of Aram and suffered a severe famine, he went through the event in which, as Elisha prophesied, the price of grain plummeted the next day and the economic crisis was resolved (2 Kings 7:1-18). He was wounded while fighting the army of Aram at Ramoth-gilead and returned to Jezreel to be healed, and the dynasty came to an end through Jehu's coup (2 Kings 8:28-29, 9:24).
character: He removed the idol of Baal that his parents Ahab and Jezebel had made, but he did not turn away from the sin of Jeroboam and still committed sin (2 Kings 3:2-3). He blamed Elisha for the suffering Israel was undergoing in the course of the war with Aram and tried to kill him (2 Kings 6:31), yet he also showed a double-sidedness by going to Elisha to seek counsel in a national crisis (2 Kings 6:32-33). Also, when his palace was besieged by Aram, he wore sackcloth and mourned, revealing his wretched state of mind (2 Kings 6:30).

call: Priest sent by Jehoshaphat (teacher of the law)
introduce: Jehoram was a man who served in the time of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, one of the priests sent at the king's command to go around the cities throughout Judah and teach the people the book of the law of the LORD.
lifetime: In the third year of the reign of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, the king sent priests, together with officials and Levites, to teach the people in all the cities of Judah, and the name Jehoram is included in the list of the priests sent at that time (2 Chronicles 17:7-8).
event: Following the instruction of King Jehoshaphat, together with the other priests and Levites he went around the cities of Judah and fulfilled the role of teaching the people the book of the law of the LORD (2 Chronicles 17:9).

introduce: He was one of the twelve officers set over all Israel in the time of King Solomon, the son of Paruah, and he was in charge of Issachar. The twelve officers provided food for the king and his household, each for one month in the year (1 Kings 4:7, 4:17).
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Paruah (1 Kings 4:17), and he was the officer in charge of Issachar among the twelve officers whom Solomon appointed over all Israel (1 Kings 4:7, 4:17).
event: The twelve officers each provided food for the king and his household for one month in the year, and Jehoshaphat also carried out this duty as the officer in charge of Issachar (1 Kings 4:7, 4:17).

call: Fourth king of Judah in the south
introduce: He was the fourth king of the southern kingdom of Judah, a son of King Asa, who took the throne at the age of 35 and reigned in Jerusalem for 25 years. He was a ruler who walked in the way of David and carried out religious and military reorganization.
lifetime: He took the throne at the age of 35 and reigned 25 years (2 Chronicles 20:31). He formed a marriage alliance with Ahab king of the northern kingdom of Israel and established a united front (2 Chronicles 18:1). He took part in the battle of Ramoth-gilead against Aram (2 Chronicles 18:28), and afterward went through the event of confronting the allied forces of Moab, Ammon, and Maon (2 Chronicles 20:1). In his last years he cooperated with Ahaziah king of Israel to build ships, but he experienced the wrecking of those ships (2 Chronicles 20:35-37).
event: He carried out a reform of education, sending officials and Levites throughout the southern kingdom of Judah to teach the book of the law (2 Chronicles 17:7-9). He built fortified cities and store cities throughout the land and strengthened his military power (2 Chronicles 17:12). He reorganized the judicial system, establishing courts in Jerusalem and emphasizing fair judgment (2 Chronicles 19:5-11). When Moab and Ammon invaded with their allied forces, he responded by fasting together with the people and won the victory (2 Chronicles 20:1-30).
character: He walked in the earlier ways of his ancestor David and did not seek the Baals (2 Chronicles 17:3). Diplomatically he formed a close relationship with the northern kingdom of Israel, but he was also criticized in the course of the military alliance (2 Chronicles 19:2). He is regarded as a man with the ability to govern, as seen in systematizing the national defense and administrative organization (2 Chronicles 17:12-19).

call: Father of King Jehu (son of Nimshi)
introduce: He is known as the father of Jehu king of the northern kingdom of Israel and the son of Nimshi. He is a namesake of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and according to the biblical record he never took the throne of Israel.
lifetime: As the father of Jehu, in 2 Kings 9:2 and 9:14 Jehu is introduced as "the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi."
event: No deeds of Jehoshaphat himself are recorded in the Bible; he is mentioned only as the father of Jehu in the passage where Jehu conspires against Joram (2 Kings 9:14).

introduce: Joshaphat was a Mithnite whose name is on the list of David's mighty men, listed together with Hanan the son of Maacah (1 Chronicles 11:43).
lifetime: While David was on the throne, he was included, and his name entered, in the list of mighty men who possessed military ability (1 Chronicles 11:43).

introduce: One of the sons of Obed-edom of the tribe of Levi, a man recorded in the divisions of the gatekeepers in the time of David.
lifetime: He is recorded as the second son of Obed-edom (1 Chronicles 26:4), and the descendants of Obed-edom are listed in the divisions of the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:1, 26:8).
event: Together with the descendants of Obed-edom, he was listed among those who served in the house of the LORD as heads of divisions of the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:8, 26:12). No specific deeds of Jehozabad personally are recorded in the Bible.
character: Throughout their generations his house was recognized as capable men able to bear the duty before God, and as a son of Obed-edom he was assigned, together with his brothers, to the work of guarding the temple (1 Chronicles 26:8).

call: Priest who blew the trumpet before the ark
introduce: A man mentioned in 1 Chronicles, one of the priests who blew the trumpet before the ark in the reign of King David.
lifetime: When David brought the ark of God up to Jerusalem, he was entrusted with the duty of blowing the trumpet before the ark (1 Chronicles 15:24). In the course of carrying the ark he carried out his task together with the other priests (1 Chronicles 15:24).
event: When David brought up the ark of God, he was listed as one who blew the trumpet before the ark of God together with the priests Shebaniah, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer (1 Chronicles 15:24).
character: He carried out the priestly office and assisted David's religious ceremonial occasions (1 Chronicles 15:24). The Bible records nothing about his specific personality or character (1 Chronicles 15:24).

call: Seventeenth king of Judah in the south
introduce: He was the seventeenth king of the southern kingdom of Judah, a son of Josiah, and he is also called by the name Shallum. He reigned about three months around 609 BC, and his reign coincides with the period of political upheaval of the kingdom of Judah after the death of Josiah.
lifetime: After Josiah was killed in the battle of Megiddo, he was set up as king by the people of Jerusalem (2 Kings 23:30). He took the throne at the age of 23 (2 Kings 23:31), but after only three months of reign he was deposed by Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt and imprisoned at Libnah (2 Kings 23:33). Afterward he was taken to Egypt and died there (2 Kings 23:34).
event: During his short reign the political sovereignty of Judah was greatly damaged. Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt deposed him, imposed a fine of 100 talents of silver and a talent of gold, and set his brother Eliakim on the throne as king and changed his name to Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:33-34). Jeremiah prophesied that he would be taken to Egypt and never return to his homeland (Jeremiah 22:10-12).
character: He is recorded as a king who did evil in the sight of the LORD, following all that his fathers had done (2 Kings 23:32). This is connected with the unstable religious and political situation of the kingdom of Judah at that time.

call: High priest who set Joash on the throne
introduce: He was a high priest of the kingdom of Judah; in the days when Athaliah ruled, his wife Jehosheba hid Joash (2 Chronicles 22:11), and in the seventh year he made a covenant with the commanders of hundreds and was the religious leader who set Joash on the throne as king.
lifetime: When Athaliah destroyed all the royal offspring, Jehoiada's wife Jehosheba stole Joash away and hid him, and Joash was hidden in the house of the LORD for six years (2 Chronicles 22:11-12, 2 Kings 11:3). In the seventh year Jehoiada made a covenant with the commanders of hundreds and showed them the king's son (2 Kings 11:4); he put the crown on the king's son, gave him the book of the law, and anointed him king (2 Kings 11:12), and he commanded the commanders of hundreds to put Athaliah to death (2 Kings 11:15). Joash was seven years old when he began to reign (2 Kings 11:21), and he did what was right in the sight of the LORD all the days that Jehoiada instructed him (2 Kings 12:2). Jehoiada died at the age of one hundred and thirty and was buried in the city of David among the kings (2 Chronicles 24:15-16).
event: It was all the people who tore down the house of Baal, broke in pieces its altars and images, and killed Mattan the priest of Baal, and Jehoiada the priest appointed officers over the house of the LORD (2 Kings 11:18). Jehoiada also made a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people that they should be the LORD's people, and also between the king and the people (2 Kings 11:17). After King Joash summoned Jehoiada the high priest and the priests and rebuked them for not repairing the damage of the house, Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the altar on the right side as one enters the house of the LORD, and the priests who guarded the threshold put into it all the silver that was brought into the house of the LORD (2 Kings 12:7-9).
character: He exercised outstanding strategic judgment in protecting and maintaining the kingship (2 Kings 11:4). He was a man greatly respected by the people, and he was recognized for his great contribution to the nation's welfare to the extent that after his death he was buried among the kings in the city of David (2 Chronicles 24:16). The period in which Joash did what was right in the sight of the LORD is limited to the time when Jehoiada was giving him instruction (2 Kings 12:2).

introduce: Jehoiada was the son of Benaiah, a man recorded in 1 Chronicles 27:34 as having become "next after Ahithophel" together with Abiathar. The preceding verse (27:33) introduces Ahithophel as the king's counselor.
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Benaiah, and in the enumeration of David's governing organization he became, together with Abiathar, next after Ahithophel (1 Chronicles 27:34).
event: Apart from having become next after Ahithophel together with Abiathar, no specific deeds of his are recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 27:34).
character: As a man who enjoyed the trust of King David, he took the role of providing counsel in national crises (1 Chronicles 27:34). Along with the military influence of his father Benaiah, he is regarded as a specialized adviser who deeply understood the political situation within the royal house and assisted David (1 Chronicles 27:34).

introduce: Jehoiada was a priest at the end of the kingdom of Judah, a man mentioned in Jeremiah 29:26 where it is said that Zephaniah was made priest in his place and appointed chief officer in the house of the LORD.
lifetime: In the letter sent by Shemaiah of Babylon in Jeremiah 29:25-26, it is mentioned that Zephaniah became priest in place of the priest Jehoiada. This is all the Bible records about him.
event: In the letter Shemaiah sent to the priest Zephaniah and others, it is mentioned that Zephaniah was appointed chief officer in the house of the LORD in place of the priest Jehoiada (Jeremiah 29:25-26). The duty of putting madmen and self-styled prophets in stocks and neck irons is described as entrusted not to Jehoiada but to Zephaniah who replaced him, and no deeds of Jehoiada himself are recorded.

call: Military commander in the time of Jehoshaphat
introduce: A commander in the time of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, recorded as having led 280,000 soldiers (2 Chronicles 17:15).
lifetime: In the list recording the number of Judah's soldiers in the time of Jehoshaphat, the commander Jehohanan is recorded next after Adnah, the chief of the commanders of thousands belonging to Judah (2 Chronicles 17:14-15).
event: In the time of King Jehoshaphat, as a commander, he led 280,000 soldiers (2 Chronicles 17:15). All these were men who served the king (2 Chronicles 17:19).

call: Father of Ishmael (father of a commander of hundreds)
introduce: Jehohanan was a man of the period of the kingdom of Judah, recorded as the father of Ishmael.
lifetime: The Bible records him only as the father of Ishmael the commander of hundreds, and there is no record of the rest of his life (2 Chronicles 23:1).
event: His son Ishmael was one of the commanders of hundreds with whom the priest Jehoiada took courage in the seventh year and made a covenant (2 Chronicles 23:1). No deeds of Jehohanan himself are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: A man mentioned as one of the descendants of Bebai among those who returned from the Babylonian captivity in the time of Ezra.
lifetime: He is one of the descendants of Bebai among the Israelites who returned from the Babylonian captivity (Ezra 10:28).
event: He was included in the list of those who, having taken foreign women as wives, pledged to send those women away in obedience to Ezra's command for religious purification (Ezra 10:28).

call: Son of Eliashib (owner of the priest's chamber)
introduce: A man recorded as the son of Eliashib in the time of Ezra. Ezra 10 records that Ezra rose up from before the house of God and went into his chamber.
lifetime: It is recorded that Ezra rose up from before the house of God and went into the chamber of Johanan the son of Eliashib (Ezra 10:6).
event: Ezra went into his chamber and, grieved over the sin of those who had been taken captive, neither ate bread nor drank water (Ezra 10:6).
character: The Bible gives no specific description of his personal character or personal traits. However, it is confirmed that he carried out the priestly office handed down in his house through the generations and was involved in the administrative affairs of the temple in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 12:22).

call: Thanksgiving singer at the dedication of the wall
introduce: Jehohanan was a man whose name is recorded among the company giving thanks and praise at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah.
lifetime: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem led by Nehemiah, his name was recorded together with Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, and others (Nehemiah 12:42).
event: When the two companies giving thanks and praise stood in the house of God at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, he was there with Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer, and the singers sang loudly (Nehemiah 12:40-42).
character: He carried out the priestly office and took faithful part in religious ceremonies, and at the national and religious event of the dedication of the wall he took on the duty of playing the trumpet, performing a musical role connected with the temple (Nehemiah 12:41).

call: Priest of the house of Amariah
introduce: Jehohanan is a man recorded as head of the priests in the days of Joiakim after the return from the Babylonian captivity, the head of the house of Amariah.
lifetime: Among those who were heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim, Jehohanan is recorded for the house of Amariah (Nehemiah 12:12-13).
event: His name was recorded as head of the house of Amariah in the list of the heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12-13).

introduce: Jehohanan was a man active at the time of the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem led by Nehemiah, governor of Judah in the Persian Empire; he is a man with the family information that he was the son of Tobiah and the son-in-law of Meshullam.
lifetime: He was the son of Tobiah the Ammonite and took as his wife the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah (Nehemiah 6:18). Because he had taken the daughter of Meshullam, many in Judah were bound by oath to Tobiah (Nehemiah 6:18).
event: Because he had taken the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah, many in Judah were bound by oath to Tobiah (Nehemiah 6:18). Meanwhile, the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah regularly sent letters to Nehemiah to make him afraid (Nehemiah 6:17, 6:19).

introduce: Jether is a man who appears in the Old Testament, the father of Amasa, who was the commander of King David's army. In Chronicles he is recorded as Jether the Ishmaelite, and in 2 Samuel he is also referred to by the name Ithra.
lifetime: As an Ishmaelite, he married Abigail, David's sister, and she bore Amasa (1 Chronicles 2:16-17). In 2 Samuel he is recorded as Ithra the Israelite, and it is stated that he was the husband of Abigail (2 Samuel 17:25).
event: His wife Abigail was the sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother (2 Samuel 17:25), and Zeruiah and Abigail are recorded as sisters of the sons of Jesse (David) (1 Chronicles 2:16-17). His son Amasa was made commander of the army by Absalom in place of Joab (2 Samuel 17:25).

call: Son of Jada of the descendants of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah
introduce: Jether is a man of the house of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah recorded in 1 Chronicles 2 of the Old Testament, the son of Jada and one belonging to the genealogy of the great-grandsons of Jerahmeel.
lifetime: Jether was born as the son of Jada and is mentioned within the genealogical system of the house of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2:32).

introduce: A man who was one of the officials in charge of the king's property in the reign of King David of Israel; as a Meronothite he was in charge of the donkeys (1 Chronicles 27:30-31).
lifetime: In the time of King David, as a Meronothite, he carried out the duty of managing the king's donkeys (1 Chronicles 27:30-31).
event: He was in charge of the donkeys as one of those entrusted with the property of King David (1 Chronicles 27:30-31).

introduce: Jesher is a man recorded as one of the sons whom Caleb, the son of Hezron of the tribe of Judah, fathered.
lifetime: He is one of Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon, the sons whom Caleb the son of Hezron fathered by his wife Azubah and by Jerioth (1 Chronicles 2:18).

meaning: One who will save his people, Savior
introduce: He is a man who appears in the genealogy of Jesus recorded in the Gospel of Luke, the son of Eliezer and the father of Er. He is classed as one of the physical ancestors of Jesus of Nazareth.
lifetime: According to the genealogy in Luke, he is the son of Eliezer, and his son is recorded as Er (Luke 3:28-29).

meaning: One who will save his people, Savior
introduce: Jesus called Justus is a man who appears in the New Testament letter to the Colossians, one of the fellow workers of Jewish (of the circumcision) origin who were with the apostle Paul while he was imprisoned.
lifetime: He was with Paul at the time Paul was in bonds and imprisoned (Colossians 4:3, 4:10), and he is included among those who send greetings to the believers at Colossae (Colossians 4:11).
event: Among those of the circumcision, he is recorded as one who worked with Paul for the kingdom of God and who was a comfort to Paul (Colossians 4:11).
character: Although he was a circumcised man with a Jewish background, he was a person who cooperated with Paul for the kingdom of God (Colossians 4:11).

call: Levite in the time of Hezekiah
introduce: Jeshua was a Levite who in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah took charge of duties connected with the distribution of the temple offerings. He is recorded as serving under Kore the son of Imnah, the Levite keeper of the East Gate.
lifetime: In the time of Hezekiah, he held office in the cities of the priests under Kore the son of Imnah, the Levite keeper of the East Gate (2 Chronicles 31:14-15).
event: Together with Eden, Miniamin, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, he held office in the cities of the priests and distributed to their brothers by divisions, old and young alike (2 Chronicles 31:15).
character: It can be seen from the biblical record that he was a trustworthy man, for he faithfully carried out the important administrative task of distributing the offerings among those living in the cities of the priests (2 Chronicles 31:15).

introduce: A Levite who served in the time of Ezra, recorded as the father of Jozabad.
lifetime: When Ezra came to Jerusalem and the silver, the gold, and the vessels were weighed, the one who was with Eleazar the son of Phinehas was Jozabad the son of Jeshua the Levite, and in this way it is recorded that he was the father of Jozabad (Ezra 8:33). No deeds of his own are recorded in the Bible.
event: No event of Jeshua himself is recorded in the Bible. His son Jozabad was with Eleazar and Noadiah when, on the fourth day, in the house of God the silver, the gold, and the vessels were weighed and placed into the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest (Ezra 8:33).

call: Leader of the descendants of Pahath-moab
introduce: Jeshua is a man recorded in the list of those who returned to Jerusalem after finishing the Babylonian captivity as "the descendants of Pahath-moab, namely of Jeshua and Joab."
lifetime: In the count of the people of Israel who came out with Zerubbabel, the descendants of Pahath-moab, namely of Jeshua and Joab, are recorded as 2,812 (Ezra 2:2, 2:6). Nehemiah 7:11 records the same list as 2,818.
event: No specific event of his own is recorded in the Bible.

call: Father of Ezer (father of the ruler of Mizpah)
introduce: Jeshua is a man recorded as the father of Ezer, ruler of Mizpah, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah.
lifetime: Nehemiah 3:19 records that Ezer the son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired a section of the wall, and so it is confirmed that Jeshua was the father of Ezer. No deeds of his own are recorded in the Bible (Nehemiah 3:19).
event: No event of Jeshua himself is recorded in the Bible. His son Ezer repaired a section of the wall as far as the opposite of the armory at the angle of the wall (Nehemiah 3:19).

introduce: Jeshua was a Levite who served in the time of Nehemiah after the return from the Babylonian captivity, a man who performed the duty of interpreting and teaching the law to the people of Israel.
lifetime: He appears as one of the Levites who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem (Nehemiah 12:8). Afterward, at the reading of the law after the completion of the wall led by Nehemiah, he took the role of a teacher helping the people to understand the word (Nehemiah 8:7).
event: When Ezra read the book of the law before the people, the Levites, including Jeshua, made all the people understand the reading by giving the sense of the law while the people stood in their place (Nehemiah 8:7-8).
character: As a Levite carrying out his duty, he showed the aspect of a specialized educator conveying the content of the law to the people (Nehemiah 8:7). He also took the role of establishing order in cooperation with the leaders in the process of the community's religious reform and renewal of the covenant (Nehemiah 10:9).

call: Son of Azaniah (Levite who sealed the covenant)
introduce: One of the Levites who took part in sealing the covenant after the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, recorded as the son of Azaniah.
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian captivity he carried out his duty as a Levite in Jerusalem, and in the process of covenant renewal and sealing led by Nehemiah he signed as one of the representatives of the Levites (Nehemiah 10:9).
event: In Nehemiah 10, when the people of Israel, the priests, and the Levites swore before God that they would keep the law, even under a curse, his name is included in the list of the Levites who took part in the sealing (Nehemiah 10:9).

call: Tenth king of the northern kingdom of Israel (judge of Ahab)
introduce: Jehu was the tenth king of the northern kingdom of Israel, the grandson of Nimshi and the son of Jehoshaphat, the one who destroyed the house of Ahab and brought the dynasty of Omri to an end. He was anointed by a young prophet sent by Elisha, conspired against Joram and killed King Joram, and took the throne, and he ruled Israel for a total of 28 years (2 Kings 10:36).
lifetime: Jehu was originally a commander of the army of King Joram of the northern kingdom of Israel and was at war with Aram at Ramoth-gilead (2 Kings 9:14). He was anointed king by a young prophet sent by Elisha (2 Kings 9:6), drove his chariot to Jezreel, and killed King Joram and Ahaziah king of Judah (2 Kings 9:24-27). Afterward he had Jezebel thrown down (2 Kings 9:30-33), the seventy sons of Ahab in Samaria were killed by the people of Samaria according to Jehu's letter (2 Kings 10:6-7), and Jehu destroyed the house of Ahab by killing those who were left of the house of Ahab in Jezreel (2 Kings 10:11). In Samaria he carried out a religious purge by gathering and killing the worshipers of Baal (2 Kings 10:25), and after he died he was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoahaz reigned in his place (2 Kings 10:35).
event: He killed those belonging to the house of Ahab and brought down the house of Ahab (2 Kings 10:11, 10:17). He tore down the pillar and the house of Baal and killed the worshipers of Baal on a large scale, and so destroyed Baal out of Israel (2 Kings 10:27-28). But Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, which were in the worship of the golden calves at Bethel and Dan (2 Kings 10:29). During his reign the LORD began to cut off parts of Israel, and Hazael king of Aram defeated them throughout the territory of Israel (2 Kings 10:32).
character: He is described as a rough and violent man, to the point of driving his chariot like a madman (2 Kings 9:20). In the process of seizing power he showed a very thorough and ruthless side, and he even used deception to achieve his purpose (2 Kings 10:18-19). He claimed to be a man with zeal for the LORD, but for the sake of political stability and the maintenance of the religious system he showed an attitude of political pragmatism by keeping the existing system of golden-calf idolatry as it was (2 Kings 10:16, 10:29).

introduce: A man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
lifetime: According to the detailed genealogy, Jehu is mentioned as one of the sons of Obed (1 Chronicles 2:38).

introduce: Jehu is a man mentioned in 1 Chronicles 4, the son of Joshibiah of the tribe of Simeon. He is recorded as one of those who continued the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon.
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Joshibiah, the grandson of Seraiah, the great-grandson of Asiel (1 Chronicles 4:35). His name is included in the list of the tribe of Simeon enumerated between verses 34 and 37 of 1 Chronicles 4 (1 Chronicles 4:35).
event: Together with those listed above he was recorded as a chief of the families of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:38). Seeking pasture for their flocks, they came to the border of Gedor, on the east side of the valley, and found rich and good pasture (1 Chronicles 4:39-40), and in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah they struck down the tents of the descendants of Ham there and the Meunites, destroyed them utterly, and settled in their place (1 Chronicles 4:41).
character: The biblical record gives no description of his personal character or specific traits. However, he held the position of a leader representing his own house, and he is classed as one who took the leading role in the territorial expansion of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:35-38).

introduce: A man of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as one of the mighty men who came to David when David stayed at Ziklag to escape Saul.
lifetime: He was from the tribe of Benjamin, the kinsmen of Saul, and belonged to the company of mighty men who came to help David while David was at Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:1-2). He is recorded as Jehu the Anathothite, and his name is mentioned among the mighty men of the tribe of Benjamin who helped David (1 Chronicles 12:3).
event: He was included among the mighty men of the tribe of Benjamin who came to help David when David lived at Ziklag to escape the pursuit of King Saul (1 Chronicles 12:1-3). He joined David's camp and fulfilled the role of helping David (1 Chronicles 12:1).

introduce: A man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a son born to Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron and a great-grandson of Judah, by his other wife Atarah.
lifetime: He was born to Atarah, another wife of Jerahmeel the son of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2:26). His sons are recorded as Shammai and Jada (1 Chronicles 2:28).
event: According to the biblical record, there is no account of any particular political or religious accomplishment or specific event that he performed.

introduce: Oded was a prophet of the LORD in Samaria in the time of Ahaz king of Judah, who, when the army of Israel was returning to Samaria with the people of Judah taken captive, met them and told them to release the captives and send them back.
lifetime: He was active when Pekah king of Israel killed 120,000 mighty men of Judah in one day and the sons of Israel took the people of Judah captive and carried them off to Samaria (2 Chronicles 28:6-8). He went out to meet the army returning to Samaria and warned them of the wrath of God (2 Chronicles 28:9).
event: To the army of Israel that intended to make the people of Judah slaves, he pointed out that the LORD, being angry with Judah, had given them into their hands, but that they had slaughtered them in a rage that reached up to heaven, and he told them to release the captives they had brought and let them return, proclaiming that the wrath of the LORD was upon them (2 Chronicles 28:9-11). Afterward some of the chiefs of the sons of Ephraim rose up and stopped them from bringing in the captives (2 Chronicles 28:12-13), and those who were named took the captives, clothed them, fed them, gave them drink, set the weak on donkeys, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brothers (2 Chronicles 28:14-15).
character: Before the army of northern Israel, which was intoxicated with its own victory, he showed the resolve to deliver the message of God without fear (2 Chronicles 28:9). He displayed the aspect of a realistic mediator, stressing the injustice of slaughtering and enslaving the people of Judah, who were their own kinsmen, and urging humane measures (2 Chronicles 28:11-13).

call: Son of Becher of the tribe of Benjamin
introduce: A man recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:8, mentioned as one of the sons of Becher of the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: In the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin he was born as a son of Becher, and he forms a brotherhood with Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth (1 Chronicles 7:8).
character: He is included in the list as one of the sons who make up the house of Becher, and the Bible records no information about his specific deeds or personal characteristics (1 Chronicles 7:8).

call: Son of Imri of the descendants of Perez of the tribe of Judah
introduce: A man recorded as a descendant of Perez of the tribe of Judah and the son of Imri. He is a namesake of Omri king of the northern kingdom of Israel. In the genealogy of Uthai, a descendant of Judah who lived in Jerusalem after returning from Babylon, he appears as the father of Ammihud, Uthai's father (1 Chronicles 9:3-4).
lifetime: In the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 9:4 he is recorded as the son of Imri, the father of Ammihud, and the grandfather of Uthai who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:3-4). There is no record of Omri's own deeds or residence.

call: Officer of the tribe of Issachar in the time of David (son of Michael)
introduce: A man recorded in 1 Chronicles, of the line of leaders who governed the tribe of Issachar in the time of David. He is recorded as the son of Michael and was one of the officials in charge of the tribes under David's system of government.
lifetime: In the period when David reigned as king of Israel, he was recorded as the officer of Issachar among those who administered the tribes of Israel, and he was the son of Michael (1 Chronicles 27:16, 27:18).
event: He was recorded as the officer of Issachar in the list of those who administered the tribes of Israel (1 Chronicles 27:16, 27:18). The Bible has no record of anything specific that he did.

meaning: Servant of Edom, one who serves
introduce: Obed-edom was the head of a gatekeepers' division in the time of David (1 Chronicles 26:4-8, 12). He and his sixty-eight brothers were appointed as gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 16:38), and those born to him numbered sixty-two (1 Chronicles 26:8). Because of the words in 1 Chronicles 26:5, 'for God had blessed Obed-edom,' some regard him as the same person as Obed-edom of Gath, who kept the ark for three months (2 Samuel 6:10-12; 1 Chronicles 13:13-14), or as Obed-edom the gatekeeper and musician before the ark (1 Chronicles 15:18-24; 16:5), but the text does not say that they are the same person.
lifetime: He and his sixty-eight brothers were appointed as gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 16:38). His sons were Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sachar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth, Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth (1 Chronicles 26:4-5), and he, his sons, and his brothers were capable men who performed their duties well (1 Chronicles 26:8).
event: The sons of Shemaiah, his firstborn, were mighty men of valor who ruled over their fathers' houses (1 Chronicles 26:6-7), and those born to Obed-edom numbered sixty-two (1 Chronicles 26:8). When lots were cast for who would guard the gates, the south fell to Obed-edom and the storehouse to his sons (1 Chronicles 26:13-15).
character: According to the biblical record, Obed-edom led a house that was reckoned as men of ability and great strength (1 Chronicles 26:8). Also, as a Levite who feared God and applied himself faithfully to the work of the temple, he carried out his duty with precision, and his household prospered to the point that, having many descendants, it could make up an important organization of the gatekeepers of the temple (1 Chronicles 26:4-8).

meaning: Servant of Edom, one who serves
introduce: Obed-edom is a man who appears in 2 Chronicles 25:24, recorded as the one who in the time of Amaziah king of Judah guarded the gold and silver and the vessels in the house of God (2 Chronicles 25:24).
lifetime: After Amaziah king of Judah was defeated in the war with Jehoash king of Israel, when Jehoash broke down the wall of Jerusalem and took all the gold and silver and the vessels found in the house of God with Obed-edom, Obed-edom is mentioned as the one who was guarding them (2 Chronicles 25:23-24).
event: Jehoash king of Israel came to Jerusalem and took all the gold and silver and the vessels found in the house of God with Obed-edom, and the treasures of the king's house, and hostages as well, and returned to Samaria (2 Chronicles 25:24). The text makes no mention of Obed-edom's own actions.

introduce: Zabad fathered Ephlal, and Ephlal fathered Obed
lifetime: He was a descendant of Attai, who was born to the daughter of Sheshan of the house of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah and became the wife of Jarha his Egyptian servant; Attai fathered Nathan, Nathan fathered Zabad, Zabad fathered Ephlal, and Ephlal fathered Obed (1 Chronicles 2:34-37).
event: He was born of Ephlal and fathered Jehu (1 Chronicles 2:37-38). Apart from the genealogy, no personal deeds of his are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Obed is a name that in Hebrew carries the meaning of worshiper or servant, a man mentioned as one of David's mighty men, the military organization of King David. According to the biblical record he is classed as one of the influential mighty men who made up David's military base.
lifetime: During David's reign he carried out military duties at his side (1 Chronicles 11:47). Detailed records of his life, such as the specific background of how he joined David's army or his birthplace, do not remain in the Bible.
event: His name is recorded in the list enumerating David's mighty men, together with Eliel and Jaasiel the Mezobaite (1 Chronicles 11:47). There is no separate record of any particular battle or specific military exploit that he performed.

introduce: Obed was a grandson of Obed-edom of the tribe of Levi, a son of Shemaiah recorded in the divisions of the gatekeepers in the time of David (1 Chronicles 26:1, 1 Chronicles 26:4-7).
lifetime: Obed was a son of Shemaiah and a brother of Othni, Rephael, and Elzabad, and the sons of Shemaiah are recorded as men of ability, descendants of Obed-edom who did that work well (1 Chronicles 26:6-8).
event: In the record of the divisions of the gatekeepers in the time of David, his name appears as one of the sons of Shemaiah (1 Chronicles 26:7). The Bible does not record any specific gate or duty that he held.
character: The Bible records that his brothers of the house, including Obed, were all men of ability and strength (1 Chronicles 26:7).

call: Father of Azariah (father of a commander of hundreds)
introduce: A man who appears in 2 Chronicles 23, the father of Azariah, one of the commanders of hundreds who took part in the process of setting Joash king of Judah on the throne and driving out Queen Athaliah.
lifetime: He is mentioned as the father of Azariah, one of the commanders of hundreds with whom the priest Jehoiada made a covenant in order to restore the kingship of Judah (2 Chronicles 23:1).
event: After the priest Jehoiada made a covenant with the commanders of hundreds, and they gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah and the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel and came to Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 23:1-2), he is recorded as the father of Azariah, the commander of hundreds who took part in that covenant (2 Chronicles 23:1). No deeds of Obed himself are recorded.

introduce: Ozem is a man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, a son of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2:25).
lifetime: He was born as a son of Jerahmeel, a great-grandson of Judah, and his brothers were Ram the firstborn, Bunah, Oren, and Ahijah (1 Chronicles 2:25).
event: According to the biblical record, there is no account of any personal accomplishment or particular event of Ozem (1 Chronicles 2:26).

introduce: Oholibamah is a man who appears in the list enumerating the chiefs of Edom, classed in the biblical text as a chief, that is, a ruler or head of a tribe, of Edom.
lifetime: Oholibamah is mentioned as one of the chiefs who lived in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:41). He is also included in the list of the chiefs of Edom in the record of Chronicles (1 Chronicles 1:52).
event: His name is recorded as one of the chiefs of Edom who descended from Esau (Genesis 36:40-41, 1 Chronicles 1:52). The Bible has no record of any personal deeds of his.

call: Eleventh king of Judah in the south
introduce: Jotham was the eleventh king of the southern kingdom of Judah, a son of King Uzziah. He took the throne at the age of 25 and reigned in Jerusalem for 16 years.
lifetime: From the time his father Uzziah was struck with leprosy and lived in a separate house, he took over the king's duties and governed the people (2 Kings 15:5). After his father's death he began to rule alone at the age of 25 and reigned a total of 16 years (2 Kings 15:32-33). After Jotham died, his son Ahaz succeeded to the throne (2 Kings 15:38).
event: He built the upper gate of the house of the LORD and built extensively on the wall of Ophel (2 Chronicles 27:3). He built cities in the hill country of Judah and built fortresses and towers in the wooded areas (2 Chronicles 27:4). He fought with the king of the Ammonites and prevailed over them, so that the Ammonites gave him that year a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat, and ten thousand of barley, and they paid the same in the second and third years (2 Chronicles 27:5). During his reign the LORD began to send Rezin king of Aram and Pekah king of Israel against Judah (2 Kings 15:37).
character: Jotham did what was right before the LORD his God, but unlike his father Uzziah he did not enter the temple of the LORD (2 Chronicles 27:2). During his reign the people still followed corrupt ways (2 Chronicles 27:2). He became mighty because he ordered his ways firmly (2 Chronicles 27:6).

call: Fifth king of Judah in the south (son of Jehoshaphat)
introduce: Jehoram was the fifth king of the southern kingdom of Judah, a son of Jehoshaphat, who took the throne having married Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab. His reign lasted eight years, and he ruled in Jerusalem.
lifetime: As a son of Jehoshaphat he became king at the age of 32 and reigned eight years (2 Chronicles 21:5). He married a daughter of Ahab, followed the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the sight of the LORD (2 Chronicles 21:6). At the beginning of his reign he strengthened his hold on the kingship by killing all his brothers with the sword and some of the princes of Israel as well (2 Chronicles 21:4). In his last years he suffered from an incurable disease of the bowels and died, and the people made no fire in his honor (2 Chronicles 21:18-20).
event: Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah and set up a king over themselves (2 Kings 8:20). Jehoram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots, and rising by night he struck the Edomites who had surrounded him and the commanders of their chariots, but the people fled to their tents, and Edom has been in revolt from under the hand of Judah (2 Kings 8:21-22). In his time Libnah also revolted (2 Kings 8:22). He built high places in the hill country of Judah and made the inhabitants of Jerusalem commit fornication, as it were, by serving idols, and led Judah astray (2 Chronicles 21:11). The Philistines and the Arabians invaded Judah and carried away all the possessions found in the king's house, together with his sons and his wives, so that no son was left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest (2 Chronicles 21:16-17).
character: By forming a marriage relationship with the house of Ahab, he played a decisive role in introducing the evil tradition of Israel into Judah (2 Chronicles 21:6). He showed a ruthless and power-seeking side, so much so that he took power by killing his brothers (2 Chronicles 21:4). His spiritual corruption was so serious that he received a letter of judgment against his evil deeds from the prophet Elijah (2 Chronicles 21:12-15). After he died of a painful disease, he suffered the shame of not being buried in the tombs of the kings (2 Chronicles 21:20).

introduce: Joram was a descendant of Eliezer the son of Moses, a Levite recorded as the son of Jeshaiah and the father of Zichri. His name appears in the genealogy of the Levites who were in charge of the treasuries in the time of King David (1 Chronicles 26:20-26).
lifetime: Joram is recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Levi as a descendant of Rehabiah the son of Eliezer (1 Chronicles 26:25). His grandson Shelomith and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the dedicated things in the time of King David (1 Chronicles 26:25-26). Nothing is recorded about Joram's own duties.
event: Shelomith, the grandson of Joram, and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the dedicated things that King David, the heads of fathers' houses, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the commanders of the army had dedicated (1 Chronicles 26:25-26). Joram's own deeds are not recorded in the Bible.

call: Second king of Edom (a man of Bozrah)
introduce: Jobab is a man recorded in Genesis and 1 Chronicles, from Bozrah in the region of Edom, the second king who ruled the land of Edom.
lifetime: Jobab was the son of Zerah of Bozrah and is recorded as one of the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the sons of Israel (Genesis 36:33, 1 Chronicles 1:44). After Bela died, he succeeded him on the throne (Genesis 36:33, 1 Chronicles 1:44).
event: After Jobab, Husham became king of Edom (Genesis 36:34, 1 Chronicles 1:45).

introduce: Jobab was the king of Madon in the northern region of Canaan in the age of Joshua's conquest, one of the core members of the coalition of northern Canaanite kings formed to resist the army of Israel.
lifetime: He joined the coalition that Jabin king of Hazor had summoned to attack Israel, and opposed Israel (Joshua 11:1). He engaged the army of Israel in the battle at the waters of Merom but was defeated (Joshua 11:5-8).
event: Jabin king of Hazor sent word to the kings, including Jobab king of Madon, and summoned them, and these kings gathered and encamped together at the waters of Merom to fight with Israel (Joshua 11:1-5). When Joshua came suddenly against them at the waters of Merom, the LORD gave them into the hand of Israel, and the coalition was routed (Joshua 11:7-8).

introduce: A man who appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the sons whom Shaharaim fathered by his wife Hodesh (1 Chronicles 8:9).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons whom Shaharaim fathered in the land of Moab by his wife Hodesh after sending away his two wives Hushim and Baara (1 Chronicles 8:8-9).
event: There is no recorded content concerning his life or any particular accomplishment (1 Chronicles 8:9).

introduce: Jobab is a man of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in the genealogies of the Old Testament, the son of Elpaal (1 Chronicles 8:18).
lifetime:
He was born as a son of Elpaal, a man of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:18).
He is a brother of Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber, Ishmerai, and Izliah (1 Chronicles 8:17-18).
Apart from this, no specific records of his life, such as birth, activity, or death, appear in the Bible (1 Chronicles 8:18).

introduce: Jozabad was a man of the tribe of Levi who in the time of King Hezekiah of the southern kingdom of Judah was entrusted with the care of the offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated gifts within the temple.
lifetime: By the order of King Hezekiah and of Azariah, who was over the house of God, he became one of the ten overseers who took care of the contributions, the tithes, and the dedicated things under Conaniah the Levite and his brother Shimei (2 Chronicles 31:12-13).
event: When they faithfully brought in the contributions, the tithes, and the dedicated things, Conaniah was in charge of the work and his brother Shimei was second (2 Chronicles 31:12), and Jozabad became one of those who took care of these things under Conaniah and Shimei (2 Chronicles 31:13).
character: According to the biblical record, he enjoyed the king's trust and is described as a man with the disposition of an assistant who faithfully carried out practical work together with Conaniah (2 Chronicles 31:13). His name Jozabad carries the meaning that the LORD judges.

call: Levite leader in the time of Josiah
introduce: Jozabad is a man recorded as one of the chiefs of the Levites at the Passover in the time of Josiah king of Judah (2 Chronicles 35:9).
lifetime: Jozabad's name is entered as one of the chiefs of the Levites at the Passover that King Josiah kept (2 Chronicles 35:9). He is one of the chiefs who gave the Passover offerings to the Levites, together with Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah, Nethanel, Hashabiah, and Jeiel (2 Chronicles 35:9).
event: Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, and Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, the chiefs of the Levites, gave the Levites five thousand sheep and five hundred bulls as Passover offerings (2 Chronicles 35:9).

call: Son of Jeshua (counter of the temple vessels)
introduce: Jozabad was a member of the community that returned from Babylon in the time of Ezra, a Levite who was present when the silver, the gold, and the vessels were weighed in the house of God and placed into the hand of Meremoth the priest (Ezra 8:33).
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Jeshua the Levite (Ezra 8:33).
event: On the fourth day, when the silver, the gold, and the vessels were weighed in the house of God and placed into the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest, he was there with Eleazar the son of Phinehas and Noadiah the son of Binnui (Ezra 8:33). At that time everything was counted and weighed, and the whole weight was written down at that time (Ezra 8:34).

call: Priest of the descendants of Pashhur
introduce: Jozabad was a man active in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile, whose name is mentioned in the process of settling the matter of marriage with foreign women led by Ezra (Ezra 10:22).
lifetime: He is classed as one of the descendants of Pashhur, and in the community that returned from exile he is included in the list of those who pledged, under Ezra, to send away their foreign wives (Ezra 10:22).
event: He took part in the religious rite of purification led by Ezra and is recorded as one of those who pledged to send away their foreign wives (Ezra 10:22).

call: Levite who married a foreign woman
introduce: One of the Levites in the community of Israel that returned in the time of Ezra who had taken foreign women as wives and was afterward directed to put this away.
lifetime: He belonged to the company of Jews who returned from the Babylonian captivity, and his name was mentioned in the course of the inquiry led by Ezra into separation from foreign wives (Ezra 10:23).
event: When Ezra drew up the list of those among the sons of Israel who had married foreign women, Jozabad was included in the list of Levites who had foreign wives (Ezra 10:23).

introduce: Jozabad was one of the Levites who, in the Judean community that returned from the Babylonian captivity, carried out the role of teaching the law to the people (Nehemiah 8:7).
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian captivity, when Ezra read the book of the law to the people in the square before the Water Gate, he carried out the duty of helping the people understand the law and explaining it while they stood in their place (Nehemiah 8:7).
