event: When Ezra read the book of the law of God, he helped the people understand the law together with Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah (Nehemiah 8:7).

call: Overseer of the outside work of the temple
introduce: Jozabad was one of the heads of the Levites who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, a man in charge of the outside work of the house of God (Nehemiah 11:16).
lifetime: After returning from Babylon, he is included in the list of the Levites who came to live in Judah and Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:16). As one of the leaders of the Levites who settled in Jerusalem, he was in charge of the external affairs connected with the temple (Nehemiah 11:16).
event: Together with Shabbethai, as a head of the Levites, he was in charge of the outside work of the house of God (Nehemiah 11:16).

introduce: Jozabad was one of the commanders of thousands of the tribe of Manasseh in David's military organization who came over to David (1 Chronicles 12:20).
lifetime: He was one of the commanders of thousands from the tribe of Manasseh who returned to David when David went to Ziklag, after going with the Philistines to fight against Saul (1 Chronicles 12:20).
event: He is recorded as one of the commanders of thousands from the tribe of Manasseh who returned to David when David went to Ziklag, and this company helped David against the band of raiders, and all of them were mighty men of valor and became commanders in the army (1 Chronicles 12:20-21).

introduce: The Joseph mentioned in Numbers 1:32 and Joshua 17:17 refers to the eleventh son of Jacob and the ancestor of the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh. The Joseph mentioned in Numbers is used as a term for the descendants of Joseph, and the Joseph mentioned in Joshua signifies the confederation of tribes composed of Ephraim and Manasseh.
lifetime: It was used as a name that refers to the descendants of Ephraim and Manasseh born of Joseph the son of Jacob. In Numbers 1:32 it appears in the passage counting those born of the sons of Ephraim the son of Joseph (Numbers 1:32). In Joshua 17:17, Ephraim and Manasseh are called together the house of Joseph, and it is mentioned in connection with the distribution of their inheritance (Joshua 17:17).
event: In Numbers, those born of the sons of Ephraim the son of Joseph, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war, were counted (Numbers 1:32), and Joshua told the house of Joseph, that is, Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should not have one portion only, but that the hill country would also be theirs, and that they should clear the forest (Joshua 17:17-18).

call: Father of Igal (father of a spy)
introduce: A man who appears in Numbers 13, mentioned as the father of Igal, the spy of the tribe of Issachar.
lifetime: When one representative from each tribe was chosen to spy out the land of Canaan, he was recorded as the father of Igal, the representative of the tribe of Issachar (Numbers 13:7).
event: His son Igal is recorded as the representative of the tribe of Issachar among the heads of the tribes whom Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:3-7).

introduce: Joseph, one of the descendants of Asaph, was from the tribe of Levi, a member of the temple choir organization that continued from the time of David and a man who carried out musical duties.
lifetime: As one of the sons of Asaph, he was under the direction of his father Asaph and prophesied according to the order of the king (1 Chronicles 25:2). When the duties were assigned by lot, he was drawn first (1 Chronicles 25:9).
event: When David set apart from among the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun those who were to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals, Joseph was one of his sons under the direction of Asaph (1 Chronicles 25:1-2). When, small and great alike, they cast lots for their duties, Joseph's lot came out first (1 Chronicles 25:8-9).

introduce: Joseph, a descendant of Bani, is recorded as one of those who in the community that returned after the exile had taken foreign women as wives.
lifetime: As a descendant of Bani, he is included in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives at the time of Ezra's reform (Ezra 10:42).
event: In connection with Ezra's command to put away the foreign women (Ezra 10:10-11), his name was recorded among those of the descendants of Bani who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:42, 10:44).

call: Priest of the house of Shebaniah
introduce: A man who appears in the list of priestly houses recorded in Nehemiah 12, the one who represented the house of Shebaniah among the heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:14).
lifetime: He is one of those who were heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim, and for the house of Shebaniah, Joseph is recorded (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:14).
event: He was included in the list of the heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim and is recorded as the one who represented the house of Shebaniah (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:14).

introduce: Joseph is a figure recorded in the Bible as a carpenter from Nazareth, the husband of Mary, and the legal father of Jesus. He is mentioned as one who inherited the bloodline of the house of David.
lifetime: He was betrothed to Mary, but learned that Mary had conceived by the Holy Spirit (Matthew 1:18). Having been told in a dream by an angel that the child had been conceived by the Holy Spirit, he took Mary as his wife (Matthew 1:20-24). Afterward he traveled to Bethlehem to register in the census, and there Jesus was born (Luke 2:4-7). He fled with his family to Egypt to escape the persecution of King Herod (Matthew 2:13-14), and afterward returned and settled in Nazareth (Matthew 2:22-23). The Bible does not specify his life after the record of his visit to the temple in Jerusalem when Jesus was twelve years old (Luke 2:41-51).
event: When Caesar Augustus issued a decree that all the world should be registered, he went up from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Bethlehem to be registered (Luke 2:1-4). When Herod sought the child Jesus, he took his family and fled to Egypt as the angel directed, and protected the child's life (Matthew 2:13-14). He also had the child circumcised after he was born (Luke 2:21), and took Jesus to the temple in Jerusalem to carry out the rite of purification according to the law (Luke 2:22-24).
character: Joseph is described as a righteous man, and when he learned of his betrothed's pregnancy he intended to divorce her quietly so as not to expose her publicly (Matthew 1:19). He showed an attitude of immediate obedience to the angel's instructions, and acted without delay each time he received instructions in a dream (Matthew 1:24, 2:14, 2:21). He is recorded as a carpenter who earned his living by labor (Matthew 13:55).

introduce: Joseph of Arimathea is a figure who appears in the Gospels of the New Testament, a member of the Jewish council who took care of the body of Jesus and laid it in his own tomb. He was of wealthy status and is recorded as one of the disciples who followed Jesus.
lifetime: He was a member of the council from Arimathea and was one who was waiting for the kingdom of God (Mark 15:43). He was a disciple of Jesus but kept it secret for fear of the Jews (John 19:38). After the death of Jesus he went to Pilate and begged for the body of Jesus (Luke 23:52). He laid Jesus in his own new tomb and rolled a great stone against the door of the tomb (Matthew 27:60).
event: He was a man who had not consented to the decision and action of the council (Luke 23:51). After the death of Jesus he asked Pilate directly for the body and obtained permission (Mark 15:43, John 19:38). He took down the body, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and laid it in his own new tomb that was cut in the rock (Luke 23:53, Matthew 27:60). Together with Nicodemus, who came bringing a mixture of aloes, he carried out the burial procedure of wrapping the body in linen cloths according to the burial custom of the Jews (John 19:39-40).
character: He was a good and righteous man (Luke 23:50). He was rich (Matthew 27:57), and a member of the council who had influence in society at that time (Mark 15:43). He was a man of such courage that he boldly went to Pilate in spite of the opposition of the Jewish leaders (Mark 15:43).

introduce: A figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke, the son of Jonam and the father of Judas. He is recorded as one of the direct ancestors of Jesus.
lifetime: Joseph, as the son of Jonam, is one of the persons who make up the genealogy of Jesus (Luke 3:30). He is mentioned as the father of Judas (Luke 3:30).

introduce: A figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus recorded in Luke 3, the Joseph who is the son of Mattathias and corresponds to an ancestor of Jesus.
lifetime: In the line of Jesus that goes up through Nathan and David, this person is recorded as the son of Mattathias and the father of Jannai (Luke 3:24-25).
event: In the biblical record, no specific achievement or event connected with this person is mentioned (Luke 3:24).

introduce: Joseph is a figure mentioned as one of the brothers of Jesus of Nazareth. According to the records of Matthew and Mark, he is classed with James, Simon, and Judas as the brothers of Jesus.
lifetime: He appears as a member of Jesus' family amid the critical eyes of the people of Nazareth, and his name is given explicitly in Matthew 13:55 and Mark 6:3. John 7:5 records that the brothers of Jesus did not believe in him, and Acts 1:14 records that the brothers of Jesus devoted themselves to prayer with Mary his mother, but there is no verse that singles out Joseph individually.
event: He was spoken of by the people of Nazareth as one of the brothers of Jesus called James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas (Matthew 13:55). The brothers of Jesus did not believe in him during his public ministry (John 7:5), but it is recorded that after the ascension of Jesus his brothers were among the company devoting themselves to prayer with Mary his mother (Acts 1:14).
character: The biblical record gives no direct description of his personal character, but he is understood as one who dealt with Jesus familiarly as a blood relative and in the end accepted his teaching and joined the community (Matthew 13:55, Acts 1:14).

meaning: The LORD is salvation, he heals
introduce: Josiah is the son of Zephaniah, a man in whose house, as recorded in Zechariah 6, Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who had come from Babylon, were staying (Zechariah 6:10).
lifetime: He is introduced as the son of Zephaniah, and Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who had come from Babylon among the exiles, were staying in his house (Zechariah 6:10). There is no other record of his life in the Bible.
event: The word of the LORD came to Zechariah, saying that Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who had come from Babylon, had entered the house of Josiah, and that he should go into that house, take silver and gold from them, make a crown, and set it on the head of Joshua the high priest (Zechariah 6:9-11). Josiah himself is not the object of this instruction; his name is mentioned only as the owner of the house.

introduce: Joah is the third son of Obed-edom of the descendants of Korah in the tribe of Levi, a man who carried out the office of temple gatekeeper in the time of David.
lifetime: He was born as one of the sons of Obed-edom, and during the reign of King David he was given the task of gatekeeper, guarding the gates of the temple together with his brothers (1 Chronicles 26:4).
event: When the temple gatekeepers cast lots by clans for guarding each gate, the lot for the south fell to Obed-edom, and the lot for the storehouse fell to his sons, Joah among them (1 Chronicles 26:13, 26:15).
character: According to the biblical record, Joah and his house were blessed by God with many descendants, and all of them were judged to be able men with the strength to perform their duties (1 Chronicles 26:6, 26:8).

call: Son of Joahaz (royal recorder of King Josiah)
introduce: Joah was a man active in the time of King Josiah of the kingdom of Judah, the son of Joahaz. He is recorded as one of those whom the king sent, together with Shaphan the son of Azaliah and Maaseiah the governor of the city, in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign to repair the house of the LORD (2 Chronicles 34:8).
lifetime: Joah appears as one of those whom the king sent in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign, when he had finished purging the land and the house and wished to repair the house of the LORD (2 Chronicles 34:8). The Bible does not record the time of his birth or death, nor his deeds after this event.
event: King Josiah, in order to repair the house of the LORD, sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah and Maaseiah the governor of the city, together with Joah the son of Joahaz the recorder (2 Chronicles 34:8).

introduce: A man who held an administrative office connected with the property of David in the time of King David. He was responsible for the oil stores belonging to the royal house.
lifetime: His name is entered in the list of those who were over the property of King David, and there is no record in the Bible of his life apart from the work he held (1 Chronicles 27:28, 27:31).
event: As one of those over the property of King David, he had charge of the stores of oil (1 Chronicles 27:28, 27:31).

introduce: Joash was the father of the judge Gideon and an Abiezrite, a man who lived in Ophrah and who owned an altar of Baal and an Asherah image.
lifetime: Joash was an Abiezrite who lived in Ophrah (Judges 6:11), and he had an altar of Baal and the Asherah beside it (Judges 6:25). After his son Gideon tore down the altar of Baal and cut down the Asherah, he was surrounded by the men of the town, who demanded that he bring out his son (Judges 6:30). His son Gideon, after he died, was buried in the tomb of Joash his father at Ophrah of the Abiezrites (Judges 8:32).
event: When his son Gideon destroyed the altar of Baal that belonged to his house, he spoke in defense of Gideon to the people who came to protest. He argued that if Baal was a god he would contend for himself, and so took Gideon's side, and from that day Gideon was called Jerubbaal (Judges 6:31-32).
character: Even under the pressure of the townspeople who sought to kill his son, he was a man of realistic and compromising thinking, defending his son with an argument that denied the divinity of Baal (Judges 6:31).

introduce: Joash was a prince in the time of Ahab king of Israel, whose name is mentioned once in 1 Kings 22, when the king commanded that Micaiah be taken away (1 Kings 22:26).
lifetime: His name is mentioned when the king of Israel commanded that Micaiah be taken and carried back to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son (1 Kings 22:26, 2 Chronicles 18:25). There is no other record of his life in the Bible.
event: He is named as the one to whom the king of Israel told that Micaiah be taken and carried back, with Amon the governor of the city, to Joash the king's son, and put in prison (1 Kings 22:26-27).

introduce: The eighth king of the southern kingdom of Judah, a figure who continued the lineage of the Davidic dynasty. He was the son of King Ahaziah, the only one who survived the slaughter of Athaliah, and he ascended the throne at the age of seven.
lifetime: After his father Ahaziah died, when his grandmother Athaliah destroyed all the royal family, he was hidden by his aunt Jehosheba (2 Kings 11:2). He hid in the temple for six years, and when Jehoiada the priest made a covenant with the captains of hundreds and brought out the king's son and anointed him king, he was enthroned at the age of seven (2 Kings 11:4-12, 11:21). At first, while he was instructed by Jehoiada, he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD (2 Kings 12:2), but after Jehoiada died he listened to the princes of Judah, forsook the house of the LORD, and served the Asherim and idols (2 Chronicles 24:17-18), and in the end he was murdered in the house of Millo by a revolt of his servants (2 Kings 12:20-21).
event: When Joash was enthroned, Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, and all the people tore down the house of Baal and killed Mattan the priest of Baal (2 Kings 11:17-18). To repair the aged temple building, he collected contributions from the people and carried out the repair work (2 Kings 12:4-16). When Hazael king of Aram came up against Jerusalem, there was an incident in which he gave the treasures of the temple and the palace and so turned back the invasion (2 Kings 12:17-18). After Jehoiada died, when Zechariah the son of Jehoiada rebuked the king's wicked deeds, at the king's command they stoned him in the court of the temple (2 Chronicles 24:20-22).
character: While the priest Jehoiada was alive, he showed himself doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD (2 Kings 12:2). But after Jehoiada died, he was swayed by the words of those in power around him, let idol worship go unchecked, persecuted prophets, and showed serious apostasy in the latter part of his reign (2 Chronicles 24:17-19). Toward the house of Jehoiada, which had saved his life, he showed a two-faced side that cast aside kindness (2 Chronicles 24:22).

introduce: Jehoash was the twelfth king of the northern kingdom of Israel, the son of Jehoahaz and the third ruler of the dynasty of Jehu. He was the ruler who recovered from Ben-hadad the son of Hazael king of Aram the cities that his father had lost in war (2 Kings 13:25).
lifetime: Jehoash reigned sixteen years in Samaria after his father Jehoahaz (2 Kings 13:10). In the time of his father Jehoahaz, Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel all the days (2 Kings 13:22). When Elisha fell sick and was about to die, he went to him and wept, lamenting the loss of the chariots of Israel and its horsemen (2 Kings 13:14). According to the prophecy of Elisha he won three victories over Aram and recovered the cities his father had lost (2 Kings 13:25). Afterward he won the war against Amaziah king of Judah, broke down the wall of Jerusalem, and plundered the treasures of the temple (2 Kings 14:11-14). When his reign ended he was buried in Samaria with his fathers (2 Kings 13:13).
event: Jehoash achieved the recovery of part of Israel's territory in military terms (2 Kings 13:25). He also defeated Amaziah king of Judah at Beth-shemesh, took him captive, and achieved the military feat of advancing to Jerusalem (2 Kings 14:11-13). Through this victory he secured military superiority, tearing down four hundred cubits of the wall of Jerusalem and taking the gold and silver articles of the house of the LORD and of the palace to bring to Samaria (2 Kings 14:13-14).
character: Jehoash is judged a king who did evil in the sight of the LORD, and he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin (2 Kings 13:11). Although he called Elisha the father of Israel and showed himself relying on him (2 Kings 13:14), the general tone of his rule simply followed the religious practices of the house of Jehu (2 Kings 13:11).

introduce: A figure mentioned in 1 Chronicles 4:22, recorded in the passage listing the descendants of Shelah the son of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:21-22). In the same verse, the man who ruled in Moab, Jashubi-lehem, and others are recorded together.
lifetime: He is a person recorded among the descendants of Shelah the son of Judah, listed together with Jokim, the men of Cozeba, the one who ruled in Moab, and others (1 Chronicles 4:21-22). All of these are recorded as having been potters, dwelling among plantations and hedges and dwelling with the king to do his work (1 Chronicles 4:23).
event: No specific event is recorded; he is a figure in the genealogy, one of the descendants of Shelah listed in reliance on ancient records (1 Chronicles 4:22).

introduce: From the tribe of Benjamin, one of the mighty men who joined David when he stayed at Ziklag to escape Saul. He is recorded as the son of Shemaah the Gibeathite, after Ahiezer the chief (1 Chronicles 12:3).
lifetime: He was one of the mighty men of the tribe of Benjamin who came to David when he had fled to Ziklag to escape the persecution of Saul (1 Chronicles 12:1-3). He is recorded as the son of Shemaah the Gibeathite (1 Chronicles 12:3).
event: When David was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul the son of Kish, he was among the mighty men who came to him and helped him in the battle (1 Chronicles 12:1). These men were armed with bows and could use both the right hand and the left in slinging stones and shooting arrows, and were kinsmen of Saul from the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 12:2-3).
character: He was a skilled soldier with outstanding fighting ability, good at shooting the bow and able to sling stones or shoot arrows with either hand (1 Chronicles 12:2). The mighty men of Benjamin who joined David's camp are marked by choosing David and giving him their loyalty, although they were kinsmen of Saul (1 Chronicles 12:2).

call: Father of Joah, scribe of Josiah
introduce: Joahaz is a man recorded as the father of Joah, who was sent to repair the temple in the time of King Josiah. 2 Chronicles 34:8 records him as "Joahaz the recorder, father of Joah" (2 Chronicles 34:8).
event: In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, among those whom the king sent to repair the temple, together with Shaphan and Maaseiah, was his son Joah (2 Chronicles 34:8). The deeds of Joahaz himself are not recorded in the text.

call: Chief of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:35)
introduce: A descendant of the tribe of Simeon, a man whose name is recorded in the list of chiefs of the tribe of Simeon in 1 Chronicles 4:35 (1 Chronicles 4:35, 4:38).
lifetime: A man belonging to the list of chiefs of the tribe of Simeon, and those entered in this list are recorded as having been active in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:35, 4:38, 4:41).
event: Those entered above, seeking pasture for their flocks, came to the entrance of Gedor, east of the valley, and found rich and good pasture; in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah they struck the Meunites who were there, destroyed them utterly, and lived there in their place (1 Chronicles 4:39-41).

introduce: Joel is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, the father of Shemaiah and a man belonging to the genealogy of the descendants of Reuben.
lifetime: Joel was a descendant of the tribe of Reuben, and his existence is mentioned because his son Shemaiah appears in the genealogical record of the descendants of Reuben (1 Chronicles 5:4).
event: Joel's son Shemaiah is recorded as a person who, as a descendant of Joel, continues the genealogy of the descendants of Reuben (1 Chronicles 5:4).

call: Chief of the tribe of Gad
introduce: Joel is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, one of the chiefs belonging to the tribe of Gad among the twelve tribes of Israel. He is recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Gad who lived in the region of Bashan and Gilead.
lifetime: He is recorded as a chief of the descendants of Gad, and next to him are listed Shapham, Jaanai, and Shaphat in Bashan (1 Chronicles 5:12). The descendants of Gad lived in the land of Bashan opposite the Reubenites as far as Salecah (1 Chronicles 5:11), and lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon (1 Chronicles 5:16).
event: Joel is recorded as a chief of the descendants of Gad, and this genealogy was recorded in the days of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel (1 Chronicles 5:12, 5:17).

introduce: Joel is a man recorded as a descendant of Korah in the line of Kohath of the descendants of Levi, who became an ancestor of Heman (1 Chronicles 6:33-37).
lifetime: Joel is recorded as the son of Azariah and the father of Elkanah (1 Chronicles 6:36). He stands in the line of the descendants of Korah among the descendants of Kohath of the tribe of Levi (1 Chronicles 6:33-37).
event: The biblical text does not specify any particular historical event or achievement that Joel carried out (1 Chronicles 6:36).

introduce: Joel is a man recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:3 of the Old Testament, a male mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Issachar. He is recorded as the son of Izrahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Tola, the son of Issachar (1 Chronicles 7:1-3).
lifetime: Joel is recorded as one of the sons of Izrahiah, namely Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, and all five, Izrahiah included, were chiefs (1 Chronicles 7:3). His great-grandfather Tola was a son of Issachar (1 Chronicles 7:1-2).

call: Brother of Nathan (a mighty man of David)
introduce: A man recorded in the list of David's mighty men, the brother of Nathan (1 Chronicles 11:38). His name appears in the passage listing David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:26-47).
lifetime: He is recorded in the list of David's mighty men as the brother of Nathan (1 Chronicles 11:38).
event: The biblical text records no specific event done by Joel; his name is recorded only as the brother of Nathan in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:38).

introduce: Joel is a chief of the descendants of Gershon of the tribe of Levi who appears in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, a man active during the reign of King David.
lifetime: One of the descendants born of Ladan, a descendant of Gershon, he carried out his duties in the time of King David within the family headed by Jehiel, a son of Ladan (1 Chronicles 23:8).
event: When David was about to bring up the ark of the LORD, he was recorded as a chief of the descendants of Gershom together with 130 of his relatives (1 Chronicles 15:7), and he is included among those whom David called as chiefs of the Levites and commanded to consecrate themselves and bring up the ark of the LORD (1 Chronicles 15:11-12).

introduce: Joel is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, a Levite in the time of King David who was in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:22).
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Jehieli, a chief belonging to Ladan the Gershonite, and as the brother of Zetham (1 Chronicles 26:21-22).
event: Zetham the son of Jehieli and his brother Joel were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:22).

introduce: A man recorded as the officer over the half-tribe of Manasseh during the reign of King David in the period of the kingdom of Israel (1 Chronicles 27:16, 27:20).
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Pedaiah, and in the time of King David he was the officer over the half-tribe of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 27:20).
event: In the list of those who were over the tribes of Israel, he is recorded as the officer over the half-tribe of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 27:16, 27:20).

call: Son of Azariah (Levite in the time of Hezekiah)
introduce: A Levite who appears in 2 Chronicles, a man who took part in the work of purifying the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah. He belonged to the descendants of Kohath and is recorded as the son of Azariah.
lifetime: In the period when Hezekiah ruled Judah, he performed, as a Levite, duties connected with the purification of the temple (2 Chronicles 29:12).
event: By the command of King Hezekiah, he is recorded as a descendant of Kohath among the Levites who gathered their brothers and consecrated themselves to cleanse the house of the LORD (2 Chronicles 29:12, 29:15). All the uncleanness that the priests brought out from inside the temple, the Levites carried outside to the brook Kidron (2 Chronicles 29:16).

introduce: Joel is a man who appears in Ezra 10, an Israelite man recorded among the descendants of Nebo as one who had taken a foreign woman (Ezra 10:43-44).
lifetime: One of the descendants of Nebo, he is recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:43-44). The Bible gives no separate record of his life or of his return.
event: In the time of Ezra, his name is recorded as one of the descendants of Nebo among those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:43-44).

introduce: Joel, the man recorded in Nehemiah 11, became the overseer of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:7-9).
lifetime: He was the son of Zichri and one of the descendants of Benjamin (Nehemiah 11:9). He became the overseer of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:7-9).
event: He became the overseer of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (Sallu, Gabbai, Sallai, and others), and Judah the son of Hassenuah was second over the city (Nehemiah 11:7-9).

introduce: Joel is a figure mentioned as the author of the book of Joel in the Old Testament, and the son of Pethuel. The Hebrew name Joel carries the meaning that the LORD is God.
lifetime: Little is known of Joel's life from the biblical record. It is only recorded that the word of the LORD came to Joel the son of Pethuel (Joel 1:1).
event: He witnessed the calamity of the locust swarm and through it proclaimed the coming day of the LORD (Joel 1:4, Joel 1:15). He urged the people of Judah to fast, to gather in a solemn assembly, and to repent, and he prophesied that the Spirit would be poured out on all flesh and of judgment on the Gentile nations (Joel 2:15, Joel 2:28, Joel 3:2).

call: Son of Shimri (one of David's thirty mighty men)
introduce: Joha is a man included in the list as one of David's mighty men within the military organization during David's reign (1 Chronicles 11:45).
lifetime: He is recorded as the brother of Jediael the son of Shimri, and was a Tizite (1 Chronicles 11:45).
event: His name is recorded in the list of David's mighty men as Jediael the son of Shimri and his brother Joha the Tizite (1 Chronicles 11:45). The text records no specific event that he did.

introduce: Johanan is a figure mentioned as the eldest son of Josiah, the sixteenth king of the kingdom of Judah. According to the record of Chronicles, he is listed first among the four sons of Josiah.
lifetime: He is recorded as the firstborn son of King Josiah (1 Chronicles 3:15).
event: After the death of King Josiah, Johanan's younger brothers Jehoahaz (Shallum), Jehoiakim, and Zedekiah became kings of Judah, but there is no record that Johanan ascended the throne (1 Chronicles 3:15; 2 Kings 23:30, 23:34, 24:17; Jeremiah 22:11).

call: Eldest son of Elioenai (descendant of David)
introduce: Johanan is a figure who appears in the genealogy of the house of David, a member of the tribe of Judah recorded as one of the seven sons of Elioenai, a descendant of Zerubbabel.
lifetime: According to 1 Chronicles 3, which records the family tree of the house of David after the return from the Babylonian captivity, Johanan was born as a son of Elioenai (1 Chronicles 3:24).
event: Apart from his name in the genealogy showing that he was a descendant of the house of David, the biblical text describes no specific historical achievement or particular event of Johanan (1 Chronicles 3:24).

call: Father of Azariah (high priest in the time of Solomon)
introduce: He is mentioned as the father of Azariah the high priest who was active in the time of Solomon. In the genealogy of Chronicles he is recorded as a descendant of Zadok and a member of the high priestly family.
lifetime: As the father of the high priest Azariah, he is the one who begot Azariah (1 Chronicles 6:10). He is recorded as the son of Azariah the son of Ahimaaz, and so is a great-grandson of Zadok (1 Chronicles 6:8-9).
event: Apart from his place in the genealogy as the father of Azariah the high priest who served in the temple Solomon built, the Bible records no specific historical activity that he carried out himself (1 Chronicles 6:9).

introduce: Jehohanan was from the tribe of Benjamin, one of the mighty men who joined David's army and helped him when David stayed at Ziklag to escape Saul (1 Chronicles 12:1-4).
lifetime: Although he was a man of the tribe of Benjamin and a kinsman of Saul, when David was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul the son of Kish, he was among the mighty men who came to him and helped him in the battle (1 Chronicles 12:1-4).
event: He is recorded as one of the mighty men who came to David when David was hiding at Ziklag to escape Saul, and this company had the skill to shoot well with the bow and to sling stones or shoot arrows with either hand (1 Chronicles 12:1-4).

introduce: Johanan is a figure who appears in 1 Chronicles 12 of the Old Testament, a mighty man of the tribe of Gad who went over to David.
lifetime: He was one of the Gadite mighty men who went over to David at the stronghold in the wilderness, and is recorded as the eighth (1 Chronicles 12:8, 12:12).
event: Johanan was one of the mighty men among the Gadites who went over to David at the stronghold in the wilderness (1 Chronicles 12:8), and is recorded as the eighth of the descendants of Gad (1 Chronicles 12:12). These descendants of Gad were captains of the army, the least of them equal to a hundred and the greatest to a thousand (1 Chronicles 12:14).
character: The mighty men of the tribe of Gad, Johanan among them, were described as having faces like the faces of lions and being as swift as gazelles on the mountains (1 Chronicles 12:8). They were all men skilled with the large shield and spear, and had the capacity of commanders able to lead an army (1 Chronicles 12:8, 12:14). Among them, Johanan was a capable military leader who stood eighth in order (1 Chronicles 12:12).

call: Father of Azariah (father of an Ephraimite leader)
introduce: Jehohanan is a man recorded in 2 Chronicles 28:12 as the father of Azariah, a chief of the descendants of Ephraim. The Bible records no deeds of Jehohanan himself.
lifetime: When the army of Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel took many captives from Judah and was returning to Samaria (2 Chronicles 28:6-9), his son Azariah, together with several chiefs of the descendants of Ephraim, rose up and stood against those coming from the battle (2 Chronicles 28:12).
event: Jehohanan's son Azariah, together with Berechiah the son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah the son of Shallum, and Amasa the son of Hadlai, prevented the captives from being brought in (2 Chronicles 28:12-13), and those named above clothed the captives, gave them sandals, fed them and gave them drink, and brought them to Jericho to their brothers (2 Chronicles 28:15).

introduce: Johanan the son of Hakkatan was one of the descendants of Azgad who, in the time of Artaxerxes king of Persia, finished life in Babylonian captivity and returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.
lifetime: His name is recorded in the list of those who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem with Ezra (Ezra 8:12). He is recorded as the son of Hakkatan among the descendants of Azgad and joined the company of returnees (Ezra 8:12).
event: Among the company that Ezra gathered by the river that runs toward Ahava (Ezra 8:15), Johanan the son of Hakkatan of the descendants of Azgad was recorded along with 110 men (Ezra 8:12).

introduce: Johanan is a man recorded in Nehemiah 12 as a son of Eliashib. The heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites were recorded in the book of the chronicles up to his time (Nehemiah 12:22-23).
lifetime: In Nehemiah 12 he is named together with Eliashib, Joiada, and Jaddua, and in their days all the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites were recorded in the book (Nehemiah 12:22). The heads of the fathers' houses of the descendants of Levi were recorded in the book of the chronicles up to the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib (Nehemiah 12:23).
event: Recorded as a son of Eliashib (Nehemiah 12:23), in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua all the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites were recorded in the book, and the priests were recorded in the book in the reign of Darius the Persian (Nehemiah 12:22). The heads of the fathers' houses of the descendants of Levi were recorded in the book of the chronicles up to his time (Nehemiah 12:23).

introduce: The apostle John, a Galilean fisherman by origin, was one of the twelve disciples of Jesus, the son of Zebedee and Salome and the brother of James. He is known as the author of the Gospel of John, 1 John, 2 John, 3 John, and Revelation in the New Testament, and in the Synoptic Gospels he appears as a key disciple who, together with Peter and James, accompanied Jesus at the principal scenes of his ministry.
lifetime: He was engaged in fishing on the Sea of Galilee with his father Zebedee when he was called by Jesus and became a disciple (Matthew 4:21-22). From the early days of Jesus' ministry to its end he was present at the major events, and he was one of the disciples who stayed at the scene when Jesus was crucified (John 19:26). After the ascension of Jesus he was one of the disciples gathered in Jerusalem (Acts 1:13), and Paul mentioned him as one of those who were regarded as pillars (Galatians 2:9). While on the island called Patmos because of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus, he wrote down the revelation (Revelation 1:9).
event: He was one of the three disciples who witnessed the transfiguration of Jesus on the mountain (Matthew 17:1). Before Jesus was arrested he prepared the Passover meal together with Peter (Luke 22:8), and at the foot of the cross he was entrusted by Jesus with the care of his mother and took her into his own home (John 19:27). It is also recorded that after Jesus rose from the dead he ran ahead of Peter to confirm the empty tomb (John 20:4).
character: Jesus gave him, together with his brother James, the nickname Boanerges, meaning sons of thunder (Mark 3:17). He once showed a hasty and passionate side, asking to call down fire from heaven to consume the villagers who would not receive Jesus (Luke 9:54). Yet he is frequently mentioned as the disciple whom Jesus loved, and in his later years he showed a different side from his early days, such as writing letters that stress love (John 13:23, 1 John 4:7-8).

call: Relative of the high priest Annas
introduce: A figure whose name appears in Acts 4:6, one of those who took part in the council together with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, Alexander, and the family of the high priest. The text gives no separate explanation that he was a relative of Annas.
lifetime: After the healing of the lame man by Peter and John (Acts 3:1-10), he took part in the council that met together with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, Alexander, and the family of the high priest (Acts 4:6). The Bible has no other record of his birth, family line, or office.
event: While the apostles were speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them and arrested the apostles and put them in custody (Acts 4:1-3), and the next day he also took part in the council that gathered in Jerusalem (Acts 4:5-6). The council had the apostles stand in their midst and asked by what power or by what name they had done this (Acts 4:7). The text records no word or action of his in this questioning.

introduce: The father of Peter and Andrew who appears in the New Testament, a man recorded as John, which is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Jonah.
lifetime: Simon Peter was called by Jesus Simon son of John (John 1:42, John 21:15-17), and Peter and his brother Andrew are said to have been men of Bethsaida (John 1:40, John 1:44). The Bible gives no specific record of John's own life.
event: His name appears in the scene where Jesus looked at Simon and said, You are Simon the son of John (John 1:42). There is no record of any other social activity or public achievement.

introduce: Uthai is a man recorded as one of the descendants of Bigvai in the list of heads of fathers' houses who went up from Babylon with Ezra (Ezra 8:14). The Bible gives no separate account of his family line or personal deeds.
lifetime: In the list of the heads who went up from Babylon with Ezra in the time of King Artaxerxes, Uthai and Zabud are recorded among the descendants of Bigvai, and the men with them numbered seventy (Ezra 8:1, Ezra 8:14).
event: His name is recorded as one of the descendants of Bigvai in the list of the heads who went up with Ezra (Ezra 8:14). Nothing else that he did personally is recorded in the text.

call: father of Geber (father of Solomon's district officer)
introduce: He is recorded in 1 Kings 4:19 as the father of Geber, the officer over the land of Gilead. One of the twelve officers whom Solomon appointed (1 Kings 4:7) was his son Geber; there is no record that Uri himself was an officer.
lifetime: He is recorded as the father of Geber, one of the twelve district officers of Solomon's time (1 Kings 4:19). The Bible has no further record of his birth or of the particulars of his personal life.
event: His son Geber became Solomon's officer over the land of Gilead, that is, the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and the country of Og king of Bashan; there is no record that Uri himself took part in any act of government (1 Kings 4:19). Only the fact that his family produced a high official within King Solomon's administrative system is mentioned.

introduce: Uri is one of the persons mentioned in the process of dissolving the marriages with foreign women under Ezra's leadership after the return from the Babylonian exile. In the list of Ezra chapter 10 he is recorded as one of the gatekeepers (Ezra 10:24).
lifetime: His name appears among the gatekeepers in the list of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:24, Ezra 10:44). There is no other record of his lineage or life.
event: His name was entered in the list as one who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:24, Ezra 10:44). In the same chapter the people made a covenant with God to send away all the foreign wives and their children (Ezra 10:3).

introduce: Uriah is a figure who appears in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah in the Old Testament; he is a priest recorded as the grandson of Hakkoz and the father of Meremoth.
lifetime: He was a priest of the period of the return from exile, the grandson of Hakkoz and the father of Meremoth (Ezra 8:33, Nehemiah 3:21). His son Meremoth, on the day of the service, weighed and received the silver, the gold, and the vessels in the house of God (Ezra 8:33), and repaired a section of the wall (Nehemiah 3:21).

call: Priest in the time of Ahaz
introduce: A priest active in the time of King Ahaz of the kingdom of Judah, who was instructed to build in the temple at Jerusalem an altar identical to the altar pattern seen at Damascus.
lifetime: When King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria and saw the altar there, he sent to Uriah the priest a sketch of the altar and its pattern, with all the details of its construction (2 Kings 16:10). Uriah built the altar in accordance with everything that King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, before the king returned from Damascus (2 Kings 16:11). After the king returned and offered sacrifices upon that altar, he commanded Uriah to burn upon the great altar the morning burnt offering, the evening grain offering, and the rest, and Uriah the priest did according to all that King Ahaz commanded (2 Kings 16:12-16).
event: He built the altar according to the pattern King Ahaz had sent from Damascus and set it in Jerusalem (2 Kings 16:11). He did according to all that King Ahaz commanded, including the command to offer the burnt offering and the grain offering on the great altar (2 Kings 16:15-16).
character: He yielded to the king's power and immediately carried out the commands that altered the ordinances of the temple (2 Kings 16:16).

call: leader who stood at Ezra's right hand
introduce: In Nehemiah chapter 8, he is one of the men who stood at the right hand of Ezra the scribe when Ezra stood on the wooden platform made for the occasion.
lifetime: When Ezra the scribe stood on the wooden platform, those standing at his right hand are recorded as Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, and he is one of them (Nehemiah 8:4). His lineage and office are not recorded in this passage.
event: His name is recorded as one of those who stood at Ezra's right hand when Ezra stood on the platform at the reading of the book of the law (Nehemiah 8:4). The text records no specific action of his.

introduce: He is the Uriah recorded in Isaiah 8:2 as a faithful witness, a priest. In the same verse Zechariah the son of Jeberekiah is named along with him as a witness, but there is no record that Uriah was his son.
lifetime: He is called Uriah the priest in Isaiah 8:2. After the LORD told Isaiah to write Maher-shalal-hash-baz on a large tablet (Isaiah 8:1), Isaiah said he would call Uriah the priest, a faithful witness, and Zechariah the son of Jeberekiah to attest it (Isaiah 8:2).
event: In Isaiah 8:2 he was designated to be called as a faithful witness and to give testimony. Apart from this verse, none of his deeds is recorded.
character: He is recorded as a faithful witness, a priest summoned to attest for Isaiah (Isaiah 8:2).

introduce: A man from Kiriath-jearim who prophesied in the name of the LORD against Jerusalem and Judah.
lifetime: He was the son of Shemaiah of Kiriath-jearim (Jeremiah 26:20). He prophesied in the name of the LORD against this city and this land, in words like all those of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 26:20). When King Jehoiakim and all his mighty men and all the princes heard his words, the king sought to put him to death, and in fear he fled to Egypt (Jeremiah 26:21). The king sent Elnathan the son of Achbor and certain men with him into Egypt (Jeremiah 26:22), and they brought him out of Egypt and took him to the king. The king struck him down with the sword and cast his dead body into the burial place of the common people (Jeremiah 26:23).
event: He prophesied against this city and this land as Jeremiah did (Jeremiah 26:20). When King Jehoiakim and all his mighty men and princes heard his words and sought to put him to death, he fled to Egypt (Jeremiah 26:21). King Jehoiakim sent Elnathan the son of Achbor and certain men, who brought him out of Egypt and took him to the king, and the king killed him with the sword (Jeremiah 26:22-23). In the same chapter Ahikam the son of Shaphan protected Jeremiah so that he was not put to death (Jeremiah 26:24).

call: man of Gibeah (maternal grandfather of King Abijah)
introduce: Uriel was a man of Gibeah, recorded as the father of Micaiah, the mother of Abijah king of Judah (that is, Abijah's maternal grandfather).
lifetime: He was a man of Gibeah, and his daughter Micaiah was the mother of Abijah king of Judah (2 Chronicles 13:2).
event: His daughter Micaiah is recorded as the mother of King Abijah (2 Chronicles 13:2). No deeds of Uriel himself are recorded.

introduce: Uz was a descendant of Seir the Horite in the land of Edom, recorded as a son of Dishan (Genesis 36:20-21, Genesis 36:28).
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Dishan, a descendant of Seir, and is a child of Dishan together with Aran (Genesis 36:28, 1 Chronicles 1:42).
event: No deeds of Uz himself are recorded; it is his father Dishan who is listed as a chief of the Horites in Genesis 36:21 and 30.

call: firstborn son of Nahor and Milcah
introduce: Uz is the firstborn of the eight sons born to Abraham's brother Nahor by his wife Milcah (Genesis 22:20-23). His brother Kemuel is recorded as the father of Aram (Genesis 22:21).
lifetime: He was born as the eldest son of Nahor and Milcah (Genesis 22:21). His brothers were Buz, Kemuel, Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel (Genesis 22:21-22).

call: eldest son of Eshek (Benjamite mighty-man chief)
introduce: Ulam was a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as the first son of Eshek. Within the genealogical system of the Bible he is classified as an ancestor of the mighty men who carried on the line of the house of Benjamin.
lifetime: Ulam is recorded as the eldest son of Eshek of the tribe of Benjamin, and he had younger brothers Jeush and Eliphelet (1 Chronicles 8:39).
event: The sons of Ulam were mighty men of valor, archers, and had many sons and grandsons, 150 in all (1 Chronicles 8:40).
character: The Bible describes him and his descendants all as mighty men of valor who were archers, which suggests that his house was a warrior group of outstanding military ability (1 Chronicles 8:40).

call: owner of the garden of Uzza
introduce: Uzza is the name that appears in 2 Kings 21:18 in the name "the garden of Uzza," the palace garden in which Manasseh king of Judah was buried. The Bible gives no description of a person named Uzza himself.
lifetime: No concrete record of Uzza's life remains in the Bible, and the text gives no explanation that he owned the garden or came from any particular family (2 Kings 21:18).
event: After King Manasseh died, he was buried in his palace garden, that is, the garden of Uzza (2 Kings 21:18). His son King Amon is recorded in 2 Kings 21:26 as having been buried in his own tomb in the garden of Uzza.

introduce: Uzzah is a son of Shimei, of the descendants of Merari of the tribe of Levi, and is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 6:29 of the Old Testament. He is distinguished from his namesake Uzzah the son of Abinadab and is recorded as a particular ancestor within the Levitical genealogy.
lifetime: Uzzah was a descendant of Merari; in the line running through Mahli and Libni he is the son of Shimei, and his son was Shimea (1 Chronicles 6:29-30).

introduce: Uzza, mentioned in 1 Chronicles 8:7, is a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as one of the sons of Gera.
lifetime: Uzza, as a son of Gera, belongs to the family line of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:7). Gera is recorded as one of the sons of Ehud, namely Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera (1 Chronicles 8:6-7).

call: ancestor of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: He is mentioned as the ancestor of a family (the descendants of Uzza) of the Nethinim, who served in the temple, among the people of Israel who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel.
lifetime: In the roll of the men of the people of Israel who came up with Zerubbabel and others, he is enrolled in the list of the Nethinim as the one from whom the descendants of Uzza came (Ezra 2:2, Ezra 2:43, Ezra 2:49).
event: His descendants were recorded in the list of those who returned as a family of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:49, Nehemiah 7:51). No deeds of Uzza himself are recorded.

introduce: Uzzi is a figure appearing in 1 Chronicles 7:2 of the Bible, recorded as a son of Tola of the tribe of Issachar and as a chief.
lifetime: Uzzi was a son of Tola, the son of Issachar. The sons of Tola were six men, Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, all heads of their father Tola's house (1 Chronicles 7:1-2). The son of Uzzi was Izrahiah (1 Chronicles 7:3).
event: The sons of Tola were mighty men of valor throughout their generations, and in the days of David their number was 22,600 (1 Chronicles 7:2). The sons of Uzzi's son Izrahiah, namely Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, were all chiefs as well (1 Chronicles 7:3).

call: father of Elah of the tribe of Benjamin
introduce: Uzzi is a man of the tribe of Benjamin who appears in the biblical record as the father of Elah.
lifetime: Uzzi was one of the descendants of Benjamin; he fathered Elah, and his son Elah lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:8).

introduce: A Levite living in Jerusalem, the son of Bani, who after the return from exile served as overseer of the Levites residing in Jerusalem.
lifetime: He was of the descendants of Asaph, that is, a descendant of Mica in the fourth generation, the great-grandson of Mattaniah, the grandson of Hashabiah, and the son of Bani (Nehemiah 11:22). He became overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem and had charge of the work of the house of God (Nehemiah 11:22).
event: As overseer of the Levites living in Jerusalem, he carried out the responsibility of having charge of the work of the house of God (Nehemiah 11:22).

call: priest of the house of Jedaiah
introduce: He is a chief of the house of Jedaiah among those recorded as heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12, Nehemiah 12:19).
lifetime: He is a man belonging to the house of the priest Jedaiah. Mattenai is recorded as head of the house of Joiarib, and Uzzi as head of the house of Jedaiah (Nehemiah 12:19).
event: His name is recorded as head of the house of Jedaiah in the list of those who became heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12, Nehemiah 12:19).

introduce: Uzziah is a Levite who appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Kohath recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:24, the son of Uriel and the father of Shaul.
lifetime: In the genealogy of the descendants of Kohath, Uzziah is a grandson of Tahath (through Tahath and Uriel) and is entered as the father of Shaul (1 Chronicles 6:24). Concrete dates or deeds of his life are not recorded in detail in the Bible.

call: father of Jonathan (father of the overseer of the storehouses)
introduce: Uzziah is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 27:25 and is recorded as the father of Jonathan, who in the time of King David had charge of the storehouses in the fields, the cities, the villages, and the fortresses (1 Chronicles 27:25).
lifetime: There is no record of Uzziah's own life; the only fact is that Jonathan, who had charge of the storehouses, is introduced as "the son of Uzziah" (1 Chronicles 27:25).
event: Nothing Uzziah himself did is recorded in the Bible. His son Jonathan had charge of the storehouses in the fields, the cities, the villages, and the fortresses (1 Chronicles 27:25).

call: priest of the descendants of Harim
introduce: Uzziah is a figure recorded in Ezra chapter 10, one of the descendants of Harim among the company of priests who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:18, 10:21).
lifetime: In the time of Ezra, he is recorded in the list of priests who had taken foreign women as one of the descendants of Harim, namely Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah (Ezra 10:21).
event: Apart from the fact that his name is entered in this list, no deeds of Uzziah himself are recorded in the Bible (Ezra 10:21).

introduce: Uzziah is recorded as the father of Athaiah, a descendant of Perez of the tribe of Judah. Nehemiah 11:4 introduces Athaiah, a descendant of Perez among the descendants of Judah who lived in Jerusalem, as "the son of Uzziah and the grandson of Zechariah," showing that Uzziah was the son of Zechariah and the father of Athaiah (Nehemiah 11:4).
lifetime: Nehemiah chapter 11 is a list of the people who lived in Jerusalem, and among them Athaiah the son of Uzziah is recorded as a descendant of Perez among the descendants of Judah (Nehemiah 11:4). There is no record of Uzziah's own life; he appears only as the father of Athaiah.

introduce: Uzzia is a man whose name is entered as an Ashterathite in the list of David's mighty men recorded in 1 Chronicles chapter 11 (1 Chronicles 11:44).
lifetime: He is recorded as Uzzia the Ashterathite in the list of David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles chapter 11 (1 Chronicles 11:44).
event: Beyond his name being entered in the list of David's mighty men, no concrete deeds of Uzzia himself are recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 11:44).

call: son of Ishi (chief of the tribe of Simeon)
introduce: Uzziel is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles chapter 4 of the Bible, a son of Ishi and one of the chiefs belonging to the tribe of Simeon.
lifetime: A descendant of the tribe of Simeon and a son of Ishi, he is mentioned as one of the four sons of Ishi together with Pelatiah, Neariah, and Rephaiah (1 Chronicles 4:42).
event: Uzziel and his brothers Pelatiah, Neariah, and Rephaiah became leaders of five hundred of the sons of Simeon, went to Mount Seir, struck down the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped, and lived there to this day (1 Chronicles 4:42-43).

introduce: Uzziel is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles, mentioned as a family member among the sons of Bela of the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: Uzziel is recorded as one of the five sons of Bela, namely Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri (1 Chronicles 7:7). As head of a family he stands within the genealogical system of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:7).
character: In the biblical record, no personal temperament or specific traits of Uzziel are described separately (1 Chronicles 7:7).

call: descendant of Jeduthun (Levite in the time of Hezekiah)
introduce: Uzziel is a man of the descendants of Jeduthun among the descendants of Levi, a Levite who took part in the work of cleansing the temple in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah (2 Chronicles 29:14).
lifetime: In the days when King Hezekiah reigned, Uzziel carried out his duty in the temple as a Levite (2 Chronicles 29:14). He is classified as one of the descendants of Jeduthun (2 Chronicles 29:14).
event: Uzziel is one of the Levites who set about cleansing the temple of the kingdom of Judah at the command of King Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 29:14-15). The Levites gathered their brothers, consecrated themselves, and went in to cleanse the house of the LORD; all the unclean things that the priests brought out from inside the temple the Levites took and carried out to the Kidron Valley (2 Chronicles 29:15-16).

introduce: Uzziel took part in the work of repairing the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, and is recorded as the son of Harhaiah.
lifetime: In the project of repairing the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, it is recorded that Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths, and others made repairs (Nehemiah 3:8).
event: Uzziel, son of Harhaiah the goldsmith, repaired one section in the course of the wall repairs (Nehemiah 3:8).

call: son of Nathan (one of David's Thirty)
introduce: One of David's Thirty, recognized for outstanding valor within David's army, and the son of Nathan of Zobah.
lifetime: He is recorded in the list of David's mighty men as Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah (2 Samuel 23:36). In 1 Chronicles 11:38 the name Igal does not appear, but "Joel the brother of Nathan" is recorded (1 Chronicles 11:38).
event: He is recorded as a member of the list of David's mighty men, but no concrete military exploits or personal events of his are recorded in the Bible (2 Samuel 23:36).

introduce: Igal is a figure appearing in 1 Chronicles 3:22 of the Bible, a son of Shemaiah included in the list that records the genealogy of the house of David. He is a descendant of the Davidic dynasty and a grandson of Shecaniah, and is classified as one of the generations of the Davidic royal line recorded by the Chronicler.
lifetime: Igal was born as a son of Shemaiah of the Davidic royal line (1 Chronicles 3:22). As a child of Shemaiah, a descendant of Shecaniah of the line of David, he is mentioned as one of the six sons in the Davidic family line (1 Chronicles 3:22).
event: He is recorded as a person who carried on the genealogy of the house of David, and apart from that there is no record in the Bible of any political activity led by Igal or of any particular event concerning him (1 Chronicles 3:22).

introduce: A figure appearing in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher, recorded as one of the sons of Zophah (1 Chronicles 7:36-37).
lifetime: In the genealogy of the tribe of Asher his name is entered as one of the sons of Zophah (Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah, Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera) (1 Chronicles 7:36-37). Zophah is the son of Helem (1 Chronicles 7:35).
event: In the biblical record no concrete accomplishment or particular event of Ithran himself appears; he is mentioned only as a person who carried on the genealogy of the tribe of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:37).

call: disciple who received the proverbs of Agur
introduce: Ithiel is a figure appearing in Proverbs chapter 30, recorded as the recipient of the teaching that Agur delivered to Ithiel and Ucal.
lifetime: In the biblical record, no concrete information is found about Ithiel's birth, upbringing, or life as a whole (Proverbs 30:1).
event: Apart from the fact that he received wise proverbs from Agur, no separate historical event or accomplishment is recorded (Proverbs 30:1).

call: father of Zaccur (father of a wall repairer)
introduce: Imri is recorded as the father of Zaccur, who took part in the work when Nehemiah rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:2).
lifetime: The Bible has no record of Imri's own life; his name appears only as identifying information in the record that his son Zaccur built part of the wall (Nehemiah 3:2).
event: There is no record that Imri himself carried out any building activity; his son Zaccur built the section next to the men of Jericho in the repair of the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:2).

call: self-styled prophetess of the church in Thyatira
introduce: A figure of the church in Thyatira mentioned in Revelation chapter 2, a woman who called herself a prophet and led the members astray into sexual immorality and idolatry. She is understood to be referred to by the name of Jezebel, the wife of Ahab king of Israel in Old Testament times.
lifetime: Active within the church in Thyatira, she seduced the members through her teaching (Revelation 2:20). The Lord warned that he would cast her on a bed, and cast those who commit adultery with her into great tribulation unless they repent of her deeds (Revelation 2:22). He also said he would strike her children dead (Revelation 2:23).
event: Claiming to be a prophet, she took the lead in teaching the members sexual immorality and in causing them to eat things sacrificed to idols (Revelation 2:20). She was given time to repent but refused to repent of her immorality (Revelation 2:21). As a result she became the cause of the message of judgment against her and her followers being delivered to the church in Thyatira (Revelation 2:22-23).
character: She was characterized by teaching her doctrine as the deep things of Satan (Revelation 2:24). She held a self-proclaimed identity as a prophet, and exerted the influence of misleading those around her and leading them into immoral conduct and idolatry (Revelation 2:20). Despite God's warning of judgment, she showed a stubborn attitude of not turning back from her deeds (Revelation 2:21).

call: man of Gibeon (chief of the Thirty at Ziklag)
introduce: Ishmaiah the Gibeonite is one of the mighty men who came to David and joined him while he stayed at Ziklag, and is recorded as the leader among David's Thirty.
lifetime: Ishmaiah was a Gibeonite from the tribe of Benjamin who went over to David while David was at Ziklag, fleeing from Saul (1 Chronicles 12:4).
event: He is called a mighty man among the Thirty and a leader over the Thirty (1 Chronicles 12:4). No concrete deeds of Ishmaiah himself are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Ishmael is recorded as the father of Zebadiah, who governed all the matters of the king in the days of Jehoshaphat king of Judah. 2 Chronicles 19:11 calls Zebadiah "the ruler of the house of Judah" (2 Chronicles 19:11).
lifetime: There is no record of Ishmael's own life in the Bible. His son Zebadiah is mentioned as the one who governed all the matters of the king when Jehoshaphat in Jerusalem appointed men from among the Levites, the priests, and the heads of the families of Israel to give judgment (2 Chronicles 19:8) (2 Chronicles 19:11).
event: No event carried out by Ishmael himself is recorded in the Bible. His son Zebadiah is mentioned as governing "all the matters of the king" when King Jehoshaphat reorganized the judicial system (2 Chronicles 19:11).

introduce: Ishmael is a man of the tribe of Benjamin, a son of Azel mentioned through the genealogy of the house of Saul. He is recorded as the third of Azel's six sons (Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan) (1 Chronicles 8:38).
lifetime: He was born as a son of Azel, a man of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:38). He stands within the genealogical system that continues from the descendants of Jonathan the son of Saul (1 Chronicles 8:33-38).

introduce: Ishmael was a son of Jehohanan and one of the commanders of hundreds with whom the priest Jehoiada made a covenant in order to set Joash, the son of Ahaziah king of Judah, on the throne (2 Chronicles 23:1).
lifetime: After Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, destroyed all the royal offspring of the house of Judah (2 Chronicles 22:10-11), in the seventh year the priest Jehoiada made a covenant with the commanders of hundreds, namely Azariah the son of Jeroham, Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, Azariah the son of Obed, Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri (2 Chronicles 23:1). This was in order to set the king's son Joash on the throne (2 Chronicles 23:3).
event: The priest Jehoiada gave the commanders of hundreds the spears and shields of King David that were in the house of God (2 Chronicles 23:9), and when Athaliah cried out "Treason!", he ordered the commanders of hundreds who were in charge of the army to bring her out between the ranks (2 Chronicles 23:13-14). Ishmael is one of the commanders of hundreds whose names are entered in 2 Chronicles 23:1.

call: priest of the descendants of Pashhur
introduce: The Ishmael recorded in Ezra 10 was a member of the Judean community that returned from Babylon after the exile, and a descendant of Pashhur, a priestly family.
lifetime: In the time of Ezra he is recorded as belonging to the descendants of Pashhur, a priestly family (Ezra 10:22).
event: In the time of Ezra, his name is entered as one of the descendants of Pashhur in the list of the priests who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:18, 10:22). Apart from this list, no deeds of Ishmael himself are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, a grandson of Elishama of the royal family and one of the king's chief officers, is the man who struck down with the sword Gedaliah the son of Ahikam at Mizpah, whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor (Jeremiah 41:1-2).
lifetime: Ishmael, the grandson of Elishama and the son of Nethaniah, was of the royal family and one of the king's chief officers (Jeremiah 41:1). It was said that Baalis king of the Ammonites had sent him to take Gedaliah's life, but Gedaliah did not believe it (Jeremiah 40:14). Ishmael went to Mizpah with ten men and ate bread with Gedaliah (Jeremiah 41:1), then struck him down with the sword and killed him (Jeremiah 41:2); afterward he went to the Ammonites (Jeremiah 41:15).
event: Ishmael killed all the Jews who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, and the Chaldean soldiers who were there (Jeremiah 41:2-3). On the second day after he had killed Gedaliah, when no one knew of it (Jeremiah 41:4), eighty men from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria were about to go to the house of the LORD, and Ishmael went out weeping to meet them and told them to come to Gedaliah (Jeremiah 41:5-6); he slaughtered them in the middle of the city and threw them into a cistern, but did not kill ten of them because they said they had hidden stores of food (Jeremiah 41:7-8). He also intended to take captive the king's daughters and all the people who remained at Mizpah and go over to the Ammonites (Jeremiah 41:10), but when Johanan the son of Kareah and the commanders of the forces heard of his evil, they went to fight him and met him at the great waters of Gibeon, and the people who were with Ishmael turned and went back to Johanan (Jeremiah 41:11-14); Ishmael escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites (Jeremiah 41:15).
character: He used deceitful tricks, deceiving others in order to achieve his purpose (Jeremiah 41:6-7). He also tried to consolidate a power base through his royal status, and showed a politically extremist tendency, with strong hostility toward the Babylonian system of rule (Jeremiah 40:14, 41:2). Since the warning of Johanan implies that he was planning to murder Gedaliah, it can be seen that he was of a calculating character who carefully prepared the assassination in advance (Jeremiah 40:14).

introduce: The firstborn son born to Abraham and Sarah's maidservant Hagar, he became the progenitor of the Ishmaelite clan.
lifetime: He was born when Abraham was 86 years old, as the son of Hagar (Genesis 16:15-16). Around the time Isaac was weaned, he was driven out of the house together with Hagar at the demand of Sarah, who had seen Ishmael mocking Isaac (Genesis 21:9-14). After surviving a crisis of death in the wilderness of Beersheba, he lived in the wilderness of Paran and became an archer, and took a wife from the land of Egypt (Genesis 21:16-21). Later, when Abraham died, he buried him together with Isaac in the cave of Machpelah (Genesis 25:9). He breathed his last at the age of 137 (Genesis 25:17).
event: He became an archer and lived in the wilderness of Paran (Genesis 21:20-21). His descendants lived from Havilah to Shur, near Egypt on the way to Asshur, and became chiefs of many tribes (Genesis 25:16-18). Esau, the son of Isaac, besides his own wives took Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael as a wife, thereby forming a bond of kinship (Genesis 28:9).
character: In his relations with people he is depicted as having a rough disposition, such that it was said his hand would be against everyone and everyone's hand against him (Genesis 16:12). He also received the prophecy that he would live in hostility toward all his brothers (Genesis 16:12).

introduce: Ishpah is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, appearing as a son of Beriah within the genealogical system of a family of the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: Ishpah is recorded as a son of Beriah, a descendant of Benjamin, and is mentioned together with Michael and Joha as sons of Beriah (1 Chronicles 8:16). His father Beriah, together with Shema, became a chief of the inhabitants of Aijalon (1 Chronicles 8:13).
event: No event or accomplishment carried out by Ishpah himself is recorded in the Bible. His father Beriah, together with Shema, became a chief of the inhabitants of Aijalon and drove out the inhabitants of Gath (1 Chronicles 8:13).

introduce: Izhar is a son of Kohath the son of Levi, and a person in a brotherly relation with Amram, Hebron, and Uzziel (Exodus 6:18). He is classified as one of the principal ancestors within the family of the descendants of Kohath of the tribe of Levi (1 Chronicles 23:12).
lifetime: Izhar was born as a son of Kohath and is a person who forms part of the genealogy of the family of the descendants of Kohath (Numbers 3:27). He is recorded after Amram among the sons of Kohath, and since Amram fathered Aaron and Moses, he corresponds to an uncle of Moses and Aaron (Exodus 6:18, 20). Among his sons was Shelomoth, and among the sons of Shelomoth was Jahath (1 Chronicles 24:22).
event: Izhar became the ancestor of the Izharite family, one of the families of the descendants of Kohath (Numbers 3:27). 1 Chronicles 24:22 records Shelomoth among the sons of Izhar.

call: Father of Zoheth and Ben-zoheth (Judah's genealogy)
introduce: Ishi is a person recorded as the father of Zoheth and Ben-zoheth in the genealogy of the descendants of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:20).
lifetime: Ishi is recorded as the father of his sons Zoheth and Ben-zoheth (1 Chronicles 4:20). The Bible has no record of his parents or his birth.
event: No accomplishment or historical event carried out by Ishi himself is recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 4:20).

call: chief of the tribe of Simeon (father of the conquerors of Mount Seir)
introduce: Ishi is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles 4:42, recorded as the father of Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the leaders who took five hundred of the sons of Simeon to Mount Seir.
lifetime: Ishi is recorded as the father of Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel among the descendants of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:42). Apart from this, the Bible has no record concerning Ishi's own life.
event: His sons Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel became leaders of five hundred of the sons of Simeon, went to Mount Seir, struck down the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped, and lived there (1 Chronicles 4:42-43). No deeds of Ishi himself are recorded in the Bible.

call: valiant chief of the half-tribe of Manasseh
introduce: Ishi is a figure appearing in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, a head of a family belonging to the half-tribe of Manasseh (East Manasseh) and one of its military leaders.
lifetime: Ishi was a member of the half-tribe of Manasseh who lived in the region of Bashan east of the Jordan, and as a chief of his family he held a position of leadership within the tribe (1 Chronicles 5:24).
event: Ishi, together with Eber, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, is recorded as a chief of the half-tribe of Manasseh, and they were all chiefs famous for their valor (1 Chronicles 5:24).
character: The Bible calls the chiefs, Ishi among them, valiant warriors, which shows that they were influential leaders with military ability (1 Chronicles 5:24).

call: eldest son of Asher (progenitor of the Imnite clan)
introduce: Imnah is a son of Asher and a grandson of Jacob, and an ancestor of the Imnite clan belonging to the tribe of Asher.
lifetime: Imnah was born as the eldest son of Asher (Genesis 46:17). He was included when Jacob's family migrated to Egypt (Genesis 46:17), and afterward his descendants formed the Imnite family, one of the families of the descendants of Asher (Numbers 26:44).
event: His descendants formed the Imnite clan and were recorded as one of the families of the descendants of Asher in the census of Israel (Numbers 26:44). The name Imnah appears in historical documents not so much in connection with a particular event or accomplishment as a founder of a family line that makes up the genealogy of the tribe of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:30).

call: father of Kore (father of the keeper of the temple offerings)
introduce: Imnah was a Levite, recorded as the father of Kore, who in the time of Hezekiah had charge of the offerings given to God (2 Chronicles 31:14).
lifetime: He is recorded as the father of Kore.

call: family of returnees who could not prove their genealogy
introduce: A designation for those among the returnees from the Babylonian exile who could not prove their ancestral genealogy. They came up from places such as Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer, but were unable to show whether their clan and genealogy belonged to Israel.
lifetime: After finishing their captivity in Babylon, they returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:1-2, 59). Among the returnees there were some who could not show whether their clan and genealogy belonged to Israel (Nehemiah 7:61).
event: They faced the situation of being unable to establish whether they were children of Israel, because they could not make known their ancestral genealogy (Ezra 2:59). They were those who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, but they could not show whether their clan and genealogy belonged to Israel (Nehemiah 7:61).

call: father of Zadok (father of a wall repairer)
introduce: Immer is a figure appearing in the Old Testament, recorded as the father of Zadok, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:29).
lifetime: Immer is recorded as the father of Zadok. His son Zadok, when the wall of Jerusalem was repaired, repaired the section opposite his own house (Nehemiah 3:29).
event: Immer's son Zadok, at the time of the wall repair work, repaired the section opposite his own house (Nehemiah 3:29). No deeds of Immer himself are recorded in the Bible.

call: father of Pashhur (father of the chief official of the temple)
introduce: Immer is a priest appearing in the Old Testament, the father of Pashhur, who was chief official in the house of the LORD (Jeremiah 20:1).
lifetime: Immer is introduced as a priest, and his son Pashhur was chief official in the house of the LORD (Jeremiah 20:1). No deeds of Immer himself are recorded in the Bible.
event: His son Pashhur had the prophet Jeremiah beaten and put in the stocks at the Upper Gate of Benjamin in the house of the LORD (Jeremiah 20:2).

introduce: Ittai was a military figure who distinguished himself during the reign of King David, one of the Thirty, the band made up of David's most valiant warriors. He is a different person from Ittai the Gittite; he is recorded as a son of Ribai and as coming from the tribe of Benjamin.
lifetime: He is entered in the list as a member of the Thirty, David's elite military organization (2 Samuel 23:29). In 1 Chronicles 11:31 the same person is recorded under the name Ithai.
event: In 1 Chronicles 11:31 as well, he is recorded in the list of David's mighty men as Ithai the son of Ribai of Gibeah, of the descendants of Benjamin.

introduce: Iddo is a person belonging to the genealogy of the descendants of Gershom of the tribe of Levi, and according to the biblical record is one of the members who make up the genealogy of the Levites (1 Chronicles 6:21).
lifetime: Iddo is a descendant of Gershom, the son of Joah and the father of Zerah (1 Chronicles 6:21). In the genealogy of the descendants of Gershom of the tribe of Levi, he stands at a link in the family line running from ancestor to descendant (1 Chronicles 6:20-21).

call: Son of Zechariah (leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead)
introduce: Iddo is recorded as the officer over the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead in the time of King David, and his father was Zechariah (1 Chronicles 27:21).
lifetime: In the list of those who were in charge of the tribes of Israel in David's time, the officer over the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead is recorded as Iddo the son of Zechariah (1 Chronicles 27:16, 21).
event: He is recorded as the officer over the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead (1 Chronicles 27:21). The biblical record does not specify any concrete military or administrative event that he carried out (1 Chronicles 27:21).

introduce: Iddo is a prophet and recorder appearing in the books of Chronicles in the Old Testament, who was active from the time of Solomon through the times of Rehoboam and Abijah and recorded the deeds and prophecies of the kings.
lifetime: He was active from the reign of Solomon to the times of Rehoboam and Abijah (2 Chronicles 9:29, 2 Chronicles 12:15, 2 Chronicles 13:22). His period of activity is concentrated around the division of the kingdom of Judah and the early monarchy.
event: The acts of Solomon, from first to last, are also written in the visions of Iddo the seer, that is, the book Iddo wrote concerning Jeroboam the son of Nebat (2 Chronicles 9:29). The acts of Rehoboam, from first to last, were written in the genealogical records of Shemaiah the prophet and Iddo the seer (2 Chronicles 12:15), and the rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways and his words, were written in the treatise of the prophet Iddo (2 Chronicles 13:22).
character: He was called a seer or prophet, and combined the roles of a historian who recorded the deeds of the kings of his day and a prophet who conveyed visions (2 Chronicles 9:29). His writings were used as important reference works when the Chronicler described the history of the kings of Judah (2 Chronicles 12:15, 13:22).

call: grandfather of the prophet Zechariah (chief of priests)
introduce: Iddo is a person of a priestly family appearing in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah in the Old Testament, the grandfather of the prophet Zechariah and the father of Berechiah. He is recorded as one of the religious leaders of the period of the return from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: Iddo was one of the heads of the priestly families who returned from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 12:4). He is included in the list of priests who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1). His grandson Zechariah prophesied as a prophet (Ezra 5:1, Ezra 6:14).
