event: In the days of Joiakim, the head of the house of Iddo was Zechariah (Nehemiah 12:12, 16). The prophet Zechariah is recorded as the grandson of Iddo and the son of Berechiah (Ezra 5:1, Zechariah 1:1).

introduce: Iddo is a person from a priestly family of the period of the return from the Babylonian exile, recorded in the list of priests who returned to Judah with Zerubbabel and Jeshua.
lifetime: After the Babylonian exile, Iddo is recorded in the list of priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1, 4). In the days of Joiakim, the head of the house of Iddo was Zechariah (Nehemiah 12:12, 16).
event: As a member of a priestly family, his name was entered in the list of priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:4). In the days of Joiakim, Zechariah is recorded as head of the house of Iddo (Nehemiah 12:12, 16).

call: chief of Casiphia (leader of the Nethinim)
introduce: Iddo was a chief of the region of Casiphia at the time of the return from the Babylonian exile; he is the one to whom, when Ezra was seeking men to minister for the house of God, word was sent that he and his brothers, the Nethinim living in the region of Casiphia, should bring men to minister.
lifetime: He was a chief of the region of Casiphia (Ezra 8:17), and when Ezra was seeking men to minister for the house of God, he received, through the chiefs whom Ezra sent, the message that he and his brothers, the Nethinim living in the region of Casiphia, should bring men to minister (Ezra 8:16-17).
event: The chiefs whom Ezra had sent went to the region of Casiphia and told Iddo and his brothers, the Nethinim, to bring men to minister for the house of God (Ezra 8:16-17). Afterward, together with the Levites, 220 of the Nethinim whom David and the officials had appointed to serve the Levites were brought, and their names were recorded (Ezra 8:18-20).

introduce: Jaddai is a person recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra as one of the descendants of Nebo (Ezra 10:43-44).
lifetime: He is recorded in Ezra 10:43 as one of the descendants of Nebo, and that list concerns those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:43-44).
event: His name is entered in the list as one of those involved in the incident of separation from foreign women led by Ezra (Ezra 10:43). All the men in the list to which he belongs are those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:44).

introduce: Issachar is a figure appearing in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, the seventh son of Obed-edom, a descendant of Korah. He is recorded as coming from a family of gatekeepers of the tribe of Levi.
lifetime: He was born as one of the sons of Obed-edom the Korahite, and is stated to be the seventh son (1 Chronicles 26:5). Together with the other sons of Obed-edom, he belonged to a family chosen to carry out the duty of guarding the gates of the temple (1 Chronicles 26:4-5).
event: In the time of King David, lots were cast for each gate for the duty of temple gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:12-13), and his father Obed-edom drew the south and his sons drew the storehouses (1 Chronicles 26:15). This means that he was included in the temple administration system as a member of the house of Obed-edom, who was blessed by God with many sons (1 Chronicles 26:5).
character: The biblical record makes no mention of his personal temperament or any specific traits.

introduce: Isshiah is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles chapter 24 of the Old Testament, the son of Rehabiah, the son of Eliezer the son of Moses, and a descendant of Levi. In 1 Chronicles chapter 24 he is mentioned as a chief among the sons of Rehabiah.
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Rehabiah, the son of Eliezer the son of Moses (1 Chronicles 23:15-17), and in 1 Chronicles 24:21 he is recorded as a chief among the sons of Rehabiah.
event: In the record of the remaining descendants of Levi in David's time, Isshiah is recorded as a chief among the sons of Rehabiah (1 Chronicles 24:20-21).

introduce: A member of the house of Kohath among the descendants of Levi, recorded as a son of Uzziel.
lifetime: Isshiah is recorded as a son of Uzziel the son of Kohath (Exodus 6:18, 1 Chronicles 23:20). He is also mentioned again, in the process of ordering the genealogy of the Levites in the time of King David, as the brother of Micah the son of Uzziel (1 Chronicles 24:24-25).
event: When David distinguished and organized the duties of the descendants of Levi, Isshiah was included in that genealogy as one of the descendants of Uzziel (1 Chronicles 24:24-25).

introduce: Isshijah is one of the descendants of Harim recorded as having taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:31, 44).
lifetime: He is recorded in Ezra 10:31 as one of the descendants of Harim.
event: Isshijah is included in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra as one of the descendants of Harim (Ezra 10:31, 44).

introduce: Izziah is an Israelite recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra as one of the descendants of Parosh (Ezra 10:25, 44).
lifetime: He is recorded in Ezra 10:25 as one of the descendants of Parosh among Israel, and that list concerns those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:25, 44).
event: In the reform led by Ezra, his name was recorded as one of the descendants of Parosh in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:25, 44).

introduce: Isshiah was a Korahite, one of the mighty men who joined David and helped him when David stayed at Ziklag to escape Saul.
lifetime: He was a Korahite who came to David when David was hiding at Ziklag because of Saul the son of Kish, and was among the mighty men who helped him in the battle (1 Chronicles 12:1, 12:6).
event: Together with the Korahites Elkanah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, he was recorded in the list of the mighty men who came to David at Ziklag to help him in battle (1 Chronicles 12:6). His other deeds are not recorded in the Bible.
character: He was a mighty man with skilled combat ability, who could use both the right and left hands to sling stones or shoot arrows with the bow (1 Chronicles 12:2).

introduce: A military leader active in the time of Uzziah of the kingdom of Judah, one of those who commanded the king's army.
lifetime: During the reign of King Uzziah he was one of the king's officers and had soldiers under him (2 Chronicles 26:11).
event: The soldiers under him went out by troops to fight, according to the number counted by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer (2 Chronicles 26:11).

introduce: Hananiah is recorded as the father of the official Zedekiah in the time of Jehoiakim king of Judah (Jeremiah 36:12).
lifetime: In the text there are no deeds of Hananiah himself; it records only that among the officials who sat in the scribe's chamber of the king's palace, after Baruch read the scroll in the ninth month of the fifth year of Jehoiakim, there was "Zedekiah the son of Hananiah" (Jeremiah 36:9-12).
event: His son Zedekiah was sitting in the scribe's chamber with all the officials (Jeremiah 36:12). The Bible does not record anything Hananiah himself did.

introduce: Hananiah the son of Azzur was a prophet from Gibeon who was active in the time of the prophet Jeremiah. He is the man who opposed Jeremiah through his prophecy, in the early part of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, that the yoke of Babylon would be broken.
lifetime: He was born as the son of Azzur of Gibeon, and in the fourth year of Zedekiah king of Judah he prophesied in the temple at Jerusalem before the priests and all the people (Jeremiah 28:1). He contradicted the prophecy of Jeremiah and asserted that they would soon be freed from the oppression of Babylon, but he died in the seventh month of that same year (Jeremiah 28:17).
event: Hananiah prophesied that the LORD had broken the yoke of the king of Babylon, and that within two years all the vessels and exiles that had been taken to Babylon would return (Jeremiah 28:2-4). He took the wooden yoke that Jeremiah was wearing on his neck and broke it, performing a symbolic act that in the same way the yoke of the king of Babylon would be broken (Jeremiah 28:10-11). Afterward he received from Jeremiah the pronouncement of judgment on his false prophecy, and by dying in the seventh month of that year, his prophecy was not fulfilled (Jeremiah 28:15-17).
character: He openly challenged the authority of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 28:1). From a nationalistic standpoint, through a prophecy that justified resistance to Babylon, he put forward claims that fit the political situation of the time (Jeremiah 28:2-4).

call: grandfather of Irijah, captain of the guard
introduce: Hananiah is recorded as the grandfather of Irijah, the captain of the guard, and the father of Shelemiah (Jeremiah 37:13).
lifetime: The Bible only introduces Irijah, the captain of the guard who seized Jeremiah at the Gate of Benjamin, as "the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah"; there is no record of Hananiah's own life (Jeremiah 37:13).
event: The one who seized Jeremiah at the Gate of Benjamin, saying that he was deserting to the Chaldeans, and took him to the officials, was not Hananiah but his grandson Irijah (Jeremiah 37:13-14). No deeds of Hananiah himself are recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Hananiah is a figure appearing in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in 1 Chronicles chapter 8, a member of the tribe recorded as a son of Shashak.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Shashak, one of the families of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:24-25). 1 Chronicles 8:28 says that those listed in this genealogy were "heads of families, chiefs throughout their generations," and that they lived in Jerusalem.
event: No concrete deeds or historical events of his are recorded in the Bible; he is mentioned only as a name in the genealogy (1 Chronicles 8:24).

introduce: Hananiah is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles chapter 3 of the Old Testament, a son of Zerubbabel, the royal descendant of Judah at the time of the return from the Babylonian exile. He is classified as one of the persons who carried on the lineage of the house of David.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3:19). His brother was Meshullam, and their sister Shelomith is recorded with them (1 Chronicles 3:19). His sons are recorded as Pelatiah and Jeshaiah (1 Chronicles 3:21).
event: Apart from his being included in the genealogy of the generations after the return from the Babylonian exile in the house of David, no record of any concrete historical activity or event carried out by him appears in the Bible (1 Chronicles 3:19).

introduce: Hananiah is a figure appearing in Ezra chapter 10 of the Old Testament, recorded as one of the descendants of Bebai in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:28).
lifetime: In Ezra 10:28, among the descendants of Bebai, Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai are recorded as having taken foreign women (Ezra 10:28, 10:44).
event: In the time of Ezra, his name is recorded as one of the descendants of Bebai in the list of those who had taken foreign women (Ezra 10:28, 10:44).

introduce: A man who took part in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, and who had the occupation of perfumer.
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, when the wall of Jerusalem lay broken down and the project of repairing the wall was begun under Nehemiah's leadership, he joined in it (Nehemiah 3:8).
event: At the time of the repair work on the wall of Jerusalem, Hananiah, apart from his own trade as a perfumer, played the role of repairing a part of the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:8).
character: Besides his professional occupation as a perfumer, he took part voluntarily in the public project of rebuilding the wall and bore manual labor, which shows that various classes of society at that time cooperated in repairing the wall (Nehemiah 3:8).

introduce: Hananiah the son of Shelemiah was a man who took part in the project of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile, an Israelite who played the role of repairing a particular section of the wall.
lifetime: At the time of the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem led by Nehemiah, Hananiah took part in order to repair one part of the wall (Nehemiah 3:30). There is no other mention in the Bible of his father Shelemiah, so his family background and the details of his later life cannot be ascertained.
event: In the work of rebuilding the wall, Hananiah repaired one section together with Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph (Nehemiah 3:30).

call: commander of the fortress of Jerusalem
introduce: Hananiah is one of the persons whom Nehemiah, after building the wall, put in charge of Jerusalem, recorded as the commander of the fortress (Nehemiah 7:2).
lifetime: He was put in charge of Jerusalem together with Nehemiah's brother Hanani, and was recorded as a man who was faithful and who feared God more than most (Nehemiah 7:2).
event: After the city had been built, the doors set in place, and the gatekeepers, the singers, and the Levites appointed, Nehemiah put him in charge of Jerusalem, as the commander of the fortress, together with Hanani (Nehemiah 7:1-2).
character: The Bible records that among people he was outstanding in the fear of God, and he was regarded as having a character far more faithful than ordinary people (Nehemiah 7:2).

introduce: An Israelite who appears as one of those who set their seal to the covenant document after the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:23).
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, he lived in Jerusalem and took part in the process of renewing the covenant led by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:1). In this list, Hananiah is recorded as one of the leaders who set their seal (Nehemiah 10:23).
event: He joined in signing and sealing the covenant document by which the people of Israel pledged to observe the law of God and to keep all the commandments and ordinances written in the law of Moses (Nehemiah 10:29). In this process he affixed his own seal as one of the leaders who took part in the covenant (Nehemiah 10:23).

call: Priestly head of the family of Jeremiah
introduce: A priest of the time of Nehemiah, recorded as head of the priests of the house of Jeremiah in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12).
lifetime: He is recorded as one who became head of the priests in the days of Joiakim, as head of the house of Jeremiah (Nehemiah 12:12).
event: At the dedication ceremony held after the completion of the wall of Jerusalem, he took a trumpet as one of the priests (Nehemiah 12:41).

introduce: Hanani is a seer who was active in the time of King Asa of the kingdom of Judah, recorded as the father of the prophet Jehu.
lifetime: He appears after the incident in which King Asa, when Baasha king of Israel built Ramah to prevent traffic with Judah, sent silver and gold to Ben-hadad king of Aram, asked for his help, and made an alliance (2 Chronicles 16:1-7). The Bible has no record of his detailed life or death after he pointed out King Asa's fault (2 Chronicles 16:7-10).
event: He characterized King Asa's act of making an alliance with the king of Aram as relying on the king of Aram instead of relying on God, and criticized it strongly (2 Chronicles 16:7). Reminding the king of the earlier event in which God had defeated the army of the Cushites and the Libyans, he proclaimed that the eyes of the LORD range throughout the whole earth to help those whose hearts are fully devoted to Him (2 Chronicles 16:8-9). Because of this, King Asa became angry and punished him by putting him in prison (2 Chronicles 16:10).
character: Even before the king's power, he showed an unyielding uprightness that did not hesitate to speak frankly about wrong state administration and wrong judgment in matters of faith (2 Chronicles 16:7). He had a logical attitude, citing past historical events as grounds and analyzing and conveying the situation objectively (2 Chronicles 16:8).

introduce: Hanani is a figure appearing in 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles of the Old Testament, the father of the prophet Jehu and a seer who was active in the time of King Asa of Judah.
lifetime: Hanani was a seer who was active in relation to the royal house during the reign of King Asa of the southern kingdom of Judah (2 Chronicles 16:7). He rebuked Asa for making an alliance with Ben-hadad king of Aram to ward off an invasion by the northern kingdom of Israel and for sending the treasures of the temple (2 Chronicles 16:7). Afterward he incurred the anger of King Asa and was put in prison (2 Chronicles 16:10). His son Jehu is also recorded as a prophet who was active in the times of Baasha and Jehoshaphat (1 Kings 16:1, 2 Chronicles 19:2).
event: Hanani pointed out that Asa had made a treaty with the king of Aram instead of relying on God, and criticized this as the result of not relying on God (2 Chronicles 16:7-8). He reminded the king of the earlier event in which God had defeated the army of the Cushites and the Libyans, and rebuked the king's unbelief (2 Chronicles 16:8-9). Because of this incident King Asa became angry with him, put him in prison, and at that time oppressed some of the people (2 Chronicles 16:10).
character: Hanani showed an upright character that did not bend its position even before the king's power and delivered a critical message (2 Chronicles 16:7). He had a logical attitude, recognizing the context before and after the event and analyzing the present situation by citing earlier historical facts (2 Chronicles 16:8). He also showed a firmness that did not stop his prophetic mission even in the situation of imprisonment brought on by the oppression of power (2 Chronicles 16:10).

call: priest of the descendants of Immer
introduce: Hanani is a figure appearing in Ezra chapter 10 of the Old Testament, one of the descendants of Immer, a priestly family, in the list of those who had taken foreign women after the return from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: As one of the descendants of Immer, he was recorded in the list of the priests who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:18, 10:20).
event: His name is recorded in the list of those who had taken foreign women in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:20, 10:44). The text has no individual record that he pledged to send away his wife.

introduce: Hanani is a figure appearing in the book of Nehemiah of the Old Testament, a brother of the leader Nehemiah at the time of the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem, and an official who held administrative responsibility for Jerusalem.
lifetime: When Nehemiah was in the citadel of Susa, one of his brothers, Hanani, came from Judah with some men (Nehemiah 1:2). Afterward, when the wall of Jerusalem had been built, Nehemiah put Hanani and Hananiah the commander of the fortress in charge of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 7:2).
event: He came from Judah and reported to Nehemiah the condition of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 1:2-3). After the wall was built, he undertook the governing of Jerusalem together with Hananiah the commander of the fortress (Nehemiah 7:2).
character: Hanani was evaluated by Nehemiah as one outstanding among the people in the fear of God (Nehemiah 7:2). He was also faithful to people, and many people trusted him (Nehemiah 7:2).

call: priest at the dedication of the wall
introduce: Hanani is a man of a priestly family who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, a priest with a trumpet who is mentioned as one who held the musical instruments of David (Nehemiah 12:36).
lifetime: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem led by Nehemiah, he took part in the procession, holding the musical instruments of David the man of God and sounding the trumpet (Nehemiah 12:36).
event: In the dedication procession held after the completion of the wall of Jerusalem, with Ezra the scribe going before, he followed after and played the role of marching along the wall sounding the trumpet (Nehemiah 12:36).

introduce: Hanan is a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin recorded in the genealogy of the house of Saul. His is a name mentioned when the genealogy of the descendants of Benjamin is set out in 1 Chronicles chapters 8 and 9.
lifetime: Hanan is recorded as the last, the sixth, of the six sons of Azel (1 Chronicles 8:38). Also in 1 Chronicles chapter 9 he appears in the same way as a son of Azel (1 Chronicles 9:44).

introduce: Hanan the son of Maacah is a person recorded in the list of David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles chapter 11 (1 Chronicles 11:43).
lifetime: Hanan the son of Maacah is included and mentioned in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:43).

call: ancestor of a family of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Hanan is a person recorded as the ancestor of one of the Nethinim who returned from the captivity in Babylon. He appears in the lists of returnees in Ezra and Nehemiah, and forms a genealogy as the founder of a family of temple servants.
lifetime: Hanan is mentioned as the ancestor of the Nethinim who returned to Jerusalem in the course of the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 7:49). He is entered as the ancestor of that family within the list of the descendants of the Nethinim who returned under the leadership of Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:46).
event: The descendants of Hanan were classified as Nethinim carrying out duties in the temple and took part in the service of the temple at Jerusalem (Ezra 2:46). After the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem led by Nehemiah, his descendants were active as members of a religious community that helped the smooth operation of the temple (Nehemiah 7:49).

introduce: Hanan is one of the Levites who, after the return from the Babylonian exile, when Ezra read the law in Jerusalem, interpreted the law for the people and made them understand it.
lifetime: As a Levite who returned from Babylon, when Ezra read the law in the square before the Water Gate in Jerusalem, together with the other Levites he read the book of the law of God and explained its meaning so that the people might understand the law (Nehemiah 8:7-8).
event: When Ezra read the law, Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites made the people standing in that place understand the law (Nehemiah 8:7).

introduce: He is one of the Levites who returned to Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah and set their seal to the covenant pledging to keep the law of God.
lifetime: As a member of the returned community that came back to Jerusalem after finishing the captivity in Babylon, he took part in the renewal of the covenant led by Nehemiah and set his seal (Nehemiah 10:10).
event: In the covenant by which the people of Israel swore to separate themselves from the foreigners and follow the law of God, he put his name in the list of the Levites and set his seal (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:9-10, 10:28-29).

introduce: Hanan is a person who appears as one of the leaders who made a covenant with God and set their seal after the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah.
lifetime: His name is recorded in the list of leaders who signed when the covenant was concluded in Jerusalem under the leadership of Nehemiah after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 10:22).
event: He is one of those who set their seal to the covenant in which the people of Israel swore to separate themselves from the foreigners, to keep the law, not to intermarry with the people of the land, and not to buy goods on the Sabbath and holy days (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:28-31). His name is recorded in the list of the heads of the people (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:22).

introduce: Hanan is one of the persons of leadership rank who set their seal to the covenant document that the people of Israel made with God, under the leadership of Nehemiah the governor of Judah, after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 10:1). His name is recorded in the list of the heads of the people (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:26).
lifetime: He is recorded among the names that set their seal to the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:26), and belongs to the list of the heads of the people (Nehemiah 10:14).
event: He is included in the list of those who affixed their seals that appears in Nehemiah chapter 10 (Nehemiah 10:26). This covenant contains the oath to keep the law, not to intermarry with the people of the land, and to observe the Sabbath (Nehemiah 10:28-31).

call: son of Zaccur (keeper of the storehouses)
introduce: Hanan is a person appearing in the book of Nehemiah of the Old Testament, the grandson of Mattaniah and the son of Zaccur. He is the man whom Nehemiah made next in rank when he appointed the treasurers of the storehouses, and his duty was to distribute to their brothers.
lifetime: Hanan is the son of Zaccur, the grandson of Mattaniah (Nehemiah 13:13). Nehemiah appointed as treasurers Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, and made Hanan next in rank (Nehemiah 13:13).
event: Nehemiah appointed Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites as treasurers of the storehouses, and made Hanan next in rank (Nehemiah 13:13). This was because they were regarded as faithful, and their duty was to distribute to their brothers (Nehemiah 13:13).
character: According to the biblical record, Hanan was regarded as faithful and was entrusted with the duty (Nehemiah 13:13). This suggests that he was a person who, together with administrative ability, was trusted by the one who appointed him (Nehemiah 13:13).

call: eldest son of Reuben (progenitor of the Hanochite clan)
introduce: Hanoch is the first of the four sons of Reuben, the eldest son of Jacob, and the person who became the progenitor of the Hanochite clan within the tribe of Reuben, one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
lifetime: When Jacob migrated to Egypt with his sons, he went with them, and at that time he is recorded as one of the sons of Reuben (Genesis 46:9). Afterward, when the people of Israel came out of Egypt and were counted in the census, he is mentioned as the one who formed the Hanochite family of the descendants of Reuben (Numbers 26:5).
event: In the census of Israel he was entered as the founder of the Hanochite clan and became one pillar making up the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben (Numbers 26:5, 1 Chronicles 5:3).

introduce: Hanun was the sixth son of Zalaph, a man who took part in the historic work of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: Hanun was born as the sixth son of Zalaph, and in the project of repairing the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, he repaired one section together with Hananiah the son of Shelemiah (Nehemiah 3:30).
event: In the work of repairing the wall of Jerusalem, he played the role of repairing one section of the wall together with others (Nehemiah 3:30).

call: commander of the residents of Zanoah (repairer of the Valley Gate)
introduce: One of the persons who took part in the project of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, he is the man who repaired the Valley Gate together with the residents of Zanoah.
lifetime: He took part in the work of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem together with the residents of Zanoah (Nehemiah 3:13).
event: Hanun, together with the residents of Zanoah, repaired the Valley Gate, setting up the gate, installing its doors, bolts, and bars, and also repaired a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Dung Gate (Nehemiah 3:13).

introduce: Hadoram is the man who appears in 2 Chronicles 10:18 as the overseer of the forced laborers in the time of Rehoboam, and in the parallel text he is recorded as Adoniram. Adoniram appears as a supervisor in the time of David and in the time of Solomon, and in Solomon's time he was overseer of the workers sent to Lebanon.
lifetime: In Solomon's time Adoniram the son of Abda was a supervisor (1 Kings 4:6) and was overseer of the workers sent to Lebanon (1 Kings 5:14). When Solomon's son Rehoboam received the demand of Israel at Shechem, he sent Hadoram, the overseer of the forced laborers, but the Israelites stoned him to death (2 Chronicles 10:18, 1 Kings 12:18).
event: When the people of Israel demanded of Rehoboam that he lighten the hard service and heavy yoke that the king's father had imposed (2 Chronicles 10:4), Rehoboam sent Hadoram, the overseer of the forced laborers. But the Israelites stoned him to death, and King Rehoboam hurriedly mounted his chariot and fled to Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 10:18).

call: ancestor of a commoner family that returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: He is mentioned as the ancestor of a commoner family among the people of Israel who returned to Jerusalem under the leadership of Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile. He appears in the genealogies and the lists of returnees in Ezra and Nehemiah, and the descendants of Harim are clearly classified as members of the returned community.
lifetime: The descendants of Harim, 320 persons, are recorded in the list of those who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:32, Nehemiah 7:35).
event: The descendants of Harim, 320 persons, are recorded in the list of those who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem and Judah (Ezra 2:32). Among the Israelites who had taken foreign women, Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon, and others are recorded as descendants of Harim (Ezra 10:31).

call: ancestor of a priestly family that returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Harim is the ancestor of a priestly family that returned from the captivity in Babylon, recorded in the lists of returnees of Ezra and Nehemiah as the descendants of Harim among the priests, 1,017 persons.
lifetime: The descendants of Harim, 1,017 persons, are recorded in the list of priests who returned from Babylon (Ezra 2:36-39). In the list of returnees recorded by Nehemiah as well, the descendants of Harim the priest are recorded again with the same number (Nehemiah 7:42).
event: The priestly family bearing the name Harim was a large family with a total of 1,017 descendants at the time of the return from the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:39). The same person, or a family of the same name, is recorded with the same number as a priestly family in the list of returnees of the time of Nehemiah as well (Nehemiah 7:42).

introduce: Harim is a person of a priestly family that returned from the captivity in Babylon, one of the leaders who sealed the covenant made after the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah.
lifetime: Harim is recorded in the list of the priests who set their seals to the covenant led by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:5, 10:8).
event: His name is recorded as one of the priests who sealed the covenant of the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:5, 10:8). In the record of those who became heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim, there is Adna in the house of Harim (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:15).

call: leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Harim is one of the heads of the people who set their seal to the covenant concluded under the leadership of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:27).
lifetime: Harim is recorded as one of the heads of the people who set their seals to the covenant led by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:27).
event: Harim set his seal to the covenant as one of the heads of the people (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:27). It was a covenant in which, together with the rest of the people, they swore with a curse to separate themselves from the foreigners and to keep the law of God (Nehemiah 10:28-30).

call: leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Hariph is a person whose name is recorded among the heads of the people who set their seal to the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:19).
lifetime: Hariph is recorded by name as one of the heads of the people who set their seals to the covenant led by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:19). No other deeds of his are recorded in the Bible.
event: Hariph is included in the list of the leaders who signed the sealed covenant document drawn up when the people of Israel resolved before God to keep the law and maintain a holy community (Nehemiah 10:19).

introduce: Hashabiah is recorded as the great-grandfather of Shemaiah, a Levite of the descendants of Merari. The Bible does not record any deeds of Hashabiah himself.
lifetime: Hashabiah appears only in the phrase "the great-grandson of Hashabiah" in the genealogy of Shemaiah the Levite (Nehemiah 11:15, 1 Chronicles 9:14). The Bible has no record of Hashabiah's own life.
event: Shemaiah is the son of Hasshub, the grandson of Azrikam, the great-grandson of Hashabiah, and the great-great-grandson of Bunni (Nehemiah 11:15). Nothing Hashabiah himself did is recorded; the one recorded as a Levite living in Jerusalem is Shemaiah (Nehemiah 11:15).

introduce: Hashabiah is a Levite singer appearing in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, a son of Jeduthun, who in the time of David was entrusted with the duty of playing instruments and offering praise in the temple.
lifetime: Hashabiah, as a son of Jeduthun, was assigned by lot to the twelfth division among the singers whom David set apart for the service of the temple (1 Chronicles 25:19). As one of the sons of Jeduthun, under the direction of his father Jeduthun he played the lyre in giving thanks and praise to the LORD (1 Chronicles 25:3), and served by singing in the house of the LORD God with cymbals, harps, and lyres (1 Chronicles 25:6).
event: When David cast lots for the duties of those whom he had set apart for service from among the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun (1 Chronicles 25:1, 25:8), Hashabiah drew the twelfth, and with him were his sons and brothers, twelve in all (1 Chronicles 25:19).

introduce: A Levite of the descendants of Hebron in the time of David king of Israel, who served King David in an office west of the Jordan.
lifetime: During David's reign he was entrusted with the responsibility of caring for the affairs of Israel west of the Jordan (1 Chronicles 26:30).
event: Hashabiah of the Hebronites and his relatives, 1,700 capable men, had charge of the affairs of Israel west of the Jordan for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king (1 Chronicles 26:30).

call: son of Kemuel (officer of the Levites)
introduce: A man of the tribe of Levi recorded, in the time of King David, as the officer of the Levites among those in charge of the tribes of Israel.
lifetime: Hashabiah the son of Kemuel is recorded as the officer of the Levites among those in charge of the tribes of Israel in the time of David (1 Chronicles 27:16-17).
event: In the list of those in charge of the tribes of Israel, the officer of the Levites was Hashabiah the son of Kemuel, and the officer of the descendants of Aaron was Zadok (1 Chronicles 27:17).

call: Levite leader in the time of Josiah
introduce: Hashabiah is recorded as an officer of the Levites in the time of Josiah king of Judah, one of the officers who gave the Levites Passover offerings at Josiah's Passover.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the officers of the Levites at the Passover kept in the eighteenth year of King Josiah (2 Chronicles 35:9, 35:19).
event: Hashabiah, together with the officers of the Levites, Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah, Nethanel, Jeiel, and Jozabad, gave the Levites five thousand sheep and five hundred bulls as Passover offerings (2 Chronicles 35:9).

call: Merarite Levite who returned with Ezra
introduce: Hashabiah is a Levite who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra at the time of the return from the Babylonian exile, a person belonging to the descendants of Merari.
lifetime: When the company that had come up from Babylon with Ezra assembled at the canal that flows to Ahava, Ezra, finding that there were no descendants of Levi, sent men to bring Levites, and Hashabiah was among them (Ezra 8:15-19). He left the river of Ahava with Ezra's company and went to Jerusalem (Ezra 8:31).
event: Ezra sent the leaders to Iddo, the leader of the region of Casiphia, to bring men to minister for the house of God (Ezra 8:16-17). As a result, Hashabiah, and Jeshaiah of the descendants of Merari, with his brothers and his sons, twenty men, were brought (Ezra 8:19).

call: priest in charge of the silver and gold of the temple
introduce: Hashabiah is one of the twelve leading priests whom Ezra set apart when he came up from Babylon, and who were entrusted with the silver, the gold, and the vessels offered for the house of God.
lifetime: Ezra set apart twelve of the leading priests, namely Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers (Ezra 8:24), and weighed out to them the silver, the gold, and the vessels offered for the house of God (Ezra 8:25). In the chambers of the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, before the leading priests, the heads of the Levites, and the heads of the families of Israel, Ezra charged them to guard them carefully until they weighed them out (Ezra 8:28-29).
event: Ezra weighed out the silver, the gold, and the vessels that the king, his counselors, his leaders, and the people of Israel had offered for the house of God, and gave them to the twelve, including Sherebiah and Hashabiah (Ezra 8:24-25).

introduce: Hashabiah, as ruler of half of the district of Keilah, repaired the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah on behalf of that district.
lifetime: In the repair of the wall of Jerusalem, he repaired the section next to Rehum the son of Bani the Levite, on behalf of the district of Keilah (Nehemiah 3:17).
event: Hashabiah, as ruler of half of the district of Keilah, repaired the wall of Jerusalem on behalf of that district (Nehemiah 3:17).

introduce: Hashabiah is a person of the tribe of Levi who was active in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile. He is recorded as one of those who signed the covenant document concluded under Nehemiah's leadership (Nehemiah 10:11).
lifetime: Hashabiah is recorded by name as a Levite among those who set their seals to the covenant in which the people of Israel pledged to keep the law of God (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:9-11).
event: His name is recorded among the Levites who set their seals to the covenant of the time of Nehemiah, which pledged to separate from the foreigners, to keep the law of God, and to observe the ordinances concerning the Sabbath and the work of the house of God (Nehemiah 10:11, 10:28-39).

introduce: Hashabiah is a Levite recorded in Nehemiah 11:22 as the grandfather of Uzzi, a descendant of Asaph the singer. The Bible does not record any deeds of Hashabiah himself.
lifetime: In Nehemiah 11:22, Uzzi, a descendant of Asaph, is recorded as the great-great-grandson of Mica, the great-grandson of Mattaniah, the grandson of Hashabiah, and the son of Bani. The Bible has no record of Hashabiah's own life.
event: Nothing Hashabiah himself did is recorded. The one who became the elder who led in thanksgiving and prayer was Mattaniah the son of Mica (Nehemiah 11:17), and the one who became overseer of the Levites living in Jerusalem and had charge of the work of the house of God was Uzzi (Nehemiah 11:22).

call: priest of the house of Hilkiah
introduce: Hashabiah represented the house of Hilkiah among those who were heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim.
lifetime: In the list of those who were heads of the priests in the days of Joiakim, Hashabiah is recorded as head of the house of Hilkiah (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:21).
event: He is recorded as the person who represented the house of Hilkiah as head of the priests in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:12, 12:21).

call: giver of thanks and praise at the dedication of the wall
introduce: Hashabiah is a person recorded as a chief of the Levites in the days of Joiakim, of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the scribe.
lifetime: Hashabiah is recorded as a chief of the Levites, and this record concerns the days of Joiakim, of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest and scribe (Nehemiah 12:24, 12:26).
event: Hashabiah, together with Sherebiah and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, as chiefs of the Levites, stood opposite their brothers and praised and gave thanks to the LORD by divisions, as David the man of God had commanded (Nehemiah 12:24).

call: Levite leader at the reading of the law
introduce: Hashabneiah is one of the Levites who, at the assembly in the time of Nehemiah when the people of Israel gathered fasting and confessed their sins, told the people to bless the LORD their God (Nehemiah 9:1-5).
lifetime: Hashabneiah is recorded by name as a Levite at the assembly where the people of Israel gathered fasting and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers (Nehemiah 9:1-2, 9:5).
event: Hashabneiah, together with the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah, said to the people to stand up and bless the LORD their God, who is from everlasting to everlasting (Nehemiah 9:5).

call: ancestor of a family of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Hasupha is one of the families of the Nethinim who returned to Jerusalem by the decree of Cyrus king of Persia after the Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:43). The Nethinim are classified as those who held the office of carrying out miscellaneous duties in the temple.
lifetime: Hasupha is recorded as the name of the descendants of Hasupha, one family of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:43). The descendants of Hasupha are in the list of the people who were released from Babylon with Zerubbabel and others and returned to Jerusalem and Judah (Ezra 2:1-2, 2:43).
event: The descendants of Hasupha are recorded in the list of returnees together with the descendants of Ziha and the descendants of Tabbaoth among the Nethinim (Ezra 2:43), and the same list is recorded also in Nehemiah 7:46.

call: Ezra's associate in reading the law
introduce: Hashum is a person recorded as having stood at Ezra's left hand when Ezra read the law in Jerusalem.
lifetime: After the return from the Babylonian exile, he was one of those who stood beside Ezra when Ezra opened the book of the law in the square before the Water Gate in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 8:4).
event: When Ezra read the book of the law of God to the people, he is recorded as one of those who stood at the left hand of Ezra, who stood on the wooden platform (Nehemiah 8:4).

call: leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Hashum is one of the leaders of the Jewish community that returned in the Persian period after the Babylonian exile, a person who took part in the process of renewing and sealing the covenant led by Nehemiah.
lifetime: Hashum's name is recorded in the list of the heads of the people who set their seals in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:18).
event: Hashum is recorded as one of the leaders who set their seals to the covenant document in which the people of Israel pledged to forbid intermarriage with foreign women, to keep the law, and to observe the Sabbath (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:18).

call: son of Joktan (ancestor of a tribe of the Shemite line)
introduce: Havilah is a descendant of Shem the son of Noah, the twelfth of the thirteen sons begotten by Joktan the son of Eber. In the genealogy of the Bible he is classified as the ancestor of a tribe of the Shemite line.
lifetime: Havilah was born to Joktan the son of Eber (Genesis 10:29). It is recorded that the place where the sons of Joktan lived was the eastern hill country on the way from Mesha to Sephar (Genesis 10:30).
event: The place where he and his brothers lived was the eastern hill country on the way from Mesha to Sephar (Genesis 10:30). Genesis 2:11 has "the whole land of Havilah" which the Pishon encircles, and Genesis 10:7 records separately Havilah the son of Cush, but the Bible has no record whether these are the same person or place as Havilah the son of Joktan.

call: son of Ulla (Asherite mighty man and chief)
introduce: Hanniel is a figure appearing in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, a mighty man recorded as a son of Ulla in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.
lifetime: Hanniel is recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Asher as one of the sons of Ulla (Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia) (1 Chronicles 7:39).
event: It is recorded that the descendants of Asher to whom he belonged were heads of families, choice and mighty men of valor, chiefs among the leaders, and that the number of men fit for battle, recorded in their genealogies, was 26,000 (1 Chronicles 7:40).
character: He was regarded as a mighty man of such outstanding ability that he was chosen as a leader among the heads of his family, and his house is recorded as being skilled with the bow and having many descendants (1 Chronicles 7:40).

call: returnee with Ezra (chief of the descendants of David)
introduce: Hattush is one of the descendants of David who, after finishing the captivity in Babylon, returned to Jerusalem under the leadership of Ezra.
lifetime: As a descendant of David, he was recorded among the heads of families who came up from Babylon with Ezra (Ezra 8:1-2).
event: Among those who gathered at the river of Ahava in order to return to Jerusalem with Ezra, he was entered in that list as the representative person of the descendants of David (Ezra 8:2).

call: head of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: He is a person recorded in the list of priests who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1-2).
lifetime: He is one of the persons of the priestly families who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1-2).
event: His name is recorded in the list of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua, and they were the chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1-2, 12:7).

call: son of Azrikam of the descendants of Merari (Levite)
introduce: Hasshub is a Levite appearing in 1 Chronicles chapter 9 of the Old Testament, the son of Azrikam of the descendants of Merari and the father of Shemaiah (1 Chronicles 9:14). His son Shemaiah is recorded as one of the Levites who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:14, Nehemiah 11:15).
lifetime: Hasshub is the son of Azrikam and the grandson of Hashabiah, and his son Shemaiah is recorded as being of the descendants of Merari (1 Chronicles 9:14).
event: No deeds of Hasshub himself are recorded in the Bible; his son Shemaiah is recorded in the list of Levites who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9:14, Nehemiah 11:15).

call: leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Hasshub is recorded as one of the heads of the people who set their seal to the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:23).
lifetime: His name is recorded in the list of the heads of the people in Nehemiah chapter 10 (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:23), and he is among those who set their seal to the covenant pledging to observe and keep the law of God (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:23).
event: He is recorded as one who set his seal together with the heads of the people, and in that covenant he swore with a curse to observe and do all the commandments, ordinances, and statutes of the LORD, according to the law of God given by Moses the servant of God (Nehemiah 10:29).

introduce: Herod Antipas is the son of Herod the Great and the Herod recorded in Luke 3:1 as tetrarch of Galilee. He appears in the biblical record as the administrative head of the region of Galilee during Jesus' public ministry, and is a person who was involved in the execution of John the Baptist and in the process of the trial of Jesus.
lifetime: Luke records that in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Herod was tetrarch of Galilee (Luke 3:1). He married Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, and for this he was told by John the Baptist that it was not right (Mark 6:17-18). While Jesus was working in Galilee, it was said that he wanted to kill Jesus (Luke 13:31), and when Jesus stood before Pilate, Pilate, learning that Jesus belonged to Herod's jurisdiction, sent him to Herod, and Herod questioned Jesus (Luke 23:6-9).
event: He took the lead in the incident in which he imprisoned John the Baptist and had John beheaded as the price of the dancing of Herodias's daughter (Matthew 14:3-10). On hearing reports of what Jesus was doing, he was once perplexed whether John the Baptist, who was dead, had risen (Luke 9:7-9). In the course of Jesus' trial, when Pilate sent Jesus to him, he questioned him at length, but when he heard no answer from Jesus, he treated him with contempt and mocked him with his soldiers and sent him back to Pilate (Luke 23:7-11).
character: To maintain his power, he submitted to Roman rule while trying to strengthen his own authority within the region. He showed a human side in that he knew John the Baptist to be a righteous and holy man, feared him, and was troubled as he listened to his words, but at the same time he had both the indecisiveness and the cruelty to decide to behead John because of his own face and his oath (Mark 6:20-26). He had a cunning political sense, to the point that Jesus called him a fox (Luke 13:32), and in situations of religious conflict he took a compromising attitude.

introduce: Herod Agrippa I is the man recorded in Acts chapter 12 as "King Herod." He reached out to harm some who belonged to the church, put to death with the sword James the brother of John, and seized Peter and put him in prison (Acts 12:1-4). The Bible has no record of his family line or of his relations with the Roman emperor.
lifetime: King Herod reached out to harm some who belonged to the church, put to death with the sword James the brother of John, and also seized Peter and put him in prison (Acts 12:1-4). He went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there (Acts 12:19); on an appointed day he donned his royal robes, sat on his throne, and addressed the people, and the people shouted that it was the voice of a god, but because he did not give glory to God, an angel of the Lord struck him down, and he was eaten by worms and died (Acts 12:21-23).
event: After putting James to death with the sword, seeing that the Jews were pleased with this, he proceeded to seize Peter also (Acts 12:2-3). He put Peter in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each, intending to bring him out to the people after the Passover, but an angel of the Lord appeared and the chains fell off Peter's hands (Acts 12:4-7). Herod was in a furious dispute with the people of Tyre and Sidon, but they came to him with one accord and asked for peace (Acts 12:20); when Herod donned his royal robes and addressed the people, the people said it was the voice of a god, but because he did not give glory to God, an angel of the Lord struck him down, and he was eaten by worms and died (Acts 12:21-23).
character: To achieve his political aims he cooperated with the leaders of Judaism and showed an opportunistic side, using religious persecution as a means (Acts 12:3). He was arrogant and self-displaying enough to accept just as it was the excessive praise of the crowd toward him (Acts 12:22-23).

introduce: The Herodians are the group, shown together with the Pharisees in the Gospels of the New Testament, who opposed Jesus (Matthew 22:16, Mark 3:6, 12:13). The Bible has no detailed record of their organization or political character.
lifetime: The Pharisees went out and immediately plotted with the Herodians how they might destroy Jesus (Mark 3:6). Also the Pharisees took counsel how to entangle Jesus in his words, and sent their disciples to Jesus along with the Herodians (Matthew 22:15-16).
event: They sent some of the Pharisees and the Herodians to catch Jesus in his words (Mark 12:13), and asked whether it was lawful or not to pay taxes to Caesar (Matthew 22:17, Mark 12:14).
character: The house of Herod sought to maintain its power on the basis of loyalty to the Roman Empire, and showed a tendency to respond very cruelly and harshly to anything that threatened the basis of its rule (Matthew 2:16). The Herodians were opposed to the Pharisees in religious terms, but showed an opportunistic side in forming a temporary alliance with the Pharisees for the political purpose of eliminating Jesus (Mark 3:6). They concentrated on protecting their vested interests within the Roman administrative system rather than on the independence of the Jewish people (Matthew 22:16).

introduce: Heman is a Levite leader of praise and singer who was active in the time of David and Solomon, the grandson of Samuel and the son of Joel. He is recorded as having contributed to establishing the musical system of temple worship.
lifetime: Heman, a Kohathite, is the son of Joel the son of Samuel, and as one of the singers David appointed he was entrusted with the duty of singing in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 6:31-33). In the time of David, together with Asaph and Ethan, he played a central role in the ministry of praise, and he continued that duty after Solomon completed the temple (1 Chronicles 15:17, 2 Chronicles 5:12).
event: At David's command, Heman, together with Asaph and Ethan, was appointed as one who sounded bronze cymbals loudly (1 Chronicles 15:16-19). He was among those whom David set apart for service from the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, and his sons were under their father's direction in singing and serving in the house of the LORD God (1 Chronicles 25:1, 25:5-6). Also, in the time of King Hezekiah, when the Levites arose to cleanse the house of the LORD, Jehiel and Shimei of the descendants of Heman were among them (2 Chronicles 29:12, 29:14-15).
character: The Bible describes Heman as a seer who received the words of God, and records that God gave him fourteen sons and three daughters so that he enjoyed the blessing of children (1 Chronicles 25:5). He had the standing of a professional artist who led the ministry of spiritual music at the side of the king (1 Chronicles 25:6).

introduce: Heber is a Kenite mentioned in the Bible as the husband of Jael, classified as one of the descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses (Judges 4:11, 4:17). His wife was Jael (Judges 4:17).
lifetime: Heber, a Kenite, separated from his clan (Judges 4:11). He is mentioned as one of the descendants of Hobab the father-in-law of Moses, and pitched his tent by the great tree of Zaanannim near Kedesh (Judges 4:11).
event: There was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite (Judges 4:17). For this reason, after being defeated in battle with Israel, Sisera chose the tent of Jael, Heber's wife, as his place of flight (Judges 4:17). It was not Heber himself who killed Sisera, but his tent became the place of Sisera's end (Judges 4:21).

introduce: He is the man recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah in 1 Chronicles chapter 4 as "the father of Soco" (1 Chronicles 4:18). He is one of the persons who carry on the flow of the family line of the tribe of Judah.
lifetime: Heber is recorded as a son born to Jehudijah and as "the father of Soco" (1 Chronicles 4:18).
event: As the ancestor and father of Soco, he played a part in forming the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:18).

introduce: A person recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the descendants of the house of Benjamin.
lifetime: He is recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin as one of the sons of Elpaal (1 Chronicles 8:17-18). He is included in the genealogy of the heads of the tribe of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:17-28).

introduce: Hepher is a figure appearing in Numbers and Joshua of the Old Testament, belonging to the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh, recorded as the son of Gilead and the father of Zelophehad (Numbers 26:32-33, 27:1).
lifetime: Hepher is the son of Gilead the son of Machir (Numbers 26:29, 26:32). Gilead was the son of Machir and the grandson of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 7:17). The Hepherite family descended from him was recorded among the descendants of Gilead (Numbers 26:32).
event: In Numbers chapter 26, when Moses and Eleazar the priest counted the people of Israel on the plains of Moab, Hepher was named as the ancestor of the Hepherite family that bore his name (Numbers 26:3, 26:32). Hepher's son Zelophehad had no sons but only daughters, and in the record of the coming forward of those daughters, Hepher is mentioned as the father of Zelophehad (Numbers 26:33, 27:1).

introduce: Hepher is a person recorded as one of the children borne by the wives of Ashhur, a descendant of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:6).
lifetime: Hepher appears by name in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah as a son of Ashhur (1 Chronicles 4:6).

introduce: He is the man recorded in 1 Chronicles 11:36 as "Hepher the Mecherathite," one of the mighty men of David's army (1 Chronicles 11:26, 11:36).
lifetime: He is included in the list of the mighty men of David's army, and is recorded as a Mecherathite (1 Chronicles 11:26, 11:36).
event: He is recorded as one of those enumerated as the mighty men of the army (1 Chronicles 11:26, 11:36).

introduce: Hebron is a person belonging to the family line of Caleb of the tribe of Judah, a son of Mareshah (1 Chronicles 2:42). According to the record of Chronicles, he is a person mentioned within the genealogical system of the tribe of Judah.
lifetime: Hebron is a descendant of Mareshah the son of Caleb, and the sons of Hebron are recorded as Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema (1 Chronicles 2:42-43).
event: Hebron fathered his sons Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema, who appear as members of the genealogy forming families within the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:43).

introduce: Hebron was a son of Kohath, the son of Levi, and a grandson of Levi, a figure recorded in the genealogy of Chronicles. The family he headed formed one branch of the descendants of Kohath within the tribe of Levi.
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel (Exodus 6:18). By the time of David, his descendants are mentioned as a family unit carrying out the duties of the tribe of Levi (1 Chronicles 23:19).
event: The sons of Hebron are recorded as Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth (1 Chronicles 23:19). Of the descendants of Hebron, Hashabiah and his kinsmen, 1,700 men of valor, were entrusted with the oversight of Israel west of the Jordan, in all the work of the LORD and the service of the king (1 Chronicles 26:30).

call: leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Hezir was one of the leaders of the Jewish community who returned to Jerusalem after the exile, and one of those who set their seal together with Nehemiah.
lifetime: After returning from the Babylonian captivity, he took part in the movement of covenant renewal led by Nehemiah in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 10:1). As a leader of the people, he is included in the list of those who signed when the seal was set on the covenant document (Nehemiah 10:20).
event: He set his seal to confirm the covenant document in which the people of Judah swore never again to intermarry with foreign peoples, to observe the Sabbath and the temple, and to keep the law (Nehemiah 10:20).

introduce: Heldai is a figure appearing in the book of Zechariah of the Old Testament, one of the captives who had come back from Babylon (Zechariah 6:10). Zechariah received the word to take silver and gold from him, Tobijah, and Jedaiah and make a crown (Zechariah 6:10-11). In Zechariah 6:14 he is recorded as Helem.
lifetime: Heldai was one of the captives who had returned from Babylon, and together with Tobijah and Jedaiah he was in the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah (Zechariah 6:10). Zechariah received the word of the LORD and was commanded to go into that house and take silver and gold from them (Zechariah 6:9-11).
event: The LORD told Zechariah to take silver and gold from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, make a crown, and set it on the head of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest (Zechariah 6:10-11). He said that the crown was to be placed in the temple of the LORD as a memorial to Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen the son of Zephaniah (Zechariah 6:14).

introduce: Helez was a descendant of the tribe of Judah, the son of Azariah, the father of Eleasah, and the grandfather of Sismai. He is recorded as a figure who carries on the line of descent of the house of Perez within the genealogy of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:4-5, 2:9, 2:25-40).
lifetime: Helez was born as the son of Azariah (1 Chronicles 2:39), and he fathered Eleasah (1 Chronicles 2:39). As a descendant of Perez the son of Judah, he stood in the position of carrying on the family genealogy (1 Chronicles 2:4-5, 2:9, 2:25-39).

call: ancestor of a Levite family that returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: Hodaviah is one of the Levites of the tribe of Levi who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem after the exile, an ancestral figure appearing in the genealogy of the Levite descendants who returned with Zerubbabel. Ezra 2:40 records that the descendants of Hodaviah were included among the returning company as Levites.
lifetime: In the list of the people of Israel who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and others, the descendants of Hodaviah are recorded as Levites (Ezra 2:2, 2:40). His descendants are also included in the list of returnees in the book of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 7:43, written as Hodevah). The Bible does not state whether he himself was alive during the course of the return; he is dealt with mainly as a starting point in the family genealogy.
event: The descendants of Hodaviah were recorded in the list of returnees as Levites, seventy-four in number, together with the descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiel (Ezra 2:40; Nehemiah 7:43). No personal events of his are recorded in the Bible.

call: son of Elioenai (royal descendant of David)
introduce: Hodaviah is a descendant of David, a figure appearing in the genealogy of the royal house of Judah after the Babylonian exile. According to 1 Chronicles 3:24, he is a son of Elioenai and a member of the genealogy carrying on the line of David.
lifetime: He is a descendant of Zerubbabel and belongs to the family line of Solomon, the son of David (1 Chronicles 3:19-24). In the biblical record he is recorded only as a late figure in the genealogy continuing from the royal house of David (1 Chronicles 3:24).
event: He is recorded in the genealogy of the royal house of David as the first of the seven sons of Elioenai (1 Chronicles 3:24). No personal deeds of his are recorded in the Bible.

기타관계: David#468(kinsman of the tribe of Judah)

call: an Aroerite (father of mighty men of David)
introduce: Hotham was an Aroerite, recorded as the father of Shama and Jeiel, who were listed among the mighty men of David (1 Chronicles 11:44).
lifetime: He is introduced as an Aroerite, and his sons Shama and Jeiel were recorded in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:44). The Bible has no record of Hotham's own life.
event: His sons Shama and Jeiel were named among David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:44). No event carried out by Hotham himself is recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Hodiah was a Levite who was active in the time of Nehemiah, a man who after the return from the Babylonian exile took part in the religious rebuilding of Jerusalem and in teaching the law.
lifetime: When Ezra read the book of the law, he joined the Levites in making the people who stood in that place understand the law (Nehemiah 8:7). Afterward, when the children of Israel separated themselves from foreigners and confessed their sins, a man among the Levites recorded as Hodiah told the people to bless the LORD (Nehemiah 9:5). His name is recorded in the list of the Levites who set their seal to the covenant together with Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:10).
event: When Ezra read the book of the law in the square before the Water Gate, he, together with the other Levites, made the people who stood in that place understand the law (Nehemiah 8:7). He is also recorded as Hodiah in the list of the Levites who urged the people to stand up and bless the LORD their God (Nehemiah 9:5). His name is recorded among the Levites who set their seal to the covenant (Nehemiah 10:10).

call: leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Hodiah was one of those who, after the return from exile, set their seal in Jerusalem to the covenant document drawn up under the leadership of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:18).
lifetime: He served as one of the heads of the people in the community of Nehemiah's time (Nehemiah 10:14, 10:18). He is recorded as one of those who, together with Nehemiah, set their seal to the covenant to observe the law of God (Nehemiah 10:1, 10:18).
event: He was one of those who set their seal to the covenant in which the people of Judah pledged not to intermarry with the peoples of the land, to keep the Sabbath and the holy days, and to establish regulations for the temple (Nehemiah 10:18, 10:28-39).

call: father of Shaphat (father of the Simeonite spy)
introduce: Hori was a man of the tribe of Simeon at the time of the exodus, the father of Shaphat, who was sent out to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:5).
lifetime:
He belonged to the tribe of Simeon and fathered his son Shaphat (Numbers 13:5).
His son Shaphat was chosen as one of the commanders representing each of the tribes of Israel and spied out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:2-5).
Beyond this, no specific record of his birth or death appears (Numbers 13:5).

introduce: Hori appears in the Bible as the name of the Horites, the native people who lived in the land of Seir. Genesis 36:20 lists Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, and Anah as the descendants of Seir the Horite, the original inhabitants of that land.
lifetime: Hori is the name of the Horite people, the original inhabitants of the land of Seir (Genesis 36:20). Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan, descendants of Seir, are recorded as chiefs who came from the Horites in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:20-21, 36:29-30).
event: Genesis 14:6 records that Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him struck the Horites in their hill country of Seir. Later the descendants of Esau destroyed the Horites and settled in their place in that land (Deuteronomy 2:12, 2:22). The Bible does not separately record any individual event of Hori himself.

introduce: Huram-abi was a craftsman skilled in bronze work and metalwork whom Huram king of Tyre sent to Jerusalem to help with Solomon's building of the temple (2 Chronicles 2:13).
lifetime:
His mother was a woman of the tribe of Dan (2 Chronicles 2:14), or a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a craftsman who worked in bronze (1 Kings 7:14).
At the direction of the king of Tyre he was sent to Jerusalem to help King Solomon, and he took sole charge of making the furnishings of the temple (2 Chronicles 2:13-14).
He completed the task of making all the bronze furnishings of the temple; no specific record appears of his activities after the building of the temple or of his death (1 Kings 7:40).
event:
He made the two great bronze pillars, Jachin and Boaz, that adorned the front of the portico of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 7:15-22).
He cast the great bronze Sea, used to hold water (1 Kings 7:23-26).
He made the ten bronze movable stands and the ten bronze basins to be used in the temple (1 Kings 7:27-39).
He made all the bronze vessels for the house of the LORD, such as pots, shovels, and bowls, casting them in the plain of the Jordan (1 Kings 7:40-46).
He was versed not only in bronze work but also in gold, silver, iron, stone, and wood, in weaving with purple, blue, and crimson yarn and fine linen, and in every kind of engraving, and so contributed to the work of building the temple (2 Chronicles 2:14).
character: He is described as one filled with wisdom, understanding, and skill for all kinds of bronze work (1 Kings 7:14).

call: father of Rephaiah (ruler of a district of Jerusalem)
introduce: He is a man recorded in the account of the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah as the father of Rephaiah, who ruled half the district of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:9).
lifetime: The Bible has no record of Hur's own life, only a record that his son Rephaiah, as ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired the wall (Nehemiah 3:9).
event: His son Rephaiah, as ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired a section of the wall (Nehemiah 3:9). No event of Hur himself is recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Hushah is a name used in the Bible to indicate a man's place of origin. Sibbecai, one of David's mighty men, is recorded as a Hushathite (2 Samuel 21:18; 1 Chronicles 27:11), and Mebunnai too is recorded as a Hushathite (2 Samuel 23:27).
lifetime: There is no record of the life of Hushah itself. Sibbecai the Hushathite is recorded as a Hushathite in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:29), and as the eighth commander, for the eighth month, his division numbered 24,000 (1 Chronicles 27:11).
event: When war was waged with the Philistines at Gob, Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, one of the sons of the giant (2 Samuel 21:18), and when war was waged at Gezer, he struck down Sippai, one of the sons of the giant (1 Chronicles 20:4).

introduce: A figure of the tribe of Benjamin appearing in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, a person in the genealogy recorded as a son of Aher.
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of the descendants of Benjamin and is included in the genealogy as a son of Aher (1 Chronicles 7:12).

introduce: Hushim is a figure appearing in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the wives of Shaharaim.
lifetime: Hushim was the wife of Shaharaim, and by him she bore two sons, Abitub and Elpaal (1 Chronicles 8:11).
event: She bore Shaharaim two sons, Abitub and Elpaal, and played the role of carrying on the genealogy of the house of Shaharaim (1 Chronicles 8:11).

call: father of Ben-hur, Solomon's district governor
introduce: He is understood to be the father of Ben-hur, who was in charge of the hill country of Ephraim among the twelve district governors Solomon appointed in 1 Kings chapter 4 (1 Kings 4:7-8). The idea comes from the meaning of the name Ben-hur (son of Hur); the name Hur does not appear in the KRV text, and there is no record of Hur himself.
lifetime: His son, understood to be Ben-hur, is recorded as the governor of the hill country of Ephraim among the twelve district governors. Each of the twelve governors provided food for the king and the royal household for one month of the year (1 Kings 4:7-8).

call: ancestor of the family of Ater among the returnees
introduce: He is a figure mentioned as an ancestor of the descendants of Ater among those who finished their life of captivity in Babylon and returned to Jerusalem in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah.
lifetime: He is included among the descendants who came back to the land of Judah from among those who had been taken captive to Babylon (Ezra 2:16). In the list of returnees, he is classified as the descendants of Ater, that is, the descendants of Hezekiah, and 98 are recorded as having returned (Nehemiah 7:21).

call: leader who sealed the covenant (descendant of Ater)
introduce: Hezekiah, who appears in Nehemiah chapter 10, was one of the leaders who set their seal in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile. He is recorded as having taken part in the process of covenant renewal among the people of Israel (Nehemiah 10:17).
lifetime: As one of the people who came back to Jerusalem after finishing life in Babylonian captivity, he was included among the line of leaders who set their seal to the covenant document promising to follow the law of God under the leadership of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:17). He joined in the public pledge to set right the religious and social order of Israel after the rebuilding of the wall (Nehemiah 10:1).
event: He signed the covenant swearing to observe the law given through Moses the servant of God and to keep all the regulations and ordinances (Nehemiah 10:29). By taking part in the pledge together with the leaders of Israel, the priests, and the Levites, he played the role of strengthening the unity of the community (Nehemiah 10:17).

call: high priest who found the book of the law
introduce: A high priest who served in the time of King Josiah of the kingdom of Judah; during the repair of the temple he found the book of the law and so provided the spark for a national religious reform.
lifetime: He was the son of Shallum and the father of Azariah, a descendant of Zadok (1 Chronicles 6:12-13). In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent the scribe Shaphan to the house of the LORD and commanded him to go up to Hilkiah the high priest, have him count the silver that had been brought into the temple, and have it delivered into the hands of the supervisors of the work (2 Kings 22:3-5). At this time Hilkiah told Shaphan the scribe that he had found the book of the law in the house of the LORD, and gave him the book (2 Kings 22:8). Afterward, at the command of King Josiah, together with Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah, he went to the prophetess Huldah and inquired about the book that had been found (2 Kings 22:12-14).
event: In the course of the repair of the temple he found the book of the law and handed it to Shaphan the scribe, and Shaphan read it before the king (2 Kings 22:8, 10). When King Josiah, on hearing the contents of the book of the law, tore his clothes and wept bitterly, Hilkiah, together with Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah, visited the prophetess Huldah and sought her counsel about the fate of the nation (2 Kings 22:12, 14). This incident led King Josiah to carry out a sweeping removal of idols and a renewal of the covenant (2 Kings 23:2, 24).
character: He showed administrative ability in managing the repair of the temple with transparency and faithfulness (2 Kings 22:7). As a servant trusted by the king, he played the role of giving counsel with religious authority at a time of national crisis (2 Kings 22:14). He and his family became established as a leading family that carried on the priestly office in Judah for generations afterward (1 Chronicles 9:11).

introduce: Hilkiah is a figure appearing in 1 Chronicles of the Old Testament, a Levite of the descendants of Merari, the son of Amzi and the father of Amaziah. His descendant Ethan was, among the company David appointed to take charge of the singing of praise, the one of the descendants of Merari who served at the left hand.
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 6:46 records Hilkiah as the son of Amzi, and 6:45 records Amaziah as the son of Hilkiah. This genealogy traces back the ancestors of Ethan (1 Chronicles 6:44), who served at the left hand among the descendants of Merari in the company David appointed to sing praise (1 Chronicles 6:31, 6:44-46).
event: His descendant Ethan was the one among the company David appointed who, of the descendants of Merari, served at the left hand (1 Chronicles 6:31, 6:44). No duty or event of Hilkiah himself is recorded in this genealogy.

call: son of Hosah (gatekeeper of the temple)
introduce: One of the gatekeepers recorded in 1 Chronicles, a son of Hosah of the descendants of Merari (1 Chronicles 26:10-11).
lifetime: He belonged to the division of gatekeepers in the time of King David, a son of Hosah of the descendants of Merari, recorded as the second of Hosah's sons (1 Chronicles 26:10-11). As a head of a division of the gatekeepers, he was one of those who obtained a duty like that of his brothers and served in the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:12).
event: The sons and brothers of Hosah, thirteen persons, were recorded as gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:11). His father Hosah, together with Shuppim, was assigned by lot to guard the west, beside the Shallecheth Gate on the highway that goes up (1 Chronicles 26:16). The Bible does not separately record the gate Hilkiah himself was in charge of or any individual event.
character: The biblical record gives no specific description of his personal character or features. It can only be confirmed that, as a gatekeeper, he took part in organized service by family units according to the ordinances David established (1 Chronicles 26:11).

call: priest who stood at Ezra's right hand
introduce: Hilkiah in the book of Nehemiah is a man recorded as one who, in the period after the return from exile, stood at the right of the wooden platform when Ezra the scribe read the book of the law (Nehemiah 8:4).
lifetime: He is one of those who stood at the right of the wooden platform when Ezra the scribe stood on it to read the book of the law in the square before the Water Gate (Nehemiah 8:3-4). Nehemiah 12:7 records a Hilkiah as a chief of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jeshua, but the text does not make clear whether he is the same person as the one in 8:4.
event: When Ezra stood on the wooden platform, he stood at its right together with Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, and Maaseiah, while at the left stood Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hash-baddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam (Nehemiah 8:4). Nehemiah 8:4 records only the positions in which they stood during the reading of the law, and does not record any individual deeds of his.

introduce: One of the priests of Anathoth in the land of Benjamin, the father of the prophet Jeremiah (Jeremiah 1:1).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the priests of Anathoth in the land of Benjamin and as the father of the prophet Jeremiah (Jeremiah 1:1). His other personal life is not recorded in the Bible.
event: The book of Jeremiah introduces the words of his son Jeremiah as "the words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin" (Jeremiah 1:1). No specific duty or event that Hilkiah carried out as a priest is recorded in the Bible.

call: figure in the genealogy of Caleb's family of the tribe of Judah
introduce: A figure whose name appears in 1 Chronicles chapter 4, verse 17, as the father of Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon, recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
lifetime: A figure whose name appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles chapter 4); no direct record of his activity appears (1 Chronicles 4:17).
event: Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon are recorded as the sons of Ezrah (1 Chronicles 4:17). The text does not relate the deeds of Ezrah himself.

call: head of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel
introduce: This refers to Ezra, one of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua at the time of the return from the Babylonian captivity. He is a person distinguished as a namesake of Ezra the scribe, and is recorded as a leader-level figure in the early community of returnees, before the second return.
lifetime: He is included in the list of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1), and is recorded among those who were chiefs of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:7).
event: The one recorded as head of the priests in the days of Joiakim from the family of Ezra is Meshullam (Nehemiah 12:13). No concrete deeds of Ezra himself are recorded in the Bible.
character: As head of a priestly family he held a position of authority in the community, and contributed to maintaining religious rites and administrative order in the process of the restoration of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 12:12). In the record he is portrayed as a person clearly distinguished from Ezra the scribe in time of activity and role (Nehemiah 12:1).
