introduce: Joshua of Beth-shemesh was the landowner of the district of Beth-shemesh where the ark of God, returned from the Philistines, came to a stop; in the biblical record he is a man who owned the field in which the ark of God stayed.
lifetime: The cart that the Philistines sent back came to the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh, to where a large rock was, and stopped (1 Samuel 6:14). The large rock on which they set the ark of the LORD was still in his field at the time of the writing (1 Samuel 6:18).
event: When the cart came to his field and stopped, the people chopped up the wood of the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD (1 Samuel 6:14). The Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the chest containing the gold objects and set them on the large rock, and that day the men of Beth-shemesh offered burnt offerings and other sacrifices (1 Samuel 6:15). In this scene no action of Joshua himself is recorded, and only his field is mentioned as the place.

call: governor of the city of Jerusalem (mayor)
introduce: Joshua, recorded in 2 Kings 23:8 as the governor of the city, is a man mentioned as having the high places of the gates at the entrance of his gate at the time King Josiah carried out his religious reform.
lifetime: At the time of King Josiah's religious reform, the high places of the gates were at the entrance of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, to the left of the city gate (2 Kings 23:8). His life apart from this is not recorded in the Bible.
event: It was King Josiah who tore down the high places, and it is recorded that those high places were at the entrance of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, to the left of the city gate (2 Kings 23:8). What Joshua himself did is not recorded.
character: He had the bureaucratic characteristic of immediately carrying out the administrative orders of a centralized king. He showed the aspect of an administrator who faithfully performed the political task of religious reform (2 Kings 23:8).

introduce: He was the first high priest of the Jewish community that returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He was the son of Jehozadak, and is recorded as one who, together with Zerubbabel, led the rebuilding of the temple.
lifetime: After the edict of King Cyrus he returned to Judah with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:2). After the return he set about, with Zerubbabel, the work of building the altar of the God of Israel (Ezra 3:2), and also took part in overseeing the work on the temple (Ezra 3:8-9). Afterward, with the prophets Haggai and Zechariah helping, he began the building of the temple together with Zerubbabel (Ezra 5:1-2).
event: After the return to Jerusalem he built the altar of burnt offering, offered burnt offerings, kept the appointed feasts, and restored the sacrifices (Ezra 3:2-4). Together with Zerubbabel he resumed the building of the temple that had been halted (Ezra 5:2), and the temple was completed in the sixth year of King Darius (Ezra 6:15). In a vision he appears dressed in filthy clothes and opposed by Satan, and there is a scene in which he is changed into splendid clothes by the angel of the LORD (Zechariah 3:1-4).
character: In the course of rebuilding the temple he showed a cooperative attitude, accepting and acting on the encouragement of the prophets (Ezra 5:1-2). As a figure symbolizing the legitimacy of the priestly office that had weakened after the exile, he strongly shows the character of a symbolic representative foretelling the coming of the Messiah (Zechariah 3:8).

call: head of the half-tribe of Manasseh
meaning: Raised up and exalted by the LORD
introduce: He is one of the chiefs of the half-tribe of Manasseh who lived east of the Jordan. In the Bible he appears as one of the leaders of the prominent families of the tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan.
lifetime: His tribe, the half-tribe of Manasseh, lived from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon and was numerous (1 Chronicles 5:23), and he is recorded as one of the heads of that tribe (1 Chronicles 5:24).
event: Together with Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel he is recorded as a head of a family renowned for valor (1 Chronicles 5:24). His tribe afterward sinned against the God of their fathers and served the gods of the peoples of the land, and the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh were taken into exile by Pul and Tiglath-pileser, kings of Assyria, whom God had stirred up (1 Chronicles 5:25-26). The text does not relate his individual deeds.
character: The Bible describes him as a mighty man of valor and a famous man (1 Chronicles 5:24). This reflects the social standing and military influence he held within the half-tribe of Manasseh at that time (1 Chronicles 5:24).

meaning: Raised up and exalted by the LORD
introduce: Jeremiah is a mighty man of the tribe of Benjamin who came to David while he stayed at Ziklag and gave him military help (1 Chronicles 12:4).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the mighty men who joined David during the time he had fled from King Saul and was living at Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:1). He was from the tribe of Benjamin and a kinsman of Saul, yet he came to Ziklag to help David (1 Chronicles 12:2).
event: His name is recorded in the list of the mighty men who came to Ziklag to help David (1 Chronicles 12:4).

meaning: Raised up and exalted by the LORD
introduce: The Jeremiah mentioned in 1 Chronicles chapter 12 is one of the Gadite mighty men who went over to David in the stronghold in the wilderness while he was hiding from Saul. He is recorded fifth in the list of the Gadite mighty men (1 Chronicles 12:8, 12:10).
lifetime: The mighty men of the tribe of Gad came to David at the stronghold in the wilderness, and Jeremiah is recorded fifth in the list of those mighty men (1 Chronicles 12:8, 12:10). These Gadites became army commanders, the least of whom was in charge of a hundred men and the greatest of a thousand (1 Chronicles 12:14).
event: He is mentioned as the fifth among the Gadite mighty men who came over to David (1 Chronicles 12:10). These Gadites became army commanders (1 Chronicles 12:14).
character: The Bible describes him as a Gadite mighty man who went over to David, and relates that he and his companions had a spirit whose faces were like the faces of lions and who were as swift as gazelles on the mountains (1 Chronicles 12:8, 12:10).

meaning: Raised up and exalted by the LORD
introduce: The Jeremiah mentioned in 1 Chronicles chapter 12 is one of the Gadite mighty men who went over to David in the stronghold in the wilderness while he was hiding from Saul (1 Chronicles 12:8).
lifetime: As a mighty man of the tribe of Gad, he was among those who came to David at the stronghold in the wilderness (1 Chronicles 12:8). He is recorded tenth in the list of the Gadite mighty men (1 Chronicles 12:13).
event: He was recorded tenth among the Gadite mighty men who went over to David, men trained for battle and skilled in the use of the shield and spear (1 Chronicles 12:8, 12:13). These Gadites became army commanders, the least of whom was in charge of a hundred men and the greatest of a thousand (1 Chronicles 12:14).

call: son of Hilkiah (author of the book of Jeremiah)
meaning: Raised up and exalted by the LORD
introduce: A prophet who was active during the period of the fall of the kingdom of Judah, the son of Hilkiah, a priest of Anathoth (Jeremiah 1:1). From the thirteenth year of King Josiah until the capture of Jerusalem he received the word of the LORD (Jeremiah 1:2-3).
lifetime: He was born into a priestly household in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin, and the word of the LORD came to him in the thirteenth year of King Josiah (Jeremiah 1:1-2). The word came from the time of Josiah through the time of Jehoiakim until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah (Jeremiah 1:2-3). After the fall of Jerusalem he was brought out of the court of the guard and entrusted to Gedaliah (Jeremiah 39:14), and afterward he was led by Johanan and the army commanders into the land of Egypt (Jeremiah 43:6-7).
event: He prophesied the downfall of Judah and the invasion of Babylon, and proclaimed that whoever went out and surrendered to the Chaldeans would live (Jeremiah 21:8-9). In the time of King Jehoiakim, because of a prophecy he made in the house of the LORD, he was seized by the priests, the prophets, and all the people and faced the danger of death (Jeremiah 26:7-11). He sent a letter to the exiles in Babylon, instructing them to build houses, seek the welfare of that city, and settle there (Jeremiah 29:5-7). He had Baruch read aloud a scroll in which all the words concerning Israel, Judah, and the nations were written down, but King Jehoiakim cut it with a scribe's knife and threw it into the fire in the firepot and burned it (Jeremiah 36:2, 36:21-23).
character: Regarding his calling, he showed hesitation, saying that he was too young to bear it (Jeremiah 1:6). While delivering the prophecy of destruction toward his homeland, he showed the human anguish of deeply grieving and lamenting over the tragedy of the people (Jeremiah 9:1). Even in suffering he did not yield to threats and kept the toughness to deliver the prophetic message given to him to the end (Jeremiah 26:15).

call: head of the priests who sealed the covenant
meaning: Raised up and exalted by the LORD
introduce: He is one of the priests who set their seal to the covenant document drawn up after the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem was completed in the time of Nehemiah. He was active as a leader in the process of re-establishing the faith and legal system of the community after the return from the Babylonian exile.
lifetime: His name is recorded among the priests who set their seal to the binding covenant led by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:1-2, 10:8). The one recorded as head of the priests of the family of Jeremiah in the days of Joiakim is Hananiah (Nehemiah 12:12).
event: When the binding covenant was made and put in writing (Nehemiah 9:38), his name was entered as a priest among those who set their seal (Nehemiah 10:1-2, 10:8).

meaning: Raised up and exalted by the LORD
introduce: Jeremiah is a man recorded as the son of Habazziniah and the father of Jaazaniah, a man of the Rechabite clan (Jeremiah 35:3).
lifetime: Jaazaniah, the grandson of Habazziniah and the son of Jeremiah, together with the whole clan of the Rechabites, was brought by the prophet Jeremiah in the time of Jehoiakim into a room of the house of the LORD (Jeremiah 35:1-3). The text does not relate the life of this Jeremiah himself.
event: When his son Jaazaniah and the men of the Rechabite clan were offered wine, they refused to drink it, obeying the command of their ancestor Jonadab (Jeremiah 35:5-8). This is the conduct of his son and the Rechabite clan, and no deed of this Jeremiah himself is recorded.
character: He is a man with a law-abiding spirit and firm conviction who strictly keeps the rules his family established (Jeremiah 35:10). In spite of outside temptation and changes of circumstance, he showed a conservative and consistent attitude toward life, holding fast to the tradition of his ancestors (Jeremiah 35:16).

introduce: He is a person whose name appears when the sons of Obadiah are recorded in the genealogy of David's descendants in 1 Chronicles 3:21. The text lists side by side the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, and the sons of Shecaniah, so it does not state explicitly that Obadiah was a son of Arnan.
lifetime: In the genealogy of Zerubbabel's descendants (1 Chronicles 3:19-21), he is recorded among the sons of Obadiah (1 Chronicles 3:21).
event: In the biblical record there is no information about any specific historical achievement or particular event carried out by him.
character: Apart from the point that he is recorded by the Chronicler as a legitimate figure continuing David's line, there is no description of his character or personality.

introduce: Obadiah is a figure recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:3, a chief mentioned as a grandson of Uzzi of the descendants of Issachar and a son of Izrahiah.
lifetime: He was a son of Izrahiah, and is recorded as a chief together with Michael, Joel, and Isshiah (1 Chronicles 7:3).
event: As one with the sons of Izrahiah (Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah), it is recorded that the troops able to go out to battle by genealogy and by clan numbered 36,000 (1 Chronicles 7:4).
character: The Bible records him and his brothers as valiant commanders according to the genealogy within the tribe of Issachar (1 Chronicles 7:3).

introduce: A figure appearing in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as a descendant of Azel who carries on the line of the royal house of Saul, and as a son of Azel.
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Azel, a descendant of Jonathan the son of Saul (1 Chronicles 8:38). He is located in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin that continues from Jonathan the son of Saul (1 Chronicles 8:33-38).
character: As a member of the family line that inherits the bloodline of the royal house of Saul, he is a person who shows, through the historical record, how the later generations of the house of Saul were preserved and recorded (1 Chronicles 8:38).

introduce: A figure recorded in the list of Levites in 1 Chronicles chapter 9, a son of Shemaiah, a grandson of Galal, and a great-grandson of Jeduthun (1 Chronicles 9:16).
lifetime: He is recorded in the list as a son of Shemaiah among the Levites (1 Chronicles 9:14-16).
event: In the Bible no duty or deed of his is recorded; only his name appears, together with the genealogy (1 Chronicles 9:16).

introduce: The Obadiah mentioned in 1 Chronicles chapter 12 is one of the Gadite mighty men who went over to David in the stronghold in the wilderness while he was hiding from Saul (1 Chronicles 12:8). He is recorded second in the list of the Gadite mighty men (1 Chronicles 12:9).
lifetime: Obadiah is one of the men of the tribe of Gad who came to David at the stronghold in the wilderness (1 Chronicles 12:8). In that list he is recorded second, after Ezer the chief (1 Chronicles 12:9).
event: Obadiah is mentioned as the second in the list of the Gadite mighty men, after Ezer the chief (1 Chronicles 12:9). These Gadites are described as all mighty men, trained for battle, skilled in the use of the shield and spear (1 Chronicles 12:8). They became army commanders (1 Chronicles 12:14).
character: The Bible compares him and his companions to men whose faces were like lions and who were as swift as gazelles on the mountains, emphasizing their strong physical ability (1 Chronicles 12:8). He appears as one of the commanders of the tribe of Gad, a man possessing military leadership (1 Chronicles 12:9).

introduce: He is a man recorded in 1 Chronicles 27:19 as the father of Ishmaiah, the officer of Zebulun.
lifetime: His son Ishmaiah is recorded as the officer of Zebulun among the officers of the tribes of Israel (1 Chronicles 27:19). The life of Obadiah himself is not recorded.
event: The Bible does not record any deeds of Obadiah himself, and records only that his son Ishmaiah was the officer of Zebulun (1 Chronicles 27:19).

introduce: An official who served during the reign of Jehoshaphat, the fourth king of the southern kingdom of Judah. The meaning of the name is "servant of the LORD," and he is recorded as one of the officials who took part in the administration of the state.
lifetime: He is mentioned as one of those sent out, in the third year of King Jehoshaphat, when the officials of Judah were sent to go around the cities and teach the people (2 Chronicles 17:7). No later deeds or records of his death appear in the Bible.
event: At the direction of King Jehoshaphat, together with Ben-hail, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah, he went around the cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:7). They carried out the task of traveling throughout Judah with the book of the law of the LORD and teaching the law to the people (2 Chronicles 17:9).

introduce: Obadiah was one of the officials appointed to oversee the work of repairing the temple in the time of King Josiah of the kingdom of Judah. As a Levite he carried out the duty of overseeing the building work.
lifetime: In the eighteenth year of King Josiah of Judah, when they were about to repair the house of the LORD (2 Chronicles 34:8), he is recorded, as a Levite of the descendants of Merari, together with Jahath, as an overseer of the repair work (2 Chronicles 34:12).
event: Together with Jahath the Levite he was an overseer from the descendants of Merari, and together with Zechariah and Meshullam of the descendants of Kohath he directed the repair work (2 Chronicles 34:12). The money contributed was handed to Hilkiah, then put into the hands of those overseeing the work of the house of the LORD, and given to the workmen (2 Chronicles 34:9-10).
character: According to the biblical record, the overseers, including Obadiah, worked with great faithfulness and honesty in the course of the building work. (2 Chronicles 34:12).

introduce: He is a man who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra in the time of King Artaxerxes of Persia, after the Babylonian exile. He is recorded as coming from a leading family of the descendants of Joab.
lifetime: As a member of the descendants of Joab he returned from Babylon to Jerusalem following Ezra (Ezra 8:9).
event: His name was entered in the list of Ezra's second return as one of the descendants of Joab, and the number of men who returned with him was 218 (Ezra 8:9).

introduce: A man whose name is recorded among the priests who set their seal to the binding covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:5, 10:8).
lifetime: His name is entered in the list of the priests who set their seal to the binding covenant led by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:5, 10:8).
event: When the binding covenant was made and put in writing, his name was recorded as a priest among those who set their seal (Nehemiah 9:38, 10:5, 10:8).

introduce: One of those recorded as gatekeepers in Nehemiah chapter 12, verse 25, who guarded the storerooms at the gates (Nehemiah 12:25).
lifetime: In the days of Joiakim, of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest and scribe, Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub are recorded as gatekeepers (Nehemiah 12:25-26).
event: Together with Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub, he guarded, as a gatekeeper, by divisions, the storerooms at the gates (Nehemiah 12:25).

call: author of the book of Obadiah (prophet)
introduce: Obadiah is a name that in Hebrew means "servant of the LORD," and he is the prophet known as the author of the book of Obadiah in the Old Testament. He is recorded as one who prophesied the destruction of Edom and the restoration of Israel.
lifetime: In the biblical record no concrete information appears about Obadiah's place of origin, family, or early or later life (Obadiah 1:1). The period in which he was active is also not stated in the biblical text (Obadiah 1:11-14).
event: He engaged in prophetic activity denouncing the onlooker attitude and the plundering of Edom, the brother nation of Judah, in the time of Israel's disaster (Obadiah 1:10-12). He warned of judgment on Edom for its acts of rejoicing over Israel's suffering with a proud heart, seizing their goods, and blocking the way of those who fled (Obadiah 1:13-14). Furthermore, he proclaimed the message of restoration, that Edom would ultimately be destroyed and the house of Jacob would gain that land as an inheritance (Obadiah 1:18-19).
character: He shows a firm attitude in resolutely proclaiming the righteous judgment of God against Edom, which turned away from the pain of Israel and even joined in the invasion (Obadiah 1:3-4). He is characterized by clearly pointing out that Edom's destruction stems from their pride and their violence against their brother Jacob, and by emphasizing the sovereignty of God who rules over history (Obadiah 1:10-15).

introduce: Jonathan was the eldest son of Saul, the first king of Israel, and a man belonging to the house of Kish of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Samuel 14:1). Although he was first in the line of succession to the throne, he formed a deep bond with David, and he is a central figure of the house of Saul who played a military role in the wars with the Philistines (1 Samuel 18:1).
lifetime: Jonathan, as a son of King Saul, was active as a military commander and struck the garrison of the Philistines at Geba (1 Samuel 13:3). When David finished speaking to Saul, Jonathan's heart was joined to his, and he gave David his robe, his military clothing, his sword, his bow, and his belt (1 Samuel 18:1, 18:4). Afterward, when Saul sought to kill David, he let David know and had him hide (1 Samuel 19:1-2), and in the end he was killed by the Philistines on Mount Gilboa together with his father Saul (1 Samuel 31:1-2).
event: He crossed over to the Philistine garrison with the young man who carried his weapons and struck down about twenty men (1 Samuel 14:1, 14:13-14). When Saul sought to kill David, Jonathan warned David beforehand and had him stay hidden (1 Samuel 19:1-2). He made a covenant with David, and asked that even when the LORD cut off David's enemies from the face of the earth, David not cut off his kindness from Jonathan's house forever (1 Samuel 20:15).
character: Although he was Saul's son, he went against his father's wishes to defend David, and loved him and cherished him as his own life (1 Samuel 18:3). He was a brave soldier, so bold as to scout the enemy camp alone, and he showed faithfulness in remembering and keeping to the end the covenant he made with David (1 Samuel 20:17). Though he was in the position to inherit the throne of Saul, he showed that he recognized that David would become king (1 Samuel 23:17).

기타관계: Jarah#2277(kinsman of the tribe of Benjamin)

introduce: Jonathan was the son of Abiathar the priest, a man who formed a close relationship with the house of David. When David was away from Jerusalem because of Absalom's rebellion, he served as an informant.
lifetime: When David fled from Absalom, David told Zadok to return to the city in peace, taking Ahimaaz and Jonathan the son of Abiathar (2 Samuel 15:27), and told Hushai to report whatever he heard in the king's house by way of the two sons of the two priests, Zadok and Abiathar (2 Samuel 15:35-36). When Hushai told the two priests of the counsel of Ahithophel and his own counsel and had them pass it on to David (2 Samuel 17:15-16), Jonathan and Ahimaaz, fearing to be seen, could not enter the city and stayed by En-rogel, and when a servant girl came out and told them, they went and told David (2 Samuel 17:17). When a young man saw this and told Absalom, the two went down into a well in the courtyard of a man's house in Bahurim (2 Samuel 17:18), and the woman of the house covered the mouth of the well and spread out ground grain over it so that no one would know (2 Samuel 17:19-20).
event: Jonathan, together with Ahimaaz, came up out of the well and went to King David and told him that Ahithophel had given counsel to harm him and that he should cross the water quickly (2 Samuel 17:21), and David crossed the Jordan with all the people, and by daybreak there was no one who had not crossed (2 Samuel 17:22).
character: He had the ability to grasp the situation quickly and to deal calmly with a crisis. He showed loyalty to David at the risk of danger, and carried out a wise strategy for secret communication (2 Samuel 17:17-20).

introduce: Jonathan was one of David's mighty men, the Thirty, a son of Jashen (2 Samuel 23:32). In 1 Chronicles 11:34 he is recorded as Jonathan the son of Shagee the Hararite.
lifetime: Under King David his military ability was recognized, and he was active as a member of the Thirty, David's powerful group of mighty men (2 Samuel 23:32, 1 Chronicles 11:34).
event: As one of David's mighty men he was included in the military list and entered his name as a member of the Thirty (2 Samuel 23:32, 1 Chronicles 11:34).

introduce: The Jonathan who appears in 1 Chronicles chapter 2, verses 32 and 33, is a person in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah who is among the descendants of Jerahmeel, recorded as a son of Jada, the younger brother of Shammai the son of Onam.
lifetime: Jonathan is recorded as a son of Jada, the brother of Shammai, and his brother Jether died without sons (1 Chronicles 2:32). The sons of Jonathan are Peleth and Zaza (1 Chronicles 2:33).

introduce: Jonathan is a man recorded as David's uncle. According to 1 Chronicles 27:32, he was a man of wisdom and so became a counselor, and he also became a scribe.
lifetime: He is recorded as David's uncle, and in David's time, being wise, he became a counselor and also became a scribe (1 Chronicles 27:32). The Bible has no record of his birth or death.
event: Jonathan, being wise, became a counselor and also became a scribe (1 Chronicles 27:32).
character: The Bible describes him as a man of wisdom and a counselor (1 Chronicles 27:32). He is also regarded as a person of rich learning who possessed the intellectual ability to carry out faithfully the role of a recorder (1 Chronicles 27:32).

call: father of Ebed (of the descendants of Adin)
introduce: Jonathan is a man recorded as the father of Ebed, among the descendants of Adin (Ezra 8:6).
lifetime: Ezra 8:6 says, "of the descendants of Adin, Ebed the son of Jonathan," so Jonathan appears only as the father of Ebed. His son Ebed was recorded, with fifty men, in the list of the heads of families who came up from Babylon in the time of King Artaxerxes (Ezra 8:1, 8:6).
event: His son Ebed was entered in the list of those who came up from Babylon, as a head of a family with fifty men from among the descendants of Adin (Ezra 8:1, 8:6).

introduce: Jonathan the son of Asahel is recorded as one who, in the time of Ezra after the return from the Babylonian exile, together with Jahzeiah the son of Tikvah, opposed the effort to settle the matter of those who had taken foreign women as wives (Ezra 10:15).
lifetime: As a member of the community that returned from Babylon, he is a man who, together with Jahzeiah, took the opposing position at the official gathering convened to deal with the problem of Jews who had married foreign women (Ezra 10:15).
event: When Ezra the priest told the people to separate from the foreign women (Ezra 10:10-11), and the congregation proposed that officials be appointed to handle the matter (Ezra 10:14), Jonathan, together with Jahzeiah, rose up and opposed it, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them (Ezra 10:15).

introduce: Jonathan is a man recorded in the priestly genealogy after the return from the Babylonian exile as the son of Joiada and the father of Jaddua (Nehemiah 12:11).
lifetime: Nehemiah 12:11 records: Joiada was the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan was the father of Jaddua. Joiada is the son of Eliashib (Nehemiah 12:10). His other deeds are not recorded in the Bible.
event: Jonathan is a man whose name is entered between Joiada and Jaddua in the priestly genealogy that begins with Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:10-11).

call: priest of the family of Malluchi
introduce: Jonathan is a priest who was a head of the family of Malluchi, active in the time of Joiakim the high priest after the return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 12:14).
lifetime:
He served as the head representing the family of Malluchi, one of the priestly families, in the time of Joiakim the high priest (Nehemiah 12:12-14).
No concrete record of his birth or other family relations, or of his death, appears in the Bible (Nehemiah 12:14).

introduce: Jonathan is a man recorded as a scribe in the time of King Zedekiah in the days of Jeremiah; his house had been made a prison by the officials, and so became the place where Jeremiah was confined (Jeremiah 37:15).
lifetime: Jonathan is called "Jonathan the scribe," and his house was a house that the officials had made into a prison (Jeremiah 37:15). Jeremiah pleaded with King Zedekiah not to send him back to the house of Jonathan the scribe (Jeremiah 37:20), and the king had Jeremiah kept in the courtyard of the guard (Jeremiah 37:21). Afterward Jeremiah was to answer the officials that what he had begged before the king was not to be sent back to the house of Jonathan (Jeremiah 38:26). No action of Jonathan himself is recorded in the text.
event: When Irijah, the captain of the guard, seized Jeremiah, saying he was going to surrender to the Chaldeans, and dragged him to the officials (Jeremiah 37:13-14), the officials became angry, beat Jeremiah, and confined him in the house of Jonathan the scribe. This was because they had made that house a prison (Jeremiah 37:15). Fearing that he would die there, Jeremiah made his plea to the king, and King Zedekiah had him kept in the courtyard of the guard (Jeremiah 37:20-21), and Jeremiah was later told to answer the officials that he had begged before the king not to be sent back to the house of Jonathan (Jeremiah 38:26).

introduce: Jonathan son of Kareah was a man who had dealings with those who remained in the land of Judah after the kingdom of Judah fell and its people were taken captive to Babylon. He is mentioned as one of the army commanders who went to Gedaliah, who had been appointed governor.
lifetime: When the army commanders in the open country and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam governor over the land of Judah, they went to Gedaliah at Mizpah (Jeremiah 40:7-8). On this occasion Jonathan is recorded as one of those who went to Gedaliah, together with Johanan, another son of Kareah (Jeremiah 40:8).
event: Jonathan went to Gedaliah at Mizpah together with Johanan son of Kareah, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and others (Jeremiah 40:8), and Gedaliah swore to them not to be afraid to serve the Chaldeans, but to dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon (Jeremiah 40:9-10). Afterward Johanan son of Kareah and the army commanders came to Gedaliah and told him that Baalis king of the Ammonites had sent Ishmael to take his life, but Gedaliah did not believe them (Jeremiah 40:13-14). Jonathan's name does not appear separately in these verses.

call: Son of Uzziah (overseer of the storehouses)
introduce: Jonathan, a son of Uzziah, was one of the officials in charge of the king's property in the time of King David. He was in charge of the storehouses in the fields, the cities, the villages, and the fortresses (1 Chronicles 27:25).
lifetime: Jonathan was one of those in charge of King David's property, and he oversaw the storehouses in the fields, the cities, the villages, and the fortresses (1 Chronicles 27:25, 31).
event: Among those in charge of King David's property, Jonathan son of Uzziah oversaw the storehouses in the fields, the cities, the villages, and the fortresses, while the king's treasuries were under Azmaveth son of Adiel (1 Chronicles 27:25).

introduce: Jezreel is the name of the firstborn son born to the prophet Hosea and Gomer in the Old Testament. This name carries a symbolic meaning that foretold the fall of the dynasty of Jehu in the northern kingdom of Israel.
lifetime: He was the first son whom the prophet Hosea had by taking the harlot Gomer as his wife at God's command, and his birth is recorded as part of a prophetic act (Hosea 1:3).
event: The LORD told Hosea to name the son Jezreel, a name indicating that in a little while God would avenge the blood of Jezreel on the house of Jehu and put an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel (Hosea 1:4).

introduce: Jezreel is the name of the firstborn son whom the prophet Hosea fathered through his wife Gomer. In Hebrew it means that God plants, and the name was given a symbolic meaning foretelling the end and judgment of the dynasty of Jehu in the northern kingdom of Israel.
lifetime: He was born as the first son of the prophet Hosea and Gomer (Hosea 1:3). Hosea named his son Jezreel at God's command, and this was a sign that God would in time judge the house of Jehu in the Valley of Jezreel (Hosea 1:4).
event: The name Jezreel is linked with the event foretold for the fall of the house of Jehu in the Valley of Jezreel, a historic place in Israel (Hosea 1:4). God also said that on that day he would break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel (Hosea 1:5). Furthermore, Hosea 1:11 says that the children of Judah and the children of Israel will be gathered together, appoint one leader, and go up from the land, and that "great will be the day of Jezreel," and Hosea 2:22 says that the grain, the wine, and the oil will answer Jezreel.

introduce: A figure who appears in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke, recorded as the son of Nahum, an early Jewish figure.
lifetime: In the genealogy of Jesus recorded in the Gospel of Luke, he appears as the son of Nahum and the father of Mattathias, and David appears among his ancestors in this genealogy (Luke 3:25, 31).

introduce: Amoz is recorded as the father of the prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 1:1). He is a different person from the prophet Amos of Tekoa.
lifetime: The Bible mentions him only as the father of Isaiah, and no deeds of Amoz himself are recorded (Isaiah 1:1, 2 Kings 19:2).
event: His son, the prophet Isaiah, saw a vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah (Isaiah 1:1). Isaiah son of Amoz went to King Hezekiah and delivered the word of the LORD to him (2 Kings 20:1).

introduce: The son of Azaziah, he was an officer who led the tribe of Ephraim in the time of King David (1 Chronicles 27:20).
lifetime:
Born as a son of Azaziah, he held the office of overseeing the tribes of Israel and ruled the tribe of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 27:20).
Apart from his activity as an officer of a tribe under King David, the Bible gives no further record concerning his birth or death (1 Chronicles 27:20).

call: Last king of the northern kingdom of Israel
introduce: Hoshea was the nineteenth and last king of the northern kingdom of Israel, a son of Elah, who came to the throne by killing Pekah. His reign lasted nine years, and while ruling Samaria he was overthrown by Assyria.
lifetime: In the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah, Hoshea conspired against Pekah son of Remaliah, struck him down and killed him, and became king in his place (2 Kings 15:30). In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah he became king of Israel in Samaria and reigned nine years (2 Kings 17:1). When Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Hoshea, he became his vassal and paid tribute (2 Kings 17:3), but he sent envoys to So king of Egypt and did not pay tribute to the king of Assyria as he had done year by year. Because of this, the king of Assyria found his conspiracy, arrested him, and put him in prison (2 Kings 17:4), and besieged Samaria for three years; in the ninth year of Hoshea he took Samaria and carried the Israelites away to Assyria (2 Kings 17:5-6).
event: During his reign Hoshea was attacked by Shalmaneser king of Assyria and was reduced to paying him tribute (2 Kings 17:3). He sent envoys to So king of Egypt and did not pay the tribute he had paid the king of Assyria year by year, and the king of Assyria found his conspiracy and put him in prison (2 Kings 17:4). After that the king of Assyria besieged Samaria for three years, and in the ninth year of Hoshea he took Samaria and carried the Israelites captive to Assyria (2 Kings 17:5-6).
character: The Bible judges that Hoshea did evil in the sight of the LORD, though not as the kings of Israel who were before him (2 Kings 17:2). As the last ruler of Israel he tried to preserve his regime by shifting his diplomatic course amid international affairs, but he ended up losing his national sovereignty, overpowered by Assyria's mighty military force (2 Kings 17:4-6).

call: Leader of the people who sealed the covenant
introduce: Hoshea was one of the leaders of the community of Judah who returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, and he took part in the covenant renewal led by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:23).
lifetime: When the people who had returned from Babylon made a covenant with God and sealed it, the name Hoshea is included in the list (Nehemiah 10:1). This list consists of Nehemiah the governor, the priests, the Levites, and the leaders of the people, and Hoshea is one whose name is recorded among the leaders of the people (Nehemiah 10:14-27).
event: Hoshea, whose name is recorded among the leaders of the people (Nehemiah 10:23), is recorded as one who sealed the covenant, taking part in the oath under a curse to follow the law of God, not to give their daughters in marriage to the peoples of the land, and not to buy wares on the Sabbath or on holy days (Nehemiah 10:29-31).

call: Son of Beeri (author of the book of Hosea)
introduce: Hosea was a prophet of the northern kingdom of Israel, a son of Beeri, who was active from the time of Jeroboam II to the time of Hezekiah.
lifetime: Hosea was active beginning in the time of Jeroboam II and continuing through the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah (Hosea 1:1). At God's command he took a woman named Gomer as his wife and had children (Hosea 1:3).
event: Hosea carried out God's command to take the harlot Gomer as his wife and have children (Hosea 1:2). He had children named Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, and Lo-ammi (Hosea 1:4-9). He also experienced buying back his adulterous wife, paying fifteen pieces of silver and a homer and a half of barley (Hosea 3:2). He wrote a prophetic book criticizing the idolatry and moral decay of the northern kingdom of Israel (Hosea 4:1-19).
character: He obeyed God's command and lived a life of delivering a message through his own family affairs (Hosea 1:3). He accused Israel of apostasy and warned in strong terms (Hosea 8:1-14).

introduce: Mahli was a grandson of Levi and a son of Merari, a person belonging to the Merarite descendants of the tribe of Levi (Exodus 6:19). As a descendant of Levi he is recorded as a member of the house of Merari within the tribal structure of Israel (Numbers 3:20).
lifetime: Mahli was a son of Merari and a brother of Mushi (Exodus 6:19). He carried on the genealogical line of the house of Merari (Numbers 3:20), and he is also recorded as a son of Merari in 1 Chronicles 6:19. His son is recorded as Libni (1 Chronicles 6:29), and the sons of Mahli are said to be Eleazar and Kish (1 Chronicles 23:21).
event: The descendants of Merari were put in charge of the frames of the tabernacle, with its crossbars, posts, and bases (Numbers 3:36-37). 1 Chronicles 23:21 records the sons of Mahli as Eleazar and Kish, and Eleazar died without sons, having only daughters (1 Chronicles 23:22).

introduce: Mahli is a person who appears in the records of Chronicles, a descendant of the tribe of Levi and a member of a family that belonged to the system of temple service in the time of David and afterward.
lifetime: Mahli was a son of Mushi, Mushi was a son of Merari, and Merari was a son of Levi (1 Chronicles 6:47). Shemer was his son (1 Chronicles 6:47). The sons of Mushi were three: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth (1 Chronicles 23:23).
event: Mahli is mentioned not as the subject of a direct event but as a person who makes up the genealogy of the tribe of Levi and the line of the descendants of Merari (1 Chronicles 6:47). When David numbered the Levites, he was classified as belonging to the household of the descendants of Merari (1 Chronicles 23:23).

call: One of Jesus' twelve disciples, the betrayer
introduce: He was chosen as one of the twelve apostles of Jesus and was put in charge of the money bag, but he received thirty pieces of silver and betrayed Jesus to the chief priests. The Bible records him as "the one who betrayed Jesus" (Matthew 10:4).
lifetime: A native of Kerioth in the region of Judah, he was called to be a disciple during the public ministry of Jesus and accompanied him. But after betraying his Master, he could not bear the pangs of conscience and ended his life by hanging himself (Matthew 27:5).
event: He was in charge of the money bag among the group of disciples, but he was a thief who stole from the offerings (John 12:6). Immediately after the Last Supper, in the garden of Gethsemane, he handed Jesus over to the crowd sent by the chief priests, having arranged a kiss as the signal. Afterward, seeing that Jesus was condemned, he repented, threw the silver into the sanctuary, and killed himself, and the priests bought with that money the Potter's Field (Akeldama, the Field of Blood), a burial place for strangers.
character: He had a strong attachment to material things and showed a hypocritical side, with an outside that differed from what was within. Although he regretted betraying Jesus, he did not come to true repentance, but in despair chose self-destruction.

meaning: Simon (he hears), a man of Kerioth (Iscariot)
introduce: He is recorded as the father of Judas, one of Jesus' disciples who later betrayed him (John 6:71).
lifetime: He was a man from the region of Kerioth in southern Judea in the first century (John 6:71).
event: His son Judas was the object of the words saying that one of the twelve would betray Jesus (John 6:71); the devil put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, son of Simon, the thought of betraying Jesus (John 13:2); and Jesus dipped a piece of bread and gave it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot (John 13:26).

introduce: A man from Bethsaida in Galilee who was called by Jesus and became one of the twelve apostles. Immediately after being called, he brought his friend Nathanael (Bartholomew) to Jesus.
lifetime: He was a man of Bethsaida in Galilee, from the same town as Andrew and Peter (John 1:44). He followed Jesus throughout his public ministry, and after Jesus' ascension, when they returned from the Mount of Olives to Jerusalem, he went up to the upper room and devoted himself to prayer with one mind, together with the other disciples, the women, Mary the mother of Jesus, and Jesus' brothers (Acts 1:12-14).
event: Before the miracle of the five loaves and two fish, he was tested by Jesus, who asked, "Where shall we buy bread for these people to eat?" (John 6:5-7), and when Greeks who had come to worship at the feast wished to see Jesus, he acted as the one who guided them in between (John 12:20-22). At the Last Supper he also asked Jesus, "Show us the Father" (John 14:8).
character: He showed a rational temperament that was practical and quick at calculating, yet he had a passion for seeking the truth and the initiative to tell his neighbor at once the joy of having met the Messiah.

call: One of the seven deacons of the Jerusalem church
introduce: He was one of the seven deacons appointed for the relief ministry of the early church in Jerusalem. After the martyrdom of Stephen, he was a representative evangelist who preached the gospel in many cities from Samaria and Azotus to Caesarea.
lifetime: He was chosen as a man well spoken of by the believers of the early church and served as a deacon. When the believers were scattered by persecution, he went down to Samaria and preached the gospel; afterward he settled in Caesarea, and his four daughters were also used as prophetesses.
event: He preached the gospel in the city of Samaria, performed many signs, and brought great joy (Acts 8:4-8); led by an angel of the Lord, he went out into the desert, explained the book of Isaiah to the Ethiopian eunuch, and baptized him (Acts 8:26-39). Later, when Paul and his companions went to Jerusalem, they stayed at his house in Caesarea (Acts 21:8).
character: He had an excellent character, full of the Spirit and of wisdom and well spoken of by the people, and he was a man of faith who obeyed the guidance of the Holy Spirit immediately and wholeheartedly.

call: One of Jesus' twelve apostles (the Zealot / the Cananaean)
meaning: Zealot. "Cananaean" is not a place name but a direct transliteration of the Aramaic "qan'ana," which means zeal.
introduce: He was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus, and he is recorded as "Simon the Cananaean" in the Gospels of Matthew and Mark, and as "Simon the Zealot" in the Gospel of Luke and the Acts (Matthew 10:4, Mark 3:18, Luke 6:15, Acts 1:13).
lifetime: Apart from his name being recorded in the lists of the twelve apostles, no concrete record of his personal life or origin remains in the Bible.
character: The epithet "the Zealot" suggests a connection with the Zealots, who resisted Roman rule by force, but the Bible has no separate record of his personal deeds or character after he was called as an apostle.

call: Fifth of the ten sons of Haman
introduce: He was the fifth of the ten sons of Haman the Agagite, who tried to annihilate the Jews in the Persian empire. He appears in the book of Esther and was put to death by the Jews in the citadel of Susa.
lifetime: Born as a son of Haman, who wielded great power under King Xerxes, he enjoyed wealth and glory. But when his father Haman's plot to wipe out the Jew Mordecai and the Jewish people was overthrown by Esther and Haman was executed, he too met a miserable end.
event: After the fall of his father Haman, on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, when the Jews struck down their enemies in Susa, the capital of the Persian empire, he was killed together with his nine other brothers (Esther 9:8). On the following day, the fourteenth, with the permission of King Xerxes in response to Esther's request, the bodies of Haman's ten sons, including Adalia, were all hanged on the gallows (Esther 9:14).
character: His personal character is not specifically recorded in the Bible (Esther 9:8-10).

call: Ahiam was one of David's thirty mighty men
introduce: Ahiam is a person mentioned as one of David's thirty mighty men; 2 Samuel 23:33 records him as the son of Sharar the Hararite, and 1 Chronicles 11:35 records him as the son of Sachar the Hararite.
lifetime: His name is on the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:33, 1 Chronicles 11:35). His father and place of origin are written differently in the two lists, as Sharar/Sachar and Arar/Harar, and nothing else of his deeds is recorded in the Bible.

introduce: A person active in the time of Isaiah, a son of Jeberekiah. He was singled out as one who, together with Uriah the priest, would be called as a faithful witness to testify.
lifetime: He was named as a witness to the record concerning "Maher-shalal-hash-baz," which Isaiah was commanded to write on a large tablet (Isaiah 8:1-2). Through this he served as a public witness by whom it can be confirmed that the prophecy was recorded before the event took place (Isaiah 8:3-4).

call: Writer of the book of Zechariah
introduce: Zechariah was a prophet active in the community of Judah after the Babylonian exile, a grandson of Iddo and a son of Berechiah (Zechariah 1:1, Ezra 5:1).
lifetime: In the eighth month of the second year of Darius I (October–November 520 BC), Zechariah, together with Haggai, encouraged the temple rebuilding work of Zerubbabel, the political leader of Judah at that time. He was not merely a person who delivered a religious message; he was a person who supported, through prophecy, the project of rebuilding the temple in Jerusalem that was actually under way.

introduce: A son of Jeroboam II, king of the northern kingdom of Israel, and the last king of the dynasty of Jehu.
lifetime: After his father Jeroboam II died, he succeeded to the throne and ruled Israel in Samaria, but his reign lasted only six months. He came to the throne in the fourth generation of the descendants of Jehu, and the hereditary rule of the dynasty of Jehu ended when he was killed in the rebellion of Shallum son of Jabesh (2 Kings 14:29; 15:8–12).

call: Second (or youngest) son of Noah, father of Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan
introduce: One of the three sons of Noah (Shem, Ham, and Japheth) and one of the ancestors of humankind who survived in the ark after the great flood. He is recorded as the ancestor of the African peoples and of the peoples of the Canaanite line.
lifetime: He was born as one of the three sons whom Noah fathered after he was 500 years old (Genesis 5:32). At the time of the great flood he entered Noah's ark with his wife and his life was preserved (Genesis 7:13), and after leaving the ark he fathered four sons (Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan) (Genesis 10:6). His descendants scattered mainly over Africa and the region of Canaan in the ancient Near East, forming various peoples and nations.
event: After leaving the ark, when Noah drank wine, became drunk, and lay uncovered inside his tent, Ham saw his father's nakedness, went outside, and told his two brothers (Shem and Japheth). When Noah awoke from his wine and learned what his youngest son had done to him, he pronounced on Ham's son Canaan a curse that he would be "a servant of servants to his brothers" (Genesis 9:20-25).
character: Rashness, impiety

직업/직위: progenitor of the descendants of Ham

call: Wife of Uriah and queen of King David, mother of King Solomon
meaning: Daughter of an oath, seventh daughter, daughter of abundance
introduce: She was the daughter of Eliam (Ammiel) and the wife of Uriah the Hittite, and afterward became the wife of King David and bore Solomon. She played a decisive role in Solomon's succession to the throne after David, and she is one of the four women mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Matthew, where she is referred to as "the wife of Uriah."
lifetime: As the daughter of Eliam she married Uriah the Hittite and lived in Jerusalem. During the war with Ammon she was summoned by King David and slept with him and conceived a child, and after her husband Uriah was killed in battle she became David's wife. She lost her first child through God's discipline, but afterward bore sons including Solomon (2 Samuel 12:24, 1 Chronicles 3:5). In David's last years, together with the prophet Nathan, she thwarted Adonijah's attempt to seize the throne and placed Solomon on the throne, and during Solomon's reign she received honored treatment as queen mother (1 Kings 2:19).
event: While she was bathing, she caught the eye of David as he walked on the roof of the royal palace, and she was summoned to the palace, slept with him, and informed him of her pregnancy. To hide his sin, David sent her husband Uriah to the front line of the battle to be killed, and then took Bathsheba as his lawful wife (2 Samuel 11). When David grew old and Adonijah plotted rebellion, she went to David on the advice of the prophet Nathan and reminded him of his earlier oath to make Solomon his successor on the throne, and thus contributed decisively to Solomon's accession (1 Kings 1).
character: Prudent and bold in times of crisis, with political insight and decisiveness on behalf of her children

call: Third son of Jesse, older brother of David
meaning: Desolation, astonishment, being there (the LORD hears)
introduce: He was the third of the eight sons of Jesse of Bethlehem and the third older brother of King David. He is recorded as "Shammah" in 1 Samuel 16:9 and 2 Samuel 21:21, and as "Shimea" in 2 Samuel 13:3 and 1 Chronicles 2:13. His son Jonathan killed the tall man of Gath who had defied Israel (2 Samuel 21:20-21).
lifetime: He was born as a son of Jesse in Bethlehem of the tribe of Judah (1 Samuel 16:9). When Samuel called Jesse's sons to anoint a king, he was called out third but was not chosen. Afterward he joined the army of King Saul and took part in the war with the Philistines (1 Samuel 17:13).
event: When the prophet Samuel, at God's command, visited Jesse's house in Bethlehem to choose a new king, he came forward third, after the eldest son Eliab and the second son Abinadab, but God did not choose him (1 Samuel 16:9). Afterward, when the army faced the Philistine champion Goliath in the Valley of Elah, he went out with Saul's army together with the two older brothers above (Eliab and Abinadab) (1 Samuel 17:13). At that time David, the youngest, who had brought roasted grain and loaves to his brothers on an errand for his father, ran to the camp and greeted his brothers (1 Samuel 17:17-22).

call: Son of Joseph and Mary, Jesus' brother in the flesh
introduce: One of Jesus' younger brothers in the flesh mentioned in the New Testament, born to Joseph the carpenter and Mary. He is recorded in the Gospels, together with James, Joseph, and Judas, among the brothers of Jesus. During Jesus' public ministry he did not believe together with his brothers, but after Jesus' resurrection and ascension he joined the community of the early church and devoted himself to prayer.
lifetime: He grew up in Nazareth in Galilee as a son of Joseph the carpenter and Mary (Matthew 13:55, Mark 6:3). When Jesus taught in his hometown of Nazareth, the people of his hometown mentioned him as the carpenter's son and the brother of Simon. After Jesus' ascension, in the upper room in Jerusalem, together with his mother Mary, the other brothers, and the apostles, he prayed wholeheartedly, waiting for the coming of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost (Acts 1:13-14).
event: When Jesus taught in the synagogue of his hometown Nazareth, the villagers were amazed at his wisdom and power, yet rejected Jesus, saying, "Isn't this the carpenter's son? Isn't his mother named Mary, and aren't his brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?"; it is against this background of rejection that Simon is mentioned (Matthew 13:55, Mark 6:3). At first the brothers did not fully believe in Jesus as the Messiah, but after Jesus' suffering on the cross, resurrection, and ascension, they devoted themselves to prayer with one mind together with Mary and the disciples (Acts 1:14).

call: Nephew of Abram, ancestor of the Moabites and Ammonites
introduce: A grandson of Terah and a son of Haran, he was the nephew of Abram (Abraham), the father of faith. After his father died early, he followed his uncle Abram through Ur of the Chaldeans and Haran into the land of Canaan, and he chose the land of Sodom, which looked good to the eye, and settled there; he then went through the crisis of judgment and became the ancestor of the Moabites and the Ammonites.
lifetime: His father Haran died first in his native land, Ur of the Chaldeans, and he moved to Haran together with his grandfather Terah and his uncle Abram (Genesis 11:27-31). He migrated to Canaan with Abram and came to own large herds, but because of strife between their herdsmen he parted from Abram and, looking over the whole plain of the Jordan that was well watered, moved his tent as far as Sodom (Genesis 13:10-12). When Sodom was destroyed by sulfur and fire, he fled, led by angels, with his two daughters by way of Zoar to a cave in the mountains, and there through his two daughters he became the ancestor of the Moabites and the Ammonites (Ben-ammi) respectively (Genesis 19:30-38). In 2 Peter of the New Testament, he is also evaluated as "righteous Lot" (2 Peter 2:7).
event: While living in Sodom, he was taken captive and his possessions were plundered in the invasion of the allied forces of Chedorlaomer king of Elam, but Abram, hearing the news, led 318 trained men born in his house, pursued them, and rescued him (Genesis 14:12-16). Afterward, when the wickedness of the city of Sodom was full and the judgment of the LORD came, he received the two angels with great hospitality and protected them from the violence of the men of the city, and at the urging of the angels he fled outside the city. At that time his wife disobeyed the warning, looked back, and became a pillar of salt, and his sons-in-law who were betrothed took the warning of judgment as a joke and perished. After he took refuge in the cave in the mountains, his two daughters made their father drink wine and slept with him, and bore Moab and Ben-ammi (Genesis 19:1-38).
character: Lavish in hospitality to strangers and righteous in character, yet he left Abraham in pursuit of immediate gain.

직업/직위: ancestor of the Moabites and Ammonites

call: The man of Cyrene who carried Jesus' cross in his place
introduce: A man of Cyrene, recorded as the father of Alexander and Rufus (Mark 15:21). As Jesus was carrying the cross, he was coming in from the country, was seized by the soldiers, and was forced to carry Jesus' cross and follow him.
lifetime: Simon of Cyrene is recorded as the father of Alexander and Rufus (Mark 15:21). Coming in from the country, he was seized by the soldiers who were leading Jesus away and was made to carry the cross behind Jesus (Luke 23:26). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.
event: As Jesus was going to Golgotha carrying the cross, the soldiers forced Simon of Cyrene, who was passing by on his way in from the country, to go along and carry Jesus' cross (Matthew 27:32, Mark 15:21, Luke 23:26).
character: Obedient, silently sharing in the suffering of the cross

call: Father of Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera (head of the inhabitants of Geba)
introduce: A man of the tribe of Benjamin whose name is recorded in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 8. 1 Chronicles 8:6 records that the sons of Ehud were heads of the inhabitants of Geba. His sons were Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera (1 Chronicles 8:7), and Gera fathered Uzza and Ahihud (1 Chronicles 8:7).
lifetime: His name appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles 8, and his sons are recorded as heads of the inhabitants of Geba (1 Chronicles 8:6). The Bible has no record of Ehud's own life.
event: 1 Chronicles 8:6-7 records that the sons of Ehud, as heads of the inhabitants of Geba, took Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera captive and went to Manahath. This is a record about his sons, and Ehud's own deeds are not recorded in the text.

call: Son of Gera the Benjamite (the left-handed judge)
introduce: The second judge of Israel in the period of the judges, he delivered Israel from the eighteen years of oppression by Eglon king of Moab. He was a son of Gera of the tribe of Benjamin, and the Bible records him as "left-handed." He hid a sword with an edge on both sides, a cubit long, killed Eglon by stabbing him, and defeated the Moabite army, bringing peace to the land for eighty years.
lifetime: He was born as a son of Gera of the tribe of Benjamin (Judges 3:15). After Othniel's death, when the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD and were oppressed for eighteen years by Eglon king of Moab, he was the deliverer whom God raised up after hearing the cry of the Israelites. He went to deliver the tribute and assassinated Eglon, then blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim to gather the people and subdue Moab, and after his activity the land of Israel had peace for eighty years (Judges 3:30).
event: He was chosen as the representative of the Israelites to present the tribute sent to Eglon king of Moab. Ehud made a double-edged sword a cubit long, strapped it under his clothes on his right thigh, and went and presented the tribute to Eglon; then he returned from the stone quarries near Gilgal and asked for a private audience, saying he had a secret matter to report to the king. When the very obese Eglon rose from his upper room, Ehud drew the sword from his right thigh with his left hand and thrust it into Eglon's belly, and it went in up to the hilt, and the fat closed over the blade. Ehud locked the doors and fled to Seirah, blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, led the multitude of Israel, guarded the fords of the Jordan, and killed about ten thousand Moabite warriors, every one of them, and so broke the yoke of Moab (Judges 3:16-30).
character: A bold and meticulous strategist, a spiritual leader who combined decisiveness with the ability to carry things out

기타관계: Gera#109(kinsman of the tribe of Benjamin)

call: Eldest son of Noah (founder of the Semites)
introduce: The eldest of the three sons (Shem, Ham, and Japheth) whom Noah fathered after he was five hundred years old, he entered the ark at the time of the great flood judgment and his life was preserved. He is the direct ancestor of the Semitic peoples, including the Hebrew people, and became the ancestor in the bloodline of the Messiah, Jesus Christ.
lifetime: He was born after Noah was five hundred years old (Genesis 5:32), and at the time of the great flood he boarded the ark with his wife and was saved (Genesis 7:7). After the flood, at the age of one hundred, that is, two years after the flood, he fathered Arphaxad, and after fathering Arphaxad he lived five hundred years and had children, and he died at the age of six hundred (Genesis 11:10-11).
event: When his father Noah drank wine, became drunk, and lay uncovered inside his tent, and Ham saw this and went out and told, he and Japheth took a garment, laid it on their shoulders, walked in backward, and covered their father's nakedness (Genesis 9:23). Because of this he received from Noah a spiritual blessing: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem! May Canaan be the servant of Shem" (Genesis 9:26).
character: Godliness, filial devotion and deep reverence toward his parents

직업/직위: progenitor of the descendants of Shem

call: Fifteenth king of southern Judah, son of Manasseh, father of Josiah
meaning: Skilled craftsman, faithful one, hidden one
introduce: The fifteenth king of southern Judah, he succeeded Manasseh and became king at the age of twenty-two, but reigned in Jerusalem for two years. He followed the evil deeds of his father Manasseh, worshiped idols, and did evil in the sight of the LORD, and he was killed in the palace through the rebellion of his servants.
lifetime: He was born to King Manasseh and Meshullemeth, daughter of Haruz of Jotbah (2 Kings 21:19). He became king of Judah at the age of twenty-two and ruled in Jerusalem for two years. He walked in all the ways of his father Manasseh and served idols, and unlike Manasseh he did not humble himself before the LORD but increased his guilt all the more; at the age of twenty-four he was killed in the palace through the rebellion of his servants and was buried in his own tomb in the garden of Uzza (2 Kings 21:19-26, 2 Chronicles 33:21-25).
event: Unlike his father Manasseh, who repented in his later years, Amon sacrificed to and served all the carved images that his father had made, and did not humble himself before the LORD but increased his guilt all the more (2 Chronicles 33:22-23). Two years after he took the throne, his servants rebelled and killed the king in his palace, but the people of the land killed all who had conspired against King Amon and made his eight-year-old son Josiah king (2 Kings 21:23-24, 22:1).
character: Sunk in idolatry, unrepentant and rebellious

call: Firstborn of Ham (founder of the Cushite peoples)
introduce: The eldest son of Noah's son Ham, he is recorded in the table of nations after the flood as the ancestor of the Cushite peoples. He became the father of Nimrod, who was the first to become a mighty one on the earth, as well as of Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca.
lifetime: He was born after the flood as Ham's eldest son and was a grandson of Noah (Genesis 10:6). He fathered the sons Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca, and in particular fathered Nimrod, who was the first to become a mighty one on the earth (an outstanding hunter and ruler) (Genesis 10:7-8). His descendants spread out and settled in the upper Nile region of Africa (Ethiopia/Nubia) and the southern part of the Arabian peninsula.
event: He is listed as Ham's eldest son in the "table of nations" of Genesis 10, which deals with the origins of the peoples scattered after Noah's flood (Genesis 10:6). In particular, among his descendants Nimrod became the first mighty one on the earth and the genealogical starting point of a kingdom beginning in the major cities of the land of Shinar, such as Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh (Genesis 10:8-10).

call: Son of Zerah (tribe of Judah), a man compared with the wisdom of Solomon
introduce: Calcol is a person recorded as one of the five sons of Zerah, the son of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:4, 6). In 1 Kings 4:31 the same name appears among those whom Solomon's wisdom is said to have surpassed.
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 2:6 records the sons of Zerah as Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara, five in all (1 Chronicles 2:6). 1 Kings 4:31 records that Solomon was wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol (1 Kings 4:31). Nothing else of his life is recorded in the Bible.
event: It is recorded that Solomon's wisdom surpassed that of people including Calcol, so that his fame spread among all the surrounding nations (1 Kings 4:31). Calcol's own deeds are not recorded.

call: Son of Ehud (head of the inhabitants of Geba)
introduce: Gera is a person whose name appears, together with Naaman and Ahijah, among the sons of Ehud who were heads of the inhabitants of Geba in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8) (1 Chronicles 8:6-7).
lifetime: The sons of Ehud were heads of the inhabitants of Geba and took captives and went to Manahath, and among them the names of Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera appear (1 Chronicles 8:6-7). It is then recorded, "and he also fathered Uzza and Ahihud" (1 Chronicles 8:7), but the text of the Korean Revised Version (KRV) does not make clear who "he" is.
event: 1 Chronicles 8:6-7 records that the sons of Ehud, heads of the inhabitants of Geba, took captives to Manahath, and it names Gera together with Naaman and Ahijah. It then records, "and he also fathered Uzza and Ahihud," but the text does not make clear who "he" is (1 Chronicles 8:7).

call: Father of Shallum and Meshelemiah (Korahite gatekeeper family)
introduce: A descendant of Korah of the tribe of Levi, he is recorded as the father of Shallum and Meshelemiah (1 Chronicles 9:19; 26:1).
lifetime: The KRV records him as a grandson of Ebiasaph, a descendant of Korah (1 Chronicles 9:19). His son Shallum was the chief of the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 9:17-19), and his son Meshelemiah was recorded in the division of the gatekeepers of the Korahites (1 Chronicles 26:1).

call: Son of Imnah (Levite keeper of the East Gate in the time of Hezekiah)
introduce: A Levite who was the keeper of the East Gate in the time of Hezekiah, a son of Imnah (2 Chronicles 31:14).
lifetime: He is recorded as a Levite, a son of Imnah, and keeper of the East Gate (2 Chronicles 31:14).
event: He was put in charge of the freewill offerings given to God, to present the offerings to the LORD and to distribute all the most holy things (2 Chronicles 31:14). Under him, Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah held offices in the cities of the priests and distributed to their brothers according to their divisions (2 Chronicles 31:15).

call: Son of Japheth (father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah)
introduce: A person recorded as a son of Noah's son Japheth (Genesis 10:2).
lifetime: His name is recorded first among the sons of Japheth, and he had Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah as sons (Genesis 10:2-3). 1 Chronicles 1:6 writes Riphath as Diphath.

introduce: The daughter of Diblaim, she was the wife whom the prophet Hosea took. After the LORD told Hosea to take a harlot as his wife, Hosea took her (Hosea 1:2-3).
lifetime: She was the daughter of Diblaim (Hosea 1:3), and she became the wife of Hosea and bore a son, Jezreel, a daughter, Lo-ruhamah, and a son, Lo-ammi (Hosea 1:3-9).
event: After she was taken by Hosea, she conceived and bore a son (Hosea 1:3), conceived again and bore a daughter (Hosea 1:6), and after weaning Lo-ruhamah, she conceived again and bore a son (Hosea 1:8). The LORD commanded Hosea to name the children Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, and Lo-ammi (Hosea 1:4, 6, 9).

introduce: A person recorded in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke as the son of Elmadam and the father of Addi (Luke 3:28).
lifetime: In the genealogy of Luke 3:28, he is recorded after Elmadam and before Addi (Luke 3:28).

introduce: A person recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Reuben as the son of Shemaiah and the father of Shimei (1 Chronicles 5:4).
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Shemaiah son of Joel, and from his son Shimei the line continues through Micah, Reaiah, Baal, and Beerah, and Beerah was a leader of the descendants of Reuben (1 Chronicles 5:4-6).

introduce: In Jeremiah 29:21 he is recorded as the father of Ahab, who prophesied falsely (Jeremiah 29:21).

call: A man of Gath (the Philistine who provoked battle)
introduce: A man of Gath who came out of the camp of the Philistines and provoked battle. His height was six cubits and a span (1 Samuel 17:4).
lifetime: He was a man of Gath (1 Samuel 17:4), and he had a brother named Lahmi (1 Chronicles 20:5). He was remembered as the Philistine whom David killed in the Valley of Elah (1 Samuel 21:9).
event: He wore a bronze helmet on his head and a coat of scale armor on his body, and the shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam (1 Samuel 17:5-7). He shouted to the ranks of Israel, told them to choose one man to come down to him, and insulted the army of Israel (1 Samuel 17:8-10). David struck down that Philistine with a sling and a stone (1 Samuel 17:49-51). His sword was later kept behind the ephod, and the priest gave it to David (1 Samuel 21:9; 22:10).

introduce: In the genealogy of the descendants of Gad, he is recorded as the father of Abdiel and the grandfather of Ahi, a head of a family. The Korean Revised Version reads "Ahi son of Abdiel, the grandson of Guni" (1 Chronicles 5:15).
A person recorded as the father of the prophet Zephaniah, who received the word of the LORD in the time of Josiah king of Judah (Zephaniah 1:1).
lifetime: In the genealogy at the beginning of the book of Zephaniah, he is recorded as the father of Zephaniah, a grandson of Gedaliah (Zephaniah 1:1).

introduce: A person recorded at the head of the genealogy of Jehudi in Jeremiah 36:14. The KRV writes: "Jehudi, great-grandson of Cushi, grandson of Shelemiah, and son of Nethaniah" (Jeremiah 36:14).

call: Son of Eliphaz (grandson of Esau, chief of Edom)
introduce: A son of Eliphaz, who was the son of Adah, Esau's wife, and so a grandson of Esau; he is listed as a chief belonging to the descendants of Eliphaz among the descendants of Esau (Genesis 36:10-11, 36:15).
lifetime: He is recorded among the sons of Eliphaz together with Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam (Genesis 36:11; 1 Chronicles 1:36).
event: He is listed as a chief who came from the descendants of Eliphaz among the descendants of Esau (Genesis 36:15).

introduce: A person recorded as the father of Othniel and Seraiah (1 Chronicles 4:13). The judge Othniel is called "the brother of Caleb and the son of Kenaz" (Joshua 15:17; Judges 1:13).
lifetime: The son of his son Othniel was Hathath, and his son Seraiah fathered Joab (1 Chronicles 4:13-14).

call: Son of Hadad of Edom's royal line (reared in Pharaoh's palace)
introduce: He is the son born when Hadad, of the royal line of Edom, took as his wife the sister of Pharaoh king of Egypt's wife, that is, the sister of Queen Tahpenes (1 Kings 11:14, 11:19-20).
lifetime: Tahpenes weaned him in Pharaoh's palace, and he lived in Pharaoh's palace among the sons of Pharaoh (1 Kings 11:20).

introduce: The grandfather of the prophet Zephaniah, a person recorded in the genealogy of Zephaniah 1:1 (Zephaniah 1:1).
lifetime: Zephaniah 1:1 describes Zephaniah as "great-great-grandson of Hezekiah, great-grandson of Amariah, grandson of Gedaliah, and son of Cushi," and so records him as a descendant of Amariah and the grandfather of Zephaniah (Zephaniah 1:1).

introduce: A person recorded in the genealogy as one of the sons of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon, of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:29-31; 9:35-37).
lifetime: In the genealogies of 1 Chronicles 8:30-31 and 9:36-37 he is listed with Ahio after Nadab.

introduce: A person recorded as a son of Dishon, the son of Anah, of the Horite clan in the land of Seir (Genesis 36:26).
lifetime: He is listed as one of the sons of Dishon, namely Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran (Genesis 36:26; 1 Chronicles 1:41). The Bible records nothing else of his life.

introduce: A person recorded as the son of Shaphan and as a scribe, in whose chamber Baruch read the words of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 36:10). He is the father of Micaiah (Jeremiah 36:11).
lifetime: In the time of Jehoiakim, he was one of the officials and was sitting in the chamber of the scribe in the royal palace (Jeremiah 36:9-12).
event: Together with Elnathan and Delaiah, he urged the king not to burn the scroll, but the king would not listen (Jeremiah 36:25).

call: Father of Ammiel, the spy of the tribe of Dan
introduce: Gemalli is a person recorded as the father of Ammiel, a leader of the tribe of Dan sent to spy out the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:12).
lifetime: He appears only in Numbers 13:12 as "from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli," and the Bible records nothing else of his life.
event: Gemalli's own deeds are not recorded. His son Ammiel is recorded as one of those sent to spy out the land of Canaan, representing the tribe of Dan (Numbers 13:12).

call: Father of Hashabiah (father of Hashabiah, officer of the Levites)
introduce: Kemuel is a person recorded as the father of Hashabiah, officer of the Levites, in the list of those who were over the tribes of Israel (1 Chronicles 27:16-17).
lifetime: He is introduced only as the father of Hashabiah, officer of the Levites, "son of Kemuel," in 1 Chronicles 27:17, and the Bible has no other record of his life.

call: Son of Reuel (grandson of Esau, chief of Edom)
introduce: Nahath is a son of Reuel, born to Esau's wife Basemath, recorded as one of the chiefs who came from Reuel in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:13, 36:17).
lifetime: Basemath bore Reuel to Esau (Genesis 36:4), and the sons of Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah (Genesis 36:13). As a grandson of Esau, Nahath is recorded as "Chief Nahath" among the chiefs who came from Reuel in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:17). Nothing else of his life is recorded in the Bible.
event: Among the descendants of Esau's son Reuel are Chief Nahath, Chief Zerah, Chief Shammah, and Chief Mizzah, and they are recorded as the chiefs who came from Reuel in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:17).

call: Son of Zophai (Levite of the Kohathites, father of Eliab)
introduce: Nahath is a person of the tribe of Levi recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Kohath in 1 Chronicles 6 as the son of Zophai and the father of Eliab (1 Chronicles 6:26-27).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 6:26-27 records the descendants of Elkanah: "his son was Zophai, his son was Nahath, his son was Eliab, his son was Jeroham, his son was Elkanah." In this genealogy Nahath appears as the son of Zophai and the father of Eliab. Nothing else of his life is recorded in the Bible.

introduce: Ner is a man of the tribe of Benjamin recorded as the father of Abner, the commander of King Saul's army (1 Samuel 14:50-51). 1 Samuel 14:50 records him as the uncle of Saul.
lifetime: He is recorded in 1 Samuel 14:50-51 as the father of Abner, commander of Saul's army, and in the same verse he is called Saul's uncle (1 Samuel 14:50). Afterward Abner was called "the son of Ner" (1 Samuel 26:5, 2 Samuel 2:8, 3:23, 1 Kings 2:5).

call: Born to Nahor and his concubine Reumah
introduce: Tahash is a person recorded as one of the four (Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah) whom Reumah, the concubine of Abraham's brother Nahor, bore (Genesis 22:24).
lifetime: It is recorded that Nahor's concubine Reumah bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah (Genesis 22:24).

call: Son of Nahor (father of Abraham, Nahor, and Haran)
introduce: He is recorded as having been born as a son of Nahor and as having fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran at the age of seventy (Genesis 11:24-27). He was the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor (Joshua 24:2).
lifetime: Nahor fathered Terah at the age of twenty-nine (Genesis 11:24), and Terah fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran at the age of seventy (Genesis 11:26). His son Haran died before his father Terah in his native land, Ur of the Chaldeans (Genesis 11:28). Terah lived 205 years and died in Haran (Genesis 11:32).
event: Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot the son of Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai, Abram's wife, and left Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan, but when he reached Haran he settled there (Genesis 11:31). Later Joshua said that Terah, the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor, had lived beyond the River and served other gods (Joshua 24:2).

introduce: A person recorded as a son of Issachar, the son of Jacob (Genesis 46:13, 1 Chronicles 7:1).
lifetime: Tola, Puvah, Job, and Shimron, the sons of Issachar, are recorded among the family of Israel who went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:8, 13). Among the clans of the descendants of Issachar there was the Tolaite clan that came from Tola (Numbers 26:23).
event: The sons of Tola were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel; all of them were heads of their father Tola's house and mighty men of valor throughout the generations, and it is recorded that by the time of David their number was 22,600 (1 Chronicles 7:2).

call: A Philistine woman of Timnah (Samson's wife)
introduce: She was the daughter of a Philistine whom Samson saw in Timnah and asked to take as his wife (Judges 14:1-2). Her name is not recorded in the text.
lifetime: Samson went down to Timnah, saw one of the daughters of the Philistines, and asked his parents to get her for him as his wife (Judges 14:1-3); Samson spoke with the woman and was pleased with her (Judges 14:7). During the seven-day feast that Samson held, the Philistines told Samson's wife that unless she enticed her husband and found out the riddle, they would burn her and her father's house with fire (Judges 14:15), and when his wife wept before Samson and pressed him, Samson explained the riddle on the seventh day, and his wife told it to her own people (Judges 14:16-17). After Samson went up to his father's house, Samson's wife was given to his companion who had been his friend (Judges 14:19-20).
event: Some time later Samson visited his wife with a young goat, but her father would not let him in, thinking that Samson hated her intensely, and said that he had given her to Samson's companion (Judges 15:1-2). The Philistines went up and burned the woman and her father with fire (Judges 15:6).

call: Lot’s wife (the woman who looked back and became a pillar of salt)
introduce: Lot’s wife is a woman recorded as having come out of the city together with Lot, led by the angels, from Sodom, but having become a pillar of salt because she looked back (Genesis 19:16, 26). Her name is not recorded in the Bible.
lifetime: The angels urged Lot to bring his wife and two daughters, and when Lot hesitated, the men took hold of the hand of Lot, the hand of his wife, and the hands of his two daughters, led them out, and set them outside the city (Genesis 19:15-16). Lot’s wife became a pillar of salt because she looked back (Genesis 19:26). The Bible records nothing else of her life.
event: When the LORD rained sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah, Lot’s wife became a pillar of salt because she looked back (Genesis 19:24-26). Jesus said, “Remember Lot’s wife!” (Luke 17:32).

introduce: Lot’s younger daughter is a person recorded as having lived with her father Lot in a cave in the mountains after the destruction of Sodom and having borne a son whom she named Ben-ammi (Genesis 19:30-38). Her name is not recorded in the Bible.
lifetime: At the destruction of Sodom the men took the two daughters by the hand, led them out, and set them outside the city (Genesis 19:15-16).
