When Lot lived in the cave in the mountains with his two daughters (Genesis 19:30), she listened to her older sister, and the next night she made her father drink wine and rose and lay with her father (Genesis 19:34-35). She conceived and bore a son and named him Ben-ammi (Genesis 19:36, 38).
event: On the night after the older daughter lay with their father, the younger daughter made her father drink wine and lay with him (Genesis 19:34-35). The Ben-ammi whom she bore is recorded as the ancestor of the Ammonites of today (Genesis 19:38).

introduce: Lot’s older daughter is a person recorded as having come out of Zoar after the destruction of Sodom, lived with her father Lot in a cave in the mountains, and borne a son whom she named Moab (Genesis 19:30-37). Her name is not recorded in the Bible.
lifetime: At the destruction of Sodom the men took the two daughters by the hand, led them out, and set them outside the city (Genesis 19:15-16). When Lot was afraid to stay in Zoar and went up into the mountains and lived in a cave with his two daughters (Genesis 19:30), the older daughter told the younger that there was no man in the land to be a husband for them, so they should make their father drink wine and lie with him and preserve offspring through their father (Genesis 19:31-32). That night the older daughter made her father drink wine and went in and lay with him (Genesis 19:33), and she conceived and bore a son and named him Moab (Genesis 19:36-37).
event: After the destruction of Sodom, in the cave, she proposed to her younger sister that they preserve offspring through their father, and she was the first to lie with their father (Genesis 19:31-33). The Moab whom she bore is recorded as the ancestor of the Moabites of today (Genesis 19:37).

call: Father of Hadadezer king of Zobah
introduce: Rehob is a person recorded as the father of Hadadezer king of Zobah (2 Samuel 8:3, 12).
lifetime: 2 Samuel 8:3 records that David struck Hadadezer king of Zobah, the son of Rehub, when he was going to the Euphrates River to restore his power, and 2 Samuel 8:12 records "Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah" (2 Samuel 8:3, 12). Rehob's own life is not recorded in the Bible.
event: Rehob's own deeds are not recorded. David struck his son Hadadezer when he was going to the Euphrates River to restore his power (2 Samuel 8:3).

call: A man of Beeroth (father of Rechab and Baanah)
introduce: Rimmon is a Beerothite belonging to the tribe of Benjamin, recorded as the father of Baanah and Rechab, the commanders of Saul's son Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 4:2, 5, 9).
lifetime: 2 Samuel 4:2 records that Ish-bosheth had two commanders, Baanah and Rechab, and that they were sons of Rimmon the Beerothite of the tribe of Benjamin. Rimmon's own life is not recorded in the Bible.
event: Rimmon's own deeds are not recorded. His sons Rechab and Baanah killed Ish-bosheth and brought his head to David at Hebron, but were put to death by David (2 Samuel 4:5-12).

call: Child of Hammolecheth (born to the sister of Gilead)
introduce: Mahlah is a person recorded as a child borne by Hammolecheth, the sister of Gilead (1 Chronicles 7:18).
lifetime: In the genealogy of the descendants of Manasseh, she is recorded as one of the children whom Gilead's sister Hammolecheth bore, together with Ishhod and Abiezer (1 Chronicles 7:18).

introduce: Parosh is a person recorded as the father of Pedaiah, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:25). In the text, a family called "the descendants of Parosh" appears in the list of those who returned from exile and elsewhere (Ezra 2:3), and Parosh is also recorded among the names of the leaders of the people (Nehemiah 10:14).
lifetime: Parosh is recorded as the father of Pedaiah (Nehemiah 3:25). The Bible has no separate record of Parosh's own life.
event: Nothing is recorded as having been done by Parosh himself. His son Pedaiah repaired the section after the one repaired by Palal the son of Uzai (Nehemiah 3:25).

call: Wife of Solomon (daughter of Pharaoh king of Egypt)
introduce: Pharaoh’s daughter is the wife whom Solomon took after becoming allied by marriage with Pharaoh king of Egypt (1 Kings 3:1). Solomon built a house for her (1 Kings 7:8), and besides Pharaoh’s daughter he is recorded as having loved many foreign women (1 Kings 11:1).
lifetime: Solomon became allied by marriage with Pharaoh king of Egypt, took his daughter, brought her to the City of David, and waited until he had finished building his own palace, the house of the LORD, and the wall around Jerusalem (1 Kings 3:1). Pharaoh’s daughter went up from the City of David to the palace that Solomon had built for her (1 Kings 9:24). At that time Solomon said, “My wife must not live in the house of David king of Israel, because the places the ark of the LORD has entered are holy” (2 Chronicles 8:11).
event: Nothing is recorded as having been said or done by Pharaoh’s daughter herself. Her father Pharaoh king of Egypt came up, captured Gezer, burned it with fire, and gave that city as a present to his daughter, Solomon’s wife (1 Kings 9:16).

call: Father of Jehoshaphat (father of the officer over Issachar)
introduce: Paruah is a person recorded as the father of Jehoshaphat, who was in charge of Issachar among the twelve officers whom Solomon set over all Israel (1 Kings 4:7, 4:17).
lifetime: He appears only as "Jehoshaphat son of Paruah" in 1 Kings 4:17, and Paruah's own deeds are not recorded.

introduce: Baruch is a person recorded as the father of Maaseiah, who lived in Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, and as a son of Col-hozeh (Nehemiah 11:5). He is a different person, with a different father, from Baruch the son of Neriah, who was the scribe of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 36:4).
lifetime: Maaseiah is recorded as "the son of Baruch, the grandson of Col-hozeh, and the great-grandson of Hazaiah," so Baruch is introduced as the son of Col-hozeh and the father of Maaseiah (Nehemiah 11:5). The Bible has no separate record of Baruch's own life.
event: Nothing is recorded as having been done by Baruch himself. His son Maaseiah is on the list of leaders who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:3, 5).

introduce: Parnach is the father of Eli-zaphan, who is recorded as a leader of the tribe of the descendants of Zebulun at the time of the dividing of the land of Canaan (Numbers 34:25).
lifetime: Parnach is recorded as the father of Eli-zaphan, a leader of the tribe of the descendants of Zebulun (Numbers 34:25). The Bible has no record of Parnach's own life.

call: One of the ten sons of Haman
introduce: Parmashta is a person whose name is recorded as one of the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite (Esther 3:1, 9:9, 9:10).
lifetime: When on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men in Susa, the ten sons of Haman were killed as well, and Parmashta is listed seventh among the names of those ten sons (Esther 9:5-10). Afterward the king granted Esther's request, and the bodies of Haman's ten sons were hanged on the gallows (Esther 9:13-14).
event: Nothing is recorded as having been done by Parmashta himself. His name is on the list as one of the ten sons of Haman who were killed in the capital, Susa (Esther 9:9, 9:10, 9:12).

call: One of the ten sons of Haman
introduce: Parshandatha is a person whose name is recorded as one of the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite (Esther 3:1, 9:7, 9:10).
lifetime: When on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men in Susa, the ten sons of Haman were killed as well, and Parshandatha is recorded first among the names of those ten sons (Esther 9:5-10). Afterward the king granted Esther's request, and the bodies of Haman's ten sons were hanged on the gallows (Esther 9:13-14).
event: Nothing is recorded as having been done by Parshandatha himself. His name is on the list as one of the ten sons of Haman who were killed in the capital, Susa (Esther 9:7, 9:10, 9:12).

introduce: Baanah, a son of Rimmon the Beerothite of the tribe of Benjamin, was one of the two commanders whom Saul's son Ish-bosheth had (2 Samuel 4:2).
lifetime: He was a brother of Rechab and a son of Rimmon the Beerothite (2 Samuel 4:2, 4:6). Together with Rechab he killed Ish-bosheth and brought his head to David at Hebron, but was put to death by David's order (2 Samuel 4:5-12).
event: Rechab and Baanah came to the house of Ish-bosheth about the heat of the day, went into the middle of the house as if to get wheat, and stabbed Ish-bosheth in the belly as he lay taking his midday rest, and escaped (2 Samuel 4:5-6). They struck Ish-bosheth down in his bedchamber and cut off his head, and traveling all night by the way of the Arabah, they reached Hebron and presented it to King David (2 Samuel 4:7-8). But David had them killed, and cut off their hands and feet and hanged them by the pool at Hebron (2 Samuel 4:9-12).

call: Father of Zadok (father of one who repaired the wall)
introduce: Baana is a person who appears as the father of Zadok in the account of the repair of the wall of Jerusalem in Nehemiah 3 (Nehemiah 3:4).
lifetime: Nothing is recorded about Baana himself, and he appears in Nehemiah 3:4 only as the father of Zadok (Nehemiah 3:4).
event: His son Zadok repaired the section next to Meshullam (Nehemiah 3:4).

introduce: Baara is a person recorded as the wife of Shaharaim. Shaharaim fathered children in the country of Moab after sending away his two wives, Hushim and Baara (1 Chronicles 8:8).
lifetime: The record about her is only the one verse, 1 Chronicles 8:8, which says that Shaharaim sent her away together with Hushim (1 Chronicles 8:8).
event: It is recorded that Shaharaim sent away his two wives, Hushim and Baara (1 Chronicles 8:8).

introduce: Baaseiah is a person recorded as the son of Malchijah and the father of Michael. His name appears in the genealogy that traces the line of Asaph upward (1 Chronicles 6:39-40).
lifetime: It is recorded that Asaph was the son of Berechiah, Berechiah was the son of Shimea, Shimea was the son of Michael, Michael was the son of Baaseiah, and Baaseiah was the son of Malchijah (1 Chronicles 6:39-40). There is no other record about him.

call: Son of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon (tribe of Benjamin)
introduce: Baal is a person recorded as one of the sons of Jeiel, the ancestor of Gibeon. The firstborn of Jeiel was Abdon, and then the names are given in the order Zur, Kish, and Baal (1 Chronicles 8:29-30, 9:35-36).
lifetime: Jeiel lived in Gibeon, his wife's name was Maacah, and his sons are recorded as the firstborn Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, and Zecher (1 Chronicles 8:29-31). In 1 Chronicles 9:36-37, Ner, Zechariah, and Mikloth are also listed. There is no other record about him.

introduce: Baal is a person recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Reuben as the son of Reaiah and the father of Beerah (1 Chronicles 5:5-6).
lifetime: He appears as the son of Reaiah in the genealogy that continues through Shemaiah son of Joel, Gog, Shimei, Micah, and Reaiah, and his son is Beerah (1 Chronicles 5:4-6). There is no other record about him.

call: Son of Henadad (repairer of the wall)
introduce: Binnui, a son of Henadad, was a ruler of half the district of Keilah and repaired a section of the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:18).
lifetime: In Nehemiah 3:18 he appears as the ruler of half the district of Keilah, a son of Henadad (Nehemiah 3:18). There is no record of any other family line or life of his.
event: When the wall of Jerusalem was being repaired, Binnui repaired the next section (Nehemiah 3:18).

직업/직위: ruler of half the district of Keilah

call: A Levite who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile (list of 1 Chronicles 9:15)
introduce: Bakbakkar is a person whose name is listed in 1 Chronicles 9 among the Levites together with Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah (1 Chronicles 9:14-15).
lifetime: In the list of those who returned from Babylon and lived in their own cities and possessions, Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah are named together among the Levites (1 Chronicles 9:2, 9:14-15). There is no other record about him.

call: Son of Uzai (repairer of the wall)
introduce: Palal is a son of Uzai who repaired a section of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 3:25).
lifetime: He is introduced only as the son of Uzai in Nehemiah 3:25, and there is no record of any other family line or life of his (Nehemiah 3:25).
event: He repaired the section opposite the angle of the wall and the tower that juts out from the upper palace of the king, that is, the part near the courtyard of the guard (Nehemiah 3:25).

call: Son of Reuben (ancestor of the Palluite family, father of Eliab)
introduce: One of the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, he is the ancestor of the Palluite family that came from Pallu and the father of Eliab (Genesis 46:9, Numbers 26:5, Numbers 26:8).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi, the sons of Reuben, Jacob's firstborn (Genesis 46:8-9, Exodus 6:14, 1 Chronicles 5:3). The son of Pallu is Eliab (Numbers 26:8), and the sons of Eliab are Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram (Numbers 26:9). Pallu's own deeds are not recorded.

call: The woman who came to Caesarea with King Agrippa and paid her respects to Festus
introduce: A person recorded together with King Agrippa in Acts 25–26, who came to Caesarea with Agrippa and paid her respects to the governor Festus (Acts 25:13).
lifetime: She came to Caesarea with King Agrippa to pay respects to Festus (Acts 25:13), and the next day, having displayed great pomp together with Agrippa, she entered the auditorium with the commanders and the leading men of the city (Acts 25:23). After Paul's defense was finished, she rose together with the king and the governor (Acts 26:30).
event: The text does not record any personal words or actions of hers separately; it records only her entering the auditorium with Agrippa (Acts 25:23) and her rising together with the king and the governor (Acts 26:30).

call: Father of Zeror (great-grandfather of Kish, father of King Saul)
introduce: A person recorded as the great-grandfather of Kish, a Benjamite, a son of Aphiah and the father of Zeror (1 Samuel 9:1).
lifetime: 1 Samuel 9:1 records Kish as "son of Abiel, grandson of Zeror, great-grandson of Becorath, and great-great-grandson of Aphiah." According to this, Becorath is the father of Zeror and the son of Aphiah (1 Samuel 9:1).
event: His deeds are not recorded in the Bible; only his name appears in the genealogy of Kish (1 Samuel 9:1).

call: Son of Meshezabel, father of Meshullam, the repairer of the wall
introduce: A person recorded as a son of Meshezabel and the father of Meshullam, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 3:4).
lifetime: Nehemiah 3:4 records Meshullam as "son of Berechiah, grandson of Meshezabel," showing that Berechiah was the son of Meshezabel and the father of Meshullam. His son Meshullam repaired a section of the wall (Nehemiah 3:4) and also repaired the section opposite his own chamber (Nehemiah 3:30).
event: Berechiah's own deeds are not recorded. The daughter of his son Meshullam was taken as a wife by Jehohanan the son of Tobiah (Nehemiah 6:18).

call: Father of the prophet Zechariah (son of Iddo)
introduce: A person recorded as the father of the prophet Zechariah; the book of Zechariah introduces Zechariah as "son of Berechiah, grandson of Iddo" (Zechariah 1:1).
lifetime: In the eighth month and the eleventh month of the second year of King Darius, the word of the LORD came to "the prophet Zechariah, son of Berechiah, grandson of Iddo" (Zechariah 1:1, 1:7). According to this introduction, Berechiah is the father of Zechariah and a son of Iddo.
event: Berechiah's own deeds are not recorded, and he appears only as the father of Zechariah (Zechariah 1:1, 1:7).

introduce: A person recorded in Ezra 8:11 as the father of Zechariah, "son of Bebai," and his name also appears as the name of a family, "the descendants of Bebai" (Ezra 8:11, 10:28).
lifetime: Among the heads of families who came up from Babylon with Ezra, "from the descendants of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai" is recorded (Ezra 8:1, 8:11). In Ezra 10:28, Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai are recorded among the descendants of Bebai.
event: Bebai's own deeds are not recorded. His son Zechariah is recorded as being accompanied by twenty-eight men (Ezra 8:11).

call: Son borne by Lot’s younger daughter (ancestor of the Ammonites)
introduce: The son borne by Lot’s younger daughter, he is the ancestor of the Ammonites (Genesis 19:38).
lifetime: When Lot came out of Zoar and lived in a cave in the mountains with his two daughters (Genesis 19:30), Lot’s younger daughter conceived by her father and bore a son (Genesis 19:35-36, 19:38), and that daughter named him Ben-ammi (Genesis 19:38).
event: The text records that he is the ancestor of the Ammonites of today (Genesis 19:38).

introduce: Ben-hanan is a person recorded as a son of Shimon in the genealogy of the descendants of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:20).
lifetime: He is recorded as one of the sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon (1 Chronicles 4:20).

introduce: Ben-hail is a person recorded as one of the officials of Jehoshaphat king of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:7).
lifetime: In the third year of Jehoshaphat's reign, he sent the officials Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah to the cities of Judah to teach (2 Chronicles 17:7).
event: He is one of the officials whom Jehoshaphat sent to the cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:7). Along with them Levites and priests were sent, and they went about all the cities of Judah with the book of the law of the LORD and taught the people (2 Chronicles 17:8-9).

call: Solomon's officer over the hill country of Ephraim
introduce: Ben-hur is a person recorded as the one in charge of the hill country of Ephraim among the twelve officers whom Solomon set over all Israel (1 Kings 4:7-8).
lifetime: Solomon set twelve officers over all Israel, and each of them provided food for the king and the royal household one month in the year (1 Kings 4:7). Among those names, Ben-hur is recorded as the officer of the hill country of Ephraim (1 Kings 4:8).

직업/직위: Solomon's district governor (hill country of Ephraim)

introduce: Bela is a person recorded as the firstborn of Benjamin, a son of Jacob (1 Chronicles 8:1). He appears first in every genealogy that records the sons of Benjamin (Genesis 46:21; 1 Chronicles 7:6), and the Belaite family came from him (Numbers 26:38).
lifetime: Five sons of Bela are recorded: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri, all of whom were heads of their families and great warriors (1 Chronicles 7:7). 1 Chronicles 8:3-5 records as the sons of Bela Addar, Gera, Abihud, Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah, Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram, and Numbers 26:40 records the sons of Bela as Ard and Naaman.

introduce: Bela is a son of Beor, recorded as a king who ruled the land of Edom before there was a king ruling the children of Israel (Genesis 36:31-32; 1 Chronicles 1:43).
lifetime: He became king of Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhabah (Genesis 36:32). When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his place (Genesis 36:33; 1 Chronicles 1:44).

introduce: Bela is a person recorded as the son of Azaz in the genealogy of the descendants of Reuben in 1 Chronicles 5; he was a grandson of Shema and a great-grandson of Joel (1 Chronicles 5:8).
lifetime: Bela settled in Aroer, and his dwelling reached as far as Nebo and Baal-meon, and he also went east, and his dwelling reached from the Euphrates River to the edge of the desert, because his livestock had increased in the land of Gilead (1 Chronicles 5:8-9).

introduce: Pelet is a person recorded as a son of Jahdai (1 Chronicles 2:47).
lifetime: In the genealogy of the descendants of Judah in 1 Chronicles 2, he is recorded as one of the sons of Jahdai: Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph (1 Chronicles 2:47).

call: Son of Azel (descendant of Jonathan son of Saul)
introduce: Bocheru is a person recorded as one of the six sons of Azel in the genealogy of the descendants of Saul's son Jonathan (1 Chronicles 8:33-38).
lifetime: Azel, the son of Eleasah, had six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan (1 Chronicles 8:37-38; 9:43-44).

call: Priest of On in Egypt (father of Asenath)
meaning: The one given by the sun god (Ra)
introduce: Potiphera was a priest of On in Egypt and the father of Asenath, who became the wife of Joseph (Genesis 41:45).
lifetime: Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, was given by Pharaoh to become the wife of Joseph (Genesis 41:45), and before the years of famine came she bore Joseph two sons, who are Manasseh and Ephraim (Genesis 41:50; 46:20).
event: The Bible has no record of Potiphera's own deeds; his name appears in the record that his daughter Asenath became Joseph's wife (Genesis 41:45).

call: Fourth of the ten sons of Haman (order of the list)
introduce: Poratha is one of the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and he is recorded fourth in the list of Esther 9:7-9 (Esther 9:8).
lifetime: It is recorded that the Jews killed five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman in the capital, Susa (Esther 9:6-10), and Poratha's name appears in the list of those ten sons (Esther 9:8).
event: He is one of the ten sons of Haman who were killed by the Jews (Esther 9:6-10), and the bodies of Haman's ten sons were hanged on the gallows (Esther 9:13-14).

call: The person who sent greetings to Timothy in 2 Timothy 4:21
introduce: A person recorded in 2 Timothy 4:21 as sending greetings to Timothy together with Eubulus, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers (2 Timothy 4:21).
One of the daughters of Putiel, she was the woman who became the wife of Aaron's son Eleazar and bore Phinehas (Exodus 6:25).
lifetime: Aaron's son Eleazar took a wife from among the daughters of Putiel, and she bore Phinehas (Exodus 6:25). Her name is not recorded in the text.

introduce: Pyrrhus is a person recorded as the father of Sopater, one of the party traveling with Paul as far as Asia (Acts 20:4).
lifetime: The Bible has no record about Pyrrhus himself; his name appears in the introduction "Sopater son of Pyrrhus" in Acts 20:4.

call: Ancestor of Abihail of the descendants of Gad (father of Jahdo)
introduce: Buz is a person who appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Gad as an ancestor of Abihail, Abihail's seventh-generation ancestor and the father of Jahdo (1 Chronicles 5:11-14).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 5:14 records Abihail as the son of Huri, grandson of Jaroah, great-grandson of Gilead, great-great-grandson of Michael, fifth-generation descendant of Jeshishai, sixth-generation descendant of Jahdo, and seventh-generation descendant of Buz (1 Chronicles 5:14). In this genealogy the generation after Buz is Jahdo.
event: The Bible has no record of Buz's personal deeds; his name appears only in the genealogy of Abihail's ancestors (1 Chronicles 5:14).

call: Second son of Nahor and Milcah
introduce: Buz is a person recorded as one of the eight sons whom Abraham's brother Nahor had by his wife Milcah; he was a younger brother of the firstborn, Uz (Genesis 22:20-23).
lifetime: When Abraham heard that Milcah had borne children to his brother Nahor (Genesis 22:20), it is recorded that her firstborn was Uz and Uz's brother was Buz (Genesis 22:21). The eight sons borne by Nahor's wife Milcah are Uz, Buz, Kemuel, Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel (Genesis 22:21-23).

call: Son of Abishua (descendant of Aaron, line of Eleazar)
introduce: Bukki is a person who appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Aaron's son Eleazar, recorded as the son of Abishua and the father of Uzzi (1 Chronicles 6:4-5, 6:50-51).
lifetime: It is recorded that Abishua fathered Bukki, and Bukki fathered Uzzi (1 Chronicles 6:5). In the genealogy that lists the descendants of Aaron in the order of the sons as well, Bukki comes after Abishua, and Uzzi after him (1 Chronicles 6:50-51). Bukki's name also appears in the genealogy that traces Ezra's ancestors upward (Ezra 7:1-5).
event: The Bible has no record of Bukki's personal deeds; his name appears only in genealogies (1 Chronicles 6:5; Ezra 7:4).

call: Son of Jogli (leader of the tribe of Dan)
introduce: Bukki is a leader of the tribe of Dan, a son of Jogli (Numbers 34:22).
lifetime: When the LORD told Moses who were to divide the land of Canaan as an inheritance and told him to choose one leader from each tribe (Numbers 34:16-18), from the tribe of the descendants of Dan the name Bukki son of Jogli was on the list (Numbers 34:22).
event: He is recorded as the one representing the tribe of Dan among those whom the LORD appointed to distribute the inheritance to the Israelites in the land of Canaan (Numbers 34:22, 29).

직업/직위: clan chief of the tribe of Dan

call: A Pirathonite (one of David's mighty men)
introduce: Benaiah is a Pirathonite recorded in the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:30; 1 Chronicles 11:31). He is a different person from Benaiah son of Jehoiada.
lifetime: Benaiah the Pirathonite is on the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:30; 1 Chronicles 11:31). 1 Chronicles 27:14 records Benaiah the Pirathonite, belonging to the descendants of Ephraim, as the eleventh commander, for the eleventh month (1 Chronicles 27:14).
event: Apart from his name being on the list of David's mighty men, no personal deeds are recorded (2 Samuel 23:30). Benaiah the Pirathonite, belonging to the descendants of Ephraim, was the eleventh commander for the eleventh month, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand men (1 Chronicles 27:14).

introduce: Beor is a person recorded as the father of Balaam (Numbers 22:5).
lifetime: The Bible records no deeds or life of Beor himself, and his son Balaam is called "the son of Beor" (Numbers 22:5; Numbers 24:3; Numbers 31:8; Deuteronomy 23:4; Joshua 13:22; Joshua 24:9; Micah 6:5; 2 Peter 2:15).

call: A head of the inhabitants of Aijalon together with Beriah (descendant of Benjamin)
introduce: Shema is a descendant of Benjamin recorded, together with Beriah, as a head of the inhabitants of Aijalon (1 Chronicles 8:13).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 8 is the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:1), and 8:13 records that Beriah and Shema became heads of the inhabitants of Aijalon (1 Chronicles 8:13). The text does not state who Shema's father was.
event: Beriah and Shema became heads of the inhabitants of Aijalon and drove out the inhabitants of Gath (1 Chronicles 8:13).

직업/직위: head of the inhabitants of Aijalon

기타관계: Beriah#3599(fellow head of the inhabitants of Aijalon)

call: Son of Joel, father of Azaz (descendant of Reuben)
introduce: Shema is a person recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Reuben, a son of Joel and the father of Azaz (1 Chronicles 5:8).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 5:8 records "Bela was the son of Azaz, grandson of Shema, and great-grandson of Joel," showing that Shema was the son of Joel, the father of Azaz, and the grandfather of Bela (1 Chronicles 5:8).
event: Apart from the fact that he is recorded as Bela's grandfather, no specific event done by Shema is recorded. His settling in Aroer and reaching as far as Nebo and Baal-meon is in the record about his great-grandson Bela (1 Chronicles 5:8).

introduce: Shema is a son of Hebron belonging to the household of Caleb of the tribe of Judah, and the father of Raham (1 Chronicles 2:43-44).
lifetime: The sons of Hebron are recorded as Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema (1 Chronicles 2:43). Shema fathered Raham, and Raham was the father of Jorkeam (1 Chronicles 2:44).
event: Apart from the fact that he fathered Raham, no specific event done by Shema is recorded (1 Chronicles 2:44).

call: One of the two kings of Midian (together with Zalmunna)
introduce: Zebah is one of the two kings of Midian, a person who was pursued by Gideon and captured together with Zalmunna (Judges 8:5, 8:12).
lifetime: Zebah and Zalmunna were at Karkor (Judges 8:10). When the two kings fled, Gideon pursued them, captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and struck their whole army (Judges 8:12). Gideon rose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna (Judges 8:21).
event: Gideon asked the men of Succoth for bread and said that he was pursuing the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna (Judges 8:5). When Gideon asked Zebah and Zalmunna what kind of men those were whom they had killed at Tabor, they answered, "They were like you, all of them like princes" (Judges 8:18), and they said, "Rise yourself and strike us down, for as the man is, so is his strength" (Judges 8:21). Gideon rose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and took the crescent-shaped ornaments that had adorned the necks of their camels (Judges 8:21).

introduce: The daughter of Sheshan is the woman whom Sheshan, who had no sons, gave in marriage to the Egyptian servant Jarha, and she is the mother who bore Attai (1 Chronicles 2:34-35). Her name is not recorded in the text of the KRV.
lifetime: Sheshan had no sons but only daughters, and Sheshan gave his daughter to the Egyptian servant Jarha to be his wife (1 Chronicles 2:34-35). Through her Jarha fathered Attai (1 Chronicles 2:35).

introduce: Shelemiah is a person recorded as the son of Cushi, the father of Nethaniah, and the grandfather of Jehudi, whom the officials sent to Baruch (Jeremiah 36:14).
lifetime: Jeremiah 36:14 records "Jehudi, great-grandson of Cushi, grandson of Shelemiah, and son of Nethaniah," from which we can tell that Shelemiah was the son of Cushi, the father of Nethaniah, and the grandfather of Jehudi (Jeremiah 36:14).
event: Shelemiah's own deeds are not recorded. His grandson Jehudi, sent by all the officials, went to Baruch and told him to bring the scroll he had read in the hearing of the people (Jeremiah 36:14).

call: Son of Abdeel (the one ordered by the king to seize Baruch and Jeremiah)
introduce: Shelemiah is a son of Abdeel and one of the three men whom the king commanded to seize the scribe Baruch and the prophet Jeremiah (Jeremiah 36:26).
lifetime: The king commanded Jerahmeel, a son of the king, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to seize the scribe Baruch and the prophet Jeremiah, but the LORD hid them (Jeremiah 36:26).
event: Though he was ordered by the king to seize Baruch and Jeremiah, the LORD hid Baruch and Jeremiah (Jeremiah 36:26).

introduce: Shelemiah is a person recorded as the father of Jehucal, that is, Jucal, whom King Zedekiah sent to the prophet Jeremiah (Jeremiah 37:3, 38:1).
lifetime: King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah the priest, the son of Maaseiah, to the prophet Jeremiah (Jeremiah 37:3). Shelemiah's son Jucal is recorded among those who heard the words that Jeremiah spoke to all the people (Jeremiah 38:1).
event: Shelemiah's own deeds are not recorded.

call: Father of Hananiah (repairer of the wall)
introduce: Shelemiah is a person recorded as the father of Hananiah, who repaired a section in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 3:30).
lifetime: It is recorded that Shelemiah's son Hananiah repaired a section together with Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph (Nehemiah 3:30).
event: Shelemiah's own deeds are not recorded. His son Hananiah repaired a section together with Hanun (Nehemiah 3:30).

call: Son of Hananiah (father of Irijah, captain of the guard)
introduce: Shelemiah is a person recorded as the son of Hananiah and the father of Irijah, the captain of the guard (Jeremiah 37:13).
lifetime: By the expression "Irijah, grandson of Hananiah and son of Shelemiah," Shelemiah is recorded as the son of Hananiah and the father of Irijah (Jeremiah 37:13).
event: Shelemiah's own deeds are not recorded. His son Irijah seized the prophet Jeremiah at the Gate of Benjamin and said that he was deserting to the Chaldeans (Jeremiah 37:13).

call: Son of David (born in Jerusalem, a son of Bathsheba)
introduce: Shobab is a person recorded as one of the sons whom David fathered in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:14).
lifetime: The names of the sons David fathered in Jerusalem are recorded in the order Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon (2 Samuel 5:14; 1 Chronicles 14:4). 1 Chronicles 3:5 records that the four, Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon, were all born to Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel (1 Chronicles 3:5).

call: Son of Caleb son of Hezron (tribe of Judah)
introduce: Shobab is a person recorded as a son of Caleb, the son of Hezron of the tribe of Judah, together with Jesher and Ardon (1 Chronicles 2:18).
lifetime: The sons whom Caleb son of Hezron had by his wife Azubah and by Jerioth are recorded as Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon (1 Chronicles 2:18).

call: Son of Pashhur (father of Amzi, ancestor of Adaiah)
introduce: Zechariah is a person recorded in the genealogy of Nehemiah 11:12 as the son of Pashhur and the father of Amzi (Nehemiah 11:12).
lifetime: Nehemiah 11:12 records Adaiah as the son of Jeroham, grandson of Pelaliah, great-grandson of Amzi, great-great-grandson of Zechariah, a descendant of Pashhur in the fifth generation, and a descendant of Malchijah in the sixth generation. In this genealogy Zechariah is the son of Pashhur and the father of Amzi (Nehemiah 11:12).

call: Father of Jahaziel (son of Benaiah, of the descendants of Asaph)
introduce: Zechariah is a person recorded as the father of Jahaziel the Levite, of the descendants of Asaph, and as the son of Benaiah (2 Chronicles 20:14).
lifetime: 2 Chronicles 20:14 records that Jahaziel the Levite was the great-great-grandson of Mattaniah of the descendants of Asaph, the great-grandson of Jeiel, the grandson of Benaiah, and the son of Zechariah. In this genealogy Zechariah is the son of Benaiah and the father of Jahaziel (2 Chronicles 20:14).

call: An official whom Jehoshaphat sent to the cities of Judah to teach
introduce: Zechariah is one of the officials whom King Jehoshaphat of Judah, in the third year of his reign, sent to the various cities of Judah to teach (2 Chronicles 17:7).
lifetime: In the third year of his reign, Jehoshaphat sent his officials Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah to teach in the various cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:7).
event: Zechariah, together with the Levites sent along with the officials and the priests Elishama and Jehoram, took the book of the Law of the LORD and taught in Judah, going around through all the cities and teaching the people (2 Chronicles 17:7-9).

call: Supervisor of the temple repairs in the time of Josiah (a Levite of the Kohathites)
introduce: Zechariah is a Levite of the descendants of Kohath who supervised the work of repairing the house of the LORD in the time of King Josiah (2 Chronicles 34:12).
lifetime: In the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign, when the house of the LORD was being repaired (2 Chronicles 34:8), the overseers are recorded as the Levites Jahath and Obadiah of the descendants of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam of the descendants of Kohath (2 Chronicles 34:12).
event: Zechariah is recorded, together with Jahath, Obadiah, and Meshullam, as an overseer in charge of the work of repairing the temple (2 Chronicles 34:12).

call: Father of Uzziah (son of Amariah, a descendant of Perez)
introduce: He is a forefather of Athaiah, of the descendants of Perez among the descendants of Judah, and is recorded as the father of Uzziah and the son of Amariah (Nehemiah 11:4).
lifetime: In the genealogy of Nehemiah 11:4, Athaiah is recorded as the son of Uzziah, the grandson of Zechariah, and the great-grandson of Amariah. Therefore Zechariah is the son of Amariah and the father of Uzziah. His own deeds are not recorded.

call: Father of Iddo (father of Iddo, the chief officer of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead)
introduce: Zechariah is a person recorded as the father of Iddo, the chief officer of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead (1 Chronicles 27:21).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 27:21 records that the chief officer of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead was Iddo son of Zechariah. There is no other record about Zechariah himself (1 Chronicles 27:21).

introduce: Sheba is a person recorded as the son of Raamah, the son of Cush, the son of Ham (Genesis 10:6-7; 1 Chronicles 1:9).
lifetime: The sons of Cush are recorded as Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca, and the sons of Raamah as Sheba and Dedan (Genesis 10:7; 1 Chronicles 1:9).

call: The queen of Sheba who came to Solomon and tested him
introduce: The queen of Sheba is the queen who, having heard of Solomon's fame concerning the name of the LORD, came to Jerusalem to test him with hard questions (1 Kings 10:1-2).
lifetime: The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame and came to Jerusalem to test him with hard questions (1 Kings 10:1-2); when Solomon gave her all that she desired, whatever she asked, she returned to her own land with her servants (1 Kings 10:13).
event: When the queen of Sheba came and told him all that was on her mind, Solomon answered all her questions (1 Kings 10:2-3). Seeing Solomon's wisdom and the palace he had built, she was left breathless; she declared that the report she had heard in her own land was true and said to bless the LORD, Solomon's God (1 Kings 10:4-9). She also gave the king 120 talents of gold and a very great quantity of spices and precious stones (1 Kings 10:10). The same event is also recorded in 2 Chronicles (2 Chronicles 9:1-12). In the New Testament, Jesus said that the queen of the South, who came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, will condemn the people of this generation at the judgment (Matthew 12:42; Luke 11:31).

call: Son of Tahath (a Levite of the Kohathites, ancestor of Heman)
introduce: Zephaniah is a Levite recorded as the son of Tahath and the father of Azariah, and he appears in the genealogy of Heman of the descendants of Kohath (1 Chronicles 6:36-37).
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Tahath and the father of Azariah (1 Chronicles 6:36-37).

call: Father of Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon (a descendant of Judah)
introduce: Shimon is a person recorded as the father of Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon (1 Chronicles 4:20).
lifetime: He is recorded as having Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon as his sons (1 Chronicles 4:20).

call: Servant of Saul, later the servant of Mephibosheth
introduce: Ziba was a servant of the house of Saul who, when David sought those remaining of the house of Saul, was summoned and told where Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, was. He had fifteen sons and twenty servants (2 Samuel 9:2-4, 9:10).
lifetime: While a servant of Saul, he was summoned before David and reported that Mephibosheth was in the house of Machir son of Ammiel at Lo-debar (2 Samuel 9:2-4). David said that he had given Mephibosheth everything that belonged to Saul and all his house, and commanded Ziba, his sons, and his servants to till the land for him, bring in the produce, and provide for him; Ziba answered that he would do as commanded (2 Samuel 9:9-11). Those living in Ziba's house became servants of Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9:12).
event: When David was fleeing, Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth, met David with a pair of saddled donkeys loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine (2 Samuel 16:1). When David asked where his master's son was, Ziba reported that he was staying in Jerusalem, for he had said, "Today the house of Israel will give me back the kingdom of my father" (2 Samuel 16:3), and David said that everything belonging to Mephibosheth was Ziba's (2 Samuel 16:4). Ziba crossed the Jordan with his fifteen sons and twenty servants and came before the king (2 Samuel 19:17). When Mephibosheth said to the king, "My servant deceived me, and he has slandered your servant to my lord the king," the king said, "You and Ziba divide the land" (2 Samuel 19:26-29).

call: Son of Jehallelel (a descendant of Judah)
introduce: Ziphah is a person recorded as a son of Jehallelel, together with Ziph, Tiria, and Asarel (1 Chronicles 4:16).
lifetime: He is recorded as a son of Jehallelel (1 Chronicles 4:16).

call: Son of Arba (father of Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai)
introduce: He is a person recorded as the son of Arba and the father of three sons, Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai (Joshua 15:13, 15:14).
event: Caleb drove his three sons, Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, out of Hebron (Joshua 15:14, Judges 1:20).

introduce: He is a person recorded as the father of Shamgar the judge (Judges 3:31, 5:6).
She is one of Lamech's two wives, and the mother of Jabal (Genesis 4:19, 4:20).
lifetime: Lamech took two wives, and the name of one was Adah (Genesis 4:19). Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, hear my voice" (Genesis 4:23).
event: She bore Jabal, who became the father of those who dwell in tents and keep livestock (Genesis 4:20).

call: Wife of Esau (daughter of Elon the Hittite, mother of Eliphaz)
introduce: She is the daughter of Elon the Hittite, the wife of Esau, and the mother of Eliphaz (Genesis 36:2, 36:4).
lifetime: Esau took Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite, as his wife from among the women of Canaan (Genesis 36:2). The chiefs of Edom descended from Eliphaz are recorded as Adah's descendants (Genesis 36:16).
event: She bore Eliphaz to Esau (Genesis 36:4).

call: Son of Dishan (grandson of Seir, a Horite)
introduce: He is a person recorded as the son of Dishan, who was a son of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36:21, 36:28, 1 Chronicles 1:38, 1:42).
Aiah is a person recorded as the father of Rizpah, Saul's concubine (2 Samuel 3:7).
lifetime: It is recorded that Aiah's daughter Rizpah was Saul's concubine (2 Samuel 3:7). The Bible has no record about Aiah's own life.

introduce: Ahihud is a person recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8) as a son fathered, together with Uzza, by his father (1 Chronicles 8:7). He is a different person from Ahihud son of Shelomi, the leader of the tribe of Asher in Numbers 34:27.
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 8:7 records, "and he fathered Uzza and Ahihud." In this verse "he" appears to refer to Gera, who is named just before. There is no concrete record of his life in the Bible.

call: Son of Omri, father of Uthai (a descendant of Perez of the tribe of Judah)
introduce: Ammihud is a person recorded as the father of Uthai among the descendants of Perez, the son of Judah, and he is a son of Omri (1 Chronicles 9:4).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 9:4 records Uthai as "the son of Ammihud, the grandson of Omri, the great-grandson of Imri, and the great-great-grandson of Bani," so Ammihud is the son of Omri and the grandson of Imri. There is no concrete record of his life in the Bible.

introduce: Jalon is a person recorded as one of the sons of Ezrah in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:17).
lifetime: The sons of Ezrah are recorded as Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon (1 Chronicles 4:17). The Bible has no record of any other part of his life.

call: Eunuch in charge of the treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians
introduce: He was an Ethiopian, a eunuch of great authority who was in charge of all the treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians. He had come to Jerusalem to worship, and on his way home he met Philip, heard the gospel, and was baptized (Acts 8:27-39).
lifetime: Having come to Jerusalem to worship, he was returning in his chariot and reading the writing of the prophet Isaiah (Acts 8:27-28). After he heard from Philip the gospel about Jesus and was baptized at a place where there was water, he went on his way rejoicing, and Philip saw him no more (Acts 8:35-39). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.
event: Saying that he needed someone to guide him in understanding the writing of Isaiah, he invited Philip to sit with him in the chariot, and asked Philip whether the passage he was reading referred to the prophet himself or to someone else (Acts 8:31-34). When Philip began from that passage and taught him about Jesus, proclaiming the gospel, they came to some water, and he asked what prevented him from being baptized; he ordered the chariot to stop, went down into the water with Philip, and was baptized (Acts 8:35-38).

직업/직위: eunuch in charge of the treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians

기타관계: Philip#4634(one who preached the gospel to him and baptized him)

call: Grandson of Jacob, son of Gad
introduce: Eri is a person recorded as one of the seven sons of Gad, a son of Jacob (Genesis 46:16).
lifetime: Eri is listed as a son of Gad in the roll of the family of Israel who went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:8, 46:16). In the later census record on the plains of Moab, among the clans of the descendants of Gad appears "the Erite clan, descended from Eri" (Numbers 26:16).

call: Son of Ezrah, a descendant of Judah
introduce: He is a person recorded as a son of Ezrah, a descendant of Judah. 1 Chronicles 4:17 lists the sons of Ezrah as Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon.
lifetime: His name comes first among the sons of Ezrah, and apart from his entry in the genealogy there is no record of his life (1 Chronicles 4:17).

introduce: He is a person recorded as a son of Joktan. His name appears in Genesis 10:29 and 1 Chronicles 1:23 as one of the thirteen sons of Joktan.
lifetime: He is recorded in the genealogy as a grandson of Eber and a son of Joktan (Genesis 10:25-29), and there is no record of the rest of his life.

introduce: He is a person whose name appears in 1 Chronicles 11:35 as "Eliphal son of Ur," and he is recorded as the father of Eliphal.

call: Brother of Jesus (brother of James, Joseph, and Simon)
introduce: Judas is one of the brothers of Jesus recorded as James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas (Matthew 13:55; Mark 6:3).
lifetime: When Jesus was teaching in His hometown, the people rejected Him, saying that His mother was Mary and that His brothers were James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas (Matthew 13:55-57; Mark 6:3). The Bible does not give a separate account of the life of Judas himself.
event: The Bible does not record any separate deeds of Jesus' brother Judas; his name appears in the passage where the people of His hometown list the members of Jesus' family (Matthew 13:55; Mark 6:3).

call: The Ithrite (one of David's mighty men)
introduce: Ira is a person recorded as "Ira the Ithrite" in the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:38; 1 Chronicles 11:40).
lifetime: He was an Ithrite, and his name is listed among David's mighty men together with Gareb, who was also an Ithrite. This list is recorded as thirty-seven in all, up to Uriah the Hittite (2 Samuel 23:38-39; 1 Chronicles 11:40).
event: The Bible does not record any specific deeds of his; his name only appears in the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:38; 1 Chronicles 11:40).

call: Son of Ikkesh (the Tekoite, one of David's mighty men)
introduce: Ira is the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, a person whose name is listed among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:26; 1 Chronicles 11:28).
lifetime: He is recorded as the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite and as one of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:26; 1 Chronicles 11:28). 1 Chronicles 27:9 records him as the sixth commander, for the sixth month, and says that his division numbered 24,000 men.
event: He is listed among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:26; 1 Chronicles 11:28), and is recorded as having been in charge of a division of 24,000 men as the sixth commander, for the sixth month (1 Chronicles 27:9). The Bible does not record any other specific deeds of his.

call: Son of Uzzi (chief of the tribe of Issachar)
introduce: Izrahiah is a person recorded as a son of Uzzi, of the descendants of Issachar (1 Chronicles 7:3).
lifetime: He is the son of Uzzi, the son of Tola, the son of Issachar (1 Chronicles 7:1-3), and the father of Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah. 1 Chronicles 7:3 records that "all five of them were chiefs."
event: The Bible does not record any specific deeds of his apart from his being recorded as a chief (1 Chronicles 7:3).

introduce: He is a person recorded as the father of Shuppim and Huppim (1 Chronicles 7:12).
He is a son born to Caleb's concubine Ephah, recorded together with Moza and Gazez (1 Chronicles 2:46).
event: He fathered Gazez (1 Chronicles 2:46).

introduce: He is a son of Terah, a brother of Abram and Nahor, and the father of Lot, Milcah, and Iscah (Genesis 11:26-29).
lifetime: He died in Ur of the Chaldeans, his native land, before his father Terah (Genesis 11:28).
event: His son Lot later went to the land of Canaan with Abram (Genesis 12:4).

call: Father of Aharhel (genealogy of the descendants of Judah)
introduce: Harum is a person recorded as the father of Aharhel (1 Chronicles 4:8).
lifetime: In the genealogy of the descendants of Judah in 1 Chronicles 4, his name appears only in the phrase "the clans of Aharhel son of Harum," and his life is not recorded in the Bible (1 Chronicles 4:8).

introduce: Hazarmaveth is one of the sons born to Joktan, the son of Eber (Genesis 10:26, 1 Chronicles 1:20).
lifetime: In the list of the sons born to Joktan, his name is recorded third, after Almodad and Sheleph, and the Bible has no record of the rest of his life (Genesis 10:26, 1 Chronicles 1:20).
event: Hazarmaveth is recorded as a son of Joktan together with Almodad, Sheleph, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Obal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab (Genesis 10:26-29). Their dwelling place was the hill country of the east, on the way from Mesha toward Sephar (Genesis 10:30). The biblical text does not record any specific event that he himself carried out.

call: Wife of Ashhur (mother of Zereth, Zohar, and Ethnan)
introduce: Helah is a woman recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah as one of the two wives of Ashhur, the father of Tekoa (1 Chronicles 4:5).
lifetime: Ashhur's two wives were Helah and Naarah (1 Chronicles 4:5), and Helah's sons are recorded as Zereth, Zohar, and Ethnan (1 Chronicles 4:7).

introduce: Gazez is a person recorded as the son of Haran, who was born to Caleb's concubine Ephah (1 Chronicles 2:46).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 2:46 records that Caleb's concubine Ephah bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez, and that Haran fathered Gazez (1 Chronicles 2:46). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.

introduce: Candace is a person recorded as the queen of the Ethiopians. Acts 8:27 records that an Ethiopian eunuch who was in charge of all her treasury was a man of great authority (Acts 8:27).
lifetime: Apart from the mention of her position as queen of the Ethiopians and of the eunuch who was in charge of her treasury, the Bible has no record of the life of Candace (Acts 8:27).

기타관계: Ethiopian eunuch#4763(official in charge of the treasury)

call: Son of Hebron (Caleb's descendants, tribe of Judah)
introduce: Korah is a person recorded as one of the four sons of Hebron (Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema) (1 Chronicles 2:43).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 2:43 records that the sons of Hebron were Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema (1 Chronicles 2:43). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.

introduce: Putiel is a person recorded as the man from whose daughters Eleazar, the son of Aaron, took a wife (Exodus 6:25).
lifetime: Exodus 6:25 records that Eleazar took a wife from the daughters of Putiel, and that she bore Phinehas (Exodus 6:25). Putiel's own deeds are not recorded.

call: Son of Jeiel (of the descendants of Asaph), father of Zechariah
introduce: Benaiah is a person recorded as the son of Jeiel, of the descendants of Asaph, the father of Zechariah, and the grandfather of Jahaziel (2 Chronicles 20:14).
lifetime: 2 Chronicles 20:14 records Jahaziel the Levite as "the great-great-grandson of Mattaniah of the descendants of Asaph, the great-grandson of Jeiel, the grandson of Benaiah, and the son of Zechariah" (2 Chronicles 20:14). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.

call: Son of Amzi, father of Jeroham
introduce: Pelaliah is a person recorded as the grandson of Zechariah, the son of Amzi, and the father of Jeroham (Nehemiah 11:12).
lifetime: Nehemiah 11:12 records Adaiah as "the son of Jeroham, the grandson of Pelaliah, the great-grandson of Amzi, the great-great-grandson of Zechariah, a descendant of Pashhur in the fifth generation, and a descendant of Malchijah in the sixth generation" (Nehemiah 11:12). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.

call: Son of Bebai (chief of the Bebai clan who came up with Ezra)
introduce: Zechariah is a person recorded as the son of Bebai, who represented the descendants of Bebai among the chiefs who came up from Babylon with Ezra (Ezra 8:1, 8:11).
lifetime: Ezra 8:11 records that, from the descendants of Bebai, there was Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men (Ezra 8:11).

introduce: Zimri is a person recorded as one of the five sons of Zerah, the son of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:6).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 2:6 records that the sons of Zerah were Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara, five in all (1 Chronicles 2:6). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.

introduce: Abishua is a person recorded as one of the sons of Bela, the firstborn son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:1, 8:3-4).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 8:3-5 records the sons of Bela as Addar, Gera, Abihud, Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah, Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram (1 Chronicles 8:3-5). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.

introduce: Addar is a person recorded as one of the sons of Bela, the firstborn son of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:1, 8:3).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 8:3-5 records the sons of Bela as Addar, Gera, Abihud, Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah, Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram (1 Chronicles 8:3-5). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.

call: Son of Seraiah (grandson of Kenaz), forefather of Ge-harashim
introduce: Joab is a person recorded as the son of Seraiah, the son of Kenaz, and he is said to be the forefather of Ge-harashim (1 Chronicles 4:13-14).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 4:13-14 records that the sons of Kenaz were Othniel and Seraiah, that Seraiah fathered Joab, that Joab was the father of those living in Ge-harashim, and that they were craftsmen (1 Chronicles 4:14). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.

기타관계: Ge-harashim#125(descendant; the text records Joab as the father of those living in Ge-harashim)

introduce: Hathath is a person recorded as the son of Othniel, the son of Kenaz (1 Chronicles 4:13).
lifetime: 1 Chronicles 4:13 records that the sons of Kenaz were Othniel and Seraiah, and that the son of Othniel was Hathath (1 Chronicles 4:13). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.

call: Son of Jeiel (father of Kish, ancestor of Saul)
introduce: Ner is a person recorded in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 9 as one of the sons of Jeiel, the forefather of Gibeon (1 Chronicles 9:35-36). The same genealogy records him as an ancestor of King Saul, saying that Ner fathered Kish and Kish fathered Saul (1 Chronicles 8:33; 9:39). Whether he is the same person as Ner, the father of Abner in 1 Samuel 14:50-51 (Saul's uncle, a son of Abiel), cannot be settled from the text, so he is kept as a separate entry.
lifetime: He is listed among the sons of Jeiel in 1 Chronicles 9:36 and recorded as the father of Kish (1 Chronicles 9:36, 39). The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.

introduce: Bered was a descendant of Ephraim, recorded as the son of Shuthelah and the father of Tahath (1 Chronicles 7:20).
lifetime: In the genealogy of Ephraim in 1 Chronicles 7:20, he appears as the son of Shuthelah and the father of Tahath. The Bible has no record of the rest of his life.

call: The Shulammite woman of the Song of Solomon
introduce: She is the Shulammite woman who is called to return in the Song of Solomon (Song of Solomon 6:13). The text does not state this woman's parents or her city of origin.

introduce: He is recorded between Mica and Hashabiah in the list of Levites who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:9-11).
event: He is recorded between Mica and Hashabiah in the list of Levites who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:9-11).

call: Third son of Judah (ancestor of the Shelanite clan)
introduce: Shelah was the third son whom Judah had by the daughter of Shua the Canaanite, and the younger brother of Er and Onan (Genesis 38:2-5, 1 Chronicles 2:3). When he was born, Judah was at Chezib (Genesis 38:5).
lifetime: After Er and Onan died, Judah told his daughter-in-law Tamar to wait until Shelah grew up, but even after Shelah had grown up he did not give him to Tamar (Genesis 38:11, 14, 26). Shelah is recorded among the sons of Judah who went down to Egypt with Jacob (Genesis 46:12).
event: In the census in Numbers, the Shelanite clan, descended from Shelah, is recorded among the clans of the descendants of Judah (Numbers 26:20). First Chronicles records among Shelah's descendants Er the father of Lecah and Laadah the father of Mareshah (1 Chronicles 4:21).

introduce: Anah was a child of Zibeon the Hivite and the father of Oholibamah, the wife of Esau (Genesis 36:2, 14, 24-25). First Chronicles records him as a son of Zibeon (1 Chronicles 1:40). He is a different person from Anah the son of Seir (Genesis 36:20).
lifetime: He found the hot springs in the wilderness while he was pasturing the donkeys of his father Zibeon (Genesis 36:24).
event: Anah's children were Dishon and Oholibamah; Oholibamah became the wife of Esau and bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah (Genesis 36:14, 25). First Chronicles records Anah's son Dishon and Dishon's sons Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran (1 Chronicles 1:41).

introduce: Alphaeus is recorded as the father of James, one of the twelve apostles (Matthew 10:3, Mark 3:18, Luke 6:15, Acts 1:13).
lifetime: Scripture records nothing of Alphaeus's own deeds; his name appears only in the description "James son of Alphaeus" (Matthew 10:3).

introduce: Alphaeus is recorded as the father of Levi, who was sitting at the tax booth when Jesus called him (Mark 2:14). The Gospel of Matthew calls this man Matthew in the account of the same call (Matthew 9:9).
lifetime: Scripture records nothing of Alphaeus's own deeds; his name appears only in the description "Levi son of Alphaeus" (Mark 2:14). The text does not indicate whether he is the same person as Alphaeus the father of James (Matthew 10:3).

call: The man who held up Moses' hands (with Aaron)
introduce: Hur was a man who was with Moses and Aaron in the wilderness period after the exodus. When Israel fought against Amalek at Rephidim, he held up Moses' hands together with Aaron (Exodus 17:10-12), and when Moses went up the mountain of God, he was put in charge of the people's affairs together with Aaron (Exodus 24:14). The Bible does not state his genealogy, and whether he is the same person as Hur the grandfather of Bezalel (1 Chronicles 2:19-20) is not indicated in the text (Jewish tradition regards them as the same person).
lifetime: When Joshua fought against Amalek, Hur went up to the top of the hill with Moses and Aaron (Exodus 17:10). As he went up the mountain of God, Moses said to the elders, "Aaron and Hur are here with you. Whoever has a dispute can go to them" (Exodus 24:14).
event: When Moses' hands grew heavy, Aaron and Hur took a stone and put it under Moses so that he sat on it, and one on each side held up his hands so that they remained steady until the sun went down. As a result, Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his army (Exodus 17:12-13).

introduce: Hobab was the son of Reuel the Midianite, the man whom Moses asked to go with them on the journey through the wilderness (Numbers 10:29). In Numbers 10:29 his father Reuel is Moses' father-in-law, so Hobab would be Moses' brother-in-law, but Judges 4:11 calls Hobab 'the father-in-law of Moses.' The wording of the two passages differs.
lifetime: When Moses asked, 'Come with us, and we will treat you well,' Hobab answered, 'I will not go; instead, I am going back to my own land and my own people' (Numbers 10:29-30). Moses then asked him again to come with them, saying, 'You know how we are to camp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes' (Numbers 10:31-32).
event: According to Judges 4:11, Heber the Kenite, a descendant of 'Hobab the father-in-law of Moses,' moved away from his own people and pitched his tent by the great tree of Zaanannim, near Kedesh.

기타관계: Moses#930(brother-in-law, sister's husband (Numbers 10:29) or son-in-law (Judges 4:11), textual difference)

call: A Benjamite (father of Jakim, Shimrath, and others)
introduce: Shimei appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles 8, and Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath are recorded as his sons (1 Chronicles 8:19-21).
lifetime: The men in this list, including his sons, were all heads of families and chiefs by their generations, and they lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:28).

call: Of the descendants of Joab (father of Obadiah)
introduce: Jehiel is the father of Obadiah, who appears in the list of family heads who came up from Babylon with Ezra as 'Obadiah son of Jehiel, from the descendants of Joab' (Ezra 8:9).

call: Of the descendants of Elam (father of Shecaniah)
introduce: Jehiel is the father of Shecaniah, who appears as 'Shecaniah son of Jehiel, an Elamite' (Ezra 10:2).

call: Son of Joel (father of Amasai, descendant of Kohath)
introduce: Elkanah is a Levite of the descendants of Kohath who appears in the genealogy of Heman in 1 Chronicles 6; he is the son of Joel and the father of Amasai (1 Chronicles 6:36). Following 1 Chronicles 6:25, 'The descendants of Elkanah: Amasai, Ahimoth,' Ahimoth too is regarded as his son.

call: Father of Joah the recorder (in the time of Hezekiah)
meaning: one who gathers and heaps up
introduce: Asaph is named as the father of Joah the recorder in the time of King Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:18, 37; Isaiah 36:3, 22). The text does not show whether he is the same person as the Asaph who was in charge of praise in the time of David, or whether he is meant to be a descendant of that Asaph.

call: Father of Kish (descendant of Merari in the time of Hezekiah)
introduce: Abdi is named as 'Kish son of Abdi from the Merarites' among the Levites who set to work to cleanse the temple in the time of King Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 29:12).

Barzillai is the father of Adriel, the husband of Merab, Saul's daughter, and is recorded as 'Barzillai the Meholathite' (2 Samuel 21:8; compare 'Adriel the Meholathite' in 1 Samuel 18:19). He is a different person from Barzillai the Gileadite (2 Samuel 19:31).

call: Father of Pelatiah (in the time of Ezekiel)
introduce: Benaiah is the father of Pelatiah, a leader of the people whom Ezekiel saw in a vision at the east gate of the house of the LORD (Ezekiel 11:1, 13).

call: Son of Zimmah (Gershonite genealogy, father of Iddo)
introduce: Joah appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Gershon in 1 Chronicles 6 as the son of Zimmah and the father of Iddo (1 Chronicles 6:20-21).

call: Son of Zimmah (a Gershonite in the time of Hezekiah)
introduce: Joah is named among the Levites who set to work to cleanse the temple in the time of King Hezekiah as 'Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah from the Gershonites' (2 Chronicles 29:12).
Eliakim is a figure who appears above Jonam in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke (Luke 3:30). He belongs to a different line from Eliakim the son of Abiud in Matthew 1:13.
Joiarib is a figure who appears above Adaiah in the genealogy of Maaseiah, a descendant of Judah, in Nehemiah 11:5. He is a different person from Joiarib the priest in Nehemiah 11:10.

call: Father of Bela, king of Edom
introduce: Beor is the father of Bela, a king who ruled the land of Edom before there was a king over Israel (Genesis 36:32; 1 Chronicles 1:43). There is no text saying that he is the same person as Beor the father of Balaam (Numbers 22:5).

call: Son of Neariah (royal descendant of David)
introduce: Hizkiah is a man recorded as a son of Neariah in the genealogy of the royal descendants of David in 1 Chronicles 3 (1 Chronicles 3:23).
Shephuphan is recorded as one of the sons of Bela in the genealogy of the descendants of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles 8 (1 Chronicles 8:3-5).

call: Son of Ebiasaph (father of Tahath, descendant of Kohath)
introduce: Assir is a man recorded in the genealogy of the descendants of Kohath in 1 Chronicles 6 as the son of Ebiasaph and the father of Tahath (1 Chronicles 6:23, 37). He is a different person from Assir the son of Korah (Exodus 6:24).

Abiezer is recorded as a son born to Hammolecheth, the sister of Gilead (1 Chronicles 7:17-18). Some regard him as belonging to the same family as Iezer (Abiezer), the son of Gilead in Numbers 26:30, but the two passages record his parents differently.

call: Son of Zadok (priest in the time of Solomon)
introduce: Azariah is a man recorded in the list of King Solomon's officials as 'Azariah son of Zadok was the priest' (1 Kings 4:2).

call: Son of Caleb and Maacah (father of Madmannah)
introduce: Shaaph was a son born to Caleb's concubine Maacah and is recorded as 'Shaaph father of Madmannah' (1 Chronicles 2:48-49). He is a different person from Shaaph the son of Jahdai (1 Chronicles 2:47).

call: Levite musician before the ark (time of David)
introduce: Jehiel was a Levite of the second rank whom David appointed when he brought up the ark of God; he was one of those who played the harps according to Alamoth (1 Chronicles 15:18, 20), and he was also included among the company of Asaph who served before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:5).

call: Son of Hachmoni (attendant to the king's sons)
introduce: Jehiel was the son of Hachmoni and attended to the sons of King David (1 Chronicles 27:32).
Jehiel was a son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah and a younger brother of Jehoram (2 Chronicles 21:2). After Jehoram took the throne, he put all his brothers to the sword (2 Chronicles 21:4).

call: A Levite who oversaw the gifts in the time of Hezekiah
introduce: Jehiel was one of the Levites who, in the time of King Hezekiah, were overseers of the contributions, tithes, and dedicated gifts under the authority of Conaniah and his brother Shimei (2 Chronicles 31:12-13).

call: One in charge of the house of God in the time of Josiah
introduce: Jehiel is the man who, at the Passover of King Josiah, together with Hilkiah and Zechariah, as 'the administrators of the house of God,' gave the priests 2,600 sheep and 300 bulls as Passover offerings (2 Chronicles 35:8).

call: Son of Jeduthun (gatekeeper and musician before the ark)
meaning: Servant of Edom, one who serves
introduce: Obed-edom was a Levite whom David appointed when he brought up the ark of God; together with Jeiel he became a gatekeeper and one who played the lyres (1 Chronicles 15:18, 21), and together with Jehiah he guarded the gate before the ark (1 Chronicles 15:24). He was also included among the company of Asaph who served before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:5), and as 'Obed-edom son of Jeduthun' he became a gatekeeper together with Hosah (1 Chronicles 16:38). Whether he is the same person as Obed-edom the chief of the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26:4-8) cannot be determined from the text alone.

call: Of the descendants of Harim (a priest who took a foreign wife)
introduce: Jehiel is a priest recorded as one of the descendants of Harim in the list of those who took foreign women as wives in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:18, 21).

call: Of the descendants of Elam (one who took a foreign wife)
introduce: Jehiel is a man recorded as one of the descendants of Elam in the list of those who took foreign women as wives in the time of Ezra (Ezra 10:26).

call: Of the descendants of Asher (father of Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara)
introduce: Jether is a man recorded as the father of Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara in the genealogy of the descendants of Asher in 1 Chronicles 7 (1 Chronicles 7:38). Some regard him as the same person as Ithran the son of Zophah in the immediately preceding verse (1 Chronicles 7:37), but the text does not say so.

Zerah appears in the genealogy of Gershom, a descendant of Levi; he is the son of Iddo and the father of Jeatherai (1 Chronicles 6:21). He is a different person from Zerah the son of Adaiah in 1 Chronicles 6:41.
lifetime: He is recorded in the genealogy that continues from Gershom through Libni, Jahath, Zimmah, Joah, Iddo, Zerah, and Jeatherai (1 Chronicles 6:20-21).
